children.translated_text: But [the objection is raised]: since the Self is the object of the 'I'-cognition, it is untenable to say that it is known only in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>.

children.text:
na /
tatsākṣitvena pratyuktatvāt /
nahyahaṃpratyayaviṣayakartṛvyatirekeṇa tatsākṣī sarvabhūtasthaḥ sama ekaḥ kūṭasthanityaḥ puruṣo vidhikāṇḍe tarkasamaye vā kenacidadhigataḥ sarvasyātmā, ataḥ sa na kenacitpratyākhyātuṃ śakyo vidhiśeṣatvaṃ vā netum /
asmatvādeva ca sarveṣāṃ na heyo nāpyupādeyaḥ /
sarvaṃ hi vinaśyadvikārajātaṃ puruṣāntaṃ vinaśyati /
puruṣo vināśahetvābhāvādavināśī, vikriyāhetvabhāvācca, kūṭasthanityaḥ, ata eva nityāśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvaḥ /
tasmāt 'puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭā sā parā gatiḥ' (kāṭha. 1.3.11) 'taṃ tvaupaniṣadaṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchāmi' (bṛha. 3.9.23) iti caupaniṣadatvaviśeṣaṇaṃ puruṣasyopaniṣatsu prādhānyena prakāśyamānatva upapadyate /
ato bhūtavastuparo vedabhāgo nāstīti vacanaṃ sāhasamātram /
yadapi śāstratātparyavidāmanukramaṇam- 'dṛṣṭo hi tasyārthaḥ karmāvabodhanam' ityevamādi, taddharmajijñāsāviṣayatvādvidhipratiṣedhāśāstrābhiprāyaṃ draṣṭavyam /
apica 'āmnāyasya kriyārthatvādānarthakyamatarthānām' ityetadekāntenābhyupagacchatāṃ bhūtopadeśānārthakyaprasaṅgaḥ /
pravṛtti nivṛttividhitaccheṣavyatirekeṇa bhūtaṃ cedvastūpadiśati bhavyārthatvena, kūṭasthanityaṃ bhūtaṃ nopadiśatīti ko hetuḥ /
nahi bhūtamupadiśyamānaṃ kriyā bhavati /
akriyātve 'pi bhūtasya kriyāsādhanatvātkriyārthaṃ eva bhūtopadeśa iti cet /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
kriyārthatve 'pi kriyātivartanaśaktimadvastūpadiṣṭameva /
kriyārthatvaṃ tu prayojanaṃ tasya /
na caitāvatā vastvanupadiṣṭaṃ bhavati /
yadi nāmopadiṣṭaṃ kiṃ tava tena syāditi /
children.translated_text:
No. Because it has been explained as the witness of that [I-cognition].
For no one — not in the ritual portion [of the <s>Veda</s>], nor in the logical treatises — has ever ascertained the witness of that [I-cognition], distinct from the agent who is the object of the 'I'-cognition, abiding in all beings, uniform, single, immovable, and eternal, as the Self of all. Therefore, that [Self] cannot be denied by anyone, nor can it be made subsidiary to injunctions.
And being the Self of all, it is neither to be abandoned nor adopted.
For everything that is a product of modification, being perishable, perishes within the limits of the person [the Self]. But the person, due to the absence of a cause for destruction, is imperishable; and due to the absence of a cause for modification, is immovable and eternal. For that very reason, it is of a nature that is eternally pure, awakened, and free.
Therefore, 'There is nothing higher than the person — that is the ultimate end, that is the highest goal' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.11); and the characterization of the person as belonging to the <s>Upaniṣads</s> — 'I ask you about that person who is the subject of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.23) — is fitting, since the person is predominantly illuminated in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>.
Therefore, the statement 'there is no portion of the <s>Veda</s> that teaches established reality' is mere rashness.
As for the enumeration by those who know the purport of the <s>śāstras</s> — 'For its meaning is seen [to be]: the teaching of action' and so forth — that, being concerned with the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>, should be understood as having the intention of injunctions and prohibitions.
Moreover, for those who unconditionally accept that 'because the <s>Āmnāya</s> has action as its purpose, statements not serving that purpose are meaningless,' there is the unwanted consequence of the meaninglessness of teaching established facts.
If, apart from injunctions of activity and cessation and what is subsidiary to them, one teaches an established reality for the purpose of future benefit, what reason is there to say it does not teach an immovable, eternal, established reality?
For a fact being taught does not become an action.
If it is said that even though a fact is not an action, because a fact serves as a means for action, the teaching of a fact is itself for the sake of action —
this is not a fault.
Even if it is for the sake of action, it is a reality having the power to transcend action that is taught.
Being for the sake of action is merely its purpose.
And the reality is not thereby untaught.
'Even if it is taught, what good is it to you?' — if this is [asked]:

children.text:
ucyate- anavagatātmavastūpadeśaśca tathaiva bhavitumarhati /
tadavagatyā mithyājñānasya saṃsārahetornivṛttiḥ prayojanaṃ kriyata ityavāśiṣṭamarthavattvaṃ kriyāsādhanavastūpadeśena /
apica 'brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ' iti caivamādyā nivṛttirupadiśyate /
naca sā kriyā /
nāpi kriyāsādhanam /
akriyārthānāmupadeśo 'narthakaścet 'brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ' ityādinivṛttyupadeśānāmānarthakyaṃ prāptam /
taccāniṣṭam /
naca svābhāvaprāptahantyarthānurāgeṇa nañaḥ śakyamaprāptakriyārthatvaṃ kalpayituṃ, hananakriyānivṛttyaudāsīnyavyatirekeṇa /
nañaścaiṣa svabhāvo yatsvasaṃbandhino 'bhāvaṃ bodhayatīti /
abhāvabuddhiścaudāsīnyakāraṇam /
sā ca dagdhendhanāgnivatsvayamevopāśāmyati /
tasmātprasaktakriyānivṛttyaudāsīnyameva 'brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ' ityādiṣu pratiṣedhārthaṃ manyāmahe, anyatra prajāpatitrātādibhyaḥ /
tasmātpuruṣārthānupayogyupākhyānādibhūtārthavādaviṣayamānarthakyābhidhānaṃ draṣṭavyam /
yadapyuktaṃ- kartavyavidhyanupraveśamantareṇa vastumātramucyamānamānarthakaṃ syāt 'saptadvīpā vasumatī' tyādivaditi, tatparihṛtam /
rajuriyaṃ nāyaṃ sarpa iti vastumātrakathane 'pi prayojanasya dṛṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text:
The answer is: the teaching of a reality about the Self, not previously known, can indeed be just so. The cessation of false knowledge — which is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> — through the realization of that [Self-reality] is the purpose served. The meaningfulness of the teaching of a fact that serves as a means for action is thus undiminished.
Moreover, cessation is taught in [statements] such as 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be killed,' and the like. And that is not action. Nor is it a means for action.
If the teaching of what is not directed toward action is meaningless, then the meaninglessness of teachings of cessation like 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be killed' would follow.
And that is undesirable.
Nor, on account of attachment to the naturally obtained meaning of the verb 'to kill,' can the negative particle be construed as having the purpose of an unobtained action, apart from the indifference [produced by] the cessation of the act of killing.
For the very nature of the negative particle is that it communicates the absence of what is connected with it.
And the cognition of absence is the cause of indifference.
And that [indifference] subsides by itself, like a fire whose fuel is consumed.
Therefore, in [statements] like 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be killed,' we understand the meaning of the prohibition to be indifference through the cessation of an incipient action — except in cases like [the prohibition against killing] <s>Prajāpati's</s> creatures and similar [where other purposes apply].
Therefore, the claim of meaninglessness should be understood as pertaining to <s>arthavāda</s>-type established facts, such as narratives and the like, that do not serve the human goal.
As for the statement: 'A mere assertion of fact, without entering into an injunction of something to be done, would be meaningless — just like "The earth has seven continents"' — that has been answered.
Because even in the mere statement of fact, 'This is a rope, not a snake,' a purpose is observed.

children.text: nanu śrutabrahmaṇo 'pi yathāpūrvaṃ saṃsāritvardānānna rajusvarūpakathanavadarthavattvamityuktam /
children.translated_text: But [the objection]: even for one who has heard about <s>Brahman</s>, since transmigration continues as before, the telling of the nature of the rope does not establish meaningfulness — this was stated.

children.text:
atrocyate- nāvagatabrahmātmabhāvasya yathāpūrvaṃ saṃsāritvaṃ śakyaṃ darśayituṃ va vedapramāṇajanitabrahmātmabhāvavirodhāt /
nahi śarīrādyātmābhimānino duḥkhabhayādimattvaṃ dṛṣṭamiti tasyaiva vedapramāṇajanitabrahmātmāvagame tadabhimānanivṛttau tadeva mithyājñānanimittaṃ duḥkhabhayādimattvaṃ bhavatīti śakyaṃ kalpayitum /
nahi dhanino gṛhasthasya dhanābhimānino dhanāpahāranimittaṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭamiti tasyaiva pravrajitasya dhanābhimānarahitasya tadeva dhanāpahranimittaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavati /
naca kuṇḍalinaḥ kuṇḍalitvābhimānanimittaṃ sukhaṃ dṛṣṭamiti tasyaiva kuṇḍalaviyuktasya kuṇḍalitvābhimānanimittaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati /
taduktaṃ śrutyā- 'ārīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ' (chāndo. 8.12.1) iti /
śarīre patite 'śarīratvaṃ syāt, na jīvata iti cenna, saśarīratvasya mithyājñānanimittattvāt /
na hyātmanaḥ śarīrātmābhimānalakṣaṇaṃ mithyājñānaṃ muktvānyataḥ saśarīratvaṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum /
nityamaśarīratvamakarmanimittattvādityavocāma /
tatkṛtadharmādharmanimittaṃ saśarīratvamiti cenna, śarīrasaṃbandhasyāsiddhatvāddharmādharmayorātmakṛtatvāsiddheḥ /
śarīrasaṃbandhasya dharmādharmayostatkṛtatvasya cetaretarāśrayatvaprasaṅgādandhaparamparaiṣānāditvakalpanā /
children.translated_text:
To this the reply: it is not possible to show that for one who has realized the Self as <s>Brahman</s>, transmigration continues as before, because this contradicts the realization of the Self as <s>Brahman</s> generated by the valid means of the <s>Veda</s>.
For it cannot be supposed that the suffering, fear, and such observed in one who identifies with the body and its attributes would persist even when, through the valid means of the <s>Veda</s>, realization of the Self as <s>Brahman</s> has occurred and that false identification has been removed — that the same suffering, fear, and such caused by false knowledge would continue.
For it is not the case that the suffering caused by the false sense of ownership of wealth, observed in a wealthy householder who identifies with wealth, would persist in that same person once he has renounced and is free from the false identification with wealth.
Nor is it the case that the happiness caused by the false identification as one who wears earrings, observed in such a person, would persist in that same person once separated from earrings.
Thus the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Verily, one who is bodiless is not touched by pleasure and pain' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.1).
If [the objection is]: when the body falls, there would be bodilessness, but not while alive — no, because the embodied state is caused by false knowledge.
For it is not possible to attribute embodiment to the Self from any source other than the false knowledge characterized by identification of the Self with the body.
We have said: disembodiment is eternal, because it is not caused by action.
If it is said: embodiment is caused by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> produced by it — no, because since the connection with the body is not established, the production of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> by the Self is not established.
Since the connection with the body and the production of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> by it would involve mutual dependence, one blindly resorts to the contrivance that it is beginningless.

children.text:
kriyāsamavāyābhāvāccāmtanaḥ kartṛtvānupapatteḥ /
saṃnidhānamātreṇa rājaprabhṛtīnāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kartavyamiti cenna, dhanadānādyupārjitabhṛtyasaṃbandhatvātteṣāṃ kartṛtvopapatteḥ /
na tvātmano dhanadānādivaccharīrādibhiḥ svasvāmisaṃbandhanimittaṃ kiñcicchakyaṃ kalpayitum /
mithyābhimānastu pratyakṣaḥ saṃbandhahetuḥ /
etena yajamānatvamātmano vyākhyātam /
atrāhuḥ- dehādivyatiriktasyātmana ātmīye dehādāvabhimāno gauṇo na mithyeti cenna, prasiddhavastubhedasya gauṇatvamukhyatvaprasiddheḥ /
yasya hi prasiddho vastubhedaḥ, yathā kesarādimānākṛtiviśeṣo 'nvayavyatirekābhyāṃ siṃhaśabdapratyayabhāṅmukhyo 'nyaḥ prasiddhaḥ tataścānyaḥ puruṣaḥ prāyikaiḥ krauryaśauryādibhiḥ siṃhaguṇaiḥ saṃpannaḥ siddhaḥ, tasya puruṣe siṃhaśabdapratyayau gauṇau bhavato nāprasiddhavastubhedasya /
tasya tvanyatrānyaśabdapratyayau bhrāntinimittāveva bhavato na gauṇau /
yathā mandāndhakāre sthāṇurayamityagṛhyamāṇaviśeṣe puruṣaśabdapratyayau sthāṇuviṣayau, yathāvā śuktikāyāmakasmādrajatamiti niścitau śabdapratyayau, tadvaddehādisaṃghāte 'hamiti nirupacāreṇa śabdapratyayāvātmānātmāvivekenotpadyamānau kathaṃ gauṇau śakyau vaditum /
ātmānātmavivekināmapi paṇḍitānāmajāvipālānāmivāviviktau śabdapratyayau bhavataḥ /
tasmāddehādivyatiriktātmāstitvavādināṃ dehādāvahaṃpratyayo mithyaiva na gauṇaḥ /
tasmānmithyāpratyayanimittatvātsaśarīratvasya, siddhaṃ jīvato 'pi viduṣo 'śarīratvam /
tathāca brahmavidviṣayā śrutiḥ- ' tadyathāhinirlvayanī valmīke mṛtā pratyastā śayītaivamevedaṃ śarīraṃ śete /
athāyamaśarīro 'mṛtaḥ prāṇo brahmaiva teja eva' (bṛha. 4.4.7) iti /
'sacakṣuracakṣuriva sakarṇo 'karṇa iva savāgavāgiva samanā amanā iva saprāṇo 'prāṇa iva' iti ca /
smṛtirapi ca- 'sthitaprajñasyakā bhāṣā' (bha.gī. 2.54) ityādyā sthitaprajñalakṣaṇānyācakṣāṇā viduṣaḥ sarvapravṛttyasaṃbandhaṃ darśayati /
tasmānnāvagatabrahmātmabhāvasya yathāpūrvaṃ saṃsāritvam /
yasya tu yathāpūrvaṃ saṃsāritvaṃ nāsāvavagatabrahmātmabhāva ityanavadyam /
yatpunaruktaṃ śravaṇātparācīnayormanananididhyāsanayordarśanādvadhiśeṣatvaṃ brahmaṇo na svarūpaparyavasāyitvamiti /
children.translated_text:
And because the Self cannot be an agent due to the impossibility of conjunction with action.
If it is said that mere proximity [suffices], as agency is seen in the case of kings and such — no, because their agency is established through the relationship of servants acquired through the giving of wealth and such.
But for the Self, no relationship of master and servant with the body and such, like the giving of wealth and such, can be supposed.
False identification, however, is the evident cause of the relationship.
By this, the sacrificial agency (<s>yajamānatva</s>) of the Self has also been explained.
Here they object: the identification with the body and such, which are not the Self, is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>), not false — but no, because figurative usage presupposes a well-established distinction of objects.
For only one whose distinction of objects is well-established — as, for example, the particular form with mane and such, ascertained through presence and absence as the primary referent of the word and concept 'lion,' is well-known as one thing, and a person endowed with the lionlike qualities of cruelty and valor is known as another — for such a one, the word and concept 'lion' as applied to the person are figurative. But not for one whose distinction of objects is not established.
For such a one, the word and concept applied to another thing are due to error alone, not figurative.
Just as in dim darkness, when the specific features of a post are not grasped, the word and concept 'person' are applied to the post; or just as the definite word and concept 'silver' are applied to a mother-of-pearl shell — in the same way, in the aggregate of the body and such, the word and concept 'I,' arising without figurative usage, from the non-discrimination of Self and non-Self — how can they be said to be figurative?
Even for learned ones who discriminate between Self and non-Self, the word and concept [of 'I' as applied to the body] arise without discrimination, just as for shepherds.
Therefore, for those who maintain the existence of a Self distinct from the body and such, the 'I'-cognition directed toward the body is false alone, not figurative.
Therefore, since embodiment is caused by false cognition, the bodilessness of the knower even while alive is established.
Thus also the <s>śruti</s> pertaining to the knower of <s>Brahman</s>: 'Just as the slough of a snake lies cast off on an anthill, even so this body lies. But this one — bodiless, immortal, <s>Prāṇa</s>, is <s>Brahman</s> itself, is light itself' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.7).
And: 'Having eyes, he is as if without eyes; having ears, as if without ears; having speech, as if without speech; having mind, as if without mind; having <s>prāṇa</s>, as if without <s>prāṇa</s>.'
The <s>smṛti</s> also: 'What is the description of one of steady wisdom?' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 2.54) and such — describing the characteristics of one of steady wisdom — shows the knower's disconnection from all activity.
Therefore, for one who has realized the Self as <s>Brahman</s>, there is no transmigration as before.
But for one who does transmigrate as before, he has not realized the Self as <s>Brahman</s> — this is beyond reproach.
As for the further statement: because reflection (<s>manana</s>) and meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>), which follow hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), are seen [to be required], <s>Brahman</s> has the character of being subsidiary [to an injunction] and does not culminate in [mere] realization of its own nature —

children.text:
na /
avagatyarthatvānmanananididhyāsanayoḥ /
yadi hyavagataṃ brahmānyatra viniyujyeta bhavettadā vidhiśeṣitvam /
natu tadasti, manananididhyāsanayorapi śravaṇavadavagatyarthatvāt /
tasmānna pratapattividhiviṣayatayā śāstrapramāṇakatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ saṃbhavatītyataḥ svatantrameva brahma śāstrapramāṇakaṃ vedāntavākyasamanvayāditi siddham /
evañca sati 'athāto brahmajijñāsā' iti tadviṣayaḥ pṛthakśāstramārambha upapadyate /
pratipattividhiparatve hi 'athāto dharmajijñāse'tyevārabdhatvānna pṛthakśāstramārabhyeta /
ārabhyamāṇaṃ caivamārabhyeta - 'athātaḥ pariśiṣṭadharmajijñāseti' ' athātaḥ kratvarthapuruṣārthayorjijñāsā' (jai. 4.1.1) itivat /
brahmātmaikyāvagatistvapratijñāteti tadartho yuktaḥ śāstrārambhaḥ- 'athāto brahmajijñāsā' iti /
children.translated_text:
No. Because reflection and meditation serve the purpose of realization.
For if, once <s>Brahman</s> were realized, it were applied to something else, then it would be subsidiary to an injunction.
But that is not the case, because reflection and meditation, like hearing, serve the purpose of realization.
Therefore, it is not possible for <s>Brahman</s> to have the character of being the subject of an injunction of practice, with scripture serving as the means of valid knowledge for that purpose. Thus it is established that <s>Brahman</s> is independently known through scripture as a means of valid knowledge, from the consistent harmonization (<s>samanvaya</s>) of the <s>Vedānta</s> statements.
This being so, the commencement of a separate <s>śāstra</s> devoted to this subject — 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>' — is justified.
For if [<s>Brahman</s>-knowledge] were directed toward an injunction of practice, since it would already be commenced under 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>,' a separate <s>śāstra</s> would not be commenced.
And if it were commenced, it would be commenced thus: 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into the remaining <s>dharma</s>,' or 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into the purpose of the ritual and the purpose of the person' — as in <s>Jaimini Sūtra</s> 4.1.1.
But the realization of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and the Self is not of that [injunctive] nature — therefore, the commencement of the <s>śāstra</s> for that purpose is justified: 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: tasmādahaṃ brahmāsmītyetadavasānā eva sarve viṣayaḥ sarvāṇi cetarāṇi pramāṇāni /
children.translated_text: Therefore, all objects [of knowledge] and all other means of valid knowledge have their culmination in this: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: nahyaheyānupādeyādvaitātmāvagatau nirviṣayāṇyapramātṛkāṇi ca pramāṇāni bhavitumarhantīti /
children.translated_text: For when the non-dual Self — which is neither to be abandoned nor adopted — is realized, the means of valid knowledge become without object and without a cognizing subject.

children.text: apicāhuḥ- 'gauṇamithyātmano 'sattve putradehādibādhanāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, they say: 'When the secondary and false selves are negated — through the sublation of son, body, and such —

children.text: sadbrahmātmāhamityevaṃ bodhe kāryaṃ kathaṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: in the awakening "I am the real <s>Brahman</s>, the Self" — how could there be any action to be done?

children.text: anveṣṭavyātmavijñānātprākpramātṛtvamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Prior to the knowledge of the Self that is to be sought, the Self has the status of a knower.

children.text: anviṣṭaḥ syātpramātaiva pāpmadoṣādivarjitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Once sought, the knower itself would be [revealed as] free from sin, faults, and such.

children.text:
dehātmapratyayo yadvatpramāṇatvena kalpitaḥ /
laukikaṃ tadvadevedaṃ pramāṇaṃ tvā'tmaniścayāt'
children.translated_text: Just as the identification of the Self with the body is assumed to have validity [for practical purposes], so too this [conventional] means of knowledge [is valid only] until the ascertainment of the Self' —
thus. // 4 //

children.text: iti catuḥsūtrī samāptā /
children.translated_text: Thus the four-<s>sūtra</s> section is complete.

children.text: FN: pūrvapakṣiṇā kriyāśeṣatayā brahma pratipādyata ityuktaṃ tadvyāvṛttyarthamiti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The opponent had stated that <s>Brahman</s> is to be taught as subsidiary to action — the purpose [of this passage] is to refute that. This is the intent.

children.text: pūrṇatayā juhūdvārā kratuśeṣatāvādātmano 'pi jñānadvārā karmaśeṣatvāttadarthā vedāntāstadvidhiśeṣā bhaviṣyantītyāśaṅkyāha tatkeneti /
children.translated_text: Anticipating the objection that — just as the Self, through full offering via the sacrificial ladle, is subsidiary to the ritual according to the <s>kratuśeṣatā</s> (sacrifice-subsidiary) doctrine, so too through the door of knowledge it would be subsidiary to action, and therefore the <s>Vedānta</s> texts would be supplements to injunctions of those [actions] — he says 'by what then' (<s>tatkena</s>).

children.text:
pratipattikarma pradhānakarmaśeṣāṅgaṃ /
yatha pradhānacaruhomottaraṃ tenaiva dravyeṇa sviṣṭakṛdbalidānādi /
yathāvā śrāddhe piṇḍapradānapūjottaraṃ piṇḍānāṃ gaṅgādipravāhe prakṣepaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>pratipattikarma</s> (rite of cognition) is a subsidiary component of the principal rite. Just as after the main oblation of cooked grain, with that very substance one performs the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, offering of remains, and so forth. Or, just as in a <s>śrāddha</s> ceremony, after the offering and worship of the rice-balls, the rice-balls are cast into the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and such.

children.text: anunapraveśo 'saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anupraveśa</s>' (entry into) means connection (<s>saṃbandha</s>).

children.text: pratipattervidhirniyogastasya viṣayabhūtāṃ pratipattipratyavacchedakatvema viṣayatayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The injunction of cognition (<s>pratipatti</s>) is an injunctive command — the meaning is: it serves as that which determines the cognition that is its object, in the capacity of being its object.

children.text: agnyādidevatoddeśena puroḍāśādidravyotsargo yāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is the offering of substances such as <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) and the like, directed toward deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others.

children.text: aśarīraṃ videhaṃ, priyāpriye sukhaduḥkhe /
children.translated_text: '<s>Aśarīram</s>' means bodiless (<s>videham</s>); '<s>priyāpriye</s>' means pleasure and pain (<s>sukhaduḥkhe</s>).

children.text:
kṛtākṛtāditi /
kṛtāt kāryāt, akṛtāt kāraṇāt /
tat brahma, avet viditavat /
valkalādivaccittarañjako rāgādikaṣāyo mṛditaḥ kṣālitaḥ vināśito yasya jñānavairāgyābhyāsakṣārajalena tasmai /
adhyāsaḥ śāstrato 'tasmiṃstaddhīḥ /
ādeśa upadeśaḥ /
pralayakāle vāyuragnyādīnsaṃvṛṇoti saṃharatīti saṃvargaḥ, svāpakāle prāṇo vāgādīnsaṃharatīti saṃhārakriyāyogātsaṃvargaḥ /
tat viditājjñānaviṣayādanyadbhinnam /
atho api aviditādajñānaviṣayādapi adhi anyat /
yadvācā śabdenānabhyuditamaprakāśitaṃ, yena bhmaṇā sā vāgabhyadyate prakāśyate /
'nivṛttiviṣayatvāt' bhā.pā. /
svātmano dharmānāśrayatve 'pi nityo dharmo mokṣākhyo bhaviṣyatītyabhiprāyeṇa dharmaśabdaḥ, svarūpaparo vā /
anyo jīvātmā /
pippalaṅkarmaphalam /
abhicākaśīti prakāśate /
karmādhyakṣaḥ karmaphalapradātā /
children.translated_text: 'From the created and uncreated' — 'from the created' means from the effect; 'from the uncreated' means from the cause. 'That' is <s>Brahman</s>; '<s>avet</s>' means 'has known.' One whose impurity of passion and such — which stains the mind like bark-cloth stains — has been crushed, washed away, destroyed by the alkaline water of the practice of knowledge and dispassion — to that one [this teaching is directed]. '<s>Adhyāsa</s>' (superimposition), according to scripture, is the cognition of one thing as another. '<s>Ādeśa</s>' means instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>). At the time of dissolution, the wind absorbs fire and such — thus '<s>saṃvarga</s>' (absorption); at the time of sleep, <s>prāṇa</s> absorbs speech and such — thus '<s>saṃvarga</s>' through the connection of the act of absorption. 'Different from that' — different from, distinct from, the object of knowledge that is known. 'And moreover, beyond the unknown' — other than, beyond even what is the object of ignorance. 'That which is not expressed, not illuminated, by speech, by words — by which <s>Brahman</s> speech itself is expressed, is illuminated.' '<s>Nivṛttiviṣayatvāt</s>' — because it is the object of cessation. [The word '<s>dharma</s>'] is used with the intention that even if the Self's attributes are not established as a basis, the eternal <s>dharma</s> called liberation will exist; or it is used in the sense of essential nature. 'Another' is the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>). '<s>Pippala</s>' means the fruit of action. '<s>Abhicākaśīti</s>' means 'shines forth.' 'Overseer of action' means the bestower of the fruits of action.

children.text:
śukramiti bāhyāśuddhiviraha uktaḥ /
avraṇamasnāviramityeva kāyaniṣedhe siddhe punastanniṣedho līlādhṛtaviṣaṇvādivigrahasyāpyanṛtatāpratipādanārthaḥ /
tathāca - 'māyā hyeṣā mayā sṛṣṭā yanmāṃ paśyasi nārada /
sarvabhūtaguṇairyuktaṃ maivaṃ māṃ draṣṭumarhasī' ti /
śarīropādānabhūtāvidyārāhityāya śuddhamiti /
tannimittarāhityāyāpāpaviddhamiti /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śukram</s>' (pure) — by this, the absence of external impurity is stated. 'Without wound, without sinews' — even when the negation of the body is already accomplished by [the word] '<s>avraṇam</s>' (woundless), the further negation [with '<s>asnāviram</s>'] is for the purpose of showing the unreality even of the body assumed in sport by <s>Viṣṇu</s> and such. As [it is said]: 'For this is <s>māyā</s> created by Me — that you see Me, O <s>Nārada</s>, endowed with the qualities of all beings. You should not look upon Me thus.' '<s>Śuddham</s>' (pure) is for [showing] freedom from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is the material cause of the body. '<s>Apāpaviddham</s>' (untouched by evil) is for [showing] freedom from its efficient cause.

children.text: atrānupraveśaḥ saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>anupraveśa</s>' (entry) means connection.

children.text:
mayedaṃ kāryamityavagatimān hi niyojyo bhavati /
kṛtisādhyaśca vidhiviṣayo bhavati /
jñānasya ca kṛtyasādhyatvānnobhayamātmajñānaṃ bhavatīti bhāvaḥ /
vidhicchāyāni prasiddhayāgādividhitulyāni /
pratyagātmani srotaścittavṛttipravāhaḥ /
'kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ prāptamityeva tuṣyati' pañca. /
anusaṃjvaret śarīraṃ paritapyamānamanutapyeta /
pramāpramārūpadhīmātraviṣayaḥ pratipattiśabdaḥ /
ā. /
'yaccāpnoti yadādatte yaccātti viṣayāniha /
yaccāsya saṃtato bhāvastasmādātmeti bhaṇyate' iti /
ahaṃpratyayaviṣaya aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣaḥ /
ahaṃpratyayaviṣayo yaḥ kartā kāryakaraṇasaṃghātopahito jīvātmā tadvyatirekeṇa /
'ityevamādyā' bhā.pā. /
children.translated_text: For one who has the understanding 'this task is to be done by me' is indeed one who can be enjoined. And the object of an injunction is something accomplishable through effort. Since knowledge is not accomplishable through effort, neither [aspect] applies to self-knowledge — this is the purport. 'Shadows of injunctions' means [statements that are] similar to well-known injunctions of sacrifice and such. '<s>Pratyagātman</s>' means the innermost Self; '<s>srotas</s>' means the stream of mental modifications. 'Having done what was to be done, having attained what was to be attained — one is satisfied with just that' (<s>Pañcadaśī</s>). '<s>Anusaṃjvaret</s>' — would feel pain along with the body that is being heated. The word '<s>pratipatti</s>' refers to what is merely the object of cognition in the form of valid and invalid [knowledge]. '<s>Ā</s>.' [abbreviation for a source text]. 'That which pervades, that which absorbs, that which enjoys objects here, and that whose existence is continuous — therefore it is called <s>ātman</s>' — thus. The <s>Upaniṣadic</s> <s>Puruṣa</s> is the object of the 'I'-cognition. The individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) — the agent who is the object of the 'I'-cognition, superimposed upon the aggregate of body and organs — is different from that [<s>Upaniṣadic</s> <s>Puruṣa</s>]. 'And such beginning with these' — [from] the <s>Bhāṣya</s> section.

children.text:
baṭorvratamityupakrāntaṃ 'nekṣetodyantamādityaṃ' ityādi prajāpativratam /
vidhyanupraveśo vidhisaṃbandhaḥ /
kūṭasthasya kṛtyayogānna kartṛtvamityarthaḥ /
śabdaḥ śābdavodhaścetyarthaḥ /
nirupacāreṇa guṇajñānaṃvinā /
śravaṇamananakuśalatāmātreṇa paṇḍitānāṃ anutpannasākṣātkārāṇāmitiyāvat /
ahinirlvayanī sarpatvak valmīkādau pratyastā nikṣiptā mṛtā sarpeṇa tyaktābhimānā vartata evamityādyūhyam /
brahmasākṣātkāro 'vagatistadarthatvāt /
vidhiśeṣatvena brahmārpaṇe 'pi /
athāta iti tṛtīye śrutyādibhiḥ śeṣaśeṣitve siddhe satyanantaraṃ śeṣiṇaiva śeṣasya prayuktisaṃbhavātkonāma kratave kovā puruṣārtāyeti jijñāsā pravṛttā caturthādau /
children.translated_text: 'The observance of the celibate student' — what was begun [as a topic] — '<s>nekṣetodyantamādityam</s>' (one should not look at the rising sun) and such is the <s>Prajāpati</s> observance. 'Entry into the injunction' means connection with the injunction. The meaning is: for the immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) [Self], there is no agency because of the inapplicability of action. '<s>Śabda</s>' means both the word and the verbal understanding — this is the meaning. Without figurative usage — without the knowledge of [mere] attributes. 'By the mere skill in hearing and reflection' — meaning: of scholars who have not yet attained direct realization. 'Like a cast-off snake-skin' — a snake-skin discarded by the snake, thrown away in an ant-hill and such, dead, abandoned with [the snake's] sense of identity — it continues to exist in that way — and so forth should be understood. The direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> is understanding (<s>avagati</s>), because it has that as its purpose. Even in the case of offering to <s>Brahman</s> as subsidiary to an injunction — [this point holds]. In the third [<s>adhyāya</s>], with '<s>athāta</s>,' when the subsidiary-principal relation is established through scripture and such, since the subsidiary can be employed by the principal alone after its [establishment], the inquiry 'for what ritual or for what human purpose?' is undertaken beginning in the fourth [<s>adhyāya</s>].

children.text:
tasmāt jñānasya prameyapramātṛbādhakatvābhāvāt /
gaumeti /
putradārādiṣvātmābhimāno gauṇaḥ tatra bhedānubhavāt /
dehendriyādiṣapa tvabhedānubhavānna gauṇaḥ kintu mithyā /
tadubhayātmano 'satve putradehādibādhanāt- gauṇātmano 'satve putrakalatrādibādhanaṃ, mithyātmano 'satve dehendriyādibādhanaṃ ca /
tathāca lokayātrakāryaṃ sadbrahmāhamiti bodhakāryaṃ- advaitasākṣātkāraśca kathaṃ bhavet /
anveṣṭavyātmavijñānāt- 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā', so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ iti tadvijñānātpūrvamātmano mātṛtvaṃ pramāprameyapramāṇavibhāgaśca /
tena tadabhāve kāryaṃ notpadyata ityarthaḥ /
ātmaniścayāt ābrahmasvarūpasākṣātkārādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because knowledge does not sublate the object of knowledge or the knower. '<s>Gaum</s>' — [the example of] a cow. The identification of the Self with sons, wife, and such is secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), because difference is experienced there. But with the body, senses, and such, because no difference is experienced, [the identification] is not secondary but rather false (<s>mithyā</s>). When both [kinds of] self are negated — through the sublation of sons, body, and such: the sublation of the secondary self is [the negation of identification with] sons, wife, and such; the sublation of the false self is [the negation of identification with] body, senses, and such. And thus, how could there be any worldly activity, or any action born of the awakening 'I am the real <s>Brahman</s>' — that is, the direct realization of non-duality? 'Prior to the knowledge of the Self that is to be sought' — '<s>ya ātmāpahatapāpmā</s>' (the Self that is free from evil) — 'that is to be sought': prior to the knowledge of that, the Self has the status of a knower, with the distinction of valid cognition, object of cognition, and means of cognition. The meaning is: therefore, in the absence of that [realization], action is not produced. '<s>Ātmaniścayāt</s>' means: until the direct realization of the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: 5 īkṣatyadhikaraṇam / sū. 5 - 11
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Īkṣati Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of 'Seeing'). <s>Sūtras</s> 5-11.

children.text:
evaṃ tāvadvedāntavākyānāṃ brahmātmāvagatiprayojanānāṃ brahmātmani tātparyeṇa samanvitānāmantareṇāpi kāryānupraveśaṃ, brahmaṇi paryavasānamuktam /
brahma ca sarvajñaṃ sarvaśakti jagadutpattisthitināśakāraṇamityuktam /
sāṃkhyādayastu pariniṣṭhitaṃ vastu pramāṇāntaragamyameveti manyamānāḥ pradhānādīni kāraṇāntarāṇyanumimānāstatparatayaiva vedāntavākyāni yojayanti /
sarveṣveva vedāntavākyeṣu sṛṣṭiviṣayeṣvanumānenaiva kāryeṇa kāraṇaṃ lilakṣayiṣitam /
pradhānapuruṣasaṃyogā nityānumeyā iti sāṃkhyā manyante /
kāṇādāstvetebhya eva vākyebhya īśvaraṃ nimittakāraṇamanumimate aṇūṃśca samavāyikāraṇam /
evamanye 'pi tārkikā vākyābhāsayuktyābhāsāvaṣṭambhāḥ pūrvapakṣavādina ihottiṣṭante /
tatra padavākyapramāṇajñenācāryeṇa vedāntavākyānāṃ brahmāvagatiparatvadarśanāya vākyābhāsayuktābhāsavipratipattayaḥ pūrvapakṣīkṛtya nirākriyante /
tatra sāṃkhyāḥ pradhānaṃ triguṇamacetanaṃ jagataḥ kāraṇamiti manyamānā āhuḥ- yāni vedāntavākyāni sarvajñasya sarvaśakterbrahmaṇo jagatkāraṇatvaṃ darśayantītyavocastāni pradhānakāraṇapakṣe 'pi yojayituṃ śakyante /
sarvaśaktitvaṃ tāvatpradhānasyāpi svavikāraviṣayamupapadyate /
evaṃ sarvajñatvamapyupapadyate /
katham /
yattu jñānaṃ manyase sa sattvadharmaḥ , 'sattvātsaṃjāyate jñānam' (gī. 14.17) iti smṛteḥ /
tena ca sattvadharmeṇa jñānena kāryakāraṇavantaḥ puruṣāḥ sarvajñā yoginaḥ prasiddhāḥ /
sattvasya hi niratiśayotkarṣe sarvajñatvaṃ prasiddham /
na kevalasyākāryakāraṇasya puruṣopalabdhimātrasya sarvajñatvaṃ kiñcijjñatvaṃ vā kalpayituṃ śakyam /
triguṇatvāttu pradhānasya sarvajñānakāraṇabhūtaṃ sattvaṃ pradhānāvasthāyāmapi vidyata iti pradhānasyācetanasyaiva sataḥ sarvajñatvamupacaryate /
vedāntavākyeṣvavaśyaṃ ca tvayāpi sarvajñaṃ brahmābhyupagacchatā sarvajñānāktimattvenaiva sarvajñatvamupagantavyam /
nahi sarvaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ kurvadeva brahma vartate /
tathāhi- jñānasya nityatve jñānakriyāṃ prati svātantryaṃ brahmaṇo hīyeta /
athānityaṃ taditi jñānakriyāyā uparametāpi brahma, tadā sarvajñānāktimattvenaiva sarvajñatvamāpatati /
apica prāgutpatteḥ sarvakārakāśūnyaṃ brahmeṣyate tvayā /
naca jñānasādhanānāṃ śarīrendriyādīnāmabhāve jñānotpattiḥ kasyacidupapannā /
apica pradhānasyanekātmakasya pariṇāmāsaṃbhavātkāraṇatvopapattirmṛdādivat, nāsaṃhatasyaikātmakasya brahmaṇa ityevaṃ prāptaṃ idaṃ sūtramārabhyate-
children.translated_text: Thus far, it has been stated that the <s>Vedānta</s> passages — which have the purpose of the realization of <s>Brahman</s> as the Self, and which are consistently directed toward <s>Brahman</s> as the Self in their purport — reach their culmination in <s>Brahman</s>, even without connection to action. And it has been stated that <s>Brahman</s> is omniscient, omnipotent, and the cause of the world's origination, sustenance, and dissolution. But the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others, thinking that an established reality is cognizable only through other means of knowledge, infer alternative causes such as <s>Pradhāna</s> and construe the <s>Vedānta</s> passages as directed toward those. In all <s>Vedānta</s> passages dealing with creation, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> believe that the cause was intended to be inferred through the effect alone — that the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is always to be inferred. The <s>Kāṇādas</s> (Vaiśeṣikas), from these very passages, infer the Lord as the efficient cause and atoms as the inherent cause. Similarly, other logicians too — relying on semblances of scriptural statements and semblances of reasoning — arise as proponents of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prima facie position). There, the teacher — who knows the words, sentences, and means of valid knowledge — refutes these conflicting views based on semblances of scripture and reasoning, having first stated them as the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, in order to demonstrate that the <s>Vedānta</s> passages are directed toward the realization of <s>Brahman</s>. Therein, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, holding that the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> composed of three <s>guṇas</s> is the cause of the world, say: 'Those <s>Vedānta</s> passages which you said demonstrate that the omniscient, omnipotent <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world — those can also be construed as supporting the <s>Pradhāna</s>-cause position. Omnipotence, for a start, is applicable to <s>Pradhāna</s> too, with respect to its own transformations. Likewise, omniscience too is applicable. How? What you consider to be knowledge — that is a quality of <s>sattva</s>, as the <s>smṛti</s> states: "From <s>sattva</s> arises knowledge" (<s>Gītā</s> 14.17). And through that knowledge, which is a quality of <s>sattva</s>, persons possessed of cause and effect — omniscient <s>yogins</s> — are well-known. For when <s>sattva</s> reaches its unsurpassed excellence, omniscience is well-known. It is not possible to attribute omniscience or even partial knowledge to <s>Puruṣa</s> alone, which is without cause and effect and is mere witnessing consciousness. But since <s>Pradhāna</s> has the three <s>guṇas</s>, <s>sattva</s> — the basis of all knowledge — exists even in the <s>Pradhāna</s> state, and thus omniscience is figuratively attributed to the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> itself. And you too, who accept an omniscient <s>Brahman</s> in the <s>Vedānta</s> passages, must accept omniscience only through the possession of the power of all knowledge. For <s>Brahman</s> does not exist while actually performing the act of knowing all objects. For if knowledge were eternal, <s>Brahman</s>'s independence with respect to the act of knowing would be lost. And if it is non-eternal, then even when <s>Brahman</s> has ceased from the act of knowing, omniscience would still be attributed only through the possession of the power of all knowledge. Moreover, you accept that prior to creation, <s>Brahman</s> is devoid of all instruments. And in the absence of the instruments of knowledge — body, sense organs, and such — the arising of knowledge is not established for anyone. Furthermore, because transformation is possible for <s>Pradhāna</s>, which has a composite nature, its being a cause is justified — like clay and such — but not for <s>Brahman</s>, which is non-composite and of a single nature.' With this position having been reached, this <s>sūtra</s> is commenced —

children.text:
FN: kāryasaṃbandhaṃvināpi anumeyā iti /
buddhau yaḥ pratibimbaḥ sa tādṛśabimbapūrvakaḥ pratibimbatvāt /
darpaṇe mukhābhāsādityanumānam /
vyākaraṇamīmāṃsānyāyāḥ padavākyapramāṇāni /
vākyābhāseṣu yuktyābhāseṣu ca vipratipattiryeṣāṃ te /
jñānakriyāṃprati jñādhātvarthaṃprati, svātantryaṃ kartṛtvam /
ādipadena jñeyajñātrādisaṃgrahaḥ /
pradhānādeḥ kāraṇatvaṃ tarkapāde yuktibhirnirasyati /
brahmaṇaḥ kāraṇatvaṃ smṛtipāde samarthyate /
children.translated_text: NOTE: [The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> say] it should be inferred even without connection to an effect. The reflection in the intellect presupposes a corresponding original, because it is a reflection — like the reflection of a face in a mirror: this is the inference. Grammar, <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, and <s>Nyāya</s> are the means of valid knowledge regarding words, sentences, and [logical] proofs. Those who hold conflicting views based on semblances of scripture and semblances of reasoning. 'With respect to the act of knowing' — with respect to the meaning of the verbal root '<s>jñā</s>' (to know); 'independence' means agency. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the knower, the known, and such are included. The causality of <s>Pradhāna</s> and such is refuted in the <s>tarka</s> section (reasoning chapter) through [logical] arguments. The causality of <s>Brahman</s> is established in the <s>smṛti</s> section (tradition chapter).

children.text: īkṣater nāśabdam | BBs_1,1.5 |
children.translated_text: Because of seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>) — [<s>Pradhāna</s>] is not [the cause]; it lacks scriptural basis. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.5 |

children.text:
na sāṃkhyaparikalpitamacetanaṃ pradhānaṃ jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ śakyaṃ vedānteṣvāśrayitum /
aśabdaṃ hi tat /
kathamaśabdatvaṃ, īkṣateḥ- īkṣitṛtvaśravaṇātkāraṇasya /
katham /
evaṃhi śrūyate- 'sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam' /
(chāndo. 6.2.1) ityupakramya 'tadaikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti tattejo 'sṛjata' (chāndo. 6.2.3) iti /
tatredaṃśabdavācyaṃ nāmarūpavyākṛtaṃ jagatprāgutpatteḥ sadātmanāvadhārya tasyaiva prakṛtasya sacchabdavācyasyekṣaṇapūrvakaṃ tejaḥprabhṛteḥ sraṣṭṛtvaṃ darśayati /
tathānyatra- 'ātmā vā idameka evāgra āsīt /
nānyatkiñcana miṣat /
sa īkṣata lokānnu sṛjā iti /
sa imāṃlokānasṛjata' (aita. 1.1.1) itīkṣāpūrvikāmeva sṛṣṭimācaṣṭe /
Dvacicca ṣoḍaṣakalaṃ puruṣaṃ prastutyāha- 'sa īkṣāñcakre /
sa prāṇamasṛjata' (praśna. 6.3) iti /
īkṣateriti ca dhātvarthanirdeśo 'bhipretaḥ, yajateritivat /
na dhātunirdeśaḥ /
tena 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavidyasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ /
tasmādetadbrahma nāma rūpamannaṃ na jāyate' (muṇḍa. 1.1.9) ityevamādīnyapi sarvajñeśvarakāraṇaparāṇi vākyānudāhartavyāni /
yattūktaṃ sattvadharmeṇa jñānena sarvajñaṃ pradhānaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, tannopapadyate /
nahi pradhānāvasthāyāṃ guṇasāmyātsattvadharmo jñānaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: The unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> conceived by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> cannot be relied upon in the <s>Vedānta</s> [texts] as the cause of the world. For it lacks scriptural support (<s>aśabdam</s>). How does it lack scriptural support? Because of '<s>īkṣateḥ</s>' — because of the scriptural statement that the cause has the capacity to see (<s>īkṣitṛtva</s>). How so? For it is heard thus: 'Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning — one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) — having begun thus — 'It saw: "Let me become many; let me be born." It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3). There, having first ascertained the world — designated by the word 'this,' differentiated into names and forms — as being of the nature of Being (<s>Sat</s>) prior to its creation, [the scripture] then shows the creatorship of that very Being — the entity referred to by the word '<s>Sat</s>' — of fire and such, preceded by seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>). Likewise elsewhere: 'The Self alone was this, one only, in the beginning. Nothing else whatsoever was blinking. It saw: "Let me create the worlds." It created these worlds' (<s>Aitareya</s> 1.1.1) — thus [the scripture] speaks of creation as preceded by seeing. And again, having introduced the <s>Puruṣa</s> with sixteen parts, [the scripture] says: 'He reflected. He created <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.3). And by '<s>īkṣateḥ</s>,' what is intended is the indication of the meaning of the verbal root — like [the expression] '<s>yajateḥ</s>' — not the indication of the [bare] verbal root [itself]. Therefore, passages such as 'He who is omniscient, all-knowing, whose austerity is of the nature of knowledge — from Him are born this <s>Brahman</s>, name, form, and food' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9) — and others that are directed toward an omniscient Lord as the cause — should also be cited. As for the claim that <s>Pradhāna</s> would be omniscient through knowledge, which is a quality of <s>sattva</s> — that is untenable. For in the <s>Pradhāna</s> state, due to the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, knowledge, which is a quality of <s>sattva</s>, is not possible.

children.text:
nanūktaṃ sarvajñānaśaktimattvena sarvajñaṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
tadapi nopapadyate /
yadi guṇasāmye sati sattvavyapāśrayāṃ jñānāktimāśritya sarvajñaṃ pradhānamucyeta kāmaṃ rajastamovyapāśrayāmapi jñānapratibandhakaśaktimāśritya kiñcijjñamucyeta /
apica nāsākṣikā sattvavṛttirjānātinābhidhīyete /
na cācetanasya pradhānasya sākṣitvamasti /
tasmādanupapannaṃ pradhānasya sarvajñatvam /
yogināṃ tu cetanatvātsattvotkarṣanimittaṃ sarvajñatvamupapannamityanudāharaṇam /
atha punaḥ sākṣinimittamīkṣitṛtvaṃ kalpyeta, yathāgninimittamayaḥpiṇḍāderdagdhṛtvam /
tathāsati yannimittamīkṣitṛtvaṃ pradhānasya tadeva sarvajñaṃ mukhyaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇamiti yuktam /
yatpunaruktaṃ brahmaṇo 'pi na mukhyaṃ sarvajñatvamupapadyate, nityajñānakriyatve jñānakriyāṃprati svātantryāsaṃbhavāditi /
children.translated_text: Was it not stated that [<s>Pradhāna</s>] would be omniscient by virtue of possessing the power of all knowledge? That too is untenable. If, when the <s>guṇas</s> are in equilibrium, <s>Pradhāna</s> were called omniscient by resort to the power of knowledge dependent on <s>sattva</s>, then equally it could be called partially-knowing by resort to the power that obstructs knowledge, which is dependent on <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. Moreover, the <s>sattva</s>-function of knowing is not said to operate without a witness. And an unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> cannot serve as a witness. Therefore, the omniscience of <s>Pradhāna</s> is untenable. But for <s>yogins</s>, omniscience occasioned by the predominance of <s>sattva</s> is tenable because they are conscious — so this [example] is not applicable. Now, if the capacity of seeing were supposed to be occasioned by a witness, as the capacity of burning in an iron ball is occasioned by fire — in that case, whatever is the cause of <s>Pradhāna</s>'s seeing-capacity, that itself — the omniscient <s>Brahman</s> in the primary sense — would properly be the cause of the world. As for what was further stated — that even for <s>Brahman</s>, primary omniscience is untenable, because if the activity of knowing were eternal, there would be no autonomy with respect to the act of knowing —

children.text:
atrocyate- idaṃ tāvadbhavānpraṣṭavyaḥ, kathaṃ nityajñānakriyatve sarvajñatvahāniriti /
yasya hi sarvaviṣayāvabhāsanakṣamaṃ jñānaṃ nityamasti so 'sarvajña iti vipratiṣiddham /
anityatve hi jñānasya kadācijjānāti kadācinnajānātītyasarvajñatvamapi syāt /
nāsau jñānanityatve doṣo 'sti jñānanityatve jñānaviṣayaḥ svātantryavyapadeśo nopapadyata iti cenna, pratatauṣṇyaprakāśe 'pi savitari dahati prakāśayatīti svātantryavyapadeśadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: To this we say: first, you should be asked this — how is omniscience lost when the activity of knowing is eternal? For one who eternally possesses knowledge capable of illuminating all objects is not omniscient — this is self-contradictory. Indeed, if knowledge were non-eternal, there might be non-omniscience, since one would sometimes know and sometimes not know. That defect does not exist when knowledge is eternal. If it is said that when knowledge is eternal, the designation of autonomy with respect to the object of knowledge is untenable — no, because even in the case of the sun, whose heat and light are continuous, the autonomous designations 'it burns' and 'it illuminates' are observed.

children.text: nanu saviturdāhyaprakāśasaṃyoge sati dahati prakāśayatīti vyapadeśaḥ syāt, natu brahmaṇaḥ prāgutpatterjñānakarmasaṃyogo 'stīti viṣamo dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the designation 'it burns' and 'it illuminates' regarding the sun would apply when there is contact with things to be burned and illuminated; however, for <s>Brahman</s> prior to creation there is no contact with an object of knowledge-activity — so the example is not analogous.

children.text:
na /
asatyapi karmaṇi savitā prakāśata iti kartṛtvavyapadeśadarśanāt /
evamasatyapi jñānakarmaṇi brahmaṇaḥ 'tadaikṣata' iti kartṛtvavyapadeśopapatterna vaiṣamyam /
karmāpekṣāyāṃ tu brahmaṇīkṣitṛtvaśrutayaḥ sutarāmupapannāḥ /
kiṃ punastatkarma, yatprāgutpatterīśvarajñānasya viṣayo bhavatīti /
tattvānyatvābhyāmanirvacanīye nāmarūpe avyākṛte vyācikīrṣite iti brūmaḥ /
yatprasādāddhi yogināmapyatītānāgataviṣayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ jñānamicchanti yogaśāstravidaḥ, kimu vaktavyaṃ tasya nityasiddhasyeśvarasya sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhṛtiviṣayaṃ nityajñānaṃ bhavatīti /
yadapyuktaṃ prāgutpatterbrahmaṇaḥ śarīrādisaṃbandhamantareṇekṣitṛtvamanupapannamiti, na taccodyamavatarati, savitṛprakāśavadbrahmaṇo jñānasvarūpanityatve jñānasādhanāpekṣānupapatteḥ /
apicāvidyādimataḥ saṃsāriṇaḥ śarīrādyapekṣā jñānotpattiḥ syānna jñānapratibandhakāraṇarahitasyeśvarasya /
mantrau cemāvīśvarasya śarīrādyanapekṣatāmanāvaraṇajñānatāṃ ca darśayataḥ- 'na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate na tatsamaścābhyadhikaśca dṛśyate /
parāsya śaktirvividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca' (śvetā. 6.8) iti /
'apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ /
sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā tamāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam' (śvetā. 3.19) iti ca /
children.translated_text: No. Because even without an object [to act upon], the autonomous designation 'the sun illuminates' is observed. Likewise, even without an object of knowledge-activity, the designation of agency in '<s>Brahman</s> saw' (<s>tadaikṣata</s>) is tenable — hence there is no dissimilarity. And if object-dependence is accepted, then the scriptural statements about <s>Brahman</s>'s seeing-capacity are all the more tenable. But what is that object which, prior to creation, is the content of the Lord's knowledge? We say: it is name and form — indescribable as either identical with or different from [<s>Brahman</s>] — unmanifest, seeking to be manifested. For by whose grace the experts in <s>Yoga</s> texts accept that even <s>yogins</s> have direct perception regarding past and future objects — what need be said that the eternally established Lord has eternal knowledge regarding creation, sustenance, and dissolution? As for the objection that prior to creation, <s>Brahman</s>'s seeing-capacity is untenable without connection to a body and such — that objection does not hold, because since <s>Brahman</s>'s knowledge is eternal by nature (like the sun's illumination), there is no need for instruments of knowledge. Moreover, the arising of knowledge dependent on body and such would be the case for a transmigrating being who possesses ignorance and the rest — not for the Lord who is free from causes that obstruct knowledge. And these two <s>mantras</s> show that the Lord does not depend on body and such, and that his knowledge is unobstructed: 'He has no task nor instrument; none is seen equal to or greater than him. His supreme power is heard to be manifold and inherent — knowledge, strength, and activity' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.8). And: 'Without hands and feet, he is swift and grasping; he sees without eyes, he hears without ears. He knows what is to be known, and none knows him — they call him the first, the great <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.19).

children.text:
nanu nāsti tāvaj jñānapratibandhakāraṇavānīśvarādanyaḥ saṃsārī, 'nānyo 'stī draṣṭā nānyo 'to 'stī vijñātā' (bṛha. 3.7.23) iti śruteḥ /
tatra kimidamucyate saṃsāriṇaḥ śarīrādyapekṣā jñānotpattirneśvarasyeti /
children.translated_text: But there is no transmigrating being other than the Lord who possesses causes that obstruct knowledge — as scripture states: 'There is no other seer than this, no other knower than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23). In that case, what is meant by saying 'the arising of knowledge dependent on body belongs to the transmigrating being, not to the Lord'?

children.text:
atrocyate - satyaṃ, neśvarādanyaḥ saṃsārī /
tathāpi dehādisaṃghātopādhisaṃbandha ityata eva, ghaṭakarakagiriguhādyupādhisaṃbandha iva vyomnaḥ /
tatkṛtaśca śabdapratyayavyavahāro lokasya dṛṣṭo ghaṭacchidraṃ karakādicchidramityādirākāśāvyatireke 'pi tatkṛtā cākāśe ghaṭākāśādibhedamithyābuddhirdṛṣṭā /
tathehāpi dehādisaṃghātopādhisaṃbandhāvivekakṛteśvarasaṃsāribhedamithyābuddhiḥ /
dṛśyate cātmana eva sato dehādisaṃghāte 'nātmanyātmatvābhiniveśo mithyābuddhimātreṇa pūrveṇa /
children.translated_text: And it is observed that the Self itself, while existing [in its true nature], through mere prior false cognition, has the attachment of 'I-ness' (<s>ātmatva</s>) to the aggregate of body and such, which is not-Self.

children.text: sati caivaṃ saṃsāritve dehādyapekṣamīkṣitṛtvamupapannaṃ saṃsāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when <s>saṃsāra</s> is thus [accepted], the seeing-capacity dependent on body and such is tenable for the transmigrating being.

children.text: yadapyuktaṃ pradhānasyānekātmakatvānmṛdādivatkāraṇatvopapattirnāsaṃhatasya brahmaṇa iti, tatpradhānasyāśabdatvenaiva pratyuktam /
children.translated_text: As for what was said — that <s>Pradhāna</s>, being of manifold nature, can be a cause like clay and such, but not <s>Brahman</s>, which is uncompounded — that is already refuted by the very fact that <s>Pradhāna</s> is not indicated by scripture.

children.text: yathā tu tarkeṇāpi brahmaṇa eva kāraṇatvaṃ nirvoḍhuṃ śakyate na pradhānādīnāṃ tathā prapañcayiṣyati- 'na vilakṣaṇatvādasya'- (bra. 2.1.4) ityevamādinā // 5 //
children.translated_text: But how even through reasoning <s>Brahman</s> alone can be established as the cause, and not <s>Pradhāna</s> and such — he will elaborate on this with 'because of the dissimilarity of that' (<s>Bra</s>. 2.1.4) and so forth. // 5 //

To this we say: True, there is no transmigrating being other than the Lord. Even so, [the appearance of a separate being arises] from this very fact — the connection with the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of the aggregate of body and such — just as space [appears differentiated through] the connection with limiting adjuncts such as pots, jars, caves in mountains, and so forth. And the worldly usage of words and cognitions produced by that [limiting adjunct] is observed — 'the space of the pot,' 'the space of the jar,' and so forth — even though there is no real difference in space; and the false cognition of difference in space — such as 'pot-space' and the like — produced by that [limiting adjunct], is also observed. Similarly here too, the false cognition of difference between the Lord and the transmigrating being is produced by the failure to discriminate the connection with the limiting adjuncts of the aggregate of body and such.

children.text:
atrāha- yaduktaṃ nācetanaṃ pradhānaṃ jagatkāraṇamīkṣitṛtvāditi tadanyathāpyupapadyate, acetane 'pi cetanavadupacāradarśanāt /
yathā pratyāsannapatanatāṃ nadyāḥ kūlasyālakṣya kūlaṃ pipātiṣatītyacetane 'pi kūle cetanavadupacāro dṛṣṭaḥ, tadvadacetano 'pi pradhāne pratyāsannasarge cetanavadupacāro bhaviṣyati 'tadaikṣata' iti /
yathā loke kaściccetanaḥ snātvā bhuktvā cāparāhne grāmaṃ rathena gamiṣyāmītīkṣitvānantaraṃ tathaiva niyamena pravartate, tathā pradhānamapi mahadādyākāreṇa niyamena pravartate /
tasmāccetanavadupacaryate /
kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇādvihāya mukhyamīkṣitṛtvamaupacārikaṃ kalpyate, 'tatteja aikṣata', 'tā āpa aikṣanta' (chāndo. 6.2.3,4) iti cācetanayorapyaptejasoścetanavadupacāradarśanāt /
tasmātkartṛkamapīkṣaṇamaupacārikamiti gamyate, 'upacāraprāye vacanāt' iti /
evaṃ prāpta idaṃ sūtramārabhyate-
children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised: The statement that the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> cannot be the cause of the world because of the seeing-capacity [mentioned in scripture] — that can be explained otherwise, since even in the case of unconscious things, figurative usage as if conscious is observed. Just as, observing the imminent falling of a riverbank, one says 'the bank wants to fall' — figurative usage as if conscious is observed even regarding the unconscious bank — similarly, even regarding the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>, when creation is imminent, there could be figurative usage as if conscious in the expression '<s>tadaikṣata</s>' (it saw). Just as in the world a conscious person, having bathed, eaten, and thought 'I shall go to the village by chariot in the afternoon,' thereafter proceeds in exactly that determined manner — so too <s>Pradhāna</s> proceeds in a determined manner in the form of <s>mahat</s> and such. Therefore it is figuratively spoken of as if conscious. And why should the primary sense of seeing-capacity be abandoned in favor of a figurative one? Because figurative usage as if conscious is observed even for the unconscious water and fire in 'that fire saw' and 'those waters saw' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3-4). Therefore, seeing-capacity, even though involving an agent, is understood as figurative — 'because the statement is predominantly figurative.' Given this position, the following <s>sūtra</s> is commenced —

children.text:
FN: sāmānyataḥ sarve jānātīti sarvajñaḥ /
tattadviśeṣadharmaghaṭādipuraskāreṇa sarve vettīti sarvavit /
etadbrahma jāyamānaṃ hiraṇyagarbhākhyaṃ kāryam /
sāṃkhyīyaṃ svamatasamādhānamupanyasya dūṣayati- yattūktamiti /
acetanasyājñātṛtvaṃ tacchabdārthaḥ /
seśvarasāṃkhyamatamāha- atheti /
pratatetyasya saṃtatetyarthaḥ /
asatyapi avivakṣitepi /
prakṛtyarthavatpratyayārthasyāpi bādhābhāvātsutarāmityuktam /
kāryaṃ śarīram, karaṇamindriyajātam /
abhiniveśo mithyābhimānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: In general, one who knows everything is <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscient). One who knows everything through the specific qualities of particular things like pots and such is <s>sarvavit</s> (all-knowing). This <s>Brahman</s>, when manifesting, is the effect called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. Having presented the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> resolution of their own view, he refutes it with 'but what was stated.' The meaning of the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) is the unknowing nature of the unconscious. He states the <s>Seśvara-Sāṃkhya</s> view with 'now' (<s>atha</s>). '<s>Pratata</s>' means '<s>saṃtata</s>' (continuous). '<s>Asati</s>' means 'even when not intended.' Because the meaning of the suffix is not negated like the meaning of the root, the word '<s>sutarām</s>' (all the more) is used. '<s>Kārya</s>' is the body; '<s>karaṇa</s>' is the collection of sense-organs. '<s>Abhiniveśa</s>' is false identification.

children.text: gauṇaścennātmaśabdāt | BBs_1,1.6 |
children.translated_text: <s>Gauṇaś cen nātmaśabdāt</s> — If [it be said that seeing is] figurative, [we say] no, because of the word '<s>ātman</s>' (Self). | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.6 |

children.text:
yaduktaṃ pradhānamacetanaṃ sacchabdavācyaṃ tasminnaupacārika īkṣatiḥ, aptejasoriveti, tadasat /
kasmāt, ātmaśabdāt /
'sadeva somyedamagra āsīt' ityupakramya 'tadaikṣata tattejo 'sṛjata' (chāndo. 6.2.1,3) iti ca tejo 'bannānāṃ sṛṣṭimuktvā tadeva prakṛtaṃ sadīkṣitṛ, tāni ca tejo 'bannāni, devatāśabdena parāmṛśyāha- 'seyaṃ devataikṣata hantāhamimāstisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupravaśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi' (chāndo. 6.3.2) iti /
tatra yadi pradhānamacetanaṃ guṇavṛttyekṣitṛ kalpyeta tadeva prakṛtatvātseyaṃ devateti parāmṛśyeta /
na tadā devatā jīvātmaśabdenābhidadhyāt /
jīvo hi nāma cetanaḥ śarīrādhyakṣaḥ prāṇānāṃ dhārayitā, tatprasiddhernirvacanācca /
sa kathamacetanasya pradhānasyātmā bhavet /
ātmā hi nāma svarūpam /
nācetanasya pradhānasya cetano jīvaḥ svarūpaṃ bhavitumarhati /
atha tu cetanaṃ brahma mukhyamīkṣitṛ parigṛhyate tasya jīvaviṣaya ātmaśabdaprayoga upapadyate /
children.translated_text: But if the conscious <s>Brahman</s> is accepted as the primary seer, then the use of the word '<s>ātman</s>' with reference to the <s>jīva</s> is tenable.

children.text: tathā 'sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitadātmyamidaṃ sarvaṃ tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi śvetaketo' (chāndo. 6.14.3) ityatra 'sa ātmā' iti prakṛtaṃ sadaṇimānamātmānamātmaśabdenopadiśya 'tattvamasi śvetaketo' iti cetanasya śvetaketorātmatvenopadiśati, aptejasostu viṣayatvādacetanatvaṃ, nāmarūpavyākaraṇādau ca prayojyatvenaiva nirdeśāt, nacātmaśabdavatkiñcinmukhyatve kāraṇamastīti yuktaṃ kūlavadgauṇatvamīkṣitṛtvasya /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in 'That which is this finest essence — all this has that as its Self; that is the Real; that is the Self; that you are, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.14.3) — here, having taught with the word '<s>ātman</s>' that Being, the finest essence, is the Self as subject, he teaches 'that you are, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>' — declaring [it] as the Self of the conscious <s>Śvetaketu</s>. But water and fire are unconscious, since they are objects [of that Being]; and in the creation of names and forms, they are mentioned only as things to be directed — and there is no reason for taking their seeing-capacity as primary, as there is with the word '<s>ātman</s>.' Therefore, it is proper that their seeing-capacity is figurative, like that of a riverbank.

children.text: tayorapi ca sadadhiṣṭhitatvāpekṣamevekṣitṛtvam /
children.translated_text: And the seeing-capacity even of those two [water and fire] is dependent on being presided over by Being.

children.text: satastvātmaśabdānna gauṇamīkṣitṛtvamityuktam // 6 //
children.translated_text: But the seeing-capacity of Being is not figurative, because of the word '<s>ātman</s>' — this has been stated. // 6 //

What was said — that the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>, denoted by the word '<s>sat</s>' (Being), has figurative seeing-capacity, like water and fire — that is wrong. Why? Because of the word '<s>ātman</s>.' Having begun with 'Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning' and [then] stating 'It saw; it created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1, 3) — having described the creation of fire, water, and food — that same Being, the subject under discussion, the one with seeing-capacity — together with those [elements] fire, water, and food — is referred to with the word '<s>devatā</s>' (deity) and it says: 'This deity saw: "Let me enter these three deities with this living Self (<s>jīvātman</s>) and manifest names and forms"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2). Now, if the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> were supposed to be the seer through figurative attribution of the <s>guṇa</s>-function, then that very [<s>Pradhāna</s>], being the subject under discussion, would be referred to by 'this deity.' In that case, it would not designate the deity with the word '<s>jīvātman</s>' (living Self). For '<s>jīva</s>' means a conscious being, the ruler of the body, the sustainer of the vital breaths — this being well-known and etymologically established. How could it be the Self of the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>? For '<s>ātman</s>' means 'own nature.' The conscious <s>jīva</s> cannot possibly be the own nature of the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text:
athocyetācetane 'pi pradhāne bhavatyātmābdaḥ, ātmanaḥ sarvārthakāritvāt, yathā rājñaḥ sarvārthakāriṇi bhṛtye bhavatyātmaśabdo mamātmā bhadrasena iti /
pradhānaṃ hi puruṣasyātmano bhogāpavargo kurvadupakaroti, rājña iva bhṛtyaḥ saṃdhivigrahādiṣu vartamānaḥ /
athavaika evātmaśabdaścetanācetanaviṣayo bhaviṣyati,
children.translated_text: Now it might be said: the word '<s>ātman</s>' does apply to the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>, because the Self serves all purposes — just as the word '<s>ātman</s>' applies to a servant of a king who serves all his purposes: 'My Self is <s>Bhadrasena</s>.' For <s>Pradhāna</s> benefits the Self, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, by effecting enjoyment and liberation — like a servant of a king engaged in alliances, wars, and such. Or alternatively, the single word '<s>ātman</s>' may refer to both conscious and unconscious [entities],

children.text:
bhūtātmendriyātmeti ca prayogadarśanāt /
yathaika eva jyotiḥśabdaḥ kratujvalanaviṣayaḥ /
tatra kuta etadātmaśabdādīkṣateragauṇatvamityata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: since the usage '<s>bhūtātman</s>' (elemental self) and '<s>indriyātman</s>' (sense-self) is observed. Just as the single word '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' (light) refers to both the ritual sacrifice and fire. In that case, how can the non-figurativeness of seeing be [established] from the word '<s>ātman</s>'? To this he reads the next [<s>sūtra</s>] —

children.text:
FN: anena pūrvasṛṣṭyanubhūtena prāṇadhṛtihetunāmātmanā sadrūpeṇa yathoktā devatāḥ sargānantaraṃ praviśya nāma rūpaṃ ceti vispaṣṭamāsamantātkaravāṇīti parā devatekṣitavatītyarthaḥ /
kūlasya guṇavṛttyā pipatiṣāvadyuktamaptejasorgauṇamīkṣitṛtvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The meaning is: the supreme deity, having entered through this — the living Self, of the nature of Being, [equipped] with the previously experienced means of sustaining vital breath from a prior creation — saw [fit to] clearly and thoroughly manifest names and forms after creation, as described. The meaning is: just as the figurative desire to fall is appropriate for a riverbank through the <s>guṇa</s>-function, so too the figurative seeing-capacity of water and fire [is appropriate].

children.text: tanniṣṭhasya mokṣopadeśāt | BBs_1,1.7 |
children.translated_text: <s>Tanniṣṭhasya mokṣopadeśāt</s> — Because liberation is taught for one who is devoted to That. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.7 |

children.text:
na pradhānamacetanamātmaśabdālambanaṃ bhavitumarhati, 'sa ātmā' iti prakṛtaṃ sadaṇimānamādāya 'tattvamasi śvetaketo' iti cetanasya śvetaketormokṣayitavyasya tanniṣṭhamupadiśya 'ācāryavānpuruṣo veda' 'tasya tāvadeva ciraṃ yāvanna vimokṣye 'tha saṃpatsye' (chāndo. 6.14.2) iti mokṣopadeśāt /
yadi hyacetanaṃ pradhānaṃ sacchabdavācyaṃ tadasīti grāhayenmumukṣuṃ cetanaṃ santamacetano 'sīti tadā viparītavādī śāstraṃ puruṣasyānarthāyetyapramāṇaṃ syāt /
natu nirdeṣaṃ śāstramapramāṇaṃ kalpayituṃ yuktam /
yadi cājñasya sato mumukṣoracetanamanātmānamātmetyupadiśetpramāṇabhūtaṃ śāstraṃ sa śraddhadhānatayāndhagolāṅgūlanyāyena tadātmadṛṣṭiṃ na parityajet, tadvyatiriktaṃ cātmānaṃ na pratipadyeta, tathā sati puruṣārthādvihanyetānarthaṃ na ṛcchet /
tasmādyathā svargādyarthino 'gnihotrādisādhanaṃ yathābhūtamupadiśati tathā mumukṣorapi 'sa ātmā tattvamasi śvetaketo' iti yathābhūtamevātmānamupaduśatīti yuktam /
evañca sati taptaparaśugrahaṇamokṣadṛṣṭāntena satyābhisandhasya mokṣopadeśa upapadyate /
anyathā hyamukhye sadātmatattvopadeśe 'ahamukthamasmīti vidyāt' (ai. āra. 2.1.2.6) itivatsaṃpanmātramidamanityaphalaṃ syāt /
tatra mokṣopadeśo nopapadyeta /
tasmānna sadaṇimanyātmaśabdasya gauṇatvam /
bhṛtye tu svāmibhṛtyabhedasya pratyakṣatvādupapanno gauṇa ātmaśabdo mamātmā bhadrasena iti /
apica Dvacidgauṇaḥ śabdo dṛṣṭa iti naitāvatā śabdapramāṇaker'tho gauṇī kalpanā nyāyyā, sarvatrānāśvāsaprasaṅgāt /
yattūktaṃ cetanācetanayoḥ sādhāraṇa ātmābdaḥ kratujvalanayoriva jyotiḥśabda iti, tanna, anekārthatvāsyānyāyyatvāt /
tasmāccetanaviṣaya eva mukhya ātmaśabdaścetanatvopacārādbhūtādiṣu prayujyate bhūtātmendriyātmeti ca /
sādhāraṇatve 'pyātmaśabdasya na prakaraṇamupapadaṃ vā kiñcinniścāyakamantareṇānyataravṛttitā nirdhārayituṃ śakyate /
nacātrācetanasya niścāyakaṃ kiñcitkāraṇamasti /
prakṛtaṃ tu sadīkṣitṛ, saṃnihitaścetanaḥ śvetaketuḥ nahi cetanasya śvetaketoracetana ātmā saṃbhavatītyavocāma /
tasmāccetanaviṣaya ihātmaśabda iti niścīyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is determined that here the word '<s>Ātman</s>' pertains to the conscious.

children.text: jyotiḥśabdo 'pi laukikena prayogeṇa jvalana eva rūḍhor'thavādakalpitena tu jvalanasādṛśyena kratau pravṛtta ityadṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) too is primarily established in common usage as referring to fire, and it is used for sacrifice through a figurative resemblance devised by the <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic passage) — so it is not a [valid] counter-example.

children.text: athavā pūrvasūtra evātmaśabdaṃ nirastasamastagauṇatvasādhāraṇatvaśaṅkatayā vyākhyāya tataḥ svatantra eva pradhānakāraṇanirākaraṇaheturvyākhyeyaḥ 'tanniṣṭhasya mokṣopadeśāt' iti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having already explained the word '<s>Ātman</s>' in the previous <s>sūtra</s> so as to remove all suspicion of figurative and common usage, the independent reason for refuting <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause should then be explained [as a separate point]: 'because of the teaching of liberation for one who is devoted to that.'

children.text: tasmānnācetanaṃ pradhānaṃ sacchabdavācyam // 7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> is not what is denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>' (Being). // 7 //

The unconscious Pradhāna cannot be the referent of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self), because having taken up the subject <s>Sat</s> (Being) with its subtle nature under [the words] 'that is the Self' (sa ātmā), [the text] teaches <s>Śvetaketu</s> — who is conscious and is to be liberated — the identity with that [<s>Sat</s>] through 'You are That, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>,' and [teaches] liberation through 'A person who has a teacher knows' and 'For him, the delay is only so long until he is released; then he will attain' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.14.2). For if the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>, denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>,' were taught [to the seeker] as 'You are That,' it would make a conscious seeker of liberation understand 'You are unconscious' — then the scripture, being a speaker of the contrary, would be invalid as leading to a person's harm. But it is not proper to suppose that the authoritative scripture is invalid. And if the authoritative scripture were to teach an ignorant seeker of liberation that the non-Self, which is unconscious, is the Self — then he, being trusting, would by the logic of 'the blind man following a monkey's tail,' not relinquish the view that [the non-Self] is the Self, nor would he realize the Self that is distinct from that. In that case, he would be thwarted from the goal of human life and would come to harm. Therefore, just as scripture truly teaches one who desires heaven the means such as <s>Agnihotra</s> as they really are, so too it is reasonable that for a seeker of liberation, it teaches the Self as it really is through 'That is the Self; You are That, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' And this being so, the teaching of liberation through the illustration of grasping a heated axe and being released [when truthful] is fitting. Otherwise, if the teaching of the reality of <s>Sat</s> as the Self were figurative, it would be merely a meditation (<s>saṃpatti</s>) with impermanent results, like 'One should know: I am the <s>Uktha</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.1.2.6). In that case, the teaching of liberation would not be appropriate. Therefore, the word '<s>Ātman</s>' applied to <s>Sat</s> with its subtle nature is not figurative. In the case of a servant, however, the figurative use of '<s>Ātman</s>' is justified — as in '<s>Bhadrasena</s> is my self' — because the non-difference between master and servant is perceptible. Moreover, just because a word is seen to be figurative somewhere does not make it reasonable to construe a figurative meaning for a word that is a valid means of knowledge, because that would lead to distrust everywhere. As for the objection that the word '<s>Ātman</s>' is common to both the conscious and the unconscious, like the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) for both a sacrifice and fire — that is not so, because polysemy is improper. Therefore, the primary meaning of '<s>Ātman</s>' pertains to the conscious alone, and it is used for elements and such through the figurative extension of consciousness — as in 'the self of elements,' 'the self of the senses.' Even granting the word '<s>Ātman</s>' is used for both, without some determining factor — context or supporting evidence — it is impossible to settle on one particular meaning. And here there is no determining factor for the unconscious. But the subject is <s>Sat</s> as the seer (<s>īkṣitṛ</s>), and the conscious <s>Śvetaketu</s> is present [in the dialogue] — for we have said that an unconscious [entity] cannot be the Self of the conscious <s>Śvetaketu</s>.

children.text:
FN: atrottamapuruṣastūbhayatra prathamapuruṣe chāndasavat /
tadā cetanaṃ santaṃ mumukṣumacetano 'sītibruvacchāstraṃ viparītavādibhūtvā puṃso 'narthāyetikṛtvā syādapramāṇamiti yojanā /
atra vihatirmuktibhāktvābhāvaḥ /
'yathā satyābhisaṃdhastaptaṃ paraśuṃ sa na dahyate 'tha mucyate' iti /
ukthaṃ prāṇaḥ /
mahāvākyotthaṃ jñānamidamucyate /
children.translated_text: NOTE: Here, the first person is used for the second person in both places, in the Vedic manner. The construction is: then, [the scripture], telling the conscious seeker of liberation 'You are unconscious,' would become a speaker of the contrary, and being thus conducive to a person's harm, would be invalid. Here, '<s>vihati</s>' means the absence of attaining liberation. [The illustration is:] 'Just as one who speaks the truth, grasping a heated axe, is not burnt and is then released.' '<s>Uktha</s>' means <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath). The knowledge arising from the great statement (<s>mahāvākya</s>) is what is referred to here.

children.text: kutaśca na pradhānaṃ sacchabdavācyam /
children.translated_text: And why else is <s>Pradhāna</s> not denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>'?

children.text: heyatvāvacanācca | BBs_1,1.8 |
children.translated_text: And because it is not stated as what is to be rejected. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.8 |

children.text:
yadyānātmaiva pradhānaṃ sacchabdavācyaṃ 'sa ātmā tattvamasi' itīhopadiṣṭaṃ syātsa tadupadeśaśravaṇādanātmajñatayā tanniṣṭho mā bhūditi mukhyamātmānamupadidikṣustasya heyatvaṃ brūyāt /
yathārundhatīṃ didarśayiṣustatsamīpasthāṃ sthūlāṃ tārāmamukhyāṃ prathamamarundhatiti grāhayitvā tāṃ pratyākhyāya paścādarundhatīmeva grāhayati tadvannāyamātmeti brūyāt /
nacaivamavocat /
sanmātrātmāvagatiniṣṭhaiva hi ṣaṣṭhaprapāṭhakaparisamāptirdṛśyate /
caśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: If the non-Self — namely <s>Pradhāna</s> — were denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>' and taught here through 'That is the Self; You are That,' then [the teacher], wishing to teach the true Self so that [the student] would not remain identified with [the non-Self] through knowledge of the non-Self gained from that teaching — would state the rejectability of that [<s>Pradhāna</s>]. Just as one wishing to point out [the star] <s>Arundhatī</s>, first makes [the student] apprehend a large, prominent star near it as '<s>Arundhatī</s>' — which it is not — then rejects that and makes [the student] apprehend the actual <s>Arundhatī</s>, so too [the teacher] would say 'This is not the Self.' But he did not say this. For the conclusion of the sixth chapter is seen to rest solely on the realization of the Self as nothing but <s>Sat</s> (pure Being). The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) —

children.text: pratijñāvirodhāt | BBs_1,1.8a |
children.translated_text: Because of contradiction with the thesis. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.8a |

children.text:
pratijñāvirodhābhyuccayapradarśanārthaḥ /
satyapi heyatvavacane pratijñāvirodhaḥ prasajyeta /
kāraṇavijñānāddhi sarvaṃ vijñātamiti pratijñātam /

'uta tamādeśamaprākṣyo yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavatyamataṃ matamavijñātaṃ vijñātamiti kathaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bhavatīti yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syādvācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyam' /
children.translated_text: 'Have you asked for that teaching by which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known? How indeed, revered sir, could such a teaching be? Just as, my dear, by one lump of clay everything made of clay is known — the modification is merely a name, a verbal designation; clay alone is the reality' —

children.text: 'evaṃ somya sa ādeśo bhavati' (chāndo. 6.1.1,3) iti vākyopakrame śravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, my dear, is that teaching' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.1,3) — this is heard at the commencement of the passage.

children.text: naca sacchabdavācye pradhāne bhogyavargakāraṇe heyatvenāheyatvena vā vijñāte bhoktṛvargo vijñāto bhavati, apradhānavikāratvādbhoktṛvargasya /
children.translated_text: And when <s>Pradhāna</s>, denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>,' is the cause of the class of objects of enjoyment, then whether it is known as what is to be rejected or as what is not to be rejected, the class of experiencers is not thereby known — because the class of experiencers is not a modification of <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: tasmānna pradhānaṃ sacchabdavācyam // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Pradhāna</s> is not what is denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>.' // 8 //

— is for showing the accumulation [of reasons], including the contradiction with the thesis. For even if the rejectability were stated, there would be a contradiction with the thesis. For it was promised that through the knowledge of the cause, everything is known.

children.text: kutaśca na pradhānaṃ sacchabdavācyam-
children.translated_text: And why else is <s>Pradhāna</s> not denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>'?

children.text:
he śvetaketo, uta api ādisyata ityādeśastaṃ śāstrācāryoktigamyaṃ vastvaprākṣyaḥ pṛṣṭavānasyācāryam /
vācārabhyamāṇamuccāryamāṇaṃ nāmadheyameva vikāro na tu ghaṭaśarāvādināmātirikto mṛdi vikāro vastuto 'sti paramārthato mṛttikaiva tu satyaṃ vastvastīti /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Śvetaketu</s>, have you asked for that teaching?' — [the word] '<s>ādeśa</s>' means the entity to be known through scripture and the teacher's instruction. [He] asked his teacher. 'The modification that is being uttered, expressed, is a name only; it is merely a verbal designation — not that any modification of pot, dish, and such really exists as a thing beyond clay; in ultimate reality, clay alone is the reality, is the [true] thing' — this is the meaning.

children.text: svāpyayāt | BBs_1,1.9 |
children.translated_text: Because of return to one's own [self]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.9 |

children.text:
tadeva sacchabdavācyaṃ kāraṇaṃ prakṛtya śrūyate- 'yatraitatpuruṣaḥ svapiti nāma satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati svamapīto bhavati tasmādenaṃ svapitītyācakṣate svaṃ hyapīto bhavati' (chāndo. 6.8.1) iti /
eṣā śrutiḥ svapitītyetatpuruṣasya lokaprasiddhaṃ nāma nirvakti /
svaśabdenehātmocyate /
yaḥ prakṛtaḥ sacchabdavācyastamapīto bhavatyapigato bhavatītyarthaḥ /
apipūrvasyaiterlaryārthatvaṃ prasiddhaṃ, prabhavāpyayāvityutpattipralayayoḥ prayogadarśanāt /
manaḥpracāropādhiviśeṣasaṃbandhādindriyārthāngṛhyaṃstadviśeṣāpanno jīvo jāgarti /
tadvāsanāviśiṣṭaḥ svapnānpaśyanmanaḥśabdavācyo bhavati /
sa upādhidvayoparame suṣuptāvasthāmupādhikṛtaviśeṣābhāvātsvātmani pralīna iveti 'svaṃ hyapīto bhavati' ityucyate /
yathā hṛdayaśabdanirvacanaṃ śrutvā darśitam- 'sa vā eṣa ātmā hṛdi tasyaitadeva niruktaṃ hṛdyayamiti tasmādhṛdayamiti' (chāndo. 8.3.3) iti /
yathāvāśanāyodanyāśabdapravṛttimūlaṃ darśayati śrutiḥ- 'āpa eva tadaśitaṃ nayante' 'teja eva tatpītaṃ nayante' (chā. 6. 8. 3,5) iti ca /
evaṃ svamātmānaṃ sacchabdavācyamapīto bhavatītīmamarthaṃ svapitināmanirvacanena darśayati /
naca cetana ātmācetanaṃ pradhānaṃ svarūpatvena pratipadyeta /
yadi punaḥ pradhānamevātmīyātvātsvāśabdenaivocyeta, evamapi cetano 'cetanamapyetīti viruddhamāpadyeta /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, <s>Pradhāna</s> itself were referred to by the word '<s>sva</s>' (own) because it belongs to the Self — even so, the absurd consequence would arise that the conscious [self] goes to the unconscious.

children.text: śrutyantaraṃ ca - 'prājñenātmanā saṃpariṣvakto na bāhyaṃ kiñcana veda nāntaram' /
children.translated_text: And another scripture [states]: 'Embraced by the cognizing Self (<s>prājña ātman</s>), he knows nothing external, nothing internal' —

children.text: (bṛha. 4.3.21) iti suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ cetane 'pyayaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.21) — this shows the return in the state of deep sleep to be into a conscious [being].
