children.text: ato yasminnapyayaḥ sarveṣāṃ cetanānāṃ taccetanaṃ sacchabdavācyaṃ jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ na pradhānam // 9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, that into which all conscious beings return — that conscious [reality] denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>' is the cause of the world, not <s>Pradhāna</s>. // 9 //

Taking up that very cause denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>,' the scripture states: 'When a person sleeps, as they say, my dear, he has then merged with <s>Sat</s> (Being); he has gone to his own (<s>sva</s>). That is why they say he sleeps (<s>svapiti</s>) — for he has gone to his own' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1). This scripture etymologically explains the commonly known name '<s>svapiti</s>' (he sleeps) of a person. By the word '<s>sva</s>' (own), the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) is meant here — namely, the one referred to [earlier] as denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>.' '<s>Apīta</s>' means 'has gone to' (<s>apigata</s>). The well-known usage of '<s>i</s>' with the prefix '<s>api</s>' in the sense of the optative is established, since it is seen used for both origination and dissolution, as in '<s>prabhavāpyayau</s>.' The <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), being connected with the specific conditioning adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) such as the activity of the mind and senses, and apprehending sense-objects, wakes. When endowed with the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of those [experiences], seeing dreams, he is called by the word '<s>manas</s>' (mind). When both those conditioning adjuncts cease, in the state of deep sleep, because of the absence of distinctions produced by the conditioning adjuncts, he is said to have 'merged into his own self,' as it were — hence 'he has gone to his own.' Just as the etymology of the word '<s>hṛdaya</s>' (heart) was shown upon hearing: 'This Self is indeed in the heart; its etymology is this: he is in the heart — therefore it is called <s>hṛdaya</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.3). And just as the scripture shows the etymological basis for the usage of words like '<s>aśanāyā</s>' (hunger) and '<s>udanyā</s>' (thirst): 'Waters carry away what has been eaten' and 'Fire carries away what has been drunk' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.3,5). In the same way, [the scripture] shows through the etymology of the name '<s>svapiti</s>' that [the person] has gone to his own self, which is denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>.' And a conscious Self would not realize an unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> as its own nature.

children.text: FN: yatra suptau puṃsaḥ svapitītyetannāma bhavati tadā puruṣaḥ satā saṃpannastenaikībhūta iti yojanā /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The construction is: when a person's name 'he sleeps' occurs in sleep, then the person has merged with <s>Sat</s>, has become one with it.

children.text: kutaśca na pradhānaṃ jagataḥ kāraṇam-
children.translated_text: And why else is <s>Pradhāna</s> not the cause of the world?

children.text: gatisāmānyāt | BBs_1,1.10 |
children.translated_text: Because of the uniformity of teaching. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.10 |

children.text:
yadi tārkikasamaya iva vedānteṣvapi bhinnā kāraṇāvagatirabhaviṣyatkvaciccetanaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ Dvacidanyadeveti, tataḥ kadācitpradhānakāraṇavādānurodhenāpīkṣatyādiśravaṇamakalpayiṣyat /
natvetadasti /
samānaiva hi sarveṣu vedānteṣu cetanakāraṇāvagatiḥ /
'yathāgnerjvalataḥ sarvā diśo visphuliṅgā vipratiṣṭherannevamevaitasmādātmanaḥ sarve prāṇā yathāyatanaṃ vipratiṣṭhante prāṇebhyo devā devebhyo lokāḥ' (kau. 3.3) iti /
'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti /
'ātmata evedaṃ sarvam' (chāndo. 7.26.1) iti /
'ātmana eṣa prāṇo jāyate' (pra. 3.3) iti cātmanaḥ kāraṇatvaṃ darśayanti sarve vedāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: If in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, as in the systems of logicians, there were divergent understandings of the cause — sometimes conscious <s>Brahman</s> as the cause of the world, sometimes something else — then one might have construed the hearing of 'It willed' and such in accordance with the doctrine of <s>Pradhāna</s> as cause. But this is not so. For in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts, the understanding that the cause is conscious is uniform. 'Just as from a blazing fire, sparks fly forth in all directions — so from this Self, all vital breaths go forth, each to its own place; from the breaths, the gods; from the gods, the worlds' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.3). 'From this Self, <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) arose' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). 'All this is indeed from the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.26.1). 'From the Self is this <s>Prāṇa</s> born' (<s>Praśna</s> 3.3) — all the <s>Vedānta</s> texts show the Self to be the cause.

children.text: ātmaśabdaśca cetanavacana ityavocāma /
children.translated_text: And we have said that the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) denotes the conscious.

children.text: mahacca prāmāṇyakāraṇametadyadvedāntavākyānāṃ cetanakāraṇatve samānagatitvaṃ, cakṣurādīnāmiva rūpādiṣu /
children.translated_text: And this is a great reason for validity — that the <s>Vedānta</s> statements have uniformity of teaching regarding the conscious as the cause, like the eyes and such [converging] on form and such [objects].

children.text: ato gatisāmānyātsarvajñaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇam // 10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the uniformity of teaching, omniscient <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world. // 10 //

children.text:
FN: gatiravagatiḥ /
vipratiṣṭheran nānāgatitvena diśo daśāpi prasṛtāḥ syurityarthaḥ /
ajñātajñāpakatvaṃ prāmāṇyam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Gati</s>' means understanding. '<s>Vipratiṣṭheran</s>' means 'would spread forth in various directions, to all ten quarters' — this is the meaning. Validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is the capacity to make known what was not [previously] known.

children.text: kutaśca sarvajñaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇam-
children.translated_text: And why else is omniscient <s>Brahman</s> the cause of the world?

children.text: śrutatvāc ca | BBs_1,1.11 |
children.translated_text: Because it is heard [so stated]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.11 |

children.text: svaśabdenaiva ca sarvajña īśvaro jagataḥ kāraṇamiti śrūyate śvetāśvatarāṇāṃ mantropaniṣadi sarvajñamīśvaraṃ prakṛtya 'sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇādhipādhipo na cāsya kaścijjanitā na cādhipaḥ' (śve. 6.9) iti /
children.translated_text: And by its own express words, the omniscient Lord is heard to be the cause of the world in the <s>Mantra-Upaniṣad</s> of the <s>Śvetāśvataras</s>, where, taking up the omniscient Lord as the subject: 'He is the cause, the lord of the lords of the organs; and of Him there is no progenitor, nor any lord' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.9).

children.text: tasmāt sarvajñaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ, nācetanaṃ pradhānamanyadveti siddham // 11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, omniscient <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world — not the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>, nor anything else. This is established. // 11 //

children.text:
FN: kāraṇādhipā jīvasteṣāmadhipaḥ /
vastutantraṃ bhavejjñānaṃ karmatantramupāsanam /
āvistarāmatiśayena prakaṭam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The lords of the organs are the individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>); [He is] the lord of those. Knowledge is determined by the reality [it reveals]; meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) is determined by [ritual] action. '<s>Āvistarām</s>' means manifestly, with abundance.

children.text: 6 ānandamayādhikaraṇam / sū. 12-19
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Ānandamaya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the One Consisting of Bliss) / <s>Sūtras</s> 12-19

children.text:
'janmādyasya yataḥ' ityārabhya 'śrutatvācca' ityevamantaiḥ sūtrairyānyudāhṛtāni vedāntavākyāni teṣāṃ sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktirīśvaro jagato janmasthitilayakāraṇamityetasyārthasya pratipādakatvaṃ nyāyapūrvakaṃ pratipāditam /
gatisāmānyopanyāsena ca sarve vedāntāścetanakāraṇavādina iti vyākhyātam /

'yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati taditara itaraṃ paśyati yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛha. 4.5.15) 'yatra nānyatpaśyati nānyacchṛṇoti nānyadvijānāti sa bhūmātha yatrānyatpaśyatyanyacchṛṇotyanyadvijānāti tadalpaṃ vo vai bhūmā tadamṛtamatha yadalpaṃ tanmartyam' (chāndo. 7.24.1) 'sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vicitya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadanyadāste' (tai.ā. 3.12.7) 'niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntaṃ niravadyaṃ nirañjanam /
amṛtasya paraṃ setuṃ dagdhendhanamivānalam' (śve. 6.19) 'neti neti' (bṛ. 2.3.6) iti 'asthūlamanaṇu' (bṛ. 3.8.8) 'nyūnamanyatsthānaṃ saṃpūrṇamanyat' iti caivaṃ sahasraśo vidyāvidyāviṣayabhedena brahmaṇo dvirūpatāṃ darśayanti vākyāni /
tatrāvidyāvasthāyāṃ brahmaṇa upāsyopāsakādikṣaṇaḥ sarvo vyavahāraḥ /
tatra kānicidbrahmaṇa upāsanānyabhyudayārthāni, kānicitkramamuktyarthāni, kānicitkarmasamṛddhyarthāni /

eka eva tu paramātmeśvarastaistairguṇaviśeṣairviśiṣṭa upāsyo yadyapi bhavati tathāpi yathāguṇopāsanameva phalāni bhidyante /
'taṃ yathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati' iti śruteḥ, 'yathākraturasmiṃloke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati' (chā. 3.14.1) iti ca /
smṛteśca- 'yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram /
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ //' (gī. 8.6) iti /
children.translated_text: to that very state one goes, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, always being absorbed in that state.' (<s>Gītā</s> 8.6)

children.text:
yadyapyeka ātmā sarvabhūteṣu sthāvarajaṅgameṣu gūḍhastathāpi cittopādhiviśeṣatāratamyādātmanaḥ kūṭasthanityasyaikarūpasyāpyuttarottaramāviṣkṛtasya tāratamyamaiśvaryaśaktiviśeṣaiḥ śrūyate- 'tasya ya ātmānamāvistarāṃ veda' (ai.ā. 2.3.2.1) ityatra /
smṛtāvapi- 'yadyadvibhūtimatsarvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā /
children.translated_text: Although the one Self is hidden in all beings, moving and unmoving, nevertheless, due to the hierarchy of specific limiting adjuncts of the mind, even though the Self is immutable, eternal, and of one form, a hierarchy in its progressive manifestation is heard through specific powers of lordly sovereignty — as in: 'Of that [hierarchy], one who knows the Self more extensively [than another]' (<s>Aitareyāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.2.1). And in <s>smṛti</s>: 'Whatever being possesses splendor, prosperity, or vigor —

children.text: tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejoṃ'śasaṃbhavam /' (gī. 10.41) iti /
children.translated_text: know that to be born of a portion of My radiance.' (<s>Gītā</s> 10.41)

children.text:
yatra yatra vibhūtyādyatiśayaḥ sa sa īśvara ityupāsyatayā codyate /
evamihāpyādityamaṇḍale hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvapāpmodayaliṅgātpara eveti vakṣyati /
evaṃ 'ākāśastalliṅgāt' (bra. 1.1.22) ityādiṣu draṣṭavyam /
evaṃ sadyomuktikāraṇamapyātmajñānamupādhiviśeṣadvāreṇopadiśyamānamapyavivakṣitopādhisaṃbandhaviśeṣaṃ parāparaviṣayatvena saṃdihyamānaṃ vākyagatiparyālocanayā nirṇetavyaṃ bhavati /
yathehaiva tāvat 'ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt' iti /
evamekamapi brahmāpekṣitopādhisaṃbandhaṃ nirastopādhisaṃbandhaṃ copāsyatvena jñeyatvena ca vedānteṣūpadiśyata iti pradarśayituṃ paro grantha ārabhyate /
yacca 'gatisāmānyāt' ityacetanakāraṇanirākaraṇamuktaṃ tadapi vākyāntarāṇi brahmaviṣayāṇi vyācakṣāṇena brahmaviparītakāraṇaniṣedhena prapañcyate-
children.translated_text: Wherever there is a predominance of splendor and such, that is the Lord — thus he is enjoined as an object of meditation. Similarly here too, it will be stated that the golden person in the orb of the sun, by the mark of freedom from all evil, is the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] itself. Thus it should be understood in passages like 'Space, because of the characteristic mark' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.22) and so forth. Similarly, even Self-knowledge that is the cause of immediate liberation, though taught through the medium of specific limiting adjuncts — even when its connection with a specific limiting adjunct is not intended, or when it is doubtful whether it refers to the higher or the lower [<s>Brahman</s>] — is to be determined by examining the purport of the passage. As right here: '<s>Ānandamaya</s> (consisting of bliss), because of repetition.' Thus, to demonstrate that one and the same <s>Brahman</s> — both with its connection to limiting adjuncts and with that connection removed — is taught in <s>Vedānta</s> as an object of meditation and as an object of knowledge, the subsequent portion of the text is commenced. And the refutation of an unconscious cause stated in 'because of common purport' is also elaborated here, while interpreting other passages concerning <s>Brahman</s>, by means of negating causes contrary to <s>Brahman</s> —

Beginning with 'That from which the origin [and so forth of this world]' and ending with the <s>sūtras</s> concluding with 'because of being heard' — for the <s>Vedānta</s> passages cited therein, it has been demonstrated through reasoning that they convey the meaning that the omniscient, omnipotent Lord is the cause of the origin, sustenance, and dissolution of the world. And through the presentation of a common purport, it has been explained that all <s>Vedānta</s> texts teach a conscious cause. What, then, is the occasion for the subsequent portion of the text? It is said: <s>Brahman</s> is known in two forms — qualified by the limiting adjuncts of the distinctions of name-and-form modifications, and the opposite, devoid of all limiting adjuncts. 'Where there is, as it were, duality, there one sees another; but where everything has become one's own Self, then by what and whom would one see?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15); 'Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else — that is the Infinite (<s>Bhūmā</s>); but where one sees another, hears another, knows another — that is the finite. That which is the Infinite is the immortal; that which is the finite is mortal' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1); 'The wise one, having fashioned all forms and created all names, sits calling them' (<s>Taittirīyāraṇyaka</s> 3.12.7); 'Without parts, without action, tranquil, without blemish, without stain — the supreme bridge to immortality, like fire whose fuel has been consumed' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.19); '<s>Neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6); 'Not gross, not subtle' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8); 'One is deficient, the other is complete' — thus thousands of passages demonstrate the twofold nature of <s>Brahman</s> through the distinction of the domains of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Therein, in the state of <s>avidyā</s>, all transactional activity regarding <s>Brahman</s> — characterized by the object of worship, the worshipper, and so forth — [takes place]. Among these, some meditations on <s>Brahman</s> are for the purpose of worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>), some for the purpose of gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>), and some for the purpose of perfecting ritual action. Their differences are based on the differences in the limiting adjuncts of specific qualities. But although one and the same Supreme Self, the Lord, qualified by those various specific qualities, is to be meditated upon, the fruits differ according to the meditation on the [respective] qualities. As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'In whatever way one meditates upon Him, that one becomes' — and: 'As is one's intention in this world, so does one become upon departing' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1). And from <s>smṛti</s>: 'Whatever state one remembers when abandoning the body at the end,

children.translated_text: <s>Ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s> — [The self] consisting of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>), because of repetition. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.12 |

(tai. 2.7) 'saiṣānandasya mīmāṃsā bhavati', ' etamānandamayamātmānamupasaṃkrāmati', 'ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān na bibheti kutaścana' (tai. 2.8,9) iti /

yattūktamannamayādyamukhyātmapravāhapatitatvādānandamayasyāpyamukhyatvamiti, nāsau doṣaḥ /
ānandamayasya sarvāntaratvāt /

mukhyameva hyātmānamupadidikṣu śāstraṃ lokabuddhimanusarat, annamayaṃ śarīramanātmānamatyantamūḍhānāmātmatvena prasiddhamanūdya mūṣāniṣiktadrutatāmrādipratimāvattato 'nantaraṃ tato 'ntaramityevaṃ pūrveṇa pūrveṇa samānamuttaramuttaramanātmānamātmeti grāhayat, pratipattisaukaryāpekṣayā sarvāntaraṃ mukhyamānandamayamātmānamupadideśeti śliṣṭataram /
children.translated_text: For scripture, wishing to teach the primary Self, follows ordinary understanding: having first mentioned the body consisting of food (<s>annamaya</s>) — which, though non-self, is well known to the extremely deluded as the self — and then, like a statue successively cast in a mold, [teaching] 'within this, the next inner; within that, the next inner' — making each successive non-self understood as the self through comparison with the preceding one — scripture teaches the innermost, primary <s>ānandamaya</s> self with a view to ease of comprehension. This is more consistent.

children.text: yathārundhatīnidarśane barhvīṣvapi tārāsvamukhyāsvarundhatīṣu darśitāsu yāntyā pradarśyate sā mukhyaivārundhatī bhavati, evamihāpyānandamayasya sarvāntaratvānmukhyamātmatvam /
children.translated_text: Just as in pointing out the star <s>Arundhatī</s>, even though many non-<s>Arundhatī</s> stars are pointed to first, the one finally pointed out is indeed the real <s>Arundhatī</s> — similarly here too, because the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the innermost of all, its being the primary self is [established].

children.text: yattu brūṣe, priyādīnāṃ śirastvādikalpanānupapannā mukhyasyātmana iti, ātītānantaropādhijanitā sā na svābhāvikītyadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for your objection that the assignment of 'dear' (<s>priya</s>) and such as head and so forth is unjustifiable for the primary self — that [assignment] is caused by the adjoining limiting adjuncts and is not intrinsic — so there is no fault.

children.text: śārīratvamapyānandamayasyānnamayādiśarīraparamparayā pradarśyamānatvāt, na punaḥ sākṣādeva śārīratvaṃ saṃsārivat, tasmādāndamayaḥ para evātmā // 12 //
children.translated_text: The embodiment too of the <s>ānandamaya</s> is demonstrated through the series of bodies consisting of food and so forth; it is not direct embodiment like that of a <s>saṃsārin</s>. Therefore, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the Supreme Self indeed. // 12 //

In the <s>Taittirīya</s>, after enumerating the self consisting of food (<s>annamaya</s>), the self consisting of vital breath (<s>prāṇamaya</s>), the self consisting of mind (<s>manomaya</s>), and the self consisting of understanding (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), it is stated: 'Different from this, the inner self consisting of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>)' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5). Therein arises a doubt: does the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' here refer to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself — which is the subject introduced in 'Truth, knowledge, infinity is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1) — or is it something other than <s>Brahman</s>, like the selves consisting of food and so forth? What is the initial position? The <s>ānandamaya</s> would be something other than <s>Brahman</s>, a non-primary self. Why? Because it falls within the sequence of non-primary selves beginning with the self consisting of food. Or, perhaps, since the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the innermost of all, it would indeed be the primary self. No, because of the connection with limbs such as 'dear' (<s>priya</s>) and because it is heard to be embodied. If the <s>ānandamaya</s> were the primary self, there would be no contact with 'dear' (<s>priya</s>) and such. But here it is heard: 'Of that, <s>priya</s> (the dear) is indeed the head' — and so forth. And embodiment is heard: 'This is indeed the embodied self of the former.' That is, this <s>ānandamaya</s> is the embodied self of the former <s>vijñānamaya</s> — this is the meaning. And for one who is embodied, the contact with the pleasant and unpleasant cannot be prevented. Therefore, the <s>ānandamaya</s> self is merely a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating self) — having reached this position, this is stated: '<s>Ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>' — the <s>ānandamaya</s> self deserves to be the Supreme Self itself. Why? Because of repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>). For in the Supreme Self alone, the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss) is repeatedly employed. Having introduced the <s>ānandamaya</s>, and having stated that very one's nature as <s>rasa</s> (essence) with 'He is indeed <s>rasa</s>,' it is stated: 'Having obtained this <s>rasa</s>, one becomes blissful'; 'Who indeed would breathe, who would live, if this bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) were not in space? For He alone gives bliss' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7); 'This is the investigation of that bliss'; 'One approaches this self consisting of bliss'; 'The knower of the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> fears nothing whatsoever' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8-9); and 'He knew: bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.6). And in another <s>śruti</s>: 'Consciousness, bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.28) — thus the word '<s>ānanda</s>' is seen applied to <s>Brahman</s> itself. Thus, from the repeated application of the word '<s>ānanda</s>' to <s>Brahman</s> many times, it is understood that the <s>ānandamaya</s> self is <s>Brahman</s>. As for what was said — that the <s>ānandamaya</s> too is non-primary because it falls within the sequence of non-primary selves beginning with the <s>annamaya</s> — that is no defect, because the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the innermost of all.

children.text:
FN: tasya niṣkalatvaśrutyā niraṃśatvādityarthaḥ /
kovānyāccalet, ko vā viśiṣya prāṇyājjīvet /
ānandayāti ānandayatītyarthaḥ /
upasaṃkramaṇaṃ prāptiḥ brahmaṇaḥ svarūpamiti śeṣaḥ /
lokabuddheḥ sthūlagrāhitāmanusaradityarthaḥ /
ihāpi amukhyapravāhe patitasyāpi /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Of that' — because of the <s>śruti</s> declaring it to be without parts, the meaning is that it is without limbs. 'Who else could stir?' 'Who would especially breathe or live?' '<s>Ānandayāti</s>' means 'gives bliss.' '<s>Upasaṃkramaṇa</s>' means attainment — the remainder is 'the nature of <s>Brahman</s>.' The meaning of 'ordinary understanding' is: following the gross-grasping nature of common cognition. 'Here too' — even though [the <s>ānandamaya</s>] has fallen within the sequence of non-primary [selves].

children.text: vikāraśabdān neti cen na prācuryāt | BBs_1,1.13 |
children.translated_text: Because of the modification-denoting suffix — if [one says] no, [we reply] no, because of abundance. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.13 |

children.text:
atrāha- nānandamayaḥ para ātmā bhavitumarhati /
kasmāt, vikāraśabdāt /
prakṛtivacanādayamanyaḥ śabdo vikāravacanaḥ samadhigataḥ, ānandamaya iti mayaṭo vikārthatvāt /
tasmādannamayādiśabdavadvikāraviṣaya evānandamayaśabda iticet, na /
prācuryārthe 'pi mayaṭaḥ smaraṇāt /
'tatprakṛtavacane mayaṭ' (pā. 5.4.21) iti hi pracuratāyāmapi mayaṭ smaryate /
children.translated_text: For the rule '<s>tatprakṛtavacane mayaṭ</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 5.4.21) records the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> also in the sense of abundance.

children.text: yathā 'annamayo yajñaḥ' ityannapracura ucyate, evamānandapracuraṃ brahmānandamaya ucyate /
children.translated_text: Just as '<s>annamayo yajñaḥ</s>' (a sacrifice abounding in food) refers to one abounding in food, so too <s>Brahman</s>, abounding in bliss, is called '<s>ānandamaya</s>.'

children.text: ānandapracuratvaṃ ca brahmaṇo manuṣyatvādārabhyottarasminnuttarasminsthāne śataguṇa ānanda ityuktvā brahmānandasya niratiśayatvāvadhāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: And the abundance of bliss in <s>Brahman</s> is [established] because, starting from the human state and going to each successively higher station, a hundredfold increase of bliss is stated, culminating in the ascertainment that the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> is unsurpassed.

children.text: tasmātprācuryārthe mayaṭ // 13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> is in the sense of abundance. // 13 //

Here one objects: the <s>ānandamaya</s> cannot be the Supreme Self. Why? Because of the modification-denoting suffix. From the expression denoting the material cause, this other suffix denoting modification has been understood — the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> in '<s>ānandamaya</s>' having the sense of modification. Therefore, just as the words '<s>annamaya</s>' and such denote modifications, so too the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' denotes a modification — if this be said, no. Because the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> is also recorded in the sense of abundance.

children.text: taddhetuvyapadeśāc ca | BBs_1,1.14 |
children.translated_text: Because of the declaration of it being the cause of that [bliss]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.14 |

children.text:
itaśca prācuryārthe mayaṭ /
yasmādānandahetutvaṃ brahmaṇo vyapadiśati śrutiḥ- 'eṣa hyevānandayāti' iti /
ānandayatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: He causes bliss.

children.text: yo hyanyānānandayati sa pracurānanda iti prasiddhaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: For it is well known that whoever gives bliss to others possesses abundant bliss.

children.text: yathā loke yo 'nyeṣāṃ dhanikatvamāpādayati sa pracuradhana iti gamyate, tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, whoever brings about the wealth of others is understood to possess abundant wealth — similarly here.

children.text: tasmātprācuryārthe 'pi mayaṭaḥ saṃbhavādānandamayaḥ para evātmā // 14 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> can have the sense of abundance, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the Supreme Self indeed. // 14 //
For this additional reason, the suffix <s>mayaṭ</s> is in the sense of abundance. Because the <s>śruti</s> declares <s>Brahman</s> to be the cause of bliss: 'For He alone gives bliss.'

children.text: māntravarṇikameva ca gīyate | BBs_1,1.15 |
children.translated_text: And because the same one described in the <s>mantra</s> is celebrated. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.15 |

children.text:
itaścānandamayaḥ para evātmā /
yasmāt 'brahmavidāpnoti param' ityupakramya 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma' (tai. 2.1)
children.translated_text: For this further reason, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the Supreme Self itself. Because, having begun with 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the Supreme,' and then 'Truth, knowledge, infinity is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1) —

children.text: ityasminmantre yatprakṛtaṃ brahma satyajñānānantaviśeṣaṇairnirdharitaṃ, yasmādākāśādikrameṇa sthāvarajaṅgamāni bhūtānyajāyanta, yacca bhūtāni sṛṣṭvā tānyanupraviśya guhāyāmavasthitaṃ, sarvāntaraṃ, yasya vijñānāya 'anyo 'ntara ātmānyo 'ntara ātmā' iti prakrāntaṃ tanmāntravarṇikameva brahmeha gīyate 'anyo 'ntara ātmānandamayaḥ' (tai. 2.5) iti /
mantrabrāhmaṇayoścaikārthatvaṃ yuktaṃ, avirodhāt /
children.translated_text: And it is appropriate that the <s>mantra</s> and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> have the same meaning, since there is no contradiction.

children.text: anyathā hi prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriye syātām /
children.translated_text: For otherwise, there would be abandonment of the subject and introduction of a non-subject.

children.text: na cānnamayādibhya ivānandamayādanyo 'ntara ātmābhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: And no other inner self beyond the <s>ānandamaya</s> is mentioned, as there is beyond the <s>annamaya</s> and others.

children.text: etanniṣṭhaiva ca 'saiṣā bhārgavī vāruṇī vidyā' (tai. 3.6) tasmādānandamayaḥ para evātmā //15 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bhārgavī Vāruṇī Vidyā</s> (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.6) has this [<s>ānandamaya</s>] as its culmination. Therefore, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the Supreme Self indeed. // 15 //

— the <s>Brahman</s> that was introduced as the subject in that <s>mantra</s>, determined by the qualifications of truth, knowledge, and infinity; from which, in the sequence beginning with space, moving and stationary beings were born; which, having created those beings, entered into them and abides in the cave [of the heart]; which is the innermost of all; for the knowledge of which the progression 'the inner self within this, the inner self within that' was begun — that very <s>Brahman</s> described in the <s>mantra</s> is celebrated here as 'the inner self consisting of bliss' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5).

children.text:
FN: yasmādityasya tasmāditi vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ /
yannirdhāritaṃ tadeveha gīyata iti yojanā /
ekārthatvesatyupāyopeyatvayogādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The 'from which' is to be connected with the remote 'therefore.' The construction is: that which was determined there is the very thing celebrated here. The meaning is: given the identity of meaning, there is fitness as both means and end.

children.text: netaro 'nupapatteḥ | BBs_1,1.16 |
children.translated_text: Not the other, because of impossibility. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.16 |

children.text:
itaścānandamayaḥ para evātmā /
netaraḥ /
itara īśvarādanyaḥ saṃsārī jīva ityarthaḥ /
na jīva ānandamayaśabdenābhidhīyate /
kasmāt /
anupapatteḥ /
ānandamayaṃ hi prakṛtya śrūyate- 'so 'kāmayata /
bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti /
sa tapo 'tapyata /
sa tapastaptvā /
children.translated_text: Having practiced <s>tapas</s>,

children.text: idaṃsarvamasṛjata /
children.translated_text: He created all this —

children.text: yadidaṃ kiñca' (tai. 2.6) iti /
children.translated_text: whatever there is' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6).

children.text: tatra prākśarīrādyutpatterabhidhyānaṃ sṛjyamānānāṃ ca vikārāṇāṃ sraṣṭuravyatirekaḥ sarvavikārasṛṣṭiśca, na parasmādātmano 'nyatropapadyate // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therein, the deliberation prior to the creation of the body and such, the non-difference of the modifications being created from the creator, and the creation of all modifications — these cannot be established in anything other than the supreme Self. // 16 //

For this further reason, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the Supreme Self itself — 'not the other.' 'The other' means the <s>saṃsārin</s>, the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), who is different from the Lord — this is the meaning. The individual soul is not referred to by the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>.' Why? Because of impossibility. For, having introduced the <s>ānandamaya</s> as the subject, the <s>śruti</s> states: 'He desired: "May I become many, may I be born." He practiced <s>tapas</s>.

children.text: bhedavyapadeśāc ca | BBs_1,1.17 |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhedavyapadeśāc ca</s> — And because of the designation of difference. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.17 |

children.text:
itaśca nānandamayaḥ saṃsārī /
yasmādānandamayādhikāre- 'raso vai saḥ /
rasaṃhyevāyaṃ labdhvānandī bhavati' (tai. 2.7) iti jīvānandamayau bhedena vyapadiśati /
nahi labdhaiva labdhavyo bhavati /
kathaṃ tarhi 'ātmānveṣṭavyaḥ', 'ātmalābhānna paraṃ vidyate' iti śrutismṛtī, yāvatā na labdhaiva labdhavyo bhavatītyuktam /
bāḍham /
tathāpyātmano 'pracyutātmabhāsyaiva satastatvānavabodhanimitto dehādiṣvanātmasvātmatvaniścayo laukiko dṛṣṭaḥ /
tena dehādibhūtasyātmano 'pyātmānanviṣṭo 'nveṣṭavyo 'labdho labdhavyo 'śrutaḥ śrotavyo 'mato mantavyo 'vijñāto vijñātavya ityādibhedavyapadeśa upapadyate /
pratiṣidhyata eva tu paramārthataḥ sarvajñātparameśvarādanyo draṣṭā śrotā vā 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' (bṛ. 3.7.23) ityādinā /
parameśvarastvavidyākalpitāccharīrātkartṛbhoktṛvijñānātmākhyādanyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The supreme Lord, however, is different from the body — which is imagined by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — and from [the entity] called the cognitive self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), the agent and experiencer.

children.text: yathā māyāvinaścarmakhaḍgadharātsūtreṇākāśamadhirohataḥ sa eva māyāvī paramārtharūpo bhūmiṣṭho 'nyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the magician himself, in his true nature, standing on the ground, is different from [the appearance of] the magician bearing a leather shield and sword and climbing to the sky by a thread;

children.text: yathāvā dhaṭākāśādupādhiparicchinnādanupādhiraparicchinna ākāśo 'nyaḥ /
children.translated_text: or just as space, unconditioned and unlimited, is different from the space in a pot, which is delimited by a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>).

children.text: īdṛśaṃ ca vijñānātmaparamātmabhedamāśritya 'netaro 'nupapatteḥ', 'bhedavyapadeśācca' ityuktam // 17 //
children.translated_text: And relying on such a distinction between the cognitive self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) and the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>), it was stated: 'Not the other, because of the impossibility [of it being so]' and 'Because of the designation of difference.' // 17 //

For this reason too, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is not the transmigrating soul.
Because in the section on the <s>ānandamaya</s>: 'He is the essence (<s>rasa</s>). For having obtained this essence, one becomes blissful' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7) — this designates the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>ānandamaya</s> as different from each other.
For what has already been obtained cannot be something to be obtained again.
But then how [do we reconcile] the <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>: 'The Self is to be sought,' and 'There is nothing higher than the attainment of the Self' — given that it has been said that what is already obtained cannot be something to be obtained again?
Indeed so.
Nevertheless, the worldly ascertainment of Self-hood in the body and such, which are not the Self — caused by the non-realization of the truth even while the Self, which has never departed from its own Self-nature, exists — is observed.
Through that [false identification], even for the Self that has become identified with the body and such, the designation of difference — 'the Self sought, to be sought; the Self not obtained, to be obtained; the Self not heard, to be heard; the Self not reflected upon, to be reflected upon; the Self not known, to be known' — is justified.
But in the ultimate sense, any seer or hearer other than the omniscient supreme Lord is indeed negated: 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23) and such.

children.text:
FN: adhikāraḥ prakaraṇam /
sa ānandamayo rasaḥ sāraḥ /
akhaṇḍaikarasasya /
lokādanapeto laukiko 'prāmāṇikaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: '<s>Adhikāra</s>' means section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).
That <s>ānandamaya</s> is the essence (<s>rasa</s>), the quintessence.
Of the undivided, singular essence.
'<s>Laukika</s>' (worldly) means that which has not departed from common [perception], [hence] invalid.

children.text: kāmāc ca nānumānāpekṣā | BBs_1,1.18 |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmāc ca nānumānāpekṣā</s> — And because of desire, there is no dependence on inference. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.18 |

children.text: ānandamayādhikāre ca 'so 'kāmayata bahusyāṃ prajāyeya' (tai. 2.6) iti kāmayitṛtvanirdeśānnānumānikamapi sāṃkhyaparikalpitamacetanaṃ pradhānamānandamayatvena kāraṇatvena vāpekṣitavyam /
children.translated_text: And in the section on the <s>ānandamaya</s>, from the indication of the capacity to desire in 'It desired: "Let me become many; let me be born"' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6), the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> conceived by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> should not be relied upon either as being the <s>ānandamaya</s> or as being the cause — even through inference.

children.text: 'īkṣaternāśabdam' (bra. 1.1.5) iti nirākṛtamapi pradhānaṃ pūrvasūtrodāhṛtāṃ kāmayitṛtvaśrutimāśritya prasaṅgātpunarnirākriyate gatisāmānyaprapañcanāya // 18 //
children.translated_text: Although <s>Pradhāna</s> was already refuted by 'Because of seeing — not [<s>Pradhāna</s>]; it lacks scriptural basis' (<s>Bra</s>. 1.1.5), it is refuted again incidentally — relying on the scriptural statement of desire-capacity cited in the previous <s>sūtra</s> — for the purpose of elaborating the shared reasoning. // 18 //

children.text: asminn asya ca tadyogaṃ śāsti | BBs_1,1.19 |
children.translated_text: <s>Asminn asya ca tadyogaṃ śāsti</s> — And [scripture] teaches that this one's union with That is in this [<s>ānandamaya</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.19 |

children.text:
itaśca na pradhāne jīve vānandamayaśabdaḥ /
yasmādasminnānandamaye prakṛta ātmani pratibuddhasyāsya jīvasya tadyogaṃ śāsti /
tadātmanā yogastadyogaḥ, tadbhāvāpattiḥ /
muktirityarthaḥ /
tadyogaṃ śāsti śāstraṃ- 'yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnadṛśye 'nātmye 'nirukte 'nilayane 'bhayaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vindate /
atha so 'bhayaṃ gato bhavati /
yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnudaramantaraṃ kurute /
atha tasya bhayaṃ bhavati' (tai. 2.7) iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-
children.translated_text:
For this reason too, the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' does not refer to <s>Pradhāna</s> or the <s>jīva</s>.
Because in this <s>ānandamaya</s> — the Self that is the subject under discussion — [scripture] teaches the union (<s>yoga</s>) with That of this awakened <s>jīva</s>.
'Union with That' (<s>tadyoga</s>) means identity with That — attaining the nature of That.
The meaning is: liberation.
[Scripture] teaches this union with That: 'For when indeed this one finds fearless support in that which is invisible, bodiless, inexpressible, without foundation — then he has attained fearlessness. But when indeed this one makes even the slightest separation in it — then there is fear for him' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7).
What is stated here amounts to this:

children.text:
yadaitasminnānandamaye 'lpamapyantaramatādātmyarūpaṃ paśyati tadā saṃsārabhayānna nivartate /
yadā tvetasminnānandamaye nirantaraṃ tādātmyena pratitiṣṭhati tadā saṃsārabhayānnivartata iti /
tacca paramātmaparigrahe ghaṭate, na pradhānaparigrahe jīvaparigrahe vā /
tasmādānandamayaḥ paramātmeti sthitam /
idaṃ tviha vaktavyam- 'sa vā eṣa puruṣo 'nnarasamayaḥ' /
'tasmādvā etasmādannarasamayāt /
anyo 'ntara ātmā prāṇamayaḥ' tasmāt 'anyo 'ntara ātmā manomayaḥ' tasmāt 'anyo 'ntara ātmā vijñānamayaḥ' (tai. 2.1,2,3,4) iti ca vikārārthe mayaṭpravāhe satyānandamaya evākasmādardhajaratīyanyāyena kathamiva mayaṭaḥ prācuryarthātvaṃ brahmaviṣayatvaṃ cāśrīyata iti /
māntravarṇikabrahmādhikārāditi cet, na /
annamayādīnāmapi tarhi brahmatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
atrāha- yuktamannamayādīnāmabrahmatvaṃ, tasmāttasmādāntarasyāntarasyānyasyānyasyātmana ucyamānatvāt ānandamayāttu na kaścidanya āntara ātmocyate, tenānandamayasya brahmatvam, anyathā prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriyāprasaṅgāditi /
children.translated_text:
When one sees even the slightest difference in this <s>ānandamaya</s> — a difference not of the nature of identity — then one does not turn away from the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
But when one abides uninterruptedly in identity with this <s>ānandamaya</s>, then one turns away from the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
And that is consistent if the supreme Self is accepted [as the referent of <s>ānandamaya</s>], not if <s>Pradhāna</s> or the <s>jīva</s> is accepted.
Therefore, it is established that the <s>ānandamaya</s> is the supreme Self.
But here this must be said: 'This person is indeed of the nature of the essence of food (<s>annarasamaya</s>).' 'Other than and within this one of the nature of the essence of food is the self made of <s>prāṇa</s> (<s>prāṇamaya</s>)'; from that, 'another inner self made of mind (<s>manomaya</s>)'; from that, 'another inner self made of cognition (<s>vijñānamaya</s>)' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1-4) — when there is a flow of the suffix '<s>-maya</s>' in the sense of modification, how is it that for the <s>ānandamaya</s> alone, suddenly, by the principle of <s>ardhajaratī</s> (half-old-woman — i.e., inconsistently), the suffix '<s>-maya</s>' is taken in the sense of abundance and as referring to <s>Brahman</s>?
If it is said: because the subject is the <s>Brahman</s> [declared in the] <s>mantra</s> portion — no. For then the <s>annamaya</s> and others too would absurdly be <s>Brahman</s>.
Here the [objector] says: it is proper that the <s>annamaya</s> and others are not <s>Brahman</s>, because progressively inner and different selves are stated beyond each one; but beyond the <s>ānandamaya</s>, no other inner self is stated — therefore the <s>ānandamaya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>; otherwise there would be the fault of abandoning the subject and introducing a new subject.

children.text:
atrocyate- yadyapyannamayādibhya ivānandamayādanyo 'ntara ātmeti na śrūyate tathāpi nānandamayasya brahmatvaṃ, yata ānandamayaṃ prakṛtya śrūyate- 'tasya priyameva śiraḥ /
modo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ /
pramoda uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ /
ānanda ātmā /
brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' (tai. 2.5) iti /
tatra yadbrahma mantravarṇe prakṛtam- 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma' iti, tadiha 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityucyate /
tadvijijñāpayiṣayaivānnamayādaya ānandamayaparyantāḥ pañca kośāḥ kalpyante /
tatra kutaḥ prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriyāprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text:
To this we say: Although, unlike the <s>annamaya</s> and others, no other inner self is heard beyond the <s>ānandamaya</s>, still the <s>ānandamaya</s> is not <s>Brahman</s>. Because, having introduced the <s>ānandamaya</s> as subject, [the scripture] states: 'Joy (<s>priya</s>) is its head; delight (<s>moda</s>) is its right wing; great delight (<s>pramoda</s>) is its left wing; bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) is its self; <s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5).
Therein, the <s>Brahman</s> that was introduced as the subject in the <s>mantra</s> portion — 'Truth, knowledge, infinity is <s>Brahman</s>' — that is what is referred to here as '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support.'
It is with the very intention of making that [<s>Brahman</s>] known that the five sheaths (<s>kośas</s>), from the <s>annamaya</s> to the <s>ānandamaya</s>, are imagined.
Therein, where is the fault of abandoning the subject and introducing a new subject?

children.text:
nanvānandamayasyāvayavatvena 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityucyate, annamayādīnāmiva 'idaṃ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityādi /
tatra kathaṃ brahmaṇaḥ svapradhānatvaṃ śakyaṃ vijñātum /
children.translated_text: But [the objection]: '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support' is said as if <s>Brahman</s> were a part of the <s>ānandamaya</s>, just as for the <s>annamaya</s> and others [it is said] 'this is its tail, its support.' In that case, how can <s>Brahman</s>'s independent primacy be understood?

children.text: prakṛtatvāditi brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: We say: because it is the subject.

children.text: nanvānandamayāvayavatvenāpi brahmaṇi vijñāyamāne na prakṛtatvaṃ hīyate, ānandamayasya brahmatvāditi /
children.translated_text: But [the objection]: even when <s>Brahman</s> is known as a part of the <s>ānandamaya</s>, the subject-status is not lost, because the <s>ānandamaya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
atrocyate- tathā sati tadeva brahmānandamaya ātmāvayavī tadeva ca brahmapucchaṃ pratiṣṭhāvayava ityasāmañjasyaṃ syāt /
anyataraparigrahe tu yuktaṃ 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityatraiva brahmanirdeśa āśrayituṃ, brahmaśabdasaṃyogāt /
nānandamayavākye brahmaśabdasaṃyogābhāvāditi /
apica brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā ityuktatvedamucyate- 'tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati /
asanneva sa bhavati /
asadbrahmeti veda cet /
asti brahmeti cedveda /
santamenaṃ tato viduriti' (tai. 2.6) asmiṃśca śloke 'nanukṛṣyānandamayaṃ, brahmaṇa eva bhāvābhāvavedanayorguṇadoṣābhidhānādgamyate 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityatra brahmaṇa eva svapradhānatvamiti /
na cānandamayasyatmano bhāvābhāvāśaṅkā yuktā, priyamodādiviśeṣasyānandamayasya sarvalokaprasiddhatvāt /
kathaṃ punaḥ svapradhānaṃ sadbrahma, ānandamayasya pucchatvena nirdiśyate- 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' iti /
children.translated_text:
To this we say: In that case, there would be the incoherence that <s>Brahman</s> itself, being the <s>ānandamaya</s> self, is the whole possessing parts, and <s>Brahman</s> itself is the tail — the part that is the support.
But if one of the two [options] is accepted, it is proper to rely on the designation of <s>Brahman</s> in the statement '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support' alone, because of the presence of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' there.
Not in the statement about the <s>ānandamaya</s>, because of the absence of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' there.
Moreover, after stating '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support,' this is said: 'Regarding this, there is this verse: "One who knows <s>Brahman</s> as non-existent becomes himself non-existent. If one knows <s>Brahman</s> as existing — then they know him as existent"' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6). In this verse, the <s>ānandamaya</s> is not referred to, and from the statement of merit and demerit concerning the knowledge and non-knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> [alone], it is understood that in '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support,' <s>Brahman</s> alone has independent primacy.
And it is not proper to doubt the existence or non-existence of the <s>ānandamaya</s> self, since the <s>ānandamaya</s> — characterized by the specific [experiences of] joy, delight, and the like — is well-known to everyone.
But how is it that <s>Brahman</s>, having independent primacy and being existent, is designated as the tail of the <s>ānandamaya</s>: '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support'?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
pucchavatpucchaṃ , pratiṣṭhā parāyaṇamekanīḍaṃ laukikasyānandajātasya brahmānanda ityetadanena vivakṣyate, nāvayavatvaṃ, 'etasyaivānandasyānyāni bhūtāni mātrāmupajīvanti' (bṛha. 4.3.32) iti śrutyantarāt /
apica ānandamayasya brahmatve priyādyavayavatvena saviśeṣaṃ brahmābhyupagantavyam /
nirviśeṣaṃ tu brahma vākyaśeṣe śrūyate, vāṅmanasayoragocaratvābhidhānāt- ' yato vāco nivartante /
aprāpya manasā saha /
ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān /
na bibheti kutaścaneti' (tai. 2.9) /
apica ānandapracura ityukte duḥkhāstitvamapi gamyate prācuryasya loke pratiyogyalpatvāpekṣatvāt /
tathāca sati, 'yatra nānyatpaśti nānyacchṛṇoti nānyadvijānāti sa bhūmā' (chā. 7.24.1) iti bhūmni brahmaṇi tadvyatiriktābhāvaśrutirūparudhyeta /
pratiśarīraṃ ca priyādibhedādānandamayasyāpi bhinnatvam /
brahma tu na pratiśarīraṃ bhidyate, 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma' (taitti. 2.1) ityānantaśruteḥ, 'eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā' (śve. 6.11) iti ca śrutyantarāt /
nacānandamayasyābhyāsaḥ śrūyate /
prātipadikārthamātrameva hi sarvatrābhyasyate- 'raso vai saḥ, rasaṃhyevāyaṃ labdhvānandī bhavati, ko hyevānyātkaḥ prāṇyāt, yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt' /
'saiṣānandasya mīmāṃsā bhavati' /
'ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvānna bibheti kutaścaneti' (tai.2.7.8.9) 'ānando brahmeti vyajānāt' (tai. 6.6) iti ca /
yadica ānandamayaśabdasya brahmaviṣayatvaṃ niścitaṃ bhavet, tata uttareṣvānandamātraprayogeṣvapyānandamayābhyāsaḥ kalpyeta /
na tvānandamayasya brahmatvamasti, priyaśirastvādibhirhetubhirityavocāma /
tasmācchrutyantare 'vijñānamānandaṃ brahma' (bṛ. 3.9.28) ityānandaprātipadikasya brahmaṇi prayogadarśanāt, 'yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt' ityādirbrahmaviṣayaḥ prayogo na tvānandamayābhyāsa ityavagantavyam /
yatsvayaṃ mayaḍantasyaivānandaśabdasyābhyāsaḥ - 'etamānandamayātmānamupasaṃkrāmati' (tai. 2.8) iti, na tasya brahmaviṣayatvamasti, vikārātmanāmevānnamayādīnāmanātmanāmupasaṃkramitavyānāṃ pravāhe paṭhitatvāt /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault. What is meant to be conveyed by this is: 'tail' means 'like a tail' — a support, a resting place, a single nest for worldly bliss; the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> [is the ultimate support of all bliss] — not that it is a [literal] part. [This is understood] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'All other beings subsist on a portion of this very bliss' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.32).
Moreover, if the <s>ānandamaya</s> were <s>Brahman</s>, then <s>Brahman</s> would have to be accepted as qualified — having parts such as joy (<s>priya</s>) and so forth. But <s>Brahman</s> without qualifications is heard in the remainder of the [same] text, since it is stated to be beyond the reach of speech and mind: 'From which words turn back, together with the mind, unable to reach it; knowing the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, one fears nothing whatsoever' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.9).
Moreover, when [something] is said to be 'abundant in bliss' (<s>ānandamaya</s> in the sense of abundance), the existence of suffering is also implied, since in common usage, abundance presupposes the relative paucity of its opposite. And in that case, the <s>śruti</s> regarding <s>Brahman</s> as the <s>Bhūman</s> (infinite) — 'Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else — that is the Infinite (<s>Bhūman</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1), which states the absence of anything other [than <s>Brahman</s>] — would be obstructed.
And because of the difference of joy and such in each body, the <s>ānandamaya</s> too would be differentiated.
But <s>Brahman</s> is not differentiated according to each body, because of the <s>śruti</s> declaring it infinite: 'Truth, knowledge, infinity is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1); and from another <s>śruti</s>: 'The one God hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.11).
Nor is the repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of the <s>ānandamaya</s> heard [in the text]. For what is repeated everywhere is only the meaning of the nominal stem [<s>ānanda</s>, bliss] — 'He is the essence. For having obtained this essence, one becomes blissful' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7); 'Who indeed would breathe, who would live, if this bliss were not in space?' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7); 'This is the investigation of bliss' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8); 'Knowing the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, one fears nothing whatsoever' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.9); 'He knew: bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.6).
And if the referentiality of the word '<s>ānandamaya</s>' to <s>Brahman</s> were established, then even in the subsequent usages of the mere [stem] '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss), one could suppose it to be a repetition of '<s>ānandamaya</s>.' But the <s>ānandamaya</s> is not <s>Brahman</s>, for the reasons stated — having joy as its head and such — as we have said.
Therefore, from the usage of the nominal stem '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss) in reference to <s>Brahman</s> in another <s>śruti</s> — 'Knowledge, bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.28) — it should be understood that [passages like] 'If this bliss were not in space' and such are about <s>Brahman</s>, not a repetition of '<s>ānandamaya</s>.'
As for the repetition of the word '<s>ānanda</s>' itself with the suffix '<s>-maya</s>' — 'One approaches this self made of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>)' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8) — that does not refer to <s>Brahman</s>, since it is read in the flow of the <s>annamaya</s> and other modified, non-Self [sheaths] that are to be approached [and transcended].

children.text: nanvānandamayasyopasaṃkramitavyasyānnamayādivadbrahmatve sati naiva viduṣo brahmaprāptiphalaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: But [the objection]: if the <s>ānandamaya</s>, which is to be approached [and transcended], is not <s>Brahman</s> — just like the <s>annamaya</s> and others — then the fruit of attaining <s>Brahman</s> for the knower would not be indicated at all.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
ānandamayopasaṃkramaṇanirdeśenaiva pucchapratiṣṭhābhūtabrahmaprāpteḥ phalasyanirdiṣṭatvāt /
'tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati /
yato vāco nivartante' ityadinā ca prapañcyamānatvāt /
yā tvānandamayasaṃnidhāne 'so 'kāmayata bahusyāṃ prajāyeyeti' iyaṃ śrutirudāhṛtā sā 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityanena saṃnihitatareṇa brahmaṇā saṃbadhyamānā nānandamayasya brahmatāṃ pratibodhayati /
tadapekṣatvāccottarasya granthasya 'raso vai saḥ' ityādernānandamayaviṣayatā /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault. Because the fruit — the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>, which is the support as the tail — is indicated by the very statement of approaching the <s>ānandamaya</s>.
And because it is elaborated by [the passage] 'Regarding this too, there is this verse: "From which words turn back..."' and so forth.
As for the <s>śruti</s> cited in proximity to the <s>ānandamaya</s> — 'It desired: "Let me become many; let me be born"' — that, being connected with <s>Brahman</s>, which is more proximate through '<s>Brahman</s> is its tail, its support,' does not make the <s>ānandamaya</s> understood as <s>Brahman</s>.
And because the subsequent text — 'He is the essence' and so forth — is dependent on that [<s>Brahman</s>, not on the <s>ānandamaya</s>], it does not pertain to the <s>ānandamaya</s>.

children.text: nanu 'so 'kāmayata' iti brahmaṇi puṃliṅganirdeśo nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: But [the objection]: the masculine designation in 'He (<s>saḥ</s>) desired' is not appropriate with reference to <s>Brahman</s> [which is neuter].

children.text:
nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' ityatra puṃliṅgenāpyātmaśabdena brahmaṇaḥ prakṛtatvāt /
yā tu bhārgavī vāruṇī vidyā 'ānando brahmeti vyajānāt' iti tasyāṃ mayaḍaśravaṇāt, priyaśirastvādyaśravaṇācca yuktamānandasya brahmatvam /
tasmādaṇumātramapi viśeṣamanāśritya na svata eva priyaśirastvādi brahmaṇa upapadyate /
naceha saviśeṣaṃ brahma pratipipādayiṣitaṃ, vāṅmanasagocarātikramaśruteḥ /
tasmādannamayādiṣvivānandamaye 'pi vikārārtha eva mayaḍvijñeyo na prācuryārthaḥ /
sūtrāṇi tvevaṃ vyākhyeyāni- 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityatra kimānandamayāvayavatvena brahma vivakṣyata uta svapradhānatveneti /
pucchaśabdādavayavatveneti prāpta ucyate- 'ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt' ānandamaya ātmetyatra 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' iti svapradhānameva brahmopadiśyate, abhyasāt /
'asanneva sa bhavati' ityasminnigamanāśloke brahmaṇa eva kevalasyābhyasyamānatvāt /
vikāraśabdānneti cenna prācuryāt /
vikāraśabdenāvayavaśabdo 'bhipretaḥ /
pucchamityavayavaśabdānna svapradhānatvaṃ brahmaṇa iti yaduktaṃ, tasya parihāro vaktavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect. Because in 'From that very Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1), <s>Brahman</s> is already the subject, even though the word '<s>ātman</s>' is in the masculine gender. As for the <s>Bhārgavī Vāruṇī Vidyā</s>, in which [the conclusion is] 'He knew that bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' — in that [passage], because the suffix '<s>mayaṭ</s>' is not heard, and because [the epithets] 'having joy as its head' and such are not heard, it is proper that bliss is <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, without resorting to even the slightest distinguishing feature, the possession of 'joy as the head' and such does not apply to <s>Brahman</s> of itself. And here, <s>Brahman</s> qualified by attributes is not intended to be taught, because of the scriptural statement that [<s>Brahman</s>] transcends the range of speech and mind. Therefore, in the case of <s>ānandamaya</s> too, just as in the cases of <s>annamaya</s> and such, the suffix '<s>mayaṭ</s>' should be understood in the sense of modification, not in the sense of abundance. But the <s>sūtras</s> should be explained as follows: In '<s>brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā</s>' (Brahman is the tail, the support), is <s>Brahman</s> intended as a part of <s>ānandamaya</s>, or as having its own independent primacy? Since from the word '<s>puccha</s>' (tail) [suggesting] a part, [the conclusion that it is] a part is arrived at — to this it is said: '<s>Ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>' — in '<s>ānandamaya ātmā</s>' (the self consisting of bliss), where it says '<s>brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā</s>,' <s>Brahman</s> is taught as having its own independent primacy — because of repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>). Because in the concluding verse '<s>asanneva sa bhavati</s>' (he becomes as if non-existent), it is <s>Brahman</s> alone in its unqualified form that is repeatedly mentioned. [If it is argued] 'not so, because of the word denoting modification' — no, because [the suffix '<s>mayaṭ</s>' here is used] in the sense of abundance. By 'word denoting modification,' the word denoting a part is meant. The claim that <s>Brahman</s> does not have independent primacy because of the word '<s>puccha</s>' (tail), which is a word denoting a part — a rebuttal of that must be stated.

children.text:
atrocyate- nāyaṃ doṣaḥ, prācuryādapyavayavaśabdopapatteḥ /
prācuryaṃ prāyāpattiḥ, avayavaprāye vacanamityarthaḥ /
annamayādīnāṃ hi śiraādiṣu pucchāntevavayaveḥṣūkte tvānandamayasyāpi śiraādīnyavayavāntarāṇyuktvāvayavaprāyāpattyā 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' ityāha, nāvayavavivakṣayā /
yatkāraṇamabhyāsāditi svapradhānatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ samarthitam /
'taddhetuvyapadeśācca' /
sarvasya vikārajātasya sānandamayasya kāraṇatvena brahma vyapadiśyate- idaṃ sarvamasṛjata /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is designated as the cause of the entire class of modifications, including <s>ānandamaya</s>: 'It created all this,

children.text: yadidaṃ kiñca (tai. 2.6) iti /
children.translated_text: whatever there is' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6).

children.text: naca kāraṇaṃ sat brahma svavikārasyānandamayasya mukhyayā vṛttyāvayava upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahman</s>, being the cause, cannot properly serve as a part of its own modification, <s>ānandamaya</s>, in the primary sense.

children.text: aparāṇyapi sūtrāṇi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ pucchavākyanirdiṣṭasyaiva brahmaṇa upapādakāni draṣṭavyāni // 19//
children.translated_text: The remaining <s>sūtras</s> too should be seen as establishing that very <s>Brahman</s> indicated by the 'tail' passage, as far as applicable. // 19 //

To this it is said: This is not a defect, because the word denoting a part is justified even on the basis of abundance. 'Abundance' means predominance — the meaning is: an expression used when parts predominate. For when the parts of <s>annamaya</s> and such — head and so forth, up to the tail — have been stated, and when the other parts such as head and so forth of <s>ānandamaya</s> too have been stated, then by virtue of the predominance of [the pattern of] parts, [the scripture] says '<s>brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā</s>' — not with the intention of designating [<s>Brahman</s> as] a part. The reason being that the independent primacy of <s>Brahman</s> was established through repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>). '<s>Taddhetuvyapadeśācca</s>' (And because of the designation as its cause) —

children.text: FN: anātmye sasaṃbandhitayādhyastendriyajātenāpañcākṛtabhūtakāryeṇātmyena tādātmyādihīne, anirukte nikṛṣyocyanta iti niruktāni bhūtasūkṣmāṇi taiścābhedavarjite, niḥśeṣalayasthānaṃ nilayanaṃ māyā tacchūnye /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Anātmye</s>' — in what is not the Self, connected through superimposition with the collection of sense organs — which is the effect of the unquintuplicated subtle elements — as if it were the Self; in what is devoid of identity and such [with the Self]. '<s>Anirukte</s>' — '<s>niruktāni</s>' are the subtle elements, so called because they are etymologically explained; and [<s>ānandamaya</s> is] devoid of non-difference from those. '<s>Nilayanaṃ</s>' — the place of total dissolution; '<s>māyā</s>' — and devoid of that.

children.text:
udaramiti ut api aramalpam antaraṃ bhedam /
ānandamayāttviti brahmaṇyāntaratvamaśrutaṃ pucchatvaṃ tu śrutamityarthaḥ /
pucchamityādhāratvamātraṃ pratiṣṭheti /
ekanīḍamadhiṣṭhānaṃ sopādānasya jagataḥ /
yato yasmāt vācaḥ śaktivṛttyā tamaprakāśyaiva nivartante /
pratiyogī virodhī tasyātmatvamapekṣate /
yathā vipramayo grāma ityatra śūdralpatvam /
upakramaṇaṃ bādhaḥ /
upasaṃkratimitavyānāṃ vivekena tyājyānām /
prāyāpattiravayavakramasya buddhau prāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Udaram</s>' (interior) — '<s>ut</s>' also means small; '<s>antaram</s>' means difference. 'By the fact of being <s>ānandamaya</s>' — the meaning is: interiority with respect to <s>Brahman</s> is not heard [in scripture], but being the 'tail' is heard. '<s>Puccham</s>' means merely a support; '<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>' means foundation. '<s>Ekanīḍam</s>' — the one substratum of the world together with its material cause. 'From which' — from which [<s>Brahman</s>], speech, by its inherent power, returns without illuminating it. 'The counter-correlate, the opposite — its being the Self requires [that contrast].' Just as in 'a village predominantly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,' there is a small number of <s>śūdras</s>. '<s>Upakramaṇa</s>' means sublation. 'Of those that are to be abandoned through discrimination as things to be transcended.' '<s>Prāyāpatti</s>' — the arrival in the mind of the sequence of parts.

children.text:
antaradhikaraṇam /
20-21
children.translated_text: The <s>Antara Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of 'Within'). [<s>Sūtras</s>] 20-21.

children.text: antas taddharmopadeśāt | BBs_1,1.20 |
children.translated_text: [The one] within — because of the teaching of its characteristics. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.20 |

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'atha ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate hiraṇyaśmaśrurhiraṇyakeśa āpraṇakhātsarvaṃ eva suvarṇaḥ' 'tasya yathā kapyāsaṃ puṇḍarīkamevamakṣiṇī tasyoditi nāma sa sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhya udita udeti ha vai sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhyo ya evaṃ veda' 'ityadhidaivatam' ( chā. 1.6.7.8) /
'athādhyātmam' 'atha ya eṣo 'ntarapakṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā. 1.7.1.5) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kiṃ vidyākarmātiśayavaśātprāptotkarṣaḥ kaścitsaṃsārī sūryamaṇḍale cakṣuṣi copāsyātvena śrūyate kiṃvā nityasiddhaḥ parameśvara iti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ, saṃsārīti /
kutaḥ rūpavattvaśravaṇāt /
ādityapuruṣe tāvat 'hiraṇyaśmaśruḥ' ityādi rūpamudāhṛtam /
akṣipuruṣe 'pi tadevātideśena prāpyate- 'tasyaitasya tadeva rūpaṃ yadamuṣya rūpam' iti /
naca parameśvarasya rūpavattvaṃ yuktam, 'aśabdarmaspāmarūpamavyayam' (kā. 1.3.15) iti śruteḥ, ādhāraśravaṇācca- 'ya eṣo 'ntarāditye', 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi' iti /
nahyanādhārasya svamahimapratiṣṭhasya sarvavyāpinaḥ parameśvarasyādhāra upadiśyeta /
'sa bhagavaḥ kasminpratiṣṭhita iti sve mahimni' (chā. 7.24.1) iti /
'ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ' iti ca śrutī bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: This is recorded in scripture: 'Now, this golden person who is seen within the sun — with golden beard and golden hair, golden entirely to the very tips of the nails' — 'His eyes are like a lotus opened by a monkey's seat [i.e., the sun]; his name is <s>Ut</s> (the Risen One); he has risen above all sins; he who knows thus indeed rises above all sins' — 'Thus regarding the divine sphere' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6-7.8). 'Now, regarding the individual self' — 'Now, this person who is seen within the eye' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.1.5) and so forth. There, a doubt [arises]: Is it some transmigrating being who, by virtue of the excellence of knowledge and action, has attained eminence and is heard of as an object of meditation in the solar orb and in the eye? Or is it the eternally established supreme Lord? What is the prima facie view? That it is a transmigrating being. Why? Because of the scriptural mention of having form. Regarding the person in the sun, form is described: 'with golden beard' and such. For the person in the eye too, that same [form] is extended through analogy: 'The form of this one is the same as the form of that one.' And it is not proper for the supreme Lord to have form, because of the scripture: 'Without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.15). And because of the scriptural mention of a locus: 'this one who is within the sun,' 'this one who is within the eye.' For no locus would be taught for the supreme Lord, who is without a [particular] locus, who is established in his own glory, and who is all-pervading. 'Revered sir, in what is [<s>Brahman</s>] established? In its own glory' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1). And 'Like space, all-pervading and eternal' — these are the scriptural [statements] in your favor.

children.text:
aiśvaryamaryādāśruteśca /
' sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmātparāñco lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe devakāmānāṃ ca' (chāṃ 1.6.8) ityādityapuruṣasyaiśvaryamaryādā /
'sa eṣa ye caitasmādarvāñco lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyakāmānāṃ ca' ityakṣipuruṣasya /
naca parameśvarasya maryādāvadaiśvaryaṃ yuktam, 'eṣa sarveśvara eṣa bhūtādhipatireṣa bhūtapāla eṣa seturvidhāraṇa eṣāṃ lokānāmasaṃbhedāya' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityaviśeṣaśruteḥ /
tasmānnākṣyādityayorantaḥ parameśvara ityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- 'antastaddharmopadeśāt' iti, 'ya eṣo 'ntarāditye' 'ya eṣo 'ntarakṣiṇi' iti ca śrūyamāṇaḥ puruṣaḥ parameśvara eva, na saṃsārī /
kutaḥ, taddharmopadeśāt /
tasya hi parameśvarasya dharmā ihopadiṣṭāḥ /
tadyathā- 'tasyoditi nāma' iti śrāvayitvā asyādityapuruṣasya nāma 'sa eṣa sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhya uditaḥ' iti sarvapāpmāpagamena nirvakti /
tadeva ca kṛtanirvacanaṃ nāmākṣipuruṣasyāpyatidiśati- 'yannāma tannāma' iti /
sarvapāpmāpagamaśca paramātmana eva śrūyate- 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā' (chāṃ. 8.7.1) ityādau /
tathā cākṣuṣe puruṣe 'saivarktatsamāsa tadukthaṃ tadyajustadbrahma' ityṛksamāsādyātmakatāṃ nirdhārayati /
sā ca parameśvarasyopapadyate,
children.translated_text: And because of the scriptural mention of the limitation of lordship. 'This one rules over the worlds beyond that [sun] and the desires of the gods' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.8) — this is the limitation of lordship of the person in the sun. 'This one rules over the worlds on this side [of the sun] and the desires of human beings' — this is [the limitation of lordship] of the person in the eye. And it is not proper for the supreme Lord to have limited lordship, because of the unqualified scripture: 'He is the Lord of all; he is the ruler of beings; he is the protector of beings; he is the bridge that upholds, for the non-confusion of these worlds' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22). Therefore, the supreme Lord is not within the eye and the sun — with this view having been reached, we say: '[The one] within — because of the teaching of its characteristics' — the person heard of in 'this one who is within the sun' and 'this one who is within the eye' is the supreme Lord alone, not a transmigrating being. Why? Because of the teaching of its characteristics. For the characteristics of the supreme Lord are taught here. Namely: having declared his name as '<s>Ut</s>' (the Risen One) through the statement 'His name is <s>Ut</s>,' [the scripture] explains it through freedom from all sins: 'He has risen above all sins.' And that same name, having been etymologically explained, is extended to the person in the eye as well: 'what is the name of that one is the name of this one.' And freedom from all sins is heard only of the supreme Self: 'The Self that is free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) and so forth. Likewise, regarding the person in the eye, [the scripture] establishes the identity [of this person] with <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and such: '<s>Sa</s> is <s>Ṛk</s>, that is <s>Sāman</s>, that is <s>Yajus</s>, that is <s>Brahman</s>.' And this is appropriate for the supreme Lord,

children.text:
sarvakāraṇatvātsarvātmakatvopapatteḥ /
pṛthivyagnyādyātmake cādhidaivataṃ ṛksāme, vākprāṇādyātmake cādhyātmamanukramyāha- 'tasyarkca sāma ca geṣṇau' ityadhidaivatam /
tathādhyātmamapi- ' yāvamuṣya geṣṇau tau geṣṇau' iti /
tacca sarvātmana evopapadyate /
tadya ime vīṇāyāṃ gāyantyetaṃ te gāyanti tasmātte dhanasanayaḥ' (chā. 1.7.6) iti ca laukikeṣvapi gāneṣvasyaiva gīyamānatvaṃ darśayati /
tacca parameśvaraparigrahe dhaṭate, 'yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā /
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejoṃśasaṃbhavam /
(10.41) iti bhagavadgītādarśanāt /
children.translated_text: because being the Self of all is justified since [<s>Brahman</s>] is the cause of all. And having enumerated the divine sphere — the <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> whose nature is earth, fire, and such — and the individual sphere — whose nature is speech, <s>prāṇa</s>, and such — [the scripture] says: 'Of this one, the <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> are the two supporting beams' — regarding the divine sphere. Likewise regarding the individual sphere too: 'What are the supporting beams of that one are the supporting beams [of this one].' And this is appropriate only for the Self of all. 'Those who sing to the accompaniment of the <s>vīṇā</s> — they sing of Him; therefore they are possessors of wealth' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.6) — this shows that even in worldly songs, it is this [supreme Lord] alone who is being sung about. And this is fitting when the supreme Lord is accepted, because of the teaching of the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>: 'Whatever being is glorious, prosperous, or powerful — know that to have sprung from a fraction of My splendor' (10.41).

children.text:
lokakāmeśititṛtvamapi niraṅ kuśaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ parameśvaraṃ gamayati /
yattūktaṃ hiraṇyaśmaśrutvādirūpaśravaṇaṃ parameśvare nopapadyata iti, atra brūmaḥ- syātparameśvarasyāpīcchāvaśānmāyāmayaṃ rūpaṃ sādhakānugrahārtham /
'māyā hyeṣā mayā sṛṣṭā yanmāṃ paśyasi nārada /
sarvabhūtaguṇairyuktaṃ maivaṃ māṃ jñātumarhasi' iti smaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: And the unrestricted lordship over worlds and desires that is heard also points to the supreme Lord. As for what was said — that the scriptural mention of form such as golden beard and such is not appropriate for the supreme Lord — to this we say: even the supreme Lord may have a form made of <s>māyā</s>, assumed at will, for the purpose of blessing devotees. Because of the tradition: 'This is <s>māyā</s> created by Me — that you see Me, O <s>Nārada</s>, endowed with the qualities of all beings. You should not look upon Me thus.'

children.text:
apica yatra tu nirastasarvaviśeṣaṃ pārameśvaraṃ rūpamupadiśyate, bhavati tatra śāstram- 'śabdarmasparśamarūpamavyayam' ityādi /
sarvakāraṇattvāttu vikāradharmairapi kaiścidviśiṣṭaḥ parameśvara upāsyatvena nirdiśyate- 'sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ' (chāṃ 3.14.2) ityādinā /
tathā hiraṇyaśmaśrutvādinirdeśo 'pi bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the description of having a golden beard and such [in this passage] would also [be for the purpose of meditation].

children.text: yadapyādhāraśravaṇānna parameśvara iti, atrocyate- svamahimapratiṣṭhasyāpyādhāraviśeṣopadeśa upāsanārtho bhaviṣyati, sarvagatatvādbrahmaṇo vyomavatsarvāntaratvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: As for the objection that [the person mentioned] is not the supreme Lord because of the mention of a locus — to this it is said: Even for one who is established in his own glory, the teaching of a specific locus would be for the purpose of meditation, because <s>Brahman</s>, being all-pervading, can fittingly be within everything, like space.

children.text: aiśvaryamaryādāśravaṇamapyadhyātmādhidaivatavibhāgāpekṣamupāsanārthameva /
children.translated_text: The mention of limitation of lordship too is merely for the purpose of meditation, based on the distinction between the individual sphere and the divine sphere.

children.text: tasmātparameśvara evākṣyādityayorantarupadiśyate // 20 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is the supreme Lord alone who is taught as being within the eye and the sun. // 20 //

Moreover, where the form of the supreme Lord, devoid of all particularities, is taught, there the scripture [says]: 'Without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable,' and so forth. But because of being the cause of all, the supreme Lord is also indicated, for the purpose of meditation, as qualified by some qualities belonging to modifications: 'Of all actions, all desires, all scents, all tastes' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and so forth.

children.text:
FN: antarāditye ādityamaṇḍalamadhye /
hiraṇmayo jyotirmayaḥ /
aprāṇakhānnakhāgramabhivyāpya /
kapermarkaṭasyāsaḥ pṛṣṭa(puccha) bhāgo 'tyantatejasvī tattulyaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ yathātyantadīptimattathāsya devasyākṣiṇī prakṛṣṭadīptimatī, tasya uditīti udita udgataḥ sakāryasarvapāpāspṛṣṭa ityarthaḥ /
sa eṣa ityādhidaivikapuruṣoktiḥ /
amuṣmādādityādūrdhvagā ye lokāsteṣāmīśitā ye ca devānāṃ kāmā bhogāsteṣāṃ cetyarthaḥ /
yau sarvātmakaṛksāmātmakau tāvamuṣyādityarathasya geṣṇau pādaparvaṇī /
saniryāñcāyāṃ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Within the sun' means in the middle of the solar orb. '<s>Hiraṇmaya</s>' means made of light. '<s>Āpraṇakhāt</s>' means pervading up to the tips of the nails. '<s>Kapi</s>' is a monkey; its '<s>āsa</s>' is its seat (rear/tail), which is exceedingly lustrous; a lotus similar to that — just as that is exceedingly bright, so too the eyes of this deity are of exceptional brilliance. 'His [name] is <s>Ut</s>' — meaning <s>Udita</s> (the Risen One), untouched by all sins together with their effects. 'This one' — this is the statement about the divine person. 'The worlds that are above that sun — he is the ruler of those; and of the desires of the gods, meaning their enjoyments' — this is the meaning. The two supporting beams, which are of the nature of the all-pervading <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, are the joints of the feet [i.e., supporting structures] of that sun-chariot. '<s>Saniryāñcāyām</s>' [refers to going forth].

children.text: bhedavyapadeśāc cānyaḥ | BBs_1,1.21 |
children.translated_text: And because of the designation of difference — [the one within is] another. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.21 |

children.text:
asti cādityādiśarīrābhimānibhyo jīvebhyo 'nya īśvaro 'ntaryāmī, 'ya āditye tiṣṭhannādityāntaro yamādityo na veda yasyādityaḥ śarīraṃ ya ādityamantaro yamayatyeṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ' (bṛ. 3.7.9) iti śrutyantare bhedavyapadeśāt /
tatra hi 'ādityādantaro yamādityo na veda' iti vediturādityādvijñānātmano 'ntaryāmī spaṣṭaṃ nirdiśyate /
sa evehāpyantarāditye puruṣo bhavitumarhati, śrutisāmānyāt /
tasmātparameśvara evehopadiśyata iti siddham /
children.translated_text: And there is a Lord, an inner controller, who is other than the individual souls who identify with the bodies of the sun and such — because of the designation of difference in another scriptural passage: 'He who, standing in the sun, is interior to the sun, whom the sun does not know, whose body the sun is, who controls the sun from within — he is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.9). For there, in 'who is interior to the sun, whom the sun does not know,' the inner controller is clearly indicated as distinct from the knowing self who is the sun [i.e., the soul identified with the sun]. And this same one should be the person within the sun here [in the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage] as well, because of the similarity of the scriptural [statements]. Therefore, it is established that the supreme Lord alone is taught here.

children.text: 8 ākāśādhikaraṇam / sū. 22
children.translated_text: 8. The <s>Ākāśa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Space). <s>Sūtra</s> 22.

children.text: ākāśas talliṅgāt | BBs_1,1.22 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s> (Space) [is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of its characteristic marks. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.22 |

children.text:
idamāmananti- 'asya lokasya kā gatirityākāśa iti hovāca sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyākāśādeva samutpadyanta ākāśaṃ pratyastaṃ yantyākāśo hyevaibhyo jyāyānākāśaḥ parāyaṇam' (chāndo. 1.9.1) iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kimākāśaśabdena paraṃ brahmābhidhīyata uta bhūtākāśamiti /
kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ, ubhayatra prayogadarśanāt /
bhūtaviśeṣe tāvatsuprasiddho lokavedayorākāśaśabdaḥ /
brahmaṇyapi kvacitprayujyamāno dṛśyate /
yatra vākyaśeṣavaśādasādhāraṇaśravaṇādvā nirdhāritaṃ brahma bhavati, yathā- 'yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt' (tai. 2.7) iti 'ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā te yadantarā tadbrahma' (chā. 8.14.1) iti caivamādau /
ataḥ saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ punaratra yuktaṃ, bhūtākāśamiti /
kutaḥ, taddhi prasiddhatareṇa prayogeṇa śīghraṃ buddhimārohati /
nacāyamākāśaśabda ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇaḥ śakyo vijñātuṃ, anekārthatvaprasaṅgāt /
tasmādbrahmaṇi gauṇa ākāśaśabdo bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: They recite this: 'What is the destination of this world? — Space (<s>Ākāśa</s>), he said. For all these beings originate from space alone, and they dissolve back into space. For space is indeed greater than these; space is the ultimate refuge' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.9.1). There the doubt arises: does the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' denote the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, or the elemental space? Why the doubt? Because usage in both senses is observed. The word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is well-known in common parlance and in the <s>Vedas</s> for the particular element [space]. But it is also seen to be used sometimes for <s>Brahman</s> — where, through the context of the remaining sentence or through uncommon characteristics, <s>Brahman</s> is determined, as in: 'If this space (<s>ākāśa</s>) were not bliss' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7), and 'Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) indeed is the name of that which brings forth name and form; that which is within them — that is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1), and so on. Hence the doubt. What then is reasonable here? Elemental space, [one might say]. Why? Because, being used in the more well-known sense, it quickly enters the mind. And this word '<s>ākāśa</s>' cannot be understood as common to both, since that would entail multiple meanings. Therefore, the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' applied to <s>Brahman</s> must be figurative.

children.text:
vibhutvādibhirhi bahubhirdharmaiḥ sadṛśamākāśena brahma bhavati /
naca mukhyasaṃbhave gauṇor'tho grahaṇamarhati /
saṃbhavati ceha mukhyasyaivākāśasya grahaṇam /
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s> is similar to space in many qualities such as all-pervasiveness and such. But when the primary sense is possible, the figurative meaning should not be adopted. And here the adoption of elemental space itself in its primary sense is possible.

children.text: nanu bhūtākāśaparigrahe vākyaśeṣo nopapadyate- 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyākāśādeva samutpadyante' ityādiḥ /
children.translated_text: But if elemental space is adopted, the remainder of the sentence — 'All these beings originate from space alone' and so forth — would not be tenable.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
bhūtākāśasyāpi vāyvādikrameṇa kāraṇatvopapatteḥ /
vijñāyate hi- 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ /
ākāśādvāyuḥ /
vāyoragniḥ' (tai. 2.1) ityādi /
jyāyastvaparāyaṇatve api bhūtāntarāpekṣayopapadyete bhūtākāśasyāpi /
tasmādākāśaśabdena bhūtākāśasya grahaṇamityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- 'ākāśastalliṅgāt' ākāśaśabdena brahmaṇo grahaṇaṃ yuktam /
kutaḥ, talliṅgāt /
parasya hi brahmaṇa idaṃ liṅgam- 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyākāśādeva samutpadyante' iti /
parasmāddhi brahmaṇo bhūtānāmutpattiriti vedānteṣu maryādā /
children.translated_text: That is not a fault. Because even for elemental space, causality is tenable through the sequential order of air and such. For it is known: 'From that very Self, space was born; from space, air; from air, fire' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1), and so on. And the qualities of being greater and being the ultimate refuge are also tenable for elemental space in relation to the other elements. Given this position — that the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' refers to elemental space — we say: '<s>Ākāśas talliṅgāt</s>' — it is proper that the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' refers to <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because of the indicatory marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>]. For this is an indicatory mark of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>: 'All these beings originate from space alone.' For the origination of beings from the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is the established rule in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts.

children.text: nanu bhūtākāśasyāpi vāyvādikrameṇa kāraṇatvaṃ darśitam /
children.translated_text: But was it not shown that elemental space too has causality through the sequential order of air and such?

children.text:
satyaṃ darśitam /
tathāpi mulakāraṇasya brahmaṇo 'parigrahādākāśādevetyavadhāraṇaṃ, sarvāṇīti ca bhūtaviśeṣaṇaṃ nānukūlaṃ syāt /
tathā 'ākāśaṃ pratyastaṃ yanti' iti brahmaliṅgaṃ 'ākāśo hyevaibhyo jyāyānākāśaḥ parāyaṇam' iti ca jyāyastvaparāyaṇatve /
jyāyastvaṃ hyānāpekṣikaṃ paramātmanyevaikasminnāmnātam- 'jyāyānpṛthivyā jyāyamantarikṣājjyāyāndivo jyāyānebhyo lokebhyaḥ' (chāṃ 3.14.3) iti /
tathā parāyaṇatvamapi paramakāraṇatvātparamātmanyevopapannataram /
śrutiśca bhavati- 'vijñānamānandaṃ brahma rāterdātuḥ parāyaṇam' (bṛ. 3.9.28) iti /
api cāntavattvadoṣeṇa śālāvatyasya pakṣaṃ ninditvā, anantaṃ kiñcidvaktukāmena jaivalinā ākāśaḥ parigṛhītaḥ, taṃ cākāśamudgīthe saṃpādyopasaṃharati- 'sa eṣa parovarīyānudgīthaḥ sa eṣo 'nantaḥ' (chāṃ 1.9.2) iti /
taccānantyaṃ brahmaliṅgam /
yatpunaruktaṃ bhūtākāśaṃ prasiddhibalena prathamataraṃ pratīyata iti, atra brūmaḥ- prathamataraṃ pratītamapi sat vākyaśeṣagatānbrahmaguṇāndṛṣṭvā na parigṛhyate /
darśitaśca brahmaṇyapyākāśaśabdaḥ- 'ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā' ityādau /

tathākāśaparyāyavācināmapi brahmaṇi prayogo dṛśyate- 'ṛco akṣare parame vyomandevā adhi viśve niṣeduḥ' (ṛ.saṃ 1.164.39) 'saiṣā bhārgavī vāruṇī vidyā parame vyomanpratiṣṭhitā' (tai. 3.6) 'oṃ kaṃ brahma khaṃbrahma' (chāṃ 4.10.5) 'khaṃ purāṇam' (bṛ. 5.1) iti caivamādau /
children.translated_text: Likewise, synonyms of '<s>ākāśa</s>' are also seen to be used for <s>Brahman</s>: 'In the supreme space (<s>vyoman</s>), the imperishable, all the gods are seated upon the verses' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 1.164.39); 'This knowledge of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> is established in the supreme space' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.6); '<s>Oṃ</s> — <s>ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10.5); '<s>Kha</s> is the ancient' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.1) — and so on.
