children.text: vākyopakrame 'pi vartamānasyākāśaśabdasya vākyaśeṣavaśādyuktā brahmaviṣayatvāvadhāraṇā /
children.translated_text: And for the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' occurring at the beginning of the passage, the determination that it refers to <s>Brahman</s> is justified by the force of the remainder of the sentence.

children.text: 'agniradhīte 'nuvākam' iti hi vākyopakramagato 'pyagniśabdo māṇavakaviṣayo dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For even the word '<s>Agni</s>' (fire), occurring at the beginning of the passage 'Agni recites a lesson,' is seen to refer to a student (<s>māṇavaka</s>).

children.text: tasmādākāśaśabdaṃ brahmeti siddham // 22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' [here] denotes <s>Brahman</s>. // 22 //

True, it was shown. Even so, if the root cause <s>Brahman</s> is not adopted, the emphatic assertion 'from space alone' and the qualifier 'all' applied to beings would not be appropriate. Likewise, 'they dissolve back into space' is an indicatory mark of <s>Brahman</s>, as are the qualities of being greater and being the ultimate refuge. For the quality of being greater, in an absolute (non-relative) sense, is taught only of the one supreme Self: 'Greater than the earth, greater than the atmosphere, greater than heaven, greater than these worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.3). Similarly, being the ultimate refuge too is more appropriate for the supreme Self, because it is the ultimate cause. And there is a scriptural statement: '<s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss, the ultimate refuge of the giver of wealth' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.28). Moreover, having criticized the position of <s>Śālāvatya</s> with the fault of finitude, <s>Jaivali</s>, wishing to state something infinite, adopted space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and having connected that space with the <s>Udgītha</s>, he concludes: 'This is the <s>Udgītha</s> that is supremely great; this is infinite' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.9.2). And that infinity is an indicatory mark of <s>Brahman</s>. As for the objection that elemental space would be understood first by the force of its more well-known usage — to that we say: even though understood first, upon seeing the qualities of <s>Brahman</s> in the remainder of the sentence, it is not adopted [in its elemental sense]. And the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' has been shown to apply to <s>Brahman</s> as well: 'Space indeed is the name of that which brings forth name and form' — and so on.

children.text:
FN: vedituḥ pramātuḥ, vijñānātmanaḥ antaḥkaraṇopahitāt /
asyeti śālāvatyo brāhmaṇo jaivarājaṃ pṛcchati /
nirvahitā utpattisthitihetuḥ, te nāmarūpe yadantarā yasmādanye yasya vā madhye staḥ tannāmarūpāspṛṣṭaṃ brahmeti vākyoṣādatrākāśo brahmetyarthaḥ /
rāterdhanasya dātuḥ yajamānasya /
deśato 'nantatvaṃ paratvaṃ, guṇata utkṛṣṭatvaṃ varīyastvaṃ, kālato vastutaścāparicchinnatvamānantyam /
parebhyaḥ svarādibhyo 'tiśayena śraiṣṭhyaṃ vā parovarīyastvam /
vyoman vyomni, parame prakṛṣṭe, aśrare kūṭasthe brahmaṇi, ṛco ṛgupakṣitāḥ sarve vedā jñāpakāḥ santi /
yasminnakṣare viśvedevā adhiniṣeduradhiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Of the knower' — of the cognizer, the knowing self conjoined with the inner organ. '<s>Asya</s>' — <s>Śālāvatya</s> the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> asks king <s>Jaivali</s>. '<s>Nirvahitā</s>' — the cause of origination and sustenance; '<s>te</s>' — those name and form; '<s>yadantarā</s>' — that from which they are different, or in whose midst they exist — that, untouched by name and form, is <s>Brahman</s>: this is the meaning of the sentence, that space here means <s>Brahman</s>. '<s>Rāteḥ</s>' — of the sacrificer who is the giver of wealth. Infinity in terms of space is greatness (<s>paratva</s>); in terms of qualities, it is excellence (<s>varīyastva</s>); in terms of time and reality, it is unlimitedness (<s>ānantyam</s>). '<s>Parovarīyastvam</s>' is supreme excellence — surpassing superiority over heaven and other [realms]. '<s>Vyoman vyomni</s>' — in space, in the exalted; '<s>akṣare</s>' — in the immutable; '<s>kūṭasthe</s>' — in <s>Brahman</s>; the verses (<s>ṛcaḥ</s>) — all the <s>Vedas</s> that illumine — accompanied by the <s>Ṛk</s> [verses], exist [there]. In which imperishable [<s>Brahman</s>], all the gods are established.

children.text: 9 prāṇādhikaraṇam / sū. 23
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Prāṇa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of <s>Prāṇa</s>). <s>Sūtra</s> 23.

children.text: ata eva prāṇaḥ | BBs_1,1.23 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ata eva prāṇaḥ</s> — For the same reason, [the word] '<s>Prāṇa</s>' [denotes <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.23 |

children.text:
udgīthe- 'prastotaryā devatā prastāvamanvāyattā' ityupakramya śrūyate- katamā sā devateti prāṇā iti hovāca sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni prāṇamevābhisaṃviśanti prāṇamabhyujjihate saiṣā devatā prastāvamanvāyattā' (chāṃ. 1.11.4,5) iti /
tatra saṃśayanirṇayau pūrvavadeva draṣṭavyau /
'prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya manaḥ' (chāṃ. 6.8.2) 'prāṇasya prāṇam' (bṛ. 4.4.18)
children.translated_text: In the context of the <s>Udgītha</s>, beginning with 'O <s>Prastotṛ</s>, which deity is connected with the <s>Prastāva</s> [chant]?' it is heard: 'Which is that deity? — <s>Prāṇa</s>, he said. For all these beings enter into <s>Prāṇa</s> alone, and they rise up from <s>Prāṇa</s>. This is the deity that is connected with the <s>Prastāva</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.11.4-5). There, the doubt and its resolution should be understood just as before. '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the binding of the mind, O dear one' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.2); 'the breath of breath' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.18) —

children.text:
iti caivamādau brahmaviṣayaḥ prāṇaśabdo dṛśyate, vāyuvikāre tu prasiddhataro lokavedayoḥ, ata iha prāṇaśabdena katarasyopādānaṃ yuktamiti bhavati saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ punaratra yuktam /
vāyuvikārasya pañcavṛtteḥ prāṇasyopādānaṃ yuktam /
tatra hi prasiddhataraḥ prāṇaśabda ityavocāma /
children.translated_text: in such passages and others, the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is seen to refer to <s>Brahman</s>; but in the sense of a modification of air with five functions, it is more well-known in common parlance and the <s>Vedas</s>. Hence the doubt arises: which of the two is it proper to adopt here under the word '<s>prāṇa</s>'? What then is reasonable here? It is proper to adopt <s>prāṇa</s> as the modification of air with five functions. For, as we have said, the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is more well-known in that sense.

children.text:
nanu pūrvavadihāpi talliṅgādbrahmaṇa eva grahaṇaṃ yuktam /
ihāpi vākyaśeṣe bhūtānāṃ saṃveśanodgamanaṃ pārameśvaraṃ karma pratīyate /
children.translated_text: But as before, here too, because of the indicatory marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>], it is proper to adopt <s>Brahman</s> alone. For here too, in the remainder of the sentence, the entering and rising up of beings is understood as a divine activity of the Lord.

children.text:
na /
mukhyo 'pi prāṇe bhūtasaṃveśanodgamanasya darśanāt /
evaṃ hyāmnāyate- 'yadā vai puruṣaḥ svapiti prāṇaṃ tarhi vāgapyete prāṇaṃ cakṣuḥ prāṇaṃ manaḥ sa yadā prabudhyate prāṇadevādhi punarjāyante' (śa.brā. 10.3.3.6) iti. pratyakṣaṃ caitatsvāpakāle prāṇavṛttāvaparilupyamānāyāmindriyavṛttayaḥ parilupyante prabodhakāle ca prādurbhavantīti /
indriyasāratvācca bhūtānāmaviruddho mukhye prāṇe 'pi bhūtasaṃveśanodgamanavādī vākyaśeṣaḥ /
apicādityo 'nnaṃ codgīthapratihārayordevate prastāvadevatāyāḥ prāṇasyantaraṃ nirdiśyete /
naca tayorbrahmatvamasti, tatsāmānyācca prāṇasyāpi na brahmatvamityevaṃ prāpte sūtrakāra āha- 'ata eva prāṇaḥ' iti /
'talliṅgāt' iti pūrvasūtre nirdiṣṭam /
ata eva talliṅgātprāṇaśabdamapi paraṃ brahma bhavitumarhati /
prāṇasyāpi hi brahmaliṅgasaṃbandhaḥ śrūyate- 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni prāṇamevābhisaṃviśanti prāṇamabhyujjihate' (chāṃ 1.115) iti /
prāṇanimittau sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmutpattipralayāvucyamānau prāṇasya brahmatāṃ gamayataḥ /
children.translated_text: No. Because the entering and rising up of beings is observed even in the primary sense of <s>prāṇa</s>. For thus it is recited: 'When a person sleeps, then speech enters into <s>prāṇa</s>, the eye into <s>prāṇa</s>, the mind [into <s>prāṇa</s>]; and when he awakens, they are born again from <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 10.3.3.6). And this is directly perceived: at the time of sleep, when the function of <s>prāṇa</s> continues unimpaired, the functions of the sense-organs cease; and at the time of waking, they reappear. And since beings are essentially constituted by the senses, the remainder of the sentence speaking of the entering and rising up of beings is not contradicted even for <s>prāṇa</s> in its primary sense. Moreover, the sun and food are indicated as the deities of the <s>Udgītha</s> and <s>Pratihāra</s> — distinct from the deity of the <s>Prastāva</s>, which is <s>prāṇa</s>. And those [sun and food] are not <s>Brahman</s>; and because of [<s>prāṇa</s>'s] similarity with them, <s>prāṇa</s> too would not be <s>Brahman</s>. Given this position, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> says: '<s>Ata eva prāṇaḥ</s>' — 'for the same reason, <s>prāṇa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>].' '<s>Talliṅgāt</s>' — 'because of the indicatory marks of that' — was stated in the previous <s>sūtra</s>. For the same reason — because of the indicatory marks of that — the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' too can denote the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. For the connection of the indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> with <s>prāṇa</s> is heard: 'All these beings enter into <s>prāṇa</s> alone, and they rise up from <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.11.5). The origination and dissolution of all beings being stated as caused by <s>prāṇa</s> — this leads to [the conclusion of] the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: nanūktaṃ mukhyaprāṇaparigrahe 'pi saṃveśanod gamanadarśanamaviruddhaṃ, svāpaprabodhayordarśanāditi /
children.translated_text: But was it not stated that even if <s>prāṇa</s> in the primary sense is adopted, the observation of entering and rising up is not contradicted, since it is observed at the times of sleep and waking?

children.text:
atrocyate- svāpaprabodhayorindriyāṇāmeva kevalānāṃ prāṇāśrayaṃ saṃveśanodgamanaṃ dṛśyate, na sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām /
ihatu sendriyāṇāṃ saśarīrāṇāṃ ca jīvāviṣṭānāṃ bhūtānāṃ, 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni' iti śruteḥ /
yadāpi bhūtaśrutirmahābhūtaviṣayā parigṛhyate tadāpi brahmaliṅgatvamaviruddham /
children.translated_text: To this we say: at the times of sleep and waking, the entering and rising up of the sense-organs alone — by themselves — dependent on <s>prāṇa</s> is observed, not of all beings. But here, it is of beings possessing sense-organs, possessing bodies, and inhabited by the <s>jīva</s> — because scripture says 'all these beings.' Even when the word 'beings' is taken to refer to the great elements, the indicatory mark of <s>Brahman</s> is not contradicted.

children.text:
nanu sahāpi viṣayairindriyāṇāṃ svāpaprabodhayoḥ prāṇe 'pyayaṃ prāṇācca prabhavaṃ śṛṇumaḥ- 'yadā suptaḥsvapnaṃ na kañcana paśyatyathāsminprāṇa evaikadhā bhavati tadainaṃ vāksarvairnāmabhiḥ sahāpyeti' (kau. 3.3) iti /
tatrāpi talliṅgātprāṇaśabdaṃ brahmaiva /
yatpunarannādityasaṃnidhānātprāṇasyābrahmatvamiti, tadayuktam /
vākyaśeṣabalena prāṇaśabdasya brahmaviṣayatāṃ pratīyamānāyāṃ saṃnidhānasyākiñcitkaratvāt /
yatpunaḥ prāṇaśabdasya pañcavṛttau prasiddhataratvaṃ, tadākāśaśabdasyeva pratividheyam /
tasmātsiddhaṃ prastāvadevatāyāḥ prāṇasya brahmatvam /
atra kecidudāharanti- 'prāṇasya prāṇam', 'prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya manaḥ' iti ca /
tadayuktam /
śabdabhedātprakaraṇācca saṃśayānupapatteḥ /
yathā pituḥ piteti prayoge 'nyaḥ pitā ṣaṣṭīnirdiṣṭo 'nyaḥ prathamānirdiṣṭaḥ pituḥ piteti gamyate, tadvat 'prāṇasya prāṇam' iti śabdabhedātprasiddhātprāṇādanyaḥ prāṇasya prāṇa iti niścīyate /
nahi sa eva tasyeti bhedanirdeśārhe bhavati /
yasya ca prakaraṇe yo nirdiśyate nāmāntareṇāpi sa eva tatra prakaraṇī nirdiṣṭa iti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And when someone is mentioned in a context by another name, it is understood that the one referred to in that context is the very same one [already under discussion].

children.text: yathā jyotiṣṭomādhikāre- 'vasante vasante jyotiṣā yajeta' ityatra jyotiḥśabdo jyotiṣṭomaviṣayo bhavati, tathā parasya brahmaṇaḥ prakaraṇe 'prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya manaḥ' iti śrutaḥ prāṇaśabdo vāyuvikāramātraṃ kathamavagamayet /
children.translated_text: Just as in the context of the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice — 'In every spring, one should sacrifice with the <s>Jyotiḥ</s>' — the word '<s>jyotiḥ</s>' refers to the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice [not to light], similarly in the context of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, how could the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' heard in '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the binding of the mind, O dear one' convey merely a modification of air?

children.text: ataḥ saṃśayaviṣayatvānnaitadudāharaṇaṃ yuktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, since this [passage] is the subject of doubt, it is not proper to cite it as an example.

children.text: prastāvadevatāyāṃ tu prāṇe saṃśayapūrvapakṣanirṇayā upapāditāḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: But regarding <s>prāṇa</s> as the deity of the <s>Prastāva</s>, the doubt, the prima facie view, and the conclusion have been duly set forth. // 23 //

But we hear that even at the times of sleep and waking, the senses together with their objects enter into <s>prāṇa</s> and arise from <s>prāṇa</s>: 'When one is asleep and sees no dream whatsoever, then one becomes unified in <s>prāṇa</s> alone; then speech, together with all names, enters into it' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.3). Even there, because of the indicatory marks of that [<s>Brahman</s>], the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' denotes <s>Brahman</s> itself. As for the objection that <s>prāṇa</s> is not <s>Brahman</s> because of its proximity to [the mention of] food and the sun — that is unjustified, because when the <s>Brahman</s>-reference of the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is understood from the force of the remainder of the sentence, mere proximity is of no consequence. As for the more well-known usage of the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' for the fivefold function — that should be countered just as was done for the word '<s>ākāśa</s>.' Therefore, it is established that <s>prāṇa</s>, the deity of the <s>Prastāva</s>, is <s>Brahman</s>. Here some cite [as examples]: '<s>Prāṇasya prāṇam</s>' (breath of breath) and '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the binding of the mind, O dear one.' That is unjustified. Because, due to the difference in words and because of the [different] context, doubt does not arise. Just as in the expression 'father's father,' the father designated by the genitive is understood to be different from the father designated by the nominative, similarly from the verbal difference in '<s>prāṇasya prāṇam</s>' (breath of breath), it is determined that the 'breath of breath' is different from the well-known <s>prāṇa</s>. For the expression 'that of this' does not apply when there is designation of [one and the same thing as being different from itself].

children.text:
FN: cākrāyaṇarṣirdhanārthī rājño yajñaṃ gatvovāca- he prastotaḥ, yā devatā prastāvaṃ sāmabhaktimanvāyattānugatā /
saṃveśanodgamanaṃ layodayau /
tarhi tasyāmavasthāyāṃ, vāk anuktakarmendriyopalakṣaṇam, cakṣuḥśrotre tādṛgbuddhīndriyāṇāṃ, buddhirapi manasā lakṣyate /
bhūteṣvindriyāṇi sūkṣmatvādbhoktṛsāmīpyācca sārāṇi atasteṣāṃ layodayoktyetareṣāmapi tatsiddheḥ śeṣaghaṭanetyarthaḥ /
vākyātsaṃnidhānaṃ durlabhamityarthaḥ /
prāṇaḥ paramātmā bandhanamāśrayaḥ svarūpaṃ yasyeti vigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The sage <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s>, seeking wealth, went to the king's sacrifice and said: 'O <s>Prastotṛ</s>, which deity is connected with the <s>Prastāva</s>, a division of the <s>Sāman</s>?' 'Entering and rising up' means dissolution and origination. '<s>Tarhi</s>' — in that state; 'speech' is a marker for the organs of action that are unmentioned; 'eye and ear' similarly for the organs of knowledge; 'mind' also indicates the intellect. Because the sense-organs are the essence of beings — due to their subtlety and proximity to the experiencer — by stating their dissolution and origination, the [dissolution and origination] of the rest is also established: this is the meaning of accommodating the remainder [of the passage]. 'From the sentence, proximity is hard to obtain' — this is the meaning. '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is the supreme Self; '<s>bandhana</s>' means support, basis — the analysis is: that whose own nature is [such].

children.text: jyotiścaraṇādhikaraṇam / sū. 24-27
children.translated_text: The <s>Jyotiś-caraṇa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Light and Feet). <s>Sūtras</s> 24-27.

children.text: jyotiś caraṇābhidhānāt | BBs_1,1.24 |
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotiś caraṇābhidhānāt</s> — [The word] 'light' [denotes <s>Brahman</s>], because of the mention of 'feet.' | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.24 |

children.text:
idamāmananti- 'atha yadataḥ paro jyotirdīpyate viśvataḥpṛṣṭeṣu sarvataḥpṛṣṭeṣvanuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣvidaṃ vāva tadyadidamasminnantaḥpuruṣe jyotiḥ' (chā. 3.13.7) iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ-kimiha jyotiḥśabdenādityādi jyotirabhidhīyate kiṃvā paramātmeti /
arthāntaraviṣayasyāpi śabdasya talliṅgādabrahmaviṣayatvamuktam /
iha tu talliṅgamevāsti nāstīti vicāryate /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
ādityādikameva jyotiḥśabdena parigṛhyata iti /
kutaḥ, prasiddheḥ /
tamo jyotiriti hīmau śabdau parasparapratidvandvī vīṣayau prasiddhau /
cakṣurvṛtternirodhakaṃ śārvarādikaṃ tama ucyate /
tasyā evānugrāhakamādityādikaṃ jyotiḥ /
tathā 'dīpyate' itīyamapi śrutirādityādiviṣayā prasiddhā /
nahi rūpādihīnaṃ brahma 'dīpyate' iti mukhyāṃ śrutirmahati /
dyumaryādatvaśruteśca /
nahi carācarabījasya brahmaṇaḥ sarvātmakasya dyaurmaryādā yuktā /
kāryasya tu jyotiṣaḥ paricchinnasya dyaurmaryādā syāt /
'paro divo jyotiḥ' iti ca brāhmaṇam /
children.translated_text: They teach this: 'Now, the light that shines beyond this [world], on the backs of all, on the backs of everything, in the unsurpassed, in the highest worlds — that indeed is the same as this light within a person' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.13.7). Therein arises a doubt: does the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) here refer to physical light such as the sun and so forth, or to the Supreme Self? It has been stated that even a word whose primary reference is to something else may refer to <s>Brahman</s> on account of characteristic marks. But here it is examined whether such a characteristic mark exists or not. What is the initial position? The word '<s>jyotis</s>' grasps physical light such as the sun and so forth. Why? Because of common usage. For the two words 'darkness' and 'light' are well known as referring to mutually opposed objects. What obstructs the activity of the eye — nocturnal darkness and such — is called 'darkness.' What facilitates that very [visual] activity — the sun and such — is 'light.' Similarly, the <s>śruti</s> expression 'shines' (<s>dīpyate</s>) is also well known as referring to the sun and such. For <s>Brahman</s>, being devoid of form and such, cannot bear the primary sense of '<s>dīpyate</s>' (shines). And because of the <s>śruti</s> statement that the sky is its boundary. For it is not appropriate that the sky should be a boundary for <s>Brahman</s>, which is the seed of all moving and unmoving things and is the Self of all. But for a produced, limited light, the sky could be a boundary. And the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> states: 'The light beyond the sky.'

children.text:
nanu kāryasyāpi jyotiṣaḥ sarvatra gamyamānatvāddyumaryādāvattvamasamañjasam /
astu tarhyatrivṛtkṛtaṃ tejaḥ prathamajam /
children.translated_text: But even for a produced light, since it is perceived everywhere, it is inconsistent that the sky should be its boundary. Let it then be the primordial fire (<s>tejas</s>) that has not undergone triplication (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>).

children.text:
na /
atrivṛtkṛtasya tejasaḥ prayojanābhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: No. Because there is no purpose for the untriplicated fire.

children.text: idameva prayojanaṃ yadupāsyatvamiti cet /
children.translated_text: If one says that its very being an object of meditation is the purpose —

children.text:
na /
prayojanāntaraprayuktasyaivādityaderupāsyatvadarśanāt /
'tāsāṃ trivṛtaṃ trivṛtamekaikāṃ karavāṇi' (chā. 6.3.3) iti cāviśeṣaśruteḥ /
nacātrivṛtkṛtasyāpi tejaso dyumaryādatvaṃ prasiddham /
astu tarhi trivṛtkṛtamevat tejo jyotiḥśabdam /
children.translated_text: No. Because it is observed that meditative worship is prescribed for the sun and such, which are already employed for other purposes. And because of the unspecific <s>śruti</s>: 'Let me make each one of these [fire, water, food] threefold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.3). And it is not well known that even untriplicated fire has the sky as its boundary. Then let the triplicated fire itself be what is meant by the word '<s>jyotis</s>.'

children.text: nanūktamarvāgapi divo 'vagamyate 'gnyādikaṃ jyotiriti /
children.translated_text: But was it not stated that even below the sky, fire and such are perceived as light?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
sarvatrāpi gamyamānasya jyotiṣaḥ 'paro divaḥ' ityupāsanārthaḥ pradeśaviśeṣaparigraho na virudhyate /
natu niṣpradeśasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ pradeśaviśeṣakalpanā bhāginī /
'sarvataḥpṛṣṭeṣvanuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣu' iti cādhārabahutvaśrutiḥ kārye jyotiṣyupapadyatetarām /
'idaṃ vāva tadyadidamasminnāntaḥ puruṣe jyotiḥ' (chā. 3.13.7) iti ca kaukṣeye jyotiraṣi paraṃ jyotiradhyasyamānaṃ dṛśyate /
sārūpyanimittāścādhyasā bhavanti /
yathā- 'tasya bhūriti śira ekametadakṣaram' (bṛ. 5.5.3) iti /
kaukṣeyasya tu jyotiṣaḥ prasiddhamabrahmatvam /
'tasyaiṣā dṛṣṭiḥ' (chā. 3.13.7) 'tasyaiṣā śrutiḥ' iti cauṣṇyaghoṣaviśiṣṭatvasya śravaṇāt /
'tadetaddṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cepyupāsīta' iti ca śruteḥ /
'cakṣuṣyaḥ śruto bhavati ya evaṃ veda' (chā. 3.13.8) iti cālpaphalaśravaṇādabrahmatvam /
mahate hi phalāya brahmopāsanamiṣyate /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect. For a light that is perceived everywhere, the specification of a particular location — 'beyond the sky' — for the purpose of meditation, is not contradictory. But for <s>Brahman</s>, which is devoid of spatial location, the attribution of a specific location is not justified. And the <s>śruti</s> statement of multiplicity of substrates — 'on the backs of all, in the unsurpassed, in the highest worlds' — is more fitting for a produced light. And in 'that indeed is the same as this light within a person' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.13.7), the supreme light is seen being superimposed upon the fire in the belly. And superimpositions occur on account of similarity of form — as in 'Of that, "<s>bhūḥ</s>" is the head, this is one syllable' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.3). And the non-<s>Brahman</s>-nature of the belly-fire is well established. Because the <s>śruti</s> states it to have specific qualities of heat and sound: 'Of that, this is the sight' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.13.7) and 'of that, this is the hearing.' And because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'One should meditate on that as what is seen and heard.' And from the <s>śruti</s> statement of a minor fruit — 'One who knows thus becomes one who has eyes, one who is renowned' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.13.8) — it is non-<s>Brahman</s>. For meditation on <s>Brahman</s> is desired for a great fruit.

children.text:
nacānyadapi kiñcitsvavākye prāṇākāśavajjyotiṣo 'sti brahmaliṅgam /
naca pūrvasminnapi vākye brahma nirdiṣṭamasti, 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtam' iti chandonirdeśāt /
athāpi kathañcitpūrvasminvākye brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ syādevamapi na tasyeha pratyabhijñānamasti /
tatra hi 'tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' (3.12.1,6) iti dyauradhikaraṇatvena śrūyate /
atra punaḥ 'paro divo jyotiḥ' iti dyaurmaryādātvena /
tasmātprākṛtaṃ jyotiriha grāhyamityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ-jyotiriha brahma grāhyam /
kutaḥ. caraṇābhidhānāt /
pādābhidhānādityarthaḥ /
pūrvasminhi vākye catuṣpādbrahma nirdiṣṭam- 'tāvānasya mahimā tato jyāyāṃśca pūruṣaḥ /
pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' (chā. 3.12.6) ityanena mantreṇa /
tatra yaccatuṣpādo brahmaṇastripādamṛtaṃ dyusaṃbandhirūpaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ tadeveha dyusaṃbandhānnirdiṣṭamiti pratyabhijñāyate /
tatparityajya prākṛtaṃ jyotiḥ kalpayataḥ prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriye prasajyeyātām /
na kevalaṃ pūrvavākyājjyotirvākya eva brahmānuvṛttiḥ, parasyāmapi śāṇḍilyavidyayāmanuvartiṣyate brahma /
tasmādiha jyotiriti brahma pratipattavyam /
children.translated_text: Nor is there any other characteristic mark of <s>Brahman</s> for this light in its own passage, as there was for <s>Prāṇa</s> and space. Nor was <s>Brahman</s> mentioned in the preceding passage either, because of the reference to a meter: '<s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this, whatever exists.' Even if somehow <s>Brahman</s> were mentioned in the preceding passage, there would be no recognition of it here. For there, 'Three-quarters of it are the immortal in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.1, 6) — the sky is heard as a substrate. But here, 'the light beyond the sky' — the sky is heard as a boundary. Therefore, the ordinarily understood light should be grasped here — this being the initial position, we say: the light here is to be understood as <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because of the mention of feet (<s>caraṇa</s>). The meaning is: because of the mention of quarters (<s>pāda</s>). For in the preceding passage, the four-quartered <s>Brahman</s> was described by this <s>mantra</s>: 'Such is its greatness; and yet the <s>Puruṣa</s> is greater than this. A quarter of it is all beings; three-quarters of it are the immortal in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.6). Therein, that three-quartered, immortal form of the four-quartered <s>Brahman</s> that was described as connected with the sky — that same is recognized here because of the connection with the sky. To set that aside and imagine an ordinary light would result in the faults of abandoning the topic and introducing a non-topic. Not only from the preceding passage does <s>Brahman</s> continue into the light-passage; <s>Brahman</s> will also continue in the subsequent <s>Śāṇḍilya Vidyā</s>. Therefore, the word '<s>jyotis</s>' here is to be understood as <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yattūktam- 'jyotiradīpyate' iti caitau śabdau kārye jyotiṣi prasiddhāviti /
children.translated_text: As for what was said — that the words '<s>jyotis</s>' and '<s>dīpyate</s>' are well known in reference to produced light —

children.text:
nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
prakaraṇādbrahmāvagame satyanayoḥ śabdayoraviśeṣakatvāt /
dīpyamānakāryajyotirupalakṣite brahmaṇyapi prayogasaṃbhavāt /
'yena sūryastapati tejaseddhaḥ' (tai.brā. 3.12.9.7) iti ca mantravarṇāt /
yadvā nāyaṃ jyotiḥśabdaścakṣurvṛtterevānugrāhake tejasi vartate, anyatrāpi prayogadarśanāt /
'vācaivāyaṃ jyotiṣāste' (bṛ. 4.3.5), 'mano jyotirjuṣatām' (tai.brā. 1.6.3.3) iti ca, tasmādyadyatkasyacidavabhāsakaṃ tattajyotiḥśabdenābhidhīyate /
tathā sati brahmaṇo 'pi caitanyarūpasya samastajagadavabhāsahetutvādupapanno jyotiḥśabdaḥ /
'tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti' (kau. 2.5.15) 'taddevā jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāyurhepāsate 'mṛtam' (bṛ. 4.4.16) ityādiśrutibhyaśca /
yadapyuktaṃ dyumaryādatvaṃ sarvagatasya brahmaṇo nopapadyata iti /
atrocyate- sarvagatasyāpi brahmaṇa upāsanārthaḥ pradeśaviśeṣaparigraho na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect. Because, when <s>Brahman</s> is already ascertained from the context, these words are not differentiating [i.e., they do not exclude <s>Brahman</s>]. Because usage is possible even for <s>Brahman</s> as indicated by the shining produced light. And from the <s>mantra</s>: 'By whose splendor the sun shines, kindled' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.12.9.7). Or, the word '<s>jyotis</s>' does not apply only to the fire-element that facilitates the activity of the eye, because usage is seen in other contexts too: 'By speech alone he sits with light' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.5); 'May the mind enjoy light' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.6.3.3). Therefore, whatever illuminates anything is referred to by the word '<s>jyotis</s>.' This being so, the word '<s>jyotis</s>' is fitting for <s>Brahman</s> too, since <s>Brahman</s>, being of the nature of consciousness, is the cause of the illumination of the entire universe. And from <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'Everything shines after Him who shines; by His radiance all this is illuminated' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.5.15); 'The gods worship that light of lights as immortal life' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.16). As for the objection that the sky cannot be a boundary for all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> — to this we say: even for all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, the specification of a particular location for the purpose of meditation is not contradictory.

children.text: nanuktaṃ niṣpradeśasya brahmaṇaḥ pradeśaviśeṣakalpanā nopapadyata iti /
children.translated_text: But was it not said that the attribution of a specific location is not justified for <s>Brahman</s>, which is devoid of spatial location?

children.text:
nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
niṣpradeśasyāpi brahmaṇa upādhiviśeṣasaṃbandhātpradeśaviśeṣakalpanopapatteḥ /
tathāhi- ādityo, cakṣuṣi, hṛdaye, iti pradeśaviśeṣasaṃbandhāni brahmaṇa upāsanāni śrūyante /
etena 'viśvataḥpṛṣṭheṣu' ityādhārabahutvamupapāditam /
yadapyetaduktaṃ, auṣṇyaghoṣānumite kaukṣeye kārye jyotiṣyadhyasyamānatvātparamapi divaḥ kāryaṃ jyotireveti /
tadapyayuktam /
parasyāpi brahṇaṇo nāmādipratīkatvatkaukṣeyajyotiṣpratīkatvopapatteḥ /
'dṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cetyupāsīta' iti tu pratīkadvārakaṃ dṛṣṭatvaṃ śrutatvaṃ ca bhaviṣyati /
yadapyalpaphalaśravaṇānna brahmeti, tadapyanupapannam /
nahīyate phalāya brahmāśrayaṇīyaṃ, iyate neti niyamaheturasti /
yatra hi nirastasarvaviśeṣasaṃbandhaṃ paraṃ brahmātmatvenopadiśyate, tatraikarūpameva phalaṃ mokṣa ityavagamyate /
yatra tu guṇaviśeṣasaṃbandhaṃ pratīkaviśeṣasaṃbandhaṃ vā brahmopadiśyate, tatra saṃsāragocarāṇyevoccāvacāni phalāni dṛśyante- 'annādo vasudāno vidante vasu ya evaṃ veda' (bṛ. 4.4.24) ityādyāsu śrutiṣu /
yadyapi na svavākye kiñcijjyotiṣo brahmaliṅgamasti tathāpi pūrvasminvākye dṛśyamānaṃ grahītavyaṃ bhavati /
taduktaṃ sūtrakāreṇa- 'jyotiścaraṇābhidhānāt' iti kathaṃ punarvākyāntaragatena brahmasaṃnidhānena jyotiḥśrutiḥ svaviṣayācchakyā pracyāvayitum /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect. Because, even for <s>Brahman</s> that is devoid of spatial location, the attribution of a specific location is justified on account of its connection with specific limiting adjuncts. For thus, meditations on <s>Brahman</s> connected with specific locations — in the sun, in the eye, in the heart — are heard in scripture. By this, the multiplicity of substrates in 'on the backs of all' has been explained. As for the objection that because heat and sound are inferred in the belly-fire, even the light beyond the sky would be a produced effect — that too is improper. Because even the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, being a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) for names and such, can justifiably be a symbol for the belly-fire. And 'one should meditate on it as what is seen and heard' — the qualities of being seen and heard will apply through the symbol. As for the objection that the minor fruit-statement shows it is non-<s>Brahman</s> — that too is untenable. There is no rule that <s>Brahman</s> must be resorted to only for a [particular] great fruit and not otherwise. For where the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is taught as the Self, with all specific connections removed, there it is understood that the single fruit is liberation. But where <s>Brahman</s> is taught in connection with specific qualities or specific symbols, there the fruits, pertaining to the sphere of <s>saṃsāra</s>, are seen to be of various kinds — as in <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'An eater of food, a giver of wealth, he obtains wealth — one who knows thus' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.24). Even if there is no characteristic mark of <s>Brahman</s> in its own passage for the light, nevertheless the one seen in the preceding passage must be taken [as continuing]. This was stated by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>: '<s>Jyotiścaraṇābhidhānāt</s>' (Light, because of the mention of feet). But how can the light-<s>śruti</s> be diverted from its primary reference by <s>Brahman</s> situated in another passage?

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: 'yadataḥ paro jyotiḥ' iti prathamatarapaṭhitena yacchabdena sarvanāmnā dyusaṃbnandhātpratyabhijñāyamāne pūrvavākyanirdiṣṭe brahmaṇi svasāmārthyena parāmṛṣṭe satyarthājjyotiḥśabdasyāpi brahmaviṣayatvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because, the relative pronoun '<s>yat</s>' in 'that which is the light beyond this' — this universal pronoun, through its own capacity, refers to the <s>Brahman</s> described in the preceding passage, recognized by the connection with the sky; and when [<s>Brahman</s>] is thus grasped by the force of [the pronoun], it is reasonable that the word '<s>jyotis</s>' too comes to refer to <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmādiha jyotiriti brahma pratipattavyam // 24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the word '<s>jyotis</s>' here is to be understood as <s>Brahman</s>. // 24 //

children.text:
FN: gāyatryupādhibrahmopāstyanantaramupāstyantaroktyartho 'thaśabdaḥ /
ato dyulokātparaḥparastādyajjyotirdīpyate tadidamiti jāṭhare jyotiṣyadhyasyate /
viśvasmātprāṇivargāt sarvasmādbhūrādilokācca pṛṣṭeṣūparītyarthaḥ /
nahīti rūpādimataḥ sāvayavasyaiva dīptiyogādityarthaḥ /
yattejobannābhyāmasaṃpṛktaṃ tadatrivatkṛtamucyate /
prayojanāntaraṃ tamonāśādikam /
tāsāṃ tejobannānāmekaikaṃ dvidhā vibhajya punaścekaikaṃ bhāgaṃ dvedhā kṛtvā svabhāgāditarabhāgayornikṣipya trivṛtkaraṇaṃ saṃpadyate /
bhāginī yuktā /
ekatvasāmyādbhūrityasminnakṣare prajāpateḥ śirodṛṣṭiruktā tathātrāpi sārūpyaṃ vācyaṃ anyathādhyāsāsiddheḥ /
eṣā dṛṣṭiryadetaduṣṇimānaṃ sparśena vijānāti /
eṣā śrutiryatkarṇāvapidhāya ninadamiva śṛṇotīti śeṣaḥ /
cakṣuṣyo darśanīyaḥ /
śruto viśrutaḥ /
prākṛtaṃ prakṛterjātaṃ, kāryamiti yāvat /
brahmaṇo vyavacchidya tejaḥsamarpakatvaṃ viśeṣakatvaṃ tadabhāvo 'viśeṣakatvaṃ, aviśeṣakatvādbrahmavyāvartakatvādityarthaḥ /
pramityarthatvena upāstyarthatvena vā maryādāvattvam /
divaḥ paramapītyanvayaḥ /
kaukṣeyakaṃ hi jyotirjīvabhāvenānupraviṣṭasya paramātmano vikāraḥ jīvābhāve dehasya śaithilyāt jīvataścauṣṇyājjāyate /
tasmātpratīkopāsanamupapannam /
jīvarūpeṇānnamattītyannādaḥ, annasyāsamantāddātā vā /
vasu hiraṇyaṃ karmaphalaṃ dadātīti vasudāna iti guṇaviśeṣasaṃbandhaḥ /
sarvanāmnā svasāmarthyena svasya sarvanāmnaḥ sāmartyaṃ saṃnihitavācitvaṃ tadbalena parāmṛṣṭe satīti yojanā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The word '<s>atha</s>' introduces the meditation immediately following the <s>Gāyatrī</s>-conditioned meditation on <s>Brahman</s>. 'That which is the light beyond this — beyond the sky — shines' — this is superimposed upon the belly-fire. 'On the backs of all creatures and all worlds from <s>Bhūḥ</s> upward' — meaning 'above.' The sense of '<s>nahi</s>' is: because luminosity is appropriate only for what has form and parts. That fire which has not been mixed with water and food is called 'untriplicated.' The 'other purpose' is dispelling darkness and such. Triplication is accomplished by dividing each of the three — fire, water, and food — into two parts, then dividing each [secondary] portion in two again, and placing [the portions] into one's own share and the other's share. '<s>Bhāginī</s>' means 'justified.' Because of the similarity [shown by] oneness, the vision of <s>Prajāpati</s> as head was stated for the syllable '<s>bhūḥ</s>' — similarly here too, the similarity must be stated, since otherwise the superimposition would not be established. 'This is the sight' — one perceives this warmth through touch. 'This is the hearing' — the remainder is: one hears a sound as if by closing the ears. '<s>Cakṣuṣya</s>' means 'pleasing to the eye.' '<s>Śruta</s>' means 'famous.' '<s>Prākṛta</s>' means 'born from a cause' — that is, an effect. [Regarding the ability of the light to] differentiate <s>Brahman</s> by specifying fire — its absence is non-differentiation; because of non-differentiation, because of not excluding <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. 'Having a boundary' is [said] for the purpose of cognition or meditation. The connection is: 'even beyond the sky.' For the belly-fire is a modification of the Supreme Self that entered as the individual soul; because of the weakening of the body in the absence of the individual soul, and because heat arises from the presence of the living being, therefore the symbol-meditation is justified. 'In the individual soul form, he eats food' — <s>annāda</s> (eater of food); or, one who gives food all around. '<s>Vasudāna</s>' — one who gives wealth, i.e., the fruit of action as gold — this is the connection with a specific quality. The construction with the 'universal pronoun by its own capacity' is: when [<s>Brahman</s>] is referred to by the capacity of the universal pronoun — namely its power to denote what is proximate — then.

children.text: chando 'bhidhānān neti cen na tathā ceto'rpaṇanigadāt tathā hi darśanam | BBs_1,1.25 |
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is not [<s>Brahman</s>] because a meter is mentioned — [we say] no, because of the directing of the mind in that manner, and because such is observed. | <s>BBs</s> 1.1.25 |

children.text:
atha yaduktaṃ pūrvasminnapi vākye na brahmabhihitamiti, 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yadidaṃ kiñca' (chāṃ. 3.12.1) iti gāyatryākhyasya chandaso 'bhihitatvāditi, tatparihartavyam /
kathaṃ punaśchandobhidhānānna brahmābhihitamiti śakyate vaktuṃ, yāvatā 'tāvānasya mahimā' ityetasyāmṛci catuṣpādbrahma darśitam /
children.translated_text: Now, as for the objection that even in the preceding passage <s>Brahman</s> was not mentioned, because of the reference to the meter named <s>Gāyatrī</s> in '<s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this, whatever exists' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.1) — that must be answered. But how can it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is not mentioned just because a meter is mentioned, when in the verse 'Such is its greatness' the four-quartered <s>Brahman</s> is shown?

children.text:
naitadasti /
'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam' iti gāyatrīmupakramya tāmeva bhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayavākyapramāṇabhedairvyakhyāya 'saiṣā catuṣpādā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī tadetadṛcābhyanuktaṃ tāvānasya mahimā' iti tasyāmeva vyākhyātarūpāyāṃ gāyatryāmudāhṛto mantraḥ kathamakasmādbrahma catuṣpādabhidadhyāt /
yo 'pi tatra 'yadvai tadbrahma' (chā. 3.12.5,6) iti brahmaśabdaḥ so 'pi chandasaḥ prakṛtatvācchandoviṣaya eva 'ya etāmevaṃ brahmopaniṣadaṃ veda' (chāṃ 3.11.3) ityatra hi vedopaniṣadamiti vyācakṣate, tasmācchandobhidhānānna brahmaṇaḥ prakṛtatvamiticet /
children.translated_text: This is not so. Having taken up the <s>Gāyatrī</s> with 'The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this,' and having explained that very [<s>Gāyatrī</s>] through the distinctions of beings, earth, body, heart, speech, and means of knowledge — the <s>mantra</s> cited in the context of that very <s>Gāyatrī</s> as explained, 'This is the four-footed, sixfold <s>Gāyatrī</s>; so great is His majesty — this is declared by this <s>ṛc</s> (verse)' — how could it suddenly refer to <s>Brahman</s> with four quarters? Even the word '<s>Brahman</s>' occurring there in 'That indeed is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.5,6) also pertains to the meter (<s>chandas</s>), since the meter is the subject — as in 'He who knows this <s>Brahma-Upaniṣad</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.11.3), where they explain 'the secret of the <s>Veda</s>.' Therefore, because what is referred to is the meter, <s>Brahman</s> is not the subject — if this be objected,

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
'tathā cetorpaṇanigahāt' tathā gāyatryākhyacchandodvāreṇa tadanugate brahmaṇi cetasor'paṇaṃ cittasamādhānamanena brahmaṇavākyena nigadyate- 'gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvam' iti /
nahyakṣarasaṃniveśamātrāyā gāyatryāḥ sarvātmakatvaṃ saṃbhavati /
tasmādyādgāyatryākhyavikāre 'nugataṃ jagatkāraṇaṃ brahma tadiha sarvamityucyate /
yathā 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' (chā. 3.14.1) iti /
kāryaṃ ca kāraṇādavyatiriktamiti vakṣyāmaḥ- 'tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ' (bra. 2.1.14) ityatra /
tathānyatrāpi vikāradvāreṇa brahmaṇa upāsanaṃ dṛśyate- 'etaṃ hyeva bahvṛcā mahatyukthe mīmāṃsanta etamagnāvadhvaryava etaṃ mahāvrate chandogāḥ' (ai.ā. 3.23.12) iti /
tasmādasti chandobhidhāne 'pi pūrvasminvākye catuṣpādbrahma nirdiṣṭam /
tadeva jyotirvākye 'pi parāmṛśyata upāsanāntaravidhānāya /
apara āha- sākṣādeva gāyatrīśabdena brahma pratipādyate, saṃkhyāsāmānyāt /
yathā gāyatrī catuṣpadā ṣaḍakṣaraiḥ pādaistathā brahma catuṣpāt /
tathānyatrāpi chandobhidhāyī śabdor'thāntare saṃkhyāsāmānyātprayujyamāno dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, elsewhere too, a word denoting a meter is seen used for a different referent because of similarity of enumeration.

children.text: tadyathā- 'te vā ete pañcānye pañcānye daśa santastatkṛtam' ityupakramyāha 'saiṣā virāḍannādi' (chā. 4.3.8) iti /
children.translated_text: For example, having begun with 'Those five and those other five, being ten — that is the <s>kṛta</s> [dice throw],' [the text] says: 'That is the <s>Virāj</s>, the eater of food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.8).

children.text: asminpakṣe brahmaivābhihitamiti na chandobhidhānam /
children.translated_text: On this view, since <s>Brahman</s> itself is referred to, there is no [mere] reference to a meter.

children.text: sarvathāpyasti pūrvasminvākye prakṛtaṃ brahma // 25 //
children.translated_text: In any case, <s>Brahman</s> is the subject in the prior passage. // 25 //

this is no defect. 'Because of the directing of the mind in that manner' — in that manner, through the medium of the meter called <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the directing of the mind, the concentration of thought, upon <s>Brahman</s> which pervades that [meter] is enjoined by this statement about <s>Brahman</s>: '<s>Gāyatrī</s> is indeed all this.' For it is impossible for the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, being merely an arrangement of syllables, to be the Self of all. Therefore, what is here called 'all' is <s>Brahman</s>, the cause of the world, which pervades the modification called <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Just as 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1). And we shall state that the effect is non-different from the cause: 'That non-difference, because of the words "origin" and such' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.1.14). Similarly, elsewhere too, meditation on <s>Brahman</s> through the medium of a modification is seen: 'The followers of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> contemplate Him in the great praise (<s>Mahad Uktha</s>); the <s>Adhvaryus</s> in the fire-ritual; the <s>Chandogas</s> in the <s>Mahāvrata</s> ceremony' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.23.12). Therefore, even though the meter is referred to, <s>Brahman</s> with four quarters is indicated in the prior passage. That very [<s>Brahman</s>] is referred to in the passage about light, for the purpose of prescribing another meditation. Another [commentator] says: <s>Brahman</s> is directly conveyed by the word '<s>Gāyatrī</s>,' because of the similarity of enumeration. Just as the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter has four feet with six syllables each, so too <s>Brahman</s> has four quarters.

children.text:
FN: ya etāṃ prakṛtāṃ brahmopaniṣadaṃ vedarahasyaṃ madhuvidyārūpaṃ veda tasyodayāstamayarahitabrahmaprāptirbhavatītyarthaḥ /
etamṛgvedino mahatyukthe śastre upāsate, adhvaryavo yajurvedinaḥ kratau chandogāḥ sāmavedino mahāvrate kratau /
saṃvargavidyāyāṃ adhidaivamagnisūryacandrāmbhāṃsi vāyau līyate /
adhyatmaṃ vāk cakṣuḥśrotramanasi prāṇamapiyanti /
te vā ete pañcānye ādhidaivikāḥ, pañcānye ādhyātmikāste militvā daśa santaḥ kṛtamityucyate /
kṛtaṃ dyūtam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'He who knows this <s>Brahma-Upaniṣad</s>' — this esoteric teaching, in the form of the <s>Madhuvidyā</s> — the meaning is that he attains <s>Brahman</s>, which is without rising or setting. 'The followers of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> meditate on Him in the <s>Śastra</s> called <s>Mahad Uktha</s>; the <s>Adhvaryus</s>, the followers of the <s>Yajurveda</s>, in the sacrifice; the <s>Chandogas</s>, the followers of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, in the <s>Mahāvrata</s> sacrifice.' In the <s>Saṃvargavidyā</s>, with respect to the cosmic plane, [everything] dissolves into <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) — fire, sun, moon, and waters. With respect to the individual, speech, sight, hearing, and mind merge into <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath). 'Those five of the cosmic plane and those other five of the individual — being ten together, they are called <s>kṛta</s>.' '<s>Kṛta</s>' means the [winning throw in the] dice game.

children.text: bhūtādipādavyapadeśopapatteś caivam | BBs_1,1.26 |
children.translated_text: And because the designation of beings and such as quarters is justified in this way. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.26 |

children.text:
itaścaivamabhyupagantavyamiti, pūrvasminvākye prakṛtaṃ brahmeti /
yato bhūtādīnpādānvyapadiśati /
bhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayāni hi nirdiśyāha- 'saiṣā catuṣpadā ṣaḍvidhā gāyatrī' iti /
nahi brahmānāśrayaṇe kevalasya chandaso bhūtādayaḥ pādā upapadyante /
apica brahmānāśrayaṇe neyamṛksaṃbodhyeta- 'tāvānasya' iti /
anayā hi ṛcā svarasena brahmaivābhidhīyate, 'pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' (chā. 3.12.5) iti sarvātmatvopapatteḥ /
puruṣasūkte 'pīyamṛgbrahmaparatayaiva samāmnāyate /
smṛtiśca brahmaṇa evaṃrūpatāṃ darśayati- 'viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśena sthito jagat' (bhaga. 10.42) iti /
'yadvai tadbrahma' (chā. 3.12.7) iti ca nirdeśa evaṃ sati mukhyārtha upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And the statement 'That indeed is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.7) — this being the case — is justified in its primary meaning.

children.text: 'pañca brahmapuruṣāḥ' (chā. 3.13.6) iti ca hṛdayasuṣiṣu brahmapuruṣaśrutirbrahmasaṃbandhitāyāṃ vivakṣitāyāṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: And the scriptural reference to '<s>Brahma-Puruṣas</s>' (persons of <s>Brahman</s>) in the apertures of the heart (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.13.6) is possible when the intended meaning is a connection with <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmādasti pūrvasminvākye brahma prakṛtam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> is the subject in the prior passage.

children.text: tadeva brahma jyotirvākye dyusaṃbandhātpratyabhijñāyamānaṃ parāmṛśyata iti sthitam // 26 //
children.translated_text: That very <s>Brahman</s>, being recognized in the passage about light through its connection with heaven, is referred to [there]. This is established. // 26 //

For this reason too it should be accepted thus — that <s>Brahman</s> is the subject in the prior passage. Because [the text] designates beings and such as quarters. For, having specified beings, earth, body, and heart, it says: 'This is the four-footed, sixfold <s>Gāyatrī</s>.' For without reference to <s>Brahman</s>, beings and such cannot be quarters of the mere meter. Moreover, without reference to <s>Brahman</s>, this <s>ṛc</s> (verse) would not be addressed [to the subject]: 'So great is His majesty.' For this verse, by its own purport, refers to <s>Brahman</s> itself — 'One quarter of His is all beings; three quarters of His is the immortal in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.5) — because its being the Self of all is justified. In the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> too, this <s>ṛc</s> is traditionally recited as having <s>Brahman</s> as its subject. And the <s>Smṛti</s> also shows this nature of <s>Brahman</s>: 'Having pervaded this entire [universe] with one portion [of Myself], I remain' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 10.42).

children.text:
FN: bhūtapṛthivīśarīrahṛdayavākprāṇa iti ṣaṭprakārā gāyatryākhyasya brahmaṇaḥ śrūyante /
suṣayaśchidrāṇi /
children.translated_text: NOTE: Six aspects of <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Gāyatrī</s> are heard: beings, earth, body, heart, speech, and <s>Prāṇa</s>. '<s>Suṣayas</s>' means apertures.

children.text: upadeśabhedān neti cen nobhayasminn apy avirodhāt | BBs_1,1.27 |
children.translated_text: [If one says] no, because of the difference in instruction — [we reply] no, because there is no contradiction in both cases. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.27 |

children.text:
yadapyetaduktaṃ pūrvatra- 'tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' iti saptamyā dyaurādhāratvenopadiṣṭā iti, punaḥ 'atha yadataḥ paro divaḥ' iti pañcamyā maryādātvena, tasmādupadeśabhedānna tasyeha pratyabhijñānamasti, tatparihartavyam /
atrocyate- nāyaṃ doṣaḥ, ubhayasminnapyavirodhāt /
ubhayasminnapi saptamyante pañcamyante copadeśe na pratyabhijñānaṃ virudhyate /
yathā loke vṛkṣāgrasaṃbaddho 'pi śyena ubhayathopadiśyamāno dṛśyate, vṛkṣāgre śyeno vṛkṣāgrātparataḥ śyena iti ca /
evaṃ divyeva sadbrahma divaḥ paramityupadiśyate /
apara āha- yathā loke vṛkṣāgreṇāsaṃbaddho 'pi śyena ubhayathopadiśyamāno dṛśyate, vṛkṣāgre śyeno vṛkṣāgrātpurataḥ śyena iti ca /
children.translated_text: Another [commentator] says: just as in the world, a hawk even when not connected with the treetop is seen described in both ways — 'the hawk is at the treetop' and 'the hawk is beyond the treetop,'

children.text: evaṃ ca divaḥ paramapi sadbrahma divītyupadiśyate /
children.translated_text: so too <s>Brahman</s>, though beyond heaven, is taught as being in heaven.

children.text: tasmādasti pūrvanirdiṣṭasya brahmaṇa iha pratyabhijñānam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is recognition here of the <s>Brahman</s> indicated earlier.

children.text: ataḥ parameva brahma jyotiḥśabdamiti siddham // 27 //
children.translated_text: Hence, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is denoted by the word 'light' (<s>jyotis</s>). This is established. // 27 //

As for what was said earlier — that in the former [passage], 'Three quarters of His is the immortal in heaven,' heaven is taught through the locative as a support; while again, 'that which is beyond heaven' [teaches it] through the ablative as a boundary; therefore, because of the difference in instruction, there is no recognition of that [<s>Brahman</s>] here — this is to be addressed. To this we say: this is no defect, because there is no contradiction in both cases. In both cases — in the instruction with the locative and the instruction with the ablative — recognition is not contradicted. Just as in the world, a hawk situated at the top of a tree is seen described in both ways: 'the hawk is at the treetop' and 'the hawk is beyond the treetop.' Similarly, <s>Brahman</s> existing in heaven itself is taught as being beyond heaven.

children.text: pratardanādhikaraṇam / sū. 28-31
children.translated_text: The <s>Pratardana Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of <s>Pratardana</s>) / <s>Sūtras</s> 28-31

children.text: prāṇas tathānugamāt | BBs_1,1.28 |
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of such consistent following. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.28 |

children.text:
asti kauṣītakibrāhmaṇopaniṣadīndrapratardanākhyāyikā- 'pratardano ha vai daivodāsirindrasya priyaṃ dhāmopajagāma yuddhena ca pauruṣeṇa ca' ityārabhyāmnātā /
tasyāṃ śrūyate- 'sa hovāca praṇo 'smi prajñātmā taṃ māmāyuramṛtamityupāḥsva' iti /
tathottaratrāpi 'atha khalu prāṇa eva prajñātmedaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati' (ko. 1.1,2,3) iti /
tathā 'na vācaṃ vijijñāsīta vaktāraṃ vidyāt' ityādi /
ante ca 'sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmānando 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ' (ko. 3.8) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kimiha prāṇaśabdena vāyumātramabhidhīyata upa devatātmeti, jīvo 'thavā paraṃ brahmeti /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa Upaniṣad</s>, there is the narrative of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pratardana</s> — related beginning with '<s>Pratardana</s>, son of <s>Divodāsa</s>, reached the beloved abode of <s>Indra</s> through battle and manly valor.' In that [narrative] it is heard: 'He said: "I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the conscious Self (<s>prajñātman</s>). Meditate on me as life, as immortality"' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.1,2,3). And further on: 'Now then, <s>Prāṇa</s> alone, the conscious Self, having grasped this body, causes it to rise up.' And: 'Do not seek to know speech; know the speaker' — and so forth. And at the end: 'This <s>Prāṇa</s> alone, the conscious Self, is bliss, ageless, immortal' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.8) — and so forth. Therein arises a doubt: does the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' here refer merely to air (<s>Vāyu</s>), or to a deity, or to the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), or to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>?

children.text:
nanu 'ata eva prāṇaḥ' ityatra varṇitaṃ prāṇaśabdasya brahmaparatvam /
ihāpi ca brahmaliṅgamasti- 'ānando 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ' ityādi /
kathamiha punaḥ saṃśayaḥ saṃbhavati /
anekaliṅgadarśanāditi brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: But was not the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' as referring to <s>Brahman</s> already discussed in 'for this very reason, <s>Prāṇa</s>'? And here too there is a mark of <s>Brahman</s>: 'bliss, ageless, immortal' and such. How then can there be doubt here? We say: because of the observation of multiple indicative marks.

children.text:
na kevalamiha brahmaliṅgamevopalabhyate /
santi hītaraliṅgānyapi /
'māmeva vijānīhi' (kau. 3.1) itīndrasya vacanaṃ devatātmaliṅgam /
idaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayatīti prāṇaliṅgam /
'na vācaṃ vijijñāsīta vaktāraṃ vidyāt' ityādi jīvaliṅgam /
ata upapannaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
tatra prasiddhervāyuḥ prāṇa iti prāpta ucyate-prāṇaśabdaṃ brahma vijñeyam /
kutaḥ, tathānugamāt /
tathāhi- paurvāparyeṇa paryalocyamāne vākye padārthānāṃ samanvayo brahmapratipādanapara upalabhyate /
upakrame tāvat, 'varaṃ vṛṇīṣva' itīndreṇoktaḥ pratardanaḥ paramaṃ puruṣārthaṃ varamupacikṣepa- 'tvameva me vṛṇīśva yaṃ tvaṃ manuṣyāya hitatamaṃ manyase' iti /
tasmai hitatamatvenopadiśyamānaḥ prāṇaḥ kathaṃ paramātmā na syāt /
nahyanyatra paramātmajñānāddhitatamaprāptirasti /
'tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' (śvetā. 3.8) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tathā 'sa yo māṃ veda na ha vai tasya kenacana karmaṇā loko mīyate na steyena na bhrūṇahatyayā' (kau. 3.1) ityādi ca brahmaparigrahe ghaṭate /
brahmavijñānena hi sarvakarmakṣayaḥ prasiddhaḥ- 'kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare' (mu. 2.2.8) ityādyāsu śrutiṣu /
prajñātmatvaṃ ca brahmapakṣa evopapadyate /
nahyacetanasya vāyoḥ prajñātmatvaṃ saṃbhavati /
tathopasaṃhāre 'pi 'ānando 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ' ityānandatvādīni na brahmaṇo 'nyatra samyak saṃbhavati /
'sa na sādhunā karmaṇā bhūyānbhavati no evāsādhunā karmaṇā kanīyāneṣa hyeva sādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamebhyo lokasya unninīṣate /
children.translated_text: 'He is not increased by good action, nor diminished by evil action. It is He indeed who causes one to perform good action — one whom He wishes to lead upward from these worlds;

children.text: eṣa u bhavāsādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamebhyo lokebhyo 'dho ninīṣate' iti, 'eṣa lokādhipatireṣa lokeśaḥ' (kau. 3.8) iti ca /
children.translated_text: and it is He who causes one to perform evil action — one whom He wishes to lead downward from these worlds.' And: 'He is the lord of the worlds, He is the ruler of the worlds' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.8).

children.text: sarvametatparasmaninbrahmaṇyāśrīyamāṇe 'nugantuṃ śakyate na mukhye prāṇe /
children.translated_text: All this can be consistently followed when applied to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, but not to the vital breath (<s>Prāṇa</s>) in its primary sense.

children.text: tasmātprāṇo brahma // 28 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Prāṇa</s> [here] is <s>Brahman</s>. // 28 //

Not only are marks of <s>Brahman</s> found here. There are other marks as well. 'Know me alone' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.1) — this statement of <s>Indra</s>'s is a mark of a deity. 'Having grasped this body, causes it to rise up' — this is a mark of <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath). 'Do not seek to know speech; know the speaker' — and so forth — this is a mark of the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>). Therefore, the doubt is justified. Given this, since <s>Vāyu</s> (air) is what is well known [as <s>Prāṇa</s>] — having reached the conclusion that <s>Prāṇa</s> means <s>Vāyu</s> — it is said: what is to be known by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because of such consistent following (<s>anugama</s>). For when the passage is examined in sequence, the coherent meaning of the words is found to be directed toward teaching <s>Brahman</s>. At the outset, when <s>Indra</s> said to <s>Pratardana</s> 'Choose a boon,' <s>Pratardana</s> deferred the choice of the highest human goal to [<s>Indra</s>]: 'You yourself choose for me what you consider most beneficial for a human being.' How could the <s>Prāṇa</s> taught to him as the most beneficial not be the Supreme Self? For there is no attainment of the most beneficial other than through the knowledge of the Supreme Self — as known from scriptures such as 'Having known That alone, one passes beyond death; there is no other path for going [to liberation]' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.8). Similarly, 'He who knows me — his world is not diminished by any action, not by theft, not by embryo-killing' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.1) — and such [statements] are fitting when applied to <s>Brahman</s>. For the destruction of all <s>karma</s> through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is well known from scriptures such as 'His actions are destroyed when that higher and lower [<s>Brahman</s>] is seen' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.8). And the nature of being a conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>) is justified only in the case of <s>Brahman</s>. For the unconscious air (<s>Vāyu</s>) cannot have the nature of a conscious self. Similarly, in the conclusion too, 'bliss, ageless, immortal' — the attributes of blissfulness and such cannot properly belong to anything other than <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
FN: brahmapratipādanaparatvenaiva padānāmanvayadṛṣṭerityarthaḥ /
sa netyādinā dharmādyaspṛṣṭatvaṃ tatkārayitṛtvaṃ tadīśitṛtvaṃ ca sarvamuktam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The meaning is: because the coherent meaning of the words is seen as directed toward teaching <s>Brahman</s>. By 'He is not [increased]' and so forth, His being untouched by <s>dharma</s> and such, His being the one who causes [actions] to be performed, and His lordship — all this is stated.

children.text: na vaktur ātmopadeśād iti ced adhyātmasaṃbandhabhūmā hy asmin | BBs_1,1.29 |
children.translated_text: [If one says] it is not [<s>Brahman</s>], because of the self-instruction of the speaker — [we reply:] because there is an abundance of references to the inner self in this [passage]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.29 |

children.text:
yaduktaṃ prāṇo brahmeti, tadākṣipyate /
na paraṃ brahma prāṇaśabdam /
kasmāt, vakturātmopadeśāt /
vaktā hīndro nāma kaścidvigrahavāndevatāviśeṣaḥ svamātmānaṃ pratardanāyācacakṣe- 'māmeva vijānīhi' ityupakramya 'prāṇo 'smi prajñātmā' ityahaṅkāravādena /
sa eṣa vakturātmatvenopadiśyamānaḥ prāṇaḥ kathaṃ brahma syāt /
nahi brahmaṇo vaktṛtvaṃ saṃbhavati 'avāgamanāḥ' (bṛha /
3.8.8) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tathā vigrahasaṃbandhibhireva brahmaṇyasaṃbhavadbhirdharmairātmānaṃ tuṣṭāva- 'triśīrṣāṇaṃ tvāṣṭramahanamarunmukhānyatīñśālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyaccham' ityevamādibhiḥ /
prāṇatvaṃ cendrasya balavatvādupapadyate /
'prāṇo vai balam' iti hi vijñāyate /
balasya cendro devatā prasiddhā /
'yā ca kācidbalakṛtirindrakarmaiva ta' diti hi vadanti /
prajñātmatvamapyapratihatajñānatvāddevatātmanaḥ saṃbhavati /
apratihatajñānā devatā iti hi vadanti /
niścite caivaṃ devatātmopadeśe hitatamatvādivacanāni yathāsaṃbhavaṃ tadviṣayāṇyeva yojayitavyāni /
tasmādukturindrasyātmopadeśānna prāṇo brahmetyākṣipya pratisamādhīyate- 'adhyātmasaṃbhandhabhūmā hyasmin' iti /
adhyātmasaṃbandhaḥ pratyagātmasaṃbandhasya bhūmābāhulyasminnadhyāya upalabhyate /
'yāvaddhyasmiñsarīre prāṇo vasati tāvadāyuḥ' iti prāṇasyaiva prajñātmanaḥ pratyagbhūtasyāyuṣyapradhānopasaṃhārayoḥ svātantryaṃ darśayati na devatāviśeṣasya parācīnasya /
tathāstitve ca prāṇānāṃ niḥśreyasamityadhyātmamevendriyāśrayaṃ prāṇaṃ darśayati /

tathā 'prāṇa eva prajñātmedaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati' (kau. 3.3) iti, 'na vācaṃ vijijñāsīta vaktāraṃ vidyāt' iti cepakramya 'tadyathā rathasyāreṣu nemirarpitā nābhāvarā arpitā evamevaitā bhūtamātrāḥ prajñāmātrāsvarpitāḥ prajñāmātrāḥ prāṇe 'rpitāḥ sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmānando 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ' iti viṣayondriyavyavahārānabhibhūtaṃ pratyagātmānamevopasaṃharati /
children.translated_text: Likewise: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed, the cognitive self, having grasped this body, raises it up' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.3). And beginning with 'One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker,' [the text concludes]: 'Just as the rim is fixed upon the spokes of a wheel, and the spokes are fixed upon the hub — even so these elemental faculties (<s>bhūtamātrā</s>) are fixed upon the cognitive faculties (<s>prajñāmātrā</s>), and the cognitive faculties are fixed upon <s>prāṇa</s>. This <s>prāṇa</s> alone is the cognitive self — blissful, ageless, immortal' — thus [the text] concludes with the inner Self itself, unmastered by the operations of sense-objects and senses.

children.text: 'sa ma ātmeti vidyāt' iti copasaṃhāraḥ pratyagātmaparigrahe sādhurna parācīnaparigrahe /
children.translated_text: 'Let him know this as my Self' — this conclusion is fitting if the inner Self is accepted [as the referent], not if an external [deity] is accepted.

children.text: 'ayamātmā brahma sarvānabhūḥ' (bṛha. 2.5.19) iti ca śrutyantaram /
children.translated_text: 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>; it has become all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19) — thus [states] another <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: tasmādadhyātmasaṃbandhabāhulyādbrahmopadeśa evāyaṃ na devatātmopadeśaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the abundance of references to the inner Self (<s>adhyātma</s>), this is a teaching about <s>Brahman</s> alone, not a teaching about a divine self. // 29 //

The statement that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s> is now challenged.
The supreme <s>Brahman</s> is not [the referent of] the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>.' Why? Because of the self-instruction by the speaker.
For the speaker, a particular embodied deity named <s>Indra</s>, declared his own self to <s>Pratardana</s> — beginning with 'Know me alone' and then through an assertion of ego: 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the cognitive self (<s>prajñātman</s>).'
This <s>Prāṇa</s>, being taught as the self of the speaker — how could it be <s>Brahman</s>?
For speakership is not possible for <s>Brahman</s>, because of <s>śrutis</s> such as 'without speech, without mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8).
Likewise, he praised himself with attributes that belong only to one connected with a body and that are impossible for <s>Brahman</s>: 'I slew the three-headed son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>; I gave the ascetics whose faces were toward <s>Aruṇa</s> to the wolves' — and so forth.
And the <s>prāṇa</s>-nature of <s>Indra</s> is justified because of his great strength.
For it is known: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is strength.'
And <s>Indra</s> is the well-known deity of strength.
'Whatever deed of power there is — that is indeed the work of <s>Indra</s>' — thus they say.
The nature of being a cognitive self (<s>prajñātman</s>) is also possible for the divine self, because of having unobstructed knowledge.
'The gods have unobstructed knowledge' — thus they say.
And when the self-instruction of the divine self is thus established, statements about being most beneficial and such should be construed as referring to that [divine self] alone, as far as possible.
Therefore, having raised the objection that <s>Prāṇa</s> is not <s>Brahman</s> because of the self-instruction of the speaker <s>Indra</s>, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] resolves it: 'Because of the abundance of references to the inner Self (<s>adhyātmasaṃbandhabhūmā</s>) in this [passage].'
The abundance — the profusion — of references to the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) is found in this chapter.
'As long as <s>prāṇa</s> dwells in this body, so long is there life' — this shows the independence of <s>prāṇa</s> itself, the cognitive self that has become the inner [Self], with respect to lifespan and the principal withdrawal — not of a particular external deity.
Likewise, 'When the <s>prāṇas</s> exist, [there is] supreme good' — this shows <s>prāṇa</s> as the inner [Self], the support of the senses.

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi vakturātmopadeśaḥ-
children.translated_text: But then how [do we explain] the self-instruction by the speaker [<s>Indra</s>]?

children.text:
FN: tvaṣṭṛputraṃ viśvarūpaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ahanaṃ, arunmukhān rauti yathārthaṃ śabdayatīti rut vedāntavākyaṃ tanmukhe yeṣāṃ te runmukhāstebhyo 'nyānvedāntabahirmukhānyatīn sālāvṛkebhyo 'raṇyaśvabhyo dattavānasmi /
yasyāreṣu neminābhyormadhyasthaśalākāsu cakropāntarūpā nemirarpitā, nābhau cakrapiṇḍikāyāmarā arpitāḥ evaṃ bhūtāni pṛthivyādīni pañca mīyanta iti mātrā bhogyāḥ śabdādayaḥ pañceti daśa bhūtamātrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: [<s>Indra</s> says:] 'I slew <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the three-headed one; I gave the ascetics — those who turned away from the true meaning (<s>rut</s>), whose faces were toward <s>Aruṇa</s>, i.e., who turned their backs on <s>Vedānta</s> — those ascetics, to the wolves (<s>śālāvṛka</s>), the wild dogs.' The spokes (<s>ara</s>) are the rods between the rim (<s>nemi</s>) and the hub (<s>nābhi</s>); the rim is fixed upon the spokes, and the spokes are fixed upon the hub, the axle-center of the wheel. Similarly, the 'elemental faculties' (<s>bhūtamātrā</s>) — the five elements beginning with earth that are measured, and the five sense-objects beginning with sound that are to be experienced — [these] ten elemental faculties.

children.text: śāstradṛṣṭyā tūpadeśo vāmadevavat | BBs_1,1.30 |
children.translated_text: <s>Śāstradṛṣṭyā tūpadeśo vāmadevavat</s> — But the instruction is through the vision of scripture, like <s>Vāmadeva</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.30 |

children.text:
indro nāma devatātmānaṃ svamātmānaṃ paramātmatvenāhameva paraṃ brahmetyārṣeṇa darśanena yathāśāstraṃ paśyannupadiśati sma- 'māmeva vijānīhi' iti /
yathā 'taddhaitatpaśyannṛṣirvāmadevaḥ pratipede 'haṃ manurabhavaṃ sūryaśca' iti tadvat /
'tadyo yo devānāṃ pratyabudhyata sa eva tadabhavat' (bṛ. 1.4.10) iti śruteḥ /
yatpunaruktaṃ 'māmeva vijānīhi' ityuktvā vigrahadharmairindra ātmānaṃ tuṣṭāva tvāṣṭravadhādibhiriti, tatparihartavyam /
children.translated_text:
The divine self called <s>Indra</s> — seeing his own self as the supreme Self, [thinking] 'I am indeed the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — through the seers' vision, in accordance with scripture, instructed [<s>Pratardana</s>]: 'Know me alone.'
Just as the seer <s>Vāmadeva</s>, seeing this, realized: 'I was <s>Manu</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10) — in that same way.
Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'Whoever among the gods became awakened — he indeed became that' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10).
As for the further statement that [<s>Indra</s>], having said 'Know me alone,' praised himself with bodily attributes such as the slaying of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s son — that must be explained away.

children.text:
atrocyate- na tvāṣṭravadhādīnāṃ vijñeyendrastutyarthatvenopanyāso yasmādevaṅkarmāhaṃ tasmānmāṃ vijānīhīti /
kathaṃ tarhi /
vijñānastutyarthatvena /
yatkāraṇaṃ tvāṣṭravadhādīni sāhasānyupanyasya pareṇa vijñānastutimanusaṃdadhāti- 'tasya me tatra lobha ca na mīyate sa yo māṃ veda na ha vai tasya kena ca karmaṇā loko mīyate' ityādinā /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-
children.translated_text:
To this it is said: The mention of the slaying of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s son and such is not for the purpose of praising <s>Indra</s> as the one to be known — [as if saying] 'because I have done such deeds, therefore know me.'
But then how? For the purpose of praising knowledge.
Because, having mentioned daring deeds such as the slaying of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s son, he subsequently connects them with a praise of knowledge: 'For me who has done these things, not a hair is diminished; and for one who knows me, his world is not diminished by any deed whatsoever' — and so forth.
What is meant by this is:

children.text: yasmādīdṛśānyapi krūrāṇi karmāṇi kṛtavato mama brahmabhūtasya lomāpi na hiṃsyate, sa yo 'nyo 'pi māṃ veda na tasya kenacidapi karmaṇā loko hiṃsyata iti /
children.translated_text: Since even for me — who has become <s>Brahman</s> — though I have committed such cruel deeds, not even a hair is harmed; similarly, whoever else knows me — for that person too, the world is not harmed by any deed whatsoever.

children.text: vijñeyaṃ tu brahmaiva 'prāṇo 'smi prajñātmā' iti vakṣyamāṇam /
children.translated_text: What is to be known is <s>Brahman</s> itself — [that which is] about to be stated as 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the cognitive self.'

children.text: tasmādbrahmavākyametat // 30 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this is a statement about <s>Brahman</s>. // 30 //

children.text: jīvamukhyaprāṇaliṅgān neti cen nopāsātraividhyādāśritatvād iha tadyogāt | BBs_1,1.31 |
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvamukhyaprāṇaliṅgān neti cen nopāsātraividhyādāśritatvād iha tadyogāt</s> — If it be said that [this passage does] not [refer to <s>Brahman</s>] because of indicatory marks of the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>prāṇa</s> — no, because of the threefold [nature of] meditation, because [these marks] are dependent, and because of the connection with That here. | <s>BBs</s> 1,1.31 |

children.text:
yadyapyadhyātmasaṃbandhabhūmadarśanānna parācīnasya devatātmana upadeśaḥ tathāpi na brahmavākyaṃ bhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ, jīvaliṅgānmukhyaprāṇaliṅgācca /
jīvasya tāvadasminvākye vispaṣṭaṃ liṅgamupalabhyate 'na vācaṃ vijijñāsīta vaktāraṃ vidyāt' ityādi /
atra hi vāgādibhiḥ karaṇairvyāpṛtasya kāryakaraṇādhyakṣasya jīvasya vijñeyatvamabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text:
Even though the instruction is not about an external divine self, because of the abundance of references to the inner Self — still, it should not be a statement about <s>Brahman</s>.
Why? Because of indicatory marks of the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>prāṇa</s>.
First, the indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s> is clearly perceived in this passage: 'One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker' and so forth.
For here, the knowability of the <s>jīva</s> — the superintendent of the body and organs, engaged through the instruments of speech and such — is being stated.

children.text:
tathā mukhyaprāṇaliṅgamapi- 'atha khalu prāṇa eva prajñātmedaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati' iti /
śarīradhāraṇaṃ ca mukhyaprāṇasya dharmaḥ, prāṇasaṃvāde vāgādīnprāṇānprakṛtya- 'tānvariṣṭhaḥ prāṇa uvāca mā mohamāpadyathāhamevaitatpañcadhātmānaṃ pravibhajyaitadprāṇamavaṣṭabhya vidhārayāmi' (pra. 2.3) iti śravaṇāt /
ye tu imaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhya iti paṭhanti teṣāmimaṃ jīvamindriyagrāmaṃ vā parigṛhya śarīramutthāpayatīti vyākhyeyam /
prajñātmatvamapi jīve tāvaccetanatvādupapannam /
mukhye 'pi prāṇe prajñāsādhanaprāṇāntarāśrayatvādupapannameva /
children.translated_text:
Likewise, there is also an indicatory mark of the chief <s>prāṇa</s>: 'Now then, <s>prāṇa</s> alone, the cognitive self, having grasped this body, raises it up.'
And the sustaining of the body is a property of the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, as heard in the dialogue on the <s>prāṇas</s>, where, regarding the <s>prāṇas</s> beginning with speech: 'The most excellent <s>prāṇa</s> said to them: "Do not be deluded; I alone, dividing myself fivefold, support and sustain this body"' (<s>Praśna</s> 2.3).
For those who read 'having grasped this body,' the explanation should be: 'having grasped this <s>jīva</s>, or the collection of sense-organs, it raises up the body.'
And the nature of being a cognitive self is justified for the <s>jīva</s> first, because of its being conscious.
Even for the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, it is justified, because it is the support of the other <s>prāṇas</s> that are the means of cognition.

children.text:
jīvamukhyaprāṇaparigrahe ca prāṇaprajñātmanoḥ sahavṛttitvenābhedanirdeśaḥ svarūpeṇa ca bhedanirdeśa ityubhayayā nirdeśa upapadyate- 'yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā yā vai prajñā sa prāṇaḥ saha hyetāvasmiñśarīre vasataḥ sahotkrāmataḥ' iti /
brahmaparigrahe tu kiṃ kasmadbhidyeta /
tasmādihajīvamukhyaprāṇayorantara ubhau vā pratīyeyātāṃ na brahmeti cet, naitadevaṃ, upāsātraividyāt /
evaṃ sati trividhamupāsanaṃ prasajyeta- jīvopāsane mukhyaprāṇopāsanaṃ brahmopāsanaṃ ceti /
nacaitadekasminvākye 'bhyupagantuṃ yuktam /
upakramopasaṃhārābhyāṃ hi vākyaikatvamavagamyate /
'māmeva vijānīhi' ityupakramya 'prāṇo 'smi prajñātmā taṃ māmāyuramṛtamityupāḥsva' ityuktvānte 'sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmānando 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ' ityekarūpāvupakramopasaṃhārau dṛśyete /
tatrārthaikatvaṃ yuktamāśrayitum /
naca brahmaliṅgamanyaparatvena pariṇetuṃ śakyam /
daśānāṃ bhūtamātrāṇāṃ prajñāmātrāṇāṃ ca brahmaṇo 'nyatrārpaṇānupapatteḥ /
āśritatāvāccānyatrāpi brahmaliṅgavaśātprāṇaśabdasya brahmaṇi vṛtteḥ /
ihāpi ca hitatamopanyāsādibrahmaliṅgayogādbrahmopadeśa evāyamiti gamyate /
yattu mukhyaprāṇaliṅgaṃ darśitam- 'idaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati' iti, tadasat /
prāṇavyāpārasyāpi paramātmāyattatvātparamātmanyupacarituṃ śakyatvāt /
'na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana /
itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminnetāvupāśritau' (kāṭha. 2.5.5) iti śruteḥ /
yadapi na vācaṃ vijijñāsīta vaktāraṃ vidyāt ityādi jīvaliṅgaṃ darśitaṃ tadapi na brahmapakṣaṃ nivārayati /
nahi jīvo nāmātyantabhinno brahmaṇaḥ, 'tattvamasi', 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
buddhyādyupādhikṛtaṃ tu viśeṣamāśritya brahmaiva sañjīvaḥ kartā bhoktā cetyucyate /
children.translated_text: But it is <s>Brahman</s> itself which, having assumed the distinction created by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of intellect and such, is called the <s>jīva</s>, the agent and experiencer.

children.text: tasyopādhikṛtaviśeṣaparityāgena svarūpaṃ brahma darśayituṃ 'na vācaṃ vijijñāsīta vaktāraṃ vidyāt' ityādinā pratyagātmābhimukhīkaraṇārthamupadeśo na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: In order to show [the <s>jīva</s>'s] own nature as <s>Brahman</s>, by the abandonment of the distinction created by the limiting adjuncts — the instruction 'One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker' and so forth, whose purpose is to direct [the aspirant] toward the inner Self, is not contradictory.

children.text: 'yadvācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāgabhyudyate /
children.translated_text: 'That which is not expressed by speech, that by which speech is expressed —

children.text: tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate //
children.translated_text: know that alone as <s>Brahman</s>, not this which they worship here.'

And if the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>prāṇa</s> are accepted, the designation of non-difference between <s>prāṇa</s> and the cognitive self — by virtue of their co-existence — and the designation of difference in their own natures — both designations are justified: 'What is <s>prāṇa</s>, that is <s>prajñā</s>; what is <s>prajñā</s>, that is <s>prāṇa</s>; for these two dwell together in this body, and they depart together.'
But if <s>Brahman</s> is accepted, what would be different from what?
Therefore, either one of these two — the <s>jīva</s> or the chief <s>prāṇa</s> — or both, should be understood here, not <s>Brahman</s> — if this is the position, it is not so; because of the threefold [nature of] meditation.
If this were the case, three [different] meditations would be entailed — meditation on the <s>jīva</s>, meditation on the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, and meditation on <s>Brahman</s>.
But it is not proper to accept this in a single passage.
For the unity of the passage is understood from its opening and conclusion.
Beginning with 'Know me alone,' and having said 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the cognitive self; meditate on me as life, as immortality,' the conclusion states: 'This <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is the cognitive self — blissful, ageless, immortal.' Thus the opening and conclusion are seen to be of one form.
Therein, it is proper to adopt unity of meaning.
Nor can the indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> be construed as referring to something else.
Because the ten elemental faculties and the cognitive faculties cannot be fixed upon anything other than <s>Brahman</s>.
And because of the dependent nature [of the indicatory marks of <s>jīva</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>], elsewhere too the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' applies to <s>Brahman</s> by the force of the indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s>.
And here too, because of the connection with indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> — such as the mention of being most beneficial — it is understood that this is a teaching about <s>Brahman</s> alone.
As for the indicatory mark of the chief <s>prāṇa</s> that was pointed out — 'having grasped this body, it raises it up' — that is untenable.
Because the activity of <s>prāṇa</s> too is dependent on the supreme Self, it can be figuratively attributed to the supreme Self.
Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'No mortal lives by <s>prāṇa</s> or <s>apāna</s>; but by another do they live, upon which these two are dependent' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.5.5).
As for the indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s> pointed out — 'One should not seek to know speech; one should know the speaker' and so forth — that too does not preclude the <s>Brahman</s> interpretation.
For the <s>jīva</s> is not absolutely different from <s>Brahman</s>, because of <s>śrutis</s> such as 'You are That' and 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text:
' (ke. 1.4) ityādi ca śrutyantaraṃ vacanādikriyāvyāpṛtasyaivātmano brahmatvaṃ darśayati /
yatpunaretaduktam- 'saha hyetāvasmiñśarīre vasataḥ sahotkrāmataḥ' iti prāṇaprajñātmanorbhedadarśanaṃ brahmavāde nopapadyata iti /
children.translated_text:
(<s>Kena</s> 1.4) — this and other <s>śrutis</s> show that the Self engaged in activities of speech and such is itself <s>Brahman</s>.
As for the further statement: 'For these two dwell together in this body, and they depart together' — the perception of difference between <s>prāṇa</s> and the cognitive self — [the objection that] this is not consistent with the <s>Brahman</s> teaching —

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
jñānakriyāśaktidvayāśrayayorbuddhiprāṇayoḥ pratyagātmopādhibhūtayorabhedanirdeśopapatteḥ upādhidvayopahitasya tu pratyagātmanaḥ svarūpeṇābheda ityataḥ prāṇa eva prajñātmetyekīkaraṇamaviruddham /
athavā nopāsātraividhyādāśritatvādiha tadyogāt ityasyāyamanyor'thaḥ- na brahmavākyo 'pi jīvamukhyaprāṇaliṅgaṃ virudhyate /
katham, upāsātraividhyāt /
trividhamiha brahmopāsane vivakṣitaṃ prāṇadharmeṇa prajñādharmeṇa svadharmeṇa ca /
tatra 'āyuramṛtamupāḥsvāyuḥ prāṇaḥ' iti, 'idaṃ śarīraṃ parigṛhyotthāpayati' iti, 'tasmādetadevokthamupāsīta' iti ca prāṇadharmaḥ /
'atha yathāsyai prajñāyai sarvāṇi bhūtānyekībhavanti tadvyākhyāsyāmaḥ' ityupakramya 'vāgevāsyā ekamaṅgamadūduhattasyai nāma parastātprativihitā bhūtamātrā prajñayā vācaṃ samāruhya vācā sarvāṇi nāmānyāpnoti' ityādiḥ prajñādharmaḥ /
tā vā etā daśaiva bhūtamātrā adhiprajñaṃ daśa prajñāmātrā adhibhūtam /
yaddhi bhūtamātrā na syurna prajñāmātrāḥ syuḥ /
yaddhi prajñāmātrā na syurna bhūtamātrāḥ syuḥ /
nahyantarato rūpaṃ kiñcana siddhyet /
no etannānā /
'tadyathā rathasyāreṣu nemirarpitā nābhāvarā arpitā evamevaitā bhūtamātrāḥ prajñāmātrāsvarpitāḥ prajñāmātrāḥ prāṇe 'rpitāḥ sa eṣa prāṇa eva prajñātmā' ityādirbrahmadharmaḥ /
tasmādbrahma evaitadupādhidvayadharmeṇa svadharmeṇa caikamupāsanaṃ trividhaṃ vivakṣitam /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
Because the designation of non-difference is justified for the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the [vital] breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), which are the two limiting adjuncts of the inner Self and are the seats of the twofold power of knowledge and action. And the inner Self, as conditioned by these two limiting adjuncts, is in its own nature non-different — therefore the identification '<s>Prāṇa</s> alone is the cognitive self' is not contradictory.
Alternatively, the meaning of '<s>nopāsātraividhyādāśritatvādiha tadyogāt</s>' is this: even when it is a statement about <s>Brahman</s>, the indicatory marks of the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>prāṇa</s> are not contradictory.
How? Because of the threefold [nature of] meditation.
Here, threefold meditation on <s>Brahman</s> is intended — through the properties of <s>prāṇa</s>, through the properties of <s>prajñā</s> (cognition), and through its own properties.
Therein, the <s>prāṇa</s>-properties are: 'Meditate [on me] as life, as immortality; life is <s>prāṇa</s>'; 'having grasped this body, it raises it up'; 'therefore one should worship this alone as the <s>uktha</s>.'
