The <s>prajñā</s>-properties are: beginning with 'Now, we shall explain how all beings become one in this <s>prajñā</s>' — 'Speech alone is one of its limbs, drawn forth; its counterpart established beyond is the elemental faculty; through <s>prajñā</s>, mounting upon speech, one obtains all names' — and so forth. [The text continues:] 'These ten elemental faculties relate to <s>prajñā</s>, and the ten <s>prajñā</s>-faculties relate to the elements. If there were no elemental faculties, there would be no <s>prajñā</s>-faculties; if there were no <s>prajñā</s>-faculties, there would be no elemental faculties. No form whatsoever could be accomplished from one [alone]. This is not manifold.' 'Just as the rim is fixed upon the spokes of a wheel, and the spokes upon the hub — even so these elemental faculties are fixed upon the <s>prajñā</s>-faculties, and the <s>prajñā</s>-faculties are fixed upon <s>prāṇa</s>. This <s>prāṇa</s> alone is the cognitive self' — and so forth: this is the <s>Brahman</s>-property.
Therefore, this is <s>Brahman</s> alone — one meditation intended as threefold through the twofold properties of the limiting adjuncts and its own property.

children.text: anyatrāpi 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityādāvupādhidharmeṇa brahmaṇa upāsanamāśritam /
children.translated_text: Elsewhere too — in 'Made of mind, having <s>prāṇa</s> as body' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and such — meditation on <s>Brahman</s> through the properties of the limiting adjuncts is resorted to.

children.text: ihāpi tadyujyate vākyasyopakramopasaṃhārābhyāmekārthatvāvagamātprāṇaprajñābrahmaliṅgāvagamācca /
children.translated_text: Here too, that is appropriate — because from the beginning and conclusion of the passage, the unity of meaning is understood, and because the indicatory marks of <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Prajñā</s> (consciousness), and <s>Brahman</s> are recognized.

children.text: tasmādbrahmavākyametaditi siddham // 31 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that this is a passage about <s>Brahman</s>. // 31 //

children.text: iti śrīmacchārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye śrīśaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau prathamādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section of the first chapter in the glorious <s>Śārīraka Mīmāṃsā Bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // 1 //

children.text:
FN: yathāyogaṃ kiñcidatra jīvavākyaṃ kiñcinmukhyaprāṇavākyaṃ kiñcidbrahmavākyamityarthaḥ /
prāṇasaṃvāde- vāgādayaḥ sarve pratyekamātmanaḥ śraiṣṭhyaṃ manyamānāstannirdidhārayiṣayā prajāpatimupajagmuḥ /
sa tānuvāca yasminnutkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭhataramiva bhavati sa vaḥ śreṣṭha iti /
tataḥ krameṇa vāgādiṣūtkrānteṣvapi śarīraṃ svasthamasthat /
mukhyaprāṇasyoccikramiṣāyāṃ sarveṣāṃ vyākulatve /
variṣṭhaḥ prāṇo 'bravīdahameva pañcadhā prāṇāpānādibhāvenātmānaṃ vibhajya etadbhāti gacchatīti vānaṃ tadeva bāṇamasthiraṃ śarīramavaṣṭabhyāśrityeti /
pañca śabdādayaḥ pañca pṛthivyādaya iti daśa bhūtamātrāḥ /
pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca buddhaya iti daśa prajñāmātrāḥ /
anyatra 'ata eva prāṇa' ityādau /
yena caitanyena vāgabhyudyate preryate vadanasāmarthyamāpadyate tadeva vāgāderagamyaṃ brahma /
upāseti svatantrāṇāṃ trayāṇāmupāstau vākyabhedaḥ, natvekasyaiva brahmaṇastaddharmeṇetyarthaḥ /
tasyāyuṣṭvaṃ jīvanasya tadadhīnatvāt /
utthāpayatītyukthamiti prāṇadharmaḥ /
atheti jīvadharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The meaning is: some [passages] here are about the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), some about the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, and some about <s>Brahman</s>, as appropriate. In the dialogue of the <s>prāṇas</s>: speech and the other [faculties], each considering itself to be the most excellent, approached <s>Prajāpati</s> with the desire to ascertain that. He told them: 'That one whose departure makes the body appear most wretched — he is the most excellent among you.' Then, when speech and the others departed in sequence, the body remained well. But when the chief <s>prāṇa</s> wished to depart, all [the other faculties] became agitated. The most excellent <s>Prāṇa</s> said: 'I myself, dividing myself fivefold in the forms of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and such, supporting and sustaining this unstable body — that which goes, that is <s>vāna</s> (vehicle), that itself is <s>bāṇa</s> (arrow).' The ten material categories are: the five [subtle elements] beginning with sound, and the five [gross elements] beginning with earth. The ten cognitive categories are: the five cognitive organs and the five cognitions. Elsewhere, in '<s>ata eva prāṇa</s>' and such [passages]. That consciousness by which speech is propelled, impelled, and attains the capacity for speaking — that very thing, unreachable by speech and the other [faculties], is <s>Brahman</s>. 'Meditate' — the differentiation of passages applies to the meditation on three independent [entities: <s>jīva</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>Brahman</s>], not to one <s>Brahman</s> alone with those qualities: this is the meaning. Its being the source of life is because life depends on it. 'It raises up' — hence '<s>uktha</s>' (hymn) — this is a quality of <s>prāṇa</s>. '<s>Atha</s>' — [what follows] is a quality of the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: prathamādhyāye dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the first chapter, the second section.

children.text: atrāspaṣṭabrahmaliṅgayuktavākyānāmupāsyabrahmaviṣayāṇāṃ vicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Here is the examination of passages that have unclear indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> and that concern <s>Brahman</s> as the object of meditation.

children.text: 1 sarvatra prasiddhyadhikaraṇam / sū. 1-8
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Sarvatra Prasiddhi Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Universal Recognition). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-8.

children.text:
prathame pāde 'janmādyasya yataḥ' ityākāśādeḥ samastasya jagato janmādikāraṇaṃ brahmetyuktam /
tasya samastajagatkāraṇasya brahmaṇo vyāpitvaṃ, nityatvaṃ, sarvajñatvaṃ, sarvaśaktitvaṃ, sarvātmatvamityevañjātīyakā dharmā uktā eva bhavanti /
arthāntaraprasiddhānāṃ ca keṣāñcicchabdānāṃ brahmaviṣayatvahetupratipādanena kānicidvākyāni spaṣṭabrahmaliṅgāni saṃdihyamānāni brahmaparatayā nirṇītīni /
punarapyanyāni vākyānyaspaṣṭabrahmaliṅgāni saṃdihyante- kiṃ paraṃ brahma pratipādayantyāhosvidarthāntaraṃ kiñcidasti /
tannirṇayāya dvitīyatṛtīyau pādāvārabhyete /
children.translated_text: In the first section, it was stated that <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the origination and such of the entire world, through [the sūtra] 'that from which the origination and such of this [world proceed].' The qualities of that <s>Brahman</s>, which is the cause of the entire world, such as all-pervasiveness, eternality, omniscience, omnipotence, and being the Self of all — these have already been stated. And through demonstrating the reason for the <s>Brahman</s>-reference of certain words that are well-known in other meanings, some passages with clear indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> that were in doubt have been determined as referring to <s>Brahman</s>. Now again, other passages with unclear indicatory marks of <s>Brahman</s> are in doubt: do they teach the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, or do they refer to something else? For the determination of that, the second and third sections are commenced.

children.text: sarvatra prasiddhopadeśāt | BBs_1,2.1 |
children.translated_text: Because of the teaching of what is universally recognized [as <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.1 |

children.text:
idamāmnāyate- 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta /
atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākraturasmiṃlloke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati sa kratuṃ kurvīta', 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ' (chā. 3.14.1,2) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kimiha manomayatvādibhirdharmaiḥ śārīra ātmopāsyatvenopadiśyata āhosvitparaṃ brahmeti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
śārīra iti /
kutaḥ, tasya hi kāryakaraṇādhipateḥ prasiddho manaādibhiḥ saṃbandho na parasya brahmaṇaḥ, 'aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhraḥ' (mu. 2.1.2) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is recorded in scripture: 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>; it arises from, dissolves into, and lives in That — thus, one should meditate in tranquility. Now, a person is made of intention (<s>kratu</s>); as is his intention in this world, so does he become upon departing; let him form his intention' — '<s>manomaya</s> (mind-formed), having <s>prāṇa</s> as its body, having the form of light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1-2) and so forth. There, the doubt [arises]: Is the embodied self (<s>jīva</s>) taught here as the object of meditation, with qualities such as being <s>manomaya</s> (mind-formed) and the like? Or is it the supreme <s>Brahman</s>? What is the prima facie view? That it is the embodied self. Why? Because the well-known connection of the master of the body and organs with mind and such belongs to it [the <s>jīva</s>], not to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, as scripture states: 'Without breath, without mind, pure' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2) and so forth.

children.text: nanu 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' iti svaśabdenaiva brahmopāttaṃ, kathamiha śārīra ātmopāsya āśaṅkyate /
children.translated_text: But <s>Brahman</s> has been expressly taken up by its own word in 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' — how can the embodied self be suspected here as the object of meditation?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
nedaṃ vākyaṃ brahmopāsanāvidhiparaṃ kiṃ tarhi śamavidhiparam /
yatkāraṇaṃ 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta' ityāha /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- yasmātsarvamidaṃ vikārajātaṃ brahmaiva, tajjatvāttallatvāttadanatvācca /
naca sarvasyaikātmatve rāgādayaḥ saṃbhavanti, tasmācchānta upāsīteti /
naca śamavidhiparatve satyanena vākyena brahmopāsanaṃ niyantuṃ śakyate /
upāsanaṃ tu 'sa kratuṃ kurvīta' ityanena vidhīyate /
kratuḥ saṃkalpo dhyānamityarthaḥ /
tasya ca viṣayatvaṃna śrūyate- 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' iti jīvaliṅgam /
ato brūmo jīvaviṣayametadupāsanamiti /
'sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ' ityādyapi śrūyamāṇaṃ paryāyeṇa jīvaviṣayamupapadyate /
'eṣa ma ātmāntarhṛdaye 'ṇīyānvrīhervā yavādvā' iti ca hṛdayāyatanatvamaṇīyastvaṃ cārāgramātrasya jīvasyāvakalpate nāparicchinnasya brahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect. This passage is not directed toward enjoining the meditation on <s>Brahman</s>; rather, it is directed toward enjoining tranquility (<s>śama</s>). The reason being that [the scripture] says: 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>; it arises from, dissolves into, and lives in That — thus, one should meditate in tranquility.' What is stated is this: since all this world of modifications is nothing but <s>Brahman</s> — because it is born from That, dissolves into That, and lives in That — and since when there is the oneness of all, passion and such are not possible, therefore one should meditate in tranquility. And when the passage is directed toward enjoining tranquility, this sentence cannot be used to restrict the meditation to <s>Brahman</s>. But the meditation is enjoined by the words 'let him form his intention' (<s>sa kratuṃ kurvīta</s>). '<s>Kratu</s>' means intention, meditation — this is the meaning. And its object is not heard [as <s>Brahman</s>]; rather, '<s>manomaya</s>, having <s>prāṇa</s> as its body' — this is an indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s>. Therefore, we say that this meditation has the <s>jīva</s> as its object. Even '<s>sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ</s>' (of all actions, all desires) and such, though heard, can be accommodated as referring to the <s>jīva</s> through an indirect meaning. And 'This is my Self, within the heart, smaller than a grain of rice or barley' — the locus in the heart and the smallness are appropriate for the <s>jīva</s>, which is the size of a needle-point, not for <s>Brahman</s>, which is unlimited.

children.text: nanu 'jyāyānpṛthivyā' ityādyapi na paricchinne 'vakalpata iti /
children.translated_text: But would not 'Greater than the earth' and such also be inappropriate for one who is limited?

children.text:
atra brūmaḥ- na tāvadaṇīyastvaṃ jyāyastvaṃ cobhayamekasminsamāśrayituṃ śakyaṃ, virodhāt /
anyatarāśrayaṇe ca prathamaśrutatvādaṇīyastvaṃ yuktamāśrayituṃ, jyāyastvaṃ tu brahmabhāvāpekṣayā bhaviṣyatīti /
niścite ca jīvaviṣayatve yadante brahmasaṃkīrtanaṃ 'etadbrahma' (chā. 3.14.4) iti, tadapi prakṛtaparāmarśārthatvājjīvaviṣayameva /
tasmānmanomayatvādibhirdharmairupāsyam /
kutaḥ, sarvatra prasiddhopadeśāt /
yatsarveṣu vedānteṣu prasiddhaṃ brahmaśabdasyālambanaṃ jagatkāraṇaṃsa iha ca 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' iti vākyopakrame śrute, tadeva manomayatvādidharmairviśiṣṭamupadiśyata iti yuktam /
evañca prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriye na bhaviṣyataḥ /
children.translated_text: To this we say: It is not possible to accommodate both the qualities of being 'smaller than [an atom]' and 'greater than [the earth]' in one and the same [entity], because of the contradiction. And when one must adopt one of the two, it is proper to adopt 'smaller than' because it is heard first; 'greater than' would be from the standpoint of [its identity with] <s>Brahman</s>. And when the <s>jīva</s>-reference is determined, the mention of <s>Brahman</s> at the end — 'This is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.4) — that too refers to the <s>jīva</s>, because it is a reference back to the subject under discussion. Therefore, [the object of meditation is endowed] with the qualities of being <s>manomaya</s> and such — [this is the prima facie view]. [But the conclusion is:] Because of the teaching of what is universally recognized [as <s>Brahman</s>]. That which is the universally recognized basis of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts — [namely,] the cause of the world — and which is here heard at the beginning of the passage in 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' — it is proper that that very [<s>Brahman</s>] is taught as qualified by the attributes of being <s>manomaya</s> and such. And in this way, there will be neither abandonment of the subject nor introduction of a new subject.

children.text: nanu vākyopakrame śamavidhivivakṣayā brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ na svavivakṣayetyuktam /
children.translated_text: But it was said that <s>Brahman</s> was mentioned at the beginning of the passage with the intention of enjoining tranquility, not with the intention of being [itself] the subject.

children.text: atrocyate- yadyapi śamavidhivivakṣayā brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ tathāpi manomayatvādiṣūpadiśyamāneṣu tadeva brahma saṃnihitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: To this it is said: Even though <s>Brahman</s> was mentioned with the intention of enjoining tranquility, nevertheless, when the qualities such as being <s>manomaya</s> and such are being taught, that very <s>Brahman</s> is present [as the subject].

children.text: jīstu na saṃnihito naca svaśabdenopātta iti vaiṣamyam // 1 //
children.translated_text: But the <s>jīva</s> is not present [as the subject in the opening], nor is it taken up by its own word — hence there is a disparity [between the two candidates]. // 1 //

children.text:
FN.:tasmin jāyata iti tajjaṃ, tasmin iti tallaṃ, tasminnaniti ceṣṭata iti tadanaṃ tajjaṃ catallaṃ ca tadanaṃ ceti tajjalān /
śākapārthivādinyāyena madhyamasya tacchabdasya lopaḥ /
tajjalānamiti vaktavye chāndaso 'vayavalopaḥ /
vibhaktivyatyayena manomayaṃ prāṇaśarīraṃ bhārūpaṃ dhyāyedityarthaḥ /
yata evamāha tasmācchamavidhiparamityarthaḥ /
totraprotāyaḥśalākāgraparimāṇasyetyarthaḥ /
prāṇaḥ śarīramasyeti samāsagatasarvanāmnā saṃnihitārthena prakṛtaṃ brahma hitvā jīvamaprakṛtamicchataḥ prakṛtahāniraprakṛtaprakriyācetyarthaḥ /
vaiṣamyaṃ jīvabrahmaṇoriti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Tajja</s>' — born from That; '<s>talla</s>' — dissolving into That; '<s>tadana</s>' — living, functioning in That. '<s>Tajja</s>' and '<s>talla</s>' and '<s>tadana</s>' — thus '<s>tajjalān</s>.' The middle '<s>tad</s>'-word is dropped by the analogy of '<s>śākapārthiva</s>' and such [where a middle word is elided]. In '<s>tajjalānam</s>' when it should be said thus, the Vedic [license allows] elision of a component. With interchange of case-endings, the meaning is: 'One should meditate on [<s>Brahman</s> as] <s>manomaya</s>, having <s>prāṇa</s> as its body, having the form of light.' 'Because it says thus' — the meaning is: therefore the passage is directed toward enjoining tranquility. 'Of the measure of a needle-point' — this is the meaning. 'Having <s>prāṇa</s> as body' — with the pronoun in the compound [pointing to] a proximate referent: one who desires the <s>jīva</s>, which is not the subject, rejecting <s>Brahman</s>, which is the subject — that constitutes abandonment of the subject and introduction of a new subject: this is the meaning. 'Disparity' — [supply:] between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: vivakṣitaguṇopapatteś ca | BBs_1,2.2 |
children.translated_text: And because of the justification of the intended qualities [in <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.2 |

children.text:
vaktumiṣṭā vivakṣitāḥ /
yadyapyapauruṣeye vede vakturabhāvānneccārthaḥ saṃbhavati tathāpyupādānena phalenopacaryate /
loke hi yacchabdābhihitamupādeyaṃ bhavati tadvivakṣitamityucyate, yadanupādeyaṃ tadavivakṣitamiti /
tadamavede 'pyupādeyatvenābhihitaṃ vivakṣitaṃ bhavati, itaradavivakṣitam /
upādānānupādāne tu vedavākyatātparyābhyāmavagamyate /
tadiha ye vivakṣitā guṇā upāsanāyāmupādeyatvenopadiṣṭāḥ satyasaṃkalpaprabhṛtayaste parasminbrahmaṇyupapadyante /
satyasaṃkalpatvaṃ hi sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāreṣvapratibaddhaśaktitvātparamātmana evāvakalpate /
paramātmaguṇatvena ca 'ya ātmāpahṛtapāpmā' (chā. 8.7.1) ityatra 'satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpa' iti śrutam /
ākāśātmetyādinākāśavadātmāsyetyarthaḥ /
sarvagatatvādibhirdharṇaiḥ saṃbhavatyākāśena sāmyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ /
'jyāyānpṛthivyāḥ' ityādinā caitadeva darśayati /
yadāpyākāśa ātmā yasyeti vyākhyāyacate, tadapi saṃbhavati sarvajagatkāraṇasya sarvātmano brahma ākāśātmatvam /
children.translated_text: Those intended to be stated are 'intended' (<s>vivakṣita</s>). Although in the authorless <s>Veda</s> the meaning of intention is not possible due to the absence of a speaker, it is used figuratively through [the concept of] adoption and fruit. For in the world, what is stated by words and is to be adopted is called '<s>vivakṣita</s>' (intended), and what is not to be adopted is called '<s>avivakṣita</s>' (not intended). Similarly, even in the <s>Veda</s>, what is stated as to be adopted is 'intended,' and the rest is 'not intended.' And the adoption and non-adoption are understood from the purport of the Vedic passage. Here, those qualities that are 'intended' — that are taught as to be adopted in the meditation — such as true resolve (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>) and so forth — those are justified in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. For true resolve is appropriate only for the supreme Self, because of its unobstructed power in creation, sustenance, and dissolution. And true resolve is heard as a quality of the supreme Self in 'The Self that is free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) — 'of true desire, of true resolve.' '<s>Ākāśātmā</s>' (whose Self is space) means 'whose Self is like space' — the meaning being that <s>Brahman</s> can be compared to space through qualities such as all-pervasiveness and the like. 'Greater than the earth' and such also demonstrate this. And when it is interpreted as 'one whose Self is space' — that too is possible, since <s>Brahman</s>, as the cause of the entire world and the Self of all, can have space as its Self.

children.text:
ata eva 'sarvakarmā' ityādi /
evamihopāsyatayā vivakṣitā guṇā brahmaṇyupapadyante /
yattūktaṃ 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' iti jīvaliṅgaṃ na tadbrahmaṇyupapadyata iti, tadapi brahmaṇyupapadyata iti brūmaḥ /
sarvātmatvāddhi brahmaṇo jīvasaṃbandhīni manomayatvādīni brahmasaṃbandhīni bhavanti /
tathāca brahmaviṣaye śrutismṛtī bhavataḥ- 'tvaṃ strī tvaṃ kumāra uta vā kumārī /
tvaṃ jīrṇo daṇḍena vañcasi tvaṃ jāto bhavasi viśvatomukhaḥ' (śve. 4.3) iti, sarvataḥpāṇipādaṃ tatsarvatokṣiśiromukham /
children.translated_text: You, grown old, totter with a staff; you, being born, are the one with faces in all directions' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.3), and 'With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere,

children.text: sarvataḥśrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati (gī. 13.13) iti ca /
children.translated_text: with ears everywhere in the world, He stands pervading all' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.13).

children.text: 'aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhraḥ' iti śrutiḥ śuddhabrahmaviṣayā, iyaṃ tu 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' iti saguṇabrahmaviṣayeti viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The scripture 'Without breath, without mind, pure' refers to the unqualified <s>Brahman</s>; but this passage — '<s>manomaya</s>, having <s>prāṇa</s> as its body' — refers to the qualified <s>Brahman</s> (<s>saguṇa Brahman</s>): this is the distinction.

children.text: ato vivakṣitaguṇopapatteḥ parameva brahmehopāsyatvenopadiṣṭamiti gamyate // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because the intended qualities are justified [in <s>Brahman</s>], it is understood that the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is taught here as the object of meditation. // 2 //

For this very reason, [the scriptures say] '<s>sarvakarmā</s>' (of all actions) and so forth. Thus, the qualities intended here as objects of meditation are justified in <s>Brahman</s>. As for what was said — that '<s>manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ</s>' is an indicatory mark of the <s>jīva</s> and is not justified in <s>Brahman</s> — to that too we say it is justified in <s>Brahman</s>. For since <s>Brahman</s> is the Self of all, the qualities associated with the <s>jīva</s> — such as being <s>manomaya</s> and the like — become qualities associated with <s>Brahman</s>. And thus, in passages about <s>Brahman</s>, scripture and <s>smṛti</s> state: 'You are woman, you are boy, or indeed a girl;

children.text:
FN: upādānānupādāne parigrahaparityāgau /
tāttaryaṃ nāma phalavadarthapratītyanukūtvaṃ śabdadharmaḥ /
upakramādinā jñānāttayoravagama ityarthaḥ /
jīrṇaḥ sthaviro bhūtvā yodaṇḍena vañcati gacchati, tathā yo jātaḥ bālaḥ so 'pi tvameva /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Adoption and non-adoption' mean acceptance and rejection. 'Purport' (<s>tātparya</s>) is a quality of words that consists in being conducive to the understanding of a meaning that yields a result. From knowledge of that [purport] through the opening and concluding [statements] and such, those two [adoption and non-adoption] are understood: this is the meaning. 'Grown old, having become elderly, one who <s>vañcati</s> (goes) with a staff — and the one who is born as a child — that too is you alone.'

children.text: anupapattes tu na śārīraḥ | BBs_1,2.3 |
children.translated_text: But [it is] not the embodied self, because of the impossibility [of the qualities applying to it]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.3 |

children.text:
pūrveṇa sutreṇa brahmaṇi vivakṣitānāṃ guṇānāmupapattiruktā /
anena tu śārīre teṣāmanupapattirucyate /
tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ /
brahmaivoktena nyāyena manomayatvādiguṇaṃ, natu śārīro jīvo manomayatvādiguṇaḥ /
yatkāraṇaṃ 'satyasaṃkalpaḥ, ākāśātmā, avākī, anādaraḥ, jyāyānpṛthivyā' iti caivañjātīyakā guṇā na śārīra āñjasyenopapadyante /
śārīra iti śarīre bhava ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the previous <s>sūtra</s>, the justification of the intended qualities in <s>Brahman</s> was stated. Through this [<s>sūtra</s>], the impossibility of those [qualities] in the embodied self is stated. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) is for emphasis. It is <s>Brahman</s> alone that, by the stated reasoning, possesses the qualities of being <s>manomaya</s> and such — but the embodied <s>jīva</s> does not possess the qualities of being <s>manomaya</s> and such. The reason being that qualities of the type 'of true resolve, whose Self is space, without speech, without attachment, greater than the earth' are not directly appropriate for the embodied self. 'Embodied' (<s>śārīra</s>) means 'existing in the body' — this is the meaning.

children.text: nanvīśvaro 'pi śarīre bhavati /
children.translated_text: But does not the Lord too exist in the body?

children.text: satyam /
children.translated_text: True.

children.text: śarīre bhavati natu śarīra eva bhavati, 'jyāyānpṛthivyā jyāyānantarikṣāt', 'ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ' iti ca vyāpitatvaśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: He exists in the body, but He does not exist in the body alone — because of the scriptural statement of all-pervasiveness: 'Greater than the earth, greater than the atmosphere,' and 'Like space, all-pervading and eternal.'

children.text: jīvastu śarīra eva bhavati, tasya bhogādhiṣṭhānāccharīrādanyatra vṛttyabhāvāt // 3 //
children.translated_text: But the <s>jīva</s> exists in the body alone, because it has no activity apart from the body, which is the locus of its experience. // 3 //

children.text:
FN: vāgeva vākaḥ so 'syāstīti vākī na vākī avākī vāgādisarvendriyarahitaḥ /
āptakāmatvānna kutracitadādaro 'stītyanādaraḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Vāk</s>' itself is '<s>vākī</s>' — one who possesses that; '<s>avākī</s>' means one devoid of speech, devoid of all sense-organs beginning with speech. Because of the fulfillment of all desires, there is no attachment (<s>ādara</s>) to anything — hence '<s>anādara</s>' (without attachment).

children.text: karmakartṛvyapadeśāc ca | BBs_1,2.4 |
children.translated_text: And because of the designation as both the object and the agent of action. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.4 |

children.text:
itaśca na śārīro manomayatvādiguṇaḥ, yasmātkarmakartṛvyapadeśo bhavati 'etamitaḥ pretyābhisaṃbhavitāsmi' (chā. 3.14.4) iti /
etamiti prakṛtaṃ manomayatvādiguṇamupāsyamātmānaṃ karmatvena prāpyatvena vyapadiśati /
abhisaṃbhavitāsmīti śārīramupāsakaṃ kartṛtvena prāpakatvena /
abhisaṃbhavitāsmīti /
prāptāsmītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of '<s>abhisaṃbhavitāsmi</s>' is: 'I shall attain.'

children.text: naca satyāṃ gatāvekasya karmakartṛvyapadeśo yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when there is [actual] attainment, the designation of one and the same entity as both object and agent is not justified.

children.text: tathopāsyopāsakabhāvo 'pi bhedādhiṣṭhāna eva /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the relation of worshipped and worshipper too is based on difference alone.

children.text: tasmādapi na śārīro manomayatvādiviśiṣṭaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the one qualified by being made of mind and such is not the embodied self. // 4 //

For this further reason too, the one qualified by being made of mind and such is not the embodied self — because there is the designation of object and agent: 'I shall attain this [Self] on departing from here' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.4). 'This' — designates the subject under discussion, the Self qualified by being made of mind and such, as the object, as what is to be attained. 'I shall attain' — designates the embodied worshipper as the agent, as the attainer.

children.text: FN: etamiti prāpakatvena vyapadiśatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The connection is: 'this' designates [the Self] as what is to be attained.

children.text: śabdaviśeṣāt | BBs_1,2.5 |
children.translated_text: <s>Śabdaviśeṣāt</s> — Because of the distinctness of the word. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.5 |

children.text: itaśca śārīrādanyo manomayatvādiguṇaḥ, yasmācchabdaviśeṣo bhavati samānaprakaraṇe śrutyantari- 'yathāvrīhirvā yavo vā śyamako vā śyamākataṇḍulo vaivamayamantarātmanpuruṣo hiraṇmayaḥ' (śata. brā. 10.6.3.2) iti /
children.translated_text: For this further reason too, the one qualified by being made of mind and such is different from the embodied self — because there is a distinctness of word in another scriptural passage within the same context: 'Just as a grain of rice, or barley, or millet, or the kernel of a millet grain — so is this golden <s>Puruṣa</s> within the inner self' (<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 10.6.3.2).

children.text: śārīrasyatno yaḥ śabdo 'bhidhāyakaḥ saptamyanto 'ntarātmanniti tasmādviśiṣṭo 'nyaḥ prathamāntaḥ puruṣaśabdo manomayatvādiviśiṣṭasyātmano 'bhidhāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word ending in the locative case — '<s>antarātman</s>' — designates the embodied self; distinct from it, the other word — '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — ending in the nominative case, designates the Self qualified by being made of mind and such.

children.text: tasmāttayorbhedo 'dhigamyate // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the difference between the two is understood. // 5 //

children.text:
FN: samānaprakaraṇatvamekavidyāviṣayatvām /
antarātmanniti chāndaso vibhaktilopaḥ /
antarātmanītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Being in the same context' means being the subject of one and the same <s>vidyā</s> (meditation). '<s>Antarātmann</s>' — the dropping of the case-ending is a Vedic irregularity. The meaning is '<s>antarātmani</s>' (within the inner self).

children.text: smṛteś ca | BBs_1,2.6 |
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛteś ca</s> — And because of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition). | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.6 |

children.text:
smṛtiśca śārīraparamātmanorbhedaṃ darśayati- 'īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśer'juna tiṣṭati /
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā' /
(gī. 18.61) ityādyā /
atrāha- kaḥ punarayaṃ śārīro nāma paramātmano 'nyaḥ, yaḥ pratiṣidhyate 'anupapattestu na śārīraḥ' ityādinā /
śrutistu- 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā śrotā' (bṛha. 3.7.23) ityevañjātīyakā paramātmano 'nyamātmānaṃ vārayati /
tathā smṛtirapi- 'kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata' (gī. 13.2) ityevañjātīyaketi /
atrocyate- satyametat /
para evātmā dehendriyamanobuddhyupādhibhiḥ paricchidyamāno bālaiḥ śārīra ityupacaryate /
children.translated_text: The supreme Self itself, when delimited by the limiting adjuncts of body, senses, mind, and intellect, is figuratively called the 'embodied self' by the unwise.

children.text: yathā ghaṭakarakādyupādhivaśādaparicchinnamapi nabhaḥ paricchinnavadavabhāsate, tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as space, though unlimited, appears as if limited due to limiting adjuncts such as pots, jars, and so forth — so too [with the Self].

children.text: tadapekṣayā ca karmakartṛtvādibhedavyavahāro na virudhyate prāk 'tattvamasi' ityātmaikatvopadeśaghaṇāt /
children.translated_text: And in relation to that [appearance], the conventional usage of distinctions such as object and agent and the like is not contradicted — prior to the culmination of the teaching of the unity of the Self in 'That you are' (<s>tattvamasi</s>).

children.text: gṛhīte tvātmaikatve bandhamokṣādisarvavyavahāraparisamāptireva syāt // 6 //
children.translated_text: But once the unity of the Self is grasped, there would be the complete cessation of all conventional usage such as bondage, liberation, and the like. // 6 //

And <s>smṛti</s> shows the difference between the embodied self and the supreme Self: 'The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>, causing all beings mounted on the machine [of the body] to revolve through <s>māyā</s>' (<s>Gītā</s> 18.61) — and such passages. Here an objection is raised: Who then is this so-called embodied self different from the supreme Self, who is negated by '<s>anupapattestu na śārīraḥ</s>' (but it is not the embodied self, because of unfitness) and so forth? Scripture such as 'There is no other seer than this, no other knower' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23) denies any self other than the supreme Self. Likewise <s>smṛti</s>: 'Know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O <s>Bhārata</s>' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.2) — and such passages. To this it is said: That is true.

children.text: FN: tadapekṣayā aupādhikabhedāpekṣayā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'In relation to that' — in relation to the difference based on limiting adjuncts.

children.text: arbhakaustvāt tadvyapadeśāc ca neti cen na nicāyyatvād evaṃ vyomavac ca | BBs_1,2.7 |
children.translated_text: <s>Arbhakaukastvāt tadvyapadeśāc ca na iti cen na nicāyyatvād evaṃ vyomavac ca</s> — If [it be said] 'no, because of the smallness of the abode and because of the designation of that' — [we say] no, because [<s>Brahman</s>] is to be contemplated thus, and because it is like space. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.7 |

children.text: arbhakamalpamoko nīḍaṃ, 'eṣa ma ātmāntarhṛdaye' iti paricchinnāyatanatvāt, svaśabdena ca 'aṇīyānvrīhervā yavādvā' ityaṇīyastvavyapadeśāt, śārīra evārāgramātro jīva ihopadiśyate, na karvagataḥ paramātmeti yaduktaṃ tatparihartavyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Arbhaka</s>' means small; '<s>okas</s>' means abode — because of the limited abode, as in 'This is my Self within the heart,' and because of the designation of smallness by its own word: 'smaller than a grain of rice or barley' — [it was said that] only the embodied self, the <s>jīva</s> who is the size of an <s>ārā</s>'s point, is being taught here, not the all-pervading supreme Self. This [objection] must be answered.

children.text:
atrocyate- nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
na tāvatparicchinnadeśasya sarvagatatvavyapadeśaḥ kathamapyupapadyate /
sarvagatasya tu sarvadeśeṣu vidyamānatvātparicchinnadeśavyapadeśo 'pi kayācidapekṣayā saṃbhavati /
yathā samastavasudhādhipatirapi hi sannayodhyādhipatiriti vyapadiśyate kayā punarapekṣayā sarvagataḥ sannīśvaror'bhakaukā aṇīyāṃśca vyapadiśyata iti /
nicāyyatvādevamiti brūmaḥ /
evamaṇīyastvādiguṇagaṇopeta īśvarastatra hṛdayapuṇḍarīke nicāyyo draṣṭavya upadiśyate /
children.translated_text: To this it is said: This is not a fault. For, first, the designation of all-pervasiveness cannot possibly apply to what is of a limited location. But for what is all-pervading, since it exists in all locations, the designation of a limited location too is possible in some respect. Just as one who is the lord of the entire earth is also designated as the lord of <s>Ayodhyā</s>. In what respect, then, is the Lord, though all-pervading, designated as having a small abode and as being minute? 'Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is to be contemplated thus,' we say. The Lord, endowed with such a group of qualities as minuteness and so forth, is taught as to be contemplated, to be meditated upon, there in the lotus of the heart.

children.text:
yathā śālagrāme hariḥ /
tatrāsya buddhivijñānaṃ grāhakam /
sarvagato 'pīśvarastatropāsyamānaḥ prasīdati /
vyomavaccaitaddraṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: And this should be understood as being like space.

children.text: yathā sarvagatamapi sadvyoma sūcīpāśādyapekṣāyārbhakauko 'ṇīyaśca vyapadiśyate, evaṃ brahmāpi /
children.translated_text: Just as space, though all-pervading, is designated as having a small abode and as being minute, in relation to the eye of a needle and such — so too <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tadevaṃ nicāyyatvāpekṣaṃ brahmaṇor'bhakaukastvamaṇīyastvaṃ ca na pāramārthikam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the smallness of abode and the minuteness of <s>Brahman</s>, being relative to the purpose of contemplation, are not ultimate.

children.text: tatra yadaśaṅkyate, hṛdayāyatanatvādbrahmaṇo hṛdayāyatanānāṃ ca pratiśarīraṃ bhinnatvādbhinnāyatanānāṃ ca śukādīnāmanekatvasāvayavatvānityatvādidoṣadarśanādbrahmaṇo 'pi tatprasaṅga iti, tadapi parihṛtaṃ bhavati // 7 //
children.translated_text: And the apprehension that — because <s>Brahman</s> has the heart as its abode, and because heart-abodes differ from body to body, and because things with different abodes such as parrots and such are seen to be multiple, composite, and impermanent — <s>Brahman</s> too would be liable to these faults — that too is thereby refuted. // 7 //

Just as <s>Hari</s> [is meditated upon] in the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone. There, the intellect and understanding serve as the means of apprehension. Even though the Lord is all-pervading, when meditated upon there, he bestows his grace.

children.text:
FN: arbhakaśabdasya śiśuviṣayatvaniṣedhārthamalpamiti paryāyatvokti /
kathamapi brahmabhāvapekṣe 'pi /
nicāyyatvāddraṣṭavyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The synonym '<s>alpam</s>' (small) is given for the word '<s>arbhaka</s>' to negate the [common] meaning of 'child.' '<s>Kathamapi</s>' — even from the perspective of <s>Brahman</s>'s nature. Because [<s>Brahman</s>] is to be contemplated, because it is to be meditated upon.

children.text: saṃbhogaprāptir iti cen na vaiśeṣyāt | BBs_1,2.8 |
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃbhogaprāptir iti cen na vaiśeṣyāt</s> — If [it be said that] the experience [of pleasure and pain] would follow [for <s>Brahman</s>] — [we say] no, because of the distinction. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.8 |

children.text:
vyemavatsarvagatasya brahmaṇaḥ sarvaprāṇihṛdayasaṃbandhāt, cidrūpatayā ca śārīrādaviśiṣṭatvāt, sukhaduḥkhādisaṃbhogo 'pyaviśiṣṭaḥ prasajyeta /
ekatvācca /
nahi parasmādātmano 'nyaḥ kaścidātmā saṃsārī vidyate, 'nānyo 'to 'sti vijñātā' (bṛ. 3.7.23) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tasmātparasyeva saṃsārasaṃbhogaprāptiriti cet, na vaiśeṣyāt /
na tāvatsarvaprāṇihṛdayasaṃbandhāccharīravadbrahṇaḥ saṃbhogaprasaṅgaḥ, vaiśeṣyāt /
viśeṣo hi bhavati śārīraparameśvarayoḥ /
ekaḥ kartā bhoktā dharmādharmasādhanaḥ sukhaduḥkhādimāṃśca /
ekastadviparīto 'pahatapāpmatvādiguṇaḥ /
etasmādanayorviśeṣādekasya bhogo netarasya /
yadi ca saṃnidhānamātreṇa vastuśaktimanāśritya kāryasaṃbandho 'bhyupagamyeta, ākāśādīnāmapi dāhādiprasaṅgaḥ /
sarvagatānekātmavādināmapi samāvetau codyaparihārau /
yadapyekatvādbrahmaṇa ātmāntarābhāvāccharīrasya bhogena brahṇo bhogaprasaṅga iti /
atra vadāmaḥ- idaṃ tāvaddevānāṃpriyaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ /
kathamayaṃ tvayātmāntarābhāvo 'dhyavasita iti /
'tattavamasi' 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' 'nānyo 'to 'sti vijñātā' ityādiśāstrebhya iti cet, yathāśāstraṃ tarhi śāstrīyor'thaḥ pratipattavyo na tatrārdhajaratīyaṃ labhyam /
śāstraṃ ca tattvamasi ityapahatapāpmatvādiviśeṣaṇaṃ brahma śārīrasyātmatvenopadiśacchārīrasyaiva tāvadupabhoktṛtvaṃ vārayati /
kutastadupabhogena brahmaṇa upabhogaprasaṅgaḥ /
athāgṛhītaṃ śārīrasya brahmaṇaikatvaṃ tadā mithyājñānanimittaḥ śārīrasyopabhogaḥ, na tena paramārtharūpasya brahmaṇaḥ saṃsparśaḥ /
nahi bālaistalamalinatādibhirvyomni vikalpyamāne talamalitādiviśiṣṭameva paramārthato vyoma bhavati /
tadāha- na vaiśeṣyāditi /
naikatve 'pi śārīrasyopabhogena brahmaṇa upabhogaprasaṅgaḥ, vaiśeṣyāt /
viśeṣo hi bhavati mithyājñānasamyagjñanayoḥ /
children.translated_text: For there is a distinction between false knowledge and right knowledge.

children.text: mithyājñānakalpita upabhogaḥ, samyagjñānadṛṣṭamekatvam /
children.translated_text: The experience is fabricated by false knowledge; the oneness is seen through right knowledge.

children.text: naca mithyājñānakalpitenopabhogena samyagjñānadṛṣṭaṃ vastu saṃspṛśyate /
children.translated_text: And the reality seen through right knowledge is not touched by the experience fabricated by false knowledge.

children.text: tasmānnopabhogagandho 'pi śakya īśvarasya kalpayitum // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, not even a trace of experience can be attributed to the Lord. // 8 //

Since <s>Brahman</s>, like space, is all-pervading and connected with the hearts of all living beings, and since, being of the nature of consciousness, it is not distinct from the embodied self — the experience of pleasure, pain, and such too would follow as being non-distinct [for <s>Brahman</s>]. And because of oneness — for there is no transmigrating self other than the supreme Self, from scriptures such as 'There is no other knower than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23). Therefore, the experience of <s>saṃsāra</s> would follow for the supreme [Self] itself — if this is objected, [we say] no, because of the distinction. First, from the connection with the hearts of all living beings, the liability to experience does not follow for <s>Brahman</s>, as it does for the body — because of the distinction. For there is a distinction between the embodied self and the supreme Lord. One is the agent, the experiencer, possessed of the means of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and subject to pleasure, pain, and such. The other is of opposite character, qualified by freedom from evil and such. Because of this distinction between the two, one has experience, not the other. And if connection with an effect were accepted merely from proximity, without relying on the power of the thing, then even space and such would be liable to burning and such. This objection and its resolution are common to those who accept multiple all-pervading selves as well. As for the [objection] that because of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s>, due to the absence of another self, the embodied self's experience would entail <s>Brahman</s>'s experience — to this we say: First, the esteemed objector should be asked this: How have you determined this absence of another self? If [you say] from scriptures such as 'That you are,' 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,' 'There is no other knower than this' — then the meaning of scripture should be accepted as scripture [intends], and one cannot take only half of it, like [the logic of] the 'half-old-woman.' And the scripture that teaches 'That you are' — teaching <s>Brahman</s> qualified by freedom from evil and such as the Self of the embodied being — first of all denies the experiencer-status of the embodied being itself. How then could there be the liability of experience for <s>Brahman</s> through the experience of that [embodied being]? Or if the unity of the embodied self with <s>Brahman</s> has not been grasped, then the experience of the embodied self is caused by false knowledge, and <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is ultimate reality, is not touched by it. For when children imagine taints and such in space, space does not ultimately become possessed of taints and such. Therefore he says: 'No, because of the distinction.' Even granting oneness, the embodied self's experience does not entail <s>Brahman</s>'s experience — because of the distinction.

children.text:
FN: dharmādharmattvamupādhirityarthaḥ /
ayameva viśeṣo vaiśeṣyaṃ /
svārthe ṣyañ pratyayaḥ /
viśeṣasyātiśayārtho vā /
dharmādeḥ svāśraye phalahetutvamatiśayastasmāditi sutrārthaḥ /
vibhavo bahavaścātmana iti vādinām /
ardheti /
ardhaṃmukhamātraṃ jaratyā buddhāyāḥ kāmayate nāṅāgānīti so 'yamardhajaratīnyāyaḥ /
manomayatvādiviśiṣṭasyaiveśvarasya dhyānārthaṃ hārdatve 'pi nirdeṣatvāttasminneva śāṇḍilyavidyāvidye sarvaṃ ityādivākyaṃ samanvitamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The meaning is that <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are limiting adjuncts. This very distinction is what is meant by '<s>vaiśeṣya</s>.' The suffix '<s>ṣyañ</s>' is in the reflexive sense. Or '<s>viśeṣa</s>' means excellence. The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: because <s>dharma</s> and such are the causes of the fruits in their own substratum, therefore [there is] that excellence. 'Of many who are all-pervading selves' — refers to the proponents of [multiple selves]. '<s>Ardha</s>' — means only half, only the face of an old woman he desires, not the [other] limbs — this is the '<s>ardhajaratī</s>' (half-old-woman) maxim. Because the Lord qualified by being made of mind and such has been indicated as residing in the heart for the purpose of meditation, in that very <s>Śāṇḍilya-vidyā</s>, the sentence 'this is everything' and such is harmonized — this is the meaning.

children.text:
2 antradhikaraṇam /
9-10
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Attṛ Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Eater). <s>Sūtras</s> 9-10.

children.text: attā carācaragrahaṇāt | BBs_1,2.9 |
children.translated_text: <s>Attā carācaragrahaṇāt</s> — [<s>Brahman</s> is] the eater, because of the inclusion of the moving and the non-moving. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.9 |

children.text:
kaṭhavallīṣu paṭhyate- 'yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ cobhe bhavata odanaḥ /
mṛtyūryasyopasevanaṃ ka ityā veda yatra saḥ' (1.2.24) iti /
atra kaścidodanopasecanasūcito 'ttā pratīyate /
tatra kimagnirattā syāt, uta jīvaḥ, athavā paramātmeti saṃśayaḥ /
viśeṣānavadhāraṇāt /
trayāṇāṃ cāgnijīvaparamātmanāmasmingranthe praśnopanyāsopalabdheḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
agniratteti /
kutaḥ, 'agnirannādaḥ' (bṛ. 1.4.6) iti śrutiprasiddhibhyām /
jīvo vāttā syāt, 'tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvatti' iti darśanāt /
na paramātmā, 'anaśnannanyo 'abhicākaśīti' (muṇḍa. 3.1.1) iti darśanādityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- attātra paramātmā bhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ, carācaragrahaṇāt /
carācaraṃ hi sthāvarajaṅgamaṃ mṛtyupasecanamihādyātvena pratīyate, tādṛśasya cādyasya na paramātmano 'nyaḥ kārtsyenāttā saṃbhavati /
paramātmā tu vikārajātaṃ saṃharansarvamattītyupapadyate /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s> it is recited: 'He for whom both the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>Kṣatriya</s> [castes] are food, and death is the condiment — who indeed knows where He is?' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.24). Here a certain 'eater' is understood, indicated by the analogy of food and condiment. The doubt is: Is the eater fire, or the individual soul, or the supreme Self? Because there is no determination of the specific [referent]. And because questions about all three — fire, the individual soul, and the supreme Self — are found in this text. What then is the prima facie view? That it is fire. Why? Because of the well-known scriptural [usage]: 'Fire is the eater of food' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.6). Or the individual soul could be the eater, since it is stated: 'One of the two eats the sweet fruit' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1). Not the supreme Self, because it is stated: 'The other, not eating, merely looks on' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1). Given this position, we say: The eater here can only be the supreme Self. Why? Because of the inclusion of the moving and the non-moving. For the entire world of the moving and non-moving — the mobile and immobile — is understood here as food, with death as the condiment. And no eater of such food, in its entirety, is possible other than the supreme Self. But the supreme Self, consuming the entire class of modifications — drawing them back [into itself] — is tenable as the eater.

children.text: nanviha carācaragrahaṇaṃ nopalabhyate, kathaṃ siddhavaccarācaragrahaṇaṃ hetutvenopādīyate /
children.translated_text: But the inclusion of the moving and non-moving is not found here [in this passage] — so how can the inclusion of the moving and non-moving be adduced as a reason as if it were established?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
mṛtyupasecanatvena sarvasya prāṇinikāyasya pratīyamānatvāt, brahmakṣatrayośca prādhānyātpradarśanārthatvopapatteḥ /
yattu paramātmano 'pi nāttṛtvaṃ saṃbhavati, 'anaśnannanyo 'abhicākaśīti' iti darśanāditi /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because the entire host of living beings is understood through death being the condiment; and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Kṣatriya</s> [castes], being the foremost, are mentioned for the purpose of illustration. As for the [objection] that even the supreme Self cannot be the eater, because of the statement 'The other, not eating, merely looks on' —

children.text:
atrocyate- karmaphalabhogasyapratiṣedhakametaddarśanaṃ, tasya saṃnihitatvāt /
na vikārasaṃhārasya pratiṣedhakaṃ,
children.translated_text: To this it is said: That statement negates the enjoyment of the fruits of action, since that is what is contextually present. It does not negate the withdrawal of modifications,

children.text: sarvavedānteṣu sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārakāraṇatvena brahmaṇaḥ prasiddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: because in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts, <s>Brahman</s> is well-known as the cause of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution [of the world].

children.text: tasmātparamātmātmaivehāttā bhavitumarhati // 9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the supreme Self alone can be the eater here. // 9 //

children.text: FN: yasya paramātmano brahma kṣatraṃ cobhe jātī prasiddhānnavadodanau bhavataḥ, yasya mṛtyuḥ sarvamārakaḥ sannupasecanamodanamiśraghṛvattiṣṭhati, yatra so 'ttā kāraṇātmā vartate, taṃ nirviśeṣamātmānaṃ 'nāvirato duścaritāt' iti mantroktopāyavānyathā veda itthā itthamanyastadrahito na vedetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: Of which supreme Self, both the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Kṣatriya</s> — the well-known two castes — are food like rice, and of which death, the slayer of all, is the condiment mixed with the food [like ghee] — where that eater, the causal Self, exists — that attributeless Self one who possesses the means stated in the <s>mantra</s> 'Not one who has not ceased from evil conduct' knows in this way; another, devoid of that [means], does not know — this is the meaning.

children.text:
pradarśanamupalakṣaṇam /
naca brahkṣatre evātra vivakṣite, mṛtyūpasecanena prāṇabhṛnmātropasthāpanāt /
prāṇiṣu pradhānatvena ca brahmakṣatropanyāsasyopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Illustration' means an indication [by example]. And it is not that only the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Kṣatriya</s> are specifically intended here, since [the word] 'death as condiment' serves to evoke all living beings. And the mention of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and <s>Kṣatriya</s> is justified as being foremost among living beings.

children.text: prakaraṇāc ca | BBs_1,2.10 |
children.translated_text: <s>Prakaraṇāc ca</s> — And because of the context. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.10 |

children.text: itaśca paramātmaivehāttā bhavitumarhati, yatkāraṇaṃ prakaraṇamidaṃ paramatmanaḥ, 'na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit' (kāṭha. 1.2.18) ityādi prakṛtagrahaṇaṃ ca nyāyyam /
children.translated_text: For this further reason too, the supreme Self alone can be the eater here — because the context belongs to the supreme Self: 'He is not born, nor does he die — the wise one' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.18) and so forth; and the adoption of the subject under discussion is proper.

children.text: 'ka itthā veda yatra saḥ' iti ca durvijñānatvaṃ paramātmaliṅgam // 10 //
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed knows where He is?' — and the difficulty of knowing is an indicatory mark of the supreme Self. // 10 //

children.text: 3 guhāpraviṣṭādhikaraṇam / sū. 11-12
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Guhāpraviṣṭa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Two Who Have Entered the Cave). <s>Sūtras</s> 11-12.

children.text: guhāṃ praviṣṭāv ātmānau hi taddarśanāt | BBs_1,2.11 |
children.translated_text: <s>Guhāṃ praviṣṭāv ātmānau hi taddarśanāt</s> — The two selves that have entered the cave [are the supreme Self and the individual self], for that is what is seen [in scripture]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.11 |

children.text:
kaṭhavallīṣveva paṭhyate- 'ṛtaṃ pibantau loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe /
chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañṭagnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ' (kāṭha. 1.3.1) iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ, kimiha buddhijīvau nirdiṣṭāvuta jīvaparamātmānāviti /
yadi buddhijīvau, tato buddhipradhānātkāryakaraṇasaṃghātādvilakṣaṇo jīvaḥ pratipādito bhavati /
tadapīha pratipāditavyaṃ, 'yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye 'stītyeke nāyamastīti caike /
etadvidyāmanuśiṣṭastvayāhaṃ varāṇāmeṣa varastṛtīyaḥ' (kāṭha. 1.1.20) iti pṛṣṭatvāt /
atha jīvaparamātmānau tato jīvādvilakṣaṇaḥ paramātmā pratipādito bhavati /
tadapīha pratipādayitavyaṃ, 'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmadanyatrāsmātkṛtākṛtāt /
anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca yattatpaśyasi tadvada' (kāṭha. 1.2.14) iti pṛṣṭatvāt /
atrāhākṣeptā- ubhāpyetau pakṣau na saṃbhavataḥ /
kasmāt, ṛtapānaṃ karmaphalopabhogaḥ, sukṛtasya loke, iti ca dvivacanena dvayoḥ pānaṃ darśayati śrutiḥ /
ato buddhikṣetrajñapakṣastāvanna saṃbhavati /
ata eva kṣetrajñaparamātmapakṣo 'pi na saṃbhavati, cetane 'pi paramātmani ṛtapānāsaṃbhavāt /
'anaś nannanyo 'abhicākaśīti' iti mantravarṇāditi /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> itself it is read: 'The two who drink <s>ṛta</s> (truth/cosmic order), having entered the cave, in the supreme, in the highest place — those who know <s>Brahman</s> call them shadow and light, as do those who maintain the five fires and the three <s>Nāciketa</s> fires' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.1). Therein arises a doubt: are the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) indicated here, or the individual soul and the Supreme Self? If the intellect and the individual soul, then the individual soul is demonstrated as different from the intellect — the <s>Pradhāna</s>, the aggregate of body and organs. That too should be demonstrated here, because the question was asked: 'This doubt that arises regarding a person who has died — "he exists," say some; "he does not exist," say others — I wish to know this, instructed by you. This is the third of the boons' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.1.20). If, on the other hand, the individual soul and the Supreme Self [are meant], then the Supreme Self is demonstrated as different from the individual soul. That too should be demonstrated here, because the question was asked: 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>, other than this done and undone, other than what has been and what will be — that which you see, tell me' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.14). Here, the objector says: both these alternatives are impossible. Why? Because '<s>ṛta</s>-drinking' means the enjoyment of the fruits of action, and the <s>śruti</s>, with the dual number 'in the world of merit,' shows the drinking of both. Therefore, the alternative of intellect and individual soul is first impossible [since the intellect does not drink]. For this very reason, the alternative of individual soul and Supreme Self is also impossible, because the drinking of <s>ṛta</s> is impossible for the conscious Supreme Self — as stated in the <s>mantra</s>: 'The other, not eating, looks on.'

children.text:
atrocyate- naiṣa doṣaḥ /
chatriṇo gacchantītyekenāpi chatriṇā bahūnāṃ chatritvopacāradarśanāt /
evamekenāpi pibatā dvau pibantāvucyete /
yadvā jīvastāvatpibati, īśvarastu pāyayati /
pāyayannapi pibatītyucyate /
pācayitaryapi praktṛtvaprasiddhidarśanāt /
buddhikṣetrajñaparigraho 'pi saṃbhavati, karaṇe kartṛtvopacārāt /
edhāṃsi pacantīti prayogadarśanāt /
nacādhyatmādhikāre 'nyau kaucidhāvṛtaṃ pibantau saṃbhavataḥ /
tasmādbuddhijīvau syātāṃ, jīvaparamātmānau veti saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ. buddhikṣetrajñāviti /
kutaḥ, 'guhāṃ praviṣṭau' iti viśeṣaṇāt /
yadi śarīraṃ guhā, yadi vā hṛdayaṃ, ubhayathāpi buddhikṣetrajñau guhāṃ praviṣṭāvupapadyete /
naca sati saṃbhavesarvagatasya brahmaṇo viśiṣṭadeśatvaṃ yuktaṃ kalpayitum /
'sukṛtasya loke' iti ca karmagocarānatikramaṃ darśayati /
paramātmā tu na sukṛtasya vā duṣkṛtasya vā gocare vartate, 'na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān' iti śruteḥ /
'chāyātapau' iti ca tetanācetanayornirdeśa upapadyate /
chāyātapavatparasparavilakṣaṇatvāt /
tasmādbuddhikṣetrajñāvihocyeyātāmityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- vijñānātmaparamātmānāvihocyeyātām /
kasmāt, ātmānau hi tāvubhāvapi cetanau samānasvabhāvau /
saṃkhyāśravaṇe ca samānasvabhāveṣveva loke pratītirdṛśyate /
asya gordvitīyo 'nveṣṭavya ityukte gaureva dvitīyo 'nviṣyate, nāśvaḥ puruṣo vā /
tadiha ṛtapānena liṅgena niścite vijñānātmani dvitīyānveṣaṇāyāṃ samānasvabhāvaścetanaḥ paramātmaiva pratīyate /
children.translated_text: To this we say: this is not a defect. Just as in the expression 'those with umbrellas are going,' even when only one has an umbrella, the quality of having an umbrella is figuratively extended to many — similarly, even when only one drinks, the two are said to be drinking. Or, the individual soul drinks, while the Lord causes [it] to drink. And one who causes drinking is also said to be drinking — just as it is well known that even one who causes cooking is spoken of as the agent of cooking. The alternative of intellect and individual soul is also possible, through the figurative attribution of agency to the instrument — because the usage 'the firewood cooks' is observed. And in this context of the individual self, no other two besides the intellect and the individual soul, or the individual soul and the Supreme Self, can be the drinkers of <s>ṛta</s>. Therefore, the doubt is: are they the intellect and the individual soul, or the individual soul and the Supreme Self? What is the initial position? They are the intellect and the individual soul. Why? Because of the qualifier 'having entered the cave.' Whether the cave is the body or the heart, in either case the intellect and the individual soul are fittingly said to have 'entered the cave.' But it is not proper to imagine a specific location for all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> when there is a possibility [of another interpretation]. 'In the world of merit' also shows non-transcendence of the domain of <s>karma</s>. But the Supreme Self does not operate in the domain of merit or demerit — as stated in the <s>śruti</s>: 'It is neither increased by action nor diminished.' 'Shadow and light' too — this indication is fitting for a conscious and an unconscious being, because they are mutually different like shadow and sunlight. Therefore, the intellect and the individual soul would be referred to here — this being the position reached, we say: the individual cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) and the Supreme Self are referred to here. Why? Because both of them are conscious, of the same essential nature. And in the counting by dual number, the common understanding in the world is directed toward things of the same essential nature. When told 'a second one for this cow is to be sought,' a cow alone is sought as the second, not a horse or a person. Similarly here, when the cognizing self is ascertained through the mark of <s>ṛta</s>-drinking, in seeking the second [entity], it is the Supreme Self — being of the same conscious nature — that is understood.

children.text: nanūktaṃ guhāhitatvadarśanānna paramātmā pratyetavya iti /
children.translated_text: But was it not said that the Supreme Self should not be understood because of the observation of dwelling in the cave?

children.text:
guhāhitatvadarśanādeva paramātmāpratyetavya iti vadāmaḥ /
guhāhitatvaṃ tu śrutismṛtiṣvasakṛtparamātmana eva dṛśyate- 'guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam' (kāṭha. 1.2.12) 'yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman' (tai. 2.1) 'ātmānamanviccha guhāṃ praviṣṭam' ityādyāsu /
sarvagatasyāpi brahmaṇa upalabdhyartho deśaviśeṣopadeśo na virudhyata ityedapyuktameva /
sukṛtalokavartitvaṃ tu chatritvavadekasminnapi vartamānamubhayoraviruddham /
chāyātapāvityapyaviruddham /
chāyātapavatparasparavilakṣaṇatvātsaṃsāritvāsaṃsāritvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: because of mutual difference — like shadow and sunlight — between the states of being a transmigrator and not being a transmigrator.

children.text: avidyākṛtatvātsaṃsāritvasya /
children.translated_text: Because the state of being a transmigrator is created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),

children.text: pāramārthikatvāccāsaṃsāritvasya /
children.translated_text: and because the state of not being a transmigrator is ultimate reality.

children.text: tasmādvijñānātmaparamātamānau guhāṃ praviṣṭau gṛhyete // 11//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) and the Supreme Self are understood as having entered the cave. // 11 //

We say: precisely because of the observation of dwelling in the cave, the Supreme Self should be understood. For the dwelling of the Supreme Self in the cave is seen repeatedly in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>: 'Placed in the cave, dwelling in the deep' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.12); 'One who knows [it] as placed in the cave, in the supreme space' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1); 'Seek the Self that has entered the cave' — and in such passages. And it has already been stated that teaching a specific location for all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> for the purpose of realization is not contradictory. And being situated in the world of merit — like the quality of having an umbrella — being present in even one of the two, is not contradictory for both. 'Shadow and light' too is not contradictory —

children.text: kutaśca vijñānātmaparamātmānau gṛhyete-
children.translated_text: And for what further reason are the cognizing self and the Supreme Self understood?

children.text:
FN: ṛtaṃ satyaṃ karmaphalaṃ pibantau, bhuñjānau sukṛtasya loke samyagarjitasyādṛṣṭasya kārye dehe vartamāno parasya brahmaṇor'dhaṃ sthānamarhatīti parārdhaṃ hṛdayaṃ tasminparame śreṣṭhe yā guhā nabhokṣaṇā tāṃ praviśya sathitau chāyātapavanmitho viruddhau, tau ca brahmavidaḥ karmiṇaśca vadanti /
trirnāciketo 'gniścito yaiste 'pi vadanti /
manuṣye prete mṛtesati yeyaṃ vicikitsā saṃśayaḥ /
paralokabhoktāstītyeke nāstīti cānye /
tvayopadiṣṭo 'hametattatvaṃ jñātumicchāmītyarthaḥ /
anyatra dharmādharmābhyāmanyatra, asmātkṛtākṛtāt dharmādharmāspṛṣṭaṃ, kṛtākṛtāt kāryakāraṇādbhinnaṃ yat tadbrahma /
yadveti /
svātantryalakṣaṇaṃ hi kartṛtvaṃ tacca pāturiva pāyayiturapyastīti so 'pi kartā /
ataevāhuryaḥ kārayati so 'pi karteti /
guhāhitaṃ buddhau sthitaṃ gahvare 'nekānarthasaṃkule dehe sthitaṃ, purāṇamādipuruṣam /
parame vyoman śreṣṭhe hārdākāśe tatra guhāyāṃ buddau /
anviccha vicāraya /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Ṛta</s>' means truth, i.e., the fruit of action. 'Drinking' means enjoying. 'In the world of merit' — in the body, which is the effect of well-performed, i.e., unseen [merit]. '<s>Parārdha</s>' — the heart, which merits the supreme abode of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. 'Having entered that cave' — the space of the heart, which is supreme and excellent — and there abiding. 'Shadow and light' — mutually opposed. Those who know <s>Brahman</s> and those ritual practitioners speak of them. 'Having maintained the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire thrice' — they too speak of them. 'Regarding a person who has died' — when a person has died, 'this doubt exists.' 'He exists,' say some; 'he does not exist,' say others. 'Instructed by you, I wish to know this truth' — this is the meaning. 'Other than <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>' — different from [<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>]; 'from the done and undone' — different from the body and cause; that which is <s>Brahman</s> — 'whatever you see, tell me.' The word '<s>vā</s>' [functions like]: by his own will, the one who causes others to cook, he too is a cooker. Similarly, those who say 'whoever causes action is also an agent.' In the cave — situated in the intellect; in the deep — in the body that is beset with many calamities; the ancient — the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>. 'In the supreme space' — in the space of the heart, that is the most excellent. 'In that cave' — in the intellect. 'Seek' — investigate.

children.text: viśeṣaṇāc ca | BBs_1,2.12 |
children.translated_text: Because of the characterization. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.12 |

children.text:
viśeṣaṇaṃ ca vijñānātmaparamātmanoreva bhavati /
'ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ rathameva tu' (kā. 1.3.3) ityādinā pareṇa granthena rathirathādirūpakakalpanayā vijñānātnāṃ rathinaṃ saṃsāramokṣayorgantāraṃ kalpayati /
'so 'dhvanaḥ pāramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam' /
(kā. 1.3.9) iti ca paramātmānaṃ gantavyam /
tathā 'taṃ durdarśa gūḍhamanupraviṣṭhaṃ purāṇam /
adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti' (kā. 1.2.12) iti pūrvasminnapi granthe mantṛmantavyatvenaitāveva viśeṣitau /
prakaraṇaṃ ceda paramātmanaḥ /
brahmavido vadanti iti ca vaktṛviśeṣopādanaṃ paramātmaparigrahe ghaṭate /
tasmādiha jīvaparamātmānāvucyeyātām /
eṣa eva nyāyaḥ 'dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā' (muṇḍa. 3.1.1) ityevamādiṣvapi /
tatrāpi hyadhyātmādhikārānna prākṛtau suparṇāvucyete /
tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svāditti ityadanaliṅgādvijñānātmā bhavati /
anaś nannanyo 'bhicākaśīti ityanaśanacetanābhyāṃ paramātmā /
children.translated_text: The characterization pertains to the cognizing self and the Supreme Self alone. By the subsequent passage, beginning with 'Know the Self as the rider, and the body as the chariot' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.3) — through the metaphorical construction of rider, chariot, and so forth — the cognizing self is represented as the rider, the one who goes toward both <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation. And 'He reaches the end of the road — that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.9) — the Supreme Self is [presented as] the goal. Similarly, 'That which is hard to see, which has entered the hidden, which is seated in the deep, the ancient — having understood the God through meditation on the inner Self, the wise one abandons joy and sorrow' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.12) — in the previous passage too, these very two are characterized as the meditator and the object of meditation. And the context here is about the Supreme Self. And the specification of speakers as 'those who know <s>Brahman</s>' is fitting when the Supreme Self is accepted [as the referent]. Therefore, the individual soul and the Supreme Self are referred to here. The same reasoning [applies] in passages like 'Two birds, companions joined together' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1) and so forth. For there too, since the context concerns the individual self, the ordinary birds are not referred to. 'One of them eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> berry' — through the mark of eating, the cognizing self is [identified]. 'The other, not eating, looks on' — through the marks of not eating and consciousness, the Supreme Self [is identified].

children.text:
anantare ca mantre tāveva draṣṭṛdraṣṭavyabhāvena viśinaṣṭi- 'samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno 'nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ /
juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśamasya mahimānamiti vītaśokaḥ' (muṇḍa. 3.1.2) iti /
apara āha- 'dvā suparṇā' iti neyamṛgasyādhikaraṇasya siddhāntaṃ bhajate, paiṅgirahasyabrāhmaṇenānyathā vyākhyātatvāt /
'tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādittīti sattvamanaś nannanyo 'bhicākaśītītyanaś nannanyo 'bhipaśyati jñastāvetau sattvakṣetrajñau' iti /
sattvaśabdotītyanaś nannanyo 'bhipaśyati yaducyate, tanna, sattvakṣetrajñaśabdayorantaḥkaraṇaśarīraparatayā prasiddhatvāt /
tatraiva ca vyākhyātatvāt- 'tadetatsattvaṃ yena svapnaṃ paśyati, atha yo 'yaṃ śārīra upadraṣṭā sa kṣetrajñastāvetau sattvakṣetrajñau' iti /
nāpyasyādhikaraṇasya pūrvapakṣaṃ bhajate /
nahyatra śārīraḥ kṣetrajñaḥ kartṛtvabhoktṛtvādinā saṃsāradharmeṇopeto vivakṣyate /
kathaṃ tarhi sarvasaṃsāradharmātīto brahmabhāvaścaitanyamātrasvarūpaḥ 'anaś nannanyo 'bhicākaśīti', 'anaś nannanyo 'bhicākaśīti jñaḥ' iti vacanāt /
'tattvamasi' 'kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi' (gī. 13.2) ityādiśrutismṛtibhyaśca /
tāvatā ca vidyopasaṃhāradarśanamelamevāvakalpate, tāvetau sattvakṣetrajñau na ha vā evaṃvidi kiñcana raca ādhvaṃsate ityādi /
kathaṃ punarasminpakṣe tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādittīti sattvam ityacetane sattve bhoktṛtvāvacanamti /
ucyate- neyaṃ śrutiracetanasya sattvasya bhoktṛtvaṃ vakṣyāmīti pravṛttā /
kiṃ tarhi cetanasya kṣetrajñasyābhoktṛtvaṃ brahmasbhāvatāṃ ca vakṣyāmīti /
tadarthaṃ sukhādivikriyāvati sattve bhoktṛtvamadhyāropayati /
idaṃ hi kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ ta sattvakṣetrajñayoritaretisvabhāvāvivekakṛtaṃ kalpyate /
paramārthatastu nānyatarasyāpi saṃbhavati, acetanatvātsattvasya, avikriyatvācca kṣetrajñasya /
children.translated_text: In ultimate reality, however, it is possible for neither. Not for <s>sattva</s>, because it is non-conscious; and not for the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, because it is free from modification.

children.text: avidyāpratyupasthāpitasvabhāvatvācca sattvasya sutarāṃ na saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: And because <s>sattva</s> has a nature produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [agency and enjoyership] are all the more impossible for it.

children.text: tathāca śrutiḥ- 'yatra vā anyadiva syāttatrānyo 'nyatpaśyet' ityādinā svapnadṛṣṭahastyādivyavahāravadavidyāviṣaya eva kartṛtvādivyavahāraṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Where there is, as it were, another' — and so forth — shows that the transactional dealings of agency and such are only within the domain of <s>avidyā</s>, like the dealings with elephants and such seen in a dream.

children.text: 'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛ. 4.5.15) ityādinā ca vivekinaḥ kartṛtvādivyavaharābhāvam darśayati // 12 //
children.translated_text: 'But where everything has become one's Self alone — then by what and whom would one see?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15) — and such [passages] show the absence of the transactional dealings of agency and such for one who possesses discrimination. // 12 //

And in the immediately following <s>mantra</s>, those very two are characterized as the seer and the seen: 'On the same tree, a person, immersed, grieves, deluded by helplessness. But when he sees the other — the Lord, the beloved — and His greatness, he becomes free from sorrow' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.2). Another [commentator] says: 'Two birds' — this verse does not belong to the established conclusion of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic), because it has been otherwise interpreted in the <s>Paiṅgi Rahasya Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'One of them eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> berry — this refers to <s>sattva</s> (the intellect). The other, not eating, looks on — the other, not eating, perceives: he is the knower. These two are <s>sattva</s> (intellect) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field).' If someone argues that the word '<s>sattva</s>' [here refers to something non-conscious, and therefore the two are the intellect and the field-knower] — that is wrong. Because the words '<s>sattva</s>' and '<s>kṣetrajña</s>' are well known as referring to the inner organ and the body [respectively]. And the explanation is given right there: 'That is the <s>sattva</s> (intellect) by which one sees dreams; and this one who is embodied, the witness — he is the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. These two are <s>sattva</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>.' Nor does [this verse] belong to the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (preliminary objection) of this <s>adhikaraṇa</s>. For here the embodied <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) is not intended as being qualified by the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> such as agency and enjoyership. How then? As having transcended all properties of <s>saṃsāra</s>, as being of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, as pure consciousness — [this is shown by] the statement 'the other, not eating, looks on — the knower.' And from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> such as 'You are That' and 'Know the <s>kṣetrajña</s> to be Me as well' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.2). And with just this much, the concluding connection with <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is perfectly consistent: 'These two are <s>sattva</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>; no sin whatsoever clings to one who knows thus' — and so forth. But how, on this view, is the eating-mark applied to the non-conscious <s>sattva</s> (intellect) in 'one of them eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> berry — that is <s>sattva</s>'? We say: this <s>śruti</s> did not set out to declare the enjoyership of the non-conscious <s>sattva</s>. Rather, it sets out to declare the non-enjoyership and <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the conscious <s>kṣetrajña</s>. For this purpose, it superimposes enjoyership upon the <s>sattva</s>, which is subject to modifications such as pleasure and so forth. For this agency and enjoyership is imagined as belonging to one or the other of <s>sattva</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, due to the failure to discriminate between the nature of one and the other.

children.text:
FN: sa iti jīvaḥ sarvanāmārthaḥ /
adhvanaḥ saṃsāramārgasya /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Sa</s>' — a pronoun meaning the <s>jīva</s>. '<s>Adhvanaḥ</s>' — of the road, i.e., of the path of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: durdarśe durjñānaṃ, tata eva gūḍhamanupraviṣṭaṃ gahanatāṃ gatamīśvaram adhyātmaprayogaḥ pratyagātmanyeva cittasamādhānaṃ tenādhigamo mahāvākyajā vṛttistayā viditvetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Hard to see' — hard to know; therefore 'hidden' — having entered into the imperceptible, the God who is the Lord. '<s>Adhyātmayoga</s>' (meditation on the inner Self) — the concentration of the mind upon the inner Self itself; through attainment by that — the <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification) born from the great statements — having known [thus], this is the meaning.

children.text: sahaiva yujyete niyamyaniyāmakatveneti sayujau /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sayuja</s>' (joined together) — they are yoked together as the controller and the controlled.

children.text:
anīśayā svasyeśvaratvāpratītyā /
juṣṭaṃ dhyānādinā sevitaṃ yadā dhyānaparipākadaśāyāmīśamanyaṃ viśiṣṭarūpādbhinnaṃ pasyati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anīśayā</s>' (by helplessness) — by the non-realization of one's own lordship. '<s>Juṣṭam</s>' — served through meditation and such; 'when he sees the other' — the Lord, different from [the self in] its distinguished form, he perceives [Him].

children.text: sattvaṃ buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s>' means the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>).

children.text: tāvatā mantravyākhyāmātreṇa /
children.translated_text: 'With just that much' — with the mere explanation of the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: rajaḥ avidyā, ādhvaṃsate, saṃśliṣati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Rajas</s>' means <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). '<s>Ādhvaṃsate</s>' means 'clings to.'

children.text:
anyadivābhāsabhūtaṃ nānātvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ syāttatra avidyakabuddhyādisaṃbandhādanyo bhūtvānyacakṣuṣā paśyet /
tatrāvidyāyām /
children.translated_text: 'Where there is, as it were, another' — where the manifoldness that is [merely] apparent is seen, there — due to the connection with <s>avidyā</s>-conditioned intellect and such — becoming another, one sees another with the eye [of duality]. 'Therein' — in the domain of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: yatra tu vidyāvasthāyām /
children.translated_text: 'But where' — in the state of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).

children.text: 4 antaradhikaraṇam / sū. 13-17
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Antara Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Inner [Self]) / <s>Sūtras</s> 13-17

children.text: antara upapatteḥ | BBs_1,2.13 |
children.translated_text: <s>Antara</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of reasonableness. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.13 |

children.text:
'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmeti hovācaitadamṛtamabhayametadbrahmeti /
etadyapyasminsarpirvodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmani eva gacchati' (chā. 4.15.1) ityādi śra8yate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ kimayaṃ pratibimbātmakṣyadhikaraṇo nirdiśyate 'thavā vijñānātmā uta devatātmendriyasyādhiṣṭhātāthaveśvara iti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam, chāyātmā puruṣapratirūpā iti /
kutaḥ, tasya dṛśyamānatvaprasiddheḥ /
'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' iti ca prasiddavadupadeśāt /
vijñānātmano vāyaṃ nirdeśa iti yuktam /
sa hi cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ paśyaṃścakṣuṣi saṃnihito bhavati /
ātmaśabdaścāsminpakṣe 'nukūlo bhavati /
ādityapuruṣo vā cakṣuṣo 'nugrāhakaḥ pratīyate, 'raśmibhireṣo 'sminpratiṣṭhitaḥ' (bṛ. 5.5.2) iti śruteḥ /
amṛtatvādīnāṃ ca devatātnyapi kathañcitsaṃbhavāt /
neśvaraḥ, sthānaviśeṣanirdeśādityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ /
parameśvara evākṣiṇyabhyantaraḥ puruṣa ihopadiṣṭa iti /
kasmāt, upapatteḥ /
upapadyate hi parameśvare guṇajātamihopadiśyamānam /
ātmatvaṃ tāvanmukhyayā vṛttyā parameśvara upapadyate /
'sa ātmā tattvamasi' iti śruteḥ /
amṛtatvābhayatve ca tasminnasakṛcchrutau śrūyete /
tathā parameśvarānurūpametadakṣisthānam /
yathāhi parameśvaraḥ sarvadoṣairaliptaḥ, apahatapāpmatvādiśravaṇāt /
tathākṣisthānaṃ sarvaleparahimupadiṣṭaṃ, 'tadyadyapyasminsarpirvodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmani eva gacchati' iti śruteḥ /
saṃyadvāmatvādiguṇopadeśaśca tasminnavakalpate /
'etaṃ saṃyaddhāma ityācakṣate etaṃ hi sarvāṇi vāmānyabhisaṃyanti' /
children.translated_text: 'They call Him <s>Saṃyaddha</s> (the one in whom all meet), for all desirable things (<s>vāma</s>) converge upon Him.'

children.text: 'eṣa u eva vāmanīreṣa hi sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati' /
children.translated_text: 'He is indeed <s>Vāmanī</s> (the giver of desirable things), for He leads [beings] to all desirable things.'

children.text: ' eṣa u eva bhāmānīreṣa hi sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti' (chā. 4.15.2,3,4) iti ca /
children.translated_text: 'He is indeed <s>Bhāmanī</s> (the radiant one), for He shines in all worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.2,3,4).

children.text: ata upapatterantaraḥ parameśvaraḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of fitness, the inner one is the Supreme Lord. // 13 //

It is heard: 'The person that is seen in the eye — this is the Self, he said; this is the immortal, the fearless; this is <s>Brahman</s>. Even if one pours ghee or water on this [eye], it goes only to the edges [of the eyelids]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.1) — and so forth. Therein arises a doubt: is the one referred to here the reflection-self that resides in the eye, or the cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), or the deity-self that presides over the sense organ, or the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>)? What is the initial position? It is the shadow-self, the image of the person. Why? Because it is well known as being seen. And because the instruction 'the person that is seen in the eye' is given as though about something well known. Or the reference may reasonably be to the cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), for when it sees form through the eye, it is present in the eye. And the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) is favorable on this view. Or the solar person may be understood as the benefactor of the eye, from the <s>śruti</s>: 'He is established in this [eye] through his rays' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.2). And because immortality and such qualities are somehow possible even for a deity. Not the Lord, because of the specification of a particular location — having reached this position, we say: It is the Supreme Lord alone who is taught here as the person within the eye. Why? Because of fitness (<s>upapatti</s>). For the class of qualities taught here is fitting for the Supreme Lord. Selfhood, first of all, is fitting for the Supreme Lord in its primary sense, from the <s>śruti</s>: 'That is the Self; You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7). And immortality and fearlessness are repeatedly heard in reference to Him in the <s>śruti</s>. Similarly, this location in the eye is befitting the Supreme Lord. For just as the Supreme Lord is untainted by all defects — from the <s>śruti</s> that He is 'free from evil' and such — so too the location in the eye is taught as free from all contact: 'Even if one pours ghee or water on this [eye], it goes only to the edges' — from this <s>śruti</s>. And the teaching of qualities such as being <s>Saṃyadvāma</s> and such is fitting for Him [alone].

children.text: FN: vartmani pakṣmasthāne /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Vartmani</s>' means 'at the place of the eyelashes.'

children.text: prasiddhavadupadeśaścakṣuṣatvoktireva /
children.translated_text: The instruction 'as though about something well known' is simply the statement about being in the eye.

children.text: ihetyakṣipuruṣoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Here' refers to the statement about the person in the eye.

children.text:
saṃyaddhāmeti /
vāmāni karmaphalānyetamakṣipuruṣaṃ hetumāśritya abhisaṃyantyutpadyante /
vāmanīrvāmāni śobhanāni lokaṃ prāpayati /
bhāmanīrbhāmāni bhānāni sarvatra nayatīti /
children.translated_text: '<s>Saṃyaddha</s>' — the fruits of actions (<s>vāmāni</s>, desirable things) converge upon (<s>abhisaṃyanti</s>), i.e., arise from, this person in the eye as their cause. '<s>Vāmanī</s>' — He leads [beings] to desirable (<s>vāmāni</s>), auspicious worlds. '<s>Bhāmanī</s>' — He brings radiances (<s>bhāmāni</s>, splendors) everywhere.

children.text: sthānādivyapadeśāc ca | BBs_1,2.14 |
children.translated_text: And because of the designation of location and such. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.14 |

children.text: kathaṃ punarākaśavatsarvagatasya brahmaṇo 'kṣyalpasthānamupapadyata iti /
children.translated_text: But how can the small location of the eye be fitting for <s>Brahman</s>, which is all-pervading like space?

children.text:
atrocyate- bhavedeṣānavakḷptiḥ, yadyetadevaikaṃ sthānamasya nirdiṣṭaṃ bhavet /
santi hyanyānyapi pṛthivyādīni sthānānyasya nirdiṣṭāni- 'yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan' (bṛ. 3.7.3) ityādinā /
teṣu hi cakṣurapi nirdiṣṭam- 'yaścakṣuṣi tiṣṭhan' iti /
children.translated_text: Among those, the eye too is specified: 'He who stands within the eye.'

children.text: 'sthānādivyapadeśāt' ityādigrahaṇenaitaddarśayati- na kevalaṃ sthānamevaikamanucitaṃ brahmaṇo nirdiśyamānaṃ dṛśyate, kiṃ tarhi nāmarūpamityevañjātīyakamapyanāmarūpasya brahmaṇo 'nucitaṃ nirdiśyamānaṃ dṛśyate- 'tasyoditi nāma' 'hiraṇyaśmaśruḥ' (chā. 1.6.7,6) ityādi /
children.translated_text: By the word 'and such' (<s>ādi</s>) in 'because of the designation of location and such,' this is indicated: not only is one unfitting location seen to be designated for <s>Brahman</s>, but rather, what is unfitting for <s>Brahman</s> — which is devoid of name and form — such as name and form, is also seen designated: 'His name is <s>Ud</s> (the Risen)'; 'He has a golden beard' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.7,6) — and so forth.
