children.text: nirguṇamapi sadbrahma nāmarūpagatairguṇaiḥ saguṇamupāsanārthaṃ tatra tatropadiśyata ityetadapyuktameva /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s>, though devoid of qualities, is taught here and there as qualified by the qualities pertaining to name and form, for the purpose of meditation — this too has already been stated.

children.text: sarvagatasyāpi brahmaṇa upalabdhyarthaṃ sthānaviśeṣo na virudhyate, śālagrāma iva viṣṇorityetadapyuktameva // 14 //
children.translated_text: For all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, the specification of a particular location for the purpose of apprehension is not contradictory — just as the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone for <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this too has already been stated. // 14 //

To this we say: this objection would hold if this were the only location specified for it. But there are other locations too — earth and such — specified for it, as in 'He who stands within the earth' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.3) and so forth.

children.text: FN: sthānādanyādayo yeṣāṃ te sthānādayo nāmarūpaprakārāsteṣāṃ vyapadeśātsarvaṅgatasyaikasthānaniyamo nāvakalpate /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Location and such' — those whose 'and such' (<s>ādi</s>) are things other than location — these are the modes of name and form; because of their designation, the restriction to one location for the all-pervading [<s>Brahman</s>] is not justified.

children.text: sukhaviśiṣṭābhidhānād eva ca | BBs_1,2.15 |
children.translated_text: And because of the specific designation of being connected with happiness. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.15 |

children.text:
apica naivātra vivaditavyaṃ, kiṃ brahmāsminvākye 'bhidhīyate na veti /
sukhaviśiṣṭābhidhānameva brahmatvaṃ siddham /
sukhaviśiṣṭaṃ hi brahma yadvākyopakrame prakrāntaṃ 'prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' iti tadevehābhihitaṃ, prakṛtaparigrahasya nyāyyatvāt /
'ācāryastu te gatiṃ vaktā' (chā. 4 14.1) iti ca gatimātrābhidhānapratijñānāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there should be no dispute here as to whether <s>Brahman</s> is referred to in this passage or not. Its being <s>Brahman</s> is established by the very designation of connection with happiness (<s>sukha</s>). For the <s>Brahman</s> designated as connected with happiness that was introduced at the beginning of the passage — '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Ka</s> (happiness) is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> (space) is <s>Brahman</s>' — that very [<s>Brahman</s>] is referred to here, because it is proper to maintain the subject. And because of the promise to state only the path [to <s>Brahman</s>]: 'But the teacher will tell you the way' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.14.1).

children.text: kathaṃ punarvākyopakrame sukhaviśiṣṭaṃ brahma vijñāyata iti /
children.translated_text: But how is <s>Brahman</s> designated as connected with happiness known at the beginning of the passage?

children.text:
ucyate- 'prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' ityetadagnīnāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvopakosala uvāca- 'vijānāmyahaṃ yatprāṇo brahma kaṃ ca tu khaṃ ca na vijānāmi' iti /
tatredaṃ prativacanam- 'yadvāva kaṃ tadeva khaṃ yadeva khaṃ tadeva kaṃ' (chā. 4.10.5)
iti /
tatra khaṃśabdo bhūtākāśe nirūḍho loke /
yadi tasya viśeṣaṇatvena kaṃśabdaḥ sukhavācī nopādīyeta /
tathā sati kevale bhūtākāśe brahmaśabdo nāmādiṣviva pratīkābhiprāyeṇa prayukta iti pratītiḥ syāt /
tathā kaṃśabdasya viṣayendriyasaṃparkajanite sāmaye sukhe prasiddhatvāt, yadi tasya khaṃśabdo viśeṣaṇatvena nopādīyeta, laukikaṃ sukhaṃ brahmeti pratītiḥ syāt /
itaretaraviśeṣatau tu kaṅkhaṃśabdau sukhātmakaṃ brahma gamayataḥ /
tatra dvitīye brahmaśabde 'nupādīyamāne kaṃ khaṃ brahmetyevocyamāne kaṃśabdasya viśeṣaṇatvenaivopayuktatvātasukhasya guṇasyādhyeyatvaṃ syāt, tanmā bhūdityubhayoḥ kaṅkhaṃśabdayorbrahmaśabdaśirastvaṃ 'kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' iti /
iṣṭaṃ hi sukhasyāpi guṇasya guṇavaddhyeyatvam /
tadevaṃ vākyopakrame sukhaviśiṣṭaṃ brahmopadiṣṭam /
pratyekaṃ ca gārhapatyādayo 'gnayaḥ svaṃ svaṃ mahimānamupadiśya 'eṣā somya te 'smadvidyātmavidyā ca' ityupasaṃharantaḥ pūrvatra brahma nirdiṣṭamiti jñāpayanti /
children.translated_text: And the fires — <s>Gārhapatya</s> and the others — each having taught their own glory, conclude with 'This, my dear, is our knowledge, namely, the knowledge of the Self' — thereby indicating that <s>Brahman</s> was taught in the preceding [portion].

children.text: 'ācāryastu te gatiṃ vaktā' iti ca gatimātrābhidhānapratijñānamarthāntaravivakṣāṃ vārayati /
children.translated_text: And the promise to state only the path — 'But the teacher will tell you the way' — precludes any intention to speak of a different subject.

children.text: 'yathā puṣkarapalāśā āpo na śliṣyanta evamevaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate' (chā. 4.14.3) iti cākṣisthānaṃ puruṣaṃ vijānataḥ pāpenānupaghātaṃ bruvannakṣisthānasya puruṣasya brahmatvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And in stating that evil action does not cling to one who knows the person situated in the eye — 'Just as [water] does not cling to lotus leaves, so evil action does not cling to one who knows thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.14.3) — this shows the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the person situated in the eye.

children.text: tasmātprakṛtasyaiva brahmaṇo 'kṣisthānatāṃ saṃyadvāmatvādiguṇatāṃ coktvārcirādikāṃ tadvido gatiṃ vakṣyāmītyupakramate- 'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca' (chā. 4.15.1) iti // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having stated that the already-introduced <s>Brahman</s> is situated in the eye and has the qualities of being <s>Saṃyadvāma</s> and such, [the teacher] begins to state the path for the knower of that: 'The person that is seen in the eye — this is the Self, he said' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.1). // 15 //

It is said: having heard the statement of the fires — '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — <s>Upakosala</s> said: 'I understand that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, but I do not understand <s>Ka</s> and <s>Kha</s>.' To this the reply was: 'What indeed is <s>Ka</s>, that is <s>Kha</s>; what is <s>Kha</s>, that is <s>Ka</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10.5). Therein, the word '<s>Kha</s>' is established in common usage as referring to physical space (<s>bhūtākāśa</s>). If the word '<s>Ka</s>', meaning happiness, were not employed as its qualifier, then the word '<s>Brahman</s>' applied to mere physical space would be understood as used in the sense of a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>), as with names and such. Similarly, since the word '<s>Ka</s>' is well known as referring to ordinary happiness born of the contact of senses and objects — if the word '<s>Kha</s>' were not employed as its qualifier, one would understand that worldly happiness is <s>Brahman</s>. But when the two words '<s>Ka</s>' and '<s>Kha</s>' qualify each other, they convey <s>Brahman</s> whose nature is happiness. Therein, if a second word '<s>Brahman</s>' were not employed — if it were stated merely as '<s>Ka</s>-<s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — then since the word '<s>Ka</s>' would be used only as a qualifier, happiness as a [mere] quality would be what is to be meditated upon. To prevent this, both words '<s>Ka</s>' and '<s>Kha</s>' are given headship through the word '<s>Brahman</s>': '<s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' For it is desired that happiness too, as a quality, be meditated upon together with the possessor of that quality. Thus, at the beginning of the passage, <s>Brahman</s> designated as connected with happiness is taught.

children.text:
FN: pratīko nāmāśrayāntarapratyayasyāśrayāntare prakṣepaḥ /
kṣayitā pāratantryādirvā āmayastatsahita ityarthaḥ /
tadarthayorviśeṣitatvātchabdāvapi viśeṣitāvucyete /
viśeṣaṇatvena svasya bhūtatvavyāvartakatvena /
brahmapadaṃ śiro yayoste brahmaśirasī tayorbhāvo brahmaśirastvam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: A '<s>pratīka</s>' (symbol) is the transference of the notion of one substrate onto another substrate. '<s>Āmaya</s>' means ailment characterized by decay, dependence, and such — that which is accompanied by it: this is the meaning. Because both [words] are qualified by their respective [counterparts], the words too are said to be qualified. 'As a qualifier' — namely, as that which excludes its [other] nature as [mere] elemental [space or mundane happiness]. '<s>Brahma-śiras</s>' (having <s>Brahman</s> as head) — the two that have <s>Brahman</s> as their head; the state of being such is '<s>brahma-śirastva</s>.'

children.text: śrutopaniṣatkagatyabhidhānāc ca | BBs_1,2.16 |
children.translated_text: And because of the declaration of the path of one who has heard the esoteric teaching. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.16 |

children.text:
itaścākṣisthānaḥ puruṣaḥ parameśvaraḥ, yasmācchrutopaniṣatkasya śrutarahasyavijñānasya brahmavido yā gatirdevayānākhyā prasiddhā śrutau- 'athottareṇa tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā vidyayātmānamanviṣyādityamabhijayanta etadvai prāṇānāmāyatanametadamṛtamabhayametatparāyaṇametasmānna punarāvartante' (praśna. 1.10) iti /
smṛtāvapi- 'agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam /
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ' (gī. 8.24) iti /
children.translated_text: departing by that [path], those persons who know <s>Brahman</s> go to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Gītā</s> 8.24).

children.text: saivāhākṣipuruṣavido 'bhidhīyamānā dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: That very [path] is seen being declared for the knower of the person in the eye.

children.text: 'atha yadu caivāsmiñchavyaṃ kurvanti yadi ca nārciṣamevābhisaṃbhavanti' ityupakramya 'ādityāccandramasaṃ candramaso vidyutaṃ tatpuruṣo 'mānavaḥ sa enānbrahma gamayatyeva devapatho brahmapatha etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavamāvarte nāvartante' (chā. 4.17.5) iti /
children.translated_text: Having begun with 'Now, whether they perform the funeral rites for him or not — they reach the flame,' [the text states]: 'from the sun to the moon, from the moon to lightning; there, a person who is not human — he leads them to <s>Brahman</s>. This is the path of the gods, the path of <s>Brahman</s>. Those who attain by this [path] do not return to this human cycle' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.17.5).

children.text: tadiha brahmavidviṣayā prasiddhayā gatyākṣisthānasya brahmatvaṃ niścīyate // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the one situated in the eye is determined here through the well-known path pertaining to the knower of <s>Brahman</s>. // 16 //

For this reason too, the person situated in the eye is the Supreme Lord. Because the path that is well known in <s>śruti</s> as that of a knower of <s>Brahman</s> who has heard the esoteric teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) — the path called <s>Devayāna</s> (the path of the gods) — [is described]: 'By <s>tapas</s>, by <s>brahmacarya</s>, by faith, by knowledge, seeking the Self, they conquer the sun through the northern [path]. This is the abode of vital breaths; this is the immortal, the fearless. This is the supreme goal. From this they do not return' (<s>Praśna</s> 1.10). In <s>Smṛti</s> also: 'Fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern course —

children.text:
FN: dehapātānantaryamathaśabdārthaḥ /
etat vyaṣṭisamaṣṭikāraṇātmakaṃ hairaṇyagarbhaṃ padam /
asminnupāsake mṛte putrādayaḥ śavyaṃ śavasaṃbandhi saṃskārādikarma kurvanti /
mānavaṃ manoḥ sarge, āvarte janmamaraṇādyāvṛttiyuktam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The word '<s>atha</s>' means 'immediately after the fall of the body.' 'This' refers to the state of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, which is the cause of both individual and cosmic [manifestation]. When this worshipper dies, his sons and others perform the funeral rites (<s>śavya</s>) — rites relating to the corpse, such as cremation. '<s>Mānava</s>' refers to [the cycle] in the creation of <s>Manu</s>; '<s>āvarta</s>' means that which is accompanied by the revolving of birth, death, and so forth.

children.text: anavasthiter asaṃbhavāc ca netaraḥ | BBs_1,2.17 |
children.translated_text: Not the other [entities], because of the impossibility of fixed location and because of impossibility [of the qualities]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.17 |

children.text:
yatpunaruktaṃ chāyātmā, vijñānātmā, devatātmā vā syādakṣisthāna iti /
atrocyate- na chāyātmādiritara iha grahaṇamarhati /
kasmāt, anavasthiteḥ /
na tāvacchāyātmanaścakṣuṣi nityamavasthānaṃ saṃbhavati /
yadaiva hi kaścitpuruṣaścakṣurāsīdati tadā cakṣuṣi puruṣacchāyā dṛśyate, apagate tasminna dṛśyate /
'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣaḥ' iti ca śrutiḥ saṃnidhānātsvacakṣuṣi dṛśyamānaṃ puruṣamupāsyatvenopadiśati /
nacopāsanākāle chāyākaraṃ kañcitpuruṣaṃ cakṣuḥsamīpe saṃnidhāpyopāsta iti yuktaṃ kalpayitum /
'asyaiva śarīrasya nāśamanveṣa naśyati' (chā. 8.9.1) iti śrutiśchāyātmano 'pyanavasthitatvaṃ darśayati /
asaṃbhavācca tasminnamṛtatvādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ na chāyātmani pratītiḥ /
tathā vijñānātmano 'pi sādhāraṇe kṛtsnaśarīrendriyasaṃbandhe sati cakṣuṣyevāvasthitatvaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyam /
brahmaṇastu vyāpino 'pi dṛṣṭa upalabdhyartho hṛdayādideśaviśeṣasaṃbandhaḥ /
samānaśca vijñānātmanyapyamṛtatvādīnāṃ guṇānāmasaṃbandhaḥ /
yadyapi vijñānātmā paramātmano 'nanya eva, tathāpyavidyākāmakarmakṛtaṃ tasminmartyatvamadhyaropitaṃ bhayaṃ cetyamṛtatvābhayatve nopapadyete /
saṃyadvāmatvādayaścaitasminnanaiśvaryādanupapannā eva /
devatātmanastu 'raśmibhireṣo 'sminpratiṣṭhitaḥ' iti śruteryadyapi cakṣuṣyavasthānaṃ syāttathāpyātmatvaṃ tāvanna saṃbhavati, parāgrūpatvāt /
amṛtatvādayo 'pi na saṃbhavanti, utpattipralayaśravaṇāt /
amaratvamapi devānāṃ cirakālāvasthānāpekṣam /
aiśvaryamapi parameśvarāyattaṃ na svābhāvikam /
bhīṣāsmādvātaḥ pavate bhīṣodeti sūryaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Out of fear of Him the wind blows; out of fear of Him the sun rises;

children.text: bhīṣāsmādagniścendraśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ' (tai. 2.8) iti mantravarṇāt /
children.translated_text: out of fear of Him fire and <s>Indra</s> [function], and death runs as the fifth' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8) — from this <s>mantra</s> passage.

children.text: tasmātparameśvara evāyamakṣisthānaḥ pratyetavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this one situated in the eye is to be understood as the Supreme Lord alone.

children.text: asmiṃśca pakṣe dṛśyata iti prasiddhavadupādānaṃ śāstrādyapekṣaṃ vidvadviṣayaṃ prarocanārthamiti vyākhyeyam // 17 //
children.translated_text: And on this view, the expression 'is seen' (<s>dṛśyate</s>) should be explained as an instruction given as though about something well known — dependent on scripture and pertaining to the wise — for the purpose of generating interest. // 17 //

As for the objection that the one situated in the eye is the shadow-self, the cognizing self, or the deity-self — to this we say: the other, such as the shadow-self, does not merit being grasped here. Why? Because of the impossibility of fixed location. First, it is not possible for the shadow-self to be permanently located in the eye. For the shadow of a person is seen in the eye only when some person approaches the eye; when that person moves away, it is not seen. And the <s>śruti</s>, through 'the person that is in the eye,' teaches the person that is seen in one's own eye as an object of meditation because of its proximity. And it is not reasonable to suppose that at the time of meditation, one places some person who would cast a shadow near the eye and then meditates. The <s>śruti</s> statement 'When this body perishes, this [shadow] too perishes' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.9.1) also shows the impermanence of the shadow-self. And because of the impossibility of qualities such as immortality in the shadow-self — there is no apprehension [of <s>Brahman</s>] there. Similarly, for the cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) too — since it has a common connection with the entire body and senses — a fixed location exclusively in the eye cannot be stated. But for <s>Brahman</s>, though all-pervading, a connection with specific locations such as the heart is well known for the purpose of apprehension. And the impossibility of qualities such as immortality applies equally to the cognizing self. For although the cognizing self is indeed non-different from the Supreme Self, nevertheless, since mortality and fear are superimposed upon it through the actions born of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and desire, immortality and fearlessness are not justified [for it]. And qualities like being <s>Saṃyadvāma</s> and such are not justified for it either, due to the absence of lordly power. As for the deity-self — although from the <s>śruti</s> 'He is established in this [eye] through his rays,' it might have a location in the eye — nevertheless, selfhood is first of all not possible, because its form is turned outward. And immortality and such are also impossible, because arising and dissolution are heard [of deities]. The immortality of the gods too is relative — dependent on enduring for a long time. And their lordly power too is dependent on the Supreme Lord, not intrinsic —

children.text:
FN.:asya chāyākarasya bimbasya /
parāk bāhyaṃ jagat /
bhīṣā bhayena, asmāt brahmaṇaḥ, pavate calati /
uktāpekṣayā pañcamo mṛtyuḥ samāptāyuṣāṃ nikaṭe dhāvatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Asya</s>' — of this, the reflected image of the original. '<s>Parāk</s>' — the external world. '<s>Bhīṣā</s>' — out of fear; '<s>asmāt</s>' — from this <s>Brahman</s>; '<s>pavate</s>' — moves, stirs. In relation to what was said, death, the fifth, runs near to those whose lifespan has ended — this is the meaning.

children.text: 5 antaryāmyadhikaraṇam / sū. 18-20
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Antaryāmy Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Inner Controller). <s>Sūtras</s> 18-20.

children.text: antaryāmyadhidaivādhilokādiṣu taddharmavyapadeśāt | BBs_1,2.18 |
children.translated_text: The inner controller in the divine, cosmic, and other [spheres] — because of the designation of its characteristics. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.18 |

children.text:
'ya imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni yo 'ntaro yamayati' ityupakramya śrūyate- 'yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhanpṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīmantaro yamayatyeṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ' (bṛha. 3.7.1,2) ityādi /
atrādhidaivatamadhilokamadhivedamadhiyajñamadhibhūtamadhyātmaṃ ca kaścidantaravasthito yamayitāntaryāmīti śrūyate /
sa kimadhidaivādyabhimānī devatātmā kaścitkiṃvā prāptāṇimādyaiśvaryaḥ kaścidyogī kiṃvā paramātmā kiṃvārthāntaraṃ kiñcidityapūrvasaṃjñādarśanātmasaṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvannaḥ pratibhāti, saṃjñayā aprasiddhatvātsaṃjñino 'pyasiddhenārthāntareṇa kenacidbhavitavyamiti /
athavā nānirūpitarūpamarthāntaraṃ śakyamastyabhyupagantum /
antaryāmiśabdaścāntaryamanayogena pravṛtto nātyantamaprasiddhaḥ /
tasmātpṛthivyādyabhimānī kaściddevo 'ntaryāmī syāt /
tathāca śrūyate- 'pṛthivyeva yasyāyatanamagnirloko mano jyotiḥ' (bṛ. 3.9.10) ityādi /
sa ca kāryakāraṇavattvātpṛthivyādīnantastiṣṭhanyamayatīti yuktaṃ devatātmano yamayitṛtvam /
yogino vā kasyacitsiddhasya sarvānupraveśena yamayitṛtvaṃ syāt, natu paramātmā pratīyeta, akāryakaraṇatvādityevaṃ prāpta idamucyate- yo 'ntaryāmyadhidaivādiṣu śrūyate sa paramātmaiva syānnānya iti /
kutaḥ, taddharmavyapadeśāt /
tasya hi paramātmano dharmā iha nirdiśyamānā dṛśyante /
pṛthivyādi tāvadadhidaivatādibhedabhinnaṃ samastaṃ vikārajātamantastiṣṭanyamayatīti paramātmano yamayitṛtvaṃ dharma upapadyate /
sarvavikārakāraṇatve sati sarvaśaktyupapatteḥ /
eṣa ta 'ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ' iti cātmatvāmṛtatve mukhye paramātmana upapadyete /
'yaṃ pṛthivī na veda' iti ca pṛthivīdevatāyā avijñeyamantaryāmiṇaṃ bruvandevatātmano 'nyamantaryāmiṇaṃ darśayati /
'pṛthivī devatā hyahamasmi pṛthivītyatmānaṃ vijānīyāt' /
tathā 'adṛṣṭo 'śrutaḥ' ityādivyapadeśo rūpādivihīnatvātparamātmana upapadyata iti /
yattvakāryakaraṇasya paramātmano yamayitṛtvaṃ nopapadyata iti /
children.translated_text:
Beginning with 'He who, being within, controls this world and the other world and all beings,' it is heard: 'He who, standing in the earth, is interior to the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who controls the earth from within — He is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.1-2) and so forth.
Here, someone stationed within the divine sphere, the cosmic sphere, the Vedic sphere, the sacrificial sphere, the elemental sphere, and the individual sphere is heard of as an inner controller who controls.
Is this some deity-self who presides over the divine and other [spheres]? Or some <s>yogin</s> who has attained the lordly powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness)? Or the supreme Self? Or some other thing entirely? — this doubt arises because the designation is unprecedented.
What first occurs to us? Since the designation is unfamiliar, the one designated must be some unfamiliar entity.
Alternatively, one cannot accept an entity of undetermined nature as something entirely different.
And the word 'inner controller' (<s>antaryāmin</s>), being employed through the connection with the activity of controlling from within, is not entirely unfamiliar.
Therefore, some god presiding over the earth and such could be the inner controller.
Thus it is also heard: 'The earth alone is its abode, fire its world, the mind its light' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.10) and such.
And because of possessing cause and effect, it is proper that the deity-self controls the earth and such from within — thus the controllership of a deity-self [is plausible].
Or some accomplished <s>yogin</s> could have controllership through entering all things; but the supreme Self should not be understood, because of its not having cause and effect — given this position, it is said: The one heard of as the inner controller in the divine and other [spheres] must be the supreme Self alone, not another.
Why? Because of the designation of its characteristics.
For the characteristics of the supreme Self are seen to be indicated here.
First, that it controls, standing within, the entire class of modifications differentiated into the divine and other divisions beginning with the earth — controllership is a characteristic that is fitting for the supreme Self.
Because, being the cause of all modifications, the possession of all powers is justified.
'He is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal' — and Self-hood and immortality, in the primary sense, are fitting for the supreme Self.
'Whom the earth does not know' — by stating that the inner controller is unknowable to the earth-deity, [the text] shows an inner controller different from the deity-self.
'For the earth-deity would know: "I am the earth."'
Likewise, the designations 'unseen' and 'unheard' and such are fitting for the supreme Self, because of its being devoid of form and such.
As for the [objection] that controllership is not fitting for the supreme Self, since it has no body and organs —

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
yānniyacchati tatkāryakaraṇaireva, tasya kāryakaraṇattvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because its having body and organs is justified through the very body and organs of those whom it controls.

children.text: tasyāpyanyo niyantetyanavasthādoṣaśca na saṃbhavati, bhedābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And the defect of infinite regress — that even its controller would need a controller — is not possible, because there is no [real] difference.

children.text: bhede hi satyanavasthādoṣopapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: For the defect of infinite regress arises only when difference exists.

children.text: tasmātparamātmaivāntaryāmī // 18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the inner controller is the supreme Self alone. // 18 //
This is not a fault.

children.text: FN: āyatanaṃ śarīraṃ, lokyate 'neneti lokacakṣuḥ, jyotirmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Āyatana</s>' means body; '<s>loka</s>' means the eye by which one sees; '<s>jyotis</s>' means the mind.

children.text: na ca smārtam ataddharmābhilāpāt | BBs_1,2.19 |
children.translated_text: Nor [is the inner controller] the [<s>Pradhāna</s>] of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) — because of the mention of characteristics that do not belong to it. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.19 |

children.text:
syādetat /
adṛṣṭatvādayo dharmāḥ sāṃkhyasmṛtikalpitasya pradhānasyāpyupapadyante, rūpādihīnatayā tasya tairabhyupagamāt /
'apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ prasuptamiva sarvataḥ' (manu. 1.5) iti hi smaranti, tasyāpi niyantṛtvaṃ sarvavikārakāraṇatvādupapadyate /
tasmātpradhānamantaryāmiśabdaṃ syāt /
'īkṣaternāśabdam' (bra. 1.1.5) ityatra nirākṛtamapi satpradhānamihādṛṣṭatvādivyapadeśasaṃbhavena punarāśaṅkyate /
ata uttaramucyate- naca smārte pradhānamantaryāmiśabdaṃ bhavitumarhati /
kasmāt,ataddharmābhilāpāt /
yadyapyadṛṣṭatvādivyapadeśaḥ pradhānasyasaṃbhavati tathāpi na draṣṭṛtvādivyapeśaḥ saṃbhavati, pradhānasyācetanatvena tairabhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: Although the designation of invisibility and such is possible for <s>Pradhāna</s>, still the designation of being a seer and such is not possible, since <s>Pradhāna</s> is accepted by them as unconscious.

children.text: 'adṛṣṭo draṣṭāśrutaḥ śrotāmato mantāvijñāto vijñātā' (bṛha. 3.7.23) iti hi vākyaśeṣa iha bhavati /
children.translated_text: For the remainder of the passage states: 'Unseen, [he is] the seer; unheard, [he is] the hearer; unthought, [he is] the thinker; unknown, [he is] the knower' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23).

children.text: ātmatvamapi na pradhānasyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: Selfhood too is not fitting for <s>Pradhāna</s>.

It might be thought: the characteristics of invisibility and such are also fitting for the <s>Pradhāna</s> conceived by the <s>Sāṃkhya smṛti</s>, since it too is accepted by them as devoid of form and such.
'Unthinkable, unknowable, as if asleep everywhere' (<s>Manusmṛti</s> 1.5) — thus they remember. Its controllership too is justified because it is the cause of all modifications.
Therefore, <s>Pradhāna</s> could be [the referent of] the word 'inner controller.'
Although <s>Pradhāna</s> was rejected in 'Because of seeing — not [<s>Pradhāna</s>]; it lacks scriptural basis' (<s>Bra</s>. 1.1.5), it is here again suspected because of the possibility of the designation of invisibility and such [applying to it].
Hence the answer: Nor can the <s>Pradhāna</s> of <s>smṛti</s> be [the referent of] the word 'inner controller.'
Why? Because of the mention of characteristics that do not belong to it.

children.text:
yadi pradhānamātmatvadraṣṭṛtvādyasaṃbhavānnāntaryāmyabhyupagamyate, śārīrastarhyantaryāmī bhavatu /
śārīro hi cetanatvāddraṣṭā śrotā mantā vijñātā ca bhavati, ātmā ca pratyaktvāt /
amṛtaśca, dharmādharmaphalopabhogopapatteḥ /
adṛṣṭatvādayaśca dharmāḥ śārīre parasiddhāḥ darśanādikriyāyāḥ kartari pravṛttivirodhāt /
'na dṛṣṭerdraṣṭāraṃ paśyeḥ' (bṛ. 3.4.2) ityādiśrutibhyaśca /
tasya ca kāryakaraṇasaṃghātamantaryamayituṃ śīlaṃ, bhoktṛtvāt /
tasmācchārīro 'ntaryāmītyata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text:
If <s>Pradhāna</s> is not accepted as the inner controller because of the impossibility of Selfhood and seer-hood — then let the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>) be the inner controller.
For the embodied self, being conscious, is a seer, hearer, thinker, and knower; and it is the Self, because of being the innermost. And it is immortal, because the enjoyment of the fruits of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> [across lives] is justified [only for a persistent entity].
And the characteristics of being unseen and such are established for the embodied self in the opposite way — because of the contradiction with being the agent of the activity of seeing and such.
Because of <s>śrutis</s> such as 'You cannot see the seer of seeing' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.2).
And it is the nature of the embodied self to control the aggregate of body and organs from within, because of being an experiencer.
Therefore, the embodied self is the inner controller — to this, the next [<s>sūtra</s>] is read:

children.text: FN: amṛtaśceti vināśino dehāntarabhogānupapatterityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'And immortal' — the meaning is: because the enjoyment of another body [in the next life] would be unjustified for what is perishable.

children.text: kartarīti kriyāyāṃ guṇaḥ kartā, pradhānaṃ karma, tatraikasyāṃ kriyāyāmekasya guṇatvapradhānatvayorvirodhānna kartuḥ karmatvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the agent' — the quality is the agent in the action, the principal is the action (<s>karma</s>); since one and the same [entity] cannot be both the quality [agent] and the principal [action/object] in a single action, the agent cannot be the object — this is the meaning.

children.text: śarīraś cobhaye 'pi hi bhedenainam adhīyate | BBs_1,2.20 |
children.translated_text: And the embodied self — because both [recensions] recite it as different from this [inner controller]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.20 |

children.text:
neti pūrvasūtrādanuvartate /
śārīraśca nāntaryāmīṣyate /
kasmāt /
yadyapi draṣṭṛtvādayo dharmastasya saṃbhavanti tathāpi ghaṭākāśavadupādhiparicchinnatvānna kārtsyena pṛthivyādiṣvantaravasthātuṃ niyantuṃ ca śaknoti /
apicobhaye 'pi hi śākhinaḥ kāṇvā mādhyandinānāścāntaryāmiṇo bhedenainaṃ śārīraṃ pṛthivyādivadadhiṣṭhānatvena niyamyatvena cādhīyate- 'yo vijñāne tiṣṭhan' (bṛ. 3.7.22) iti kāṇvāḥ /
'ya ātmani tiṣṭhan' iti mādhyandināḥ /
'ya ātmani tiṣṭhan' ityasminstāvatpāṭhe bhavatyātmaśabdaḥ śārīrasya vācakaḥ /
'yo vijñāne tiṣṭhan' ityasminnapi pāṭhe vijñānaśabdena śārīra ucyate /
vijñānamayo hi śārīraḥ /
tasmācchārīradanya īśvaro 'ntaryāmīti siddham /
kathaṃ punarekasmindehe dvau draṣṭāravupapadyete, yaścāyamīśvaro 'ntaryāmī yaścāyamitaraḥ śārīraḥ /
kā punarihānupapattiḥ /
'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' ityādi śrutivacanaṃ virudhyeta /
atra hi prakṛtādantaryāmiṇo 'nyaṃ draṣṭāraṃ, śrotāraṃ, mantāraṃ, vijñātāraṃ cātmānaṃ pratiṣedhati /
niyantrantarapratiṣedhārthametadvacanamiticet, na, niyantrantarāprasaṅgādaviśeṣaśravaṇācca /
atrocyate-
children.translated_text:
'Not' — carries over from the previous <s>sūtra</s>.
And the embodied self is not accepted as the inner controller.
Why?
Although the characteristics of seer-hood and such are possible for it, still, because of being delimited by limiting adjuncts like pot-space, it is not able to stand within or control the earth and such in their entirety.
Moreover, both recensions — the <s>Kāṇvas</s> and <s>Mādhyandinas</s> — recite the embodied self as different from the inner controller, as something to be presided over and controlled — like the earth and such.
'He who stands in cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>)' — thus the <s>Kāṇvas</s>.
'He who stands in the self (<s>ātman</s>)' — thus the <s>Mādhyandinas</s>.
In the reading 'He who stands in the self,' the word '<s>ātman</s>' denotes the embodied self.
In the reading 'He who stands in cognition' too, the word '<s>vijñāna</s>' refers to the embodied self.
For the embodied self is '<s>vijñānamaya</s>' (made of cognition).
Therefore, it is established that the inner controller is the Lord, different from the embodied self.
But how can two seers be justified in a single body — this inner-controlling Lord and the other, the embodied self?
What is the problem here?
[The objection is that] the scriptural statement 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23) and such would be contradicted.
For that [text] denies any self that is a seer, hearer, thinker, or knower, other than the inner controller who is the subject of discussion.
If it is said that this statement is meant to deny any other controller — no, because there is no occasion for another controller, and because the scriptural text is heard without distinction.
To this it is said:

children.text:
avidyāpratyupasthāpitakāryakaraṇopādhinimitto 'yaṃ śārīrāntaryāmiṇorbhedavyapadeśo na pāramārthikaḥ /
eko hi pratyagātmā bhavati, na dvau pratyagātmānau saṃbhavataḥ /
ekasyaiva tu bhedavyavahāra upādhikṛto yathā ghaṭākāśo mahākāśa iti /
children.translated_text: But the conventional usage of difference pertaining to one and the same [Self] is created by limiting adjuncts — just as [the distinction between] pot-space and the great space.

children.text: tataśca jñātṛjñeyādibhedaśrutayaḥ pratyakṣādīni ca pramāṇāni saṃsārānubhavo vidhipratiṣedhaśāstraṃ ceti sarvametadupapadyate /
children.translated_text: And thus, all of this — the scriptures speaking of the distinction of knower and known, the means of valid knowledge such as perception, the experience of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the scripture of injunctions and prohibitions — all this is justified.

children.text: tathāca śrutiḥ 'yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati taditara itaraṃ paśyati' itvavidyāviṣaye sarve vyavahāraṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>śruti</s> too: 'Where there is duality, as it were, there one sees the other' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14) — shows all conventional usage in the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: 'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' iti vidyāviṣaye sarve vyavahāraṃ vārayati // 20 //
children.translated_text: 'But where all has become the Self alone, then by what would one see what?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14) — bars all conventional usage in the domain of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). // 20 //

This designation of difference between the embodied self and the inner controller is occasioned by the limiting adjuncts of body and organs presented by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — it is not ultimate.
For the inner Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) is one alone; two inner selves are not possible.

children.text: adṛśyatvādhikaraṇam / sū. 21-23
children.translated_text: The <s>Adṛśyatva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Invisibility). <s>Sūtras</s> 21-23.

children.text: adṛśyatvādiguṇako dharmokteḥ | BBs_1,2.21 |
children.translated_text: The one possessed of the qualities of invisibility and such [is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of the statement of [its] characteristics. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.21 |

children.text:
'atha parā yayā tadakṣaramadhigamyate', 'yattadadreśyamagrāhyamagotramavarṇamacakṣuḥśrotraṃ tadapāṇipādaṃ nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ tadavyayaṃ yadbhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ' (muṇḍa. 1.1.5,6) iti śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kimayamadreśyatvādiguṇako bhūtayoniḥ pradhānaṃ syāduta śārīra āhosvitparameśvara iti /
tatra pradhānamacetanaṃ bhūtayoniriti yuktaṃ, acetanānāmeva taddṛṣṭāntatvenopādānāt /
'yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhyate ca yathā pṛthivyāmoṣadhaḥ saṃbhavanti /
yathā sataḥ puruṣotkeśalomāni tathākṣarātsaṃbhavatīha viśvam' (muṇḍa. 1.1.7) iti /
children.translated_text:
'Now, [there is] the higher [knowledge] by which that Imperishable is realized' — 'That which is invisible, ungraspable, without lineage, without color, without eyes and ears, without hands and feet — eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent, extremely subtle — that is the Imperishable, which the wise perceive as the source of beings' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.5-6) — thus it is heard.
Therein, the doubt arises: Is this source of beings, possessing the qualities of invisibility and such, <s>Pradhāna</s>? Or the embodied self? Or the supreme Lord?
There, it is fitting that the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> is the source of beings, since only unconscious things are cited as illustrations for it:
'As the spider sends forth and withdraws [its thread], as herbs grow from the earth,
as hair grows from a living person — so from the Imperishable does the universe arise here' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.7).

children.text: nanūrṇanābhiḥ puruṣaśca cetanāviha dṛṣṭāntatvenopāttau /
children.translated_text: But the spider and the person [cited as examples] are conscious!

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ /
nahi kevalasya cetanasya tatra sūtrayonitvaṃ keśalomayonitvaṃ cāsti /
cetanādhiṣṭhitaṃ hyacetanamūrṇanābhiśarīraṃ sūtrasya yoniḥ, puruṣaśarīraṃ ca keśalomnāmiti prasiddham /
apica pūrvatrādṛṣṭatvādyabhilāṣasaṃbhave 'pi draṣṭṛtvādyabhilāṣāsaṃbhavānna pradhānamabhyupagatam /
iha tvadṛśyatvādayo dharmāḥ pradhāne saṃbhavanti /
nacātra virudhyamāno dharmaḥ kaścidabhilapyate /
children.translated_text:
Not so, we say.
For it is not the case that mere consciousness [by itself] has the property of being the source of thread or hair.
Rather, the unconscious body of the spider, presided over by consciousness, is the source of thread; and the body of the person [is the source] of hair — this is well-known.
Moreover, even though the designation of invisibility and such was possible earlier [in the case of <s>Pradhāna</s>], because of the impossibility of the designation of seer-hood and such, <s>Pradhāna</s> was not accepted.
But here, the characteristics of invisibility and such do apply to <s>Pradhāna</s>.
And no contradictory characteristic is mentioned here.

children.text: nanu 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit' (muṇḍa. 1.1.9) ityayaṃ vākyaśeṣo 'cetane pradhāne na saṃbhavanti, kathaṃ pradhānaṃ bhūtayoniḥ pratijñāyata iti /
children.translated_text: But the remainder of the passage — 'Who is omniscient, all-knowing' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9) — is not possible for the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>! How then can <s>Pradhāna</s> be claimed as the source of beings?

children.text:
atrocyate- 'yayā tadakṣaramadhigamyate' 'yattadadreśyam' ityakṣaraśabdenādṛśyatvādiguṇakaṃ bhūtayoniṃ śrāvayitvā punarante śrāvayiṣyati- 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' (muṇḍa. 2.1.2) iti /
tatra yaḥ paro 'kṣarācchrutaḥ sa sarvajñaḥ sarvavitsaṃbhaviṣyati /
pradhānameva tvakṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭaṃ bhūtayoniḥ /
yadā tu yoniśabdo nimittavācī tadā śārīro 'pi bhūtayoniḥ syāt, dharmādharmābhyāṃ bhūtajātasyopārjanāditi /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- yoyamadṛśyatvādiguṇako bhūtayoniḥ sa parameśvara eva syānnānya iti /
kathametadavagamyate /
dharmokteḥ /
parameśvarasya hi dharma ihocyamāno dṛśyate- 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit' iti /
nahi pradhānasyācetanasya śārīrasya vopādhiparicchinnadṛṣṭeḥ sarvajñatvaṃ sarvavittvaṃ vā saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text:
To this it is said: Having taught the source of beings, possessing the qualities of invisibility and such, through the word 'Imperishable' (<s>akṣara</s>) — in 'by which that Imperishable is realized' and 'That which is invisible' — [the scripture] will again teach at the end: 'Higher than the Imperishable is the Supreme' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2).
There, it is the one heard of as higher than the Imperishable who will be omniscient and all-knowing.
But the <s>Pradhāna</s> itself, designated by the word 'Imperishable,' is the source of beings.
Or, when the word 'source' (<s>yoni</s>) has the meaning of efficient cause, even the embodied self could be the source of beings, since it acquires the world of beings through <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
Given this position, it is said: This source of beings, possessing the qualities of invisibility and such, can only be the supreme Lord, not another.
How is this understood?
Because of the statement of [its] characteristics.
For the characteristic of the supreme Lord is seen to be stated here: 'Who is omniscient, all-knowing.'
For neither the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> nor the embodied self — whose vision is delimited by limiting adjuncts — can possess omniscience or all-knowingness.

children.text: nanvakṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭādbhūtayoneḥ parasyaiva tatsarvajñatvaṃ ca na bhūtayoniviṣayamityuktam /
children.translated_text: But it was said that the omniscience and all-knowingness belong to the one [spoken of as] higher than the source of beings designated by the word 'Imperishable' — and do not pertain to the source of beings itself!

children.text:
atrocyate- naivaṃ saṃbhavati /
yatkāraṇaṃ 'akṣarātsaṃbhavatīha viśvam' iti prakṛtaṃ bhūtayonimiha jāyamānaprakṛtitvena nirdiśyānantaramapi jāyamānaprakṛtitvenaiva sarvajñaṃ nirdiśati- 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavidyasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ /
tasmādetadbrahma nāma rūpamannaṃ ca jāyate' iti /
tasmānnirdeśasāmyena pratyabhijñāyamānatvātprakṛtasyaivākṣarasya bhūtayoneḥ sarvajñatvaṃ sarvavittvaṃ ca dharma ucyata iti gamyate /
'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' ityatrāpi na prakṛtādbhūtayonerakṣarātparaḥ kaścidabhidhūyate /
kathametadavagamyate /
'yenākṣaraṃ puruṣaṃ veda satyaṃ provāca tāṃ tattvato brahmavidyām' (muṇḍa. 1.2.13) iti prakṛtya tasyaivākṣarasya bhūtayoneradṛśyatvādiguṇakasya vaktavyatvena pratijñātatvāt /
kathaṃ tarhi 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' iti vyapadiśyata iti, uttarasūtre tadvakṣyāmaḥ /
apicātra dve vidye veditavye ukte- 'parā caivāparā ca' iti /
tatrāparāmṛgvedādilakṣaṇāṃ vidyāmuktvā bravīti- 'atha parā yayā tadakṣaramadhigamyate ityādi /
tatra parasyā vidyāyā viṣayatvenākṣaraṃ śrutam /
yadi punaḥ parameśvarādanyadadṛśyatvādiguṇakamakṣaraṃ parikalpyeta neyaṃ parā vidyā syāt /
parāparavibhāgo hyayaṃ vidyayorabhyudayaniḥśreyasaphalatayā parikalpyate /
naca pradhānavidyā niḥśreyasaphalā kenacidabhyupagamyate /
tisraśca vidyāḥ pratijñāyeran, tvatpakṣe 'kṣarādbhūtayoneḥ parasya paramātmanaḥ pratipādyamānatvāt /
dve eva tu vidye veditavye iha nirdiṣṭe /
'kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati' (muṇḍa. 1.1.3) iti caikavijñānena sarvavijñānāpekṣaṇaṃ sarvātmake brahmaṇi vivakṣyamāṇe 'vakalpyate, nācetanamātraikāyatane pradhāne, bhogyavyatirikte vā bhoktari /
apica 'sa brahmavidyāṃ sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhāmatharvāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha' (muṇḍa. 1.1.1) iti brahmavidyāṃ prādhānyenopakramya parāparavibhāgena parāṃ vidyāmakṣarādhigamanīṃ darśayaṃstayā brahmavidyātvaṃ darśayati /
sā ca brahmavidyāsamākhyā tadadhigamyasyākṣarasyābrahmatve bādhitā syāt /
aparargvedādilakṣaṇā karmavidyā brahmavidyopakrama upanyasyate brahmavidyāpraśaṃsāyai /
'plavā hyete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktamavaraṃ yeṣu karma /
etacchreyo yo 'bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punarevāpiyanti' (muṇḍa. 1.2.7) ityevamādinindāvacanāt /
ninditvā cāparāṃ vidyāṃ tato viraktasya paravidyādhikāraṃ darśayati- 'parīkṣya lokānkarmacitānbrāhmaṇo nirvedamāyānnāstyakṛtaḥ kṛtena /
tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurumevābhigacchetsamitpāṇiḥ śretriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham' (muṇḍa. 1.2.12) iti /
yattūktamacetanānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ dṛṣṭāntatvenopādānāddārṣṭāntikenāpyacetanena bhūtayoninā bhavitavyamiti /
tadayuktam /
children.translated_text: that is unjustified.

children.text: nahi dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayoratyantasāmyena bhavitavyamiti niyamo 'sti /
children.translated_text: For there is no rule that there must be absolute similarity between the example and the thing exemplified.

children.text: apica sthūlāḥ pṛthivyādayo dṛṣṭāntatvenopāttā iti na sthūla eva dārṣṭāntiko bhūtayonirabhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the gross [entities] such as earth and others are employed as examples — therefore it is not to be assumed that the thing exemplified, the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, is also gross.

children.text: tasmādadṛśyatvādiguṇako bhūtayoniḥ parameśvara eva // 21 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, possessing qualities such as invisibility, is the supreme Lord alone. // 21 //

To this it is said: This is not possible. The reason being that, having indicated the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> (source of beings) that is the subject under discussion — through 'From the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), this universe comes into being' — as having the nature of the source from which things are born, subsequently too, it designates [that same entity] as omniscient, in the very same capacity of being the source of origination: 'He who is omniscient, all-knowing, whose austerity is of the nature of knowledge — from Him are born this <s>Brahman</s>, name, form, and food' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9). Therefore, because the subject under discussion — the very <s>Akṣara</s>, the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> — is recognized through the similarity of designation, it is understood that omniscience and all-knowingness are stated as its qualities. And in '<s>akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ</s>' (beyond the Imperishable is the Supreme), no one distinct from the subject — the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, the <s>Akṣara</s> — is being referred to. How is this understood? Because, having introduced the passage 'He who knows the <s>Akṣara</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Real — he taught that <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, the science of <s>Brahman</s>, the foundation of all sciences, to him in its truth' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.13), and because it was promised that the very same <s>Akṣara</s>, the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, with qualities such as invisibility, was to be stated. As to how, then, '[something] beyond the Imperishable is the Supreme' is described — we shall explain that in the following <s>sūtra</s>. Moreover, here two sciences are stated as to be known: 'the higher and the lower' (<s>parā</s> and <s>aparā</s>). There, having stated the lower science characterized by the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and such, [the text] says: 'Now, the higher, by which that <s>Akṣara</s> is realized' and so forth. There, the <s>Akṣara</s> is heard as the object of the higher science. But if an <s>Akṣara</s> with qualities of invisibility and such were conceived as other than the supreme Lord, this would not be the higher science. For this division of sciences into higher and lower is conceived on the basis of having worldly prosperity and liberation as their respective fruits. And no one accepts the knowledge of <s>Pradhāna</s> as having liberation as its fruit. And three sciences would have to be postulated — in your view, since the supreme Self beyond the <s>Akṣara</s> (the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>) would also need to be taught. But only two sciences are indicated here as to be known. And the aspiration expressed in 'Revered Sir, by knowing what does all this become known?' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.3) — the desire for the knowledge of everything through the knowledge of one thing — is appropriate when <s>Brahman</s>, which is the Self of all, is intended, not in the case of <s>Pradhāna</s>, which is merely the substratum of the unconscious, nor in the case of the experiencer who is distinct from what is experienced. Moreover, having commenced with <s>Brahmavidyā</s> as the principal topic — 'He taught this <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, the foundation of all sciences, to <s>Atharvan</s>, his eldest son' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.1) — and showing through the division of higher and lower that the higher science is the one by which the <s>Akṣara</s> is realized, [the text] thereby shows its character as <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. And that designation '<s>Brahmavidyā</s>' would be contradicted if the <s>Akṣara</s> that is to be realized through it were not <s>Brahman</s>. The lower science characterized by the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and such, the science of ritual action, is introduced at the commencement of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> for the purpose of glorifying <s>Brahmavidyā</s> — because of the words of censure such as: 'Unsafe indeed are these boats in the form of sacrifices — eighteen [participants] — in which is declared the inferior action. Those fools who delight in this as the best, again and again they enter old age and death' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.7). And having censured the lower science, [the text] shows the qualification for the higher science for one who has become dispassionate from that: 'Having examined the worlds attained by action, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should arrive at dispassion — the uncreated [liberation] is not [attained] by the created [action]. For the purpose of knowing that, let him approach a teacher, fuel in hand — one learned in scripture, established in <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.12). As for what was said — that since unconscious things such as earth and others are employed as examples, the thing exemplified — the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> too — must be unconscious —

children.text: FN: adreśyamadṛśyaṃ jñānendriyaiḥ, agrāhyaṃ karmendriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Adṛśyam</s>' (invisible) means imperceptible to the cognitive organs; '<s>agrāhyam</s>' (ungraspable) means [imperceptible] to the organs of action.

children.text: ūrṇanābhirlūtākīṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ūrṇanābhi</s>' means a spider.

children.text: pūrvatra pūrvasminnadhikaraṇe /
children.translated_text: '<s>Pūrvatra</s>' means in the preceding <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (topic).

children.text:
nahīti /
'aktāḥ śarkarā upadadhātī' tyatra 'tejo vai ghṛtaṃ' iti śeṣānnirṇayavadatrāpi adṛśyavādeḥ śeṣānnirṇayaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nahi</s>' — just as in 'One places the smeared pebbles,' the remainder of the sentence is determined by 'Ghee is indeed fire' — similarly here too, the remainder of the sentence is determined by the statement about the invisible [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: yena jñānenākṣaraṃ prakṛtaṃ bhūtayoniṃ puruṣaṃ satyaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: By which knowledge one knows the <s>Akṣara</s>, the subject under discussion, the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Real.

children.text: sarvavidyānāṃ pratiṣṭhā samāptiryasyām /
children.translated_text: 'The foundation of all sciences' means: that in which all sciences find their culmination.

children.text:
plavante gacchanti asthāyina iti plavāḥ /
aṣṭādaśeti ṣoḍaśārtvijaḥ yajamānaḥ patnī cetyaṣṭādaśa /
yeṣūktaṃ avaramanityaṃ karma yajñaḥ /
apiyanti prāpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: 'They float, they go, they are impermanent — hence <s>plavāḥ</s>' (unsafe boats). 'Eighteen' means: the sixteen officiating priests, the sacrificer, and his wife — these are eighteen. 'In which' — the inferior, impermanent action, namely sacrifice, 'is declared.' '<s>Apiyanti</s>' means 'they attain' [old age and death].

children.text:
pratyakṣādinā karmasādhyāṃllokānanityatayā jñātvā nirvedaṃ vairāgyaṃ gacchet /
kutaḥ, kṛtena karmaṇā akṛto mokṣo nāsti /
children.translated_text: Having known through perception and other [means] that the worlds attainable through action are impermanent, one should arrive at dispassion (<s>nirveda</s>), at detachment. Why? Because the uncreated liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) does not come about through created action.

children.text: viśeṣaṇabhedavyapadeśābhyāṃ ca netarau | BBs_1,2.22 |
children.translated_text: And because of the qualifying attribute and the designation of difference — [the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>] is not the other two. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.22 |

children.text:
itaśca parameśvara eva bhūtayonirnetarau śārīraḥ pradhānaṃ vā /
kasmāt /
viśeṣaṇabhedavyapadeśābhyām /
viśinaṣṭi hi prakṛtaṃ bhūtayoniṃ śārīrādvilakṣaṇatvena- ' divyo hyamūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ /
aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhraḥ' (muṇḍa. 2.1.2) iti /
nahyetaddivyādiviśeṣaṇamavidyāpratyupasthāpitanāmarūpaparicchedābhimāninastaddharmānsvātmani kalpayataḥ śārīrasyopapadyate /
tasmātsākṣādaupaniṣadaḥ puruṣa ihocyate /
tathā pradhānādapi prakṛtaṃ bhūtayoniṃ bhedena vyapadiśati- 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' iti /
akṣaramavyākṛtaṃ nāmarūpabījaśaktirūpaṃ bhūtasūkṣmamīśvarāśrayaṃ tasyaivopādhibhūtaṃ sarvasmādvikārātparo yo 'vikārastasmātparataḥ para iti bhedena vyapadeśātparamātmānamiha vivakṣitaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Akṣara</s> is the unmanifest — the potency in the form of the seed of name and form, the subtle element, dependent on the Lord, serving as his limiting adjunct — and [the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is] beyond all modifications, who is the unmodified one, is supreme beyond that imperishable: by designating a difference [between the two], [the scripture] shows that the supreme Self is intended here.

children.text: nātra pradhānaṃ nāma kiñcitsvatantraṃ tattvamabhyupagamya tasmādbhedavyapadeśa ucyate /
children.translated_text: It is not that some independent category called <s>Pradhāna</s> is accepted here and then a difference from it is designated.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi yadi pradhānamapi kalpyamānaṃ śrutyavirodhenāvyākṛtādiśabdavācyaṃ bhūtasūkṣmaṃ parikalpyeta parikalpyatām /
children.translated_text: Rather, even if what is hypothetically conceived as <s>Pradhāna</s> — without contradicting scripture — is conceived as the subtle element designated by words such as '<s>avyākṛta</s>' (unmanifest) — let it be so conceived.

children.text: tasmādbhedavyapadeśātparameśvaro bhūtayonirityetadiha pratipādyate // 22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the designation of difference, it is established here that the supreme Lord is the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>. // 22 //

For this reason too, the supreme Lord alone is the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> — neither the other two: the embodied self nor <s>Pradhāna</s>. Why? Because of the qualifying attribute and the designation of difference. For [the scripture] qualifies the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, the subject under discussion, as being of a nature distinct from the embodied self: 'The divine, formless <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is both external and internal, unborn, without breath, without mind, pure' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2). For this qualifying attribute of being divine and so forth is not appropriate for the embodied self, which, through the delimitation by name and form presented by <s>avidyā</s>, identifies itself [with them] and falsely attributes their properties to its own self. Therefore, the directly indicated <s>Upaniṣadic Puruṣa</s> is spoken of here. Likewise, [the scripture] designates the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> under discussion as different from <s>Pradhāna</s>: '<s>akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ</s>' (beyond the Imperishable is the Supreme).

children.text: kutaśca parameśvaro bhūtayoniḥ-
children.translated_text: For what further reason is the supreme Lord the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>?

children.text:
FN: aśnoti vyāpnoti svavikārajātamityakṣaram /
avyākṛtamavyaktam /
nāmarūpayorbījamīśvarastasya śaktirūpam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Akṣara</s>' — that which pervades its own class of modifications — hence the 'imperishable.' '<s>Avyākṛtam</s>' means the unmanifest. It is the potency in the form of the seed of names and forms, belonging to the Lord.

children.text: rūpopanyāsāc ca | BBs_1,2.23 |
children.translated_text: And because of the presentation of [cosmic] form. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.23 |

children.text:
apica 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' ityasyānantaram 'etasmājjāyate prāṇaḥ' iti prāṇaprabhṛtīnāṃ pṛthivīparyantānāṃ tatvānāṃ sargamuktvā tasyaiva bhūtayoneḥ sarvavikārātmakaṃ rūpamupanyasyamānaṃ paśyāmaḥ- 'agnirmūrdhā cakṣuṣī candrasūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāgvivṛtāśca vedāḥ /
vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvamasya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hyeṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā' (muṇḍa. 2.1.4) iti /
tacca parameśvarasyaivocitaṃ, sarvavikārakāraṇatvāt /
na śārīrasya tanumahimnaḥ /
nāpi pradhānasyāyaṃ rūpopanyāsaḥ saṃbhavati, sarvabhūtāntarātmatvāsaṃbhavāt /
tasmātparameśvara eva bhūtayonirnetarāviti gamyate /
kathaṃ punarbhūtayonerayaṃ rūpopanyāsa iti gamyate, prakaraṇāt, 'eṣaḥ' iti ca prakṛtānukarṣaṇāt /
bhūtayoniṃ hi prakṛtya 'etasmājjāyate prāṇaḥ', 'eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā' iti vacanaṃ bhūtayoniviṣayameva bhavati /
yathopādhyāyaṃ prakṛtyaitasmādadhīṣvaiṣa vedavedāṅgapāraga iti vacanamupādhyāyaviṣayaṃ bhavati tadvat /
kathaṃ punaradṛśyatvādiguṇakasya bhūtayonervigrahavadrūpaṃ saṃbhavati /
sarvātmatvavivakṣayedamucyate natu vigrahavattvavivakṣayetyadoṣaḥ /
'ahamannamahamannādaḥ' (tai. 3.10.6) ityādivat /
anye punarmanyante- nāyaṃ bhūtayone rūpopanyāsaḥ, jāyamānatvenopanyāsāt /
'etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca /
khaṃ vāyurjyotirāpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī' iti hi pūrvatra prāṇādipṛthivyantaṃ tattvajātaṃ jāyamānatvena niradikṣat /
uttaratrāpi ca 'tasmādagniḥ samidho yaśca sūryaḥ' ityevamādi, 'ataśca sarvā oṣadhayo rasāśca' ityevamantaṃ jāyamānatvenaiva nirdekṣyati /
ihaiva kathamakasmādantarāle bhūtayone rūpamupanyaset /
sarvātmatvamapi sṛṣṭiṃ parisamāpyopadekṣyati- 'puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma' (muṇḍa. 2.1.10) ityādinā /
śrutismṛtyośca trailokyaśarīrasya prajāpaterjanmādi nirdiśyamānamupalabhāmahe- 'hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgne bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt /
sa dādhāra pṛthivī dyāmutemāṃ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema' (ṛ.sa. 10.121.1) iti /
samavartatetyajāyatetyarthaḥ /
tathā 'sa vai puruṣa ucyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'He is called <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: ādikartā sa bhūtānāṃ brahmāgre samavartata' iti ca /
children.translated_text: The first creator of beings, <s>Brahmā</s> came into being in the beginning.'

children.text: vikārapuruṣasyāpi sarvabhūtāntarātmatvaṃ saṃbhavati, prāṇātmanā sarvabhūtānāmadhyātmamavasthānāt /
children.translated_text: Even for the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is a modification [i.e., <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>], being the inner Self of all beings is possible, since he abides within all beings as their <s>prāṇa</s>-self.

children.text: asminpakṣe 'puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma' ityādi sarvarūpopanyāsaḥ parameśvarapratipattiheturiti vyākhyeyam // 23 //
children.translated_text: According to this view, 'This <s>Puruṣa</s> indeed is all this — action' and such — the entire presentation of the cosmic form is to be explained as the reason for recognizing the supreme Lord. // 23 //

Moreover, after '<s>akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ</s>' (beyond the Imperishable is the Supreme), having stated the creation of the categories from <s>prāṇa</s> down to earth with 'From this are born <s>prāṇa</s>,' we see the cosmic form of that very <s>Bhūtayoni</s> being presented, consisting of all modifications: 'Fire is his head, the sun and moon are his eyes, the directions are his ears, the revealed <s>Vedas</s> are his speech, air is his breath, the universe is his heart, from his feet is the earth — he indeed is the inner Self of all beings' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.4). And this is appropriate for the supreme Lord alone, because he is the cause of all modifications. Not for the embodied self, whose greatness is meager. Nor is this presentation of form possible for <s>Pradhāna</s>, because being the inner Self of all beings is not possible [for it]. Therefore, it is understood that the supreme Lord alone is the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, not the other two. How, then, is it understood that this presentation of form belongs to the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>? Because of the context, and because of the reference back to the subject with the word '<s>eṣaḥ</s>' (this). For having taken the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> as the subject, the statements 'From this are born <s>prāṇa</s>...' and 'This is the inner Self of all beings' pertain to the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> alone. Just as when a teacher is taken as the subject, the statement 'Study from him; this one is proficient in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>' pertains to the teacher — similarly here. But how can a bodily form be possible for the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, who possesses qualities such as invisibility? This is said with the intention of expressing his being the Self of all, not with the intention of expressing his having a body — hence there is no fault. Like 'I am food, I am the eater of food' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.10.6) and such [passages]. Others, however, maintain: This is not a presentation of the form of the <s>Bhūtayoni</s>, because [these entities] are presented as being born [from him]. For in the preceding [verse], 'From this are born <s>prāṇa</s>, mind, all the sense organs, space, air, fire, water, and earth, the sustainer of all' — the entire set of categories from <s>prāṇa</s> to earth was indicated as being born. And subsequently too, 'From him [arises] fire, whose fuel is the sun' and so forth, ending with 'And from him all herbs and their essences' — [these] will be indicated as being born. How then could one suddenly, in the middle, present a form of the <s>Bhūtayoni</s> without any reason? And the teaching that he is the Self of all will be given after completing [the description of] creation: 'This <s>Puruṣa</s> indeed is all this — action...' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.10) and so forth. And in scripture and <s>smṛti</s>, we find the origination and such of <s>Prajāpati</s>, who has the three worlds as his body, being described: '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> came into being at the beginning; born, he was the one lord of creation. He upheld this earth and this heaven — to which god shall we offer oblation?' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.121.1). '<s>Samavartatā</s>' means 'was born.'

children.text: FN: agnirdyulokaḥ vivṛtā veda vāk, padbhyāṃ pādau /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Agni</s>' is the celestial world; '<s>vivṛtā vedā vāk</s>' means speech [is] the revealed <s>Vedas</s>; '<s>padbhyām</s>' means 'from [his] feet.'

children.text: tanumahimno 'lpaśakteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of meager greatness' means 'of little power.'

children.text: yaśca sūryo dyulokāgneḥ samidha iva bhāsakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And the sun' — the illuminator of the celestial world, like fuel for fire.

children.text:
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ agre samavartata /
jātaḥ san bhūtagrāmasyaikaḥ patirbabhūveti śeṣaḥ /
kasmai prajāpataye /
vidhema paricarema /
children.translated_text: '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> came into being in the beginning.' 'Born, he became the one lord of the host of beings' — this is to be supplied. 'To which [god]' — to <s>Prajāpati</s>. '<s>Vidhema</s>' means 'let us serve.'

children.text: vaiśvānarādhikaraṇam / sū. 24-32
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśvānara Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>). <s>Sūtras</s> 24-32.

children.text: vaiśvānaraḥ sādhāraṇaśabdaviśeṣāt | BBs_1,2.24 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiśvānara</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of the particular [meaning of the] common word. | <s>BBs</s> 1,2.24 |

children.text: 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma' iti, 'ātmānamevemaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ saṃpratyadhyeṣi tameva no brūhi' (chā. 5.11.1,6) iti copakramya dyusūryavāyvākāśavāripṛthivīnāṃ sutejastvādiguṇayogamekaikopāsananindayā ca vaiśvānaraṃ pratyeṣāṃ mūrdhādibhāvamupadiśyāmnāyate-
children.translated_text: Having commenced with 'Who is our Self? What is <s>Brahman</s>?' and 'You are studying this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self — tell us about him' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.11.1, 6), and having rejected the individual meditation on heaven, sun, air, space, water, and earth — each with qualities such as being 'of good lustre' — and having taught the status of each as the head and so forth of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, [the scripture] records —

children.text:
'yastvetamevaṃ prādeśamātramabhivimānamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaramupāḥse sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣvātmasvannamatti tasya ha vā etasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāścakṣurviśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā saṃdeho bahulo bastireva rayiḥ pṛthivyeva pādāvura eva vedirlomāni barhirhṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo mano 'nvāhāryapacana āsyamāvahanīyaḥ' (chā. 5.18.2) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kiṃ vaiśvānaraśabdena jāṭharo 'gnirupadiśyata uta bhūtāgniratha tadabhimāninī devatā athavā śārīra āhosvitparameśvara iti /
kiṃ punaratra saṃśayakāraṇam /
vaiśvānara iti jāṭharabhūtāgnidevatānāṃ sādhāraṇaśabdaprayogādātmeti ca śārīraparameśvarayoḥ /
tatra kasyopādānaṃ nyāyyaṃ kasya vā hānamiti bhavati saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam, jāṭharo 'gniriti /
kutaḥ /
tatra hi viśeṣaṇa kvacitprayogo dṛśyate- 'ayamagnirvaiśvānaro yo 'yamantaḥ puruṣe yenedamannaṃ pacyate yadidamadyate' (bṛha. 5.9) ityādau /
agnimātraṃ vā syāt, sāmānyenāpi prayogadarśanāt 'viśvasmā agniṃ bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaraṃ ketumahnāmakṛṇvan' (ṛ.saṃ. 10.88.12) ityādau /
agniśarīrā vā devatā syāt, tasyāmapi prayogadarśanāt 'vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma rājā hi kaṃ bhuvanānāmabhiśrīḥ' (ṛ.saṃ. 1.18.1) ityevamādyāyāḥ śruterdevatāyāmaiśvaryādyupetāyāṃ saṃbhavāt /
athātmaśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyādupakrame ca 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma' iti kevalātmaśabdaprayogādātmaśabdavaśena ca vaiśvānaraśabdaḥ pariṇeya ityucyate, tathāpi śārīra ātmā syāt, tasya bhauktṛtvena vaiśvānarasaṃnikarṣāt /
prādeśamātramiti ca viśeṣaṇasya tasminnupādhiparicchinne saṃbhavāt /
tasmānneśvaro vaiśvānara ityevaṃ prāpte tata idamucyate- vaiśvānaraḥ paramātmā bhavitumarhatīti /
kutaḥ, sādhāraṇaśabdaviśeṣāt /
sādhāraṇaśabdayorviśeṣaḥ sādhāraṇaśabdaviśeṣaḥ /
yadyapyetāvubhāvapyātmavaiśvānaraśabdau sādhāraṇaśabdau, vaiśvānaraśabdastu trayasya sādhāraṇaḥ, ātmaśabdaśca dvayasya tathāpi viśeṣo dṛśyate, yena parameśvaraparatvaṃ tayorabhyupagamyate, 'tasya ha vā etasyāmātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāḥ' ityādi /
atra hi parameśvara eva dyumūrdhatvādiviśiṣṭo 'vasthāntaragataḥ pratyagātmatvenopanyasta ādhyānāyeti gamyate, kāraṇatvāt /
kāraṇasya hi sarvābhiḥ kāryagatābhiravasthābhiravasthāvattvāddyulokādyavayavatvamupapadyate /
'sa sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣvātmasvannamatti' iti ca sarvalokādyāśrayaṃ phalaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ paramakāraṇaparigrahe saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: 'He eats food in all worlds, in all beings, in all selves' — this fruit, heard as depending on all worlds and such, is possible only when the supreme cause is adopted.

children.text: 'evaṃ hāsya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante' (chā. 5.24.3) iti ca tadvidaḥ sarvapāpmapradāhaśravaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Thus all his sins are burned away' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.24.3) — the hearing of the burning away of all sins of one who knows that [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] [also supports this].

children.text: 'ko na ātmā kiṃ brahma' iti cātmabrahmaśabdābhyāmupakrama ityevametāni liṅgāni parameśvaramevāvagamayanti /
children.translated_text: 'Who is our Self? What is <s>Brahman</s>?' — the introduction with the words '<s>ātman</s>' and '<s>Brahman</s>.' Thus, these indicatory marks lead to the understanding of the supreme Lord alone.

children.text: tasmātparameśvara eva vaiśvānaraḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the supreme Lord alone. // 24 //

'But he who meditates on this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self, measured by a span, as the Self that perceives directly — he eats food in all worlds, in all beings, in all selves. Of this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self, the head is indeed the luminous [heaven], the eye is the manifold [sun], the breath is the diversely moving [air], the trunk is the abundant [atmosphere], the bladder is indeed wealth [water], the feet are the earth, the chest is the altar, the hairs are the sacrificial grass, the heart is the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire, the mind is the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> fire, the mouth is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.2) and so forth. There the doubt arises: is the word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' teaching the digestive fire, or the elemental fire, or the deity presiding over it, or the embodied self, or the supreme Lord? What then is the cause of the doubt? Because the word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' is used in common for the digestive fire, the elemental fire, and the deity; and the word '<s>ātman</s>' for both the embodied self and the supreme Lord. The doubt is: which of these is it proper to adopt, and which to reject? What then is the prima facie view? The digestive fire. Why? Because the qualifying usage of [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is sometimes seen in that sense: 'This fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which is within a person, by which this food that is eaten is digested' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.9) and so forth. Or it might be fire in general, since general usage is also seen: 'The gods made fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — the banner of days — for all the world and all beings' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.88.12) and so forth. Or the deity having fire as its body, since usage for that too is seen: 'May we be in the grace of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, for he is king, the splendor of worlds' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 1.18.1) — from such scripture, being tenable for a deity endowed with sovereignty and such. Now, if it is said that because of the co-reference with the word '<s>ātman</s>', and because in the introduction only the word '<s>ātman</s>' is used — 'Who is our Self? What is <s>Brahman</s>?' — the word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' should be interpreted in accordance with the word '<s>ātman</s>' — even so, it would be the embodied self, because of its proximity to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> through being the enjoyer. And the qualifier 'measured by a span' is possible for the [self] delimited by limiting adjuncts. Therefore, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is not the Lord — with this position reached, it is said: <s>Vaiśvānara</s> can only be the supreme Self. Why? Because of the specific meaning of the common words. The specific meaning of the common words is: although both the words '<s>ātman</s>' and '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' are common terms — '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' being common to three [referents] and '<s>ātman</s>' to two — nevertheless, a specification is seen by which the reference of both to the supreme Lord is accepted: 'Of this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> Self, the head is indeed the luminous [heaven]' and so forth. For here, the supreme Lord alone, qualified by having the heavens as his head and such, is understood as being presented in another state — as the inner Self — for the purpose of meditation, because he is the cause. For the cause, being present in all states of its effects, can fittingly have the heavenly world and such as its limbs.

children.text:
FN: ko na iti /
prācīnaśālasatyayajñendradyumnajanabuḍilāḥ sametyetthaṃ mīmāṃsāṃ cakruḥ kekayarājaṃ gatvā /
adhyeṣi smarasi /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Who [is our Self]?' — <s>Prācīnaśāla</s>, <s>Satyayajña</s>, <s>Indradyumna</s>, <s>Jana</s>, and <s>Buḍila</s>, having assembled, deliberated thus and went to king <s>Kekayas</s>. 'Do you study? Do you remember?'

children.text:
ābhimukhyenāparokṣatayā viśvaṃ mimīte jānātītyabhivimānastam /
saṃdeho dehasya madhyabhāgaḥ /
rayirdhanam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Abhivimāna</s>' — he who directly (<s>abhimukhyena</s>), non-mediately (<s>aparokṣatayā</s>), measures (knows) all — [the Self] is that. '<s>Saṃdeha</s>' — the middle portion of the body. '<s>Rayi</s>' — wealth.

children.text:
viśvasmai bhuvanāya vaiśvānaramagnimahnāṃ ketuṃ cihnaṃ sūryamakṛṇvandevāḥ /
tadudaye dinavyavahārāt /
children.translated_text: 'The gods made <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire the banner (<s>ketu</s>) of days — the sun — for all the world and all beings.' Because of it, at sunrise, the day's transactions [begin].

children.text:
vaiśvānarasya devasya sumatau śobhanabuddhau vayaṃ syāma bhavema /
tasyāsmadvaṣayā sumatirbhavatvityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May we be in the grace — the favorable disposition — of the god <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.' The meaning is: may his favorable disposition be directed toward us.

children.text: avasthāntaramadhyātmamadhidaivamityevaṃrūpam /
children.translated_text: 'Another state' means such forms as the cosmic (<s>adhidaiva</s>) and individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) [perspectives].

children.text: yathāgnau nikṣiptamiṣīkātūlaṃ dahyate evaṃ hāsya viduṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a tuft of cotton cast into fire is burned — so too [the sins] of this knower.

children.text: smaryamāṇam anumānaṃ syād iti | BBs_1,2.25 |
children.translated_text: <s>Smaryamāṇam anumānaṃ syād iti</s> — The inference [is drawn] from what is remembered [in <s>smṛti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.25 |

children.text: itaśca parameśvara eva vaiśvānaraḥ, yasmātparameśvarasyaivāgnirāsyaṃ dyaurmūrdhetīdṛśaṃ trailokyātmakaṃ rūpaṃ smaryate- 'yasyāgnirāsyaṃ dyaurmūrdhā khaṃ nābhiścaraṇau kṣitiḥ /
children.translated_text: For this further reason too, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the supreme Lord — because such a form, consisting of the three worlds, with fire as the mouth and heaven as the head, is remembered only of the supreme Lord: 'He whose mouth is fire, whose head is heaven, whose navel is space, and whose feet are the earth,

children.text: sūryaścakṣurdiśaḥ śrotraṃ tasmai lokātmane namaḥ //
children.translated_text: whose eye is the sun, whose ears are the directions — homage to that <s>Lokātman</s> (Soul of the World)!'

children.text:
' iti /
etatsmaryamāṇaṃ rūpaṃ mūlabhūtāṃ śrutimanumāpayadasya vauśvānaraśabdasya parameśvaraparatve 'numānaṃ liṅgaṃ gamakaṃ syādityarthaḥ /
itiśdo hetvarthaḥ /
yasmādidaṃ gamakaṃ tasmādapi vaiśvānaraḥ paramātmaivetyarthaḥ /
yadyapi stutiriyaṃ 'tasmai lokātmane namaḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: Even though this is a praise — 'Homage to that Soul of the World.'

children.text: stutitvamapi nāsati mūlabhūte vedavākye samāyagīdṛśena rūpeṇa saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Even being a praise does not arise in a form such as this without a root Vedic statement.

children.text: 'dyāṃ mūrdhānaṃ yasya viprā vadanti khaṃ vai nābhiṃ candrasūryau ca netre /
children.translated_text: 'He whose head the wise call the sky, whose navel is space, whose eyes are the moon and sun,

children.text: diśaḥ śrotre viddhi pādau kṣitiṃ ca so 'cintyātmā sarvabhūtapraṇetā //
children.translated_text: whose ears are the directions, and whose feet are the earth — he, the inconceivable Self, is the impeller of all beings.'

This remembered form, implying a root <s>śruti</s>, serves as an inference — an indicatory mark, a pointer — for the reference of this word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' to the supreme Lord. The word '<s>iti</s>' has the sense of reason. The meaning is: since this is a pointer, therefore too <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the supreme Self alone.

children.text: ' ityevañjātīyakā ca smṛtirihodāhartavyā // 25 //
children.translated_text: Such <s>smṛti</s> passages of this kind should also be cited here. // 25 //

children.text: śabdādibhyo 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhānāc ca neti cen na tathā dṛṣṭyupadeśād asambhavāt puruṣamapi cainam adhīyate | BBs_1,2.26 |
children.translated_text: <s>Śabdādibhyo 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhānāc ca neti cen na tathā dṛṣṭyupadeśād asambhavāt puruṣam api cainam adhīyate</s> — If [it be said] 'no, because of the words and such, and because of being established within' — [we say] no, because thus [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is taught as a mode of contemplation, because [the alternative interpretation is] impossible, and because they also recite this [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] as a <s>Puruṣa</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.26 |

children.text:

kutaḥ, śabdādibhyo 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhānācca /
śabdastāvadvaiśvānaraśabdo na parameśvare saṃbhavati, arthāntare rūḍhatvāt /
tathāgniśabdaḥ 'sa eṣo 'gnirvaiśvānaraḥ' iti /

yadapyuktaṃ- mūrdhaiva sutejā ityāderviśeṣātkāraṇātparamātmā vaiśvānara iti /
atra brūmaḥ- kuto hyeṣa nirṇayaḥ, yadubhayathāpi viśeṣapratibhāne sati parameśvaraviṣaya eva viśeṣa āśrayaṇīyo na jāṭharaviṣaya iti /
athavā bhūtāgnerantarbahiścāvatiṣṭhamānasyaiṣa nirdeśo bhaviṣyati /
tasyāpi hi dyulokādisaṃbandho mantravarṇādavagamyate- 'yo bhānunā pṛthivī dyāmutemāmātatāna rodasī antarikṣam' (ṛ.sa. 10.88.3) ityādau /
athavā taccharīrāyā devatāyā aiśvaryayogāddyulokādyavayavatvaṃ bhaviṣyati /
tasmānna parameśvaro vaiśvānara iti /
atrocyate- na tathādṛṣṭyupadeśāditi /
na śabdādibhyaḥ kāraṇebhyaḥ parameśvarasya pratyākhyānaṃ yuktam /
kutaḥ, tathā jāṭharāparityāgena dṛṣṭyupadeśāt /
parameśvaradṛṣṭirhi jāṭhare vaiśvānara ihopadiśyate, 'mano brahmetyupāsīta' (chā. 3.18.1) ityādivat /
athavā jāṭharavaiśvānaropādhibhiḥ parameśvara iha draṣṭavyatvenopadiśyate, 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityādivat /
yadi ceha parameśvaro na vivakṣyeta kevala eva jāṭharo 'gnirvivakṣyeta tato mūrdhaiva sutejā ityādirviśeṣasyāsaṃbhava eva syāt /
yathā tu devatābhūtāgnivyapāśrayeṇāpyayaṃ viśeṣa upapādayituṃ na śakyate tathottarasūtre vakṣyāmaḥ /
yadi ca kevala eva jāṭharo vivakṣyeta, puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitatvaṃ kevalaṃ tasya syānna tu puruṣatvam /
puruṣamapi cainamadhīyate vājasaneyinaḥ- 'sa eṣo 'gnirvaiśvānaro yatpuruṣaḥ sa yo haitamevamagniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' (śa.brā. 10.6.1.11) iti /
parameśvarasya tu sarvātmatvātpuruṣatvaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitatvaṃ cobhayamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: But for the supreme Lord, because of being the Self of all, both the character of being a <s>Puruṣa</s> and being established within a person are tenable.

children.text: ye tu 'puruṣavidhamapi cainamadhīyate' iti sūtrāvayavaṃ paṭhanti, teṣāmeṣor'thaḥ- kevalajāṭharaparigrahe puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitatvaṃ kevalaṃ syānna puruṣavidhatvam /
children.translated_text: Those who read the <s>sūtra</s>-component as '<s>puruṣavidham api cainam adhīyate</s>' — for them the meaning is this: if only the digestive fire were adopted, being established within a person would apply to it, but not the character of having the form of a person.

children.text: puruṣavidhamapi cainamadhīyate vājasaneyinaḥ- 'puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' iti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> also recite this as having the form of a person: 'having the form of a person, established within a person.'

children.text: puruṣavidhatvaṃ ca prakaraṇādyadadhidaivataṃ dyumūrdhatvādi pṛthivīpratiṣṭhitatvāntaṃ, yaccādhyātmaṃ prasiddhaṃ mūrdhatvādi cubukapratiṣṭhitatvāntaṃ tatparigṛhyate // 26 //
children.translated_text: The 'form of a person' is, from the context, understood to include both the cosmic [perspective] — having the heavens as the head and such, ending with being established on the earth — and the individual [perspective] — the well-known head and such, ending with being established on the chin. // 26 //

Here an objection is raised: The supreme Lord cannot be <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. Why? Because of the words and such, and because of being established within. First, the word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' cannot apply to the supreme Lord, since it is fixed in another meaning. Likewise, the word '<s>Agni</s>' in 'This is the fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.' From the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.): 'the heart is the <s>Gārhapatya</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.2) and such — the elaboration of the three sacrificial fires. And 'The first [portion] of what is eaten should be offered' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1) and such — the mention of being the basis for the <s>prāṇa</s>-offerings. From these reasons, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> should be understood as the digestive fire. Also, being 'established within' is heard: 'one who knows [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] as established within a person.' And that is possible for the digestive fire. As for the argument that because of the specification 'the head is the luminous [heaven]' and such, being the cause, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the supreme Self — to this we say: On what basis is this determination made, that when specification is apparent in both ways, the specification referring to the supreme Lord alone should be adopted, not the one referring to the digestive fire? Or alternatively, this description would apply to the elemental fire, which is established both within and outside. For its connection with the heavenly world and such is understood from <s>mantra</s> texts: 'He who by his radiance pervaded the earth, the sky, and both heaven and earth and the atmosphere' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.88.3) and so forth. Or, the deity having fire as its body, because of possessing sovereignty, could have the heavenly world and such as its limbs. Therefore, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is not the supreme Lord. To this it is said: 'No, because thus [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is taught as a mode of contemplation.' The rejection of the supreme Lord on the grounds of words and such is not justified. Why? Because thus — without abandoning the digestive fire — the contemplation of the supreme Lord is taught [here]. For the vision of the supreme Lord in the digestive <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is what is taught here — as in 'one should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.1) and such. Or alternatively, the supreme Lord is taught here as to be contemplated through the limiting adjuncts of the digestive <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — as in 'made of mind, having <s>prāṇa</s> as the body, having light as the form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and such. If the supreme Lord were not intended here, and only the mere digestive fire were intended, then the specification 'the head is the luminous [heaven]' and such would simply be impossible. And how even by relying on the deity and the elemental fire this specification cannot be justified — that we shall state in the next <s>sūtra</s>. And if only the mere digestive fire were intended, being established within a person would apply to it alone, but not the character of being a <s>Puruṣa</s>. And the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> also recite this as a <s>Puruṣa</s>: 'This is the fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s> which is the <s>Puruṣa</s>. He who knows this fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — having the form of a person, established within a person' (<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 10.6.1.11).

children.text: FN: bhaktamannaṃ homīyaṃ homasādhanaṃ tena prāṇāgnihotraṃ kāryamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Bhakta</s>' means eaten food; '<s>homīya</s>' means to be used for offering — the meaning is: thereby the <s>prāṇa-agnihotra</s> (offering to the vital breaths) should be performed.

children.text:
imāṃ pṛthivīmuta dyāmapi dyāvāpṛthivyāveva rodasī yo bhānurūpeṇātatāna vyāptavān /
antarikṣaṃ ca tayormadhyamātatāna sa devo dyulokādyavayavo dhyeya ityarthaḥ /
