children.translated_text: 'This earth and also the sky' — he who by his luminous form '<s>ātatāna</s>' (pervaded) earth and heaven, the two <s>rodasī</s>, and the atmosphere between them — that god, having the heavenly world and such as his limbs, is to be meditated upon — this is the meaning.

children.text:
yat yaḥ /
puruṣaḥ pūrṇaḥ /
yo veda sa sarvatra bhuṅkte /
children.translated_text: '<s>Yat</s>' means 'who.' '<s>Puruṣa</s>' means 'the complete one.' He who knows thus — he enjoys everywhere.

children.text: ata eva na devatā bhūtaṃ ca | BBs_1,2.27 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ata eva na devatā bhūtaṃ ca</s> — For this very reason, [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is neither the deity nor the element [fire]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.27 |

children.text:
yatpunaruktaṃ bhūtāgnerapi mantravarṇe dyulokādisaṃbandhadarśanānmūrdhaiva sutejā ityādyavayavakalpanaṃ tasyaiva bhaviṣyatīti, yaccharīrāyā devatāyā vaiśvaryayogāditi, tatparihartavyam /
atrocyate- ata evoktebhyo hetubhyo na devatā vaiśvānaraḥ /
tathābhūtāgnirapi na vaiśvānaraḥ /
nahi bhūtāgnerauṣṇyaprakāśamātrātmakasya dyumūrdhatvādikalpanopapadyate, vikārasya vikārāntarātmatvāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: For the attribution of the heavens as the head and such is not tenable for the elemental fire, whose nature is merely heat and light — because one modification cannot have the nature of another modification.

children.text: tathā devatāyāḥ satyapyaiśvaryayoge na dyumūrdhatvādikalpanā saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even though the deity possesses sovereignty, the attribution of the heavens as the head and such is not possible for it.

children.text: akāraṇatvātparameśvarādhīnaiśvaryatvācca /
children.translated_text: Because it is not the [ultimate] cause, and because its sovereignty depends on the supreme Lord.

children.text: ātmaśabdāsaṃbhavaśca sarveṣveṣu pakṣeṣu sthita eva // 27 //
children.translated_text: And the impossibility of the word '<s>ātman</s>' [applying to them] holds in all these positions. // 27 //

As for the statement that because the connection of the elemental fire with the heavenly world and such is seen in the <s>mantra</s> texts, the attribution of limbs such as 'the head is the luminous [heaven]' would apply to it; and that for the deity having fire as its body, because of possessing sovereignty [this would hold] — that must be refuted. To this it is said: For the very reasons stated, the deity is not <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. Likewise, the elemental fire too is not <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: sākṣād apy avirodhaṃ jaiminiḥ | BBs_1,2.28 |
children.translated_text: <s>Sākṣād apy avirodhaṃ Jaiminiḥ</s> — <s>Jaimini</s> [holds] that there is no contradiction even in direct [worship of the supreme Lord]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.28 |

children.text:
pūrve jāṭharāgnipratīko jāṭharāgnyupādhiko vā parameśvara upāsya ityuktamantaḥpratiṣṭhitatvādyanurodhena /
idānīṃ tu vinaiva pratīkopādhikalpanābhyāṃ sākṣādapi parameśvaropāsanaparigrahe na kaścidvirodha iti jaiminirācāryo manyante /
children.translated_text: Previously it was said that the supreme Lord is to be meditated upon either as having the digestive fire as a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>), or as having the digestive fire as a limiting adjunct — in conformity with the statement of being 'established within' and such. But now, even without imagining either a symbol or a limiting adjunct, there is no contradiction in directly adopting the worship of the supreme Lord — so the teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds.

children.text: nanu jāṭharāgnyaparigrahe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitatvavacanaṃ śabdadīni ca kāraṇāni virudhyeranniti /
children.translated_text: But if the digestive fire is not adopted, would not the statement about being 'established within,' and the reasons such as the words, be contradicted?

children.text:
atrocyate- antaḥpratiṣṭhitatvavacanaṃ tāvanna virudhyate /
nahīha 'puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' iti jāṭharāgnyabhiprāyeṇedamucyate /
tasyāprakṛtatvādasaṃśabditatvācca /
kathaṃ tarhi yatprakṛtaṃ mūrdhādicubukānteṣu puruṣāvayaveṣu puruṣavidhitvaṃ kalpitaṃ tadabhiprāyeṇedamucyate- 'puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' iti /
children.translated_text: To this we say: the statement of being 'established within' is first not contradictory. For the statement 'one who knows it as person-shaped, established within the person' is not made here with reference to the gastric fire. Because it [the gastric fire] is not the topic and has not been mentioned. How then? With reference to the person-shaped form attributed to the bodily limbs from the head to the chin, which is the topic under discussion — with this intention it is stated: 'One who knows it as person-shaped, established within the person.'

children.text:
yathā vṛkṣe śākhāṃ pratiṣṭhitāṃ paśyatīti tadvat /
athavā yaḥ prakṛtaḥ paramātmādhyātmamadhidaivataṃ ca puruṣavidhitvopādhistasya yatkevalaṃ sākṣirūpaṃ tadabhiprāyeṇedamucyate- 'puruṣe 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhitaṃ veda' iti /
niścite ca pūrvāparālocanavaśena paramātmaparigrahe tadviṣaya eva vaiśvānaraśabdaḥ kenacidyogena vartiṣyate /
viśvaścāyaṃ naraśceti, viśveṣāṃ vāyaṃ naraḥ, viśve vā narā asyeti viśvānaraḥ, paramātmā, sarvātmatvāt /
viśvānara eva vaiśvānaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvānara</s> itself is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: taddhito 'nanyārthaḥ, rākṣasavāyasādivat /
children.translated_text: The <s>taddhita</s> suffix adds no separate meaning, like [the suffixes in] <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Vāyasa</s>, and such.

children.text: agniśabdo 'pyagraṇītvādiyogāśrayaṇena paramātmaviṣaya eva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>Agni</s>' (fire) too, through recourse to etymological derivations such as 'being the foremost,' will apply to the Supreme Self.

children.text: gārhapatyādikalpanaṃ prāṇāhutyadhikaraṇatvaṃ ca paramātmano 'pi sarvātmatvādupapadyate // 28 //
children.translated_text: The attribution of being [the fires] <s>Gārhapatya</s> and such, and being the substrate of the <s>Prāṇāhuti</s> oblations, is also fitting for the Supreme Self, because of His being the Self of all. // 28 //

Like seeing a branch as established in a tree — just so. Or, the Supreme Self, which is the topic, for which the person-shape is a limiting adjunct in both the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) and cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) aspects — with reference to its pure witness-form — this is stated: 'One who knows it as established within the person.' And when the acceptance of the Supreme Self is determined through consideration of what comes before and after, the word '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' will apply to it through some connection. '<s>Viśva</s>' (all) and '<s>nara</s>' (person) — 'He is all and He is a person'; or 'He is the person (<s>nara</s>) of all (<s>viśva</s>)'; or 'all persons (<s>narāḥ</s>) are His' — [thus] <s>Viśvānara</s>, the Supreme Self, because of being the Self of all.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ parameśvaraparigrahe prādeśamātraśrutirupapadyata iti tāṃ vyākhyātumārabhate-
children.translated_text: But how, if the Supreme Lord is accepted, can the <s>śruti</s> statement of being 'a span in measure' be justified? To explain that, he begins —

children.text: FN: antaḥpratiṣṭhitatvaṃ mādhyasthyaṃ sākṣitvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Being established within' — the meaning is: being in the middle, being the witness.

children.text: atra nare 'saṃjñāyā' miti pūrvapadasya dīrghatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the word '<s>nara</s>,' the lengthening of the first member is by the rule 'not in a proper name.'

children.text: ananyārthatvaṃ prakṛtyarthātiriktārthaśūnyatvam /
children.translated_text: 'Not having a separate meaning' means being devoid of any meaning beyond that of the base word.

children.text: abhivyakter ity āśmarathyaḥ | BBs_1,2.29 |
children.translated_text: Because of manifestation — so [holds] <s>Āśmarathya</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.29 |

children.text: atimātrasyāpi parameśvarasya prādeśamātratvamabhivyaktinimittaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Even for the Supreme Lord, who is beyond all measure, being 'a span in measure' could be due to manifestation.

children.text: abhivyajyate kila prādeśamātraparimāṇaḥ parameśvara upāsakānāṃ kṛte /
children.translated_text: Namely, the Supreme Lord manifests as having the measure of a span for the sake of the meditators.

children.text: pradeśeṣu vā hṛdayādiṣūpalabdhisthāneṣu viśeṣaṇābhivyajyate /
children.translated_text: Or, in specific locations — the heart and such — which are the places of apprehension, a specific [form] is manifested.

children.text: ataḥ parameśvare 'pi prādeśamātraśrutirabhivyakterupapadyata ityāśmarathya ācāryo manyate // 29 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even for the Supreme Lord, the <s>śruti</s> statement of being 'a span in measure' is justified because of manifestation — so holds teacher <s>Āśmarathya</s>. // 29 //

children.text: FN: atikrāntā mātrāḥ parimāṇaṃ yasya tasyeti yāvat /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Beyond all measure' means: one whose measures, i.e., dimensions, are transcended — this is the meaning.

children.text: pradeśeṣu vā mīyata iti prādeśamātraḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, 'a span in measure' means: one who is measured in specific locations.

children.text: anusmṛter bādariḥ | BBs_1,2.30 |
children.translated_text: Because of being recollected — so [holds] <s>Bādari</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.30 |

children.text:
prādeśamātrahṛdayapratiṣṭhena vāyaṃ manasānusmaryate tena prādeśamātra ityucyate /
yathā prasthamitāyavāḥ prasthā ityucyante tadvat /
yadyapi ca yaveṣu svagatameva parimāṇaṃ prasthasaṃbandhādvyajyate /
naceha parameśvaragataṃ kiñcitparimāṇamasti yaddhṛdayasaṃbandhādvyajyate /
children.translated_text: here, however, there is no dimension belonging to the Supreme Lord that would be expressed through the connection with the heart.

children.text: tathāpi prayuktāyāḥ pradeśamātraśruteḥ saṃbhavati yathākathañcidanusmaraṇamālambanamityucyate /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, since the employed <s>śruti</s> statement of 'a span in measure' has some basis of recollection, however that may be, this is stated.

children.text: prādeśamātratvena vāyamaprādeśamātro 'pyanusmaraṇīyaḥ prādeśamātraśrutyarthavattāyai /
children.translated_text: Or, though not actually a span in measure, He is to be recollected as a span in measure, so that the <s>śruti</s> statement 'a span in measure' may have meaning.

children.text: evamanusmṛtinimittā parameśvare prādeśamātraśrutiriti bādarirācāryo manyate // 30 //
children.translated_text: Thus, teacher <s>Bādari</s> holds that the <s>śruti</s> statement of being 'a span in measure' with regard to the Supreme Lord is caused by recollection. // 30 //

Or, He is recollected through the mind as established in the heart that is a span in measure — therefore He is called 'a span in measure.' Just as barley measured by a <s>prastha</s> measure are called '<s>prasthas</s>' — similarly. And although the barley possess their own intrinsic dimension, which is expressed through the connection with the <s>prastha</s> measure,

children.text:
FN: prādeśena manasā mīyata iti vā /
prayuktāyāstadarthe vartamānāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Or, measured by the mind that is a span.' '<s>Prayuktāyāḥ</s>' — of that which is employed, i.e., which functions for that purpose.

children.text: saṃpatter iti jaiminis tathā hi darśayati | BBs_1,2.31 |
children.translated_text: Because of meditation (<s>saṃpatti</s>) — so [holds] <s>Jaimini</s>; for thus [scripture] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.31 |

children.text:
saṃpattinimittā vā syātprādeśamātraśrutiḥ /
kutaḥ /
tathāhi- samānaprakaraṇaṃ vājasaneyibrāhmaṇaṃ dyuprabhṛtīnpṛthivīparyantāṃstrailokyātmano vaiśvānarasyāvayavānadhyātmamūrdhaprabhṛtiṣu cubukaparyanteṣu dehāvayaveṣu saṃpādayatprādeśamātrasaṃpattiṃ parameśvarasya darśayati- 'prādeśamātramiva ha vai devāḥ suviditā abhisaṃpannāstathā nu va etānvakṣyāmi yathā prādeśamātramevābhisaṃpādayiṣyāmīti /
sa hovāca mūrdhānamupadiśannuvācaiṣa vā atiṣṭhā vaiśvānara iti /
cakṣuṣī upadiśannuvācaiṣa vai sutejā vaiśvānara iti /
nāsike upadiśannuvācaiṣa vai pṛthagvartmātmā vaiśvānara iti /
mukhyamākāśamupadiśannuvācaiṣa vai bahulo vaiśvanara iti /
mukhyā apa upadiśannuvācaiṣa vai rayirvaiśvānara iti /
cubukamupadiśannuvācaiṣa vai pratiṣṭhā' iti /
cubukamityadharaṃ mukhaphalakamucyate /
yadyapi vājasaneyake dyauratiṣṭhātvaguṇāsamāmnāyata ādityaśca sutejastvaguṇaḥ /
chāndogye punardyaiḥ sutejastvaguṇā samāmnāyata ādityaśca viśvarūpaguṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, on the other hand, the sky is taught with the attribute of being <s>Sutejā</s> and the sun with the attribute of being <s>Viśvarūpa</s> (universal form).

children.text: tathāpi naitāvatā viśeṣeṇa kiñciddhīyate, prādeśamātraśruteraviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, nothing is diminished by this much difference, since the <s>śruti</s> statement of 'a span in measure' makes no distinction.

children.text: sarvaśākhāpratyayatvācca /
children.translated_text: And because it is recognized across all branches of the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: saṃpattinimittāṃ prādeśamātraśrutiṃ yuktatarāṃ jaimnirācāryo manyate // 31 //
children.translated_text: Teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds that the <s>śruti</s> statement of 'a span in measure' caused by meditation is more reasonable. // 31 //

Or, the <s>śruti</s> statement of being 'a span in measure' could be due to meditation (<s>saṃpatti</s>). Why? For thus — the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s>, which is on the same topic, shows the meditation of 'a span in measure' for the Supreme Lord by meditationally assigning the limbs of the three-world-Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — the sky and such down to the earth — to the bodily limbs from the head to the chin in the individual aspect: 'O gods, you indeed know the well-known [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] as meditated upon to be a span in measure. Thus indeed I shall explain to you how I shall make it a span in meditation. He [<s>Aśvapati</s>] said, pointing to the head: "This indeed is <s>Atiṣṭhā</s> (the one standing above), the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>." Pointing to the eyes: "This indeed is <s>Sutejā</s> (the brilliant one), the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>." Pointing to the nostrils: "This indeed is <s>Pṛthagvartmā</s> (the one of separate paths), the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>." Pointing to the space within the mouth: "This indeed is <s>Bahula</s> (the abundant one), the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>." Pointing to the waters in the mouth: "This indeed is <s>Rayi</s> (wealth), the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>." Pointing to the chin: "This indeed is <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (the foundation)."' The chin (<s>cubuka</s>) refers to the lower plate of the mouth. Although in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> recension, the sky is taught with the attribute of being <s>Atiṣṭhā</s> and the sun with the attribute of being <s>Sutejā</s>,

children.text: āmananti cainam asmin | BBs_1,2.32 |
children.translated_text: And the <s>Jābālas</s> teach of Him in this [location]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.2.32 |

children.text:
āmananti cainaṃ parameśvaramasminmūrdhacubukāntarāle jābālāḥ- 'ya eṣo 'nto 'vyakta ātmā so 'vimukte pratiṣṭhita iti /
so 'vimuktaḥ kasminpratiṣṭhita iti /
varaṇāyāṃ nāsyāṃ ca madhye pratiṣṭhita iti /
kā vai varaṇā kā ca nāsīti' /
tatra cemāmeva nāsikāṃ varaṇā nāsīti nirucya yā sarvāṇīndriyakṛtāni pāpāni vārayatīti sā varaṇā, sarvāṇīndriyakṛtāni pāpāni nāśayatīti sā nāsīti /
punarāmananti- 'ka tamaccāsya sthānaṃ bhavatīti /
bhruvordhāraṇasya ca yaḥ saṃdhiḥ sa eṣa dyulokasya parasya ca saṃdhirbhavatīti' (jābā. 1) /
tasmādupapannā parameśvare prādeśamātraśrutiḥ /
abhivimānaśrutiḥ pratyagātmatvābhiprāyā /
pratyagātmatayā sarvaiḥ prāṇibhirabhivimīyata ityabhimānaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Jābālas</s> teach of Him — the Supreme Lord — in this space between the head and the chin: 'This unmanifest inner Self is established in <s>Avimukta</s>. In what is <s>Avimukta</s> established? It is established between <s>Varaṇā</s> and <s>Nāsī</s>. What indeed is <s>Varaṇā</s> and what is <s>Nāsī</s>?' And there, [the text] etymologically explains <s>Varaṇā</s> and <s>Nāsī</s> as this very nose: 'That which wards off (<s>vārayati</s>) all sins committed by the senses — that is <s>Varaṇā</s>. That which destroys (<s>nāśayati</s>) all sins committed by the senses — that is <s>Nāsī</s>.' Again they teach: 'What then is the place and location for that [meditation]? The junction of the eyebrows and the bridge of the nose — that is the junction of this world and the yonder world' (<s>Jābāla</s> 1). Therefore, the <s>śruti</s> statement of being 'a span in measure' is justified with respect to the Supreme Lord. The <s>śruti</s> statement of 'self-cognition' (<s>abhivimāna</s>) has its intention in the inner Self. [The Supreme Lord] is cognized by all living beings as the inner Self — this is the [meaning of] self-cognition (<s>abhimāna</s>).

children.text:
abhigato vāyaṃ pratyagātmatvādvimānaśca mānaviyogādityabhivimānaḥ /
abhivimimīyate vā sarve jagatkāraṇatvādityabhivimānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, He is 'reached' (<s>abhigata</s>) because of being the inner Self, and 'beyond measure' (<s>vimāna</s>) because of being free from measures — this is <s>abhivimāna</s>. Or, He is measured out (<s>abhivimimīyate</s>), i.e., created, as the entire world, because of being the cause of the universe — this is <s>abhivimāna</s>.

children.text: tasmātparameśvaro vaiśvānara iti siddham // 32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is the Supreme Lord. // 32 //

children.text: iti śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye prathamādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Śārīraka Mīmāṃsā Bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 2 //

children.text: FN: avimukte avidyopādhikalpitāvacchede jīvātmi bhedakalpanayā pratiṣṭhita upāsyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'In <s>Avimukta</s>' — in the limited [space], the individual Self produced by the limiting adjunct of <s>avidyā</s>, He is to be meditated upon as established through the imagination of difference.

children.text: varaṇā bhrūḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Varaṇā</s>' is the eyebrow.

children.text: vimīyate jñāyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vimīyate</s>' means 'is known.'

children.text: abhivimīmīte nirmimīte /
children.translated_text: '<s>Abhivimīmīte</s>' means 'creates.'

children.text: prathamādhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The third <s>pāda</s> of the first <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text:
atrāspaṣṭabrahmaliṅgānāṃ prāyo jñeyabrahmaviṣayāṇāṃ vicāraḥ /
evaṃ pādatrayeṇāpi vākyavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Herein is the investigation of those that have unclear marks of <s>Brahman</s>, mostly pertaining to the <s>Brahman</s> to be known. Thus, through three <s>pādas</s>, the investigation of [Vedānta
statements is [conducted].]

children.text: 1 dyubhvādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 1-7
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Dyubhvādi Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Sky, Earth, and So Forth) / <s>Sūtras</s> 1-7

children.text: dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ svaśabdāt | BBs_1,3.1 |
children.translated_text: The support (<s>āyatana</s>) of the sky, earth, and so forth [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the proper word (<s>svaśabda</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.1 |

children.text:
idaṃ śrūyate- 'yasmindyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣamotaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiśca sarvaiḥ /
tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānamanyā vāco vimucyathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ' (muṇḍa. 2.2.5) iti /
atra yadetaddyuprabhṛtīnāmotatvavacanādāyatanaṃ kiñcidavagamyate, tatkiṃ paraṃ brahma syādāhosvidarthāntaramiti saṃdihyate /
tatrārthāntaraṃ kimapyāyatanaṃ syāditi prāptam /
kasmāt, 'amṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ' iti śravaṇāt /
pāravānhi loke setuḥ prakhyātaḥ /
naca parasya brahmaṇaḥ pāravattvaṃ śakyamabhyupagantuṃ, 'anantamapāram' (bṛha. 2.4.12) iti śravaṇāt /
arthāntare cāyatane parigṛhyamāṇe smṛtiprasiddhaṃ pradhānaṃ parigrahītavyaṃ, tasya kāraṇatvādāyatanatvopapatteḥ /
śrutiprasiddho vā vāyuḥ syāt, 'vāyurvai gautama tatsūtraṃ vāyunā vai gautama sūtreṇāyaṃ ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavanti' (bṛha. 3.7.2) iti vāyorapi vidhāraṇatvaśravaṇāt /
śārīro vā syāt /
tasyāpi bhoktṛtvādbhogyaṃ prapañcaṃ pratyāyatanatvopapatterityevaṃ prāpta idamāha- dyubhvādyāyatanamiti /
dyauśca bhūśca dyubhuvau dyubhuvāvādī yasya tadidaṃ dyubhvādi /
yadetadasminvākye dyauḥ pṛthivyantarikṣaṃ manaḥ prāṇā ityevamasmākaṃ jagadotatvena nirdiṣṭaṃ tasyāyatanaṃ paraṃ brahma bhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ /
svaśabdāt, ātmaśabdādityarthaḥ /
ātmaśabdo hīha bhavati- 'tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam' iti /
ātmaśabdaśca paramātmaparigrahe samyagavakalpate nārthāntaraparigrahe /
kvacicca svaśabdenaiva brahmaṇa āyatanatvaṃ śrūyate-' sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ' (chā. 6.8.4) iti /
svaśabdenaiva ceha purastādupariṣṭācca brahma saṃkīrtyate- 'puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam' iti /
'brahmaivedamamṛtaṃ purastādbrahma paścādbrahma dakṣiṇaścottareṇa' (muṇḍa. 2.2.11) iti ca /
tatra tvāyatanāyatanayadbhāvaśravaṇāt /
sarvaṃ brahmeti ca sāmānādhikaraṇyāt /
yathānekātmako vṛkṣaḥ śākhā skandho mūlaṃ cetyevaṃ nānāraso vicitra ātmetyāśaṅkā saṃbhavati, tāṃ nivartayituṃ sāvadhāraṇamāha- 'tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam' iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- na kāryaprapañcaviśiṣṭo vicitra ātmā vijñeyaḥ /
kintarhyavidyākṛtaṃ kāryaprapañcaṃ vidyayā pravilāpayantastamevaikamāyatanabhūtamātmānaṃ jānathaikarasamiti /
yathā yasmānnāste devadattastadānayetyukta āsanamevānayati na devadattam /
tadvadāyatanabhūtasyaivaikarasasyātmano vijñeyatvamupadiśyate /
vikārānṛtābhisaṃdhasya cāpavādaḥ śrūyate- 'mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati' (kā. 2.4.11) iti /
sarvaṃ brahmeti tu sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ prapañcapravilāpanārthaṃ nānekarasatāpratipādanārtham /
'sa yathā saindhavaghano 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsno rasaghana evaivaṃ vā are 'yamātmānantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva' (bṛha. 4.5.13) ityekarasatāśravaṇāt /
tasmāddyubhvādyāyatanaṃ paraṃ brahma /
yattūktaṃ, setuśruteḥ setośca pāravattvopapatterbrahmaṇor'thāntareṇa dyubhvādyāyatanena bhavitavyamiti /
atrocyate- vidhāraṇatvamātramatra setuśrutyā vivakṣyate na pāravattvādi /
nahi mṛddārumayo loke seturdṛṣṭa ityatrāpi mṛddārumaya evaseturabhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that because a bridge in the world is seen to be made of clay and wood, the bridge here too must be accepted as being of clay and wood.

children.text: setuśabdārtho 'pi vidhāraṇatvamātrameva na pāravattvādi ṣiño bandhanakarmaṇaḥ setuśabdavyutpatteḥ /
children.translated_text: The etymological meaning of the word '<s>setu</s>' (bridge) is merely 'sustaining,' not 'having a farther shore' and such — because the word '<s>setu</s>' is derived from the root '<s>ṣi</s>' meaning 'to bind.'

children.text: apara āha- 'tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam' iti yadetatsaṃkīrtitamātmajñānaṃ, yaccaitat 'anyā vāco vimuñcatha' iti vāgvimocanaṃ, tadatrāmṛtatvasādhanatvāt, 'amṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ' iti setuśrutyā saṃkīrtyate na tu dyubhvādyāyatanam /
children.translated_text: Another [commentator] says: the knowledge of the Self that was proclaimed thus — 'Know that one alone as the Self' — and the release of speech proclaimed thus — 'Let go of other speech' — this, being a means to immortality, is proclaimed by the <s>śruti</s> on the bridge: 'This is the bridge to immortality' — but not the abode of heaven, earth, and such.

children.text: tatra yaduktaṃ setuśruterbrahmaṇor'thāntareṇa dyubhvādyāyatanena bhāvyamityetadayuktam // 1 //
children.translated_text: Regarding this, what was said — that because of the <s>śruti</s> on the bridge, the [abode of heaven, earth, and such] must be something other than <s>Brahman</s>, namely the abode of heaven, earth, and such — that is improper. // 1 //

This is heard: 'That in which the sky, the earth, and the intermediate space are woven, together with the mind and all the vital breaths — know That alone as the one Self; abandon other words. This is the bridge to immortality' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5). Here, what is understood as something that is the support (<s>āyatana</s>) [of these], from the statement that the sky and such are woven in it — is it the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, or something else? The doubt arises. The initial position: it would be some other support, different [from <s>Brahman</s>]. Why? Because of the <s>śruti</s> 'this is the bridge to immortality.' For in the world, a bridge is well known as having a farther shore. And it is not possible to accept that the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> has a farther shore, from the <s>śruti</s>: 'infinite, without a farther shore' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.12). And if some other support is to be accepted, the <s>Pradhāna</s> well known in <s>Smṛti</s> should be taken, because being a cause, it is fitting as a support. Or it could be <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), well known from <s>śruti</s>: 'Wind, O <s>Gautama</s>, is that thread; by <s>Vāyu</s> as the thread, O <s>Gautama</s>, this world and all beings are strung together' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.2) — because the sustaining function is heard even for <s>Vāyu</s>. Or it could be the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>), because it too, being an experiencer, could fittingly be the support for the experienced phenomenal world. This being the position reached, he says: 'The support of the sky, earth, and so forth.' 'Sky and earth' (<s>dyubhuvau</s>) are the beginning (<s>ādi</s>) of which — that is 'sky-earth-and-so-forth' (<s>dyubhvādi</s>). That which in this passage is indicated as the world — sky, earth, intermediate space, mind, vital breaths — woven upon this [support] — its support (<s>āyatana</s>) deserves to be the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because of the proper word (<s>svaśabda</s>), meaning the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self). For the word '<s>Ātman</s>' occurs here: 'Know That alone as the one Self.' And the word '<s>Ātman</s>' is properly applicable when the Supreme Self is accepted, not when something else is accepted. And in some places, the support-nature of <s>Brahman</s> is heard through its own proper word: 'O dear one, all these creatures are rooted in Being (<s>Sat</s>), resting upon Being, established in Being' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.4). And by its own proper word, both before and after, <s>Brahman</s> is celebrated: '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is this universe — action, <s>tapas</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme immortal'; and '<s>Brahman</s> alone is this immortal — <s>Brahman</s> in front, <s>Brahman</s> behind, <s>Brahman</s> to the south and to the north' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.11). Therein, from the <s>śruti</s> statement of the relation of support and supported, and from the co-reference of 'all is <s>Brahman</s>' — the doubt might arise that the Self has many natures, variegated — like a tree that has multiple aspects: branches, trunk, and root. To remove that, he says with emphasis: 'Know That alone as the one Self.' This is what is meant: the Self should not be known as variegated, qualified by the phenomenal world of effects. Rather, dissolving through knowledge the phenomenal world of effects created by <s>avidyā</s>, know That one Self alone — the one that is the support, of one essence. Just as when told 'Bring that upon which <s>Devadatta</s> is sitting,' one brings the seat, not <s>Devadatta</s> — similarly, it is taught that the one that is the support, of one essence, is what is to be known. And a repudiation of the validity of modifications is heard: 'He who sees manifoldness here goes from death to death' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.4.11). And the co-reference 'all is <s>Brahman</s>' is for the purpose of dissolving the phenomenal world, not for establishing that [<s>Brahman</s>] has many essences. Because the <s>śruti</s> states the oneness of essence: 'Just as a lump of salt is without inside, without outside, is entirely a mass of taste — even so, this Self is without inside, without outside, is entirely a mass of consciousness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.13). Therefore, the support of the sky, earth, and so forth is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. As for the objection that, because of the <s>śruti</s> about the bridge and because a bridge has a farther shore, the support of the sky and such must be something other than <s>Brahman</s> — to this we say: only the sense of sustaining is intended here by the <s>śruti</s> about the bridge, not having a farther shore and such.

children.text: FN: amṛtasyeti śravaṇāt seturiti śravaṇāditi yojanā /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The construction is: because of the hearing [of the word] 'of immortality,' and because of the hearing [of the word] 'bridge.'

children.text: seturiti śravaṇāditi vyācaṣṭhe- pāravānhīti /
children.translated_text: He explains 'because of the hearing [of the word] bridge' as follows: 'for it has a farther shore' —

children.text:
saṃdṛbdhani saṃgrathitāni /
sāmānādhikaraṇyāt vicitra ātmeti saṃbandhaḥ /
vikāre 'nṛte kalpite abhisaṃdho 'bhimāno yasya /
sinoti badhnātīti setuḥ /
padārthaikadeśo vidhāraṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Saṃdṛbdhāni</s>' means 'bound together, interwoven.' Because of co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), the connection is: the Self is variegated. One whose identification (<s>abhisandha</s>), whose conception, is directed toward a modification that is unreal and imagined. '<s>Setu</s>' — from the root '<s>si</s>' (to bind) — means that which binds. The meaning of '<s>vidhāraṇa</s>' (sustaining) is a part of the [word's] meaning.

children.text: muktopasṛpyavyapadeśāc ca | BBs_1,3.2 |
children.translated_text: And because of the designation of being approachable by the liberated. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.2 |

children.text:
itaśca parameva brahma dyubhvādyāyatanam /
yasmānmuktopasṛpyatāsya vyapadiśyamānā dṛśyate /
muktairupasṛpyam muktopasṛpyam /
dehādiṣvanātmasvahamasmītyātmabuddhiravidyā, tatastatpūjanādau rāgastatparibhavādau dveṣastaducchedadarśanādbhayaṃ mohaścetyevamayamanantabhedo 'narthavrātaḥ saṃtataḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ pratyakṣaḥ /
tadviparyayeṇāvidyārāgadveṣādidoṣamuktairupasṛpyaṃ gamyametaditi dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ prakṛtya vyapadeśo bhavati /
katham, 'bhidyate hṛdayagranthiśchidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ /
kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare' (muṇḍa. 2.2.8) ityuktvā bravīti- 'tathā vidvānnāmarūpādvimuktaḥ parātparaṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam' (muṇḍa. 3.2.7) iti /
brahmaṇaśca muktopasṛpyatvaṃ prasiddhaṃ śāstre- 'yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ /
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute' (bṛha. 4.4.7) ityevamādau /
pradhānādīnāṃ tu na kvacinmuktopasṛpyamasti prasiddham /
apica 'tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānamanyā vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiva setuḥ' iti vāgvimokapūrvakaṃ vijñeyatvamiha dyubhvādyāyatanasyocyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, here, the knowability of the abode of heaven, earth, and such is stated as preceded by the release of speech: 'Know that one alone as the Self; let go of other speech — this is the bridge to immortality.'

children.text: tacca śrutyantare brahmaṇo dṛṣṭam- 'tameva dhīro vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvati brāhmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that is seen in another <s>śruti</s> in reference to <s>Brahman</s>: 'Having known That alone, the wise <s>brāhmaṇa</s> cultivates insight (<s>prajñā</s>);

children.text: nānudhyāyādvahūñśabdānvāco viglāpanaṃ hi tat' (bṛha. 4.4.21) iti /
children.translated_text: let him not think upon many words, for that is mere weariness of speech' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.21).

children.text: tasmādapi dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ paraṃ brahma // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the abode of heaven, earth, and such is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. // 2 //

For this reason too, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is the abode of heaven, earth, and such. Because its being approachable by the liberated is seen to be designated. '<s>Muktopasṛpya</s>' means 'approachable by the liberated.' <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the identification 'I am [the body]' with regard to what is not the Self — the body and such. From that arise attachment toward honoring those [body, etc.], hatred toward their disrespect, fear from seeing their destruction, and delusion — thus this endless mass of affliction, continuous, is directly experienced by all of us. By the reverse of that — by those who are freed from the defects of <s>avidyā</s>, attachment, hatred, and such — the designation is made, taking up the abode of heaven, earth, and such [as the subject]: 'this is what is to be approached, to be attained.' How? Having stated: 'The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are resolved, and one's <s>karmas</s> are destroyed, when that higher and lower [<s>Brahman</s>] is seen' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.8) — [the text] then says: 'Thus the wise one, freed from name and form, attains the <s>Puruṣa</s> that is higher than the high, the divine one' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.7). And that <s>Brahman</s> is approachable by the liberated is well known in scripture: 'When all the desires that dwell in the heart are released, then the mortal becomes immortal; here he attains <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.7) — and in such [passages]. But for <s>Pradhāna</s> and such, there is nowhere any well-known [teaching of] approachability by the liberated.

children.text:
FN: prajñā vākyārthadhīḥ /
brāhmaṇapadamanuktadvijopalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Prajñā</s>' means the cognition of the meaning of the [great] statement. The word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' is indicative of the twice-born in general [not mentioned explicitly].

children.text: nānumānam atacchabdāt | BBs_1,3.3 |
children.translated_text: It is not the inferred [<s>Pradhāna</s>], because of the absence of that word. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.3 |

children.text:
yathā brahmaṇaḥ pratipādakaḥ vaiśeṣiko heturukto naivamarthāntarasya vaiśeṣiko hetuḥ pratipādako 'stītyāha /
nānumānikaṃ sāṃkhyasmṛtiparikalpitaṃ pradhānamiha dyubhvādyāyatanatvena pratipattavyam /
kasmāt, atacchabdāt /
tasyācetanasya pradhānasya pratipādakaḥ śabdastacchabdaḥ, na tacchabdo 'tacchabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word (<s>śabda</s>) that would convey that unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> would be '<s>tacchabda</s>' (a word for that). What is not such a word is '<s>atacchabda</s>' (not-that-word).

children.text: na hyatrācetanasya pradhānasya pratipādakaḥ kaścicchabdo 'sti, yenācetanaṃ pradhānaṃ kāraṇatvenāyatanatvena vāvagamyeta /
children.translated_text: For there is no word here whatsoever that conveys the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s>, by which the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> could be understood as the cause or as the abode.

children.text: tadviparītasya cetanasya pratipādakaśabdo 'trāsti- 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit' (muṇḍa.1.1.9) ityādiḥ /
children.translated_text: But there is here a word conveying the opposite — the conscious [<s>Brahman</s>] — namely: 'He who is omniscient, who knows all' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9) — and such.

children.text: ata eva na vāyurapīha dyubhvādyātanatvenāśrīyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: For this very reason, <s>Vāyu</s> (air) too is not here accepted as the abode of heaven, earth, and such. // 3 //

Just as a specific reason establishing <s>Brahman</s> was stated, no such specific reason establishing something else exists — this is what [the <s>sūtra</s>] says. The <s>Pradhāna</s> imagined by the <s>Sāṃkhya Smṛti</s>, which is inferred, is not to be understood here as the abode of heaven, earth, and such. Why? Because of the absence of that word (<s>atacchabda</s>).

children.text: prāṇabhṛc ca | BBs_1,3.4 |
children.translated_text: Nor the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> [i.e., the individual soul]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.4 |

children.text: yadyapi prāṇabhṛto vijñānātmana ātmatvaṃ cetanatvaṃ ca saṃbhavati tathāpyupādhiparicchinnajñānasya sarvajñatvādyasaṃbhave satyasmādevātacchabdātprāṇabhṛdapi na dyubhvādyāyatanāśrayitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although selfhood and consciousness are possible for the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s>, the cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), nevertheless — since omniscience and such are impossible for one whose knowledge is delimited by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) — for this very reason, because of the absence of that word (<s>atacchabda</s>), the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> too should not be accepted as the abode of heaven, earth, and such.

children.text: nacopādhiparicchinnasyāvibhoḥ prāṇabhṛto dyubhvādyāyatanatvamapi samyaksaṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Nor is it truly possible for the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s>, who is delimited by limiting adjuncts and is not all-pervading, to be the abode of heaven, earth, and such.

children.text: pṛthagyogakaraṇamuttarārtham // 4 //
children.translated_text: The separate formulation [of this <s>sūtra</s>] serves a later purpose. // 4 //

children.text: kutaśca na prāṇabhṛddyabhvādyāyatanatvenāśritavyaḥ-
children.translated_text: And why else should the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> not be accepted as the abode of heaven, earth, and such?

children.text: bhedavyapadeśāt | BBs_1,3.5 |
children.translated_text: Because of the designation of difference. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.5 |

children.text: bhedavyapadeśaśceha bhavati- 'tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānam' iti jñeyajñātṛbhāvena /
children.translated_text: And here there is a designation of difference — 'Know that one alone as the Self' — in the form of a knower-known relationship.

children.text: tatra prāṇabhṛttāvanmumukṣutvāj jñātā, pariśeṣādātmaśabdavācyaṃ brahma dyubhvādyāyatanamiti gamyate, na prāṇabhṛt // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therein, the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s>, being the knower due to being a seeker of liberation, by elimination, <s>Brahman</s> — which is denoted by the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) — is understood to be the abode of heaven, earth, and such, not the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s>. // 5 //

children.text: kutaśca na prāṇabhṛddyubhvādyāyatanatvenāśrayitavyaḥ-
children.translated_text: And why else should the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> not be accepted as the abode of heaven, earth, and such?

children.text: prakaraṇāt | BBs_1,3.6 |
children.translated_text: Because of the context. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.6 |

children.text: prakaraṇaṃ cedaṃ paramātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: For this is the context of the Supreme Self.

children.text: 'kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati' (mu. 1.1.3) ityekavijñānena sarvavijñānāpekṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: 'When, O revered sir, which one thing is known, all this becomes known?' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.3) — because there is an expectation that through the knowledge of one, all should be known.

children.text: paramātmani hi sarvātmake vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ syānna kevale prāṇabhṛti // 6 //
children.translated_text: For when the Supreme Self, which is the Self of all, is known, all this would become known — not when the mere bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> [is known]. // 6 //

children.text: kutaśca na prāṇabhṛḍyubhvādyāyatanatvenāśrayitavyaḥ-
children.translated_text: And why else should the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> not be accepted as the abode of heaven, earth, and such?

children.text: sthityadanābhyāṃ ca | BBs_1,3.7 |
children.translated_text: And because of [the mention of] remaining and eating. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.7 |

children.text:
dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ ca prakṛtya 'dvā supraṇā sayujā sakhāyā' (mu. 3.1.1) ityatra sthityadane nirdiśyete /
'tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvatti' itikarmaphalāśanaṃ, 'anaśnannanyo 'bhicākaśīti' ityaudāsīnyenāvasthānaṃ ca /
tābhyāṃ ca sthityadanābhyāmīśvarakṣetrajñau tatra gṛhyete /
yadi ceśvaro dyubhvādyāyatanatvena vivakṣitastatastasya prakṛtasyeśvarasya kṣetrajñātpṛthagvacanamavakalpate /
anyathā hyaprakṛtavacanamākasmikamasaṃbaddhaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Taking up the abode of heaven, earth, and such as the subject, in the passage 'Two birds, companions, joined together, cling to the same tree' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1), remaining and eating are indicated. 'One of them eats the sweet <s>pippala</s> fruit' — this is the eating of the fruits of action; 'the other, not eating, looks on' — this is remaining in detachment. By these two — remaining and eating — the Lord and the field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>, individual soul) are grasped there. And if the Lord is intended as the abode of heaven, earth, and such, then the separate statement about the Lord as distinct from the field-knower is fitting for the [already] introduced [subject]. Otherwise, a statement about an unintroduced [subject] would be sudden and unconnected.

children.text: nanu tavāpi kṣetrajñasyeśvarātpṛthagvacanamākasmikameva prasajyeta /
children.translated_text: But would not the separate statement about the field-knower as distinct from the Lord equally be sudden on your view?

children.text:
na /
tasyāvivakṣitatvāt /
kṣetrajñau hi kartṛtvena bhoktṛtvena ca pratiśarīraṃ buddhyādyupādhisaṃbaddho lokata eva prasijaddho nāsau śrutyā tātparyeṇa vivakṣyate /
īśvarastu lokato 'prasiddhatvācchrutyā tātparyeṇa vivakṣyata iti na tasyākasmikaṃ vacanaṃ yuktam /
'guhāṃ praviṣṭāvātmānau hi' ityatrāpyetaddarśitaṃ 'dvā suparṇā' ityasyāmṛcīśvarakṣetrajñāvucyete iti /
yadāpi paiṅgyupaniṣatkṛtena vyākhyānenāsyāmṛci sattvakṣetrajñāvucyete tadāpi na virodhaḥ kaścit /
katham /
prāṇabhṛddhīha ghaṭādicchidravatsattvādyupādhyabhimānitvena pratiśarīraṃ gṛhyamāṇo dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ na bhavatīti niṣidhyate /
yastu sarvaśarīreṣūpādhibhirvinopalakṣyate na bhavatīti niṣidhyate /
yastu sarvaśarīreṣūpādhibhirvinopalakṣyate paramātmaiva sa bhavati /
yathā ghaṭādicchidrāṇi ghaṭādibhirupādhibhirvinopalakṣyamāṇāni mahākāśa eva bhavanti, tadvatprāṇabhṛtaḥ parasmādanyatvānupapatteḥ pratiṣedho nopapadyate /
tasmātsattvādyupādhyabhimānina eva dyubhvādyāyatanatvapratiṣedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: No. Because that [the field-knower] is not intended [as the subject here]. For the field-knower — connected in each body with the limiting adjuncts of intellect and such, through agency and enjoyership — is well known in the world and is not intended to be taught by the <s>śruti</s> with emphasis. But the Lord, being not well known in the world, is intended to be taught by the <s>śruti</s> with emphasis — so His statement is not sudden. In the passage 'The two selves that have entered the cave' too, it was shown that in this verse 'Two birds,' the Lord and the field-knower are spoken of. And even when, according to the interpretation offered by the <s>Paiṅgya Upaniṣad</s>, <s>Sattva</s> (intellect) and the field-knower are spoken of in this verse, there is no contradiction. How so? Because the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s>, being apprehended in each body through identification with limiting adjuncts like <s>Sattva</s> (intellect) — like the space in pots and such [limited by] the pots and such — is here denied to be the abode of heaven, earth, and such. But the one who is recognized in all bodies without limiting adjuncts — that is indeed the Supreme Self. Just as the spaces in pots and such, when recognized without the limiting adjuncts of pots and such, are simply the great space (<s>mahākāśa</s>) — similarly, since the non-difference of the bearer of <s>Prāṇa</s> from the Supreme is not unjustified, the denial [of being the abode] is not unjustified. Therefore, the denial of being the abode of heaven, earth, and such applies only to the one who identifies with limiting adjuncts like <s>Sattva</s>.

children.text: tasmātparameva brahma dyubhvādyāyatanam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is the abode of heaven, earth, and such.

children.text: tadetat 'adṛśyatvādiguṇako dharmokteḥ' ityanenaiva siddham /
children.translated_text: This is already established by the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'Because of the qualities beginning with invisibility being stated' (<s>BBs</s> 1.2.21).

children.text: tasyaiva hi bhūtayonivākyasya madhya idaṃ paṭhitam 'yasmindyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣam' iti /
children.translated_text: For this [passage] 'In which heaven, earth, and the intermediate space' is recited in the middle of that very passage on the source of beings [that was discussed there].

children.text: prapañcārthaṃ tu punarupanyastam // 7 //
children.translated_text: But it is taken up again for the purpose of elaboration. // 7 //

children.text: 2 bhūmādhikaraṇam / sū. 8-9
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Bhūmā Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Infinite) / <s>Sūtras</s> 8-9

children.text: bhūmā saṃprasādād adhyupadeśāt | BBs_1,3.8 |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūmā</s> (the Infinite) [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the instruction about what is superior to <s>Saṃprasāda</s> (the serene one). | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.8 |

children.text:
idaṃ samāmananti- 'bhūmā tveva vidijñāsitavya iti bhūmānaṃ bhagavo vijijñāsa iti /
yatra nānyatpaśyati nānyacchṛṇoti nānyadvijānāti sa bhūmātha yatrānyatpaśyatyanyacchṛṇotyanyadvijānāti tadalpam' (chā. 7.23,24) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ /
bhūmeti tāvadbahutvamabhidhīyate, 'bahorlopo bhū ca bahoḥ' (pā. 6.4.158) iti bhūmaśabdasya bhāvapratyayāntatāsmāraṇāt /
kimātmakaṃ punastadbahutvamiti viśeṣākāṅkṣāyāṃ 'prāṇo vā āśābhūyān' (chā. 7.15.1) iti saṃnidhānātprāṇo bhūmeti pratibhāti /
tathā 'śrutaṃ hyeva me bhagavaddṛśebhyastarati śokamātmaviditi so 'haṃ bhagavaḥ śocāmi taṃ mā bhagavāñśokasya pāraṃ tārayatu' (chāṃ. 7.1.3) iti prakaraṇotthānātparamātmā bhūmetyapi pratibhāti /
tatra kasyopādanaṃ nyāyyaṃ kasya vā hānamiti bhavati saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
prāṇo bhūmeti /
kasmāt /
children.translated_text: They teach this: '<s>Bhūmā</s> (the Infinite) indeed is to be inquired into.' 'I wish to know the <s>Bhūmā</s>, revered sir.' 'Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else — that is the <s>Bhūmā</s> (Infinite). But where one sees another, hears another, knows another — that is the finite (<s>alpa</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.23-24) — and so forth. Therein there is a doubt. '<s>Bhūmā</s>' conveys abundance (<s>bahutva</s>), since the word '<s>bhūma</s>' is remembered as ending in an abstract suffix — from the grammatical rule '<s>bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 6.4.158). When the specific question arises — 'of what nature is that abundance?' — from the proximity [of the preceding discussion] '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is greater than hope' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.15.1), it appears that <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Bhūmā</s>. Similarly, since the context arose from [the request]: 'I have heard from those like your revered self that the knower of the Self crosses over sorrow. I, revered sir, am sorrowful; may your revered self take me across to the farther shore of sorrow' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.3) — it also appears that the Supreme Self is the <s>Bhūmā</s>. Therein, the doubt arises: which one is it proper to adopt, and which to reject? What is the initial position? The <s>Bhūmā</s> is <s>Prāṇa</s>. Why?

children.text:
bhūyaḥ praśnaprativacanaparaṃparādarśanāt /
yathā hi 'asti bhagavo nāmno bhūyaḥ' iti, 'vāgvāva nāmno bhūyasī' iti /
tathā 'asti bhagavo nāmno bhūyaḥ' iti, mano vāva vāco bhūyaḥ' iti ca nāmādibhyo hyā prāṇādbhūyaḥpraśnaprativacanapravāhaḥ pravṛttaḥ /
naivaṃ prāṇātparaṃ bhūyaḥpraśnaprativacanaṃ dṛśyate 'sti bhagavaḥ prāṇādbhūya ityādo vāva prāṇādbhūya iti /
prāṇameva tu nāmādibhya āśāntebhyo bhūyāsaṃ 'prāṇo vā āśāyā bhūyān' ityādinā saprapañcamuktvā prāṇadarśinaścātivāditvam- 'ativādyasītyativādyasmīti brūyānnāpahnuvīta' ityabhyanujñāya 'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati' iti prāṇavratamativāditvamanukṛṣyāparityajyaiva prāṇaṃ satyādiparamparayā bhūmānamavatārayanprāṇameva bhūmānaṃ manyanta iti gamyate /
kathaṃ punaḥ prāṇe bhūmani vyākhyāyamāne 'yatra nānyatpaśyati' ityetadbhūmno lakṣaṇaparaṃ vacanaṃ vyākhyāyeteti /
ucyate- suṣuptyavasthāyāṃ prāṇagrasteṣu karaṇeṣu darśanādivyavahāranivṛttidarśanātsaṃbhavati prāṇasyāpi 'yatra nānyatpaśyati' ityetallakṣaṇam /
tathāca śrutiḥ 'na śṛṇoti na paśyati' ityādinā sarvakaraṇavyāpārapratyastamayarūpāṃ suṣuptyavasthāmuktvā 'prāṇāgnaya evaitasminpure jāgrati' (pra. 4.2.3) iti tasyāmevāvasthāyāṃ pañcavṛtteḥ prāṇasya jāgaraṇaṃ bruvatī prāṇapradhānāṃ suṣuptyavasthāṃ darśayati /
yaccaitadbhūmnaḥ sukhatvaṃ śrutam- 'yo vai bhūmā tatsukham' (chā. 7.23) iti, tadapyaviruddham /
'atraiṣa devaḥ svapnānna paśyatyatha yadetasmiñśarīre sukhaṃ bhavati' (pra. 4.6) iti suṣuptyavasthāyāmeva sukhaśravaṇāt /
yacca 'yo vai bhūmā tadamṛtam' (chā. 7.24.1) iti tadapi prāṇasyāviruddhaṃ, 'prāṇo vā amṛtam' (kau. 3.2) iti śruteḥ /
kathaṃ punaḥ prāṇaṃ bhūmānaṃ manyamānasya tarati śokamātmavit ityātmavividiṣayā prakaraṇasyotthānamupapadyate /
prāṇa evehātmā vivakṣita iti brūmaḥ /
tathāhi-' prāṇo ha pitā prāṇo mātā prāṇo bhrātā prāṇaḥ svasā prāṇa ācāryaḥ prāṇo brāhmaṇaḥ' (chā. 7.15.1) iti prāṇameva sarvātmānaṃ karoti /
'yathā vā arā nābhau samarpitā evamasminprāṇe sarvaṃ samarpitam' iti ca sarvātmatvāranābhinidarśanābhyāṃ ca saṃbhavati vaipulyātmikā bhūmarūpatā prāṇasya /
tasmātprāṇo bhūmetyevaṃ prāptam /
tata idamucyate- paramātmaiveha bhūmā bhavitumarhati na prāṇaḥ /
kasmāt /
saṃprasādādadhyupadeśāt /
saṃprasāda iti suṣuptaṃ sthānamucyate, samyakprasīdatyasminniti nirvacanāt /
bṛhadāraṇyake ca svapnajāgaritasthānābhyāṃ saha pāṭhāt tasyāṃ ca saṃprasādāvasthāyāṃ prāṇo jāgartīti prāṇo 'tra saṃprasādo 'bhipreyate /
prāṇādūrdhvaṃ bhūmna upadiśyamānatvādityarthaḥ /
prāṇa eva cedbhūmāsyātsa eva tasmādūrdhvamupadiśyetetyaśliṣṭamevaitatsyāt /
nahi nāmaiva nāmno bhūya iti nāmna ūrdhvamupadiṣṭam /
kiṃ tarhi nāmno 'nyadarthāntaramupadiṣṭaṃ vāgākhyam- 'vāgvāva nāmno bhūyasī' iti /
tathā vāgādibhyo 'pyā prāṇādarthāntarameva tatra tatrordhvamupadiṣṭam /
tadvatprāṇādūrdhvamupadiśyamāno bhūmā prāṇādarthāntarabhūto bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text:
Because of the observed succession of questions and answers about what is greater.
For just as: 'Is there, revered sir, something greater than name?' — 'Speech is indeed greater than name.' Likewise: 'Is there, revered sir, something greater than name?' — 'Mind is indeed greater than speech.' For the flow of questions and answers about what is greater proceeds from name and such up to <s>prāṇa</s>.
But no question and answer about something greater beyond <s>prāṇa</s> is seen of the form: 'Is there, revered sir, something greater than <s>prāṇa</s>?' — 'Hope (<s>āśā</s>) is indeed greater than <s>prāṇa</s>.'
Rather, having stated in full detail that <s>prāṇa</s> is greater than name and such up to hope — '<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed greater than hope' — and having approved the superiority-claimant status of one who sees <s>prāṇa</s>: 'One may say "I am a superior speaker," and should not deny it' — [the text] then says: 'But he truly speaks with superiority who speaks with truth.' Drawing along the superiority-claimant status pertaining to <s>prāṇa</s> without abandoning <s>prāṇa</s>, and introducing the <s>Bhūman</s> (Infinite) through the succession of truth and such — it is understood that [the teacher] considers <s>prāṇa</s> itself to be the <s>Bhūman</s>.
But how, when <s>prāṇa</s> is explained as the <s>Bhūman</s>, would the statement characterizing the <s>Bhūman</s> — 'Where one sees nothing else' — be explained?
The answer: In the state of deep sleep, when the sense-organs are absorbed into <s>prāṇa</s>, since the cessation of operations such as seeing is observed, the characterization 'where one sees nothing else' is possible even for <s>prāṇa</s>.
Thus the <s>śruti</s> too: having described the state of deep sleep as the cessation of all sense-organ operations — 'He does not hear, he does not see' and so forth — then stating 'The <s>prāṇa</s>-fires alone are awake in this city' (<s>Praśna</s> 4.2.3), showing the wakefulness of <s>prāṇa</s> with its five functions in that very state, [the scripture] indicates the state of deep sleep as dominated by <s>prāṇa</s>.
And the happiness of the <s>Bhūman</s> that was heard — 'That which is the <s>Bhūman</s>, that is happiness' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.23) — this too is not contradicted.
Because happiness is heard in the state of deep sleep itself: 'Here this deity does not see dreams; then whatever happiness there is in this body' (<s>Praśna</s> 4.6).
And 'That which is the <s>Bhūman</s>, that is immortal' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1) — this too is not contradicted for <s>prāṇa</s>, because of the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is immortal' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.2).
But how, for one who considers <s>prāṇa</s> to be the <s>Bhūman</s>, does the opening of the section with the desire to know the Self — 'The knower of the Self crosses over sorrow' — make sense?
We say: <s>prāṇa</s> itself is intended here as the Self.
For thus: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the father, <s>prāṇa</s> is the mother, <s>prāṇa</s> is the brother, <s>prāṇa</s> is the sister, <s>prāṇa</s> is the teacher, <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.15.1) — thus [the text] makes <s>prāṇa</s> the Self of all.
And 'Just as spokes are fixed in the hub, so in this <s>prāṇa</s> everything is fixed' — through the illustration of the spokes-and-hub showing it to be the Self of all, the expansive form of <s>Bhūman</s>-nature is possible for <s>prāṇa</s>.
Therefore, <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Bhūman</s> — given this position, this is said: The supreme Self alone can be the <s>Bhūman</s> here, not <s>prāṇa</s>.
Why?
Because of the teaching above <s>saṃprasāda</s> (deep sleep).
<s>Saṃprasāda</s> refers to the state of deep sleep, from the etymology: 'in which one becomes completely serene (<s>samyak prasīdati</s>).'
And in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, from its being read together with the states of dream and waking; and in that <s>saṃprasāda</s> state, '<s>prāṇa</s> is awake' — thus <s>prāṇa</s> is what is meant by <s>saṃprasāda</s> here.
The meaning is: because the <s>Bhūman</s> is taught as being above <s>prāṇa</s>.
For if <s>prāṇa</s> itself were the <s>Bhūman</s>, then that very thing would be taught as above itself — and this would be incoherent.
For name itself is not taught as greater than name.
Rather, something different from name, called speech, is taught as [greater]: 'Speech is indeed greater than name.'
Likewise, from speech and such up to <s>prāṇa</s>, something different is taught above each.
Similarly, the <s>Bhūman</s>, being taught above <s>prāṇa</s>, must be something different from <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text:
nanviha nāsti praśno 'sti bhagavaḥ prāṇādbhūya iti, nāpi prativacanamasti prāṇādvāva bhūyo 'stīti, kathaṃ prāṇādadhi bhūmopadiśyate /
prāṇaviṣayameva cātivāditvāmuttaratrānukṛṣyamāṇaṃ paśyāmaḥ- 'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati' iti /
tasmānnāsti prādadhyupadeśa iti /
children.translated_text:
But here there is no question 'Is there, revered sir, something greater than <s>prāṇa</s>?', nor is there an answer 'There is indeed something greater than <s>prāṇa</s>' — so how is the <s>Bhūman</s> taught as above <s>prāṇa</s>?
And we see the superiority-claimant status pertaining to <s>prāṇa</s> being carried forward subsequently: 'But he truly speaks with superiority who speaks with truth.'
Therefore, there is no teaching above <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: atrocyate- na tāvatprāṇaviṣayasyaivātivāditvasyaitadanukarṣaṇamiti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ, viśeṣavādāt 'yaḥ satyenātivadati' iti /
children.translated_text: To this it is said: First, it cannot be said that it is the superiority-claimant status pertaining only to <s>prāṇa</s> that is being carried forward — because of the qualifying statement 'who speaks with truth.'

children.text:
nanu viśeṣavādo 'pyayaṃ prāṇaviṣaya eva bhaviṣyati /
katham /
yathaiṣo 'gnihotrī yaḥ satyaṃ vadatītyukte na satyavadanenāgnihotritvaṃ, kena tarhi, agnihotreṇaiva /
satyavadanaṃ tvagnihotriṇo viśeṣa ucyate /
tathā 'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati' ityukte na satyavadanenātivāditvam, kena tarhi, prakṛtena prāṇavijñānenaiva /
satyavadanaṃ tu prāṇavido viśeṣo vivakṣyata iti /
children.translated_text:
But this qualifying statement too will pertain to <s>prāṇa</s> alone.
How?
Just as when it is said 'This one is a fire-sacrificer who speaks truth' — it is not by speaking truth that he becomes a fire-sacrificer, but by the fire-sacrifice itself. Truth-speaking is stated as a qualification of the fire-sacrificer.
Similarly, when it is said 'But he truly speaks with superiority who speaks with truth' — it is not by truth-speaking that one attains superiority-claimant status, but by the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s> that is the subject under discussion. Truth-speaking is intended as a qualification of the knower of <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ /
śrutyarthaparityāgaprasaṅgāt /
śrutyā hyatra satyavadanenātivāditvaṃ pratīyate- 'yaḥsatyenātivadati so 'tivadati' iti /
nātra prāṇavijñānasya saṃkīrtanamasti /
prakaraṇāttu prāṇavijñānaṃ saṃbadhyeta /
tatra prakaraṇānurodhena śrutiḥ parityaktā syāt /
prakṛtavyāvṛttyarthaśca tuśabdo na saṃgacchate 'eṣa tu vā ativadati' iti /
'satyaṃ tveva vijijñāsitavyam' (chā. 7.16) iti ca prayatnāntarakaraṇamarthāntaravivakṣāṃ sūcayati /
tasmādyathaikavedapraśaṃsāyāṃ prakṛtāyāmeṣa tu mahābrāhmaṇo yaścaturo vedānadhīta ityekavedebhyor'thāntarabhūtaścaturvedaḥ praśasyate tādṛgetaddraṣṭavyam /
naca praśnaprativacanarūpayaivārthāntaravivakṣayā bhavitavyamiti niyamo 'sti /
prakṛtasaṃbandhāsaṃbhavakāritatvādarthāntaravivakṣāyāḥ /
tatra prāṇāntamanuśāsanaṃ śrutvā tūṣṇībhūtaṃ nāradaṃ svayameva sanatkumāro vyutpādayati /
yatprāṇavijñānena vikārānṛtaviṣayeṇātivāditvamanativāditvameva tat 'eṣa tu vā ativadati yaḥ satyenātivadati' iti /
tatra satyamiti paraṃ brahmocyate, paramārtharūpatvāt /
'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma' (tai. 2.1) iti ca śrutyantarāt /
tathā vyutpāditāya nāradāya 'so 'haṃ bhagavaḥ satyenātivadāni' ityevaṃ pravṛttāya vijñānādisādhanaparamparayā bhūmānamupadiśati /
tatra yatprāṇādadhi satyaṃ vaktavyaṃ pratijñātaṃ tadeveha bhūmetyucyata iti gamyate /
tasmādasti prāṇādadhi bhūmna upadeśa ityataḥ prāṇādanyaḥ paramātmā bhūmā bhavitumarhati /
evañcehātmavividiṣayā prakaraṇasyotthānamupapannaṃ bhaviṣyati /
prāṇa evehātmā vivakṣita ityetadapi nopapadyate /
nahi prāṇasya mukhyayā vṛttyātmatvamasti /
nacānyatra paramātmajñānācchokavinivṛttirasti, 'nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' (śve. 6.15) iti śrutyantarāt /
'taṃ mā bhagavāñśokasya pāraṃ tārayatu' (chā. 7.1.3) iti copakramyopasaṃharati- 'tasmai mṛditakaṣāyāya tamasaḥ pāraṃ darśayati bhagavānsanatkumāraḥ' (chā. 7.26.2) iti /
tama iti śokādikāraṇamavidyocyate /
prāṇānte cānuśāsane na prāṇasyānyāyattatocyeta /
'ātmataḥ prāṇaḥ' (chā. 7.26.2) iti ca brāhmaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'From the Self, <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.26.1) — thus the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> text.

children.text: prakaraṇānte paramātmavivakṣā bhaviṣyati, 'bhūmā tu prāṇa eveti cet' na /
children.translated_text: The intention to speak of the supreme Self will come at the end of the section — 'But if [it is said that] the <s>Bhūman</s> is just <s>prāṇa</s>' — no.

children.text: 'sa bhagavaḥ kasminpratiṣṭhita iti sve mahimni' (chā. 7.24.1) ityādinā bhūmna evā prakaraṇasamāpteranukarṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the carrying forward of the <s>Bhūman</s> itself until the completion of the section through 'Revered sir, in what is [the <s>Bhūman</s>] established? — In its own glory' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1) and such.

children.text: vaipulyātmikā ca bhūmarūpatā sarvakāraṇatvātparamātmanaḥ sutarāmupapadyate // 8//
children.translated_text: And the expansive form of <s>Bhūman</s>-nature is all the more fitting for the supreme Self, because of being the cause of all. // 8 //

Not so, we say.
Because there would be the abandonment of the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>.
For the <s>śruti</s> here conveys that superiority-claimant status is through truth-speaking: 'He who speaks with superiority through truth, he speaks with superiority.'
There is no mention of the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s> here.
From the context, the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s> could be connected.
But in that case, the <s>śruti</s> would be abandoned in deference to the context.
And the word '<s>tu</s>' (but), which serves to mark a departure from the [preceding] subject, does not agree [with the <s>prāṇa</s> interpretation]: 'But he truly speaks with superiority.'
And 'Truth, however, is what one should desire to know' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.16) — the undertaking of a further effort indicates the intention to speak of a different subject.
Therefore, just as when the praise of a single <s>Veda</s> is the subject under discussion, the statement 'But this one is a great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has studied four <s>Vedas</s>' praises one who knows four <s>Vedas</s> as different from the knowers of a single <s>Veda</s> — this should be seen similarly.
And there is no rule that the intention to speak of a different subject must take only the form of a question and answer.
Because the intention to speak of a different subject is occasioned by the impossibility of connecting [the new topic] with the subject under discussion.
There, having heard the instruction up to <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>Nārada</s> falls silent, and <s>Sanatkumāra</s> himself takes the initiative to instruct [further].
The superiority-claimant status that was through the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s> — which pertains to the false realm of modifications — is [shown to be] not true superiority: 'But he truly speaks with superiority who speaks with truth.'
There, 'truth' (<s>satya</s>) refers to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, because of its being of the nature of ultimate reality.
And from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Truth, knowledge, infinity is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1).
Thus, to <s>Nārada</s> who has been so guided and who has undertaken [the quest] saying 'May I, revered sir, speak with superiority through truth' — through the succession of means beginning with knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) and such, [<s>Sanatkumāra</s>] teaches the <s>Bhūman</s>.
Therein, it is understood that what was promised as the truth to be stated above <s>prāṇa</s> — that is what is here called the <s>Bhūman</s>.
Therefore, there is a teaching of the <s>Bhūman</s> above <s>prāṇa</s>, and hence the <s>Bhūman</s> must be the supreme Self, different from <s>prāṇa</s>.
And thus the opening of the section with the desire to know the Self will be justified.
As for the claim that '<s>prāṇa</s> itself is intended here as the Self' — that too is untenable.
For <s>prāṇa</s> does not have Selfhood in the primary sense.
And the removal of sorrow occurs through no knowledge other than the knowledge of the supreme Self, because of another <s>śruti</s>: 'There is no other path for going [to liberation]' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.15).
And having begun with 'Lead me, revered sir, across to the other shore of sorrow' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.3), [the text] concludes: '<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, the revered one, shows the other shore of darkness to him whose impurities have been rubbed away' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.26.2).
'Darkness' (<s>tamas</s>) refers to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the cause of sorrow and such.
And if the instruction were only up to <s>prāṇa</s>, the dependence of <s>prāṇa</s> on something else would not be stated.

children.text:
FN: vyavahārātitaṃ pūrṇaṃ vastu bhūmā /
bhagavaddṛśebhyo yuṣmatsadṛśebhyaḥ /
devaḥ buddhyādyupādhiko jīvaḥ /
prakaraṇāttu saṃbadhyeta ativāditve hetutveneti śeṣaḥ /
prayatnāntaraṃ vicāraḥ /
vijñānamatra nididhyāsanādi /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The <s>Bhūman</s> is the complete, absolute reality that transcends conventional usage. 'From revered ones like yourself, from those like you.' '<s>Deva</s>' means the <s>jīva</s> conditioned by the limiting adjuncts of intellect and such. 'From the context' — the remainder is: as the reason for superiority-claimant status. '<s>Prayatnāntara</s>' means investigation. '<s>Vijñāna</s>' here means <s>nididhyāsana</s> (meditation) and such.

children.text: dharmopapatteś ca | BBs_1,3.9 |
children.translated_text: And because of the fitness of the characteristics. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.9 |

children.text:
apica ye bhūmni śrūyante dharmāste paramātmanyupapadyante /
'yatra nānyatpaśyati nānyacchṛṇoti nānyadvajānāti sa bhūmā' iti darśanādivyavahārābhāvaṃ bhūmānyavagamayati /
paramātmani cāyaṃ darśanādivyavahārābhāvo 'vagataḥ /
'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛ. 4.5.15) ityādiśrutyantarāt /
yo 'pyasau suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ darśanādivyavahārābhāva uktaḥ so 'pyātmana evāsaṅgatvavivakṣayokto na prāṇasvabhāvavivakṣayā, paramātmaprakaraṇāt /
yadapi tasyāmavasthāyāṃ sukhamuktaṃ, tadapyātmana eva sukharūpatvavivakṣayoktam /
yata āha- 'eṣo 'sya parama ānanda etasyaivānandasyānyāni bhūtāni mātrāmupajīvanti' (bṛ. 4.3.32) iti /
ihāpi 'yo vai bhūmā tatsukhaṃ nālpe sukhamasti bhūmaiva sukham' iti sāmayasukhanirākaraṇena brahmaiva sukhaṃ bhūmānaṃ darśayati /
'yo vai bhūmā tadamṛtam' ityamṛtatvamapīha śrūyamāṇaṃ paramakāraṇaṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text: 'That which is the <s>Bhūman</s>, that is immortal' — the immortality heard here too points to the ultimate cause.

children.text: vikārāṇāmṛtatvasyāpekṣikatvāt, 'ato 'nyadārtam' (bṛ. 3.4.2) iti ca śrutyantarāt /
children.translated_text: Because the immortality of modifications is only relative; and because of another <s>śruti</s>: 'Other than this, [everything] is afflicted' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.2).

children.text: tathāca satyatvaṃ svamahimapratiṣṭhitatvaṃ sarvagatatvaṃ sarvāttmatvamiti caite dharmāḥ śrūyamāṇāḥ paramātmanyevopapadyante nānyatra /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the characteristics heard here — being truth, being established in its own glory, being all-pervading, and being the Self of all — are fitting for the supreme Self alone, not for anything else.

children.text: tasmādbhūmeti siddham // 9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the <s>Bhūman</s>] is established as the supreme Self. // 9 //

Moreover, the characteristics that are heard regarding the <s>Bhūman</s> are fitting for the supreme Self.
'Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else — that is the <s>Bhūman</s>' — this makes known that the <s>Bhūman</s> is [the state] where there is the absence of the operations of seeing and such.
And this absence of the operations of seeing and such has been understood regarding the supreme Self.
From another <s>śruti</s>: 'But where all has become the Self alone, then by what would one see what?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15).
As for the absence of the operations of seeing and such stated in the state of deep sleep — that too is stated with the intention of expressing the unattached nature of the Self, not with the intention of expressing the nature of <s>prāṇa</s> — because the section is about the supreme Self.
And the happiness that was stated in that state — that too is stated with the intention of expressing the blissful nature of the Self.
Because [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'This is its supreme bliss. The other beings subsist on a portion of this very bliss' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.32).
Here too, 'That which is the <s>Bhūman</s>, that is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The <s>Bhūman</s> alone is happiness' — by negating conventional happiness, [the text] shows <s>Brahman</s> itself as the happiness that is the <s>Bhūman</s>.

children.text:
FN: ukto na śṛṇotītyādinā /
āmayena duḥkhena sahitaṃ sāmayam /
ārte naśvaram /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Stated' — by 'He does not hear' and such. '<s>Sāmaya</s>' means associated with <s>āmaya</s> (affliction/illness), i.e., with suffering. '<s>Ārta</s>' means perishable.

children.text: 3 akṣarādhikaraṇam / sū. 10-12
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Akṣara Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Imperishable). <s>Sūtras</s> 10-12.

children.text: akṣaram ambarāntadhṛteḥ | BBs_1,3.10 |
children.translated_text: The Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) [is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of sustaining what is up to and including space (<s>ambara</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.10 |

children.text:
'kasminnu khalvākāśa otaśca protaśceti /
sa hovācaitadvai tadakṣaraṃ gārgi brāhmaṇā abhivadantyasthūlamanaṇu' (bṛ. 3.8.7,8)ityādi śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ- kimakṣaraśabdena varṇa ucyate kiṃvā parameśvara iti /
tatrākṣarasamāmnāya ityādāvakṣaraśabdasya varṇe prasiddhatvāt prasiddhyatikramasya cāyuktatvāt 'oṅkāra evedaṃ sarvam' (chā. 2.23.3) ityādau ca śrutyantare varṇasyāpyupāsyatvena sarvātmakatvāvadhāraṇāt, varṇa evākṣaraśabda iti, evaṃ prāpta ucyate- para evātmākṣaraśabdavācyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
'In what is space woven, warp and woof?' He said: 'This is that which the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> call the Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s> — not gross, not subtle' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.7-8) and so forth — thus it is heard.
Therein, the doubt arises: Does the word 'Imperishable' (<s>Akṣara</s>) refer to a phoneme, or to the supreme Lord?
Since in expressions like '<s>akṣarasamāmnāya</s>' (the traditional arrangement of phonemes) and such, the word '<s>akṣara</s>' is well-known in the sense of a phoneme, and since it would be improper to depart from the well-known meaning; and since in another <s>śruti</s> — 'The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> indeed is all this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.3) — even a phoneme, as an object of meditation, is determined to be the Self of all — therefore, the word '<s>akṣara</s>' refers to a phoneme alone — given this position, it is said: The supreme Self alone is denoted by the word '<s>Akṣara</s>.'

children.text:
kasmāt /
ambarāntadhṛteḥ- pṛthivyāderākāśāntasya vikārajātasya dhāraṇāt /
tatra hi pṛthivyādeḥ samastavikārajātasya kālatrayavibhaktasya 'ākāśa eva tadotaṃ ca protaṃ ca' ityākāśe pratiṣṭhitatvamuktvā 'kasminnu khalvākāśa otaśca protaśca' ityanena praśnenedamakṣaramavatāritam /
tathācopasaṃhṛtam- 'etasminnu khalvakṣare gārgyākāśa otaśca protaśca' iti /
children.translated_text: And thus it is summed up: 'In this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, space is woven lengthwise and crosswise' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.9).

children.text: naceyamambarāntadhṛtirbrahmaṇo 'nyatra saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: And this maintenance of everything up to space is not possible for anything other than <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yadapi 'oṅkāra evedaṃ sarvam' iti tadapi brahmapratipattisādhanatvātstutyarthaṃ draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: As for the statement 'Oṃkāra alone is all this' — that too is to be seen as serving the purpose of praising, because it is a means for the realization of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmānna kṣaratyaśnute ceti nityatvāvyāpitatvābhyāmakṣaraṃ parameva brahma // 10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because it does not perish and because it pervades — on account of its eternality and all-pervasiveness — the <s>Akṣara</s> (Imperishable) is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone. // 10 //

Why?
Because of sustaining what is up to and including space (<s>ambara</s>) — because of sustaining the entire class of modifications from earth up to space.
For there, having stated that the entire class of modifications from earth and such, divided across the three times, is established in space — 'Space alone is that in which [everything] is woven, warp and woof' — by the question 'In what is space woven, warp and woof?', this Imperishable is introduced.

children.text:
'syādetat kāryasya cetkāraṇādhīnatvamambarāntadhṛtirabhyupagamyate, pradhānakāraṇavādino 'pīyamupapadyate /
kathamambarāntadhṛterbrahmatvapratipattiḥ' /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: 'It might be said: if the maintenance of everything up to space is conceded on the basis of an effect's dependence on its cause, then even for the proponent of <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause, this is tenable. How then can one ascertain from the maintenance of everything up to space that it is <s>Brahman</s>?' Therefore, the reply is read —

children.text: FN: 'rūḍhiryogamapaharati' iti nyāyenāha- prasiddhīti /
children.translated_text: NOTE: He says '<s>prasiddhi</s>' (well-known meaning) on the principle that 'the conventional meaning overrides the etymological meaning.'

children.text: sā ca praśāsanāt | BBs_1,3.11 |
children.translated_text: And that [maintenance] — because of [its] commanding. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.11 |

children.text:
sā cāmbarāntadhṛtiḥ parameśvarasyaiva karma /
kasmāt /
praśāsanāt /
praśāsanaṃ hīha śrūyate- 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ' (bṛ. 3.8.9) ityādi /
children.translated_text: For commanding is heard here: 'Under the mighty command of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon stand held apart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.9) and so forth.

children.text: praśāsanaṃ ca pārameśvaraṃ karma /
children.translated_text: And commanding is an activity of the supreme Lord.

children.text: nācetanasya pradhānasya praśāsanaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: The unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> does not command.

children.text: na hyacetanānāṃ ghaṭādikāraṇānāṃ mṛdādīnāṃ ghaṭādiviṣayaṃ praśāsanamasti // 11 //
children.translated_text: For there is no commanding by unconscious causes like clay and such over their effects like pots and such. // 11 //
And that maintenance of everything up to space is the activity of the supreme Lord alone. Why? Because of commanding.

children.text: anyabhāvavyāvṛtteśca | BBs_1,3.12 |
children.translated_text: And because of the exclusion of the nature of anything else. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.12 |

children.text:
anyabhāvavyāvṛtteśca kāraṇādbrahmaivākṣaraśabdavācyam /
tasyaivāmbarāntadhṛtiḥ karma nānyasya kasya cit /
kimidamanyabhāvavyāvṛtteriti /
anyasya bhāvo 'nyabhāvasyasmādvyāvṛttiranyabhāvavyāvṛttiriti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati-
children.translated_text: And because of the exclusion of the nature of anything else, it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is denoted by the word '<s>Akṣara</s>.' The maintenance of everything up to space belongs to it alone, and to no one else. What is meant by 'the exclusion of the nature of anything else'? The exclusion from this [<s>Akṣara</s>] of the nature (<s>bhāva</s>) of anything else (<s>anya</s>) — that is 'the exclusion of the nature of anything else.' What is being stated is this —

children.text:
yadanyadbrahmaṇo 'kṣaraśabdavācyamihāśaṅkyate tadbhāvādidamambarāntavidhāraṇamakṣaraṃ vyāvartayati śrutiḥ- 'tadvā etadakṣaraṃ gārgyadṛṣṭaṃ daṣṭraśrutaṃ śrotramataṃ mantravijñātaṃ vijñātṛ' (bṛ. 3.8.11) iti /
tatrādṛṣṭatvādivyapadeśaḥ pradhānasyāpi saṃbhavati /
draṣṭṛtvādivyapadeśastu na saṃbhavatyacenatvāt /
tathā 'nānyadato 'sti draṣṭṛ nānyadatosti śrotṛ nānyadato 'sti mantṛ nānyadato 'sti vijñātṛ' ityātmabhedapratiṣedhāt na śārīrasyāpyupādhimato 'kṣaraśabdavācyatvam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, because of the denial of any difference of Self — 'There is no other seer than this, no other hearer than this, no other thinker than this, no other knower than this' — the embodied self, insofar as it is delimited by limiting adjuncts, is also not denoted by the word '<s>Akṣara</s>.'

children.text: 'acakṣuṣkamaśrotramavāgamanaḥ' (bṛ. 3.8.8) iti copādhimattāpratiṣedhāt /
children.translated_text: And because of the denial of possession of limiting adjuncts — 'Without eyes, without ears, without speech, without mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8).

children.text: nahi nirupādhikaḥ śārīro nāma bhavati /
children.translated_text: For there is no embodied self without limiting adjuncts.

children.text: tasmātparameva brahmākṣaramiti niścayaḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the definitive conclusion is that the <s>Akṣara</s> (Imperishable) is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone. // 12 //

Whatever is suspected to be denoted by the word '<s>Akṣara</s>' other than <s>Brahman</s> — from the nature of that, the scripture excludes this <s>Akṣara</s> that maintains everything up to space: 'That <s>Akṣara</s>, O <s>Gārgī</s>, is unseen but is the seer, unheard but is the hearer, unthought but is the thinker, unknown but is the knower' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11). There, the designation of being unseen and such is possible even for <s>Pradhāna</s>. But the designation of being the seer and such is not possible — because of its being unconscious.

children.text: 4 īkṣatikarmavyapadeśādhikaraṇam / sū. 13
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Īkṣatikarma-vyapadeśa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Designation as the Object of Seeing). <s>Sūtra</s> 13.

children.text: īkṣatikarmavyapadeśāt saḥ | BBs_1,3.13 |
children.translated_text: Because of the designation as the object of seeing — it is He [<s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.13 |

children.text:
'etadvai satyakāma paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yadoṅkārastasmādvidvānetenaivāyatanenaikataramanveti iti prakṛtya śrūyate- 'yaḥ punaretaṃ trimātreṇomithyetenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣamabhidhyāyīta' (pra. 5.2,5) iti /
kimasminvākye paraṃ brahmābhidhyātavyamudiśyata āhosvidaparamiti /
etenaivāyatanena paramaparaṃ caikataramanvetīti prakṛtatvātsaṃśayaḥ /
tatrāparamidaṃ brahmeti prāptam /
kasmāt /
'sa tejasi sūrye saṃpannaḥ'' 'sa sāmabhirunnīyate brahmalokam' iti ca tadvido deśaparicchinnasya phalasyocyamānatvāt /
nahi parabrahmaviddeśaparicchinnaṃ phalamaśnuvīteti yuktam, sarvagatatvātparasya brahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having introduced 'This indeed, O <s>Satyakāma</s>, is both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s> — that which is <s>Oṃkāra</s>; therefore, the knower, through this very means, reaches one of the two' — it is heard: 'But he who meditates on the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> with this very syllable <s>Oṃ</s> having three <s>mātrās</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 5.2, 5). The question [is]: In this sentence, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> indicated as what is to be meditated upon, or the lower? The doubt arises because both [the higher and the lower] are introduced as subjects — 'Through this very means, one reaches one of the two.' There, the prima facie view is that this is the lower <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because a spatially limited fruit is stated for the knower of that: 'He, established in the light, in the sun' and 'He is led by the <s>Sāman</s> hymns to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.' For it is not appropriate that the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> should attain a spatially limited fruit, since the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is all-pervading.

children.text: nanvāparabrahmaparigrahe paraṃ puruṣamiti viśeṣaṇaṃ nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: But if the lower <s>Brahman</s> is accepted, the qualifying term 'supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' would not be appropriate.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
piṇḍāpekṣayā prāṇasya paratvopapatteḥ /
ityevaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- parameva brahmehābhidhyātavyamupadiśyate /
kasmāt /
īkṣatikarmavyapadeśāt /
īkṣatirdarśanam /
darśanavyāpyamīkṣatikarmā /
īkṣatikarmatvenāsyābhidhyātavyasya puruṣasya vākyaśeṣe vyapadeśo bhavati- 'sa etasmājjīvaghanātparātparaṃ puriśayaṃ puraṣamīkṣate' iti /
tatrābhidhyāyateratathābhūtamapi vastu karma bhavati /
manorathakalpitasyāpyabhidhyāyatikarmatvāt /
īkṣatestu tathābhūtameva vastu loke karma dṛṣṭamityataḥ paramātmaivāyaṃ samyagdarśanaviṣayabhūta īkṣatikarmatvena vyadiṣṭa iti gamyate /
sa eva ceha parapuruṣaśabdābhyāmabhidhyātavyaḥ pratyabhijñāyate /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect. Because the supremacy of <s>Prāṇa</s> [i.e., <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>] relative to the gross [body is tenable]. With this position having been reached, it is stated: It is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone that is taught here as the object of meditation. Why? Because of the designation as the object of seeing. '<s>Īkṣati</s>' means seeing; the object of the activity that seeing comprises is the <s>īkṣatikarma</s>. In the remainder of the passage, this <s>Puruṣa</s> who is to be meditated upon is designated as the object of seeing: 'He sees this <s>Puruṣa</s> who dwells in the citadel [of the body], who is higher than the highest from this mass of living [souls]' (<s>Praśna</s> 5.5). Now, the object of '<s>abhidhyāyati</s>' (meditating upon) can be even a thing that is not real [in its conceived form] — since even what is imagined in daydreaming can be the object of meditating. But the object of '<s>īkṣati</s>' (seeing) is observed in the world to be only a thing that is real. Therefore, it is understood that this supreme Self, being the object of right vision, is designated as the object of seeing. And this same [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is recognized here as the one to be meditated upon, through the words '<s>para</s>' (supreme) and '<s>puruṣa</s>'.
