children.text: nanvabhidhyāne paraḥ puruṣa uktaḥ, īkṣaṇe tu parātparaḥ, kathamitara itaratra pratyabhijñāyata iti /
children.translated_text: But in the context of meditation, the 'supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' was mentioned, whereas in the context of seeing, it is 'the one higher than the highest' — how is one recognized in the other?

children.text:
atrocyate- parapuruṣaśabdau tāvadubhayatra sādhāraṇau /
nacātra jīvanaghanaśabdena prakṛto 'bhidhyātavyaḥ paraḥ puruṣaḥ parāmṛśyate, yena tasmātparātparo 'yamīkṣitavyaḥ puruṣo 'nyaḥ syāt /
kastarhi jīvaghana iti /
ucyate- ghano mūrtiḥ /
jīvalakṣaṇo ghano jīvaghanaḥ /
saindhavakhilyavadyaḥ paramātmano jīvarūpaḥ khilyabhāva upādhikṛtaḥ paraśca viṣayendriyebhyaḥ so 'tra jīvaghana iti /
apara āha- 'sa sāmabhirunnīyate brahmalokam' ityatītānantaravākyanirdiṣṭo yo brahmalokaḥ paraśca lokāntarebhyaḥ so 'trajīvaghana ityucyate /
jīvānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ karaṇaparivṛtānāṃ sarvakaraṇātmani hiraṇyagarbhe brahmalokanivāsini saṃghātopapatterbhavati brahmaloko jīvaghanaḥ /
tasmātparo yaḥ paramātmekṣaṇakarmabhūtaḥ sa evābhidhyāne 'pi karmabhūta iti gamyate /
paraṃ puruṣamiti ca viśeṣaṇaṃ paramātmaparigraha evāvakalpate /
paro hi puruṣaḥ paramātmaiva bhavati yasmātparaṃ kiñcidanyannāsti, 'puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ' iti ca śrutyantarāt /
'paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yadoṅkāraḥ' iti ca vibhajyānantaramoṅkāreṇa paraṃ puruṣamabhidhyātavyaṃ bruvanparameva brahmaparaṃ puruṣaṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text: And [the scripture], having divided 'The <s>Oṃkāra</s> is both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>,' and then immediately stating that the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is to be meditated upon through <s>Oṃkāra</s>, points to the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone as the 'supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>.'

children.text: 'yathā pādodarastvacā vinirmucyata evaṃ ha vai sa pāpmanā vinirmucyate' iti pāpmavinirmokaphalavacanaṃ paramātmānamihābhidhyātavyaṃ sūcayati /
children.translated_text: 'Just as a snake is freed from its skin, so he is freed from sin' — this statement of the fruit of freedom from sin indicates that it is the supreme Self who is to be meditated upon here.

children.text: atha yaduktaṃ paramātmābhidhyāyino na deśaparicchinnaphalaṃ yujyata iti /
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was said — that a spatially limited fruit is not appropriate for one who meditates on the supreme Self —

children.text: atrocyate- trimātreṇoṅkāreṇālambanena paramātmānamabhidhyāyataḥ phalaṃ brahmalokaprāptiḥ krameṇa ca samyagdarśanotpattiriti kramamuktyabhiprāyametadbhaviṣyatītyadoṣaḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: To this it is said: For one who meditates on the supreme Self using the three-<s>mātrā</s> <s>Oṃkāra</s> as a support, the fruit is the attainment of the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, and through gradual stages, the arising of right knowledge — this is to be understood as intending gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>), and so there is no fault. // 13 //

To this it is said: First, the words '<s>para</s>' (supreme) and '<s>puruṣa</s>' are common to both [contexts]. And here, the <s>Puruṣa</s> who was introduced as the subject and who is 'supreme' — the one to be meditated upon — is not referred back to by the term '<s>jīvaghana</s>' (mass of living souls), such that this <s>Puruṣa</s> to be seen, who is 'higher than that,' would be someone different. Then what is '<s>jīvaghana</s>'? It is said: '<s>Ghana</s>' means a solid mass. A solid mass characterized by the <s>jīva</s> is '<s>jīvaghana</s>.' Like a block of salt — the supreme Self's <s>jīva</s>-form, the state of being a [mere] fragment, is caused by limiting adjuncts; and it is supreme relative to the sense-objects and sense-organs — that is here called '<s>jīvaghana</s>.' Another [interpreter] says: The world of <s>Brahmā</s> indicated in the immediately preceding passage — 'He is led by the <s>Sāman</s> hymns to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>' — which is supreme relative to other worlds — that is here called '<s>jīvaghana</s>.' For the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, the abode of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> who is the Self of all sense-organs, is '<s>jīvaghana</s>' because all <s>jīvas</s> surrounded by their instruments come together there. The supreme Self, who is the object of seeing, is higher than that — and that same [supreme Self] is to be understood as the object of meditation too. And the qualifying term 'supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' is appropriate only when the supreme Self is accepted. For the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is none other than the supreme Self, beyond whom there is nothing else — as another scripture states: 'There is nothing higher than the <s>Puruṣa</s>; that is the culmination, that is the supreme goal' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.11).

children.text:
FN: paraṃ nirviśeṣam, aparaṃ kāryaṃ, āyatanena prāptisādhanena, anveti prāpnoti /
aparaṃ brahma hiraṇyagarbhaḥ /
piṇḍaḥ sthūlo virāṭ tadapekṣayā sūtrasya paratvamti samādhyarthaḥ /
vyāpyaṃ viṣayaḥ /
saindhavākhilyo lavaṇapiṇḍaḥ, khilyabhāvo 'lpatvam /
pādodaraḥ sarpaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Para</s>' means the attributeless; '<s>apara</s>' means the effected [<s>Brahman</s>]; '<s>āyatana</s>' means the means of attainment; '<s>anveti</s>' means attains. The lower <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. '<s>Piṇḍa</s>' means the gross [body], i.e., <s>Virāṭ</s>; relative to that, the supremacy of <s>Sūtra</s> [<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>] — this is the reconciliation. '<s>Vyāpya</s>' means object. '<s>Saindhavākhilya</s>' is a block of salt; '<s>khilyabhāva</s>' means smallness. '<s>Pādodara</s>' means a snake.

children.text: 5 daharādhikaraṇam / sū. 14-21
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Dahara Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Small [Space]). <s>Sūtras</s> 14-21.

children.text: dahara uttarebhyaḥ | BBs_1,3.14 |
children.translated_text: The small [space is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of the subsequent [reasons]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.14 |

children.text:
'atha yadidamasminbrahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminnantarākāśastasminyadantastadanveṣṭavyaṃ tadbhāva vijijñāsitavyam' /
(chā. 8.1.1) ityādivākyaṃ samāmnāyate /
tatra yo 'yaṃ dahare hṛdayapuṇrīke dahara ākāśaḥ śrutaḥ sa kiṃ bhūtākāśo 'thavā vijñānātmā'thavā paramātmeti saṃśayyate /
kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
ākāśabrahmapuraśabdābhyām /
ākāśaśabdo hyayaṃ bhūtākāśe parasmiṃśca prayujyamāno dṛśyate /
tatra kiṃ bhūtākāśa eva daharaḥ syātkiṃvā para iti saṃśayaḥ /
tathā brahmapuramiti kiṃ jīvo 'tra brahmanāmā tasyedaṃ puraṃ śarīraṃ brahmapuramathavā parasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ puraṃ brahmapuramiti /
tatra jīvasya parasya vānyatarasya purasvāmino daharākāśatve saṃśayaḥ /
tatrākāśaśabdasya bhūtākāśe rūḍhatvādbhūtākāśa eva daharaśabda iti prāptam /
tasya ca daharāyatanāpekṣayā daharatvam /
'yāvānvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhadaya ākāśaḥ' iti ca bāhyāyantarabhāvakṛtabhedasyopamānopameyabhāvaḥ dyāvāpṛthivyādi ca tasminnantaḥ samāhitaṃ, avakāśātmanākāśasyaikatvāt /
athavā jīvo dahara iti prāptam, brahmapuraśabdāt /
jīvasya hīdaṃ puraṃ saccharīraṃ brahmapuramityucyate /
tasya svakarmaṇopārjitatvāt /
bhaktyā ca tasya brahmaśabdavācyatvam /
nahi parasya brahmaṇaḥ śarīreṇa svasvāmibhāvaḥ saṃbandho 'sti /
tatra purasvāminaḥ puraikadeśe 'vasthānaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā rājñaḥ /
manaupādhikaśca jīvaḥ, manaśca prāyeṇa hṛdaye pratiṣṭhitamityato jīvasyaivedaṃ hṛdaye 'ntaravasthānaṃ syāt /
daharatvamapi tasyaiva ārāgropamitatvādavakalpate /
ākāśopamitatvādi ca brahmābhedavivakṣayā bhaviṣyati /
nacātra daharasyākāśasyānveṣyatvaṃ vijijñāsitavyatvaṃ ca śrūyate /
'tasminyadantaḥ' iti paraviśeṣaṇatvenopādānāditi /
ata uttaraṃ brūmaḥ- parameśvara evātra daharākāśo bhavitumarhati na bhūtākāśo jīvo vā /
kasmāt /
uttarebhyo vākyaśeṣagatebhyo hetubhyaḥ /
tathāhi- anveṣṭavyatayā vihitasya daharasyākāśasya 'taṃ cedbrūyuḥ' ityupakramya 'kiṃ tadatra vidyate yadanveṣṭavyaṃ yadbhāva vijijñāsitavyam' ityevamākṣepapūrvakaṃ pratisamādhānavacanaṃ bhavati /
'sa brūyādyavānvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśa ubhe asmindyāvāpṛthivī antareva samāhite' (chā. 8.1.3) ityādi /
tatra puṇḍarīkadaharatvena prāptadaharatvasyākāśasya prasiddhākāśaupamyena daharatvaṃ nivartayanbhūtākāśatvaṃ daharasyākāśasya nivartayatīti gamyate /
yadyapyākāśaśabdo bhūtākāśe rūḍhastathāpi tenaiva tasyopamā nopapadyata iti bhūtākāśaśaṅkā nivartitā bhavati /
children.translated_text: 'Now, in this citadel of <s>Brahman</s> there is a small lotus — a dwelling — and within it a small space. What is within that is to be sought; that indeed is to be known' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1) — such a passage is recorded. There, this small space within the small lotus of the heart — is it elemental space, or the knowing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), or the supreme Self? This is the doubt. Whence the doubt? From the words '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) and '<s>brahmapura</s>' (citadel of <s>Brahman</s>). For the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is seen to be used both for elemental space and for the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>]. So the doubt arises: Is this small [space] elemental space, or the supreme? Likewise, '<s>brahmapura</s>' (citadel of <s>Brahman</s>) — is the <s>jīva</s> here called '<s>Brahman</s>,' and this body is its citadel, hence '<s>brahmapura</s>'? Or is it the citadel of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself? There, when either the <s>jīva</s> or the supreme [Self] — whoever is the owner of the citadel — is doubted as being the small space, the doubt arises. The prima facie view is: Since the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is conventionally established for elemental space, the word '<s>dahara</s>' (small) refers to elemental space alone. And its smallness is relative to its small locus [the lotus of the heart]. And 'As vast as this [external] space, so vast is this space within the heart' — the comparison between outer and inner, based on the division created by being external and internal, is that of the compared and the comparand; and heaven and earth and such are contained within it — because of the oneness of space in its aspect of providing room. Alternatively, the prima facie view is that the <s>jīva</s> is the small [space] — because of the word '<s>brahmapura</s>.' For this body of the <s>jīva</s>, the embodied one, is called '<s>brahmapura</s>.' Because it is acquired by his own <s>karma</s>. And the <s>jīva</s> can be called '<s>Brahman</s>' figuratively. For the supreme <s>Brahman</s> has no relation of owner-owned with a body. And it is observed that the owner of a citadel dwells in a particular part of the citadel — as a king does. And the <s>jīva</s> has the mind as its limiting adjunct, and the mind is generally established in the heart — therefore it is the <s>jīva</s> alone that would have this abode within the heart. Smallness too is appropriate for it alone, since it is compared to the point of a needle. And the comparison with space and such would be from the standpoint of expressing non-difference from <s>Brahman</s>. And it is not the small space itself that is heard here as to be sought and to be known — but rather 'what is within it,' since it is taken up as a further qualifier. Therefore, the reply: The supreme Lord alone can be the small space here — not elemental space nor the <s>jīva</s>. Why? Because of the subsequent reasons — the reasons found in the remainder of the passage. For the small space that was enjoined as to be sought — beginning with 'If they were to say to him' and raising the objection 'What is there within it that is to be sought, that indeed is to be known?' — the resolution follows: 'He should say: "As vast as this [external] space, so vast is this space within the heart; both heaven and earth are contained within it"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.3) and so forth. There, by removing the smallness of the space — which had been considered small because of the smallness of the lotus — through its comparison with the well-known [external] space, [the text] is understood to be removing its being elemental space. For even though the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is conventionally established for elemental space, a comparison of that [elemental space] with itself is not appropriate — so the suspicion that it is elemental space is removed.

children.text: nanvekasyāpyākāśasya bāhyābhyantaratvakalpitena bhedenopamānopameyabhāvaḥ saṃbhavatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: But it was said that even for one and the same space, the comparison of outer and inner is possible on the basis of a difference that is merely conceived!

children.text:
naivaṃ saṃbhavati /
agatikā hīyaṃ gatiḥ, yatkālpanikabhedāśrayaṇam /
apica kalpayitvāpi bhedamupamānopameyabhāvaṃ varṇayataḥ paricchinnatvādabhyantarākāśasya na bāhyākāśaparimāṇatvamupapadyeta /
children.translated_text: That is not possible. For this is a recourse taken only when there is no other option — this resort to a merely conceived difference. Moreover, even if one were to conceive a difference and then describe a comparison, since the inner space is limited [by the lotus of the heart], its being equal in measure to the outer space would not be tenable.

children.text: nanu parameśvarasyāpi 'jyāyānākāśāt' (śata. brā. 10.6.6.2) iti śrutyantarānnaivākāśaparimāṇatvamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: But even for the supreme Lord, because of another scripture — 'Greater than space' (<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 10.6.6.2) — being equal in measure to space would not be tenable.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
puṇḍarīkaveṣṭanaprāptadaharatvanivṛttiparatvādvākyasya na tāvattvapratipādanaparatvam /
ubhayapratipādane hi vākyaṃ bhidyeta /
naca kalpitabhede piṇḍarīkaveṣṭita ākāśaikadeśe dyāvāpṛthivyādīnāmantaḥsamādhānamupapadyate /
'eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyurvīśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' iti cātmatvāpahatapāpmatvādayaśca guṇā na bhūtākāśe saṃbhavanti /
yadyapyātmaśabdo jīve saṃbhavati tathāpītarebhyaḥ kāraṇebhyo jīvāśaṅkāpi nivartitā bhavati /
nahyupādhiparicchinnasyārāgropamitasya jīvasya puṇḍarīkaveṣṭhanakṛtaṃ daharatvaṃ śakyaṃ nivartayitum /
brahmābhedavivakṣayā jīvasya sarvagatatvādi vivakṣyeteti cet /
yadātmatayā jīvasya sarvagatatvādi vivakṣyeta tasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ sākṣātsarvagatatvādivivakṣyatāmiti yuktam /
yadapyuktaṃ brahmapuramiti jīvena parasyopalakṣitatvādrājña iva jīvasyaivedaṃ purasvāminaḥ puraikadeśavartitvamastviti /
atra brūmaḥ- parasyaivedaṃ brahmaṇaḥ puraṃ saccharīraṃ brahmapuramityucyate, brahmaśabdasya tasminmukhyatvāt /
tasyāpyasti pureṇānena saṃbandhaḥ, upalabdhyadhiṣṭhānatvāt /
'sa etasmājjīvaghanātparātparaṃ puriśayaṃ puruṣamīkṣate' (praṃ 5.5) 'sa vā ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvāsu pūrṣu puriśayaḥ' (bṛ. 2.5.18) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
athavā jīvapura evāsminbrahma saṃnihitamupalakṣyate /
yathā śālagrāme viṣṇaḥ saṃnihita iti tadvat /
'tadyatheha karmacito lokaḥ kṣīyata evamevāmutra puṇyacito lokaḥ kṣīyate' (chā. 8.1.6) iti ca karmaṇāmantavatphalamuktvā 'atha ya ihātmānamanuvidya vrajatyetāṃśca satyānkāmānsteṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati' iti prakṛtadaharākāśavijñānasyānantaphalatvaṃ vadanparamātmatvamasya sūcayati /
yadapyetaduktaṃ, na daharasyākāśasyānveṣṭavyatvaṃ vijijñāsitavyaṃ ca śrutaṃ, paraviśeṣaṇatvenopādānāditi atra brūmaḥ- yadyākāśo nānveṣṭavyatvenoktaḥ syāt 'yāvānvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhadaya ākāśaḥ' ityādyākāśasvarūpapradarśanaṃ nopayujyate /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because the statement's purpose is to negate the smallness that would result from being enclosed in the lotus [of the heart] — its purpose is not to teach the truth of that [smallness]. For if both were to be taught, the statement would be split. And in a merely imagined division — a portion of space enclosed in the lotus — the placing of heaven, earth, and such within is not tenable. Moreover, the qualities of selfhood, freedom from evil, and such — 'This is the Self, free from evil, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst, whose desires are real, whose will is real' — these are not possible for elemental space. And even though the word '<s>ātman</s>' is possible for the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>), the suspicion of the <s>jīva</s> is also removed by other reasons. For the smallness created by the enclosure of the lotus cannot be negated for the <s>jīva</s>, who is delimited by limiting adjuncts and is compared to the point of an <s>ārā</s>. If it is said that the all-pervasiveness and such of the <s>jīva</s> could be stated with the intention of non-difference from <s>Brahman</s> — [we say:] when the all-pervasiveness and such is stated for the <s>jīva</s> as [having <s>Brahman</s> as] its Self, it is proper that this be stated directly of <s>Brahman</s> itself with its all-pervasiveness and such. As for the argument that because the city is called '<s>Brahmapura</s>' (city of <s>Brahman</s>), the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] is indicated by the <s>jīva</s>, and so — like a king — this dwelling in one part of the city belongs to the <s>jīva</s> as the owner of the city — to this we say: This very body, the city, is called '<s>Brahmapura</s>' (city of <s>Brahman</s>) — belonging to the supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself, because the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is primary [in reference to] that. And <s>Brahman</s> too has a connection with this city, since it is the locus of perception and presiding authority — from scriptures such as: 'He beholds the <s>Puruṣa</s> dwelling in the city, higher than the high, beyond the mass of the <s>jīva</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 5.5) and 'This <s>Puruṣa</s> dwells in all cities, in all bodies' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.18). Or alternatively, in this city of the <s>jīva</s>, <s>Brahman</s> is indicated as present and near — just as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is near in the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone. And having stated the finite fruit of actions: 'Just as here the world that is won by action is destroyed, so too in the other world the world won by merit is destroyed' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.6) — [the scripture] then, by saying 'But those who depart hence, having found the Self, and these real desires — for them in all worlds there is freedom of movement' — stating the infinite fruit of the knowledge of the <s>dahara</s> space that is the subject — it indicates the Supreme-Self-nature of this [space]. As for the argument that the <s>dahara</s> space is not heard as something to be sought and to be inquired into, since it is adopted as a qualification of something else — to this we say: if space were not stated as something to be sought, then the display of the nature of space in 'as vast as this space is, so vast is this space within the heart' and such would not be useful.

children.text:
nanvetadapyantarvartivastusadbhāvapradarśanāyaiva pradarśyate /
'taṃ cedbrūyuryadidamasminbrahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ kiṃ tadatra vidyate yadanveṣṭavyaṃ yadbhāva vijijñāsitavyam' ityākṣipya parihārāvasara ākāśaupamyopakrameṇa dyāvāpṛthivyādīnāmantaḥsamāhitatvadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: But this [display of the nature of space] too is shown merely for revealing the existence of the entity within [the heart]. After raising the objection — 'If in this city of <s>Brahman</s> there is a small lotus abode, and within it a small space — what is there in it that is to be sought, that is to be inquired into?' — the resolution begins with the analogy to space, showing that heaven, earth, and such are placed within it.

children.text:
naitadevam /
evaṃ hi sati yadantaḥsamāhitaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyādi tadanveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyaṃ cokta syāt /
tatra vākyaśeṣo nopapadyeta /
children.translated_text: In that case, the remainder of the sentence would not be tenable.

children.text: 'asminkāmāḥ samāhitāḥ' 'eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā' iti hi prakṛtaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyādisamādhānādhāramākāśamākṛṣya 'atha ya ihātmānamanuvidya vrajantyetāṃśca satyānkāmān' iti samuccayārthena caśabdenātmānaṃ kāmādhārāśritāṃśca kāmānvijñeyānvākyaśeṣo darśayati /
children.translated_text: For 'in it, desires are placed' and 'This is the Self, free from evil' — here, drawing in the subject-space — the foundation of the placement of heaven, earth, and such — the remainder of the sentence shows with the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) in the cumulative sense: 'But those who depart hence, having found the Self, and these real desires' — [showing] the Self and the desires dependent on the desire-foundation as what is to be known.

children.text: tasmādvākyopakrame 'pi dahara evākāśo hṛdayapuṇḍarīkādhiṣṭhānaḥ sahāntaḥsthaiḥ samāhitaiḥ pṛthivyādibhiḥ satyaiśca kāmairvijñeya ukta iti gamyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even at the beginning of the passage, it is understood that the <s>dahara</s> space itself — stationed in the lotus of the heart, together with the established earth and such and the real desires within — is stated as what is to be known.

children.text: sa coktebhyo hetubhyaḥ parameśvara iti // 14 //
children.translated_text: And for the stated reasons, that [<s>dahara</s> space] is the supreme Lord. // 14 //
That is not so. For if it were so, what is placed within — heaven, earth, and such — would be said to be what is to be sought and to be inquired into.

children.text:
FN: brahmapuraṃ śarīraṃ, daharaṃ sūkṣmaṃ, puṇḍarīkaṃ tadākāratvātprakṛtaṃ hṛdayameva /
tatra parasya saṃnidherveśmaśabdaḥ /
bhaktyā caitanyaguṇayogena /
vigatā jighatsā jagdhumicchā yasya /
babhukṣāśūnya ityarthaḥ /
daharatvaṃ alpatvam /
ādipadaṃ sarvādhāratvādisaṃgrahārtham /
pūrṣu śarīreṣu, puri hṛdaye vā śete iti puruṣaḥ /
anuvidya dhyāyenānubhūya /
samāhitāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Brahmapura</s>' — the city, i.e., the body. '<s>Dahara</s>' — subtle. '<s>Puṇḍarīka</s>' — the heart itself, because of its lotus-shape, is the subject. There, the word '<s>veśma</s>' (abode) is because of the nearness of the Supreme [there]. '<s>Bhaktyā</s>' — through the connection of the quality of consciousness. '<s>Vigata jighatsā</s>' — that from which the desire to eat has departed. The meaning is: free from hunger. '<s>Daharatva</s>' — smallness. The word '<s>ādi</s>' is for including all-supportingness and such. '<s>Pūrṣu</s>' — in bodies; '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — one who lies (<s>śete</s>) in the city (<s>pur</s>) or in the heart. '<s>Anuvidya</s>' — having known through meditation, having experienced. '<s>Samāhitāḥ</s>' — established.

children.text: gatiśabdābhyāṃ tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ ca | BBs_1,3.15 |
children.translated_text: <s>Gatiśabdābhyāṃ tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ ca</s> — Because of the [terms] 'going' and 'word,' for thus it is seen, and [there is] the indicatory mark too. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.15 |

children.text:
daharaḥ parameśvara uttarebhyo hetubhya ityuktam /
ta evottare hetava idānīṃ prapañcyante /
itaśca parameśvara eva daharaḥ, yasmāddaharavākyaśeṣe parameśvarasyaiva pratipādakau gatiśabdau bhavataḥ- 'imāḥ sarvāḥ prajā aharahargacchantya etaṃ brahmalokaṃ na vindanti' (chā. 8.3.2) iti /
tatra prakṛtaṃ daharaṃ brahmalokaśabdenābhidhāya tadviṣayā gatiḥ prajāśabdavācyānāṃ jīvānāmabhidhīyamānā daharasya brahmatāṃ gamayati /
tathā hyaharaharjīvānāṃ suṣuptavasthāyāṃ brahmaviṣayaṃ gamanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutyantare- 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) ityevamādau /
loke 'pi kila gāḍhaṃ suṣuptamācakṣate brahmībhūto brahmatāṃ gata iti /
tathā brahmalokaśabdo 'pi prakṛte dahare prayujyamāno jīvabhūtākāśaśaṅkāṃ nivartayanbrahmatāmasya gamayati /
children.translated_text: The <s>dahara</s> [space] is the supreme Lord — from the reasons that follow — it was stated. Those subsequent reasons are now elaborated. For this further reason too, the <s>dahara</s> is the supreme Lord — because in the remainder of the <s>dahara</s> passage, the two terms 'going' and 'word' pertain to the supreme Lord alone: 'All these creatures, going day after day to this <s>Brahmaloka</s>, do not find [it]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.2). There, having designated the subject <s>dahara</s> [space] by the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' (world of <s>Brahman</s>), the 'going' — of the living beings denoted by the word 'creatures' — being stated with reference to that, leads to [the conclusion of] the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the <s>dahara</s>. For thus, the daily going of living beings to <s>Brahman</s> in the state of deep sleep is seen in another scripture: 'Then, O dear one, he becomes united with Being' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1) and such passages. In common parlance too, they reportedly describe deep sleep as 'he has become <s>Brahman</s>, he has gone to the state of <s>Brahman</s>.' Likewise, the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' being used for the subject <s>dahara</s> — dispelling the suspicion of <s>jīva</s> or elemental space — leads to its <s>Brahman</s>-nature.

children.text: nanu kamalāsanalokamapi brahmalokaśabdo gamayet /
children.translated_text: But could not the word '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' also convey the world of <s>Brahmā</s> (the Lotus-Seated [creator])?

children.text: gamayedyadi brahmaṇo loka iti ṣaṣṭhīsamāsavṛttyā vyutpādyeta /
children.translated_text: It would, if it were analyzed with a genitive compound construction: 'the world of <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: sāmānādhikaraṇavṛttyā tu vyutpādyamāno brahmaiva loko brahmaloka iti parameva brahma gamayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: But when analyzed with an appositional compound construction, '<s>Brahmaloka</s>' — meaning '<s>Brahman</s> itself is the world' — would convey the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone.

children.text: etadeva cāhararbrahmalokagamanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brahmaśabdasya sāmānādhikaraṇyavṛttiparigrahe liṅgam /
children.translated_text: And this very daily going to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> that is seen [in deep sleep] is the indicatory mark for adopting the appositional construction of the word '<s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: nahyaharaharimāḥ prajāḥ kāryabrahmalokaṃ satyalokākhyaṃ gacchantīti śakyaṃ kalpayitum // 15 //
children.translated_text: For it cannot be imagined that all these creatures go daily to the effect-world of <s>Brahmā</s>, called <s>Satyaloka</s>. // 15 //

children.text: dhṛteś ca mahimno 'syāsminn upalabdheḥ | BBs_1,3.16 |
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛteś ca mahimno 'syāsminn upalabdheḥ</s> — And because of sustaining, and because this greatness is found in it. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.16 |

children.text:
dhṛteśca hetoḥ parameśvara evāyaṃ daharaḥ /
katham /
'daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' iti hi prakṛtyākāśaupamyapūrvakaṃ tasminsarvasamādhānamuktvā tāṃ sminneva cātmaśabdaṃ prayujyāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇayogaṃ copaduśya tamevānativṛttaprakaraṇaṃ nirdiśati- 'atha ya ātmā sa seturvidhṛtireṣalokānāmasaṃbhedāya' (chā. 8.4.1) iti /
tatra vidhṛtirityātmaśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyādvidhārayitocyate, kticaḥ kartari smaraṇāt /
yathodakasaṃtānasya vidhārayitā loke setuḥ kṣetrasaṃpadāmasaṃbhedāya, evamayamātmātmaiṣāmadhyātmādibhedabhinnānāṃ lokānāṃ varṇāśramādīnāṃ ca vidhāritā seturasaṃbhedāyāsaṃkarāyeti /
evamiha prakṛte dahare vidhāraṇalakṣaṇaṃ mahimānaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the subject <s>dahara</s> here, [the scripture] shows the greatness characterized by sustaining.

children.text: ayaṃ ca mahimā parameśvara eva śrutyantarādupalabhyate 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ' ityādeḥ /
children.translated_text: And this greatness is found from another scripture to belong to the supreme Lord alone: 'Under the command of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon stand sustained' and so forth.

children.text: tathānyatrāpi niścite parameśvaravākye śrūyate- 'eṣa sarveśvara eṣa bhūtādhipatireṣa bhūtapāla eṣa seturvidhāraṇa eṣāṃ lokānāmasaṃbhedāya' iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in another passage that is determined to be about the supreme Lord, it is heard: 'This is the Lord of all; this is the ruler of beings; this is the protector of beings; this is the bridge, the sustainer, for the non-confusion of these worlds.'

children.text: evaṃ dhṛteśca hetoḥ parameśvara evāyaṃ daharaḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: Thus, for the reason of sustaining too, this <s>dahara</s> is the supreme Lord alone. // 16 //

And for the reason of 'sustaining' too, this <s>dahara</s> is the supreme Lord alone. How so? Having stated, under the subject '<s>dahara</s> is the space within,' preceded by the analogy to space, the placement of everything in it — and having used the word '<s>ātman</s>' for that very [space] and taught the connection with qualities such as freedom from evil — [the scripture] then points to that very same subject without having departed from the context: 'Now, the Self is the bridge, the sustainer, for the non-confusion of these worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.1). There, '<s>vidhṛti</s>' (sustaining), being in appositional construction with the word '<s>ātman</s>,' designates the sustainer — since the <s>ktic</s> suffix is remembered in the agentive sense. Just as in the world a bridge is the sustainer of the flow of water, for the non-confusion of fields and their crops — so too this Self is the sustainer-bridge of these worlds — differentiated into such categories as individual, cosmic, and so forth — and of the <s>varṇas</s>, <s>āśramas</s>, and such — for their non-confusion, for the prevention of their intermixture.

children.text: FN: seturasaṃkarahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Setu</s>' (bridge) is the cause of non-intermixture.

children.text: prasiddheś ca | BBs_1,3.17 |
children.translated_text: <s>Prasiddheś ca</s> — And because of being well-known. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.17 |

children.text: itaśca parameśvara eva 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' ityucyate /
yatkāraṇamākāśaśabdaḥ parameśvare prasiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) is well-known in reference to the supreme Lord.

children.text: 'ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā' (chā. 8.1.4), 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyākāśādeva samutpadyante' (chā. 1.9.1) ityādiprayogadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ākāśa</s> indeed is the name of that which brings forth name and form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.4); 'All these beings originate from space alone' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.9.1) — because of observing such usages.

children.text: jīve tu na kvacidākāśaśabdaḥ prayujyamāno dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: But the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is nowhere seen to be used for the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: bhūtākāśastu satyāmapyākāśaśabdaprasiddhāvupamānopameyabhāvādyasaṃbhavānna grahītavya ityuktam // 17 //
children.translated_text: As for elemental space — even though the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is well-known for it, it is not to be adopted because of the impossibility of the comparison-compared relationship and such — this has been stated. // 17 //
For this further reason too, the supreme Lord alone is spoken of in 'the small space within.'

children.text: FN: ā samāntātkāśate dīpyata ityākāśaḥ svayañjyotirīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Ākāśa</s>' — that which shines (<s>kāśate</s>) completely (<s>ā samantāt</s>) is <s>ākāśa</s> — the self-luminous Lord.

children.text: itaraparāmarśāt sa iti cen nāsaṃbhavāt | BBs_1,3.18 |
children.translated_text: <s>Itaraparāmarśāt sa iti cen nāsaṃbhavāt</s> — If [it be said] 'it is that [<s>jīva</s>], because of the reference to the other [<s>jīva</s>]' — [we say] no, because of impossibility. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.18 |

children.text:
yadi vākyaśeṣabalena dahara iti parameśvaraḥ parigṛhyetāstītarasyāpi jīvasya vākyaśeṣe parāmarśaḥ - 'atha ya eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrātsamutthāya paraṃ jyotirūpasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca' (chā. 8.3.4) iti /
atra hi saṃprasādaśabdaḥ śrutyantare suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ dṛṣṭatvāttadavasthāvantaṃ jīvaṃ śaknotyupasthāpayituṃ nārthāntaram /
tathā śarīravyapāśrayasyeva jīvasya śarīrātsamutthānaṃ saṃbhavati /
yathākāśavyapāśrayāṇāṃ vāyvādīnāmākāśātsamutthānaṃ tadvat /
yathā cādṛṣṭo 'pi loke parameśvaraviṣaya ākāśaśabdaḥ parameśvaradharmasamabhivyāhārāt 'ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā' ityevamādau parameśvaraviṣayo 'bhyupagata evaṃ jīvaviṣayo 'pi bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: If the <s>dahara</s> is accepted as the supreme Lord based on the force of the remainder of the sentence, there is also a reference to the other — the <s>jīva</s> — in the remainder of the sentence: 'Now, this serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), having risen from this body and having reached the supreme light, manifests in his own form. This is the Self, he said' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.4). For here, the word '<s>saṃprasāda</s>' — being seen in another scripture in reference to the state of deep sleep — can present the <s>jīva</s> in that state, and nothing else. Also, the rising from the body is possible for the <s>jīva</s> — who, as it were, depends on the body — just as the rising of wind and such from space, which, as it were, depends on space. And just as the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' — though not seen in worldly usage for the supreme Lord — was accepted as referring to the supreme Lord because of co-occurrence with qualities of the supreme Lord in 'Space indeed is the name of that which brings forth name and form' and such passages — similarly, it could also refer to the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: tasmāditaraparāmarśāt 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśa' ityatra sa eva jīva ucyate iti cet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the reference to the other [<s>jīva</s>], what is called the <s>dahara</s> space within is the <s>jīva</s> itself — if this is said,

children.text:
naitadevaṃ syāt /
kasmāt. asaṃbhavāt /
nahi jīvo buddhyādyupādhiparicchedābhimānī sannākāśenopamīyeta /
nacopādhidharmānabhimanyamānasyāpahatapāpmatvādayo dharmāḥ saṃbhavanti /
children.translated_text: Nor are the qualities of freedom from evil and such possible for one who identifies with the qualities of limiting adjuncts.

children.text: prapañcitaṃ caitatprathamasūtre /
children.translated_text: And this was elaborated upon in the first <s>sūtra</s> [of this topic].

children.text: atirekāśaṅkāparihārāyātra tu punarupanyastam /
children.translated_text: But here it is mentioned again for the purpose of dispelling the apprehension of an additional [possibility].

children.text: paṭhiṣyati copariṣṭāt 'anyārthaśca parāmarśaḥ' (bra. 1.3.20) iti // 18 //
children.translated_text: And he will read later: 'And the reference [to the <s>jīva</s>] has a different purpose' (<s>BBs</s> 1.3.20). // 18 //
this is not so. Why? Because of impossibility. For the <s>jīva</s>, who identifies with the limiting adjuncts of intellect and such, cannot be compared to space.

children.text: FN: samyakprasīdatyasmiñjīvo viṣayendriyasaṃyogajanitaṃ kāluṣyaṃ jahātīti suṣuptiḥ saṃprasādo jīvasyāvasthābhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Saṃprasāda</s>' — in it the <s>jīva</s> becomes fully serene, abandoning the turbidity produced by the contact of sense-organs and objects — deep sleep is '<s>saṃprasāda</s>,' a particular state of the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: 'saṃprasāde ratvā caritvā' iti bṛhadāraṇyakasthaṃ śrutyantaram /
children.translated_text: 'Having sported in the state of deep sleep, having moved about' — this is another scripture, from the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>.

children.text: upādhidharmāḥ pāpmādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The qualities of the limiting adjuncts are evil and such.

children.text: uttarāc ced āvirbhūtasvarūpas tu | BBs_1,3.19 |
children.translated_text: <s>Uttarāc ced āvirbhūtasvarūpas tu</s> — If, because of the subsequent [passage], [the <s>jīva</s>] has its true nature manifest — but... | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.19 |

children.text:
itaraparāmarśādyā jīvāśaṅkā jātā sāsaṃbhavānnirākṛtā /
athedānīṃ mṛtasyevāmṛtasekātpunaḥ samutthānaṃ jīvāśaṅkāyāḥ kriyate uttarasmātprajāpatyādvākyāt /
tatrahi 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā' ityapahatapāpmatvādiguṇakamātmānamanveṣṭavyaṃ vijijñāsitavyaṃ ca pratijñāya 'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmā'
children.translated_text: The suspicion of the <s>jīva</s> that arose from the reference to the other was refuted on grounds of impossibility. Now, as if reviving the dead with a sprinkle of immortality, the suspicion of the <s>jīva</s> is raised again — from the subsequent passage of <s>Prajāpati</s>. For there, having proclaimed the Self qualified by freedom from evil and such — 'The Self that is free from evil' — as what is to be sought and to be inquired into, [<s>Prajāpati</s>] saying: 'This <s>Puruṣa</s> who is seen in the eye — this is the Self'

children.text:
(chā. 8.7.4) iti bruvannakṣisthaṃ draṣṭāraṃ jīvamātmānaṃ nirdiśati /
'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi' (chā. 8.9.3) iti ca tameva punaḥ punaḥ parāmṛśya 'ya eṣa svapne mahīyamānaścaratyeṣa ātmā' (chā. 8.10.1) iti 'tadyatraitatsuptaḥ samastaḥ saṃprasannaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānātyeṣa ātmā' iti ca jīvamevāvasthāntaragataṃ vyācaṣṭe /
tasyaiva cāpahatapāpmatvādi darśayati- 'etadamṛtamabhayametadbrahma' iti /
children.translated_text: (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.4) — points to the <s>jīva</s>, the seer stationed in the eye, as the Self. And 'I shall explain this further to you' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.9.3) — referring to that very same [<s>jīva</s>] again and again — 'This one who moves about glorified in dream — this is the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.10.1), and 'When one is asleep, composed, serene, and knows no dream — this is the Self' — [<s>Prajāpati</s>] explains the <s>jīva</s> itself as having entered different states. And he shows freedom from evil and such as belonging to that very [<s>jīva</s>]: 'This is the immortal, the fearless — this is <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text:
nāhaṃ khalvayamevaṃ saṃpratyātmānaṃ jānātyayamahamasmīti no evemāni bhūtāni' (chā. 8.11.1,2) iti ca suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ doṣamupalabhya 'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi no evānyatraitasmāt iti copakramya śarīrasaṃbandhanindāpūrvakaṃ 'eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrātsamutthāya paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ' iti jīvameva śarīrātsamutthitamuttamapuruṣaṃ darśayati /
tasmādasti saṃbhavo jīve pārameśvarāṇāṃ dharmāṇām /
ataḥ 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' iti jīva evokta iti cetkaścidbrūyāt, taṃ prati brūyāt- 'āvirbhūtasvarūpastu' iti /
tuśabdaḥ pūrvapakṣavyāvṛttyarthaḥ /
nottarasmādapi vākyādiha jīvasyāśaṅkā saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This one surely does not now know himself — "I am this" — nor indeed these beings' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.11.1,2) — thus, having noted the defect in the state of deep sleep, and having begun with 'I shall explain this very one to you further; it is not other than this,' and having preceded it with a censure of the connection with the body — 'This serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), rising up from this body and attaining the supreme light, manifests in his own form; he is the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' — [the text] shows the <s>jīva</s> itself, having risen from the body, to be the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therefore, there is the possibility of the Lord's attributes belonging to the <s>jīva</s>. Hence, if someone were to say that 'The space within this [heart] that is small' refers to the <s>jīva</s> — to that person, one should reply: 'But [it is <s>Brahman</s>], because [the <s>jīva</s> is spoken of as having] its own nature manifested.' The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for distinguishing from the opponent's view. The meaning is: from the subsequent passage too, the suspicion that the <s>jīva</s> is meant does not arise here.

children.text:
kasmāt /
yatastatrāpyāvirbhūtasvarūpo jīvo vivakṣyate /
āvirbhūtaṃ svarūpamasyetyāvirbhūtasvarūpaḥ /
bhūtapūrvagatyā jīvavacanam /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- 'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi ityakṣilakṣitaṃ draṣṭāraṃ nirdiśyodaśarāvabrāhmaṇenainaṃ śarīrātmatāyā vyutthāpya 'etaṃ tveva te' iti punaḥpunastameva vyākhyāyeyatvenākṛṣya svapnasuṣuptopanyāsakrameṇa 'paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate' iti yadasya pāramārthikaṃ svarūpaṃ paraṃ brahma tadrūpatayainaṃ jīvaṃ vyācaṣṭe na jaivena rūpeṇa /
yatparaṃ jyotirūpasaṃpattavyaṃ śrutaṃ tatparaṃ brahma /
taccāpahatapāpmatvādidharmakaṃ, tadeva ca jīvasya pāramārthikaṃ svarūpaṃ 'tattvamasi' ityādiśāstrebhyaḥ, netaradupādhikalpitam /
yāvadeva hi sthāṇāviva puruṣabuddhiṃ dvaitalakṣaṇāmavidyāṃ nivartayankūṭasthanityadṛksvarūpamātmānamahaṃ brahmāsmīti na pratipadyate tāvajjīvasya jīvatvam /
yadā tu dehendriyamanobuddhisaṃghātādvyutthāpya śrutyā pratibodhyate, nāsi tvaṃ dehendriyamanobuddhisaṃghātaḥ, nāsi saṃsārī, kiṃ tarhi tadyatsatyaṃ sa ātmā caitanyamātrasvarūpastattvamasīti, tadā kūcasthanityadṛksvarūpamātmānaṃ pratibudadhyāsmāccharīrādyabhimānātsamuttiṣṭhansa eva kūṭasthanityadṛksvarūpa ātmā bhavati /
'sa yo ha vai tatparamaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' (muṇḍa. 3.2.1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tadeva cāsya pāramārthikaṃ svarūpaṃ yena śarīrātsamutthāya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate /
kathaṃ punaḥ svaṃ ca rūpaṃ svenaiva niṣpadyata iti saṃbhavati kūṭasthanityasya suvarṇādīnāṃ tu dravyāntarasaṃparkādabhibhūtasvarūpāṇāmanabhivyaktāsādhāraṇaviśeṣāṇāṃ kṣāraprakṣepādibhiḥ śodhyamānānāṃ svarūpeṇābhiniṣpattiḥ syāt /
tathā nakṣatrādīnāmahanyabhibhūtaprakāśānāmabhibhāvakaviyoge rātrau svarūpeṇābhiniṣpattiḥ syāt /
natu tathātmacaitanyajyotiṣo nityasya kenacidabhibhavaḥ saṃbhavatyasaṃsargitvādvyomna iva, dṛṣṭavirodhācca /
dṛṣṭiśrutimativijñātayo hi jīvasya svarūpam /
tacca śarīrādasamutthitasyāpi jīvasya sadā niṣpannameva dṛśyate /
sarvo hi jīvaḥ paśyanśṛṇvanmanvāno vijānanvyavaharatyanyathā vyavahārānupapatteḥ /
tacceccharīrātsamutthitasya niṣpadyeta prāksamutthānāddṛṣṭo vyavahāro virudhyeta /
ataḥ kimātmakamidaṃ śarīrātsamutthānaṃ, kimātmikā vā svarūpeṇābhiniṣpattiriti /
children.translated_text: Why? Because what is intended there too is the <s>jīva</s> whose own nature has become manifested. '<s>Āvirbhūtasvarūpa</s>' means 'one whose own nature has become manifested.' The reference to the <s>jīva</s> is based on its prior state. What is being said is this: having pointed out the seer who is indicated by the eye through 'This person that is seen in the eye,' and having, through the <s>Udaśarāva Brāhmaṇa</s> (the passage about the water-vessel), raised him out of the identification with the body — and then, drawing him in again and again as the subject to be explained through 'I shall explain this very one to you further' — through the progression of the presentations of dream and deep sleep — what is described as 'attaining the supreme light, he manifests in his own form' is this: his ultimate nature, which is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, is what the <s>jīva</s> is described as — not in its individual (<s>jaiva</s>) form. The supreme light that is to be attained, as heard, is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And that [<s>Brahman</s>] has attributes such as freedom from evil; and that alone is the ultimate nature of the <s>jīva</s>, from scriptures like 'You are That' — not the other [nature], which is imagined through limiting adjuncts. For as long as one does not realize the Self — whose nature is the immutable, eternal Witness — as 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,' by removing the <s>avidyā</s> characterized by duality (like the cognition of a person in a post), so long does the <s>jīva</s>'s state of being a <s>jīva</s> persist. But when, through scripture, one is awakened — being raised up from the aggregate of body, senses, mind, and intellect: 'You are not the aggregate of body, senses, mind, and intellect; you are not a <s>saṃsārin</s>; rather, you are that which is real, the Self, whose nature is pure consciousness alone — You are That' — then one realizes the Self whose nature is the immutable, eternal Witness; rising up from the identification with body and such, that very immutable, eternal Witness-natured Self one becomes. From scriptures such as: 'He who knows that Supreme <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.1). And that alone is its ultimate nature, by which, 'rising from the body, it manifests in its own form.' But how is it possible that one's own form manifests through itself, when it is immutably eternal? For substances like gold, whose own nature is overpowered by contact with other substances, and whose distinctive characteristics are not manifested — when they are purified by the addition of alkali and such, a manifestation in their own form may occur. Similarly, for stars and such, whose radiance is overpowered during the day — when the overpowering agent departs at night, there would be a manifestation in their own form. But no such overpowering of the eternal light of Self-consciousness is possible — because of its non-attached nature, like space — and because of contradiction with what is observed. For seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing are the <s>jīva</s>'s own nature. And that is seen to be always accomplished even for the <s>jīva</s> that has not risen from the body. For every <s>jīva</s> engages in activity while seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing — otherwise activity would be impossible. And if [those functions] were accomplished only for one who has risen from the body, the observed activity prior to rising would be contradicted. Therefore, what is the nature of this 'rising from the body,' and what is the nature of 'manifesting in one's own form'?

children.text:
atrocyate- prāgvivekavijñānotpatteḥ śarīrendriyamanobuddhiviṣayavedanopādhibhiraviviktamiva jīvasya dṛṣṭyādijyotiḥsvarūpaṃ bhavati /
yathā śuddhasya sphaṭikasya svācchyaṃ śauklyaṃ ca svarūpaṃ prāgvivekagrahaṇādraktanīlādyupādhibhiraviviktamiva bhavati /
pramāṇajanitavivekagrahaṇāttu parācīnaḥ sphaṭikaḥ svācchyena śauklyena ca svenarūpeṇābhiniṣpadyata ityucyate prāgapi tathaiva san /
tathā dehādyupādhyaviviktasyaiva sato jīvasya śrutikṛtaṃ vivekavijñānaṃ śarīrātsamutthānaṃ vivekavijñānaphalaṃ svarūpeṇābhiniṣpattiḥ kevalātmasvarūpāvagatiḥ /
tathā vivekāvivekamātreṇaivātmano 'śarīratvaṃ saśarīratvaṃ ca, mantravarṇāt 'aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu' (kā. 1.2.22) iti, 'śarīrastho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate' (gī.13.31) iti ca saśarīratvāśarīratvaviśeṣābhāvasmaraṇāt /
tasmādvivekavijñānābhāvādanāvirbhūtasvarūpaḥ sanvivekavijñānādāvirbhūtasvarūpa ityucyate /
natvānyādṛśāvāvirbhāvānāvirbhāvau svarūpasya saṃbhavataḥ svarūpatvādeva /
evaṃ mithyājñānakṛta eva jīvaparameśvarayorbhedo na vastukṛtaḥ, vyomavadasaṅgatvāviśeṣāt /
kutaścidevaṃ pratipattavyam /
yato 'ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' ityupadiśya 'etadamṛtamabhayametadbrahma' ityupadiśati /
yo 'kṣiṇi prasiddho draṣṭā draṣṭṛtvena vibhāvyate so 'mṛtābhayalakṣaṇādbrahmaṇo 'nyaścetsyāttato 'mṛtābhayabrahmasāmānādh ikaraṇyaṃ na syāt /
nāpi praticchāyātmāyamakṣilakṣito nirdiśyate, prajāpatermṛṣāvāditvaprasaṅgāt /
tathā dvitīye 'pi paryāye 'ya eṣaḥ svapne mahīyamānaścarati' iti na prathamaparyāyanirdiṣṭādakṣipuruṣāddraṣṭuranyo nirdiṣṭaḥ, 'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi' ityupakramāt /
kiñcāhamadya svapne hastinamadrākṣaṃ nedānīṃ taṃ paśyāmīti dṛṣṭameva pratibuddhaḥ pratyācaṣṭe /
draṣṭāraṃ tu tameva pratyabhijānāti ya evāhaṃ svapnamadrākṣaṃ sa evāhaṃ jāgaritaṃ paśyamīti /
tathā tṛtīye 'pi paryāye 'nahi khalvayamevaṃ saṃpratyātmānaṃ jānātyayamahamasmīti no evemāni bhūtāni iti suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ viśeṣavijñānābhāvameva darśayati na vijñātāraṃ pratiṣedhati /
yattu tatra 'vināśamevāpīto bhavati' iti tadapi viśeṣavijñānavināśābhiprāyameva na vijñātṛvināśābhiprāyam /
'nahi vijñāturvijñāterviparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvāt' (bṛ. 4.3.30) iti śrutyantarāt /
tathā caturthe 'pi paryāye 'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi no evānyatraitasmāt' ityupakramya 'maghavanmartyaṃ vā idaṃ śarīram' ityādinā prapañcena śarīrādupādhisaṃbandhapratyākhyānena saṃprasādaśabdoditaṃ jīvaṃ 'svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate' iti brahmasvarūpāpannaṃ darśayanna parasmādbrahmaṇo 'mṛtābhayasvarūpādanyaṃ jīvaṃ darśayati /
kecittu paramātmavivakṣāyāṃ 'etaṃ tveva te' iti jīvākarṣaṇamanyāyyaṃ manyamānā etameva vākyopakramasūcitamapahatapāpmatvādiguṇakamātmānaṃ te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmīti kalpayanti /
teṣāmetamiti saṃnihitāvalambinī sarvanāmaśrutirviprakṛṣyeta /
bhūyaḥśrutiścoparudhyeta, paryāyāntarābhihitasya paryāyāntare 'nabhidhīyamānatvāt /
'etaṃ tveva te' iti ca pratijñāya prākcaturthātparyāyādanyamanyaṃ vyācakṣāṇasya prajāpateḥ pratārakatvaṃ prasajyeta /
tasmādyadavidyāpratyupasthāpitapāramārthikaṃ jaivaṃ rūpaṃ kartṛbhoktṛrāgadveṣādidoṣakaluṣitamanekānarthayogi tadvilayanena tadviparītamapahatapāpmatvādiguṇakaṃ pārameśvaraṃ svarūpaṃ vidyayā pratipādyate, sarpādivilayaneneva rajjvādīn /
apare tu vādinaḥ pāramārthikameva jaivaṃ rūpamiti manyante 'smadīyāśca kecit /
teṣāṃ sarveṣāmātmaikatvasamyagdarśanapratipakṣabhūtānāṃ pratibodhāyedaṃ śārīrakamārabdham /
eka eva parameśvaraḥ kūṭasthanityo vijñānadhāturavidyayā māyayā māyāvivadanekadhā vibhāvyate nānyo vijñānadhāturastīti /
yattvidaṃ parameśvaravākye jīvamāśaṅkhya pratiṣedhati sūtrakāraḥ - 'nāsaṃbhavāt' (bra.1.3.18) ityādinā /
tatrāyamabhiprāyaḥ - nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāve kūṭasthanitye ekasminnasaṅge paramātmani tadviparītaṃ jaivaṃ rūpaṃ vyomnīva talamalādiparikalpitam /
tadātmaikatvapratipādanaparairvākyairnyāyopetairdvaitavādapratiṣedhaiścāpaneṣyāmīti paramātmano jīvādanyatvaṃ draḍhayati /
children.translated_text: Through statements aimed at teaching the oneness of the Self, supported by reasoning, and through the denial of the doctrine of duality — 'I shall remove that [imagined difference]' — thus he reinforces that the <s>jīva</s> is not different from the Supreme Self.

children.text: jīvasya tu na parasmādanyatvaṃ pratipipādayiṣati kiṃ tvanuvadatyevāvidyākalpitaṃ lokaprasiddhaṃ jīvabhedam /
children.translated_text: But he does not seek to establish the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> from the Supreme; rather, he merely restates (<s>anuvadati</s>) the difference of the <s>jīva</s> [from <s>Brahman</s>] that is imagined through <s>avidyā</s> and is well known in the world.

children.text: evaṃ hi svābhāvikakartṛtvabhoktṛtvānuvādena pravṛttāḥ karmavidhayo na virudhyanta iti manyate /
children.translated_text: For he considers that in this way, the injunctions of ritual action, which proceed on the basis of the restatement of natural agency and enjoyership, are not contradicted.

children.text: pratipādyaṃ tu śāstrārthamātmaikatvameva darśayati- 'śāstradṛṣṭyā tūpadeśo vāmadevavat' (bra. 1.1.30) ityādināvarṇiścāsmābhirvidvadbhedena karmavidhivirodhaparihāraḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: But he demonstrates that the meaning of scripture to be taught is the oneness of the Self alone — through 'But the instruction is from the standpoint of scripture, like <s>Vāmadeva</s>' (<s>BBs</s> 1.1.30) and such [<s>sūtras</s>]. And the resolution of the contradiction with injunctions of ritual action through the distinction of the knower [from the ignorant] has been explained by us. // 19 //

To this we say: prior to the arising of discriminative knowledge, the light-nature of the <s>jīva</s> — consisting of seeing and such — exists as if undiscriminated from the limiting adjuncts of body, senses, mind, intellect, objects, and experiences. Just as the transparency and whiteness that are the own nature of a pure crystal exist as if undiscriminated from the red, blue, and other limiting adjuncts, prior to the grasping of discrimination. But after the grasping of discrimination produced by a valid means of knowledge, the crystal is said to 'manifest in its own form' of transparency and whiteness — even though it was the same even before. Similarly, for the <s>jīva</s> — which [always] exists as undiscriminated from the limiting adjuncts of body and such — the discriminative knowledge produced by scripture is the 'rising from the body,' and the result of discriminative knowledge — the 'manifesting in one's own form' — is the realization of the pure Self-nature alone. Likewise, the bodiless and embodied states of the Self are [based] on the mere presence or absence of discrimination — as indicated by the <s>mantra</s>: 'Bodiless within bodies' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.22); and from the <s>Smṛti</s>: 'Though dwelling in the body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, He neither acts nor is tainted' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.31) — recalling no difference between the embodied and bodiless states. Therefore, one whose own nature was unmanifested due to the absence of discriminative knowledge is said to have its own nature manifested through discriminative knowledge. But no other kind of manifestation and non-manifestation of one's own nature is possible — because it is one's own nature itself. Thus, the difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Supreme Lord is created by false knowledge alone, not by reality — because of the non-difference in non-attachment, like space. How is this to be understood? Because, having taught 'This person that is seen in the eye,' [the text] teaches 'This is the immortal, the fearless; this is <s>Brahman</s>.' If the well-known seer in the eye, who is characterized as the seer, were different from <s>Brahman</s> — which is characterized by immortality and fearlessness — then the co-referential predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with immortal, fearless <s>Brahman</s> would not obtain. Nor is the one indicated by the eye here the reflection-self — for that would entail the absurd consequence of <s>Prajāpati</s> being a liar. Similarly, in the second turn [of teaching] too: 'This one who moves about exalted in dreams' — no one other than the seer, the person in the eye who was indicated in the first turn, is indicated, because of the opening statement 'I shall explain this very one to you further.' Moreover, one who has woken up reports what was seen: 'I saw an elephant in my dream today; I do not see it now.' But the seer — him one recognizes as the same: 'The very I who saw the dream am the same I who now see the waking state.' Similarly, in the third turn too: 'This one surely does not now know himself — "I am this" — nor indeed these beings' — [the text] shows only the absence of particular cognition in the state of deep sleep, but does not negate the knower. And the statement there — 'He has reached destruction, as it were' — is intended as the destruction of particular cognition, not the destruction of the knower — from another <s>śruti</s>: 'For there is no destruction of the knower's knowing, because of its imperishability' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.30). And in the fourth turn too, having begun with 'I shall explain this very one to you further; it is not other than this,' and through the elaboration beginning with 'O <s>Maghavan</s>, this body is mortal' — showing through the rejection of the connection with the body and its limiting adjuncts that the <s>jīva</s> referred to by the word '<s>Saṃprasāda</s>' (the serene one) 'manifests in its own form' as having attained the nature of <s>Brahman</s> — [<s>Prajāpati</s>] does not show a <s>jīva</s> other than the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is immortality and fearlessness. But some, thinking that when the Supreme Self is intended, drawing in the <s>jīva</s> through 'this very one' would be unreasonable — construe: 'I shall explain to you further this very Self indicated at the beginning of the passage, characterized by freedom from evil and such.' For them, the <s>śruti</s> text '<s>etam</s>' (this one), which relies on what is proximate, would be pulled away [from its referent]. And the <s>śruti</s> word '<s>bhūyaḥ</s>' (further) would be obstructed — since what was described in one turn is not [further] described in another turn. And having promised 'this very one,' if <s>Prajāpati</s>, prior to the fourth turn, explains something different in each turn — the charge of deception against <s>Prajāpati</s> would arise. Therefore, what is the form of the <s>jīva</s> that is not ultimate but is presented by <s>avidyā</s> — soiled by the defects of agency, enjoyership, attachment, aversion, and such, conjoined with manifold afflictions — through the dissolution of that [false form], its opposite — the ultimate, lordly nature characterized by freedom from evil and such — is taught through <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), just as the rope and such are [revealed] through the dissolution of the snake and such. But other disputants — and some among our own school — hold that the individual (<s>jaiva</s>) form is ultimately real. For the awakening of all of them, who hold views opposed to the correct vision of the oneness of the Self, this <s>Śārīraka</s> (the treatise on the embodied [Self]) was commenced. The one Supreme Lord alone — immutably eternal, the substratum of consciousness — through <s>avidyā</s>, through <s>māyā</s>, appears manifold like a magician; there is no other substratum of consciousness. And the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, suspecting the <s>jīva</s> in a passage about the Supreme Lord, denies it through 'Not, because of impossibility' (<s>BBs</s> 1.3.18) and such. The purport there is this: upon the one Supreme Self — whose nature is eternal purity, awareness, and freedom, immutably eternal, non-attached — the individual form, which is the opposite of that, is imagined, like dirt and stain upon space.

children.text: mahīyamāno vāsanāmayairviṣayaiḥ pūjyamāna iti svapnaparyāye, tadyatreti suṣuptiparyāye ca jīvameva prajāpatirvyācaṣṭa ityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Moving about exalted' — being honored by objects made of <s>vāsanās</s> (impressions) — in the dream-turn. 'Where' — in the deep-sleep turn. <s>Prajāpati</s> explains the <s>jīva</s> itself — this is the syntactic connection.

children.text: aheti nipātaḥ khede /
children.translated_text: '<s>Aha</s>' is a particle expressing distress.

children.text: etasmātprakṛtādātmano 'nyatra anyam /
children.translated_text: 'From this,' the Self that is the subject, 'elsewhere' — another.

children.text: udaśarāveti udakapūrṇe śarāve pratibimbātmānaṃ dehaṃ svasyājñātaṃ yattanmahyaṃ vācyamityuktaḥ śrutyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Udaśarāva</s>' — the meaning of the <s>śruti</s> is: in a vessel filled with water, the reflection-self — the body, unknown to oneself — 'that which is unknown to me, please tell me.'

children.text: vyutthāpya vicārya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vyutthāpya</s>' means 'having analyzed.'

children.text: abhiniṣpadyata ityatra etaduktaṃ bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: At 'manifests' — the connection is with 'what is being said is this.'

children.text: abhibhāvakaḥ saurālokāstadviyoge /
children.translated_text: The overpowering agents are the solar rays and such; upon their departure —

children.text: vedanā harṣaśokādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vedanā</s>' means experiences such as joy, sorrow, and such.

children.text: vivekavijñānaṃ tvaṃpadārthaśodhanam /
children.translated_text: 'Discriminative knowledge' means the purification of the meaning of the word 'You' (<s>tvam</s>-<s>padārtha</s>).

children.text: anyādṛśau satyau /
children.translated_text: 'Of another kind' — being real.

children.text: aṃśādiśūnyatvamasaṅgatvam /
children.translated_text: Non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatva</s>) means being devoid of parts and such.

children.text: ayaṃ suṣuptaḥ, saṃprati suṣuptau, ahaṃ ātmānaṃ ahaṅkārāspadamātmānaṃ na jānāti /
children.translated_text: 'This one is in deep sleep' — '<s>saṃprati</s>' means 'now, in deep sleep' — he does not know himself — the self that is the locus of the ego-sense.

children.text: nahīti ātmānaḥ svabhāvabhūtavijñāpternānyathābhāvo yogyatvādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nahi</s>' — the meaning is: because the cognizing nature that belongs to the Self's own nature cannot become otherwise, due to its fitness [for being eternal].

children.text: vilayanena śodhanena /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vilayana</s>' means purification.

children.text: vidyayā mahāvākyena /
children.translated_text: 'Through <s>vidyā</s>' means through the <s>mahāvākya</s> (great statement).

children.text:
vākyāni tattvamasyādīni jīvabrahmaṇoścaitanyāviśeṣāttadākāreṇākārāntareṇa vā bhedāyogo nyāyaḥ /
nehanānenetyādayo dvaitavādaniṣedhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The statements — 'You are That' and such — [establish that] because there is no difference in consciousness between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s>, the impossibility of difference in that form or in any other form is the logical reasoning. 'There is no diversity here whatsoever' and such are the denials of the doctrine of duality.

children.text: anyārthaś ca parāmarśaḥ | BBs_1,3.20 |
children.translated_text: And the reference [to the <s>jīva</s> in the Lord's passage] serves another purpose. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.20 |

children.text: atha yo daharavākyaśeṣe jīvaparāmarśo darśitaḥ - 'atha ya eṣa saṃprasādaḥ' (chā. 8.3.4) ityādi, sa dahare parameśvare vyākhyāyamāne na jīvopāsanopadeśo na prakṛtaviśeṣopadeśa ityarthakatvaṃ prāpnotīti /
ata āha- anyārtho 'yaṃ jīvaparāmarśau na jīvasvarūpaparyavasāyī kiṃ tarhi parameśvarasvarūpaparyavasāyī /
children.translated_text: Therefore he says: this reference to the individual soul serves another purpose — it does not culminate in the nature of the individual soul, but rather culminates in the nature of the Supreme Lord.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How so?

children.text: saṃprasādaśabdodito jīvo jāgaritavyavahāre dehendriyapañjarādhyakṣo bhūtvā tadvāsanānirmitāṃśca svapnānnāḍīcaro 'nubhūya śrāntaḥ śaraṇaṃ prepsurubhayarūpādapi śarīrābhimānātsamutthāya suṣuptāvasthāyāṃ paraṃ jyotirākāśaśabditaṃ paraṃ brahmopasaṃpadya viśeṣavijñānavattvaṃ ca parityajya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate /
children.translated_text: The individual soul, denoted by the word '<s>saṃprasāda</s>' (the serene one), having been the presider over the cage of the body and senses during the waking state, and having experienced the dreams constructed by the impressions of that [waking] state while traversing the <s>nāḍīs</s> — being exhausted and seeking shelter, having risen above the identification with the body in both its forms [waking and dream] — in the state of deep sleep, it approaches the supreme light designated by the word 'space,' the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and having abandoned the state of possessing specific cognitions, it attains its own true nature.

children.text: yadasyopasaṃpattavyaṃ paraṃ jyotiryena svena rūpeṇāyamabhiniṣpadyate sa eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇa upāsya ityevamartho 'yaṃ jīvaparāmarśaḥ parameśvaravādino 'pyupapadyate // 20 //
children.translated_text: That supreme light which is to be approached by it, and by which its own true nature is attained — 'this is the Self, free from evil' and possessing such qualities — is to be meditated upon. Thus, this reference to the individual soul, having this meaning, is justified even for one who holds the doctrine of the Supreme Lord [as the <s>Dahara</s> space]. // 20 //

Now, the reference to the individual soul shown in the remainder of the <s>Dahara</s> passage — 'Now, he who is this serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.4) and so forth — when the Supreme Lord is being explained as the <s>Dahara</s> [space], would not attain meaningfulness as teaching meditation on the individual soul or as teaching a specific feature of the topic.

children.text: alpaśruter iti cet tad uktam | BBs_1,3.21 |
children.translated_text: If [one objects] because of the <s>śruti</s> of smallness — that has been addressed. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.21 |

children.text: yadapyuktam, 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' ityākāśasyālpatvaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ parameśvare nopapadyate, jīvasya tvārāgropanimitasyālpatvamavakalpata iti tasya parihāro vaktavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for the objection that the smallness heard in 'the small space within this [heart]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1) is not fitting for the Supreme Lord, whereas smallness is justifiable for the individual soul because of its being of minute size — the refutation of that must be stated.

children.text: ukto hyasya parihāraḥ parameśvarasyāpekṣikamalpatvamavakalpata iti 'arbhakaukastvāttadvyapadeśācca neti cenna nicāyyatvādevaṃ vyomavacca' (bra. 1.2.7) ityatra /
children.translated_text: The refutation of this has already been stated — that relative smallness is justifiable even for the Supreme Lord — in the passage '<s>Arbhakaukastvāt</s> — because of the smallness of the abode, and because of that designation — if one says no, [we say] no, because of being determined, and like space' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.7).

children.text: sa eveha parihāro 'nusaṃdhātavya iti sūcayati /
children.translated_text: He indicates that the same refutation should be connected here.

children.text: śrutyaiva cedamalpatvaṃ pratyuktaṃ prasiddhenākāśenopamimānayā 'yāvānvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ' iti // 21 //
children.translated_text: And this very smallness is countered by the <s>śruti</s> itself, by comparing [the <s>Dahara</s> space] with the well-known space: 'As vast as this space is, so vast is this space within the heart.' // 21 //

children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Anukṛti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Imitation) / <s>Sūtras</s> 22-23

children.translated_text: Because of imitation, and because of that [fourth line]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.22 |

kasmāt /

children.translated_text: They teach: 'The sun does not shine there, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine — what then of this fire? Him alone, as He shines, everything shines after; by His light all this is illuminated' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.10). When the doubt arises — is the one after whose shining everything shines and by whose light all this is illuminated, some particular luminous element, or the conscious Self (<s>Prājña Ātman</s>)? — the initial position is: it is a luminous element. Why? Because the shining of luminous entities like the sun and such is negated. For it is well known that luminous entities like the moon and stars, which are of the nature of fire-element, do not shine during the day when the sun, which is also of the nature of fire-element, is shining. Similarly, everything that does not shine along with the sun — including the moon, stars, and such — that [superior light] too is understood to be of the nature of fire-element. And the 'shining after' (<s>anubhāna</s>, imitation) is also justifiable only for what is of the same nature as fire-element, because imitation is observed among things of the same nature — like 'he follows the one who goes.' This being the position reached, we say: it deserves to be the conscious Self (<s>Prājña Ātman</s>) itself. Why? Because of imitation (<s>anukṛti</s>). This imitation — the 'shining after' stated in 'Him alone, as He shines, everything shines after' — is justified when the conscious Self is accepted. 'Of the nature of radiance, of true will' (<s>Chāndogya</s>

yathā sūryādijyotiḥsattānimittā sarvasya rūpajātasyābhivyaktistadvat /

prakṛtaṃ ca brahma 'yasmindyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣamotam' (mu. 2.2.5) ityādinā /
anantaraṃ ca 'hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣphalam /

children.translated_text: And the negation of their shining is also justified with respect to <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yato yadupalabhante tatsarvaṃ brahmaṇaiva jyotiṣopalabhyate, brahma tu nānyena jyotiṣopalabhyate svayaṃ jyotiḥsvarūpatvāt, yena sūryādayastasminbhāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Because whatever [entities] apprehend, all that is apprehended only through the light of <s>Brahman</s>; but <s>Brahman</s> is not apprehended through any other light — because it is of the nature of self-luminosity — by which the sun and such would shine in it.

children.text: brahma hyānyadvyanakti natu brahmānyena vyajyate /
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s> illuminates other things, but <s>Brahman</s> is not illuminated by another.

children.text: 'ātmanaivāyaṃ jyotiṣāste' (bṛ. 4.3.6), 'āgṛhyo nahi gṛhyate' (bṛ. 4.2.4) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: 'By the Self alone one sits with light' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.6); 'It is ungraspable, for it cannot be grasped' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.2.4) — from such <s>śruti</s> passages. // 22 //

3.14.2) — for thus they teach the conscious Self. But it is not well known that the sun and such shine after some particular luminous element. And because of the sameness of the luminous elements — sun and such — there is no dependence on another luminous element after which they would shine. For a lamp does not shine after another lamp. As for the objection that imitation is observed among things of the same nature — this is not an invariable rule. For imitation is also observed among things of different natures — as when a heated iron ball, imitating fire, burns after the fire that burns; or when earthly dust, carried along, follows the wind that carries. By '<s>anukṛteḥ</s>' (because of imitation), he indicates the [first part about] 'shining after.' And by '<s>tasya ca</s>' (and because of that), he indicates the fourth quarter of this verse. 'By His light all this is illuminated' — this statement that the shining of the sun and such is caused by [<s>Brahman</s>] points to the conscious Self. 'The gods worship that light of lights as immortal life' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.16) — for thus they teach the conscious Self. That the light of the sun and such should shine by means of another luminous element is both unknown and contradictory, because one luminous element would counteract another. Alternatively, this statement that the shining is caused by [<s>Brahman</s>] does not refer only to the sun and such entities enumerated in the verse. Rather, because of the unqualified <s>śruti</s> 'all this,' the manifestation of this entire realm of names, forms, actions, agents, and fruits is caused by the presence of the light of <s>Brahman</s> — just as the manifestation of the entire realm of visible forms is caused by the presence of the light of the sun and such. 'The sun does not shine there' — by introducing the word 'there' (<s>tatra</s>), [the text] shows reference to the topic. And the topic is <s>Brahman</s>, [introduced] by 'that in which heaven, earth, and the intermediate space are woven' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.5) and so forth. And immediately following: 'In the supreme golden sheath, <s>Brahman</s> is stainless, without parts; that which is bright, the light of lights — that is what the knowers of the Self know.' How is it the light of lights? From this arose [the verse]: 'The sun does not shine there.' As for the objection that the negation of the shining of the luminous entities like the sun is only possible with respect to another luminous element, just as the sun [negates] the others — there, it has been shown that no such other luminous element is possible.

children.text: FN: tatra tārakāntarāṇi candrādi ca na bhāti taṃ na bhāsayatīti yāvat /

children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Pramita Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Measured One) / <s>Sūtras</s> 24-25

children.text:
'aṅguṣṭamātraḥ puruṣaḥ madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati' iti śrūyate /
tathā aṅguṣṭamātraḥ puruṣo jyotirivādhūmakaḥ /
īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śva etadvai tat' (kā. 2.4.13) iti ca /
tatra yo 'yamaṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣaḥ śrūyate sa kiṃ vijñānātmā kiṃvā paramātmeti saṃśayaḥ /
tatra parimāṇopadeśāttāvadvijñānātmeti prāptam /
nahyanantāyāmavistārasya paramātmano 'ṅguṣṭhaparimāṇamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: For the measure of a thumb is not justified for the Supreme Self, which is of infinite length and breadth.

children.text: vijñānātmananastūpādhimattvātsaṃbhavati kayācitkalpanayāṅguṣṭhamātratvam /
children.translated_text: But for the cognizing self, because of possessing limiting adjuncts, being of the measure of a thumb is possible through some conception.

children.text: smṛteśca- 'atha satyavataḥ kāyātpāśabaddhaṃ vaśaṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: And from <s>Smṛti</s>: 'Then from the body of the truthful one, bound by the noose, under [<s>Yama</s>'s] control,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ niścakarṣaṃ yamo balāt' //
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> forcibly extracted the <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb.'

It is heard: 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb stands in the middle of the self.' And: 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb — like a light without smoke, the Lord of the past and future — He is the same today and tomorrow. This indeed is That' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.4.13). Therein, the doubt arises: is this <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb that is heard the cognizing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) or the Supreme Self? The initial position: because of the teaching of a specific measure, it would be the cognizing self.
(<s>Mahābhārata</s> 3.297.17)

children.text:
iti /
nahi parameśvaro balādyamena niṣkraṣṭuṃ śakyastena tatra saṃsāryaṅguṣṭhamātro niścitaḥ sa evehāpītyevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - paramātmaivāyamaṅguṣṭhamātraparimitaḥ puruṣo bhavitumarhati /
kasmāt, śabdāt, 'īśāno bhūtabhavyasya' iti /
nahyanyaḥ parameśvarādbhūtabhavyasya niraṅ kuśamīśitā /
'etadvai tat' iti ca prakṛtaṃ pṛṣṭamihānusaṃdadhāti /
children.translated_text: 'This indeed is That' — by this, [the text] connects the topic here with what was asked.

children.text: etadvai tadyatpṛṣṭaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: 'This indeed is That — the <s>Brahman</s> that was asked about.'

children.text: pṛṣṭaṃ ceha brahma 'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmādanyatrāsmātkṛtākṛtāt /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Brahman</s> asked about here is: 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>, other than this done and undone,

children.text: anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca yattatpaśyasi tadvada' (kā. 1.2.14) iti śabdādevetyabhidhānaśrutereveśāna iti parameśvaro 'yaṃ gamyata ityarthaḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: other than the past and the future — that which you see, tell me' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.14). From the word alone — meaning from the <s>śruti</s> statement 'the Lord' itself — this is understood to be the Supreme Lord. This is the meaning. // 24 //

For the Supreme Lord cannot be forcibly extracted by <s>Yama</s>; therefore, the transmigrating self of the measure of a thumb is determined there, and the same [transmigrating self] is here too — this being the position reached, we say: this <s>Puruṣa</s>, measured as the size of a thumb, deserves to be the Supreme Self itself. Why? Because of the word — 'the Lord of the past and future.' For no one other than the Supreme Lord is the unrestricted ruler of the past and future.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ sarvagatasya paramātmanaḥ parimāṇopadeśa ityatra brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: But how can a specific measure be taught for the all-pervading Supreme Self? To this we say:

children.text: FN: ātmani dehe madhye hṛdayasapranītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'In the self' — meaning in the body, in the middle, i.e., in the region of the heart.

children.text: bhūtabhavyagrahaṇaṃ bhavato 'pi pradarśanārtham kālatrayaniyantetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mention of 'past and future' is to show [His lordship over] the present as well — the meaning is: He governs the three times.

children.text: kayāciditi hṛdayakamalakośasya jīvopalabdhisthānasyāṅguṣṭhamātratayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Through some [conception]' — the meaning is: because the lotus of the heart, the place where the individual soul is apprehended, is of the measure of a thumb.

children.text: hṛdyapekṣayā tu manuṣyādhikāratvāt | BBs_1,3.25 |
children.translated_text: With reference to the heart, because the teaching is meant for humans. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.25 |

children.text:
sarvagatasyāpi paramātmano hṛdaye 'vasthānamapekṣyāṅguṣṭhamātratvamidamucyate /
ākāśasyeva vaṃśaparvāpekṣamaratrimātratvam /
nahyañjasātimātrasya paramātmano 'ṅguṣṭhamātratvamupapadyate /
na cānyaḥ paramātmana iha grahaṇamarhatīśānaśabdādibhya ityuktam /
children.translated_text: Even for the all-pervading Supreme Self, this measure of a thumb is stated with reference to being situated in the heart. Just as the measure of a palm-span is [stated] for space with reference to the internode of a bamboo. For it is not justified that the Supreme Self, who is beyond all measure, should [literally] be of the measure of a thumb. And it has been stated that no one other than the Supreme Self can be grasped here, because of the word 'Lord' and such.

children.text:
nanu pratiprāṇibhedaṃ hṛdayānāmanavasthitatvādapekṣamapyaṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ nopapadyata ityata uttaramucyate- manuṣyādhikāratvāditi /
śāstraṃ hyaviśeṣapravṛttamapi manuṣyānevādhikaroti,
children.translated_text: But since the hearts of different living beings differ in their dimensions, even the relative measure of a thumb is not justified — to this the reply is given: because the teaching is meant for humans. For scripture, though applicable without distinction, qualifies only humans,

children.text:
śaktatvādarthitvādaparyudastatvādupanayanādiśāstrācceti varṇitametadadhikāralakṣaṇe (jai. 6.1) /
manuṣyāṇāṃ ca niyataparimāṇaḥ kāyaḥ /
aucityena niyataparimāṇameva caiṣāmaṅguṣṭhamātraṃ hṛdayam /
ato manuṣyādhikāratvācchāstrasya manuṣyahṛdayāvasthānāpekṣamaṅguṣṭhamātratvamupapannaṃ paramātmanaḥ /
yadapyuktaṃ parimāṇopadeśātsmṛteśca saṃsāryevāyamaṅguṣṭamātraḥ pratyetavya iti, tatpratyucyate- 'sa ātmā tattvamasi' ityādivatsaṃsāriṇa eva sato 'ṅguṣṭhamātrasya brahmatvamidamupadiśyata iti /
dvirūpā hi vedāntavākyānāṃ pravṛttiḥ, kvacitparamātmasvarūpanirūpaṇaparā kvacidvijñānātmanaḥ paramātmaikatvopadeśaparā /
tadatra vijñānātmanaḥ paramātmanaikatvamupadiśyate nāṅguṣṭhamātratvaṃ kasyacit /
children.translated_text: Therein, what is taught here is the oneness of the cognizing self with the Supreme Self — not that anyone is [literally] of the measure of a thumb.

children.text: etamevārthaṃ pareṇa sphuṭīkariṣyati- 'aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: The subsequent [verse] will make this very meaning clear: 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb, the inner Self, is always seated in the heart of people.

children.text: taṃ svāccharīrātpravṛhenmuñjādiveṣikāṃ dhairyeṇa /
children.translated_text: One should draw Him out from one's own body, as one draws the stalk from a <s>muñja</s> grass, with courage.

children.text: taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtam' (kā. 2.6.17) iti //25 //
children.translated_text: One should know Him as the bright, the immortal' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6.17). // 25 //

because of their capability, desire [for liberation], and non-exclusion, and because of the scripture on <s>Upanayana</s> (initiation) and such — as has been discussed in the section on qualifications (<s>Jaimini</s> 6.1). And for humans, the body has a fixed measure. And the heart of humans is fittingly of the fixed measure of a thumb. Therefore, because the scripture's teaching is meant for humans, the measure of a thumb for the Supreme Self is justified with reference to being situated in the human heart. As for the objection that, because of the teaching of a specific measure and because of <s>Smṛti</s>, this thumb-sized [<s>Puruṣa</s>] should be understood as the transmigrating self — to that we reply: just as in 'That Self, you are That' and such, the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the transmigrating self, which is of the measure of a thumb, is here taught. For the <s>Vedānta</s> passages proceed in two ways: sometimes aiming at determining the nature of the Supreme Self, and sometimes aiming at teaching the oneness of the cognizing self with the Supreme Self.

children.text: FN: sakaniṣṭhaḥ karo 'ratniḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The forearm with the little finger is an <s>aratni</s> (cubit).

children.text: atra manuṣyaśabdastraivarṇikaparaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the word 'human' refers to the three upper <s>varṇas</s>.

children.text: 'śūdro yajñe 'navakḷptaḥ' iti paryudāsāt, upanīyata, tamadhyāpayīta, iti śūdrādhikāravāraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Śūdra</s> is not qualified for sacrifice' — because of this exclusion; '[one should] initiate [him], [one should] teach him' — [these rules] prevent the qualification of <s>Śūdras</s>.

children.text:
śarīrātsthūlātsūkṣmācca taṃ jīvaṃ pravṛhetpṛthakkaryāt /
dhairyeṇa śamādineti yāvat /
children.translated_text: From the body — both gross and subtle — one should draw out that <s>jīva</s>, separating it from the effect. 'With courage' means with <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and such [disciplines].

children.text: 8 devatādhikaraṇam / sū. 26-33
children.translated_text: 8. The <s>Devatā Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Deity) / <s>Sūtras</s> 26-33

children.text: tadupary api bādarāyaṇaḥ saṃbhavāt | BBs_1,3.26 |
