children.translated_text: Those above [humans] too — [this is the view of] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because of the possibility. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.26 |

children.text:
aṅguṣṭhamātraśrutirmanuṣyahṛdayāpekṣayā manuṣyādhikāratvācchāstrasyetyuktaṃ, tatprasaṅgenedamucyate /
bāḍhaṃ manuṣyādhikāreti śāstram /
natu manuṣyānevetīha brahmajñāne niyamo 'sti /
teṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāmupariṣṭādye devādayastānapyadhikaroti śāstramiti bādarāyaṇa ācāryo manyante /
kasmāt /
saṃbhavāt /
saṃbhavati hi teṣāmapyarthitvādyadhikārakāraṇam /
tatrārthitvaṃ tāvanmokṣaviṣayaṃ devādīnāmapi saṃbhavati vikāraviṣayavibhūtyanityatvālocanādinimittam /
tathā sāmarthyamapi teṣāṃ saṃbhavati, mantrārthavādetihāsapurāṇalokebhyo vigrahavattvādyavagamāt /
naca teṣāṃ kaścitpratiṣedho 'sti /
nacopanayanaśāstreṇaiṣāmadhikāro nivartyeta, upanayanasya vedādhyayanārthatvāt /
teṣāṃ ca svayaṃpratibhātavedatvāt /
apicaiṣāṃ vidyāgrahaṇārthaṃ brahmacaryādi darśayati- 'ekaśataṃ ha vai varṣāṇi maghavānprajāpatau brahmacaryamuvāsa' (chā. 8.11.3), 'bhṛgurvai vāruṇiḥ /
varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra /
adhīhi bhagavo brahma' (tai. 3.1) ityādi /
yadapi karmasvanadhikārakāraṇamuktam- 'na devānāṃ devatāntarābhāvāt' iti, 'na ṛṣīṇāmārṣeyāntarābhāvāt' (jai.6.1.6,7) iti /
na tadvidyāsvasti /
nahīndrādīnāṃ vidyāsvadhakriyamāṇānāmindrādyuddeśena kiñcitkṛtyamasti /
children.translated_text: For when <s>Indra</s> and others are performing knowledge-practices, there is nothing to be done with reference to <s>Indra</s> and others [as deities of offering].

children.text: naca bhṛgvādīnāṃ bhṛgvādisagotratayā /
children.translated_text: Nor is there [a problem] for <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others on account of their being of the same lineage as <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others.

children.text: tasmāddevādīnāmapi vidyāsvadhikāraḥ kena vāryate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what prevents the gods and others from being qualified for knowledge-practices?

children.text: devādyadhikāre 'pyaṅguṣṭamātraśrutiḥ svāṅguṣṭhāpekṣayā na virudhyate // 26 //
children.translated_text: Even when the gods and others are accepted as qualified, the scriptural reference to the thumb-measure is not contradicted, being relative to their own thumb. // 26 //

It was stated that the scriptural reference to the thumb-measure is with reference to the human heart, because the scripture has human beings as its qualified [subjects]. In that connection, this is stated: The scripture indeed has human beings as its qualified subjects. But there is no restriction that only human beings [are qualified] for this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. The teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds that the scripture qualifies even the gods and others who are above those human beings. Why? Because of the possibility. For even for them, the cause of qualification such as the desire [for liberation] and the like is possible. In that regard, the desire pertaining to liberation is possible even for the gods and others — occasioned by the reflection on the impermanence of the prosperity pertaining to the realm of modifications. Likewise, the capacity too is possible for them, since from <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, <s>itihāsas</s>, <s>purāṇas</s>, and common experience, their possession of bodily forms and such is understood. And there is no prohibition regarding them. Nor would their qualification be negated by the rules of <s>upanayana</s> (investiture), since <s>upanayana</s> is for the purpose of Vedic study. And for them, the <s>Vedas</s> are self-revealed. Moreover, [scripture] shows their observance of celibate studentship and such for the purpose of acquiring knowledge: '<s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>) indeed lived as a celibate student with <s>Prajāpati</s> for one hundred and one years' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.11.3); '<s>Bhṛgu</s>, the son of <s>Varuṇa</s>, approached his father <s>Varuṇa</s> [and said]: "Teach me, revered sir, <s>Brahman</s>"' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.1) — and so forth. As for the reasons stated for the lack of qualification of [gods] in ritual actions: 'Not the gods, because of the absence of another deity [to whom offerings could be directed]' and 'Not the <s>ṛṣis</s>, because of the absence of another <s>ṛṣi</s>'s lineage [to which the ritual could be attributed]' (<s>Jaimini</s> 6.1.6-7) — that [restriction] does not apply to [meditative] knowledge.

children.text: FN: devānāṃ karmasu nādhikāraḥ, devatāntarāṇāmuddeśyānāmabhāvāditi prathamasūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The meaning of the first <s>sūtra</s> is: The gods are not qualified in ritual actions, because of the absence of other deities as recipients [of offerings].

children.text: ṛṣīṇāmapi na, ṛṣyāntarābhāvādṛṣiyukte karmaṇyaśakteriti dvitīyasūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of the second <s>sūtra</s> is: The <s>ṛṣis</s> too are not [qualified], because of the absence of another <s>ṛṣi</s>'s lineage — [meaning] they are unable in a ritual that requires a <s>ṛṣi</s> [officiator].

children.text: tat asāmarthyarūpaṃ kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: That [lack of qualification in ritual] is a reason in the form of incapacity.

children.text: virodhaḥ karmaṇīti cen nānekapratipatter darśanāt | BBs_1,3.27 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said there would be] a contradiction in ritual — [we say] no, because of the observation that multiple forms are assumed. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.27 |

children.text:
syādetat, yadi vigrahavattvādyabhyupagamena devādīnāṃ vidyāsvadhikāro varṇyeta vigrahavattvādṛtvigādindrādīnāmapi svarūpasaṃnidhānena karmāṅgabhāvo 'bhyupagamyeta /
tadā ca virodhaḥ karmaṇi syāt /
nahīndrādīnāṃ svarūpasaṃnidhānena yāge 'ṅgabhāvo dṛśyate /
naca saṃbhavati /
bahuṣu yāgeṣu yugapadekasyendrasya svarūpasaṃnidhānatānupapatteriti cet /
nāyamasti virodhaḥ /
kasmāt /
anekapratipatteḥ /
ekasyāpi devatātmano yugapadanekasvarūpapratipattiḥ saṃbhavati /
kathametadavagamyate /
darśanāt /
children.translated_text: From observation.

children.text: tathāhi-'kati devāḥ' ityupakramya 'trayaśca trī ca śatā trayaśca trī ca sahasrā' iti nirucya 'katama te' ityasyāṃ pṛcchāyām 'mahimāna evaiṣāmete trayastriṃśattveva devāḥ' (bṛ. 3.9.1,2) iti nirbruvatī śrutirekaikasya devatātmano yugapadanekarūpatāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: For, having begun with 'How many are the gods?' and having resolved: 'Three hundred and three, and three thousand and three' — in response to the question 'Which are those?' — the <s>śruti</s>, declaring 'These are only their manifestations; the gods are indeed just thirty-three' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.1-2), shows that each divine self simultaneously has multiple forms.

children.text: tathā trayastriṃśato 'pi ṣaḍādyantarbhāvakrameṇa 'katama eko deva iti prāṇaḥ' iti prāṇaikarūpatāṃ devānāṃ darśayantī tasyaikasya prāṇasya yugapadanekarūpatāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, even the thirty-three, through the process of subsumption into six and then further — 'Which is the one god? <s>Prāṇa</s>' — showing the unity of the gods in the form of <s>Prāṇa</s>, [the text] shows the simultaneous multiplicity of forms of that one <s>Prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tathā smṛtirapi- 'ātmano vai śarīrāṇi bahūni bharatarṣabha //
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>smṛti</s> too [states]: 'The <s>yogin</s>, having attained power, may create

It might be said: If by accepting that the gods and others have bodily forms, their qualification in knowledge-practices is maintained, then since the gods have bodily forms, the bodily presence of <s>Indra</s> and others as officiating priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) and their status as components of the ritual would also have to be accepted. In that case, there would be a contradiction in ritual. For the bodily presence of <s>Indra</s> and others as components of a sacrifice is not observed. And it is not possible — because of the impossibility of one <s>Indra</s> being bodily present simultaneously in many sacrifices. If this is the objection — this contradiction does not exist. Why? Because of multiple forms being assumed. Even for a single divine self, the simultaneous assumption of multiple forms is possible. How is this understood?

children.text: yogī kuryādbalaṃ prāpya taiśca sarvairmahīṃ caret //
children.translated_text: many bodies from his own self, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>, and with all of them may traverse the earth.

children.text: prāpnuyādviṣayānkaiścidugraṃ tapaścaret //
children.translated_text: With some he may enjoy objects, with others he may practice fierce austerity.

children.text: saṃkṣipecca punastāni sūryo raśmigaṇāniva' //
children.translated_text: And he may withdraw them again, as the sun [withdraws] its rays.'

children.text: ityevañjātīyakā prāptāṇimādyaiśvaryāṇāṃ yogināmapi yugapadanekaśarīrayogaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Such passages show that even <s>yogins</s> who have attained powers like <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming atomic) and such can simultaneously be connected with multiple bodies.

children.text: kimu vaktavyamājānasiddhānāṃ devānām /
children.translated_text: What need be said, then, of the gods, whose [powers] are innately established?

children.text: anekarūpapratipattisaṃbhavāccaikaikā devatā bahubhī rūpairātmānaṃ pravibhajya bahuṣu yāgeṣu yugapadaṅgabhāvaṃ gacchatīti /
children.translated_text: Since assuming multiple forms is possible, each deity, dividing itself into many forms, can simultaneously serve as a component in many sacrifices.

children.text: paraiśca na dṛśyate 'ntardhānādikriyāyogādityupapadyate //
children.translated_text: And it is tenable that they are not seen by others — because of [their] capacity for actions such as becoming invisible.

children.text: anekapratipatterdarśanādityasyāparā vyākhyā- vigrahavatāmapi karmāṅgabhāvacodanāsvanekā pratipattirdṛśyate /
children.translated_text: An alternative interpretation of 'because of the observation that multiple forms are assumed': Even in injunctions regarding bodily agents as components of ritual, multiple modes of being a component are observed.

children.text: kvacideko 'pi vigrahavānanekatra yugapadaṅgabhāvaṃ na gacchati, yathā bahubhirbhojayadbhirnaiko brāhmaṇo yugapadbhojyate /
children.translated_text: In some cases, even one bodily agent does not simultaneously serve as a component in multiple [rituals] — just as one <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is not simultaneously fed by many hosts.

children.text: kvaciccaiko 'pi vigrahavānanekatra yugapadaṅgabhāvaṃ gacchati, yathā bahubhirnamaskurvāṇaireko brāhmaṇo yugapannamaskriyate /
children.translated_text: But in some cases, one bodily agent does simultaneously serve as a component in multiple [rituals] — just as one <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is simultaneously saluted by many people saluting.

children.text: tadvadihoddeśaparityāgātmakatvādyāgasya vigrahavatīmapyekāṃ devatāmuddiśya bahavaḥ svaṃ svaṃ dravyaṃ yugapatparityakṣyantīti vigrahavattve 'pi devatānāṃ na kiñcitkarmaṇi virudhyate // 27//
children.translated_text: Similarly here, since sacrifice has the nature of offering by relinquishing [one's own possessions] for a particular deity, many [sacrificers] can simultaneously relinquish their own substances directed toward even one deity that has a bodily form — thus, even if the deities have bodily forms, nothing is contradicted in ritual. // 27 //

children.text: FN: darśanāt śrutiprāmāṇyāt /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Darśanāt</s>' means from the authority of <s>śruti</s>.

children.text:
vaiśvadevaśāstrasya hi nividi kati devā ityupakramya śākalyāya yājñavalkyena trayaścettyuttaram /
nivinnāma śasyamānadevatāsaṃkhyāvācakāni mantrapadāni /
children.translated_text: For in the <s>nividh</s> (invocatory formula) of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> ritual, having begun with 'How many are the gods?', <s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied to <s>Śākalya</s>: 'Three hundred and three,' etc. '<s>Nividh</s>' means the <s>mantra</s>-words that express the number of deities being praised.

children.text: balaṃ yogasiddhim /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bala</s>' (power) means the attainment of <s>yogic</s> perfection.

children.text:
'aṇimā mahimā caiva garimā prāptirīśitā /
prākamyaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ ca tatra kāmāvasāyitā' ityaṇimādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Aṇimā</s>, <s>mahimā</s>, <s>garimā</s>, <s>prāpti</s>, <s>īśitā</s>, <s>prākāmya</s>, <s>vaśitva</s>, and <s>kāmāvasāyitā</s>' — these are the <s>aṇimā</s> and other [eight powers].

children.text: ājānasiddhānāṃ janmanaiva prāptiśayānām /
children.translated_text: 'Innately established' means those whose attainments are present from birth.

children.text: śabda iti cen nātaḥ prabhavāt pratyakṣānumānābhyām | BBs_1,3.28 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said there would be] a contradiction in [the eternality of] words — [we say] no, because [the world] originates from these [words], as [shown by] direct testimony and inference. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.28 |

children.text:
mā nāma vigrahavattve devādīnāmabhyupagamyamāne karmaṇi kaścidvirodhaḥ prasañji /
śabde tu virodhaḥ prasajyeta /
katham /
autpattikaṃ hi śabdasyārthena saṃbandhamāśritya 'anapekṣatvāt' iti vedasya prāmāṇyaṃ sthāpitam /
idānīṃ tu vigrahavatī devatābhyupagamyamānā yadyapyaiśvaryayogādyugapadanekakarmasaṃbandhīni havīṃṣi bhuñjīta tathāpi vigrahayogādasmadādivajjananamaraṇavatī seti nityasya śabdasya nityenārthena nitye saṃbandhepratīyamāne yadvaidike śabde prāmāṇyaṃ sthitaṃ tasya virodhaḥ syāditi cet /
nāyamapyasti virodhaḥ /
kasmāt /
ataḥ prabhavāt /
ata eva hi vaidikācchabdādevādikaṃ jagatprabhavati /
children.translated_text: Let there not be any contradiction in ritual when the gods are accepted as having bodily forms. But there would be a contradiction regarding words. How? For the validity of the <s>Veda</s> was established by relying on the beginningless relation between word and meaning — '<s>anapekṣatvāt</s>' (because of its independence [from any author]). But now, if the deities are accepted as having bodily forms, then even though they might, by their lordly power, simultaneously enjoy the oblations connected with many rituals, nevertheless, being possessed of bodies, they would, like us, be subject to birth and death. In that case, when the eternal word is understood as having an eternal relation with an eternal meaning, the validity that was established for Vedic words would be contradicted — if this is the objection, this contradiction too does not exist. Why? Because [the world] originates from these [words]. For from these very Vedic words, the world of gods and others originates. But was it not determined in 'That from which the origin and such of this [world proceed]' (<s>BBs</s> 1.1.2) that the world originates from <s>Brahman</s> — how then is it said here that it originates from words? Moreover, even if the origination from Vedic words is accepted, how is the contradiction regarding words thereby resolved — since the meanings [of words], namely the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Viśvedevas</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, and such, are non-eternal, being subject to origination? And when those [meanings] are non-eternal, what prevents the Vedic words — '<s>Vasu</s>,' '<s>Āditya</s>,' and such — that designate them from being non-eternal? For it is well-known in the world that when a son is born to <s>Devadatta</s>, a name '<s>Yajñadatta</s>' is given to him. Therefore, there is indeed a contradiction regarding words — if this is the objection,

children.text:
nanu janmādyasya yataḥ (bra. 1.1.2) ityatra brahmaprabhavatvaṃ jagato 'vadhāritaṃ, kathamiha śabdaprabhavatvamucyate /
apica yadi nāma vaidikācchabdādasya prabhavo 'bhyupagataḥ, kathametāvatā virodhaḥ śabde parihṛtaḥ yāvatā vasavo rudrā ādityā viśvedevā maruta ityeter'thā anityā evotpattimattvāt /
tadanityatve ca tadvācināṃ vaidikānāṃ vasvādiśabdānāmanityatvaṃ kena nivāryate /
prasiddhaṃ hi loke devadattasya putra utpanne yajñadatta iti tasya nāma kriyata iti /
tasmādvirodha eva śabda iti cet /
children.translated_text: No. Because the eternality of the relation between word, meaning, and referent — as in '<s>go</s>' (cow) and such — is observed. For even though the individual instances of cows and such are subject to origination, their universal forms (<s>ākṛti</s>) are not subject to origination.

children.text:
na /
gavādiśabdārthasaṃbandhanityatvadarśanāt /
nahi gavādivyaktīnāmutpattimattve tadākṛtīnīmapyutpattimattvaṃ syāt /
dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ hi vyaktaya evotpadyante nākṛtayaḥ /
ākṛtibhiśca śabdānāṃ saṃbandho na vyaktibhiḥ /
vyaktīnāmānantyātsaṃbandhagrahaṇānupapatteḥ /
vyaktiṣūtpadyamānāsvapyākṛtīnāṃ nityatvācca gavādiśabdeṣu kaścidvirodho dṛśyate /
tathā devādivyaktiprabhavābhyupagame 'pyākṛtinityatvānna kaścidvasvādiśabdeṣu virodha iti draṣṭavyam /
ākṛtiviśeṣastu devādīnāṃ mantrārthavādādibhyo vigrahavattvādyavagamādavagantavyaḥ /
sthānaviśeṣasaṃbandhanimittāścendrādiśabdāḥ senāpatyādiśabdavat /
tataśca yo yastattatsthānamadhirohati sa sa indrādiśabdairabhidhīyata iti na doṣo bhavati /
nacedaṃ śabdaprabhavatvaṃ brahmaprabhavatvavadupādānakāraṇābhiprāyeṇocyate /
kathaṃ tarhi sthite vācakātmanā nitye śabde nityārthasaṃbandhini śabdavyavahārayogyārthavyaktiniṣpattirataḥ prabhava ityucyate kathaṃ punaravagamyate śabdātprabhavati jagaditi /
pratyakṣānumānābhyām /
pratyakṣaṃ śrutiḥ, prāmāṇyaṃ pratyanapekṣatvāt /
anumānaṃ smṛtiḥ, prāmāṇyaṃ prati sāpekṣatvāt /
te hi śabdapūrvo sṛṣṭiṃ darśayataḥ /
'ete iti vai prajāpatirdevānasṛjatāsṛgramiti manuṣyānindava iti pitṛṃstiraḥ pavitramiti grahānāśava iti stotraṃ viśvānīti śastramabhisaubhagetyanyāḥ prajāḥ' iti śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With the words "<s>ete</s>" <s>Prajāpati</s> created the gods, with "<s>asṛgram</s>" the humans, with "<s>indavaḥ</s>" the ancestors, with "<s>tiraḥ pavitram</s>" the libation-vessels, with "<s>āśavaḥ</s>" the <s>stotra</s> [chants], with "<s>viśvāni</s>" the <s>śastra</s> [recitations], with "<s>abhisaubhaga</s>" the other beings' — thus the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: tathānyatrāpi 'sa manasā vācaṃ mithunaṃ samabhavat' (bṛ. 1.2.4) ityādinā tatratatra śabdapūrvikā sṛṣṭiḥ śrāvyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise elsewhere too, 'He coupled with speech through the mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.2.4) — and such passages in various places declare that creation is preceded by words.

children.text: smṛtirapi- 'anādinidhanā nityā vāgutsṛṣṭā svayaṃbhuvā /
children.translated_text: And <s>smṛti</s> also [states]: 'Beginningless and endless, eternal — the Word (<s>Vāc</s>) was emitted by the Self-Born One;

children.text: ādau vedamayī divyā yataḥ sarvā pravṛttayaḥ' //
children.translated_text: In the beginning, divine, consisting of the <s>Vedas</s> — from which all activities proceed.'

No. Because the eternality of the relation between word, meaning, and referent — as in '<s>go</s>' (cow) and such — is observed. For even though the individual instances of cows and such are subject to origination, their universal forms (<s>ākṛti</s>) are not subject to origination. For of substances, qualities, and actions, it is only the individual instances that are originated, not the universal forms. And the relation of words is with universal forms, not with individual instances — because, since individual instances are infinite, the apprehension of the relation [with all of them] would be impossible. And since the universal forms are eternal even when individual instances are being originated, no contradiction is seen in words like '<s>go</s>' (cow) and such. Likewise, it should be seen that even when the origination of individual instances of gods and such is accepted, there is no contradiction in the words '<s>Vasu</s>' and such, because of the eternality of the universal forms. And the specific universal form of the gods and such is to be understood from <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, and such, since from these we understand their possession of bodily forms and the like. And the words '<s>Indra</s>' and such are connected with particular positions — like the words '<s>commander-in-chief</s>' and such. Therefore, whoever ascends to that particular position is designated by the words '<s>Indra</s>' and such — so there is no fault. And this origination from words is not stated in the sense of a material cause, as in the case of origination from <s>Brahman</s>. Rather, how [is it stated]? The words — eternal in their nature as designators — being connected with eternal meanings: the origination of individual instances of things fit for verbal usage from these [words] is called origination from words. But how is it understood that the world originates from words? From direct testimony and inference. 'Direct testimony' means <s>śruti</s>, since its validity is independent [of any other source]. 'Inference' means <s>smṛti</s>, since its validity depends [on <s>śruti</s>]. For both of these show that creation is preceded by words.

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: utsargo 'pyayaṃ vācaḥ saṃpradāyapravartanātmako draṣṭavyaḥ, anādinidhanāyā anyādṛśasyotsargasyāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: And this 'emission' of speech should be understood as the setting in motion of tradition — since any other kind of emission of [speech] which is beginningless and endless is impossible.

children.text: tathā 'nāma rūpaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ ca pravartanam /
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'The names, forms, and activities of beings —

children.text: vedaśabdebhya evādau nirmame sa maheśvaraḥ' //
children.translated_text: from the words of the <s>Veda</s> alone, in the beginning, that great Lord fashioned.'

children.text: (manu. 1.21) iti /
' sarveṣāṃ tu sa nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthakpṛthak /
children.translated_text: 'And of all [beings], the names and activities, each separately,

children.text: vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthaksaṃsthāśca nirmame' //
children.translated_text: and their separate forms — from the words of the <s>Veda</s> alone, in the beginning, he fashioned.'

children.text:
iti ca /
apica cikīrṣitamarthamanutiṣṭhaṃstasya vācakaṃ śabdaṃ pūrvaṃ smṛtvā paścāttamarthamanuṣṭhatīti sarveṣāṃ naḥ pratyakṣametat /
tathā prajāpaterapi sraṣṭuḥ sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ vaidikāḥ śabdā manasi prādurbabhūvuḥ, paścāttadanugatānarthānsasarjeti gamyate /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'sa bhūriti vyāhāratsa bhūmimasṛjata' (tai.brā. 2.2.4.2) ityevamādikā bhūrādiśabdebhya eva manasi prādurbhūtebhyo bhūrādilokānsṛṣṭāndarśayati /
kimātmakaṃ punaḥ śabdamabhipretyedaṃ śabdaprabhavatvamucyate /
sphoṭamityāha /
varṇapakṣe hi teṣāmutpannapradhvaṃsitvānnityebhyaḥ śabdebhyo devādivyaktīnāṃ prabhava ityanupapannaṃ syāt /
utpannadhvaṃsinaśca varṇāḥ, pratyuccāraṇamanyathā cānyathā ca pratīyamānatvāt /
tathāhi- adṛśyamāno 'pi puruṣaviśeṣo 'dhyayanadhvaniśravaṇādeva viśeṣato nirdhāryate devadatto 'yamadhīte yajñadatto 'yamadhīte iti /
nacāyaṃ varṇaviṣayo 'nyathātvapratyayo mithyājñānaṃ, bādhakapratyayābhāvāt /
naca varṇebhyor'thāvagatiryuktā /
na hyekaiko varṇor'thaṃ pratyāyayet, vyabhicārāt /
naca varṇasamudāyapratyayo 'sti, kramavattvādvarṇānām /
children.translated_text: Thus. Moreover, one who is about to carry out an intended task first remembers the word that designates it, and then carries out that task — this is a matter of direct experience for all of us. Similarly, it is understood that for <s>Prajāpati</s> too, the creator, prior to creation, the Vedic words arose in the mind, and afterward he created the things conforming to them. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'He uttered "<s>Bhūḥ</s>" — and created the earth' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.2.4.2) — such [passages] show that the worlds — earth and such — were created from the words '<s>Bhūḥ</s>' and such that first arose in the mind. But with what kind of word in mind is this 'origination from words' stated? He says: the <s>sphoṭa</s> (the word-whole). For on the view that [words consist of] phonemes, since those are originated and destroyed [with each utterance], the origination of individual instances of gods and such from eternal words would be untenable. And phonemes are originated and destroyed, because they are perceived differently with each pronunciation. For even an unseen particular person is determined specifically just by hearing the sound of recitation: 'This is <s>Devadatta</s> reciting; this is <s>Yajñadatta</s> reciting.' And this perception of difference regarding phonemes is not false knowledge, because there is no sublating cognition. And it is not proper that the meaning should be understood from phonemes. For individual phonemes cannot convey meaning, because of their inconsistency [in conveying the same meaning]. And there is no cognition of a collection of phonemes, because phonemes are sequential.

children.text:
pūrvapūrvavarṇānubhavajanitasaṃskārasahito 'ntyo varṇor'thaṃ pratyāyayiṣyatīti yadyucyeta /
tanna /
saṃbandhagrahaṇāpekṣo hi śabdaḥ svayaṃ pratīyamānor'thaṃ pratyāyayeddhūmādivat /
naca pūrvapūrvavarṇānubhavajanitasaṃskārasahitasyāntyavarṇasya pratītirasti, apratyakṣatvātsaṃskārāṇām /
kāryapratyāyitaiḥ saṃskāraiḥ sahito 'ntyo varṇorthaṃ pratyāyayiṣyatīti cet /
children.translated_text:
If it is said that the last phoneme, assisted by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by the experience of each preceding phoneme, will convey the meaning —
no.
For a word, requiring the apprehension of its relation [to its meaning], would convey meaning when it is itself cognized — like smoke and such [which convey fire].
But there is no cognition of the last phoneme assisted by the impressions generated by the experience of each preceding phoneme, since impressions are not directly perceptible.
If it is said that the last phoneme, assisted by impressions that are inferred through their effects, will convey the meaning —

children.text:
na /
saṃskārakāryasyāpi smaraṇasya kramavartitvāt /
tasmātsphoṭa eva śabdaḥ /
sa caicaikavarṇapratyayāhitasaṃskārabīje 'ntyavarṇapratyayajanitapari pāke pratyayinyekapratyayaviṣayatayā jhaṭiti pratyavabhāsate /
nacāyamekapratyayo varṇaviṣayā smṛtiḥ /
varṇānāmanekatvādekapratyayaviṣayatvānupapatteḥ /
tasya ca pratyuccāraṇaṃ pratyabhijñāyamānatvānnityatvam /
bhedapratyayasya varṇaviṣayatvāt /
tasmānnityācchabdasphoṭarūpādabhidhāyakātkriyākārakaphalalakṣaṇaṃ jagadabhidheyabhūtaṃ prabhavatīti /
varṇā eva tu na śabdaḥ iti bhagavānupavarṣaḥ.
children.translated_text:
No.
Because even memory, which is the effect of the impressions, operates sequentially.
Therefore, <s>sphoṭa</s> alone is the word.
And that [<s>sphoṭa</s>] — when, in the cognizing mind where the seed is the impression deposited by each individual phoneme-cognition, the maturation is produced by the cognition of the last phoneme — flashes forth instantaneously as the object of a single cognition.
And this single cognition is not a memory having phonemes as its object.
Because the phonemes being multiple, their being the object of a single cognition is unjustified.
And [<s>sphoṭa</s>] is eternal, because it is recognized as the same at each utterance.
Because the cognition of difference pertains to the phonemes [not to the <s>sphoṭa</s>].
Therefore, from the eternal word in the form of <s>sphoṭa</s>, which is the signifier, the world — characterized by action, instrument, and result — which is the signified, comes into being.
But the blessed <s>Upavarṣa</s> [holds that] phonemes alone are the word, not <s>sphoṭa</s>.

children.text:
nanūtpannapradhvaṃsitvaṃ varṇānmuktaṃ, tanna /
ta eveti pratyabhijñānāt /
sādṛśyātpratbhijñānaṃ keśādiṣviveti cet /
children.translated_text:
But the objection was made that phonemes are subject to arising and destruction — no, that is not so.
Because of the recognition 'these are the same [phonemes].'
If it is said that the recognition is due to similarity, as in [the case of] hair and such —

children.text:
na /
pratyabhijñānasya pramāṇāntareṇa bādhānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because recognition, being a valid means of knowledge, cannot be contradicted by another means of knowledge.

children.text: pratyabhijñānamākṛtinimittamiti cet /
children.translated_text: If it is said that the recognition is based on the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>) [rather than the particular] —

children.text:
na /
vyaktipratyabhijñānāt /
yadi hi pratyuccāraṇaṃ gavādivyaktivadanyā anyā varṇavyaktayaḥ pratīyeraṃstata ākṛtinimittaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ syāt /
natvetadasti /
varṇavyaktaya eva hi pratyuccāraṇaṃ pratyabhijñāyante /
dvirgośabda uccārita iti hi pratipattirna tu dvau gośabdāviti /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because the recognition is of the particular instance (<s>vyakti</s>).
For if, at each utterance, different particular instances of phonemes were cognized — as different particular instances of cows are — then the recognition would be based on the universal form.
But that is not the case.
For the particular instances of phonemes themselves are recognized at each utterance.
The cognition is 'the <s>go</s>-word has been uttered twice' — not 'there are two <s>go</s>-words.'

children.text: nanu varṇā apyuccāraṇabhedena bhinnaḥ pratīyante devadattayajñadattayoradhyayanadhvaniśravaṇādeva bhedapratīterityuktam /
children.translated_text: But it was said that phonemes too are perceived as different through differences in utterance — from the very hearing of the sounds of recitation by <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s>, the cognition of difference is evident.

children.text:
atrābhidhīyate- sati varṇaviṣaye niścite pratyabhijñāne saṃyogavibhāgābhivyaṅgyatvādvarṇānāmabhivyañjakavaicitryanimitto 'yaṃ varṇaviṣayo vicitraḥ pratyayo na svarūpanimittaḥ /
apica varṇavyaktibhedavādināpi pratyabhijñānasiddhaye varṇākṛtayaḥ kalpayitavyāḥ /
tāsu ca paropādhiko bhedapratyaya ityabhyupagantavyam /
tadvaraṃ varṇavyaktiṣveva paropādhiko bhedapratyayaḥ svarūpanimittaṃ ca pratyabhijñānamiti kalpanālāghavam /
eṣa eva ca varṇaviṣayasya bhedapratyayasya bādhakaḥ pratyayo yatpratyabhijñānam /
kathaṃ hyekasminkālaṃ bahūnāmuccārayatāmeka eva sangakāro yugapadanekarūpaḥ syāt /
udāttaścānudāttaśca svaritaśca sānunāsikaśca niranunāsikaśceti /
athavā dhvanikṛto 'yaṃ pratyayabhedo na varṇakṛta ityadoṣaḥ /
kaḥ punarayaṃ dhvanirnāma /
yo dūrādākarṇayato varṇavivekamapratipadyamānasya karṇapathamavatarati /
pratyāsīdataśca paṭumaṭutvādibhedaṃ varṇeṣvāsañjayati /
children.translated_text:
To this it is said: Given the established recognition pertaining to phonemes, since phonemes are manifested by the conjunction and disjunction [of articulatory organs], this varied cognition pertaining to phonemes is caused by the variety in the manifesting agents, not by their own nature.
Moreover, even one who holds that particular instances of phonemes are different would have to posit phoneme-universals (<s>varṇākṛti</s>) to account for recognition.
And regarding those [universals], it would have to be accepted that the cognition of difference is extrinsically conditioned.
It is therefore more economical to hold that the cognition of difference in the particular phoneme-instances themselves is extrinsically conditioned, and the recognition is based on their own nature — this involves less conceptual proliferation.
And this very recognition serves as the sublator of the cognition of difference pertaining to phonemes.
For how could a single <s>saṅkāra</s> (phoneme) uttered at one time by many persons simultaneously be of multiple forms?
[It would have to be] <s>udātta</s> (high-pitched), <s>anudātta</s> (low-pitched), <s>svarita</s> (circumflex), nasalized and non-nasalized.
Alternatively, this difference in cognition is produced by the accompanying sound (<s>dhvani</s>), not by the phoneme — hence no fault.
What then is this so-called <s>dhvani</s>?
It is that which enters the range of hearing of one who is at a distance and cannot discern individual phonemes.
And for one who comes closer, it produces [the impression of] differences such as clarity and unclearness in the phonemes.

children.text:
tannibandhanāścodāttādayo viśeṣā na varṇasvarūpanibandhanāḥ, varṇānāṃ pratyuccārāṇaṃ pratyabhijñāyamānatvāt /
evañca sati sālambanā udāttādipratyayā bhaviṣyanti /
itaradhā hi varṇānāṃ pratyabhijñāyamānānāṃ nirbhedatvātsaṃyogavibhāgakṛtā udāttādiviśeṣāḥ kalperan /
saṃyogavibhāgānāṃ cāpratyakṣatvācca tadāśrayā viśeṣā varṇeṣvadhyavasituṃ śakyanta ityato nirālambanā evaita udāttādipratyayāḥ syuḥ /
apica naivaitadabhiniveṣṭavyamudāttādibhedena varṇānāṃ pratyabhijñāyamānānāṃ bhedo bhavediti /
nahyanyasya bhedenānyasyābhidyamānasya bhedo bhavitumarhati /
nahi vyaktibhedena jātiṃ bhinnāṃ manyante /
varṇebhyaścārthapratīteḥ saṃbhavātsphoṭakalpanānarthikā /
na kalpayāmyahaṃ sphoṭaṃ pratyakṣameva tvenamavagacchāmi, ekaikavarṇagrahaṇāhitasaṃskārāyāṃ buddhau jhaṭiti pratyava ūbhāsanāditi cet /
children.translated_text:
The specific features such as <s>udātta</s> and the rest are based on that [<s>dhvani</s>], not on the own nature of the phonemes — because the phonemes are recognized as the same at each utterance.
And thus, the cognitions of <s>udātta</s> and the rest will have a basis [in the <s>dhvani</s>].
Otherwise — for phonemes that are recognized [as the same] and are without difference — the specific features of <s>udātta</s> and the rest would have to be produced by conjunction and disjunction.
And since conjunctions and disjunctions are not directly perceptible, the specific features dependent on them could not be ascertained in the phonemes — hence these cognitions of <s>udātta</s> and the rest would be baseless.
Moreover, one should not insist that because the <s>udātta</s> and the rest are different, the phonemes that are recognized [as the same] must also be different.
For the difference of one thing does not entail the difference of another thing that is not different.
Just as one does not consider the universal (<s>jāti</s>) to be different because of the difference of individuals.
And since the cognition of meaning from phonemes is possible, the postulation of <s>sphoṭa</s> is unnecessary.
'I do not postulate <s>sphoṭa</s>; I directly perceive it — because it flashes forth instantaneously in the mind that has received the impressions deposited by the apprehension of each individual phoneme' — if this is claimed,

children.text:
na /
asyā api buddhervarṇaviṣayatvāt /
ekaikavarṇagrahaṇottarakālā hīyamekā buddhirgauriti samastavarṇaviṣayā nārthāntaraviṣayā /
kathametadavagamyate /
yato 'syāmapi buddhau gakārādayo varṇā anuvartante natu dakārādayaḥ /
yadi hyasyā buddhergakārādibhyor'thāntaraṃ sphoṭo viṣayaḥ syāttato dakārādaya iva gakārādayo 'pyasyā buddhervyāvarteran /
natu tathāsti /
tasmādiyamekabuddhirvarṇaviṣayaiva smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because this cognition too has phonemes as its object.
For this single cognition arising after the apprehension of each individual phoneme — '<s>gauḥ</s>' (cow) — has all the phonemes together as its object, not some other object.
How is this ascertained?
Because in this cognition too, the phonemes <s>g</s>, <s>au</s>, and the rest persist, but not <s>d</s>, <s>a</s>, and the rest.
For if the object of this cognition were <s>sphoṭa</s>, which is something other than the phonemes <s>g</s>, <s>au</s>, and the rest — then <s>g</s>, <s>au</s>, and the rest would be excluded from this cognition, just as <s>d</s>, <s>a</s>, and the rest are.
But that is not the case.
Therefore, this single cognition is a memory having phonemes as its object.

children.text:
nanvanekatvādvarṇānāṃ naikabuddhiviṣayatopapadyata ityuktaṃ, tatpratibrūmaḥ - saṃbhavatyanekasyāpyekabuddhiviṣayatvaṃ, paṅ ktirvanaṃ senā daśa śataṃ sahasramityādidarśanāt /
yā tu gaurityeko 'yaṃ śabda iti buddhiḥ, sā bahuṣveva varṇeṣvekārthāvacchedanibandhanaupacārikī vanasenādibuddhivadeva /
children.translated_text:
But it was said that because phonemes are multiple, their being the object of a single cognition is unjustified — to this we reply: It is possible for even a multiplicity to be the object of a single cognition, as is seen in cases like 'a row,' 'a forest,' 'an army,' 'ten,' 'a hundred,' 'a thousand,' and such.
As for the cognition 'this word "<s>gauḥ</s>" is one' — that is a figurative [ascription] grounded in the determination of a single referent among the many phonemes — just like the cognitions of 'forest' and 'army.'

children.text:
atrāha- yadi varṇā eva sāmastyenaikabuddhiviṣayatāmāpadyamānāḥ padaṃ syustato jārā rājā kapiḥ pikaḥ ityādiṣu padaviśeṣapratipattirna syāt /
ta eva hi varṇā itaratra cetaratra ca pratyavabhāsanta iti /
atra vadāmaḥ - satyapi samastavarṇapratyavamarśe yathā kramānurodhinya eva pipīlikāḥ paṅ ktibuddhimārohanti, evaṃ kramānurodhana eva varṇāḥ padabuddhimārokṣyanti /
tatra varṇānāmaviśeṣe 'pi kramaviśeṣakṛtā padaviśeṣapratipattirna virudhyate /

vṛddhavyavahāre ceme varṇāḥ kramādyanugṛhītā gṛhītārthaviśeṣasaṃbandhāḥ santaḥ svavyavahāro 'pyekaikavarṇagrahaṇānantaraṃ samastapratyavamarśinyāṃ buddhau tādṛśā eva pratyavabhāsamānāstaṃ tamarthamavyabhicāreṇa pratyāyayiṣyantīti varṇavādino laghīyasī kalpanā /
children.translated_text: And in the stage of language acquisition (<s>vṛddhavyavahāra</s>), these phonemes — aided by order and such, having acquired the connection with specific meanings — being apprehended as just such [in one's own usage too], in the cognition of collective apprehension that arises after the apprehension of each individual phoneme, appearing in exactly that form, will unerringly convey that particular meaning. Thus the position of the varṇavādin (phoneme-theorist) involves less conceptual proliferation.

children.text: sphoṭavādinastu dṛṣṭahāniradṛṣṭakalpanā ca /
children.translated_text: But the <s>sphoṭavādin</s>'s position involves the abandonment of what is perceived and the postulation of what is not perceived.

children.text: varṇāśceme krameṇa gṛhyamāṇāḥ sphoṭaṃ vyañjayanti sa sphoṭor'thaṃ vyanaktīti garīyasī kalpanā syāt, athāpi nāma pratyuccāraṇamanye 'nye varṇāḥ syuḥ, tathāpi pratyabhijñālambanabhāvena varṇasāmānyānāmavaśyābhyupagantavyatvādyā varṇeṣvarthapratipādanaprakriyā racitā sā sāmānyeṣu saṃcārayitavyā /
children.translated_text: If these phonemes, apprehended sequentially, manifest <s>sphoṭa</s>, and that <s>sphoṭa</s> manifests the meaning — this would involve greater conceptual proliferation. Even if, hypothetically, different phonemes occurred at each utterance, still, since phoneme-universals must necessarily be accepted as the basis for recognition, the process of conveying meaning that was constructed for [individual] phonemes must be transferred to the universals.

children.text: tataśca nityebhyaḥ śabdebhyo devādivyaktīnāṃ prabhava ityaviruddham // 28 //
children.translated_text: And thus, it is not contradictory [to hold] that the entities such as gods and others come forth from the eternal words. // 28 //

Here [the sphoṭavādin] objects: If phonemes themselves, by being collectively the object of a single cognition, were the word, then the cognition of specific words would not occur in [pairs like] '<s>jārā</s>' and '<s>rājā</s>,' '<s>kapiḥ</s>' and '<s>pikaḥ</s>' — since the very same phonemes appear in one as in the other.
To this we reply: Even though there is a collective apprehension of all the phonemes, just as ants climbing in a particular order produce the cognition of a row, so too phonemes in a particular order will produce the cognition of a word.
Therein, even though the phonemes are the same, the cognition of specific words through the specific ordering is not contradicted.

children.text:
FN: autpattikaṃ svābhāvikaṃ /
vasutvādijātivācakācchabdāttajjātīyāṃ cikīrṣitāṃ vyakti buddhāvālikhya tasyāḥ prabhavanaṃ, tadidaṃ tatprabhavatvam /
ākṛtīnāṃ jātīnām /
'ete asṛgramindavastiraḥ pavitramāśavaḥ /
viśvānyabhisaubhagā' iti /
etanmantrasthaiḥ padaiḥ smṛtvā brahmā devādīnasṛjata /
tatra saṃnihitavācakaitacchabdo devānāṃ karaṇeṣvanugrāhakatvena saṃnihitānāṃ smārakaḥ /
asṛk rudhiraṃ tatpradhānadeharamaṇānmanuṣyāṇāmagraśabdasmārakaḥ /
candrasthānāṃ pitṛṇāminduśabdaḥ smārakaḥ /
pavitraṃ somaṃ svāntavistaraskurvatāṃ grahāṇāṃ tiraḥpavitraśabdaḥ smārakaḥ /
ṛ.(?).ucośnuvatāṃ stotrāṇāmāśuśabdaḥ stotrānantaraṃ prayogaṃ viśatāṃ śastrāṇāṃ viśvaśabdaḥ /
saṃpradāyo guruśiṣyaparaṃparādhyayanam /
saṃsthā avasthāḥ /
varṇarūpaṃ tadatiriktasphoṭarūpaṃ veti kiṃśabdārthaḥ /
sphuṭate varṇairvyajyata iti sphoṭo varṇābhivyaṅgyor'thastasya vyañjako gavādiśabdo nityastamabhipretyedamucyata iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ /
vyabhicārādekasmādvarṇādarthapratītyadarśanāt varṇāntaravaiyarthyapratītyadarśanāccetyarthaḥ /
ekaiketi yathā ratnatattvaṃ bahubhiścākṣuṣapratyayaiḥ sphuṭaṃ bhāsate tathā gavādipadasphoṭo gakārādyekaikavarṇakṛtapratyayaiḥ sphoṭaviṣayairāhitāḥ saṃskārā bījaṃ yasmin citte tasmin antyavarṇakṛtapratyayena janitaḥ paripāko 'ntyaḥ saṃskāro yasminpratyayini citte ekaṃ gauriti padamiti pratyayaḥ pratyakṣastadviṣayatayā spaṣṭamavabhāsata ityarthaḥ /
vapanānantaraṃ ta eveme keśā iti dhīrbhrāntiriti yuktam, bhedadhīvirodhāt /
tālvādideśaiḥkoṣṭhasthavāyusaṃyogavibhāgābhyāṃ vicitrābhyāṃ vyaṅgyatvādvarṇeṣu vaicitryadhīrityarthaḥ /
yo 'vatarati sa dhvaniriti śeṣaḥ /
varṇātiriktaḥ śabdaḥ dhvanirityarthaḥ /
pratyuccāraṇaṃ varṇā anuvartante dhvanirvyāvartata iti bhedaḥ /
apratyakṣatvaṃ aśrāvaṇatvam /
yathā khaṇḍamuṇḍādiviruddhānekavyaktiṣvabhinnaṃ gotvaṃ tathā dhvaniṣu varṇā abhinnā evetyarthaḥ /
udāttādirdhvanistadbhedena hetunā varṇānāmapīti yojanā /
arthāvacchedor'thaṃ niścayaḥ /
pratyavamarśaḥ smṛtiḥ /
vyutpattidaśā vṛddhavyavahāraḥ /
kramādityādiśabdena saṃkhyā gṛhyate /
svasvavyavahāro madhyamavṛddhasya pravṛttyavasthā /
tādṛśatvaṃ vyutpattidaśādṛṣṭakramādyanugṛhītatvam /
dṛṣṭaṃ varṇānāmarthabodhakatvaṃ, adṛṣṭaḥ sphoṭaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: '<s>Autpattika</s>' means natural, inherent. From a word denoting a universal such as '<s>vasutva</s>' (the nature of being a <s>Vasu</s>) and such, one sketches in the mind the particular instance of that universal that one wishes to create, and then its coming forth — that is its 'origination-from-that' (<s>tatprabhavatvam</s>). '<s>Ākṛti</s>' means universals (<s>jāti</s>).
'<s>Ete asṛgramindavastiraḥ pavitramāśavaḥ / viśvānyabhisaubhagā</s>' — through the words occurring in this <s>mantra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> created the gods and others, having recollected [them].
There, the word '<s>etat</s>' reminds of the gods who are present in the sense-organs as presiding [deities]. '<s>Asṛk</s>' (blood) — whose primary substance is a body delighting in blood — the word '<s>agra</s>' reminds of human beings. The word '<s>indu</s>' reminds of the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>) who are stationed in the moon. The word '<s>tiraḥpavitra</s>' reminds of the <s>graha</s>-vessels which spread the <s>soma</s> [juice] within them. The word '<s>āśu</s>' [reminds] of the <s>stotras</s> (hymns of praise) that flow in the <s>Ṛk</s> [verses]. The word '<s>viśva</s>' [reminds] of the <s>śastras</s> (recitations) which enter into the ritual application after the <s>stotras</s>.
'<s>Saṃpradāya</s>' means the study passed down through the succession of teacher and pupil. '<s>Saṃsthā</s>' means states or conditions.
The meaning of the word '<s>kim</s>' [in the debate]: Is the word of the form of phonemes, or of the form of <s>sphoṭa</s> distinct from phonemes?
'<s>Sphoṭa</s>' — that which is manifested (<s>sphuṭate</s>) by phonemes, whose manifesting agent is a word like '<s>go</s>' — that <s>sphoṭa</s>, the meaning manifested by the phonemes, whose manifesting agent is the word '<s>go</s>' and such, is eternal; intending that, this is stated — thus the connection with the preceding.
'<s>Vyabhicāra</s>' — because the cognition of meaning from a single phoneme is not observed, and because the uselessness of the remaining phonemes is implied — this is the meaning.
'<s>Ekaiketi</s>' — just as the true nature of a gem shines clearly through many visual cognitions, so too the word-<s>sphoṭa</s> of a word like '<s>go</s>' — in the mind where the seed consists of impressions deposited by cognitions produced by each individual phoneme such as <s>g</s> and so forth, and where the maturation (the final impression) is produced by the cognition of the last phoneme — a single cognition, whose content is the word '<s>gauḥ</s>,' as direct perception, clearly appears as the object of that — this is the meaning.
'After shaving [the head], the cognition "these are the same hairs" is an error' — this is proper, because it contradicts the cognition of difference.
'Because the phonemes are manifested by the varied conjunctions and disjunctions of the internal air with the articulatory positions such as the palate and such, the varied cognition in the phonemes' — this is the meaning.
'That which enters the range [of hearing] is the <s>dhvani</s>' — this is the completion.
The meaning is: <s>dhvani</s> is a sound distinct from the phonemes.
The difference is: at each utterance, the phonemes persist while the <s>dhvani</s> varies.
'<s>Apratyakṣatva</s>' means non-audibility.
Just as the universal '<s>gotva</s>' (cow-ness) is undifferentiated across many different individuals such as hornless, polled, and so forth — so too the phonemes are undifferentiated across the <s>dhvanis</s> — this is the meaning.
<s>Udātta</s> and the rest — the <s>dhvani</s>, and by that cause of difference, the phonemes too [seem different] — this is the construal.
'<s>Arthāvaccheda</s>' is the determination of meaning. '<s>Pratyavamarśa</s>' is memory.
The stage of language acquisition is '<s>vṛddhavyavahāra</s>.' By '<s>kramādi</s>' ('order and such'), number is also included.
'One's own usage' (<s>svasvavyavahāra</s>) is the stage of application of the intermediate and advanced [learner].
'Being of that kind' means being endowed with the order and such seen in the stage of language acquisition.
What is observed is the capacity of phonemes to convey meaning; what is unobserved is the <s>sphoṭa</s>.

children.text: ata eva ca nityatvam | BBs_1,3.29 |
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, [there is] eternality. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.29 |

children.text: svatantrasya karturasmaraṇādibhiḥ sthite vedasya nityatve devādivyaktiprabhavābhyupagamena tasya virodhamāśaṅkya 'ataḥ prabhavāt' iti parihṛtyedānīṃ tadeva vedanityatvaṃ sthitaṃ draḍhayati- ata eva ca nityatvamiti /
ata eva niyatākṛterdevāderjagato vedaśabdaprabhavatvādvedaśabde nityatvamapi pratyetavyam /
children.translated_text: For this very reason — because the world of entities such as gods and others, having fixed universal forms, comes forth from the words of the <s>Veda</s> — the eternality of the words of the <s>Veda</s> too should be understood.

children.text: tathāca mantravarṇaḥ - 'yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyāntāmanvavindannṛṣiṣu praviṣṭām (ṛ.sa. 10.71.3) iti sthitāmeva vācamanuvinnāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Thus also the <s>mantra</s>-text: 'Through sacrifice, they followed the track of speech; they found it entered into the seers' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.71.3) — this shows that speech was already established and was [merely] found.

children.text: vedavyāsaścaivameva smarati- 'yugānte 'ntarhitānvedānsetihāsānmaharṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Vedavyāsa</s> too remembers thus: 'The <s>Vedas</s> and the <s>Itihāsas</s>, hidden at the end of the age, the great seers

children.text: lebhire tapasā pūrvamanujñātāḥ svayaṃbhuvā' iti // 29 //
children.translated_text: obtained through austerity in former times, authorized by the Self-born [<s>Brahmā</s>].' // 29 //

Having established the eternality of the <s>Veda</s> through the impossibility of recollecting an independent creator and such, and having anticipated the contradiction of that [eternality] by the acceptance that the entities such as gods and others come forth [from words], and having resolved it with '<s>ataḥ prabhavāt</s>' (because of origination from that) — now he reinforces the very established eternality of the <s>Veda</s>: 'And for this very reason, [there is] eternality.'

children.text: FN: yajñena pūrvasukṛtena karmaṇā vāco vedasya padavīyaṃ mārgayogyatāṃ grahaṇayogyatāṃ āyannāptavantaḥ, tataḥstāṃ vācamṛṣiṣu praviṣṭāṃ vidyamānāṃ anvavindannanulabdhavanto yājñikā itiyāvat /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Through sacrifice' — through prior meritorious action (<s>sukṛta</s>) — they attained '<s>padavīya</s>,' the fitness for the path, the fitness for apprehension, of speech, the <s>Veda</s>; then they found (<s>anvavindan</s>) that speech existing within the seers, entered into [them] — meaning: the sacrificers [obtained the <s>Veda</s>].

children.text: anuvinānnāmupalabdhām /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anuvinnām</s>' — [previously] obtained.

children.text: pūrvamavāntarakalpādau /
children.translated_text: 'In former [times]' — at the beginning of the preceding sub-cycle (<s>avāntarakalpa</s>).

children.text: samānanāmarūpatvāccāvṛttāvapyavirodho darśanāt smṛteś ca | BBs_1,3.30 |
children.translated_text: <s>Samānanāmarūpatvāc cāvṛttāv apy avirodho darśanāt smṛteś ca</s> — And because of the sameness of names and forms, there is no contradiction even in [cosmic] recurrence — from observation and from <s>smṛti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.30 |

children.text:
athāpi syāt /
yadi paśvādivyaktivaddevādivyaktayo 'pi saṃtatyaivotpadyerannirudhyeraṃśca tato 'bhidhānābhidheyābhidhātṛvyavahārāvicchedātsaṃbandhanityatvena virodhaḥ śabde parihriyeta /
yadā tu khalu sakalaṃ trailokyaṃ parityaktanāmarūpaṃ nirlepaṃ pralīyate prabhavati cābhinavamiti śrutismṛtivādā vadanti tadā kathamavirodha iti /
tatredamabhidhīyate- samānanāmarūpatvāditi tadāpi saṃsārasyānāditvaṃ tāvadabhyupagantavyam /
pratipādayiṣyati cācāryaḥ saṃsārasyānāditvaṃ - 'upapadyate cāpyupalabhyate' ca (bra. 2.1.36) iti /
anādau ca saṃsāre yathā svāpaprabodhayoḥ pralayaprabhavaśravaṇe 'pi pūrvaprabodhavaduktaprabodhe 'pi vyavahārānna kaścidvirodhaḥ, evaṃ kalpāntaraprabhavapralayayoriti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Now one might further say: If the manifestations of gods and such, like the manifestations of cattle and such, were produced and destroyed merely through lineage-continuity, then the contradiction regarding the word [i.e., the eternality of the word-object relationship] would be resolved through the unbroken continuity of the designation, the designated, and the designator. But when the entire three worlds — having abandoned names and forms, becoming untainted — dissolve, and emerge anew, as the teachings of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> declare — then how can there be no contradiction? To this, it is said: 'Because of the sameness of names and forms' — even then, the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> must first be accepted. And the teacher will demonstrate the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> with 'it is established, and it is also observed' (<s>BBs</s> 2.1.36). And in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, just as in sleep and waking — even when dissolution and emergence are heard of — there is no contradiction from the standpoint of conventional usage in the stated emergence [being like] the previous waking, so too should it be understood regarding the emergence and dissolution of different cosmic cycles.

children.text:
svāpaprabodhayośca pralayaprabhavau śrūyete- 'yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kañcana paśyatyathāsminprāṇa evaikadhā bhavati tadenaṃ vāksarvairnābhiḥ sahāpyeti cakṣuḥ sarvai rūpaiḥ sahāpyeti śrotraṃ sarvaiḥ śabdaiḥ sahāpyeti manaḥ sarvairdhyānaiḥ sahāphayeti sa yadā pratibudhyate yathāgnerjjvalataḥ sarvā diśo visphuliṅgā vipratiṣṭherannevamevaitasmādātmanaḥ sarve prāṇā yathātanaṃ vipratiṣṭante prāṇebhyo devā devebhyo lokāḥ (kau. 3.3) iti /
syādetat /
svāpe puruṣāntaravyavahārāvicchedātsvayaṃ ca suptaprabuddhasya pūrvaprabodhavyavahārānusaṃdhānasaṃbhavādaviruddham /
mahāpralaye tu sarvavyavahārocchedājjanmāntaravyavahāravacca kalpāntaravyavahārasyānusaṃdhātumaśakyatvādvaiṣamyamiti /
children.translated_text: And in sleep and waking, dissolution and emergence are heard: 'When one is asleep and sees no dream whatsoever, then one becomes unified in <s>prāṇa</s> alone; then speech, together with all names, enters into it; the eye, together with all forms; the ear, together with all sounds; the mind, together with all thoughts. When one awakens — just as from a blazing fire sparks scatter in all directions, so from this Self all the <s>prāṇas</s> go forth to their respective stations; from the <s>prāṇas</s>, the gods; from the gods, the worlds' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.3). One might say: In sleep, because the conventional transactions of other people continue unbroken, and because the person who has slept and awoken can recollect the prior waking transactions, there is no contradiction. But in the great dissolution, because all transactions are cut off, and because — like the transactions of another birth — the transactions of another cosmic cycle cannot be recollected, the case is dissimilar.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
satyapi sarvavyavahārocchedini mahāpralaye parameśvarānugrahādīśvarāṇāṃ hiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ kalpāntaravyavahārānusaṃdhānopapatteḥ /
yadyapi prākṛtāḥ prāṇino na janmāntaravyavahāramanusamadadhānā dṛśyanta iti, tathāpi na prākṛtavadīśvarāṇāṃ bhavitavyam /
tathāhi prāṇitvāviśeṣe 'pi manuṣyādistambaparyanteṣu jñānaiśvaryādipratibandhaḥ pareṇa pareṇa bhūyānbhavandṛśyate, tathā manuṣyādistambaparyanteṣu hiraṇyagarbhaparyanteṣu jñānaiśvaryādyabhivyaktirapi pareṇa pareṇa bhūyasī bhavatītyetacchrutismṛtivādeṣvasakṛdanuśrūyamāṇaṃ na śakyaṃ vaditum /
tataścātītakalpānuṣṭhitaprakṛṣṭajñānakarmaṇāmīśvarāṇāṃ hiraṇyagarbhādīnāṃ vartamānakalpādau prādurbhavatāṃ parameśrānugṛhītānāṃ suptapratibuddhatvakalpāntaravyavahārānusaṃdhānopapattiḥ /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'yo brahmaṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ yo vai vedāṃśca prahiṇoti tasmai /
taṃ ha devamātmabuddhiprakāśaṃ mumukṣurvai śaraṇamahaṃ prapadye' (śve, 6.18) iti /
smaranti ca śaunakādayaḥ 'madhucchandaḥprabhṛtibhirṛṣibhirdarśitayyo dṛṣṭāḥ' iti /
prativedaṃ caivameva kāṇḍarṣyādayaḥ smaryante /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Even though the great dissolution cuts off all [ordinary] transactions, by the grace of the supreme Lord, the lords such as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and others can recollect the transactions of the previous cosmic cycle. Even though ordinary beings are not seen to recollect the transactions of another birth, the lords need not be like ordinary beings. For thus: even though all are equally living beings — from humans down to grass — the obstruction of knowledge, sovereignty, and such is observed to progressively increase in the descending order. Similarly, from humans down to grass and up to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the manifestation of knowledge, sovereignty, and such also progressively increases — this is heard repeatedly in the teachings of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> and cannot be denied. Therefore, for the lords such as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — who performed distinguished knowledge and action in past cosmic cycles, who appear at the beginning of the present cycle, and who are graced by the supreme Lord — the recollection of the previous cycle's transactions is tenable, like that of one who has slept and awoken. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'He who first creates <s>Brahmā</s> and who delivers the <s>Vedas</s> to him — to that God who illuminates the self through the intellect, I, a seeker of liberation, take refuge' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.18). And <s>Śaunaka</s> and others record: 'Those <s>mantras</s> that were seen by <s>ṛṣis</s> beginning with <s>Madhucchandas</s> are revealed [to them].' And for each <s>Veda</s>, the <s>kāṇḍa-ṛṣis</s> and such are similarly recorded.

children.text:
śrutirapyṛṣijñānapūrvakameva mantreṇānuṣṭhānaṃ darśayati- 'yo havā aviditārṣeyacchandodaivatabrāhmaṇena mantreṇa yajayati vādhyāpayati vā sthāṇuṃ vacrchati gartaṃ vā pratipadyate'' (sarvānu. pari.) ityupakramya tasmādetāni mantre mantre vidyāt' iti /
prāṇināṃ ca sukhaprāptaye dharmo vidhīyate /
duḥkhaparihārāya cādharmaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: And <s>adharma</s> is prohibited for the avoidance of suffering.

children.text: dṛṣṭānuśravikasukhaduḥkhaviṣayau ca rāgadveṣau bhavato na vilakṣaṇaviṣayāvityato dharmādharmaphalabhūtottarā sṛṣṭirniṣpadyamānā pūrvasṛṣṭisadṛśyeva niṣpadyate /
children.translated_text: And attachment and aversion have as their objects the pleasures and pains that are seen and heard of — not objects of a different nature. Therefore, the subsequent creation — which is the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — when produced, is produced similar to the previous creation.

children.text: smṛtiśca bhavati- 'teṣāṃ ye yāni karmāṇi prāksṛṣṭyāṃ pratipedire /
children.translated_text: And there is a <s>smṛti</s>: 'Whatever actions beings had performed in the previous creation —

children.text: tānyeva te prapadyante sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: those very [actions] they take up again, being created again and again.

The <s>śruti</s> too shows that the performance of rites with <s>mantras</s> is preceded by <s>ṛṣi</s>-knowledge: beginning with 'He who performs sacrifice or teaches with a <s>mantra</s> of which he does not know the <s>ṛṣi</s>, meter, deity, and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [explanation] — he hits a post or falls into a pit' — [it concludes]: 'therefore, one should know these [details] for every <s>mantra</s>.' And <s>dharma</s> is enjoined for living beings for the attainment of happiness.

children.text: hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharmāvṛtānṛte /
children.translated_text: Harmful and harmless, gentle and cruel, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, truth and falsehood —

children.text: tadbhāvitāḥ prapadyante tasmāttattasya rocate' //
children.translated_text: they are habituated to those [tendencies]; therefore, each of those [tendencies] pleases them.'

children.text:
iti /
pralīyamānamapi cedaṃ jagacchaktyaśeṣameva pralīyate /
śaktimūlameva ca prabhavati /
itarathākasmikatvaprasaṃṅāt /
nacānekākārāḥ śaktayaḥ śakyāḥ kalpayitum /
tataśca vicchidya vicchidyāpyudbhavatāṃ bhūrādilokapravāhāṇāṃ, devatiryaṅmanuṣyalakṣaṇānāṃ ca prāṇinikāyapravāhāṇāṃ, varṇāśramadharmaphalavyavasthānāṃ cānādau saṃsāre niyatatvamindriyaviṣayasaṃbandhaniyatatvavatpratyetavyam /
nahīndriyaviṣayasaṃbandhādervyavahārasya pratisargamanyathātvaṃ ṣaṣṭhendriyaviṣayakalpaṃ śakyamutprekṣitum /
ataśca sarvakalpānāṃ tulyavyavahāratvātkalpāntavyavahārānusaṃdhānakṣamatvācceśvarāṇāṃ samānanāmarūpā eva pratisargaṃ viśeṣāḥ prādurbhavanti /
samānanāmarūpatvāccāvṛttāvapi mahāsargamahāpralayakṣaṇāyāṃ jagato 'bhyupagamyamānāyāṃ na kaścicchabdaprāmāṇyādivirodhaḥ /
samānanāmarūpatāṃ ca śrutismṛtī darśayataḥ - 'sūryācandramasau dhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat /
divaṃ ca pṛthivī cāntarikṣamatho svaḥ' (ṛ.saṃ. 10. 190.3) iti /
yathā pūrvasminkalpe sūryācandramaḥprabhṛti jagatkḷptaṃ tathāsminnapi kalpe parameśvaro 'kalpayadityarthaḥ /
tathā 'agnirvā akāmayata annādo devānāṃsyāmiti /
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'Fire desired: "Let me become the food-eater of the gods."

children.text: sa etamagnaye kṛttikābhyaḥ puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ niravapat' (tai.brā. 3.1.4.1) iti nakṣatreṣṭividhau yo 'gnirniravapadyasmai vāgnaye niravapattayoḥ samānanāmarūpatāṃ darśayatītyevañjātīyakā śrutirihodāhartavyā /
children.translated_text: He offered this eight-portioned cake to <s>Agni</s> [paired with] the <s>Kṛttikās</s>' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.1.4.1) — in the injunction of the constellation-sacrifice, this shows the sameness of names and forms of the fire (<s>Agni</s>) who offered and the <s>Agni</s> to whom the offering was made — and <s>śruti</s> passages of this kind should be cited here.

children.text: smṛtirapi- 'ṛṣīṇāṃ nāmadheyāni yāśca vedeṣu dṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>smṛti</s> also: 'The names of the <s>ṛṣis</s>, and the revelations that are in the <s>Vedas</s> —

children.text: śarvaryante prasūtānāṃ tānyevaibhyo dadātyajaḥ //
children.translated_text: to those who are born at the end of the night [of dissolution], the Birthless One gives those very same [names and revelations].

Thus. And even when this world dissolves, it dissolves only along with its potencies (<s>śakti</s>). And it arises based on those very potencies. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of randomness. And the potencies of manifold forms cannot be newly imagined. Therefore, for the streams of worlds beginning with <s>Bhūḥ</s> and so forth — which arise after being interrupted again and again — and for the streams of living beings characterized as gods, animals, and humans — and for the fixed arrangement of the fruits of <s>dharma</s> pertaining to <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> — their regularity in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> should be understood as being like the regularity of the connection between sense-organs and their objects. For the difference of the conventional transactions from one creation to another — [which would require] a sixth sense-organ or object — cannot be imagined. Therefore, since all cosmic cycles have the same transactions, and since the lords are capable of recollecting the transactions of [previous] cycles, the particular [entities] that arise at each new creation have the same names and forms. And because of the sameness of names and forms, even when recurrence — characterized by the great creation and the great dissolution — of the world is accepted, there is no contradiction with the authority of the word and such. And <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> show the sameness of names and forms: 'The creator fashioned the sun and moon, as before; heaven, earth, the atmosphere, and the celestial world' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.190.3). The meaning is: just as in the previous cycle the world was fashioned beginning with the sun and moon — so too in this cycle the supreme Lord fashioned [it].

children.text: yathartuṣvṛtuliṅgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye /
children.translated_text: Just as in the seasons, the characteristics of the seasons — having manifold forms — [recur] in the cycle,

children.text: dṛśyante tāni tānyeva tathā bhāvā yugādiṣu //
children.translated_text: those very same ones are seen — so too do the entities [recur] at the beginnings of <s>Yugas</s>.

children.text: yathābhimānino 'tītāstulyaste sāṃpratairiha /
children.translated_text: Just as the presiding deities of the past are equal to those of the present here,

children.text: devā devairatātairhi rūpairnāmabhireva ca //
children.translated_text: the gods [of the past are the same as] the gods [of the present] — indeed, with the same forms and names.

children.text: ' ityevajātīyakā draṣṭavyā // 30 //
children.translated_text: Such <s>smṛti</s> passages of this kind should be considered. // 30 //

children.text: FN: abhidhātṛśabdenādhyāpakādhyetārāvuktau /
children.translated_text: Footnote: By the word '<s>abhidhātṛ</s>' (designator), both teacher and student are meant.

children.text: tadāpi mahāpralayamahāsargāṅgīkāre 'pīti yāvat /
children.translated_text: 'Even then' — meaning: even when the great dissolution and great creation are accepted.

children.text:
yadepyupakramādathaśabdaḥ tadetyarthaḥ /
prāṇaḥ paramātmā tatra jīva ekībhavati enaṃ prāṇaṃ sa jīvaḥ tadaitīti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>atha</s>' at the beginning [is expletive] — that is the meaning. '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is the supreme Self; the <s>jīva</s> becomes unified therein; the rest is: that <s>jīva</s> enters that <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmāt prāṇātmanaḥ, āyatanaṃ golakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the Self that is <s>prāṇa</s>; '<s>āyatana</s>' means the eye-socket.

children.text: itiśabdo yadyapītyanena saṃbadhyate /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>iti</s>' is connected with '<s>yadi</s>' (if).

children.text: 'hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartate'tyādayaḥ śrutivādāḥ, 'jñānamapratimaṃ yasye'tyādayaḥ smṛtivādāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> came into being' and such are the teachings of <s>śruti</s>; 'whose knowledge is incomparable' and such are the teachings of <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: prahiṇoti gamayati tasya buddhau vedanāvirbhāvayati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prahiṇoti</s>' means 'causes to go, manifests knowledge in his intellect.'

children.text: ṛgvedo daśamaṇḍalātmakaḥ maṇḍalānāṃ daśatayamātrāstīti tatra bhavā ṛco dāśatayyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛgveda</s> consists of ten <s>maṇḍalas</s>; the <s>maṇḍalas</s> are only ten in number; the <s>ṛks</s> belonging to them are '<s>dāśatayyaḥ</s>' (of the ten).

children.text: arṣeya ṛṣiyogaḥ, chando gāyatryādi, daivatagnyādi, brāhmaṇaṃ viniyogaḥ etānyaviditāni yasminmantre, sthāṇuṃ sthāvaraṃ, gartaṃ narakam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ārṣeya</s>' — the connection with the <s>ṛṣi</s>; '<s>chandas</s>' — <s>Gāyatrī</s> and such; '<s>daivata</s>' — <s>Agni</s> and such; '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — the application. These are unknown in which <s>mantra</s>. '<s>Sthāṇu</s>' — a stationary state; '<s>garta</s>' — hell.

children.text:
teṣāṃ prāṇināṃ madhye /
tānyeva tajjātīyānyeva /
children.translated_text: 'Of those' — among those living beings. 'Those very' — of that very same type.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhendriyaṃ manaḥ 'manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇī'ti smṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: The sixth sense-organ is the mind — from the <s>smṛti</s>: 'the senses, with the mind as the sixth.'

children.text: nakṣatrabahutvādbahuvacanam kṛttikādevāyāgnaye, aṣṭasu kapāleṣu pacanīyaṃ havirniruptavān /
children.translated_text: The plural is because of the plurality of constellations. <s>Kṛttikā</s> — the deity <s>Agni</s>; the oblation to be cooked on eight potsherds — he offered.

children.text:
deveṣviti viṣayasaptamī /
śarvaryante pralayānte /
ṛturliṅgāni navapallavādīni /
paryaye ghaṭīyantravadāvṛttau /
children.translated_text: 'Among the gods' — the locative is objective. '<s>Śarvaryante</s>' — at the end of the dissolution. '<s>Ṛtuliṅgāni</s>' — the signs of the seasons, such as new sprouts and such. '<s>Paryaye</s>' — in the cycle, like a water-wheel.

children.text: bhāvāḥ padārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāvāḥ</s>' — entities, things.

children.text: madhvādiṣv asaṃbhavād anadhikāraṃ jaiminiḥ | BBs_1,3.31 |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhvādiṣv asaṃbhavād anadhikāraṃ Jaiminiḥ</s> — <s>Jaimini</s> [holds] that because of the impossibility [of their qualification] in the honey-meditation and such, [the gods] have no qualification [for <s>brahmavidyā</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.31 |

children.text:
iha devādīnāmapi brahmavidyāyāmastyadhikāra iti yatpratijñātaṃ tatparyāvartyate /
devādīnāmanadhikāraṃ jaiminirācāryo manyante /
kasmāt /
madhvādiṣvasaṃbhavāt /
brahmavidyāyāmadhikārābhyupagame hi vidyātvāviśeṣānmadhvādividyāsvapyadhikāro 'bhyupagamyeta /
nacaivaṃ saṃbhavati /
katham /
'asau vā ādityo devamadhu' (chā. 3.1.1) ityatra manuṣyā ādityaṃ madhvadhyāsenopasīran /
devādiṣu hyupāsakeṣyabhyupagamyamāneṣvādityaḥ kamanyamādityamupāsīta /
punaścādityavyapāśrayāṇi pañca rohitādīnyamṛtānyupakramya vasavo rudrā ādityā marutaḥ sādhyāśca pañca devagaṇāḥ krameṇa tattatamṛtamupajīvantītyupadiśya 'sa ya etadevamamṛtaṃ veda vasūnāmevaiko bhūtvāgninaiva mukhenaitadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati' ityādinā vasvādyupajīvyānyamṛtāni vijānatāṃ vasvādimahimaprāptiṃ darśayati /
vasvādayastu kānanyānvasvādīnamṛtopajīvino vijānīyuḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Vasus</s> and such — what other <s>Vasus</s> and such whose nectar-subsistence would they know?

children.text: kaṃ vānyaṃ vasvādimahimānaṃ prepseyuḥ /
children.translated_text: And what other glory of the <s>Vasus</s> and such would they seek to obtain?

children.text: 'tathā agniḥ pādo vāyuḥ pāda ādityaḥ pādo diśaḥ pādaḥ' (chā. 3.18.2), 'vāyurvāva saṃvargaḥ'' (chā. 4.3.1) 'ādityo brahmetyādeśaḥ' (chā. 3.11.1) ityādiṣu devatātmopāsaneṣu na teṣāmeva devatātmānamadhikāraḥ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: In 'Fire is one quarter; air is one quarter; the sun is one quarter; the directions are one quarter' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.2), '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the absorber' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.1), 'The sun is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the teaching' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.11.1) — in these and such meditations that have deities as their self, the qualification of those very deities themselves is not possible.

children.text: tathā 'imāveva gotamabharadvājā vayameva gotamo 'yaṃ bharadvājaḥ' (bṛ. 2.2.4) ityādiṣvipyṛṣisaṃbandheṣūpāsaneṣu na teṣāmevarṣīṇāmadhikāraḥ saṃbhavati // 31 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, in 'These are indeed <s>Gotama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>; we ourselves are <s>Gotama</s>, he is <s>Bharadvāja</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.2.4) and such meditations connected with <s>ṛṣis</s>, the qualification of those very <s>ṛṣis</s> is not possible. // 31 //

Here, what was asserted — that even the gods and such have qualification for <s>brahmavidyā</s> — is reconsidered. The teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds that the gods and such have no qualification. Why? Because of the impossibility in the honey-meditation and such. For if qualification for <s>brahmavidyā</s> were accepted, then — because there is no distinction among <s>vidyās</s> (meditations) — qualification for the honey-meditation and such too would have to be accepted. But that is not possible. How so? In 'This sun is indeed the divine honey' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.1.1), humans meditate on the sun as honey. If the gods and such were accepted as meditators, which other sun would the sun [itself] meditate on? Furthermore, having introduced the five nectars dependent on the sun — beginning with the red and such — [the text] teaches that the five groups of gods — <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Sādhyas</s> — sequentially subsist on each respective nectar; and having [then said] 'He who thus knows this nectar, becoming one of the <s>Vasus</s>, with <s>Agni</s> as his mouth, sees this nectar and is satisfied' — [the text] shows the attainment of the glory of the <s>Vasus</s> and such for those who know the nectars subsisted upon by the <s>Vasus</s> and such.

children.text: kutaśca devādīnāmadhikāraḥ -
children.translated_text: And for what further reason do the gods and such have [no] qualification?

children.text: FN: pañceti caturvedokarmāṇi praṇavaścati pañca kusumāni tebhyaḥ somājyādidravyāṇi hutāni rohitādīni lohitaṃ, śuklaṃ, kṛṣṇaṃ, paraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ, madhye kṣobhata iva, ityuktāni pañca rohitādīnyamṛtāni tattanmantrabhāgaiḥ prāgādyūrdhvāntapañcadigavasthitābhirādityaraśmināḍībhirmadhvaṣūpasthitacchidrarūpābhirādityamaṇḍalamānītāni yaśastejaindriyavīryānnātmanā pariṇatāni pañcadikṣu sthitairvasvādibhirupajīvyānīti dhyāyanto vasvādiprāptiruktetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The 'five' are the rites of the four <s>Vedas</s> plus <s>Oṃ</s> — these five flowers; from them, the substances like <s>soma</s>, ghee, and such, when offered, are the five nectars beginning with the red — red, white, dark, extremely dark, and the middle one that appears to quiver — described [as such], [which are] the five nectars beginning with the red, brought to the solar orb through the channels of solar rays situated in the five directions — east and so forth up to the zenith — having the nature of openings in the honey [structure] — and transformed into the forms of fame, radiance, vigor, strength, and food — subsisted upon by the <s>Vasus</s> and such situated in the five directions: meditating thus, the attainment of the glory of the <s>Vasus</s> and such is stated — this is the meaning.

children.text: jyotiṣi bhāvāc ca | BBs_1,3.32 |
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotiṣi bhāvāc ca</s> — And because in the [celestial] light, [the gods] exist. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.32 |

children.text:
yadidaṃ jyotirmaṇḍalaṃ dyusthānamahorātrābhyāṃ bambhramajjagadavabhāsayati tasminnādityādayo devatāvacanāḥ śabdāḥ prayujyante /
lokaprasiddharvākyaśeṣaprasiddheśca /
naca jyotirmaṇḍalasya hṛdayādinā vigraheṣu cetanayārthitvādinā vā yogo 'vagantuṃ śakyate mṛtādivadacetanatvāvagamāt /
etenāgnyādayo vyākhyātāḥ /
syādetat /
mantrārthavādetihāsapurāṇalokebhyo devādānāṃ vigrahavattvādyavagamādayamadoṣa iti /
children.translated_text: This orb of light, stationed in heaven, revolving by day and night, illuminating the world — in it, the words referring to deities like the sun and such are used. This is well-known in the world and from the context of sentences. And it cannot be understood that the orb of light has a connection with a body like a heart, or with desires arising from consciousness — because, like a dead thing, it is understood to be unconscious. By this, [the case of] fire and such is explained. One might say: Because the gods' possession of bodies and such is understood from <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, <s>itihāsas</s>, <s>purāṇas</s>, and common parlance — this is not a defect.

children.text:
netyucyate /
nahi tāvalloko nāma kiñcitsvatantraṃ pramāṇamasti /
pratyakṣādibhya eva hyavicāritaviśeṣebhyaḥ pramāṇebhyaḥ prasiddhyanartho lokātprasidhyatītyucyate /
nacātra pratyakṣādīnāmanyatamaṃ pramāṇamasti /
itihāsapurāṇamapi pauruṣeyatvātpramāṇāntaramūlamākāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: Even the <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>, being of human authorship, require a basis in some other means of valid knowledge.

children.text: arthavādā api vidhinaikavākyatvātstutyarthāḥ santo na pārthagarthyena devādīnāṃ vigrahādisadbhāve kāraṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: Even the eulogistic passages (<s>arthavāda</s>), being part of a single sentence with an injunction and serving the purpose of praise, do not — by an independent meaning — become a cause for establishing the existence of embodied forms and such of deities.

children.text: mantrā api śrutyādiviniyuktāḥ prayogasamavāyino 'bhidhānārthā na kasyacidarthasya pramāṇamityācakṣate /
children.translated_text: They say that even <s>mantras</s>, being assigned by <s>śruti</s> and such to ritual application, and being co-extensive with the performance and meant for designation — are not a means of knowledge for any [independent] referent.

children.text: tasmādabhāvo devādīnāmadhikārasya // 32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the qualification of deities and such is negated. // 32 //

No — it is said. For the world (<s>loka</s>) is not an independent means of valid knowledge. It is said that the worldly knowledge about the existence of forms and such of deities becomes well known from the very means of valid knowledge — perception and such — whose specific details have not been critically examined. And here [regarding deities' forms and such], none of the means of knowledge such as perception and the like is present.

children.text:
FN: 'vajrahastaḥ purandaraḥ' ityādayo mantrāḥ 'so 'rodīt' ityādayor'thavādāḥ, 'iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā' ityādītihāsapurāṇāni, loke 'pi yamaṃ daṇḍahastaṃ, indraṃ vajrahastaṃ, likhantīti vigrahādipañcakasadbhāvādanadhikāradoṣo nāstītyarthaḥ /
'vigraho haviṣāṃ bhoga aiśvaryaṃ ca prasannatā /
phalapradānamityetatpañcakam vigrahādikam' iti /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Vajrahastaḥ purandaraḥ</s>' (Thunderbolt-handed destroyer of cities) and such are <s>mantras</s>; 'He wept' and such are <s>arthavāda</s> passages; '<s>Iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā</s>' (The gods grant desired enjoyments) and such are from <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>. In the world too, people depict <s>Yama</s> as holding a staff and <s>Indra</s> as holding a thunderbolt — thus, because the five [attributes] beginning with embodiment exist, there is no fault of disqualification: this is the meaning. 'Embodiment, the enjoyment of oblations, lordly power, graciousness, and the bestowal of fruits — this is the fivefold [set] beginning with embodiment.'

children.text: bhāvaṃ tu bādarāyaṇo 'sti hi | BBs_1,3.33 |
children.translated_text: But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds] that there is [qualification], for it exists. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.33 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pūrvapakṣaṃ vyavartayati /
bādarāyaṇastvācāryo bhāvamadhikārasya devādīnāmapi manyante /
yadyapi madhvādividyāsu devatādivyāmiśrāsvāsaṃbhavo 'dhikārasya tathāpyasti hi śuddhāyāṃ brahmavidyāyāṃ saṃbhavaḥ /
arthitvasāmarthyapratiṣedhādyapekṣatvādadhikārasya /
naca kvacidasaṃbhava ityetāvatā yatra saṃbhavastatrāpyadhikāro 'podyeta /
manuṣyāṇāmapi na sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ sarveṣu rājasūyādiṣvadhikāraḥ saṃbhavati /
tatra yo nyāyaḥ so 'trāpi bhaviṣyati /
brahmavidyāṃ ca prakṛtya bhavati darśanaṃ śrautaṃ devādyadhikārasya sūcakam- 'tadyo yo devānāṃ pratyabudhyata sa eva tadabhavattatharṣīṇāṃ tathā manuṣyāṇām' (bṛ. 1.4.10) iti /
'te hocurhanta tamātmānamanvicchāmo yamātmānamanviṣya sarvāṃśca lokānāpnoti sarvāṃśca kāmān' iti /
'indro ha vai devānāmabhipravrāja virocana'surāṇām' (chā. 8.7.2) ityādi ca /
samārtamapi gandharvayājñavalkyasaṃvādādi /
yadapyuktaṃ jyotiṣi bhāvācceti /
atra brūmaḥ jyotirādiviṣayā api ādityādayo devatāvacanāḥ śabdāścetanāvantamaiśvaryādyupetaṃ taṃ taṃ devatātmānaṃ samarpayanti, mantrārthavādādiṣu tathā vyavahārāt /
asti hyaiśvaryayogāddevatānāṃ jyotirādyātmabhiścāvasthātuṃ yatheṣṭaṃ ca taṃ taṃ vigrahaṃ grahītuṃ sāmarthyam /
tathāhi śrūyate subrahmaṇyārthavāde- medhātithermeṣeti /
'medhātithiṃ ha kāṇvāyanamindro meṣo bhūtvā jahāra' (ṣaḍviṃśa. brā. 1.1) iti /
smaryate ca- 'ādityaḥ puruṣo bhūtvā kuntīmupajagāma ha' iti /
mṛdādiṣvapi cetanā adhiṣṭhitāro 'bhyupagamyante- mṛdabravīdāpobruvannityādidarśanāt /
jyotirādestu bhūtadhātorādityādiṣvacetanatvamabhyupagamyate /
cetanāstvadhiṣṭhitāro devatātmano mantrārthavādādivyavahārādityuktam /
yadapyuktaṃ mantrārthavādayoranyāyārthatvānna devatāvigrahādiprakāśanasāmarthyamiti /
atra brūmaḥ - pratyayāpratyayau hi sadbhāvāsadbhāvayoḥ kāraṇaṃ, nānyarthatvamananyārthatvaṃ vā /
tathāhyanyārthamapi prasthitaḥ pathi patitaṃ tṛṇaparṇādyastītyeva pratipadyate /
atrāha- viṣama upanyāsaḥ /
tatra hi tṛṇaparṇādiviṣayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ pravṛttamasti yena tadastitvaṃ pratipadyate /
atra punarvidhyuddeśaikavākyabhāvena stutyarther'thavādena pārthagarthyena vṛttāntaviṣayā pravṛttiḥ śakyādhyavasātum /
nahi 'na surāṃ pibet' iti nañvati vākye padatrayasaṃbandhātsurāpānapratiṣedha evaikor'tho 'vagamyate /
na punaḥ surāṃ pibediti padadvayasaṃbandhātsurāpānavidhirapīti /
atrocyate- viṣama upanyāsaḥ /
yuktaṃ yatsurāpānapratiṣedhe padānvayasyaikatvādavāntaravākyārthasyāgrahaṇam /
vidhyuddeśārthavādayostvarthavādasthāni padāni pṛthaganvayavṛttāntaviṣayaṃ pratipadyānantaraṃ kaimarthyavaśena kāmaṃ vidheḥ stāvakatvaṃ pratipadyante /
yathāhi- 'vāyavyaṃ śvetamālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ' ityatra vidhyuddeśavartināṃ vāyavyādipadānāṃ vidhinā saṃbandhaḥ, naivaṃ 'vāyurvai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā vāyumeva svena bhāgadheyenopadhāvati sa evainaṃ bhūtiṃ gamayati' ityeṣāmarthavādagatānāṃ padānām /
nahi bhavati vāyurvā ālabheteti kṣepiṣṭhā devatā vā ālabhetetyādi /
vāyusvabhāvasaṃkīrtanena tvavāntaramanvayaṃ pratipadyaivaṃ viśiṣṭadaivatyamidaṃ karmeti vidhiṃ stuvanti /
tadyatra so 'vāntaravākyārthaḥ pramāṇāntaragocaro bhavati tatra tadanuvādenarthavādaḥ pravartate /
yatra pramāṇāntaraviruddhastatra guṇavādena /
yatra tu tadubhayaṃ nāsti tatra kiṃ pramāṇāntarābhāvādguṇavādaḥ syādāhosvitpramāṇāntarāvirodhādvidyamānavāda iti pratītiśaraṇairvidyamānavāda āśrayaṇīyo na guṇavādaḥ /
etena mantro vyākhyātaḥ /
apica vidhibhirevendrādidaivatyāni havīṃṣi codayadbhirapekṣitamindrādīnāṃ svarūpam /
nahi svarūparahitā indrādayaścetasyāropayituṃ śakyante /
naca cetasyanārūḍhāyai tasyai tasyai devatāyai haviḥ pradātuṃ śakyate /
śrāvayati ca- 'yasyai devatāyai havirgṛhītaṃ syāttāṃ dhyāyedvaṣaṭkariṣyan' (ai.brā. 3.8.1) iti /
naca śabdamātramarthasvarūpaṃ saṃbhavati, śabdārthayorbhedāt /
tatra yādṛśaṃ mantrārthavādayorindrādīnāṃ svarūpamavagataṃ na tattādṛśaṃ śabdapramāṇakena pratyākhyatuṃ yuktam /
itihāsapurāṇamapi vyākhyātena mārgeṇa saṃbhavanmantrārthavādamūlatvātprabhavati devatāvigrahādi sādhayitim /
pratyakṣādimūlamapi saṃbhavati /
bhavati hyasmākamapratyakṣamapi cirantanānāṃ pratyakṣam /
tathāca vyāsādayo devādibhiḥ pratyakṣaṃ vyavaharantīti smaryate /
yastu brūyādidānīntanānāmiva pūrveṣāmapi nāsti devādibhirvyavahartuṃ sāmarthyamiti sa jagadvaicitryaṃ pratiṣedhet /
idānīmiva ca nānyadapi sārvabhaumaḥ kṣatriyo 'stīti brūyāt /
tataśca rājasūyādicodanoparundhyāt /
idānīmiva ca kālāntare 'pyavyavasthitaprāyānvarṇāśramadharmānpratijānīta /
tataśca vyavasthāvidhāyi śāstramanarthakaṃ syāt /
tasmāddharmotkarṣavaśāccirantanā devādibhiḥ pratyakṣaṃ vyavajahnuriti śliṣyate /
