apica smaranti- 'svādhyāyādiṣṭadevatāsaṃprayogaḥ' (yo.sū. 2.44) ityādi /
yogo 'pyaṇimādyaiśvaryarprāptiphalaḥ smaryamāṇo na śakyate sāhasamātreṇa pratyākhyātum /
śrutiśca yogamāhātmyaṃ prakhyāpayati- 'pṛthivyaptejo 'nilakhe samutthite pañcātmake yogaguṇe pravṛtte /
na tasya rogo na jarā na mṛtyuḥ prāptasya yogāgnimayaṃ śarīram'' (śvaṃ. 2.12) iti /
ṛṣīṇāmapi mantrabrāhmaṇadarśināṃ sāmarthyaṃ nāsmadīyena sāmarthyenopamātuṃ yuktam /
tasmātsamūlamitihāsapurāṇam /
lokaprasiddhirapi na sati saṃbhave nirālambanādhyavasātuṃ yuktā /
children.translated_text: Worldly common knowledge too, when there is a [valid] basis, should not be concluded to be baseless.

children.text: tasmādupapanno mantrādibhyo devādīnāṃ vigrahavattvādyavagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the understanding from <s>mantras</s> and such that deities possess embodied forms and such is well justified.

children.text: tataścārthitvādisaṃbhavādupapanno devādīnāmapi brahmavidyāyāmadhikāraḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore, since desire and such [qualifications] are possible, the qualification of deities and such even for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is well justified.

children.text: kramamuktidarśanānyapyevamevopapadyante // 33 //
children.translated_text: The teachings of gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>) are also justified in this very manner. // 33 //

The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) sets aside the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>. The teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds that there is qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) for deities and such as well. Although the qualification is impossible in meditations that involve deities as ingredients, such as the <s>Madhu Vidyā</s> and such — nevertheless, qualification is possible in the pure knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>. Because qualification depends on desire, capability, the absence of prohibition, and such. And from the mere fact that it is impossible somewhere, qualification is not to be denied where it is possible. Even among humans, not all <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and such have qualification for all [rituals] such as the <s>Rājasūya</s> and such. Whatever principle applies there will apply here too. And there is a scriptural observation, concerning the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, that indicates the qualification of deities and such: 'Whoever among the gods realized That became That; likewise among the sages; likewise among humans' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10). And: 'They said: Come, let us seek that Self by seeking which one obtains all worlds and all desires.' And: '<s>Indra</s> went forth from among the gods, <s>Virocana</s> from among the <s>Asuras</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.2) — and so forth. There is also the dialogue between the <s>Gandharva</s> and <s>Yājñavalkya</s> and such [narratives] of similar import. As for the objection that because [deities] abide in [physical] light and such [they cannot be qualified] — to this we say: even the words denoting deities that refer to the sun and such as objects of light and such — they present that particular deity-self as possessing consciousness and endowed with sovereignty and such, because of the usage in <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavāda</s>, and such [that attributes consciousness to them]. For deities, through their connection with sovereignty, have the power to abide in forms of light and such, and to assume whatever embodied form they wish. For thus it is heard in the <s>arthavāda</s> of the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> [litany]: '<s>Medhātithi</s>, the ram' — '<s>Indra</s>, having become a ram, carried away <s>Medhātithi Kāṇvāyana</s>' (<s>Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa</s> 1.1). And in <s>Smṛti</s>: 'The Sun, having become a man, approached <s>Kuntī</s>.' Even in [elements like] clay and such, conscious presiding deities are accepted — from observing [expressions like] 'Clay spoke,' 'Waters spoke,' and such. For the elemental constituent (<s>bhūtadhātu</s>) of light and such, unconsciousness is accepted in the sun and such. But the conscious presiding deity-selves [are known] from the usage in <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavāda</s>, and such — this has been said. As for the objection that <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavāda</s>, having a different purpose, do not have the power to reveal the embodiment and such of deities — to this we say: cognition and non-cognition are the cause of [determining] existence and non-existence, not the fact of having another purpose or not having another purpose. For indeed, even one who has set out for another purpose apprehends 'this grass, leaf, and such on the path exists.' To this it is replied: the example is not parallel. For there, perception, directed at grass and leaves as its objects, is operative, by which their existence is apprehended. But here, through being part of a single sentence with the injunctive statement for the purpose of praise, the operation of the <s>arthavāda</s> toward an independent factual reference can be decisively negated. For in the sentence 'One should not drink liquor' (<s>na surāṃ pibet</s>), from the connection of the three words together with the negative particle, only one meaning is understood — the prohibition of drinking liquor. Not that from the connection of the two words 'should drink liquor,' an injunction to drink liquor is also [understood]. To this we reply: the example is not parallel. It is proper that in the prohibition of drinking liquor, since the syntactic connection of the words is unitary, the subsidiary sentence-meaning is not grasped [separately]. But in the case of an injunctive statement and an <s>arthavāda</s>, the words situated in the <s>arthavāda</s> first apprehend a factual referent through independent syntactic connection, and then subsequently, through the force of purposefulness, they come to function as praise of the injunction. Just as in 'One who desires prosperity should offer a white [animal] to <s>Vāyu</s>' — here, the words '<s>Vāyavya</s>' (pertaining to <s>Vāyu</s>) and such that are in the injunctive statement have a connection with the injunction; but not so the words in the <s>arthavāda</s>: '<s>Vāyu</s> is indeed the swiftest deity; one approaches <s>Vāyu</s> with his own share; he alone leads one to prosperity.' For it is not the case that 'One should offer <s>Vāyu</s>' or 'One should offer the swiftest deity' and such [are the meaning]. Rather, through the proclamation of <s>Vāyu</s>'s nature, they first apprehend an independent syntactic meaning and then praise the injunction [by showing]: 'This ritual has such a distinguished deity.' Now, where that independent sentence-meaning falls within the range of another means of knowledge, there the <s>arthavāda</s> operates by restating it. Where it contradicts another means of knowledge, there it operates as figurative speech (<s>guṇavāda</s>). But where neither of these obtains — is it figurative speech because of the absence of another means of knowledge, or is it a statement of actual fact because there is no contradiction with another means of knowledge? — for those who take refuge in [immediate] cognition, the statement of actual fact (<s>vidyamānavāda</s>) should be adopted, not figurative speech. By this, the <s>mantra</s> too is explained. Moreover, the injunctions themselves — which enjoin oblations having <s>Indra</s> and such as deities — require the essential nature of <s>Indra</s> and such. For <s>Indra</s> and such, devoid of essential nature, cannot be brought to mind. And an oblation cannot be offered to a particular deity that has not been brought to mind. And the <s>śruti</s> teaches: 'One should meditate on the deity for whom the oblation has been taken up, at the moment of uttering <s>vaṣaṭ</s>' (<s>Aitareya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.8.1). And a mere word cannot be the essential nature of the referent, because word and meaning are different. Since the essential nature of <s>Indra</s> and such understood from <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavāda</s> is of such-and-such a kind, it is not proper to reject it by [another] word-based means of knowledge. <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> too, through the method explained — being possibly rooted in <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavāda</s> — are capable of establishing the embodiment and such of deities. They can also be rooted in perception and such. For what is not perceptible to us may have been perceptible to the ancients. And thus it is remembered that <s>Vyāsa</s> and others interacted with gods and such through direct perception. One who would say that the ancients, like the people of today, had no capacity to interact with gods and such — he would deny the diversity of the world. He would also say that, as today, there is no universal sovereign <s>kṣatriya</s>. And thereby he would obstruct the injunctions of the <s>Rājasūya</s> and such. And he would claim that even in other ages, the duties of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> were mostly unsettled, as today. And thereby the scripture that ordains regulations would become purposeless. Therefore, it is consistent that the ancients, through the excellence of their <s>dharma</s>, interacted with gods and such through direct perception. Moreover, they remember: 'Through study, communion with the desired deity' (<s>Yogasūtra</s> 2.44) — and such. <s>Yoga</s> too, which is remembered as having as its fruit the attainment of powers like <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) and such, cannot be dismissed by mere audacity. And the <s>śruti</s> proclaims the greatness of <s>Yoga</s>: 'When the fivefold quality of <s>Yoga</s> — arising from earth, water, fire, air, and space — has manifested, there is no disease, no old age, no death for one who has attained the <s>Yoga</s>-fire body' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 2.12). And the capacity of the <s>ṛṣis</s>, who are seers of the <s>mantras</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, should not be measured by our own capacity. Therefore, <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> have a valid foundation.

children.text: FN: yataḥ sarveṣāṃ sarvatrādhikāro na saṃbhavati tato na cāpodyetetyanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: The syntactic connection is: since the qualification of all in all [meditations] is not possible, therefore it is not denied [where it is possible].

children.text: tadbrahma yo devānāṃ madhye pratyaktvenābudhyata /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> — whoever among the gods realized it as the inner Self —

children.text: ādigrahaṇenetihāsapurāṇadharmaśāstrāṇi gṛhyante /
children.translated_text: By the word 'beginning with' (<s>ādi</s>), <s>Itihāsa</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> are included.

children.text: vidhyuddeśo vidhivākyaṃ tadekavākyatayā /
children.translated_text: 'Injunctive statement' (<s>vidhyuddeśa</s>) means the injunctive sentence; by being part of a single sentence with that —

children.text: vṛttānto bhūtārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vṛttānta</s>' means an actual occurrence.

children.text: śliṣyate yujyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śliṣyate</s>' means 'is consistent.'

children.text: mantrajapāddevatāsāṃnidhyaṃ tatsaṃbhāṣaṇaṃ ceti sūtrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is: through the recitation of <s>mantras</s>, the proximity of the deity and conversation with it [become possible].

children.text: apaśūdrādhikaraṇam / sū. 34-38
children.translated_text: The <s>Apaśūdra Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Exclusion of <s>Śūdras</s>) / <s>Sūtras</s> 34-38

children.text: śugasya tadanādaraśravaṇāt tadādravaṇāt sūcyate hi | BBs_1,3.34 |
children.translated_text: [The word '<s>Śūdra</s>' is used] in the sense of grief, because of the hearing of his disregard, and because of his rushing toward [<s>Raikva</s>]; for it is indicated. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.34 |

children.text:
yathā manuṣyādhikāraniyamamapodya devādīnāmapi vidyāsvadhikāra uktastathaiva dvijātyadhikāraniyamāpavādena śūdrasyāpyadhikāraḥ syādityetāmāśaṅkāṃ nivartayitumidamadhikaraṇamārabhyate /
tatra śūdrasyāpyadhikāraḥ syādasti tāvatprāptam /
arthitvasāmarthyayoḥ saṃbhavāt /
'tasmācchūdroyajñe 'navakḷptaḥ' (tai.saṃ. 8.1.1.6) itivat 'śūdro vidyāyāmanavakḷptaḥ' iti ca niṣedhāśravaṇāt /
yacca karmasvanadhikārakāraṇaṃ śūdrasyānagnitvaṃ na tadvidyāsvavikārasyāpavādakaṃ liṅgam /
nahyāhavanīyādirahitena vidyā vedituṃ na śakyate /
bhavati ca liṅgaṃ śūdrādhikārasyopoddhalakam /
saṃvargavidyāyāṃ hi jānaśrutiṃ pautrāyaṇaṃ śuśrūṣuṃ śūdraśabdena parāmṛśati- 'aha hāretvā śūdra tavaiva saha gobhirastu' (chāṃ 4.2.3) iti /
viduraprabhṛtayaśca śūdrayoniprabhavā api viśiṣṭavijñānasaṃpannāḥ smaryante /
tasmādadhikriyate śūdro vidyāsviti /
children.translated_text: Just as, having set aside the restriction of qualification to humans alone, the qualification of deities and such in the <s>vidyās</s> (meditations) was stated — similarly, as an exception to the restriction of qualification to the twice-born, there might also be qualification for a <s>Śūdra</s> — to remove this apprehension, this topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) is commenced. Therein, the initial position is that a <s>Śūdra</s> too would have qualification. Because desire and capability are possible [for a <s>Śūdra</s>]. And because no prohibition is heard [specifically] such as '<s>Śūdra</s> is not qualified for <s>vidyā</s>,' as there is 'Therefore, the <s>Śūdra</s> is not qualified for the sacrifice' (<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 8.1.1.6). And the cause of disqualification from ritual actions for the <s>Śūdra</s> — namely the absence of sacred fires — is not a mark that invalidates [his qualification] for the <s>vidyās</s>, since the <s>vidyās</s> are non-ritual. For one cannot say that <s>vidyā</s> cannot be known without the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other fires. And there is a mark supporting the qualification of the <s>Śūdra</s>. For in the <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s>, <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s>, who was eager to learn, is referred to by the word '<s>Śūdra</s>': 'Ah, come now, <s>Śūdra</s>! Let [the wealth] remain with you together with the cows' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.2.3). And <s>Vidura</s> and others, though born from <s>Śūdra</s> wombs, are remembered as endowed with distinguished knowledge. Therefore, the <s>Śūdra</s> is qualified for the <s>vidyās</s> — [this is the initial position].

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - na śūdrasyādhikāraḥ, vedādhyayanābhāvāt /
adhītavedo hi viditavedārtho vedārtheṣvadhikriyate /
naca śūdrasya vedādhyayanamasti, upanayanapūrvakatvādvedādhyayanasya /
upanayanasya ca varṇatrayaviṣayatvāt /
yattvarthitvaṃ na tadasati sāmarthye 'dhikārakāraṇaṃ bhavati /
sāmarthyamapi na lokikaṃ kevalamadhikārakāraṇaṃ bhavati /
śāstrīyer'the śāstrīyasya sāmarthyasyāpekṣitatvāt /
śāstrīyasya ca sāmarthyasyādhyayananirākaraṇena nirākṛtatvāt /
yaccedaṃ 'śūdro yajñe 'navakḷptaḥ' iti tannyāyapūrvakatvādvidyāyāmapyanavakḷptatvaṃ dyotayati, nyāyasya sādhāraṇatvāt /
yatpunaḥ saṃvargavidyāyāṃ śūdraśabdaśravaṇaṃ liṅgaṃ manyase, na talliṅgaṃ nyāyābhāvāt /
nyāyokte hi liṅgadarśanaṃ dyotakaṃ bhavati /
nacātra nyāyo 'sti /
kāmaṃ cāyaṃ śūdraśabdaḥ saṃvargavidyāyāmevaikasyāṃ śūdramadhikuryāt, tadviṣayatvāt, na sarvāsu vidyāsu /
arthavādasthāttu na kvacidapyayaṃ śūdramadhikartumutsahate /
śakyate cāyaṃ śūdraśabdo 'dhikṛtavaṣayo yojayitum /
kathamityucyate- 'kambara enametatsantaṃ sayugvānamiva raikvamāttha'' (chā. 4.1.3) ityasmāddhaṃsavākyādātmano 'nādaraṃ śrutavato jānaśruteḥ pautrāyaṇasya śugutpede, tāmṛṣīraikvaḥ śūdraśabdenānena sūcayaṃbabhūvātmanaḥ parokṣajñatākhyāpanāyeti gamyate /
jātiśūdrasyānadhikārāt /
children.translated_text: This being the position reached, we say: the <s>Śūdra</s> has no qualification, because of the absence of Vedic study. For one who has studied the <s>Veda</s> and has understood its meaning is qualified for the purposes of the <s>Veda</s>. And there is no Vedic study for a <s>Śūdra</s>, because Vedic study is preceded by <s>Upanayana</s> (initiation). And <s>Upanayana</s> pertains only to the three [upper] <s>varṇas</s>. As for the desire [for knowledge] — that, in the absence of capability, does not constitute a ground for qualification. And mere worldly capability alone is not a ground for qualification, because scriptural capability is required for scriptural purposes. And scriptural capability has been negated by the negation of [Vedic] study. And the statement 'the <s>Śūdra</s> is not qualified for sacrifice' — because it is based on reasoning, indicates non-qualification in <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) as well, since the reasoning is of general application. As for the occurrence of the word '<s>Śūdra</s>' in the <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s> that you consider a mark [of qualification] — that is not a mark, because of the absence of reasoning [supporting it]. For the observation of a mark is illuminating [only] when it is supported by reasoning. And there is no reasoning here [to support Śūdra qualification]. At most, this word '<s>Śūdra</s>' could qualify a <s>Śūdra</s> for only that one <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s>, since it pertains to that [alone], but not for all <s>vidyās</s>. And being situated in an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage), it is not able to qualify a <s>Śūdra</s> anywhere at all. Moreover, this word '<s>Śūdra</s>' can be construed as referring to one who is [already] qualified [i.e., not a <s>Śūdra</s> by birth]. How? — it is explained: when <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> heard from the swan-dialogue — 'O rogue! As if you speak of <s>Raikva</s> with the cart!' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.1.3) — disrespect toward himself, sorrow arose in him. <s>Ṛṣi Raikva</s> indicated that [sorrow] with this word '<s>Śūdra</s>' — to make known his knowledge of the other's inner state. This is understood. Because a <s>Śūdra</s> by birth has no qualification.

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ śūdraśabdena śugutpannā sūcyata iti /
children.translated_text: But how is the arising of sorrow indicated by the word '<s>Śūdra</s>'?

children.text: ucyate- tadādravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: It is said: because of running toward it (<s>tad-ādravaṇa</s>).

children.text: śucamabhidudrāva, śucā vābhidudruve, śucā vā raikvamabhidudrāveti śūdraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He ran toward sorrow' (<s>śucam abhidudrāva</s>), or 'he was overcome by sorrow' (<s>śucā abhidudruve</s>), or 'he ran to <s>Raikva</s> out of sorrow' (<s>śucā Raikvam abhidudrāva</s>) — [hence] '<s>Śūdra</s>.'

children.text: avayavārthasaṃbhavādrūḍhārthasya cāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Because the component-meaning [of the word] is possible, while the conventional meaning [<s>Śūdra</s> by birth] is not possible [in this context].

children.text: dṛśyate cāyamartho 'syāmākhyāyikāyām // 34 //
children.translated_text: And this meaning is seen in this very narrative. // 34 //

children.text: FN: anavakḷpto 'samarthaḥ tasmādanagnitvāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Anavakḷpta</s>' means 'incapable' — therefore, because of not having the [sacrificial] fire.

children.text:
aheti nipātaḥ khedārthaḥ /
hāreṇa niṣkeṇa itvāgantā ratho hāretvā saca gobhiḥ saha he śūdra, tavaivāstu kimalpenānena mama gārhyasthyānupayogineti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The particle '<s>aha</s>' expresses irritation. '[Coming] with a necklace, a gold [coin], having come by chariot, and with cows — O <s>Śūdra</s>, let these be yours! What use is this little [offering] to me, who has no need for household [amenities]?' — this is the sense.

children.text: yajñetyupalakṣaṇaṃ vidyāyāmanavakḷpta ityasya /
children.translated_text: 'In sacrifice' is illustrative — meaning: he is not qualified in <s>vidyā</s> [either].

children.text: 'niṣādasthapatiṃ yājayet' iti niṣādasthapatiścodyate, śūdraḥ saṃvargavidyāyām /
children.translated_text: 'One should perform sacrifice for the <s>Niṣāda</s> chief' — the <s>Niṣāda</s> chief is enjoined [in sacrifice]; the <s>Śūdra</s>, in the <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s>.

children.text:
kaṃ u are iti padacchedaḥ /
u śabdopyarthaḥ /
yugvā gantrī śakaṭī tathā saha sthitaṃ raikvamivaitadvacanamāttha /
children.translated_text: The word-division is: '<s>kaṃ u are</s>.' The particle '<s>u</s>' is a mere expletive. '<s>Yugvā</s>' means 'going,' a cart; [the swan says]: 'You speak this word as if about one associated with <s>Raikva</s> who is with his cart.'

children.text: kṣatriyatvagateś cottaratra caitrarathena liṅgāt | BBs_1,3.35 |
children.translated_text: And because his <s>Kṣatriya</s> status is understood further on, from the mark of [association with] <s>Caitraratha</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.35 |

children.text:
itaśca na jātiśūdro jānaśrutiḥ /
yatkāraṇaṃ prakaraṇanirūpaṇena kṣatriyatvamasyottaratra caitrarathenābhipratāriṇā kṣatriyeṇa samabhivyāhārādgamyate /
uttaratra hi saṃvargavidyāvākyaśeṣe caitrarathirabhipratārī kṣatriyaḥ saṃkīrtyate- ' atha ha śaunakaṃ ca kapoyamabhipratāraṇaṃ ca kākṣaseniṃ pariviṣyamāṇau brahmacārī vibhikṣe' (chā. 4.3.5) iti /
caitrarathitvaṃ cābhipratāriṇaḥ kāpeyayogādavagantavyam /
kāpeyayogo hi citrarathasyāvagataḥ 'etena vai citrarathaṃ kāpeyā ayājayan' (tāṇḍa.brā. 20.12.5) iti /
samānānvayānāṃ ca prāyeṇa samānānvayā yājakā bhavanti /
'tasmāccaitrarathirnāmakaḥ kṣatrapatirajāyata' iti ca kṣatrapatitvāvagamātkṣatriyatvamasyāvagantavyam /
tena kṣatriyeṇābhipratāriṇā saha samānāyāṃ vidyayāyāṃ saṃkīrtanaṃ jānaśruterapi kṣatriyatvaṃ sūcayati /
children.translated_text: The mention of <s>Jānaśruti</s> together with that <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>Abhipratārin</s> in the same <s>vidyā</s> indicates that <s>Jānaśruti</s> too is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.

children.text: samānānāmeva hi prāyeṇa samabhivyāhārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: For generally, only those of the same [class] are mentioned together.

children.text: kṣattṛpreṣaṇādyaiśvaryayogācca jānaśruteḥ kṣatriyatvāvagatiḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Jānaśruti</s>'s <s>Kṣatriya</s> status is understood from his possessing sovereignty indicated by the sending of a <s>kṣattṛ</s> (charioteer/attendant) and so forth.

children.text: ato na śūdrasyādhikāraḥ // 35 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Śūdra</s> has no qualification. // 35 //

For this further reason, <s>Jānaśruti</s> is not a <s>Śūdra</s> by birth. Because, through contextual investigation, his <s>Kṣatriya</s> status is understood further on from his being mentioned together with <s>Abhipratārin</s> the <s>Caitraratha</s>, who is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>. For further on, in the remainder of the <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s> passage, <s>Abhipratārin Caitrarathi</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, is mentioned: 'Then, a <s>brahmacārin</s> begged from <s>Śaunaka Kāpeya</s> and <s>Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni</s> while they were being served food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.5). And the <s>Caitrarathi</s> status of <s>Abhipratārin</s> should be understood from his connection with the <s>Kāpeya</s> [lineage]. For the <s>Kāpeya</s> connection with <s>Citraratha</s> is known: 'With this [rite] the <s>Kāpeyas</s> caused <s>Citraratha</s> to perform sacrifice' (<s>Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa</s> 20.12.5). And those of the same lineage generally have sacrificial priests of the same lineage. And from the understanding that he is a ruler (<s>kṣatrapati</s>) — '[therefore] one named <s>Caitrarathi</s> was born as a ruler' — his <s>Kṣatriya</s> status should be understood.

children.text:
FN: saṃvargavidyāvidhyanantaramarthavādārambhārtho 'thābdaḥ /
ha śabdo vṛttāntāvadyotī /
śunakaputraṃ kapigotraṃ purohitamabhipratārināmakam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The word '<s>atha</s>' introduces the <s>arthavāda</s> that follows the injunction of the <s>Saṃvarga Vidyā</s>. The particle '<s>ha</s>' indicates a past event. [<s>Śaunaka</s>] the <s>Kāpeya</s> — the son of <s>Śunaka</s>, of the <s>Kapi</s> lineage, the family priest — and [<s>Abhipratārin</s>] named <s>Abhipratārin</s>.

children.text: kṣattā sūtastasya raikvānveṣaṇāya preṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The <s>kṣattṛ</s> is a charioteer; the sending of him to search for <s>Raikva</s>.

children.text: saṃskāraparāmarśāt tadabhāvābhilāpāc ca | BBs_1,3.36 |
children.translated_text: Because of the reference to purificatory rites, and because of the statement of their absence [for the <s>Śūdra</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.36 |

children.text:
itaśca na śūdrasyādhikāraḥ, yadvidyāpradeśeṣūpanayanādayaḥ saṃskārāḥ parāmṛśyante- 'taṃ hopaninye' (śa.brā. 11.5.3.13) /
' adhīhi bhagava iti hopasasāda' (chā. 7.1.1) ' brahmaparā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ paraṃ brahmānveṣamāṇā eṣa ha vai tatsarvaṃ vakṣyatīti te ha samitpāṇayo bhagavantaṃ pippalādamupasannāḥ' (pra. 1.1) iti ca /
' tānhānupanīyaiva' (chā. 5.11.7) ityapi pradarśitaivopanayanaprāptirbhavati /
śūdrasya saṃskārābhāvo 'bhilapyate, 'śūdraścaturtho varṇa ekajātiḥ' (manu. 10.4)
children.translated_text: For this further reason, the <s>Śūdra</s> has no qualification — because in passages teaching <s>vidyā</s>, purificatory rites such as <s>Upanayana</s> are referred to: 'He initiated him' (<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 11.5.3.13); 'Teach me, revered sir — thus he approached' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.1); 'Devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, established in <s>Brahman</s>, seeking the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — "He will tell us all of that" — with sacrificial fuel in hand, they approached the venerable <s>Pippalāda</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 1.1). And even 'without having initiated them' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.11.7) demonstrates that the attainment of <s>Upanayana</s> [is normally expected]. The absence of purificatory rites for the <s>Śūdra</s> is stated — from the <s>Smṛti</s>: 'The <s>Śūdra</s> is the fourth <s>varṇa</s>, of single birth (<s>ekajāti</s>)' (<s>Manu</s> 10.4) —

children.text: ityekajātitvasmaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: because of the <s>Smṛti</s> statement that he is of single birth [i.e., without the second birth of initiation].

children.text: 'na śūdro pātakaṃ kiñcinna ca saṃskāramarhati' (manu. 10.12.6) ityādibhiśca // 36 //
children.translated_text: And: 'The <s>Śūdra</s> incurs no sin [from non-observance of rites], nor does he deserve purificatory rites' (<s>Manu</s> 10.126) — and such [passages]. // 36 //

children.text: FN: adhīhi upadiśeti yāvat /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Adhīhi</s>' means 'teach' — this is the meaning.

children.text:
brahmaparā vedapāragāḥ /
paraṃ nirguṇaṃ brahma /
upāsannā upāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahmaparā</s>' means those who have mastered the <s>Veda</s>. 'The Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' means the attributeless <s>Brahman</s>. '<s>Upāsannā</s>' means 'approached.'

children.text: anupanīyaiveti hīnavarṇenottamavarṇā anupanīyaivopadeṣṭavyā ityācārajñāpanārthamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without having initiated them' — the meaning is: for the purpose of making known the custom that those of higher <s>varṇa</s> should be taught even without initiation by one of lower <s>varṇa</s>.

children.text: ekajātiranupanītaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of single birth' means 'not initiated.'

children.text: tadabhāvanirdhāraṇe ca pravṛtteḥ | BBs_1,3.37 |
children.translated_text: And because [the teacher] proceeded [with initiation] upon determining the absence of that [<s>Śūdra</s> status]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.37 |

children.text: itaśca na śūdrasyādhikāraḥ /
children.translated_text: For this further reason, the <s>Śūdra</s> has no qualification.

children.text: yatsatyavacanena śūdratvābhāve nirdhārite jābālaṃ gautama upanetumanuśāsituṃ ca pravavṛte 'naitadbrāhmaṇo vivaktumarhati samidhaṃ somyāharopa tvā neṣye na satyādagāḥ' (chā. 4.4.5) iti śrutiliṅgāt // 37 //
children.translated_text: Because, when the absence of <s>Śūdra</s> status was determined through truthful speech, <s>Gautama</s> proceeded to initiate and instruct <s>Jābāla</s> — from the <s>śruti</s> indication: 'A non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would not be capable of speaking thus. Bring fuel, dear one; I shall initiate you. You have not deviated from the truth' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.4.5). // 37 //

children.text: FN: nāhaṃ gotraṃ vedmi na mātā vetti parantu tathoktam upanayanārthamācāryaṃ gatvā satyakāmo jābālo 'smīti brūhītyanena satyavacanena /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'I do not know my lineage; my mother does not know [either]' — but it was said thus: 'For the purpose of initiation, go to the teacher and say: I am <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>' — by this truthful speech.

children.text: śravaṇādhyayanārthapratiṣedhāt smṛteś ca | BBs_1,3.38 |
children.translated_text: Because of the prohibition of hearing, study, and their meaning in <s>Smṛti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.38 |

children.text:
itaśca na śūdrasyādhikāraḥ /
yadasya smṛteḥ śravaṇādhyayanārthapratiṣedho bhavati /
vedaśravaṇapratiṣedho vedādhyayanapratiṣedhastadarthajñānānuṣṭhānayośca pratiṣedhaḥ śūdrasya smaryate /
śravaṇapratiṣedhastāvat 'athāsya vedamupaśṛṇvatastrapujatubhyāṃ śrotrapratipūraṇam' iti /
'padyu ha vā etacchmaśānaṃ yacchūdrastasmācchūdrasamīpe nādhyetavyam' iti ca /
ata evādhyayanapratiṣedhaḥ /
yasya hi samīpe 'pi nādhyetavyaṃ bhavati sa kathamaśrutamadhīyīta /
bhavati ca vedoccāraṇe jihvācchedo dhāraṇe śarīrabheda iti /
ata eva cārthādarthajñānānuṣṭhānayoḥ pratiṣedho bhavati 'na śūdrasya matiṃ dadyāt' iti, 'dvijātīnāmadhyayanamijyā dānam' iti ca /
children.translated_text: And from this, the prohibition of knowledge and practice of the meaning follows as a matter of course — 'One should not give instruction to a <s>Śūdra</s>' — and: 'Study, sacrifice, and gift-giving are for the twice-born.'

children.text: yeṣāṃ punaḥ pūrvakṛtasaṃskāravaśādviduradharmavyādhaprabhṛtīnāṃ jñānotpattisteṣāṃ na śakyate phalaprāptiḥ pratiṣeddhuṃ, jñānasyaikāntikaphalatvāt /
children.translated_text: But for those such as <s>Vidura</s>, <s>Dharmavyādha</s>, and others, in whom knowledge arises through the power of purificatory impressions from past lives, the attainment of the fruit cannot be denied, because knowledge has an invariable fruit.

children.text: 'śrāvayeccaturo varṇān' iti cetihāsapurāṇādhigame cāturvarṇyasyādhikārasmaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: And because the <s>Smṛti</s> records the qualification of all four <s>varṇas</s> for the study of <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>: 'One should cause the four <s>varṇas</s> to hear [them].'

children.text: vedapūrvakastu nāstyadhikāraḥ śūdrāṇāmiti sthitam // 38//
children.translated_text: But there is no qualification preceded by Vedic [study] for <s>Śūdras</s> — this is established. // 38 //

For this further reason, the <s>Śūdra</s> has no qualification — because there is in <s>Smṛti</s> a prohibition for him regarding hearing, study, and their meaning. The prohibition of hearing the <s>Veda</s>, the prohibition of studying the <s>Veda</s>, and the prohibition of the knowledge and practice of its meaning are recorded for the <s>Śūdra</s> in <s>Smṛti</s>. The prohibition of hearing is: 'If he listens to the <s>Veda</s>, his ears are to be filled with [molten] lead and lac.' And: 'Indeed, the <s>Śūdra</s> is a walking cremation ground; therefore, one should not study in the proximity of a <s>Śūdra</s>.' From this, the prohibition of study [follows] as well. For one in whose proximity one should not even study — how could he study what he has never heard? And for uttering the <s>Veda</s>, there is cutting of the tongue; for memorizing it, splitting of the body — [so it is said].

children.text: FN: trapujatubhyāṃ saṃtāpadrutābhyāṃ sīsalākṣābhyām /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'With lead and lac' — with lead and lac that have been heated and melted.

children.text:
padyu pādayuktaṃ /
saṃcārasamarthamiti yāvat /
children.translated_text: '<s>Padyu</s>' means 'equipped with feet,' i.e., capable of moving about.

children.text: matirvedārthajñānam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mati</s>' means knowledge of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: 10 kampanādhikaraṇam / sū. 39
children.translated_text: 10. The <s>Kampana Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Trembling) / <s>Sūtra</s> 39

children.text: kampanāt | BBs_1,3.39 |
children.translated_text: Because of [the reference to] trembling. | <s>BBs</s> 1.3.39 |

children.text:
avasitaḥ prāsaṅgiko 'dhikāravicāraḥ /
prakṛtāmevedānīṃ vākyārthavicāraṇāṃ pravartayiṣyāmaḥ /
'yadidaṃ kiñca jagatsarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam /
mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyataṃ ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti' (kā. 2.6.2) iti /
etadvākyaṃ 'ejṛ kampane' iti dhātvarthānugamāllakṣitam /
asminvākye sarvamidaṃ jagatprāṇāśrayaṃ spandate, mahacca kiñcidbhayakāraṇaṃ vajraśabditamudyataṃ, tadvijñānāccāmṛtatvaprāptiriti śrūyate /
tatra ko 'sau prāṇaḥ kiṃ tadbhayānakaṃ vajramityapratipattervicāre kriyamāṇe prāptaṃ tāvatprasiddheḥ pañcavṛttirvāyuḥ prāṇa iti /
prasiddhereva cāśanirvajraṃ syāt /
vāyoścedaṃ māhātmyaṃ saṃkīrtyate /
katham /
sarvamidaṃ jagatpañcavṛttau vāyau prāṇaśabdite pratiṣṭhāyaijati /
vāyunimittameva ca mahadbhayānakaṃ vajramudyamyate /
vāyau hi parjanyabhāvena vivartamāne vidyutstanayitruvṛṣṭyaśanayo vivartanta ityācakṣate /
vāyuvijñānādeva cedamamṛtatvam /
tathāhi śrutyantaram- 'vāyureva vyaṣṭirvāyuḥ samaṣṭirapa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda' iti /
children.translated_text: The incidental investigation of qualification has been concluded. Now we shall resume the investigation of the meaning of passages, which is the topic at hand. 'Whatever there is in this entire world trembles, having issued forth from <s>Prāṇa</s>; a great fear, an upraised thunderbolt — those who know this become immortal' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6.2). This passage has been noticed because of conformity with the root meaning '<s>ejṛ kampane</s>' (to tremble). In this passage it is heard: this entire world, depending on <s>Prāṇa</s>, trembles; and something great, a cause of fear, designated by the word 'thunderbolt,' is raised; and from the knowledge of that, there is attainment of immortality. Therein, when an investigation is undertaken due to the uncertainty about who this <s>Prāṇa</s> is and what this fearful thunderbolt is — the initial position is: from common usage, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the air (<s>Vāyu</s>) with its fivefold function. And from common usage, the thunderbolt would be lightning. The greatness of <s>Vāyu</s> is being celebrated here. How? This entire world, depending on the air — denoted by the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' — with its fivefold function, trembles. And the great, fearful thunderbolt is wielded on account of <s>Vāyu</s>. For they say that when <s>Vāyu</s> transforms into the form of rain-clouds, lightning, thunder, rain, and thunderbolts arise. And this immortality is from the knowledge of <s>Vāyu</s> alone. For thus another <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the individual; <s>Vāyu</s> is the aggregate. One conquers repeated death — one who knows thus.'

children.text:
tasmādvāyurayamiha pratipattavya iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- brahmaivedamiha pratipattavyam /
kutaḥ /
pūrvottarālocanāt /
pūrvottarayorhi granthabhāgayorbrahmaivanirdiśyamānamupalabhāmahe /
ihaiva kathamakasmādantarāle vāyuṃ nirdiśyamānaṃ pratipadyemahi /
pūrvatra tāvat 'tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate /

prāṇaśabdo 'pyayaṃ prayuktaḥ, 'prāṇasya prāṇam' (bṛ. 4.4.18) iti darśanāt /
ejayitṛtvamapīdaṃ paramātmana evopapadyate na vāyumātrasya /
tathācoktam- 'na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana /
itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminnetāvupāśritau' (kā. 2.5.5) iti /
uttaratrāpi 'bhayādasyāgnistapati bhayāttapati sūryaḥ /
bhayādindraśca vāyuśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ' (kā. 2.6.3) iti brahmaiva nirdekṣyate na vāyuḥ /
savāyukasya jagato bhayahetutvābhidhānāt /
tadevehāpi saṃnidhānānmahadbhayaṃ, vajramudyatamiti ca bhayahetutvapratyabhijñānānnirdiṣṭamiti gamyate /
vajraśabdo 'pyayaṃ bhayahetutvasāmānyātprayuktaḥ /
yathāhi vajramudyataṃ mamaiva śirasi nipatedyadyahamasya śāsanaṃ na kuryāmityanena bhayena jano niyamena rājādiśāsane pravartata evamidamagnivāyusūryādikaṃ jagadasmādeva brahmaṇo bibhyanniyamena svavyāpāre pravartata iti bhayānakaṃ vajropamitaṃ brahma /
tathāca brahmaviṣayaṃ śrutyantaram- 'bhīṣāsmādvātaḥ pavate /
bhīṣodeti sūryaḥ /
bhīṣāsmādagniścendraśca /
mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ' (tai. 8.1) iti /
amṛtatvaphalaśravaṇādapi brahmaivedamiti gamyate /
brahmajñānāddhyamṛtatvaprāptiḥ /
'tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' (śve. 6.15) iti mantravarṇāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, Vāyu (air) is to be understood here — given this position, we say: It is <s>Brahman</s> alone that is to be understood here. Why? From the examination of what precedes and what follows. For in both the preceding and subsequent portions of the text, we find <s>Brahman</s> alone being indicated. How could we accept that Vāyu is suddenly indicated here in the middle, without any reason? In the preceding [passage]: 'That indeed is the Pure, that is <s>Brahman</s>, that is called the Immortal; all the worlds rest in it, and none goes beyond it' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6.1) — <s>Brahman</s> is indicated; and that same [<s>Brahman</s>] is understood to be indicated here too, because of its proximity, and because [the statement] 'All the world trembles in <s>Prāṇa</s>' is recognized as referring to the same [entity] that serves as the resting-place of the worlds. The word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' too is used [for <s>Brahman</s>], as seen in 'the breath of breath' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.18). And this power to cause trembling too is appropriate for the supreme Self alone, not for mere Vāyu. As it is stated: 'No mortal lives by <s>prāṇa</s> or by <s>apāna</s>; they live by another, in which these two are based' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.5.5). In the subsequent [passage] too — 'From fear of Him, fire burns; from fear, the sun shines; from fear, <s>Indra</s> and Vāyu and Death, the fifth, run' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6.3) — it is <s>Brahman</s> alone that will be indicated, not Vāyu, since it is stated as the cause of fear for the world including Vāyu. And that same [<s>Brahman</s>] is understood to be indicated here too — because of its proximity, and because [the expression] 'a great terror, like an upraised thunderbolt' is recognized as referring to the same cause of fear. The word 'thunderbolt' (<s>vajra</s>) too is used here because of the common quality of being a cause of fear. Just as, with the fear 'the upraised thunderbolt will fall on my very head if I do not obey its command,' people invariably engage in obedience to the command of a king and such — so too this world of fire, wind, sun, and such, fearing this very <s>Brahman</s>, invariably engages in its own activities — thus <s>Brahman</s> is fearsome, compared to a thunderbolt. And there is a <s>śruti</s> from another text about <s>Brahman</s>: 'From fear of Him the wind blows; from fear the sun rises; from fear <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>, and Death the fifth, run' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8.1). From hearing of immortality as the fruit too, it is understood that this is <s>Brahman</s> alone. For the attainment of immortality comes from the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> — from the text of the <s>mantra</s>: 'By knowing Him alone, one crosses over death; there is no other path for going' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.15).

children.text: yattu vāyuvijñānātkvacidamṛtatvamabhihitaṃ tadāpekṣikam /
tatraiva prakaṇāntarakaraṇena paramātmānamabhidhāya 'anto 'nyadārtam' (bṛ. 3.4) iti vāyvāderārtatvābhidhānāt /
children.translated_text: Because in that very context, having introduced the supreme Self by creating a different section, [the scripture] states the afflicted nature of Vāyu and the rest: 'Other than this, [everything] is afflicted' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4).

children.text: prakaraṇādapyatra paramātmaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the context too, the supreme Self is determined here.

children.text: anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmādanyatrāsmatkṛtākṛtāt /
children.translated_text: 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>, other than what is done and what is not done here,

children.text: anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca yattatpaśyasi tadvada (kā. 1.2.14) iti paramātmanaḥ pṛṣṭatvāt // 39 //
children.translated_text: other than the past and the future — whatever you see, tell me that' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.14) — because the supreme Self was the topic of the question. // 39 //
As for the immortality stated somewhere as resulting from the knowledge of Vāyu — that is relative.

children.text:
FN: bhīṣā bhītyā /
asmādbrahmaṇo nimittāditi yāvat /
pañcānāṃ grahaṇaṃ brahmādistambāntacarācaropalakṣaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Bhīṣā</s>' means through fear. 'From this' means from <s>Brahman</s> as the cause. The mention of five is to indicate all moving and non-moving [beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass.

children.text: 'apapunarmṛtyuṃ jayati' iti śrutyā hyapamṛtyorvijaya ukto na tu paramamṛtyuvijaya ityāpekṣikatvam /
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> 'He conquers re-death' speaks of the conquest of secondary death, not of the supreme death — hence the relativity.

children.text: 11 jyotiradhikaraṇam / sū. 40
children.translated_text: 11. The <s>Jyotir Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Light). <s>Sūtra</s> 40.

children.text: jyotir darśanāt | BBs_1,3.40 |
children.translated_text: Light [is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of observation. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.40 |

children.text:
'eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrātsamutthāya paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate' (chā. 8.12.3) iti śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayyate, kiṃ jyotiḥśabdaṃ cakṣurviṣayatamopahaṃ tejaḥ kiṃvā paraṃ brahmeti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /

naceha tadvatkiñcitsvārthaparityāge kāraṇaṃ dṛśyate /
tathāca nāḍīkhaṇḍe- 'atha yatraitadasmāccharīrādutkrāmatyathaitaireva raśmibhirūrdhvamākramate' (chā. 8.6.5) iti mumukṣorādityaprāptirabhihitā /
tasmātprasiddhameva tejo jyotiḥśabdamiti /

tasya hīha prakaraṇe vaktavyatvenānuvṛttirdṛśyate, ' ya ātmāpahatapāpmā' (chā. 8.7.1) ityapahatapāpmatvādiguṇakasyātmanaḥ prakaraṇādāvanveṣṭavyatvena vijijñāsitavyatvena ca pratijñānāt /
'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi' (chā. 8.9.3) iti cānusaṃdhānāt /
'aśarīraṃ vāvasantaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ'(chā. 8.12.1) iti cāśarīratāyai jyotiḥsaṃpatterasyābhidhānāt /
brahmabhāvāccānyatrāśarīratānupapatteḥ 'paraṃ jyotiḥ' 'sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ' (chā. 8.12.3) iti ca viśeṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: And because bodilessness is not possible anywhere other than in the state of <s>Brahman</s>; and because of the qualifiers 'supreme light' and 'He is the highest <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3).

children.text: yattūktaṃ mumukṣorādityaprāptirabhihiteti /
children.translated_text: As for what was said — that reaching the sun is described for the one seeking liberation —

children.text: nāsāvātyantiko mokṣo gatyutkrāntisaṃbandhāt /
children.translated_text: that is not ultimate liberation, because it is connected with departure and going.

children.text: nahyātyantike mokṣe gatyutkrāntī sta iti vakṣyāmaḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: For we shall state that in ultimate liberation there is neither departure nor going. // 40 //

'This serene one, rising from this body and reaching the supreme light, emerges in his own form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3) — thus it is heard. There, the doubt arises: Does the word '<s>jyotis</s>' (light) denote the material light that dispels darkness for the eyes, or the supreme <s>Brahman</s>? What is the prima facie view? That it is the well-known material light. Why? Because the word '<s>jyotis</s>' is conventionally established in that sense. For in '<s>jyotiścaraṇābhidhānāt</s>' (<s>BBs</s> 1.1.24), the word '<s>jyotis</s>' abandoned its own meaning and referred to <s>Brahman</s> because of the context. But here, nothing comparable is seen as a reason for abandoning the own meaning. And in the passage on the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels): 'When he departs from this body, he ascends by these very rays' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5) — the one seeking liberation is described as reaching the sun. Therefore, the well-known material light is [meant by] the word '<s>jyotis</s>' — given this position, we say: It is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone that is [meant by] the word '<s>jyotis</s>.' Why? Because of observation. For the continuation of that [<s>Brahman</s>] as the topic to be discussed is observed in this context, since at the beginning of the section, the Self endowed with qualities such as freedom from evil — 'The Self that is free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) — was promised as to be sought and to be known. And because of the reconnection: 'I will explain this further to you' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.9.3). And because bodilessness is stated as the reason for reaching the light: 'Pleasure and pain do not touch one who is bodiless' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.1).

children.text:
FN: 'atha yā etā hṛdayasya nāḍyaḥ' ityādi nāḍīkhaṇḍaḥ /
tatrādityagrahānurodhena mumukṣostatprāptirabhihiteti saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Now, these channels of the heart...' and so forth is the passage on the <s>nāḍīs</s>. The connection is: in accordance with the mention of the sun there, the reaching of that [sun] by the one seeking liberation is stated.

children.text: 12 arthāntaratvavyapadeśādhikaraṇam / sū. 41
children.translated_text: 12. The <s>Arthāntaratva-vyapadeśa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Designation as Being of a Different Nature). <s>Sūtra</s> 41.

children.text: ākāśo 'rthāntaratvādivyapadeśāt | BBs_1,3.41 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s> (Space) [is <s>Brahman</s>] — because of the designation [of the entity] as being of a different nature and so forth. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.41 |

children.text:
'ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā te yadantarā tadbrahma tadamṛtaṃ sa ātmā' (chā. 8.14.1) iti śrūyate /
tatkimākāśasabdaṃ paraṃ brahma kiṃvā prasiddhameva bhūtākāśamiti vicāre bhūtaparigraho yuktaḥ /
ākāśaśabdasya tasminrūḍhatvāt, nāmarūpanirvahaṇasya cāvakāśādānadvāreṇa tasminyojayituṃ śakyatvāt, sraṣṭṛtvādeśca spaṣṭasya brahmaliṅgasyāśravaṇāditi /
evaṃ prāpta idamucyate- parameva brahmehākāśaśabdaṃ bhavitumarhati /
kasmāt /
arthāntaratvādivyapadeśāt /
'te yadantarā tadbrahma' iti hi nāmarūpābhyāmarthāntarabhūtamākāśaṃ vyapadiśati /
naca brahmaṇo 'nyannāmarūpābhyāmarthāntaraṃ saṃbhavati' sarvasya vikārajātasya nāmarūpābhyāmeva vyākṛtatvāt /
nāmarūpayorapi nirvahaṇaṃ niraṅ kuśaṃ na brahmaṇo 'nyatra saṃbhavati /
'anena jīvenātmanānupraviśyanāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi' (chā. 6.3.2) ityādibrahmakartṛtvaśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: 'Space (<s>Ākāśa</s>) is indeed the name of the one that brings forth names and forms; what is within them — that is <s>Brahman</s>, that is the Immortal, that is the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1) — thus it is heard. Is the entity denoted by the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, or the well-known elemental space? In this examination, the adoption of the element would be appropriate — because the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' is conventionally established in that sense, and because the bringing forth of names and forms can be attributed to it through [the function of] providing room, and because no clear indicatory mark of <s>Brahman</s> such as creatorship is heard. Given this position, it is said: It is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone that the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' properly denotes here. Why? Because of the designation as being of a different nature and so forth. For in 'What is within them — that is <s>Brahman</s>' — space is designated as being of a different nature from names and forms. And nothing other than <s>Brahman</s> can be of a different nature from names and forms, since the entire class of modifications is differentiated by names and forms alone. And the unrestricted bringing forth of names and forms is not possible for anything other than <s>Brahman</s> — because the <s>śruti</s> attributes the agency to <s>Brahman</s>: 'Having entered with this living Self, let me manifest names and forms' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2).

children.text: nanu jīvasyāpi pratyakṣaṃ nāmarūpaviṣayaṃ nirvoḍhutvamasti /
children.translated_text: But even the <s>jīva</s> directly has the capacity to bring forth names and forms!

children.text: bāḍhamasti /
abhedastviha vivakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the non-difference [of the <s>jīva</s> from <s>Brahman</s>] is what is intended here.

children.text: nāmarūpanirvahaṇābhidhānādeva ca sraṣṭṛtvādi brahmaliṅgamabhihitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And from the very statement of bringing forth names and forms, the indicatory mark of <s>Brahman</s> such as creatorship is [implicitly] stated.

children.text: 'tadbrahma tadamṛtaṃ sa ātmā' (chā. 8.14) iti ca brahmavādasya liṅgāni /
children.translated_text: And 'That is <s>Brahman</s>, that is the Immortal, that is the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14) — these are indicatory marks of the discourse about <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: 'ākāśastalliṅgāt' (bra. 1.1.22) ityasyaivāyaṃ prapañcaḥ // 41 //
children.translated_text: This is an elaboration of the very [<s>sūtra</s>] '<s>Ākāśas talliṅgāt</s>' (<s>BBs</s> 1.1.22). // 41 //
Indeed it does.

children.text: FN: nāmarūpe śabdāthā tadantaḥpātinastadbhinnatvaṃ tatkartṛtvaṃ cāyuktamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: Names and forms are the referents of words; that [<s>Brahman</s>] which encompasses them — being both different from them and their creator — would be inappropriate [if it were merely space]: this is the meaning.

children.text: 13 suṣuptyutkrāntyadhikaraṇam / sū. 42-43
children.translated_text: 13. The <s>Suṣuptyutkrānti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Deep Sleep and Departure). <s>Sūtras</s> 42-43.

children.text: suṣuptyutkrāntyor bhedena | BBs_1,3.42 |
children.translated_text: Because of the designation as different [from the embodied self] in deep sleep and at departure. | <s>BBs</s> 1,3.42 |

children.translated_text: Because [<s>Janaka</s>] asks at every step: 'Henceforth, teach only toward liberation.'

children.text: yacca 'ananvāgatastena bhavatyasaṅgo hyayaṃ puruṣaḥ' (bṛ. 4.3.14,15) iti pade pade prativakti /
children.translated_text: And because [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] replies at every step: 'He is not followed by that; for this <s>Puruṣa</s> is unattached' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.14-15).

children.text: tasmādasaṃsārisvarūpapratipādanaparamevaitadvākyamityavagantavyam // 42 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this passage is to be understood as directed toward establishing the nature of the non-transmigrating [Self]. // 42 //

'Designation' (<s>vyapadeśa</s>) carries over [from the previous sūtra]. In the sixth chapter of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, having begun with 'Which is the Self? — This one made of knowledge (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), the person who is the light among the vital breaths, within the heart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7), an elaborate exposition concerning the Self was given. The doubt is: Is this passage directed merely toward describing the nature of the transmigrating self, or toward establishing the nature of the non-transmigrating [Self]? What is the prima facie view? That it concerns only the nature of the transmigrating self. Why? Because of the opening and conclusion. In the opening, 'This one made of knowledge, among the vital breaths' — because of the indicatory mark of the embodied self. And in the conclusion, 'This great, unborn Self, the one made of knowledge among the vital breaths' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) — because that [embodied self] is not abandoned. And in the middle too, because of the elaboration of the dream-state and other states of that same [embodied self]. Given this position, we say: This passage is directed toward the teaching of the supreme Lord, not merely toward describing the transmigrating self. Why? Because in deep sleep and at departure, the supreme Lord is designated as different from the body. In deep sleep: 'This person, embraced by the omniscient (<s>prājña</s>) Self, knows nothing external, nothing internal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.21) — here, the supreme Lord is designated as different from the embodied self. There, 'person' (<s>puruṣa</s>) would be the embodied self, since it is the knower — and since the denial [of knowing external and internal] is possible only when the possibility [of knowing] exists. '<s>Prājña</s>' would be the supreme Lord, since He is never separated from <s>prajñā</s> (knowledge) characterized by omniscience. Likewise, at departure too: 'This embodied self (<s>śārīra ātmā</s>), mounted upon by the omniscient (<s>prājña</s>) Self, departs groaning' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.35) — here too, the supreme Lord is designated as different from the <s>jīva</s>. There too, the embodied one (<s>śārīra</s>) would be the <s>jīva</s>, since it is the owner of the body. And '<s>prājña</s>' is that very supreme Lord. Therefore, because of the designation as different in deep sleep and at departure, it is understood that the supreme Lord is intended here. As for what was said — that because of the indicatory marks of the embodied self at the beginning, middle, and end, this passage concerns it — to this we say: In the opening, 'This one made of knowledge, among the vital breaths' — the nature of the transmigrating self is not what is intended; rather, having mentioned the transmigrating self, [the text] intends to declare its identity with the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Because the continuation of the subsequent text — 'He seems to think, seems to move' — and so forth is observed as being directed toward negating the qualities of the transmigrating being. Likewise in the conclusion too, [the text] concludes just as it began: 'This great, unborn Self, the one made of knowledge among the vital breaths.' The one who is seen as the transmigrant — 'this one made of knowledge among the vital breaths' — 'this great, unborn Self' is the supreme Lord, established by us: this is the meaning. As for those who, from the middle presentation of the dream-state and other states, think the transmigrating self's nature is intended — one who has been sent eastward would not arrive in the west. Because through the presentation of the dream-state and other states, [the text] does not intend to express the possession of states or the state of transmigration; rather, it intends [to express] the absence of states and the absence of transmigration. How is this understood?

children.text: 1 ānumānikādhikaraṇam / sū. 1-7
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Ānumānika Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of What Is Established by Inference). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-7.

children.text: ānumānikam apy ekeṣām iti cen na śarīra-rūpaka-vinyasta-gṛhīter darśayati ca | BBs_1,4.1 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ānumānikam apy ekeṣām iti cen na śarīra-rūpaka-vinyasta-gṛhīteḥ darśayati ca</s> — If it be said that even the entity established by inference [i.e., <s>Pradhāna</s>] is found [in the scripture] of some [recensions] — [we say] no, because [the term] is understood as placed in the metaphor of the body; and [scripture] also shows [this]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.1 |

children.text:
brahmajijñāsāṃ pratijñāya brahmaṇo lakṣaṇamuktam- 'janmādyasya yataḥ' (bra. 1.1.2) iti /
tallakṣaṇaṃ pradhānasyāpi samānamityāśaṅkya tadaśabdatvena nirākṛtam- 'īkṣaternāśabdam' (bra. 1.1.5) iti /
gatismānyaṃ ca vedāntavākyānāṃ brahmakāraṇavādaṃ prati vidyate na pradhānakāraṇavādaṃ pratīti prapañcitaṃ gatena granthena /
idaṃ tvidānīmavaśiṣṭamāśaṅkṣyate- yaduktaṃ pradhānasyāśabdatvaṃ tadasiddhaṃ, kāsucicchāsvāsu pradhānasamarpaṇābhāsānāṃ śabdanāṃ śrūyamāṇatvāt /
ataḥ pradhānasya kāraṇatvaṃ vedasiddhameva mahadbhiḥ paramarṣibhiḥ kapilaprabhṛtibhiḥ parigṛhītamiti prasajyate /
tadyāvatteṣāṃ śabdānāmanyaparatvaṃ na pratipādyate tāvatsarvajñaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇamiti pratipāditamapyākulībhavet /
atasteṣāmanyaparatvaṃ darśayituṃ paraḥ saṃdarbhaḥ pravartate /
ānumānikamapyanumānanirūpitamapi pradhānamekeṣāṃ śākhināṃ śabdavadupalabhyate /
kāṭhake hi paṭhyate- 'mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ' (1.3.11) iti /
tatra ya eva yannāmāno yatkramācca mahadavyaktapuruṣāḥ smṛtiprasiddhāsta eveha pratyabhijñāyante /
tatrāvyaktamiti smṛtiprasiddheḥ, śabdādihīnatvācca na vyaktamavyaktamiti vyutpattisaṃbhavāt, smṛtiprasiddhaṃ pradhānamabhidhīyate /
tasya śabdavattvādaśabdatvamanupapannam /
tadeva ca jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ śrutismṛtinyāyaprasiddhibhya iti cet /
children.translated_text:
Having announced the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>, the defining characteristic of <s>Brahman</s> was stated: 'That from which the origin and so forth of this [world proceed]' (<s>Bra</s>. 1.1.2). Having suspected that this defining characteristic applies equally to <s>Pradhāna</s>, it was refuted by its lacking scriptural basis: 'Because of seeing — not [<s>Pradhāna</s>]; it lacks scriptural basis' (<s>Bra</s>. 1.1.5). And that there is a consistent drift (<s>gati</s>) of the <s>Vedānta</s> passages toward the <s>Brahman</s>-causation doctrine, not toward the <s>Pradhāna</s>-causation doctrine — this was elaborated in the preceding text.
But now this remaining objection is raised: The stated scriptural baselessness of <s>Pradhāna</s> is not established, because in some scriptural recensions, words that appear to refer to <s>Pradhāna</s> are heard.
Hence it follows that the causality of <s>Pradhāna</s> — being established by the <s>Veda</s> itself — was accepted by great sages of the highest order, beginning with <s>Kapila</s>.
Until the other-directedness of those words is demonstrated, even what has been established — that the omniscient <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world — would become confused.
Therefore, to show the other-directedness of those words, the following discussion proceeds.
'That which is established by inference' — even what is determined by inference, <s>Pradhāna</s> — is found, as if supported by scripture, in [the text] of some recensions.
For in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> it is read: 'Higher than the <s>Mahat</s> is the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>); higher than the <s>Avyakta</s> is the <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.11).
There, <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Avyakta</s>, and <s>Puruṣa</s> — having the very same names, the very same sequence, and being well-known in <s>Sāṃkhya smṛti</s> — are recognized here [in the <s>śruti</s>].
There, the word '<s>avyakta</s>' — being well-known in <s>smṛti</s>, and because of the etymological possibility '<s>na vyaktam avyaktam</s>' (what is not manifest is <s>avyakta</s>), since it is devoid of sound and such — denotes <s>Pradhāna</s>, which is well-known in <s>smṛti</s>.
Since it has a scriptural basis, the claim of its scriptural baselessness is untenable.
And that [<s>Pradhāna</s>] alone is the cause of the world — from <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, reasoning, and common acceptance — if this is the position:

children.text:
naitadevam /
nahyetatkāṭakaṃ vākyaṃ smṛtinyāyaprasiddhayormahadavyaktayorastitvaparam /
nahyatra yādṛśaṃ smṛtiprasiddhaṃ svatantraṃ kāraṇaṃ triguṇaṃ pradhānaṃ tādṛśaṃ pratyabhijñāyate /
śabdamātraṃ hyatrāvyaktamitipratyabhijñāyate /
sa ca śabdo na vyaktamavyaktamiti yaugikatvādanyasminnapi sūkṣme sudurlakṣye ca prayujyate /
nacāyaṃ kasmiṃścidrūḍhaḥ /
yā tu pradhānavādināṃ rūḍhiḥ sā teṣāmeva pāribhāṣikī satī na vedārthanirūpaṇe kāraṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyate /
naca kramamātrasāmānyātsamānārthapratipattirbhavatyasati tadrūpapratyabhijñāne /
nahyaśvasthāne gāṃ paśyannaśvo 'yamityamūḍho 'dhyavasyati /
prakaraṇanirūpaṇāyāṃ cātra na paraparikalpitaṃ pradhānaṃ pratīyate /
śarīrarūpakavinyasgṛhīteḥ /
śarīraṃ hyatra ratharūpakavinyastamavyaktaśabdena parigṛhyate /
kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: prakaraṇātpariśeṣācca /
children.translated_text: Because of the context and the process of elimination.

children.text: tathāhyanantarātīto grantha ātmaśarīravādināṃ rathirathādirūpakakḷptiṃ darśayati- 'ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ rathameva tu /
children.translated_text: For the text immediately preceding shows the construction of a chariot-metaphor by those who speak of the Self and the body: 'Know the Self as the rider, and the body as the chariot.

children.text: buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca //
children.translated_text: Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.

This is not so.
For this <s>Kāṭhaka</s> passage is not devoted to establishing the existence of <s>Mahat</s> and <s>Avyakta</s> as they are well-known in <s>smṛti</s> and logic.
For here, the kind of independent, three-<s>guṇa</s> <s>Pradhāna</s> that is well-known in <s>smṛti</s> as the cause is not recognized.
Only the mere word '<s>avyakta</s>' is recognized here.
And that word — being etymological (<s>yaugika</s>), meaning '<s>na vyaktam</s>' (not manifest) — is used for anything that is subtle and hard to discern.
Nor is it a conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>) term fixed in any [particular] sense.
The conventional usage that the <s>Pradhāna</s> theorists have is their own technical usage, and being [merely] technical, it does not become authoritative in the determination of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>.
Nor does the mere similarity of sequential order lead to the apprehension of identical meaning, in the absence of the recognition of its [specific] form.
For no undeluded person, seeing a cow where a horse should be, would determine 'this is a horse.'
And when the context is examined, the <s>Pradhāna</s> conceived by others is not understood here.
'Because [the term] is understood as placed in the metaphor of the body' — for the body is here taken up with the word '<s>avyakta</s>,' being placed in the metaphor of a chariot.

children.text: indriyāṇi hayānāhurviṣayāṃsteṣu gocarān /
children.translated_text: The senses, they say, are the horses; the sense-objects are the paths.

children.text: ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: The wise call the Self, conjoined with the senses and mind, the experiencer.'

children.text:
' (kā. 1.3.3,4) iti /
taiścendriyādibhirasaṃyataiḥ saṃsāramadhigacchati /
saṃyataistvadhvanaḥ pāraṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padamāpnoti darśayitvā, kiṃ tadadhvanaḥ pāraṃ viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padamityasyāmākāṅkṣāyāṃ, tebhya eva prakṛtebhya indriyādibhyaḥ paratvena paramātmānamadhvanaḥ pāraṃ viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ darśayati- 'indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā arthebhyaśca paraṃ manaḥ /
manasastu parā buddhirbuddherātmā mahānparaḥ /
mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ /
puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ' (kā. 1.3.10,11) iti /
tatra ya evendriyādayaḥ pūrvasyāṃ ratharūpakakalpanāyāmaśvādibhāvena prakṛtāsta eveha parigṛhyante prakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriyāparihārāya /
tatrendriyamanobuddhayastāvatpūrvatreha ca samānaśabdā eva /
arthā ye śabdādayo viṣayā indriyahayagocaratvena nirdiṣṭāsteṣāṃ cendriyebhyaḥ paratvam /
'indriyāṇāṃ grahatvaṃ viṣayāṇāmatigrahatvam' (bṛ. 3.2) iti śrutiprasiddheḥ /
viṣayebhyaśca manasaḥ paratvaṃ, manomūlatvādviṣayendriyavyavahārasya /
manasastu parā buddhiḥ /
buddhiṃ hyāruhya bhogyajātaṃ bhoktāramupasarpati /
buddherātmā mahānparaḥ, yaḥ sa 'ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi' iti rathitvenopakṣiptaḥ /
kutaḥ /
ātmaśabdāt /
bhoktuśca bhogopakaraṇātparatvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: And because it is fitting that the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) is higher than the instruments of experience.

children.text: mahattvaṃ cāsya svāmitvādupapannam /
children.translated_text: And its greatness (<s>mahattva</s>) is fitting because of its being the master (<s>svāmin</s>).

children.text: athavā 'mano mahāntamatirbrahmā pūrbuddhiḥ khyatirīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: 'Mind, the great one, understanding, <s>Brahmā</s>, the original, intellect, discernment, the lord,

children.text: prajñā saṃviccitiścaiva smṛtiśca paripaṭhyate //
children.translated_text: wisdom, consciousness, and memory — [these] are listed [as names of the intellect].'

(<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.3-4). Having shown that with uncontrolled senses and such, one reaches <s>saṃsāra</s>, but with controlled ones, one attains the far shore of the journey — the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — and in the expectation 'What is this far shore of the journey, the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?' — [the text] shows, in ascending order from the very same sense-organs and such that were the subject of discussion, the supreme Self as the far shore of the journey, the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>: 'Higher than the senses are the sense-objects; higher than the sense-objects is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; higher than the intellect is the great Self (<s>mahān ātmā</s>); higher than the <s>Mahat</s> is the Unmanifest; higher than the Unmanifest is the <s>Puruṣa</s>; there is nothing higher than the <s>Puruṣa</s> — that is the culmination, that is the supreme goal' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.10-11).
There, the very sense-organs and such that were introduced as horses and such in the preceding chariot-metaphor are taken up here — to avoid abandoning the subject and introducing a new subject.
Therein, senses, mind, and intellect have the same words in both the earlier and the present [passage].
The sense-objects — sounds and such — which were designated as the paths of the horse-senses — their being higher than the senses [is stated].
Because of the scriptural well-known [principle]: 'The senses are graspers; the sense-objects are over-graspers' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2).
And the mind is higher than the sense-objects, because the operation of the sense-objects and senses is rooted in the mind.
And the intellect is higher than the mind.
For it is by mounting upon the intellect that the class of objects to be enjoyed approaches the experiencer.
'Higher than the intellect is the great Self' — this is the one who was introduced as the rider in 'Know the Self as the rider.'
Why?
Because of the word '<s>ātman</s>' (Self).

children.text:
' iti smṛteḥ, 'yo brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ yo vai vedāṃśca prahiṇoti tasmai' (śve. /
6.18) iti ca śruteryā prathamajasya hiraṇyagarbhasya buddhiḥ sā sarvāsāṃ buddhīnāṃ parā pratiṣṭhā /
seha mahānātmetyucyate /
sā ca pūrvatra buddhigrahaṇenaiva gṛhītā satī hirugīhopadiśyate /
tasyā apyasmādīyābhyo buddhibhyaḥ paratvopapatteḥ /
etasmiṃstu pakṣe paramātmaviṣayeṇaiva pareṇa puruṣagrahaṇena rathina ātmano grahaṇaṃ draṣṭavyam /
paramārthataḥ paramātmavijñānātmanorbhedābhāvāt /
tadevaṃ śarīramevaikaṃ pariśiṣyate /
itarāṇīndriyādīni prakṛtānyeva paramapadadidarśayiṣayā samanukrāmanpariśiṣyamāṇenehāntyenāvyaktaśabdena pariśiṣyamāṇaṃ prakṛtaṃ śarīraṃ darśayatīti gamyate /
children.translated_text:
Thus, from the <s>smṛti</s>; and from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Who first creates <s>Brahmā</s> and delivers the <s>Vedas</s> to him' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.18) — the intellect of the first-born <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the supreme foundation of all intellects.
That is here called the 'great Self' (<s>mahān ātmā</s>).
And it, already grasped by the earlier mention of 'intellect,' is taught separately [here].
Because its being higher than our [individual] intellects is fitting.
But in this interpretation, the mention of the Self as the rider should be understood as being grasped by the subsequent mention of '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — which refers to the supreme Self.
Because in ultimate reality, there is no difference between the supreme Self and the cognitive self (<s>vijñānātman</s>).
Thus, the body alone is left over [unaccounted for].
The other items — senses and such — being already introduced, and being enumerated in ascending order to show the supreme state — [the text], by the final remaining word '<s>avyakta</s>,' shows the body, which is what remains and was already introduced [in the chariot metaphor] — this is understood.

children.text: śarīrendriyamanobuddhiviṣayavedanāsaṃyuktasya hyavidyāvato bhoktuḥ śarīrādīnāṃ rathādirūpakakalpanayā saṃsāramokṣagatinirūpaṇena pratyagātmabrahmāvagatiriha vivakṣitā /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of making known the inner Self as <s>Brahman</s> is intended here — through the construction of the chariot-metaphor of the body and such, and through the delineation of the paths of <s>saṃsāra</s> and liberation — for the experiencer who, due to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), is conjoined with body, senses, mind, intellect, sense-objects, and feelings.

children.text: tathāca 'eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhātmā na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Thus: 'He, the Self hidden in all beings, does not shine forth.

children.text: dṛśyate tvagryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ' //
children.translated_text: But is seen by the sharp and subtle intellect of those who see the subtle.'

children.text: (kā. 1.3.12) iti vaiṣṇavasya paramapadasya duravagamatvamuktvā tadavagamārthaṃ yogaṃ darśayati- 'yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñastadyacchejjñāna ātmani /
children.translated_text: (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.12). Having stated the difficulty of realizing that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, [the text] shows the yoga for its realization: 'The wise one should restrain speech in the mind; that [mind] he should restrain in the knowing Self;

children.text: jñānamātmani mahati niyacchettadyacchecchānta ātmani' //
children.translated_text: Knowledge he should restrain in the great Self; and that he should restrain in the tranquil Self.'

children.text:
(kā. 1.3.13) iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- vācaṃ manasi saṃyacchet vāgādibāhyendriyavyāpāramutsṛjya manomātreṇāvatiṣṭheta /
mano 'pi viṣayavikalpābhimikhaṃ vikalpadoṣadarśanena jñānaśabdoditāyāṃ buddhāvadhyavasāyasvabhāvāyāṃ dhārayet /
children.translated_text: The mind too — which tends toward the differentiation of sense-objects — should be held, through seeing the defect of such differentiation, in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), which is of the nature of determination and is denoted by the word '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge).

children.text: tāmapi buddhiṃ mahatyātmani bhoktaryagryāyāṃ vā buddhau sūkṣmatāpādanena niyacchet /
children.translated_text: That intellect too should be restrained in the great Self — the experiencer — or [alternatively], by making [the intellect] subtle, in the most refined intellect.

children.text: mahāntaṃ tvātmānaṃ śānta ātmani prakaraṇavati parasminpuruṣe parasyāṃ kāṣṭhāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayediti ca /
children.translated_text: And the great Self should be established in the tranquil Self — the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the subject of the context, the supreme culmination.

children.text: tadevaṃ pūrvāparālocanāyāṃ nāstyatra paraparikalpitasya pradhānasyāvakāśaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, upon examining the preceding and subsequent [context], there is no room here for the <s>Pradhāna</s> conceived by others. // 1 //
(<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.13). What is stated here is this: One should restrain speech in the mind — giving up the operations of the external senses beginning with speech, one should abide in the mind alone.

children.text: FN: pradhānasya vaidikaśabdaśūnyatvena /
children.translated_text: Footnote: Because <s>Pradhāna</s> lacks any Vedic word [supporting it].

children.text: avaśiṣṭamanāśaṅkitamanirākṛtaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'What remains' — what is left over, not yet suspected, not yet refuted.

children.text: pratītyā pradhānārpakatve 'pi vastuto neti vaktumābhāsapadam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ābhāsa</s>' (semblance) — even if by [prima facie] understanding it seems to refer to <s>Pradhāna</s>, in reality it does not — hence the term '<s>ābhāsa</s>-word.'

children.text: apiśabdādekaśabdācca brahmāṅgīkāreṇa pūrvapakṣo vicāraścāyaṃ kvācitka iti sūcitam /
children.translated_text: From the word '<s>api</s>' (even) and the word '<s>ekeṣām</s>' (of some), it is indicated that with the acceptance of <s>Brahman</s> [as the referent], this prima facie objection and examination is only occasional.

children.text: smārtakramarūḍhibhyāmavyaktaśabdaḥ pradhānaparaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>avyakta</s>' refers to <s>Pradhāna</s> by virtue of <s>smṛti</s>-sequence, [<s>smṛti</s>-]form, and conventional usage.

children.text:
ajāmekāṃ ityādyā śrutiḥ /
'hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate' ityādyā smṛtiḥ /
'yadalpaṃ tajjaḍaprakṛtikaṃ' iti nyāyaḥ /
tato brahmaiva jagatkāraṇamiti matakṣatiriti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ajām ekām</s>' (the one unborn female) — this is the <s>śruti</s> [passage]. 'The cause is called <s>prakṛti</s>' — this is the <s>smṛti</s>. 'What is small [in knowledge] is of the nature of inert <s>prakṛti</s>' — this is the reasoning. Therefore, [the opponent argues,] the position that <s>Brahman</s> alone is the cause of the world would be undermined.

children.text:
rūpakakḷptiḥ sādṛśyakalpanā /
pragraho 'śvaraśanā /
teṣu hayeṣu /
gocarān mārgān /
ātmā dehaḥ /
gṛhṇanti puruṣapaśuṃ badhnātīti grahā indriyāṇi /
tebhyaḥ śreṣṭhā atigrahā viṣayāḥ /
paratvaṃ śraiṣṭhyābhiprāyaṃ natvāntaratveneti bhāvaḥ /
buddheḥ paraḥ pratyabhijñāyata iti śeṣaḥ /
hiruk pṛthak /
vedanā sukhādyanubhavaḥ /
vāgityatra dvitīyālopaśchāndasaḥ manasī iti dīrghaśca /
agryā samādhiparipākajā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Rūpakakalpti</s>' is the construction of a simile. '<s>Pragraha</s>' is the bridle. '<s>Teṣu</s>' — among those horses. '<s>Gocarān</s>' — paths. '<s>Ātmā</s>' — the body. '<s>Grahāḥ</s>' — the senses, because they grasp (<s>gṛhṇanti</s>) and bind the person-animal. '<s>Atigrahāḥ</s>' — the sense-objects, which are superior to those [senses]. '<s>Paratva</s>' is intended in the sense of superiority, not in the sense of [being] other — this is the purport. 'Higher than the intellect is [the great Self] that is recognized' — this is the completion. '<s>Hiruk</s>' means separately. '<s>Vedanā</s>' is the experience of pleasure and such. In '<s>vāg</s>' [should be read as] the accusative — this is a Vedic irregularity; and the long vowel in '<s>manasī</s>' [likewise]. '<s>Agryā</s>' — born of the maturation of <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ tu tadarhatvāt | BBs_1,4.2 |
children.translated_text: But [the <s>avyakta</s> refers to] the subtle [body] — because of its fitness [for that designation]. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.2 |

children.text:
uktametatprakaraṇaparīśeṣābhyāṃ śarīramavyaktaśabdaḥ na pradhānamiti /
idamidānīmāśaṅkyate- kathamavyaktaśabdārhatvaṃ śarīrasya, yāvatā sthūlatvātspṛṣṭataramidaṃ śarīraṃ vyaktaśabdārhamaspaṣṭavacanastvavyaktaśabda iti /
ata uttaramucyate- sūkṣmaṃ tviha kāraṇātmanā śarīraṃ vivakṣyate sūkṣmasyāvyaktaśabdārhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Hence the answer: The body is intended here in its causal aspect — as subtle — because what is subtle is fit for the word '<s>avyakta</s>.'

children.text: yadyapi sthūlamidaṃ śarīraṃ na svayamavyaktaśabdamarhati, tathāpi tasya tvārambhakaṃ bhūtasūkṣmamavyaktaśabdamarhati /
children.translated_text: Although this gross body itself does not deserve the word '<s>avyakta</s>,' still, the subtle element (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>) that is its originator does deserve the word '<s>avyakta</s>.'

children.text: prakṛtiśabdaśca vikāre dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>prakṛti</s>' (source/nature) is seen [to be used] for a modification [as well].

children.text: yathā 'gobhiḥ śrīṇīta matsaram' (ṛ.sa. 9.46.4) iti śrutiśca- 'tadbhedaṃ tarhyavyākṛtamāsīt' (bṛ. 1.4.7) itīdameva vyākṛtanāmarūpavibhinnaṃ jagatprāgavasthāyāṃ parityaktavyākṛtanāmarūpaṃ bījaśaktyavasthamavyaktaśabdayogaṃ darśayati // 2 //
children.translated_text: As in [the Vedic passage]: 'One should mix <s>soma</s> with milk' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 9.46.4). And the <s>śruti</s> — 'That was then in an undifferentiated state' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.7) — shows this very world, which is now differentiated by manifest names and forms, as having been in its prior state — having abandoned manifest names and forms, in the state of seed-potency, deserving the designation 'unmanifest.' // 2 //

It was stated that, based on the context and the process of elimination, the word '<s>avyakta</s>' refers to the body, not to <s>Pradhāna</s>. Now this objection is raised: How is the body fit for the word '<s>avyakta</s>' (unmanifest), since, being gross, this body is more palpably manifest and deserves the word '<s>vyakta</s>' (manifest), whereas the word '<s>avyakta</s>' means what is unclear?

children.text: FN: prakṛtervikārāṇāmananyatvātprakṛteravyaktatvaṃ vikāre upacaryate /
children.translated_text: Footnote: Because the modifications are not different from their material cause, the unmanifestness of the material cause is figuratively applied to the modification.

children.text: gobhirgovikāraiḥ payobhiḥ matsaraṃ somaṃ śrīṇīta miśritaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: 'With cows' — with products of cows, i.e., with milk. '<s>Matsara</s>' — <s>soma</s>. '<s>Śrīṇīta</s>' — one should mix.

children.text: tat ha kila tarhi prāgavasthāyāmidaṃ jagadavyākṛtaṃ avyaktamāsīt /
children.translated_text: '<s>Tat</s>' — that. '<s>Tarhi</s>' — then. In its prior state, this world was '<s>avyākṛtam</s>' — unmanifest.

children.text: tadadhīnatvād arthavat | BBs_1,4.3 |
children.translated_text: <s>Tadadhīnatvād arthavat</s> — Because of being dependent on That, it is meaningful. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.3 |

children.text:
atrāha- yadi jagadidamanabhivyaktanāmarūpaṃ bījātmakaṃ prāgavasthamavyaktaśabdārhamabhyupagamyeta, tadātmanā ca śarīrasyāpyavyaktaśabdārhatvaṃ pratijñāyeta, sa eva tarhi pradhānakāraṇavāda evaṃ satyāpadyeta /
asyaiva jagataḥ prāgavasthāyāḥ pradhānatvenābhyupagamāditi /
children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised: If this world, with its unmanifest names and forms, in the state of seed, in its prior condition, deserving the designation 'unmanifest,' were accepted — and if the body too were accepted as deserving the designation 'unmanifest' by virtue of having that as its nature — then the very doctrine of <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause would be arrived at, in such a case. Because the prior state of this very world is accepted as the <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: atrocyate- yadi vayaṃ svatantrāṃ kāñcitprāgavasthāṃ jagataḥ kāraṇatvenābhyupagacchema, prasañjyema tadā pradhānakāraṇavādam /
children.translated_text: To this it is said: If we were to accept some independent prior state of the world as the cause, then we would indeed be open to the <s>Pradhāna</s>-as-cause doctrine.

children.text:
parameśvarādhīnā tviyamasmābhiḥ prāgavasthā jagato 'bhyupagamyate na svatantrā /
sā cāvaśyābhyupagantavyā /
arathavatī hi sā /
nahi tayā vinā parameśvarasya sraṣṭṛtvaṃ siddhayati /
śaktirahitasya tasya pravṛttyanupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: But this prior state of the world that we accept is dependent on the supreme Lord, not independent. And it must necessarily be accepted. For it is meaningful. Without it, the creatorship of the supreme Lord cannot be established. Because, if He were devoid of potency, His activity would be untenable.

children.text:
muktānāṃ ca punaranutpattiḥ /
kutaḥ /
vidyayā tasyā bījaśakterdāhāt /
avidyātmikā hi bījaśaktiravyaktaśabdanirdeśyā parameśvarāśrayā māyāmayī mahāsuptiḥ, yasyāṃ svarūpapratibodharahitāḥ śerate saṃsāriṇo jīvāḥ /
tadetadavyaktaṃ kvacidākāśaśabdanirdiṣṭam- 'etasminnu khalvakṣare gārgyākāśa otaśca protaśca' (bṛ. 3.8.11) iti śruteḥ /
kvacidakṣaraśabdoditam- 'akṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' (mu. 2.1.2) iti śruteḥ /
kvacinmāyeti sūcitam- 'māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyānmāyinaṃ tu maheśvaram' (śve. 4.10) iti mantravarṇāt /
avyaktā hi sā māyā, tattvānyatvanirūpaṇasyāśakyatvāt /
tadidaṃ 'mahataḥ paramavyaktam' ityuktamavyaktaprabhavatvānmahataḥ, yadā hairaṇyagarbhī buddhirmahān /
yadā tu jīvo mahāṃstadāpyavyaktādhīnatvājjīvabhāvasya mahataḥ paramavyaktamityuktam /
avidyā hyavyaktam /
avidyāvattvenaiva jīvasya sarvaḥ saṃvyavahāraḥ saṃtato vartate /
mahataḥ paratvamabhedopacārāttadvikāre śarīre parikalpyate /
satyapi śarīravadindriyādīnāṃ tadvikāratvāviśeṣe śarīrasyaivābhedopacārādavyaktaśabdena grahaṇaṃ, indriyādīnāṃ svaśabdaireva gṛhītatvātpariśiṣṭatvācca śarīrasya /
children.translated_text: And those who are liberated are not reborn. Why? Because, through knowledge, that seed-potency is burned away. For the seed-potency — which is of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is to be designated by the word 'unmanifest,' which abides in the supreme Lord, which is of the nature of <s>māyā</s>, a great sleep — in which the transmigrating <s>jīvas</s>, devoid of the awakening of their true nature, lie sleeping. This 'unmanifest' is sometimes designated by the word '<s>ākāśa</s>': 'In this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the space is woven warp and weft' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11). Sometimes it is expressed by the word '<s>akṣara</s>' (imperishable): 'Higher than the high, beyond the <s>Akṣara</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2).
