Sometimes it is indicated as '<s>māyā</s>': 'Know <s>Māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the wielder of <s>Māyā</s> to be the great Lord' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.10). For that <s>māyā</s> is unmanifest, because it is impossible to determine it as either identical with or different from [<s>Brahman</s>]. This is what is meant by 'higher than the great is the unmanifest' — because the 'great' (<s>mahat</s>) arises from the unmanifest. When the 'great' is the intellect belonging to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — [the unmanifest is higher than that]. But when the 'great' is the <s>jīva</s> — even then, because the <s>jīva</s>'s state depends on the unmanifest, it is said that the unmanifest is higher than the great. For the 'unmanifest' is <s>avidyā</s>. It is only insofar as the <s>jīva</s> possesses <s>avidyā</s> that all its conventional transactions continue unbroken. The 'higher-than-the-great' status is figuratively attributed to the body, which is a modification of that [<s>avidyā</s>], because of [the scripture's] figurative identification [of the body with the unmanifest]. Even though the sense-organs and such are equally modifications [of <s>avidyā</s>], just like the body, the body alone is grasped by the word 'unmanifest' through figurative identification — because the sense-organs and such have already been grasped by their own terms, and the body remains as what is left over.

children.text:
anye tu varṇayanti- dvividhaṃ hi śarīraṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca /
sthūlaṃ yadidamupalabhyate /
sūkṣmaṃ yaduttaratra vakṣyate- 'tadantarapratipattau raṃhati saṃpariṣvaktaḥ praśnanirūpaṇābhyām' (bṛ. 3.1.1) iti /
taccobhayamapi śarīramaviśeṣātpūrvatra rathatvena saṃkīrtitam /
iha tu sūkṣmamavyaktaśabdena parigṛhyate /
sūkṣmasyāvyaktaśabdārhatvāt /
tadadhīnatvācca bandhamokṣavyavahārasya jīvāttasya paratvam /
yathārthādhīnatvādindriyavyāpārasyendriyebhyaḥ paratvamarthānāmiti /
taistvetadvaktavyaṃ, aviśeṣeṇa śarīradvayasya pūrvatra rathatvena saṃkīrtitatvātsamānayoḥ prakṛtapariśiṣṭatvayoḥ kathaṃ sūkṣmameva śarīramiha gṛhyate na punaḥ sthūlamapīti /
āmnātasyārthaṃ pratipattuṃ prabhavāmo nāmnātaṃ paryanuyoktum /
āmnātaṃ cāvyaktapadaṃ sūkṣmameva pratipādayituṃ śaknoti netaradvyaktatvāttasyeti cet /
children.translated_text: But others explain: the body is of two kinds — gross and subtle. The gross is this one that is perceived. The subtle is what will be described later: 'In the passage to another [body], it departs, enveloped, as is understood from questioning and explanation' (<s>BBs</s> 3.1.1). And both kinds of body are mentioned earlier as 'the chariot,' without distinction. But here, the subtle body is grasped by the word 'unmanifest.' Because the subtle is deserving of the designation 'unmanifest.' And because the transactions of bondage and liberation depend on it, the <s>jīva</s>'s being 'higher than' it [follows]. Just as, because the activity of the sense-organs depends on the objects, the objects are 'higher than' the senses. But those [commentators] should say this: since both kinds of body were mentioned earlier as 'the chariot' without distinction — of the two [bodies] that are equally the subject under discussion and equally the remainder [to be dealt with] — how is it that only the subtle body is grasped here and not also the gross? [If they say:] We have the capacity to understand the meaning of what has been recited, not to interrogate what has been recited. And the recited word 'unmanifest' is capable of conveying only the subtle, not the other [gross body], because of the latter's manifest nature — [we say:]

children.text:
na /
ekavākyatādhīnatvādarthapratipatteḥ /
nahīme pūrvottare āmnāte ekavākyatāmanāpadya kañcidarthaṃ pratipādayataḥ, parakṛtahānāprakṛtaprakriyāprasaṅgāt /
nacākāṅkṣāmantareṇaikavākyatāpratipattirasti /
tatrāvaśiṣṭāyāṃ śarīradvayasya grāhyatvākāṅkṣāyāṃ yathākāṅkṣaṃ saṃbandhe 'nabhyupagamyamāna ekavākyataiva bādhitā bhavati kuta āmnātasyārthapratipattiḥ /
nacaivaṃ mantavyaṃ duḥśodhatvātsūkṣmasyaiva śarīrasyeha grahaṇaṃ, sthūlasya tu dṛṣṭabībhatsatayā suśodhatvādagrahaṇamiti /
yato naiveha śodhanaṃ kasyacidvivakṣyate /
nahyatra śodhanavidhāyi kiñcidākhyātamasti /
children.translated_text: For there is no injunctive verb here that enjoins purification.

children.text: anantaranirdiṣṭatvāttu kiṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padamitīdamiha vivakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Rather, because of the immediately subsequent statement, what is intended here is: 'What is that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?'

children.text: tathāhīdamasmātparamidamasmātparamityuktvā 'puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcit' ityāha /
children.translated_text: For having said 'this is higher than this, this is higher than this,' [the text] says: 'There is nothing higher than the <s>Puruṣa</s>.'

children.text: sarvathāpi tvānumānikanirakaraṇopapattestathā nāmāstu, na naḥ kiñcicchidyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: In any case, however — since the refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> inference is successful — let it be as you say; nothing of ours is compromised. // 3 //

No. Because the understanding of meaning depends on the unity of the sentence. For these prior and subsequent recited [passages] cannot convey any meaning without forming a single sentence — because [otherwise] there would be the absurd consequence of abandoning the connected and introducing the unconnected. And without mutual expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), the understanding of a single sentence does not arise. And when the expectancy of grasping both kinds of body remains — if the connection as per the expectancy is not accepted — the very unity of the sentence would be contradicted, so how could there be understanding of the meaning of the recited [text]? Nor should one think: because the subtle body is difficult to purify [i.e., to transcend], it alone is grasped here; but the gross body, because of the disgust observed toward it being easy to purify, is not grasped. For indeed, no purification of anything whatsoever is intended here.

children.text: FN: tarhi tadā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Tarhi</s>' — then.

children.text: māyāmayī prasiddhamāyopamitā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Māyāmayī</s>' — comparable to well-known <s>māyā</s> (illusion).

children.text: buddhyādyupādhibhedājjīvā iti bahūktiḥ /
children.translated_text: The plural 'the <s>jīvas</s>' is because of their multiplicity through differences in the limiting adjuncts of intellect and such.

children.text: anavacchinnatvādākāśatvaṃ, tattvajñānaṃ vinānivṛtterakṣaratvaṃ, vicitrakāryatvānmāyātvamiti bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is called '<s>ākāśa</s>' because of its unlimitedness; '<s>akṣara</s>' because it does not cease without the knowledge of truth; '<s>māyā</s>' because of producing manifold effects — this is the distinction.

children.text: tat avyaktam /
children.translated_text: That is the 'unmanifest.'

children.text: gobalīvardapadavadetaddraṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: This should be understood like the usage of '<s>go</s>' for both a cow and a bull.

children.text: ekārthabodhakānāṃ śabdānāṃ mitha ākāṅkṣyaikasyāṃ buddhāvarūḍhatvamekavākyatā /
children.translated_text: The unity of the sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) is when words conveying a single meaning mutually expect each other and come together in one cognition.

children.text: grāhyatvākāṅkṣā ekavākyatā /
children.translated_text: The expectancy of grasping [both bodies] is [the basis for] the unity of the sentence.

children.text: dṛṣṭā bībhatsā ghṛṇā yasmin tasya bhāvastattā tayetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dṛṣṭabībhatsatā</s>' — the state of having observed disgust — this is the meaning.

children.text: sarvathā sthūlasūkṣmayoranyataragrahe 'pīti yāvat /
children.translated_text: 'In any case' — meaning: even if only one of the two, gross or subtle, is grasped.

children.text: jñeyatvāvacanāc ca | BBs_1,4.4 |
children.translated_text: <s>Jñeyatvāvacanāc ca</s> — And because of the absence of a statement of knowability. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.4 |

children.text:
jñeyatvena ca sāṃkhyaiḥ pradhānaṃ smaryate guṇapuruṣāntarajñānātkaivalyamitivadbhiḥ /
nahi guṇasvarūpamajñātvā guṇebhyaḥ puruṣasyāntaraṃ śakyaṃ jñātumiti /
kvacicca vibhūtiviśeṣaprāptaye pradhānaṃ jñeyamiti smaranti /
nacedagihāvyaktaṃ jñeyatvenocyate /
padamātraṃ hyavyaktaśabdaḥ /
nehāvyaktaṃ jñātavyamupāsitavyaṃ ceti vākyamasti /
children.translated_text: There is no statement here such as 'the unmanifest is to be known' or 'is to be meditated upon.'

children.text: nacānupadiṣṭapadārthajñānaṃ puruṣārthamiti śakyaṃ pratipattum /
children.translated_text: And the knowledge of an object that has not been taught [by scripture] cannot be understood as serving human purpose.

children.text: tasmādapi nāvyaktaśabdena pradhānamabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore too, the word 'unmanifest' does not denote <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: asmākaṃ tu ratharūpakakḷptaśarīrādyanusaraṇena viṣṇoreva paramaṃ padaṃ darśayitumayamupanyāsa ityanavadyam // 4 //
children.translated_text: But for us, this passage — tracing the body and such that have been figuratively fashioned as the chariot — serves to reveal the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — and this is irreproachable. // 4 //

And the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, who hold that liberation comes from the knowledge of the difference between the <s>guṇas</s> and the <s>Puruṣa</s>, remember <s>Pradhāna</s> as something to be known. For without knowing the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>, the difference of the <s>Puruṣa</s> from the <s>guṇas</s> cannot be known. And in some contexts, they remember <s>Pradhāna</s> as to be known for the attainment of a particular divine power. But the 'unmanifest' here is not stated as something to be known. For the word 'unmanifest' is merely a term [in the passage].

children.text: vadatīti cen na prājño hi prakaraṇāt | BBs_1,4.5 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vadatīti cen na prājño hi prakaraṇāt</s> — If [it be said that the scripture] does state [its knowability] — [we say] no, because the context concerns the <s>Prājña</s> (the knowing one, i.e., the supreme Self). | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.5 |

children.text: atrāha sāṃkhyaḥ - jñeyatvāvacanāt ityasiddham /
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> objects: The [argument from the] absence of a statement of knowability is not established.

children.text: katham /
children.translated_text: How so?

children.text: śrūyate hyuttaratrāvyaktaśabdoditasya pradhānasya jñeyatvavacanam- 'aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityamagandhavacca yat /
children.translated_text: For further on, the knowability of <s>Pradhāna</s>, denoted by the word 'unmanifest,' is heard to be stated: 'That which is without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable — likewise without taste, eternal, without smell,

children.text: anādyanantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya taṃ mṛtyumukhātpramucyate' //
children.translated_text: without beginning and without end, higher than the great, constant — by discerning That, one is released from the mouth of death.'

children.text:
(kā. 2.3.15) iti /
atra hi yādṛśaṃ śabdādihīnaṃ pradhānaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ smṛtau nirūpitaṃ tādṛśameva nicāyyatvena nirdiṣṭaṃ, tasmātpradhānamevedaṃ, tadeva cāvyaktaśabdanirdiṣṭamiti /
children.translated_text: (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.3.15). For here, the <s>Pradhāna</s> — devoid of sound and such, higher than the great — as described in <s>Sāṃkhya Smṛti</s>, is stated as precisely that which is to be discerned. Therefore, this is <s>Pradhāna</s> itself, and it is this that is designated by the word 'unmanifest.'

children.text:
atra brūmaḥ - neha pradhānaṃ nicāyyatvena nirdiṣṭam /
prājño hīha paramātmā nicāyyatveta nirdiṣṭaṃ iti gamyate /
kutaḥ /
prakaraṇāt /
prājñasya hi prakaraṇaṃ vitataṃ vartate /
'puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ' ityādinirdeśāt, 'eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhotmā na prakāśate' iti ca durjñātatvavacanena tasyaiva jñeyatvākāṅkṣaṇāt /
'yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñaḥ' iti ca tajjñānāyaiva vāgādisaṃyamasya vihitatvāt /
mṛtyumukhapramokṣaṇaphalatvācca /
nahi pradhānamātraṃ nicāyya mṛtyumukhātpramucyata iti sāṃkhyairiṣyate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> do not hold that one is released from the mouth of death merely by discerning <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: cetanātmavijñānāddhi mṛtyumukhātpramucyate iti teṣāmabhyupagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Rather, their position is that one is released from the mouth of death through the knowledge of the conscious Self.

children.text: sarveṣu vedānteṣu prājñasyaivātmano 'śabdādidharmatvamabhilapyate /
children.translated_text: In all <s>Vedānta</s> texts, the quality of being without sound and such is predicated only of the <s>Prājña</s> Self.

children.text: tasmānna pradhānasyātra jñeyatvamavyaktaśabdanirdiṣṭatvaṃ vā // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the knowability and the designation by the word 'unmanifest' do not belong to <s>Pradhāna</s> here. // 5 //

To this we say: <s>Pradhāna</s> is not stated here as to be discerned. Rather, it is understood that the <s>Prājña</s> — the supreme Self — is stated here as to be discerned. Why? Because of the context. For the context of the <s>Prājña</s> extends throughout — from the statement: 'There is nothing higher than the <s>Puruṣa</s>; that is the ultimate, that is the supreme goal.' And because of the statement of being hard to know — 'This Self, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth' — there is the expectation of its knowability. And in 'Let the wise one restrain speech and mind' — the restraint of speech and such is enjoined for the very purpose of knowing That. And because the fruit is release from the mouth of death.

children.text: FN: aśabdamityādiṣu pratyekaṃ nityaśabdaḥ saṃbadhyate /
children.translated_text: Footnote: In 'without sound' and such, the word 'eternal' (<s>nitya</s>) is to be connected with each [attribute individually].

children.text: trayāṇām eva caivam upanyāsaḥ praśnaś ca | BBs_1,4.6 |
children.translated_text: <s>Trayāṇām eva caivam upanyāsaḥ praśnaś ca</s> — And in this [text], the presentation and the question pertain to only three [subjects]. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.6 |

children.text:
itaśca na pradhānasyāvyaktaśabdavācyatvaṃ jñeyatvaṃ vā /
yasmāntrayāṇāmeva padārthānmagnijīvaparamātmanāmasmingranthe kaṭhavallīṣu varapradhānasāmarthyādvaktavyatopanyāso dṛśyate /
tadviṣaya eva ca praśnaḥ /
nāto 'nyasya praśna upanyāso vāsti /
children.translated_text: There is no question or presentation pertaining to anything else.

children.text: tatra tāvat 'sa tvamagniṃ svargyamadhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi taṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam' (kā. 1.1.13) ityagniviṣayaḥ praśnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, first the question about fire: 'You know the fire that leads to heaven, O Death — tell me that; I am full of faith, tell me' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.1.13).

children.text: 'yeyaṃ prete' vicikitsā manuṣye 'stītyeke nāyamastīti caike /
children.translated_text: 'This doubt that exists regarding a man who has died — "he exists," say some; "he does not exist," say others —

children.text: etadvidyāmanuśiṣṭastvayāhaṃ varāṇāmeṣa varastṛtīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: I wish to know this, instructed by you. This is the third of the boons.'

For this further reason too, the designation by the word 'unmanifest' and the knowability do not belong to <s>Pradhāna</s>. Because in this text — the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> — by the power of the boon-context, the presentation of only three subjects — fire, the individual soul, and the supreme Self — is seen to require being discussed. And the questions too pertain to those very [three subjects].

children.text: ' (kā. 1.1.20) iti jīvaviṣayaḥ praśnaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.1.20) — this is the question about the individual soul.

children.text: 'anyatra dharmādantrādharmānyatrāsmatkṛtākṛtāt /
children.translated_text: 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>; other than this done and undone;

children.text: anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca yattatpaśyasi tadvada //
children.translated_text: other than what has been and what will be — what you see, tell me that.'

children.text:
' (kā. 1.2.14) iti paramātmaviṣayaḥ /
prativacanamapi 'lokādimamagniṃ tamuvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakāyāvatīrvā yathā vā' (kā. 1.1.15) ityagniviṣayam /
'hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam /
yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama /
yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ /
sthāṇumanye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam' (kā. 2.5.6,7) iti /
vyavahitaṃ jīvaviṣayam /
'na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit' (kā. 1.2.18) ityādibahuprapañcaṃ paramātmaviṣayam /
naivaṃ pradhānaviṣayaḥ praśno 'sti /
apṛṣṭatvāccānupanyasanīyatvaṃ tasyeti /
children.translated_text: (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.14) — this is the question about the supreme Self. The answer too: 'He taught him the fire that is the beginning of the world, what the bricks are, how many, and how' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.1.15) — pertains to fire. 'Come, I shall tell you this secret, the eternal <s>Brahman</s>, and what happens to the Self after encountering death, O <s>Gautama</s>. Some enter a womb for embodiment; others go to a stationary form — according to their <s>karma</s>, according to their knowledge' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.5.6-7) — this, though separated [from the question], pertains to the individual soul. 'He is not born, nor does he die — the wise one' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.18) and so forth — with extensive elaboration — pertains to the supreme Self. But there is no question pertaining to <s>Pradhāna</s>. And because [<s>Pradhāna</s>] was not asked about, it need not be presented.

children.text:
atrāha- yo 'yamātmaviṣayaḥ praśno yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye 'stīti, kiṃ sa evāyam 'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmāt' iti punaranukṛṣyate, kiṃvā tato 'nyo 'yamapūrvaḥ praśna utthāpyata iti /
kicātaḥ /
sa evāyaṃ praśnaḥ punaranukṛṣyata iti yadyucyeta, dvayorātmaviṣayayoḥ praśnayorekatāpatteragniviṣaya ātmaviṣayaśca dvāveva praśnāvityato na vaktavyaṃ trayāṇāṃ praśnopanyāsāviti /
athānyo 'yamapūrvaḥ praśnaḥ utthāpyata ityucyeta tato yathaiva varapradānavyatirekeṇa praśnakalpanāyāmadoṣa evaṃ praśna vyatirekeṇāpi pradhānopanyāsakalpanāyāmadoṣaḥ syāditi /
children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised: This question about the Self — 'This doubt regarding a man who has died, "he exists"' — is it the same [question] that is reiterated with 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>' — or is this a different, new question being raised? What follows from this? If it is said that this is the same question being reiterated — then since two questions about the Self would be reduced to one, there would be only two questions — about fire and about the Self — and therefore one should not say 'the presentation and question pertain to three.' But if it is said that this is a different, new question being raised — then just as there is no fault in imagining a question beyond what was granted as boons, so too there would be no fault in imagining a presentation of <s>Pradhāna</s> beyond the questions.

children.text:
atrocyate- naivaṃ vayamiha varapradānavyatirekeṇa praśnaṃ kañcitkalpayāmo vākyopakramasāmarthyāt /
varapradānopakramā hi mṛtyunaciketaḥsaṃvādarūpā vākyapravṛttirāsamāpteḥ kaṭhavallīnāṃ lakṣyate /
mṛtyuḥ kila nāciketase pitrā prahitāya trīnvarānpradadau /
naciketāḥ kila teṣāṃ prathamena vareṇa saumanasyaṃ vavre /
dvitīyenāgnividyām, tṛtīyenātmavidyām, 'yeyaṃ prete' iti 'varāṇāmeva varastṛtīyaḥ' (kā. 1.1.20) iti liṅgāt /
tatra yadyanyatra dharmādityanyo 'yamapūrvaḥ praśna utthāpyeta tato varapradānavyatirekeṇāpi praśnakalpanādvākyaṃ bādhyetha /
children.translated_text: To this we say: we do not here imagine any question apart from the granting of boons, because of the force of the passage's opening. For the discourse — in the form of a dialogue between <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) and <s>Naciketas</s> — which opens with the granting of boons, is seen to continue to the end of the <s>Kaṭha Vallīs</s>. <s>Mṛtyu</s> granted three boons to <s>Naciketas</s>, who had been sent forth by his father [to the realm of Death]. <s>Naciketas</s>, with the first of those boons, chose his father's goodwill; with the second, the knowledge of the fire[-altar] (<s>Agnividyā</s>); and with the third, the knowledge of the Self (<s>Ātmavidyā</s>) — as indicated by: 'concerning this doubt about one who has died' and 'It is the third of the three boons' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.1.20). Now, if a new, unprecedented question — distinct from '<s>dharma</s> and such' — were raised elsewhere, then by imagining a question apart from the granting of boons, the passage would be contradicted.

children.text:
nanu praṣṭhavyabhedādapūrvo 'yaṃ praśno bhavitumarhati /
pūrvo hi praśno jīvaviṣayaḥ /
yoyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye 'sti nāstīti vicikitsābhidhānāt /
jīvaśca dharmādigocaratvānnānyatra dharmāditi praśnamarhati /
prājñastu dharmādyatītatvādanyatra anyatra dharmāditi praśnamarhati /
praśnacchāyā ca na samānā lakṣyate /
pūrvasyāstitvanāstitvaviṣayatvāduttarasya dharmādyatītavastuviṣayatvāt /
tasmātpratyabhijñānābhāvātpraśnabhedaḥ /
na pūrvasyaivottaratrānukarṣaṇamiti cet /
na /
jīvaprājñayorekatvābhyupagamāt /
bhavetpraṣṭavyabhedātpraśnabhedo yadyanyo jīvaḥ prājñātsyāt /
na tvanyatvamasti /
tattvamasītyādiśrutyantarebhyaḥ /
iha cānyatra dharmādityasya praśnasya prativacanaṃ 'na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit' iti janmamaraṇapratiṣedhena pratipādyamānaṃ śārīraparameśvarayorabhedaṃ darśayati /
sati hi prasaṅge pratiṣedho bhāgī bhavati /
children.translated_text: For a negation is meaningful only when there is a ground for the [erroneous] attribution.

children.text: prasaṅgaśca janmamaraṇayoḥ śarīrasaṃsparśācchārīrasya bhavati na parameśvarasya /
children.translated_text: And the ground for the [attribution of] birth and death belongs to the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>), through its connection with the body — not to the Supreme Lord.

children.text: tathā- 'svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati /
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'The wise one, having known the great, all-pervading Self,

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati //
children.translated_text: by whom one sees both the end of dream and the end of waking — does not grieve.' //

But because of a difference in what is being asked, this could be a new question. For the earlier question concerns the <s>jīva</s> — since it says: 'There is this doubt about a person who has died — [some say] it exists, [others say] it does not exist.' And the <s>jīva</s>, being within the sphere of <s>dharma</s> and such, cannot be the subject of the question 'that which is beyond <s>dharma</s>.' But the Omniscient (<s>Prājña</s>, i.e., <s>Brahman</s>), being beyond <s>dharma</s> and such, can be the subject of the question 'that which is beyond <s>dharma</s> and such.' And the tenor of the two questions does not appear to be the same — the former being about existence and non-existence, the latter about a reality beyond <s>dharma</s> and such. Therefore, because of the absence of recognition [of the same subject], there is a difference of questions; the former is not simply continued in the latter — if this be said, No. Because the identity of the <s>jīva</s> and the Omniscient is accepted. There would be a difference of questions due to a difference in what is asked, if the <s>jīva</s> were different from the Omniscient. But there is no such difference — from scriptures like 'You are That.' And here, the reply to this question 'that which is beyond <s>dharma</s>' — 'He is not born, nor does He die' — shows, by the negation of birth and death, the non-difference of the embodied self from the Supreme Lord.

children.text:
(kā. 2.4.4) iti svapnajāgaritadṛśo jīvasyaiva mahattvavibhutvaviśeṣaṇasya mananena śokavicchedaṃ darśayanna prājñādanyo jīva iti darśayati /
prājñavijñānāddhi śokaviccheda iti vedāntasiddhāntaḥ /
tathāgre- 'yadeveha tadamutra yadamutra tadanviha /
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati /
children.translated_text: He who sees as if there is diversity here goes from death to death.' //

children.text: ' (kā.2.4.10) iti jīvaprājñabhedadṛṣṭimapavadati /
children.translated_text: (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.4.10) — [the text] refutes the view that there is a difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Omniscient.

children.text: tathā jīvavīṣayasyāstitvanāstitvapraśnasyānantaram 'anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva' ityārabhya mṛtyunā taistaiḥ kāmaiḥ pralobhyamāno 'pi naciketā yadā na cacāla, tadainaṃ mṛtyurabhyudayanīḥśreyasavibhāgapradarśanena vidyāvidyāvibhāgapradarśanena ca 'vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo 'lolupanta' (kā.1.2.4) iti praśasya praśnamapi tadīyaṃ praśaṃsanyaduvāca- 'taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍhamanupraviṣṭhaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam /
children.translated_text: Similarly, after the question concerning the existence or non-existence of the <s>jīva</s>, when <s>Mṛtyu</s>, beginning with 'Choose another boon, O <s>Naciketas</s>,' tried to tempt <s>Naciketas</s> with various desires and <s>Naciketas</s> did not waver — then <s>Mṛtyu</s>, having praised <s>Naciketas</s> by showing the distinction between worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), and by showing the distinction between <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — 'I consider <s>Naciketas</s> to be one who desires knowledge; the many desires did not make you waver' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.4) — also praised his question with the praiseworthy [words]: 'Hard to see, hidden, entered into the cave, situated in the depth, primordial —

children.text: adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti //
children.translated_text: knowing the God through the attainment of <s>Adhyātma-Yoga</s> (meditation on the inner Self), the wise one abandons joy and sorrow.' //

(<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.4.4) — by showing that cessation of grief comes from the contemplation (<s>manana</s>) of the <s>jīva</s> — the seer of dream and waking — who is qualified by greatness and all-pervasiveness, [the text] shows that the <s>jīva</s> is not other than the Omniscient. For cessation of grief comes from the knowledge of the Omniscient — this is the established doctrine of <s>Vedānta</s>. Similarly, further on: 'What is here, that is there; what is there, that is here.',

children.text:
' (kā.1.2.12) iti, tenāpi jīvaprājñayorabheda eveha vivakṣata iti gamyate /
yatpraśnanimittāṃ ca praśaṃsāṃ mahatīṃ mṛtyoḥ pratyapadyata naciketā yadi taṃ vihāya praśaṃsānantaramanyameva praśnamupakṣipedasthāna eva sā sarvā praśaṃsā prasāritā syāt /
tasmāt 'yeyaṃ prete' ityasyaiva praśnasyaitadanukarṣaṇam 'anyatra dharmāt' iti /
yattu praśnacchāyāvailakṣaṇyamuktaṃ tadadūṣaṇam /
tadīyasyaiva viśeṣasya punaḥ pṛcchyamānatvāt /
pūrvatra hi dehādivyatiriktasyātmano 'stitvaṃ pṛṣṭamuttaratra tu tasyaivāsaṃsāritvaṃ pṛcchyata iti yāvaddhyavidyā na nivartate tāvaddharmādigocaratvaṃ jīvasya jīvatvaṃ ca na nivartate /
tannivṛttau tu prājña eva tattvamasīti śrutyā pratyāyyate /
nacāvidyāvattve tadapagame ca vastunaḥ kaścidviśeṣo 'sti /
yathā kaścitsaṃtamase patitāṃ kāñcidrajjumahiṃ manyamāno bhīto vepamānaḥ palāyate, taṃ cāparo brūyānmā bhaṣīrnāyamahī rajjureveti /
sa ca tadupaśrutyāhikṛtaṃ bhayamutsṛjedvepathuṃ palāyanaṃ ca /
natvahibuddhikāle tadapagamakāle ca vastunaḥ kaścidviśeṣaḥ syāt /
tathaivaitadapi draṣṭavyam /
tataśca 'na jāyate mriyate vā' ityevamādyapi bhavatyastitvapraśnasya prativacanam /
sūtraṃ tvavidyākalpitajīvaprājñabhedāpekṣayā yojayitavyam /
ekatve 'pi hyātmaviṣayasya praśnasya prāyaṇāvasthāyāṃ dehavyatiriktāstitvamātravicikitsānātkartṛtvādisaṃsārasvabhāvānapohanācca pūrvasya paryāyasya jīvaviṣayatvamutprekṣyate /
children.translated_text: For even though the question about the Self is one, because of the doubt in the state of departure [from the body] concerning mere existence apart from the body, and because of not [yet] removing the <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature characterized by agency and such — the former turn of the question is imagined to concern the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: uttarasya tu dharmādyatyayasaṃkīrtanātprājñaviṣayatvamiti /
children.translated_text: But the latter [is imagined to concern] the Omniscient, because of the proclamation of going beyond <s>dharma</s> and such.

children.text: tataśca yuktāgnijīvaparamātmakalpanā /
children.translated_text: And therefore, the interpretation in terms of fire, <s>jīva</s>, and Supreme Self is justified.

children.text: pradhānakalpanāyāṃ tu na varapradānaṃ na praśno na prativacanamiti vaiṣamyam // 6 //
children.translated_text: But in the interpretation as <s>Pradhāna</s>, neither the granting of boons, nor the question, nor the reply would fit — this is the discrepancy. // 6 //

(<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.12) — from this too it is understood that the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the Omniscient is what is intended here. And if, having received from <s>Mṛtyu</s> the great praise occasioned by the question, <s>Naciketas</s> were to set that [question] aside and, right after the praise, introduce a completely different question — then all that praise would have been expended in vain. Therefore, 'that which is beyond <s>dharma</s>' is a continuation of this very question 'concerning this doubt about one who has died.' As for the objection that the tenor of the questions is different — that is not a defect. Because a specific aspect of the same [subject] is being asked about again. For in the former [question], the existence of the Self as distinct from the body and such was asked about; in the latter, the non-<s>saṃsārin</s> nature of that very [Self] is being asked about. For as long as <s>avidyā</s> does not cease, so long the <s>jīva</s>'s being within the sphere of <s>dharma</s> and such, and its state of being a <s>jīva</s>, do not cease. But upon the cessation of that [<s>avidyā</s>], it is made known through scripture as the Omniscient itself — 'You are That.' And there is no real difference in the entity whether in the state of <s>avidyā</s> or upon its removal. Just as someone, thinking a certain rope fallen in darkness to be a snake, runs away frightened and trembling; and another tells him: 'Don't be afraid — this is not a snake, it's only a rope.' And he, hearing that, abandons the fear and trembling caused by the [imagined] snake. But there is no real difference in the object between the time of the snake-cognition and the time of its removal. Just so should this be understood too. And therefore, 'He is not born, nor does He die' and such is also a reply to the question about existence. The <s>sūtra</s>, however, is to be construed with reference to the <s>avidyā</s>-imagined difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Omniscient.

children.text:
FN: mṛtyunā naciketasaṃprati trīnvarānavṛṇīṣvetyuktestrayāṇāmeva praśno naciketasā kṛtaḥ /
upanyāsaśca mṛtyunā kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: Because <s>Mṛtyu</s> told <s>Naciketas</s> 'Choose three boons,' the question was posed by <s>Naciketas</s> for only three [boons]. And the introduction was made by <s>Mṛtyu</s>.

children.text: he mṛtyo, sa mahyaṃ dattavarastvaṃ svargahetumagnimadhyeṣi smarasi /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Mṛtyu</s>, you remember the fire that is the means to heaven — that boon was given to me by you.'

children.text:
prete mṛte /
dehādanyo 'sti naveti saṃśayo.'sti ata etadātmatattvamasaṃdigdhaṃ jānīyāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prete</s>' means 'when one has died.' The doubt is: does anything other than the body exist or not? The meaning is: I wish to know this reality of the Self without doubt.

children.text: śrutamupanyāsam /
children.translated_text: 'Having heard' — the introduction.

children.text: varapradhānamupakramo yasyāḥ sā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Varapradhāna</s>' — that whose opening is the [granting of] boons.

children.text: prahitāya yamalokaṃ prati preṣitāya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prahitāya</s>' — 'having been sent forth' — toward the realm of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: gocaratvādaśrayatvāt /
children.translated_text: '<s>Gocaratvāt</s>' — because of being within [its] sphere.

children.text: bhāgī yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāgī</s>' means 'appropriate, justified.'

children.text:
anto 'vasthā /
yena sākṣiṇā pramātā paśyati tamātmānamiti saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anta</s>' means 'state.' The connection is: '[the Self] by which — the witness — the cognizer sees; [know] that Self.'

children.text: iha dehe yaccaitanyaṃ tadevāmutra sūryādau /
children.translated_text: 'Here' — the consciousness that is in the body is the same as 'there' — in the sun and such.

children.text: yasmin praśno yatpraśnastaṃ vihāyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: having set aside the question about which the question was posed.

children.text: viśeṣoktisamāptāvitiśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>iti</s>' occurs at the completion of the specification.

children.text: mahadvac ca | BBs_1,4.7 |
children.translated_text: Like [the word] '<s>Mahat</s>' (Great). | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.7 |

children.text:
yathā mahacchabdaḥ sāṃkhyaiḥ sattāmātre 'pi prathamaje prayukte na tameva vaidike 'pi prayoge 'bhidhatte /
'buddherātmā mahānparaḥ' (kā. 1.3.10), 'mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānam' (kā. 1.2.22) 'vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam' (śve. 3.8)
children.translated_text: Just as the word '<s>Mahat</s>' is used by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> for the first-born [modification] in mere existence (<s>sattāmātra</s>), [that word in] Vedic usage does not denote that same [<s>Sāṃkhya</s> category]. [This is known] from reasons such as the use of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) [in conjunction]: 'The <s>Mahat</s> Self is beyond the <s>Buddhi</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.3.10); 'The great, all-pervading Self' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.22); 'I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.8) —

children.text: ityevamādāvātmaśabdaprayogādibhyo hetubhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: — and such [passages where <s>Mahat</s> is used] together with the word '<s>Ātman</s>' and other reasons.

children.text: tathāvyaktaśabdo 'pi na vaidike prayoge pradhānamabhidhātumarhati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the word '<s>Avyakta</s>' (Unmanifest) too, in Vedic usage, does not deserve to denote <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: ataśca nāsyānumānikasya śabdavattvam // 7 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, this inferred [<s>Pradhāna</s>] does not have the status of being supported by scripture. // 7 //

children.text: 2 camasādhikaraṇam / sū. 8-10
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Camasa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Cup) / <s>Sūtras</s> 8-10

children.text: camasavadaviśeṣāt | BBs_1,4.8 |
children.translated_text: Like the cup, because of non-specificity. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.8 |

children.text:
punarapi pradhānavādyaśabdatvaṃ pradhānasyāsiddhamityāha /
kasmāt /
mantravarṇāt- 'ajāmekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ sṛjamānāṃ sarūpāḥ /
ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogāmajo 'nyaḥ' (śve. 4.5) iti /
atra hi mantre lohitaśuklakṛṣṇaśabdai rajaḥsattvatamāṃsyabhidhīyante /
lohitaṃ rajo rañjanātmakatvāt /
śuklaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśātmakatvāt /
kṛṣṇaṃ tama āvaraṇātkatvāt /
teṣāṃ sāmyāvasthāvayavadharmairvyapadiśyate lohitaśuklakṛṣṇamiti /
na jāyata iti cājā syāt, 'mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtiḥ' ityabhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: Yet again, it is said that the status of having scriptural support for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine of <s>Pradhāna</s> is not established. Why? From the <s>mantra</s> text: 'The unborn one (<s>ajā</s>), the single one, red, white, and black, producing many offspring of the same form — the one unborn male (<s>aja</s>) lies with her, delighting [in her]; the other unborn male abandons her, whose pleasures have been enjoyed' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.5). For in this <s>mantra</s>, the words red, white, and black denote <s>Rajas</s>, <s>Sattva</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> [respectively]. Red is <s>Rajas</s>, because of its nature as coloring [i.e., passion]. White is <s>Sattva</s>, because of its nature as illumination. Black is <s>Tamas</s>, because of its nature as concealment. Their state of equilibrium is designated by the properties of their components: red, white, and black. And '<s>Ajā</s>' means 'she who is not born,' because of the acceptance [by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>] that 'the root <s>Prakṛti</s> is not a modification.'

children.text:
nanvajāśabdaśchāgāyāṃ rūḍhaḥ /
bāḍham /
sā tu rūḍhiriha nāśrayituṃ śakyā, vidyāprakaraṇāt /
sā ca vahnīḥ prajāstraiguṇyānvitā janayati /
tāṃ prakṛtimaja ekaḥ puruṣo juṣamāṇaḥ prīyamāṇaḥ sevamāno vānuśete /
tāmevāvidyāyātmatvenopagamya sukhī duḥkhī mūḍho 'hamityavivekatayā saṃsarati /
anyaḥ punarajaḥ puruṣe utpannavivekajñāno virakto jahātyenāṃ prakṛtiṃ bhuktabhogāṃ kṛtabhogāpavargāṃ parityajati /
mucyata ityarthaḥ /
tasmācchrutimūlaiva pradhānādikalpanāmiti /
children.translated_text: But the word '<s>ajā</s>' is conventionally established as meaning 'she-goat.' Granted. But that conventional meaning cannot be adopted here, because of the context of a <s>vidyā</s> (meditation). And she, [the unborn one], generates many offspring endowed with the three <s>guṇas</s>. The one unborn (<s>aja</s>) <s>Puruṣa</s>, delighting in her, taking pleasure in her, or attending upon her, lies alongside [her]. Having accepted that <s>Prakṛti</s> as himself through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [thinking] 'I am happy, I am miserable, I am deluded' — without discrimination, he transmigrates. But the other unborn (<s>aja</s>) <s>Puruṣa</s>, in whom discriminative knowledge has arisen, being dispassionate, abandons her — [this] <s>Prakṛti</s> whose pleasures have been enjoyed — relinquishes her upon the completion of experience. He is liberated — this is the meaning. Therefore, the conception of <s>Pradhāna</s> and such is indeed rooted in <s>śruti</s> — [so says the opponent].

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - nānena mantreṇa śrutimattva sāṃkhyavādasya śakyamāśrayitum /
nahyayaṃ mantraḥ svātantryeṇa kañcidapi vādaṃ samarthayitumutsahate /
sarvatrāpi yayā kayācitkalpanayājātvādisaṃpādanopapatteḥ /
sāṃkhyavāda evehābhipreta iti viśeṣāvadhāraṇakāraṇābhāvāt /
camasavat /
yathāhi arvāgbalaścamasa ūrdhvabudhnaḥ (bṛ. 2.2.3) ityasminamantre svātantryeṇāyaṃ nāmāsau camaso 'bhipreta iti na śakyate nirūpayitum /
children.translated_text: For just as in the <s>mantra</s> 'A cup with its opening downward and its bottom upward' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.2.3), it cannot be independently determined that this particular cup is intended,

children.text: sarvatrāpi yathākathañcidarvāgbilatvādikalpanopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: because on any interpretation whatsoever, the attribution of having its opening downward and such can be accomplished,

children.text: evamihāpyaviśeṣo 'jāmekāmityasya mantrasya /
children.translated_text: so here too, the <s>mantra</s> 'The unborn one, the single one' is similarly non-specific.

children.text: nāsminmantre pradhānamevājābhipreteti śakyate niyantum // 8 //
children.translated_text: It cannot be determined that only <s>Pradhāna</s> is meant by '<s>ajā</s>' in this <s>mantra</s>. // 8 //

This being the position reached, we say: the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine cannot claim scriptural support through this <s>mantra</s>. For this <s>mantra</s> is not capable of establishing any doctrine independently. Because on any interpretation whatsoever, the attribution of 'unborn-ness' and such can be accomplished. Because there is no ground for specifically determining that the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine alone is intended here. [This is] like the cup.

children.text:
tatra tu 'idaṃ tacchira eṣa hyarvāgbilaścamasa ūrdhvabudhnaḥ' iti vākyaśeṣāccamasaviśeṣapratipattirbhavati /
iha punaḥ keyamajā pratipattavyeti /
atra brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: There [in the cup passage], from the remainder of the sentence — 'This is that head; for this is the cup with its opening downward and its bottom upward' — the determination of the particular cup comes about. But here, which '<s>ajā</s>' is to be understood? To this we say —

children.text:
FN: ajāmekāṃ- na jāyata ityajā tāṃ mulaprakṛtiṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ rajaḥsatvamoguṇāṃ sarūpāstriguṇātmikāḥ prajā janayantīṃ eko 'jo jīvastāṃ śabdādiviṣayarūpatāpannāṃ juṣamāṇaḥ sannanuśete nirantaraṃ muhyati /
jīvena bhukto bhogo yasyāṃ yasyā vā tāṃ jīvena bhujyamānāmanyaḥ paramātmā jahāti nāsyāmāsaktiṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Ajāmekāṃ</s>' — she who is not born is <s>ajā</s>; that root <s>Prakṛti</s>, red, white, and black, [i.e.,] with the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Rajas</s>, <s>Sattva</s>, and <s>Tamas</s>; '<s>sarūpāḥ</s>' — the offspring of three-<s>guṇa</s> nature that she generates. One unborn (<s>aja</s>) <s>jīva</s>, delighting in her who has assumed the form of sense-objects like sound and such, lies alongside [her] — continuously is deluded. The other — the Supreme Self — abandons her, whose pleasures have been enjoyed by the <s>jīva</s>, or her who is being enjoyed by the <s>jīva</s> — does not form attachment to her.

children.text: avayavāḥ pradhānasya raja ādayasteṣāṃ dharmā rañjakatvādayastaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The components of <s>Pradhāna</s> are <s>Rajas</s> and such; their properties are coloring [passion] and such; 'by those' [is the designation].

children.text:
prajāyanta iti prajā mahadādayaḥ /
traiguṇyaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prajāḥ</s>' — those that are born — are <s>Mahat</s> and such. '<s>Traiguṇya</s>' means pleasure, pain, and delusion.

children.text: atrātmatvaṃ tādātmyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ātmatva</s>' here means identity.

children.text:
śabdādyupalabdhirbhogaḥ /
guṇapuruṣānyatādhīrapavṛjyate 'nenetyapavargaḥ /
children.translated_text: The experience of sound and such is enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>). Discriminative knowledge of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and the <s>Puruṣa</s> is cessation (<s>apavarga</s>).

children.text: jyotirupakramā tu tathā hy adhīyata eke | BBs_1,4.9 |
children.translated_text: But [the passage] beginning with light [refers to <s>Brahman</s>], for thus some recite. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.9 |

children.text:
parameśvarādutpannā jyotiḥpramukhā tejobannalakṣaṇā caturvidhasya bhūtagrāmasya prakṛtibhūteyamajā pratipattavyā /
tuśabdo 'vadhāṇārthaḥ /
bhūtatrayalakṣaṇaiveyamajā vijñeyā na guṇatrayalakṣaṇā /
kasmāt /
tathāhyeke śākhinastejobannānāṃ parameśvarādutpattimāmnāya teṣāmeva rohitādirūpatāmāmananti- 'yadagre rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejastadrūpaṃ yacchukraṃ tadapāṃ yatkṛṣṇaṃ tadannasya' iti /
tānyeveha tejobannāni pratyabhijñāyante rohitādiśabdasāmānyāt /
rohitādīnāṃ ca śabdānāṃ rūpaviśeṣeṣu mukhyatvādbhāktatvācca guṇaviṣayatvasya /
asaṃdigdhena ca saṃdigdhasya nigamanaṃ nyāyyaṃ manyante /
tathehāpi 'brahmavādino vadanti /
kiṅkāraṇaṃ brahma' (śve. 1.1) ityupakramya 'te dyānayogānugatā apaśyandevātmaśaktiṃ svaguṇairnigūḍhām' (śve.
children.translated_text: This <s>ajā</s> (the unborn [she-goat]) — born from the supreme Lord, characterized by the group of luminous [fire], [water], and food, being the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the fourfold class of beings beginning with the luminous [fire] — should be understood as the triad of fire, water, and food. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) is for emphasis. This <s>ajā</s> should be understood as characterized by the three elements — fire, water, and food — not as characterized by the three <s>guṇas</s> [of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>]. Why? Because thus certain <s>śākhins</s> (followers of [Vedic] branches), having taught the origination of fire, water, and food from the supreme Lord, teach the red and other colors as belonging to those very [elements]: 'The red color that was at first is the color of fire; the white is that of water; the black is that of food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.4.1). Those very fire, water, and food are recognized here [in the <s>ajā</s> mantra] because of the commonality of the words 'red' and the like. And because the words 'red' and the like are primary [i.e., literal] with respect to specific colors, while the attribution to <s>guṇas</s> [of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>] would be secondary [figurative]. And [the logicians] consider it proper to determine the doubtful by means of the undoubted. Similarly here too, having introduced [the topic] with '<s>Brahmavādins</s> say: What is the cause? Is it <s>Brahman</s>?' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 1.1), [the text says:] 'They, absorbed in meditation-yoga, perceived the self-power of the Lord, hidden by its own qualities' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s>

children.text: 1.3) iti pārameśvaryāḥ śakteḥ samastajagadvidhāyinyā vākyopakrame 'vagamāt /
children.translated_text: 1.3) — because at the beginning of the passage, the power of the Lord, which ordains the entire universe, is apprehended.

children.text: vākyaśeṣe 'pi 'māyāṃ tu prakṛti vidyānmāyinaṃ tu maheśvaram' iti 'yo yoniṃ yonimadhitiṣṭhatyekaḥ' (śve. 4.10,11) iti ca tasyā evāvagamānna svatantrā kācitprakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ nāmajāmantreṇāmnāyata iti śakyate vaktum /
children.translated_text: And in the remainder of the passage too — 'Know <s>māyā</s> as <s>prakṛti</s>, and the wielder of <s>māyā</s> as the great Lord' and 'He who presides over every <s>yoni</s> (source), the One' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.10, 11) — because of the apprehension of that very [power of the Lord], it cannot be said that some independent <s>prakṛti</s> called '<s>pradhāna</s>' is taught by the <s>ajā</s> mantra.

children.text: prakaraṇāttu saiva daivī śaktiravyākṛtanāmarūpā nāmarūpayoḥ prāgavasthānenāpi mantreṇāmnāyata ityucyate /
children.translated_text: Rather, from the context, it is said that the very same divine power, [which is] the unmanifest name-and-form — the prior state of name and form — is taught by this mantra as well.

children.text: tasyāśca svavikāraviṣayeṇa trairūpyeṇa trairūpyamuktam // 9 //
children.translated_text: And the three-colored nature of that [<s>ajā</s>] is explained by the three colors pertaining to its own modifications. // 9 //

children.text:
kathaṃ punastejobannātmanā trairūpyeṇa trirūpājā pratipattuṃ śakyate /
yāvatā na tāvattejobanneṣvajākṛtirasti /
naca tejobannānāṃ jātiśravaṇādajātinimitto 'pyajāśabdaḥ saṃbhavatīti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: But how can the <s>ajā</s> be understood as three-colored with the three colors of fire, water, and food? For fire, water, and food do not have the form of an <s>ajā</s> (she-goat). Nor can the word '<s>ajā</s>' be based on the birth (<s>jāti</s>) of fire, water, and food — since fire, water, and food are [themselves] born. To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the reply:

children.text:
FN: śākhinaśchandogāḥ /
te brahmavādino 'nayā rītyā vimṛśya dyānayogenānugatāḥ paramātmānamanu praviṣṭāḥ /
avidyāśaktiryoniḥ sā ca pratijīvaṃ nānetyuktamato vīpsopapannā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Śākhinaḥ</s>' means the <s>Chāndogyas</s> (followers of the <s>Chāndogya</s> branch). Those <s>Brahmavādins</s>, having deliberated in this manner, absorbed in meditation-yoga — [they] entered into the supreme Self. The power of <s>avidyā</s> is the <s>yoni</s> (source), and since it is different for each <s>jīva</s>, repetition [of the word '<s>yoni</s>'] is justified.

children.text: kalpanopadeśāc ca madhvādivadavirodhaḥ | BBs_1,4.10 |
children.translated_text: <s>Kalpanopadeśāc ca madhvādivadavirodhaḥ</s> — And because of the teaching being figurative, there is no contradiction, as with honey and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.10 |

children.text:
nāyamajākṛtinimitto 'jāśabdaḥ /
nāpi yaugikaḥ /
kiṃ tarhi kalpanopadeśo 'yam /
ajārūpakakḷptistejobannalakṣaṇāyāścarācarayonerupadiśyate /
yathāhi loke yadṛcchayā kācidajā rohitaśuklakṛṣṇaṇavarṇā syādbahubarkarā sarūpabarkarā ca tāṃ ca kaścidajo juṣamāṇo 'nuśayīta, kaściccaināṃ bhuktabhogāṃ juhyāt, evamiyamapi tejobannalakṣaṇā bhūtaprakṛtistrivarṇā bahu sarūpaṃ carācaralakṣaṇaṃ vikārajātaṃ janayati aviduṣā ca kṣetrajñenopabhujyate viduṣā ta parityajata iti /
nacedamāśaṅkitavyamekaḥ kṣetrajño 'nuśete 'nyo jahātītyataḥ kṣetrajñabhedaḥ pāramārthikaḥ pareṣāmiṣṭaḥ prāpnotīti /
nahīyaṃ kṣetrajñabhedapratipipādayiṣā kintu bandhamokṣavyavasthāpratipipādayiṣā tveṣā /
prasiddhaṃ tu bhedamanudya bandhamokṣavyavasthā pratipādyate /
bhedastūpādhinimitto mithyājñānakalpito na pāramārthikaḥ /
'eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā' ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'One God, hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.11) and the like.

children.text: madhvādivat /
children.translated_text: As with honey and the like.

children.text: yathā 'ādityasyāmadhuno madhutvam' (chā. 3.1), 'vācāścādhenordhenutvam (bṛ. 5.8), 'dyulokādīnāṃ cānagnīnāmagnitvam' (bṛ. 8.2.9) ityevañjātīyakaṃ kalpyate, evamidamanajāyā ajātvaṃ kalpyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as 'the honey-hood of the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.1), 'the cow-hood of speech' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.8), and 'the fire-hood of the sky-world and others that are not fires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 8.2.9) — such figurative identifications are made, so too the she-goat-hood of the non-she-goat is figuratively attributed — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādavirodhastejobanneṣvajāśabdaprayogasya // 10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no contradiction in the use of the word '<s>ajā</s>' for fire, water, and food. // 10 //

This word '<s>ajā</s>' is not based on the she-goat form. Nor is it etymological [i.e., meaning 'unborn']. What then? This is a figurative teaching. A figurative identification with the form of a she-goat (<s>ajā</s>) is taught for the source of the moving and non-moving [creation], which is characterized by fire, water, and food. Just as in the world, some she-goat might happen to be red, white, and black in color, bearing many kids of similar color, and some he-goat, enjoying her, would lie beside her, while another would abandon her after having enjoyed her — so too this elemental <s>prakṛti</s> characterized by fire, water, and food, being three-colored, produces a multifold progeny of similar form consisting of the moving and non-moving [creation], and is enjoyed by the ignorant <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower, i.e., individual soul), while the wise one abandons her. And one should not suspect that [the objection] 'one <s>kṣetrajña</s> enjoys while another abandons — therefore a real plurality of <s>kṣetrajñas</s>, accepted by the opponents, follows.' For this is not intended to establish a plurality of <s>kṣetrajñas</s>; rather, this is intended to establish the distinction between bondage and liberation. The distinction between bondage and liberation is taught by presupposing the well-known [empirical] plurality. But the plurality is caused by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), imagined through false knowledge — not ultimately real.

children.text:
FN: bahubarkarā bahuśāvā /
barkaro bālapaśuḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Bahubarkarā</s>' means having many kids. '<s>Barkara</s>' is a young animal.

children.text: 3 sāṃkhyopasaṃgrahādikaraṇam / sū. 11-13
children.translated_text: Section 3: <s>Sāṃkhyopasaṃgrahādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 11-13

children.text: na saṃkhyopasaṃgrahādapi nānābhāvād atirekāc ca | BBs_1,4.11 |
children.translated_text: <s>Na saṃkhyopasaṃgrahādapi nānābhāvādatirekācca</s> — Not even from the inclusion of the [Sāṃkhya] number, because of the diversity [of the entities counted], and because of the excess. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.11 |

children.text:
evaṃ parigṛhīte 'pyajāmantre punaranyasmānmantrātsāṃkhyaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhate /
'yasminpañca pañcajanā ākāśaśca pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
tameva manya ātmānaṃ vidvānbrahmāmṛto 'mṛtam' (bṛ. 4.4.17) iti /
asminmantre pañca pañcajanā iti pañcasaṃkhyāviṣayāparā pañcasaṃkhyā śrūyate pañcadvayaśabdadarśanāt /
ta ete pañcapañcakāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ saṃpadyante /
tathā pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā yāvantaḥ saṃkhyeyā ākāṅkṣyantelatāvantyeva ca tattvāni sāṃkhyaiḥ saṃkhyāyante- 'mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtirmahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta /
ṣoḍaśakaśca vikāro na prakṛtirna vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ' (sāṃkhyakā. 3) iti /
tayā śrutiprasiddhayā pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā teṣāṃ smṛtiprasiddhānāṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvānāmupasaṃgrahātprāptaṃ punaḥ śrutimattvameva pradhānādīnām /
tato brūmaḥ - na saṃkhyopasaṃgrahādapi pradhānādīnāṃ śrutimattvaṃ pratyāśā kartavyā /
kasmāt /
nānābhāvāt /
nānā hyetāni pañcaviṃśatistattvāni /
naiṣāṃ pañcaśaḥ pañcaśaḥ sādhāraṇo dharmo 'sti, yena pañcaviṃśaterantarāle parāḥ pañca pañcasaṃkhyā niveśeran /
children.translated_text: Even though the <s>ajā</s> mantra has been thus explained, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [proponent] takes his stand again on the basis of another mantra: 'In whom the five groups of five and space are established — Him alone I consider as the Self; the wise one, <s>Brahman</s>, the immortal [knowing] the immortal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.17). In this mantra, [with the words] 'five groups of five' (<s>pañca pañcajanāḥ</s>), another number of five is heard as qualifying [the first] five, because two words for 'five' are seen. These five fives amount to twenty-five. And those twenty-five entities enumerated by the number twenty-five are exactly as many as the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> count as their <s>tattvas</s>: '<s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> is unmodified; the seven beginning with <s>mahat</s> are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and modifications; the group of sixteen is modification [alone]; <s>puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor modification' (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 3). Since those twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, well known from <s>smṛti</s>, are included in the twenty-five number well known from <s>śruti</s>, the <s>pradhāna</s> and the rest would again obtain scriptural authority. To this we say: Not even from the inclusion of the number should one expect scriptural authority for the <s>pradhāna</s> and the rest. Why? Because of the diversity. For these twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> are diverse. They do not have a common property in groups of five by which an additional five, [as] a second group of five, could be accommodated within the twenty-five.

children.text:
nahyekanibandhanamantareṇa nānābhūteṣu dvitvādikāḥ saṃkhyā niviśante /
athocyeta pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyaiveyamavayavadvāreṇa lakṣyate, yathā 'pañca sapta ca varṣāṇi na vavarṣa śatakratuḥ' iti dvādaśavārṣikīmanāvṛṣṭiṃ kathayanti tadvaditi /
tadapi nopapadyate /
ayamevāsminpakṣe doṣo yallakṣaṇāśrayaṇīyā syāt /
children.translated_text: For without a single common basis, numbers such as 'two' and the like do not apply to diverse entities. And if it be said that this is simply the number twenty-five indicated through its component parts — just as they describe a twelve-year drought by saying 'five and seven years <s>Śatakratu</s> did not rain' — even that does not hold. The very same fault applies to this alternative — namely, that a figurative expression would have to be resorted to.

children.text:
paraścātra pañcaśabdo janaśabdena samastaḥ pañcajanā iti, pāribhāṣikeṇa svareṇaikapadatvaniścayāt /
prayogāntare ca 'pañcānāṃ tvā pañcajanānām' (tai. 1.6.2.2) ityaikapadyaikasvaryaikavibhaktikatvāvagamāt /
samastasya na vīpsā pañca pañceti /
naca pacakadvayagrahaṇaṃ pañca pañceti /
naca pañcasaṃkhyāyā ekasyāḥ pañcasaṃkhyayā parayā viśeṣaṇaṃ pañca pañcakā iti /
upasarjanasya viśeṣaṇenāsaṃyogāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the second word 'five' here is compounded with the word '<s>jana</s>' (people) to form '<s>pañcajanāḥ</s>' — because of the certainty that it is a single word, from the conventional accent. And from the usage elsewhere — 'Of the five groups of five peoples' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2.2) — the understanding of single-word-hood, single-accent, and single-case-ending is confirmed. A compound word does not undergo repetition as '<s>pañca pañca</s>.' Nor is it the grasping of two groups of five, '<s>pañca pañca</s>.' Nor is it one number five being qualified by another number five as 'five fives.' Because a subordinate element does not combine with a qualifier [in this way].

children.text:
nanvāpannapañcasaṃkhyakā janā eva punaḥ pañcasaṃkhyayā viśeṣyamāṇāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ pratyeṣyante /
yathā pañca pañcapūlya iti pañcavaṃśatipūlāḥ pratīyante tadvat /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the peoples who have already acquired the number five are further qualified by another number five — and thus twenty-five would be understood. Just as 'five groups of five bundles' yields twenty-five bundles.

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ /
yuktaṃ yatpañcapūlīśabdasya samāhārābhiprāyatvātkatīti satyāṃ bhedākāṅkṣāyāṃ pañca pañcapūlya iti viśeṣaṇam /
iha tu pañca pañca janā ityādita eva bhedopādānātkatītyasatyāṃ bhedākāṅkṣāyāṃ na pañca pañcajanā iti viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavet /
bhavadapīdaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ pañcasaṃkhyāyā eva bhavet, tatra cokto doṣaḥ /
tasmātpañca pañcajanā iti na pañcaviṃśatitattvābhiprāyam /
atirekācca na pañcaviṃśatitattvābhiprāyam /
atirekācca na pañcaviṃśatitattvābhiprāyam /
atireko hi bhavatyātmākāśābhyāṃ pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyāyāḥ /
ātmā tāvadiha pratiṣṭhāṃ pratyādhāratvena nirdiṣṭaḥ /
yasminniti saptamisūcitasya ''tameva manya ātmānam' ityātmatvenānukarṣaṇāt /
ātmā ca cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ /
sa ca pañcaviṃśatāvantargata eveti na tasyaivādhāratvamādheyatvaṃ ca yujyate /
arthāntaraparigrahe ca tattvasaṃkhyātirekaḥ siddhāntaviruddhaḥ prasajyeta /
tathā 'ākāśaśca pratiṣṭhitaḥ' ityākāśasyāpi pañcaviṃśatavantargatasya na pṛthagupādānaṃ nyāyyam /
arthāntaraparigrahe coktaṃ dūṣaṇam /
kathaṃ ca saṃkhyāmātraśravaṇe satyaśrutānāṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvānāmupasaṃgrahaḥ pratīyate /
janaśabdasya tatveṣvarūḍhatvāt /
arthāntaropasaṃgrahe 'pi saṃkhyopapatteḥ /
kathaṃ tarhi pañca pañcajanā iti /

ucyate- 'diksaṃkhye saṃjñāyām' (pā. sū. 2.1.50) iti viśeṣaṇasmaraṇātsaṃjñāyāmeva pañcaśabdasya janaśabdena samāsaḥ tataśca rūḍhatvābhiprāyeṇaiva kecitpañcajanā nāma vivakṣyante na sāṃkhyatattvābhiprāyeṇa /
children.translated_text: It is said: Because of the <s>Pāṇinian sūtra</s> 'Numbers and directions [are compounded with nouns] in the sense of a proper name' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 2.1.50) — remembering that the qualifier [applies] only in the sense of a proper name — the compounding of the word 'five' with the word '<s>jana</s>' is only in the sense of a proper name. Therefore, with the intention of conventional usage, certain [entities] called '<s>pañcajanas</s>' are intended — not with the intention of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> <s>tattvas</s>.

children.text: te katītyasyāmākāṅkṣāyāṃ punaḥ pañceti prayujyate /
children.translated_text: When the question arises 'how many are they?' — the word 'five' is used again.

children.text: pañcajanā nāma ye kecitte ca pañcaivetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: whatever [entities] are called '<s>pañcajanas</s>' — they are indeed five.

children.text: saptarṣayaḥ sapteti yathā // 11 //
children.translated_text: Just as [one says] 'the seven seers are seven.' // 11 //

No, we say. It is proper that, because the word '<s>pañcapūlī</s>' (group of five bundles) is intended as a collective, [the question] 'how many?' — when there is an expectation of differentiation — receives the qualification 'five groups of five bundles.' But here, since 'five, five peoples' already states the differentiation from the very beginning, [and] when there is no expectation of [further] differentiation through 'how many?', the construction 'five <s>pañcajanas</s>' would not serve as a qualification. Even if this were a qualification, it would be a qualification of the number five alone — and the fault [of that] has already been stated. Therefore, 'five <s>pañcajanas</s>' is not intended to refer to twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>. And because of the excess too, it is not intended to refer to twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>. And because of the excess too, it is not intended to refer to twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>. For there is an excess over the number twenty-five by the Self and space. First, the Self is here indicated as the substratum [by the word] 'in whom' — as a receptacle for the [entities said to be] established [in it]. Because the locative 'in whom' is drawn back by 'Him alone I consider as the Self' — [identifying it] as the Self. And the Self is the conscious <s>puruṣa</s>. And since that [<s>puruṣa</s>] is already included within the twenty-five, it is not proper for the same [entity] to be both the receptacle and that which is contained. And if some other entity were taken [as the receptacle], the excess beyond the number of <s>tattvas</s> would contradict the [<s>Sāṃkhya</s>] doctrine. Similarly, 'and space is established' — since space too is already included within the twenty-five, its separate mention is not proper. And if some other entity were taken, the stated fault [of excess] applies. And how, from merely hearing a number, can the inclusion of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> — which are not heard [in the text] — be understood? Because the word '<s>jana</s>' is conventional [only] for persons [not for <s>tattvas</s>]. And because the number is compatible even with the inclusion of other entities. How then [should] 'five <s>pañcajanas</s>' [be understood]?

children.text: ke punaste pañcajanā nāmeti, taducyate-
children.translated_text: Who then are those [entities] called '<s>pañcajanas</s>'? To that it is said:

children.text:
FN: mūlaprakṛtiravikṛtiḥ anyasya kasyacidvikāro na /
mahadahaṅkārapañcatanmātrāṇi sapta prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ /
mahānahaṅkārasya prakṛtirmūlaprakṛtervikṛtiḥ /
ahaṅkāro 'pi tāmasastanmātrāṇāṃ prakṛtiḥ /
sāttvikastvekādaśendriyāṇāṃ tanmātrāṇyākāśādīnāṃ sthūlānāṃ prakṛtayaḥ /
pañcabhūtānyekādaśendriyāṇi ṣoḍaśako gaṇo vikāra eva /
pṛthivyādīnāṃ ghaṭādiprakṛtitve 'pi tattvāntarāprakṛtitvādvikṛtaya eva /
puruṣastu kauṭasthyātprakṛtivikṛtitvavirahītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Mūlaprakṛti</s> is unmodified' — [it is] not a modification of anything else. The seven — <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and the five <s>tanmātras</s> — are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and modifications. <s>Mahat</s> is the <s>prakṛti</s> of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and a modification of <s>mūlaprakṛti</s>. <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> in its <s>tāmasika</s> aspect is the <s>prakṛti</s> of the <s>tanmātras</s>. In its <s>sāttvika</s> aspect, [it is the <s>prakṛti</s>] of the eleven sense-organs. The <s>tanmātras</s> are the <s>prakṛtis</s> of the gross [elements] — space and the rest. The five elements and eleven sense-organs — the group of sixteen — are modifications alone. Even though earth and the rest are <s>prakṛtis</s> of pots and such, they are [only] modifications because they are not <s>prakṛtis</s> of any other <s>tattva</s>. But <s>puruṣa</s>, because of its immutability, is devoid of both <s>prakṛti</s>-hood and modification-hood — this is the meaning.

children.text: bhedo viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Bheda</s>' (difference) means differentiation.

children.text: atireka ādhikyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Atireka</s>' (excess) means surplus.

children.text: uktadoṣaḥ saṃkhyādhikyam /
children.translated_text: The stated fault is the surplus of the number.

children.text: prāṇādayo vākyaśeṣāt | BBs_1,4.12 |
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇādayo vākyaśeṣāt</s> — [They are] the <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest, because of the remainder of the passage. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.12 |

children.text:
'yasminapañca pañcajanāḥ' ityata uttarasminmantre brahmasvarūpanirūpaṇāya prāṇādayaḥ pañca nirdiṣṭāḥ - 'prāṇasya prāṇamuta cakṣuṣaścakṣuruta śrotrasya śrotramannasyānnaṃ manaso ye mano viduḥ' iti /
te 'tra vākyaśeṣagatāḥ saṃnidhānātpañcajanā vivakṣyante /
kathaṃ punaḥ prāṇādiṣu janaśabdaprayogaḥ /
tattveṣu vā kathaṃ janaśabdaprayogaḥ /
samāne tu prasiddhyatikrame vākyaśeṣavaśātprāṇādaya eva gpahītavyā bhavanti /
janasaṃbandhācca prāṇādayo janaśabdabhājo bhavanti /
janavacanaśca puruṣaśabdaḥ prāṇeṣu prayuktaḥ 'te vā ete pañca brahmapuruṣāḥ' (chā. 3.13.6) ityatra /
'prāṇo ha pitā prāṇo ha mātā' (chā.7.15.1) ityādi ca brāhmaṇam /
samāsabalācca masudāyasya rūḍhatvamaviruddham /
kathaṃ punarasati prathamprayoge rūḍhiḥ śakyāśrayitum /
śakyodbhidādivadityāha /
prasiddhārthasaṃnidhāne hyaprasiddhārthaḥ śabdaḥ prayujyamānaḥ samabhivyāhārāttadviṣayo niyamyate, yathā 'udbhidā yajeta' 'yūpaṃ chinatti' 'vediṃ karoti' iti /
tathāyamapi pañcajanaśabdaḥ samāsānvākhyānādavagatasaṃjñābhāvaḥ saṃjñyākāṅkṣī vākyaśeṣasamabhivyāhṛteṣu prāṇādiṣu vartiṣyate /
kaiścittu devāḥ pitaro gandharvā asurā rakṣāṃsi ca pañca pañcajanā vyākhyātāḥ /
anyaiśca catvāro varṇā niṣādapañcamāḥ parigṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: And by others, the four <s>varṇas</s> with the <s>Niṣāda</s> as the fifth are accepted [as the five peoples].

children.text: kvacicca 'yatpāñcajanyayā viśā' (ṛ.saṃ. 8.53.7) iti prajāparaḥ prayogaḥ pañcajanaśabdasya dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: And somewhere the usage of the word '<s>pañcajana</s>' is seen with the meaning of 'people': 'with the people born of the five' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 8.53.7).

children.text: tatparigpahe 'pīha na kaścidvarodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if that [interpretation] is accepted, there is no obstruction here.

children.text: ācāryastu na pañcaviśatestattvānamiha pratītirastītyevaṃparatayā 'prāṇādayo vākyaśeṣāt' iti jagāda // 12 //
children.translated_text: But the teacher [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>], holding the view that there is no awareness here of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> [of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>], declared '<s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest, because of the remainder of the sentence.' // 12 //

From 'in whom the five <s>pañcajanas</s>' — in the next mantra following that, for the purpose of determining the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, five [entities] beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> are indicated: 'Those who know the <s>prāṇa</s> of <s>prāṇa</s>, the eye of the eye, the ear of the ear, the food of food, and the mind of the mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.2). Those, being in the remainder of the passage and [therefore] in proximity, are intended as the <s>pañcajanas</s>. But how can the word '<s>jana</s>' be used for the <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest? Or [for that matter], how can the word '<s>jana</s>' be used for the [<s>Sāṃkhya</s>] <s>tattvas</s>? Since both equally transgress the well-known [meaning], by the force of the remainder of the passage, the <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest alone should be accepted. And because of their connection with people (<s>jana</s>), the <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest can bear the designation '<s>jana</s>.' And the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' — which denotes people — is used for the <s>prāṇas</s> in: 'These indeed are the five <s>Brahma</s>-persons (<s>brahmapuruṣāḥ</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.13.6). And there is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> passage: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the father, <s>prāṇa</s> is the mother' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.15.1) and the like. And by the force of the compound, the conventional [meaning] of the aggregate is not contradicted. But how can conventional usage be relied upon when there is no prior [attested] usage? It is said: just as with [words like] '<s>udbhid</s>' (a type of sacrifice) and the like. For when a word with an unknown meaning is used in the proximity of a word with a known meaning, it is determined through contextual association to refer to that [known meaning] — as in 'one should sacrifice with the <s>udbhid</s>,' 'one cuts the sacrificial post,' 'one makes the altar.' Similarly, this word '<s>pañcajana</s>' too — whose status as a proper name is understood from the analysis of the compound, and which seeks a referent — will apply to the <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest, which are contextually associated in the remainder of the passage. But some have explained the five <s>pañcajanas</s> as <s>devas</s>, <s>pitṛs</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>rakṣases</s>.

children.text:
bhaveyustāvatprāṇādayaḥ pañcajanā mādhyandinānāṃ ye 'nnaṃ prāṇādiṣvāmananti /
kāṇvānāṃ tu kathaṃ prāṇādayaḥ pañcajanā bhaveyurye 'nnaṃ prāṇādiṣu nāmanantīti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: Let <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest be the five peoples for the <s>Mādhyandinas</s>, who recite food among the [categories beginning with] <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest. But for the <s>Kāṇvas</s>, who do not recite food among [the categories beginning with] <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest — how could <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest be the five peoples? Therefore, the following answer is given:

children.text:
FN: utaśabdoṣapyarthaḥ /
ye prāṇādiprerakaṃ tatsākṣiṇamātmānaṃ viduste brahmavida ityarthaḥ /
janavācakaḥ śabdo janaśabdaḥ pañcajanaśabda iti yāvat /
śūdrāyāṃ brāhmaṇājjāto niṣādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The word '<s>uta</s>' has the meaning of 'also.' Those who know the Self that impels <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest and is their witness — they are the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. The word denoting 'people' is '<s>jana</s>'; '<s>pañcajana</s>' means the same. A <s>Niṣāda</s> is one born of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> from a <s>Śūdra</s> woman.

children.translated_text: By light (<s>jyotis</s>), for some [recensions], when food is absent. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.13 |

children.text:
asatyapi kāṇvānāmanne jyotiṣā teṣāṃ pañcasaṃkhyā pūryeta /
te 'pi hi 'yasminpañca pañcajanāḥ ityataḥ pūrvasminmantre brahmasvarūpanirūpaṇāyaiva jyotiradhīyate- 'taddevā jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ' iti /
kathaṃ punarubhayeṣāmapi tulyavadidaṃ jyotiḥ paṭhyamānaṃ samānamantragatayā pañcasaṃkhyayā keṣāñcidgrṛhyate keṣāñcinneti /
apekṣābhedādityāha /
mādhyandinānāṃ hi samānamantrapaṭhitaprāṇādipañcajanalābhānnāsminmantrāntarapaṭhite jyotiṣvapekṣā bhavati /
tadalābhāttu kāṇvānāṃ bhavatyapekṣā /
apekṣābhedācca samāne 'pi mantre jyotiṣo grahaṇāgrahaṇe /
children.translated_text: And because of the difference in need, the grasping and non-grasping of 'light' in the same <s>mantra</s> [by different recensions is explained].

children.text: yathā samāne 'pyatirātre vacanabhedātṣoḍaṣino grahaṇāgrahaṇe tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as in the same <s>Atirātra</s> [rite], because of a difference of statement, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> cup is grasped [by some] and not grasped [by others] — so too here.

children.text: tadevaṃ na tāvacchrutiprasiddhiḥ kācitpradhānaviṣayāsti /
children.translated_text: Thus, so far, there is no establishment through <s>śruti</s> of any [doctrine] concerning <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: smṛtinyāyaprasiddhī tu parihariṣyete // 13 //
children.translated_text: But the establishments through <s>Smṛti</s> and reasoning will be refuted [later]. // 13 //

Even in the absence of food for the <s>Kāṇvas</s>, their count of five would be completed by 'light' (<s>jyotis</s>). For they too, in the <s>mantra</s> preceding 'In whom the five peoples and the five peoples [dwell],' recite light precisely for the purpose of ascertaining the nature of <s>Brahman</s>: 'That is the light of lights, [known by] the gods.' But how can this light, which is recited equally by both [recensions] in the same <s>mantra</s>, be counted in the group of five by some and not by others? He says: because of the difference in need. For the <s>Mādhyandinas</s>, having already obtained the five peoples — <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest — as recited in the same <s>mantra</s>, there is no need for the light recited in another <s>mantra</s>. But for the <s>Kāṇvas</s>, not having obtained [the fifth], the need arises.

children.text: FN: atra ṣoḍaśigrahaṇāgrahaṇavadvākyabhedājjyotiṣo vikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: Here, like the grasping and non-grasping of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> cup, there is an alternative regarding light, because of the difference of statements.

children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that the elaboration of creation and the like serves the purpose of understanding <s>Brahman</s>: 'Through food, dear one, as the sprout, trace water as the root; through water, dear one, as the sprout, trace fire as the root; through fire, dear one, as the sprout, trace Being as the root' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.4).

children.text: mṛdādidṛṣṭāntaiśca kāryasya kāraṇenābhedaṃ vadituṃ sṛṣṭyādiprapañcaḥ śrāvyata iti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And through the illustrations of clay and the like, it is understood that the elaboration of creation and the like is recited for the purpose of declaring the non-difference of the effect from the cause.

children.text: tathāca saṃpradāyavido vadanti- 'mṛllohavisphuliṅgādyaiḥ sṛṣṭiryā coditānyathā /
children.translated_text: And the knowers of tradition say: 'The creation that was taught through [illustrations of] clay, iron, sparks, and the like —

children.text: upāyaḥ so 'vatārāya nāsti bhedaḥ kathañcana //
children.translated_text: that is a device for introduction [to the teaching of <s>Brahman</s>]; there is no difference whatsoever.

The characteristics of <s>Brahman</s> have been established. The general purport of the <s>Vedānta</s> statements as pertaining to <s>Brahman</s> has been established. And the non-scriptural status of <s>Pradhāna</s> has been established. Therein, this further objection is raised: it is not possible to accept that <s>Brahman</s> is the cause beginning with origination, or that the general purport of the <s>Vedānta</s> statements pertains to <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because of the observation of discrepancies. For in each <s>Vedānta</s> text, a different creation is found, because of the variety of sequence and the like. Thus, somewhere the creation beginning with space is taught: 'From the Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). Somewhere the creation beginning with fire: 'It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3). Somewhere the creation beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>: 'He created <s>Prāṇa</s>; from <s>Prāṇa</s>, faith' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.4). Somewhere the creation of the worlds is taught without any sequence: 'He created these worlds — <s>Ambhas</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Mara</s>, <s>Āpas</s>' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 4.2.1). Likewise, somewhere a creation preceded by non-being is recited: 'Non-being indeed was this in the beginning; from that, being was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7), and 'Non-being indeed was this in the beginning; that was being; that came into existence' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.19.1). Somewhere, by refuting the doctrine of non-being, a creation preceded by being is declared: beginning with 'Some say: Non-being indeed was this in the beginning,' and [concluding with] 'How could being arise from non-being? Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1-2). Somewhere the differentiation of the world is stated as self-accomplished: 'This was then undifferentiated; it became differentiated by name and form' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.7). Thus, since there are manifold discrepancies, and since an alternative is not tenable regarding an [actual] entity — it is not proper that the <s>Vedānta</s> statements are directed toward ascertaining <s>Brahman</s> as the cause of the world. Rather, on the basis of the establishment through <s>Smṛti</s> and reasoning, [it would be proper to] accept another cause. Having stated this [prima facie view], we say: even though space and the like — the things created — differ in each <s>Vedānta</s> text with respect to sequence and such, there is no discrepancy regarding the creator. Why? Because the statement [about <s>Brahman</s>] is the same as it has been designated. For just as in one <s>Vedānta</s> text, the omniscient, omnipotent, all-Self, one without a second [<s>Brahman</s>] is designated as the cause — so too in other <s>Vedānta</s> texts, [<s>Brahman</s>] of that very same nature is designated. For example: 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). Here, by the word 'knowledge' and the subsequent statement of desire [directed at <s>Brahman</s>], [the text] showed <s>Brahman</s> as conscious, and declared it as the cause — as <s>Īśvara</s>, not directed by another. By the subsequent word 'Self,' through its successive entry into the sheaths of food and the rest, it established [<s>Brahman</s>] as the inner Self of all. And with 'Let me become many, let me be born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6) — by the mention of becoming many with reference to the Self — it spoke of the non-difference of the modifications created from the creator. Likewise, with 'It created all this, whatever there is' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6) — by designating the creation of the entire world — it declares the creator as without a second prior to creation. The same characteristics of <s>Brahman</s> known as the cause here are known elsewhere too: 'Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning, one only, without a second. It deliberated: Let me become many, let me be born. It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1,3). Likewise: 'The Self alone was this, one only, in the beginning; nothing else whatsoever was active. It deliberated: Let me create the worlds' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 4.1.1-2). Since the class of statements directed toward ascertaining the nature of the cause is of uncontested meaning in every <s>Vedānta</s> text — the discrepancy that is seen pertains only to the effects: somewhere the creation begins with space, somewhere with fire, and so forth. And it cannot be said that because of a discrepancy regarding the effects, <s>Brahman</s> too — which is uncontestedly apprehended as [the cause] in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts — should be regarded as not intended. Because of over-extension. And the teacher will resolve the discrepancy regarding effects too, beginning from 'Not space, because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.3.1). There might also be uncontested status of the effects — because of not being [intended to be] taught [as the main point]. For this elaboration of creation and the like is not what is intended to be taught. For no human purpose dependent on it is seen or heard. Nor can one be imagined — because from the opening and concluding statements in each context, which pertain to <s>Brahman</s>, the single-sentence reading with those [<s>Brahman</s>]-statements is understood.
