children.text: yathā lūyate kedāraḥ svayameveti satyeva pūrṇake lavitari /
children.translated_text: Just as 'the field is being reaped' [is said] even when there is indeed a reaper who reaps it himself,

children.text: yadvā karmaṇyevaiṣa lakāror'thākṣiptaṃ kartāramapekṣya draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, this passive voice (<s>lakāra</s>) should be understood as implying an agent through the meaning of the action —

children.text: yathā gamyate grāma iti // 15 //
children.translated_text: just as 'the village is being gone to.' // 15 //

'Non-being indeed was this in the beginning' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7) — here, non-being devoid of a Self is not being taught as the cause. For having rejected the doctrine of non-being — 'He becomes non-being; if one knows <s>Brahman</s> as non-being, [one becomes non-being]; but if one knows that <s>Brahman</s> is — then they know him as existent' — and having ascertained <s>Brahman</s>, characterized by existence, as the inner Self through the successive [series of] sheaths beginning with the food-sheath, [the text says] 'He desired' — drawing together [the reference to] that very [<s>Brahman</s>] that was the subject — and having taught the creation in full elaboration from Him, and having concluded with 'They call that the Real (<s>satya</s>),' and [saying] 'On that very subject, there is this verse' — it cites this verse in connection with the very subject under discussion: 'Non-being indeed was this in the beginning.' Now if non-being devoid of a Self were meant in this verse, then, because of the drawing together of something different, and because of the citation of something different [from what was established], the statement would become incoherent. Therefore, since the word '<s>sat</s>' (being) is generally well known in reference to entities differentiated by name and form, <s>Brahman</s> — which is 'being' [in truth] — is figuratively spoken of as 'as if non-being' prior to creation, with reference to the absence of [manifest] differentiation. This same construal applies to 'Non-being indeed was this in the beginning' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.19.1) as well — because of the drawing together: 'that was being' (<s>tad sad āsīt</s>). For if absolute non-existence were accepted, what would be drawn together as 'that was being'? In 'Some say: Non-being indeed was this in the beginning' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) too, this is not a presentation of an opposing view based on the intent of another <s>śruti</s> — because an alternative is not possible regarding an [actual] entity, as it is in the case of [ritual] actions. Therefore, this should be understood as: the presentation and rejection of the doctrine of non-being — imagined by those of dull intellect — is for the purpose of strengthening the position of being, which is accepted by <s>śruti</s>. In 'This was then undifferentiated' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.7) too, the differentiation of the world is not being described as without a superintendent — because of the drawing together of the superintendent who enters the differentiated effects: 'This [<s>Brahman</s>] has entered here, up to the very fingertips.' For if differentiation without a superintendent were accepted, then the immediately following reference — drawing together the subject by the pronoun 'He' — [asking] who would be drawn together as having entered the effects? And the <s>śruti</s> speaks of the entry of the conscious Self into the body. Because of the hearing of consciousness for the one who has entered: 'seeing as the eye, hearing as the ear, thinking as the mind.' Moreover, just as this world is at present being differentiated by name and form with a superintendent — so too, it is understood, it was at the beginning of creation. Because an imagined conjecture contrary to what is observed is untenable. And another <s>śruti</s> too — 'Having entered by means of this living Self, let me differentiate names and forms' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2) — shows the differentiation of the world as [occurring] with a superintendent.

kauṣītakibrāhmaṇe bālākyajātaśatrusaṃvāde śrūyate- 'yo vai bālāka eteṣāṃ kartā yasya vai tatkarma sa veditavyaḥ' (kau. brā. 4.19) iti /

kiṃ tāvatprāptam /

parispandalakṣaṇasya ca karmaṇaḥ prāṇāśrayatvāt /
vākyaśeṣe ca 'athāsminprāṇa evaikadhā bhavati' iti prāṇaśabdadarśanāt /

pāriśeṣyātpratyakṣasaṃnihitaṃ jagatsarvanāmnaitacchabdena nirdiśyate /
kriyata iti ca tadaiva jagatkarma /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Bālāki</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, it is heard: 'He who, O <s>Bālāki</s>, is the maker of these — He whose work this is — He is to be known' (<s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s> 4.19). Therein, the question is: is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) being taught as the one to be known, or the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, or the Supreme Self? What is the initial position? It is <s>Prāṇa</s>. Why? Because of the hearing 'whose work this is.' And because activity characterized by motion is dependent on <s>Prāṇa</s>. And because in the remainder of the passage, the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is seen: 'then in this <s>Prāṇa</s> alone it becomes unified.' And because the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is well known [as referring to] the chief vital breath. And those <s>puruṣas</s> (persons) that were earlier designated by <s>Bālāki</s> — 'the person in the sun, the person in the moon' and so forth — for them too, <s>Prāṇa</s> can be the maker, because the presiding deities are particular states of <s>Prāṇa</s>. Because of the well-known teaching from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Who is the one god? <s>Prāṇa</s>. He is <s>Brahman</s>; they call Him <s>Tyat</s> (That)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.9). Or alternatively, it is the <s>jīva</s> that is here taught as the one to be known. For the <s>jīva</s> too can be presented as having action characterized by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> in the statement 'whose work this is.' The <s>jīva</s> too, being an enjoyer, can appropriately be the maker of these <s>puruṣas</s> who serve as instruments of enjoyment. And in the remainder of the passage, indications of the <s>jīva</s> are understood. For the reason that <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, wishing to enlighten <s>Bālāki</s> — who had approached for the knowledge of the <s>puruṣa</s> presented as the maker of these [presiding deities] and as the one to be known — addressed a sleeping person, and upon the sleeping person not hearing the words of address, demonstrated the non-enjoyer nature of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the other [faculties], and awakened him [to show] the <s>jīva</s> as the enjoyer distinct from <s>Prāṇa</s> and the others. Similarly, further on too, indications of the <s>jīva</s> are understood: 'Just as a chief lives on his subjects, and just as the subjects live on the chief — so indeed this conscious self (<s>prajñātman</s>) lives on these selves, and so these selves live on this self' (<s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s> 4.20). And the word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is appropriate for the <s>jīva</s>, because the <s>jīva</s> sustains <s>Prāṇa</s>. Therefore, one of the two — the <s>jīva</s> or the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> — should be understood here, not the Supreme Lord, because no indication of Him is discerned — this being the position reached, we say: this maker of these <s>puruṣas</s> must be the Supreme Lord alone. Why? Because of the strength of the opening statement (<s>upakrama</s>). For here, <s>Bālāki</s> commenced a dialogue with <s>Ajātaśatru</s> [saying]: 'Let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>.' He mentioned several <s>puruṣas</s> presiding over the sun and such, which did not partake of the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>, and then fell silent. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> [said]: 'You have indeed spoken to me falsely [saying] "Let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>"' — thus rejecting him as one who had spoken of what is not the true <s>Brahman</s>, he pointed to another — the maker of those — as the one to be known. If that [maker] too did not partake of the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>, the opening statement would be contradicted. Therefore, this must be the Supreme Lord alone. And the agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) regarding these <s>puruṣas</s> cannot be independently established for anyone other than the Supreme Lord. The statement 'whose work this is' is not a reference to activity characterized by motion, nor to activity characterized by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — because neither of these is the topic at hand, and because neither has been mentioned. Nor is this a reference to the <s>puruṣas</s> [themselves] — because those have already been referred to as 'the maker of these <s>puruṣas</s>.' And because of the discrepancy in gender and number, this is not a reference to the action of the <s>puruṣas</s> (in the sense of 'doing') or to the fruit of action — because both of those are already subsumed under the word 'maker.' By elimination, the entire world, which is directly present and perceptible, is denoted by the word 'this' (<s>etat</s>). And the world is indeed 'action' (<s>karma</s>) in the sense that 'it is made' (<s>kriyate</s>).

children.text: nanu jagadapyaprakṛtamasaṃśabditaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: But is not the world also not the topic at hand and also unmentioned?

children.text:
satyametat /
tathāpyasati viśeṣopādāne sādhāraṇenārthena saṃnidhānena saṃnihitavastumātrasyāyaṃ nirdeśa iti gamyate na viśiṣṭasya kasyacit /
viśeṣasaṃnidhānābhāvāt /
pūrvatra ca jagadekadeśabhūtānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ viśeṣopādānadaviśeṣitaṃ jagadevehopādīyata iti gamyate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- ya eteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ jagadekadeśabhūtānāṃ kartā, kimanena viśeṣeṇa, yasya kṛtsnameva jagadaviśeṣitaṃ karmeti /
vāśabda ekadeśāvacchinnakartṛtvavyāvṛttyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) serves to exclude the restricted agency [limited to particular <s>puruṣas</s>].

children.text: ye bālākinā brahmatvābhimatāḥ puruṣāḥ kīrtitāsteṣāmabrahmatvakhyāpanāya viśeṣopādānam /
children.translated_text: The specific mention [of the <s>puruṣas</s>] is for the purpose of declaring that those <s>puruṣas</s> whom <s>Bālāki</s> regarded as <s>Brahman</s> are not <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: evaṃ brāhmaṇaparivrājakanyāyena sāmānyaviśeṣābhyāṃ jagataḥ kartā veditavyatayopadiśyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, by the method of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-and-<s>parivrājaka</s> [analogy], the maker of the world is taught as the one to be known, by means of both the general and the particular.

children.text: parameśvaraśca sarvajagataḥ kartā sarvavedānteṣvavadhāritaḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: And it is established in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts that the Supreme Lord is the maker of the entire world. // 16 //

This is true. Nevertheless, in the absence of any specific qualifier, by its general meaning and by proximity, this is understood as a reference to whatever is directly present — not to anything specific. Because there is no specific [referent] nearby. And since earlier, specific <s>puruṣas</s> — which are parts of the world — were specifically mentioned, what is understood as being referred to here without specification is the world itself. The meaning is this: He who is the maker of these <s>puruṣas</s> that are parts of the world — what is the point of this specification? — He whose action is the entire unspecified world [is to be known].

children.text:
FN.:etajjagadyasya karma /
kriyata iti vyutpattyā kāryamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'This world whose action [it is]' — by the etymology 'it is made' (<s>kriyate</s>), the meaning is 'effect.'

children.text:
sa prāṇaḥ /
tyat parokṣam /
children.translated_text: 'He' is <s>Prāṇa</s>. '<s>Tyat</s>' means 'that which is distant [i.e., transcendent].'

children.text: yatkāraṇaṃ yasmājjīvaṃ bodhayati tasmādasti suptotthāpanaṃ jīvaliṅgamiti yojanā /
children.translated_text: Since he awakens the <s>jīva</s> — therefore, the waking of the sleeping person is an indication of the <s>jīva</s>; this is the construction.

children.text: brāhmaṇa bhojayitavyāḥ parivrājakaścetyukte sāmānyaviśeṣābhyāṃ saṃnihitasarvabrāhmaṇavat /
children.translated_text: Just as when it is said '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> should be fed and also a <s>parivrājaka</s>' — by the general and the particular, all <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are present [are included].

children.text: jīvamukhyaprāṇaliṅgān neti cet tadvyākhyātam | BBs_1,4.17 |
children.translated_text: If [you say] no, because of indications of the <s>jīva</s> and chief <s>Prāṇa</s> — that has been explained. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.17 |

children.text: ata yaduktaṃ vākyaśeṣagatājjīvaliṅgānmukhyaprāṇaliṅgācca tayorevānyatarasyeha grahaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ na parameśvarasyeti /
children.translated_text: As for the objection stated — that because of indications of the <s>jīva</s> found in the remainder of the passage, and because of indications of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, one of those two should be understood here, not the Supreme Lord —

children.text:
tatparihartavyam /
yatrocyate- parihṛtaṃ caitat 'nopāsātraividhyādāśritatvādiha tadyogāt' (bra. sū. 1.1.31) ityatra /
trividhaṃ hyatropāsanamevaṃ sati prasajjyeta jīvopāsanaṃ mukhyaprāṇopāsanaṃ brahmopāsanaṃ ceti /
na caitannyāyyam /
upakramopasaṃhārābhyāṃ hi brahviṣayatvamasya vākyasyāvagamyate /
tatropakramasya tāvadbrahmaviṣayatvaṃ darśitam /
upasaṃhārasyāpi niratiśayaphalaśravaṇādbrahmaviṣayatvaṃ dṛśyate- 'sarvānpāpmano 'pahṛtya sarveṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ svārājyamādhipatyaṃ paryeti ya evaṃ veda' iti /
children.translated_text: that must be refuted. In response to which it is said: this has already been refuted in the passage '<s>Nopāsā-traividhyād āśritatvād iha tad-yogāt</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.31). For in that case, a threefold meditation would result — meditation on the <s>jīva</s>, meditation on the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, and meditation on <s>Brahman</s>. And this is not proper. For from the opening and concluding statements, the <s>Brahman</s>-subject-matter of this passage is understood. The <s>Brahman</s>-subject-matter of the opening statement has already been shown. The concluding statement too is seen to be about <s>Brahman</s>, because of the hearing of an unsurpassable result: 'Having warded off all sins, he attains supremacy, sovereignty, and overlordship over all beings — he who knows thus.'

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati pratardanavākyanirṇayenaivedamapi vākyaṃ nirṇīyeta /
na nirṇīyate /
'yasya caitatkarma' ityasya brahmaviṣayatvena tatrānirdhāritatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the statement 'whose work this is' was not determined there as referring to <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmādatra jīvamukhyaprāṇaśaṅkā punarutpadyamānā nirvartyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the doubt regarding the <s>jīva</s> and the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>, arising here again, is resolved [afresh].

children.text: prāṇaśabdo 'pi brahmaviṣayo dṛṣṭaḥ 'prāṇabandhanaṃ hi somya manaḥ' (chā. 6.8.2) ityatra /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>Prāṇa</s>' is also seen to refer to <s>Brahman</s> — in the passage '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the binding, O dear one, of the mind' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.2).

children.text: jīliṅgamapyupakramopasaṃhārayorbrahmaviṣayatvādabhedābhiprāyeṇa yojayitavyam // 17 //
children.translated_text: The indication of the <s>jīva</s> too, since the opening and concluding statements establish the <s>Brahman</s>-subject-matter, should be construed with the intention of [teaching] non-difference [between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Brahman</s>]. // 17 //
But if this is so, would not this passage be settled by the same determination as the <s>Pratardana</s> passage? It is not settled [thereby].

children.text: FN.:śraiṣṭhyaṃ guṇādhikyam, ādhipatyaṃ niyanitṛtvam, svārājyamaniyamyatvamiti bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Śraiṣṭhya</s>' means excellence of qualities; '<s>ādhipatya</s>' means the status of being a controller; '<s>svārājya</s>' means the status of being uncontrolled — this is the distinction.

children.text: anyārthaṃ tu jaiminiḥ praśnavyākhyānābhyām api caivam eke | BBs_1,4.18 |
children.translated_text: But <s>Jaimini</s> [holds] that [the reference to the <s>jīva</s>] serves another purpose, because of the question and the explanation, and also because some [recensions state] thus. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.18 |

children.text:
apica naivātra vivaditavyaṃ jīvapradhānaṃ vedaṃ vākyaṃ syādbrahmapradhānaṃ veti /
yato 'nyārthaṃ jīvaparāmarśaṃ brahmapratipattyarthamasminvākye jaiminirācāryo manyante /
kasmāt /
praśnavyākhyānābhyām /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there need be no dispute here as to whether this passage is primarily about the <s>jīva</s> or primarily about <s>Brahman</s>. Because the teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds that the reference to the <s>jīva</s> in this passage serves another purpose — namely, the understanding of <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because of the question and the explanation.

children.text:
praśnastāvatsuṣuptapuruṣapratibodhanena prāṇādivyatirikte jīve pratibodhite punarjīvavyatiriktaviṣayo dṛśyate- 'kvaiṣa etadbālāke puruṣo 'śayiṣṭa kva vā etadabhūtkuta etadāgāt' (kau.brā. 4.19) iti /
prativacanamapi 'yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kañcana paśyatyathāsminprāṇa evaikadhā bhavati' ityādi 'etasmādātmanaḥ prāṇā yathāyatanaṃ vipratiṣṭhante prāṇebhyo devā devebhyo lokāḥ' (kau.brā. 4.20) iti ca /
suṣuptikāle ca pareṇa brahmaṇā jīva ekatāṃ gacchati /
parasmācca brahmaṇaḥ prāṇādikaṃ jagajjāyata iti vedāntamaryādā /
tasmādyatrāsya jīvasya niḥsaṃbodhatāsvacchatārūpaḥ svāpa upādhijanitaviśeṣavijñānarahitaṃ svarūpaṃ, yatastaddhaṃśarūpamāgamanaṃ, so 'tra paramātmā veditavyatayā śrāvita iti gamyate /
apicaivameke śākhino vājasaneyino 'sminneva bālākyajātaśatrusaṃvāde spaṣṭaṃ vijñānamayaśabdena jīvamāmnāya tadvyatiriktaṃ paramātmānamāmananti- 'ya eṣa vijñānamayapuruṣaḥ kvaiṣa tadābhūtkuta etadāgāt' (bṛ. 2.1.16) iti praśne /
prativacane 'pi 'ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasmiñśete' iti /
children.translated_text: And in the answer too: 'He who is this space within the heart — in Him he sleeps.'

children.text: ākāśaśabdaśca paramātmani prayuktaḥ 'daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' (chā. 8.1.1) ityatra /
children.translated_text: And the word 'space' (<s>ākāśa</s>) is used for the Supreme Self in the passage 'the small [space] within this — [that is] the space' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1).

children.text: 'sarva eta ātmano vyuccaranti' iti copādhimatāmātmanāmanyato vyuccaraṇamāmanantaḥ paramātmānameva kāraṇatvenāmanantīti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And by teaching that the conditioned selves issue forth from another, they indicate the Supreme Self as the cause — and this is understood.

children.text: prāṇanarākaraṇasyāpi suṣuptapuruṣotthāpanena prāṇādivyatiriktopadeśo 'bhyuccayaḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: Even the awakening of the sleeping person, which was done for the purpose of demonstrating the distinction [of the <s>jīva</s>] from <s>Prāṇa</s> and the others, serves as an additional [argument for the Supreme Self], since the teaching [concerns what is] distinct from <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest. // 18 //

As for the question — after the sleeping person was awakened and the <s>jīva</s> distinct from <s>Prāṇa</s> and the other [faculties] was brought to awareness, a further question is seen whose subject is other than the <s>jīva</s>: 'Where was this person lying, O <s>Bālāki</s>? Where was he? From where did he come?' (<s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s> 4.19). The answer too [points beyond the <s>jīva</s>]: 'When he sleeps and sees no dream, then in this <s>Prāṇa</s> alone he becomes unified' and so forth, up to 'From this Self, the vital breaths go forth to their respective stations; from the vital breaths, the gods; from the gods, the worlds' (<s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s> 4.20). And in the state of deep sleep, the <s>jīva</s> attains oneness with the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And from the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest of the world are born — this is the established position of the <s>Vedānta</s>. Therefore, where this <s>jīva</s>'s sleep — whose nature is the absence of specific cognition and the state of transparency — [occurs], and from where its return in partial form [takes place] — that Supreme Self is here taught as the one to be known. Moreover, thus some followers of a [particular] branch — the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> — in this very dialogue between <s>Bālāki</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having explicitly mentioned the <s>jīva</s> with the word '<s>vijñānamaya</s>' (consisting of knowledge), teach the Supreme Self as distinct from it — in the question: 'Where was this person consisting of knowledge? Where was he? From where did he come?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.16).

children.text:
FN: niḥsaṃbodhatā viśeṣadhīśūnyatā /
svacchatā vikṣepamalaśūnyatvam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Absence of specific cognition' (<s>niḥsaṃbodhatā</s>) means the void of particular knowledge. 'Transparency' (<s>svacchatā</s>) means the absence of the impurity of distraction.

children.text: 6 vākyānvayādhikaraṇam / sū. 19-22
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Vākyānvaya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Sentence-Coherence) / <s>Sūtras</s> 19-22

children.text: vākyānvayāt | BBs_1,4.19 |
children.translated_text: Because of the coherence of the sentence. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.19 |

children.text:
bṛhadāraṇyake maitreyībrāhmaṇe 'dhīyate- 'na vā are patyuḥ kāmāya' ityupakramya 'na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavatyātmanastu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavatyātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyo maitreyyātmano vā are darśanena śravaṇena matyā vijñānenedaṃ sarvaṃ viditam' /
(bṛ. 4.5.6) iti, tatraitadvicikitsyate- kiṃ vijñānātmaivāyaṃ draṣṭavyaśrotavyatvādirūpeṇopadiśyata āhosvitparamātmeti /
kutaḥ punareṣā vicikitsā /
priyasaṃsūcitenātmanā bhokatropakramādvijñānatmopadeśa iti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
vijñānātmopadeśa iti /
kasmāt /
upakramasāmarthyāt /
patijāyāputravittādikaṃ hi bhogyabhūtaṃ sarvaṃ jagadātmārthatayā priyaṃ bhavatīti priyasaṃsūcitaṃ bhoktāramātmānamukramyānantaramidamātmano darśanādyupadiśyamānaṃ kasyānyasyātmanaḥ syāt /
madhye 'pi 'idaṃ mahadbhūtamanantamapāraṃ vijñānaghana evaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tānyevānuvinaśyati na pretya saṃjñāsti' iti prakṛtasyaiva mahato bhūtasya draṣṭavyasya bhūtebhyaḥ samutthānaṃ vijñānātmabhāvena bruvanvijñānātmanaṃ evedaṃ draṣṭavyatvaṃ darśayati /
tathā 'vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt' iti kartṛvacanena śabdenopasaṃharanvijñānātmānamevehopadiṣṭaṃ darśayati /
tasmādātmavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ bhoktrarthatvādbhogyajātasyaupacārikaṃ draṣṭavyamiti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ paramātmopadeśa evāyam /
kasmāt /
vākyānvayāt /
vākyaṃ hīdaṃ paurvāparyeṇāvekṣyamāṇaṃ paramātmānaṃprati anvitāvayavaṃ lakṣyate /
kathamiti, tadupapādyate- 'amṛtatvasya tu nāśāsti vittena' iti yājñavalkyādupaśrutya 'yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syāṃ kimahaṃ tena kuryāṃ yadeva bhagavānveda tadeva me brūhi' ityamṛtatvamāśāsānāya maitreyyā yājñavalkya ātmavijñānamidamupadiśati /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, in the <s>Maitreyī-brāhmaṇa</s>, it is read — beginning with 'Not for the sake of the husband, indeed' and [continuing]: 'Not for the sake of everything is everything dear, but for the sake of the Self is everything dear. The Self, indeed, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, is to be seen, heard, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon; by the seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing of the Self, all this is known' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6). Therein, this is doubted: Is only the individual knowing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) being taught here in the form of being 'to be seen, heard,' and so forth, or the supreme Self? Whence does this doubt arise? Because the passage begins with a reference to the enjoyer-self indicated by [the term] 'dear,' [it could be] a teaching about the individual knowing self. What, then, is the prima facie view? That it is a teaching about the individual knowing self. Why? Because of the force of the opening. For the entire world consisting of husband, wife, sons, wealth, and so forth — being the objects of enjoyment — is dear for the sake of the Self. Having thus introduced the Self as the enjoyer, indicated through [the notion of] dearness, this teaching about the seeing and such of the Self that immediately follows — whose Self could it pertain to other [than the enjoyer]? In the middle too — 'This great being, infinite, boundless, is a mass of knowledge alone; having arisen from these elements, it perishes along with them; after death there is no consciousness' — by stating the arising of the great being that is to be seen, of which this is the topic, from the elements in the form of the individual knowing self, [the text] shows that this 'being to be seen' pertains to the individual knowing self alone. Likewise, by concluding with the agent-denoting word: 'The knower — by what could one know it?' — [the text] shows that it is the individual knowing self alone that is taught here. Therefore, by knowledge of the Self, all knowledge is [attained] — this should be understood figuratively, because the class of objects of enjoyment exists for the sake of the enjoyer. Given this position, we say: This is indeed a teaching about the supreme Self. Why? Because of the syntactic connection of the passage. For this passage, when examined in its full sequence of preceding and subsequent portions, is seen to have its parts connected with reference to the supreme Self. How so? — this is demonstrated: Having heard from <s>Yājñavalkya</s> that 'there is no hope of immortality through wealth,' <s>Maitreyī</s>, who desired immortality, saying 'Of what use to me is that by which I shall not become immortal? Tell me, revered sir, just what you know' — to her, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> teaches this knowledge of the Self.

children.text:
nacānyatra paramātmavijñānādamṛtvamastīti śrutismṛtivādā vadanti /
tathā cātmavijñānena sarvavijñānamucyamānaṃ nānyatra paramakāraṇavijñānānmukhyamavakalpate /
nacaitadaupacārikamāśrayituṃ śakyaṃ, yatkāraṇamātmavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ pratijñāyānantareṇa granthena tadevopapādayati- 'brahma taṃ parādādyo 'nyatrātmano brahma veda' ityādinā /
yo hi brahmakṣatrādikaṃ jagadātmanonyatra svātantryeṇa labdhasadbhāvaṃ paśyati taṃ mithyādarśinaṃ tadeva mithyādṛṣṭaṃ brahmakṣatrādikaṃ jagatparākarotīti bhedadṛṣṭimapodya 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' iti sarvasya vastujātasyātmāvyatirekamavatārayati /
dundubhyādidṛṣṭāntaiśca (bṛ. 4.5.8) tamevāvyatirekaṃ draḍhayati /
children.translated_text: And through the illustrations of the drum and such (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.8), [the text] further confirms that very non-difference.

children.text: 'asya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitametadyadṛgvedaḥ' ( bṛ. 4.5.11) ityādinā ca prakṛtasyātmano nāmarūpakarmaprapañcakāraṇatāṃ vyācakṣāṇaḥ paramātmānamenaṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text: 'That which is the breathing forth of this great being — that is the <s>Ṛg Veda</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.11) — and so forth: by explaining the causal agency of the Self under discussion with respect to the entire elaboration of names, forms, and actions, [the text] leads [us] to [understand] this as the supreme Self.

children.text: tathaivaikāyanaprakriyāyāmapi (bṛ. 4.5.12) saviṣayasya sendriyasya sāntaḥkaraṇasya prapañcasyaikāyanamanantaramabāhyaṃ kṛtsnaṃ prajñānaghanaṃ vyācakṣāṇaḥ paramātmānamenaṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the procedure of the single abode (<s>ekāyana</s>) too (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.12), by explaining that the entire elaboration — together with its objects, sense-organs, and inner instrument — has a single abode, without exterior and without interior, as a solid mass of <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness), [the text] leads [us] to [understand] this as the supreme Self.

children.text: tasmātparamātmana evāyaṃ darśanādyupadeśa iti gamyate // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is understood that this teaching of seeing and such pertains to the supreme Self alone. // 19 //

And nowhere other than in the knowledge of the supreme Self do the <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> statements declare immortality. Moreover, the statement that by knowledge of the Self all is known cannot properly apply to anything other than knowledge of the supreme cause. Nor can this be taken figuratively, because, having promised that by knowledge of the Self all is known, the subsequent text demonstrates precisely that — through [passages such as]: '<s>Brahman</s> has abandoned him who knows <s>Brahman</s> as other than the Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.7), and so forth. For one who sees the world consisting of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class, the <s>kṣatriya</s> class, and such as having independent existence apart from the Self — that world of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and such, being falsely seen, abandons that person of false vision. Thus, having refuted the vision of difference, [the text] establishes the non-difference of all that exists from the Self through: 'All this is nothing but this Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.7).

children.text: yatpunaruktaṃ priyasaṃsūcitopakramādvijñānātmana evāyaṃ darśanādyupadeśa iti, atra brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: As for what was said — that because the passage begins with [a reference to] the enjoyer-self indicated by dearness, this teaching of seeing and such pertains to the individual knowing self alone — to that we say:

children.text:
FN: idaṃ pratyak /
mahadaparicchinnam /
bhūtaṃ satyam /
anantaṃ nityam /
apāraṃ sarvagataṃ cedekarasam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'This' means the inner [Self]. 'Great' means unlimited. 'Being' (<s>bhūta</s>) means real. 'Infinite' means eternal. 'Boundless' means all-pervading — and if so, of one essence.

children.text: vijñātāraṃ vijñānakartāram /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vijñātṛ</s>' means the agent of knowing (<s>vijñāna</s>).

children.text: na vittena tatsādhyena karmaṇetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not through wealth' means: not through action, which is the means to that [wealth] — this is the meaning.

children.text:
'nānyaḥ panthā', 'na karmaṇā' ityādayaḥ śrutivādāḥ /
'jñānādeva tu kaivalyaṃ' ityādayaḥ smṛtivādāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no other path' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.15), 'Not through action' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.3), and such are <s>śruti</s> statements. 'Liberation comes through knowledge alone,' and such are <s>smṛti</s> statements.

children.text: parākaroti śreyomārgāndbhraṃśayati /
children.translated_text: 'Abandons' (<s>parākaroti</s>) means: causes to fall from the path to the highest good.

children.text: ṛgvedādikaṃ nāma, iṣṭaṃ hutamiti karma, ayaṃ ca loka iti rūpam /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Ṛg Veda</s>' and such are names; '<s>iṣṭa</s>' (what is offered) and '<s>huta</s>' (what is oblated) are actions; and 'this world' is form.

children.text: prakriyā prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prakriyā</s>' (procedure) means a section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>).

children.text: pratijñāsiddher liṅgam āśmarathyaḥ | BBs_1,4.20 |
children.translated_text: Because it is an indicatory mark for the establishment of the proposition — [this is the view of] <s>Āśmarathya</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.20 |

children.text: astyatra pratijñā 'ātmani vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati' 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' iti ca /
children.translated_text: There is here a proposition: 'When the Self is known, all this becomes known' and 'All this is nothing but this Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6-7).

children.text: tasyāḥ pratijñāyāḥ siddhiṃ sūcayatyetalliṅgaṃ yatpriyasaṃsūcitasyātmano draṣṭavyatvādisaṃkīrtanam /
children.translated_text: This indicatory mark — namely, the mention of the Self indicated by dearness as 'to be seen' and such — points to the establishment of that proposition.

children.text: yadi hi vijñānātmā paramātmano 'nyaḥ syāttataḥ paramātmavijñāne 'pi vijñānātmā na vijñāta ityekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ yatpratijñātaṃ taddhīyeta /
children.translated_text: For if the individual knowing self were other than the supreme Self, then even upon the knowledge of the supreme Self, the individual knowing self would not be known — and thus the proposition that by one knowledge all is known would be undermined.

children.text: tasmātpratijñāsiddhyarthaṃ vijñānātmaparamātmanorabhedāṃśenopakramaṇamityāśmarathya ācāryo manyate // 20 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the opening with [a reference to] the non-difference of the individual knowing self and the supreme Self serves the purpose of establishing the proposition — so thinks the teacher <s>Āśmarathya</s>. // 20 //

children.text: utkramiṣyata evaṃ bhāvād ity auḍulomiḥ | BBs_1,4.21 |
children.translated_text: Because of the state of being about to depart — [this is the view of] <s>Auḍulomi</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.21 |

children.text: vijñānātmana eva dehendriyamanobuddhisaṃghātopādhisaṃparkātkaluṣībhūtasya jñānadhyānādisādhanānuṣṭhānāsaṃprasannasya dehādisaṃghātādutkramiṣyataḥ paramātmaikyopapatteridamabhedenopakramaṇamityauḍulomirācāryo manyate /
śrutiścaivaṃ bhavati- 'eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrātsamutthāya paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate' (chā. 8.12.3) iti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> states thus: 'This serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), rising from this body and reaching the supreme light, emerges in his own form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3).

children.text: kvacicca jīvāśrayamapi nāmarūpaṃ nadīnidarśanena jñāpayati- 'yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre 'staṃ gacchanti nāmarūpe vihāya /
children.translated_text: And in some places, [the text] shows through the illustration of rivers that names and forms too are dependent on the <s>jīva</s>: 'As flowing rivers, going toward the ocean, disappear, having abandoned name and form,

children.text: tathā vidvānnāmarūpādvimuktaḥ parātparaṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam' (muṇḍa. 3.2.8) iti /
children.translated_text: so the wise one, freed from name and form, reaches the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is beyond the beyond, the divine one' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.8).

children.text: yathā loke nadyaḥ svāśrayameva nāmarūpaṃ vihāya samudramupayantyevaṃ jīvo 'pi svāśrayameva nāmarūpaṃ vihāya paraṃ puruṣamupaitīti hi tatrārthaḥ pratīyate dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayostulyatāyai // 21 //
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, rivers, abandoning their own names and forms, reach the ocean — so too the <s>jīva</s>, abandoning its own names and forms, reaches the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>: this is the meaning understood there, for the sake of correspondence between the illustration and the thing illustrated. // 21 //

The individual knowing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), which has become turbid through contact with the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of the aggregate of body, sense-organs, mind, and intellect, and which has become purified through the practice of means such as knowledge and meditation — for such a self, about to depart from the aggregate of body and such, the opening with non-difference is fitting because of the propriety of [its] unity with the supreme Self — so thinks the teacher <s>Auḍulomi</s>.

children.text: FN: samutthānamutkrāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Rising' (<s>samutthāna</s>) means departure (<s>utkrānti</s>).

children.text: avasthiter iti kāśakṛtsnaḥ | BBs_1,4.22 |
children.translated_text: Because of abiding — [this is the view of] <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.22 |

children.text:
asyaiva paramātmano 'nenāpi vijñānātmabhāvenāvasthānādupapannamidamabhedenopakramaṇamiti kāśakṛtsna ācāryo manyate /
tathāca brāhmaṇam- 'anena jīvenātmanāmupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi' (chā. 6.3.2) ityevañjātīyakaṃ parasyaivātmano jīvabhāvenāvasthānaṃ darśayati /
mantravarṇaśca- 'sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vicitya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadanyadāste (tai.ā. 3.12.7) ityevañjātīyakāḥ /
naca tejaḥ prabhṛtīnāṃ sṛṣṭau jīvasya pṛthaksṛṣṭiḥ, śrutā, yena parasmādātmano 'nyastadvikāro jīvaḥ syāt /
kāśakṛtsnasyācāryasyāvikṛtaḥ parameśvaro jīvo nānya iti matam /
children.translated_text: This very supreme Self abides even in this form as the individual knowing self — and therefore the opening with non-difference is fitting: so thinks the teacher <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>. And thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]: 'Having entered with this living Self, let me manifest names and forms' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2) — such passages show the abiding of the supreme Self itself in the form of the <s>jīva</s>. And the <s>mantra</s> text: 'The wise one, having fashioned all forms and created all names, sits uttering [them]' (<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 3.12.7) — such [passages are] of this kind. And in the creation of fire and the rest, no separate creation of the <s>jīva</s> is heard [in <s>śruti</s>], by which the <s>jīva</s> would be a modification different from the supreme Self. The view of the teacher <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> is that the supreme Lord, unmodified, is the <s>jīva</s> — and not anything else.

children.text:
āśmarathyasya tu yadyapi jīvasya parasmādananyatvamabhipretaṃ, tathāpi pratijñāsiddheriti sāpekṣatvābhidhānātkāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ kiyānapyabhipreta iti gamyate /
auḍulomipakṣe punaḥ spaṣṭamevāvasthāntarāpekṣau bhedābhedau gamyete tatra kāśakṛtsnīyaṃ mataṃ śrutyanusārīti gamyate, pratipādayiṣitārthānusārāt 'tattvamasi' ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
evañca sati tajjñānādamṛtatvamavakalpate /
vikārātmakatve hi jīvasyābhyupagamyamāne vikārasya prakṛtisaṃbandhe pralayaprasaṅgānna tajjñānādamṛtamavakalpeta /
ataśca svāśrayasya nāmarūpasyāsaṃbhavādupādhyāśrayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ jīva upacaryate /
ata evotpattirapi jīvasya kvacidagnivisphuliṅgodāharaṇena śrāvyamāṇopādhyāśrayaiva veditavyā /
yadapyuktaṃ prakṛtasyaiva mahato bhūtasya draṣṭavyasya bhūtebhyaḥ samutthānaṃ vijñānātmabhāvena darśayanvijñānātmana evedaṃ draṣṭavyatvaṃ darśayatīti, tatrāpiyameva trisūtrī yojayitavyā /
'pratijñāsiddherliṅgamāśmarathyaḥ' /
idamatra pratijñātam- 'ātmani vidite sarvaṃ viditaṃ bhavati' 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' (bṛ. 2.4.6) iti ca /
upapāditaṃ ca, sarvasya nāmarūpakarmaprapañcasyaikaprasavatvādekapralayatvācca dundubhyādidṛṣṭāntaiśca kāryakāraṇayoravyatirekapratipādanāt /
tasyā eva pratijñāyāḥ siddhiṃ sūcatyetalliṅgaṃ yanmahato bhūtasya draṣṭavyasya bhūtebhyaḥ samutthānaṃ vijñānātmabhāvena kathitamityāśmarathya ācāryo manyate /
abhede hi satyekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ pratijñātamavakalpayata iti /
'utkramiṣyata evaṃbhāvādityauḍulomiḥ' /
utkramiṣyato vijñānātmano jñānadhyānādisāmarthyātsaṃprasannasya pareṇātmanaikyasaṃbhavādidamabhedābhidhānamityauḍulomirācāryo manyate /
'avasthiteriti kāśakṛtsnaḥ' /
asyaiva paramātmano 'nenāpi vijñānātmabhāvenāvasthānādupapannamidamabhedābhidhānamiti kāśakṛtsna ācāryo manyate /
children.translated_text: As for <s>Āśmarathya</s>, although the non-otherness of the <s>jīva</s> from the supreme Self is intended, nevertheless, because of the statement involving a dependent relation ('because it is an indicatory mark for the establishment of the proposition'), some degree of cause-effect relation is understood to be intended. In the position of <s>Auḍulomi</s>, however, difference and non-difference dependent on different states are clearly understood. In that case, the view of <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s> is understood to accord with <s>śruti</s>, because it follows the intended meaning — from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) and the like. And this being so, immortality through the knowledge of That becomes tenable. For if the <s>jīva</s> were accepted as being of the nature of a modification, then — because of the inevitable dissolution when the modification returns to its source — immortality through the knowledge of That would not be tenable. And therefore, since names and forms dependent on [the <s>jīva</s>'s] own nature are impossible, the names and forms dependent on limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) are figuratively attributed to the <s>jīva</s>. Hence, even the origination of the <s>jīva</s> that is heard in some places through the illustration of sparks from fire is to be understood as dependent on limiting adjuncts alone. As for what was said — that by showing the arising of the great being that is to be seen from the elements in the form of the individual knowing self, [the text] shows that this 'being to be seen' pertains to the individual knowing self — there too, this very triad of <s>sūtras</s> should be applied. 'Because it is an indicatory mark for the establishment of the proposition — <s>Āśmarathya</s>': Here this was promised — 'When the Self is known, all becomes known' and 'All this is nothing but this Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6). And it was demonstrated — because the entire elaboration of names, forms, and actions has a single origin and a single dissolution, and because of the establishment of the non-difference of cause and effect through the illustrations of the drum and such. This indicatory mark — namely, the statement that the great being that is to be seen arises from the elements in the form of the individual knowing self — points to the establishment of that very proposition: so thinks the teacher <s>Āśmarathya</s>. For if non-difference is true, then the proposition that by one knowledge all is known becomes tenable. 'Because of the state of being about to depart — <s>Auḍulomi</s>': For the individual knowing self that is about to depart, through the power of means such as knowledge and meditation, having become purified, the possibility of unity with the supreme Self [arises] — therefore this statement of non-difference: so thinks the teacher <s>Auḍulomi</s>. 'Because of abiding — <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>': This very supreme Self abides even in this form as the individual knowing self — and therefore this statement of non-difference is fitting: so thinks the teacher <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>.

children.text: nanūcchedābhidhānametat 'etebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tānyevānuvinaśyati na pretya saṃjñāsti' (bṛ. 2.4.12) iti, kathamedabhedābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: But is not this a statement of annihilation — 'Having arisen from these elements, it perishes along with them; after death there is no consciousness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.12)? How then is this a statement of non-difference?

naiṣa doṣaḥ /
viśeṣavijñānavināśābhiprāyametadvināśābhidhānaṃ nātmocchedābhiprāyam /

'sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1) 'ātmaivedaṃ sarvam' (chā. 7.25.2),' brahmaivedaṃ sarvam' (muṇḍa. 2.2.11), 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' (bṛ. 2.4.6), 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā'
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
This statement of destruction is intended as the destruction of particular cognition (<s>viśeṣavijñāna</s>), not intended as the annihilation of the Self.
Because, after being questioned — 'Here indeed, O revered one, you have bewildered me: after death there is no consciousness' — the <s>śruti</s> itself shows a different meaning: 'I do not speak of delusion; this Self is indeed indestructible, of the nature of non-annihilation — but its association with limiting adjuncts (<s>mātrā</s>) [ceases]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.12-13).
What is stated here amounts to this: This Self, which is a mass of consciousness (<s>vijñānaghana</s>), is eternally immutable (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>) — there is no possibility of its annihilation.
But its association with the limiting adjuncts (<s>mātrā</s>) — characterized as the elements and sense-organs, produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — ceases through knowledge.
And since, in the absence of that association, the particular cognition that was the subject [of discussion] is absent, it was said 'after death there is no consciousness.'
As for the objection that was raised — 'Since [the passage] concludes with the instrumental construction "by what means would one know the knower?" it should be understood as pertaining to the cognitive self (<s>vijñānātman</s>)' — that too must be resolved by the very same view of <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>.
Moreover, beginning with 'Where there is, as it were, duality, there one sees the other' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.13), [the <s>śruti</s>] elaborates the particular cognition — characterized by seeing and such — of that very [Self] in the domain of <s>avidyā</s>, and then with 'But where everything has become the Self alone, then by what and whom would one see?' and such, it states the absence of that very particular cognition — characterized by seeing and such — in the domain of knowledge.
And again, anticipating the doubt that even in the absence of objects one might know the Self, it says 'By what means would one know the knower?'
Therefore, since the sentence is devoted to establishing the absence of particular cognition, it is understood that the root '<s>jñā</s>' (to know) alone, in its bare form, is indicated by the agent-denoting suffix '<s>tṛ</s>' — following the convention of previously established usage in the agent sense.
And the scriptural basis of <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>'s view has been shown previously.
Therefore, the difference between the cognitive self (<s>vijñānātman</s>) and the supreme Self — due to the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of body and such, constructed by the superimposition of name-and-form through <s>avidyā</s> — is not ultimate; this meaning must be accepted by all <s>Vedānta</s> teachers.
Because of <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning, one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1), 'The Self alone is all this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2), '<s>Brahman</s> alone is all this' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.11), 'All this is the Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6), 'There is no other seer than this'

(bṛ. 3.7.23), 'nānyadato 'sti draṣṭṛ' (bṛ. 3.8.11) ityevaṃrūpābhyaḥ śrutibhyaḥ /
smṛtibhyaśca 'vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti' (gī. 7.19), 'kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata' (gī. 13.2), 'samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram' (gī. 13.27) ityevaṃrūpābhyaḥ /

śthitaprajñalakṣaṇasmṛteśca (gī. 2.54) /
sthite ca kṣetrajñaparamātmaikatvaviṣaya samyagdarśane kṣetrajñaḥ paramātmeti nāmamātrabhaidāt, kṣetrajño 'yaṃ paramātmano bhinnaḥ paramātmāyaṃ kṣetrajñādbhinna ityevañjātīyaka ātmabhaidaviṣayo nirbandho nirarthakaḥ /

yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyām' (tai. 2.1) iti kāñcidevaikāṃ guhāmadhikṛtyaitaduktam /

children.translated_text: And there is no other [entity] besides <s>Brahman</s> hidden in the cave, because the <s>śruti</s> states the entry of the creator himself: 'Having created it, he entered into that very [creation]' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6).

children.text: ye tu nirbandhaṃ kurvanti te vedāntārthaṃ bādhamānāḥ śreyodvāraṃ samyagdarśanameva bādhante /
children.translated_text: But those who persist [in maintaining difference] — negating the meaning of the <s>Vedānta</s> — obstruct right vision itself, which is the door to the highest good.

children.text: kṛtakamanityaṃ ca mokṣaṃ kalpayanti /
children.translated_text: And they conceive of liberation as something produced and therefore impermanent.

children.text: nyāyena ca na saṃgacchanta iti // 22 //
children.translated_text: And they do not accord with reason. // 22 //

(<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23), 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11) — from <s>śruti</s> passages of this kind.
And from <s>smṛti</s> passages such as: '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is all' (<s>Gītā</s> 7.19), 'Know me also as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower) in all fields, O <s>Bhārata</s>' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.2), 'The supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings' (<s>Gītā</s> 13.27) — from <s>smṛti</s> passages of this kind.
And because the vision of difference is negated: 'He who [thinks] "that one is other, I am other" — he does not know; he is like an animal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10), 'He goes from death to death who sees, as it were, multiplicity here' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.19) — from passages of this kind.
And because all modifications are negated in the Self: 'This great, unborn Self — ageless, undying, immortal, fearless — is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.25).
And otherwise, for those seeking liberation, the attainment of uncontradicted knowledge (<s>nirapavāda-vijñāna</s>) would be impossible, and the attainment of firmly ascertained meaning would be impossible.
For uncontradicted knowledge — which removes all further inquiry — pertaining to the Self, is desired; and because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'Those whose understanding is firmly ascertained through <s>Vedānta</s> knowledge' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.6).
And: 'What delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who sees oneness?' (<s>Īśā</s> 7).
And because of the <s>smṛti</s> describing the characteristics of one of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>) (<s>Gītā</s> 2.54).
And when right vision — whose content is the oneness of <s>kṣetrajña</s> and supreme Self — is established, since the <s>kṣetrajña</s> and the supreme Self differ only in name, the insistence on the topic of difference in the Self — [claiming] 'this <s>kṣetrajña</s> is different from the supreme Self, the supreme Self is different from the <s>kṣetrajña</s>' — is pointless.
For this Self is one; it is spoken of in many ways merely through difference of names.
For [the passage] 'True, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>; he who knows it as hidden in the cave' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1) — this is not said with reference to some one particular cave;

children.text: mohaṃ mohakaraṃ vākyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Moha</s>' means a statement that causes delusion.

children.text: ucchittirnāśastadvānna bhavitītyanucchittidharmā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ucchitti</s>' means destruction; one whose nature is that it does not occur is '<s>anuccchittidharmā</s>' (of the nature of non-annihilation).

children.text: kāñcit jīvasthānādanyām /
children.translated_text: [The cave is] some [cave] other than the abode of the individual self (<s>jīva</s>).

children.text: ye tu āśmarathyaprabhṛtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those' [refers to teachers] such as <s>Āśmarathya</s> and others.

children.text: prakṛtyadhikaraṇam / sū. 23-27

children.text: prakṛtiś ca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhāt | BBs_1,4.23 |

evaṃ pratijñādṛṣṭāntau śrautau noparudhyete /
pratijñā tāvat- 'uta tamādeśamaprākṣyo yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavatyamataṃ matamavijñātaṃ vijñātam' (chā. 6.1.2) iti /
tatra caikena vijñātena sarvamandavijñātamapi vijñātaṃ bhavatīti pratīyate /
taccopādānakāraṇavijñāne sarvavijñānaṃ saṃbhavatyupādānakāraṇavyatirekātkāryasya /
nimittakāraṇāvyatirekāstu kāryasya nāsti, loke takṣṇaḥ prāsādavyatirekadarśanāt /
dṛṣṭānto 'pi yathā 'somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syādvācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyam' ityupādānakāraṇagocara evamāmnāyate /
tathā 'ekena lohamaṇinā sarvaṃ lohamayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt' 'ekena nakhanikṛntanena sarvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt' (chā. 6.1.4,5,6) iti ca /
tathānyatrāpi 'kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati (muṇḍa. 1.1.2) iti pratijñā /
'yathā pṛthivyāmoṣadhayaḥ saṃbhavanti' ( muṇḍa. 1.1.7) iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
tathā 'ātmani kalvare dṛṣṭe śrute mate vijñāta idaṃ sarvaṃ viditam' iti pratijñā /
'sa yathā dundubherhanyamānasya na bāhyāñśabdāñśaknuyādgrahaṇāya dundubhestu grahaṇena dundubhyāghātasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ' (bṛ. 4.5.6,7) iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
evaṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ prativedāntaṃ pratijñādṛṣṭāntau prakṛtitvasādhanau pratyetavyau /
yata itīyaṃ pañcamī 'yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante' ityatra 'janikartuḥ prakṛtiḥ' (pā.sū. 1.4.30) iti viśeṣasmaraṇātprakṛtilakṣaṇa evāpādāne draṣṭavyā /
nimittatvaṃ tvadhiṣṭhātrantarābhāvādadhigantavyam /

yathā hi loke mṛtsuvarṇādikamupādānakāraṇaṃ kulālasuvarṇakārādīnadhiṣṭhātṛnapekṣya pravartate naivaṃ brahmaṇa upādānakāraṇasya sato 'nyo 'dhiṣṭhātāpekṣyo 'sti, prāgutpatterekamevādvitīyamityavadhāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: For just as in the world, the material cause — clay, gold, and such — does not operate without depending on a superintendent such as a potter, goldsmith, and such, so too, since <s>Brahman</s> as material cause has no other superintendent to depend on — because of the determination 'before creation, [there was] one only, without a second.'

children.text: adhiṣṭhātrantarābhāvo 'pi pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhādevodito veditavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The absence of another superintendent too should be understood as stated precisely because of the non-contradiction of the declaration and illustration.

children.text: adhiṣṭhātari hyupādānādanyasminnabhyupagamyamāne punarapyekavijñānena sarvavijñānasyāsaṃbhavātpratijñādṛṣṭāntoparodha eva syāt /
children.translated_text: For if another superintendent different from the material cause were accepted, then the impossibility of knowledge of everything through the knowledge of one thing would again [arise], and there would be a contradiction of the declaration and illustration.

children.text: tasmādadhiṣṭhātrantarābhāvādātmanaḥ kartṛtvamupādānāntarābhāvācca prakṛtitvam // 23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the absence of another superintendent, the Self has agency; and because of the absence of another material cause, [the Self has] the nature of material cause. // 23 //

Just as <s>dharma</s> is to be inquired into because it is the cause of worldly prosperity, so <s>Brahman</s> is to be inquired into because it is the cause of the highest good — thus it was stated.
And <s>Brahman</s> was defined as 'that from which the origin and so forth of this [world proceed]' (<s>Bra</s>. 1.1.2).
That definition applies equally whether [<s>Brahman</s> is] the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) — as clay is to pots and bracelets — or merely the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) — as a potter or goldsmith — hence the doubt arises: What is the nature of <s>Brahman</s>'s causality?
There, it initially appears that [<s>Brahman</s>] is merely the efficient cause alone.
Why?
Because [scripture] states that [<s>Brahman</s>] acts after deliberation (<s>īkṣā</s>).
For <s>Brahman</s>'s agency is understood as preceded by deliberation — from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'It deliberated' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.3), 'It created <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.4), and others.
And agency preceded by deliberation is seen only in efficient causes such as potters and such.
And in the world, the accomplishment of the result of an action is seen to be preceded by many factors of action.
And it is reasonable to transfer that principle even to the primordial agent.
And because lordship is well-established.
For of lords such as kings, <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Manu</s>), and others, only efficient causality is understood; likewise, it is reasonable to understand only efficient causality for the supreme Lord.
And this world-effect is seen to be composite, insentient, and impure; its cause too must be of the same kind, because similarity between cause and effect is observed.
But <s>Brahman</s> is not understood to have such characteristics — from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'Without parts, without activity, tranquil, without fault, without stain' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.19).
By the process of elimination, one must accept some other material cause of <s>Brahman</s> — possessing qualities of impurity and such — well-known in <s>smṛti</s> [i.e., <s>Pradhāna</s>].
[This is] because the <s>śruti</s> statements of <s>Brahman</s>'s causality culminate merely in efficient causality — thus [runs the objection].
Having set forth this [objection], we say: <s>Brahman</s> must be accepted as both the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>, the material source) and the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>).
Not merely as the efficient cause alone.
Why?
Because of the non-contradiction of the declaration (<s>pratijñā</s>) and the illustration (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>).
Thus, the declaration and illustration, both being scriptural, are not contradicted.
The declaration is: 'Have you asked for that instruction by which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.2).
There, it is understood that by knowing one thing, everything — even what was not known — becomes known.
And [such] knowledge of everything is possible only when [<s>Brahman</s> is] the material cause, because the effect does not differ from the material cause.
But because the effect does differ from the efficient cause, [such comprehensive knowledge] does not follow — since in the world, the carpenter is seen as distinct from the palace.
The illustration too — 'O dear one, just as by one lump of clay, everything made of clay becomes known; the modification is merely a name, a verbal handle; clay alone is the reality' — is taught as pertaining to the material cause.
Likewise: 'By one gold ornament, everything made of gold becomes known,' 'By one nail-cutter, everything made of iron becomes known' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.4-6).
Similarly elsewhere: 'O revered one, by knowing what does all this become known?' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.2) — this is the declaration.
'Just as from the earth, herbs are born' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.7) — this is the illustration.
Likewise: 'When the Self is seen, heard, thought upon, and known, all this is known' — this is the declaration.
'Just as one cannot grasp the external sounds of a drum being beaten, but by grasping the drum or the beater of the drum, the sound is grasped' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6-7) — this is the illustration.
Thus, in each <s>Vedānta</s> [text], the declaration and illustration should be understood as establishing material causality, as the case may be.
The fifth case ending in 'from which these beings are born' — since <s>Pāṇini</s> specifically remembers 'the source of the agent of production [takes the fifth case]' (<s>Pāṇini Sūtra</s> 1.4.30) — should be understood as the ablative denoting the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>).
But efficient causality is to be understood from the absence of another superintendent.

children.text: kutaścātmanaḥ kartṛtvaprakṛtitve-
children.translated_text: And for what further reason does the Self have both agency and the nature of material cause?

children.text: FN: vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Vimarśa</s>' means doubt.

children.text: niṣkalaṃ niravayavam, niṣkriyamacalam, śāntamapariṇāmi, niravadyaṃ nirastasamastadoṣam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Niṣkala</s>' means without parts; '<s>niṣkriya</s>' means unmoving; '<s>śānta</s>' means without transformation; '<s>niravadya</s>' means free from all defects.

children.text: lohaṃ suvarṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Loha</s>' means gold.

children.text: nakhanikṛntanaṃ kārṣṇāyasakṛtanakhalavanaśastraṃ lohapiṇḍo vā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nakhanikṛntana</s>' means a nail-cutting instrument made of iron, or a lump of iron.

children.text: dundubhyāghātasya janakasya janyatayā saṃbandhī vā śabdo viśeṣaśabda ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sound of the drum-beater' — meaning, the sound related [to the beater] as effect to cause; or [it means] a particular kind of sound.

children.text: abhidhyopadeśāc ca | BBs_1,4.24 |
children.translated_text: Because of the teaching of deliberation (<s>abhidhyā</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.24 |

children.text: abhidhyopadeśaścātmanaḥ kartṛtvaprakṛtitve gamayati 'so 'kāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti' 'tadaikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya' iti ca /
children.translated_text: The teaching of deliberation also establishes the Self's agency and material causality: 'It desired: "May I become many, may I be born forth"' and 'It deliberated: "May I become many, may I be born forth."'

children.text: tatrābhidhyānapūrvikāyāḥ svātantryapravṛtteḥ karteti gamyate /
children.translated_text: Therein, from the autonomous activity preceded by deliberation, it is understood that [<s>Brahman</s>] is the agent.

children.text: bahu syāmiti pratyagātmaviṣayatvādbahubhavanābhidhyānasyaprakṛtirityapi gamyate // 24 //
children.translated_text: And because the deliberation of becoming many pertains to one's own inner Self — 'May I become many' — it is also understood that [<s>Brahman</s>] is the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>). // 24 //

children.text: FN: abhidhyā sṛṣṭisaṃkalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Abhidhyā</s>' means the intention of creation.

children.text: sākṣāc cobhayāmnānāt | BBs_1,4.25 |
children.translated_text: And because both [origination and dissolution] are directly stated (<s>sākṣāt</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.25 |

children.text:
prakṛtitvasyāyamabhyuccayaḥ /
itaśca prakṛtirbrahma, yatkāraṇaṃ sākṣādbrahmaiva kāraṇamupādāyobhau prabhavapralayāvāmnāyate- 'sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyākāśādeva samutpadyante /
ākāśaṃ pratyastaṃ yanti' (chā. 1.9.1) iti /
yaddhi yasmātprabhavati yasmiṃśca pralīyate tattasyopādānaṃ prasiddham /
children.translated_text: For that from which something originates and into which it dissolves — that is well-known as its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>).

children.text: yathā vrīhiyavādīnāṃ pṛthivī /
children.translated_text: Just as the earth is [the material cause] of rice, barley, and such.

children.text: sākṣādite sākṣāditi copādānāntarānupādānaṃ darśayatyākāśādeveti /
children.translated_text: And the word 'directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>) — repeated as 'directly' — shows that there is no other material cause taken up, [as indicated by] 'from space alone.'

children.text: pratyastamayaśca nopādānādanyatra kāryasya dṛṣṭaḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: And dissolution is not seen [to occur] in anything other than the material cause of an effect. // 25 //

children.text: FN: abhyuccayo hetvantaram /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Abhyuccaya</s>' means an additional argument.

children.text: ātmakṛteḥ pariṇāmāt | BBs_1,4.26 |
children.translated_text: Because of self-making — [that is,] because of transformation. | <s>BBs</s> 1,4.26 |

children.text:
itaśca prakṛtirbrahma, yatkāraṇaṃ brahmaprakriyāyām 'tadātmānaṃ svayamakuruta' (tai. 2.7) ityātmanaḥ karmatvaṃ kartṛtvaṃ ta darśayati /
ātmānamiti karmatvaṃ, svayamakuruteti kartṛtvam /
kathaṃ punaḥ pūrvasiddhasya sataḥ kartṛtvena vyavasthitasya kriyamāṇatvaṃ śakyaṃ saṃpādayitum /
pariṇāmāditi brūmaḥ /
pūrvasiddho 'pi hi sannātmā viśeṣeṇa vikārātmanā pariṇamayāmāsātmānamiti /
vikārātmanā ca pariṇāmo mṛdādyāsu prakṛtiṣūpalabdhaḥ /
svayamiti ca viśeṣaṇānnimittāntarānapekṣatvamapi pratīyate /
children.translated_text: And by the qualifying word 'by Himself,' independence from any other instrumental cause is also understood.

children.text: pariṇāmāditi vā pṛthaksūtram /
children.translated_text: Or, '<s>pariṇāmāt</s>' (because of transformation) is a separate <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: tasyaiṣor'thaḥ - itaśca prakṛtirbrahma, yatkāraṇaṃ brahmaṇa eva vikārātmanā pariṇāmaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyenāmnāyate 'sacca tyaccābhavat /
children.translated_text: Its meaning is as follows: And for this further reason <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause, because the transformation of <s>Brahman</s> itself in the form of modifications is taught through co-referential predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>): 'It became the existent (<s>sat</s>) and the beyond (<s>tyat</s>),

children.text: niruktaṃ cāniruktaṃ ca' (tai. 2.6) ityādineti // 26 //
children.translated_text: the defined and the undefined' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6) and so on. // 26 //

And for this further reason <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>): because, in the context of the <s>Brahman</s>-discussion, [the <s>śruti</s>] 'He made Himself by Himself' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7) shows the Self as both the object and the agent of action. 'Himself' indicates objecthood; 'made by Himself' indicates agenthood. But how can one who is already established and determined as the agent be made into something that is being acted upon? We say: through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). For even though the Self is already established, He transformed Himself specifically in the form of modifications — and transformation in the form of modifications is observed in material causes such as clay and the like.

children.text: FN: sat pratyakṣaṃ bhūtatrayam, tyat parokṣaṃ bhūtadvayam, niruktaṃ vaktuṃ śakyaṃ ghaṭādi, aniruktaṃ vaktumaśakyaṃ kapotarūpādikam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Sat</s>' — the perceptible three elements; '<s>tyat</s>' — the imperceptible two elements; '<s>nirukta</s>' — what can be expressed, such as a pot; '<s>anirukta</s>' — what cannot be expressed, such as a pigeon-colored form.

children.text: yoniś ca hi gīyate | BBs_1,4.27 |
children.translated_text: <s>Yoniś ca hi gīyate</s> — And because [<s>Brahman</s>] is celebrated as the source (<s>yoni</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.27 |

children.text:
itaśca prakṛtirbrahma yonirityapi paṭhyate vedānteṣu 'kartāramīśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim' (muṇḍa. 3.1.3) iti, 'yadbhūtayoni paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ' (muṇḍa. 1.16) iti ca /
yoniśabdaśca prakṛtivacanaḥ samadhigato loke 'pṛthivī yoniroṣadhivanaspatīnām' iti /
strīyonerapyastyevāyavadvāreṇa garbhaṃ pratyupādānakāraṇatvam /
kacitsthānavacano 'pi yoniśabdo dṛṣṭaḥ - 'yoniṣṭa indra niṣade akāri' (ṛ.saṃ. 1.104.1) iti /
vākyaśeṣāttvatra prakṛtivacanatā parigṛhyate 'yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhyate ca' (muṇḍa. 1.1.7) ityevañjātīyakāt /
evaṃ prakṛtitvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prasiddham /
yatpunaridamuktamīkṣāpūrvakaṃ kartṛtvaṃ nimittakāraṇeṣveva kulālādiṣu loke dṛṣṭaṃ nopādāneṣvityādi, tatpratyucyate- na lokavadiha bhavitavyam /
nahyayamanumānagamyor'thaḥ /
children.translated_text: For this matter is not the object of inference or [ordinary] perception.

children.text: śabdagamyatvāttvasyārthasya yathāśabdamiha bhavitavyam /
children.translated_text: Rather, since this matter is to be known through scripture (<s>śabda</s>), one must proceed here in accordance with scripture.

children.text: śabdaścekṣiturīśvarasya prakṛtitvaṃ pratidayatātyavocāma /
children.translated_text: And we have already stated that scripture teaches the material-cause-hood of the seeing Lord.

children.text: punaścaitatsarvaṃ vistareṇa prativakṣyāmaḥ // 27 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, we shall refute all this again in detail later. // 27 //

And for this further reason <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause: because it is also read as the source (<s>yoni</s>) in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts — 'the maker, the Lord, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the womb of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.3), and 'what the wise ones perceive as the womb of beings' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.6). And the word '<s>yoni</s>' is understood in common usage as denoting a material cause: 'the earth is the source of herbs and trees.' Even a woman's womb has the nature of being a material cause with respect to the embryo, through the medium of its parts. The word '<s>yoni</s>' is also seen sometimes as denoting a mere location — 'O <s>Indra</s>, a seat (<s>yoni</s>) has been made for you to sit' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 1.104.1). But here, the meaning of 'material cause' is adopted because of the remainder of the sentence: 'As a spider projects and withdraws' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.7) and similar passages. Thus, the status of <s>Brahman</s> as the material cause is well established. Now, as for the objection that was raised — that deliberate agenthood preceded by seeing (<s>īkṣā</s>) is observed in the world only in efficient causes like the potter, not in material causes — to that we reply: it need not be as in the world here.

children.text: FN: kartāraṃ kriyāśaktimantam, īśaṃ niyantāram, puruṣaṃ pratyañcam, brahma pūrṇam, yoniṃ prakṛtim /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Kartāram</s>' — possessing the power of action; '<s>īśam</s>' — the controller; '<s>puruṣam</s>' — the inner one; '<s>brahma</s>' — the complete; '<s>yonim</s>' — the material cause.

children.text: he indra, te tava niṣade upaveśanāya yoniḥ sthānaṃ mayā akāri kṛtam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, a seat (<s>yoni</s>) — a place for sitting — has been made for you by me.

children.text: 8 sarvavyākhyānādhikaraṇam / sū. 28
children.translated_text: Section 8: <s>Sarvavyākhyānādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 28

children.text: etena sarve vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ | BBs_1,4.28 |
children.translated_text: <s>Etena sarve vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ</s> — By this, all [rival theories] are explained [i.e., refuted] — explained. | <s>BBs</s> 1.4.28 |

children.text: 'īkṣaternāśabdam' (bra.sū. 1.1.5) ityārabhya pradhānakāraṇavādaḥ sūtraireva punaḥ punarāśaṅkya nirākṛtaḥ,
children.translated_text: Beginning with 'Because of seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>), [it is] not the non-verbal [<s>Pradhāna</s>]' (<s>BBs</s> 1.1.5), the doctrine of <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause has been repeatedly raised as an objection through the <s>sūtras</s> and refuted.

children.text:
tasya hi pakṣasyopodbalakāni kānicilliṅgābhāsāni vedānteṣvāpātena mandamatīnpratibhāntīti /
sa ca kāryakāraṇananyatvābhyupagamātpratyāsanno vedāntavādasya /
devalaprabhṛtibhiśca kaiściddharmasūtrakāraiḥ svagrantheṣvāśritaḥ, tena tatpratiṣedhe yatno 'tīva kṛto nāṇvādikāraṇavādapratiṣedhe /
te 'pi tu brahmakāraṇavādapakṣasya pratipakṣatvātpratiṣeddhavyāḥ /
teṣāmapyupodvalakaṃ vaidikaṃ kiñcilliṅgamāpātena mandamatīnprati bhāyāditi /
children.translated_text: For there may be some Vedic apparent indicator that, at first glance, appears to the dull-witted to support them too.

children.text: ataḥ pradhānamallanibarhaṇanyāyenātidiśati- etena pradhānakāraṇavādapratiṣedhanyāyakalāpena sarve 'ṇvādikāraṇavādā api pratiṣiddhatayā vyākhyātā veditavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] extends [the refutation] by the principle of 'defeating the chief wrestler': by this system of reasoning that refutes the <s>Pradhāna</s>-as-cause doctrine, all the doctrines of atoms and such as the cause are also to be understood as refuted — as [already] explained.

children.text: teṣāmapi pradhānavadaśabdatvācchabdavirodhitvācceti /
children.translated_text: For they too, like <s>Pradhāna</s>, are non-scriptural (<s>aśabda</s>) and contrary to scripture.

children.text: vyākhyātā vyākhyātā iti padābhyāso 'dhyāyaparisamāptiṃ dyotayati // 28 //
children.translated_text: The repetition of the word 'explained, explained' (<s>vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ</s>) indicates the conclusion of the chapter. // 28 //

For there are certain apparent indicators (<s>liṅgābhāsa</s>) in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts that at first glance appear to the dull-witted to support that position. And that [<s>Sāṃkhya</s>] doctrine is close to the <s>Vedānta</s> position because of the acceptance of the non-difference of effect from cause. And it has been adopted in their own works by certain <s>dharmasūtra</s>-authors beginning with <s>Devala</s>. Therefore, great effort has been made to refute it, and not [as much] to refute the doctrine of atoms and such as the cause. But those [atomic theories] too must be refuted, because they are counter-positions to the doctrine of <s>Brahman</s> as the cause.

children.translated_text: In the first <s>adhyāya</s>, it was established through the demonstration of the harmonization of <s>Vedānta</s> passages that the omniscient, all-ruling [<s>Brahman</s>] is the originating cause of the world — like clay, gold, and such for pots, ornaments, and the like; that it is the sustaining cause of the world once produced, by being its controller — like a magician of his illusion; and that it is the cause of the re-absorption of the projected world back into its own Self — like the earth of the fourfold class of beings. And that It alone is the Self of all. And the doctrines of <s>Pradhāna</s> and such as the cause were refuted on the ground of being non-scriptural. Now, to accomplish the removal of contradiction from <s>smṛti</s> and reasoning with respect to one's own position, to show that the rival doctrines of <s>Pradhāna</s> and such are supported only by pseudo-reasoning, and to demonstrate the non-discordance of the creation-processes across the various <s>Vedānta</s> texts — for the establishment of this body of meaning, the second <s>adhyāya</s> is commenced. Therein, first raising the objection from <s>smṛti</s>-contradiction and then resolving it —

children.translated_text: What was said — that <s>Brahman</s> alone, the omniscient, is the cause of the world — that is improper. Why? Because of the fault of leaving no scope for <s>smṛti</s>. The <s>smṛti</s> called the <s>Tantra</s> [i.e., <s>Sāṃkhya</s>], composed by the supreme <s>ṛṣi</s>, accepted by the learned, and the other <s>smṛtis</s> that follow it — would, in that case, be rendered scopeless. For in those [texts], the insentient <s>Pradhāna</s>, independently, is posited as the cause of the world. The <s>smṛtis</s> of <s>Manu</s> and others, at least, have scope because they fulfill the purpose required by the body of <s>dharma</s> characterized by the Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) of <s>agnihotra</s> and such — [specifying] for this <s>varṇa</s>, at this time, such is the procedure — investiture (<s>upanayana</s>), such is the conduct, such is the study of the <s>Veda</s>, such is the union with a wife. And they prescribe the various <s>dharmas</s> of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> as human goals. But there is no scope for the <s>smṛtis</s> of <s>Kapila</s> and others in the domain of things to be practiced. For they were composed with reference solely to right knowledge as the means to liberation. If they too were rendered scopeless, the very purposelessness of those [<s>smṛtis</s>] would follow. Therefore, the <s>Vedānta</s> texts should be interpreted in a way that does not contradict them. But how can the meaning of <s>śruti</s> — ascertained through reasons such as 'seeing' (<s>īkṣati</s>) and the like as [establishing] that the omniscient <s>Brahman</s> alone is the cause of the world — be again challenged by the fault of leaving no scope for <s>smṛti</s>? This challenge may well be [raised] by those of independent intellect. But people of dependent intellect, for the most part unable to ascertain the meaning of <s>śruti</s> independently, would rely on <s>smṛtis</s> with well-known authors. And on their strength, they would seek to determine the meaning of <s>śruti</s>. And they would not trust our explanation, out of great respect for the authors of the <s>smṛtis</s>. And the unobstructed <s>ṛṣi</s>-knowledge of <s>Kapila</s> and others is traditionally remembered. And there is a <s>śruti</s>: 'He who first creates <s>Brahmā</s>, and who delivers the knowledge to him — to that God who is <s>Kapila</s>, born at the beginning, whom one would see being born and sustained by knowledge' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 5.2). Therefore, it is impossible to suppose that their view is not in accordance with truth. And they establish their position with the support of reasoning. Therefore, too, the <s>Vedānta</s> texts should be interpreted on the strength of <s>smṛti</s> — this is the re-challenge. To this, the resolution is: 'No — because there would be the fault of leaving no scope for other <s>smṛtis</s>.' If the doctrine of the Lord as cause were challenged by the fault of leaving no scope for <s>smṛti</s>, then even so, other <s>smṛtis</s> that teach the Lord as the cause would be rendered scopeless. We shall cite them: Having introduced the supreme <s>Brahman</s> with 'That which is subtle, unknowable,' and having said 'For He is called the inner Self of beings, the <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field)' — [the <s>smṛti</s>] says: 'From that arose the unmanifest, possessed of three <s>guṇas</s>, O best of the twice-born.' And elsewhere too: 'The unmanifest dissolves into the <s>Puruṣa</s>, O <s>Brahman</s>, the qualityless one.' 'And hear this summary from me: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the ancient, is all this. He creates everything at the time of creation and devours it again at the time of dissolution' — thus in the <s>Purāṇa</s>. And in the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>: 'I am the origin and dissolution of the entire world' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 7.6). And <s>Āpastamba</s> too reads the supreme Self as the material cause: 'From Him all bodies originate; He is the root, the eternal, the permanent' (<s>Āpastamba Dharmasūtra</s> 1.8.23.2). Thus, in numerous <s>smṛtis</s> too, the Lord is declared as the cause and as the material source. To one who takes his stand on the strength of <s>smṛti</s>, we shall reply on the strength of <s>smṛti</s> itself — hence this raising of the fault of leaving no scope for other <s>smṛtis</s>. But the purport of the <s>śrutis</s> toward the doctrine of the Lord as cause has already been demonstrated. And when there is a conflict among <s>smṛtis</s>, and one or the other must necessarily be accepted and the other rejected, those <s>smṛtis</s> that follow <s>śruti</s> are authoritative, and the others are to be disregarded. As stated in the definition of valid means of knowledge: 'In case of conflict, [the <s>smṛti</s>] that is not [supported by <s>śruti</s>] should be disregarded — for there is [merely] inference [behind it]' (<s>Jaimini Sūtra</s> 1.3.3). And it is impossible to suppose that anyone can apprehend supersensible matters without <s>śruti</s>, because there is no basis [for such apprehension].

No. Because even perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) is dependent [on something else]. For perfection depends on the practice of <s>dharma</s>. And that <s>dharma</s> is characterized by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>). Therefore, the meaning of the previously established <s>codanā</s> cannot be called into doubt on the basis of the words of a subsequently perfected person. And even if one were to resort to the authority of perfected beings — since there are many perfected beings — when there is a conflict of <s>smṛtis</s>, as demonstrated, there is no means of resolution other than resorting to <s>śruti</s>. Even for one of dependent intellect, a partisan attachment to a particular <s>smṛti</s> without reason is not proper. For if someone were to be partial to any [arbitrary] view, then — because of the diversity of human opinions — there would follow the failure to establish any truth whatsoever. Therefore, for such a person too, by presenting the conflict among <s>smṛtis</s> and by discriminating the domain where <s>smṛti</s> follows [<s>śruti</s>], the intellect should be gathered onto the right path. And the <s>śruti</s> that was cited as showing the pre-eminence of <s>Kapila</s>'s knowledge — on the basis of that, the <s>Kāpila</s> doctrine, even though it contradicts <s>śruti</s>, cannot be credited — because the word '<s>Kāpila</s>' is merely a general term [that could refer to anyone named <s>Kapila</s>]. And because there is a tradition of another <s>Kapila</s> — named <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who scorched the sons of <s>Sagara</s>.
