evaṃ viśvabhujādau yojyam /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: 'In the second [<s>adhyāya</s>], non-contradiction with <s>smṛti</s> and reasoning, and the unsoundness of other [doctrines]; consistency with <s>śruti</s> regarding elements and the enjoyer, and non-contradiction even with indicatory-mark <s>śruti</s>' — this is the summary verse.
'The supreme sage' is <s>Kapila</s>.
'Others' are those composed by <s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and others.
'They would understand the <s>śruti</s>'s meaning figuratively' — this is the sense.
'Subtlety' means being beyond the senses.
'Unknowability' means inaccessibility to other means of knowledge.
'Bodies' means <s>Brahmā</s> and others.
'Eternal' means immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>).
When there is contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, the authority of <s>smṛti</s> is to be disregarded without consideration.
'For' — because in the absence of contradiction, <s>śruti</s> serves as inference.
'Of the burner' [means] of the one who heats.
'<s>Viśvamūrdhā</s>' [means] His heads are everywhere because He alone is reflected everywhere.
The same should be applied to '<s>viśvabhuja</s>' and so forth.

children.text: kutaśca smṛtyanavakāśaprasaṅgo na doṣaḥ -
children.translated_text: And for what other reason is the consequence that <s>smṛti</s> has no scope not a defect?

children.text: itareṣāṃ cānupalabdheḥ | BBs_2,1.2 |
children.translated_text: And because of the non-apprehension of the others. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.2 |

children.text: pradhānāditarāṇi yāni pradhānapariṇāmatvaṃ na samṛtau kalpitāni mahadādīni na tāni vede loke vopalabhyante /
children.translated_text: Those [entities] other than <s>Pradhāna</s>, such as <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, which are postulated in the <s>Smṛti</s> as being transformations of <s>Pradhāna</s> — those are not apprehended either in the <s>Veda</s> or in ordinary experience.

children.text:
bhūtendriyāṇi tāvallokavedaprasiddhatvācchakyante smartum /
alokavedaprasiddhatvāttu mahadādīnāṃ ṣaṣṭhasyevendriyārthasya na smṛtiravakalpate /
yadapi kvacittatparamiva śravaṇamavabhāsate tadapyatatparaṃ vyākhyātam 'ānumānikamapyekeṣām' (bra. 1.4.1) ityatra /
children.translated_text: Even where the <s>śruti</s> appears to speak of something as referring to those [Sāṃkhya categories], that too has been explained as not having that purport, in the section on '<s>Ānumānikam apy ekeṣām</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.4.1).

children.text: kāryasmṛteraprāmāṇyātkāraṇasmṛterapyaprāmāṇyaṃ yuktamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is: since the <s>smṛti</s> of the effect is without authority, it is reasonable that the <s>smṛti</s> of the cause too is without authority.

children.text: tasmādapi na smṛtyanavakāśaprasaṅgo doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this standpoint also, the consequence that <s>smṛti</s> has no scope is not a defect.

children.text: tarkāvaṣṭambhaṃ tu 'na vilakṣaṇatvāt' (bra. 2.1.4) ityārabhyonmathiṣyati // 2 //
children.translated_text: As for the reliance on reasoning, that will be demolished beginning from '<s>Na vilakṣaṇatvāt</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.1.4). // 2 //

The elements and sense organs, being well known in both ordinary experience and the <s>Veda</s>, can be remembered [in <s>smṛti</s>].
But because <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, being the sixth [category] like the sense-objects, are not well known in ordinary experience or the <s>Veda</s>, <s>smṛti</s> regarding them is not warranted.

children.text: 2 yogapratyuktyadhikaraṇam / sū. 3
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Yogapratyukti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Refutation of <s>Yoga</s>) / <s>Sūtra</s> 3

children.text: etena yogaḥ pratyuktaḥ | BBs_2,1.3 |
children.translated_text: By this, <s>Yoga</s> [too] is refuted. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.3 |

children.text:
etena sāṃkhyasmṛtipratyākhyānena yogasmṛtirapi pratyākhyātā draṣṭavyetyatidiśati /
tatrāpi śrutivirodhena pradhānaṃ svatantrameva kāraṇaṃ, mahadādīni ca kāryāṇyalokavedaprasiddhāni kalpyante /
children.translated_text:
He indicates by extension (<s>atideśa</s>) that by this refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya smṛti</s>, the <s>Yoga smṛti</s> too should be regarded as refuted.
For there too, in contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s> alone is postulated as an independent cause, and <s>Mahat</s> and the rest — effects not known in ordinary experience or the <s>Veda</s> — are postulated.

children.text: nanvevaṃ sati samānanyāyatvātpūrveṇaivaitadgataṃ kimarthaṃ punaratidiśyate /
children.translated_text: But if this is so, since the reasoning is the same, this [matter] was already covered by the previous [<s>sūtra</s>] — why is it extended again?

children.text:
asti hyatrābhyadhikāśaṅkā /
samyagdarśanābhyupāyo hi yogo vede vihitaḥ 'śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ' (bṛ. 2.4.5) iti /
'tryunnataṃ sthāpya samaṃ śarīram' (śve. 2.8) ityādinā cāsanādikalpanāpuraḥsaraṃ bahuprapañcaṃ yogavidhānaṃ śvetāśvataropaniṣadi dṛśyate /
liṅgāni ca vaidikāni yogaviṣayāṇi sahasraśa upalabhyante 'tāṃ yogamiti manyante sthirāmindriyadhāraṇām' (kā. 2.6.18) iti 'vidyāmetāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam (kā. 2.6.18) iti caivamādīni /
yogaśāstre 'pi 'atha tattvadarśanopāyo yogaḥ' iti samyagdarśanābhyupāyatvenaiva yogoṅgīkriyate /
ataḥ saṃpratipannārthaikadeśatvādaṣṭakādismṛtivadyogasmṛtirapyanapavadanīyā bhaviṣyatīti /
iyamapyadhikā śaṅkātideśena nivartyate /
arthaikadeśasaṃpratipattāvapyarthaikadeśavipratipatteḥ pūrvoktāyā darśanāt /
satīṣvapyadhyātmaviṣayāsu bahvīṣu smṛtiṣu sāṃkhyayogasmṛtyoreva nirākaraṇe yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ /
sāṃkhyayogau hi paramapuruṣārthasādhanatvena loke prakhyātau, śiṣṭaiśca parigṛhītau, liṅgena na śrautenopabṛṃhitau /
'tatkāraṇaṃ sāṃkhyayogābhipannaṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ' (śvaṃ. 6.13) iti /
nirākaraṇaṃ tu na sāṃkhyajñānena vedanirapekṣeṇa yogamārgeṇa vā niḥśreyasamadhigamyata iti /
śrutirhi vaidikādātmaikatvavijñānādanyanniḥśreyasasādhanaṃ vārayati 'tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' (śvaṃ. 3.8) iti /
dvaitino hi te sāṃkhyā yogāśca nātmaikatvadarśinaḥ /
yattu darśanamuktaṃ 'tatkāraṇaṃ sāṃkhyayogābhipannam' iti, vaidikameva tatra jñānaṃ dhyānaṃ ca sāṃkhyayogaśabdābhyāmabhilapyate pratyāsatterityavagantavyam /
yena tvaṃśena na virudhyete teneṣṭameva sāṃkhyayogasmṛtyoḥ sāvakāśatvam /
tadyathā- 'asaṅgo hyayaṃ puruṣaḥ' (bṛ. 4.3.16) ityevamādiśrutiprasiddhameva puruṣasya viśuddhatvaṃ nirguṇapuruṣanirūpaṇena sāṃkhyairabhyupagamyate /
tathāca yogairapi 'atha parivrāḍvivarṇavāsā muṇḍo 'parigrahaḥ' (jābā. 5) ityevamādi śrutiprasiddhameva nivṛttiniṣṭhatvaṃ pravrajyādyupadeśenānugamyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Yogins</s> too, through their teachings of renunciation and the like, follow what is already well known from <s>śruti</s> such as 'Then the renunciant, wearing discolored garments, shaven-headed, without possessions' (<s>Jābāla Upaniṣad</s> 5).

children.text: etena sarvāṇi tarkasmaraṇāni prativaktavyāni /
children.translated_text: By this [refutation], all [systems based on] reasoning and tradition should be considered answered.

children.text: tānyapi tarkopapattibhyāṃ tattvajñānāyopakurvantīti cedupakurvantu nāma /
children.translated_text: If [it is argued that] those too, through reasoning and logical proof, assist in the knowledge of truth — let them assist indeed.

children.text: tattvajñānaṃ tu vedāntavākyebhya eva bhavati 'nāvedavinmanute taṃ bṛhantam' (tai. brā. 3.12.9.7) 'taṃ tvaupaniṣadaṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchāmi' (bṛ. 3.9.23) ityevamādiśrutibhyaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: But the knowledge of truth arises from the statements of <s>Vedānta</s> alone, as [stated in] such <s>śrutis</s> as 'One who does not know the <s>Veda</s> does not know that Great One' (<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.12.9.7) and 'I ask you about that <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the subject of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.23). // 3 //

Because there is an additional doubt here. For <s>Yoga</s>, as a means to right knowledge, is prescribed in the <s>Veda</s>: '[The Self] is to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.5). And in the <s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s>, an elaborate prescription of <s>Yoga</s> is seen, preceded by instructions on posture and the like: 'Holding the body steady with the three [upper parts] erect' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 2.8). And Vedic indicatory marks concerning <s>Yoga</s> are found by the thousands: 'They consider that firm holding of the senses to be <s>Yoga</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6.18), and 'This knowledge and the entire discipline of <s>Yoga</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6.18), and so forth. In the <s>Yoga</s> scripture too, 'Now, <s>Yoga</s> is the means to the vision of truth' — <s>Yoga</s> is acknowledged precisely as a means to right knowledge. Therefore, since it agrees with an accepted position on one point, like the <s>Smṛti</s> of <s>Aṣṭaka</s> and others, the <s>Yoga smṛti</s> too should not be invalidated — [such is the doubt]. This additional doubt too is removed by the extension (<s>atideśa</s>). For even when there is agreement on one part of the doctrine, disagreement on another part has been shown previously. Even though there are many <s>smṛtis</s> dealing with spiritual subjects, effort has been made to refute specifically the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga smṛtis</s>. For <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> are renowned in the world as means to the highest human goal, are accepted by the learned, and are supported by indicatory marks — though not by direct <s>śruti</s> statements. As [the <s>Śvetāśvatara</s>] says: 'Knowing that God who is the cause, who is approached by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, one is freed from all bonds' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.13). But the refutation is [only] this: that the highest good is not attained through <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge independent of the <s>Veda</s>, or through the path of <s>Yoga</s> [alone]. For <s>śruti</s> precludes any means to the highest good other than the Vedic knowledge of the oneness of the Self: 'Having known Him alone, one transcends death; there is no other path for going there' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.8). For those <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and <s>Yogins</s> are dualists, not seers of the oneness of the Self. As for the citation 'That cause approached by <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>' — it should be understood that there the Vedic knowledge and meditation alone are designated by the words '<s>Sāṃkhya</s>' and '<s>Yoga</s>' due to their proximity [in meaning]. And insofar as they do not contradict [the <s>Veda</s>], the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga smṛtis</s> are indeed accepted as having scope. For example, the purity of the <s>Puruṣa</s> that is well known from <s>śruti</s> such as 'For this <s>Puruṣa</s> is unattached' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.16) is accepted by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> through their doctrine of the attributeless <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: FN: trīṇi urogrīvaśirāṃsyunnatāni yasmiñśarīre tattryunnatam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Tryunnatam</s>' — that body in which the three [parts] — the chest, neck, and head — are raised upward.

children.text:
tarko 'numānamanugrāhyaṃ mānam /
upapattiranugrāhikā yuktiriti bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text:
'<s>Tarka</s>' is inference; '<s>anugrāhyam mānam</s>' means a supporting means of knowledge.
'<s>Upapatti</s>' is a supporting argument — this is the distinction.

children.text: vilakṣaṇatvādhikaraṇam / sū. 4-12
children.translated_text: The <s>Vilakṣaṇatva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Dissimilarity) / <s>Sūtras</s> 4-12

children.text: na vilakṣaṇatvād asya tathātvaṃ ca śabdāt | BBs_2,1.4 |
children.translated_text: [<s>Brahman</s> is] not [the cause of the world] because of the dissimilarity of this [world from <s>Brahman</s>]; and its being so [i.e., the world being the effect of <s>Brahman</s>] is from scripture (<s>śabda</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.4 |

children.text:
brahmāsya jagato nimittakāraṇaṃ prakṛtiścetyasya pakṣasyākṣepaḥ smṛtinimittaḥ parihṛtaḥ /
tarkanimitta idānīmākṣepaḥ parihriyate /
kutaḥ punarasminnavadhārita āgamārthe tarkanimittasyākṣepasyāvakāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The objection based on <s>smṛti</s> against the thesis that <s>Brahman</s> is both the efficient cause and the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) of this world has been resolved. Now the objection based on reasoning is being resolved. But how can there be scope for an objection based on reasoning when the scriptural meaning has been ascertained?

children.text:
nanu dharma iva brahmaṇyanapekṣa āgamo bhavitumarhati /
bhavedayamavaṣṭambho yadi pramāṇāntarānavagāhya āgamamātraprameyo 'yamarthaḥ syādanuṣṭheyarūpa iva dharmaḥ /
pariniṣpannarūpaṃ tu brahmāvagamyate /
pariniṣpanne ca vastuni pramāṇāntarāṇāmastyavakāśo yathā pṛthivyādiṣu /
yathāca śrutīnāṃ parasparavirodhe satyekavaśenetarā nīyante, evaṃ pramāṇāntaravirodhe 'pi tadvaśenaiva śrutirnīyeta /
dṛṣṭasāmyena cādṛṣṭamarthaṃ samarthayantī yuktiranubhavasya saṃnikṛṣyate /
viprakṛṣyate tu śrutiraitihyamātreṇa svārthābhidhānāt /
anubhavāvasānaṃ ca brahmavijñānamavidyāyā nivartakaṃ mokṣasādhanaṃ ca dṛṣṭaphalatayeṣyate /
śrutirapi- 'śrotavyo mantavyaḥ' iti śravaṇavyatirekeṇa mananaṃ vidadhatī tarkamapyatrādartavyaṃ darśayati /
atastarkanimittaḥ punarākṣepaḥ kriyate 'na vilakṣaṇatvādasya' iti /
yaduktaṃ cetanaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ prakṛtiriti /
tannopapadyate /
kasmāt /
vilakṣaṇatvādasya vikārasya prakṛtyāḥ /
idaṃ hi brahmakāryatvenābhipreyamāṇaṃ jagat brahmavilakṣaṇamacetanamaśuddhaṃ ca dṛśyate /
brahma ca jagadvilakṣaṇaṃ cetanaṃ śuddhaṃ ca śrūyate /
naca vilakṣaṇatvaṃ prakṛtivikārabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ /
nahi rucakādayo vikārā mṛtprakṛtikā bhavanti śarāvādayo vā suvarṇaprakṛtikāḥ /
mṛdaiva tu mṛdānvitā vikārāḥ kriyante suvarṇena ca suvarṇānvitāḥ /
tathedamapi jagadacetanaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohānvitaṃ sadacetanasyaiva sukhaduḥkhamohātmakasya kāraṇasya kāryaṃ bhavitumarhatīti na vilakṣaṇasya brahmaṇaḥ /
brahmavilakṣaṇaṃ cāsya jagato 'śuddhyacetanatvadarśanādavagantavyam /
aśuddhaṃ hi jagatsukhaduḥkhamohātmakatayā prītiparitāpaviṣādādihetutvātsvarganarakādyuccāvacaprapañcatvācca /
acetanaṃ cedaṃ jagaccetanaṃ prati kāryakāraṇabhāvenopakaraṇabhāvopagamāt /
nahi sāmye satyupakāryopakārakabhāvo bhavati /
nahi pradīpau parasparasyopakurutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely, as with <s>dharma</s>, scripture should be independent regarding <s>Brahman</s>. This reliance [on scripture alone] would hold if this subject matter were knowable only through scripture and were of the nature of something to be performed, like <s>dharma</s>. But <s>Brahman</s> is understood as something of an already established nature. And regarding an already established entity, there is scope for other means of knowledge, just as with earth and the like. And just as when <s>śrutis</s> mutually contradict each other, one is construed in accordance with the other — so too, when there is contradiction with another means of knowledge, <s>śruti</s> should be construed in accordance with that. And reasoning, which establishes an unseen matter through analogy with what is seen, is proximate to experience, whereas <s>śruti</s>, merely through tradition, is remote, since it merely states its meaning [verbally]. And the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, which culminates in experience, is the remover of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the means to <s>mokṣa</s> — it is desired as having a visible result. And <s>śruti</s> too, by prescribing reflection (<s>manana</s>) in addition to hearing — '[The Self] is to be heard, to be reflected upon' — shows that reasoning too is to be applied here. Therefore, the objection based on reasoning is raised again: '[<s>Brahman</s> is] not [the cause] because of the dissimilarity of this [world].' What was stated — that conscious <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world, its material source — that is not tenable. Why? Because of the dissimilarity of this effect from its material cause. For this world, which is intended as the effect of <s>Brahman</s>, is seen to be dissimilar to <s>Brahman</s> — insentient and impure. And <s>Brahman</s> is heard [in <s>śruti</s>] as dissimilar to the world — conscious and pure. And dissimilarity between material cause and effect is not observed. For the modifications such as bracelets are not made of clay, nor are dishes made of gold. Rather, modifications of clay are made with clay, and those of gold with gold. Likewise, this world too — being insentient and pervaded by pleasure, pain, and delusion — should be the effect of a cause that is itself insentient and of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, not of <s>Brahman</s> which is dissimilar. And from the observation that this world is impure and insentient, it should be understood as dissimilar to <s>Brahman</s>. For the world is impure, being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, being the cause of satisfaction, torment, and despondency, and being a manifold of high and low [realms] such as heaven and hell. And this world, being insentient, assumes the status of an instrument in relation to the conscious [being] through the relation of cause and effect. For when there is equality, the relation of the served and the server does not arise. For two lamps do not serve each other.

children.text: nanu cetanamapi kāryakāraṇaṃ svāmibhṛtyanyāyena bhokturupakariṣyati /
children.translated_text: But [one might argue that] even a conscious [entity as] cause and effect could serve the enjoyer, by the analogy of master and servant.

children.text:
na /
svāmibhṛtyayorapyacetanāṃśasyaiva cetanaṃ pratyupakārakatvāt /
yo hyekasya cetanasya parigraho buddhyādicetanabhāgaḥ sa evānyasya cetanasyopakaroti natu svayameva cetanaścetanāntarasyopakarotyapakaroti vā /
niratiśayā hyakartāraścetanā iti sāṃkhyā manyante /
tasmādacetanaṃ kāryakāraṇam /
naca kāṣṭaloṣṭādīnāṃ cetanatve kiṃ citpramāṇamasti /
prasiddhaścāyaṃ cetanācetanavibhāgo loke /
tasmādbrahmavilakṣaṇatvānnedaṃ jagattatprakṛtikam /
yo 'pi kaścidācakṣīta śrutvā jagataścetanaprakṛtikatāṃ tadbalenaiva samastaṃ jagaccetanamavagamayiṣyāmi /
prakṛtirūpasya vikāre 'nvayadarśanāt /
avibhāvanaṃ tu caitanyasya pariṇāmaviśeṣādbhaviṣyati /
yathā spaṣṭacaitanyānāmapyātmanāṃ svāpamūrcchādyavasthāsu caitanyaṃ na vibhāvyata evaṃ kāṣṭhaloṣṭādīnāmapi caitanyaṃ na vibhāvayiṣyate /
etasmādeva ca vibhāvitāvibhāvitatvakṛtādviśeṣādrūpādibhāvābhāvābhyāṃ ca kāryakāraṇānāmātmanāṃ ca cetanatvāviśeṣe 'pi guṇapradhānabhāvo na virotsyate /
yathā ca pārthivatvāviśeṣe 'pi māṃsasūpaudanādīnāṃ pratyātmavartino viśeṣātparasparopakāritvaṃ bhavatyevamihāpi bhaviṣyati /
pravibhāgaprasiddhirapyata eva na virotsyata iti /
tenāpi kathañciccetanācetanatvalakṣaṇaṃ vilakṣaṇatvaṃ parihriyeta /
śuddhyaśuddhitvalakṣaṇaṃ tu vilakṣaṇatvaṃ naiva parihriyate /
nacetaradapi vilakṣaṇatvaṃ parihartuṃ śakyata ityāha- tathātvaṃ ca śabdāditi /
anavagamyamānamevaṃ hīdaṃ loke samastasya vastunaścetanatvaṃ cetanaprakṛtikatvaśravaṇācchabdaśaraṇatayā kevalayotprekṣata, tacca śabdenaiva virudhyate /
children.translated_text: For this sentience of the totality of things, which is not apprehended in the world, is merely conjectured on the sole basis of scripture — from hearing that [the world] has a sentient cause. And that [conjecture] is contradicted by scripture itself.

children.text: yataḥ śabdādapi tathātvamavagamyate /
children.translated_text: Because from scripture too, that nature [i.e., dissimilarity from <s>Brahman</s>] is apprehended.

children.text: tathātvamiti prakṛtivilakṣaṇatvaṃ kathayati /
children.translated_text: 'That nature' means the dissimilarity from the material cause — this is what he states.

children.text: śabda eva 'vijñānaṃ cāvijñānaṃ ca' (te. 2.6) iti kasyacidvibhāgasyācetanatāṃ śrāvayaṃścetanādbrahmaṇo vilakṣaṇamacetanaṃ jagacchrāvayati // 4 //
children.translated_text: Scripture itself, by teaching the insentience of a certain portion — 'the sentient and the insentient' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6) — teaches that the insentient world is dissimilar from the sentient <s>Brahman</s>. // 4 //

No. Because even in the case of master and servant, it is only the insentient aspect of a sentient being that serves another sentient being. For the possessions of one sentient being — namely, the sentient portion consisting of intellect and such — serve another sentient being; but a sentient being itself does not directly serve or harm another sentient being. For the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> hold that sentient beings are unsurpassably inactive. Therefore, [only] the insentient is the [real] cause and effect. And there is no evidence whatsoever for the sentience of wood, clods of earth, and such. And this distinction between sentient and insentient is well established in the world. Therefore, because of being dissimilar to <s>Brahman</s>, this world is not of <s>Brahman</s>'s nature. If someone were to say: 'Having heard that the world has a sentient cause, I shall understand by that very authority that the entire world is sentient — because the nature of the material cause is seen to continue in the effect. But the non-manifestation of consciousness [in some things] will be due to particular modifications. Just as even for selves whose consciousness is manifest, consciousness is not manifested in states of sleep, fainting, and such — so too for wood, clods of earth, and such, consciousness will not be manifested. And from this very distinction based on manifestation and non-manifestation, even though there is no difference in the sentience of effects, causes, and selves, the relationship of subordinate and principal will not be contradicted — by the presence and absence of form and such. And just as among things of earthy nature, flesh, broth, rice, and such serve one another due to particular [properties] pertaining to each individual — so too will it be here. And the well-known distinction [between sentient and insentient] will not be contradicted for this very reason' — even by that person, the dissimilarity characterized by sentience and insentience would somehow be removed. But the dissimilarity characterized by purity and impurity is never removed. And the other dissimilarity too cannot be removed — thus he says: 'And that nature [is established] from scripture.'

children.text:
FN: avaṣṭambho dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
aitihyamātreṇa parokṣatayeti yāvat /
sukhaduḥkhamohāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi /
upajanāpāyavaddharmayogo 'tiśayastadabhāvo niratiśayatvam /
itaraccetanācetanatvarūpam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Avaṣṭambha</s>' means an illustrative example. 'By mere tradition, indirectly' — this is the meaning. Pleasure, pain, and delusion are <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s>. Superiority is the possession of qualities such as arising and passing away; the absence of that is unsurpassability. The other [dissimilarity] is that characterized by sentience and insentience.

children.text:
nanu cetanatvamapi kvacidacetanatvābhimatānāṃ bhūtendriyāṇāṃ śrūyate /
yathā 'mṛdabravīt' 'āpo 'bruvan' ( śa.pa.brā. 6.1.3.2.4) iti, 'tatteja aikṣata' 'tā āpa aikṣanta' (chā. 6.2.3,4) iti caivamādyā bhūtaviṣayā cetanatvaśrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: But is not sentience also heard of for elements and sense organs that are regarded as insentient? For instance, 'the earth spoke,' 'the waters said' (<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 6.1.3.2.4) — and 'that fire willed,' 'those waters willed' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3-4) — such is the <s>śruti</s> regarding the sentience of elements.

children.text:
indriyaviṣayāpi 'te heme prāṇā ahaṃśreyase vivadamānā brahma jagmuḥ' (bṛ. 6.1.7) iti, 'te ha vācamūcustvaṃ na udgāyeti' (bṛ. 1.3.2) ityevamādyendriyaviṣayeti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: And regarding the sense organs too: 'These vital breaths, disputing among themselves about their own superiority, went to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.7), and 'They said to Speech: "You sing the <s>Udgītha</s> for us"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.2) — such and similar [passages]. To this he replies:

children.text: abhimānivyapadeśas tu viśeṣānugatibhyām | BBs_2,1.5 |
children.translated_text: But this is designation through presiding [deities], because of specific distinction and continuity. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.5 |

children.text:
tuśabda āśaṅkāmapanudati /
na khalu mṛdabravīdityevañjātīyakayā śrutyā bhūtendriyāṇāṃ cetanatvamāśaṅkanīyam /
yato 'bhimānivyapadeśa eṣaḥ /
mṛdādyabhimāninyo vāgādyabhimāninyaśca cetanā devatā vadanasaṃvadanādiṣu cetanociteṣu vyavahāreṣu vyapadiśyante na bhūtendriyamātram /
kasmāt /
viśeṣānugatibhyām /
viśeṣo hi bhoktṛṇāṃ bhūtendriyāṇāṃ ca cetanācetanapravibhāgalakṣaṇaḥ prāgabhihitaḥ /
sarvacetanatāyāṃ cāsau nopapadyeta /
apica kauṣītakinaḥ prāṇasaṃvāde karaṇamātrāśaṅkāvinivṛttaye 'dhiṣṭhātṛcetanaparigrahāya devatāśabdena viśiṣanti- 'etā ha vai devatā ahaṃśreyase vivadamānāḥ' iti /
'tā vā etāḥ sarvā devatāḥ prāṇe niḥśreyasaṃ viditvā' (2.14) iti ca /
anugatāśca sarvatrābhimāninyaścetanādevatā mantrārthavādetihāsapurāṇādibhyo 'vagamyante /
'agnirvāgbhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśat' (ai.ā. 2.4.2.4) ityevamādikā ca śrutiḥ karaṇeṣvanugrāhikāṃ devatāmanugatāṃ darśayati /
prāṇasaṃvādavākyaśeṣe ca 'te ha prāṇāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitarametyocuḥ' (chā. 5.1.7) iti śreṣṭhatvanirdhāraṇāya prajāpatigamanaṃ, tadvacanācaikaikotkramaṇenānvayavyatirkābhyāṃ prāṇaśraiṣṭhyapratipattiḥ /
'tasmai baliharaṇam' (bṛ. 6.1.13) iti caivañjātīyako 'smadādiṣviva vyavahāro 'nugamyamāno 'bhimānivyapadeśaṃ draḍhayati /
children.translated_text: 'The offering of tribute to him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.13) — such transactions, as observed among us [sentient beings], when seen to be continuously [attributed to deities], confirm the designation through presiding [deities].

children.text: 'tatteja aikṣata' ityapi parasyā eva devatāyā adhiṣṭātryāḥ svavikāreṣvanugatāyā iyamīkṣā vyapadiśyata iti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Even in 'That fire willed,' this willing should be seen as attributed to the supreme deity — who, as the presider, is continuously present in her own modifications.

children.text: tasmādvilakṣaṇamevedaṃ brahmaṇo jagat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this world is indeed dissimilar from <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: vilakṣaṇatvācca na brahmaprakṛtikamityākṣipte pratividhatte // 5 //
children.translated_text: And since the world is dissimilar, it cannot have <s>Brahman</s> as its material cause — having raised this objection, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] now replies: // 5 //

The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) removes the apprehension. One should not apprehend the sentience of elements and sense organs from <s>śruti</s> passages like 'the earth spoke.' Because this is a designation through presiding [deities]. The sentient deities presiding over earth and such, and over speech and such, are designated in activities appropriate to sentient beings — such as speaking and conversing — not the mere elements and sense organs. Why? Because of specific distinction and continuity. For the specific distinction — characterized by the division between sentient and insentient — of enjoyers and elements-and-sense-organs was stated earlier. And if everything were sentient, that [distinction] would not be possible. Moreover, the followers of the <s>Kauṣītaki</s> [recension], in the dialogue about <s>Prāṇa</s>, in order to remove the apprehension that [the faculties] are mere instruments and to establish the inclusion of presiding sentient deities, qualify [them] with the word 'deity': 'These deities, disputing among themselves about their own superiority' and 'All these deities, having recognized the supremacy in <s>Prāṇa</s>' (2.14). And the presiding sentient deities are continuously understood everywhere — from <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and such. And the <s>śruti</s> '<s>Agni</s>, having become speech, entered the mouth' (<s>Aitareya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.4.2.4) and such shows the presiding deity as continuously present in the sense organs. And in the remainder of the <s>Prāṇa</s> dialogue passage: 'Those vital breaths went to <s>Prajāpati</s>, their father, and said' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.1.7) — [they went] to determine supremacy, and by His instruction, through the individual departure [of each faculty] and the method of agreement and difference, the supremacy of <s>Prāṇa</s> is established.

children.text:
FN: saṃvadanaṃ vivādaḥ /
viśiṃṣanti vāgādīnprāṇādīniti śeṣaḥ /
ahaṃśreyase svasvaśreṣṭhatvāya /
niḥśreyasaṃ śraiṣṭhyam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Saṃvadana</s>' means dispute. '[They] qualify' — speech and such, <s>Prāṇa</s> and such — this is to be supplied. '<s>Ahaṃśreyase</s>' means for [establishing] one's own superiority. '<s>Niḥśreyasa</s>' means supremacy.

children.text: dṛśyate tu | BBs_2,1.6 |
children.translated_text: But it is seen. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.6 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati /
yaduktaṃ vilakṣaṇatvānnedaṃ jagadbrahmaprakṛtikamiti /
nāyamekāntaḥ /
dṛśyate hi loke cetanatvena prasiddhebhyaḥ puruṣādibhyo vilakṣaṇānāṃ keśanakhādīnāmutpattiḥ, acetanatvena ca prasiddhebhyo gomayādibhyo vṛścikādīnām /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the position. As for the statement that because of dissimilarity, this world does not have <s>Brahman</s> as its material cause — this is not an absolute [rule]. For it is seen in the world that hair, nails, and such, which are dissimilar, arise from persons and such who are well known as sentient; and scorpions and such [arise] from cow-dung and such, which are well known as insentient.

children.text: nanvacetanānyeva puruṣādiśarīrāṇyacetanānāṃ keśanakhādīnāṃ kāraṇāni, acetanānyeva ca vṛścikādiśarīrāṇyacetanānāṃ gomayādīnāṃ kāryāṇīti /
children.translated_text: But are not the bodies of persons and such, which are insentient, the causes of insentient hair, nails, and such? And are not the bodies of scorpions and such, which are sentient [only through being ensouled], the effects of insentient cow-dung and such?

children.text:
ucyate- evamapi kiñcidacetanaṃ cetanasyāyatanabhāvamupagacchati kiñcinnetyastyeva vailakṣaṇyam /
mahāṃścāyaṃ pāriṇāmikaḥ svabhāvaviprakarṣaḥ puruṣādīnāṃ keśanakhādīnāṃ ca svarūpādibhedāt /
tathā gomayādīnāṃ vṛścikādīnāṃ ca /
atyantasārūpye ca prakṛtivikārabhāva eva pralīyeta /
athocyetāsti kaścitpārthivatvādisvabhāvaḥ puruṣādīnāṃ keśanakhādiṣvanuvartamāno gomayādīnāṃ vṛścikādiṣviti /
brahmaṇo 'pi tarhi sattālakṣaṇaḥ svabhāva ākāśādiṣvanuvartamānodṛśyate /
vilakṣaṇatvena ca kāraṇena brahmaprakṛtitvaṃ jagato dūṣayatā kimaśeṣasya brahmasvabhāvasyānanuvartanaṃ vilakṣaṇatvamabhipreyata uta yasya kasyacidasya caitanyasyeti vaktavyam /
prathame vikalpe samastaprakṛtivikārocchedaprasaṅgaḥ /
nahyasatyatiśaye prakṛtivikāra iti bhavati /
dvitīye cāsiddhatvam /
dṛśyate hi sattālakṣaṇo brahmasvabhāva ākāśādiṣvanuvartamāna ityuktam /
tṛtīye tu dṛṣṭāntābhāvaḥ /
kiṃ hi yaccaitanyenānanvitaṃ tadabrahmaprakṛtikaṃ dṛṣṭamiti brahmavādinaṃ pratyudāhriyeta /
samastasya vastujāyasya brahmaprakṛtitvābhyupagamāt /
āgamavirodhastu prasiddha eva /
cetanaṃ brahmajagataḥ kāraṇaṃ prakṛtiścetyāgamatātparyasya prasādhitatvāt /
yattūktaṃ pariniṣpannatvādbrahmaṇi pramāṇāntarāṇi saṃbhaveyuriti /
tadapi manorathamātram /
rūpādyabhāvāddhi nāyamarthaḥ pratyakṣasya gocaraḥ /
liṅgādyabhāvācca nānumānādīnām /
āgamamātrasamadhigamya eva tvayamartho dharmavat /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'naiṣā tarkeṇa matirāpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha' (kā. 1.2.9) iti /
'ko addhā veda ka iha pravocat' /
'iyaṃ visṛṣṭiryata ābabhūva' (ṛ.saṃ 1.30.6) iti caite ṛcau siddhānāmapīśvarāṇāṃ durbodhatāṃ jagatkāraṇasya darśayataḥ /
smṛtirapi bhavati- 'acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃstarkeṇa yojayet' iti /
'avyakto 'yamacintyo 'yamavikāryoyamucyate' (gī. 2.25) iti ca /
'na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ /
ahamādirhi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ' (gī. 10.2) iti caivañjātīyakā /
yadapi śravaṇavyatirekeṇa mananaṃ vidadhacchabda eva tarkamapyādartavyaṃ darśayatītyuktam /
nānena miṣeṇa śuṣkatarkasyātrātmalābhaḥ saṃbhavati /
śrutyanugṛhīta eva hyatra tarko 'nubhavāṅgatvenāśrīyate /
svapnāntabuddhāntayorubhayoritaretaravyabhicārādātmano 'nanvāgatatvaṃ, saṃprasāde ca prapañcaparityāgena sadātmanā saṃpatterniṣprapañcasadātmatvaṃ, prapañcasya brahmaprabhavatvātkāryakāraṇānanyatvanyāyena brahmāvyatireka ityevañjātīyakaḥ /
'tarkāpratiṣṭhānāt' (bra. 2.1.11) iti ca kevalasya tarkasyavipralambhakatvaṃ darśayiṣyati /
yo 'pi cetanakāraṇaśravaṇabalenaiva samastasya jagataścetanatāmutprekṣate tasyāpi vijñānaṃ cāvijñānaṃ ca iti cetanācetanavibhāgaśravaṇaṃ vibhāvanāvibhāvanābhyāṃ caitanyasya śakyata eva yojayitum /
parasyaiva tvidamapi vibhāgaśravaṇaṃ na yujyate /
katham /
children.translated_text: How so?

children.text: paramakāraṇasya hyatra samastajagadātmanā samavasthānaṃ śrāvyate 'vijñānaṃ cāvijñānaṃ cābhavat' iti /
children.translated_text: For here, the subsistence of the supreme cause in the form of the entire world is being taught: 'It became the sentient and the insentient.'

children.text: tatra yathā cetanasyācetanabhāvo nopapadyate vilakṣaṇatvāt, evamacetanasyāpi cetanabhāvo nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: Therein, just as the sentient's becoming insentient is not possible because of dissimilarity, so too the insentient's becoming sentient is not possible.

children.text: pratyuktatvāttu vilakṣaṇatvasya yathāśrutyaiva kāraṇaṃ grahītavyaṃ bhavati // 6 //
children.translated_text: But since the [objection based on] dissimilarity has been answered, the cause should be accepted just as scripture states. // 6 //

It is replied: even so, [the fact that] some insentient thing comes to serve as the abode of a sentient being while another does not — this itself constitutes dissimilarity. And this natural disparity in transformation between persons and such on the one hand, and hair, nails, and such on the other, is great — because of the difference in their intrinsic nature and form. Likewise between cow-dung and such, and scorpions and such. And if there were complete similarity, the very relationship of material cause and effect would dissolve. Now, if it were said that there is some earthy nature and such that continues from persons and such into hair, nails, and such, and from cow-dung and such into scorpions and such — then too, <s>Brahman</s>'s nature characterized by existence (<s>sattā</s>) is seen to continue into space and such. And the one who refutes the <s>Brahman</s>-origin of the world on the ground of dissimilarity must state: does he mean by 'dissimilarity' the non-continuation of every aspect of <s>Brahman</s>'s nature, or [the non-continuation] of some particular [aspect], namely consciousness? In the first alternative, all cause-effect relationships would be destroyed — for there is no cause-effect relationship without some [shared] characteristic. In the second, [the objection is] unestablished — for it has been stated that <s>Brahman</s>'s nature characterized by existence is seen to continue into space and such. And in the third [alternative — a specific kind of dissimilarity], there is no counter-example. For what [instance] could be cited against the <s>Vedāntin</s> where something not pervaded by consciousness is seen to not have <s>Brahman</s> as its material cause? — since the <s>Brahman</s>-origin of the totality of existing things is accepted. And the conflict with scripture is already well established — since it has been demonstrated that the purport of scripture is that sentient <s>Brahman</s> is the cause and material source of the world. As for the statement that other means of knowledge would be applicable to <s>Brahman</s> because it is an established entity — that too is mere wishful thinking. For since <s>Brahman</s> lacks form and such, this object is not within the range of perception. And since it lacks inferential marks and such, it is not [within the range] of inference and other [means of knowledge]. Rather, this object, like <s>dharma</s>, is to be apprehended from scripture alone. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'This understanding is not to be obtained by reasoning; [it is] taught by another — well known for realization, dear one' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.2.9). And 'Who indeed knows? Who here can declare?' and 'This creation — whence it arose' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 1.30.6) — these <s>ṛc</s> verses show the difficulty of comprehending the cause of the world even for accomplished seers. <s>Smṛti</s> also says: 'Those entities that are inconceivable — one should not attempt to reason about them.' And: 'This [Self] is called unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchangeable' (<s>Gītā</s> 2.25). And: 'Neither the hosts of gods know My origin, nor the great sages; for I am the source of the gods and great sages in every way' (<s>Gītā</s> 10.2) — and such passages. As for the statement that scripture, by enjoining <s>manana</s> (reflection) in addition to hearing, shows that reasoning too should be attended to — by this pretext, dry reasoning cannot gain entry here. For only reasoning that is supported by <s>śruti</s> is relied upon here, as ancillary to realization. [Such reasoning includes]: the non-continuation of the Self [in any single state], since both dream and waking states deviate from each other; and by the relinquishing of the phenomenal world in deep sleep and attaining the nature of pure Being, [the Self's] nature as phenomenally undifferentiated pure Being [is established]; and because the phenomenal world originates from <s>Brahman</s>, by the principle of non-difference of cause and effect, the non-separateness from <s>Brahman</s> [is established] — such is the type [of reasoning]. And '<s>tarkāpratiṣṭhānāt</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.1.11) — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] will show the deceptive nature of mere reasoning. And for the one who conjectures the sentience of the entire world on the strength of hearing that the cause is sentient — for him too, the hearing 'the sentient and the insentient' — the hearing of the division between sentient and insentient — can indeed be reconciled through [the distinction of] manifestation and non-manifestation of consciousness. But for the opponent, this hearing of division is not justified.

children.text:
FN: pāriṇāmikastattatkeśādigatapariṇāmātmaka ityarthaḥ /
eṣā vedāntaśāstrajanyā matistarkeṇa svamatyūhamātreṇāpaneyā bādhārhā na /
yadvā tarkeṇa prāptavyā netyarthaḥ /
kintu anyena nipuṇenācāryeṇa proktaprabodhitā satī sujñānāya sākṣātkārāya bhavati /
he preṣṭha priyatameti nāciketasaṃprati yamasaṃbodhanam /
iyaṃ visṛṣṭirākāśādisṛṣṭiḥ kutaḥ kasmājjātā kasmācca sthitiṃ prāptetyaddhā tattvena ko veda, na ko 'pi /
kaḥ pravocat na ko 'pi pravaktābhūt /
vipralambhakatvaṃ arthaviśeṣāvyavasthāpakatvam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Pāriṇāmika</s>' means 'of the nature of the transformation that pertains to hair and such' — this is the meaning. 'This understanding (<s>mati</s>) born of <s>Vedānta</s> scripture is not to be dismissed — i.e., not fit to be refuted — by reasoning, i.e., by mere intellectual conjecture.' Or alternatively: 'it is not to be attained by reasoning' — this is the meaning. 'Rather, taught — i.e., awakened — by another, by a skilled teacher, it becomes [the means] for realization, for direct experience. O dear one (<s>preṣṭha</s>), dearest one' — this is <s>Yama</s>'s address to <s>Naciketas</s>. 'This creation' — the creation of space and such — 'whence was it born, and from what did it attain stability?' — who knows this in truth (<s>addhā</s>)? No one. Who can declare it? No one could declare it. '<s>Vipralambhakatva</s>' means the inability to establish any definite conclusion.

children.text: asad iti cen na pratiṣedhamātratvāt | BBs_2,1.7 |
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is non-existent (<s>asat</s>) — no, because [the <s>śruti</s> statement] is a mere negation. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.7 |

children.text:
yadi cetanaṃ śuddhaṃ śabdavihīnaṃ ca brahma tadviparūtasyācetanasyāśuddhasya śabdādimataśca kāryasya kāraṇamiṣyetāsattarhi kāryaṃ prāgutpatteriti prasajyeta /
aniṣṭaṃ caitatsatkāryavādinastaveti cet /
children.translated_text: If sentient, pure, and sound-less <s>Brahman</s> is accepted as the cause of an effect that is its opposite — insentient, impure, and possessed of sound and such — then the effect would be non-existent before its origination. And this is undesirable for one who holds the doctrine of the pre-existence of the effect (<s>satkāryavāda</s>) — [is this the objection]?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
pratiṣedhamātratvāt /
pratiṣedhamātraṃ hīdaṃ nāsya pratiṣedhasya pratiṣedhyamasti /
nahyayaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ prāgutpatteḥ sattvaṃ kāryasya pratiṣeddhuṃ śaknoti /
katham /
yathaiva hīdānāmapīdaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇātmanā sadevaṃ prāgutpatterapīti gamyate /
nahīdānāmapīdaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇātmānamantareṇa svatantramevāsti /
'sarvaṃ taṃ parādādyo 'nyatrātmanaḥ sarvaṃ veda' (bṛ. 2.4.6)
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because it is merely a negation. For this is merely a negation — this negation has nothing that is negated [as a positive entity]. For this negation is not capable of negating the existence of the effect prior to its origination. How so? Just as even now the effect exists in the form of the cause, so too prior to origination — this is understood. For even now this effect does not exist independently, apart from the nature of the cause. Because of the hearing: 'All this has abandoned him who sees all as other than the Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6)

children.text:
ityādiśravaṇāt /
kāraṇātmanā tu sattvaṃ kāryasya prāgutpatteraviśiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: and similar [texts]. But the existence of the effect in the form of the cause prior to origination is no different [from its existence now].

children.text: nanu śabdādihīnaṃ brahmajagataḥ kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: But is not <s>Brahman</s>, the cause of the world, devoid of sound and such [qualities]?

children.text: bāḍham /
children.translated_text: Indeed so.

children.text: natu śabdādimatkāryaṃ kāraṇātmanā hīnaṃ prāgutpatteridānīṃ vāsti /
children.translated_text: But the effect possessing sound and such does not exist devoid of the nature of the cause — neither prior to origination nor now.

children.text: tena na śakyate vaktuṃ prāgutpatterasatkāryamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it cannot be said that the effect is non-existent prior to origination.

children.text: vistareṇa caitatkāryakāraṇānanyatvavāde vakṣyāmaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: And we shall discuss this at length in the section on the non-difference of cause and effect. // 7 //

children.text: apītau tadvatprasaṅgād asamañjasam | BBs_2,1.8 |
children.translated_text: At dissolution, because of the contingency of the same [defects applying to the cause], [the doctrine would be] inconsistent. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.8 |

children.text: atrāha- yadi sthaulyasāvayavatvācetanatvaparicchinnatvāśuddhyādidharmakaṃ kāryaṃ brahmakāraṇamabhyupagamyeta tadapītau pralaye pratisaṃsṛjyamānaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇāvibhāgamāpadyamānaṃ kāraṇamātmīyena dharmeṇa dūṣayedityapītau kāraṇasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ kāryasyevāśuddhyādirūpaprasaṅgātsarvajñaṃ brahma jagatkāraṇamityasamañjasamidamaupaniṣadaṃ darśanam /
children.translated_text: Here it is objected: If the effect — possessing properties such as grossness, compositeness, non-consciousness, limitedness, impurity, and such — is accepted as having <s>Brahman</s> as its cause, then at dissolution (<s>apīti</s>), when the effect is being reabsorbed and attaining non-distinction from the cause, it would contaminate the cause with its own properties. Thus, because of the contingency that even <s>Brahman</s>, the cause, would at dissolution have the same properties of impurity and such as the effect, the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> doctrine that the omniscient <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world would be inconsistent.

children.text: apica samastasya vibhāgasyāvibhāgaprāpteḥ punarutpattau niyamakāraṇābhāvādbhoktṛbhogyādivibhāgenotpattirna prāpnotītyasamañjasam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, since when all differentiation reaches a state of non-differentiation, there would be no determining cause for re-origination with the differentiation of enjoyer, enjoyed, and such, [the doctrine would be] inconsistent.

children.text: apica bhoktṛṇāṃ pareṇa brahmaṇāvibhāgaṃ gatānāṃ karmādinimittapralaye 'pi punarutpattāvabhyupagamyamānāyāṃ muktānāmapi punaruttattiprasaṅgādasamañjasam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if at dissolution the enjoyers, having attained non-distinction with the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, are accepted as being re-originated even though <s>karma</s> and other causes have been dissolved — then because of the contingency that even the liberated would be re-born, [the doctrine would be] inconsistent.

children.text: athedaṃ jagadapītāvapi vibhaktameva pareṇa brahmaṇāvatiṣṭheta, evamapyapītīśca na saṃbhavati, kāraṇāvyatiriktaṃ ca kāryaṃ na saṃbhavatītyasamañjasameveti // 8 //
children.translated_text: And if this world were to remain differentiated even at dissolution, distinct from the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — even so, dissolution would not be possible, and the effect's non-difference from the cause would also be impossible — so it is inconsistent in any case. // 8 //

children.text: atrocyate-
children.translated_text: To this it is said:

children.text: na tu dṛṣṭāntabhāvāt | BBs_2,1.9 |
children.translated_text: But [this is] not [a fault], because of the existence of illustrations. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.9 |

children.text:
naivāsmadīye darśane kiñcidasāmañjasyamasti /
yattāvadabhihitaṃ kāraṇamapigacchatkāryaṃ kāraṇamātmīyena dharmeṇa dūṣayediti, tadadūṣaṇam /
kasmāt /
dṛṣṭāntābhāvāt /
santi hi dṛṣṭāntā yathā kāraṇamapigacchatkāryaṃ kāraṇamātmīyena dharmeṇa na dūṣayati /
tadyathā śarāvādayo mṛtprakṛtikā vikārā vibhāgāvasthāyāmuccāvacamadhyamaprabhedāḥ santaḥ punaḥ prakṛtimapigacchanto na tāmātmīyena dharmeṇa saṃsṛjanti /
rucakādayaśca suvarṇavikārā apītau na suvarṇamātmīyena dharmeṇa saṃsṛjanti /
pṛthivīvikāraścaturvidho bhūtagrāmo na pṛthivīmapītāvātmīyena dharmeṇa saṃsṛjati /
tvatpakṣasya tu na kaściddṛṣṭānto 'sti /
apītireva hi na saṃbhavedyadi kāraṇe kāryaṃ svadharmeṇaivāvatiṣṭheta /
ananyatve 'pi kāryakāraṇayoḥ kāryasya kāraṇātmatvaṃ natu kāraṇasya kāryātmatvaṃ 'ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ' iti vakṣyāmaḥ (bra.sū. 2.1.14) /
atyalpaṃ cedamucyate kāryamapītāvātmīyena dharmeṇa kāraṇaṃ saṃsṛjediti /
sthitāvapi samāno 'yaṃ prasaṅgaḥ, kāryakāraṇayorananyatvābhyupagamāt /
'idaṃ sarva yadayamātmā' (bṛ. 2.4.6), 'ātmaivedaṃ sarvam' (chā. 7.25.2), 'brahmaivedamamṛtaṃ purastāt' (mu. 2.2.11), 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma' (chā. 3.14.1) ityevamādyābhirhi śrutibhiraviśeṣeṇa triṣvapi kāleṣu kāryasya kāraṇānanyatvaṃ śrāvyate /
tatra yaḥ parihāraḥ kāryasya taddharmāṇāṃ cāvidyādhyāropitatvānna taiḥ kāraṇaṃ saṃsṛjyata iti, apītāvapi sa samānaḥ /
asti cāyamaparo dṛṣṭānto yathā svayaṃ prasāritayā māyayā māyāvī triṣvapi kāleṣu na saṃspaśyate, avastutvāt, evaṃ paramātmāpi saṃsāramāyayā na saṃspṛśyata iti /
yathā ca svapnadṛgekaḥ svapnadarśanamāyayā na saṃspṛśyata iti /
prabodhasaṃpradāyorananvāgatatvāt /
evamavasthātrayasākṣyeko 'vyabhicāryavasthātrayeṇa vyabhicāriṇā na saṃspṛśyate /
māyāmātraṃ hyetadyatparamātmano 'vasthātrayātmanāvabhāsanaṃ rajjvā iva sarpādibhāveneti /
atroktaṃ vedāntārthasaṃpradāyavidbhirācāryaiḥ - 'anādimāyayā supto yadā jīvaḥ prabudhyate /
ajamanidramasvapnamadvaitaṃ budhyate tadā' (gauḍapā. kāri. 1.16) iti /
tatra yaduktamapītau kāraṇasyāpi kāryasyeva sthaulyādidoṣaprasaṅga ityetadayuktam /
yatpunaretaduktaṃ samastasya vibhāgasyāvibhāgaprāpteḥ punarvibhāgenotpattau niyamakāraṇaṃ nopapadyata iti /
ayamapyadoṣaḥ /
dṛṣṭāntabhāvādeva /
yathāhi suṣuptisamādhyādāvapi satyāṃ svābhāvikyāmavibhāgaprāptau mithyājñānasyānapoditatvātpūrvavatpunaḥ prabodhe vibhāgo bhavatyevamihāpi bhaviṣyati /
śrutiścātra bhavati- 'imāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sati saṃpadya na viduḥ sati saṃpadyāmaha iti ta iha vyāghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yadyadbhavanti tadā bhavanti' (chā. 6.9.2,3) iti /
yathā hyavibhāge 'pi paramātmani mithyājñānapratibaddho vibhāgavyavahāraḥ svapnavadavyāhataḥ sthito dṛśyate, evamapītāvapi mithyājñānapratibaddhaiva vibhāgaśaktiranumāsyate /
etena muktānāṃ punarutpattiprasaṅgaḥ pratyuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, the contingency of re-birth of the liberated is also answered.

children.text: samyagjñānena mithyājñānasyāpoditatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because false knowledge has been sublated by right knowledge.

children.text: yaḥ punarayamante 'paro vikalpa utprekṣito 'thedaṃ jagadapītāvapi vibhaktameva pareṇa brahmaṇāvatiṣṭheteti, so 'pyanabhyupagamādeva pratiṣiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: As for the further alternative imagined at the end — 'that this world might remain differentiated even at dissolution, distinct from the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — that too is refuted simply because it is not accepted [by us].

children.text: tasmātsamañjasamidamaupaniṣadaṃ darśanam // 9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>Upaniṣadic</s> doctrine is consistent. // 9 //

There is no inconsistency whatsoever in our doctrine. As for the objection that the effect, returning to the cause, would contaminate the cause with its own properties — that is not a contamination. Why? Because of the existence of illustrations. For there are illustrations showing that an effect returning to its cause does not contaminate the cause with its own properties. For example, modifications of clay such as pots and dishes, which during the state of differentiation have distinctions of high, low, and middle, when returning to their source-material do not impart their own properties to it. And modifications of gold such as ornaments, at dissolution, do not impart their own properties to the gold. And the fourfold class of living beings, being modifications of earth, do not impart their own properties to earth at dissolution. But for your position there is no illustration at all. For dissolution itself would be impossible if the effect were to persist in the cause with its own properties. Even though cause and effect are non-different, the effect has the nature of the cause, but the cause does not have the nature of the effect — this we shall state in '<s>Ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ</s>' (<s>BBs</s> 2.1.14). And it is too little to say that the effect at dissolution would contaminate the cause with its own properties. For the same contingency applies even during the state of persistence, since the non-difference of cause and effect is accepted. [As the texts state:] 'All this is nothing but this Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6), 'The Self alone is all this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2), 'This immortal <s>Brahman</s> alone is before' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.11), 'All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1) — by such <s>śrutis</s>, the non-difference of the effect from the cause is declared without distinction in all three times. The resolution there — that the effect and its properties are superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and therefore the cause is not contaminated by them — applies equally at the time of dissolution as well. And there is this further illustration: just as a magician is never touched in all three times by his own self-projected <s>māyā</s>, because it is unreal — so too the supreme Self is not touched by the <s>māyā</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And just as one who sees a dream is not touched by the <s>māyā</s> of the dream-vision — because it does not carry over into the waking state and [the state of] deep sleep. So too the one witness of the three states is not touched by the three states, which are changeful — whereas It is unchanging. For this appearance of the supreme Self in the form of the three states is nothing but <s>māyā</s> — like a rope [appearing] in the form of a snake and such. On this topic, the teachers who know the tradition of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s> have stated: 'When the <s>jīva</s>, sleeping from beginningless <s>māyā</s>, awakens, then it knows the unborn, sleepless, dreamless, non-dual [reality]' (<s>Gauḍapāda Kārikā</s> 1.16). Therefore, the objection that at dissolution there would be the contingency of faults such as grossness attaching to the cause just as to the effect — that is unfounded. As for the further objection — that when all differentiation reaches non-differentiation, there can be no determining cause for re-origination with differentiation — this too is not a fault. Because of the existence of illustrations. For just as even in deep sleep, <s>samādhi</s>, and such, when there is a natural attainment of non-differentiation, differentiation occurs again upon awakening because false knowledge has not been sublated — so too it will be in the case [of cosmic dissolution]. And the <s>śruti</s> on this point states: 'All these creatures, having merged into Being, do not know that they have merged into Being. Whatever they were here — whether tiger, lion, wolf, boar, worm, moth, gadfly, or mosquito — that they become again' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.9.2-3). For just as, even in the supreme Self which is non-differentiated, the transactions of differentiation, bound by false knowledge, are seen to persist undisturbed like a dream — so too, even at dissolution, the power of differentiation is to be inferred as bound by false knowledge alone.

children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Apigacchat</s>' means being dissolved.

children.text: vibhāgāvasthā sthitikālaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'State of differentiation' (<s>vibhāgāvasthā</s>) means the time of persistence.

children.text:
sati brahmaṇi ekībhūya na vidurityajñānoktiḥ /
iha suṣupteḥ prāk prabodhe yena jātyādinā vibhaktā bhavanti tadā punarutthānakāle tathaiva bhavantīti vibhāgoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having become one in Being (<s>Brahman</s>), they do not know' — this is a statement about ignorance. 'Here' — prior to deep sleep, upon awakening, they become differentiated by species and such in the same manner as before the time of re-arising: this is the statement about differentiation.

children.text: svapakṣadoṣāc ca | BBs_2,1.10 |
children.translated_text: And because of the faults in the opponent's own position. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.10 |

children.text:
svapakṣe caite prativādinaḥ sādhāraṇā doṣāḥ prāduṣyuḥ /
kathamityucyate /
yattāvadabhihitaṃ vilakṣaṇatvānnedaṃ jagadbrahmaprakṛtikamiti, pradhānaprakṛtikatāyāmapi samānametat, śabdādihīnātpradhānācchabdādimato jagata utpattyabhyupagamāt /
ata eva ca vilakṣaṇakāryotpattyabhyupagamātsamānaḥ prāgutpatterasatkāryavādaprasaṅgaḥ /
tathāpītau kāryasya kāraṇavibhāgābhyupagamāttadvatprasaṅgo 'pi samānaḥ /
tathā mṛditasarvaviśeṣeṣu vikāreṣvapītāvavibhāgātmatāṃ gateṣvidamasya puruṣasyopādānamidamasyeti prākpralayātpratipuruṣaṃ ye niyatā bhedā na te tathaiva punarutpatau niyantuṃ śakyante kāraṇābhāvāt /
vinaiva kāraṇena niyame 'bhyupagamyamāne kāraṇābhāvasāmyānmuktānāmapi punarbandhaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: These very faults would arise in the opponent's own position as well. How? — it is stated: As for the objection 'Because of the dissimilarity [between cause and effect], this world is not originated from <s>Brahman</s>' — the same applies to origination from <s>Pradhāna</s>, since there too the origination of a world possessing sound and such from <s>Pradhāna</s> which is devoid of sound and such is accepted. And precisely because the origination of a dissimilar effect is accepted, the same contingency of the non-existence of the effect prior to origination (<s>asatkāryavāda</s>) applies. Likewise, because the merging of the effect into a state of non-distinction from the cause at dissolution is accepted, the same contingency of contamination applies. Likewise, when at dissolution all modifications, with their specific distinctions obliterated, have attained a state of non-differentiation — 'this is the <s>upādāna</s> (material cause) of this <s>puruṣa</s>, this is of that one' — the specific distinctions that were determinate for each <s>puruṣa</s> prior to dissolution cannot be determined in the same way upon re-origination, because of the absence of a [determining] cause. And if the determination is accepted as occurring without any cause, then because of the equal absence of a cause, there would be the contingency of the liberated also being bound again.

children.text: atha kecidbhedā apītāvavibhāgamāpadyante kenacinneti cet /
children.translated_text: If [it be said that] some distinctions do not attain non-differentiation at dissolution while others do —

children.text: ye nāpadyante teṣāṃ pradhānakāryatvaṃ na prāpnotītyevamete doṣāḥ sādhāraṇatvānnānyatarasminpakṣe codayitavyā bhavantītyadoṣatāmevaiṣāṃ draḍhayati /
children.translated_text: then those that do not attain [non-differentiation] would not qualify as effects of <s>Pradhāna</s>. Thus these faults, being common [to both positions], should not be raised against either position alone — [the text] thereby strengthens the faultlessness of these [objections].

children.text: avaśyāśrayitavyatvāt // 10 //
children.translated_text: Because [the resolution] must necessarily be accepted [by both sides]. // 10 //

children.text: FN: prāduṣyuḥ prādurbhaveyuḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Prāduṣyuḥ</s>' means 'would arise.'

children.text: tarkāpratiṣṭhānād apy anyathānumeyam iti ced evam apy anirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ | BBs_2,1.11 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that] because reasoning has no firm foundation, the matter should be inferred otherwise — even so, the contingency of no liberation [would remain]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.11 |

children.text:
itaśca nāgamagamyer'the kevalena tarkeṇa pratyavasthātavyam /
yasminnirāgamāḥ puruṣotprekṣāmātranibandhanāstarkā apratiṣṭhitā bhavanti /
utprekṣāyā niraṅ kuśatvāt /
tathāhi kaiścidabhiyuktairyatnenotprekṣitāstarkā abhiyuktarairanyairābhāsyamānā dṛśyante /
tairapyutprekṣitāḥ santastato 'nyairābhāsyanta iti na pratiṣṭhitatvaṃ tarkāṇāṃ śakyamāśrayituṃ, puruṣamativairūpyāt /
atha kasyacitprasiddhamāhātmyasya kapilasya cānyasya vā saṃmatastarkaḥ pratiṣṭhita ityāśrīyeta /
evamapyapratiṣṭhitatvameva /
prasiddhamāhātmyānumatānāmapi tīrthakarāṇāṃ kapilakaṇabhukprabhṛtīnāṃ parasparavipratipattidarśanāt /
atocyetānyathā vayamanumāsyāmahe yathā nāpratiṣṭhādoṣo bhaviṣyati /
nahi pratiṣṭhitastarka eva nāstīti śakyate vaktum /
etadapi hi tarkāṇāmapratiṣṭhitatvaṃ tarkeṇaiva pratiṣṭhāpyate /
keṣāñcittarkāṇāmapratiṣṭhitatvadarśanenānyeṣāmapi tajjātīyakānāṃ tarkāṇāmapratiṣṭhitatvāt /
sarvatarkāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ ca lokavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgaḥ /
atītavartamānādhvasāmyena hyanāgate 'pyadhvani sukhaduḥkhaprāptiparihārāya pravartamāno loko dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: for it cannot be said that firmly established reasoning simply does not exist. For even this groundlessness of reasonings is itself established by reasoning alone — from observing the groundlessness of some reasonings, the groundlessness of other reasonings of the same kind [is inferred]. And if all reasoning were groundless, there would be the contingency of the cessation of worldly transactions.

children.text: śrutyarthavipratipattau cārthābhāsanirākaraṇena samyagarthanirdhāraṇaṃ tarkeṇaiva vākyavṛttinirūpaṇarūpeṇa kriyate /
children.translated_text: For the world is seen to engage [in activity] in the future, just as in the past and present, for the sake of attaining happiness and avoiding suffering.

children.text: manurapi caivaṃ manyate- 'pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhāgamam /
children.translated_text: And when there is disagreement about the meaning of <s>śruti</s>, the determination of the correct meaning is accomplished by reasoning itself — in the form of ascertaining the purport of the sentence — by eliminating apparent meanings.

children.text: trayaṃ suviditaṃ kāryaṃ dharmaśuddhimabhīpsitā //
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> also holds this view: 'Perception, inference, and scripture of various traditions —

For this further reason, one should not rely on reasoning alone to oppose a matter established by scripture. Because reasonings that are without scriptural basis, founded merely on human speculation, have no firm standing — due to the unrestrained nature of speculation. For it is seen that reasonings carefully devised by some learned persons are shown to be fallacious by other, more learned persons. And those devised by the latter are in turn shown to be fallacious by yet others. Thus the firm standing of reasonings cannot be relied upon, because of the diversity of human intellects. And if one were to accept as firmly established the reasoning approved by some person of well-known greatness — be it <s>Kapila</s> or anyone else — even so, there would be no firm standing. Because mutual disagreement is seen even among founders of systems who are of well-known greatness — <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Kaṇabhuk</s> (i.e., <s>Kaṇāda</s>), and others. If it be said: 'We will reason in such a way that the fault of groundlessness will not arise' —

children.text: ' iti /
children.translated_text: these three, well understood, should be employed by one who desires purity of <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: 'ārṣaṃ dharmopadeśaṃ ca vedaśāstravirodhinā /
children.translated_text: 'The sacred teaching of <s>dharma</s> given by the sages,

children.text: yastarkeṇānusaṃdhatte sa dharmaṃ veda netaraḥ //
children.translated_text: one who investigates with reasoning that does not contradict Vedic scripture — he alone knows <s>dharma</s>, not another. //

children.text:
' (12.105,106) iti ca bruvan /
ayameva tarkasyālaṅkāro yadapratiṣṭhitatvaṃ nāma /
evaṃhi tāvadyattarkaparityāgena niravadyastarkaḥ pratipattavyo bhavati /
nahi pūrvajo mūḍha āsīdityātmanāpi mūḍhena bhavitavyamiti kiñcidasti pramāṇam /
tasmānna tarkāpratiṣṭhānaṃ doṣa iti cet, evamapyavimokṣaprasaṅgaḥ /
yadyapi kvacidviṣaye tarkasya pratiṣṭhitatvamupalakṣyate tathāpi prakṛte tāvadviṣaye prasajyata evāpratiṣṭhitatvadoṣādanirmokṣastarkasya /
nahīdamatigambhīraṃ bhāvayāthātmyaṃ muktinibandhanamāgamamantareṇotprekṣitumapi śakyam /
rūpādyabhāvāddhi nāyamarthaḥ pratyakṣagocaraḥ, liṅgādyabhāvācca nānumānādīnāmiti cāvocāma /
apica samyagjñānānmokṣa iti sarveṣāṃ mokṣavādināmabhyupagamaḥ /
tacca samyagjñānamekarūpaṃ vastutantratvāt /
ekarūpeṇa hyavasthito yor'thaḥ sa paramārthaḥ /
loke tadviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ samyagjñānamityucyate yathāgniruṣṇā iti /
tatraivaṃ sati samgjñāne puruṣāṇāṃ vipratipattiranupapannā /
tarkajñānānāṃ tvanyonyavirodhātprasiddhā vipratipattiḥ /
yaddhi kenacittārkikeṇedameva samyagjñānamiti pratipāditaṃ tadapareṇa vyutthāpyate, tenāpi pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ tato 'pareṇa vyutthāpyata iti prasiddhaṃ loke /
kathamekarūpānavasthitaviṣayaṃ tarkaprabhavaṃ samyagjñānaṃ bhavet /
naca pradhānavādī tarkavidāmuttama iti sarvāstārkikaiḥ parigṛhīto yena tadīyaṃ mataṃ samyagjñānamiti pratipadyemahi /
naca śakyante 'tītānāgatavartamānāstārkikā ekasmindeśe kāle ca samāhartuṃ yena tanmatirekarūpaikārthaviṣayā samyaṅmatiriti syāta /
vedasya tu nityatve vijñānotpattihetutve ca sati vyavasthitārthaviṣayatvopapattestajjanitasya jñānasya samyaktvamatītānāgatavartamānaiḥ sarvairapi tārkikairapahnotumaśakyam /
children.translated_text: But since the <s>Veda</s> is eternal and is the cause of the arising of knowledge, and since it is reasonable that [the <s>Veda</s>] pertains to an established subject matter, the rightness of the knowledge generated by it cannot be denied even by all logicians — past, future, and present.

children.text: ataḥ siddhamasyaivaupaniṣadasya jñānasya samyagjñānatvam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that this <s>Upaniṣadic</s> knowledge alone is right knowledge.

children.text: ato 'nyatra samyagjñānatvānupapatteḥ saṃsārāvimokṣa eva prasajyeta /
children.translated_text: Since right knowledge is impossible elsewhere, non-liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> would be the necessary consequence [of relying on reasoning alone].

children.text: ata āgamavaśenāgamānusāritarkavaśena ca cetanaṃ brahmajagataḥ kāraṇaṃ prakṛtiśceti sthitam // 11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that conscious <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world and the material source — by the force of scripture and by the force of reasoning that follows scripture. // 11 //

— thus speaking (Mahābhārata 12.105-106).
This itself is the adornment of reasoning — namely, its groundlessness.
For indeed, one must accept faultless reasoning only by abandoning [faulty] reasoning.
There is no proof that 'because a predecessor was deluded, one must oneself also be deluded.'
If it be objected that the groundlessness of reasoning is therefore not a fault — even so, the consequence of non-liberation would follow.
For even if the stability of reasoning is observed in some subject matter, still, in the present subject matter, there is no escape from the fault of groundlessness of reasoning.
For this supremely profound true nature of reality, which is the foundation of liberation, cannot even be conjectured without scripture (<s>āgama</s>).
Because of the absence of form and such, this subject is not within the range of perception; and because of the absence of a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and such, it is not [within the range] of inference and such — this we have already stated.
Moreover, all proponents of liberation accept that liberation comes from right knowledge.
And that right knowledge is of one form, because it depends on the nature of the thing itself.
For that reality which is established in one form — that is the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>).
In the world, knowledge pertaining to that is called right knowledge — just as 'fire is hot.'
This being so, disagreement among people regarding right knowledge is impossible.
But among knowledge-claims based on reasoning, disagreement is well-known due to their mutual contradiction.
For what is established as right knowledge by one logician is overturned by another; what is established by that one is overturned by yet another — this is well-known in the world.
How could right knowledge arise from reasoning, whose object is not established in one form?
Nor is the proponent of <s>Pradhāna</s> accepted by all logicians as the foremost among those who know reasoning, so that we might accept his view as right knowledge.
Nor is it possible to assemble all logicians — past, future, and present — in one place and time, so that their collective view, being of one form and pertaining to one object, might be [called] right understanding.

children.text: FN: tarkasya kaivalyamanugrāhyāgamarāhityam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'The isolation of reasoning' (<s>kaivalya</s>) means its lack of a supporting scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

children.text: dharmasya śuddhiradharmādbhedanirṇayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The purification of <s>dharma</s>' means the ascertainment of its distinction from <s>adharma</s>.

children.text:
atigamabhīratvamāgamātirmekāmānāyogyatvam /
bhāvayāthātmyaṃ kāraṇagatamadvitīyatvam /
muktinibandhanaṃ paramānandasaccidekatānatvam /
children.translated_text:
'The supreme depth' means the unsuitability [of this subject] for reasoning alone as a means of knowledge.
'The true nature of reality' (<s>bhāvayāthātmya</s>) means the non-duality belonging to the cause.
'The foundation of liberation' means the uninterrupted nature of supreme bliss, existence, and consciousness.

children.text: 4 śiṣṭaparigrahādhikaraṇam / sū. 12
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Śiṣṭaparigrahādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of What Is Not Accepted by the Learned). <s>Sūtra</s> 12.

children.text: etena śiṣṭāparigrahā api vyākhyātāḥ | BBs_2,1.12 |
children.translated_text: By this, those [doctrines] not accepted by the learned are also explained. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.12 |

children.text: vaidikasya darśanasya pratyāsannatvādgurutaratarkabalopetatvādvedānusāribhiśca kaiścicchiṣṭhaiḥ kenacidaṃśena parigṛhītatvātpradhānakāraṇavādaṃ tāvadvyapāśritya yastarkanimitta ākṣepo vedāntavākyeṣūdbhāvitaḥ sa parihṛtaḥ /
idānīmaṇvādivādavyapāśrayeṇāpi kaiścinmandamatibhirvedāntavākyeṣu punastarkanimitta ākṣepa āśaṅkyata ityataḥ pradhānamallanibarhaṇanyāyenātidiśati /
children.translated_text: Now, it is apprehended that an objection motivated by reasoning may again be raised against <s>Vedānta</s> passages by certain dull-witted persons relying on the atomist and similar doctrines — hence [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] extends [the refutation] by the principle of 'defeating the chief wrestler' (<s>pradhāna-malla-nibarhaṇa-nyāya</s>).

children.text: parigṛhyanta iti parigrahāḥ na parigrahā aparigrahāḥ śiṣṭānāmaparigrahāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Grammatical analysis:] '<s>Parigrahāḥ</s>' means those that are accepted; '<s>aparigrahāḥ</s>' means those that are not accepted; '<s>śiṣṭānām aparigrahāḥ</s>' means those not accepted by the learned.

children.text: etena prakṛtena pradhānakāraṇavādanirākaraṇakāraṇena śiṣṭairmanuvyāsaprabhṛtibhiḥ kenacidaṃśaṃnāparigṛhītā ye 'ṇvādikāraṇavādāste 'pi pratiṣiddhatayā vyākhyātā nirākṛtā draṣṭavyāḥ tulyatvānnirākaraṇakāraṇasya nātra punarāśaṅkitavyaṃ kiñcidasti /
children.translated_text: By this — by the very reason that was used to refute the <s>Pradhāna</s>-causation doctrine — those doctrines of atom-causation and such, which have not been accepted in any aspect by the learned such as <s>Manu</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and others, should also be considered as refuted and explained [as untenable], since the reason for refutation is the same. Nothing further needs to be objected here.

children.text: tulyamātrāpi paramagambhīrasya jagatkāraṇasya tarkānavagāhyatvaṃ tarkasyāpratiṣṭhitatvamanyathānumāne 'pyavimokṣa āgamavirodhaścetyevañjātīyakaṃ nirākaraṇam // 12 //
children.translated_text: The same type of refutation applies equally: the unfathomability of the supremely profound cause of the world by reasoning, the groundlessness of reasoning, the consequence of non-liberation even in alternative inference, and the contradiction with scripture — such is the nature of the refutation. // 12 //

Relying on the <s>Pradhāna</s>-causation doctrine — because it is close to the Vedic view, because it is supported by stronger reasoning, and because it has been accepted in some aspect by certain learned persons who follow the <s>Veda</s> — the objection motivated by reasoning that was raised against <s>Vedānta</s> passages has [now] been answered.

children.text: 5 bhoktrāpattyādhikaraṇam / sū. 13
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Bhoktrāpatti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Consequence for the Experiencer). <s>Sūtra</s> 13.

children.text: bhoktrāpatter avibhāgaś cet syāl lokavat | BBs_2,1.13 |
children.translated_text: If [there is] non-distinction because of the consequence of [<s>Brahman</s> becoming] the experiencer — [we say] it would be as in the world. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.13 |

children.text:
anyathā punarbrahmakāraṇavādastarkabalenaivākṣipyate /
yadyapi śrutiḥ pramāṇaṃ svaviṣaye bhavati tathāpi pramāṇāntareṇa viṣayāpahāre 'nyaparā bhavitumarti /
yathā mantrārthavādau /
tarke 'pi svaviṣayādanyatrāpratiṣṭhitaḥ syāt yathā dharmādharmayoḥ /
kimato yadyevam /
ata idamayuktaṃ yatpramāṇāntaraprasiddhārthabādhanaṃ śruteḥ /
kathaṃ punaḥ pramāṇāntaraprasiddhor'thaḥ śrutyā bādhyata iti /
children.translated_text:
In yet another way, the doctrine of <s>Brahman</s>-causation is challenged by the force of reasoning alone.
Although <s>śruti</s> is authoritative in its own domain, still, when its subject matter is taken away by another means of knowledge, it becomes [merely] figurative.
Just as <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s> [are taken figuratively].
Reasoning too might be groundless in domains other than its own — as in the case of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
What follows from this?
From this, it is improper for <s>śruti</s> to negate a meaning established by another means of knowledge.
But how is a meaning established by another means of knowledge negated by <s>śruti</s>?

children.text:
atrocyate- prasiddho hyayaṃ bhoktṛbhogyavibhāgo loke bhoktā cetanaḥ śārīro bhogyāḥ śabdādayo viṣayā iti /
yathā bhoktā devadatto bhojya odana iti /
tasya ca vibhāgasyābhāvaḥ prasajyeta yadi bhoktā bhogyabhāvamāpadyeta /
bhogyaṃ vā bhoktṛbhāvamāpadyeta /
tayoścetaretarabhāvāpattiḥ paramakāraṇādbrahmaṇo 'nanyatvātprasajyeta /
nacāsya prasiddhasya vibhāgasya bādhanaṃ yuktam /
yathā tvadyatve bhoktṛbhogyayorvibhāgo dṛṣṭastathātītānāgatayorapi kalpayitavyaḥ /
tasmātprasiddhasyāsya bhoktṛbhogyavibhāgasyābhāvaprasaṅgādayuktamidaṃ brahmakāraṇatāvadhāraṇamiti cetkaściccodayettaṃ pratibrūyāt- syāllokavaditi /
upapadyata evāyamasmatpakṣe 'pi vibhāgaḥ evaṃ loke dṛṣṭatvāt /
tathāhi- samudrādudakātmano 'nanyatve 'pi tadvikārāṇāṃ phenavīcītaraṅgādīnāmitaretaravibhāga itaretarasaṃśleṣādilakṣaṇaśca vyavahāra upalabhyate /
naca samudrādudakātmano 'nanyatve 'pi tadvikārāṇāṃ phenataraṅgādīnāmitaretarabhāvāpattirbhavati /
naca teṣāmitaretarabhāvānāpattāvapi samudrātmano 'nyatvaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And even though they do not undergo mutual transformation, there is no otherness [of the modifications] from the ocean itself.

children.text: evamihāpi naca bhoktṛbhogyayoritaretarabhāvāpattiḥ, naca parasmādbrahmaṇo 'nyatvaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Similarly here too, there will be neither mutual transformation of the experiencer and the experienced, nor otherness from the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yadyapi bhoktā na brahmaṇo vikāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Although the experiencer is not a modification of <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: 'tatsṛṣṭvā tadevānuprāviśat' (tai. 2.6) iti sraṣṭurevāvikṛtasya kāryānupraveśena bhoktṛtvaśravaṇāt, tathāpi kāryamanupraviṣṭasyāstyupādhinimitto vibhāga ākāśasyeva ghaṭādyupādhinimitta ityataḥ paramakāraṇabrahmaṇo 'nanyatvaṃ'pyupapadyate bhoktṛbhogyalakṣaṇo vibhāgaḥ samudrataraṅgādinyāyenetyuktam // 13 //
children.translated_text: Because the <s>śruti</s> states that the creator himself, unmodified, entered into the creation — 'Having created it, he entered into that very [creation]' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6) — and [thus] experiencership is heard of the creator who entered into the effect; nevertheless, for the one who has entered the effect, there is a distinction caused by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), just as space [has distinction] caused by the limiting adjuncts of pots and such — and therefore, even though [the experiencer] is non-different from the supreme cause <s>Brahman</s>, the distinction characterized by experiencer and experienced is possible, by the analogy of the ocean and its waves and such — this has been stated. // 13 //

To this it is said: For the distinction between experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) and experienced (<s>bhogya</s>) is well-established in the world — the experiencer is the conscious embodied self, the experienced objects are sounds and such.
Just as <s>Devadatta</s> is the experiencer and cooked rice is the experienced.
The absence of that distinction would follow if the experiencer were to become the experienced,
or the experienced were to become the experiencer.
And this mutual transformation of the two would follow from their non-difference from the supreme cause, <s>Brahman</s>.
And it is not proper to negate this well-established distinction.
Just as the distinction of experiencer and experienced is seen in the present, so too it should be inferred for the past and the future.
Therefore, because of the consequence of the absence of this well-established distinction of experiencer and experienced, this determination of <s>Brahman</s>'s causality is improper — if someone were to object thus, one should reply: 'It would be as in the world.'
This distinction is possible even in our position, because it is seen to be so in the world.
For example — even though waves, foam, and bubbles, which are modifications of water, are not other than the ocean, which is of the nature of water, still the mutual distinction and mutual connection and such of those modifications — foam, waves, bubbles, and the like — are observed.
And even though they are not other than the ocean, which is of the nature of water, still there is no mutual transformation of those modifications — foam, waves, and the like.

children.text:
FN: anyaparatvaṃ gauṇārthakatvam /
vibhāgo janma /
yadvā tathāpītiśabdenaivoktaḥ parihāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: '<s>Anyaparatva</s>' means having a figurative meaning.
'<s>Vibhāga</s>' means origination.
Alternatively, the resolution is stated by the word '<s>tathāpi</s>' (nevertheless) itself.

children.text: 6 ārambhaṇādhikaraṇam / sū. 14-20
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Ārambhaṇādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Origination). <s>Sūtras</s> 14-20.

children.text: tadananyatvam ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ | BBs_2,1.14 |
children.translated_text: The non-difference of that [effect from the cause] — because of the word '<s>ārambhaṇa</s>' (origination) and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.14 |

children.text:
abhyupagamya cemaṃ vyāvahārikaṃ bhoktṛbhogyalakṣaṇaṃ vibhāgaṃ syāllokavaditi parihāroṣa'bhihitaḥ /
natvayaṃ vibhāgaḥ paramārthato 'sti yasmāttayoḥ kāryakāraṇayorananyatvamavagamyate /
kāryamākāśādikaṃ bahuprapañcaṃ jagat, kāraṇaṃ paraṃbrahma, tasmātkāraṇātparamārthato 'nanyatvaṃ vyatirekeṇābhāvaḥ kāryasyāvagamyate /
kutaḥ /
ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ /
ārambhaṇaśabdastāvat /
ekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ pratijñāya dṛṣṭāntāpekṣāyāmucyate- 'yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syādvācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyam' (chā. 6.1.1) iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- ekena mṛtpiṇḍena paramārthato mṛdātmanā vijñātena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ ghaṭaśarāvodañcanādikaṃ mṛdātmakatvāviśeṣādvijñātaṃ bhavet /
yato vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ vācaiva kevalamastītyārabhyate /
vikāro ghaṭaḥ śarāva udañcanaṃ ceti /
natu vastuvṛttena vikāro nāma kaścidasti /
nāmadheyamātraṃ hyetadanṛtaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyamiti /
eṣa brahmaṇo dṛṣṭāntaḥ āmnātaḥ /
tatra śrutādvācārambhaṇaśabdāddārṣṭāntike 'pi brahmavyatirekeṇa kāryajātasyābhāva iti gamyate /
punaśca tejobannānāṃ brahmakāryatāmuktvā tejobannakāryāṇāṃ tejobannavyatirekeṇābhāvaṃ bravīti- 'apāgādagneragnitvaṃ vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇītyeva satyam' (chā. 6.4.1) ityādinā /
ārambhaṇaśabdādibhya ityādiśabdāt 'aitadātmyamidaṃ sarvaṃ tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7), 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' (bṛ. 2.4.6), 'brahmaivedaṃ sarvam' (mu. 2.2.11), 'ātmaivedaṃ sarvam' (chā. 7.25.2), 'neha nānāsti kiñcana' (bṛ.4.4.19) ityevamādyapyātmaikatvapratipādanaparaṃ vacanajātamudāhartavyam /
nacānyathaikavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ saṃpadyate /
tasmādyathā ghaṭakarakādyākāśānāṃ mahākāśānanyatvaṃ, yathāca mṛgatṛṣṇikodakādīnāmūṣarādibhyo 'nanyatvaṃ dṛṣṭanaṣṭasvarūpatvātsvarūpeṇānupākhyatvāt, evamasya bhogyabhoktrādiprapañcajātasya brahmavyatirekeṇābhāva iti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text:
Having granted this empirical (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) distinction characterized by experiencer and experienced, the resolution 'it would be as in the world' was stated.
But this distinction does not exist in ultimate reality, because the non-difference of the two — cause and effect — is understood.
The effect is the world of manifold diversity beginning with space (<s>ākāśa</s>); the cause is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; and from that cause, in ultimate reality, the non-difference — that is, the non-existence apart [from the cause] — of the effect is understood.
From what?
From the word '<s>ārambhaṇa</s>' (origination) and such.
First, the word '<s>ārambhaṇa</s>': Having declared that by knowing one thing, everything becomes known, and when an illustration is sought, it is said: 'O dear one, just as by one lump of clay, everything made of clay becomes known; the modification is merely a name, a verbal handle (<s>vācārambhaṇa</s>); clay alone is the reality' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.1).
What is stated here amounts to this: By one lump of clay — known in its ultimate reality as being of the nature of clay — everything made of clay — pots, saucers, water-vessels, and such — becomes known, because there is no distinction in being of the nature of clay.
Because the modification is merely a name, a verbal handle — it is originated by speech alone.
The modification — pot, saucer, water-vessel, and such —
