yathā loke devāḥ pitara ṛṣaya ityevamādayo mahāprabhāvāścetanā api santo 'napekṣyaiva kiñcidbāhyaṃ sādhanamaiśvaryaviśeṣayogādabhidhyānamātreṇa svata eva bahūni nānāsaṃsthāni śarīrīṇi prāsādādīni ca rathādīni ca nirmimāṇā upalabhyante mantrārthavādetihāsapurāṇaprāmāṇyāt /
tantunābhaśca svata eva tantūnsṛjati /
balākā cāntareṇaiva śukraṃ garbhaṃ dhatte /
padminī cānapekṣya kiñcitprastānasādhanaṃ sarontarātsarontaraṃ pratiṣṭhate /
evaṃ cetanamapi brahmānapekṣya bāhyaṃ sādhanaṃ svata eva jagatsrakṣyati /
sa yadi brūyādya ete devādayo brahmaṇo dṛṣṭāntā upāttāste dārṣṭrāntikena brahmaṇā na samānā bhavanti /
śarīrameva hyacetanaṃ devādīnāṃ śarīrāntarādivibhūtyutpādana upādānaṃ natu cetana ātmā /
tantunābhyā ca kṣudratarajantubhakṣaṇāllālā kaṭhinatāmāpadyamānā tanturbhavati /
balākā ca stanayitnuravaśravaṇādgarbhaṃ dhatte /
padminī ca cetanaprayuktā satyacetanevaiva śarīreṇa sarontaropasarpaṇe vyāpriyate /
tasmānaite brahmaṇo dṛṣṭāntā iti /
taṃ prati brūyānnāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: To that one should reply: This is not a fault.

children.text: kulālādidṛṣṭāntavailakṣaṇyamātrasya vivakṣitatvāditi /
children.translated_text: Because only the dissimilarity from the illustration of the potter and such is intended.

children.text: yathā hi kulālādīnāṃ devādīnāṃ ca samāne cetanatve kulālādayaḥ kāryārambhe bāhyaṃ sādhanamapekṣante na devādayaḥ, tathā brahma cetanamapi na bāhyaṃ sādhanamapekṣiṣyata ityetadvākyaṃ devādyudāharaṇena vivakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as, given that potters and gods share the common feature of being conscious, potters require external means for initiating their work while gods do not — so too, <s>Brahman</s>, though conscious, will not require external means: this is the statement that we intend to make through the example of gods and such.

children.text: tasmādyathaikasya sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tathā sarveṣāmeva bhavitumarhatīti nāstyekānta ityabhiprāyaḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the purport is: Since the capacity observed in one [conscious being] may well belong to all, there is no absolute rule [that conscious agents always need external means]. // 25 //

One might say: It is possible for milk and such, which are insentient, to transform into curds and such without depending on external means — because it is observed.
But conscious [agents] such as potters and the like are seen to undertake their respective tasks only by depending on an aggregate of means.
How would <s>Brahman</s>, being conscious and truly without assistance, proceed [to create]?
[We reply:] 'As in the case of gods and such.'
Just as in the world, gods, ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>), sages, and other such beings of great power — even though conscious — without depending on any external means, by the power of their special lordship, through mere deliberation (<s>abhidhyāna</s>), by themselves alone, are observed to create manifold bodies and forms, palaces, chariots, and the like — on the authority of <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, <s>itihāsas</s>, and <s>purāṇas</s>.
And the spider (<s>tantunābha</s>) produces threads from itself alone.
And the crane (<s>balākā</s>) conceives its embryo without [the intervention of] semen.
And the lotus (<s>padminī</s>), without depending on any means of locomotion, moves from one pond to another.
Similarly, even conscious <s>Brahman</s>, without depending on external means, will create the world from itself alone.
If one were to say: These illustrations of gods and such that are cited for <s>Brahman</s> are not comparable to <s>Brahman</s> as the thing illustrated.
For it is the insentient body alone of the gods and such that is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) for producing extraordinary manifestations such as other bodies — not the conscious self.
And in the case of the spider, from the consumption of tiny insects, the saliva becomes hardened and becomes the thread.
And the crane conceives the embryo from hearing the sound of thunder.
And the lotus, being directed by a conscious [agent], engages in locomotion from pond to pond by means of its insentient body alone.
Therefore, these are not illustrations for <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text:
FN: lokyate jñāyater'thoneneti loko mantrārthavādādiśāstraṃ vṛddhavyavahāraśca /
abhidhyānaṃ saṃkalpaḥ /
yathā bhārate śrīkṛṣṇasya saṃkalpamātreṇa draupadyāḥ paṭaparamparotpattiḥ tathā asahāyasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ kāraṇatvam /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: '<s>Loka</s>' means the scriptures such as <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, and such, and the conduct of the wise — [it is so called] because the meaning is known (<s>lokyate</s>) through it.
'<s>Abhidhyāna</s>' means intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>).
Just as in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the garments of <s>Draupadī</s> were produced in succession by the mere will of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — so too, the causality of <s>Brahman</s>, even without assistance, [is established].

children.text: 9 kṛtsnaprasaktyadhikaraṇam / sū. 26-29
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Kṛtsnaprasakti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Consequence of Complete [Transformation]). <s>Sūtras</s> 26-29.

children.text: kṛtsnaprasaktir niravayavatvaśabdakopo vā | BBs_2,1.26 |
children.translated_text: Either the consequence of complete [transformation], or — [if only partial,] a contradiction with the statement of partlessness. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.26 |

children.text:
cetanamekamadvitīyaṃ brahma kṣīrādivaddevādivaccānapekṣya bāhyasādhanaṃ svayaṃ pariṇamamānaṃ jagataḥ kāraṇamiti sthitam /
śāstrārthapariśuddhaye tu punarākṣipati /
kṛtsnaprasaktiḥ kṛtsnasya brahmaṇaḥ kāryarūpeṇa pariṇāmaḥ prāpnoti,
children.translated_text:
It has been established that conscious <s>Brahman</s>, one without a second, like milk, like gods, and such, without depending on external means, transforming by itself, is the cause of the world.
But for the purpose of purifying the meaning of the scripture, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] raises a further objection.
[The objection is:] The consequence of complete [transformation] — the transformation of <s>Brahman</s> in its entirety into the form of the effect — would follow,

children.text:
niravayavatvāt /
yadi brahma pathivyādivatsāvayavamabhaviṣyattato 'syaikadeśaḥ paryaṇaṃsyadekadeśaścāvāsthāsyat /
niravayavaṃ tu brahma śrutibhyo 'vagamyate- 'niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntaṃ niravadyaṃ nirañjanam' (śve. 6.19), 'divyo hyamūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sabāhyābhyantarohyajaḥ' (mu. 2.1.2), 'idaṃ mahadbhūtamanantamapāraṃ vijñānaghana eva' (bṛ. 2.4.12), 'sa eṣa neti netyātmā' (bṛ. 3.9.26), 'asthūlamanaṇu' (bṛ. 3.8.8) ityādyābhyaḥ sarvaviśeṣapratiṣedhinībhyaḥ /
tataścaikadeśapariṇāmasaṃbhavātkṛtsnapariṇāmaprasaktau satyāṃ mūlocchedaḥ prasajyeta /
draṣṭavyatopadeśānarthakyaṃ cāpannamayatnadraṣṭatvātkāryasya, tadvyatiriktasya ca brahmaṇo 'saṃbhavāt ajatvādiśabdakopaśca /
children.translated_text: And the purposelessness of the teaching 'it is to be seen' would result, since the effect would be seen without effort; and since <s>Brahman</s> as something distinct from [the effect] would be impossible, there would also be a conflict with scriptural words such as 'unborn' and the like.

children.text: athaitaddoṣaparijihīrṣayā sāvayavameva brahmābhyupagamyeta tathāpi ye niravayavatvasya pratipādakāḥ śabdā udāhṛtāste prakuṣyeyuḥ /
children.translated_text: And if, in order to avoid this fault, <s>Brahman</s> were accepted as having parts — even then, the scriptural texts cited as establishing partlessness would be contradicted.

children.text: sāvayavatve cānityatvaprasaṅga iti /
children.translated_text: And if [<s>Brahman</s>] has parts, there would be the contingency of impermanence.

children.text: sarvathāyaṃ pakṣo na ghaṭayituṃ śakyata ityākṣipati // 26 //
children.translated_text: In every way, this position cannot be made consistent — thus [the opponent] raises the objection. // 26 //

because [<s>Brahman</s>] is without parts.
If <s>Brahman</s> had parts like earth and such, then one part of it would transform while another part would remain.
But <s>Brahman</s> is understood from the <s>śruti</s> to be without parts — from passages such as 'Without parts, without activity, tranquil, without fault, without stain' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.19), 'The divine <s>Puruṣa</s> is formless, both internal and external, unborn' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2), 'This great being, infinite, limitless, is a mass of consciousness alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.12), 'This Self is "not this, not this"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.26), 'Neither gross nor subtle' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8) — and other [passages] that negate all distinguishing features.
And since partial transformation is impossible, when the consequence of complete transformation arises, the uprooting [of <s>Brahman</s> itself] would follow.

children.text:
FN: paryaṇaṃsyat pariṇato 'bhaviṣyat /
ekadeśaścāvasthāsyadapariṇato 'bhaviṣyat /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Paryaṇaṃsyat</s>' means 'would have transformed.' 'And one portion would remain' — [meaning] would not have transformed.

children.text: śrutes tu śabdamūlatvāt | BBs_2,1.27 |
children.translated_text: But [this is not so], because of <s>śruti</s>, since [<s>Brahman</s>] is rooted in scripture. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.27 |

children.text:
tuśabdenākṣepaṃ pariharati /
na khalvasmatpakṣe kaścidapi doṣo 'sti /
na tāvatkṛtsnaprasaktirasti /
kutaḥ /
śruteḥ /
yathaiva hi brahmaṇo jagadutpattiḥ śrūyata evaṃ vikāravyatirekeṇāpi brahmaṇo 'vastānaṃ śrūyate, prakṛtivikārayorbhedena vyapadeśāt 'seyaṃ devataikṣata hantāhamimāstisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi' (chā. 6.3.2) iti, 'tāvānasya mahimā tato jyāyāṃśca puruṣaḥ /
pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' (chā. 3.12.6) iti caivañjātīyakāt /
tathā hṛdayāyatanatvavacanātsatsaṃpattivacanācca /
yadi ca kṛtsnaṃ brahma kāryābhāvenopayuktaṃ syāt 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati' (chā. 6.81) iti suṣuptigataṃ viśeṣaṇamanupapannaṃ syāt /
vikṛtena brahmaṇā nityasaṃpannatvādivikṛtasya ca brahmaṇo 'bhāvāt /
tathendriyagocaratvapratiṣedhādbrahmaṇo vikārasya cendriyagocaratvopapatteḥ /
tasmādastyavikṛtaṃ brahma /
naca niravayavatvaśabdakopo 'sti, śrūyamāṇatvādeva niravayavatvasyāpyabhyupagamyamānatvāt /
śabdamūlaṃ ca brahma śabdapramāṇakaṃ nendriyādipramāṇakaṃ tadyathāśabdamabhyupagantavyam /
śabdaścobhayamapi brahmaṇaḥ pratipādayatyakṛtsnaprasaktiṃ niravayavatvaṃ ca /
laukikānāmapi maṇimantrauṣadhiprabhṛtīnāṃ deśakālanimittavaicitryavaśācchaktayo viruddhānekakāryaviṣayā dṛśyante /
tā api tāvannopadeśamantareṇa kevalena tarkeṇāvagantuṃ śakyante 'sya vastuna etāvatya etatsahāya etadviṣayā etatprayojanāśca śaktaya iti /
children.translated_text: Those [powers] too cannot be ascertained by mere reasoning alone, without instruction — [one cannot determine] 'this thing has powers of such extent, with such auxiliaries, pertaining to such objects, and having such purposes.'

children.text: kimutācintyasvabhāvasya brahmaṇo rūpaṃ vinā śabdena na nirūpyeta /
children.translated_text: How much less, then, could the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is inconceivable, be determined without scripture?

children.text: tathācāhuḥ paurāṇikāḥ - 'acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃstarkeṇa yojayet /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (the authors of the <s>Purāṇas</s>) say: 'Those things that are inconceivable — one should not try to apply reasoning to them.

children.text: prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṃ yacca tadacintyasya lakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: That which is beyond the material natures (<s>prakṛtis</s>) — that is the mark of the inconceivable.'

By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] resolves the objection. There is indeed no fault whatsoever in our position. First, there is no [problem of] total involvement [of <s>Brahman</s> in transformation]. Why? Because of <s>śruti</s>. For just as the origination of the world from <s>Brahman</s> is heard, so too the subsistence of <s>Brahman</s> apart from its modifications is heard — because of the designation of the material cause and its modifications as distinct: 'This deity thought: "Come, let me enter these three deities with this living Self and manifest names and forms"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2), and 'Such is His greatness, yet greater than that is the <s>Puruṣa</s>; one quarter of Him is all beings, three quarters of Him is the immortal in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.6) — and from passages of this kind. Likewise, from the statement that [<s>Brahman</s>] has the heart as its abode, and from the statement of merging into Being [in deep sleep]. For if the whole of <s>Brahman</s> were used up in becoming the effect, then the qualification pertaining to deep sleep — 'You are then, dear one, merged in Being' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1) — would be untenable. Because [the <s>jīva</s>] would always be merged in the transformed <s>Brahman</s>, and because unmodified <s>Brahman</s> would not exist. Likewise, because the <s>śruti</s> negates [<s>Brahman</s>] as being within the range of the senses, and because it is tenable that the modification is within the range of the senses. Therefore, unmodified <s>Brahman</s> exists. And there is no conflict with the scriptural texts [establishing] partlessness, because partlessness too is accepted precisely as it is heard in <s>śruti</s>. And <s>Brahman</s> is rooted in scripture — its valid means of knowledge is scripture, not the senses and such; it should be accepted as scripture states. And scripture establishes both of <s>Brahman</s>'s [aspects] — the non-total involvement [in transformation] and partlessness. Even among worldly things such as gems, <s>mantras</s>, medicinal herbs, and the like, powers relating to multiple contradictory effects are seen, by virtue of the variety of place, time, and cause.

children.text: ' iti tasmācchabdamūla evātīndriyārthayāthātmyādhigamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the ascertainment of the true nature of supersensuous objects is rooted in scripture alone.

children.text:
nanu śabdenāpi na śakyate viruddhor'thaḥ pratyāyayituṃ niravayavaṃ ca brahma pariṇamate naca kṛtsnamiti /
yadi niravayavaṃ brahma syānnaiva pariṇameta /
kṛtsnameva vā pariṇameta /
atha kenacidrūpeṇa pariṇameta kenaciccāvatiṣṭheteti rūpabhedakalpanātsāvayavameva prasajyeta /
kriyāviṣaye hi 'atirātre ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhṇāti' 'nātirātre ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhṇāti' ityevañjātīyakāyāṃ virodhapratītāvapi vikalpāśrayaṇaṃ virodhaparihārakāraṇaṃ bhavati puruṣatantratvāccānuṣṭhānasya /
iha tu vikalpāśrayaṇenāpi na virodhaparihāraḥ saṃbhavatyapuruṣatantratvādvastunaḥ tasmāddurghaṭametaditi /
children.translated_text: But can scripture itself convey a contradictory meaning — that <s>Brahman</s> is partless and yet transforms, and not totally? If <s>Brahman</s> were partless, it would not transform at all; or it would transform entirely. And if it were to transform in one aspect and remain in another, then — because of the supposition of a distinction of aspects — it would turn out to have parts. In the domain of action, where there is a perceived contradiction like 'One takes the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> cup at the <s>atirātra</s>' and 'One does not take the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> cup at the <s>atirātra</s>' — the resort to optionality serves as a means to resolve the contradiction, because ritual performance is dependent on human will. But here, even by resorting to optionality, the resolution of the contradiction is not possible, because the nature of a thing is not dependent on human will. Therefore, this is difficult to reconcile — [so says the objector].

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
avidyākalpitarūpabhedābhyupagamāt /
nahyavidyākalpitena rūpabhedena sāvayavaṃ vastu saṃpadyate /
nahi timiropahatanayanenāneka iva candramā dṛśyamāno 'neka eva bhavati /
avidyākalpitena ca nāmarūpalakṣaṇena rūpabhedena vyākṛtāvyākṛtātmakena tattvānyatvābhyāmanirvacanīyena brahma pariṇāmādisarvavyavahārāspadatvaṃ pratipadyate /
pāramārthikena ca rūpeṇa sarvavyavahārātītamapariṇamatavatiṣṭhate /
vācārambhaṇamātratvāccāvidyākalpitasya nāmarūpabhedasyeti na niravayavatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ kupyati /
naceyaṃ pariṇāmaśrutiḥ pariṇāmapratipādanārthā, tatpratipattau phalānavagamāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is this scriptural statement of transformation intended for establishing transformation — because no result is known from comprehending that.

children.text: sarvavyavahārahīnabrahmātmabhāvapratipādanārthā tveṣā, tatpratiphalāvagamāt /
children.translated_text: Rather, this [statement] is intended for establishing the identity of the Self with <s>Brahman</s>, which is devoid of all conventional activity — because a result is known from comprehending that.

children.text: 'sa eṣa neti netyātmā' ityupakramyāha- 'abhayaṃ vai janaka prāpto 'si' (bṛ. 4.2.4) iti /
children.translated_text: Having begun with 'This Self is "not this, not this"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.26), [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'O <s>Janaka</s>, you have attained fearlessness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.2.4).

children.text: tasmādasmatpakṣe na kaścidapi doṣaprasaṅgo 'sti // 27 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in our position, there is no contingency of any fault whatsoever. // 27 //

This is not a fault. Because the distinction of aspects is accepted as imagined through <s>avidyā</s>. For a thing does not become composite through a distinction of aspects imagined through <s>avidyā</s>. For the moon, perceived as many by one whose eyes are afflicted by <s>timira</s> (an eye disease), does not become many. And through the distinction of aspects characterized by name and form — imagined through <s>avidyā</s>, consisting of the manifest and the unmanifest, indeterminable as either identical with or different from [<s>Brahman</s>] — <s>Brahman</s> becomes the substratum of all conventional activity such as transformation and the like. But in its ultimate nature, it remains beyond all conventional activity, untransformed. And because the distinction of name and form imagined through <s>avidyā</s> is merely a verbal handle (<s>vācārambhaṇa-mātra</s>), the partlessness of <s>Brahman</s> is not violated.

children.text: ātmani caivaṃ vicitrāś ca hi | BBs_2,1.28 |
children.translated_text: And in the Self too, because of manifold [creation]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.28 |

children.text: apica naivātra vivaditavyaṃ kathamekasminbrahmaṇi svarūpānupamardenaivānekākārā sṛṣṭiḥ syāditi /
children.translated_text: Moreover, one should not dispute about how, in the one <s>Brahman</s>, manifold creation can occur without any impairment of its own nature.

children.text: yata ātmanyapyekasminsvapnadṛśi svarūpānupamardenaivānekākārā sṛṣṭiḥ paṭhyate- 'na tatra rathā na rathayogo na panthāno bhavantyatha rathārathayogānpathaḥ sṛjate' ( bṛ. 4.3.10) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: For even in the one Self that perceives dreams, manifold creation is described as occurring without impairment of its own nature: 'There are no chariots there, no horses yoked to chariots, no roads — yet it creates chariots, horses yoked to chariots, and roads' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.10) — and so forth.

children.text: loke 'pi devādiṣu māyāvyādiṣu ca svapnarūpānupamardenaiva vicitrā hastyaśvādisṛṣṭayo dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: In the world too, among gods, magicians, and such, manifold creations of elephants, horses, and the like are seen without impairment of [the creators'] own form.

children.text: tathaikasminnapi brahmaṇi svarūpānupamardenaivānekākārā sṛṣṭirbhaviṣyatīti // 28 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the one <s>Brahman</s> too, manifold creation will occur without impairment of its own nature. // 28 //

children.text: svapakṣadoṣāc ca | BBs_2,1.29 |
children.translated_text: And because of the faults in the opponent's own position. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.29 |

children.text:
pareṣāmapyeṣa samānaḥ svapakṣe doṣaḥ /
pradhānavādino 'pi hi niravayavamaparicchinnaṃ śabdādihīnaṃ pradhānaṃ sāvavasya paricchinnasya śabdādimataḥ kāryasya kāraṇamiti svapakṣaḥ /
tatrāpi kṛtsnaprasaktirniravayavatvātpradhānasya prāpnoti niravayavatvābhyupagamakopo vā /
children.translated_text: For the opponents too, the same fault arises in their own position. For the proponents of <s>Pradhāna</s> too, their own position is that partless, unlimited <s>Pradhāna</s>, devoid of sound and such, is the cause of the effect that has parts, is limited, and possesses sound and such. There too, the [problem of] total involvement arises because of the partlessness of <s>Pradhāna</s> — or the acceptance of partlessness is contradicted.

children.text:
nanu naiva tairniravayavaṃ pradhānamabhyupagamyate, sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇā nityāsteṣāṃ sāmyāvasthā pradhāne tairevāvayavaistatsāvayavamiti /
naivañjātīyakena sāvayavatvena prakṛto doṣaḥ parihartuṃ pāryate /
yataḥ sattvarajastamasāmapyekaikasya samānaṃ niravayavatvam /
ekaikameva cetaradvayānugṛhītaṃ sajātīyasya prapañcasyopādānamiti samānatvātsvapakṣadoṣaprasaṅgasya /
tarkapratiṣṭhānātsāvayavatvameveti cet /
children.translated_text: But [the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> say]: <s>Pradhāna</s> is not accepted by them as partless — <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s>, the three <s>guṇas</s>, are eternal; the state of equilibrium of these is <s>Pradhāna</s>; with these very parts it has parts. [We reply:] This kind of having-parts cannot resolve the fault under discussion. For each of <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> individually is equally partless. And each one, assisted by the other two, being the material cause of the phenomenal world of its own kind — because of this similarity, the contingency of the fault in one's own position [remains]. If [you say] that having parts is established by reasoning —

children.text:
evavamapyanityatvādidoṣaprasaṅgaḥ /
atha śaktaya eva kāryavaicitryasūcitā avayavā ityabhiprāyaḥ /
tāstu brahmavādino 'pyavaśiṣṭāḥ /
tathāṇuvādino 'pyaṇuraṇvantareṇa saṃyujyamāno niravayavatvādyadi kārtsyena saṃyujyeta tataḥ prathimānupapatteraṇumātratvaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, for the proponents of atoms too: an atom, being joined with another atom — since it is partless — if it is joined entirely, then because the expansion [of the composite] cannot be explained, there would be the contingency of [the composite] being merely atomic in size.

children.text: athaikadeśena saṃyujyeta tathāpi niravayavatvābhyupagamakopa iti svapakṣe 'pi samāna eṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If it is joined by one part, then even so, the acceptance of partlessness would be contradicted — thus the same fault exists in their own position as well.

children.text: samānatvācca nānyanyatarasminneva pakṣa upakṣeptavyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: And because it is common [to both sides], it should not be raised against one position alone.

children.text: parihṛtastu brahmavādinā svapakṣe doṣaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: But the proponent of <s>Brahman</s> has resolved the fault in his own position. // 29 //

even so, there would be the contingency of faults such as impermanence. Or if the intended meaning is that the powers implied by the variety of effects are the 'parts' — then those [powers] remain for the proponent of <s>Brahman</s> as well.

children.text: FN: vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ hyaṇubhyāṃ saṃyujya hyaṇukamekamārabhyate, taistribhirhyaṇukaistryaṇukamekamārabhyata iti prakriyā /
children.translated_text: NOTE: For the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, the procedure is: two atoms join to produce one dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>), and three such dyads produce one triad (<s>tryaṇuka</s>).

children.text: 10 sarvopetādhikaraṇam / sū. 30-31
children.translated_text: 10. The <s>Sarvopetādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Being Endowed with Everything). <s>Sūtras</s> 30-31.

children.text: sarvopetā ca taddarśanāt | BBs_2,1.30 |
children.translated_text: [<s>Brahman</s>] is endowed with everything — because that is observed [in scripture]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.30 |

children.text:
ekasyāpi brahmaṇo vicitraśaktiyogādupapadyate vicitro vikāraprapañca ityuktam /
tatpunaḥ kathamavagamyate paraṃ brahmeti /
taducyate /
sarvopetā ca taddarśanāt /
sarvaśaktiyuktā ca parā devatetyabhyupagantavyam /
children.translated_text: The supreme deity is to be accepted as endowed with all powers.

children.text: kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: taddarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because that is observed [in scripture].

children.text: yathāhi darśayati śrutiḥ sarvaśaktiyogaṃ parasyā devatāyāḥ - 'sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvamidamabhyātto 'vākyanādaraḥ' (chā. 3.14.4), 'satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' (chā. 8.7.1), 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit' (muṇḍa. 1.1.9), 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgisūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ' (bṛ. 3.8.9) ityevañjātīyakā // 30 //
children.translated_text: For <s>śruti</s> shows the connection of all powers with the supreme deity: '[That which is] of all actions, all desires, all fragrances, all tastes, pervading all this, silent, unconcerned' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.4), 'Of true desire, of true resolve' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1), 'Who is omniscient, who knows all' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9), 'Under the rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon are held in their places' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.9) — passages of this kind. // 30 //

It has been said that, because of the one <s>Brahman</s>'s connection with manifold powers, the manifold elaboration of modifications is tenable. How, then, is it understood that this is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>? To that it is said: [<s>Brahman</s>] is endowed with everything — because that is observed.

children.text:
FN: abhyāttaḥ abhitovyāptaḥ /
avākī vāgindriyaśūnyaḥ /
anādaro niṣkāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Abhyātta</s>' means pervading on all sides. '<s>Avākī</s>' means devoid of the organ of speech. '<s>Anādara</s>' means free from desire.

children.text: vikaraṇatvān neti cet tad uktam | BBs_2,1.31 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said] no, because [<s>Brahman</s>] is without instruments — that has been stated. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.31 |

children.text:
syādetat vikaraṇāṃ parāṃ devatāṃ śāsti śāstram- 'acakṣuṣkamaśrotramavāgamanāḥ' (bṛ.3.8.8) ityevañjātīyakam /
kathaṃ sā sarvaśaktiyuktāpi satī kāryāya prabhavet /
devādayo hi cetanāḥ sarvaśaktiyuktā api santa ādhyatmikakāryakaraṇasaṃpannā eva tasmaitasmai kāryāya prabhavanto vijñāyante /
kathañca 'neti neti' (bṛ. 3.9.23) iti pratiṣiddhasarvaviśeṣāyā devatāyāḥ sarvaśaktiyogaḥ saṃbhavediti cet /
children.translated_text: It might be said: The scripture teaches the supreme deity as without instruments — 'Without eyes, without ears, without speech, without mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8) — passages of this kind. How could that [deity], even though endowed with all powers, be capable of producing effects? For the gods and other sentient beings, even though endowed with all powers, are known to be capable of producing this or that effect only when equipped with the personal instruments of body and organs. And how could the connection with all powers be possible for the deity whose every specific attribute has been negated by 'not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.26)? — if this is the objection,

children.text: yadatra vaktavyaṃ tatpurastādevoktam /
śratyavagāhyamevedamatigambhīraṃ brahma na tarkāvagāhyam /
children.translated_text: This exceedingly profound <s>Brahman</s> is to be fathomed through scripture alone, not through reasoning.

children.text: naca yathaikasya sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tathānyasyāpi sāmarthyena bhavitavyamiti niyamo 'stīti /
children.translated_text: And there is no rule that the capacity of one [thing] as observed must be the same for another.

children.text: pratiṣiddhasarvaviśeṣasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ sarvaśaktiyogaḥ saṃbhavatītyetadapyavidyākalpitarūpabhedopanyāsenoktameva /
children.translated_text: And that even <s>Brahman</s> whose every specific attribute has been negated can have the connection with all powers — this too has been stated through the presentation of the distinction of aspects imagined through <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: tathāca śāstram- 'apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ' (śvaṃ. 3.19) ityakaraṇasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ sarvasāmarthyayogaṃ darśayati // 31 //
children.translated_text: And thus the scripture: 'Without hands and feet, [yet] swift and grasping; He sees without eyes, He hears without ears' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.19) — shows the connection of all capacities even for <s>Brahman</s> which is without instruments. // 31 //
whatever is to be said on this point has already been said before.

children.text: 11 prayojanavattvādhikaraṇam. sū. 32-33
children.translated_text: 11. The <s>Prayojanavattvādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Purposefulness). <s>Sūtras</s> 32-33.

children.text: na prayojanavattvāt | BBs_2,1.32 |
children.translated_text: [Creation is] not [possible], because of the purposefulness [of all activities]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.32 |

children.text:
anyathā punaścetanakartṛtvaṃ jagata ākṣipati /
na khalu cetanaḥ paramātmedaṃ jagadbimbaṃ viracayitumarhati /
kutaḥ /
prayojanavattvātpravṛttīnām /
cetano hi loke buddhipūrvakārī puruṣaḥ pravartamāno na mandopakramāmapi tāvatpravṛttimātmaprayojanānupayogināmārabhamāṇo dṛṣṭaḥ /
kimuta gurutarasaṃrambhām /
bhavati ca lokaprasiddhyanuvādinī śrutiḥ- 'na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavatyātmanastu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati' (bṛ. 2.4.5) iti gurutarasaṃrambhā ceyaṃ pravṛttiryaduccāvacaprapañcaṃ jagadbimbaṃ viracayitavyam /
yadīyamapi pravṛttiścetanasya paramātmana ātmaprayojanopayoginī parikalpyeta paritṛptitvaṃ paramātmanaḥ śrūyamāṇaṃ bādhyeta /
prayojanābhāve vā pravṛttyabhāvo 'pi syāt /
children.translated_text: Or, in the absence of purpose, there would be no activity at all.

children.text: atha cetano 'pi sannunmatto buddhyaparādhādantareṇaivātmaprayojanaṃ pravartamāno dṛṣṭastathā paramātmāpi pravartiṣyata ityucyeta /
children.translated_text: And if it were said that even a sentient being, being mad, can act without his own purpose due to a deficiency in intellect — and that the supreme Self would likewise act [senselessly] —

children.text: tathā sati sarvajñatvaṃ paramātmanaḥ śrūyamāṇaṃ bādhyeta /
children.translated_text: in that case, the omniscience of the supreme Self, which is heard [in scripture], would be contradicted.

children.text: tasmādaśliṣṭā cetanātsṛṣṭiriti // 32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, creation from a sentient [being] is untenable. // 32 //

In yet another way, the sentient agency [of <s>Brahman</s>] with respect to the world is objected to. The sentient supreme Self cannot indeed fashion this image of the world. Why? Because [all] activities are purposeful. For in the world, a sentient person who acts deliberately is not seen to undertake even the slightest activity that does not serve his own purpose — let alone one of great exertion. And there is a <s>śruti</s> that accords with worldly experience: 'Not for the sake of everything is everything dear, but for the sake of the Self is everything dear' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.5). And this is an activity of great exertion — namely, fashioning the image of the world with its elaboration of high and low. If even this activity of the sentient supreme Self were imagined as serving His own purpose, then the statement heard in <s>śruti</s> that the supreme Self is completely fulfilled would be contradicted.

children.text: FN: buddhyaparādho vivekābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Deficiency in intellect' (<s>buddhyaparādha</s>) means the absence of discrimination.

children.text: lokavat tu līlākaivalyam | BBs_2,1.33 |
children.translated_text: But it is mere play, as in the world. | <s>BBs</s> 2,1.33 |

children.text:
tuśabdenākṣepaṃ pariharati /
yathā loke kasyacidāptaiṣaṇasya vā vyatiriktaṃ kiñcitprayojanamabhisaṃdhāya kevalaṃ līlārūpāḥ pravṛttayaḥ krīḍāvihāreṣu bhavanti, yathā cocchvāsapraśvāsādayo 'nabhisaṃdhāya bāhyaṃ kiñcitprayojanaṃ svabhāvādeva saṃbhavanti evamīśvarasyāpyanapekṣya kiñcitprayojanāntaraṃ svabhāvādeva kevalaṃ līlārūpā pravṛttirbhaviṣyati /
na hīśvarasya prayojanāntaraṃ nirūpyamāṇaṃ nyāyataḥ śrutito vā saṃbhavati /
naca svabhāvaḥ paryanuyoktuṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: By the word '<s>tu</s>' (but), [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] resolves the objection. Just as in the world, for someone who has fulfilled his desires, activities in play and sport take the form of mere sport (<s>līlā</s>), without intending any separate purpose — and just as breathing in and out and the like occur naturally without intending any external purpose — so too, for the Lord, without depending on any other purpose, activity will occur naturally in the form of mere sport. For no other purpose for the Lord can be found, whether by reasoning or from <s>śruti</s>. And one cannot interrogate inherent nature.

children.text: yadyapyasmākamiyaṃ jagadbimbaviracanā gurutarasaṃrambhevābhāti tathāpi parameśvarasya līlaiva kevaleyaṃ, aparimitaśaktitvāt /
children.translated_text: Even though this fabrication of the world-image appears to us as an undertaking of the greatest magnitude, nevertheless for the supreme Lord it is mere sport, because of His unlimited power.

children.text: yadi nāma loke līlāsvapi kiñcitsūkṣmaṃ prayojanamutprekṣyeta tathāpi naivātra kiñcitprayojanamutprekṣituṃ śakyate, āptakāmaśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if in the world some subtle purpose could be imagined even in sport, nevertheless no purpose whatsoever can be imagined here — because of the <s>śruti</s> declaration that [He is] one whose desires are fulfilled (<s>āptakāma</s>).

children.text: nāpyapravṛttirunmattapravṛttirvā, sṛṣṭiśruteḥ, sarvajñaśruteśca /
children.translated_text: Nor [can it be said that there is] inactivity or the activity of a madman — because of the <s>śruti</s> on creation, and because of the <s>śruti</s> on omniscience.

children.text: naceyaṃ paramārthaviṣayā sṛṣṭiśrutiḥ avidyākalpitanāmarūpavyavahāragocaratvāt, brahmātmabhāvapratipādanaparatvāccetyetadapi naiva vismartavyam // 33 //
children.translated_text: And this <s>śruti</s> on creation does not pertain to ultimate reality — because it falls within the domain of conventional activity involving names and forms imagined through <s>avidyā</s>, and because its primary aim is to teach the identity of the Self with <s>Brahman</s>. This too should not be forgotten. // 33 //

children.text: FN: vyatiriktaṃ līlāyāḥ sakāśāditi yāvat /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Separate' — that is, separate from sport.

children.text: sṛṣṭiśruterapravṛttirnāsti, sarvajñatvaśruterunmattatā nāstīti vibhāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s> on creation, there is no [ground for asserting] inactivity; because of the <s>śruti</s> on omniscience, there is no [ground for asserting] madness — this is the division.

children.text: vaiṣamyanairghṛṇyādhikaraṇam / sū. 34-36
children.translated_text: Section: <s>Vaiṣamyanairghṛṇyādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 34-36

children.text: vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvāt tathā hi darśayati | BBs_2,1.34 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvāt tathā hi darśayati</s> — Partiality and cruelty [do] not [attach to the Lord], because [He acts] with regard [to <s>karma</s>]; for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.34 |

children.text:
punaśca jagajjanmādihetutvamīśvarasyākṣipyate sthūṇānikhanananyāyena pratijñātasyārthasya dṛḍhīkaraṇāya /
neśvaro jagataḥ kāraṇamupapadyate /
kutaḥ /
vaiṣamyanairghṛṇyaprasaṅgāt /
kāṃścidatyantasukhabhājaḥ karoti devādīn, kāṃścidatyantaduḥkhabhājaḥ paśvādīn, kāṃścinmadhyamabhogabhājo manuṣyādīnītyevaṃ viṣamāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ nirmimāṇasyaiśvarasya pṛthagjanasyeva rāgadveṣopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: And again, the Lord's being the cause of the world's origination and so forth is objected to — for the purpose of strengthening the thesis that has been established, by the principle of driving the post deeper. The Lord is not tenable as the cause of the world. Why? Because of the consequence of partiality and cruelty. He makes some — such as gods — recipients of the utmost happiness; some — such as animals — recipients of the utmost suffering; and some — such as humans — recipients of middling enjoyment. For an Lord who creates such an unequal creation, attachment and aversion would follow, as for an ordinary person.

children.text:
śrutismṛtyavadhāritasvacchatvādīśvarasvabhāvavilopaḥ prasajyeta /
tathā khalajanairapi jugupsitaṃ nirghṛṇatvamatikrūratvaṃ duḥkhayogavidhānātsarvaprajopasaṃhārācca prasajyeta /
tasmādvaiṣamyanairghṛṇyaprasaṅgānneśvaraḥ kāraṇamityevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye neśvarasya prasajyete /
kasmāt /
sāpekṣatvāt /
yadi hi nirapekṣaḥ kevala īśvaro viṣamāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ nirmimīte syātāmetau doṣau vaiṣamyaṃ nairghṛṇyaṃ ca /
natu nirapekṣasya nirmātṛtvamasti /
sāpekṣo hīśvaro viṣamāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ nirmimīte /
kimapekṣata iti cet /
dharmādharmāvapekṣata iti vadāmaḥ /
ataḥ sṛjyamānaprāṇidharmādharmāpekṣā viṣamā sṛṣṭiriti nāyamīślavarasyāparādhaḥ /
īśvarastu parjanyavaddraṣṭavyaḥ /
yathāhi parjanyo vrīhiyavādisṛṣṭau sādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ bhavati, vrīhiyavādivaiṣamye tu tattadbījagatānyevāsādhāraṇāni sāmarthyāni kāraṇāni bhavanti, evamīśvaro devamanuṣyādisṛṣṭau sādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kṣavati /
devamanuṣyādivaiṣamye tu tattajjīvagatānyevāsādhāraṇāni karmāṇi kāraṇāni bhavantyevamīśvaraḥ sāpekṣatvānna vaiṣamyanairghṛṇyābhyāṃ duṣyati /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate sāpekṣa īśvaro nīcamadhyamottamaṃ saṃsāraṃ nirmimīta iti /
children.translated_text: But how is it known that the Lord creates the lower, middle, and higher [forms of] <s>saṃsāra</s> with regard [to <s>karma</s>]?

children.text: tathāhi darśayati śrutiḥ - 'eṣa hyeva sādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamebhyo lokebhya unninīṣata eṣa u evāsādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamadho ninīṣate' (kau.brā. 3.8) iti /
children.translated_text: For thus the <s>śruti</s> shows: 'For He indeed makes him whom He wishes to lead up from these worlds do a good deed; and He indeed makes him whom He wishes to lead down do a bad deed' (<s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s> 3.8).

children.text: 'puṇyo vai puṇyena karmaṇā bhavati pāpaḥ pāpena' (bṛ. 3.2.13) iti ca /
children.translated_text: And: 'By meritorious action one becomes meritorious; by sinful action one becomes sinful' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.13).

children.text: smṛtirapi prāṇikarmaviśeṣāpekṣameveśvarasyānugrahītatvaṃ ca darśayati- 'ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham' (bha.gī. 4.11) ityevañjātīyakā // 34 //
children.translated_text: And <s>smṛti</s> too shows that the Lord's graciousness depends on the specific <s>karmas</s> of living beings: 'In whatever manner they approach Me, in that very manner I favor them' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 4.11) — and similar passages. // 34 //

The Lord's nature — His purity and such, as ascertained from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> — would be undermined. Likewise, cruelty — extreme harshness, despised even by wicked people — would follow from the ordaining of suffering and from the annihilation of all creatures. Therefore, because of the consequence of partiality and cruelty, the Lord is not the cause — thus having reached this conclusion, we say: Partiality and cruelty do not attach to the Lord. Why? Because [He acts] with regard [to <s>karma</s>]. For if the Lord alone, independently, without regard [to anything], were to create an unequal creation, then these two faults — partiality and cruelty — would follow. But He does not create independently. The Lord creates the unequal creation with regard [to something]. With regard to what? We say: with regard to <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. Therefore, the unequal creation depends on the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> of the beings being created — and this is not a fault of the Lord. The Lord should be viewed as like a rain-cloud. Just as a rain-cloud is a general cause in the production of rice, barley, and the like, while the uncommon capacities residing in the respective seeds are the specific causes for the differences among rice, barley, and the like — so too the Lord is a general cause in the creation of gods, humans, and the like. But for the differences among gods, humans, and the like, the specific <s>karmas</s> residing in the respective <s>jīvas</s> are the causes. Thus, because of acting with regard [to <s>karma</s>], the Lord is not tainted by partiality and cruelty.

children.text: FN: pṛthagjanaḥ pāmaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Pṛthagjana</s>' — an ordinary person.

children.text: yaṃ janumunninīṣate ūrdhvaṃ netumicchati taṃ sādhu kārayatyeṣa īśvara ityanvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The one whom [the Lord] wishes to lead upward — the construction is: this Lord causes him to perform good deeds.

children.text: na karmāvibhāgād iti cen nānāditvād | BBs_2,1.35 |
children.translated_text: <s>Na karmāvibhāgād iti cen nānāditvāt</s> — If [it be said that partiality and cruelty follow] because there is no differentiation of <s>karma</s> [prior to creation] — [we say] no, because of [<s>saṃsāra</s>'s] beginninglessness. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.35 |

children.text:
'sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1) iti prāksṛṣṭeravibhāgāvadhāraṇānnāsti karma yadapekṣya viṣamā sṛṣṭiḥ syāt /
sṛṣṭyuttarakālaṃ hi śarīrādivibhāgāpekṣaṃ karma, karmāpekṣaśca śarīrādivibhāga itītaretarāśrayatvaṃ prasajyeta /
ato vibhāgādūrdhvaṃ karmāpekṣa īśvaraḥ pravartatāṃ nāma /
prāgvibhāgādvaicitryanimittasya karmaṇo 'bhāvāttulyaivādyā sṛṣṭiḥ prāpnotīti cet /
children.translated_text: 'Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning — one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) — since the absence of differentiation prior to creation is ascertained, there is no <s>karma</s> with reference to which an unequal creation could be made. For <s>karma</s> depends on the differentiation of bodies and such, which comes after creation; and the differentiation of bodies and such depends on <s>karma</s> — thus there would be the fault of mutual dependence. Therefore, let the Lord act with reference to <s>karma</s> from the time after differentiation. But prior to differentiation, because of the absence of <s>karma</s> as the ground for variety, the first creation would turn out to be uniform — if this is the objection —

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: anāditvātsaṃsārasya /
children.translated_text: Because <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless.

children.text: bhavedeṣa doṣo yadyādimānsaṃsāraḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: This would be a fault if <s>saṃsāra</s> had a beginning.

children.text: anādau tu saṃsāre bījāṅ kuravaddhetumadbhāvena karmaṇaḥ sargavaiṣamyasya ca pravṛttirna virudhyate // 35 //
children.translated_text: But in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, like the [mutual dependence of] seed and sprout, the causally grounded progression of <s>karma</s> and the inequality of creation is not contradicted. // 35 //

children.text:
kathaṃ punaravagamyate 'nādireṣa saṃsāra iti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: But how is it known that this <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless? To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the next [<s>sūtra</s>] —

children.text: upapadyate cāpy upalabhyate ca | BBs_2,1.36 |
children.translated_text: <s>Upapadyate cāpy upalabhyate ca</s> — And it is logically established, and it is also observed. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.36 |

children.text:
upapadyate ca saṃsārasyānāditvam /
ādimattve hi saṃsārasyākasmādudbhūtermuktānāmapi punaḥ saṃsārodbhūtiprasaṅgaḥ, akṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgaśca, sukhaduḥkhādivaiṣamyasya nirnimittatvāt /
naceśvaro vaiṣamyaheturityuktam /
nacāvidyā kevalā vaiṣamyasya kāraṇaṃ, ekarūpatvāt /
rāgādikleśavāsanākṣiptakarmāpekṣā tvavidyā vaiṣamyakarī syāt /
naca karmāntareṇa śarīraṃ saṃbhavati, naca śarīramantareṇa karma saṃbhavatītītaretarāśrayatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
anāditve tu bījāṅ kuranyāyenopapatterna kaściddoṣo bhavati /
upalabhyate ca saṃsārasyānāditvaṃ śrutismṛtyoḥ /
śrutau tāvat 'anena jīvenātmanā' (chā. 6.3.2) iti sargapramukhe śārīramātmānaṃ jīvaśabdena prāṇadhāraṇanimittenābhilapannanādiḥ saṃsāra iti darśayati /
ādimattve tu prāganavadhāritaprāṇaḥ san kathaṃ prāṇādadhāraṇanimittena jīvaśabdena sargapramukhe 'bhilapyeta /
naca dhārayiṣyatītyato 'bhilapyeta /
anāgatāddhi saṃndhādatītaḥ saṃbandho balavānbhavati, abhiniṣpannatvāt /
children.translated_text: For a past connection is stronger than a future one, because it is already accomplished.

children.text: 'sūryācandramasau dhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat' (ṛ.saṃ 10.190.3) iti ca mantravarṇaḥ pūrvakalpasadbhāvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And the Vedic verse 'The creator fashioned the sun and moon as before' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.190.3) shows the existence of a prior cosmic cycle.

children.text: smṛtāvapyanāditvaṃ saṃsārasyopalabhyate- 'na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na cādirna ca saṃpratiṣṭhā' (gī. 15.3) iti /
children.translated_text: And in <s>smṛti</s> too, the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> is observed: 'Its form is not perceived here as such; neither its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation' (<s>Gītā</s> 15.3).

children.text: purāṇe cātītānāgatānāṃ ca kalpanāṃ na parimāṇamastīti sthāpitam // 36 //
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Purāṇas</s> it is established that the number of past and future cosmic cycles has no limit. // 36 //

And the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> is logically established. For if <s>saṃsāra</s> had a beginning, then — arising without cause — there would follow the consequence of <s>saṃsāra</s> arising even for the liberated, and the consequence of incurring results not brought about [by action] — since the inequality of happiness, suffering, and such would be without cause. And it has already been said that the Lord is not the cause of inequality. Nor is <s>avidyā</s> alone the cause of inequality, because it is of one form [i.e., uniform]. But <s>avidyā</s>, impelled by the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) such as attachment and the like, and dependent on <s>karma</s>, could produce inequality. And <s>karma</s> is not possible without a body, and a body is not possible without <s>karma</s> — thus there would be the consequence of mutual dependence. But if [<s>saṃsāra</s> is] beginningless, then by the principle of seed and sprout, it is logically established, and there is no fault. And the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> is also observed in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. In <s>śruti</s>: 'With this living Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2) — at the commencement of creation, by designating the embodied Self with the word '<s>jīva</s>' (living being), which is occasioned by the sustaining of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless. For if [<s>saṃsāra</s>] had a beginning, then — not having previously sustained <s>prāṇa</s> — how could [the Self] be designated at the commencement of creation with the word '<s>jīva</s>' which is occasioned by the sustaining of <s>prāṇa</s>? Nor [can it be said that] it is designated [so] because it will sustain [<s>prāṇa</s>] —

children.text: 13 sarvadharmopapattyadhikaraṇam. sū. 37
children.translated_text: Section 13: <s>Sarvadharmopapattyadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 37

children.text: sarvadharmopapatteś ca | BBs_2,1.37 |
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvadharmopapatteś ca</s> — And because all properties are established [in <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.1.37 |

children.text: cetanaṃ brahma jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ prakṛtiścetyasminnavadhārite vedārthe parairupakṣiptānvilakṣaṇatvādīndoṣānparyahārṣīdācāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ascertained from the <s>Vedas</s> that conscious <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of the world and its material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>), the teacher resolved the faults — such as dissimilarity and the like — raised by the opponents.

children.text: idānīṃ parapakṣapratiṣedhapradhānaṃ prakaraṇaṃ prāripsamāṇaḥ svapakṣaparigrahapradhānaṃ prakaraṇamupasaṃharati /
children.translated_text: Now, wishing to commence the section primarily devoted to the refutation of rival doctrines, he concludes the section primarily devoted to the establishment of his own position.

children.text: yasmādasminbrahmaṇi kāraṇe parigṛhyamāṇe pradarśitena prakāreṇa sarve kāraṇadharmā upapadyante 'sarvajñaṃ sarvaśakti mahāmāyaṃ ca brahma' iti, tasmādanatiśaṅkanīyamidamaupaniṣadaṃ darśanamiti // 37 //
children.translated_text: Because when this <s>Brahman</s> is accepted as the cause, in the manner demonstrated, all the properties of a cause are established — [namely] that '<s>Brahman</s> is omniscient, omnipotent, and possessed of great <s>māyā</s>' — therefore this <s>Upaniṣadic</s> doctrine is not to be doubted. // 37 //

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye dvitīyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 1 //

children.text: racanānupapatteś ca nānumānaṃ | BBs_2,2.1 |
children.translated_text: <s>Racanānupapatteś ca nānumānam</s> — And because of the impossibility of construction, [<s>Pradhāna</s>] is not [established by] inference. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.1 |

children.text:
yadyapīdaṃ vedāntavākyānāmaidaṃparyaṃ nirūpayituṃ śāstraṃ pravṛttaṃ na tarkśāstravat devalābhir yuktibhiḥ kaṃcit siddhāntaṃ sādhayituṃ dūṣayituṃ vā pravṛttam /
tathāpi vedāntavākyam api vyācakṣāṇaiḥ samyagdarśanapratipakṣabhūtāni sāṃkhyādidarśanāni nirākaraṇīyāṇīti tadarthaḥ paraḥ pādaḥ pravartate /
vedāntārthanirṇayasya ca samyagdarśanārthatvāt tannirṇayena svapakṣasthāpanaṃ prathamaṃ kṛtaṃ taddyabhyarhitaṃ parapakṣapratyākhyānād iti /
nanu mumukṣūṇāṃ mokṣasādhanatvena samyagdarśananirūpaṇāya svapakṣasthāpanam eva kevalaṃ kartuṃ yuktaṃ kiṃ parapakṣanirākaraṇena paradveṣakareṇa /
bāḍham evam /
tathāpi mahājanaparigṛhītāni mahānti sāṃkhyāditantrāṇi samyagdarśanāpadeśena pravṛttānyupalabhya bhavet keṣāṃcin mandamatīnām etāny api samyagdarśanāyopadeyānītyapekṣā /
tathā yuktagāḍhatvasaṃbhavena sarvajñabhāṣitatvācca śraddhā ca teṣvityatastadasāratopapādanāya prayatyate /
nanu 'īkṣaternāśabdam' (bra,sū. 1.1.5), 'kāmācca nānumānāpekṣā' (bra,sū. 1.1.18) 'etena sarve vyākhyātā vyākhyātāḥ' (bra,sū. 1.4.28) iti ca pūrvatrāpi sāṃkhyādipakṣapratikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ, kiṃ punaḥ kṛtakaraṇeneti /
taducyate- sāṃkhyādayaḥ svapakṣasthāpanāya vedāntavākyānyapyudāhṛtya svapakṣānuguṇenaiva yojayanto vyācakṣate, teṣāṃ yadvyākhyānaṃ tadvyākhyanābhāsaṃ na samyagvyakhyānamityetāvatpūrvaṃ kṛtam /
iha tu vākyanirapekṣaḥ svatantrastadyuktipratiṣedhaḥ kriyata ityeṣa viśeṣaḥ /
tatra sāṃkhyā manyante- yathā ghaṭaśarāvādayo bhedā mṛdātmanānvīyamānā mṛdātmakasāmānyapūrvakā loke dṛṣṭāḥ, tathā sarva eva bāhyādhyātmikā bhedāḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmatayānvīyamānāḥ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakasāmānyapūrvikā bhavitumarhanti /
yattatsukhaduḥkhamohātmakaṃ sāmānyaṃ tatttriguṇaṃ pradhānaṃ mṛdvadacetanaṃ cetanasya puruṣārthaṃ sādhayituṃ svabhāvenaiva vicitreṇa vikārātmanā vivartata iti /
tathā pariṇāmādibhirapi liṅgaistadeva pradhānamanuminute /
tatra vadāmaḥ - yadi dṛṣṭāntabalenaivaitannirūpyeta, nācetanaṃ loke cetanānadhiṣṭhitaṃ svatantraṃ kiñcidviśiṣṭapuruṣārthanirvartanasamarthānvikārānviracayaddṛṣṭam /
gehaprāsādaśayanāsanavihārabhūmyādayo hi loke prajñāvadbhiḥ śilpibhiryathākālaṃ sukhaduḥkhaprāptiparihārayogyā racitā dṛśyante /
tathedaṃ jagadakhilaṃ pṛthivyādi nānākarmaphalopabhogayogyaṃ bāhyam, ādhyatmikaṃ ca śarīrādi nānājātyanvitaṃ pratiniyatāvayavavinyāsamanekakarmaphalānubhavādhiṣṭhānaṃ dṛśyamānaṃ prajñāvadbhiḥ saṃbhāvitatamaiḥ śilpibhirmanasāpyālocayitumaśakyaṃ sat kathamacetanaṃ pradhānaṃ racayet /
loṣṭapāṣāṇādiṣvadṛṣṭatvāt /
mṛdādiṣvapi kumabhakārādyadhiṣṭhiteṣu viśiṣṭākārā racanā dṛśyate tadvatpradhānasyāpi cetanāntarādiṣṭhitatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
naca mṛdādyupādānasvarūpavyapāśrayeṇaiva dharmeṇa mūlakāraṇamavadhāraṇīyaṃ na bāhyakumbhakārādivyapāśrayeṇeti kiñcinniyāmakamasti /
nacaivaṃ sati kiñcidvirudhyate, pratyuta śrutiranugṛhyate cetanakāraṇasamarpaṇāt /
ato racanānupapatteśca hetornācetanaṃ jagatkāraṇamanumantavyaṃ bhavati /
anvayādyanupapatteśceti caśabdena hetorasiddhiṃ samuccinoti /
nahi bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ bhedānāṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatayānvaya upapadyate, sukhādīnāṃ cāntaratvapratīteḥ, śabdādīnāṃ cātadrūpatvapratīteḥ /
tannimittatvapratīteśca /
children.translated_text: And because [pleasure and the like] are perceived as caused by those [sounds and such].

children.text: śabdādyaviśeṣe 'pi ca bhāvanāviśeṣātsukhādiviśeṣopalabdheḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, even when sound and the like are undifferentiated, because of differentiation in mental disposition, differentiation of pleasure and the like is observed.

children.text: tathā parimitānāṃ bhedānāṃ mūlāṅ kurādīnāṃ saṃsargapūrvakatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāhyādhyātmikānāṃ bhedānāṃ parimitatvātsaṃsargapūrvakatvamanumimānasya sattvarajastamasāmapi saṃsargapīrvakatvaprasaṅgaḥ parimitatvaviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, having observed that limited diversities such as root-sprouts and the like are preceded by combination [of parts], one who infers that external and internal diversities too — being limited — must be preceded by combination, would face the consequence that <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s> too must be preceded by combination, since they are specifically limited.

children.text: kāryakāraṇabhāvastu prekṣāpūrvakanirmitānāṃ śayanāsanādīnāṃ dṛṣṭa iti na kāryakāraṇabhāvādbāhyādhyātmikānāṃ bhedānāmacetanapūrvakatvaṃ śakyaṃ kalpayitum // 1 //
children.translated_text: But the relation of cause and effect is observed only in things fashioned with deliberation, such as beds, seats, and the like. Therefore, from the relation of cause and effect, one cannot postulate that external and internal diversities are preceded by an insentient [cause]. // 1 //

Although this <s>śāstra</s> has undertaken to ascertain the purport of the <s>Vedānta</s> sentences, and has not undertaken — like a treatise on logic — to establish or refute any thesis through mere reasoning alone, nevertheless, even while explicating the <s>Vedānta</s> statements, the philosophical systems such as <s>Sāṃkhya</s> that oppose right knowledge must be refuted — for this purpose the second <s>pāda</s> proceeds. And since the ascertainment of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s> serves the purpose of right knowledge, through that ascertainment the establishment of one's own position was accomplished first — being more worthy than the refutation of opposing positions. But [one might object:] for seekers of liberation, it is proper to establish one's own position alone for the purpose of ascertaining right knowledge as the means to liberation — what is the use of refuting opposing positions, which engenders hostility? Quite so. Nevertheless, seeing that the great systems such as <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, which are accepted by many people, have set forth their doctrines under the pretext of right knowledge, some persons of dull intellect might develop the expectation that these too should be adopted for the sake of right knowledge. Moreover, because of the possibility that [these systems] contain tightly-woven reasoning, and because they are said to have been spoken by omniscient [sages], faith arises in them — therefore effort is made to demonstrate their lack of substance. But [one might ask:] was not the refutation of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other positions already accomplished earlier, through [the <s>sūtras</s>] '<s>Īkṣater nāśabdam</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.5), '<s>Kāmāc ca nānumānāpekṣā</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.18), and '<s>Etena sarve vyākhyātāḥ</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.4.28) — why repeat what has already been done? To this it is replied: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others, for the purpose of establishing their own position, cite <s>Vedānta</s> statements too and interpret them in conformity with their own doctrine. That their interpretation is merely an apparent interpretation and not a correct one — only this much was accomplished earlier. But here, an independent refutation of their reasoning, without reference to [scriptural] statements, is being undertaken — this is the distinction. In this regard, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> hold: just as in the world, diverse objects such as pots and dishes, pervaded by the nature of clay, are seen to be preceded by a general [substance] of the nature of clay — so too, all external and internal diversities, being pervaded by the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, should be preceded by a general [substance] of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion. That general [substance] of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion is the three-<s>guṇa</s> <s>Pradhāna</s>, which — like clay, being insentient — transforms itself through its own diverse nature in the form of modifications, in order to accomplish the purposes of the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s>. Likewise, through inferential marks such as transformation and the like, that very <s>Pradhāna</s> is inferred. To this we say: if this were to be determined solely on the strength of examples — then in the world, nothing insentient, not governed by a conscious [being], is seen to independently fashion modifications capable of accomplishing the specific purposes of persons. For houses, palaces, beds, seats, pleasure grounds, and the like are seen in the world to be fashioned at the appropriate time by intelligent artisans, suitable for the attainment and avoidance of pleasure and pain. Similarly, this entire external world — earth and such — suitable for the enjoyment of the fruits of various actions, and the internal [world] — bodies and such — belonging to various species, having a fixed arrangement of limbs, serving as the locus for the experience of manifold fruits of action, [all of this,] being seen [to be of such complexity] that even the most accomplished artisans imaginable cannot mentally conceive it — how could insentient <s>Pradhāna</s> fashion it? Because this is not observed in clods of earth, stones, and the like. And even in clay and such, when governed by a potter and the like, a design of specific form is seen — similarly, for <s>Pradhāna</s> too, there would be the consequence of being governed by another conscious [being]. And there is no determining principle that the root cause should be ascertained only through the property that belongs to the material cause, such as clay, and not through the property that belongs to an external [agent] such as the potter. And when this is so, nothing is contradicted — rather, <s>śruti</s> is supported, since it establishes a conscious cause. Therefore, from the reason of the impossibility of design, an insentient [entity] should not be inferred as the cause of the world. 'And because of the impossibility of <s>anvaya</s> (invariable concomitance) and such' — by the word 'and' [in the <s>sūtra</s>], he adds further grounds of unestablishedness. For the invariable concomitance of external and internal diversities with [the nature of] pleasure, pain, and delusion is not tenable — because pleasure and the like are perceived as internal, and because sound and the like are perceived as not being of that nature.

children.text: FN: apadeśena vyājena /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Apadeśena</s>' means by pretext.

children.text: pravṛtteś ca | BBs_2,2.2 |
children.translated_text: And because of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.2 |

children.text:
āstāṃ tāvadiyaṃ racanā /
tatsiddhyarthā yā pravṛttiḥ sāmyāvasthānātpracyutiḥ sattvarajastamasāmaṅgāṅgibhāvarūpāpattirviśiṣṭakāryābhimukhapravṛttitā sāpi nācetanasya pradhānasya svatantrasyopapadyate, mṛdādiṣvadarśanādrathādiṣu ca /
nahi mṛdādayo rathādayo vā svayamacetanāḥ santaścetanaiḥ kulālādibhiraśvādibhirvānadhiṣṭhitā viśiṣṭakāryābhimukhapravṛttayo dṛśyante dṛṣṭāccādṛṣṭisiddhiḥ /
ataḥ pravṛttyanupapatterapi hetornācetanaṃ jagatkāraṇamanumātavyaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Let this design be set aside. The activity that is meant to accomplish it — the departure from the state of equilibrium, the assumption of the relation of principal and subordinate among <s>Sattva</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Tamas</s>, the engagement directed toward a specific effect — that too is not tenable for an insentient <s>Pradhāna</s> acting independently, because this is not observed in clay and the like, or in chariots and the like. For neither clay and the like, nor chariots and the like, being themselves insentient, are seen to engage in producing a specific effect without being governed by conscious [agents] such as potters, horses, and the like. And from what is observed, what is unobserved is established. Therefore, from the reason of the impossibility of activity too, an insentient [entity] should not be inferred as the cause of the world.

children.text: nanu cetanasyāpi pravṛttiḥ kevalasya na dṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: But even for a conscious [being], activity by itself alone is not observed.

children.text:
satyametat /
tathāpi cetanasaṃyuktasya rathāderacetanasya pravṛttidṛṣṭā /
natvacetanasaṃyuktasya cetanasya pravṛttirdṛṣṭā /
kiṃ punaratra yuktam /
yasminpravṛttirdṛṣṭā tasya sota yatasaṃyuktasya dṛṣṭā tasya seti /
children.translated_text: This is true. Nevertheless, the activity of an insentient [thing] such as a chariot conjoined with a conscious [being] is observed. But the activity of a conscious [being] conjoined with an insentient [thing] is not [similarly] observed [as depending on the insentient]. What then is reasonable here? [Is it] that activity belongs to that in which it is observed, or that it belongs to that conjoined with which it is observed?

children.text:
nanu yasmindṛśyate pravṛttistasyaiva seti yuktamubhayoḥ pratyakṣatvāt /
natu pravṛttyāśrayatvena kevalaścetano rathādivatpratyakṣaḥ /
pravṛtyāśrayadehādisaṃyuktasyaiva tu cetanasya sadbhāvasiddhiḥ kevalācetanarathādivailakṣaṇyaṃ jīvadehasya dṛṣṭamiti /
ata eva ca pratyakṣe dehe sati darśanādasati cādarśanāddehasyaiva caitanyamapīti laukāyatikāḥ pratipannāḥ /
tasmādacetanasyaiva pravṛttiriti /
children.translated_text: Well, [one might say:] it is reasonable that [activity] belongs to that very [entity] in which it is directly seen — since both [the substratum and the activity] are perceptible. But a conscious [being] by itself is not perceptible as a substratum of activity, as a chariot and the like are. Rather, the existence of a conscious [being] is established only as conjoined with a body and such — the substratum of activity — and the body of a living being is seen to be different from an insentient chariot and the like. And precisely because of this — because of the observation [of consciousness] when the perceptible body is present, and its non-observation when [the body] is absent — the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists) have concluded that consciousness belongs to the body itself. Therefore, activity belongs to the insentient alone.

children.text:
tadabhidhīyate- na brūmo yasminnacetane pravṛttirdṛśyate na tasya seti /
bhavatu tasyaiva sā /
sā tu cetanādbhavatīti brūmaḥ /
tadbhāve bhāvāttadabhāve cābhāvāt /
yathā kāṣṭhādivyapāśrayāpi dāhaprakāśalakṣaṇā vikriyānupalabhyamānāpi ca kevale jvalane jvalanādeva bhavati, tatsaṃyoge darśanāttadviyoge cādarśanāttadvat /
laukāyatikānāmapi cetana eva deho 'cetanānāṃ rathādīnāṃ pravartako dṛṣṭa ityavipratiṣiddhaṃ cetanasya pravartakatvam /
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: we do not say that activity does not belong to the insentient [thing] in which it is observed. Let it indeed belong to that. But we say that it [the activity] comes from the conscious [being]. Because of its presence when that [conscious being] is present, and its absence when that is absent. Just as the modification characterized by burning and illumination, even though subsisting in firewood and such, and even though not perceived in fire by itself, comes from fire alone — because of the observation [of burning] when there is contact with it and the non-observation when there is separation from it — so too in this case. And even according to the <s>Lokāyatikas</s>, the conscious body alone is seen to set insentient things like chariots in motion — thus the capacity of the conscious [being] to initiate activity is uncontradicted.

children.text: nanu tava dehādisaṃyuktasyāpyātmano vijñānasvarūpamātravyatirekeṇa pravṛttyanupapatteranupapannaṃ pravartakatvamiti cet /
children.translated_text: But [one might object:] even for you, since activity is impossible for the Self beyond its mere nature as consciousness (<s>vijñānasvarūpa</s>), even when conjoined with the body and such, its capacity to initiate [activity] is untenable.

children.text:
na /
ayaskāntavadrūpādivacca pravṛttirahitasyāpi pravartakatvopapatteḥ /
yathāyaskānto maṇiḥ svayaṃ pravṛttirahito 'pyayasaḥ pravartako bhavati /
yathā vā rūpādayo viṣayāḥ svayaṃ pravṛttirahitā api cakṣurādīnāṃ pravartakābhavanti /
evaṃ pravṛttirahito 'pīśvaraḥ sarvagataḥ sarvātmā sarvajñaḥ sarvaśaktiśca san sarvaṃ pravartayedityupapannam /
children.translated_text: No. Because even for one devoid of activity, the capacity to initiate [activity] is tenable — like a magnet, and like form and such [sense-objects]. Just as a lodestone, though itself devoid of activity, causes iron to move; and just as forms and such sense-objects, though themselves devoid of activity, cause the eye and other [sense organs] to function — so too, even though <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is devoid of activity, being all-pervading, the Self of all, omniscient, and omnipotent, it is tenable that He sets everything in motion.

children.text: ekatvātpravartyābhāve pravartakatvānupapattiriti cet /
children.translated_text: If [it is objected that] because of [His] oneness, in the absence of something to be moved, the capacity to initiate [activity] is untenable —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: avidyāpratyupasthāpitanāmarūpamāyāveśavaśenāsakṛtpratyuktatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because this has been repeatedly answered — through the entry into the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of name and form presented by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: tasmātsaṃbhavati pravṛttiḥ sarvajñakāraṇatve natvacetanakāraṇatve // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, activity is possible when the cause is omniscient, but not when the cause is insentient. // 2 //

children.text: FN: ubhayoḥ pravṛttitadāśrayayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Both' — i.e., activity and its substratum.

children.text: payo 'mbuvac cet tatrāpi | BBs_2,2.3 |
children.translated_text: If [you say it is] like milk and water — even there also. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.3 |

children.text:
syādetat /
yathā kṣīramacetanaṃ svabhāvenaiva vatsavivṛddhyarthaṃ pravartate, yathāca jalamacetanaṃ svabhāvenaiva lokopakārāya syandata evaṃ pradhānamacetanaṃ svabhāvenaiva puruṣārthasiddhaye pravartiṣyata iti /
children.translated_text: One might argue: just as milk, though insentient, by its own nature alone flows for the nourishment of the calf; and just as water, though insentient, by its own nature alone flows for the benefit of the world — so too <s>Pradhāna</s>, though insentient, will by its own nature alone engage in accomplishing the purposes of the <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text:
naitatsādhūcyate /
yatastatrāpi payombunoścetanādhiṣṭhitayoreva pravṛttirityanumimīmahe /
ubhayavādiprasiddhe rathādavacetane kevale pravṛttyadarśanāt /
śāstraṃ ca 'yo 'psu tiṣṭhan yo 'po 'ntaro yamayati' (bṛ. 3.7.4), 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi prācyonyā nadyaḥ syandante' (bṛ. 3.8.9) ityevañjātīyakaṃ samastasya lokaparispanditasyeśvarādhiṣṭhitatāṃ śrāvayati /
tasmātsādhyapakṣanikṣiptatvātpayombuvadityanupanyāsaḥ /
cetanāyāśca dhenvāḥ snehecchayā payasaḥ pravartakatvopapatteḥ /
vatsacoṣaṇena ca payasa ākṛṣyamāṇatvāt /
nacāmbuno 'pyatyantamanapekṣā, nimnabhūmyādyapekṣatvātsyandanasya /
children.translated_text: And even water is not completely independent [in its flow], because flowing depends on sloping terrain and the like.

children.text: cetanāpekṣatvaṃ tu sarvatropadarśitam /
children.translated_text: But dependence on a conscious [being] has been shown everywhere.

children.text: 'upasaṃhāradarśanānneti cenna kṣīravaddhi' (bra.sū. 2.1.24) ityatra tu bāhyanimittanirapekṣamapi svāśrayaṃ kāryaṃ bhavatītyetallokadṛṣṭyā nidarśitam /
children.translated_text: In the [<s>sūtra</s>] '<s>Upasaṃhāradarśanān neti cen na kṣīravad dhi</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.1.24), however, it was shown from the standpoint of ordinary experience that an effect can occur independently of any external efficient cause, relying on its own material basis alone.

children.text: śāstradṛṣṭyā tu punaḥ sarvatraiveśvarāpekṣatvamāpadyamānaṃ na parāṇudyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: But from the standpoint of scripture, the dependence on <s>Īśvara</s> everywhere — which inevitably follows — is not repudiated. // 3 //

This is not well stated. For even there, we infer that the activity of milk and water is only under the governance of a conscious [being]. Because activity is not observed in merely insentient [things] such as chariots, which are accepted [as insentient] by both parties. And scripture of the following kind declares that the entire movement of the world is under the governance of <s>Īśvara</s>: 'He who stands in the waters, who is within the waters, who controls the waters' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.4), and 'Under the command of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the eastern rivers flow' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.9). Therefore, since [the example of milk and water] falls within the very thesis to be proved, 'like milk and water' is not a [valid] example. Moreover, the flow of milk is tenable as caused by the affection and desire of the conscious cow. And because the milk is drawn out by the sucking of the calf.

children.text:
FN: sādhyavattā pakṣeṇa tulyatvāt /
anupanyāsaḥ na vicārabhūmiḥ /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: Because of its being equivalent to the thesis to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).
'<s>Anupanyāsaḥ</s>' means it is not a subject for deliberation.

children.text: vyatirekānavasthiteś cānapekṣatvāt | BBs_2,2.4 |
children.translated_text: And because of the non-establishment of what is different [from the <s>guṇas</s>], and because of its independence (<s>anapekṣatva</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.4 |

children.text: sāṃkhyānāṃ trayo guṇāḥ sāmyenāvatiṣṭhamānāḥ pradhānam /
children.translated_text: According to the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, the three <s>guṇas</s> subsisting in equilibrium constitute <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: natu tadvyatirekeṇa pradhānasya pravartakaṃ nivartakaṃ vā kiñcidbāhyamapekṣyamavastitamasti /
children.translated_text: But nothing external to [those <s>guṇas</s>] is established as either the initiator or the cessator of <s>Pradhāna</s>'s [activity], apart from those [<s>guṇas</s> themselves].

children.text: puruṣastūdāsīno na pravartako na nivartaka ityato 'napekṣaṃ pradhānaṃ, anapekṣatvācca kadācitpradhānaṃ mahadādyākāreṇa pariṇamate kadācinna pariṇamata ityetadayuktam /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Puruṣa</s>, being indifferent, is neither the initiator nor the cessator. Therefore <s>Pradhāna</s> is independent (<s>anapekṣa</s>). And because of this independence, [the position] that <s>Pradhāna</s> sometimes transforms into the form of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, and sometimes does not transform — this is untenable.

children.text: īśvarasya tu sarvajñatvātsarvaśaktitvānmahāmāyatvācca pravṛttyapravṛttī na virudhyete // 4 //
children.translated_text: But for <s>Īśvara</s>, because of His omniscience, omnipotence, and great <s>māyā</s>-power, activity and non-activity are not contradictory. // 4 //

children.text: anyatrābhāvāc ca na tṛṇādivat | BBs_2,2.5 |
children.translated_text: And because of the absence [of such spontaneous transformation] elsewhere, [it is] not like grass and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.5 |

children.text:
syādetat /
yathā tṛṇapallavodādi nimittāntaranirapekṣaṃ svabhāvādeva kṣīrādyākāreṇa pariṇamata evaṃ pradhānamapi mahadādyākāreṇa pariṇaṃsyata iti /
kathaṃ ca nimittāntaranirapekṣaṃ tṛṇādīti gamyate /
nimittāntarānupalambhāt /
yadi hi kiñcinnimittamupalabhemahi tato yathākāmaṃ tena tṛṇādyupādāya kṣīraṃ saṃpādayemahi, natu saṃpādayāmahe /
children.translated_text: One might argue: just as grass, shoots, and such transform into the form of milk and the like by their own nature alone, without depending on any other efficient cause — so too <s>Pradhāna</s> will transform into the form of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest. And how is it known that grass and the like are independent of any other efficient cause? Because no other efficient cause is apprehended. For if we apprehended some [other] efficient cause, then we could take grass and such at will and produce milk with it — but we cannot do so.

children.text: tasmātsvābhāvikastṛṇādeḥ pariṇāmastathā pradhānasyāpi syāditi /
children.translated_text: Therefore the transformation of grass and the like is natural, and similarly, [one might argue,] the transformation of <s>Pradhāna</s> should also be [natural].

children.text:
atrocyate- bhavettṛṇādivatsvābhāvikaḥ pradhānasyāpi paraṇāmo yadi tṛṇāderapi svābhāvikaḥ pariṇāmo 'bhyupagamyeta /
natvabhyupagamyate, nimittāntaropalabdheḥ /
kathaṃ nimittāntaropalabdhiḥ, anyatrābhāvāt /
dhenvaiva hyupayuktaṃ tṛṇādi kṣīro bhavati na prahīṇamanaḍudādyupayuktaṃ vā /
yadi hi nirnimittametatsyāddhenuśarīrasaṃbandhādanyatrāpi tṛṇādi kṣīrībhavet /
naca yathākāmaṃ mānuṣairna śakyaṃ saṃpādayitumityetāvatā nirnimittaṃ bhavati /
bhavati hi kiñcitkāryaṃ mānuṣasaṃpādyaṃ kiñciddaivasaṃpādyam /
manuṣyā api śaknuvatyevocitenopāyena tṛṇādyupādāya kṣīraṃ saṃpādayitum /
children.translated_text: Even humans are able, by the proper method, to produce milk from grass and such.

children.text: prabhūtaṃ hi kṣīraṃ kāmayamānāḥ prabhūtaṃ ghāsaṃ dhenuṃ cārayanti /
children.translated_text: For those desiring abundant milk give abundant fodder to the cow to graze.

children.text: tataśca prabhūtaṃ kṣīraṃ labhante /
children.translated_text: And thereby they obtain abundant milk.

children.text: tasmānna tṛṇādivatsvābhāvikaḥ pradhānasya pariṇāmaḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the transformation of <s>Pradhāna</s> is not spontaneous like that of grass and such. // 5 //

To this it is replied: the transformation of <s>Pradhāna</s> would be spontaneous like that of grass and such, only if the transformation of grass and such were also accepted as spontaneous. But it is not so accepted, because another efficient cause is observed. How is another efficient cause observed? Because of its absence elsewhere. For grass and such become milk only when consumed by a cow, not when [merely] discarded or consumed by a bull and such. For if this [transformation] were without an efficient cause, grass and such would become milk even apart from contact with the cow's body. And the mere fact that humans cannot produce [milk from grass] at will does not make it without an efficient cause. For some effects are producible by humans, while others are producible by [forces of] nature alone — as the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> themselves hold. But when a specific efficient cause is directly observed for a particular transformation, it is not right to say that [the transformation] is without an efficient cause.

children.text: FN: prahīṇaṃ naṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Prahīṇa</s>' means 'discarded.'

children.text: abhyupagame 'py arthābhāvāt | BBs_2,2.6 |
children.translated_text: Even if [spontaneous transformation] is accepted, because of the absence of purpose. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.6 |

children.text:
svābhāvikī pradhānapravṛttirna bhavatīti sthāpitam /
athāpi nāma bhavataḥ śraddhāmanurudhyamānāḥ svābhāvikīmeva pradhānasya pravṛttimabhyupagacchema tathāpi doṣo 'nuṣajyetaiva /
kutaḥ /
arthābhāvāt /
yadi tāvatsvābhāvikī pradhānasya pravṛttirna kiñcidanyadihāpekṣata ityucyeta tato yathaiva sahakāri kiñcinnāpekṣata evaṃ prayojanamapi kiñcinnāpekṣiṣyate ityataḥ pradhānaṃ puruṣasyārthaṃ sādhayituṃ pravartata itīyaṃ pratijñā hīyeta /
sa yadi brūyātsahakāryeva kevalaṃ nāpekṣate na prayojanamapīti /
tathāpi pradhānapravṛtteḥ prayojanaṃ vivektavyaṃ bhogo vā syādapavargo vobhayaṃ veti /
bhogaścetkīdṛśo 'nādheyātiśayasya puruṣasya bhogo bhavet /
anirmokṣaprasaṅgaśca apavargaścetprāgapi pravṛtterapavargasya siddhatvātpravṛttiranarthikā syāt /
śabdādyanupalabdhiprasaṅgaśca /
ubhayārthatābhyupagame 'pi bhoktavyānāṃ pradhānamātrāṇāmānantyādanirmokṣaprasaṅga eva /
nacautsukyanivṛttyarthā pravṛttiḥ /
nahi pradhānasyācetanasyautsukyaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: For eagerness is not possible for <s>Pradhāna</s>, which is insentient.

children.text: naca puraṣasya nirmalasya niṣkalasyautsukyam /
children.translated_text: Nor is there eagerness for <s>Puruṣa</s>, which is stainless and without parts.

children.text: dṛkśaktisargaśaktivaiyarthyabhayāccetpravṛttistarhi dṛkśaktyanucchedavatsargaśaktyanucchedātsaṃsārānucchedādanirmokṣaprasaṅga eva /
children.translated_text: And if [<s>Pradhāna</s>] acts out of fear that the capacity of vision (<s>dṛkśakti</s>) and the capacity of creation (<s>sargaśakti</s>) would become purposeless — then, just as the capacity of vision is never destroyed, so too the capacity of creation would never be destroyed, and since <s>saṃsāra</s> would never cease, there would be the contingency of no liberation at all.

children.text: tasmātpradhānasya puruṣārthā pravṛttirityetadayuktam // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the assertion that <s>Pradhāna</s>'s activity is for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is unjustified. // 6 //

It has been established that the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> is not spontaneous. But even if, acceding to your belief, we were to accept the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> as indeed spontaneous — even then, a fault would follow. Why? Because of the absence of purpose. If it is said that the spontaneous activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> does not depend on anything else — then just as it does not depend on any auxiliary, so too it will not depend on any purpose. Therefore, the assertion that '<s>Pradhāna</s> acts to accomplish the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose' would be abandoned. If one were to say: 'It merely does not depend on an auxiliary, but it does depend on a purpose' — then [we reply:] in that case, whose purpose does <s>Pradhāna</s> serve by acting? If it is said to be the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose — then the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose is either enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) or liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). But neither of these can motivate <s>Pradhāna</s>'s activity, because there is no eagerness in <s>Pradhāna</s> or <s>Puruṣa</s> for either.

children.text: FN: arthābhāvāt puruṣārthābhāvaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Because of the absence of purpose' means: because of the contingency of the absence of the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose.

children.text: sukhaduḥkha prāptiparihārarūpātiśayaśūnyasya /
children.translated_text: [<s>Puruṣa</s> is] devoid of any superiority in the form of the attainment and avoidance of pleasure and pain.

children.text: mīyante bhujyante iti mātrā bhogāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mātrā</s>' — things that are measured (experienced) — means enjoyments.

children.text: puruṣāśmavad iti cet tathāpi | BBs_2,2.7 |
children.translated_text: If [one says] like the <s>Puruṣa</s> and the stone — even so, [the fault remains]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.7 |

children.text:
syādetat /
yathā kaścitpuruṣo dṛkśaktisaṃpannaḥ pravṛttiśaktihīnaḥ paṅguraparaṃ puruṣaṃ pravṛttiśaktisaṃpannaṃ dṛkśaktihīnamandhamadhiṣṭhāya pravartayati /
yathā vāyaskānto 'śmā svayamapravartamāno 'pyayaḥ pravartayati /
evaṃ puruṣaḥ pradhānaṃ pravartayiṣyatīti dṛṣṭāntapratyayena punaḥ pratyavasthānam /
