children.text: evaṃ cātmākārtsnyam | BBs_2,2.34 |
children.translated_text: And thus, the incompleteness of the self [would follow]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.34 |

children.text:
yathaikasmindharmiṇi viruddhadharmāsaṃbhavo doṣaḥ syādvāde prasakta evamātmano 'pi jīvasyākārtsnyamaparo doṣaḥ prasajyeta /
katham /
śarīraparamātmāṇo hi jīva ityārhatā manyante /
śarīraparimāṇatāyāṃ ca satyāmakṛtsno 'sarvagataḥ paricchinna ātmetyato ghaṭādivadanityatvamātmanaḥ prasajyeta /
śarīrīṇāṃ cānavasthitaparimāṇatvānmanuṣyajīvo manuṣyaśarīraparimāṇo bhūtvā punaḥ kenacitkarmavipākena hastijanma prāpnuvanna kṛtsnaṃ hastiśarīraṃ vyāpnuyāt /
puttikājanma ca prāpmuvanna kṛtsnaḥ puttikāśarīre saṃmīyeta /
samāna eṣa ekasminnapi janmani kaumārayauvanasthavireṣu doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Just as the impossibility of contradictory properties in one substratum is a fault that follows in the <s>syādvāda</s>, so too another fault — the incompleteness of the self — would follow.
How?
For the Jainas hold that the <s>jīva</s> (soul) is of the size of the body.
And if [the soul is] of the size of the body, then — being incomplete, not all-pervading, delimited — the self, like a pot and such, would be impermanent.
And since embodied beings have bodies of unstable dimensions, a human <s>jīva</s> — being of human body-size — would, upon obtaining an elephant-birth through some <s>karma</s>-ripening, not pervade the entire elephant-body.
And upon obtaining the birth of an ant, it would not fit entirely within the ant's body.
The same fault applies even within a single lifetime — in childhood, youth, and old age.

children.text:
syādetat /
antāvayavo jīvastasya ta evāvayavā alpe śarīre saṃkuceyurmahati ca vikuceyuriti /
teṣāṃ punaranantānāṃ jīvāvayavānāṃ samānadeśatvaṃ pratihanyate vā naveti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: But one must state whether the infinitely many parts of the <s>jīva</s>, being in the same location, obstruct each other or not.

children.text: pratighāte tāvannānantāvayavāḥ paricchinne deśe saṃmīyeran /
children.translated_text: If they obstruct each other, then infinitely many parts could not fit in a delimited space.

children.text: apratighāte 'pyekāvayavadeśatvopapatteḥ sarveṣāmavayavānāṃ prathimānupapatterjīvasyāṇumātratvaprasaṅgaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If they do not obstruct each other, then — since all parts could exist in the space of a single part — because the extension of all parts would be impossible, the consequence would be that the <s>jīva</s> is merely of atomic size.

children.text: apica śarīramātraparicchinnānāṃ jīvāvayavānāmānantyaṃ notprekṣitumapi śakyam // 34 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, it is not possible even to conjecture that the parts of a <s>jīva</s> delimited to a mere body could be infinite. // 34 //
It might be said: The <s>jīva</s> has parts without end, and those very parts contract in a small body and expand in a large one.

children.text: FN: karmavipākaḥ karmaṇāmabhivyaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Karmavipāka</s>' means the manifestation of <s>karmas</s>.

children.text: atha prayāyeṇa bṛhaccharīrapratipattau kecijjīvāvayavā upagacchanti tanuśarīrapratipattau ca kecidapagacchantītyucyeta tatrāpyucyate-
children.translated_text: If it were said that upon obtaining a larger body, certain parts of the <s>jīva</s> join [it], and upon obtaining a smaller body, certain [parts] depart — to that too we say:

children.text: na ca paryāyād apy avirodho vikārādibhyaḥ | BBs_2,2.35 |
children.translated_text: Nor is there non-contradiction even through alternation — because of modification and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.35 |

children.text:
naca paryāyeṇāpyavayavopagamāpagamābhyāmetaddehaparimāṇatvaṃ jīvasyāvirodhenopapādayituṃ śakyate /
kutaḥ /
vikārādidoṣaprasaṅgāt /
avayavopagamāpagamābhyāṃ hyaniśamāpūryamāṇasyāpakṣīyamāṇasya ca jīvasya vikriyāvattvaṃ tāvadaparihāryam, vikriyāvattve ca carmādivadanityaṃ prasajyeta /
tataśca bandhamokṣābhyupagamo bādhyeta karmāṣṭakapariveṣṭitasya jīvasyālābuvatsaṃsārasāgare nimagnasya bandhanocchedādūrdhvagāmitvaṃ bhavatīti /
kiñcānyat /
āgacchatāmapagacchatāṃ cāvayavānāmāgamāpāyadharmavattvādevānāmātvaṃ śarīrādivat /
tataścāvasthitaḥ kaścidavayava ātmeti syāt /
naca sa nirūpayituṃ śakyate 'yamasāviti /
kiñcānyat /
āgacchantaścaite jīvāvayavāḥ kutaḥ prādurbhavantyapagacchantaśca kva vā līyanta iti vaktavyam /
nahi bhūtebhyaḥ prādurbhaveyurbhūteṣu ca nilīyeran, abhautikatvājjīvasya /
nāpi kaścidanyaḥ sādhāraṇo 'sādhāraṇo vā jīvānāmavayavādhāro nirūpyate pramāṇābhāvāt /
kiñcānyat /
anavadhṛtasvarūpaścaivaṃsatyātmā syāt /
āgacchatāmapagacchatāṃ cāvayavānāmaniyataparimāṇatvāt /
ata evamādidoṣaprasaṅgānna paryāyeṇāpyavayavopagamāpagamāvātmana āśrayituṃ śakyate /

athavā pūrveṇa sūtreṇa śarīraparimāṇasyātmana upacitāpacitaśarīrāntarapratipattāvakārtsnyaprasañjanadvāreṇānityatāyāṃ coditāyāṃ punaḥ paryāyeṇa parimāṇānavasthāne 'pi srotaḥsaṃtānanityatānyāyenātmano nityatā syāt /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, by the previous <s>sūtra</s>, when the impermanence of the body-sized self has been objected to — on the ground that when acquiring a different body of greater or lesser size, [the self's] non-total [transformation would mean] a portion remains unused — then again, even though the size is not stable due to [gradual change], the self could be eternal by the principle of the eternality of a stream (<s>srotaḥ-saṃtāna</s>).

children.text: yathā raktapaṭānāṃ vijñānānavasthāne 'pi tatsaṃtānanityatā tadvaddhisicāmapītyāśaṅkyānena sūtreṇottaramucyate /
children.translated_text: Just as for dyed cloths, even though the individual cognitions [of each cloth] are not stable, the continuity of the series is eternal — so too for the <s>Digambaras</s> (Jains) — anticipating this objection, the answer is given by this <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: saṃtānasya tāvadavastutve nairātmyavādaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: First, if the stream has no substantial reality, there would be the contingency of the doctrine of no-self (<s>nairātmyavāda</s>).

children.text: vastutve 'pyātmano vikārādidoṣaprasaṅgādasya pakṣasyānupapattiriti // 35 //
children.translated_text: And even if [the stream] has substantial reality, because of the contingency of faults such as modification for the self, this position is untenable. // 35 //

Nor can this body-sized-ness of the <s>jīva</s> be established without contradiction even by the gradual acquisition and loss of parts. Why? Because of the contingency of faults such as modification. For a <s>jīva</s> that is constantly being filled and depleted through the acquisition and loss of parts — its being subject to modification is first of all unavoidable; and being subject to modification, it would be impermanent like skin and such. And consequently, the acceptance of bondage and liberation would be contradicted — [the doctrine that] the <s>jīva</s>, wrapped in the eightfold <s>karma</s>, sunk in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> like a gourd, rises upward upon the cutting of bondage. Furthermore: the parts that come and go — since they have the nature of arriving and departing — would themselves be [impermanent], like the body and such. And then some remaining part would be the self. But that cannot be determined as 'this is it.' Furthermore: it must be stated — these parts of the <s>jīva</s> that come, from where do they appear? And those that depart, where do they dissolve? For they could not appear from the elements nor dissolve into the elements, because the <s>jīva</s> is non-elemental. Nor can any other — common or uncommon — substratum of the <s>jīva</s>'s parts be determined, because of the absence of a means of knowledge. Furthermore: the self would thus have an undetermined nature — because of the indefinite size [resulting from] parts that are coming and going. Therefore, because of the contingency of such faults, even the gradual acquisition and loss of parts cannot be resorted to for the self.

children.text: FN: dehabhedena parimāṇasyātmanaścānavasthāne 'pi nāśe 'pi srotaḥpravāhaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Even though the size does not remain stable — even upon destruction — there is a stream-like flow' — with the change of bodies.

children.text: vigataṃ sig vastraṃ visico digambarāsteṣāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Visic</s>' means cloth; '<s>visica</s>' means the unclothed ones (<s>Digambaras</s>) — this is the meaning.

children.text: antyāvasthiteś cobhayanityatvād aviśeṣaḥ | BBs_2,2.36 |
children.translated_text: And because of the permanence of the final state, and because both [the prior and final states] would be equally eternal, there is no distinction. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.36 |

children.text: apicāntyasya mokṣāvasthābhāvino jīvaparimāṇasya nityatvamiṣyate jainaiḥ /
tadvatpūrvayorapyavidyamadhyamayorjīvaparimāṇayornityatvaprasaṅgādaviśeṣaprasaṅgaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Since there would equally be the contingency of eternality for the two prior sizes of the <s>jīva</s> — the lower and the middle — there would be no distinction.

children.text: ekaśarīraparimāṇataiva syānnopacitāpacitaśarīrāntaraprāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: It would have the size of one body only, and there would be no acquisition of different bodies of greater or lesser size.

children.text: athavāntyasya jīvaparimāṇasyāvasthitatvātpūrvayorapyavasthayoravasthitaparimāṇa eva jīvaḥ syāt, tataścāviśeṣeṇa sarvadaivāṇurmahānvā jīvo 'bhyupagantavyo na śarīraparimāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, since the <s>jīva</s>'s size remains stable in the final state, the <s>jīva</s> should have a stable size in the prior states as well. And therefore, the <s>jīva</s> should be accepted without distinction as either always atomic or always large — not as body-sized.

children.text: ataśca saugatavadārhatamapi matamasaṃgatamityupekṣitavyam // 36 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the Jain doctrine too, like the Buddhist doctrine, is incoherent and should be disregarded. // 36 //
Moreover, the Jains accept that the final size of the <s>jīva</s> — the one that obtains in the state of liberation — is eternal.

children.text: patyadhikaraṇam / sū. 37-41
children.translated_text: The <s>Patyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Lord [as merely efficient cause]). <s>Sūtras</s> 37-41.

children.text: patyur asāmañjasyāt | BBs_2,2.37 |
children.translated_text: Because of the inconsistency of the Lord (<s>Pati</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.37 |

children.text:
idānīṃ kevalādhiṣṭhātrīśvarakāraṇavādaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
tatkathamavagamyate /
'prakṛtiśca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhāt' 'abhidhyopadeśācca' (bra. 1.4.23,24) ityatra prakṛtibhāvenādhiṣṭhātṛbhāvena cobhayasvabhāvasyeśvarasya svayamevācāryeṇa pratiṣṭhāpitatvāt /
yadi punaraviśeṣeṇeśvarakāraṇavādamātramiha pratiṣidhyeta pūrvottaravirodhādvyāhatābhivyāhāraḥ sūtrakāra ityetadāpadyeta /
tasmādaprakṛtiradhiṣṭhātā kevalaṃ nimittakāraṇamīśvara ityeṣa pakṣo vedāntavihitabrahmaikatvapratipakṣatvādyatnenātra pratiṣidhyate /
sā ceyaṃ vedabāhyeśvarakalpanānekaprakārā /
children.translated_text: Now the doctrine that the Lord is merely a presiding efficient cause is refuted. How is this known? From the fact that in '<s>Prakṛtiś ca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhāt</s>' and '<s>Abhidhyopadeśāc ca</s>' (<s>BBs</s> 1.4.23-24), the teacher himself established the Lord as having both natures — as the material cause and as the presiding [efficient cause]. If the doctrine of the Lord as cause were refuted without qualification here, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> would be making contradictory statements — contradicting his earlier and later positions. Therefore, the position that the Lord is merely an efficient cause — a presider without being the material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>) — is refuted here with effort, because it is opposed to the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> established by <s>Vedānta</s>. And this imagining of a Lord outside the <s>Veda</s> takes many forms.

children.text:
kecittāvatsāṃkhyayogavyapāśrayāḥ kalpayanti pradhānapuruṣayoradhiṣṭhātā kevalaṃ nimittakāraṇamīśvara itaretaravilakṣaṇāḥ pradhānapuruṣeśvarā iti /
māheśvarāstu manyante kāryakāraṇayogavidhiduḥkhāntāḥ pañca padārthāḥ paśupatineśvareṇa paśupāśavimokṣaṇāyopadiṣṭāḥ paśupatirīśvaro nimittakāraṇamiti varṇayanti /
tathā vaiśeṣikādayo 'pi kecitkathañcitsvaprakriyānusāreṇa nimittakāraṇamīśvara iti varṇayanti /
ata uttaramucyate- 'patyurasāmañjasyāt' iti /
patyurīśvarasya pradhānapuruṣayoradhiṣṭhātṛtvena jagatkāraṇatvaṃ nopapadyate /
kasmāt /
asāmañsyāt /
kiṃ punarasāmañjasyam /
hīnamadhyamottamabhāvena hi prāṇibhedānvidadhata īśvarasya rāgadveṣādidoṣaprasakterasmadādivadanīśvaratvaṃ prasajyeta /
prāṇikarmāpekṣitatvādadoṣa iti cet /
children.translated_text: Some, relying on <s>Sāṅkhya-Yoga</s>, imagine: the Lord is a mere presider over <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, a merely efficient cause; <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the Lord are mutually distinct, each with distinct characteristics. The <s>Māheśvaras</s> (Śaivites) hold: there are five categories — effect, cause, <s>yoga</s>, ritual practice, and [the state of] the cessation of suffering — taught by Lord <s>Paśupati</s> for the liberation of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) from its bonds (<s>pāśa</s>); <s>Paśupati</s>, the Lord, is the efficient cause. Likewise, certain <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others too, in some fashion following their own system, describe the Lord as the efficient cause. To this, the answer is given: 'Because of the inconsistency of the Lord.' The Lord (<s>Pati</s>)'s being the cause of the world merely as a presider over <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is untenable. Why? Because of inconsistency. What inconsistency? For a Lord who creates beings with distinctions of lower, middle, and higher [stations] — because of the contingency of faults such as attachment and aversion, as for an ordinary person — [He] would turn out to be not a Lord at all. If [you say] there is no fault because [He acts] with regard to the <s>karma</s> of beings —

children.text:
na /
karmeśvarayoḥ pravartyapravartayitṛtve itaretarāśrayadoṣaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: No. Because of the contingency of the fault of mutual dependence between <s>karma</s> and the Lord — between the impelled and the impeller.

children.text: nānāditvāditi cet /
children.translated_text: If [you say there is no fault] because [<s>saṃsāra</s>] is beginningless —

children.text:
na /
vartamānakālavadatīteṣvapi kāleṣvitaretarāśrayadoṣāviśeṣādandhaparamparānyāyāpatteḥ /
apica 'pravartanālakṣaṇā doṣāḥ' (nyāyasū. 1.1.18) iti nyāyavitsamayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the principle of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> states: 'Faults are characterized by impelling to activity' (<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.18).

children.text: nahi kaścidadoṣaprayuktaḥ svārthe parārthe vā pravartamāno dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For no one is seen to engage in activity — whether for his own sake or for the sake of another — without being impelled by some fault [i.e., desire, aversion, or delusion].

children.text: svārthaprayukta eva ca sarvo janaḥ parārthe 'pi pravartata ityevamapyasāmañjasyaṃ, svārthavattvādīśvarasyānīśvaratvaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: And since every person engages in activity for another's sake only when impelled by his own self-interest — there is this inconsistency too: because of having self-interest, the Lord would not be a Lord.

children.text: puruṣaviśeṣatvābhyupagamācceśvarasya puruṣasya caudāsīnyābhyupagamādasāmañjasyam // 37 //
children.translated_text: And because the Lord is accepted as a special <s>puruṣa</s>, and because indifference is accepted for [all] <s>puruṣas</s> — there is inconsistency. // 37 //
No. Because the fault of mutual dependence is equally [present] in past times as in the present — resulting in the consequence of an infinite blind regression (<s>andha-paramparā</s>).

children.text: FN: sāṃkhyayogavyapāśrayāḥ hiraṇyagarbhapatañjaliprabhṛtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Those relying on <s>Sāṅkhya-Yoga</s>' means <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Patañjali</s>, and the like.

children.text: māheśvarāścatvāraḥ - śaivāḥ, pāśupatāḥ, kāruṇikasiddhāntinaḥ, kāpālikāśceti /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Māheśvaras</s> are four: <s>Śaivas</s>, <s>Pāśupatas</s>, <s>Kāruṇika-siddhāntins</s>, and <s>Kāpālikas</s>.

children.text: paśavo jīvāsteṣāṃ pāśo bandhastannāśāyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Paśus</s>' are the <s>jīvas</s>; '<s>pāśa</s>' is their bondage; for the destruction of that — this is the meaning.

children.text: saṃbandhānupapatteś ca | BBs_2,2.38 |
children.translated_text: And because the relation [of the Lord with Pradhāna] is untenable. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.38 |

children.text:
punarapyasmāñjasyameva /
nahi pradhānapuruṣavyatirikta īśvaro 'ntareṇasaṃbandhaṃ pradhānapuruṣayorīśitā /
na tāvatsaṃyogalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandhaḥ saṃbhavati, pradhānapuruṣeśvarāṇāṃ sarvagatatvānniravayavatvācca /
nāpi samavāyalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, āśrayāśrayibhāvānirūpaṇāt /
nāpyanyaḥ kaścitkāryagamyaḥ saṃbandhaḥ śakyate kalpayituṃ, kāryakāraṇabhāvasyaivādyāpyasiddhatvāt /
brahmavādinaḥ kathamiti cet /
children.translated_text: Again, inconsistency indeed. For the Lord, being distinct from <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, cannot be the ruler of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> without a relation. The relation cannot be of the nature of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), because <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the Lord are all-pervading and partless. Nor can the relation be of the nature of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), because the substratum-superstratum relationship cannot be determined. Nor can any other relation, inferable from an effect, be posited — because the very cause-effect relation has not yet been established. If [you ask] how does this [work] for the proponent of <s>Brahman</s>?

children.text:
na /
tasya tādātmyalakṣaṇasaṃbandhopapatteḥ /
apicāgamabalena brahmavādī kāraṇādisvarūpaṃ nirūpayatīti nāvaśyaṃ tasya yathādṛṣṭameva sarvamabhyupagantavyamiti niyamo 'sti /
parasya tu dṛṣṭāntabalena kāraṇādisvarūpaṃ nirūpayato yathādṛṣṭameva sarvamabhyupagantavyamityayamastyatiśayaḥ /
parasyāpi sarvajñapraṇītāgamasadbhāvātsamānamāgamabalamiti cet /
children.translated_text: No [difficulty]. Because for him, the relation characterized as identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) is tenable. Moreover, the proponent of <s>Brahman</s> determines the nature of the cause and such on the strength of scripture — hence there is no necessity for him to accept everything exactly as it is observed [in worldly experience]. But for the opponent, who determines the nature of the cause and such on the strength of analogy — there is this additional [requirement] that everything must be accepted exactly as observed. If [you say] the opponent too has an equally valid scripture, since it was authored by an omniscient being —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: itaretarāśrayatvaprasaṅgādāgamapratyayatvātsarvajñatvasiddhiḥ sarvajñapratyayāccāgamasiddhiriti /
children.translated_text: Because of the contingency of mutual dependence: the establishment of omniscience depends on the credibility of the scripture, and the credibility of the scripture depends on [the author's] omniscience.

children.text: tasmādanupapannā sāṃkhyayogavādināmīśvarakalpanā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the imagining of a Lord by the proponents of <s>Sāṅkhya-Yoga</s> is untenable.

children.text: evamanyāsvapi vedabrahmāsvīśvarakalpanāsu yathāsaṃbhavamasāmañjasyaṃ yojayitavyam // 38 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, in other extra-Vedic conceptions of a Lord too, the inconsistency should be applied as applicable. // 38 //

children.text: adhiṣṭhānānupapatteś ca | BBs_2,2.39 |
children.translated_text: And because the presiding [of the Lord over Pradhāna] is untenable. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.39 |

children.text: itaścānupapattistārkikaparikalpitasyeśvarasya /
children.translated_text: For this further reason, the Lord as conceived by the logicians is untenable.

children.text: sa hi parikalpyamānaḥ kumabhakāra iva mṛdādīni pradhānādīnyadhiṣṭhāya pravartayet /
children.translated_text: For such a conceived [Lord] would operate upon <s>Pradhāna</s> and the like by presiding over them — just as a potter [presides] over clay and such.

children.text: nacaivamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: But this is untenable.

children.text: nahyapratyakṣaṃ rūpādihīnaṃ ca pradhānamīśvarasyādhiṣṭheyaṃ saṃbhavati mṛdādivailakṣaṇyāt // 39 //
children.translated_text: For <s>Pradhāna</s>, being imperceptible and devoid of form and such, cannot be the object of the Lord's presiding — because it is dissimilar to clay and such. // 39 //

children.text: karaṇavac cen na bhogādibhyaḥ | BBs_2,2.40 | /
children.translated_text: If [you say it is] like the instruments [of the body] — [we say] no, because of enjoyment and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.40 |

children.text:
syādetat /
yathā karaṇagrāmaṃ cakṣurādikamapratyakṣaṃ rūpādihīnaṃ ca puruṣo 'dhitiṣṭhatyevaṃ pradhānamapīśvaro 'dhiṣṭhāsyatīti /
tathāpi nopapadyate /
bhogādidarśanāddhi karaṇagrāmasyādhiṣṭhitatvaṃ gamyate /
nacātra bhogādayo dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: It might be said: Just as a person presides over the aggregate of instruments — eyes and such — which are imperceptible and devoid of form and such, so too the Lord would preside over <s>Pradhāna</s>. Even so, it is untenable. For the fact that the aggregate of instruments is presided over is understood from the observation of enjoyment and such. But here, no enjoyment and such are observed [for the Lord].

children.text:
karaṇagrāmasāmye vābhyupagamyamāne saṃsāriṇāmiveśvarasyāpi bhogādayaḥ prasajyeran /
anyathā vā sūtradvayaṃ vyākhyāyate- adhiṣṭhānānupapatteśca itaścānupapattistārkikaparikalpisyeśvarasya /
sādhiṣṭhāno hi loke saśarīro rājā rāṣṭrasyeśvaro dṛśyate na niradhiṣṭhānaḥ /
ataśca taddṛṣṭāntavaśenādṛṣṭamīśvaraṃ kalpayitumicchata īśvarasyapi kiñciccharīraṃ karaṇāyatanaṃ varṇayitavyaṃ syāt /
naca tadvarṇayituṃ śakyate /
sṛṣṭyuttarakālabhāvitvāccharīrasya prāksṛṣṭestadanupapatteḥ /
niradhiṣṭhānatve ceśvarasya pravartakatvānupapattiḥ /
evaṃ loke dṛṣṭatvāt /
'karaṇavaccenna bhogādibhyaḥ' /
children.translated_text: 'If [you say it is] like the instruments — [we say] no, because of enjoyment and such.'

children.text: atha lokadarśanānusāreṇeśvarasyāpi kiñcitkāraṇānāmāyatanaṃ śarīraṃ kāmena kalpyeta /
children.translated_text: And if some body — an abode of instruments — were willfully posited for the Lord, following worldly analogy —

children.text: evamapi nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: even so, it is untenable.

children.text: saśarīratve hi sati saṃsārivadbhogādiprasaṅgādīśvarasyāpyanīśvaratvaṃ prasajyeta // 40 //
children.translated_text: For if [the Lord] has a body, then — because of the contingency of enjoyment and such, like a transmigrating being — the Lord would turn out to be not a Lord at all. // 40 //

Or, if the same [status as] the aggregate of instruments were accepted [for Pradhāna], then the Lord too, like transmigrating beings, would be subject to enjoyment and such. Alternatively, the two <s>sūtras</s> may be explained thus: 'And because the presiding is untenable' — for this further reason, the Lord conceived by the logicians is untenable. For in the world, a king who is the lord of a kingdom is seen as embodied, having a support — not without a support. And therefore, for one who wishes to conceive an unseen Lord on the basis of that analogy, some body — an abode of instruments — would have to be described for the Lord as well. But that cannot be described. Because the body comes into being only after creation — prior to creation it is untenable. And if the Lord is without a support, His capacity to impel [creation] is untenable — because this is observed in the world.

children.text:
FN: bhogaḥ sukhaduḥkhānubhavaḥ /
ādipadādviṣayānubhavagrahaḥ /
karaṇānyatra santīti karaṇavaccharīram /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Enjoyment' (<s>bhoga</s>) means the experience of pleasure and pain. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and such), the experience of sense-objects is included. 'An abode of instruments' (<s>karaṇavat</s>) means a body [that houses instruments].

children.text: antavattvam asarvajñatā vā | BBs_2,2.41 |
children.translated_text: [There would be either] finitude or non-omniscience. | <s>BBs</s> 2,2.41 |

children.text:
itaścānupapattistārkikaparikalpitasyeśvarasya /
sa hi sarvajñastairabhyupagamyate 'nantaśca /
anantaṃ ca pradhānamanantāśca puruṣā mitho bhinnā abhyupagamyate /
tatra sarvajñeśvareṇa pradhānasya puruṣāṇāmātmanaśceyattā paricchidyeta vā na vā paricchidyeta /
ubhayathāpi doṣo 'nuṣakta eva /
katham /
pūrvasmiṃstāvadvikalpa iyattāparicchinnatvātpradhānapuruṣeśvarāṇāmantavattvamavaśyaṃ bhāvyevaṃ loke dṛṣṭatvāt /
yaddhi loka iyattāparicchinnaṃ vastu paṭādi tadantavaddṛṣṭaṃ tathā pradhānapuruṣeśvaratrayamapīyattāparicchinnatvādantavatsyāt /
saṃkhyāparimāṇaṃ tāvatpradhānapuruṣeśvaratrayarūpeṇa paricchinnam /
svarūpaparimāṇamapi tadgatamīśvareṇa paricchidyeteti /
puruṣagatā ca mahāsaṃkhyā /
tataśceyattāparicchinnānāṃ madhye ye saṃsāriṇaḥ saṃsārānmucyante teṣāṃ saṃsāro 'ntavānsaṃsāritvaṃ ca teṣāmantavat /
evamitareṣvapi krameṇa mucyamāneṣu saṃsārasya saṃsāriṇāṃ cāntavattvaṃ syāt /
pradhānaṃ ca savikāraṃ puruṣārthamīśvarasyādhiṣṭheyaṃ saṃsāritvenābhimataṃ tacchūnyatāyāmīśvaraḥ kimadhitiṣṭhet /
kiṃviṣaye vā sarvajñateśvarate syātām /
pradhānapuruṣeśvarāṇāṃ caivamantavattve satyādimattvaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the Lord are thus finite, there would be the contingency of their having a beginning.

children.text: ādyantavattve ca śūnyavādaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if they have both a beginning and an end, there would be the contingency of the doctrine of the void (<s>śūnyavāda</s>).

children.text: atha mā bhūdeṣa doṣa ityuttaro vikalpo 'bhyupagamyeta na pradhānasya puruṣāṇāmātmanaśceyatteśvareṇa paricchidyata iti, tata īśvarasya sarvajñatvābhyupagamahāniraparo doṣaḥ prasajyeta /
children.translated_text: If, to avoid this fault, the alternative were accepted — that the number of <s>Pradhāna</s>, the <s>Puruṣas</s>, and the Self is not determined by the Lord — then another fault would follow: the loss of the acceptance of the Lord's omniscience.

children.text: tasmādapyasaṃgatastārkikaparigṛhīta īśvarakāraṇavādaḥ // 41 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this standpoint too, the doctrine of the Lord as cause as adopted by the logicians (<s>Tārkikas</s>) is untenable. // 41 //

For this further reason, the Lord conceived by the logicians is untenable. For He is accepted by them as omniscient and infinite. And <s>Pradhāna</s> is accepted as infinite, and the <s>Puruṣas</s>, mutually distinct, are accepted as infinite. In that case, would the extent of <s>Pradhāna</s>, of the <s>Puruṣas</s>, and of Himself be delimited by the omniscient Lord, or not? In both cases, a fault necessarily follows. How? In the first alternative — because of being delimited in extent, <s>Pradhāna</s>, the <s>Puruṣas</s>, and the Lord would necessarily be finite — because this is observed in the world. For whatever thing in the world is delimited in extent — such as a cloth — is seen to be finite. Likewise, the triad of <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the Lord, being delimited in extent, would be finite. First, the numerical measure is delimited in the form of the triad of <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the Lord. And the intrinsic measure pertaining to each would also be delimited by the Lord. And the great number pertaining to the <s>Puruṣas</s> [is also delimited]. And then, among those who are delimited in extent, the transmigrating ones who are liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s> — for them, <s>saṃsāra</s> would be finite, and their transmigrating nature would be finite. And likewise, as others are progressively liberated, <s>saṃsāra</s> and the transmigrators would become finite. And <s>Pradhāna</s> together with its modifications, being meant for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>, being the object of the Lord's presiding, being regarded as transmigrating — when it becomes empty [of purpose], what would the Lord preside over? And with respect to what would there be omniscience or lordship?

children.text: FN: saṃkhyā vā parimāṇaṃ veyattā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Number or measure' — that is '<s>iyattā</s>' (determinateness).

children.text: 8 utpattyasaṃbhavādhikaraṇam / sū. 42-45
children.translated_text: Section 8: <s>Utpattyasaṃbhavādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 42-45

children.text: utpattyasaṃbhavāt | BBs_2,2.42 |
children.translated_text: <s>Utpattyasaṃbhavāt</s> — Because of the impossibility of origination. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.42 |

children.text:
yeṣāmaprakṛtiradhiṣṭhātā kevalanimittakāraṇamīśvaro 'bhimatasteṣāṃ pakṣaḥ pratyākhyātaḥ /
yeṣāṃ punaḥ prakṛtiścādhiṣṭhātā cobhayātmakaṃ kāraṇamīśvaro 'bhimatasteṣāṃ pakṣaḥ pratyākhyāyayate /
children.translated_text: The position of those for whom the Lord — who is not the material cause but only the superintending efficient cause — has been refuted. Now the position of those for whom the Lord is both the material cause and the superintendent — a cause of both natures — is being refuted.

children.text:
nanu śrutisamāśrayaṇenāpyevaṃrūpa eveśvaraḥ prāṅnirdhāritaḥ prakṛtiścādhiṣṭhātā ceti /
śrutyanusāriṇī ca smṛtiḥ pramāṇamiti sthitiḥ /
tatkasya hetoreṣa pakṣaḥ pratyācikhyāsita iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the Lord of precisely this form — both material cause and superintendent — was previously established by resorting to <s>śruti</s>. And the established principle is that <s>smṛti</s> that follows <s>śruti</s> is authoritative. For what reason then is this position sought to be refuted?

children.text:
ucyate- yadyapyevajātīyakoṃ'śaḥ samānatvānna visaṃvādagocaro bhavattyastitvaṃśāntaraṃ visaṃvādasthānamityatastatpratyākhyānāyāramabhaḥ /
tatra bhāgavatā manyante /
bhagavānevaiko vāsudevo nirañjanajñānasvarūpaḥ paramārthatattvaṃ, sa caturdhātmānaṃ pravibhajya pratiṣṭhito vāsudevavyūharūpeṇa saṃkarṣaṇavyūharūpeṇa pradyumnavyūharūpeṇāniruddhavyūharūpeṇa ca /
vāsudevo nāma paramātmocyate /
saṃkarṣaṇo nāma jīvaḥ /
pradyumno nāma manaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is said: Even though a certain aspect [of this position] is common [with ours] and therefore not subject to disagreement, there is another aspect that is a ground for disagreement — and it is for refuting that [aspect] that [this discussion] is commenced. Therein, the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> hold the following: The blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> alone — whose nature is untainted knowledge — is the ultimate reality. He manifests Himself in four ways and is established in the form of the <s>Vāsudeva-vyūha</s>, the <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa-vyūha</s>, the <s>Pradyumna-vyūha</s>, and the <s>Aniruddha-vyūha</s>. <s>Vāsudeva</s> is designated as the supreme Self; <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> as the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul); <s>Pradyumna</s> as the mind;

children.text:
aniruddho nāmāhaṅkāraḥ /
teṣāṃ vāsudevaḥ parā parakṛtiritare saṃkarṣaṇādayaḥ kāryam /
tamitthaṃbhūtaṃ parameśvaraṃ bhagavantamabhigamanopādānejyāsvādhyāyayogairvarṣaśatamiṣṭvā kṣīṇakleśo bhagavantameva pratipadyata iti /
tatra yattāvaducyeta yo 'sau nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktātprasiddhaḥ paramātmā sarvātmā sa ātmānātmānamanekadhā vyūhyāvasthita iti, tanna nirākriyate, 'sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati' (chā. 7.26.2) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ paramātmano 'nekadhābhāvasyādhigatatvāt /
yadapi tasya bhagavato 'bhigamanādilakṣaṇamārādhanamajasramananyacittatayābhipreyate,
children.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s> as the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>). Among them, <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the higher nature (<s>parā prakṛti</s>); the others — <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> and the rest — are the effect. Having worshipped that supreme Lord of such a nature for a hundred years through approach (<s>abhigamana</s>), acquisition [of worship materials] (<s>upādāna</s>), worship (<s>ijyā</s>), study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and <s>yoga</s> (meditation), one whose afflictions are destroyed attains the blessed Lord Himself. Therein, the claim that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — who is well known as the supreme Self beyond the unmanifest — establishes Himself by manifesting Himself in manifold ways — that is not refuted, because from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'He becomes one, He becomes three' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.26.2) and the like, the manifold manifestation of the supreme Self is established. And the claim that the worship of the blessed Lord — characterized by approach and the like — is to be performed incessantly with undivided mind —

children.text:
tadapi na pratiṣidhyate /
śrutismṛtyorīśvarapraṇidhānasya prasiddhatvāt /
yatpunaridamucyate vāsudevātsaṃkarṣaṇa utpadyate saṃkarṣaṇācca pradyumnaḥ pradyumnāccāniruddha iti /
atra brūmaḥ - na vāsudevasaṃjñakātparamātmanaḥ saṃkarṣaṇasaṃjñakasya jīvasyotpattiḥ saṃbhavati /
anityatvādidoṣaprasaṅgāt /
utpattimattve hi jīvasyānityatvādayo doṣāḥ prasajyeran /
tataśca naivāsya bhagavatprāptirmokṣaḥ syāt /
kāraṇaprāptau kāryasya pravilayaprasaṅgāt /
pratiṣedhiṣyati cācāryo jīvasyotpattim- 'nātmāśruternityatvācca tābhyaḥ' (bra.sū. 2.3.17) iti /
tasmādasaṃgataiṣā kalpanā /
children.translated_text: that too is not rejected. Because devotion to the Lord is well known from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. But the claim that <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, designated as the <s>jīva</s>, arises from <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and that <s>Pradyumna</s> arises from <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s> from <s>Pradyumna</s> — to this we say: The origination of the <s>jīva</s>, designated <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, from the supreme Self, designated <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is not possible. Because of the consequence of faults such as non-eternality. For if the <s>jīva</s> had an origination, faults such as non-eternality would follow. And consequently, the attainment of the blessed Lord would never constitute liberation for it — because of the consequence that the effect would dissolve upon reaching the cause. And the teacher will deny the origination of the <s>jīva</s>: 'The Self [does not originate], because of <s>śruti</s> and because of eternality — from those [scriptural passages]' (<s>BBs</s> 2.3.17). Therefore, this conception is untenable.

children.text:
FN: vyūho mūrtiḥ /
vākkāyacetasāmavadhānapūrvakaṃ devatāgṛhagamanamabhigamanam, pūjādravyāṇāmarjanamupādānam, ijyā pūjā, svādhyāyo 'ṣṭākṣarādijapaḥ, yogo dhyānam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Vyūha</s>' means a manifest form (<s>mūrti</s>). Approach (<s>abhigamana</s>) is going to the temple of the deity, preceded by the dedication of speech, body, and mind. Acquisition (<s>upādāna</s>) is the gathering of materials for worship. Worship (<s>ijyā</s>) is the ritual offering (<s>pūjā</s>). Study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is the recitation of the eight-syllable <s>mantra</s> and the like. <s>Yoga</s> is meditation.

children.text: na ca kartuḥ karaṇam | BBs_2,2.43 |
children.translated_text: <s>Na ca kartuḥ karaṇam</s> — And the instrument does not [arise] from the agent. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.43 |

children.text:
itaścāsaṃgataiṣā kalpanā /
yasmānna hi loke karturdevadattādeḥ karaṇaṃ paraśvādyutpadyamānaṃ dṛśyate /
varṇayanti ca bhāgavatāḥ karturjīvātsaṃkarṣaṇasaṃjñakātkaraṇaṃ manaḥ pradyumnasaṃjñakamutpadyate /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bhāgavatas</s> describe that from the agent — the <s>jīva</s> designated <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> — the instrument, the mind designated <s>Pradyumna</s>, originates.

children.text: kartṛjācca tasmādaniruddhasaṃjñako 'haṅkāra utpadyata iti /
children.translated_text: And from that [mind], born of the agent, the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) designated <s>Aniruddha</s> originates.

children.text: nacaitaddṛṣṭāntamantareṇādhyavasātuṃ śaknumaḥ /
children.translated_text: And we cannot ascertain this without an illustration [from experience].

children.text: nacaivaṃbhūtāṃ śrutimupalabhāmahe // 43 //
children.translated_text: Nor do we find a <s>śruti</s> of this kind. // 43 //
For this further reason, this conception is untenable. Because in the world, the instrument — such as an axe — is not seen to originate from the agent, <s>Devadatta</s> and such.

children.text: vijñānādibhāve vā tadapratiṣedhaḥ | BBs_2,2.44 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vijñānādibhāve vā tadapratiṣedhaḥ</s> — Or, if [they are held to be] in the state of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) and so forth, [even then] the non-refutation of that [fault remains]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.44 |

children.text:
athāpi syānna caite saṃkarṣaṇādayo jīvādibhāvenābhipreyante kiṃ tarhīśvarā evaite sarve jñānaiśvaryaśaktibalavīryatejobhiraiśvaryairdharmairanvitā abhyupagamyante vāsudevā evaite sarve nirdeṣā niradhiṣṭhāna niravadyāśceti /
tasmānnāyaṃ yathāvarṇita utpattyasaṃbhavo doṣaḥ prāpnotīti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, [the <s>Bhāgavata</s> might say:] These <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> and the rest are not intended as the <s>jīva</s> and such. Rather, all of them are accepted as Lords endowed with the divine attributes of knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, vigor, and splendor — and all of them are <s>Vāsudevas</s>, described as free from attachment, not produced from <s>Prakṛti</s>, and free from defects. Therefore, the fault described — the impossibility of origination — does not apply.

children.text:
atrocyate- evamapi tadapratiṣedha utpattyasaṃbhavasyāpratiṣedhaḥ prāpnotyevāmutpattyasaṃbhavo doṣaḥ prakārāntareṇetyabhiprāyaḥ /
katham /
yadi tāvadayamabhiprāyaḥ parasparabhinnā evaite vāsudevādayaścatvāra īśvarāstulyadharmāṇo naiṣāmekātmakatvamastīti, tato 'nekeśvarakalpanānārthakyam, ekenaiveśvareṇeśvarakāryasiddheḥ /
siddhāntahāniśca /
bhagavānekaiko vāsudevaḥ paramārthatattvamityabhyupagamāt /
athāyamabhiprāya ekasyaiva bhagavata ete catvāro vyūhāstulyadharmāṇa iti, tathāpi tadavastha evotpattyasaṃbhavaḥ /
nahi vāsudevātsaṃkarṣaṇasyotpattiḥ saṃbhavati saṃkarṣaṇācca pradyumnasya pradyumnāccāniruddhasya, atiśayābhāvāt /
bhavitavyaṃ hi kāryakāraṇayoratiśayena yathā mṛdghaṭayoḥ /
nahyasatyatiśaye kāryaṃ kāraṇamityavakalpate /
children.translated_text: For in the absence of gradation, the cause-effect relation does not hold.

children.text: naca pañcarātrasiddhāntibhirvāsudevādiṣvekasminsarveṣu vā jñānaiśvaryāditāratamyakṛtaḥ kaścidbhedo 'bhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Pañcarātra</s> adherents do not accept any difference among <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the rest — whether in one or in all of them — based on a gradation in knowledge, sovereignty, and the like.

children.text: vāsudevā eva hi sarve vyūhā nirviśeṣā iṣyante /
children.translated_text: For all the <s>vyūhas</s> are desired to be <s>Vāsudevas</s>, without distinction.

children.text: nacaite bhagavadvyūhāścatuḥsaṃkhyāyāmevāvatiṣṭheran, brahmādistambaparyantasya samastasyaiva jagato bhagavadvyūhatvāvagamāt // 44 //
children.translated_text: And these manifestations of the blessed Lord would not be limited to the number four — because the entire world, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, is understood to be a manifestation of the blessed Lord. // 44 //

To this it is said: Even so, the non-refutation of the impossibility of origination still follows — the impossibility of origination as a fault applies in another way. This is the intent. How so? If this is the intent — that these four, <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the rest, are mutually distinct Lords with equal attributes, and they do not have a single essential nature — then the postulation of multiple Lords would be purposeless, since the work of the Lord can be accomplished by a single Lord alone. And [this would also involve] the loss of one's own doctrine — because [the <s>Bhāgavatas</s>] accept that the one blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> alone is the ultimate reality. But if this is the intent — that these four <s>vyūhas</s> with equal attributes are [manifestations] of the one blessed Lord — even then, the impossibility of origination remains as it is. For the origination of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> from <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and of <s>Pradyumna</s> from <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, and of <s>Aniruddha</s> from <s>Pradyumna</s> is not possible — because of the absence of any gradation. For there must be a gradation between cause and effect, as between clay and a pot.

children.text: FN: nirdeṣā rāgādiśūnyāḥ, niradhiṣṭhānā prakṛtyajanyāḥ, niravadyā nāśādirahitā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Nirdeṣā</s>' — free from attachment and the like; '<s>niradhiṣṭhāna</s>' — not produced from <s>Prakṛti</s>; '<s>niravadya</s>' — free from destruction and the like — this is the meaning.

children.text: vipratiṣedhāc ca | BBs_2,2.45 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vipratiṣedhāc ca</s> — And because of [internal] contradictions. | <s>BBs</s> 2.2.45 |

children.text: vipratiṣedhaścāsmiñchāstre bahuvidha upalabhyate guṇaguṇitvakalpanādilakṣaṇaḥ /
jñānaiśvaryaśaktibalavīryatejāṃsi guṇāḥ, ātmāna evaite bhagavanto vāsudevā ityādidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because it is seen [stated] that knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, vigor, and splendor are qualities — and that these blessed <s>Vāsudevas</s> themselves are the Self [i.e., the possessor].

children.text: vedavipratiṣedhaśca bhavati /
children.translated_text: And there is contradiction with the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: caturṣu vedeṣu paraṃ śreyo 'labdhvā śāṇḍilya idaṃ śāstramadhigatavānityādivedanindādarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because statements disparaging the <s>Vedas</s> are seen, such as: '<s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, not having found the highest good in the four <s>Vedas</s>, studied this scripture [the <s>Pañcarātra</s>].'

children.text: tasmādasaṃgataiṣā kalpaneti siddham // 45 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that this conception is untenable. // 45 //
And in this scripture [of the <s>Bhāgavatas</s>], many kinds of internal contradictions are found — such as the conception of qualities and their possessor.

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye dvitīyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 2 //

children.text: iti dvitīyādhyāyasya sāṃkhyādimatānāṃ duṣṭatvapradarśanaṃ nāma dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s>, called 'Demonstrating the Defectiveness of the Doctrines of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and Others.' //

children.text: dvitīyādhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Second <s>Adhyāya</s>, Third <s>Pāda</s>.

children.text: atra pāde pañcamahābhūtajīvādiśrutīnāṃ virodhaparihāraḥ 1
viyadadhikaraṇam / sū. 1-7
children.translated_text: Section 1: <s>Viyadadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 1-7
In this <s>pāda</s>: the resolution of contradictions among the <s>śruti</s> passages concerning the five great elements, the <s>jīva</s>, and the like.

children.text: na viyadaśruteḥ | BBs_2,3.1 |
children.translated_text: <s>Na viyad aśruteḥ</s> — Space (<s>vyoman</s>) [is not produced], because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s> [statement to that effect]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.1 |

children.text:
vedānteṣu tatra tatra bhinnaprasthānā utpattiśrutaya upalabhyante /
kecidākāśasyotpattimāmananti, kecinna /
tathā kecidvāyorutpattimāmananti, kecinna /
evaṃ jīvasya prāṇānāṃ ca /
evameva kramādidvārako 'pi vipratiṣedhaḥ śrutyantareṣūpalakṣyate /
vipratiṣedhācca parapakṣāṇāmanapekṣitatvaṃ sthāpitaṃ tadvatsvapakṣasyāpi vipratiṣedhādevānapekṣitatvamāśaṅkyetetyataḥ sarvavedāntagatasṛṣṭiśrutyarthanirmalatvāya paraḥ paprañca ārabhyate /
tadarthanirmalatve ca phalaṃ yathoktāśaṅkānivṛttireva /
tatra prathamaṃ tāvadākāśamāśritya cintyate kimasyākāśasyotpattirastyuta nāstīti /
tatra tāvatpratipadyate- 'na viyadaśruteḥ' iti /
na khalvākāśamutpadyate /
kasmāt /
aśruteḥ /
nahyasyotpattiprakaraṇe śravaṇamasti /

chāndogye hi 'sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1) iti sacchabdavācyaṃ brahma prakṛtya 'tadaikṣata', 'tattejo 'sṛjata' (chā. 6.2.3) iti ca pañcānāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ madhyamaṃ teja ādiṅkṛtvā trayāṇāṃ tejobannānāmutpattiḥ śrāvyate /
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, having introduced <s>Brahman</s> — denoted by the word '<s>Sat</s>' (Being) — with 'Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning — one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1), and [having stated] 'It deliberated,' 'It created fire (<s>tejas</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3) — the origination of three [elements] — fire, water, and food — is taught, beginning with fire, the middle one among the five great elements.

children.text: śrutiśca naḥ pramāṇamatīndriyārthavijñānotpattau /
children.translated_text: And <s>śruti</s> is our authority for the knowledge of supersensible matters.

children.text: nacātra śrutirastyākāśasyotpattipratipādinī /
children.translated_text: And here there is no <s>śruti</s> teaching the origination of space.

children.text: tasmānnāstyākāśasyotpattiriti // 1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, space has no origination. // 1 //

In the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, creation-statements with differing procedures are found here and there. Some teach the origination of space (<s>ākāśa</s>); some do not. Similarly, some teach the origination of air (<s>vāyu</s>); some do not. Likewise for the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>prāṇas</s>. Similarly, contradictions regarding sequence and the like are also observed in other <s>śruti</s> texts. And since it was established that the rival doctrines are to be disregarded because of [internal] contradictions — lest it be suspected that one's own position too, because of contradictions, should be disregarded — for the purpose of clarifying the meaning of all the creation-<s>śrutis</s> found in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, an extensive discussion is now commenced. And the fruit of clarifying their meaning is precisely the removal of the apprehension described. Therein, first, considering with respect to space: does this space have an origination or not? On this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] first establishes: 'Space [is not produced], because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s>.' Space is certainly not produced. Why? Because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s> [statement]. For there is no teaching of its origination in the creation-context.

children.text: asti tu | BBs_2,3.2 |
children.translated_text: <s>Asti tu</s> — But it does [have an origination]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.2 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣāntaraparigrahe /
mā nāmākāśasya chāndogye bhūdutpattiḥ, śrutyantare tvasti /
taittirīyakā hi samāmananti- 'satyaṃ jñānamantaṃ brahma' iti prakṛtya 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti /
tataśca śrutyorvipratiṣedhaḥ kvacittejaḥpramukhā sṛṣṭiḥ kvacidākāśapramukheti /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) marks the adoption of the alternative position. Even if space has no origination in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, it does in another <s>śruti</s>. For the <s>Taittirīyakas</s> teach: having introduced [<s>Brahman</s>] with 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' — 'From that very Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). And thus there is a contradiction between the <s>śrutis</s> — in one [text], creation begins with fire; in another, with space.

children.text: nanvekavākyatānayoḥ śrutyoryuktā /
children.translated_text: Objection: Is not a single-sentence reading (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) of the two <s>śrutis</s> appropriate?

children.text:
satyam /
sā yuktā natu sāvagantuṃ śakyate /
kutaḥ /
'tattejo 'sṛjata' (chā. 6.2.3) iti sakṛcchrutasya sraṣṭuḥ sraṣṭavyadvayena saṃbandhānupapatteḥ, 'tattejo 'sṛjata', 'tadākāśamasṛjata' iti /
children.translated_text: True. Such a reading is appropriate, but it cannot be achieved. Why? Because it is impossible to connect the creator — who is heard only once — with two things to be created: 'It created fire' and 'It created space' [as if both were first-created].

children.text: nanu sakṛcchrutasyāpi kartuḥ kartavyadvayena saṃbandho dṛśyate,yathā sūpaṃ paktvaudanaṃ pacatīti, evaṃ tadākāśaṃ sṛṣṭvā tattejo 'sṛjatīti yojayiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: Objection: But even a once-mentioned agent can be connected with two things to be done — as in 'having cooked the curry, he cooks the rice.' So I shall construe: 'having created space, It created fire.'

children.text:
naivaṃ yujyate /
prathamajatvaṃ hi chāndogye tejaso 'vagamyate taittirīyake cākāśasya /
nacobhayoḥ prathamajatvaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: And both cannot be first-born.

children.text: etenetaraśrutyakṣaravirodho 'pi vyākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this, the contradiction with the literal text of the other <s>śruti</s> is also explained.

children.text: 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai. 2.1) ityatrāpi tasmādākāśaḥ saṃbhūtastasmāttejaḥ saṃbhūtamiti sakṛcchrutasyāpādānasya saṃbhavanasya ca viyattejobhyāṃ yugapatsaṃbandhānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: In 'From that very Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1) too — the impossibility of simultaneously connecting the source (heard only once) with both space and fire as products [is the issue] — since from that [Self] space was born, and from that [Self] fire was born [cannot both be 'first'].

children.text: 'vāyoragniḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti ca pṛthagāmnānāt // 2 //
children.translated_text: And because of the separate mention — 'From air, fire' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). // 2 //
This is not proper. For in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, fire is understood to be first-born, and in the <s>Taittirīya</s>, space.

children.text: asminvipratiṣedhe kaścidāha-
children.translated_text: In this contradiction, someone says —

children.text: gauṇyasaṃbhavāt | BBs_2,3.3 |
children.translated_text: <s>Gauṇy asaṃbhavāt</s> — [The <s>Taittirīya</s> statement is] figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>), because of impossibility. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.3 |

children.text:
nāsti viyata utpattiraśrutereva /
yā tvitarā viyadutpattivādinī śrutirudāhṛtā sā gauṇī bhavitumarhati /
kasmāt /
asaṃbhavāt /
nahyākāśasyotpattiḥ saṃbhāvayituṃ śakyā śrīmatkaṇabhugabhiprāyānusāriṣu jīvatsu /
te hi kāraṇasāmāgryasaṃbhavādakāśasyotpattiṃ vārayanti /
samavāyyasamavāyinimittakāraṇebhyo hi kila sarvamutpadyamānaṃ samutpadyate /
dravyasya caikajātīyakamanekaṃ ca dravyaṃ samavāyikāraṇaṃ bhavati /
nacākāśasyaikajātīyakamanekaṃ ca dravyamārambhakamasti, yasminsamavāyikāraṇe satyasamavāyikāraṇe ca tatsaṃyoga ākāśa utpadyeta /
tadabhāvāttu tadanugrahapravṛttaṃ nimittakāraṇaṃ dūrāpetamevākāśasya bhavati /
utpattimatāṃ ca tejaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ pūrvottarakāyorviśeṣaḥ saṃbhāvyate prāgutpatteḥ prakāśādikāryaṃ na babhūva paścācca bhavatīti /
ākāśasya punarna pūrvottarakālayorviśeṣaḥ saṃbhāvayituṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: But for space, a difference between the earlier and later states cannot be conceived.

children.text: kiṃ hi prāgutpatteranavakāśamasuṣiramacchidraṃ babhūveti śakyate 'dhyavasātum /
children.translated_text: For can it be determined that before [its] origination there was no room, no hollowness, no openness?

children.text: pṛthivyādivaidharmyācca vibhutvādilakṣaṇādākāśasyājatvasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of [space's] dissimilarity from earth and the like — characterized by all-pervasiveness and such — the unoriginatedness of space is established.

children.text: tasmādyathā loka ākāśaṃ kurvākāśo jāta ityevañjātīyako gauṇaḥ prayogo bhavati, yathāca ghaṭākāśaḥ karakākāśo gṛhākāśa ityekasyāpyākāśasyaivañjātīyako bhedavyapadeśo gauṇo bhavati, vede 'pi 'āraṇyānākāśeṣvālabheran' iti, evamutpattiśrutirapi gauṇī draṣṭavyā // 3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as in ordinary usage there is figurative usage of the kind 'make space,' 'space has arisen'; and just as even for the one [single] space, designations of division such as 'the space of a pot,' 'the space of a water-jar,' 'the space of a house' are figurative — and even in the <s>Veda</s> [we find]: 'One should sacrifice in the forest spaces' — similarly, the <s>śruti</s> teaching the origination [of space] should also be understood as figurative. // 3 //

Space has no origination — precisely because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s> [teaching it]. And the other <s>śruti</s> that was cited as teaching the origination of space must be figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>). Why? Because of impossibility. For the origination of space cannot be conceived — as long as those who follow the esteemed <s>Kaṇabhuj</s> (i.e., <s>Kaṇāda</s>, the founder of <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>) are alive. For they preclude the origination of space because the aggregate of causes [required for it] is not possible. For everything that comes into being arises from the three causes: the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>), the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>), and the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>). And the inherent cause of a substance is a substance that is of the same kind [as the effect] and is multiple. But there is no substance of the same kind as space that is multiple and could serve as its originating [inherent cause] — in the presence of which inherent cause, together with its non-inherent cause (i.e., the conjunction of those substances), space could be produced. And because of the absence of that [inherent cause], the efficient cause — which operates in dependence on its support — is also far removed from space. And for things that have origination, such as fire and the rest, a difference between the earlier and later states can be conceived: before origination, the effect of illumination and such did not exist; after [origination], it does.

children.text: śabdācca | BBs_2,3.4 |
children.translated_text: And because of scripture (<s>śabda</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.4 |

children.text:
śabdaḥ khalvākāśasyājatvaṃ khyāpayati /
yata āha- 'vāyuścāntarikṣaṃ caitadamṛtam' (bṛ. 2.3.3) iti /
nahyamṛtasyotpattirupapadyate /
ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ iti cākāśena brahma sarvagatatvanityatvābhyāṃ dharmābhyāmupamimāna ākāśasyāpi tau dharmau sūcayati /
naca tādṛśasyotpattirupapadyate /
'sa yathānanto 'yamākāśa evamananta ātmā veditavyaḥ' iti codāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Just as this space is infinite, so the Self is to be known as infinite' — and this is an illustration [establishing the same point].

children.text: 'ākāśaśarīraṃ brahma' (tai. 1.6.2), 'ākāśa ātmā' (tai. 1.7.1) iti ca /
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s> whose body is space' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2), and 'Space is the Self' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.7.1) — [these passages also support this].

children.text: nahyākāśasyotpattimattve brahmaṇastena viśeṣeṇa saṃbhavati nīlenevotpalasya /
children.translated_text: For if space had an origination, describing <s>Brahman</s> with this attribute [of space] would not be possible — just as [describing] a lotus with [the attribute of] blue [is possible only because both exist together].

children.text: tasmānnityamevākāśena sādhāraṇaṃ brahmeti gamyate // 4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is understood that <s>Brahman</s>, being eternal, shares [this property] with space. // 4 //

Scripture indeed declares the unoriginatedness of space. For it says: 'Air and the intermediate space — this is immortal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.3). And the origination of what is immortal is not tenable. And 'All-pervading and eternal, like space' — by comparing <s>Brahman</s> with space through the two properties of all-pervasiveness and eternality, it indicates those two properties for space as well. And the origination of something of such a nature is not tenable.

children.text: syāc caikasya brahmaśabdavat | BBs_2,3.5 |
children.translated_text: And it may be [figurative], as in the case of the word '<s>Brahman</s>,' for a single [word]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.5 |

children.text:
idaṃ padottaraṃ sūtram /
syādetat /
kathaṃ punarekasya saṃbhūtaśabdasya 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai.
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> follows [as a response to] the preceding verse. One might ask: how can one and the same word '<s>saṃbhūta</s>' (born) — continuing from the context 'From that very Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s>

children.text: 2.1) ityasminnadhikāre pareṣu tejaḥprabhṛtiṣvanuvartamānasya mukhyatvaṃ saṃbhavatyākāśe ca gauṇatvamiti /
children.translated_text: 2.1) — be literal when it carries over to the subsequent [elements] such as fire and the rest, and yet figurative with respect to space?

children.text:
ata uttaramucyate- syāccaikasyāpi saṃbhūtaśabdasya viṣayaviśeṣavaśādgauṇo mukhyasya prayogo brahmaśabdavat /
yathaikasyāpi brahmaśabdasya 'tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva, tapo brahma' (tai. 3.2) ityasminnadhikāre 'nnādiṣu gauṇaḥ prayoga ānande ca mukhyaḥ /
yathā ca tapasi brahmavijñānasādhane brahmaśabdo bhaktyā prayujyate 'ñjasā tu vijñeye brahmaṇi tadvat /
kathaṃ punaranutpattau nabhasaḥ 'ekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1) itīyaṃ pratijñā samarthyate /
children.translated_text: To this the answer is given: Even a single word '<s>saṃbhūta</s>' may have a figurative usage alongside its literal usage, depending on the specific subject matter — just like the word '<s>Brahman</s>.' For even the single word '<s>Brahman</s>,' in the context '<s>Tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva</s>, <s>tapo brahma</s>' ('Seek to know <s>Brahman</s> through <s>tapas</s>; <s>tapas</s> is <s>Brahman</s>,' <s>Taittirīya</s> 3.2), is used figuratively with respect to food and such, and literally with respect to <s>Ānanda</s> (bliss). And just as the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is used figuratively for <s>tapas</s>, which is a means of knowing <s>Brahman</s>, but directly for the <s>Brahman</s> that is to be known — so too [the word '<s>saṃbhūta</s>' is figurative for space and literal for the rest]. But how can the promise 'One only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) be maintained if space is not originated?

children.text:
nanu nabhasā dvitīyena sadvitīyaṃ brahma prāpnoti /
kathaṃ ca brahmaṇi vidite sarvaṃ viditaṃ syāditi /
children.translated_text: Indeed, with space as a second [entity], <s>Brahman</s> would become 'with a second.' And how could 'by knowing <s>Brahman</s>, everything is known' [be fulfilled]?

children.text:
taducyate- ekameveti tāvatsvakāryāpekṣayopapadyate /
yathā loke kaścitkumbhakārakule pūrvedyurmṛddaṇḍacakrādīni copalabhyāparedyuśca nānāvidhānyamatrāṇi prasāritānyupalabhya brūyānmṛdevaikākinī pūrvedyurāsīditi sa ca tayāvadhāraṇayā mṛtkāryajātameva pūrvedyurnāsīdityabhipreyānna daṇḍacakrādi, tadvadadvitīyaśrutiradhiṣṭhātrāntaraṃ vārayati /
yathā mṛdo 'matraprakṛteḥ kumbhakāro 'dhiṣṭhātā dṛśyate naivaṃ brahmaṇo jagatprakṛteranyo 'dhikṛtāstīti /
naca nabhasāpi dvitīyena sadvitīyaṃ brahma prasajyate /
lakṣaṇānyatvanimittaṃ hi nānātvam /
naca prāgutpatterbrahmanabhasorlakṣaṇānyatvamasti kṣīrodakayoriva saṃsṛṣṭyorvyāpitvāmūrtatvadidharmasāmānyāt /
sargakāle tu brahma jagadutpādayituṃ yatate stimitamitaravattiṣṭati /
tenānyatvamavasīyate /
tathāca 'ākāśaśarīraṃ brahma' (tai. 1.6.2) ityādiśrutibhyo 'pi brahmākāśayorabhedopacārasiddhiḥ /
ata eva ca brahmavijñānena sarvavijñānasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And precisely for this reason, through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, the knowledge of everything is established.

children.text: apica sarvaṃ kāryamutpadyamānamākāśenāvyatiriktadeśakālamevotpadyate, brahmaṇā cāvyatiriktadeśakālamevākāśaṃ bhavatīti, ato brahmaṇā tatkāryeṇa ca vijñātena sahavijñātamevākāśaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, every effect, when it originates, originates in a place and time not different from space, and space exists in a place and time not different from <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, when <s>Brahman</s> and its effects are known, space is known along with them.

children.text: yathā kṣīrapūrṇe ghaṭe katicidabbindavaḥ prakṣiptāḥ santaḥ kṣīragrahaṇenaiva gṛhītā bhavanti, nahi kṣīraprahaṇādabbindavugrahaṇaṃ pariśiṣyate, evaṃ brahmaṇā tatkāryaiścāvyatiriktadeśakālatvādgṛhītameva brahmagrahaṇena nabho bhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as when a few drops of water are cast into a pot full of milk, they are grasped by the very grasping of the milk — for no grasping of the water-drops remains apart from the grasping of the milk — so too, because of its non-difference in place and time from <s>Brahman</s> and its effects, space is already grasped by the grasping of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmādbhāktaṃ nabhasaḥ saṃbhavaśravaṇamiti // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the hearing of the origination of space is figurative. // 5 //

To this it is said: 'One only' is first of all tenable with reference to its own effects. Just as in the world, someone in a potter's household, having observed clay, rods, wheels, and such on one day, and then seeing various vessels spread out on the next day, would say 'the clay alone was solitary yesterday' — and by that determination he intends that it was the class of effects of the clay that did not exist yesterday, not the rods, wheels, and such — similarly, the <s>śruti</s> 'without a second' precludes another superintendent. Just as for clay — the material cause of vessels — a potter is seen as superintendent, no such other superintendent exists for <s>Brahman</s> — the material cause of the world. And <s>Brahman</s> does not become 'with a second' even through space as a second [entity]. For duality is caused by difference of characteristics. And prior to creation, there is no difference of characteristics between <s>Brahman</s> and space — just as between milk and water when they are mixed — because of the commonality of properties such as all-pervasiveness and formlessness. But at the time of creation, <s>Brahman</s> exerts itself to produce the world, while [space] remains still, like something other [than the active cause]. By this, the otherness [between them] is determined. And from <s>śrutis</s> such as '<s>Brahman</s> whose body is space' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2), the establishment of non-difference between <s>Brahman</s> and space through figurative identification [is achieved].

children.text:
FN: abhedopacāro bhaktiḥ /
kulaṃ gṛham /
amatrāṇi ghaṭādīni /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: 'Figurative identification' (<s>abhedopacāra</s>) is '<s>bhakti</s>' (secondary usage).
'<s>Kula</s>' means house.
'<s>Amatrāṇi</s>' means pots and such.

children.text: evaṃ prāpta idamāha -
children.translated_text: Having thus established [this position], he now says —

children.text: pratijñāhānir avyatirekāc chabdebhyaḥ | BBs_2,3.6 |
children.translated_text: The abandonment of the promise, because of non-difference, and from the scriptural texts. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.6 |

children.text:
'yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavatyamataṃ matamavijñātaṃ vijñātam' (chā. 6.1.1) iti, 'ātmani khalvare dṛṣṭe śrute mate vijñāta idaṃ sarvaṃ viditam' (bṛ. 4.5.6) iti, 'kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati' (muṇḍa. 1.1.3) iti, 'na kācana maddhahirdhā vidyāsti' iti caivaṃrūpā prativedāntaṃ pratijñā vijñāyate /
tasyāḥ pratijñāyā evamahāniranuparodhaḥ syāt, yadyavyatirekaḥ kṛtsnasya vastujātasya vijñeyādbrahmaṇaḥ syāt /
vyatireke hi satyekavijñānena sarvaṃ vijñāyata itīyaṃ pratijñā hrīyeta /
sa cāvyatireka evamupapadyate yadi kṛtsnaṃ vastujātamekasmādbrahmaṇa utpadyeta /
śabdebhyaśca prakṛtivikārāvyatirekanyāyenaiva pratijñāsiddhiravagamyate /
tathāhi- 'yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavati' iti pratijñāya mṛdādidṛṣṭāntaiḥ kāryakāraṇābhedapratipādanaparaiḥ pratijñaiṣā samarthyate /
tatsādhanāyaiva cottare śabdāḥ 'sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1), 'tadaikṣata', 'tattejo 'sṛjata' (chā. 6.2.3) ityevaṃ kāryajātaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pradarśyāvyatirekaṃ pradarśayanti- 'aitadātmyamidaṃ sarvam' (chā. 6.8.7)
children.translated_text: 'By which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.1), and 'When the Self has been seen, heard, thought, and known, then all this is known' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6), and 'By knowing what, O revered sir, does all this become known?' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.3), and 'There is nothing whatsoever separate from Me' — such a promise is found in every <s>Vedānta</s> text. The non-abandonment of that promise — its being unimpaired — would [hold] only if the entire class of entities were non-different from <s>Brahman</s>, the object of knowledge. For if there were difference, the promise 'by one knowledge, everything is known' would be violated. And that non-difference is tenable only if the entire class of entities originates from the one <s>Brahman</s>. And from the scriptural texts too, it is understood that the fulfillment of the promise operates precisely through the principle of the non-difference of material cause and effects. For having made the promise 'By which the unheard becomes heard,' [the text] supports this promise through the illustrations of clay and such, which serve to demonstrate the non-difference of effect from cause. And the subsequent texts too, for the purpose of establishing that very [non-difference], present the class of effects as originating from <s>Brahman</s> — 'Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning, one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1), 'It deliberated,' 'It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3) — and then demonstrate non-difference: 'All this has that as its Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7),

children.text:
ityārabhyāprapāṭhakaparisamāpteḥ /
tadyadyākāśaṃ na brahmakāryaṃ syānna brahmaṇi vijñāta ākāśaṃ vijñāyeta, tataśca pratijñāhāniḥ syāt /
naca pratijñāhānyā vedasyāprāmāṇyaṃ yuktaṃ kartum /
tathāhi- prativedāntaṃ te te śabdāstena tena dṛṣṭāntena tāmeva pratijñāṃ khyapayanti 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' (bṛ. 2.4.6),' brahmaivedamamṛtaṃ purastāt' (muṇḍa. 2.2.11) ityevamādayaḥ /
tasmājjvalanādivadeva gaganamapyutpadyate /
yaduktamaśruterna viyadutpadyata iti, tadayuktaṃ, viyadutpattiviṣayaśrutyantarasya darśitatvāt 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti /
satyaṃ darśitam /
viruddhaṃ tu 'tattejo 'sṛjata' ityanena śrutyantareṇa /
na /
ekavākyatvātsarvaśrutīnām /
bhavatyekavākyatvamaviruddhānām /
iha tu virodha uktaḥ, sakṛcchrutasya sraṣṭuḥ sraṣṭavyadvayasaṃbandhāsaṃbhavāddvayośca prathamajatvāsaṃbhavādvikalpāsaṃbhavācceti /
children.translated_text: continuing up to the conclusion of the chapter. Now, if space were not an effect of <s>Brahman</s>, then when <s>Brahman</s> is known, space would not be known — and consequently, the promise would be violated. And it is not proper to make the <s>Veda</s> unauthoritative through the violation of the promise. For throughout the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, various scriptural passages, through various illustrations, proclaim this very promise: 'All this is this Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6), 'This <s>Brahman</s> alone is the immortal [that extends] in front' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.11), and such passages. Therefore, space too originates, just like fire and such. As for the argument that 'space is not originated, because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s>' — that is untenable, because another <s>śruti</s> teaching the origination of space has been shown: 'From that very Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). True, it has been shown. But it contradicts the other <s>śruti</s>: 'It created fire.' No. Because all <s>śrutis</s> form a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>). But single-sentence reading is [possible only] for non-contradictory [passages]. Here, however, a contradiction was pointed out — the impossibility of connecting the creator (heard only once) with two things to be created, the impossibility of both being first-born, and the impossibility of an alternative.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
tejaḥsargasya taittirīyake tṛtīyatvaśravaṇāt 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ /
ākāśādvāyuḥ /
vāyoragniḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti /
aśakyā hīyaṃ śrutiranyathā pariṇetum /
śakyā tu pariṇetuṃ chāndogyaśrutistadākāśaṃ vāyuṃ ca sṛṣṭvā 'tattejo 'sṛjata' iti /
nahīyaṃ śrutistejojanipradhānā satī śrutyantaraprasiddhāmākāśasyotpattiṃ vārayituṃ śaknoti /
ekasya vākyasya vyāpāradvayāsaṃbhavāt /
sraṣṭvā tveko 'pi krameṇānekaṃ sraṣṭavyaṃ sṛjet /
ityekavākyatvakalpanāyāṃ saṃbhavatyāṃ na viruddhārthatvena śrutirhātavyā /
nacāsmābhiḥ sakṛcchrutasya sraṣṭuḥ sraṣṭavyadvayasaṃbandho 'bhipreyate śrutyantaravaśena sraṣṭavyāntaropasaṃgrahāt /
yathāca 'sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalān' (chā. 3.14.1) ityatra sākṣādeva sarvasya vastujātasya brahmajatvaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ na pradeśāntaravihitaṃ tejaḥpramukhamutpattikramaṃ vārayati, evaṃ tejaso 'pi brahmajatvaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ na śrutyantaravihitaṃ nabhaḥpramukhamutpattikramaṃ vārayitumarhati /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because in the <s>Taittirīya</s>, the creation of fire is heard as [occurring] third: 'From that very Self, space was born. From space, air. From air, fire' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). For this <s>śruti</s> cannot be construed otherwise. But the <s>Chāndogya śruti</s> can be construed [as meaning]: 'Having created space and air, It created fire.' For this <s>śruti</s>, whose primary purpose is [to teach] the origination of fire, cannot preclude the origination of space that is established by another <s>śruti</s> — because a single sentence cannot accomplish two purposes [simultaneously]. But even a single creator, [acting] sequentially, may create many things to be created. Thus, when the single-sentence reading is possible, <s>śruti</s> should not be abandoned as having a contradictory meaning. And we do not intend that the creator — heard only once — is connected with [only] two things to be created, because through the force of another <s>śruti</s>, additional things to be created are included. And just as in 'All this indeed is <s>Brahman</s>; <s>tajjalān</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1), where the origination of the entire class of entities from <s>Brahman</s> is directly heard, [this] does not preclude the order of creation beginning with fire that is prescribed elsewhere — similarly, the hearing of the origination of fire from <s>Brahman</s> should not preclude the order of creation beginning with space that is prescribed in another <s>śruti</s>.

children.text:
nanu śamavidhānārthametadvākyam, 'tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta' iti śruteḥ, naitatsṛṣṭivākyaṃ, tasmādetanna pradeśāntarasiddhaṃ kramamuparoddhumarhatīti /
'tattejo 'sṛjata' ityetatsṛṣṭivākyam /
tasmādatra yathāśruti kramo grahītavya iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: but this passage ['All this indeed is <s>Brahman</s>; <s>tajjalān</s>'] is for the purpose of prescribing tranquility — as per the <s>śruti</s> '<s>tajjalān</s> — one should worship [<s>Brahman</s>] as tranquil.' This is not a creation-passage. Therefore, it should not obstruct the sequence established in another place. 'It created fire' — this is a creation-passage. Therefore, the order therein should be taken as per the literal text.

children.text:
netyucyate /
nahi tejaḥprāthamyānurodhena śrutyantaraprasiddho viyatpadārthaḥ parityaktavyo bhavati, padārthadharmatvātkramasya /
apica 'tattejo 'sṛjata' iti nātra kramasya vācakaḥ kaścicchabdo 'sti /
children.translated_text: Not so, it is replied. For the entity 'space,' well established by another <s>śruti</s>, should not be abandoned [merely] to preserve the priority of fire — because the sequence is a property of the entities [described]. Moreover, in 'It created fire,' there is no specific word here that expresses sequence.

children.text:
arthāttu kramo 'vagamyate /
sa ca 'vāyoragniḥ' ityanena śrutyantaraprasiddhena krameṇa nivāryate /
vikalpasamuccayau tu viyattejasoḥ prathamajatvaviṣayāvasaṃbhavānabhyupagamābhyāṃ nivāritau /
tasmānnāsti śrutyorvipratiṣedhaḥ /
apica chāndogye 'yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavati' ityetāṃ pratijñāṃ vākyopakrame śrutāṃ samarthayitumasamāmnātamapi viyadutpattāvupasaṃkhyātavyaṃ, kimaṅga punastaittirīyake samāmnātaṃ nabho na saṃgṛhyate /
yaccoktamākāśasya sarveṇānanyadeśakālatvādbrahmaṇā tatkāryaiśca saha viditameva tadbhavatyato na pratijñā hīyate, naca 'ekamevādvitīyam' iti śrutikopo bhavati, kṣīrodakavadbrahmanabhasoravyatirekopapatteriti /
children.translated_text: Rather, the sequence is understood from the context. And that [contextually inferred sequence] is overridden by the sequence established in another <s>śruti</s>: 'From air, fire' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). As for the alternative and the cumulative [readings] regarding the first-born status of space and fire — these were excluded because of the impossibility [of both being first-born] and because [an alternative reading] is not accepted. Therefore, there is no contradiction between the <s>śrutis</s>. Moreover, in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, [even though space is] not mentioned, it must be included [in the creation sequence] in order to vindicate the promise 'By which the unheard becomes heard' heard at the beginning of the passage — how much more so when the <s>Taittirīya</s> explicitly teaches [the origination of] space, should it not be accepted? And as for the argument that, because of the non-difference of space from <s>Brahman</s> in place and time — like milk and water — space is already known along with <s>Brahman</s> and its effects, and therefore the promise is not violated, and the <s>śruti</s> 'one only, without a second' is not disturbed —

children.text:
atrocyate /
na kṣīrodakanyāyenedamekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ netavyam /
mṛdādidṛṣṭāntapraṇayanāddhi prakṛtivikāranyāyenaivedaṃ sarvavijñānaṃ netavyamiti gamyate /
kṣīrodakanyāyena ca sarvavijñānaṃ kalpyamānaṃ na samyagvijñānaṃ syāt /
nahi kṣīrajñānagṛhītasyodakasya samyagvijñānagṛhītamasti /
naca vedasya puruṣāṇāmiva māyālīkavañcanādibhirarthāvadhāraṇamupapadyate /
sāvadhāraṇā ceyam /
children.translated_text: And this [teaching] is emphatic.

children.text: 'ekamevādvitīyam' iti śrutiḥ kṣīrodakanyāyena nīyamānā pīḍyeta /
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> 'one only, without a second' would be strained if construed according to the milk-water principle.

children.text: naca svakāryāpekṣayedaṃ vastvekadeśaviṣayaṃ sarvavijñānamekamevādvitīyatāvadhāraṇaṃ ceti nyāyyaṃ, mṛdādiṣvapi hi tatsaṃbhavānna tadapūrvavadupanyasitavyaṃ bhavati 'śvetaketo yannu somyedaṃ mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdho 'syuta tamādeśamaprākṣyo 'yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavati' (chā. 6.1.1) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: Nor is it proper [to say] that this 'knowledge of everything' is directed at a partial object [only], and that the emphatic assertion of being 'one only, without a second' is [merely partial] — because even in clay and such [illustrations], since that [partial knowledge] is possible, it need not be presented as something novel with [the introduction]: 'O <s>Śvetaketu</s>, you who are greatly proud, instructed, and arrogant — have you asked for that teaching by which the unheard becomes heard?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.1) and the like.

children.text: tasmādaśeṣavastuviṣayamevedaṃ sarvavijñānaṃ sarvasya brahmakāryatāpekṣayopanyasyata iti draṣṭavyam // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it should be understood that this 'knowledge of everything' is presented as directed at all objects without exception, by virtue of everything being an effect of <s>Brahman</s>. // 6 //

To this it is said: This 'knowledge of everything through one' should not be construed according to the principle of milk and water [i.e., knowing the water mixed in milk by knowing the milk]. For from the employment of illustrations such as clay, it is understood that this 'knowledge of everything' is to be construed according to the principle of material cause and modification. And if 'knowledge of everything' were imagined according to the milk-water principle, it would not be complete knowledge. For the water grasped through knowledge of milk is not grasped by complete knowledge. And it is not tenable that the <s>Veda</s> determines its meaning through deception and trickery, as is the case with human beings.

children.text:
yatpunaretaduktamasaṃbhavād gauṇī ganasyotpattiśrutiriti /
atra brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: Now, as for the statement that the creation-<s>śruti</s> regarding space is figurative because of impossibility — to that we say:

children.text: yāvadvikāraṃ tu vibhāgo lokavat | BBs_2,3.7 |
children.translated_text: <s>Yāvadvikāraṃ tu vibhāgo lokavat</s> — But differentiation [extends] to the extent of modification, as in the world. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.7 |

children.text:
tuśabdo 'saṃbhavāśaṅkāvyāvṛttyarthaḥ /
na khalvākāśotpattāvasaṃbhavāśaṅkā kartavyā /
yato yāvatkiñcidvikārajātaṃ dṛśyate ghaṭaghaṭikodañcanādi vā kaṭakakeyūrakuṇḍalādi vā sūcīnārācanistriṃśādi vā tāvāneva vibhāgo loke lakṣyate /
natvavikṛtaṃ kiñcitkutaścidvibhaktamupalabhyate /
vibhāgaścākāśasya pṛthivyādibhyo 'vagamyate /
tasmātso 'pi vikāro bhavitumarhati /
etena dikkālamanaḥparamāṇvādīnāṃ kāryatvaṃ vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) is for removing the suspicion of impossibility. The suspicion of impossibility regarding the origination of space should not be entertained. Because whatever class of modifications is seen — whether pots, small pots, and water-buckets, or bracelets, armlets, and earrings, or needles, arrows, and swords — to exactly that extent, differentiation is observed in the world. But nothing unmodified is ever found to be differentiated from anything. And the differentiation of space from earth and the like is ascertained. Therefore, it too must be a modification. By this, the status as effects of directions, time, mind, atoms, and the like is also explained.

children.text: nanvātmāpyākāśādibhyo vibhakta iti tasyāpi kāryatvaṃ ghaṭādivatprāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the Self too is differentiated from space and the like; therefore, it too would be an effect, like a pot.

children.text:
na /
'ātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti śruteḥ /
yadi hyātmāpi vikāraḥ syāttasmātparamanyanna śrutamityākāśādi sarvaṃ kāryaṃ nirātmakamātmanaḥ kāryatve syāt /
tathāca śūnyavādaḥ prasajyeta /
ātmatvāccātmano nirākaraṇaśaṅkānupapattiḥ /
nahyātmāgantukaḥ kasyacit, svayaṃsiddhatvāt /
nahyātmātmanaḥ pramāṇamapekṣya sidhyati /
tasya hi pratyakṣādīni pramāṇānyaprasiddhaprameyasiddhaya upādīyante /
nahyākāśādayaḥ padārdhāḥ pramāṇanirapekṣāḥ svayaṃsiddhāḥ kenacidabhyupagamyante /
ātmā tu pramāṇādivyavahārāśrayatvātprāgeva pramāṇādivyavahārātsidhyati /
naceddṛśasya nirākaraṇaṃ saṃbhavati /
āgantukaṃ hi vastu nirākriyate na svarūpam /
ya eva hi nirākartā tadeva tasya svarūpam /
nahyagnerauṣṇyamagninā nirākriyate /
tathāhamevedānīṃ jānāmi vartamānaṃ vastvahamevātītamatītataraṃ cājñāsiṣamahamevānāgatamanāgatataraṃ ca jñāsyāmītyatītānāgatavartamānabhāvenānyathābhavatyapi jñātavye na jñāturanyathābhāvo 'sati, sarvadā vartamānasvabhāvatvāt /
tathā bhasmībhavatyapi dehe cātmana ucchedo vartamānasvabhāvādanyathāsvabhāvatvaṃ vā na saṃbhāvayituṃ śakyam /
evamapratyākhyeyasvabhāvatvādevākāryatvamātmanaḥ kāryatvaṃ cākāśasya /
yattūktaṃ samānajātīyamanekaṃ kāraṇadravyaṃ vyomno nāstīti, tatpratyucyate- na tāvatsamānajātīyamevārabhate na bhinnajātīyamiti niyamo 'sti /
nahi tantūnāṃ tatsaṃyogānāṃ ca samānajātīyatvamasti, dravyaguṇatvābhyupagamāt /
naca nimittakāraṇānāmapi turīvemādīnāṃ samānajātīyatvaniyamo 'sti /
syādetat /
samavāyikāraṇaviṣaya eva samānajātīyatvābhyupagamo na kāraṇāntaraviṣaya iti /
tadapyanaikāntikam /
sūtragobālairhyanekajātīyairekā rajjuḥ sṛjyamānā dṛśyate /
tathā sūtrairūrṇādibhiśca vicitrānkambalānvitanvate /
sattvadravyatvādyapekṣayā vā samānajātīyatve kalpyamāne niyamānarthakyaṃ, sarvasya sarveṇa samānajātīyakatvāt /
nāpyanekamevārabhate naikamiti niyamo 'sti /
aṇumanasorādyakarmārambhābhyupagamāt /
ekaiko hi paramāṇirmanaścāyaṃ karmārabhate na dravyāntaraiḥ saṃhatyetyabhyupagamyate /
children.translated_text: No. Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'From that Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). For if the Self too were a modification, then — since nothing further is heard beyond it — all of space and the rest would be without a Self, [and] would be selfless if the Self were an effect.
