And thus the doctrine of the void (<s>śūnyavāda</s>) would follow. And because the Self is the Self, the suspicion of its refutation is untenable. For the Self is not adventitious for anyone, because it is self-established. For the Self does not require a means of knowledge to establish itself. For the means of knowledge such as perception are employed for the establishment of objects not yet established. But space and the other entities — no one accepts them as self-established and independent of means of knowledge. But the Self, being the basis of all transactions involving means of knowledge, is established even prior to the transactions of means of knowledge. And the refutation of such a [self-established entity] is not possible. For an adventitious entity can be refuted — not one's own nature. For whatever is the refuter — that itself is its own nature. For the heat of fire is not refuted by fire. Similarly, 'I know the present object right now; I knew the past and the more remote past; I shall know the future and the more remote future' — though the objects of knowledge undergo change as past, future, and present, the knower undergoes no change, because it is always of a present nature. Similarly, even when the body is reduced to ashes, neither the destruction of the Self nor any change from its present nature can be imagined. Thus, precisely because its nature cannot be denied, the Self is not an effect — and space is an effect. Now, as for the objection that there is no causal substance of the same class, and multiple [causal substances], for space — to that it is replied: First, there is no rule that only a same-class [substance] produces [an effect] and not a different-class one. For threads and their conjunction are not of the same class, because they are accepted as substance and quality respectively. Nor is there a rule of same-class-ness for efficient causes such as the shuttle, loom, and the like. [Objection:] Perhaps the claim of same-class-ness applies only to the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>), not to other kinds of causes. That too is not conclusive. For a single rope is seen being made from threads, cotton-fibers, and hair of different classes. Similarly, they weave variegated blankets from threads and wool. Or if same-class-ness is imagined with respect to being, substance-hood, and the like, then the restriction is meaningless — because everything is of the same class as everything else [in those respects]. Nor is there a rule that only multiple [substances] produce [an effect] and not a single one. Because of the acceptance that an individual atom and this mind each initiates its own initial motion — for each individual atom and mind is accepted as initiating motion without combining with other substances.

children.text: dravyārambha evānekārambhakatvaniyama iti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: the rule of multiple [causes] producing applies only to the origination of substance —

children.text:
na /
pariṇāmābhyupagamāt /
bhavedeṣa niyamo yadi saṃyogasacivaṃ dravyaṃ dravyāntarasyārambhakamabhyupagamyeta /
tadeva tu dravyaṃ viśeṣavadavasthāntaramāpadyamānaṃ kāryaṃ nāmābhyupagamyate /
tacca kvacidanekaṃ pariṇamate mṛdbījādyaṅ kurādibhāvena /
kvacidekaṃ pariṇamate kṣīrādi dadhyādibhāvena /
neśvaraśāsanamastyanekameva kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ janayatīti /
ataḥ śrutiprāmāṇyādekasmādbrahmaṇa ākāśādimahābhūtotpattikrameṇa jagajjātamiti niścīyate /
tathācoktam- 'upasaṃhāradarśanānneti cenna kṣīravaddhi' (bra. sū. 2.1.14) iti /
yaccoktamākāśasyotpattau na pūrvottarakālayorviśeṣaḥ saṃbhāvayituṃ śakyata iti /
tadayuktam /
yenaiva hi viśeṣeṇa pṛthivyādibhyo vyatiricyamānaṃ nabhaḥ svarūpavadidānīmadhyavasīyate sa eva viśeṣaḥ prāgutpatternāsīditi gamyate /
yathā ca brahma na sthūlādibhiḥ pṛthivyādisvabhāvaiḥ svabhāvavat, 'asthūlamanaṇu' (bṛ. 3.8.8) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ, evamākāśasvabhāvenāpi na svabhāvavadanākāśamiti śruteravagamyate /
tasmātprāgutpatteranākāśamiti sthitam /
yadapyuktaṃ pṛthivyādivaidharmyādākāśasyājatvamiti /
tadapyasat /
śrutivirodhe satyutpattyasaṃbhavānumānasyābhāsatvopapatteḥ /
utpattyanumānasya ca darśitatvāt /
anityamākāśamanityaguṇāśrayatvādghaṭādivadityādiprayogasaṃbhavācca /
ātmanyanaikāntikamiti cet /
children.translated_text: No. Because transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is accepted [as the mode of causation]. This rule would hold if a substance, assisted by conjunction, were accepted as the originator of another substance. But the very same substance, undergoing a different state with specific characteristics, is accepted as the effect. And sometimes one [substance] transforms into many — as clay and seeds into sprouts and the like. And sometimes one [substance] transforms [into another form by itself] — as milk into curds and the like. There is no decree of the Lord that only multiple causes can produce an effect. Therefore, on the authority of <s>śruti</s>, it is ascertained that the world was born from the one <s>Brahman</s> in the sequence of the great elements — space and the rest. And thus it has been said: '[The objection that] because dissolution is not observed [in <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> is not the cause] — [we say] no, because it is like milk' (<s>BBs</s> 2.1.14). As for the objection that no difference between the prior and subsequent states of space can be imagined — that is improper. For the very characteristic by which space is now ascertained as having its own nature, distinct from earth and the like — that very characteristic did not exist prior to origination, it is understood. And just as <s>Brahman</s> does not have as its nature the gross and other characteristics belonging to earth and the like — from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'neither gross nor subtle' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8) — so too, it is understood from <s>śruti</s> that [<s>Brahman</s>] does not have as its nature the nature of space — [i.e.,] it is non-spatial. Therefore, it is established that prior to origination, there was no space. And as for the objection that space is unborn because of its dissimilarity from earth and the like — that too is invalid. Because when there is contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, the inference of impossibility of origination turns out to be a mere semblance. And because the inference of origination has been demonstrated. And because inferences such as 'space is non-eternal, because it is the substratum of non-eternal qualities, like a pot' are possible. [Objection:] This is inconclusive with respect to the Self —

children.text:
na /
tasyaupaniṣadaṃ pratyanityaguṇāśrayatvāsiddheḥ /
vibhutvādīnāṃ cākāśasyotpattivādinaṃ pratyasiddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: No. Because for the follower of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the substratum-of-non-eternal-qualities-status of the Self is not established. And because properties such as pervasiveness and the like [attributed to space] are not established for a proponent of the origination of space.

children.text:
yaccoktametacchabdācceti, tatrāmṛtatvaśrutistāvadviyatyamṛtā divaukasa itivaddraṣṭavyā /
utpattipralayayorupapāditatvāt /
'ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ' ityapi prasiddhamahattvenākāśenopamānaṃ kriyate niratiśayamahattvāya nākāśasamatvāya /
yatheṣuriva savitā dhāvatīti kṣipragatitvāyocyate neṣutulyagatitvāya tadvat /
etenānantatvopamānaśrutirvyākhyātā /
'jyāyānākāśāt' ityādiśrutibhyaśca brahmaṇa ākāśasyonaparimāṇatvasiddhiḥ /
'na tasya pratimāsti' (śve. 4.19)
children.translated_text: As for the objection based on 'this word' [referring to passages that describe space as eternal] — in that regard, the <s>śruti</s> that speaks of the immortality of space should be understood like 'the <s>devas</s> are immortal in heaven' — i.e., as relative. Because origination and dissolution have been established. And the comparison 'like space, all-pervading and eternal' — here the comparison is made with space, which is well known for its greatness, for the sake of [illustrating] unsurpassable greatness — not for the sake of identity with space. Just as 'the sun runs like an arrow' is said for the sake of swiftness, not for the sake of being equal in speed to an arrow — similarly. By this, the <s>śruti</s> that compares with infinity is also explained. And from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'greater than space' and the like, the inferiority of space's measure compared to <s>Brahman</s> is established. 'There is no likeness of Him' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.19) —

children.text: iti ca brahmaṇo 'nupamānatvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: — shows that <s>Brahman</s> has no equal.

children.text: 'ato 'nyadārtam' (bṛ. 3.4.2) iti ca brahmaṇo 'nyeṣāmākāśādīnāmārtatvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And 'whatever is other [than <s>Brahman</s>] is afflicted' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.2) shows the afflicted nature of space and the other [entities] that are other than <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tapasi brahmaśabdavadākāśasya janmaśrutergauṇatvamityetadākāśasaṃbhavaśrutyanumānābhyāṃ parihṛtam /
children.translated_text: The claim that the <s>śruti</s> of space's origination is figurative — like the word '<s>Brahman</s>' in the context of <s>tapas</s> — has been resolved by the <s>śruti</s> of space's origination and by inference.

children.text: tasmādbrahmakāryaṃ viyaditi siddham // 7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that space is an effect of <s>Brahman</s>. // 7 //

children.text:
FN: dravyāntaraiḥ samavāyibhiḥ /
śabdāśrayatvaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'By other substances' — [meaning] by inherent [causes]. '[Sound-]substratum-hood' is the distinguishing characteristic [of space].

children.text: 2 mātariśvādhikaṇam / sū. 8
children.translated_text: Section 2: <s>Mātariśvādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 8

children.text: etena mātariśvā vyākhyātaḥ | BBs_2,3.8 |
children.translated_text: <s>Etena mātariśvā vyākhyātaḥ</s> — By this, <s>Mātariśvan</s> (air, <s>Vāyu</s>) is explained. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.8 |

children.text:
atideśo 'yam /
etena viyadvyākhyānena mātariśvāpi viyadāśrayo vāyurvyākhyātaḥ /
tatrāpyete yathāyogaṃ pakṣā racayitavyāḥ /
na vāyurutpadyate chāndogānāmutpattiprakaraṇe 'nāmnānādityekaḥ pakṣaḥ /
asti tu taittirīyāṇāmutpattiprakaraṇa āmnānam 'ākāśādvāyuḥ' (tai. 2.1) iti pakṣāntaram /
tataśca śrutyorvipratiṣedhe sati gauṇī vāyorutpattiśrutisaṃbhavādityaparo 'bhiprāyaḥ /
asaṃbhavaśca 'saiṣānastamitā devatā yadvāyuḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.22) ityastamayapratiṣedhāt, amṛtatvādiśravaṇācca /
children.translated_text: And the impossibility [is argued from]: 'This is the deity that does not set — namely, air' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.22) — because of the denial of setting, and because of the teaching of immortality and the like.

children.text: pratijñānuparodhādyāvadvikāraṃ ca vibhāgābhyupagamādutpadyate vāyuriti siddhāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the established conclusion is that air is produced — because of the non-obstruction of the thesis [that everything other than <s>Brahman</s> is an effect], and because of the acceptance of differentiation to the extent of modification.

children.text: astamayapratiṣedho 'paravidyāviṣaya āpekṣikaḥ /
children.translated_text: The denial of setting pertains to the sphere of lower knowledge (<s>aparavidyā</s>) and is relative —

children.text: agnyādīnāmiva vāyorastamayābhāvāt //
children.translated_text: because air, like fire and the like, does not [permanently] set.

This is an extension. By this explanation of space, <s>Mātariśvan</s> too — air, which has space as its substratum — is explained. Here too, the positions should be formulated as appropriate. One position: air is not produced — because it is not mentioned in the creation-context of the <s>Chāndogyas</s>. The alternative: but it is [produced] — because it is mentioned in the creation-context of the <s>Taittirīyakas</s>: 'From space, air' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1). And when there is contradiction between the <s>śrutis</s>, there is another view that the creation-<s>śruti</s> regarding air is figurative, because of impossibility.

children.text: kṛtapratividhānaṃ cāmṛtatvādiśravaṇam /
children.translated_text: And the teaching of immortality and the like has already been addressed.

children.text: nanu vāyorākāśasya ca tulyayorutpattiprakaraṇe śravaṇāśravaṇayorekamevādhikaraṇamubhayaviṣayamastu kimatideśenāsati viśeṣa iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since space and air are equal in having both hearing and non-hearing [of their creation] in respective creation-contexts, let there be a single topic covering both — why an extension when there is no difference?

children.text: ucyate- satyamevametat /
children.translated_text: It is said: True, this is so.

children.text: tathāpi mandadhiyāṃ śabdamātrakṛtāśaṅkānivṛttyartho 'yamatideśaḥ kriyate /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, this extension is made for the purpose of removing the doubt of those of dull intellect, caused merely by the [different] words.

children.text: saṃvargavidyādiṣu hyupāsyatayā vāyormahābhāgatvaśravaṇāt, astamayapratiṣedhādibhyaśca bhavati nityatvāśaṅkā kasyaciditi // 8 //
children.translated_text: For because air's great glory is heard as something to be meditated upon in the <s>Saṃvarga-vidyā</s> and the like, and because of the denial of its setting, the doubt of its eternality may arise for some. // 8 //

children.text: 3 asaṃbhavādhikaraṇam / sū. 9
children.translated_text: Section 3: <s>Asaṃbhavādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 9

children.text: asaṃbhavas tu sato 'nupapatteḥ | BBs_2,3.9 |
children.translated_text: <s>Asaṃbhavas tu sato 'nupapatteḥ</s> — But the impossibility [of origination is established] for Being (<s>sat</s>, i.e., <s>Brahman</s>), because of the illogicality [of its origination]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.9 |

children.text:
viyatpavanayorasaṃbhāvyamānajanmanorapyutpattimupaśrutya brahmaṇo 'pi bhavetkutaścidutpattiriti syātkasyacinmatiḥ /
tathā vikārebhya evākāśādibhya uttareṣāṃ vikārāṇāmutpattimupaśrutyākāśasyāpi vikārādeva brahmaṇa utpattiriti kaścinmanyeta /
tāmāśaṅkāmapanetumidaṃ sūtram- 'asaṃbhavastu' iti /
na khalu brahmaṇaḥ sadātmakasya kutaścidanyataḥ saṃbhava utpattirāśaṅkitavyā /
kasmāt /
anupapatteḥ /
sanmātraṃ hi brahma /
na tasya sanmātrādevotpattiḥ saṃbhavati, asatyatiśaye prakṛtivikārabhāvānupapatteḥ /
nāpi sadviśeṣāddṛṣṭaviparyayāt /
sāmānyāddhi viśeṣā utpadyamānā dṛśyante mṛdāderghaṭādayo natu viśeṣebhyaḥ sāmānyam /
nāpyasato nirātmakatvāt /
'kathamasataḥ sajjāyeta' (chā. 8.7.1) iti cākṣepaśravaṇāt /
'sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇādhipādhipo na cāsya kaścijjanitā na cādhipaḥ' (śve. 6.9) iti ca brahmaṇo janayitāraṃ vārayati /
children.translated_text: 'He is the cause, the lord of the lords of the instruments; He has no progenitor, nor any lord' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.9) — [this <s>śruti</s>] also bars any progenitor of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: vivatvapavanayoḥ punarutpattiḥ pradarśitā natu brahmaṇaḥ sāstīti vaiṣamyam /
children.translated_text: The origination of space and air has been demonstrated — but no such [origination] of <s>Brahman</s> exists. This is the distinction.

children.text: naca vikārebhyo vikārāntarotpattidarśanādbrahmaṇo 'pi vikāratvaṃ bhavitumarhatīti mūlaprakṛtyanabhyupagame 'navastāprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: And from the observation that modifications originate from other modifications, it would not follow that <s>Brahman</s> too is a modification — because if a root material cause (<s>mūlaprakṛti</s>) were not accepted, there would be the consequence of infinite regress.

children.text: yā mūlaprakṛtirabhyupagamyate tadeva ca no brahmetyavirodhaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: And the root material cause that is accepted — that itself is our <s>Brahman</s>. Thus there is no contradiction. // 9 //

Having heard of the origination even of space and air — whose origination seemed unimaginable — someone might think: perhaps <s>Brahman</s> too has an origination from something. Likewise, having heard that later modifications arise from earlier modifications — from space and the like — someone might think that space too is a modification, and that <s>Brahman</s> originates from a modification. To remove this doubt, this <s>sūtra</s> [is given]: 'But the impossibility [of origination is established] for Being.' The origination of <s>Brahman</s> — which is of the nature of Being (<s>sat</s>) — from anything else should certainly not be suspected. Why? Because of the illogicality. For <s>Brahman</s> is mere Being. Its origination from mere Being itself is not possible — because in the absence of a gradation, the relation of material cause and modification is untenable. Nor from a particular being, because the contrary is observed. For particulars are seen to originate from the universal — pots and such from clay — but not a universal from particulars. Nor from non-being — because of its utter lack of nature. And because the <s>śruti</s> rejects [this]: 'How could being arise from non-being?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.2).

children.text: 4 tejo 'dhikaraṇam / sū. 10
children.translated_text: Section 4: <s>Tejoadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 10

children.text: tejo 'tas tathā hy āha | BBs_2,3.10 |
children.translated_text: <s>Tejo 'tas tathā hy āha</s> — Fire [is born] from that [<s>Brahman</s>]; for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] says. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.10 |

children.text:
chāndogye sanmūlatvaṃ tejasaḥ śrāvitaṃ, taittirīyake tu vāyumūlatvaṃ, tatra tejoyoniṃ prati śrutivipratipattau satyāṃ prāptaṃ tāvadbrahmayonikaṃ teja iti /
kutaḥ /
'sadeva' ityupakramya 'tattejo 'sṛjata' ityupadeśāt /
sarvavijñānapratijñāyāśca brahmaprabhavatve sarvasya saṃbhavāt /
'tajjalān' (chā. 8.7.1) iti cāviśeṣaśruteḥ 'etasmājjāyate prāṇaḥ' (muṇḍa. 2.1.3) iti copakramya śrutyantare sarvasyāviśeṣeṇa brahmajatvopadeśāt /
taittirīyake ca 'sa tapastaptvā /
idaṃ sarvamasṛjata /
yadidaṃ kiñca' (tai. 3.6.1) ityaviśeṣaśravaṇāt /
tasmāt 'vāyoragniḥ' iti kramopadeśo draṣṭavyo vāyoranantaramagniḥ saṃbhūta iti /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate- tejo 'to mātariśvano jāyata iti /
kasmāt /
tathāhyāha- 'vāyoragniḥ' iti /
avyavahite hi tejaso brahmajatve satyasati vāyujatve vāyoragniritīyaṃ śrutiḥ kadarthitā syāt /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, fire is taught as having Being (<s>Sat</s>) as its root, but in the <s>Taittirīya</s>, it is taught as having air as its root. When there is thus a conflict between <s>śrutis</s> regarding the source of fire, the initial position is: fire has <s>Brahman</s> as its source. Why? Because having commenced with 'Being alone' [the <s>Chāndogya</s>] teaches 'That created fire.' And because the promise of the knowledge of everything [through one thing] is fulfilled if everything originates from <s>Brahman</s>. And because of the unqualified <s>śruti</s> '<s>tajjalān</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1), and because, having commenced with 'From this are born <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.3), another <s>śruti</s> teaches the origination of everything from <s>Brahman</s> without distinction. And in the <s>Taittirīya</s> too, because of the unqualified hearing: 'Having performed <s>tapas</s>, He created all this — whatever there is' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.6.1). Therefore, the sequential teaching 'From air, fire' should be understood [merely] as indicating that fire arose next after air, [not necessarily from air]. This being the position reached, it is said: fire is born from <s>Mātariśvan</s> (air). Why? Because thus [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'From air, fire.' For if fire had been produced directly from <s>Brahman</s> — without having been produced from air — then this <s>śruti</s> 'From air, fire' would be contradicted.

children.text: nanu kramārthaiṣā bhaviṣyatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: But this [statement] will be merely for indicating sequence — so it has been said.

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ - 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (tai. 2.1.1) iti purastātsaṃbhavatyapādānasyātmanaḥ pañcamīnirdeśātsa, tasyaiva ca saṃbhavaterihādhikārāt, parastādapi ca tadadhikāre 'pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ' (tai. 2.1.1) ityapādānapañcamīdarśanādvāyoragnirityapādānapañcamyevaiṣeti gamyate /
apica vāyorūrdhvamagniḥ saṃbhūta iti kalpya upapadārthayogaḥ kḷptastu kārakārthayogo vāyoragni saṃbhūta iti /
tasmādeṣā śrutirvāyuyonitvaṃ tejaso 'vagamayati /
children.translated_text: No, we say — because in the preceding [passage] 'From this very Self, space arose' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1), the fifth (ablative) case is used for the Self as the source, and because the same topic of origination (<s>saṃbhūti</s>) applies here, and because further on too, within the same topic, the ablative indicating source is seen — 'From earth, herbs' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1) — therefore 'From air, fire' is understood as an ablative of source. Moreover, the interpretation 'Fire arose after air' would require a forced construal, whereas the established grammatical meaning 'Fire arose from air' requires no force. Therefore, this <s>śruti</s> conveys that fire has air as its source.

children.text: nanvitarāpi śrutirbrahmayonitvaṃ tejaso 'vagamayati 'tattejo 'sṛjata' iti /
children.translated_text: But does not the other <s>śruti</s> too convey that fire has <s>Brahman</s> as its source — 'That created fire'?

children.text:
na /
tasyāḥ pāramparyajatve 'pyavirodāt /
yadāpi hyākāśaṃ vāyuṃ ca sṛṣṭvā vāyubhāvāpannaṃ brahma tejo 'sṛjateti kalpyate, tadāpi brahmajatvaṃ tejaso na virudhyate /
yathā tasyāḥ śrutaṃ tasyā dadhi tasyā āmikṣetyādi /
darśayati ca brahmaṇo vikārātmanāvastānaṃ 'tadātmānaṃ svayamakuruta' (tai. 2.7.1) iti /
tathāceśvarasmaraṇaṃ bhavati- 'buddirjñānamasaṃmohaḥ' (bha.gī. 10.4) ityādyanukramya 'bhavati bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ' (bha.gī. 10.5) iti /
yadyapi buddhyādayaḥ svakāraṇebhyaḥ pratyakṣaṃ bhavanto dṛśyante tathāpi sarvasya bhāvajātasya sākṣātpraṇāḍyā veśvaravaṃśyatvāt /
etenākramavatsṛṣṭivādinyaḥ śrutayo vyākhyātāḥ /
children.translated_text: by this, the <s>śruti</s> passages that teach creation without [specifying] sequence are also explained.

children.text: tāsāṃ sarvathopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because those [non-sequential passages] are compatible in every way [with sequential creation].

children.text: kramavatsṛṣṭivādinīnāṃ tvanyathānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: But those <s>śrutis</s> that teach creation with sequence cannot be interpreted otherwise.

children.text: pratijñāpi sadvaṃśyatvamātramapekṣate nāvyavahitajanyatvamityavirodhaḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: And even the promise [of knowing everything through one thing] requires only descent from Being (<s>sat</s>), not immediate origination [from <s>Brahman</s>] — hence there is no contradiction. // 10 //

No. Because that [<s>Chāndogya</s> statement] is compatible even with mediate origination. For even when it is construed that <s>Brahman</s>, having created space and air and having assumed the state of air, created fire — even then, the origination of fire from <s>Brahman</s> is not contradicted. Just as [in the expression] 'her heated [milk], her curds, her <s>āmikṣā</s>' and such [— the cow is the ultimate source even of curds]. And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows <s>Brahman</s>'s abiding in the form of modifications: 'It made itself by itself' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7.1). And thus there is also the <s>Smṛti</s> of the Lord — having enumerated 'Intelligence, knowledge, non-delusion' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 10.4) and such, [it says]: 'The diverse states of beings arise from Me alone' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 10.5). For even though intellect and such are seen to arise directly from their own [immediate] causes, since all classes of beings are ultimately of the Lord's lineage through succession,

children.text: FN: kadarthitā pīḍitā bādhiteti yāvat /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Kadarthitā</s>' means violated, contradicted — this is the meaning.

children.text: tadadhikāre saṃbhūtyadhikāre /
children.translated_text: 'In that topic' — in the topic of origination.

children.text:
tasyā dhenoḥ śrutaṃ taptaṃ kṣīraṃ sākṣātkāryaṃ, dadhyādikaṃ tu pāramparyajamityarthaḥ /
dadhisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ kaṭhinakṣīramāmikṣā /
children.translated_text: 'Her heated [milk]' — the heated milk of that cow is the direct product; curds and such are mediate products — this is the meaning. '<s>Āmikṣā</s>' is hardened milk mixed with curds.

children.text: praṇāḍyā paramparayā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Praṇāḍyā</s>' means 'through succession.'

children.text: 5 abadhikaraṇam / sū. 11
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Ab-Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Water) / <s>Sūtra</s> 11

children.text: āpaḥ | BBs_2,3.11 |
children.translated_text: Water. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.11 |

children.text: 'atastathāhyāha' ityanuvartate /
āpo 'tastejaso jāyante /
children.translated_text: Water [arises] from fire for the same reason.

children.text: kasmāt /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: tathāhyāha- 'tadapo 'sṛjata' iti 'agnerāpaḥ' iti ca vacane nāsti saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because thus [the <s>śruti</s>] says — 'That created water' and 'From fire, water' — there is no doubt about these statements.

children.text: tejasastu sṛṣṭiṃ vyākhyāya pṛthivyā vyākhyāsyannapo 'ntariyāmityāpa iti sūtrayāṃbabhūva // 11 //
children.translated_text: But having explained the creation of fire and being about to explain [the creation of] earth, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] composed the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>āpaḥ</s>' (water) [to show that] water [is created] in between. // 11 //
'From that; for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] says' — this continues [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>].

children.text: 6 pṛthivyadhikārādhikaraṇam / sū. 12
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Pṛthivyadhikāra Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Earth) / <s>Sūtra</s> 12

children.text: pṛthivy adhikārarūpaśabdāntarebhyaḥ | BBs_2,3.12 |
children.translated_text: Earth — because of the context, form, and other scriptural statements. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.12 |

children.text:
'tā āpa aikṣanta bahvayaḥ syāma prajāyemahīti tā annamasṛjanta' (chā. 6.2.4) iti śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimanenānnaśabdena vrīhiyavādyabhyavahāryai caudanādyucyate kiṃ vā pṛthivīti /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvadvrīhiyavādyodanādi vā parigrahītavyamiti /
tatra hyannaśabdaḥ prasiddho loke vākyaśeṣo 'pyetamarthamupodvalayati /
'tasmādyatra kvaca varṣati tadeva bhūyiṣṭamannaṃ bhavatīti' /
vrīhiyavādyeva hi sati varṣaṇe bahu bhavati na pṛthivīti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ pṛthivyeveyamannaśabdenādbhyo jāyamānā vivakṣyata iti /
kasmāt /
adhikārādrūpācchabdāntarācca /
adhikārastāvat- 'tattejo 'sṛjata' 'tadapo 'sṛjata' iti mahābhūtaviṣayo vartate /
tatra kramaprāptāṃ pṛthivīṃ mahābhūtaṃ vilaṅghya nākasmādvrīhyādiparigraho nyāyyaḥ /
tathā rūpamapi vākyaśeṣe pṛthivyanuguṇaṃ dṛśyate 'yatkṛṣṇaṃ tadannasya' iti /
nahyodanāderabhyavahāryasya kṛṣṇatvaniyamo 'sti /
nāpi vrīhyādīnām /
children.translated_text: It is heard: 'Those waters willed: "May we be many; may we be born." They created food (<s>anna</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.4). Therein, the doubt arises: does this word '<s>anna</s>' (food) refer to consumable things like rice, barley, cooked rice, and such, or to earth? The initial position is: rice, barley, cooked rice, and such should be understood. For the word '<s>anna</s>' is well known in the world [as referring to food], and the remainder of the passage also supports this meaning: 'Therefore, wherever it rains, food becomes most abundant.' For it is rice, barley, and such that become abundant when it rains, not earth. This being the position reached, we say: it is earth itself that is intended by the word '<s>anna</s>' as being born from water. Why? Because of the context, form, and other scriptural statements. As for the context — [the passage] 'That created fire,' 'That created water' deals with the great elements. Therein, skipping over earth, which is the next great element in sequence, and arbitrarily selecting rice and such would not be justified. And as for form — in the remainder of the passage, a form consistent with earth is seen: 'What is black — that is of food.' For there is no rule that cooked rice and such consumables are black, nor that rice and such [grains are black].

children.text: nanu pṛthivyā api naiva kṛṣṇatvaniyamo 'sti payaḥpāṇḍurasyāṅgārarohitasya ca kṣetrasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: But even earth does not have a rule of being black — since fields are seen to be white like milk or red like embers.

children.text:
nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
bāhulyāpekṣatvāt /
bhūyiṣṭhaṃ hi pṛthivyāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rūpaṃ na tathā śvetarohite /
paurāṇikā api pṛthivīcchāyāṃ śarvarīmupadiśanti /
sā ca kṛṣṇābhāsetyataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rūpaṃ pṛthivyā iti śliṣyate /
śrutyantaramapi samānādhikāramadbhyaḥ pṛthivīti bhavati /
'tadyadapāṃ śara āsīttatsamahanyata sā pṛthivyabhavat' (bṛ. 1.2.2) iti ca /
pṛthivyāstu vrīhyāderutpattiṃ darśayati- 'pṛthivyā oṣadhaya oṣadhībhyo 'nnam' iti ca /
evamadhikārādiṣu pṛthivyāḥ pratipādakeṣu satsu kuto vrīhyādipratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the context and such establish earth, whence the understanding of rice and such?

children.text: prasiddhirapyadhikārādibhireva bādhyate /
children.translated_text: Even the common usage [of the word <s>anna</s> as food] is overridden by the context and such.

children.text: vākyaśeṣo 'pi pārthivatvādannādyasya taddvāreṇa pṛthivyā evādbhyaḥ prabhavatvaṃ sūcayatīti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: And the remainder of the passage too should be understood as indicating — because food and such are of earthy nature — the origination of earth itself from water, through the medium [of food].

children.text: tasmātpṛthivīyamannaśabdeti // 12 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this [word] '<s>anna</s>' means earth. // 12 //

This is not a fault. Because [the rule applies] with reference to the majority. For predominantly the form of earth is black, not so the white and red. The <s>Purāṇic</s> writers also teach that the shadow of the earth is night. And that [shadow] has a black appearance — therefore 'the form of earth is black' is consistent. Another <s>śruti</s> also has the same reference — water and earth [in sequence]: 'The solid essence of the waters was consolidated; that became earth' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.2.2). But the origination of rice and such from earth is shown [in a later passage]: 'From earth, herbs; from herbs, food.'

children.text: FN: tattatra sṛṣṭikāle yadapāṃ śaraḥmaṇḍavadghanībhāva āsītsa eva samahanyata kaṭhinaḥ saṃghāto 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'That' — at the time of creation, the solid essence (<s>śara</s>) of the waters, i.e., the solidified state [of waters], was consolidated, i.e., became a hard mass.

children.text: 7 tadabhidhyānādhikaraṇam / sū. 13
children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Tadabhidhyāna Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of His Meditation) / <s>Sūtra</s> 13

children.text: tadabhidhyānād eva tu talliṅgāt saḥ | BBs_2,3.13 |
children.translated_text: Because of His meditation alone, because of the marks [pointing to] Him, He [is the creator]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.13 |

children.text:
kimimāni viyadādīni bhūtāni svayameva svavikārānsṛjantyāhosvatparameśvara eva tena tenātmanāvatiṣṭhamāno 'bhidhyāyaṃstaṃ taṃ vikāraṃ sṛjatīti saṃdehe sati prāptaṃ tāvatsvayameva sṛjantīti /
kutaḥ /
'ākāśādvāyurvāyoragniḥ' ityādisvātantryaśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Do these elements — space and such — create their own modifications by themselves, or does the Supreme Lord Himself, abiding in the form of each [element], create each modification through meditation? When this doubt arises, the initial position is: they create by themselves. Why? Because of the hearing of their independence: 'From space, air; from air, fire' and such.

children.text: nanvacetanānāṃ svatantrāṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ pratiṣiddhā /
children.translated_text: But the activity of insentient things acting independently has been refuted.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
'tatteja aikṣata tā āpa aikṣanta' (chā. 6.2.4) iti ca bhūtānāmapi cetanatvaśravaṇāditi /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- sa eva parameśvarastena tenātmanāvatiṣṭhamāno 'bhidhyāyaṃstaṃ taṃ vikāraṃ sṛjatīti /
kutaḥ /
talliṅgāt /
tathāhi śāstram- 'yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīmantaro yamayati' (bṛ. 3.7.3) ityevañjātīyakaṃ sādhyakṣāṇameva bhūtānāṃ pravṛttiṃ darśayati /
tathā so 'kāmayata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya iti prastutya 'sacca tyaccābhavat /
tadātmānaṃ svayamakuruta' (tai. 2.6.1) iti ca tasyaiva ca sarvātmabhāvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault — because sentience is heard even of the elements: 'That fire willed; those waters willed' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.4). This being the position reached, it is stated: it is the Supreme Lord Himself who, abiding in the form of each [element], creates each modification through meditation. Why? Because of the marks [pointing to] Him. For thus scripture — 'He who, standing in the earth, is interior to the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who controls the earth from within' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.3) — such passages show that the activity of elements is superintended [by the Lord]. And having introduced 'He desired: "May I become many; may I be born"' — [the text] shows: 'He became the existent and the beyond; He made Himself by Himself' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6.1) — and shows His being the Self of all.

children.text: yattvīkṣaṇaśravaṇamaptejasostatparameśvarāveśavaśādeva draṣṭavyam 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' (bṛ. 3.7.23) itīkṣitrantarapratiṣedhāt, prakṛtatvācca sata īkṣituḥ 'tadaikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya' ityatra // 13 //
children.translated_text: And the hearing of willing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) on the part of water and fire should be understood as due to the presence of the Supreme Lord within them — because the negation of another seer [is stated]: 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23), and because the topic is the seer who is Being (<s>Sat</s>): 'That willed: "May I become many; may I be born"' [in the <s>Chāndogya</s>]. // 13 //

children.text: FN: parameśvarasyāntaryāmibhāvenāveśaḥ saṃbandhastadvaśādbhūteṣvīkṣaṇaṃ śravaṇaṃ naitāvatā teṣāṃ cetanatvaṃ svātantryaṃ vetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The presence of the Supreme Lord as the inner controller — that is the connection; because of that, the willing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) in the elements is heard. This does not make them sentient or independent — this is the meaning.

children.text: 8 viparyayādhikaraṇam / sū. 14
children.translated_text: 8. The <s>Viparyaya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Reverse Order) / <s>Sūtra</s> 14

children.text: viparyayeṇa tu kramo 'ta upapadyate ca | BBs_2,3.14 |
children.translated_text: But the order [of dissolution] is the reverse; from that [it follows], and it is justified. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.14 |

children.text:
bhūtānāmutpattikramaścintitaḥ /
athedānīmapyayakramaścintyate /
kimaniyatena krameṇāpyaya utpattikrameṇāthavā tadviparīteneti /
trayo 'pi cotpattisthitipralayā bhūtānāṃ brahmāyattāḥ śrūyante- 'yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante /
yena jātāni jīvanti yatprayantyabhisaṃviśanti' (tai. 3.1.1) iti /
tatrāniyamo 'viśeṣāditi prāptam /
athavotpatteḥ kramasya śrutatvāpralayasyāpi kramākāṅkṣiṇaḥ sa eva kramaḥ syāditi /
evaṃ prāptaṃ tato brūmaḥ viparyayeṇa tu pralayakramo 'ta utpattikramādbhavitumarhati /
tathāhi loke dṛśyate yena krameṇa sopānamārūḍhastato viparītena krameṇāvarohatīti /
apica dṛśyate mṛdo jātaṃ ghaṭaśarāvādyapyayakāle mṛdbhāvamapyetyadbhyaśca jātaṃ himakarakādyabbhāvamapyetīti /
ataścopapadyata etat /
yadpṛthivyadbhyo jātā satī sthitikālavyatikrāntāvapo 'pīyādāpaśca tejaso jātāḥ satyastejo 'pīyuḥ /
evaṃ krameṇa sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmataraṃ cānantaramanantaraṃ kāraṇamapītya sarvaṃ kāryajātaṃ paramakāraṇaṃ paramasūkṣmaṃ ca brahmāpyetīti veditavyam /
nahi svakāraṇavyatikrameṇa kāraṇakāraṇe kāryāpyayo nyāyyaḥ /
smṛtāvapyutpattikramaviparyayeṇaivāpyayakramastatra tatra darśitaḥ - 'jagatpratiṣṭhā devarṣe pṛthivyapsu pralīyate /
jyotiṣyāpaḥ pralīyante jyotirvāyau pralīyate' ityevamādau /
utpattikramastūtpattāveva śrutatvānnāpyaye bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: But the order of creation, having been heard only in the context of creation, should not apply to dissolution.

children.text: nacāsāvayogyatvādapyayenākāṅkṣyate /
children.translated_text: Nor does [the order of creation] demand [application to] dissolution, since it is unsuitable for it.

children.text: nahi kārye dhriyamāṇe kāraṇasyāpyayo yuktaḥ kāraṇāpyaye kāryasyāvasthānānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: For it is not justified that the cause should dissolve while the effect persists — because if the cause dissolves, the effect cannot subsist.

children.text: kāryāpyaye tu kāraṇasyāvasthānaṃ yuktaṃ mṛdādiṣvevaṃ dṛṣṭatvāt // 14 //
children.translated_text: But the subsistence of the cause when the effect dissolves is justified — because this is seen [to be the case] with clay and such. // 14 //

The order of creation of the elements has been considered. Now the order of dissolution (<s>apyaya</s>) is considered. Is the dissolution in an unregulated order, in the order of creation, or in the reverse order? And creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the elements are all heard as dependent on <s>Brahman</s>: 'That from which these beings are born, that by which, when born, they live, that into which, departing, they enter' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.1.1). Therein, the initial position is: there is no regulation, because of the absence of a specific [scriptural statement]. Or alternatively, since the order of creation is heard, the order of dissolution too — which requires a [definite] order — would be the same. This being the position reached, we say: but the order of dissolution should be the reverse of the order of creation. For thus it is seen in the world that one who has climbed stairs descends in the reverse order. Moreover, it is seen that a pot, dish, and such, produced from clay, return to the state of clay at the time of dissolution; and ice, hail, and such, produced from water, return to the state of water. Therefore, this too is justified — that earth, having been produced from water, at the end of its period of stability, returns to water; and water, having been produced from fire, returns to fire. Thus, [each effect], returning step by step to its next subtler and subtler immediate cause, the entire class of effects should be understood as returning to the supreme cause, which is the most subtle — <s>Brahman</s>. For it is not justified that an effect should return to the cause of its cause, bypassing its own [immediate] cause. In <s>Smṛti</s> too, the order of dissolution is shown in various places as the reverse of the order of creation: 'The support of the world, O divine sage — earth dissolves into water; water dissolves into fire; fire dissolves into air' — and so on.

children.text: FN: krameṇa paramparayā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Krameṇa</s>' means 'by succession.'

children.text: 9 antarāvijñānādhikaraṇam / sū. 15
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Antarāvijñāna Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Intervening [Creation of] Consciousness and Mind) / <s>Sūtra</s> 15

children.text: antarā vijñānamanasī krameṇa talliṅgād iti cen nāviśeṣāt | BBs_2,3.15 |
children.translated_text: If [it is said that] consciousness and mind [are created] in between, in sequence, because of marks [indicating] that — no, because of the absence of distinction. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.15 |

children.text:
bhūtānāmutpattipralayāvanulomapratilomakramābhyāṃ bhavata ityuktam /
ātmādirutpattiḥ pralayaścātmānta ityapyuktam /
sendriyasya tu manaso buddheśca sadbhāvaḥ prasiddhaḥ śrutismṛtyoḥ /
'buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca /
indriyāṇi hayānāhuḥ' (kaṭha. 3.3) ityādiliṅgebhyaḥ /
tayorapi kasmiścidantarāle krameṇotpattipralayāvupasaṃgrāhyau, sarvasya vastujātasya brahmajatvābhyupagamāt /
apicātharvaṇa utpattiprakaraṇe bhūtānāmātmanaścāntarāle karaṇānyanukramyante /
'etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca /
khaṃ vāyurjyotirāpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī' (muṇaḍa. 2.1.3) iti /
tasmātpūrvoktotpattipralayakramabhaṅgaprasaṅgo bhūtānāmiti cet /
children.translated_text: It was stated that the origination and dissolution of the elements follow the direct and reverse orders. It was also stated that origination begins with the Self and dissolution ends with the Self. But the existence of the mind — together with its sense organs — and of the intellect is well known from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, from indicatory marks such as 'Know the intellect to be the charioteer, and the mind to be the reins; they call the senses the horses' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.3) and the like. Their origination and dissolution too must be included in some intermediate [position in the sequence] — because it is accepted that the entire class of entities originates from <s>Brahman</s>. Moreover, in the <s>Atharva</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>], in the creation-context, the sense organs are enumerated between the elements and the Self: 'From Him are born <s>Prāṇa</s>, mind, and all the sense organs, as well as space, air, fire, water, and earth — the support of all' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.3). Therefore, [one might argue,] there would be the consequence of disrupting the previously stated order of creation and dissolution of the elements.

children.text:
na /
aviśeṣāt /
yadi tāvadbhautikāni karaṇāni tato bhūtotpattipralayābhyāmevaiṣāmutpattipralayau bhavata iti naitayoḥ kramāntaraṃ mṛgyam /
bhavati ca bhautikatve liṅgaṃ karaṇānām /
'annamayaṃ hi somya mana oṣadhayaḥ prāṇastejomayī vāk' (chā. 6.5.4) ityevajātīyakam /
vyapadeśo 'pi kvacidbhūtānāṃ karaṇānāṃ ca brāhmaṇaparivrājakanyāyena netavyaḥ /
atha tvabhautikāni karaṇāni tathāpi bhūtotpattikramo na karaṇairviśeṣyate prathamaṃ karaṇānyutpadyante caramaṃ bhūtāni prathamaṃ vā bhūtānyutpadyante caramaṃ vā karaṇānīti /
ātharvaṇe tu samāmnāyakramamātraṃ karaṇānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Atharva</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>], the enumeration of sense organs and elements is merely the order of recitation (<s>samāmnāyakrama</s>).

children.text: na tatrotpattikrama ucyate /
children.translated_text: It does not state the order of origination.

children.text: tathānyatrāpi pṛthageva bhūtakramātkaraṇakrama āmnāyate- 'prajāpatirvā idamagra āsītsa ātmānamaikṣata sa mano 'sṛjata tanmana evāsīttadātmānamaikṣata tadvācamasṛjata' ityādinā /
children.translated_text: Elsewhere too, the order of creation of the sense organs is taught separately from the order of the elements: '<s>Prajāpati</s> was this [universe] in the beginning. He reflected upon Himself. He created mind. That was mind indeed. He reflected upon Himself. He created speech' — and so on.

children.text: tasmānnāsti bhūtotpattikramasya bhaṅgaḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no disruption of the order of elemental creation. // 15 //

No. Because of the absence of any [real] distinction. If the sense organs are made of the elements (<s>bhautika</s>), then their origination and dissolution occur through the origination and dissolution of the elements themselves — so no separate order need be sought for them. And there is an indicatory mark for the elemental nature of the sense organs: 'For the mind, dear one, is made of food; <s>Prāṇa</s> is made of plants; speech is made of fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.5.4) — of such a kind. And even the [separate] designation of elements and sense organs in some places should be understood by the principle of '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>parivrājakas</s>' [i.e., the general term includes the specific]. But even if the sense organs are not made of elements, the order of elemental creation is not affected by the sense organs — [the question of] whether the sense organs are created first and the elements last, or the elements first and the sense organs last [does not disturb the elemental sequence].

children.text: FN: anyaparāḥ śabdā liṅgānītyucyante /
children.translated_text: Footnote: Words that convey another purpose are called indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text: idaṃ sthūlamutpatteḥ prāk prajāpatiḥ sūtrātmā āsīt /
children.translated_text: Prior to the creation of this gross [world], <s>Prajāpati</s> was the <s>Sūtrātman</s> (cosmic thread-self).

children.text: 10 carācaravyapāśrayādhikaraṇam / sū. 16
children.translated_text: 10. The <s>Carācaravyapāśraya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Dependence on Movable and Immovable Beings) / <s>Sūtra</s> 16

children.text: carācaravyapāśrayas tu syāt tadvyapadeśo bhāktas tadbhāvabhāvitvāt | BBs_2,3.16 |
children.translated_text: But [birth and death] depend on the movable and immovable [bodies]; the designation [of birth and death for the <s>jīva</s>] is figurative (<s>bhākta</s>), because [birth and death] exist only when those [bodies] exist. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.16 |

children.text:
sto jīvasyāpyutpattipralayau, jāto devadatto mṛto devadatta ityevajātīyakāllaukikavyapadeśāt jātakarmādisaṃskāravidhānācceti syātkasyacdbhrāntistāmapanudāmaḥ /
na jīvasyotpattipralayau staḥ, śāstraphalasaṃbandhopapatteḥ /
śarīrānuvināśini hi jīve śarīrāntakagateṣṭāniṣṭaprāptiparihārārthau vidhipratiṣedhāvanartakau syātām /
śrūyate ca- 'jīvāpetaṃ vāva kiledaṃ mriyate na jīvo mriyate' (chā. 6.11.3) iti /
children.translated_text: There may be a mistaken understanding in someone — that the <s>jīva</s> too has origination and dissolution, based on ordinary usage such as '<s>Devadatta</s> is born, <s>Devadatta</s> has died,' and from the prescription of sacraments such as the birth-rite (<s>jātakarma</s>) and the like. Let us dispel that. The <s>jīva</s> does not have origination and dissolution — because of the logical connection of the <s>jīva</s> with the fruits of [prescribed] actions. For if the <s>jīva</s> were to perish along with the body, injunctions and prohibitions — whose purpose is the attainment and avoidance of desirable and undesirable [results] in future embodiments — would be pointless. And <s>śruti</s> says: 'It is indeed this [body] that is deserted by the <s>jīva</s> that dies — the <s>jīva</s> does not die' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.11.3).

children.text: nanu laukiko janmamaraṇavyapadeśo jīvasya darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the ordinary designation of birth and death for the <s>jīva</s> was pointed out.

children.text:
satyaṃ darśitaḥ /
bhāktastveṣa jīvasya janmamaraṇavyapadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: True, it was pointed out. But this designation of birth and death for the <s>jīva</s> is figurative (<s>bhākta</s>).

children.text: kimāśrayaḥ punarayaṃ mukhyo yadapekṣayā bhākta iti /
children.translated_text: What then is the primary [referent] in dependence on which [the designation for the <s>jīva</s>] is figurative?

children.text:
ucyate- carācaravyapāśrayaḥ /
sthāvarajaṅgamaśarīraviṣayau janmamaraṇaśabdau /
sthāvarajaṅgamāni hi bhūtāni jāyante ca mriyante cātastadviṣayau janmamaraṇaśabdau mukhyau santau tatsthe jīvātmanyupacaryate, tadbhāvabhāvitvāt /
śarīraprādurbhāvatirobhāvayorhi satorjanmamaraṇaśabdau bhavato nāsatoḥ /
nahi śarīrasaṃbandhādanyatra jīvo jāto mṛto vā kenacillakṣyate /
'sa vā ayaṃ puruṣo jāyamānaḥ śarīramabhisaṃpadyamānaḥ sa utkrāman mriyamāṇaḥ (bṛ. 4.3.8) iti ca śarīrasaṃyogaviyoganimittāveva janmamaraṇaśabdau darśayati /
jātakarmādividhānamapi dehaprādurbhāvāpekṣameva draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: The prescription of sacraments such as the birth-rite (<s>jātakarma</s>) and the like should also be understood as having reference to the appearance of the body.

children.text: abhāvājjīvaprādurbhāvasya /
children.translated_text: Because there is no appearance of the <s>jīva</s> [as such].

children.text: jīvasya parasmādātmana utpattirviyadādīnāmivāsti nāsti vetyetaduttareṇa sūtreṇa vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Whether the <s>jīva</s> has an origination from the supreme Self — like space and the like — or does not, will be stated by the following <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: dehāśrayau tāvajjīvasya sthūlāvutpattipralayau na sta ityetadanena sūtreṇāvocat // 16 //
children.translated_text: By this <s>sūtra</s>, [the teacher] has stated that the gross origination and dissolution that depend on the body do not belong to the <s>jīva</s>. // 16 //

It is said: it depends on movable and immovable [bodies]. The words 'birth' and 'death' pertain to the bodies of stationary and mobile beings. For stationary and mobile beings are indeed born and die — therefore the words 'birth' and 'death,' being primarily applicable to those [bodies], are figuratively applied to the <s>jīva</s> that abides in them — because [birth and death of the <s>jīva</s>] exist only when those [bodies] exist. For the words 'birth' and 'death' apply when the appearance and disappearance of the body exist, not when they do not. For no one observes a <s>jīva</s> being born or dying apart from its connection with a body. And 'This person, being born — entering into a body; he, departing — dying' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.8) shows that the words 'birth' and 'death' are occasioned precisely by the conjunction and disjunction with the body.

children.text: FN: jīvāpetaṃ jīvena tyaktamidaṃ śarīram /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Jīvāpetam</s>' — 'deserted by the <s>jīva</s>' means this body [left] by the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: 11 ātmādhiraṇam / sū. 17
children.translated_text: 11. The <s>Ātma Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Self) / <s>Sūtra</s> 17

children.text: nātmā śruter nityatvāc ca tābhyaḥ | BBs_2,3.17 |
children.translated_text: The Self [does not originate], because of <s>śruti</s>, and because of eternality — from those [scriptural passages]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.17 |

children.text:
astyātmā jīvākhyaḥ śarīrendriyapañjarādhyakṣaḥ karmaphalasaṃbandhī /
sa kiṃ vyomādivadutpadyate brahmaṇa āhosvidbrahmavadeva notpadyata iti śrutivipratipatterviśayaḥ /
kāsucicchrutiṣvagnivisphuliṅgādinidarśanairjīvātmanaḥ parasmādbrahmaṇa utpattirāmnāyate, kāsucittvavikṛtasya parasya brahmaṇaḥ kāryapraveśena jīvabhāvo vijñāyate nacotpattirāmnāyata iti /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvadutpadyate jīva iti /
kutaḥ /
pratijñānuparodhādeva /
ekasminvidite sarvamidaṃ viditam itīyaṃ pratijñā sarvasya vastujātasya brahmaprabhavatve sati noparudhyeta /
tattvāntaratve tu jīvasya pratijñeyamuparudhyeta /
nacāvikṛtaḥ paramātmaiva jīva iti śakyate vijñātuṃ, lakṣaṇabhedāt /
apahṛtapāpmatvādidharmako hi paramātmā, tadviparīto hi jīvaḥ /
vibhāgāccāsya vikāratvasiddhiḥ /
yāvānhyākāśādiḥ pravibhaktaḥ sa sarvo vikārastasya cākāśāderutpattiḥ samadhigatā /
jīvātmāpi puṇyāpuṇyakarmā sukhaduḥkhayukpratiśarīraṃ pravibhakta iti tasyāpi prapañcotpattyavasara utpattirbhavitumarhati /
apica 'yathāgneḥ kṣudrā visphuliṅgā vyuccārantyevamevāsmādātmanaḥ sarve prāṇāḥ' (bṛ. 2.1.20) iti prāṇāderbhogyajātasya sṛṣṭiṃ śiṣṭvā 'sarva eva ātmano vyuccaranti' iti bhoktṛṇīmātmanāṃ pṛthaksṛṣṭiṃ śāsti /
'yathā sudīptātpāvakādvisphuliṅgāḥ sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ /
tathākṣarādvividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ prajāyante tatra caivāpiyanti' (muṇḍa. 2.1.1) iti ca jīvātmanāmutpattipralayāvucyete /
sarūpavacanāt,
children.translated_text: There exists a Self called the <s>jīva</s>, the presiding lord of the cage of body and senses, connected with the fruits of action. Does it originate from <s>Brahman</s> like space and the like, or does it not originate, like <s>Brahman</s> itself? — this is the subject of inquiry, because of conflicting <s>śruti</s> passages. In some <s>śrutis</s>, the origination of the <s>jīva</s> from the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is taught through illustrations such as sparks from fire. In others, it is understood that the unmodified supreme <s>Brahman</s> assumes the status of the <s>jīva</s> through entry into [its own] effects, and no origination is taught. Therein, the prima facie view is: the <s>jīva</s> does originate. Why? Precisely because of the non-violation of the promise. The promise 'by knowing one, all this is known' would not be violated only if the entire class of entities, including the <s>jīva</s>, originates from <s>Brahman</s>. But if the <s>jīva</s> were a different reality, this promise would be violated. Nor can it be understood that the unmodified supreme Self itself is the <s>jīva</s> — because of the difference in characteristics. For the supreme Self has properties such as freedom from evil and the like, while the <s>jīva</s> is the opposite. And from its differentiation, its status as a modification is established. For whatever is differentiated — like space and the rest — is a modification, and the origination of space and the like has been ascertained. The <s>jīva</s> too — having meritorious and demeritorious actions, endowed with pleasure and pain, differentiated in each body — should therefore have an origination at the time of cosmic manifestation. Moreover, [the <s>śruti</s>:] 'Just as tiny sparks fly forth from fire, so from this Self, all <s>prāṇas</s> [go forth]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.20) — having taught the creation of the class of enjoyable [objects] such as <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest, [the text] teaches a separate creation of the enjoyers — the selves — with 'all selves go forth.' And 'Just as from a blazing fire, sparks by the thousands fly forth, having the same form — so from the Imperishable, O dear one, diverse beings are born, and they return to it' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.1) — here too the origination and dissolution of the <s>jīvas</s> are stated. Because of the expression 'having the same form' (<s>sarūpa</s>),

children.text:
jīvātmāno hi paramātmanā sarūpā bhavanti caitanyayogāt /
naca kvacidaśravaṇamanyatra śrutaṃ vārayitumarhati /
śrutyantaragatasyāpyaviruddhasyādhikasyārthasya sarvatropasaṃhartavyatvāt /
praveśaśrutirapyevaṃ sati vikārabhāvāpattyaiva vyākhyātavyā, 'tadātmānaṃ svayamakuruta' ityādivat /
tasmādutpadyate jīva iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - nātmā jīva utpadyata iti /
kasmāt /
aśruteḥ /
nahyasyotpattiprakaraṇe śravaṇamasti bhūyaḥsu pradeśeṣu /
children.translated_text: for the <s>jīvas</s> have the same form as the supreme Self, due to their connection with consciousness. And the non-mention [of the <s>jīva</s>'s origination] in some [creation-contexts] cannot preclude what is mentioned in another — because a non-contradictory additional meaning found in another <s>śruti</s> must be incorporated everywhere. The 'entry' <s>śruti</s> too, this being the case, should be explained as resulting in the status of a modification — like 'He made Himself by Himself' and the like. Therefore, the <s>jīva</s> does originate. Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: the Self — the <s>jīva</s> — does not originate. Why? Because of <s>śruti</s>. For there is no hearing [of its origination] in the creation-contexts of most passages.

children.text: nanu kvacidaśravaṇamanyatra śrutaṃ na vārayitītyuktam /
children.translated_text: But was it not said that the non-mention in one place does not preclude what is mentioned elsewhere?

children.text:
satyamuktam /
utpattireva tvasya na saṃbhavatīti vadāmaḥ /
kasmāt /
nityatvācca tābhyaḥ /
caśabdādajatvādibhyaśca /
nityatvaṃ hyasya śrutibhyo 'vagamyate tathājatvamavikāritvamavikṛtasyaiva brahmaṇo jīvātmanāvasthānaṃ brahmātmanā ceti /
nacaivaṃrūpasyotpattirupapadyate /
tāḥ kāḥ śrutayaḥ /
'na jīvo mriyate' (chā. 6.11.3), 'sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma' (bṛ. 4.4.22), 'na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit' (kaṭhaṃ 2.18), 'ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇaḥ' (kaṭha. 2.18). 'tatsṛṣṭvā tadevānuprāviśat' (tai. 2.6.1), 'anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi' (chā. 6.3.2), 'sa eṣa iha praviṣṭa ā nakhāgrebhyaḥ' (bṛ. 1.4.7), 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' (bṛ. 1.4.19), 'ayamātmā brahma sarvānubhūḥ' (bṛ. 2.5.19) ityevamādyā nityatvavādinyaḥ satyo jīvasyotpattiṃ pratibadhnanti /
children.translated_text: True, that was said. But we say that its origination is simply not possible. Why? Because of eternality — from those [scriptural passages]. And by the word 'and' [in the <s>sūtra</s>], because of [its being] unborn and such. For its eternality is understood from the <s>śrutis</s>, and likewise its unborn nature, its immutability, and the fact that the unmodified <s>Brahman</s> itself abides as the <s>jīva</s>, and that [the <s>jīva</s>] has <s>Brahman</s> as its Self. And the origination of something of this nature is not tenable. What are those <s>śrutis</s>? 'The <s>jīva</s> does not die' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.11.3); 'This great unborn Self is un-aging, undying, immortal, fearless — <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22); 'The wise one is not born, nor does it die' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.18); 'Unborn, eternal, everlasting, this ancient one' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.18); 'Having created it, He Himself entered into it' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6.1); 'Having entered by means of this <s>jīva</s> Self, let Me differentiate names and forms' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2); 'This [<s>Brahman</s>] has entered here, up to the very fingertips' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.7); 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7); 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.19); 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>, the experiencer of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19) — such <s>śrutis</s>, which speak of eternality, preclude the origination of the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: nanu pravibhaktatvādvikāro vikāratvāccotpadyata ityuktam /
children.translated_text: But was it not stated that [the <s>jīva</s>] is a modification because of being differentiated, and originates because of being a modification?

children.text:
atrocyate- nāsya pravibhāgaḥ svato 'sti /
'eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā' (śve. 6.11) iti śruteḥ /
buddhyādyapādhinimittaṃ tvasya pravibhāgapratibhānamākāśasyeva ghaṭādisaṃbandhanimittam /
tathāca śāstram- 'sa vā ayamātmā brahma vijñānamayo manomayaḥ prāṇamayaścakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.5) ityevamādi brahmaṇa evāvikṛtasya sato 'pyekasyānekabuddhyādimayatvaṃ darśayati /
tanmayatvaṃ cāsya viviktasvarūpānabhivyaktyā taduparaktasvarūpatvaṃ strīmayo jālma ityādivaddraṣṭavyam /
yadapi kvacidasyotpattipralayaśravaṇaṃ tadapyata evopādhisaṃbandhānnetavyam /
upādhyutpattyāsyotpattistatpralayena ca pralaya iti /
tathāca darśayati- 'prajñānaghana evaitebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tānyevānu vinaśyati na pretya saṃjñāsti' (bṛ. 4.5.13) iti /
tathopādhipralaya evāyaṃ nātmavilaya ityetadapyatraiva 'mā bhagavānmohāntamāpīpadanna vā ahamimaṃ vijānāmi na pretya saṃjñāsti' iti praśnapūrvakaṃ pratipādayati- 'na vā are 'haṃ mohaṃ bravīmyavināśī vā are 'yamātmānucchittidharmā mātrāsaṃsargastvasya bhavati' (bṛ. 4.5.14) iti /
pratijñānuparodho 'pyavikṛtasyaiva brahmaṇo jīvabhāvābhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: And the non-violation of the promise [is maintained] precisely through accepting the <s>jīva</s>-status of the unmodified <s>Brahman</s> itself.

children.text: lakṣaṇabhedo 'pyanayorupādhinimitta eva /
children.translated_text: And the difference of characteristics between them [the supreme Self and the <s>jīva</s>] is caused by the limiting adjuncts alone.

children.text: 'ata ūrdhvaṃ vimokṣāyaiva brūhi' (bṛ. 4.3.15) iti ca prakṛtasyaiva vijñānamayasyātmanaḥ sarvasaṃsāradharmapratyākhyānena paramātmabhāvapratipādanāt /
children.translated_text: And because of the teaching that the very Self consisting of knowledge (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) that is the subject [of the passage] attains the status of the supreme Self through the negation of all properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> — [as in:] 'Henceforth, tell me only what conduces to liberation' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.15).

children.text: tasmānaivātmotpadyate pravilīyate ceti // 17 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the Self neither originates nor dissolves. // 17 //

To this it is replied: its differentiation does not belong to it intrinsically. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'The one God, hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.11). Rather, its appearance of differentiation is caused by the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) such as the intellect and the like — just as the [apparent] differentiation of space is caused by its connection with pots and such. And the scripture shows: 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>, made of knowledge, made of mind, made of <s>Prāṇa</s>, made of sight, made of hearing' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.5) — thus showing that <s>Brahman</s>, even though unmodified and one, has the status of being 'made of' multiple [faculties such as] intellect and the like. And its being 'made of' them should be understood as its nature being colored by them, through the non-manifestation of its own distinct nature — like 'besotted with women' (<s>strīmaya</s>) in the sense of being dominated by them. And where the origination and dissolution of the [<s>jīva</s>] are heard in some [passages], that too should be construed as referring to the connection with limiting adjuncts. Through the origination of the <s>upādhi</s>, its origination [is spoken of]; through the dissolution of the <s>upādhi</s>, its dissolution. And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows this: 'Being a mass of consciousness alone, having risen from these elements, it perishes along with them; there is no consciousness after death' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.13). And that this is merely the dissolution of the <s>upādhi</s>, not the destruction of the Self — this too is explained in the very same passage, preceded by a question: 'O revered sir, you have brought me to the utmost confusion — I do not understand this: there is no consciousness after death.' To which [<s>Yājñavalkya</s> replies]: 'I am not saying anything confusing. This Self is indeed indestructible, of undying nature. But it has contact with the sense-faculties (<s>mātrā</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.14).

children.text: FN: uparodho bādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Uparodha</s>' means contradiction.

children.text: sarūpaśabdo jīvavācīti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>sarūpa</s>' (same form) denotes the <s>jīva</s> — this is the completion [of the sentence].

children.text:
jālmaḥ kāmajaḍaḥ /
sa yathā strīparatantraḥ strīmayo vpadiśyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Jālma</s>' means one stupefied by desire. Just as such a person, being dependent on a woman, is called '<s>strīmaya</s>' (woman-absorbed).

children.text: etebhyo dehātmanā pariṇatebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ sāmyenotthāya janitvā tānyeva līyamānānyanu paścādvinaśyati /
children.translated_text: 'Having risen from these elements that have assumed the form of the body — having been born by becoming identical with them — it perishes following them, i.e., after they dissolve.'

children.text: mohaṃ mohakaraṃ vākyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Moha</s>' means a statement that causes confusion.

children.text: 12 jñādhikaraṇam / sū. 18
children.translated_text: 12. The <s>Jña Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Knower) / <s>Sūtra</s> 18

children.text: jño 'ta eva | BBs_2,3.18 |
children.translated_text: The knower (<s>jña</s>) — for this very reason. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.18 |

children.text:
sa kiṃ kaṇabhujānāmivāgantukacaitanyaḥ svato 'cetana āhosvitsāṃkhyānāmiva nityacaitanyasvarūpa eveti vādivipratipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
āgantukamātmanaścaitanyamātmamanaḥsaṃyogajamagnighaṭasaṃyogajaroh itādiguṇavaditi prāptam /
children.translated_text: Is [the Self] of the nature of adventitious consciousness — like [the Self] of the followers of <s>Kaṇabhuj</s> (<s>Kaṇāda</s> / <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>), being inherently insentient — or is it of the nature of eternal consciousness, like [the Self] of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>? — this is the doubt, because of the disagreement among theorists. What is the prima facie view? [The view is that] consciousness is adventitious to the Self, born from the conjunction of Self and mind — like the quality of redness born from the conjunction of fire and a pot.

children.text:
nityacaitanyatve hi suptamūrcchitagrahāviṣṭānāmapi cātanyaṃ syāt /
te pṛṣṭāḥ santo na kiñcidvayamacetayāmahīti jalpanti svasthāśca cetayamānā dṛśyante /
ataḥ kādācitkacaitanyatvādāgantukacaitanya ātmeti /
children.translated_text: For if consciousness were eternal, then even those who are asleep, fainted, or possessed by a spirit should have consciousness. And when questioned, they say 'We were not conscious of anything,' while when restored to normalcy, they are seen to be conscious. Therefore, since consciousness is occasional, the Self has adventitious consciousness.

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate- jño nityacaitanyo 'yamātmāta eva, yasmādeva notpadyate parameva brahmāvikṛtamupādhisaṃparkājjīvabhāvenāvatiṣṭhate /
parasya hi brahmaṇaścaitanyasvarūpatvamāmnātam- 'vijñānamānandaṃ brahma' (bṛ. 3.9.28), 'satyaṃ jñānamantaṃ brahma' (tai. 2.1.1), 'anantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva' (bṛ. 4.5.13), ityādiṣu śrutiṣu /
tadeva cetparaṃ brahma jīvastasmājjīvasyāpi nityacaitanyasvarūpatvamagnyauṣṇyaprakāśavaditi gamyate /
vijñānamayaprakriyāyāṃ ca śrutayo bhavanti- asuptaḥ 'suptānabhicākaśīti' (bṛ. 4.3.11) 'atrāyaṃ puruṣaḥ svayañjyotirbhavati' (bṛ. 4.3.9) iti, 'nahi vijñāturnirvijñāterviparilāpo vidyate' (bṛ. 4.3.30) ityevaṃrūpāḥ /
'atha yo vededaṃ jighrāṇīti sa ātmā' (chā. 8.12.4) iti ca sarvaiḥ karaṇadvārairidaṃ vededaṃ vedeti vijñānenānusaṃdhānāttadrūpatvasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having reached this conclusion [that the jīva is produced], [the siddhānta] is stated: This Self is a knower, of eternal consciousness — [it arises] from this very [Brahman]. For it is none other than the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — unmodified — that, through contact with limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), abides in the condition of the <s>jīva</s>. For the nature of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> as consciousness is taught [in śruti]: '<s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.28), '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1), 'Without an interior, without an exterior, entirely a mass of consciousness alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.13), and the like. If the <s>jīva</s> is indeed the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, then the <s>jīva</s> too is of the nature of eternal consciousness — like the heat and light of fire; this is understood. And in the discussion of the <s>vijñānamaya</s> (consciousness-constituted [Self]), there are <s>śrutis</s>: 'Itself unsleeping, it looks over the sleeping ones' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.11), 'Here this <s>Puruṣa</s> becomes self-luminous' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.9), 'For there is no cessation of the knowing of the knower' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.30) — of such a kind. And 'Now, he who knows "Let me smell this" — that is the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.4) — through the continuous tracking via consciousness, through all the gateways of the sense-organs, 'I know this, I know this' — the establishment of its [consciousness-]nature is achieved.

children.text: nityasvarūpacaitanyatve ghrāṇādyānarthakyamiti cet /
children.translated_text: Objection: If consciousness is the eternal nature [of the Self], the sense-organs like the nose and such would be purposeless.

children.text:
na /
gandhādiviṣayaviśeṣaparicchedārthatvāt /
tathāhi darśayati- 'gandhāya ghrāṇam' ityādi /
yattu suptādayo na cetayanta iti tasya śrutyaiva parihāro 'bhihitaḥ /
suṣuptaṃ prakṛtya 'yadvai tanna paśyati paśyanvai tanna paśyati- nahi draṣṭurddaṣṭerviparilopo vidyate 'vināśitvānna tu taddvitīyamasti tato 'nyadvibhaktaṃ yatpaśyet' (bṛ. 4.3.23) ityādinā /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- viṣayābhāvādiyamacetayamānatā na caitanyābhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: What is stated amounts to this: this absence of awareness [in sleep] is due to the absence of objects — not due to the absence of consciousness.

children.text: yathā viyadāśrayasya prakāśasya prakāśyabhāvādanabhivyaktirna svarūpābhāvāttadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as the non-manifestation of light that has space as its substratum is due to the absence of objects to be illuminated — not due to the absence of its own nature — so too.

children.text: vaiśeṣikāditarkaśca śrutivirodha ābhāsībhavati /
children.translated_text: And the reasoning of the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others, being in conflict with <s>śruti</s>, becomes a mere semblance.

children.text: tasmānnityacaitanyasvarūpa evātmeti niścinumaḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, we ascertain that the Self is of the nature of eternal consciousness alone. // 18 //

No. Because they serve the purpose of delimiting particular objects such as smell and the like. For thus [the śruti] shows: 'The nose is for smell' and so forth. As for the [objection] that those who are asleep and the like are not conscious — the resolution of that has already been stated by <s>śruti</s> itself. Having introduced deep sleep, [the śruti says:] 'That which one does not see [in sleep] — one does not see [then]; yet there is no cessation of the seeing of the seer — because of its imperishability. But there is no second thing, separate from it, that it could see' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.23) and so forth.

children.text: FN: svayamasupto bhāsamāna evātmā suptānvāgādīnuparavyāpārānabhicākaśīti abhipaśyati /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The Self, itself unsleeping and shining, looks over — that is, observes — the sleeping ones, [i.e.,] the speech and other [faculties] whose activities have ceased.

children.text: paricchedo vṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Pariccheda</s>' means a mental modification (<s>vṛtti</s>).

children.text: gandhāya tadgocarāntaḥkaraṇavṛttaye /
children.translated_text: 'For smell' — [means] for the mental modification (<s>antaḥkaraṇavṛtti</s>) whose object is that [smell].

children.text: 13 utkrāntigatyadhikaraṇam / sū. 19-32
children.translated_text: Section 13: <s>Utkrāntigatyādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 19-32

children.text: utkrāntigatyāgatīnām | BBs_2,3.19 |
children.translated_text: <s>Utkrāntigatyāgatīnām</s> — Because of [the śrutis teaching] departure, going, and returning. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.19 |

children.text:
idānīṃ tu kiṃparimāṇo jīva iti cintyate /
kimaṇuparimāṇa uta madhyamaparimāṇa āhosvinmahāparimāṇa iti /
children.translated_text: Now the question is considered: of what dimension is the <s>jīva</s>? Is it of atomic dimension, or of medium dimension, or of great dimension?

children.text:
nanu ca nātmotpadyate nityacaitanyaśyāyamityuktam /
ataśca para evātmā jīva ityāpatati /
parasyā cātmano 'nantaratvamāmnātaṃ, tatra kuto jīvasya parimāṇacintāvatāra iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it was said that the Self is not produced and is of eternal consciousness. And therefore it follows that the <s>jīva</s> is the supreme Self itself. And the supreme Self is taught as being without interior [or exterior]. In that case, where does the consideration of the dimension of the <s>jīva</s> come in?

children.text:
ucyate- satyametat /
utkrāntigatyāhagatiśravaṇāni tu jīvasya paricchedaṃ prāpayanti /
svaśabdena cāsya kvacidaṇuparimāṇatvamāmnāyate /
tasya sarvasyānākulatvopapādānāyāyamārambhaḥ /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvadutkrāntigatyāgatīnāṃ śravaṇātparicchinno 'ṇuparimāṇo jīva iti /
utkrāntistāvat- 'sa yadāsmāccharīrādutkrāmati sahaivaitaiḥ sarvairutkrāmati' (kauṣīta. 3.3) iti /
gatirapi 'ye vai ke cāsmāllokātprayanti candramasameva te sarve gacchanti' (kauṣīta. 1.2) iti /
āgatirapi 'tasmāllokātpunaraityasmai lokāya karmaṇe' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti /
children.translated_text: And returning: 'From that world, one returns again to this world for action' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6).

children.text: āsāmutkrāntigatyāgatīnāṃ śravaṇātparicchinnastāvajjīva iti prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: From the teaching of these — departure, going, and returning — the <s>jīva</s> is at least limited [in dimension].

children.text: nahi vibhoścalanamavakalpata iti /
children.translated_text: For movement is not possible for what is all-pervading.

children.text: sati ca paricchede śarīraparimāṇatvasyārhataparīkṣāyāṃ nirastatvādaṇurātmeti gamyate // 19 //
children.translated_text: And once limitedness is [established], since body-sized dimension has been eliminated as unworthy upon examination — it is understood that the Self is atomic. // 19 //

It is said: True, this is so. But the teachings of departure, going, and returning lead to [the conclusion of] the <s>jīva</s>'s limitedness. And by its own [scriptural] word, its atomic dimension is sometimes taught. The commencement [of this discussion] is for the purpose of making all of this consistent. Therein, the prima facie view is: from the teaching of departure, going, and returning, the <s>jīva</s> is limited and of atomic dimension. Departure: 'When it departs from this body, it departs together with all of these' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.3). Going: 'Indeed, all those who depart from this world go to the moon' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.2).

children.text: svātmanā cottarayoḥ | BBs_2,3.20 |
children.translated_text: <s>Svātmanā cottarayoḥ</s> — And [the connection] of the latter two [i.e., going and returning] is by its own Self. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.20 |

children.text:
utkrāntiḥ kadācidacalato 'pi grāmasvāmyanivṛttivaddehasvāmyanivṛttyā karmakṣayeṇāvakalpeta /
uttare tu gatyāgatī nācalataḥ saṃbhavataḥ /
svātmanā hi tayoḥ saṃbandho bhavati, gameḥ kartṛsthakriyātvāt /
amadhyamaparimāṇasya ca gatyāgatī aṇutva eva saṃbhavataḥ /
satyośca gatyāgatyorutkrāntirapyapasṛptireva dehāditi pratīyate /
nahyanapasṛtya dehādgatyāgatī syātām /
dehapradeśānāṃ cotkrāntāvapādānatvavacanāt /
children.translated_text: And because the parts of the body are mentioned as the points of departure at the time of departure.

children.text: 'cakṣuṣo vā mūrdhno vānyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhyaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.2) iti /
children.translated_text: 'From the eye, or from the top of the head, or from other parts of the body' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2).

children.text: 'sa etāstejomātrāḥ samabhyādadāno hṛdayamevānvavakrāmati' (bṛ. 4.4.1), 'śukramādāya punaraiti sthānam' (bṛ. 4.3.11) iti cottare 'pi śarīre śarīrasya gatyāgatī bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having gathered these luminous particles, it enters the heart itself' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.1), and 'Taking the luminous [particles], it goes back to its abode' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.11) — and even within the subsequent body, going and returning of the body-possessor are [observed].

children.text: tasmādapyasyāṇutvasiddhiḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, its atomic nature is established. // 20 //

Departure might sometimes be conceived even for something that does not move — like the loss of ownership over a village, through the cessation of ownership over a body due to the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>. But the latter two — going and returning — are not possible for what does not move. For the connection with these two is by the Self itself, because the action of going belongs to the agent. And going and returning are possible only for what is of atomic dimension — not of medium dimension. And since going and returning are established, departure too is understood as actual departure from the body. For without departing from the body, going and returning would not be possible.

children.text: FN: apādānatvamavadhitvam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Apādānatva</s>' means the status of being the point of departure.

children.text: nāṇuratacchruter iti cen netarādhikārāt | BBs_2,3.21 |
children.translated_text: <s>Nāṇur atacchruter iti cen netarādhikārāt</s> — If [it be said that] the Self is not atomic, because of <s>śruti</s> [teaching] the contrary — [we say] no, because [that śruti] pertains to the other [i.e., the supreme Self]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.21 |

children.text:
athāpi syānnāṇurayamātmā /
kasmāt /
atacchruteḥ /
aṇutvaviparītaparimāṇaśravaṇādityarthaḥ /
'sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmā yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu (bṛ. 4.4.12), 'ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ', 'satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma' (tai. 2.1.1) ityevañjātīyakā hi śrutirātmano 'ṇutve vipratiṣidhyeteti cet /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the Self is not atomic. Why? Because of <s>śruti</s> teaching the contrary — the meaning is: because of the teaching of a dimension opposite to atomicity. 'This great, unborn Self, which is constituted of consciousness, is among the <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22), 'All-pervading like space, and eternal,' 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1) — such <s>śruti</s> would contradict the atomicity of the Self. If this is the objection —

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
kasmāt /
itarādhikārāt /
parasya hyātmanaḥ prakriyāyāmeṣā parimāṇāntaraśrutiḥ /
parasyaivātmanaḥ prādhānyena vedānteṣu veditavyatvena prakṛtatvāt /
virajaḥ para ākāśādityevaṃvidhācca parasyaivātmanastatra tatra viśeṣādhikārāt /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Why? Because [that śruti] pertains to the other. For this <s>śruti</s> teaching another dimension belongs to the discussion of the supreme Self. Because the supreme Self is the primary subject to be known in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts. And because of specific [passages] such as 'beyond the pure, beyond the space' and the like, [which indicate] that the supreme Self alone is the specific subject in each place.

children.text: nanu 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti śārīra eva mahattvasaṃbandhitvena pratinirdiśyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: But in 'this which is constituted of consciousness among the <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22), it is the embodied [Self] that is specifically indicated as being connected with greatness.

children.text: śāstradṛṣṭyā tveṣa nirdeśo vāmadevavaddraṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But this indication should be viewed from the standpoint of scripture — like [the identification of] <s>Vāmadeva</s> [with <s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: tasmātprājñaviṣayatvātparimāṇāntaraśravaṇasya ca jīvasyāṇutvaṃ virudhyate // 21 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the <s>śruti</s> teaching another dimension pertains to the <s>Prājña</s> (the supreme Self), the atomicity of the <s>jīva</s> is not contradicted. // 21 //

children.text: FN: itarādhikārāt brahmaprakaraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Because of pertaining to the other' — [means] because [it pertains to] the context of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: svaśabdonmānābhyāṃ ca | BBs_2,3.22 |
children.translated_text: <s>Svaśabdonmānābhyāṃ ca</s> — And because of its own [scriptural] word and measure. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.22 |

children.text: itaścāṇurātmā yataḥ sākṣādevāsyāṇutvavācī śabdaḥ śrūyate- 'eṣo 'ṇurātmā cetasā veditavyo yasminprāṇaḥ pañcadhā saṃviveśa' (muṇḍa. 3.1.9) iti /
prāṇasaṃbandhācca jīva evāyamaṇurabhihita iti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And because of the connection with <s>prāṇa</s>, it is understood that this atomic [Self] declared is the <s>jīva</s> itself.

children.text: tathonmānamapi jīvasyāṇimānaṃ gamayati- 'bālāgraśatabhāgasya śatadhā kalpitasya ca /
children.translated_text: And the measure (<s>unmāna</s>) too conveys the atomicity of the <s>jīva</s>: 'Of the hundredth part of the tip of a hair, further divided a hundredfold —

children.text: bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ' (śve. 5.8) iti /
children.translated_text: that is the portion [called] the <s>jīva</s>; thus it should be known' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 5.9).

children.text: 'ārāgramātro hyavaroṣapi dṛṣṭaḥ' (śve. 5.8) iti conmānāntaram // 22 //
children.translated_text: And 'Of the measure of a mere point of a goad, it is seen to be even smaller' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 5.8) — this is another measure. // 22 //

The Self is atomic for this further reason: because a word directly declaring its atomicity is heard in <s>śruti</s>: 'This atomic Self is to be known by the mind, in which the <s>prāṇa</s> has entered fivefold' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.9).

children.text:
nanvaṇutve satyekadeśasthasya sakaladehagatopalabdhirvirudhyate /
dṛśyate ca jāhnavīhradanimagnānāṃ sarvāṅgaśaityopalabdhirnidāghasamaye ca sakalaśarīraparitāpopalabdhiriti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But if [the Self] is atomic and stationed in one part [of the body], the experience of the entire body would be contradicted.
