For one observes the experience of coldness in all limbs when plunged in the current of the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges), and the experience of heat in the entire body during the summer.

children.text:
FN: uddhṛtyamānamunmānam /
bālaḥ keśaḥ /
totraprotāyaḥśalākāgramarāgraṃ tasmāduddhṛtā mātrā mānaṃ yasya sa jīvastathā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Unmāna</s>' means a measure that is extracted. '<s>Bāla</s>' means a hair. The tip of a goad — the point of a needle or spike — the measure extracted from that, which the <s>jīva</s> has — thus [it is described].

children.text: ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: To this, [the sūtrakāra] reads the next [sūtra] —

children.text: avirodhaś candanavat | BBs_2,3.23 |
children.translated_text: <s>Avirodhaś candanavat</s> — There is no contradiction, as in the case of sandalwood paste. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.23 |

children.text: yathā hi haricandanabinduḥ śarīraikadeśasaṃbaddho 'pi sansakaladehavyapinamāhlādaṃ karotyevamātmāpi dehaikadeśebhyaḥ sakaladehavyāpinīmupalabdhiṃ kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: Just as a drop of <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood), though connected with one part of the body, produces a cooling sensation that pervades the entire body — so too the Self, even from one part of the body, will produce experience pervading the entire body.

children.text: tvaksaṃbandhanāccāsya sakalaśarīragatā vedanā na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: And because of its connection with the skin, its experience extending over the whole body is not contradicted.

children.text: tvagātmanorhi saṃbandhaḥ kṛtsnāyāṃ tvaci vartate tvakca kṛtsnaśarīravyāpinīti // 23 //
children.translated_text: For the connection of the Self with the skin extends over the entire skin, and the skin pervades the entire body. // 23 //

children.text: avasthitivaiśeṣyād iti cen nābhyupagamād dhṛdi hi | BBs_2,3.24 |
children.translated_text: <s>Avasthitivaiśeṣyād iti cen nābhyupagamād dhṛdi hi</s> — If [it be said that there is a fault] because of the special location [not being established] — [we say] no, because it is accepted; for [the Self is] in the heart. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.24 |

children.text:
atrāha yaduktamavirodhaścandanavaditi, tadayuktaṃ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭrāntikayoratulyatvāt /
siddhe hyātmano dehaikadeśasthatve candanadṛṣṭānto bhavati /
pratyakṣaṃ tu candanasyāvasthitivaiśeṣyamekadeśasthatvaṃ sakaladehāhlādanaṃ ca /
ātmanaḥ punaḥ sakaladehopalabdhimātraṃ pratyakṣaṃ naikadeśavartitvam /
anumeyaṃ tu taditi yadapyucyeta /
nacātrānumānaṃ saṃbhavati /
kimātmanaḥ sakalaśarīragatā vedanā tvagindriyasyeva sakaladehavyāpinaḥ sataḥ kiṃvā vibhornabhasa ivāhosviccandanabindorivāṇorekadeśasthasyeti saṃśayānativṛtteriti /
children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised: The statement 'there is no contradiction, as with sandalwood' is improper, because the illustration and the illustrated are not on equal footing. For the sandalwood illustration applies only if the Self's location in one part of the body is already established. The special location of sandalwood — its being in one part — and its producing a cooling sensation in the entire body are directly perceived. But for the Self, only the experience of the entire body is directly perceived — not its being stationed in one part. And if one were to say that [the latter] is to be inferred — even so, inference is not possible here, because the doubt is not resolved: is the experience of the entire body due to [the Self] pervading the entire body like the skin, or to [its being] all-pervading like space, or to [its being] atomic and stationed in one part like a drop of sandalwood?

children.text:
atrocyate- nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
kasmāt /
abhyupagamāt /
abhyupagamyate hyātmano 'pi candanasyeva dehaikadeśavṛttitvamavasthitivaiśeṣyam /
kathamityucyate /
hṛdi hyeṣa ātmā paṭhyate vedāntaṣu /
'hṛdi hyeṣa ātmā'
children.translated_text: To this it is said: This is not a fault. Why? Because it is accepted. For the Self too, like sandalwood, is accepted as being stationed in one part of the body — the special location. How? It is said: For this Self is read [as being] in the heart in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts. 'For this Self is in the heart' —

children.text: (praśna. 3.6), 'sa vā eṣa ātmā hṛdi' (chā. 8.3.3), 'katama ātmeti yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdyantarjyotiḥ puruṣaḥ' (bṛ. 4.3.7) ityādyupadeśebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: (<s>Praśna</s> 3.6), 'This Self is in the heart' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.3), 'Which Self? — this one constituted of consciousness among the <s>prāṇas</s>, the inner light, the <s>Puruṣa</s> in the heart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7) — from such teachings.

children.text: tasmāddṛṣṭāntadārṣṭrāntikayoravaiṣamyādyuktamevaitadavirodhaścandanavaditi // 24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since there is no disparity between the illustration and the illustrated, it is proper to say 'there is no contradiction, as with sandalwood.' // 24 //

children.text: guṇādvā lokavat | BBs_2,3.25 |
children.translated_text: <s>Guṇād vā lokavat</s> — Or, because of [its] quality [pervading], as in the world. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.25 |

children.text: caitanyaguṇavyāptervāṇorapi sato jīvasya sakaladehavyāpi kāryaṃ na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: Or, because of the pervasion of its quality — consciousness — even for the <s>jīva</s> that is atomic, the function pervading the entire body is not contradicted.

children.text: yathā loke maṇipradīpaprabhṛtīnāmapavarakaikadeśavartināmapi prabhāpavarakavyāpinī satī kṛtsne 'pavarake kāryaṃ karoti tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, gems, lamps, and such — though stationed in one part of a room — their radiance, pervading the room, produces a function in the entire room — so too.

children.text: syātkadāciccandanasya sāvayavatvātsūkṣmāvayavavisarpaṇenāpi sakaladeha āhlādayitṛtvaṃ va tvaṇorjīvasyāvayavāḥ santi yairayaṃ sakaladehaṃ viprasarpedityāśaṅkya guṇādvā lokavadityuktam // 25 //
children.translated_text: Lest one suspect that sandalwood, being composed of parts, might produce cooling in the entire body through the spreading of its subtle parts — but the atomic <s>jīva</s> has no parts by which it could spread throughout the entire body — anticipating this, [the sūtrakāra] said 'or, because of [its] quality, as in the world.' // 25 //

children.text:
kathaṃ punarguṇo guṇivyatirekeṇānyatra varteta /
nahi paṭasya śuklo guṇaḥ paṭavyatirekeṇānyatra vartamāno dṛśyate /
pradīpabhāvadbhavediti cet /
children.translated_text: But how could a quality exist elsewhere, separate from its possessor? For the white quality of a cloth is not seen to exist elsewhere, separate from the cloth. If [one says:] it would be like the radiance of a lamp —

children.text:
na /
tasyā api dravyatvābhyupagamāt /
nibiḍāvayavaṃ hi tejodravyaṃ pradīpaḥ /
praviralāvayavaṃ tu tejodravyameva prabheti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: No. Because that [radiance] too is accepted as a substance. For a lamp is a fire-substance with dense particles. And radiance is fire-substance itself with sparse particles. To this, [the sūtrakāra] reads the next [sūtra] —

children.text: vyatireko gandhavat | BBs_2,3.26 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vyatireko gandhavat</s> — The separation [of a quality from its possessor exists], as in the case of smell. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.26 |

children.text:
yathā guṇasyāpi sato gandhasya gandhavaddravyavyatirekeṇa vṛttirbhavati /
aprāpteṣvapi kusumādiṣu gandhavatsu kusumagandhopalabdheḥ /
evamaṇorapi sato jīvasya caitanyaguṇavyatireko bhaviṣyati /
ataścānaikāntikametadguṇatvādrūpādivadāśrayaviśleṣānupapattiriti /
guṇasyaiva sato gandhasyāśrayaviśleṣadarśanāt /
gandhasyāpi sahaivāśrayeṇa viśleṣa iti cet /
children.translated_text: Just as smell — even being a quality — has a functioning separate from the smell-possessing substance. For the smell of flowers is perceived even when the flowers and such smell-possessing [substances] have not been reached [i.e., are distant]. So too, even for the atomic <s>jīva</s>, there will be a separation of the quality of consciousness [from its location]. And therefore, the [argument] 'because of being a quality, like color and the like, the impossibility of separation from the substratum' is inconclusive. Because smell, being a quality, is observed to separate from its substratum. [Objection:] Even the smell separates together with its substratum —

children.text:
na /
yasmānmūladravyādviśleṣitasya kṣayaprasaṅgāt /
akṣīyamāṇamapi tatpūrvāvasthāto gamyate /
anyathā tatpūrvāvasthairgurutvādibhirhīyeta /
syādetat /
gandhāśrayāṇāṃ viśliṣṭānāmavayavānāmalpatvātsannapi viśeṣo nopalakṣyate /
children.translated_text: No. Because if separated from the root substance, [the substratum would undergo] perishing. Even though not [visibly] perishing, it [the substratum] departs from its prior state — this is understood. Otherwise, it would lose [properties like] heaviness and such that belong to its prior state. [Objection:] Perhaps because of the smallness of the separated particles that are the substratum of smell, the difference, though existing, is not noticed.

children.text: sūkṣmā hi gandhaparamāṇavaḥ sarvato viprasṛptā gandhabuddhimutpādayanti nāsikāpuṭamanupraviśanta iti cet /
children.translated_text: [Objection continued:] For the subtle smell-atoms, having spread in all directions, produce the cognition of smell by entering the nostrils —

children.text:
na /
atīndriyatvātparamāṇūnāṃ sphuṭagandhopalabdheśca nāgakesarādiṣu /
naca loke pratītirgandhavaddravyamāghrātamiti /
gandha evāghrāta iti tu laukikāḥ pratīyanti /
rūpādiṣvāśrayavyatirekānupalabdhergandhasyāpyayukta āśrayavyatireka iti cet /
children.translated_text: No. Because atoms are beyond the senses, and because distinct smell is perceived in <s>nāgakesara</s> (cobra saffron) and such [substances]. And in the world, the cognition is not 'a substance possessing smell has been smelled.' Rather, ordinary people cognize 'smell alone has been smelled.' If [you say]: because the separation of form and such from their substratum is not perceived, the separation of smell from its substratum too is unjustified —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: pratyakṣatvādanumānāpravṛtteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the directness of perception, there is no scope for inference.

children.text: tasmādyadyathā loke dṛṣṭaṃ tattathaivānumantavyaṃ nirūpakairnānyathā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever is perceived in the world as it is — that alone should be inferred accordingly by careful investigators, and not otherwise.

children.text: nahi raso guṇo jihvayopalabhyata ityato rūpādayo 'pi guṇā jihvāyaivopalabhyeragniriti niyantuṃ śakyate // 26 //
children.translated_text: For it cannot be determined that, because taste, a quality, is apprehended by the tongue, therefore form and the other qualities too should be apprehended by the tongue alone. // 26 //

children.text: FN: guṇasya dravyavyatireka āśrayaviśleṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'The separation of a quality from substance' means the disjunction from the substratum.

children.text: tathā ca darśayati | BBs_2,3.27 |
children.translated_text: And thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.27 |

children.text: hṛdayāyatanatvamaṇuparimāṇatvaṃ cātmano 'bhidhāya tasyaiva 'ā lomasya ā nakhāgrebhyaḥ' (chā. 8.8.1) iti caitanyena guṇena samastaśarīravyāpitvaṃ darśayati // 27 //
children.translated_text: Having stated that the self has the heart as its abode and atomic size, [the <s>śruti</s>] then shows the pervading of the entire body by that very [self] through the quality of consciousness: 'Up to [each] hair, up to the tips of the nails' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.8.1). // 27 //

children.text: pṛthagupadeśāt | BBs_2,3.28 |
children.translated_text: Because of the separate teaching. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.28 |

children.text: 'prajñayā śarīraṃ samāruhya' (kauṣī. 3.6) iti cātmaprajñayoḥ kartṛkaraṇabhāvena pṛthagupadeśāccaitanyaguṇenaivāsya śarīravyāpitā gamyate /
children.translated_text: 'Having mounted the body with <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness)' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.6) — and because of the separate teaching of the self and <s>prajñā</s> in the relation of agent and instrument, the pervading of the body by it is understood to be through the quality of consciousness alone.

children.text: 'tadeṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānena vijñānamādāya' (bṛ. 2.1.17) iti ca kartuḥ śārīratpṛthagvijñānasyopadeśa etamevābhiprāyamupodbalayati /
children.translated_text: 'Having taken the <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge) of these <s>prāṇas</s> with [his own] <s>vijñāna</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.17) — the teaching of <s>vijñāna</s> as separate from the agent, the embodied self, further strengthens this very intention.

children.text: tasmādaṇurātmeti // 28 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the self is atomic. // 28 //

children.text: FN: vijñānamindriyāṇāṃ jñānaśaktiṃ vijñānena caitanyaguṇenādāya śeta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Vijñāna</s>' means the cognitive capacity of the sense-organs; 'having taken with <s>vijñāna</s>, with the quality of consciousness, it sleeps' — this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: Given this position, we say:

children.text: tadguṇasāratvāt tu tadvyapadeśaḥ prājñavat | BBs_2,3.29 |
children.translated_text: But the designation [of the self as atomic] is because of the essentiality of its (<s>buddhi</s>'s) qualities — like [the designation of] the Omniscient (<s>prājña</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.29 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyavartayati /
naitadastyaṇurātmeti /
utpattyaśravaṇāddhi parasyaiva tu brahmaṇaḥ praveśaśravaṇāttādātmyopadeśācca parameva brahma jīva ityuktam /
parameva cedbrahma jīvastasmādyāvatparaṃ brahma tāvāneva jīvo bhavitumarhati /
parasya ca brahmaṇo vibhutvamāmnātam /
tasmādvibhurjīvaḥ /
tathāca 'sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmā yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityevañjātīyakā jīvaviṣayā vibhutvavādāḥ śrautāḥ smārtāśca samarthitā bhavanti /
nacāṇorjīvasya sakalaśarīragatā vedanopapadyate /
tvaksaṃbandhātsyāditi cet /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the position. This is not so — the self is not atomic. For since no origination [of the <s>jīva</s>] is heard, and since the entering of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is heard, and because of the teaching of identity — it has been said that the <s>jīva</s> is nothing but the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And if the <s>jīva</s> is indeed the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, then the <s>jīva</s> should be as great as the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And the all-pervasiveness of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is stated in <s>śruti</s>. Therefore, the <s>jīva</s> is all-pervading. And thus, statements of all-pervasiveness pertaining to the <s>jīva</s> — both <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) and <s>smārta</s> — such as 'This great, unborn Self, who is this one made of knowledge among the vital breaths' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) and the like, are vindicated. And for an atomic <s>jīva</s>, sensation pervading the entire body would not be tenable. If [you say] it would be tenable through [the <s>jīva</s>'s] contact with the skin —

children.text:
na /
kaṇṭakatodane 'pi sakalaśarīragataiva vedanā prasajyeta /
tvakkaṇṭakayorhi saṃyogaḥ kṛtsnāyāṃ tvaci vartate tvakca kṛtsnaśarīravyāpinīti /
pādatala eva tu kaṇṭakanunno vedanāṃ prati labhate /
nacāṇorguṇavyāptirupapadyate, guṇasya guṇideśatvāt /
guṇatvameva hi guṇinamanāśritya guṇasya hīyeta /
pradīpaprabhāyāśca dravyāntaratvaṃ vyākhyātam /
gandho 'pi guṇatvābhyupagamātsāśraya eva saṃcaritumarhati /
anyathā guṇatvahāniprasaṅgāt /
tathācoktaṃ dvaipāyanena- 'upalabhyāpsu cedgandaṃ kecidbrūyuranaipuṇāḥ /
pṛthivyāmeva taṃ vidyādapo vāyuṃ ca saṃśritam' iti /
yadi ca caitanyaṃ jīvasya samastaṃ śarīraṃ vyāpnuyānnāṇurjīvaḥ syāt /
caitanyameva hyasya svarūpamagnerivauṣṇyaprakāśau /
children.translated_text: No. Because even when pricked by a thorn, the sensation would pervade the entire body. For the conjunction of thorn and skin exists [potentially] throughout the entire skin, and the skin pervades the entire body. But one who is pricked by a thorn only in the sole of the foot experiences sensation [only there]. And for an atomic [self], the pervading of [its] quality is not tenable — because a quality exists where the qualified exists. For the very quality-ness of a quality would be lost if it did not depend on the qualified. And it has been explained that the light of a lamp is a different substance [not a quality that spreads from its substratum]. And smell too, being accepted as a quality, should travel only together with its substratum — otherwise, the loss of its quality-ness would follow. And thus <s>Dvaipāyana</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) has said: 'If some unskilled persons should say that smell is perceived in water — one should know that [the smell] belongs to earth alone, which has entered the water together with air.' And if consciousness were to pervade the entire body of the <s>jīva</s>, the <s>jīva</s> would not be atomic. For consciousness is indeed its very nature — just as heat and light are [the nature] of fire.

children.text:
nātra guṇaguṇivibhāgo vidyata iti śarīraparimāṇatvaṃ ca pratyākhyātam /
pariśeṣādvibhurjīvaḥ /
kathaṃ tarhyaṇutvādivyapadeśa ityata āha- tad guṇasāratvāttu tadvyapadeśaḥ iti /
tasyā buddherguṇāstadguṇā icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhamityevamādayastadguṇāḥ sāraḥ pradhānaṃ yasyātmanaḥ saṃsāritve saṃbhavati sa tadguṇasārastasya bhāvastadguṇasāratvam /
nahi buddherguṇairvinā kevalasyātmanaḥ saṃsāritvamasti /
buddhyupādhirdharmādhyāsanimittaṃ hi kartṛtvabhoktṛtvādilakṣaṇaṃ saṃsāritvamakartṛrabhoktuścāsaṃsāriṇo nityamuktasya sata ātmanaḥ /
tasmāttadguṇasāratvādbuddhiparimāṇenāsya parimāṇavyapadeśaḥ /
tadutkrāntyādibhiścāsyotkrāntyadivyapadeśo na svataḥ /
tathāca- 'bālāgraśatabhāgasya śatadhā kalpitasya ca /
bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sa cānantyāya kalpate' (śve. 5.9) ityaṇutvaṃ jīvasyoktvā tasyaiva punarānantyamāha /
taccaivameva samañjasaṃ syādyadyaupacārikamaṇutvaṃ jīvasya bhavetpāramārthikaṃ cānantyam /
nahyubhayaṃ mukhyamavakalpeta /
nacānantyamaupacārikamiti śakyaṃ vijñātuṃ, sarvopaniṣatsu brahmātmabhāvasya pratipādayiṣitatvāt /
tathetarasminnapyunmāne 'buddherguṇenātmaguṇena caiva ārāgramātro hyavaro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ' (śve. 6.8) iti ca buddhiguṇasaṃbandhenaivārāgramātratāṃ śāsti na svenaivātmanā /
'eṣo 'ṇurātmā cetasā veditavyaḥ' (muṇḍa. 3.1.9) ityatrāpi na jīvasyāṇuparimāṇatvaṃ śiṣyate, parasyaivātmanaścakṣurādyanavagrāhyatvena jñānaprasādagamyatvena ca prakṛtatvāt /
jīvasyāpi ca mukhyāṇuparimāṇatvānupapatteḥ /
tasmāddurjñānatvābhiprāyamidamaṇutvavacanamupādhyabhiprāyaṃ vā draṣṭavyam /
tathā 'prajñayā śarīraṃ samāruhya' (kauṣī. 3.6) ityevañjātīyakeṣvapi bhedopadeśeṣu buddhyauvopādhibhūtayā jīvaḥ śarīraṃ samāruhyetyevaṃ yojayitavyam /
vyapadeśamātraṃ vā, śilāputrakasya śarīramityavadat /
nahyatra guṇaguṇivibhāgo 'pi vidyata ityuktam /
hṛdayāyatanatvavacanamapi buddhereva tadāyatanatvāt /
tathotkrāntyādīnāmapyupādhyāyattatāṃ darśayati- 'kasminnvahamutkrānta utkrānto bhaviṣyāmi kasminvā pratiṣṭhite pratiṣṭhāsyāmīti' (praśna. 6.3) 'sa prāṇamasṛjata' (pra. 6.4) iti /
utkrāntyabhāve hi gatyāgatyorapyabhāvo vijñāyate /
nahyanapasṛpasya dehādgatyāgatī syātām /
children.translated_text: For one who has not departed from the body, there would be no going and coming.

children.text: evamupādhiguṇasāratvājjīvasyāṇutvādivyapadeśaḥ prājñavat /
children.translated_text: Thus, the designation of atomicity and such for the <s>jīva</s> is because of the essentiality of the qualities of the <s>upādhi</s> — like [the designation of] the Omniscient (<s>prājña</s>).

children.text: yathā prājñasya paramātmanaḥ saguṇeṣūpāsaneṣūpādhiguṇasāratvādaṇīyastvādivyapadeśaḥ- 'aṇīyānvrīhervā yavādvā' (chā. 3.1.14.2) 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityevaṃprakārastadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as for the Omniscient, the supreme Self, in meditations on the qualified [<s>Brahman</s>], there is the designation of 'smaller than' and such — because of the essentiality of the qualities of the <s>upādhi</s>: 'Smaller than a grain of rice or a grain of barley' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2), 'Made of mind, with <s>prāṇa</s> as body, of all fragrances, of all tastes, of true desire, of true resolve' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) — such are the types [of designation]; so too [for the <s>jīva</s>].

children.text: syādetadyadi buddhiguṇasāratvādātmanaḥ saṃsāritvaṃ kalpyeta, tato buddhyātmanorbhinnayoḥ saṃyogāvasānamavaśyaṃbhāvītyato buddhiviyoge satyātmano vibhaktasyānālakṣyatvādasattvamasaṃsāritvaṃ vā prasajyeteti // 29 //
children.translated_text: It might be said: If the <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature of the self is imagined as due to the essentiality of the qualities of <s>buddhi</s>, then — since <s>buddhi</s> and the self are different — the cessation of their conjunction is inevitable. And when <s>buddhi</s> separates, the self, being distinct, would either become non-existent due to being unrecognizable, or would become non-transmigrating. // 29 //

Here there is no distinction between quality and qualified — and therefore the body-sized-ness [of the self] has also been rejected. By elimination, the <s>jīva</s> is all-pervading. How then is there the designation of atomicity and such? To this [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: 'But the designation is because of the essentiality of its qualities.' The qualities of that <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, and such — are 'its qualities'; their being the essence, the predominant [factor], for the self when <s>saṃsāra</s> is possible — that is the 'essentiality of its qualities.' For without the qualities of <s>buddhi</s>, the self by itself has no <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature. For the <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature characterized by agenthood, experiencer-ship, and such — conditioned by the <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct) of <s>buddhi</s>, caused by the superimposition of <s>dharma</s> — belongs to the self that is [in reality] a non-agent, non-experiencer, non-transmigrating, eternally liberated being. Therefore, because of the essentiality of <s>buddhi</s>'s qualities, the designation of the self's size follows the size of <s>buddhi</s>. And the designation of departure and such for the self is due to the departure and such of that [<s>buddhi</s>] — not inherently. And thus: 'The <s>jīva</s> should be known as a hundredth part of the hundredth part of a hair-tip — and yet it is fit for infinity' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 5.9) — having stated the atomicity of the <s>jīva</s>, [the <s>śruti</s>] then states its infinity. And this would be consistent only if the atomicity of the <s>jīva</s> were figurative and its infinity real. For both cannot be literal. And it is not possible to understand the infinity as figurative — because throughout all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the identity of the self with <s>Brahman</s> is what is intended to be taught. Likewise, in the other measurement too — 'By the quality of <s>buddhi</s> and by the quality of the self, it is seen as [small as] a hair-tip, even the lower [self]' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.8) — [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches the hair-tip-ness only in connection with the quality of <s>buddhi</s>, not by the self's own [nature]. In 'This atomic self is to be known by the mind' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.9) too, the atomic size is not being taught for the <s>jīva</s> — because the topic is the supreme Self itself, as being ungraspable by eyes and such and accessible only through the clarity of knowledge. And because literal atomic size is also untenable for the <s>jīva</s>. Therefore, this statement of atomicity should be understood as intended [to express] the difficulty of knowing, or as referring to the <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct). Likewise, in passages such as 'Having mounted the body with consciousness' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.6) and similar teachings of distinction — the construction should be: the <s>jīva</s>, by means of <s>buddhi</s> which is the <s>upādhi</s>, mounts the body. Or it is merely a designation — like saying 'the body of a <s>śilāputraka</s>' (a stone doll, which has no real body). For it has been said that here there is no distinction between quality and qualified. The statement that the heart is its abode also [applies] because <s>buddhi</s> alone has that as its abode. Likewise, [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that departure and such too are dependent on the <s>upādhi</s>: 'When I depart, shall I be departed? When I am established, shall I be established?' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.3), 'He created <s>Prāṇa</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.4). For in the absence of departure, the absence of going and coming too is understood.

children.text: ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: To this, the next [<s>sūtra</s>] gives the answer:

children.text: yāvadātmabhāvitvāc ca na doṣas taddarśanāt | BBs_2,3.30 |
children.translated_text: And there is no fault, because [the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s>] lasts as long as the self [is in <s>saṃsāra</s>]; for that is observed. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.30 |

children.text:
neyamanantaranirdiṣṭadoṣaprāptirāśaṅkanīyā /
kasmāt /
yāvadātmabhāvitvādbuddhisaṃyogasya /
yāvadayamātmā saṃsārī bhavati, yāvadasya samyagdarśanena saṃsāritvaṃ na nivartate, tāvadasya buddhyā saṃyogo na śāmyati /
yāvadeva cāyaṃ buddhyupādhisaṃbandhastāvajjīvasya jīvatvaṃ saṃsāritvaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: This contingency of the fault just stated should not be apprehended. Why? Because the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s> lasts as long as the self [is in <s>saṃsāra</s>]. As long as this self is a transmigrator, as long as its <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature is not removed by right knowledge — for so long, its conjunction with <s>buddhi</s> does not cease. And for as long as this connection with the <s>upādhi</s> of <s>buddhi</s> [lasts] — for that long the <s>jīva</s>'s <s>jīva</s>-nature and <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature [continue].

children.text:
paramārthatastu na jīvo nāma buddhyupādhisaṃbandhaparikalpitasvarūpavyatirekeṇāsti /
nahi nityamuktasvarūpātsarvajñādīśvarādanyaścetano dhāturdvitīyo vedāntārthanirūpaṇāyāmupalabhyate /
'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā śrotā mantā vijñātā' (bṛ. 3.7.23), 'nānyadato 'sti draṣṭṛ śrotṛ mantṛ vijñātṛ' (chā. 6.8.7), 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.1.6), 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' (bṛ. 1.4.7) ityādiśrutebhyaḥ /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate yāvadātmabhāvī buddhisaṃyoga iti /
taddarśanādityāha /
tathāhi śāstraṃ darśayati- 'yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdyantarjyotiḥ puruṣaḥ sa samānaḥ sannubhau lokāvanusaṃcarati dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva' (bṛ. 4.3.4) ityādi /
tatra vijñānamaya iti buddhimaya ityetaduktaṃ bhavati /
pradeśāntare 'vijñānamayo manomayaḥ prāṇamayaścakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaḥ' iti vijñānamayasya manaādibhiḥ saha pāṭhāt /
buddhimayatvaṃ ca tadguṇasāratvamevābhipreyate /
yathā loke strīmayo devadatta iti strīrāgādipradhāno 'bhidhīyate tadvat /
'sa samānaḥ sannubhau lokāvanusaṃcarati' iti ca lokāntaragamane 'pyaviyogaṃ buddhyā darśayati /
kena samānastasyaivabuddhyeti gamyate saṃnidhānāt /
tacca darśayati - 'dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva' (bṛ. 4.3.7) iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- nāyaṃ svato dhyāyati, nāpi calati, dhyāyantyāṃ buddhau dhyāyatīva calantyāṃ buddhau calatīveti /
apica mithyājñānapuraḥsaro 'yamātmano buddhyupādhisaṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, this connection of the self with the <s>upādhi</s> of <s>buddhi</s> is preceded by false knowledge.

children.text: naca mithyājñānasya samyagjñānādanyatra nivṛttirastītyato yāvadbrahmātmatānavabodhasyāvadayaṃ buddhyupādhisaṃbandho na śāmyati /
children.translated_text: And since false knowledge has no cessation except through right knowledge, this connection with the <s>upādhi</s> of <s>buddhi</s> does not cease until the realization of the identity of the self with <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: darśayati ca- 'vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntamādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ purastāt /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows: 'I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the color of the sun, beyond darkness.

children.text: tameva viditvātimṛtyumeti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' (śve. 3.8) iti // 30 //
children.translated_text: Only by knowing Him does one cross over death; there is no other path for going' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.8). // 30 //

But in ultimate reality, the <s>jīva</s> — apart from the nature imagined through connection with the <s>upādhi</s> of <s>buddhi</s> — does not exist as a separate entity. For no second conscious element, other than the eternally free, omniscient Lord, is found in the investigation of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s>. [This follows] from <s>śrutis</s> such as: 'There is no other seer, hearer, thinker, or knower than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23), 'There is no seer, hearer, thinker, or knower other than this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10). But how is it known that the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s> lasts as long as the self [is in <s>saṃsāra</s>]? 'For that is observed,' says [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>]. For thus the scripture shows: 'This person who is made of knowledge, the light among the vital breaths within the heart — he, remaining the same, wanders through both worlds; he seems to think, seems to move' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7), and so forth. There, 'made of knowledge' (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) means 'made of <s>buddhi</s>' — this is what is stated. Because in another passage, '<s>vijñānamaya</s>' is listed together with 'made of mind' and such: '<s>vijñānamaya</s>, made of mind, made of <s>prāṇa</s>, made of sight, made of hearing.' And being 'made of <s>buddhi</s>' is intended as the essentiality of <s>buddhi</s>'s qualities. Just as in the world, '<s>Devadatta</s> is woman-made' means he is one whose predominant [trait] is attachment to women — similarly. 'He, remaining the same, wanders through both worlds' — this shows that even in going to another world, there is no separation from <s>buddhi</s>. With whom does he remain the same? — with <s>buddhi</s> itself, it is understood from the proximity. And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that: 'He seems to think, he seems to move' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7). This is what is meant: He does not think by himself, nor does he move; when <s>buddhi</s> thinks, he seems to think; when <s>buddhi</s> moves, he seems to move.

children.text:
FN: vijñānamayo buddhipracuraḥ /
ādityavarṇaṃ svaprakāśam /
tamasaḥ parastādajñānāspṛṣṭam /
satā paramātmanā /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Vijñānamaya</s>' means predominantly [composed] of <s>buddhi</s>. 'Of the color of the sun' means self-luminous. 'Beyond darkness' means untouched by ignorance. 'In Being' — in the supreme Self.

children.text:
nanu suṣuptapralayayorna śakyate buddhisaṃbandhaṃ ātmano 'bhyupagantum /
'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati svamapīto bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti vacanāt /
kṛtsnavikārapralayābhyupagamācca /
tatkathaṃ yāvadātmabhāvitvaṃ buddhisaṃbandhasyetyatrocyate-
children.translated_text: But in deep sleep and dissolution, the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s> cannot be accepted for the self — because of the statement 'You are then merged in Being, dear one' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1), and because of the acceptance that all modifications dissolve completely. Then how is the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s> said to last as long as the self [is in <s>saṃsāra</s>]? — to this it is said:

children.text: puṃstvādivat tv asya sato 'bhivyaktiyogāt | BBs_2,3.31 |
children.translated_text: But like masculinity and such — because of the connection with manifestation of what exists [in latent form]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.31 |

children.text:
yathā loke puṃstvādīni bījātmanā vidyamānānyeva bālyādiṣvanupalabhyamānānyavidyamānavadabhipreyamāṇāni yauvanādiṣvāvirbhavanti, nāvidyamānānyutpadyante ṣaṇḍādīnāmapi tadutpattiprasaṅgāt, evamayamapi buddhisaṃbandhaḥ śaktyātmanā vidyamāna eva suṣuptapralayayoḥ punaḥ prabodhaprasavayorāvirbhavati /
evaṃ hyetadyujyate /
nahyākasmikī kasyacidutpattiḥ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: For the causeless origination of anything whatsoever is not possible.

children.text: atiprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because of over-extension [i.e., anything could arise from anything].

children.text: darśayati ca suṣuptādutthānamavidyātmakabījasadbhāvakāritam- 'sati saṃpadya na viduḥ sati saṃpadyamāha' iti ta iha vyāghro vā saṃho vā' (chā. 6.9.3) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that the arising from deep sleep is caused by the existence of the seed consisting of <s>avidyā</s>: 'Having merged in Being, they do not know that they have merged in Being; whatever they were here — whether tiger or lion' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.9.3) — and so forth.

children.text: tasmātsiddhametadyāvadātmabhāvī buddhyādyupādhisaṃbandha iti // 31 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the conjunction with the <s>upādhis</s> such as <s>buddhi</s> lasts as long as the self [is in <s>saṃsāra</s>]. // 31 //

Just as in the world, masculinity and such — existing in seed-form — though not perceived in childhood and such, being regarded as non-existent, manifest in youth and such; and they do not arise from non-existence, because then they would arise even in eunuchs and the like — so too, this conjunction with <s>buddhi</s>, existing in the form of a latent capacity, though [seemingly absent] in deep sleep and dissolution, manifests again upon waking and creation. For only thus is this consistent.

children.text: nityopalabdhyanupalabdhiprasaṅgo 'nyataraniyamo vānyathā | BBs_2,3.32 |
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the consequence of perpetual apprehension or perpetual non-apprehension — or [there must be] a restriction on one or the other. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.32 |

children.text:
taccātmana upādhibhūtamantaḥkaraṇaṃ mano buddhirvijñānaṃ ctitamiti cānekadhā tatra tatrābhilapyate /
kvacicca vṛttivibhāgena saṃśayādivṛttikaṃ mana ityucyate, niścayādivṛttikaṃ buddhiriti /
taccaivaṃbhūtamantaḥkaraṇamavaśyamastītyabhyupagantavyam /
anyathā hyanabhyupagamyamāne tasminnityopalabdhyanupalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ syāt /
ātmendriyaviṣayāṇāmupalabdhisādhanānāṃ saṃnidhāne sati nityamevopalabdhiḥ prasajyeta /
atha satyapi hetusamavadhāne phalābhāvastato nityamevānupalabdhiḥ prasajyeta /
nacaivaṃ dṛśyate /
athavānyatarasyātmana indriyasya vā śaktipratibandho 'bhyupagantavyaḥ /
nacātmanaḥ śaktipratibandhaḥ saṃbhavati /
avikriyatvāt /
nāpīndriyasya /
nahi tasya pūrvottarayoḥ kṣaṇayorapratibaddhaśaktikasya sato 'kasmācchaktiḥ pratibadhyeta /
tasmādyasyāvadhānānavadhānābhyāmupalabdhyanupalabdhī bhavatastanmanaḥ /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'anyatrātmanā abhūvaṃ nādarśamanyatramanā abhūvaṃ nāśrauṣam' (bṛ. 1.5.3) iti, 'manasā hyeva paśyati manasā śṛṇoti' (bṛ. 1.5.3) iti /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'My mind was elsewhere, I did not see; my mind was elsewhere, I did not hear' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.3), and 'For one sees with the mind, one hears with the mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.3).

children.text: kāmādayaścāsya vṛttaya iti darśayati 'kāmaḥ saṃkalpo vicikitsā śraddhāśraddhā dhṛtiradhṛtirhīrbhīrityetatsarvaṃ mana eva' (bṛ. 1.5.3) iti /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that desire and the like are its functions: 'Desire, intention, doubt, faith, lack of faith, steadfastness, unsteadfastness, modesty, fear — all this is indeed the mind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.3).

children.text: tasmādyuktametat /
children.translated_text: Therefore this is fitting.

children.text: 'tadguṇasāratvāttadvyapadeśaḥ' iti // 32 //
children.translated_text: 'Because it is essentially of the nature of their qualities, it is designated by their names' — thus [the <s>sūtra</s> is concluded]. // 32 //

And that inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), which serves as a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of the Self, is referred to in various places by multiple names — mind (<s>manas</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), and thought (<s>citta</s>).
And sometimes, by the division of functions, it is called '<s>manas</s>' when it has the function of doubt and the like, and '<s>buddhi</s>' when it has the function of determination and the like.
That such an inner organ must necessarily exist — this must be accepted.
For otherwise — if it were not accepted — the consequence of either perpetual apprehension or perpetual non-apprehension would follow.
When the means of apprehension — namely the self, the sense-organs, and the objects — are all present, apprehension would always follow.
Or, if even when the causes are all assembled, the result does not occur, then non-apprehension would always follow.
But this is not observed.
Alternatively, one would have to accept an obstruction of the power of one or the other — either the self or the sense-organ.
But an obstruction of the self's power is not possible,
because it is without modification.
Nor of the sense-organ's power.
For when its power is unobstructed in both the preceding and subsequent moments, there is no reason why its power should be obstructed [in between].
Therefore, that through whose attention and inattention apprehension and non-apprehension occur — that is the mind.

children.text: 14 kartrādhikaraṇam / sū. 33-40
children.translated_text: 14. The <s>Kartṛ Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Agent). <s>Sūtras</s> 33-40.

children.text: kartā śāstrārthavattvāt | BBs_2,3.33 |
children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> is an agent — because of the purposefulness of scripture. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.33 |

children.text:
tadguṇasāratvādhikāreṇaivāparo 'pi jīvadharmaḥ prapañcyate /
kartā cāyaṃ jīvaḥ syāt /
kasmāt /
śāstrārthatvāt /
evañca 'yajeta' 'juhuyāt' 'dadyāt' ityevaṃvidhaṃ vidiśāstramarthavadbhavati /
anyathā tadanarthakaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, it would be purposeless.

children.text: taddhi kartuḥ sataḥ kartavyaviśeṣamupadiśati /
children.translated_text: For [scripture] teaches a specific action to be performed to an existing agent.

children.text: nacāsati kartṛtve tadupapadyeta /
children.translated_text: And in the absence of agency, that [teaching] would not be possible.

children.text: tathedamapi śāstramarthavadbhavati eṣa hi draṣṭā śrotā mantā boddhā kartā vijñānātmā puruṣaḥ (pra. 5.9) iti // 33 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, this scripture too becomes purposeful: 'For he is the seer, the hearer, the thinker, the knower, the agent — the <s>vijñānātman</s>, the <s>puruṣa</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 5.9). // 33 //

Under the same topic of [the <s>jīva</s>'s] being essentially of the nature of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] qualities, another property of the <s>jīva</s> is elaborated.
This <s>jīva</s> would be an agent.
Why?
Because of the purposefulness of scripture.
And thus, injunctive scripture of the kind 'one should sacrifice,' 'one should offer oblations,' 'one should give' becomes purposeful.

children.text: vihāropadeśāt | BBs_2,3.34 |
children.translated_text: Because of the teaching of movement [in dreams]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.34 |

children.text: itaśca jīvasya kartṛtvaṃ, yajjīvaprakriyāyāṃ saṃdhye sthāne vihāramupadiśati- 'sa īyate 'mṛto yatra kāmam' (bṛ. 4.3.12) iti, 'sve śarīre yathākāmaṃ parivartate' (bṛ. 2.1.18) iti ca // 34 //
children.translated_text: For this further reason the <s>jīva</s> has agency: in the context of the <s>jīva</s>, [scripture] teaches movement in the intermediate state [of dreams]: 'He moves about there as an immortal, wherever he wishes' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.12), and 'He moves about at will in his own body' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.18). // 34 //

children.text: FN: saṃdhye sthāne svapnāvasthānam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'The intermediate state' (<s>saṃdhya sthāna</s>) is the dream-state.

children.text: īyate gacchati /
children.translated_text: '<s>Īyate</s>' means goes.

children.text: upādānāt | BBs_2,3.35 |
children.translated_text: Because of [the teaching of] taking up [instruments]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.35 |

children.text: itaścāsya kartṛtvaṃ, yajjīvaprakriyāyāmeva karaṇānāmupādānaṃ saṃkīrtayati- 'tadeṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānena vijñānamādāya' (bṛ. 21.1.17) iti, 'prāṇāngṛhītvā' (bṛ. 2.1.18) iti ca // 35 //
children.translated_text: For this further reason the <s>jīva</s> has agency: in the very same context of the <s>jīva</s>, [scripture] mentions the taking up of instruments: 'Taking the cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) of those <s>prāṇas</s> (sense-organs) by means of cognition' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.17), and 'Having grasped the <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.18). // 35 //

children.text: FN: prāṇānāmindryāṇāṃ vijñānena buddhyā vijñānaṃ grahaṇaśaktimādāya svāpe jīvo hṛdayametīti yojanā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The construal is: the <s>jīva</s>, having taken the grasping capacity (<s>vijñāna</s>) of the sense-organs (<s>prāṇas</s>) by means of the intellect (<s>vijñāna</s>, i.e., <s>buddhi</s>), goes to sleep in the heart.

children.text: vyapadeśāc ca kriyāyāṃ na cen nirdeśaviparyayaḥ | BBs_2,3.36 |
children.translated_text: And because of the designation [of the <s>jīva</s>] in action — and if not, there would be a reversal of the designation. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.36 |

children.text: itaśca jīvasya kartṛtvaṃ, yadasya laukikīṣu vaidikīṣu ca kriyāsu kartṛtvaṃ vyapadiśati śāstram- 'vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute karmāṇi tanute 'pi ca' (tai. 2.5.1) iti /
children.translated_text: For this further reason the <s>jīva</s> has agency: scripture designates its agency in both worldly and Vedic actions — 'The cognitive self (<s>vijñāna</s>) performs the sacrifice, and performs the rituals too' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5.1).

children.text:
nanu vijñānacchabdo buddhau samadhigataḥ /
kathamanena jīvasya kartṛtvaṃ sūcyata iti /
children.translated_text:
Objection: The word '<s>vijñāna</s>' is understood as [referring to] the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>).
How does it indicate the <s>jīva</s>'s agency?

children.text:
netyucyate /
jīvasyaivaiṣa nirdeśo na buddheḥ /
na cejjīvasya syānnirdeśaviparyayaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: For if it were not a designation of the <s>jīva</s>, there would be a reversal of the designation.

children.text: vijñānenetyevaṃ niradekṣyāt /
children.translated_text: [The text] would have used the instrumental case — '<s>vijñānena</s>' (by means of cognition).

children.text: tathā hyanyatra buddhivivakṣāyāṃ vijñānaśabdasya karaṇavibhaktinirdeśo dṛśyate 'tadeṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānena vijñānamādāya' (bṛ. 2.1.17) iti /
children.translated_text: For elsewhere, when the intellect is intended, the word '<s>vijñāna</s>' is seen in the instrumental case: 'Taking the cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) of those <s>prāṇas</s> by means of cognition (<s>vijñānena</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.17).

children.text: iha tu ' vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute' (tai. 2.5.1) iti kartṛsamānādhikaraṇanirdeśādbuddhivyatiriktasyaivātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ sūcyata ityadoṣaḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: But here, since '<s>vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute</s>' ('the cognitive self performs the sacrifice') (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5.1) — with the designation in co-referentiality with the agent — it is the agency of the Self distinct from the intellect that is indicated. Thus there is no fault. // 36 //

No, we say.
This is a designation of the <s>jīva</s> alone, not of the intellect.

children.text:
atrāha- yadi buddhivyatirikto jīvaḥ kartā syātsa svatantraḥ sanpriyaṃ hitaṃ caivātmano niyamena saṃpādayenna viparītam /
viparītamapi tu saṃpādayannupalabhyate /
naca svatantrasyātmana īdṛśī pravṛttiraniyamenopapadyata iti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text:
Here it is objected: If the <s>jīva</s>, distinct from the intellect, were the agent, then — being autonomous — it would invariably accomplish only what is pleasing and beneficial for itself, and not the contrary.
But it is observed to accomplish the contrary as well.
And for an autonomous Self, such engagement without restriction is not possible.
Therefore, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the following reply:

children.text: upalabdhivadaniyamaḥ | BBs_2,3.37 |
children.translated_text: The absence of restriction [is] as in the case of apprehension. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.37 |

children.text:
yathāyamātmopalabdhiṃ prati svatantro 'pyaniyameneṣṭamaniṣṭaṃ copalabhata evamaniyamenaiveṣṭamaniṣṭaṃ ca saṃpādayiṣyati /
upalabdhāvapyasvātantryamupalabdhihetūpādānopalambhāditi cet /
children.translated_text:
Just as this Self, though autonomous with respect to apprehension, apprehends without restriction both what is desired and what is not desired — so too it will accomplish without restriction both what is desired and what is not desired.
If it be said that even in apprehension, the Self is not autonomous — because the apprehension-causes are perceived as being taken up [from outside],

children.text:
na /
viṣayaprakalpanāmātraprayojanatvādupalabdhihetūnām /
upalabdhau tvananyāpekṣatvamātmanaścaitanyayogāt /
apicārthakriyāyāmapi nātyantamātmanaḥ svātantryamasti deśakālanimittaviśeṣāpekṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, even in purposeful action, the Self does not have absolute autonomy — because it depends on specific conditions of place, time, and occasion.

children.text: naca sahāyāpekṣasya kartuḥ kartṛtvaṃ nivartate /
children.translated_text: And the agency of an agent who depends on auxiliaries is not negated.

children.text: bhavati hyedhodakādyapekṣasyāpi paktuḥ paktṛtvam /
children.translated_text: For even a cook who depends on fuel, water, and the like has the status of cook.

children.text: sahakārivaicitryācceṣṭāniṣṭārthakriyāyāmaniyamena pravṛttirātmano na virudhyate // 37 //
children.translated_text: And because of the variety of auxiliaries, the engagement of the Self without restriction in accomplishing both desired and undesired results is not contradicted. // 37 //

No.
Because the apprehension-causes serve merely the purpose of presenting the object.
But with respect to apprehension itself, the Self does not depend on anything else — because of its possession of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>).

children.text: śaktiviparyayāt | BBs_2,3.38 |
children.translated_text: Because of the reversal of power. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.38 |

children.text:
itaśca vijñānavyatirikto jīvaḥ kartā bhavitumarhati /
yadi purvijñānaśabdavācyā buddhireva kartrī syāttataḥ śaktiviparyayaḥ syāt /
karaṇaśaktirbuddherhīyeta kartṛśaktiścāpadyeta /
satyāṃ ca buddheḥ kartṛśaktau tasyā evāhaṃpratyayaviṣayatvamabhyupagantavyam /
ahaṅkārapūrvikāyā eva pravṛtteḥ sarvatra darśanāt /
ahaṃ gacchāmyahamāgacchāmyahaṃ bhuñjo 'haṃ pibāmīti ca /
tasyāśca kartṛśaktiyuktāyāḥ sarvārthakārī karaṇamanyatkalpayitavyam /
children.translated_text: And for that [intellect], now endowed with the power of agency, another instrument serving all purposes would have to be postulated.

children.text: śakto 'pi hi sankartā karaṇamupādāya kriyāsu pravartamāno dṛśyata iti /
children.translated_text: For even a capable agent is observed to engage in activities by taking up instruments.

children.text: tataśca saṃjñāmātre vivādaḥ syānna vastubhedaḥ kaścit /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the dispute would be merely about nomenclature — not about any real difference.

children.text: karaṇavyatiriktasya kartṛtvābhyupagamāt // 38 //
children.translated_text: Because [in either case] agency is accepted as belonging to [something] distinct from the instrument. // 38 //

For this further reason the <s>jīva</s>, distinct from cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), can be the agent.
If the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — denoted by the word '<s>vijñāna</s>' — were itself the agent, then a reversal of power would result.
The intellect's power as an instrument would be lost, and the power of agency would be acquired.
And if the intellect had the power of agency, then it itself would have to be accepted as the object of the '<s>I</s>'-cognition.
Because in every case, activity is observed to be preceded by the '<s>I</s>'-cognition:
'I go,' 'I come,' 'I eat,' 'I drink.'

children.text: samādhyabhāvāc ca | BBs_2,3.39 |
children.translated_text: And because of the absence of <s>samādhi</s> [otherwise]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.39 |

children.text: yo 'pyayamaupaniṣadātmapratipattiprayojanaḥ samādhirupadiṣṭo vedānteṣu- 'ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyasitavya so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ' (bṛ. 2.4.5), 'ātmetyevaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānam' (muṇḍa. 2.2.6) ityevaṃlakṣaṇaḥ, so 'pyasatyātmanaḥ kartṛtve nopapadyeta /
children.translated_text: The <s>samādhi</s> (meditation/concentration) too — which is taught in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts for the purpose of realizing the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> Self — of the kind: 'The Self, verily, is to be seen, heard, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.5), 'He is to be sought, he is to be inquired into' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1), 'Meditate on the Self alone as the Self' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.6) — even that would not be possible if the Self lacked agency.

children.text: tasmādapyasya kartṛtvasiddhiḥ // 39 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the agency of the [<s>jīva</s>] is established. // 39 //

children.text: 15 takṣādhikaraṇam // sū. 40
children.translated_text: 15. The <s>Takṣādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Carpenter). <s>Sūtra</s> 40.

children.text: yathā ca takṣobhayathā | BBs_2,3.40 |
children.translated_text: And as with a carpenter — in both ways. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.40 |

children.text:
evaṃ tāvacchāstrārthavattvādibhirhetubhiḥ kartṛtvaṃ śārīrasya pradarśitaṃ, tatpunaḥ svābhāvikaṃ vā syādupādhinimittaṃ veti cintyate /
tatraitaireva śāstrārthavattvādibhirhetubhiḥ svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvamapavādahetvabhāvāditi /
children.translated_text:
Thus, by the reasons such as the purposefulness of scripture and the like, the agency of the embodied self has been demonstrated. Now the question arises: Is that [agency] intrinsic, or is it occasioned by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>)?
Therein, by the very same reasons — purposefulness of scripture and the like — [it appears that] agency is intrinsic, because there are no reasons for superseding [this conclusion].

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ /
na svābhāvikaṃ kartṛtvamātmanaḥ saṃbhavati, anirmokṣaprasaṅgāt /
kartṛtvasvabhāve hyātmano na kartṛtvānnirmokṣaḥ saṃbhavati, agnerivauṣṇyāt /
naca kartṛtvādanirmuktasyāsti puruṣārthasiddhiḥ, kartṛtvasya duḥkharūpatvāt /
children.translated_text:
Having set forth this [prima facie view], we say:
The agency of the Self cannot be intrinsic — because of the consequence of non-liberation.
For if agency were the nature of the Self, liberation from agency would not be possible — just as fire [cannot be liberated] from heat.
And for one not liberated from agency, the highest human goal is not attained — because agency is of the nature of suffering.

children.text:
nanu sthitāyāmapi kartṛtvaśaktau kartṛtvakāryaparihārātpuruṣārthaḥ setsyati /
tatparihāraśca nimittaparihārāt /
yathāgnerdahanaśaktiyuktasyāpi kāṣṭhaviyogāddahanakāryābhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
Objection: Even if the power of agency persists, the highest human goal will be attained through the avoidance of the effects of agency.
And that avoidance [comes] through the avoidance of the causes.
Just as fire, even though endowed with the power of burning, [produces] no burning-effect in the absence of firewood.

children.text:
na /
nimittānāmapi śaktilakṣaṇena saṃbandhena saṃbaddhānāmatyantaparihārāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because the complete avoidance of the causes — which are connected [to the Self] by a connection characterized as power — is impossible.

children.text: nanu mokṣasādhanavidhānānmokṣaḥ setsyati /
children.translated_text: Objection: Through the enjoining of the means of liberation, liberation will be attained.

children.text:
na /
sādhanāyattasyānityatvāt /
apica nityaśuddhabuddhamuktātmapratipādanānmokṣasiddhirabhimatā /
tādṛgātmapratipādanaṃ ca na svābhāvike kartṛtve 'vakalpeta /
tasmādupādhidharmādhyāsenaivātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ na svābhāvikam /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva' (bṛ. 4.3.7) iti /
'ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ(kaṇṭha. 3.4) iti copādhisaṃpṛktasyaivātmano bhoktetyādiviśeṣalābhaṃ darśayati /
nahi vivekināṃ parasmādanyo jīvo nāma kartā bhoktā vā vidyate /
'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' (bṛ. 4.3.23) ityādiśravaṇāt /
para eva tarhi saṃsārī kartā bhoktā ca prasajyeta, parasmādanyaśceccitimāñjīvaḥ kartā buddhyādisaṃghātavyatirikto na syāt /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because what depends on means is impermanent.
Moreover, liberation is held to be established through the teaching that the Self is eternally pure, awakened, and free.
And such a teaching of the Self would not be possible if agency were intrinsic.
Therefore, the agency of the Self is due to the superimposition of the properties of the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) alone — not intrinsic.
And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'As if thinking, as if moving' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7).
And 'The Self conjoined with senses, mind, and intellect — the wise call it the experiencer' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.4) — this shows that the Self acquires the designation 'experiencer' and such only when conjoined with limiting adjuncts.
For those who discriminate, there exists no agent or experiencer called '<s>jīva</s>' that is other than the supreme [Self].
Because of <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.23).
But then the supreme [Self] itself would be subject to <s>saṃsāra</s>, being agent and experiencer? [If it were said:] 'If the <s>jīva</s>, being a conscious entity other than the supreme [Self], were not the agent, it would be nothing but the aggregate of intellect and such [i.e., a mere material entity]' —

children.text:
na /
avidyāpratyupasthāpitatvātkartṛtvabhoktṛtvayoḥ /
tathāca śāstram- 'yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati taditara itaraṃ paśyati' (bṛ. 2.4.14) ityavidyāvasthāyāṃ kartṛtvabhoktṛtve darśayitvā vidyāvasthāyāṃ te eva kartṛtvabhoktṛtve nivārayati- 'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛ. 2.4.14) iti /
tathā svapnajāgaritayorātmana upādhisaṃparkakṛtaṃ śramaṃ śyenasyevākāśe viparipatataḥ śrāvayitvā tadabhāvaṃ suṣuptau prājñenātmanā saṃpariṣvaktasya śrāvayati- 'tadvā asyaitadāptakāmamātmakāmamakāmaṃ rūpaṃ śokāntaram (bṛ. 4.3.21) ityārabhya eṣāsya paramā gatireṣāsya paramā saṃpadeṣo 'sya paramo loka eṣo 'syaparama ānandaḥ (bṛ. 4.3.32) ityupasaṃhārāt /
tadetadāhācāryaḥ - yathā ca takṣobhayathā iti /
tvarthe cāyaṃ caḥ paṭhitaḥ /
naivaṃ mantavyaṃ svābhāvikamevātmanaḥ kartṛtvamagnerivauṣṇyamiti /
yathā tu takṣā loke vāsyādikaraṇahastaḥ kartā duḥkhī bhavati sa eva svagṛhaṃ prāpto vimuktavāsyādikaraṇaḥ svastho nivṛtto nirvyāpāraḥ sukhī bhavatyevamavidyāpratyupasthāpitadvaitasaṃpṛkta ātmā svapnajāgaritāvasthayoḥ kartā duḥkhī bhavati sa tacchramāpanuttaye svamātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma praviśya vimuktakāryakaraṇasaṃghāto 'kartā sukhī bhavati saṃprasādāvasthāyām /
tathā muktyavasthāyāmapyavidyādhvāntaṃ vidyāpradīpena vidhūyātmaiva kevalo nivṛttaḥ sukhī bhavati /
takṣadṛṣṭāntaścaitāvatāṃ'śena draṣṭavyaḥ /
takṣā hi viśiṣṭheṣu takṣaṇādivyāpāreṣvapekṣyaiva pratiniyatāni karaṇāni vāsyādīni kartā bhavati /
svaśarīreṇa tvakartaiva /
evamayamātmā sarvavyāpāreṣvapekṣyaiva manaādīni karaṇāni kartā bhavati, svātmanā tvakartaiveti /
natvātmanasthakṣṇa ivāvayavāḥ santi yairhastādibhiriva vāsyādīni takṣā manaādīni karaṇānyātmopādadīta nyasyedvā /
yattūktaṃ śāstrārthavattvādibhirhetubhiḥ svābhāvikamātmanaḥ kartṛtvamiti /
tanna /
vidhiśāstraṃ tāvadyathāprāptaṃ kartṛtvamupādāya kartavyaviśeṣamupadiśati na kartṛtvamātmanaḥ pratipādayati /
naca svābhāvikamasya kartṛtvamiti brahmātmatvopadeśādityavocāma /
tasmādavidyākṛtaṃ kartṛtvamupādāya vidhiśāstraṃ pravartiṣyate /
children.translated_text: No. Because agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) and enjoyership (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) are presented by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). And thus scripture — having shown agency and enjoyership in the state of ignorance: 'Where there is, as it were, duality, there one sees another' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14) — negates those very agency and enjoyership in the state of knowledge: 'But where everything has become the Self alone, by what would one see whom?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14). Similarly, having taught the fatigue of the Self — caused by its association with limiting adjuncts in the states of dream and waking — like a hawk flying about in space, [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches the absence of that [fatigue] in deep sleep, when the Self is embraced by the <s>Prājña</s> (all-knowing) Self: beginning with 'This indeed is his form — of fulfilled desire, of the nature of the Self, free from desire, free from sorrow' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.21), and concluding with 'This is his supreme attainment, this is his supreme treasure, this is his supreme world, this is his supreme bliss' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.32). This very thing the teacher [<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>] states: 'And as in the case of a carpenter, in both ways.' And the particle '<s>ca</s>' is read in the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but). One should not think that agency belongs to the Self intrinsically, as heat belongs to fire. Rather, just as a carpenter in the world, holding instruments like an axe in his hand, is an agent and suffers — and that very same [carpenter], having returned to his own home, having released the axe and other instruments, becomes self-possessed, retired, free from activity, and happy — so the Self, in contact with the duality presented by <s>avidyā</s>, is an agent and suffers in the states of dream and waking; and that very Self, in order to dispel that fatigue, entering its own Self, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, released from the aggregate of body and organs, becomes a non-agent and happy in the state of deep sleep (<s>saṃprasāda</s>). Likewise, in the state of liberation too, having dispelled the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> with the lamp of knowledge, the Self alone, in isolation, retired, is happy. And the carpenter illustration should be viewed in this limited respect. For the carpenter, in specific operations like carpentry, uses specifically determined instruments like an axe, and is thereby an agent. But with his own body [alone, without instruments], he is not an agent. Similarly, this Self, in all operations, uses instruments like the mind and such, and is thereby an agent; but with his own Self, he is never an agent. But unlike the carpenter, the Self does not have parts — limbs like hands and such — by which it could take up or set down instruments like the mind, as a carpenter [takes up] the axe with his hands. As for the argument that the Self's agency is intrinsic, based on reasons such as the meaningfulness of scripture — that is not so. For injunctive scripture, presupposing agency as [already] obtained [from ignorance], teaches specific actions to be performed — it does not establish agency for the Self. And it has been said that this agency is not intrinsic, because of the teaching that <s>Brahman</s> is the Self. Therefore, injunctive scripture will proceed by presupposing agency that is the product of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text:
kartā vijñānātmā puruṣa ityevañjātīyakamapi śāstramanuvādarūpatvādyathāprāpyamevāvidyākṛtaṃ kartṛtvamanuvadiṣyati /
etena vihāropādāne parihṛte /
tayorapyanuvādarūpatvāt /
children.translated_text: And scripture of the type 'The knower, the conscious self, the person is the agent' — being of the nature of a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) — merely restates the agency produced by <s>avidyā</s> as [already] obtained. By this, the [objections regarding] play (<s>vihāra</s>) and taking up (<s>upādāna</s>) are answered. Because those too are of the nature of restatement.

children.text:
nanu saṃdhye sthāne prasupteṣu karaṇeṣu sve śarīre yathākāmaṃ parivartata iti vihāra upadiśyamānaḥ kevalasyātmanaḥ kartṛtvamāvahati /
tathopādāne 'pi 'tadeṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānena vijñānamādāya' iti karaṇeṣu karmakaraṇavibhaktī śrūyamāṇe kevalasyātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ gamayata iti /
children.translated_text: But is it not so that in the dream state, when the organs are dormant, the [Self] moves about as it pleases in its own body — and this play being taught implies the agency of the Self alone? Similarly, regarding the taking up [of organs]: 'Taking consciousness from these vital breaths by consciousness' — when the object and instrument case-endings are heard for the organs, does this not imply the agency of the Self alone?

children.text:
atrocyate- na tāvatsaṃdhye sthāne 'tyantamātmanaḥ karaṇaviramaṇamasti / 'sadhīḥ svapno bhūtvemaṃ lokamatikrāmati' (bṛ.4.3.7) iti tatrāpi dhīsaṃbandhaśravaṇāt / tathāca smaranti- 'indriyāṇāmuparame mano 'nuparataṃ yadi / sevate viṣayāneva tadvidyātsvapnadarśanam' iti / 'kāmādayaśca manaso vṛttayaḥ' iti śrutiḥ / tāśca svapne dṛśyante / tasmātsamanā eva svapne viharati / vihāro 'pi ca tatratyo vāsanāmaya eva natu pāramārthiko 'sti / tathāca śrutirivākārānubaddhameva svapnavyāpāraṃ varṇayati- 'uteva strībhiḥ saha modamāno jakṣadutevāpi bhayāni paśyan' (bṛ. 4.3.13) iti / laukikā api tathaiva svapnaṃ kathayanti- ārukṣamiva giriśṛṅgamadrākṣamiva vanarājimiti /
tathopādāne 'pi yadyapi karaṇeṣu karmakaraṇavibhaktinirdeśastathāpi tatsaṃpṛktasyaivātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ draṣṭavyam /
kevale kartṛtvāsaṃbhavasya darśitatvāt /
bhavati ca loke 'nekaprakārā vivakṣā yodhā yudhyante yodhai rājā yudhyata iti /
apicāsminnupādāne karaṇavyāpāroparamamātraṃ vivakṣyate na svātantryaṃ kasyacidabuddhipūrvakasyāpi svāpe karaṇavyāpāroparamasya dṛṣṭatvāt /
yastvayaṃ vyapadeśo darśitaḥ 'vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute' iti, sa buddhereva kartṛtvaṃ prāpayati /
vijñānaśabdasya tatra prasiddhatvāt /
manonantaraṃ pāṭhācca /
'tasya śraddhaiva śiraḥ' (tai. 2.4) iti ca vijñānamayasyātmanaḥ śraddhādyavayavatvasaṃkīrtanāt /
śraddhādīnāṃ ca buddhidharmatvaprasiddheḥ /
'vijñānaṃ devāḥ sarve brahma jyeṣṭhamupāsate' (tai. 2.5.1) iti ca vākyaśeṣāt /
jyeṣṭhatvasya ca prathamajatvamasya buddhau prasiddhatvāt /
'sa eṣa vācaścittasyottarottarakramo yadyajñaḥ' iti ca śrutyantare yajñasya vāgbuddhisādhyatvāvadhāramāt /
naca buddheḥ śaktiviparyayaḥ karaṇānāṃ kartṛtvābhyupagame bhavati /
sarvakārakāṇāmeva svasvavyāpāreṣu kartṛtvasyāvaśyaṃbhāvitvāt /
upalabdhyapekṣaṃ tveṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ karaṇatvaṃ, sā cātmanaḥ /
naca tasyāmapyasya kartṛtvamasti /
nityolabdhisvarūpatvāt /
ahaṅkārapūrvakamapi kartṛtvaṃ nopalabdhurbhavitumarhati /
ahaṅkārasyāpyupalabhyamānatvāt /
nacaivaṃ sati karaṇāntarakalpanāprasaṅgaḥ /
buddheḥ karaṇatvābhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: because the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) is accepted as the instrument.

children.text: samādhyabhāvastu śāstrārthattvenaiva parihṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the [objection regarding the absence of] <s>samādhi</s> has already been answered by the very meaningfulness of scripture.

children.text: yathāprāptameva kartṛtvamupādāya samādhividhānāt /
children.translated_text: Because <s>samādhi</s> is enjoined by presupposing agency as [already] obtained.

children.text: tasmātkartṛtvamapyātmana upādhinimittameveti sthitam // 40 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the Self's agency too is caused by limiting adjuncts alone. // 40 //

To this it is replied: firstly, in the dream state, there is no complete cessation of the organs for the Self — because even there, the connection with the intellect (<s>dhī</s>) is heard: 'It moves beyond this world, accompanied by intellect, becoming a dream' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7). And thus they remember: 'When the sense organs are at rest, if the mind has not rested, it experiences sense objects — that should be known as dream-vision.' And the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Desire and such are modifications of the mind.' And these are seen in dreams. Therefore, [the Self] plays in dreams accompanied by the mind. And the play in that [state] is merely composed of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — it is not ultimately real. And thus even the <s>śruti</s> describes dream-activity as connected with mere appearance: 'As if rejoicing with women, as if eating, or as if seeing fearful things' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.13). And people in the world too describe dreams in the same way: 'It was as if I climbed a mountain peak; it was as if I saw a forest.' And regarding the taking up [of organs] too — even though object and instrument case-endings are used for the organs, the agency should be understood as belonging to the Self only as conjoined [with instruments], since the impossibility of agency for the Self in isolation has been shown. And in the world, there are various ways of expression: 'the warriors fight' and 'the king fights through the warriors.' Moreover, in this taking up [of organs], what is intended is merely the cessation of the organs' operations, not independence [of the Self] — because the cessation of the organs' operations is seen even for one who falls asleep without deliberation. And the designation you cited — 'Consciousness performs the sacrifice' — that confers agency on the intellect alone. Because the word '<s>vijñāna</s>' there is well known [as referring to intellect]. And because of its placement after 'mind.' And because in 'Its head is faith' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.4), the self made of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) is described as having faith and such as its limbs. And because faith and such are well known as properties of the intellect. And from the remainder of the sentence: 'All the gods worship consciousness as the eldest <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5.1). And because being 'eldest' is well known as meaning 'first-born,' [which applies] to the intellect. And because in another <s>śruti</s> — 'This progressive series of speech and mind is the sacrifice' — the determination that sacrifice is accomplished through speech and intellect [is established]. And there is no reversal of capacity for the intellect when the instruments' agency is accepted — because all causal factors necessarily have agency in their respective operations. But the instrumentality of these organs depends on apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>), and that [apprehension] belongs to the Self. And the Self has no agency even in that [apprehension] — because Its nature is eternal apprehension. And even agency preceded by ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) cannot belong to the apprehender — because the ego-sense too is something apprehended. And in this case, there is no need to posit another instrument —

children.text: FN: śokāntaraṃ duḥkhāspṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Śokāntara</s>' means untouched by suffering.

children.text: gatiḥ prāpyaṃ, loko bhogyaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: '<s>Gati</s>' means what is to be attained; '<s>loka</s>' means what is to be enjoyed; 'happiness.'

children.text: anyairapreryatvaṃ svasthatvam, mānasaprayatnarāhityaṃ nirvṛtatvam, kāyaceṣṭāśūnyatvaṃ nirvyāpāratvam /
children.translated_text: Not being impelled by others is 'being self-possessed' (<s>svastha</s>); absence of mental effort is 'being retired' (<s>nivṛtta</s>); absence of bodily activity is 'being free from operation' (<s>nirvyāpāra</s>).

children.text:
saṃprasādaḥ suṣuptiḥ /
jakṣat bhuñjānaiva /
children.translated_text: '<s>Saṃprasāda</s>' is deep sleep. '<s>Jakṣat</s>' means 'as if eating.'

children.text: 16 parāyattādhikaraṇam / sū. 41-42
children.translated_text: 16. The <s>Parāyatta Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Dependence on the Supreme) / <s>Sūtras</s> 41-42

children.text: parāt tu tacchruteḥ | BBs_2,3.41 |
children.translated_text: But from the Supreme, because of that <s>śruti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.41 |

children.text:
yadidamavidyāvasthāyāmupādinibandhanaṃ kartṛtvaṃ jīvasyābhihitaṃ, tatkimanapekṣyeśvaraṃ bhavatyāhosvidīśvarāpekṣamiti bhavati vicāraṇā /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvanneśvaramapekṣate jīvaḥ kartṛtva iti /
kasmāt /
apekṣāprayojanābhāvāt /
ayaṃ hi jīvaḥ svayameva rāgadveṣādidoṣaprayuktaḥ kārakāntarasāmagrīsamapannaḥ kartṛtvamanubhavituṃ śaknoti /
tasya kimīśvaraḥ kariṣyati /
naca loke prasiddhirasti kṛṣyādikāsu kriyāsvanaḍudādivadīśvaro 'paro 'pekṣitavya iti /
kleṣātmakena ca kartṛtvena jantūnsaṃsṛjata īśvarasya nairghṛṇyaṃ prasajyeta, viṣamaphalaṃ caiṣāṃ kartṛtvaṃ vidadhato vaiṣamyam /
children.translated_text: This agency of the <s>jīva</s>, which has been stated as conditioned by limiting adjuncts in the state of <s>avidyā</s> — does it occur without depending on the Lord, or does it depend on the Lord? This is the inquiry. The initial position is: the <s>jīva</s> does not depend on the Lord for its agency. Why? Because of the absence of any purpose or need for such dependence. For this <s>jīva</s>, being itself impelled by defects such as desire and hatred, and being equipped with the aggregate of other instrumental factors, is capable of experiencing agency. What would the Lord do for it? And there is no common understanding in the world that in activities like plowing and such, another Lord must be depended upon — as a bull and such [are depended upon]. And if the Lord were to conjoin beings with agency that is of the nature of suffering, His cruelty would follow. And if He were to assign unequal fruits to their agency, His partiality would follow.

children.text: nanu 'vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvāt' (bra. 1.4.17) ityuktam /
children.translated_text: But has it not been stated: 'There is no partiality or cruelty, because [He acts] with reference [to individual merit]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.4.17)?

children.text:
satyamuktam sati tvīśvarasya sāpekṣatvasaṃbhave /
sāpekṣatvaṃ ceśvarasya saṃbhavati satorjantūnāṃ dharmādharmayostayośca sadbhāvaḥ sati jīvasya kartṛtve /
tadeva cetkartṛtvamīśvarāpekṣaṃ syātkiṃviṣayamīśvarasya sāpekṣatvamucyeta /
akṛtābhyāgamaścaivaṃ jīvasya prasajyeta /
tasmātsvata evāsya kartṛtvamiti /
etāṃ prāptiṃ tuśabdena vyāvartya pratijānīte- 'parāt' iti /
avidyāvasthāyāṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātāvivekadarśino jīvasyāvidyātimirāndhasya sataḥ parasmādātmanaḥ karmādhyakṣātsarvabhūtādhivāsātsākṣiṇaścetayiturīśvarāttadanujñayā kartṛtvabhoktṛtvalakṣaṇasya saṃsārasya siddhiḥ, tadanugrahahetukenaiva ca vijñānena mokṣasiddhirbhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ /
tacchruteḥ /
yadyapi doṣaprayuktaḥ sāmagrīsaṃpannaśca jīvaḥ, yadyapi ca loke kṛṣyādiṣu karmasu neśvarakāraṇatvaṃ prasiddhaṃ, tathāpi sarvāsveva pravṛttiṣvīśvaro hetukarteti śruteravasīyate /
children.translated_text: Even though the <s>jīva</s> is impelled by defects and equipped with the aggregate [of instruments], and even though in the world the Lord's causality is not commonly known in activities like plowing and such — nevertheless, from <s>śruti</s> it is ascertained that the Lord is the cause-agent in all activities whatsoever.

children.text: tathāhi śrutirbhavati- 'eṣa hyeva sādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamebhyo lokebhya unninīyate /
children.translated_text: For thus the <s>śruti</s> states: 'It is He indeed who causes him to perform good action — him whom He wishes to lead upward from these worlds;

children.text: eṣa hyevāsādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamadho ninīṣate' (kauṣī. 3.8) iti /
children.translated_text: it is He indeed who causes him to perform bad action — him whom He wishes to lead downward' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.8).

children.text: 'ya ātmani tiṣṭhannātmānamantaro yamayati' iti caivañjātīyakā // 41 //
children.translated_text: And: 'He who, standing in the Self, controls the Self from within' — and such passages. // 41 //

True, this has been stated — but only if the Lord's dependence [on individual merit] is possible. And the Lord's dependence is possible [only] when beings have <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and their existence [as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>] is possible [only] when the <s>jīva</s> has agency. And if that very agency were dependent on the Lord, with respect to what would the Lord's dependence [on merit] be stated? And for the <s>jīva</s>, there would be the contingency of [receiving fruits] not earned [by its own effort]. Therefore, its agency is from itself alone. Rejecting this initial position with the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] asserts: 'From the Supreme.' In the state of <s>avidyā</s>, for the <s>jīva</s> — which is blind with the darkness of <s>avidyā</s>, seeing no distinction from the aggregate of body and organs — <s>saṃsāra</s> characterized by agency and enjoyership is accomplished by the permission of the Supreme Self, who is the overseer of actions, who dwells in all beings, who is the witness and the consciousness, the Lord. And liberation too must be accomplished through knowledge that is caused by His grace alone. Why? Because of that <s>śruti</s>.

children.text:
nanvevamīśvarasya kārayitṛtve sati vaiṣamyanairghaṇye syātāmakṛtābhyāgamaśca jīvasyeti /
netyucyate-
children.translated_text: But if the Lord is thus the impeller, would not partiality and cruelty [arise], and the contingency of the <s>jīva</s> [receiving fruits] not earned [by effort]? No, it is replied:

children.text: kṛtaprayatnāpekṣas tu vihitapratiṣiddhāvaiyarthyādibhyaḥ | BBs_2,3.42 |
children.translated_text: But He acts with reference to effort [previously] made, because of the meaningfulness of injunctions and prohibitions and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.42 |

children.text:
tuśabdaścoditadoṣavyāvartanārthaḥ /
kṛto yaḥ prayatno jīvasya dharmādharmalakṣaṇastadapekṣa evainamīśvaraḥ kārayati /
tataścaite coditā doṣā na prasajyante /
jīvakṛtadharmādharmavaiṣamyāpekṣa eva tattatphalāni viṣamaṃ vibhajetparjanyavadīśvaro nimittatvamātreṇa /
yathā loke nānāvidhānāṃ gucchagulmādīnāṃ vrīhiyavādīnāṃ cāsādhāraṇebhyaḥ svasvabījebhyo jāyamānānāṃ sādhāraṇaṃ nimittaṃ bhavati parjanyaḥ /
nahyasati parjanye rasapaṣpapalāśādivaiṣamyaṃ teṣāṃ jāyate, nāpyasatsu svasvabījeṣu, evaṃ jīvakṛtaprayatnāpekṣa īśvarasteṣāṃ śubhāśubhaṃ vidadhyāditi śliṣyate /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) serves to remove the fault that was raised. The Lord causes [the <s>jīva</s>] to act with reference to the effort made by the <s>jīva</s>, characterized by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. Therefore, the faults raised do not arise. The Lord, with reference to the inequality of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> created by the <s>jīva</s>, distributes the respective fruits unequally — serving merely as the efficient cause, like rain. Just as in the world, rain serves as the common efficient cause for diverse kinds of plants — shrubs, bushes, rice, barley, and such — each arising from their own specific seeds. For without rain, their inequality of sap, flower, leaf, and such does not arise; nor without their own respective seeds. Similarly, it is consistent that the Lord, acting with reference to the <s>jīva</s>'s own effort, assigns them auspicious and inauspicious [results].

children.text: nanu kṛtaprayatnāpekṣatvameva jīvasya parāyatte kartṛtve nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: But the very dependence on [previously] made effort is not possible when the <s>jīva</s>'s agency depends on the Supreme.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
parāyatte 'pi hi kartṛtve karotyeva jīvaḥ /
kurvantaṃ hi tamīśvaraḥ kārayati /
apica pūrvaprayatnamapekṣyedānīṃ kārayati pūrvataraṃ ca prayatnamapekṣya pūrvamakārayadityanāditvātsaṃsārasyetyanavadyam /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate kṛtapratnāpekṣa īśvara iti /
vihitapratiṣiddhāvaiyarthyādibhya ityāha /
evaṃ hi 'svargakāmo yajeta' 'brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ', ityevañjātīyakasya vihitasya pratiṣiddhasya cāvaiyarthyaṃ bhavati /
anyathā tadanarthakaṃ syāt /
īśvara eva vidhipratiṣedhayorniyujyeta /
atyantaparatantratvājjīvasya /
children.translated_text: Because the <s>jīva</s> would be completely dependent.

children.text: tathā vihitakāriṇamapyanarthena saṃsṛjetpratiṣiddhakāriṇamapyarthena /
children.translated_text: In that case, [the Lord] would conjoin even one who performs enjoined acts with misfortune, and even one who performs prohibited acts with fortune.

children.text: tataśca prāmāṇyaṃ vedasyāstamiyāt /
children.translated_text: And consequently, the authority of the <s>Veda</s> would be extinguished.

children.text: īśvarasya cātyantānapekṣatve laukikasyāpi puruṣakārasya vaiyarthyaṃ tathā deśakālanimittānāṃ pūrvoktadoṣaprasaṅgaścetyevañjātīyakaṃ doṣajātamādigrahaṇena darśayati // 42 //
children.translated_text: And if <s>Īśvara</s> is absolutely independent, even ordinary human effort would become futile, and the previously stated faults regarding place, time, and causes [would arise] — such kinds of faults he indicates by the word 'and so forth' [in the <s>sūtra</s>]. // 42 //

This is not a fault. For even though the agency depends on the Supreme, the <s>jīva</s> does indeed act. For the Lord causes him to act while he is acting. Moreover, [the Lord] causes [him to act] now with reference to prior effort, and caused [him to act] earlier with reference to still earlier effort — and because <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless, this is unobjectionable. But how is it known that the Lord acts with reference to [previously] made effort? 'Because of the meaningfulness of injunctions and prohibitions and such' — he says. For in this way, the meaningfulness of injunctions and prohibitions such as 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice' and 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should not be killed' is preserved. Otherwise, they would be purposeless — [if] the Lord alone were the determinant regardless of injunctions and prohibitions.

children.text: 17 aṃśādhikaraṇam / sū. 43-53
children.translated_text: 17. The <s>Aṃśa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Part) / <s>Sūtras</s> 43-53

children.text: aṃśo nānāvyapadeśād anyathā cāpi dāśakitavāditvam adhīyata eke | BBs_2,3.43 |
children.translated_text: [The <s>jīva</s> is] a part [of <s>Brahman</s>], because of the designations of difference; and in another way too — some recite [that <s>Brahman</s> assumes] the status of fisherman, gambler, and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.43 |

children.text:
jīveśvarayorupakāryopakārabhāva uktaḥ /
sa ca saṃbaddhayoreva loke dṛṣṭo yathā svāmibhṛtyayoryathā vāgnivisphuliṅgayoḥ /
tataśca jīveśvarayorapyupakāryopakārakabhāvābhyupagamātkiṃ svāmibhṛtyavatsaṃbandha āhosvidagnivisphuliṅgavadityasyāṃ vicikitsāyāmaniyamo vā prāpnoti /
athavā svāmibhṛtyaprakāreṣveveśitrīśitavyabhāvasya prasiddhatvāttadvidha eva saṃbandha iti prāpnoti /
ato bravītyaṃśa iti /
jīva īśvasyāṃśo bhavitumarhati, yathāgnervisphuliṅgaḥ /
aṃśa ivāṃśo nahi niravayavasya mukhyoṃ'śaḥ saṃbhavati /
kasmātpunarniravayavatvātsa eva na bhavati /
nānāvyapadeśāt /
'so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ' (chā. 8.7.1) 'etameva viditvā munirbhavati' ' ya ātmani tiṣṭhannātmānamantaro yamayati' iti caivañjātīyako bhedanirdeśo nāsati bhede yujyate /
children.translated_text: The relationship of the served and the server between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> has been stated. And that is observed in the world only between related [entities] — as between a master and servant, or as between fire and its sparks. Therefore, from the acceptance of the served-server relationship between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, the doubt arises: is the relationship like that of master and servant, or like that of fire and spark? In this uncertainty, either no fixed rule is obtained, or alternatively — since the governed-governor relationship is well known only in the case of master-servant and similar [relationships] — the relationship should be of that kind alone. Therefore he says 'a part.' The <s>jīva</s> should be a part of <s>Īśvara</s>, as a spark is of fire. 'A part as it were' (<s>aṃśa iva</s>) — for of that which has no parts, a primary 'part' is not possible. But why, given [<s>Brahman</s>'s] partlessness, is [the <s>jīva</s>] not simply identical [with <s>Brahman</s>]? Because of the designations of difference. '[He] is to be sought, [He] is to be inquired into' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1), 'Having known Him, one becomes a sage,' 'He who stands in the Self, who controls the Self from within' — such designation of difference is not appropriate in the absence of [actual] difference.

children.text:
nanu cāyaṃ nānāvyapadeśaḥ sutarāṃ svāmibhṛtyasārūpye yujyata ityata āha- anyathā cāpīti /
naca nānāvyapadeśādeva kevalādaṃśatvapratiptiḥ /
kiṃ tarhyanyathā cāpi vyapadeśo bhavatyanānātvasya pratipādakaḥ /
