tathāhi- eke śākhino dāśakitavādibhāvaṃ brahmaṇa āmanantyātharvaṇikā brahmasūkte- 'brahma dāśā brahma dāsā brahmaiveme kitavāḥ' ityādinā /
dāśā ya ete kaivartāḥ prasiddhāḥ, ye cāmī dāsāḥ svāmiṣvātmānamupakṣapayanti, ye cānye kitavā dyūtakṛtaste sarve brahmaiveti hīnajantūdāharaṇena sarveṣāmeva nāmarūpakṛtakāryakaraṇasaṃghātapraviṣṭānāṃ jīvānāṃ brahmatvamāha /
tathānyatrāpi brahmaprakriyāyāmevāyamarthaḥ prapañcyate- 'tvaṃ strī tvaṃ pumānasi tvaṃ kumāra uta vā kumārī /
tvaṃ jīrṇo daṇḍena vañcasi tvaṃ jāto bhavasi viśvatomukhaḥ' (śve. 4.3) iti /
'sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vicitya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadanyadāste' iti ca /
children.translated_text: 'Having fashioned all forms, the wise one, having created names, carries on [His] other [activities]' — [this too supports non-difference].

children.text: 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' (bṛca 3.7.23) ityādiśrutibhyaścāsyārthasya siddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23), this meaning is established.

children.text: caitanyaṃ cāviśiṣṭaṃ jīveśvarayoryathāgnivisphuliṅgayorauṣṇyam /
children.translated_text: And the consciousness is undifferentiated between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, just as heat is [undifferentiated] between fire and its spark.

children.text: ato bhedābhedāvagamābhyāmaṃśatvāvagamaḥ // 43 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the apprehension of both difference and non-difference, the understanding of [the <s>jīva</s>'s] part-status is arrived at. // 43 //

But this designation of difference would be even more appropriate for the master-servant model — therefore he says: 'and in another way too.' And the understanding of [the <s>jīva</s>'s] being a part does not arise from the designation of difference alone. What then? There is also a designation that conveys non-duality. For certain followers of a branch [of the <s>Veda</s>] — the <s>Ātharvanikas</s> — recite the status of fisherman, gambler, and such for <s>Brahman</s>, in the <s>Brahmasūkta</s>: '<s>Brahman</s> [is] the fishermen, <s>Brahman</s> [is] the servants, <s>Brahman</s> alone [is] these gamblers' and so on. 'Fishermen' are the well-known fishermen (<s>kaivartas</s>); 'servants' are those who exhaust themselves in service to masters; and 'gamblers' are those who play dice — all of them are <s>Brahman</s> alone. By the illustration of lowly creatures, [the <s>śruti</s>] declares the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of all <s>jīvas</s> that have entered into the aggregates of body and senses constituted by name and form. Elsewhere too, in the context of the elaboration of <s>Brahman</s>, this very meaning is set forth: 'You are woman, You are man; You are a youth and also a maiden. You are the old man tottering with a staff; being born, You become facing all directions' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.3).

children.text: kutaścāṃśatvāvagamaḥ -
children.translated_text: And for what further reason is [its] part-status understood?

children.text: mantravarṇāc ca | BBs_2,3.44 |
children.translated_text: And because of the words of the <s>mantra</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.44 |

children.text:
mantravarṇaścaitamarthamavagamayati 'tāvānasya mahimā tato jyāyāṃśca puruṣaḥ /
pādo 'sya sarvābhūtāni tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' (chā. 3.12.6) iti /
atra bhūtaśabdena jīvapradhānāni sthāvarajaṅgamāni nirdiśati /
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'beings' (<s>bhūta</s>), stationary and mobile [beings] — primarily the <s>jīvas</s> — are denoted.

children.text: 'ahiṃsansarvabhūtānyanyatra tīrthebhyaḥ' iti prayogāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the usage: 'not harming any being, except at holy places (<s>tīrthas</s>).'

children.text: aṃśaḥ pādo bhāga ityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text: 'Part' (<s>aṃśa</s>), 'quarter' (<s>pāda</s>), 'portion' (<s>bhāga</s>) — these are synonymous.

children.text: tasmādapyaṃśatvāvagamaḥ // 44 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the understanding of part-status [is obtained]. // 44 //

The words of the <s>mantra</s> too convey this meaning: 'Such is His greatness; and the <s>Puruṣa</s> is even greater. All beings are one quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of Him; the immortal three quarters are in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.6).

children.text: kutaścāṃśatvāvagamaḥ -
children.translated_text: And for what further reason is [its] part-status understood?

children.text: api ca smaryate | BBs_2,3.45 |
children.translated_text: And moreover, it is remembered [in <s>Smṛti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.45 |

children.text: īśvaragītāsvapi ceśvaraṃśatvaṃ jīvasya smaryate- 'mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ' (15.7) iti /
tasmādapyaṃśatvāvagamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the understanding of part-status [is obtained].

children.text: yattūktaṃ svāmibhṛtyādiṣveveśitrīśitavyabhāvo loke prasiddha iti /
children.translated_text: As for the argument that the governed-governor relationship is well known in the world only in cases like master and servant —

children.text: yadyapyeṣā loke prasiddhastathāpi śāstrāttvatrāṃśāṃśitvamīśitrīśitavyabhāvaśca niścīyate /
children.translated_text: although that is well known in the world, nevertheless, from scripture, the part-whole relationship and the governed-governor relationship are both ascertained here.

children.text: niratiśayopādhisaṃpannaśceśvaro nihīnopādhisaṃpannāñjīvānpraśāstīti na kiñcidvipratiṣidhyate // 45 //
children.translated_text: And that <s>Īśvara</s>, endowed with the highest limiting adjuncts, governs the <s>jīvas</s>, who are endowed with inferior limiting adjuncts — in this there is no contradiction. // 45 //

In the songs of <s>Īśvara</s> (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s>) too, the part-status of the <s>jīva</s> in relation to <s>Īśvara</s> is remembered: 'An eternal part of Myself alone has become the <s>jīva</s> in the world of living beings' (15.7).

children.text:
atrāha- nanu jīvasyeśvarāṃśatvābhyupagame tadīyena saṃsāraduḥkhopabhogenāṃśina īśvarasyāpi duḥkhitvaṃ syāt /
yathā loke hastapādādyanyatamāṅgagatena duḥkhenāṅgino devadattasya duḥkhitvaṃ tadvat /
tataśca tatprāptānāṃ mahattaraṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnuyāt /
ato varaṃ pūrvāvasthaḥ saṃsāra evāstviti samyagdarśanānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ syāditi /
children.translated_text: Here it is objected: If the <s>jīva</s>'s part-status in relation to <s>Īśvara</s> is accepted, then by [the <s>jīva</s>'s] experiencing the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Īśvara</s> too — as the whole (<s>aṃśin</s>) — would become a sufferer. Just as in the world, when suffering occurs in one of the limbs — hand, foot, and the like — <s>Devadatta</s>, the limbed one (<s>aṅgin</s>), becomes a sufferer. And consequently, [<s>Īśvara</s>] would attain even greater suffering than what has already befallen [the <s>jīva</s>]. Therefore, it would be better for <s>saṃsāra</s> to continue in its previous state — and the consequence would be that right knowledge becomes purposeless.

children.text: atrocyate-
children.translated_text: To this it is replied:

children.text: prakāśādivan naivaṃ paraḥ | BBs_2,3.46 |
children.translated_text: Like light and such — the supreme [Self] is not so [i.e., does not suffer]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.46 |

children.text:
yathā jīvaḥ saṃsāraduḥkhamanubhavati naivaṃ para īśvaro 'nubhavatīti pratijānīmahe /
jīvo hyavidyāveśavaśāddehādyātmabhāvamiva gatvā tatkṛtena duḥkhena duḥkhyahamityavidyayā kṛtaṃ duḥkhopabhogamabhimanyate /
naivaṃ parameśvarasya dehādyātmabhāvo duḥkhābhimāno vāsti /
jīvasyāpyavidyākṛtanāmarūpanirvṛttadehendriyādyupādhyavivekabhramanimitta eva duḥkhābhimāno natu pāramārthiko 'sti /
yathāca svadehagatadāhacchedādinimittaṃ duḥkhaṃ tadabhimānabhrāntyānubhavati tathā putramitrādigocaramapi duḥkhaṃ tadabhimānabhrāntyaivānubhavatyahameva putro 'hameva mitramityevaṃ snehavaśena putramitrādiṣvabhiniviśamānaḥ /
tataśca niścitametadavagamyate- mithyābhimānabhramanimitta eva duḥkhānubhava iti /
vyatirekadarśanāccaivamavagamyate /
tathāhi- putramitrādimatsu bahuṣūpaviṣṭeṣu tatsaṃbandhābhimāniṣvitareṣu ca putro mṛto mitraṃ mṛtamityevamādyudghoṣite yeṣāmeva putramitrādimattvābhimānasteṣāmeva tannimittaṃ duḥkhamutpadyate nābhimānahīnānāṃ parivrājakādīnām /
ataśca laukikasyāpi puṃsaḥ samyagdarśanārthavattvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ, kimuta viṣayaśūnyādātmano 'nyadvastvantaramapaśyato nityacaitanyamātrasvarūpasyeti /
tasmānnāsti samyagdarśanānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ /
prakāśādivaditi nidarśanopanyāsaḥ /
yathā prakāśaḥ sauraścāndramaso vā viyadvyāpyavatiṣṭhamāno 'ṅgulyādyupādhisaṃbandhātteṣvṛjuvakrādibhāvaṃ pratipadyamāneṣu tattadbhāvamiva pratipadyamāno 'pi na paramārthatastadbhāvaṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Just as light — solar or lunar — pervading space, when the limiting adjuncts such as a finger and the like assume states of being straight, bent, and such, appears to assume those states as well — yet does not in reality assume those states.

children.text: yathā cākāśo ghaṭādiṣu gacchatsu gacchanniva vibhāvyamāno 'pi na paramārthato gacchati, yathā codaśarāvādikampanāttadgate sūryapratibimbe kampamāne 'pi na tadvānsūryaḥ kampate, evamavidyāpratyupasthāpite buddhyādyupahite jīvākhyeṃ'śe duḥkhāyamāne 'pi na tadvānīśvaro duḥkhāyate /
children.translated_text: And just as space, when pots and such move, appears to move along with them — yet does not in reality move; and just as when the reflection of the sun in water contained in a dish trembles due to the trembling of the dish, the sun itself does not tremble — so too, when the part called the <s>jīva</s>, which is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> and conditioned by the intellect and the like, suffers, <s>Īśvara</s> — who possesses that [<s>jīva</s> as His part] — does not suffer.

children.text: jīvasyāpi tu duḥkhaprāptiravidyānimittaivetyuktam /
children.translated_text: And it was stated that even the <s>jīva</s>'s attainment of suffering has <s>avidyā</s> alone as its cause.

children.text: tathācāvidyānimittajīvabhāvavyudāsena brahmabhāvameva jīvasya pratipādayanti vedāntāḥ 'tattvamasi' ityevamādayaḥ, tasmānnāsti jaivena duḥkhena paramātmano duḥkhitvaprasaṅgaḥ // 46 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Vedānta</s> texts such as 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) teach the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the <s>jīva</s> itself, through the removal of the <s>jīva</s>-status caused by <s>avidyā</s>. Therefore, there is no consequence that the supreme Self becomes a sufferer through the suffering of the <s>jīva</s>. // 46 //

We affirm that the supreme <s>Īśvara</s> does not experience suffering in the way the <s>jīva</s> experiences the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For the <s>jīva</s>, under the influence of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), as if assuming the nature of body and such as its own Self, superimposes upon itself — through <s>avidyā</s> — the experience of suffering: 'I am suffering.' But for the supreme <s>Īśvara</s>, there is neither the identification with body and such, nor the superimposition of suffering. Even for the <s>jīva</s>, the superimposition of suffering has as its sole cause the error of non-discrimination of the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) such as body, senses, and the like — constituted by name and form brought about by <s>avidyā</s> — and is not ultimately real. And just as [a person] experiences suffering caused by burning, cutting, and such of one's own body through the error of identification, so too one experiences suffering pertaining to sons, friends, and the like through the error of identification alone — entering into [identification with] sons, friends, and the like through affection: 'I myself am the son, I myself am the friend.' And from this, it is ascertained with certainty that the experience of suffering has as its sole cause the error of false identification. And this is understood from the observation of the contrary. For when many people — including both those who identify with sons, friends, and the like, and others [who do not] — are seated, and when it is announced 'the son has died, the friend has died' and so forth, suffering on that account arises only in those who have the identification with sons, friends, and the like — not in those who lack identification, such as renunciants. And thus, the purposefulness of right knowledge is observed even for an ordinary person — how much more for one whose nature is eternal pure consciousness alone, who sees no other entity apart from the Self, which is void of objects. Therefore, there is no consequence of right knowledge becoming purposeless. The expression 'like light and such' introduces an illustration.

children.text: FN: itareṣvabhimānaśūnyeṣu /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'In others' — those who are devoid of identification.

children.text: smaranti ca | BBs_2,3.47 |
children.translated_text: And they (<s>Smṛti</s> texts) remember [this]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.47 |

children.text:
smaranti ca vyāsādayo yathā jaivena duḥkhena na paramātmā duḥkhāyata iti /
'tatra yaḥ paramātmā hi sa nityo nirguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
na lipyate phalaiścāpi padmapatramivāmbhasā /
karmātmā tvaparo yo 'sau mokṣabandhanaiḥ sa yujyate /
sa saptadaśakenāpi rāśinā yujyate punaḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: He is also connected with the aggregate of seventeen [constituents].'

children.text: caśabdātsamāmananti ceti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the word 'and' [in the <s>sūtra</s>], the completion of the sentence is: 'and they also recite [in <s>śruti</s>].'

children.text: 'tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti' (śve. 4.6) iti /
children.translated_text: 'Of the two [birds], one eats the sweet fig; the other, not eating, merely looks on' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.6).

children.text: 'ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ' (kaṭha. 5.11) iti ca // 47 //
children.translated_text: 'The one who is the inner Self of all beings — He is not stained by the suffering of the world, being transcendent' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.11). // 47 //

And <s>Vyāsa</s> and others remember that the supreme Self does not suffer through the suffering of the <s>jīva</s>: 'Therein, the one who is the supreme Self — He is remembered as eternal and attributeless. He is not stained by [the <s>jīva</s>'s] fruits — like a lotus petal by water. But the other one — the <s>karmātman</s> (the self of action) — he is subject to bondage and liberation.

children.text: atrāha- yadi tarhyeka eva sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmantarātmā syātkathamanujñāparihārau syātāṃ lokikau vaidikau ceti /
children.translated_text: Here it is objected: If there is indeed a single inner Self of all beings, how could there be injunctions and prohibitions — both worldly and Vedic?

children.text:
nanu cāṃśo jīva īśvarasyetyuktam /
tadbhedāccānujñāparihārau tadāśrayāvavyatikīrṇāvupapadyete kimatra codyata iti /
children.translated_text: But was it not stated that the <s>jīva</s> is a part of <s>Īśvara</s>? And because of the difference between them, injunctions and prohibitions — which pertain to the [<s>jīva</s>] — are tenable without confusion. What is objectionable here?

children.text:
ucyate- naitadevam /
anaṃśitvamapi hi jīvasyābhedavādinyaḥ śrutayaḥ pratipādayanti- 'tatsṛṣṭvā tadevānuprāviśat' (te. 2.6.1), 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' (bṛ. 3.7.23), 'mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati' (bṛ. 4.4.19), 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' (bṛ. 1.4.10) ityevañjātīyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: It is replied: it is not so. For the <s>śrutis</s> that teach non-difference also teach the partlessness of the <s>jīva</s> [i.e., its complete identity with <s>Brahman</s>]: 'Having created it, He Himself entered into it' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6.1), 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23), 'He who sees plurality here goes from death to death' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.19), 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10) — such [<s>śrutis</s>] are of this kind.

children.text: nanu bhedābhedāvagamābhyāmaṃśatvaṃ siddhyatītyuktam /
syādetadevaṃ yadyubhāvapi bhedābhedau pratipipādayiṣitau syātām, abheda eva tvatra pratipipādayiṣito brahmātmatvapratipattau puruṣārthasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: This would be so if both difference and non-difference were intended to be taught. But here, non-difference alone is intended to be taught — because the highest human goal is accomplished through the understanding that [the <s>jīva</s>] has <s>Brahman</s> as its Self.

children.text: svabhāvaprāptastu bhedo 'nūdyate /
children.translated_text: Difference, which is naturally available [i.e., empirically evident], is merely acknowledged incidentally.

children.text: naca niravayavasya brahmaṇo mukhyoṃ'śo jīvaḥ saṃbhavatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: And it was stated that a primary 'part' of partless <s>Brahman</s> is not possible for the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: tasmātparaḥ evaikaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmantarātmā jīvabhāvenāvasthita ityato vaktavyānujñāparihāropapattiḥ // 47 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the one supreme [Self] alone abides as the inner Self of all beings in the form of the <s>jīva</s> — the tenability of injunctions and prohibitions must be explained. // 47 //
But was it not stated that the part-status is established from the apprehension of both difference and non-difference?

children.text:
FN: tatra jīvaparayormadhye /
karmātmā karmāśrayo jīvaḥ /
saptadaśakena daśendrayāṇi pañca prāṇaḥ mano buddiśceti saptadaśasaṃkhyāko rāśirliṅgam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Therein' — between the <s>jīva</s> and the supreme [Self]. '<s>Karmātman</s>' — the <s>jīva</s>, whose substratum is action. 'The aggregate of seventeen' — the aggregate consisting of the ten senses, the five <s>prāṇas</s>, mind, and intellect — numbering seventeen — is the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyu - iha brahmaṇi yo nāneva kalpitabhedaśāli cetanācetanātmakaṃ viśvaṃ paśyati sa mṛtyoranantaraṃ mṛtyuṃ janmamaraṇādiparamparārūpaṃ saṃsāraṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who sees plurality here' (<s>mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyu</s>) — he who, in <s>Brahman</s>, sees the world consisting of sentient and insentient [entities] as if having imagined differences, that person attains death after death, i.e., the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> in the form of an unending series of births and deaths — this is the meaning.

children.text: tāṃ brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: That [explanation of injunctions and prohibitions], we now state:

children.text: anujñāparihārau dehasambandhāj jyotirādivat | BBs_2,3.48 |
children.translated_text: Injunction and prohibition are [tenable] because of the connection with the body — like light and such. | <s>BBs</s> 2.3.48 |

children.text:
'ṛtau bhāryāmupeyāt' ityanujñā /
''gurvāṅganāṃ nopagacchet' iti parihāraḥ /
tathā 'agnīṣomīyaṃ paśuṃ saṃjñapayet' ityanujñā /
'na hiṃsyātsarvābhūtāni' iti parihāraḥ /
evaṃ loke 'pi mitramupasevitavyamityanujñā /
śatruḥ parihartavya iti parihāraḥ /
evaṃprakārāvanujñāparihārāvekatve 'pyātmano dehasaṃbandhātsyātām /
dehaiḥ saṃbandho dehasaṃbandhaḥ /
kaḥ punardehasaṃbandhaḥ /
dehādirayaṃ saṃghāto 'hamevetyātmani viparītapratyayotpattiḥ /
dṛṣṭā ca sā sarvaprāṇināmahaṃ gacchāmyahamāgacchāmyahamandho 'hamanandho 'haṃ mūḍho 'hamamūḍha ityevamātmikā /
nahyasyāḥ samyagdarśanādanyannivārakamasti /
children.translated_text: 'One should approach one's wife during her season' — this is an injunction. 'One should not approach the wife of one's teacher' — this is a prohibition. Likewise, 'One should immolate the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal' — this is an injunction. 'One should not harm any being' — this is a prohibition. Similarly, in ordinary life: 'A friend should be served' — this is an injunction. 'An enemy should be avoided' — this is a prohibition. Such injunctions and prohibitions are tenable even when the Self is one, because of the connection with the body. 'Connection with bodies' is what is meant by 'body-connection.' What is this body-connection? It is the arising of a contrary cognition in the Self: 'This aggregate of body and such is myself alone.' And that [contrary cognition] is observed in all living beings — of the form: 'I go,' 'I come,' 'I am blind,' 'I am not blind,' 'I am deluded,' 'I am not deluded.' And there is no means other than right knowledge to remove this [false identification].

children.text:
prāktu samyagdarśanātpratataiṣā bhrāntiḥ sarvajantuṣu /
tadevamavidyānimittadehādyupādhisaṃbandhakṛtādviśeṣādaikātmyābhyupagame 'pyanujñāparihārāvavakalpyete /
samyagdarśinastarhyanujñāparihārānarthakyaṃ prāptam /
children.translated_text: Prior to right knowledge, this error is pervasive in all living beings. Thus, even while accepting the oneness of the Self, injunctions and prohibitions are made possible by the distinction created by the connection with the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) of body and such, caused by <s>avidyā</s>. But then, for one who has right knowledge, the purposelessness of injunctions and prohibitions would follow.

children.text:
na /
tasyakṛtārthatvānniyojyatvānupapatteḥ /
heyopādeyayorhi niyojyo niyoktavyaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: No. Because such a person, having accomplished [the goal], is not fit to be enjoined. For one who is to be enjoined must have something to be avoided and something to be adopted.

children.text: ātmanastvatiriktaṃ heyamupādeyaṃ vā vastvapaśyankathaṃ niyujyeta /
children.translated_text: But one who sees no entity — to be avoided or adopted — other than the Self: how could such a person be enjoined?

children.text:
nacātmātmanyeva niyojyaḥ syāt /
śarīravyatirekadarśina eva niyojyatvamiti cet /
children.translated_text: And the self cannot be enjoined upon itself. If [you say] it is only one who sees the self as different from the body that is subject to injunctions —

children.text:
na /
tatsaṃhatatvābhimānāt /
satyaṃ vyatirekadarśino niyojyatvaṃ tathāpi vyomādivaddehādyasaṃhatatvamapaśyata evātmano niyojyatvābhimānaḥ /
nahi dehādyasaṃhatatvadarśinaḥ kasyacidapi niyogo dṛṣṭaḥ /
kimutaikātmyadarśinaḥ /
naca niyogābhāvātsamyagdarśino yatheṣṭaceṣṭāprasaṅgaḥ /
sarvatrābhimānasyaiva pravartakatvādibhimānābhāvācca samyagdarśinaḥ /
tasmāddehasaṃbandhādevānujñāparihārau /
jyotirādivat /
yathā jyotiṣa ekatve 'pyagniḥ kravyātparihriyate netaraḥ /
yathāca prakāśa ekasyāpi savituramedhyadeśasaṃbaddhaḥ parihriyate netaraḥ śucibhūmiṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as the light of the single sun, when connected with an impure place, is avoided — but not [when it falls on] a pure ground.

children.text: yathā bhaumāḥ pradeśā vajravaiḍūryādaya upādīyante /
children.translated_text: And just as among earthly substances, diamonds, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's eye), and such are accepted,

children.text: bhaumā api santo narakalevarādayaḥ parihriyante /
children.translated_text: while earthly substances such as corpses and dead bodies are avoided.

children.text: yathā mūtraparīṣaṃ gavāṃ pavitratayā parigṛhyate tadeva jātyantare parivarjyate tadvat // 48 //
children.translated_text: And just as the urine and dung of cows is accepted as purificatory, while the same [substances] from other species are avoided — similarly. // 48 //

No. Because of the identification with the aggregate of body and such. True, the subject of injunctions is one who sees the difference [between self and body]. Nevertheless, just as with space and the like, the identification [with the body] — that is, the sense that the self is not unconnected with the body and such — is the ground for [the notion of being] subject to injunctions. For no one who sees the self's unconnectedness with the body and such has ever been observed to be subject to any injunction — much less one who sees the oneness [of the Self with <s>Brahman</s>]. And because of the absence of injunctions, it does not follow that one who has right knowledge would act as he pleases. Because in all cases it is identification alone that is the cause of activity, and because identification is absent in one who has right knowledge. Therefore, the acceptance and avoidance [of actions] are precisely due to the connection with the body — just as with light and such. Just as, though light is one, the cremation fire is avoided but not the other [fire].

children.text: FN: pratatā saṃtatā /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Pratatā</s>' means continuous.

children.text: viśeṣo bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Viśeṣa</s>' means distinction.

children.text: kravyaṃ māṃsamattīti kravyāt smāśānāgniḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kravyāt</s>' — one who eats flesh (<s>kravya</s>, i.e., raw meat) — [refers to] the cremation fire.

children.text: asantateś cāvyatikaraḥ | BBs_2,3.49 |
children.translated_text: And because of [the <s>jīvas</s>'] non-continuity [across bodies], there is no intermixture. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.49 |

children.text:
syātāṃ nāmānujñāpariharāvekasyāpyatmano dehaviśeṣayogāt /
yatsvayaṃ karmaphalasaṃbandhaḥ sa caikātmyābhyupagame vyatikīryeta svāmyekatvāditi cet /
children.translated_text: Let there be acceptance and avoidance for the one self based on the connection with different bodies. But the connection with the fruits of one's own <s>karma</s> — that, on the acceptance of oneness of the self, would become mixed up, since there would be one owner [for all] — if this is the objection,

children.text:
naitadevam /
asaṃtateḥ /
nahi kartṛbhoktṛścātmanaḥ saṃtataḥ sarvaiḥ śarīraiḥ saṃbandho 'sti /
upādhitantro hi jīva ityuktam /
children.translated_text: this is not so. Because of non-continuity. For the self as agent and experiencer does not have a continuous connection with all bodies. For it has been said that the <s>jīva</s> is dependent on limiting adjuncts.

children.text: upādhyasaṃtānācca nāsti jīvasaṃtānaḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of the non-continuity of the <s>upādhis</s>, there is no continuity of the <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: tataśca karmavyatikaraḥ phalavyatikaro vā na bhaviṣyati // 49 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, there will be no intermixture of <s>karma</s> or of its fruits. // 49 //

children.text: ābhāsa eva ca | BBs_2,3.50 |
children.translated_text: And [the <s>jīva</s>] is indeed a reflection (<s>ābhāsa</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.50 |

children.text:
ābhāsa eva caiṣa jīvaḥ parasyātmano jalasūryakādivatpratipattavyaḥ /
na sa eva sākṣāt /
nāpi vastvantaram /
ataśca yathā naikasmiñjalasūryake kampamāne jalasūryakāntaraṃ kampate, evaṃ naikasmiñjīve karmaphalasaṃbandhini jīvāntarasya tatsaṃbandhaḥ /
evamapyavyatikara eva karmaphalayoḥ /
ābhāsasya cāvidyākṛtatvāttadāśrayasya saṃsārasyāvidyākṛtatvopapattiriti /
tadvyudāsena ca pāramārthikasya brahmātmabhāvasyopadeśopapattiḥ /
yeṣāṃ tu bahava ātmānaste ca sarve sarvagatāsteṣāmevaiṣa vyatikaraḥ prāpnoti /
katham /
bahavo vibhavaścātmānaścaitanyamātrasvarūpā nirguṇā niratiśayāśca tadarthaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ tannimittaiṣāṃ bhogāpavargasiddhiriti sāṃkhyāḥ /
sati bahutve vibhutve ca ghaṭakuḍyādisamānā dravyamātrasvarūpāḥ svato 'cetanā ātmanastadupakaraṇāni cāṇūni manāṃsyacetanāni /
tatrātmadravyāṇāṃ manodravyāṇāṃ ca saṃyogānnavecchādayo vaiśeṣikā ātmaguṇā utpadyante /
te cāvyatirekeṇa pratyekamātmasu samavayanti sa saṃsāraḥ /
teṣāṃ navānāmātmaguṇānāmatyantānutpādo mokṣa iti kāṇādāḥ /
tatra sāṃkhyānāṃ tāvaccaitanyasvarūpatvātsarvātmanāṃ saṃnidhānādyaviśeṣāccaikasya sukhaduḥkhasaṃbandhe sarveṣāṃ sukhaduḥkhasaṃbandhaḥ prāpnoti /
syādetat /
pradhānapravṛtteḥ paruṣakaivalyārthatvādvyavasthā bhaviṣyati /
anyathā hi svavibhūtikhyāpanārthā pradhānapravṛttiḥ syāt /
tathācānirmokṣaḥ prasajyeteti /
naitatsāram /
nahyabhilaṣitasiddhinibandhanā vyavasthā śakyā vijñātum /
upapattyā tu kayācidvyavasthocyeta /
children.translated_text: A determination might be stated by some tenable ground.

children.text: asatyāṃ punarupapattau kāmaṃ mā bhūdabhilaṣitaṃ puruṣakaivalyaṃ, prāpnoti tu vyavasthāhetvabhāvādvyatikaraḥ /
children.translated_text: But in the absence of a tenable ground, let the desired isolation of the <s>puruṣa</s> simply not occur — but intermixture does follow, because of the absence of a ground for determination.

children.text: kāṇādānāmapi yadaikenātmanā manaḥ saṃyujyate tadātmāntarairapi nāntarīyakaḥ saṃyogaḥ syātsaṃnidhānādyaviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Kāṇādas</s> too, when the mind conjoins with one self, the conjunction with the other selves too is inevitable — because there is no distinction in their presence [everywhere].

children.text: tataśca hetvaviśeṣātphalāviśeṣa ityekasyātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoge sarvātmanāmapi samānaṃ sukhaduḥkhitvaṃ prasajyeta // 50 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, because of the non-distinction of the cause, there would be non-distinction of the result — when one self is connected with pleasure and pain, the same pleasure-and-pain-ness would follow for all selves as well. // 50 //

And this <s>jīva</s> is to be understood as a mere reflection (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of the supreme Self — like the reflection of the sun in water and such. It is not directly that [supreme Self]; nor is it a separate real entity. And therefore, just as when one reflection of the sun in water trembles, another reflection of the sun does not tremble — so too, when one <s>jīva</s> is connected with <s>karma</s> and its fruits, another <s>jīva</s> is not thereby connected. Thus, in this way too, there is no intermixture of <s>karma</s> and fruits. And because the reflection is created by <s>avidyā</s>, it is fitting that <s>saṃsāra</s>, which depends on it, is also created by <s>avidyā</s>. And by the removal of that [<s>avidyā</s>], the teaching of the ultimately real identity of the self with <s>Brahman</s> is also fitting. But for those who [hold that] the selves are many, and all of them are all-pervading — for them, this very intermixture would follow. How? The <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> [hold]: the selves are many, all-pervading, of the nature of mere consciousness, quality-less, and unsurpassable; <s>Pradhāna</s> serves all of them in common; and their attainment of enjoyment and liberation is caused by that [<s>Pradhāna</s>]. Given their multiplicity and all-pervasiveness, the selves — being mere substance in form, like space, pots, walls, and such — are intrinsically non-conscious. And their instruments, the atomic minds, are non-conscious. For the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, from the conjunction of the self-substances with the mind-substances, the nine <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> qualities of the self — desire and the like — are produced. And these inhere in each self without distinction — that is <s>saṃsāra</s>. And the absolute non-production of those nine qualities of the self is liberation — thus [hold] the <s>Kāṇādas</s>. Among these, for the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> first — since all selves are of the nature of consciousness, and since there is no distinction in the presence [of all selves everywhere] — when one [self] is connected with pleasure and pain, all would be connected with pleasure and pain. It might be said: the determination [arises] because the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the sake of the isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) of the <s>puruṣa</s>. For otherwise, the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> would be for the purpose of displaying its own glory. And then there would be the consequence of no liberation. This is not cogent. For a determination based on the accomplishment of what is desired [by each individual] cannot be comprehended [as a valid restriction].

children.text:
syādetat /
adṛṣṭanimitto niyamo bhaviṣyatīti /
netyāha-
children.translated_text: It might be said: the determination will be due to <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit). To that [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says:

children.text: adṛṣṭāniyamāt | BBs_2,3.51 |
children.translated_text: Because of the non-determinacy of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.51 |

children.text: bahuṣvātmasvākāśavatsarvagateṣu pratiśarīraṃ bāhyābhyantarāviśeṣeṇa saṃnihiteṣu manovākkāyairdharmalakṣaṇamadṛṣṭamuparjyate /
children.translated_text: When the selves are many and all-pervading like space — present in every body without distinction, internally and externally — <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, characterized as <s>dharma</s>, is accumulated through the activities of speech, mind, and body.

children.text: sāṃkhyānāṃ tāvattadanātmasamavāyi pradhānavarti pradhānasādhāraṇyānna pratyātmaṃ sukhaduḥkhopabhogasya niyāmakamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, since [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>] does not inhere in the self and operates within <s>Pradhāna</s> which is common [to all], it is not tenable as determining the enjoyment of pleasure and pain for each self individually.

children.text: kāṇādānāmapi pūrvavatsādhāraṇenātmamanaḥsaṃyogena nirvartitasyādṛṣṭasyāpyasyaivātmana idamadṛṣṭamiti niyame hetvabhāvādeṣa eva doṣaḥ // 51 //
children.translated_text: For the <s>Kāṇādas</s> too, since <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is produced by the conjunction of self and mind — which is common [to all selves] as stated before — this very fault [applies], because of the absence of a ground for the determination that 'this <s>adṛṣṭa</s> belongs to this self alone.' // 51 //

children.text:
syādetat /
ahamidaṃ phalaṃ prāpnavānīdaṃ pariharāṇītthaṃ prayatā itthaṃ karavāṇītyevaṃvidhā abhisaṃdhyādayaḥ pratyātmaṃ pravartamānā adṛṣṭasyātmanāṃ ca svasvāmibhāvaṃ niyaṃsyantīti /
netyāha-
children.translated_text: It might be said: intentions (<s>abhisandhi</s>) and the like — of the kind 'Let me attain this fruit,' 'Let me avoid this,' 'Let me exert thus,' 'Let me act thus' — operating individually for each self, will determine the ownership relation of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> and the selves. To that [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says:

children.text: abhisandhyādiṣv api caivam | BBs_2,3.52 |
children.translated_text: The same [fault applies] even in the case of intentions and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.52 |

children.text: abhisaṃdhyādīnāmapi sādhāraṇenaivātmamanaḥsaṃyogena sarvātmasaṃnidhau kriyamāṇānāṃ niyamahetutvānupapatteruktadoṣānuṣaṅga eva // 52 //
children.translated_text: Because even intentions and the like, being produced by the conjunction of self and mind which is common [to all selves] in the presence of all selves, cannot serve as the ground for determination — the fault stated [above] necessarily follows. // 52 //

children.text: pradeśād iti cen nāntarbhāvāt | BBs_2,3.53 |
children.translated_text: If [you say the determination comes] from the spatial portion [of the self], [we say] no — because of [all selves'] being included [in every location]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,3.53 |

children.text:
athocyeta vibhutve 'pyatmanaḥ śarīrapratiṣṭhena manasā saṃyogaḥ śarīrāvacchinna evātmapradeśe bhaviṣyatīti ataḥ pradeśakṛtā vyavasthābhisaṃdhyādīnāmadṛṣṭasya sukhaduḥkhayośca bhaviṣyatīti /
tadapi nopapadyate /
kasmāt /
antarbhāvāt /
vibhutvāviśeṣāddhi sarva evātmānaḥ sarvaśarīreṣvantarbhavanti /
tatra na vaiśeṣikaiḥ śarīrāvacchinno 'pyātmānaḥ pradeśaḥ kalpayituṃ śakyaḥ /
kalpyamāno 'pyayaṃ niṣpradeśasyātmanaḥ pradeśaḥ kālpanikatvādeva na pāramārthikaṃ kāryaṃ niyantuṃ śaknoti /
śarīramapi sarvātmasaṃnidhāvutpadyamānamasyaivātmano netareṣāmiti na niyantuṃ śakyam /
pradeśaviśeṣābhyupagame 'pi ca dvayorātmanoḥ samānasukhaduḥkhabhājoḥ kadācidekenaiva tāvaccharīreṇopabhogasiddhiḥ syāt /
samānapradeśasyāpi dvayorātmanoradṛṣṭasya saṃbhavāt /
tathāhi- devadatto yasminpradeśe sukhaduḥkhamanvabhūttasmātpradeśādapakrānte taccharīre yajñadattaśarīre ca taṃ pradeśamanuprāpte tasyāpītareṇa samānaḥ sukhaduḥkhānubhavo dṛśyate sa na syādyadi devadattayajñadattayoḥ samānapradeśamaniṣṭaṃ na syāt /
svargādyanupabhogaprasaṅgaśca pradeśavādinaḥ syāt /
brāhmaṇādiśarīrapradeśeṣvadṛṣṭaniṣpatteḥ pradeśāntaravartitvācca svārgādyupabhogasya /
sarvagatatvānupapattiśca bahūnāmātmanāṃ, dṛṣṭāntābhāvāt /
vada tāvattvaṃ ke bahavaḥ samānapradeśāśceti /
rūpādaya iti cet /
na /
teṣāmapi dharmyaṃśenābhedāllakṣaṇabhedācca /
natu bahūnāmātmanāṃ lakṣaṇabhedo 'sti /
antyaviśeṣavaśādbhedopapattiriticet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: even though the self is all-pervading, the conjunction with the mind — which is established in a body — occurs only in the portion of the self delimited by the body; therefore, the determination of intentions and such, of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, and of pleasure and pain will be based on the spatial portion [of the self] — that too is untenable. Why? Because of being included [in every location]. Because of the non-distinction in all-pervasiveness, all selves are included in all bodies. Therefore, for the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, no body-delimited spatial portion of one self can be posited [as distinct from another]. Even if such a spatial portion were posited for the partless self — precisely because it is fabricated — it cannot determine a real result. And the body too, arising in the presence of all selves, cannot be determined [to belong] to this self and not to others. Moreover, even if a distinction of spatial portions were accepted, two selves sharing the same pleasure and pain might sometimes have their enjoyment accomplished by a single body — since <s>adṛṣṭa</s> of two selves existing in the same spatial portion is possible. For example: when <s>Devadatta</s> has departed from the spatial portion in which he experienced pleasure and pain — and when [his body in] that location [is gone] and the body of <s>Yajñadatta</s> has arrived at that spatial portion — the latter too is seen to have the same experience of pleasure and pain as the former, which would not happen if <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s> did not share a common spatial portion for <s>adṛṣṭa</s>. And for one who holds the spatial-portion [doctrine], there would be the contingency of non-enjoyment of heaven and such — because <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is produced in the spatial portion of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s body and such, while the enjoyment of heaven and such is in a different spatial portion. And the all-pervasiveness of many selves is itself untenable — because of the absence of an illustration. State, then: what are the many things that exist in the same place? If [you say] form and the like — no. Because they too are non-different in their substance-aspect, and because their defining marks are different [from those of selves]. But for the many selves there is no difference of defining marks. If [you say] difference is possible because of ultimate particulars (<s>antyaviśeṣa</s>) —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: bhedakalpanāya antyaviśeṣakalpanāyāścetaretarāśrayatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the positing of difference and the positing of ultimate particulars are mutually dependent on each other.

children.text: ākāśādīnāmapi vibhutvaṃ brahmavādino 'siddhaṃ kāryatvābhyupagamāt, tasmādātmaikatvapakṣa eva sarvadoṣābhāva iti siddham // 53 //
children.translated_text: And the all-pervasiveness of space and the like too is not established for the proponent of <s>Brahman</s> — because of the acceptance that they are effects. Therefore, it is established that only in the position of the oneness of the self is there an absence of all these faults. // 53 //

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau śrīśārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye dvitīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 3 //

children.text: dvitīyādhyāye caturthaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fourth <s>pāda</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: atra pāde liṅgaśarīraśrutīnāṃ virodhaparihāraḥ
children.translated_text: In this <s>pāda</s>, the resolution of the contradiction in the <s>śrutis</s> regarding the subtle body [is presented].

children.text: 1 prāṇotpattyadhikaraṇam / sū. 1-4
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Prāṇotpattyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Origination of the Vital Breaths). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-4.

children.text: tathā prāṇāḥ | BBs_2,4.1 |
children.translated_text: So too the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths). | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.1 |

children.text:
viyadādiviṣayaḥ śrutivipratiṣedhastṛtīyena pādena parihṛtaḥ /
caturthenedānīṃ prāṇaviṣayaḥ parihriyate /
'tatra tāvat tattejo 'sṛjata' (chāndo. 6.2.3) iti, 'tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ' (taitti. 2.1.1) iti caivamādiṣūtpattiprakaraṇeṣu prāṇānāmutpajirnāmnāyate kvaciccānutpattirevaiṣāmāmnāyate 'asadvā idamagra āsīt' (tai. 2.7) 'tadāhuḥ kiṃ tadasadāsīdityṛṣayo vāva te 'gre 'sadāsīt /
tadāhuḥ ke te ṛṣaya iti /
prāṇā vāva ṛṣayaḥ' ityatra prāgutpatteḥ prāṇānāṃ sadbhāvaśravaṇāt /
anyatra tu prāṇānāmapyutpattiḥ paṭhyate- 'yathāgnerjvalataḥ kṣudrā visphuliṅgā vyuccarantyevamevaitasmādātmanaḥ sarve prāṇāḥ' iti, 'etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca' (muṇḍa. 2.1.3) iti, 'sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmāt' (mu. 2.1.8) iti, 'sa prāṇamasṛjata prāṇācchraddhāṃ khaṃ vāyurjyotirāpaḥ pṛthivīndriyaṃ mano 'nnam' (pra. 6.4) iti caivamādipradeśeṣu /
tatra tatra śrutivipratiṣedhādanyataranirdhāraṇakāraṇānirūpaṇāccāpratipattiḥ prāpnoti /
athavā prāgutpatteḥ sadbhāvaśravaṇādgauṇī prāṇānāmutpattiriti prāpnoti /
ata uttaramidaṃ paṭhati- 'tathā prāṇāḥ' iti /
kathaṃ punaratra tathetyakṣarānulomyaṃ prakṛtopamānābhāvāt /
sarvagatātmabahutvavādidūṣaṇamatītānantarapādānte prakṛtaṃ tattāvannopamānaṃ saṃbhavati sādṛśyābhāvāt /
sādṛśye hi satyupamānaṃ syāt /
yathā siṃhastathā balavarmoti /
adṛṣṭasāmyapratipādanārthamiti yadyucyeta, yathādṛṣṭasya sarvātmasaṃnidhāvutpadyamānasyāniyatatvamevaṃ prāṇānāmapi sarvātmanaḥ pratyaniyatatvamiti /
tadapi dehāniyamenaivoktatvātpunaruktaṃ bhavet /
naca jīvena prāṇā upamīyeransiddhāntavirodhāt /
jīvasya hyanutpattirākhyātā /
prāṇānāṃ tūtpattirvyācikhyāsitā /
tasmāttathetyasaṃbaddhamiva pratibhāti /
children.translated_text: The contradiction of <s>śrutis</s> regarding space and such has been resolved by the third <s>pāda</s>. Now, by the fourth, the [contradiction] regarding the <s>prāṇas</s> is being resolved. In creation-passages such as 'It created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3) and 'From that very Self, space was born' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1), the origination of the <s>prāṇas</s> is not mentioned in some places, while in other places their non-origination is mentioned: 'Non-existent indeed was this in the beginning' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7) — 'They say: What was that non-existent? — The <s>ṛṣis</s> were that non-existent in the beginning. They say: Who are those <s>ṛṣis</s>? — The <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the <s>ṛṣis</s>' — because in this passage, the existence of the <s>prāṇas</s> prior to creation is heard. But elsewhere, the origination of the <s>prāṇas</s> too is stated: 'As from a blazing fire small sparks fly in all directions — so too, from this Self, all <s>prāṇas</s> [fly forth],' and 'From this [Self] are born <s>prāṇa</s>, mind, and all the sense-organs' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.3), and 'Seven <s>prāṇas</s> arise from it' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.8), and 'He created <s>prāṇa</s>; from <s>prāṇa</s>, faith, space, air, light, water, earth, the sense-organs, mind, and food' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.4) — in such passages. Because of the contradiction of <s>śrutis</s> in various places and because no ground for determining [which view is correct] can be identified, there arises an inability to decide. Or alternatively, because of the hearing of [the <s>prāṇas</s>'] existence prior to creation, the origination of the <s>prāṇas</s> might be figurative — this too is the initial position. To this, the following answer is given: 'So too the <s>prāṇas</s>.' But how is the word 'so too' (<s>tathā</s>) applicable here, since there is nothing in the immediate context serving as the basis of comparison? The refutation of the doctrine of multiple all-pervading selves, which was completed at the end of the previous <s>pāda</s>, was the [topic just] discussed — [and] that cannot serve as a basis of comparison, because of the absence of similarity. For similarity is required for a comparison — as in 'as is a lion, so is <s>Balavarman</s>.' If it were said that [the comparison] is intended to convey a similarity of an unseen kind — namely, just as <s>adṛṣṭa</s> arising in the presence of all selves is undetermined, so too the <s>prāṇas</s> are undetermined with respect to all selves — even that would be repetitious, as it has already been stated through the undeterminedness of the body [itself]. And the <s>prāṇas</s> should not be compared with the <s>jīva</s>, as that would contradict the established doctrine. For the non-origination of the <s>jīva</s> has been declared. But the origination of the <s>prāṇas</s> is what is intended to be explained. Therefore, [the word] 'so too' appears somewhat unconnected.

kaḥ punaḥ prāṇānāṃ vikāratve hetuḥ /
śrutatvameva /
nanu keṣucitpradeśeṣu na prāṇānāmutpattiḥ śrūyata ityuktaṃ tadayuktam /
pradeśāntareṣu śravaṇāt /
nahi kvacidaśravaṇamanyatra śrutaṃ nivārayitumutsahate /
tasmācchrutatvāviśeṣādākāśādivatprāṇā apyutpadyanta iti sūktam // 1 //

yatpunaruktaṃ prāgutpatteḥ sadbhāvaśravaṇādgauṇī prāṇānāmutpattiśrutiriti /
tatpratyāha- gauṇyasaṃbhavāditi /
gauṇyā asaṃbhavo gauṇyasaṃbhavaḥ /
nahi prāṇānāmutpattiśrutirgauṇī saṃbhavati /
pratijñāhāniprasaṅgāt /
'kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati' (muṇḍa. 1.1.3) iti hyekavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ pratijñāya tatsādhanāyedamāmnāyate- 'etasmājjāyate prāṇaḥ' (muṇḍa. 2.1.3) ityādi /
sā ca pratijñā prāṇādeḥ samastasya jāgato brahmavikāratve sati prakṛtivyatirekeṇa vikārābhāvātsiddhyati /
gauṇyāṃ tu prāṇānāmutpattiśrutau pratijñeyaṃ hīyeta /
tathāca pratijñātārthamupasaṃharati- 'puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam' (muṇḍa. 2.2.11) iti, 'brahmaivedaṃ viśvamidaṃ variṣṭam' (muṇḍa. 2.2.11) iti ca /
tathā 'ātmano vā are darśanena śravaṇena matyā vijñānenedaṃ sarvaṃ viditam' ityevañjātīyakāsu śrutiṣveṣaiva pratijñā yojayitavyā /
kathaṃ punaḥ prāgutpatteḥ prāṇānāṃ sadbhāvaśravaṇam /
naitanmūlaprakṛtiviṣayam /
'aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhro hyakṣarātparataḥ paraḥ' (muṇḍa, 2.1.2) iti mūlaprakṛteḥ prāṇādisamastaviśeṣarahitatvāvadhāraṇāt /
avāntaraprakṛtiviṣayaṃ tvetatsvavavikārāpekṣaṃ pragutpatteḥ prāṇānāṃ sadbhāvāvadhāraṇamiti draṣṭavyam /
vyākṛtaviṣayāṇāmapi bhūyasīnāmavasthānāṃ śrutismṛtyoḥ prakṛtivikārabhāvaprasiddheḥ /
viyadadhikaraṇe hi 'gauṇyasaṃbhavāt' iti pūrvapakṣasūtratvādgauṇī janmaśrutirasaṃbhavāditi vyākhyātam /
pratijñāhānyā ca tatra siddhānto 'bhihitaḥ /
iha tu siddhāntasūtratvādgoṇyā janmaśruterasaṃbhavāditi vyākyātam /
tadanurodena tvihāpi gauṇī janmaśrutisaṃbhavāditi vyācakṣāṇaiḥ pratijñāhānirupekṣitā syāt // 2 //

kāryajātavaśāttvekādaśātvāmnānaṃ prāṇaviṣayaṃ pramāṇamiti sthitam /
iyamaparā sūtradvayayojanā /
saptaiva prāṇāḥ syuryataḥ saptānāmeva gatiḥ śrūyate- 'tamutkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmantaṃ sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmanti' (bṛ. 4.4.2) ityatra /
children.translated_text:
Even here [in the passage 'the navel is the tenth'], the ten <s>prāṇas</s> are spoken of with the intention of [different] openings of the body — not with the intention of [different] principles of <s>prāṇa</s>.
[This is] because of the statement 'the navel is the tenth.'
For there is no well-known <s>prāṇa</s> called 'the navel.'
But the chief <s>prāṇa</s> has the navel too as one specific seat — therefore 'the navel is the tenth' is said.
In some places, certain <s>prāṇas</s> are enumerated for the purpose of meditation; in other places, for the purpose of illustration.
Thus, when there are various scriptural statements about the number of <s>prāṇas</s>, one must discriminate — which statement has which intent.
But the statement of eleven — based on the class of functions — is the authoritative one regarding the <s>prāṇas</s>: this is established.
Here is another interpretation of the pair of <s>sūtras</s>:
There should be only seven <s>prāṇas</s>, because the departure of only seven is heard in scripture: 'When that [Self] departs, <s>prāṇa</s> departs after it; when <s>prāṇa</s> departs, all the <s>prāṇas</s> depart after it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2).

children.text:
nanu sarvaśabdo 'pyatra paṭhyate, tatkathaṃ saptanāmeva gatiḥ pratijñāyata iti /
viśeṣitatvādityāha /
saptaiva hi prāṇāścakṣurādayastvakparyantā viśeṣitā iha prakṛtāḥ 'sa yatraiva cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣaḥ parāṅparyāvartate 'thārūpajño bhavati' (bṛ. 4.4.1) 'ekībhavati na paśyatītyāhuḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.2) ityevamādinānukramaṇena /
prakṛtagāmī ca sarvaśabdo bhavati yathā sarve brāhmaṇā bhojayitavyā iti ye nimantritāḥ prakṛtā brāhmaṇāsta eva sarvaśabdenocyante nānye /
evamihāpi ye prakṛtāḥ sapta prāṇāsta eva sarvaśabdenocyante nānya iti /
children.translated_text:
Objection: But the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is also read here — so how is the departure of only seven claimed?
[To this the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: Because they are specified.
For indeed, only the seven <s>prāṇas</s> — from the eye to the skin — are specified as the subject here, through the sequential enumeration beginning with 'When the visual person turns away, one becomes unable to perceive form' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.1), 'They become unified — one does not see, they say' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2), and so forth.
And the word 'all' refers to [only] what is contextually relevant — just as in 'all <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should be fed,' where only the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are invited and are contextually relevant are referred to by the word 'all,' not others.
Similarly here too, only the seven <s>prāṇas</s> that are contextually relevant are referred to by the word 'all,' not others.

children.text: nanvatra vijñānamaṣṭamamanukrāntaṃ, kathaṃ saptānāmevānukramaṇam /
children.translated_text: Objection: But here, cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) is enumerated as the eighth — how then is the enumeration said to be of only seven?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
manovijñānayostattvābhedādvṛttibhede 'pi saptatvopapatteḥ /
tasmātsaptaiva prāṇā iti /
evaṃprāpte brūmaḥ - hastādayastvapare saptabhyo 'tiriktāḥ prāṇāḥ pratīyante-' hastau vai grahaḥ' (bṛ. 3.2.8) ityādiśrutiṣu /
grahatvaṃ ca bandhanabhāvo gṛhyate,badhyate kṣetrajño 'nena grahasaṃjñakena bandhaneneti /
sa ca kṣetrajño naikasminneva śarīre badhyate, śarīrāntareṣvi tulyatvādbandhanasya /
tasmāccharīrāntarasaṃcārīdaṃ grahasaṃjñakaṃ bandanamityarthāduktaṃ bhavati /
tathāca smṛtiḥ - puryaṣṭakena liṅgena prāṇādyena sa yujyate /
tena baddhasya vai bandho mokṣo muktasya tena ca /
iti prāṅmokṣādgrahasaṃjñakenānena bandhanenāviyogaṃ darśayati /
ātharvaṇe ca viṣayendriyānukramaṇe cakṣuṣa draṣṭavyaṃ ca ityatra tulyavaddhastādīnīndriyāṇi saviṣayāṇyanukrāmati-' hastau cādātavyaṃ copasthaścānandayitavyaṃ ca pāyuśca visarjayitavyaṃ ca pādau ca gantavyaṃ ca' ( pra. 4.8) iti /
tathā 'daśeme puruṣe prāṇā ātmaikādaśaste yadāsmāccharīrānmartyādutkrāmantyatha rodayanti' (bṛ. 3.9.4) ityekādaśānāṃ prāṇānāmutkrāntiṃ darśayati /
sarvaśabdo 'pi ca prāṇaśabdena saṃbadhyamāno 'śeṣānprāṇānabhidadhāno darśayati /
sarvaśabdo 'pi ca prāṇaśabdena saṃbadhyamāno 'śeṣānprāṇānabhidadhāno na prakaraṇavaśena saptasvevāvasthāpayituṃ śakyate, prakaraṇācchabdasya balīyastvāt /
sarve brāhmaṇā bhojayitavyā ityatrāpi sarveṣāmevāvanivartināṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ grahaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ, sarvaśabdasāmarthyāt /
sarvabhojanāsaṃbhavāttu tatra nimantritamātraviṣayā sarvaśabdasya vṛttirāśritā /
iha tu na kiñcitsarvaśabdārthasaṃkocane kāraṇamasti /
children.translated_text: But here [in the departure-passage], there is no reason to restrict the scope of the word 'all.'

children.text: tasmātsarvaśabdenātrāśeṣāṇāṃ prāṇānāṃ parigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the word 'all,' all <s>prāṇas</s> without exception are included.

children.text: pradarśanārthe ca saptānāmanukramaṇamityanavadyam /
children.translated_text: And the sequential enumeration of [only] seven is for the purpose of illustration — this is unobjectionable.

children.text: tasmādekādaśaiva prāṇāḥ śabdataḥ kāryataśceti siddham // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established — from both scripture and the class of functions — that there are exactly eleven <s>prāṇas</s>. // 6 //

This is not a fault.
Because mind and cognition are not different in essence — even though they differ in function, the number seven is tenable.
Therefore, there are only seven <s>prāṇas</s>.
Having set forth this [prima facie view], we say: The hands and other [organs of action], being additional <s>prāṇas</s> beyond the seven, are understood [to exist] — from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'The hands are indeed a grasper' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.8) and the like.
And the term '<s>graha</s>' (grasper) means a bond — by which the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower, i.e., the individual self) is bound by this bond called '<s>graha</s>.'
And the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is not bound in one body alone — because bondage is the same in other bodies [as well].
Therefore, the meaning expressed is that this bond called '<s>graha</s>' accompanies [the <s>jīva</s>] as it migrates from body to body.
And thus the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Endowed with the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), the mark-body (<s>liṅga</s>), beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, he is conjoined.
The bondage of one so bound is through that; and the liberation of the liberated is also through that.'
[This <s>smṛti</s>] shows that until liberation, there is no separation from this bond called '<s>graha</s>.'
And in the <s>Ātharvana</s> (<s>Praśna Upaniṣad</s>), in the enumeration of objects and sense-organs — 'the eye and what is to be seen' — [the text] enumerates, equally, the hands and other sense-organs with their objects: 'The hands and what is to be grasped, the organ of generation and what is to be enjoyed, the excretory organ and what is to be discharged, the feet and what is to be traversed' (<s>Praśna</s> 4.8).
Likewise, 'These ten <s>prāṇas</s> in a person, and the Self is the eleventh — when they depart from this mortal body, they cause weeping' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.4) — [this passage] shows the departure of eleven <s>prāṇas</s>.
And the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>), when connected with the word '<s>prāṇa</s>,' denoting all <s>prāṇas</s> without exception, cannot be restricted to only seven on the basis of context — because the [explicit] word is stronger than the context.
Even in 'all <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should be fed,' it is proper to include all <s>brāhmaṇas</s> without exception — because of the force of the word 'all.'

children.text:
FN: guhāyāṃ hṛdaye śerata iti guhāśayāḥ svastāneṣu nihitāḥ nikṣiptāḥ /
karmaṇā hastanirvartyādānena gṛhītaḥ saṃbaddhaḥ /
trayaḥ kālāstraikālyaṃ tadviṣaya vṛttiryasya tantraikālyavṛtti /
cakṣurādayastvakparyantā utkrāntau viśeṣitāḥ /
iha utkrāntiprakaraṇe /
prāṇādipañcakaṃ bhūtasūkṣmapañcakaṃ jñānendriyapañcakaṃ karmendriyapañcakaṃ antaḥkaraṇacatuṣṭayaṃ avidyā kāmaḥ karma ceti paryuṣṭakam /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: '<s>Guhāśaya</s>' means lying in the cave, i.e., the heart; '<s>nihita</s>' means placed, deposited.
'Grasped by action (<s>karma</s>)' means connected by the grasping that is accomplished by the hand and such.
The three times are the past, present, and future; that which has its operation in all three times is '<s>traikālyavṛtti</s>' (operating across all three times).
'From the eye to the skin, specified' — specified in the context of departure.
'Here' — in the departure-context.
The <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> consists of: the five <s>prāṇas</s>, the five subtle elements, the five cognitive sense-organs, the five organs of action, the four aspects of the inner organ, <s>avidyā</s>, desire, and <s>karma</s>.

children.text: prāṇāṇutvādhikaraṇam / sū. 7
children.translated_text: The <s>Prāṇāṇutva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Subtlety of <s>Prāṇas</s>). <s>Sūtra</s> 7.

children.text: aṇavaś ca | BBs_2,4.7 |
children.translated_text: And [they are] subtle. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.7 |

children.text:
adhunā prāṇānāmeva svabhāvāntaramabhyuccinoti /
aṇavaścaite prakṛtāḥ prāṇāḥ pratipattavyāḥ /
aṇutvaṃ caiṣāṃ saukṣmyaparicchedau na paramāṇutulyatvaṃ, kṛtsnadehavyāpikāryānupapattiprasaṅgāt /
sūkṣmā ete prāṇāḥ sthūlāścetsyurmaraṇakāle śarīrānnirgacchanto bilādahirivopalabhyeranmriyamāṇasya pārśvasthaiḥ /
paricchinnāścaite prāṇāḥ sarvagatāścetsyurutkrāntigatyāgatiśrutivyākopaḥ syāt /
tadguṇasāratvaṃ ca jīvasya na siddhyet /
sarvagatānāmapi vṛttilābhaḥ śarīradeśe syāditi cet /
children.translated_text:
Now [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] additionally states another characteristic of the <s>prāṇas</s>.
These <s>prāṇas</s> under discussion should be understood as subtle.
And their subtlety means their fineness and delimitedness — not equivalence to atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), because the consequence of the impossibility of functions pervading the entire body [would follow].
These <s>prāṇas</s> are subtle — if they were gross, then at the time of death, when departing from the body, they would be perceived by bystanders going out like a snake from a hole.
And these <s>prāṇas</s> are delimited — if they were all-pervading, then the <s>śruti</s> teaching departure, going, and coming would be contradicted.
And the <s>jīva</s>'s having their qualities as its essence would not be established.
If it be said that even for all-pervading [<s>prāṇas</s>], their function would be acquired in the region of the body,

children.text: na. vṛttimātrasya karaṇatvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: No. Because the function alone would suffice as the instrument.

children.text: yadeva hyupalabdhisādhanaṃ vṛttiranyadvā tasyaiva naḥ karaṇatvaṃ saṃjñāmātre vivāda iti karaṇānāṃ vyāpitvakalpanā nirarthikā /
children.translated_text: For whatever is the means of apprehension — whether it is function or something else — for us, that alone has the status of instrument. The dispute would be merely about nomenclature. Therefore, the postulation of all-pervasiveness for the instruments is pointless.

children.text: tasmātsūkṣmāḥ paricchinnāśca prāṇā ityadhyavasyāmaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, we conclude that the <s>prāṇas</s> are subtle and delimited. // 7 //

children.text:
FN: anudbhūtarūpasparśatvaṃ sūkṣmatvam /
paricchedo 'lpatvam /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: 'Subtlety' means having form and touch that are not manifest.
'Delimitedness' means smallness.

children.text: 4 prāṇaśraiṣṭhyādhikaraṇam / sū. 8
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Prāṇaśraiṣṭhya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Supremacy of <s>Prāṇa</s>). <s>Sūtra</s> 8.

children.text: śreṣṭhaś ca | BBs_2,4.8 |
children.translated_text: And the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>] is foremost. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.8 |

children.text:
mukhyaśca prāṇa itaraprāṇavadbrahmavikāra ityatidiśati /
taccāviseṣeṇaiva sarvaprāṇānāṃ brahmavikāratvamākhyātam /
'etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca' (muṇḍa. 2.1.3) iti sendriyamanovyatirekeṇa prāṇasyotpattiśravaṇāt /
'sa prāṇamasṛjata' (pra. 6.4) ityādi śravaṇebhyaśca /
kimarthaḥ punaratideśaḥ,
children.translated_text:
[The <s>sūtrakāra</s>] extends [the earlier teaching] — the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, like the other <s>prāṇas</s>, is a modification of <s>Brahman</s>.
And it has been stated without distinction that all the <s>prāṇas</s> are modifications of <s>Brahman</s>.
Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'From Him are born <s>prāṇa</s>, mind, and all the sense-organs' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.3) — since the origination of <s>prāṇa</s> is heard separately from [that of] the sense-organs and mind.
And from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'He created <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.4) and the like.
But what is the purpose of the extension?

children.text:
adhikāśaṅkāpākaraṇārthaḥ /
nāsadāsīye hi brahmapradhāne sūkte mantravarṇo bhavati 'na mṛtyurāsīdamṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātryā ahnu āsītpraketaḥ /
ānīdavātaṃ svadhayā tadekaṃ tasmāddhānyanna paraḥ kiñcanāsa' (ṛ.saṃ. 8.7.17) iti /
ānīditi prāṇakarmopādānātprāgutpatteḥ santamiva prāṇaṃ sūcayati /
tasmādajaḥ prāṇa iti jāyate kasyacinmatiḥ /
tāmatideśenāpanudati /
ānīcchabdo 'pi na prāgutpatteḥ prāṇasadbhāvaṃ sūcayati /
avātamiti viśeṣaṇāt /
'aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhraḥ' iti ca mulaprakṛteḥ prāṇādisamastaviśeṣarahitatvasya darśitatvāt /
tasmātkāraṇasadbhāvapradarśanārtha evāyamānīcchabda iti /
śreṣṭha iti ca mukhyaṃ prāṇamabhidadhāti- 'prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca' (chā. 5.1.1) iti śrutinirdeśāt /
jyeṣṭhaśca prāṇaḥ śukraniṣekakālādārabhya tasya vṛttilābhāt /
children.translated_text: And <s>prāṇa</s> is the eldest, because it acquires its function from the time of the depositing of semen.

children.text: na cetasya tadānīṃ vṛttilābhaḥ syādyonau niṣiktaṃ śukraṃ pūyeta na saṃbhavedvā /
children.translated_text: For if it did not acquire its function at that time, the semen deposited in the womb would putrefy and not develop.

children.text: śrotrādīnāṃ tu karṇaśaṣkulyādisthānavibhāganiṣpattau vṛttilābhānna jyeṣṭhatvam /
children.translated_text: But the sense-organs such as hearing and the rest do not have eldership — because they acquire their function only upon the formation of the specific seats such as the ear-conch and the like.

children.text: śreṣṭhaśca prāṇo guṇādhikyāt, 'na vai śakṣyāmastvadṛte jīvitum' (bṛ. 6.1.13) iti śruteḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: And <s>prāṇa</s> is foremost (<s>śreṣṭha</s>) because of the superiority of its qualities — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'We shall not be able to live without you' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.13). // 8 //

For the purpose of removing a further doubt.
For in the <s>Nāsadāsīya Sūkta</s>, which is primarily about <s>Brahman</s>, there occurs a <s>mantra</s>-passage: 'There was no death nor immortality then; there was no sign of night or day.
That One breathed (<s>ānīt</s>), without wind (<s>avātam</s>), by its own nature; apart from that, there was nothing else' (<s>Ṛgveda</s> 10.129.2).
By employing the word '<s>ānīt</s>' — which pertains to the activity of <s>prāṇa</s> — [this passage] seems to indicate that <s>prāṇa</s> existed even prior to creation.
Therefore, someone might think that <s>prāṇa</s> is unborn.
That [doubt] is dispelled by the extension.
The word '<s>ānīt</s>' too does not indicate the existence of <s>prāṇa</s> prior to creation,
because of the qualifying word '<s>avātam</s>' (without wind).
And because [the <s>śruti</s>] has shown that the root material cause (<s>mūlaprakṛti</s>) is devoid of all specific features including <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest: 'Without <s>prāṇa</s>, without mind, pure' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2).
Therefore, the word '<s>ānīt</s>' is merely for the purpose of indicating the existence of the cause.
And [the <s>sūtra</s>] says '<s>śreṣṭha</s>' (foremost) — referring to the chief <s>prāṇa</s> — because of the scriptural designation: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the eldest and the foremost' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.1.1).

children.text: FN: tarhi tadā pralayakāle mṛtyurmārako mṛtyumatkāryaṃ vā nāsīt, amṛtaṃ devabhogyaṃ nāsīt, rātryāḥ praketaścihnarūpaścandraḥ ahaḥ praketaḥ sūryaśca nāstāṃ, svadhayā pitṛdeyāgnena saha, ānīt ceṣṭāṃ kṛtavat /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Tarhi</s>' means at that time, i.e., at the time of dissolution. 'Death' (<s>mṛtyu</s>) — the destroyer, or that which has death as its effect — did not exist. '<s>Amṛta</s>' — the food of the gods — did not exist. The mark (<s>praketa</s>) of night is the moon; the mark of day is the sun — they did not exist. '<s>Svadhā</s>' — together with the fire [meant for] offerings to the ancestors. '<s>Ānīt</s>' — made movement.

children.text: 5 vāyukriyādhikaraṇam / sū. 9-12
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Vāyukriyādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Air and Activity). <s>Sūtras</s> 9-12.

children.text: na vāyukriye pṛthagupadeśāt | BBs_2,4.9 |
children.translated_text: [<s>Prāṇa</s>] is not [identical with] air or [mere] activity — because of the separate teaching. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.9 |

children.text:
sa punarmukhyaḥ prāṇaḥ kiṃsvarūpa itīdānīṃ jijñāsyate /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvacchrutervāyuḥ prāṇa iti /
evaṃ hi śrūyate- 'yaḥ prāṇaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa eṣa vāyuḥ pañcavidhaḥ prāṇo 'pāno vyāna udānaḥ samānaḥ' iti /
athavā tantrāntarīyābhiprāyātsamastakaraṇavṛttiḥ prāṇa iti prāptam /
evaṃ hi tantrāntarīyā ācakṣate- 'sāmānyā karaṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañce' ti /
atrocyate- na vāyuḥ prāṇo nāpi karaṇavyāpāraḥ /
kutaḥ - pṛthagupadeśāt /
vāyostāvatprāṇasya pṛthagupadeśo bhavati- 'prāṇa eva brahmaṇaścaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ sa vāyunā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca' (chāndo. 3.18.4) iti /
nahi vāyureva san vāyoḥ pṛthagupadiśyeta /
tathā karaṇavṛtterapi pṛthagupadeśo bhavati, vāgādīni karaṇānyanukramya tatra tatra pṛthakprāṇasyānukramaṇāt /
vṛttivṛttimatoścābhedāt /
nahi karaṇavyāpāra eva san karaṇebhyaḥ pṛthagupadiśyeta /
tathā 'etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca /
khaṃ vāyuḥ' (mu. 2.1.3) ityevamādayo 'pi vāyoḥ karaṇebhyaśca prāṇasya pṛthagupadeśā anusartavyāḥ /
naca samastānāṃ karaṇānāmekā vṛttiḥ saṃbhavati, pratyekamekaikavṛttitvātsamudāyasya cākārakatvāt /
children.translated_text:
Now the question arises: What is the nature of this chief <s>prāṇa</s>?
There, the initial position is: From <s>śruti</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> is air.
For thus [the <s>śruti</s>] declares: 'That which is <s>prāṇa</s> — that is air. That air is fivefold: <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>samāna</s>.'
Alternatively, from the view of another system, the collective function of all the instruments is <s>prāṇa</s> — this is the initial position.
For thus those of another system declare: 'The general function of the instruments — the five airs beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>.'
To this we say: <s>Prāṇa</s> is neither air, nor a mere operation of the instruments.
Why? Because of the separate teaching.
First, <s>prāṇa</s> is taught separately from air: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>; it shines and warms through air and light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.4).
For if it were air itself, it would not be taught separately from air.
Likewise, [<s>prāṇa</s>] is taught separately from the function of the instruments — because, after enumerating the instruments such as speech and the like, <s>prāṇa</s> is enumerated separately from each of them.
And because there is no difference between a function and its possessor.
For if it were merely an operation of the instruments, it would not be taught separately from the instruments.
Likewise, [passages] such as 'From Him are born <s>prāṇa</s>, mind, and all the sense-organs; space, air' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.3) and similar [texts] — which teach <s>prāṇa</s> separately from both air and the sense-organs — should also be considered.
Nor is a single collective function of all the instruments possible, since each has its own individual function, and an aggregate is not a factor of action.

children.text:
nanu pañjaracālananyāyenaitadbhaviṣyati /
yathaitapañjaravartina ekādaśapakṣiṇaḥ pratyekaṃ pratiniyatavyāpārāḥ santaḥ saṃbhūyaikaṃ pañjaraṃ cālayanti, evamekaśarīravartina ekādaśa prāṇāḥ pratyekaṃ pratiniyatavṛttayaḥ santaḥ saṃbhūyaikāṃ prāṇākhyāṃ vṛttiṃ pratilapsyanta iti /
children.translated_text:
Objection: This will be explained by the principle of the cage.
Just as eleven birds dwelling in one cage, each having its own specific function, collectively shake the one cage — so too, the eleven <s>prāṇas</s> dwelling in one body, each having its own specific function, will collectively produce the one function called <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text:
netyucyate /
yuktaṃ tatra pratyekavṛttibhiravāntaravyāpāraiḥ pañjaracālanānurūpairevopetāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ saṃbhūyaikaṃ pañjaraṃ cālayeyuriti /
tathā dṛṣṭatvāt /
iha tu śravaṇādyavāntaravyāpāropetāḥ prāṇa na saṃbhūya prāṇyuriti yuktam, pramāṇābhāvāt /
atyantavijātīyatvācca śravaṇādibhyaḥ prāṇanasya /
tathā prāṇasya śreṣṭhatvādyudghoṣaṇaṃ guṇabhāvopagamaśca taṃ prati vāgādīnāṃ, na karaṇavṛttimātre prāṇe 'vakalpate /
tasmādanyo vāyukriyābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ /
kathaṃ tarhīyaṃ śrutiḥ 'yaḥ prāṇaḥ sa vāyuḥ' iti /
children.translated_text:
No, we say.
In that [analogy], it is reasonable that birds — endowed with subsidiary functions [of their own] that are compatible with the shaking of the cage — collectively shake the one cage.
Because it is observed to be so.
But here, it is not reasonable that [the organs], endowed with subsidiary functions such as hearing and the like, collectively breathe — because there is no evidence [for this].
And because the function of breathing is utterly dissimilar to hearing and the like.
Likewise, the proclamation of the supremacy and other [qualities] of <s>prāṇa</s>, and the subordinate status of speech and the rest toward it — this is not tenable if <s>prāṇa</s> is merely the collective function of the instruments.
Therefore, <s>prāṇa</s> is different from both air and [mere] activity.
But then how is this <s>śruti</s> [to be explained]: 'That which is <s>prāṇa</s> — that is air'?

children.text: ucyate- vāyurevāyamadhyātmamāpannaḥ pañcavyūho viśeṣātmanāvatiṣṭhamānaḥ prāṇo nāma bhaṇyate na tattvāntaraṃ nāpi vāyumātram /
children.translated_text: We reply: This very air, having entered the individual body and assumed a fivefold arrangement, abiding in its specific form — is called '<s>prāṇa</s>.' It is not a separate principle, nor is it mere air.

children.text: ataścobhe api bhedābhedaśrutī na virudhyete // 9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, both the <s>śrutis</s> — of difference and of non-difference — are not contradicted. // 9 //

children.text:
syādetat /
prāṇo 'pi tarhi jīvavadasmiñśarīre svātantryaṃ prāpnoti /
śreṣṭhatvādguṇabhāvopagamācca taṃ prati vāgādīnāmindriyāṇām /
tathāhyanekavidhā vibhūtiḥ prāṇasya śrāvyate- 'supteṣu vāgādiṣu prāṇa eko hi jāgarti prāṇa eko mṛtyunānāptaḥ prāṇaḥ saṃvargo vāgādīnsaṃvṛṅ kte prāṇa itarānprāṇānrakṣati māteva putrān' iti /
tasmātprāṇasyāpi jīvavatsvātantryaprasaṅgaḥ /
taṃ pariharati-
children.translated_text: One might think: <s>Prāṇa</s> too, like the <s>jīva</s>, would attain independence in this body — because of its supremacy and because the sense organs like speech and such assume a subordinate position with respect to it. For thus the manifold glory of <s>Prāṇa</s> is taught: 'When speech and such are asleep, <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is awake; <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is not seized by death; <s>Prāṇa</s> is the absorber — it absorbs speech and the others; <s>Prāṇa</s> protects the other vital breaths like a mother protects her children.' Therefore, there would be the contingency of <s>Prāṇa</s>'s independence, just like the <s>jīva</s>. To answer this —

children.text: cakṣurādivat tu tatsahaśiṣṭyādibhyaḥ | BBs_2,4.10 |
children.translated_text: But like the eye and such, because of being taught together with them and such [reasons]. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.10 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ prāṇasya jīvavatsvātantryaṃ vyavartayati /
yathā cakṣurādīni rājaprakṛtivajjīvasya kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ ca pratyupakaraṇāni na svatantrāṇi /
tathā mukhyo 'pi prāṇo rājamantrivajjīvasya sarvārthakaratvenopakaraṇabhūto na svatantraḥ /
kutaḥ /
tatsahaśiṣṭyādibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of being taught together with them and such [reasons].

children.text: taiścakṣurādibhiḥ sahaiva prāṇaḥ śiṣyate prāṇasaṃvādādiṣu /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is taught together with those — the eye and such — in the <s>Prāṇa</s> dialogue and such [passages].

children.text: samānadharmāṇāṃ ca saha śāsanaṃ yuktaṃ bṛhadrathantarādivat /
children.translated_text: And the joint teaching of things with common properties is fitting — like <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>Sāmans</s>].

children.text: ādiśabdena saṃhatatvācetanatvādīnprāṇasya svātantryanirākaraṇahetūndarśati // 10 //
children.translated_text: By the word 'and such,' he indicates [other] reasons for negating <s>Prāṇa</s>'s independence — such as its being conjoined [with the body] and its being insentient. // 10 //

The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) removes the independence of <s>Prāṇa</s> as being like the <s>jīva</s>. Just as the eye and other sense organs — like a king's ministers — serve as instruments for the <s>jīva</s>'s agency and enjoyership and are not independent, so too the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> — like a king's prime minister — is an instrument serving the <s>jīva</s>'s all-purpose [needs] and is not independent. Why?

children.text:
syādetat /
yadi cakṣurādivatprāṇasya jīvaṃ prati karaṇabhāvo 'bhāyupagamyeta,viṣayāntaraṃ rūpādivatprasajyeta /
rūpādyālocanādibhirvṛttibhiryathāsvaṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ jīvaṃ prati karaṇabhāvo bhavati /
apicaikādaśaiva kāryajātāni rūpālocanādīni parigaṇitāni yadarthamekādaśa prāṇāḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ natu dvādaśamaparaṃ kāryajātamadhigamyate yadarthamayaṃ dvādaśaḥ prāṇaḥ pratijñāyeteti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: One might think: if <s>Prāṇa</s>'s instrumentality with respect to the <s>jīva</s> — like the eye and such — is accepted, then an additional object [of <s>Prāṇa</s>], like form and such [for the eye], would be expected. For the instrumentality of the eye and other sense organs with respect to the <s>jīva</s> arises through their respective functions — such as the apprehension of form and such. Moreover, only eleven classes of effects — apprehension of form and such — have been enumerated, for which eleven <s>prāṇas</s> have been gathered; but no twelfth class of effect is known for which this twelfth <s>prāṇa</s> could be posited. To this he replies:

children.text: akaraṇatvāc ca na doṣas tathā hi darśayati | BBs_2,4.11 |
children.translated_text: And because it is not [a sense] organ, there is no fault; for thus [scripture] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.11 |

children.text:
na tāvadviṣayāntaraprasaṅgo doṣaḥ /
akaraṇatvātprāṇasya /
nahi cakṣurādivatprāṇasya viṣayaparicchedena karaṇatvamabhyupagamyate /
nacāsyaitāvatā kāryābhāva eva /
kasmāt /
tathāhi śrutiḥ prāṇāntareṣvasaṃbhāvyamānaṃ mukhyaprāṇasya vaiśeṣikaṃ kāryaṃ darśayati prāṇasaṃvādādiṣu- 'atha ha prāṇā ahaṃśreyasi vyūdire' ityupakramya 'yasminva utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭhataramiva dṛśyate sa vaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ' (chā. 5.1.6,7) iti copanyasya pratyekaṃ vāgādyutkramaṇena tadvṛttimātrahīnaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ jīvanaṃ darśayitvā prāṇoccikramiṣāyāṃ vāgādiśaithilyāpattiṃ śarīrapātaprasaṅgaṃ ca darśayantī śrutiḥ prāṇanimittāṃ śarīrendriyasthitiṃ darśayati /
'tāvanvariṣṭhaḥ prāṇa uvāca mā mohamāpadyathāhamevaitatpañcadhātmānaṃ pravibhajyaitadbāṇamavaṣṭabhya vidhārayāmi, iti caitamevārthaṃ śrutirāha- 'prāṇena rakṣannavaraṃ kulāyam' (bṛ.
children.translated_text: There is no fault of an additional object being expected — because <s>Prāṇa</s> is not a sense organ. For <s>Prāṇa</s>'s instrumentality is not accepted as being like the eye and such — through the delimitation of a specific object. Nor does this [lack of a specific object] mean it has no function at all. Why? Because scripture shows a distinctive function of the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> that is not possible for the other vital breaths, in the <s>Prāṇa</s> dialogue and such: beginning with 'The vital breaths disputed about their own superiority' and having proposed 'That one upon whose departure the body appears most wretched — he is the best among you' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.1.6-7), [the text] shows that with the individual departure of speech and such, the living [continues] without merely that particular function, as before; but upon <s>Prāṇa</s>'s intention to depart, there is the onset of weakness in speech and the other [organs] and the contingency of bodily collapse — thus the <s>śruti</s> shows that the stability of body and sense organs is caused by <s>Prāṇa</s>. 'Then the most excellent <s>Prāṇa</s> said: "Do not be deluded; I, dividing myself fivefold, support this [body] by holding it up as an arrow"' — and the <s>śruti</s> states this very meaning: 'By <s>Prāṇa</s>, protecting the inferior nest' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>

children.text: 4.3.12) iti ca supteṣu cakṣurādiṣu prāṇanimittāṃ śarīrarakṣāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: 4.3.12) — [the text] shows that <s>Prāṇa</s> protects the body while the eye and other [organs] sleep.

children.text: 'yasmātkasmāccāṅgātprāṇa utkrāmati tadaiva tacchuṣyati' (bṛ. 1.3.19) /
children.translated_text: 'From whatever limb <s>Prāṇa</s> departs, that very [limb] dries up' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.19).

children.text: 'tena yadaśnāti yatpibati tenetarānprāṇānavati' iti ca prāṇanimittāṃ śarīrendriyapuṣṭiṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: 'By that, whatever it eats and whatever it drinks, it nourishes the other vital breaths' — thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that the nourishment of body and sense organs is caused by <s>Prāṇa</s>.

children.text: 'kasminnvahamutkrānta utkrānto bhaviṣyāmi kasminvā pratiṣṭhite pratiṣṭhāsyāmi' iti, 'sa prāṇamasṛjata' iti ca prāṇanimitte jīvasyotkrāntapratiṣṭhe darśayati // 11 //
children.translated_text: 'Upon whose departure shall I be departed? Upon whose establishment shall I be established?' and 'He created <s>Prāṇa</s>' — thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that the <s>jīva</s>'s departure and establishment are caused by <s>Prāṇa</s>. // 11 //

children.text: FN: ahaṃśreyasi svasya śreṣṭhatānimittaṃ, vyūdire vivādaṃ cakrire /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Ahaṃśreyasi</s>' — for the purpose of [establishing] one's own superiority. '<s>Vyūdire</s>' — they disputed.

children.text: aparaṃ nīcaṃ, kulāyaṃ dehākhyaṃ gṛham /
children.translated_text: '<s>Apara</s>' means inferior; '<s>kulāya</s>' means the dwelling called the body.

children.text: pañcavṛttir manovat vyapadiśyate | BBs_2,4.12 |
children.translated_text: [<s>Prāṇa</s>] has five functions and is designated like the mind. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.12 |

children.text:
itaścāsti mukhyasya prāṇasya vaiśeṣikaṃ kāryaṃ, yatkāraṇaṃ pañcavṛttirayaṃ vyapadiśyate śrutiṣu 'prāṇo 'pāno vyāna udānaḥ samānaḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.3) iti /
vṛttibhedaścāyaṃ kāryabhedāpekṣaḥ /
prāṇaḥ prāgvṛttirucchvāsādikarmā /
apānor'vāgvṛttirniśvāsādikarmā /
vyānastayoḥ saṃdhau vartamāno vīryavatkarmahetuḥ /
udāna ūrdhvavṛttirutkrāntyādihetuḥ /
samānaḥ samaṃ sarveṣvaṅgeṣu yo 'nnarasānnayatīti /
evaṃ pañcavṛttiḥ prāṇo manovat /
yathā manasaḥ pañca vṛttaya evaṃ prāṇasyāpītyarthaḥ /
śrotrādinimittāḥ śabdādiviṣayā manasaḥ pañca vṛttayaḥ prasiddhāḥ, natu kāmaḥ saṃkalpaḥ ityādyāḥ paripaṭhitāḥ parigṛhyeran /
pañcasaṃkhyātirekāt /
children.translated_text: For this further reason, the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> has a distinctive function — because it is designated as having five functions in the <s>śrutis</s>: '<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.3). And this differentiation of functions depends on the differentiation of effects. <s>Prāṇa</s> has an outward function — its action is inhalation and such. <s>Apāna</s> has a downward function — its action is exhalation and such. <s>Vyāna</s>, operating at the junction of those two, is the cause of powerful actions. <s>Udāna</s> has an upward function — it is the cause of departure [from the body] and such. <s>Samāna</s> is that which conveys the essence of food equally to all limbs. Thus, <s>Prāṇa</s> has five functions, like the mind. The meaning is: just as the mind has five functions, so too does <s>Prāṇa</s>. The five functions of the mind — having sound and such as their objects, caused by the ear and such [sense organs] — are well known. But the enumerated [functions] 'desire, volition' and such should not be accepted [as the five], because they exceed the number five.

children.text: nanvatrāpi śrotrādinirapekṣā bhūtabhaviṣyadādiviṣayāparā manaso vṛttirastīti samānaḥ pañcasaṃkhyātirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: But even here [with the five sense-based functions], there is an additional function of the mind — independent of the ear and such, having past and future and such as its objects — so the excess over the number five is the same.

children.text: evaṃ tarhi 'paramatamapratiṣiddhamanumataṃ bhavati' iti nyāyādihāpi yogaśāstraprasiddhā manasaḥ pañcavṛttayaḥ parigṛhyante 'pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtayaḥ' (pāta. yoga. sū. 1.1.6) nāma /
children.translated_text: In that case, by the principle 'that which is not refuted by the other's view is accepted as agreed upon,' the five functions of the mind well-known from the <s>Yoga</s> scripture should be accepted here too — namely, '<s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>smṛti</s> (memory)' (<s>Patañjali Yoga Sūtra</s> 1.1.6).
