children.text: bahuvṛttitvamātreṇa vā manaḥ prāṇasya nidarśanamiti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Or it should be understood that the mind serves as an illustration for <s>Prāṇa</s> merely in having multiple functions.

children.text: jīvopakaraṇatvamapi prāṇasya pañcavṛttitvānmanovaditi yojayitavyam // 12 //
children.translated_text: And it should be construed that <s>Prāṇa</s>'s instrumentality for the <s>jīva</s> is like the mind's, because of having five functions. // 12 //

children.text: FN: pramāṇaṃ pramitiḥ, viparyayo bhramaḥ, śabdajñānānupātī vastuśūnyo vikalpaḥ, tāmasī vṛttirnidrā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Pramāṇa</s>' means valid cognition; '<s>viparyaya</s>' means error; '<s>vikalpa</s>' is conceptual construction — lacking a real object but following upon verbal knowledge; '<s>nidrā</s>' is the <s>tāmasic</s> modification.

children.text: 6 śreṣṭhāṇutvādhikaraṇam / sū. 13
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Śreṣṭhāṇutva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Minuteness of the Chief [<s>Prāṇa</s>]) / <s>Sūtra</s> 13

children.text: aṇuś ca | BBs_2,4.13 |
children.translated_text: And [it is] minute. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.13 |

children.text:
aṇuścāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇaḥ pratyetavya itaraprāṇavat /
aṇutvaṃ cehāpi saukṣmyaparicchedau na paramāṇutulyatvam /
pañcabhirvṛttibhiḥ kṛtsnaśarīravyāpitvāt /
sūkṣmaḥ prāṇa utkrāntau pārśvasthenānupalabhyamānatvāt /
paricchinnaścotkrāntigatyāgatiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this chief <s>Prāṇa</s> should be understood as minute, like the other <s>prāṇas</s>. And 'minuteness' here too means subtlety and limitedness — not equality with an atom. [It pervades] the entire body through its five functions. <s>Prāṇa</s> is subtle — because at the time of departure, it is not perceived by one standing nearby. And it is limited — because of the <s>śrutis</s> about departure, going, and coming.

children.text: nanu vibhutvamapi prāṇasya samāmnāyate- 'samaḥ pluṣiṇā samo maśakena samo nāgena sama ebhistribhirlokaiḥ samo 'nena sarveṇa (bṛ. 1.3.22) ityevamādipradeśeṣu /
children.translated_text: But is not the all-pervasiveness of <s>Prāṇa</s> also taught: 'It is equal to a gnat, equal to a mosquito, equal to an elephant, equal to these three worlds, equal to this entire [universe]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.22) — in such passages?

children.text: taducyate- ādhidaivikena samaṣṭivyaṣṭirūpeṇa hairaṇyagarṇeṇa prāṇātmanaivaitadvibhutvamāmnāyate nādhyātmikena /
children.translated_text: To this it is said: this all-pervasiveness is taught of <s>Prāṇa</s> in its cosmic aspect — in its collective and individual form as belonging to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — not of the individual-level [<s>Prāṇa</s>].

children.text: apica samaḥ pluṣiṇetyādinā sāmyavacanena pratiprāṇivartinaḥ prāṇasya pariccheda eva pradarśyate tasmādadoṣaḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, by the statement of equality — 'equal to a gnat' and such — the limitedness of <s>Prāṇa</s> present in each living being is precisely what is demonstrated. Therefore, there is no fault. // 13 //

children.text: FN: pluṣirmaśakādapi sūkṣmo jantuḥ, nāgo hastī /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Pluṣi</s>' is a creature even more minute than a mosquito; '<s>nāga</s>' is an elephant.

children.text: 7 jyotirādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 14-16
children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Jyotirādi Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Fire and Such [as Presiding Deities]) / <s>Sūtras</s> 14-16

children.text: jyotirādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tu tadāmananāt | BBs_2,4.14 |
children.translated_text: But the presiding [deities], fire and such — because of the teaching of that. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.14 |

children.text:
te punaḥ prakṛtāḥ prāṇāḥ kiṃ svamahimnaiva svasmai kāryāya prabhavantyāhosviddevatādhiṣṭhitāḥ prabhavantīti vicāryate- tatra prāptaṃ tāvadyathā svakāryaśaktiyogātsvamahimnaiva prāṇāḥ pravarteranniti /
apica devatādhiṣṭhitānāṃ prāṇānāṃ pravṛttāvabhyupagamyamānāyāṃ tāsāmevādhiṣṭhātrīṇāṃ devatānāṃ bhoktṛtvaprasaṅgāccharīrasya bhoktṛtvaṃ pralīyeta /
ataḥ svamahimnaivaiṣāṃ pravṛttiriti /
evaṃ prāptaṃ idamucyate- jyotirādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tu iti /
tuśabdena pūrvapakṣo vyāvartyate /
jyotirādibhiragnyādyabhimāninībhirdevatābhiradhiṣṭhitaṃ vāgādi karaṇajātaṃ svakāryeṣu pravartata iti pratijānīte /
hetuṃ vyācaṣṭe- tadāmananāditi /
tathāhyāmananti- 'agnirvāgbhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśat' (aita. 2.4) ityādi /
agneścāyaṃ vāgbhāvo mukhapraveśaśca devatātmanādhiṣṭhātṛtvamaṅgīkṛtyocyate /
nahi devatāsaṃbandhaṃ pratyākhyāyāgnervāci mukhe vā kaścidviśeṣasaṃbandho dṛśyate /
tathā 'vāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśat' (aita. 2.4) ityevamādyapi yaujayitavyam /
tathānyatrāpi vāgeva brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ so 'gninā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca' (chā. 3.18.3) ityevamādinā vāgādīnāmagnyādijyotiṣṭvādivacanenaitamevārthaṃ draḍhayati /
'sa vai vācameva prathamāmatyavahatsā yadā mṛtyumatyamucyata so 'gnirabhavat' (bṛ. 1.3.12) iti caivamādinā vāgādīnāmagnyādibhāvāpattivacanenaitamevārthaṃ dyotayati /
sarvatra cādhyātmādhidaivatavibhāgena vāgādyagnyādyanukramaṇamanayaiva pratyāsattyā bhavati /
samṛtāvapi- 'vāgadhyātmamiti prāhurbrāhmaṇāstattvadarśinaḥ /
vaktavyamadhibhūtaṃ tu vahnistatrādhidaivacatam /
' ityādinā vāgādīnāmagnyādidevatādhiṣṭhitatvaṃ saprapañcaṃ darśitam /
yaduktaṃ svakāryaśaktiyogātsvamahimnaiva prāṇāḥ pravarteranniti /
children.translated_text: As for the statement that the <s>prāṇas</s> would function by their own power, due to their inherent capacity for their effects —

children.text: tadayuktam /
children.translated_text: that is unjustified.

children.text: śaktānāmapi śakaṭādīnāmanaḍudādyadhiṣṭhitānāṃ pravṛttidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because even things with capacity — like carts and such — are seen to function when presided over by bulls and such.

children.text: ubhayathopapattau cāgamāddevatādhiṣṭhitatvameva niścīyate // 14 //
children.translated_text: And when both interpretations are possible, it is the deity-presiding [interpretation] that is ascertained from scripture. // 14 //

Do these <s>prāṇas</s> under discussion function for their respective purposes by their own power alone, or do they function when presided over by deities? This is examined. The initial position is: the <s>prāṇas</s> would function by their own power, due to their inherent capacity for their effects. Moreover, if the functioning of the <s>prāṇas</s> when presided over by deities is accepted, then since those presiding deities would become the enjoyers, the enjoyership of the embodied [soul] would be dissolved. Therefore, they function by their own power alone. This being the position reached, it is stated: 'But the presiding [deities], fire and such.' The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the initial position. He asserts that the class of organs — speech and such — functions in their respective effects when presided over by deities such as <s>Agni</s> and others, who identify with [those organs]. He explains the reason: 'Because of the teaching of that.' For thus they teach: '<s>Agni</s>, having become speech, entered the mouth' (<s>Aitareya</s> 2.4) and such. And this becoming of <s>Agni</s> as speech and entering the mouth is stated with the acceptance of the deity's presiding role. For apart from the connection with the deity, no specific connection of <s>Agni</s> with speech or with the mouth is seen. Similarly, '<s>Vāyu</s>, having become breath, entered the nostrils' (<s>Aitareya</s> 2.4) and similar [passages] should be construed. And elsewhere too — 'Speech indeed is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>; it shines and warms with <s>Agni</s> as its light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.3) — by such statements designating speech and such as having the luminosity of <s>Agni</s> and such, this very meaning is confirmed. And: 'He first rescued speech from it; when she was freed from death, she became <s>Agni</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.12) — by such statements showing that speech and such attain the state of <s>Agni</s> and such, this very meaning is illuminated. And everywhere, the enumeration of speech and such alongside <s>Agni</s> and such, in the division of <s>adhyātma</s> (individual) and <s>adhidaivata</s> (cosmic), occurs precisely because of this close connection. In <s>Smṛti</s> too: 'The knowers of truth call speech the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>); the object to be spoken is the material (<s>adhibhūta</s>); and fire is the cosmic deity (<s>adhidaivata</s>) there' — by such [statements], the presiding of deities like <s>Agni</s> over speech and such is shown in detail.

children.text:
FN: bhāti dīpyate /
tapati svakāryaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Bhāti</s>' means 'shines.' '<s>Tapati</s>' means 'performs its own function.'

children.text: sa prāṇo vācaṃ prathamāmudgīthakarmāṇi pradhānāṃ anṛtādipāpmarūpaṃ mṛtyumatītyāvahanmṛtyunā muktāṃ kṛtvā agnidevatātmatvaṃ prāpitavān /
children.translated_text: That <s>Prāṇa</s> rescued speech — which was foremost in the <s>Udgītha</s> rites — from death in the form of the evil of falsehood and such, freeing her from death and causing her to attain the nature of the deity <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yadapyuktaṃ devatānāmevādhiṣṭhātrīṇāṃ bhoktṛtvaprasaṅgo na śārīrasyeti tatparihriyate-
children.translated_text: And the objection that was raised — that the presiding deities would become the enjoyers, not the embodied [soul] — is answered:

children.text: prāṇavatā śabdāt | BBs_2,4.15 |
children.translated_text: Because of the word [indicating] one possessing <s>Prāṇa</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.15 |

children.text:
satīṣvapi prāṇānāmadhiṣṭātrīṣu devatāsu prāṇavatā kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasvāminā śārīreṇaivaiṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ saṃbandhaḥ śruteravagamyate /
tathāhi śrutiḥ - 'atha yatraitadākāśamanuviṣaṇṇaṃ cakṣuḥ sa cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣo darśanāya takṣuratha yo vededaṃ jighrāṇīti sa ātmā gandhāya ghrāṇam' (chā. 8.124) ityevañjātīyakā śārīreṇaiva prāṇānāṃ saṃbandhaṃ śrāvayati /
children.translated_text: Even though the presiding deities of the <s>prāṇas</s> exist, it is understood from <s>śruti</s> that the connection of these <s>prāṇas</s> is with the embodied [soul] alone — the lord of the aggregate of body and organs, the one possessing <s>Prāṇa</s>. For thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Now, where this eye, which has entered the space [of the eye-socket] — he is the person of the eye, for seeing; the one who knows "let me smell this" — he is the Self, [and] the nose is for smelling' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.4) — such [passages] teach the connection of the <s>prāṇas</s> with the embodied [soul] alone.

children.text: apicānekatvātpratikaraṇamadhiṣṭhātrīṇāṃ devatānāṃ na bhoktṛtvamasmiñśarīre 'vakalpate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, because of the multiplicity of the presiding deities — one for each sense organ — their enjoyership in this body is not possible.

children.text: eko hyevamasmiñśarīre śārīro bhoktā pratisaṃdhānādisaṃbhavādavagamyate // 15 //
children.translated_text: For only one embodied [soul] in this body is understood as the enjoyer — because of the possibility of memory-connection and such. // 15 //

children.text: FN: atha dehe prāgapraveśānantaraṃ yatra golake etacchidramanupraviṣṭaṃ cakṣurindriyaṃ tatra cakṣuṣyabhimānī sa ātmā cākṣuṣaḥ tasya rūpadarśanāya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Now, in the body, after the prior entry, where the sense organ of sight has entered the aperture [of the eye-socket] — the presiding self of the eye is the cākṣuṣa [deity]; the eye is for his seeing of form.'

children.text: tasya ca nityatvāt | BBs_2,4.16 |
children.translated_text: And because of its (the embodied soul's) permanence. | <s>BBs</s> 2.4.16 |

children.text:
tasya ca śārīrasyāsmiñśarīre bhoktṛtvena nityatvena puṇyapāpopalepasaṃbhavātsukhaduḥkhopabhogasaṃbhavācca na devatānām /
tā hi parasminnaiśvarye pade 'vatiṣṭhamānā na hine 'smiñśarīre bhoktṛtvaṃ pratilabdhumarhanti /
śrutiśca bhavati- 'puṇyamevāmuṃ gacchati na ha vai devānpāpaṃ gacchati' (bṛ. 1.5.3) iti śārīreṇaiva ca nityaḥ prāṇānāṃ saṃbandha utkrāntyādiṣu tadanuvṛttidarśanāt /
'tamutkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmati prāṇamanūtkrāmantaṃ sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmanti' (bṛ. 4.4.2)
children.translated_text: And because the embodied [soul] has permanence as the enjoyer in this body, and because the staining by merit and demerit is possible [for it], and because the experience of pleasure and pain is possible [for it] — but not for the deities. For they, abiding in the supreme divine station, cannot be expected to attain enjoyership in this inferior body. And the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Merit alone goes to him; evil does not reach the gods' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.3). And the connection of the <s>prāṇas</s> with the embodied [soul] alone is permanent — because in departure and such, their following [the soul] is observed: 'When it departs, <s>Prāṇa</s> departs after it; when <s>Prāṇa</s> departs, all the <s>prāṇas</s> depart after it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2).

children.text:
ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tasmātsatīṣvapi karaṇānāṃ niyantrīṣu devatāsu na śārīrasya bhoktṛtvamapagacchati /
children.translated_text: and such <s>śruti</s> passages. Therefore, even though deities preside over the instruments, the experiencer-ship of the embodied self is not lost.

children.text: karaṇapakṣasyaiva hi devatā na bhoktṛpakṣasyeti // 16 //
children.translated_text: For the deities belong to the instrument-side, not to the experiencer-side. // 16 //

children.text: 8 indriyādhikaraṇam / sū. 17-19
children.translated_text: 8. The <s>Indriyādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Sense-organs). <s>Sūtras</s> 17-19.

children.text: ta indriyāṇi tadvyapadeśād anyatra śreṣṭhāt | BBs_2,4.17 |
children.translated_text: Those [other prāṇas] are sense-organs — because of their designation [as different from the chief <s>prāṇa</s>], excepting the chief (<s>śreṣṭha</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.17 |

children.text:
mukhyaścaika itare caikādaśa prāṇā anukrāntāḥ /
tatredamaparaṃ saṃdihyate /
kiṃ mukhyasyaiva prāṇasya vṛttibhedā itare prāṇā āhosvittattvāntarāṇīti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ, mukhyasyaivetare vṛttibhedā iti /
kutaḥ - śruteḥ /
tathāhi śrutirmukhyamitarāṃśca prāṇānsaṃnidhāpya mukhyātmatāmitareṣāṃ khyāpayati- 'hantāsyaiva sarve rūpamasāmeti ta etasyaiva sarve rūpamabhavan' (bṛ. 1.5.21) iti /
prāṇaikaśabdatvāccaikatvādhyavasāyaḥ /
itarathā hyanyāyyamanekārthatvaṃ prāṇaśabdasya prasajyeta /
ekatra vā mukhyatvamitaratra vā lākṣaṇikatvāmāpadyeta /
tasmādyathaikasyaiva prāṇasya prāṇādyāḥ pañca vṛttaya evaṃ vāgādyā apyekādaśeti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tattvāntarāṇyeva prāṇādvāgādīnīti /
kutaḥ -
children.translated_text: One chief [<s>prāṇa</s>] and eleven others have been enumerated. There arises a further doubt: Are the other <s>prāṇas</s> merely functional modifications of the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, or are they distinct principles? What is the prima facie view? That the others are merely functional modifications of the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>]. Why? From <s>śruti</s>. For the <s>śruti</s>, having brought together the chief and the other <s>prāṇas</s>, declares the identity of the others with the chief: 'Come, let us all assume the form of this one — and they all assumed the form of this one' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21). And because the single word '<s>prāṇa</s>' [is used for all], the conclusion of oneness [follows]. For otherwise, the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' would unjustifiably have multiple meanings. In one place it would be used in the primary sense, and in another in the secondary sense. Therefore, just as the five [functions] — <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — are functions of the single <s>prāṇa</s>, so too the eleven — speech and the rest — [are functions of the single <s>prāṇa</s>]. Given this position, we say: Speech and the rest are indeed distinct principles from <s>prāṇa</s>. Why?

children.text:
vyapadeśābhāvāt /
ko 'yaṃ vyapadeśabhedaḥ /
te prakṛtāḥ prāṇāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ varjayitvāvaśiṣṭā ekādaśenjadriyāṇītyucyante /
śrutāvevaṃ vyapadeśadarśanāt /
'etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca' (mu. 2.1.3) iti hyevañjātīyakeṣu pradeśeṣu pṛthakprāṇo vyapadiśyate pṛthaktcendriyāṇi /
children.translated_text: Because of [the difference in] designation. What is this difference of designation? Those <s>prāṇas</s> under discussion — remaining after excluding the chief — are called eleven sense-organs (<s>indriyas</s>). Because such a difference of designation is observed in <s>śruti</s>: 'From this [Self] are born <s>prāṇa</s>, mind, and all the sense-organs' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.3) — in passages of this kind, <s>prāṇa</s> is designated separately, and the sense-organs are designated separately.

children.text:
nanu manaso 'pyevaṃ sati varjanamindriyatvena prāṇavatsyāt, 'manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca' iti pṛthagvyapadeśadarśanāt /
satyametat /
smṛtau tvekādaśendriyāṇīti mano 'pīndriyatvena śrotrādivatsaṃgṛhyate /
prāṇasya tvindriyatvaṃ na śrutau smṛtau vā prasiddhamasti /
children.translated_text: But the status of <s>prāṇa</s> as a sense-organ is not well known either in <s>śruti</s> or in <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: vyapadeśabhedaścāyaṃ tattvabhedapakṣa upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And this difference of designation is tenable on the view that they are distinct principles.

children.text: tattvaikatve tu sa evaikaḥ sanprāṇa indriyavyapadeśaṃ labhate na labhate ceti vipratiṣiddham /
children.translated_text: But if they were one in principle, then the same single <s>prāṇa</s> would receive the designation 'sense-organ' and also not receive it — which is contradictory.

children.text: tasmāttattvāntarabhūtā mukhyāditare // 17 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the others are distinct principles from the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>]. // 17 //

But if this is so, the mind too should be excluded from the status of a sense-organ, like <s>prāṇa</s> — since a separate designation is observed in 'mind and all the sense-organs.' True, this is so. But in <s>smṛti</s>, 'there are eleven sense-organs' — the mind too is included as a sense-organ, like hearing and such.

children.text: FN: asyaiva mukhyaprāṇasya rūpaṃ asāma bhavemeti saṃkalpya, te vāgādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Let us assume the form of this very chief <s>prāṇa</s>' — having resolved thus, they — speech and the rest.

children.text: kutaśca tattavāntarabhūtāḥ -
children.translated_text: And for what further reason are they distinct principles?

children.text: bhedaśruteḥ | BBs_2,4.18 |
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s> on their difference. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.18 |

children.text: bhedena vāgādibhyaḥ prāṇaḥ sarvatra śrūyate- 'te ha vācamūcuḥ' (bṛ. 1.3.2) ityupakramya vāgādīnasurapāpmavidhvastānupanyasyopasaṃhṛtya vāgādiprakaraṇam 'atha hemamāsanyaṃ prāṇamūcuḥ' ityasuravidhvaṃsino mukhyasya prāṇasya pṛthagupakramāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is heard everywhere as different from speech and the rest. Having begun with 'They said to speech' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.2), and having described speech and the rest as stricken by the evil of the <s>Asuras</s> and presented [their section], and having concluded the section on speech and the rest — 'Then they said to this vital breath (<s>āsanya prāṇa</s>)' — [the text] makes a separate commencement for the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, the one not overcome by the <s>Asuras</s>.

children.text: tathā 'mano vācaṃ prāṇaṃ tānyātmane 'kuruta' ityevamādyā api bhedaśrutaya udāhartavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, '<s>Prāṇa</s>, mind, speech — these It made for Itself' — passages establishing difference of this kind should also be cited.

children.text: tasmādapi tattvāntarabhūtā mukhyāditare // 18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the others are distinct principles from the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>]. // 18 //

children.text: kutaśca tattvāntarabhūtāḥ -
children.translated_text: And for what further reason are they distinct principles?

children.text: vailakṣaṇyāc ca | BBs_2,4.19 |
children.translated_text: And because of dissimilarity. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.19 |

children.text:
vailakṣaṇyaṃ ca bhavati mukhyasyetareṣāṃ ca /
suṣupteṣu vāgādiṣu mukhya eko jāgarti sa eva caiko mṛtyunānāpta āptāstvitare /
tasyaiva ca sthityukrāntibhyāṃ dehadhāraṇapatanahetutvaṃ nendriyāṇām /
viṣayālocanahetutvaṃ cendriyāṇāṃ na prāṇasyevañjātīyako bhūyāllakṣaṇabhedaḥ prāṇendriyāṇām /
tasmādapyeṣāṃ tattvāntarabhāvasiddhiḥ /
yaduktam- 'ta etasyaiva sarve rūpamabhavan' (bṛ. 1.5.21) iti śruteḥ prāṇa evendriyāṇīti, tadayuktam /
tatrāpi paurvāparyālocanādbhedapratīteḥ /
tathāhi- vadiṣyāmyevāhamiti vāgdadhre' (bṛ. 1.5.21) iti vāgādīnīndriyāṇyanukramya 'tāni mṛtyuḥ śramo bhūtvopayeme tasmācchrāmyatyeva vāk' iti ca śramarūpeṇa mṛtyunā grastatvaṃ vāgādīnāmabhidhāya 'athemameva nāpnodyo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.21) iti pṛthakprāṇaṃ mṛtyunānabhibhūtaṃ tamanukrāmati /
'ayaṃ vai naḥ śreṣṭhaḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.21) iti ca śreṣṭhatāmasyāvadhārayati /
tasmāttadavirodhena vāgādiṣu parispandalābhasya prāṇāyattatvaṃ tadrūpabhavanaṃ vāgādīnāmiti mantavyaṃ na tādātmyam /
ata eva ca prāṇaśabdasyendriyeṣu lākṣaṇikatvasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And hence the establishment that the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' is used secondarily for the sense-organs.

children.text: tathāca śrutiḥ - 'ta etasyaiva sarve rūpamabhavan /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'They all assumed the form of this one;

children.text: tasmādeta etenākhyāyante prāṇāḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.21) iti mukhyaprāṇaviṣayasyaiva prāṇaśabdasyendriyeṣu lākṣaṇikīṃ vṛttiṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: therefore, they are called by the name <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21) — [this] shows the secondary usage of the word '<s>prāṇa</s>', which primarily refers to the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, when applied to the sense-organs.

children.text: tasmāttattvāntarāṇi prāṇādindriyāṇīti // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the sense-organs — from <s>prāṇa</s> onward — are distinct principles. // 19 //

And there is dissimilarity between the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>] and the others. When speech and the rest are asleep [i.e., inactive in deep sleep], the chief alone remains awake; and that one alone is not overtaken by death, while the others are overtaken. And through its staying and departing, it is the cause of the body's being sustained and falling — but not the sense-organs. And the sense-organs are the cause of apprehending objects — but not <s>prāṇa</s>. Such is the manifold difference of characteristics between <s>prāṇa</s> and the sense-organs. Therefore, from this too, the establishment that they are distinct principles [is confirmed]. As for the statement — that because of the <s>śruti</s> 'They all assumed the form of this one' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21), the sense-organs are nothing but <s>prāṇa</s> — that is incorrect. Because even there, from examining what precedes and what follows, the perception of difference [remains]. For thus — having enumerated the sense-organs, speech and the rest, with 'I shall speak' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21) and the rest, and having stated that speech and the rest are seized by Death in the form of fatigue: 'Death, becoming fatigue, seized them; therefore speech indeed becomes fatigued' — and then setting apart <s>prāṇa</s> as not overcome by death: 'But this one it did not reach — the one that is the central breath' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21) — [the text] enumerates it separately. And 'This one is the best (<s>śreṣṭha</s>) among us' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21) — [the text] establishes its superiority. Therefore, in a manner consistent with that [distinction], the statement that speech and the rest 'assumed the form' of [<s>prāṇa</s>] should be understood as meaning that speech and the rest depend on <s>prāṇa</s> for obtaining their capacity for movement — not as [expressing] identity.

children.text: FN: mṛtyurāsaṅgadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Death' (<s>mṛtyu</s>) means the fault of attachment.

children.text: vādgagdhre dhāraṇābhiprāyaṃ cakre /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vāg dadhre</s>' means speech formed the intention of sustaining.

children.text: 9 saṃjñāmūrtikḷptyadhikaraṇam / sū. 20-22
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Saṃjñāmūrtikḷptyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Formation of Names and Forms). <s>Sūtras</s> 20-22.

children.text: saṃjñāmūrtikḷptis tu trivṛtkurvata upadeśāt | BBs_2,4.20 |
children.translated_text: But the formation of names and forms [is done by the supreme Lord] — because of the teaching [that it is done] by the one performing <s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s> (triplication). | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.20 |

children.text:
satprakriyāyāṃ tejobannānāṃ sṛṣṭimabhidhāyopadiśyate- 'seyaṃ devataikṣata hantāhamimāstisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti /
tāsāṃ trivṛtaṃ trivṛtamekaikāṃ karavāṇīti' (chā. 6.3.2) /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ jīvakartṛkamidaṃ nāmarūpavyākaraṇamāhosvitparameśvarakartṛkamiti /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvajjīvakartṛkamevedaṃ nāmarūpavyākaraṇamiti /
kutaḥ - 'anena jīvenātmanā' iti viśeṣaṇāt /
yathā loke cāreṇāhaṃ parasainyamanupraviśya saṃkalayānītyevañjātīyake prayoge cārakartṛkameva satsainyasaṃkalanaṃ hetukartṛtvādrājātmanyadhyāropayati saṃkalayānītyuttamapuruṣaprayogeṇa, evaṃ jīvakartṛkameva sannāmarūpavyākaraṇaṃ hetukartṛtvāddevatātmanyadhyāropayati vyākaravāṇītyuttamapuruṣaprayogeṇa /
apica ḍitthaḍavitthādiṣu nāmasu ghaṭaśarāvādiṣu ca rūpeṣu jīvasyaiva vyākartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭam /
tasmājjīvakartṛkamevedaṃ nāmarūpavyākaraṇamityevaṃ prāpte 'bhidhatte-
children.translated_text: In the creation-procedure of Being (<s>sat</s>), having described the creation of fire, water, and food, [the text] teaches: 'This deity thought: "Come, let me enter these three deities with this living Self and manifest names and forms. Let me make each of these three threefold"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2). There, the doubt arises: Is this manifestation of names and forms done by the <s>jīva</s>, or by the supreme Lord? The prima facie view is that this manifestation of names and forms is done by the <s>jīva</s> alone. Why? Because of the qualifier 'with this living Self.' And just as in the world, in a usage like 'Let me infiltrate the enemy army through a spy and reorganize [it]' — the reorganization is done by the spy, but is figuratively attributed to the king as the instigating agent through the first-person usage 'let me reorganize' — so too, the manifestation of names and forms, though done by the <s>jīva</s>, is figuratively attributed to the deity as the instigating agent through the first-person usage 'let me manifest.' Moreover, in names such as <s>Ḍittha</s>, <s>Ḍavittha</s>, and such, and in forms such as pots, dishes, and such, it is the <s>jīva</s> alone that is observed as the manifester. Therefore, this manifestation of names and forms is done by the <s>jīva</s> alone. Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] states:

children.text:
'saṃjñāmūrtikḷptastu' iti /
tuśabdena pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati /
saṃjñāmūrtikḷptiriti nāmarūpavyākriyetyetat /
trivṛtkurvata iti parameśvaraṃ lakṣayati, trivṛtkaraṇe tasya nirapavādakartṛtvanirdeśāt /
yeyaṃ saṃjñākḷptimūrtikḷptiścāgnirādityaścandramā vidyuditi, tathā kuśakāśapalāśādiṣu paśumṛgamanuṣyādiṣu ca pratyākṛti prativyakti cānekaprakārā /
sā khalu parameśvarasyaiva tejobannānāṃ nirmātuḥ kṛtirbhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ - upadeśāt /
tathāhi- 'seyaṃ devataikṣata' ityupakramya 'vyākaravāṇi' ityuttamapuruṣaprayogeṇa parasyaiva brahmaṇo vyākartṛtvamihopadiśyate /
children.translated_text: 'But the formation of names and forms.' The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the position. 'Formation of names and forms' (<s>saṃjñāmūrtikḷpti</s>) means the manifestation of names and forms. 'By the one performing triplication' designates the supreme Lord — because His unqualified agency is stated in the triplication. This formation of names — fire, sun, moon, lightning, and such — and of forms in various categories, in each individual species and in each individual being — among <s>kuśa</s> grass, <s>kāśa</s> grass, <s>palāśa</s> leaves, and such, and among cattle, wild animals, humans, and such — is indeed the work of the supreme Lord alone, the creator of fire, water, and food. Why? Because of the teaching. For thus, having begun with 'This deity thought,' the teaching here is that the manifester is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — by the first-person usage 'let me manifest.'

children.text: nanu jīveneti viśeṣaṇājjīvakartṛkatvaṃ vyākaraṇasyādhyavasitam /
children.translated_text: But the agency of the <s>jīva</s> in manifestation was concluded from the qualifier 'with the <s>jīva</s>'!

children.text:
naitadevam /
jīvenetyetadanupraviśyetyanena saṃbadhyata ānantaryāt, na vyākaravāṇītyanena /
tena hi saṃbandhe vyākaravāṇītyayaṃ devatāviṣaya uttamapuruṣa aupacārikaḥ kalpyeta /
naca girinadīsamudrādiṣu nānāvidheṣu nāmarūpeṣvanīśvarasya jīvasya vyākaraṇasāmarthyamasti /
yeṣvapi cāsti sāmarthyaṃ teṣvapi parameśvarāyattameva tat /
naca jīvo nāma parameśvarādatyantabhinnaścāra iva rājñaḥ, ātmaneti viśeṣaṇāt /
upādhimātranibandhanatvācca jīvabhāvasya /
tena, tatkṛtamapi nāmarūpavyākaraṇaṃ parameśvarakṛtameva bhavati /
parameśvara eva ca nāmarūpayorvyākarteti sarvopaniṣatsiddhāntaḥ /
'ākāśo ha vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā' (chā. 8.14.1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tasmātparameśvarasyaiva trivṛtkurvataḥ karma nāmarūpayorvyākaraṇam /
trivṛtkaraṇapūrvakamevedamiha nāmarūpavyākaraṇaṃ vivakṣyate, pratyekaṃ nāmarūpavyākaraṇasya tejobannotpattivacanenaivoktatvāt /
tacca trivṛtkaraṇamagnyādityacandravidyutsu śrutirdarśayati- 'yadagre rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasastadrūpaṃ yacchuklaṃ tadapāṃ yatkṛṣṇaṃ tadannasya' (chā. 6.4.1) ityādinā /
tatrāgniritīdaṃ rūpaṃ vyākriyate /
sati ca rūpavyākaraṇe viṣayapratilambhādagniritīdaṃ nāma vyākriyate /
evamādityacandravidyutsvapi draṣṭavyam /
anena cāgnyādyudāharaṇena bhaumāmbhasataijaseṣu triṣvapi dravyeṣvaviśeṣeṇa trivṛtkaraṇamuktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And by this illustration of fire and such, the triplication is stated without exception for all three kinds of substances — earthy, watery, and fiery.

children.text: upakramopasaṃhārayoḥ sādhāraṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the generality of the opening and the concluding [statements].

children.text: tathāhyaviśeṣeṇaivopakramaḥ - 'imāstisro devatāstrivṛdekaikā bhavati' (chā. 6.3.4) iti /
children.translated_text: For the opening is indeed without exception: 'Let each of these three deities become threefold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.4).

children.text: aviśeṣeṇaiva copasaṃhāraḥ - 'yadu rohitamivābhūditi tejasastadrūpam' ityevamādiḥ 'yadavijñātamivābhūdityetāsāmeva devatānāṃ samāsa iti' (chā. 6.4.6.7) evamantaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: And the conclusion too is without exception: 'That which appeared red — that is the form of fire' and so forth, ending with 'That which appeared unknown — that is the combination of these very deities' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.4.6-7). // 20 //

This is not so. 'With the <s>jīva</s>' is connected with 'having entered' — because of proximity — not with 'let me manifest.' For if it were connected with that [latter], the first-person [usage] 'let me manifest,' which refers to the deity, would have to be regarded as figurative. And the <s>jīva</s>, who is not the Lord, does not have the capacity to manifest the manifold names and forms in mountains, rivers, oceans, and such. And even in those cases where it has the capacity, that too is dependent on the supreme Lord. And the <s>jīva</s> is not absolutely different from the supreme Lord — like a spy from a king — because of the qualifier 'as the Self.' And because the <s>jīva</s>'s <s>jīva</s>-nature is founded on limiting adjuncts alone. Therefore, even what is done by [the <s>jīva</s>] is done by the supreme Lord alone. And that the supreme Lord alone is the manifester of names and forms is the established conclusion of all <s>Upaniṣads</s>. From <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is indeed the accomplisher of names and forms' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1). Therefore, the manifestation of names and forms is the work of the supreme Lord who performs the triplication. The manifestation of names and forms intended here is precisely that which is preceded by triplication — because the manifestation of names and forms for each individual [element] has already been stated through the statement of the origination of fire, water, and food. And the <s>śruti</s> shows this triplication in fire, sun, moon, and lightning: 'That which is the red form in fire — that is the form of fire; that which is white — that is of water; that which is black — that is of food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.4.1) — and so forth. There, the form is manifested: 'This is fire.' And when the form is manifested, because an object is thereby obtained, the name too is manifested: 'This is fire.' The same should be understood for the sun, moon, and lightning.

children.text: FN: prakriyā prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: '<s>Prakriyā</s>' means a section.

children.text: tāsāṃ tisṛṇāmekaikāṃ devatāṃ tejobannātmanā tryātmikāṃ kariṣyāmīti śrutiḥ pañcīkaraṇopalakṣaṇārthā /
children.translated_text: 'Let me make each of the three deities — in the form of fire, water, and food — triple-natured': this <s>śruti</s> is intended to indicate <s>pañcīkaraṇa</s> (quintuplification) [as well].

children.text:
tāsāṃ tisṛṇāṃ devatānāṃ bahistrivṛtkṛtānāṃ satīnāmadhyātmamaparaṃ trivṛtkaraṇamuktam- 'imāstisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛttrivṛdekaikā bhavati' (chā. 6.4.7) iti /
tadidānīmācāryo yathāśrutyevopadarśayatyāśaṅkitaṃ kañciddoṣaṃ parihariṣyan-
children.translated_text: After the three deities have been made tripled externally, their further triplication internally (<s>adhyātma</s>) is stated: 'These three deities, having reached the person, became threefold, each threefold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.4.7). Now the teacher shows this as the <s>śruti</s> states, while resolving a certain anticipated objection —

children.text: māṃsādi bhaumaṃ yathāśabdamitarayoś ca | BBs_2,4.21 |
children.translated_text: Flesh and such are earthy — as per the scriptural word; and for the other two [likewise]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.21 |

children.text:
bhūmestrivṛtkṛtāyāḥ puruṣeṇopabhujyamānāyā māṃsādikāryaṃ yathāśabdaṃ niṣpadyate /
tathāhi śrutiḥ - 'annamaśitaṃ tredhā vidhīyate tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātustatpurīṣaṃ bhavati yo madhyamastanmāṃsaṃ yo 'ṇiṣṭhastanmanaḥ' (chā. 6.5.1) iti /
children.translated_text: From earth that has been tripled, when consumed by a person, the product of flesh and such is produced as the scripture states. For thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Food that is eaten is divided threefold; its grossest portion becomes excrement; its middle portion becomes flesh; its subtlest portion becomes mind' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.5.1).

children.text:
trivṛtkṛtā bhūmirevaiṣā vrīhiyavādyannarūpeṇādyata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
tasyāśca sthaviṣṭhaṃ rūpaṃ purīṣabhāvena bahirnirgacchati /
madhyamamadhyātmaṃ māṃsaṃ vardhayati /
aṇiṣṭhaṃ tu manaḥ /
children.translated_text: And its subtlest portion [nourishes] the mind.

children.text: evamitarayoraptejasoryathāśabdaṃ kāryamavagantavyam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, for the other two — water and fire — the products should be understood as the scripture states.

children.text: evaṃ mūtraṃ lohitaṃ prāṇaścāpāṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text: Thus, urine, blood, and <s>prāṇa</s> are the products of water.

children.text: asthi majjā vāktejasa iti // 21 //
children.translated_text: And bone, marrow, and speech are [the products] of fire. // 21 //

The intention is: it is this very tripled earth that is consumed in the form of rice, barley, and other food. And its grossest portion exits externally as excrement. Its middle portion internally nourishes the flesh.

children.text:
atrāha- yadi sarvameva trivṛtkṛtaṃ bhūtabhautikamaviśeṣaśruteḥ 'tāsa trivṛtaṃ trivṛtamekaikāmakarot' iti /
kiṅkṛtastarhyayaṃ viśeṣavyapadeśaḥ 'idaṃ teja imā āpa idamannam' iti /
tathā 'adhyātmamidamannasyāśitasya kāryaṃ māṃsādi /
idamapāṃ pītānāṃ kāryaṃ lohitādi /
idaṃ tejaso 'śitasya kāryamasthyādi' iti /
atrocyate-
children.translated_text: Here it is objected: If everything — both elemental and derivative — is entirely tripled, because of the non-discriminating <s>śruti</s> 'He made each of the three threefold' — then why is there this specific designation 'this is fire, this is water, this is food'? And likewise 'internally, flesh and such is the product of food eaten; blood and such is the product of water drunk; bone and such is the product of fire eaten'? To this it is said:

children.text: vaiśeṣyāt tu tadvādas tadvādaḥ | BBs_2,4.22 |
children.translated_text: But because of preponderance, that designation [is given] — that designation [is given]. | <s>BBs</s> 2,4.22 |

children.text:
tuśabdena coditaṃ doṣamapanudati /
viśeṣasya bhāvo vaiśeṣyam /
bhūyastvamiti yāvat /
satyapi trivṛtkaraṇe kvacitkasyacidbhūtadhātorbhūyastvamupalabhyate 'agnestejobhūyastvamudakasyābbhūyastvaṃ pṛthivyā annabhūyastvam' iti /
children.translated_text:
By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] dispels the objection raised.
The state of having a specific [predominant element] is '<s>vaiśeṣya</s>' (preponderance).
That is to say, predominance.
Even though the tripartite combination (<s>trivṛtkaraṇa</s>) [of elements] has taken place, in some [element] a preponderance of a certain elemental constituent is perceived — 'in fire, a preponderance of the fire-element; in water, a preponderance of the water-element; in earth, a preponderance of the food-element.'

children.text: vyavahāraprasiddhyarthaṃ cedaṃ trivṛtkaraṇam /
children.translated_text: And this tripartite combination is for the purpose of establishing conventional usage.

children.text: vyavahāraśca trivṛtkṛtarajjuvadekatvāpattau satyāṃ na bhedena bhūtatrayagocaro lokasya prasiddhyet /
children.translated_text: And [such] conventional usage — if things were reduced to unity like a tripartite rope — would not be established for the world as pertaining distinctly to the three elements.

children.text: tasmātsatyapi trivṛtkaraṇe vaiśeṣyādeva tejobannaviśeṣavādo bhūtabhautikaviṣaya upapadyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though the tripartite combination has taken place, because of the preponderance [of one element over the others], the designation of the specific elements — fire, water, and food — pertaining to the physical and derivative [substances] is tenable.

children.text: tadvādastadvāda iti padābhyāso 'dhyāyaparisamāptiṃ dyotayati // 22 //
children.translated_text: The repetition of the words '<s>tadvādas tadvādaḥ</s>' (that designation, that designation) indicates the conclusion of the chapter. // 22 //

children.text: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye dvitīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> (section) of the second <s>adhyāya</s> (chapter) in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the supreme wandering ascetic.

children.text: iti śrīmadbrahmasūtraśāṅkarabhāṣye 'virodhākhyo dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>adhyāya</s>, called <s>Avirodha</s> (Non-Contradiction), in the <s>Brahmasūtra Śāṅkarabhāṣya</s>.

children.text: atha tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the third <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: tṛtīye sādhanākhyādhyāye prathamapāde gatyāgaticintā-vairāgyanirūpaṇavicāraśca
children.translated_text: In the third <s>adhyāya</s>, called <s>Sādhana</s> (Means), in the first <s>pāda</s>: the investigation of the paths of going and returning, and the examination of dispassion.

children.text: 1 tadanantarapratipattyadhikaraṇam / sū. 1-7
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Tadantarapratipatty Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Attainment of Another [Body]). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-7.

children.text: tadantarapratipattau raṃhati saṃpariṣvaktaḥ praśnanirūpaṇābhyām | BBs_3,1.1 |
children.translated_text: In the attainment of another [body], [the <s>jīva</s>] goes, enveloped — because of the question and the explanation. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.1 |

children.text:
dvitīye 'dhyāye smṛtinyāyavirodho vedāntavihite brahmadarśane parihṛtaḥ /
parapakṣāṇāṃ cānapekṣatvaṃ prapañcitam /
śrutivipratiṣedhaśca parihṛtaḥ /
tatra ca jīvavyatiriktāni tattvāni jīvopakaraṇāni brahmaṇo jāyanta ityuktam /
athedānīmupakaraṇopahitasya jīvasya saṃsāragatiprakārastadavasthāntarāṇi brahmasatattvaṃ vidyābhedābhedau guṇopasaṃhārānupasaṃhārau samyagdarśanātpuruṣārthasiddhiḥ samyagdarśanopāyavidhiprabhedo muktiphalāniyamaścetyetadarthajātaṃ tṛtīye 'dhyāye nirūpayiṣyate prasaṅgāgataṃ ca kimapyanyat /
tatra prathame tāvatpāde pañcāgnividyāmāśritya saṃsāragatiprabhedaḥ pradarśyate vairāgyahetoḥ /
'tasmājjugupset' iti cānte śravaṇāt /
jīvomukhyaprāṇasacivaḥ sendriyaḥ samanasko 'vidyākarmapūrvaprajñāparigrahaḥ pūrvadehaṃ vihāya dehāntaraṃ pratipadyata ityetadavagatam /
'athainamete prāṇā abhisamāyanti' ityevamādeḥ 'anyannavataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ kurute' (bṛ. 4.4.1.4) ityevamantātsaṃsāraprakaraṇasthācchabdāt /
dharmādharmaphalopabhogasaṃbhavācca /
sa kiṃ dehaḥ bījairbhūtasūkṣmairasaṃpariṣvakto gacchatyāhosvitsaṃpariṣvakta iti cintyate /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
asaṃpariṣvakta iti /
kutaḥ karaṇopādānavadbhūtopādānasyāśrutatvāt /
'sa etāstejomātrāḥ samabhyādadānaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.1) iti hyatra tejomātrāśabdena karaṇānāmupādānaṃ saṃkīrtayati /
vākyaśeṣe cakṣurādisaṃkīrtanāt /
naivaṃ bhūtamātropādānasaṃkīrtanamasti /
sulabhāśca sarvatra bhūtamātrāḥ /
yatraiva deha ārabdhavyastatraiva santi tataśca tāsāṃ nayanaṃ niṣprayojanam /
tasmādasaṃpariṣvakto yātīti /
evaṃ prāpte paṭhatyācāryaḥ - tadantarapratipattau raṃhati saṃpariṣvakta iti /
tadantarapratipattau dehāntarapratipattau dehabījabhūtairsūkṣmaiḥ saṃpariṣvakto raṃhati gacchatītyavagantavyam /
kutaḥ - praś nanirūpaṇābhyām /
tathāhi praś naḥ - 'vettha yathā pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti' (chā. 5.3.3) iti /
nirūpaṇaṃ ca prativacanaṃ dyuparjanyapṛthivīpuruṣayoṣitsu pañcasvagniṣu śraddhāsomavṛṣṭyannaretorūpāḥ pañcāhutirdarśayitvā 'iti tu pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti' (chā. 5.9.1) iti /
tasmādadbhiḥ pariveṣṭito jīvo raṃhati vrajatīti gamyate /
children.translated_text:
In the second <s>adhyāya</s>, the contradiction of <s>smṛti</s> and reasoning with the vision of <s>Brahman</s> prescribed by the <s>Vedānta</s> was resolved.
And the non-dependence on rival doctrines was elaborated.
And the contradiction of <s>śrutis</s> was resolved.
And therein, it was stated that the principles other than the <s>jīva</s> — which serve as the <s>jīva</s>'s instruments — are born from <s>Brahman</s>.
Now, the following topics will be examined in the third <s>adhyāya</s>: the manner of <s>saṃsāra</s>-journey for the <s>jīva</s> equipped with instruments, the various states [of the <s>jīva</s>], the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>, the distinctions and non-distinctions of meditations (<s>vidyā</s>), the inclusion and non-inclusion of qualities [in meditations], the attainment of the human goal through right vision, the distinctions in the injunctive prescriptions of the means to right vision, and the non-restriction regarding the fruit of liberation — this class of topics will be examined, along with whatever else arises incidentally.
Therein, in the first <s>pāda</s>, the distinctions of the <s>saṃsāra</s>-journey are demonstrated, relying on the doctrine of the five fires (<s>pañcāgnividyā</s>), for the purpose of generating dispassion.
Because at the end [of the passage], [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'Therefore one should feel disgust' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.8).
It has been understood that the <s>jīva</s>, accompanied by the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, together with the sense-organs and mind, equipped with <s>avidyā</s>, <s>karma</s>, and prior impressions (<s>pūrvaprajñā</s>), abandons the previous body and attains another body.
[This is understood] from the scriptural passage beginning with 'Then these <s>prāṇas</s> come together around him' and ending with 'It fashions another new and more auspicious form' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.1-4), which belongs to the context of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
And because the experience of the fruits of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> is possible [only in this way].
Now the question arises: Does the <s>jīva</s>, which is [like] the body's seed, go [to the next body] unenveloped by the subtle elements (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>), or enveloped [by them]?
What is the initial position? Unenveloped.
Why? Because, just as the taking up of instruments is heard, the taking up of subtle elements is not heard.
For 'He gathers to himself these luminous particles (<s>tejomātrā</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.1) — here, by the word '<s>tejomātrā</s>,' [the <s>śruti</s>] mentions the taking up of the instruments.
[This is known] because in the remainder of the sentence, the eye and such are mentioned.
But there is no such mention of the taking up of subtle elements.
And subtle elements are readily available everywhere.
Wherever a body is to be fashioned, they are already present — hence carrying them is purposeless.
Therefore, [the <s>jīva</s>] goes unenveloped.
Having set forth this [prima facie view], the teacher reads: 'In the attainment of another [body], [the <s>jīva</s>] goes enveloped.'
In the attainment of another body, it should be understood that [the <s>jīva</s>] goes enveloped by the subtle elements that are the seeds of the body.
From what [evidence]? From the question and the explanation.
For the question is: 'Do you know how, at the fifth oblation, the waters become endowed with a human voice?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.3.3).
And the explanation — the answer — showing five oblations in the form of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>soma</s>, rain, food, and semen in the five fires — heaven, rain-cloud, earth, man, and woman — demonstrates: 'Thus, at the fifth oblation, the waters become endowed with a human voice' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.9.1).
Therefore, it is understood that the <s>jīva</s> goes — travels — enveloped by waters.

children.text: nanvanyā śrutirjalūkāvatpūrvadehaṃ na muñcati yāvanna dehāntaramākramatīti darśayati- 'tadyathā tṛṇajalāyukā' (bṛ. 4.4.3) iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But another <s>śruti</s> shows, by the analogy of a leech, that [the <s>jīva</s>] does not release the previous body until it grasps another body: 'Just as a grass-leech' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.3).

children.text:
tatrāpyappariveṣṭitasyaiva jīvasya karmopasthāpitapratipattavyadehaviṣayabhāvanādīrghībhāvamātraṃ jalūkasyopamīyata ityavrodhaḥ /
evaṃ śrutyukte dehāntarapratipattiprakāre sati yāḥ puruṣamatiprabhavāḥ kalpanā vyāpināṃ karaṇānāmātmanaśca dehāntarapratipattau karmalaśādvṛttilābhastatra bhavati /
kevalasyaivātmano vṛttilābhastatra bhavati /
indriyāṇi tu dehavadabhinavānyeva tatra tatra bhogasthāna utpadyante /
children.translated_text: or [the view that] the sense-organs, like the body, are produced anew at each place of experience;

children.text: mana eva vā kevalaṃ bhogasthānamabhipratiṣṭheta /
children.translated_text: or [the view that] the mind alone establishes itself at the place of experience;

children.text: jīva evotplutya dehāddehāntaraṃ pratipadyate śuka iva vṛkṣādvṛkṣāntaram /
children.translated_text: or [the view that] the <s>jīva</s> alone leaps from body to body like a parrot from tree to tree —

children.text: ityevamādyāḥ sarvā evānādartavyāḥ śrutivirodhāt // 1 //
children.translated_text: all such [speculations] are to be disregarded, because they contradict <s>śruti</s>. // 1 //

children.text:
FN: darśanopāyāḥ saṃnyāsādayaḥ /
prasaṅgagataṃ dehātmadūṣaṇam /
pañcasu dyuparjanyapṛthivīpuruṣayoṣitsvagnidhyānaṃ pañcāgnividyā /
karma dharmādharmākhyaṃ, pūrvaprajñā janmāntarasaṃskāraḥ /
bhāvanāyā dīrghībhāvo bhāvidehaviṣayatvam /
kevaleti saugatakalpanam /
mana iti vaiśeṣikakalpanam /
jīva iti digambarakalpanam /
lokāyatakalpanāmādyagrahaṇena saṃgṛhyati /
children.translated_text:
Footnote: 'Means of vision' — renunciation and the like.
'Incidental' — the refutation of the body-as-self [doctrine].
'The five fires' — the meditation on the five [entities] — heaven, rain-cloud, earth, man, and woman — as fires is the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s>.
'<s>Karma</s>' — <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. '<s>Pūrvaprajñā</s>' — the impressions from previous births.
'Extension of the mental conception' — [the conception's] being directed toward the future body.
'<s>Kevala</s>' [the self alone] — this is the Buddhist speculation.
'<s>Manas</s>' [the mind alone] — this is the Vaiśeṣika speculation.
'<s>Jīva</s>' [the soul alone] — this is the Digambara (Jaina) speculation.
The materialist (<s>Lokāyata</s>) speculation is included by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and such).

children.text:
nanūdāhṛtābhyāṃ praś naprativacanābhyāṃ kevalābhiradbhiḥ saṃpariṣvakto raṃhatīti prāpnoti /
apaśabdaśravaṇasāmarthyāt /
tatra kathaṃ sāmānyena pratijñāyate sarvaireva bhūtasūkṣmaiḥ saṃpariṣvakto raṃhatīti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text:
Objection: From the question and answer cited, it follows that [the <s>jīva</s>] goes enveloped by waters alone.
Because of the force of hearing the word '<s>āp</s>' (water).
How then can it be declared in general that [the <s>jīva</s>] goes enveloped by all the subtle elements?
Therefore, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the following reply:

children.text: tryātmakatvāt tu bhūyastvāt | BBs_3,1.2 |
children.translated_text: But because of the tripartite nature [of everything] — [the word 'water' is used] because of [its] predominance. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.2 |

children.text:
tuśabdena coditāmāśaṅkamucchinatti /
tryātmikā hyāpastrivṛtkaraṇaśruteḥ /
tāsvārambhikāsvābhyupagatāsvitaradapi bhūtadvayamavaśyamabhyupagantavyaṃ bhavati /
tryātmakaśca dehastrayāṇāmapi tejobannānāṃ tasminkāryopalabdheḥ /
punaśca tryātmakastridhātutvāttribhirvātapittaśleṣmābhiḥ /
na sa bhūtāntarāṇi pratyākhyāya kevalābhiradbhirārabdhuṃ śakyate /
tasmādbhūyastvāpekṣo 'yamāpaḥ puruṣavacasa iti /
praś naprativacanayorapśabdo na kaivalyāpekṣaḥ /
sarvadeheṣu hi rasalohitādidravadravyabhūyastvaṃ dṛśyate /
children.translated_text:
By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] cuts off the stated objection.
For the waters are tripartite, because of the <s>śruti</s> on the tripartite combination.
When those [waters] — which are compound [in nature] — are accepted, the other two elements must necessarily be accepted as well.
And the body is tripartite — because the effects of all three — fire, water, and food — are perceived in it.
And again, the body is tripartite because of having three constitutive humors — <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm).
It cannot be fashioned from waters alone, to the exclusion of the other elements.
Therefore, the word '<s>āp</s>' (water) in the question and answer refers to [water's] predominance.
The word '<s>āp</s>' in the question and answer does not refer to water exclusively.
For in all bodies, a predominance of liquid substances such as chyle, blood, and the like is observed.

children.text: nanu pārthivo dhāturbhūyiṣṭho deheṣūpalakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the earthy constituent is observed to be predominant in bodies.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
itarāpekṣayāpyapā bāhulyaṃ bhaviṣyati /
dṛśyate ca śukraśoṇitalakṣaṇe 'pi dehabīje dravabāhulyam /
karma ca nimittakāraṇaṃ dehāntarārambhe /
karmāṇi cāgnihotrādīni somājyapayaḥprabhṛtidravadravyavyapāśrayāṇi /
children.translated_text: And <s>karmas</s> such as the <s>agnihotra</s> and the like are dependent on liquid substances such as <s>soma</s>, ghee, milk, and the like.

children.text: karmasamavāyiścāpaḥ śraddhāśabdoditāḥ saha karmabhirdyulokākhye 'gnau hūyanta iti vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: And the waters — spoken of by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>' — being concomitant with <s>karma</s>, together with the <s>karmas</s>, are offered in the fire called the heavenly world — as will be stated [later].

children.text: tasmādapyapāṃ bāhulyaprasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the predominance of water is well established.

children.text: bāhulyāccāpśabdena sarveṣāmeva dehabījānāṃ bhūtasūkṣmāṇāmupādānamiti niravadyam // 2 //
children.translated_text: And because of [water's] predominance, the taking up of all the body-seeds — the subtle elements — by the word '<s>āp</s>' (water) is faultless. // 2 //

This is not a fault.
The abundance of water will [still hold] in comparison with the other [element, fire].
And in the body-seed too — characterized as semen and blood — an abundance of liquid is observed.
And <s>karma</s> is the efficient cause in the fashioning of another body.

children.text: prāṇagateś ca | BBs_3,1.3 |
children.translated_text: And because of the departure of the <s>prāṇas</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.3 |

children.text: prāṇānāṃ ca dehāntarapratipattau gatiḥ śrāvyate- 'tamutkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmati prāṇamanūtkrāmantaṃ sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmanti' (bṛ. 4.4.2) ityādiśrutibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The departure of the <s>prāṇas</s> is also heard in connection with the attainment of another body — from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'When it departs, <s>prāṇa</s> departs after it; when <s>prāṇa</s> departs, all the <s>prāṇas</s> depart after it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2) and the like.

children.text: sā ca prāṇānāṃ gatirnāśrayamantareṇa saṃbhavatītyataḥ prāṇagatiprayuktā tadāśrayabhūtānāmapāpamapi bhūtāntaropasṛṣṭānāṃ gatiravagamyate /
children.translated_text: And the departure of the <s>prāṇas</s> is not possible without a support — therefore, the departure of the waters [and other subtle elements] that serve as the support of the <s>prāṇas</s>, along with the other subtle elements, is understood to be occasioned by the departure of the <s>prāṇas</s>.

children.text: nahi nirāśrayāḥ prāṇāḥ kvacidgacchanti tiṣṭhanti vā jīvato darśanāt // 3 //
children.translated_text: For the <s>prāṇas</s> do not go anywhere or remain anywhere without a support — as is seen [to be the case] in a living person. // 3 //

children.text: agnyādigatiśruter iti cen na bhāktatvāt | BBs_3,1.4 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that the <s>prāṇas</s>] do not [depart with the <s>jīva</s>] — because of the hearing of their going to fire and such — [we say] no, because of the figurative nature [of that statement]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.4 |

children.text:
syādetat /
naiva prāṇā dehāntarapratipattau saha jīvena gacchanti agnyādigatiśruteḥ /
tathāhi śrutirmaraṇakāle vāgādayaḥ prāṇā agnyādīndevāgacchatīti darśayati- 'yatrāsya puruṣasya mṛtasyāgniṃ vāgapyeti vātaṃ prāṇaḥ' (bṛ. 3.2.13) ityādineti cet /
children.translated_text:
It might be said: The <s>prāṇas</s> do not go with the <s>jīva</s> in the attainment of another body — because of the <s>śruti</s> that they go to fire and such.
For the <s>śruti</s> shows that at the time of death, the <s>prāṇas</s> such as speech and the like go to the deities — fire and the like: 'When the person dies, his speech goes into fire, his <s>prāṇa</s> into the wind' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.13) and the like — if this is the objection,

children.text:
na /
bhāktatvāt /
vāgādīnāmagnyādigatiśrutirgauṇī keśeṣu cādarśanāt /
'oṣadhīrlomāni vanaspatīnkeśāḥ' (bṛ. 3.2.13) iti hi tatrāmnāyate /
nahi lomāni keśāścotplutyauṣadhīrvanaspatīṃśca gacchantīti saṃbhavati /
naca jīvasya prāṇopādhipratyākhyāne gamanamavakalpyate /
children.translated_text: And for the <s>jīva</s>, departure is not conceivable if the <s>prāṇa</s>-support is denied.

children.text: nāpi prāṇairvinā dehāntara upabhoga upapadyate /
children.translated_text: Nor is experience in another body possible without the <s>prāṇas</s>.

children.text: vispaṣṭaṃ ca prāṇānāṃ saha jīvena gamanamanyatra śrāvitam /
children.translated_text: And the departure of the <s>prāṇas</s> together with the <s>jīva</s> is clearly stated elsewhere [in scripture].

children.text: ato vāgādyadhiṣṭhātrīṇāmagnyādidevatānāṃ vāgādyupakāriṇīnāṃ maraṇakāla upakāranivṛttimātramapekṣya vāgādayo 'gnyādīngacchantītyupacaryate // 4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, at the time of death, when the deities presiding over speech and the like — fire and the like — who assist speech and the like, cease their assistance, [the <s>śruti</s>] figuratively says that speech and the like go to fire and the like — referring merely to the cessation of assistance. // 4 //

No.
Because [the statement] is figurative.
The <s>śruti</s> that speech and the like go to fire and the like is secondary (figurative) — because, regarding hair, it is not observed [to be literal].
For there [in the same passage] it is stated: 'The body-hairs [go] into herbs, the head-hairs into trees' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.13).
For it is not possible that body-hairs and head-hairs leap up and go to herbs and trees.

children.text: FN: anyatra tamutkrāmantamityādau /
children.translated_text: Footnote: 'Elsewhere' [refers to the passage] 'When it departs, <s>prāṇa</s> departs after it' and the like.

children.text: prathame 'śravaṇād iti cen na tā eva hy upapatteḥ | BBs_3,1.5 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that] the water is not heard in the first fire — [we say] no, because those very [waters are meant], since it is fitting. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.5 |

children.text:
syādetat /
kathaṃ punaḥ 'pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti' (chā. 5.3.3) ityetannirdhārayituṃ pāryate /
yāvatā naiva prathame 'gnāvapāṃ śravaṇamasti /
iha hi dyulokaprabhṛtayaḥ pañcāgnayaḥ pañcānāmāhutīnāmādāratvenādhītāḥ /
teṣāṃ ca pramukhe 'asau vāva loko gautamāgniḥ' (chā. 5.4.1) ityupakramya 'tasminnetasminnagnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati' (chā. 5.4.2)
children.translated_text:
It might be said: How can the statement that 'at the fifth oblation, the waters become endowed with a human voice' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.3.3) be established?
Since water is not heard at all in the first fire.
For here, five fires — beginning with the heavenly world — are taught as the receptacles of the five oblations.
Of these, in the foremost one — beginning with 'This world, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed the fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.4.1) — and then [continuing with]

children.text:
iti śraddhā haumyadravyatvenāveditā /
na tatrāpo haumyadravyatayā śrutāḥ /
yadi nāma parjanyādiṣūttareṣu caturṣvagniṣvapāṃ haumyadravyatā parikalpyeta parikalpyatāṃ nāma /
teṣu hotavyatayopāttānāṃ somādīnāmabbahulatvopapatteḥ /
prathame tvagnau śrutāṃ śraddhāṃ parityajyāśrutā āpaḥ parikalpyanta iti sāhasametat /
śraddhā ca nāma pratyayaviśeṣaḥ prasiddhisāmarthyāt /
tasmādayuktaḥ pañcamyāhutāvapāṃ puruṣabhāva iti cet /
children.translated_text:
'In that fire, the gods offer <s>śraddhā</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.4.2) — <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is stated as the substance to be offered.
Water is not heard there as the substance to be offered.
Even if [one were to] imagine the oblation-status of water in the remaining four fires — the rain-cloud and the rest — let it be so imagined.
Because the <s>soma</s> and other [substances] that are taken up as what is to be offered in those [fires] can be understood as having a preponderance of water.
But in the first fire, to discard the heard <s>śraddhā</s> and imagine the unheard water — this is rash.
And '<s>śraddhā</s>' is a well-known specific type of mental disposition, from the force of convention.
Therefore, the human-voice-status of the waters at the fifth oblation is untenable — if this is the objection,

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
yatastatrāpi prathame 'gnau tā evāpaḥ śraddhāśabdenābhipreyante /
kutaḥ upapatteḥ /
evaṃhyādimadhyāvasānasaṃgānādanākulametadekavākyamupapadyate /
itarathā punaḥ pañcamyāmāhutāvapāṃ puruṣavacastvaprakāre pṛṣṭe prativacanāvasare prathamāhutisthāne yadyanapo haumyadravyaṃ śraddhāṃ nāmāvatārayettato 'nyathā praśno 'nyathā prativacanamityekavākyatā na syāt /
'iti tu pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti' iti copasaṃharannetadeva darśayati /
śraddhākāryaṃ ca somavṛṣṭyādi sthūlībhavadabbahulaṃ lakṣyate /
sā ca śraddhāyā aptve yuktiḥ /
kāraṇānurūpaṃ hi kāryaṃ bhavati /
naca śraddhākhyaḥ pratyayo manaso jīvasya vā dharmaḥ sandharmiṇo niṣkṛṣya homāyoṣādātuṃ śakyate paśvādibhya iva hṛdayādīnityāpa eva śraddhāśabdā bhaveyuḥ /
śraddhāśabdaścāpsūpapadyate, vaidikaprayogadarśanāt 'śraddhā vā āpaḥ' iti /
tanutvaṃ śraddhāsārūpyaṃ gacchantya āpo dehabījabhūtā ityataḥ śraddhāśabdāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: The waters that become attenuated, that assume the likeness of <s>śraddhā</s>, and that serve as the seed of the body — for this reason they may bear the designation '<s>śraddhā</s>.'

children.text: yathā siṃhaparākramo naraḥ siṃhaśabdo bhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as a man of lion-like valor bears the designation 'lion.'

children.text: śraddhāpūrvakakarmasamavāyāccāpsu śraddhāśabda upapadyate, mañcaśabda iva puruṣeṣu /
children.translated_text: And because of the association [of waters] with action preceded by faith, the designation '<s>śraddhā</s>' is applicable to waters — just as the word '<s>mañca</s>' (platform) [is applied to] the persons [seated on it].

children.text: śraddhāhetutvācca śraddhāśabdopapattiḥ 'apo hāsmai śraddhāṃ saṃnamante puṇyāya karmaṇe' iti śruteḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: And because of being the cause of faith, the applicability of the designation '<s>śraddhā</s>' [to waters is justified] — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Waters indeed generate faith in him for meritorious action' (<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s>). // 5 //

This is not a fault. Because even there, in the first fire, those very waters are intended by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>' (faith). How so? Because of propriety. For in this way — maintaining consistency from the beginning, through the middle, to the end — this single-sentence construction becomes coherent without confusion. Otherwise, when the question has been posed concerning the manner in which waters become human-voiced at the fifth oblation, if at the point of the first oblation some non-water oblation-substance called '<s>śraddhā</s>' were introduced, then the question would be about one thing and the answer about another — and the single-sentence unity would not hold. And the concluding statement 'Thus at the fifth oblation, waters become human-voiced' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.3.3) shows precisely this. And the effects of <s>śraddhā</s> — <s>Soma</s>, rain, and so forth — as they become gross, are seen to be predominantly water. And this reasoning supports the water-nature of <s>śraddhā</s>. For the effect corresponds to its cause. And the mental state called '<s>śraddhā</s>' — being a property of the mind or of the <s>jīva</s> — cannot be extracted from its possessor and offered as an oblation, as one extracts hearts and such from animals. Therefore, it is waters alone that bear the designation '<s>śraddhā</s>.' And the word '<s>śraddhā</s>' is applicable to waters, because of the Vedic usage: '<s>Śraddhā</s> indeed is waters' (<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s>).

children.text: FN: saṃgānaṃ tamutkrāmantamityādau /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Saṃgāna</s>' [refers to the passage] beginning with 'him departing' and the like.

children.text: anapaḥ abdyo 'nyataḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anapaḥ</s>' means something other than waters.

children.text:
asmai yajamānāya /
saṃnamante janayanti /
children.translated_text: 'For him' — for the sacrificer. '<s>Saṃnamante</s>' means they produce.

children.text: aśrutatvād iti cen neṣṭādikāriṇāṃ pratīteḥ | BBs_3,1.6 |
children.translated_text: <s>Aśrutatvāditi cen neṣṭādikāriṇāṃ pratīteḥ</s> — If [it be said that the jīvas do not travel] because of [their] not being heard [in the text] — [we say] no, because those who have performed sacrifices and the like are understood [to be implied]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.6 |

children.text:
athāpi syātprativacanābhyāṃ nāmāpaḥ śraddhādikrameṇa pañcamyāmāhutau puruṣākāraṃ pratipadyeran /
natu tatsaṃpariṣvaktā jīvā raṃheyuḥ /
aśrutatvāt /
nahyatrāpāmiva jīvānāṃ śrāvayitā kaścicchabdo 'sti /
tasmādraṃhati saṃpariṣvakta ityayuktamiti cet /
children.translated_text: It might still be maintained: through the two answers [of the five-fire teaching], waters alone — in the sequence beginning with <s>śraddhā</s> — assume human form at the fifth oblation. But the <s>jīvas</s> enveloped by them do not travel [along that path]. Why? Because of not being heard [in the text]. For here, unlike for waters, there is no word that proclaims the <s>jīvas</s>. Therefore, [the statement] 'the enveloped one travels' is improper — if this is the objection,

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
kutaḥ - iṣṭādikāriṇāṃ pratīteḥ /
'atha ya ime grāma iṣṭāpūrte dattamityupāsate te dhūmamabhisaṃbhavanti' (chā. 5.10.6) ityupakramyeṣṭādikāriṇāṃ dhūmādinā pitṛyāṇena pathā candraprāptiṃ kathayati- 'ākāśāccandramasameṣa somo rājā' (chā. 5.10.4) iti /
ta evehāpi pratīyante 'tasminnetasminnagnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati tasyā āhuteḥ somo rājā saṃbhavati' (chā. 5.4.2) iti śrutisāmānyāt /
teṣāṃ cāgnihotrādarśapūrṇamāsādikarmasādhanabhūtā dadhipayaḥprabhṛtayo dravadravyabhūyastvātpratyakṣamevāpaḥ santi /
tāṃ āhavanīye hutāḥ sūkṣmā āhutyo 'pūrvarūpāḥ satyastāniṣṭādikāriṇa āśrayanti /
teṣāṃ ca śarīraṃ naidhanena vidhānenāntye 'grāvṛtvijo juhvati 'asau svargāya lokāya svāhā' iti /
children.translated_text: And their body [at death] is offered by the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (officiating priests) through the funeral rite (<s>naidhana vidhi</s>) in the final fire [with the mantra]: 'To this one, for the heavenly world, <s>svāhā</s>.'

children.text: tatastāḥ śraddhāpūrvakakarmasamavāyinya āhutimayya āpo 'pūrvarūpāḥ satyastāniṣṭādikāriṇo jīvānpariveṣṭayāmuṃ lokaṃ phaladānāya nayantīti yattadatra juhotinābhidhīyate- 'śraddhāṃ juhvati' (bṛ. 6.2.9) iti /
children.translated_text: Then those waters — associated with action preceded by faith, having the form of oblations, becoming subtle and assuming the form of <s>apūrva</s> — envelop those <s>jīvas</s> who have performed sacrifices and the like, and lead them to the other world for the conferring of fruits. This is what is denoted here by the verb 'offer' [in the passage]: 'They offer <s>śraddhā</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.9).

children.text: tathācāgnihotre ṣaṭpraśnīnirvacanarūpeṇa vākyaśeṣeṇa 'te vā ete āhutī hute utkrāmataḥ' ityevamādināgnihotrāhutyoḥ phalārambhāya lokāntaraprāptiḥ pradarśitā /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the <s>Agnihotra</s> [section], through the remainder of the passage in the form of the exposition of the six questions — 'These two oblations, having been offered, depart' and so forth — the attainment of another world for the purpose of the fruition of the <s>agnihotra</s> oblations is demonstrated.

children.text: tasmādāhutīmayībhiradbhiḥ saṃpariṣvaktā jīvā raṃhanti svakarmaphalopabhogāyeti śliṣyate // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is coherent that the <s>jīvas</s>, enveloped by waters consisting of oblations, travel for the enjoyment of the fruits of their own <s>karma</s>. // 6 //

This is not a fault. Why? Because those who have performed sacrifices and the like are understood [to be implied]. Having introduced [the topic] with 'Now, those who in the village worship [saying] "sacrifice, merit, and charity are our offerings"— they pass into smoke' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.3), [the text] narrates the reaching of the moon by the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>) through smoke and so forth for those who have performed sacrifices and the like: 'From space, to the moon — this is King <s>Soma</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.4). Those very same [performers of sacrifice] are understood here too [in the five-fire context]: 'In that fire, the <s>devas</s> offer <s>śraddhā</s>; from that oblation, King <s>Soma</s> arises' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.4.2) — because of the similarity of <s>śruti</s>. And the ritual substances such as curds, milk, and the like — which serve as the means for the rituals of <s>agnihotra</s>, <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the like performed by those [sacrificers] — are directly perceptible as waters, being predominantly liquid substances. Those oblations, offered in the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire, becoming subtle and assuming the form of <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit), are resorted to by those performers of sacrifice and the like.

children.text: FN: naidhanena antyeṣṭyākhyena /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Naidhana</s>' means pertaining to the funeral rite (<s>antyeṣṭi</s>).

children.text: asau svargāya gacchatviti mantrārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of the <s>mantra</s> is: 'May this one go to heaven.'

children.text:
kathaṃ punaridamiṣṭādikāriṇāṃ svakarmaphalopabhogāya raṃhaṇaṃ pratijñāyate /
yāvatā teṣāṃ dhūmapratīkena vartmanā candramasamadhirūḍhānāmannabhāvaṃ darśayati- 'eṣa somo rājā taddevānāmannaṃ te devā bhakṣayanti' (chā. 5.10.4) iti 'te candraṃ prāpyānnaṃ bhavanti tāṃstatra devā yathā somaṃ rājānamapyāyasvāpakṣīyasvetyevamenāṃstatra bhakṣayanti' (bṛ. 6.2.16) iti ca samānaviṣayaṃ śrutyantaram /
naca vyāghrādibhiriva devairbhakṣyamāṇānāmupabhogaḥ saṃbhavatīti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: But how is it claimed that those who have performed sacrifices and the like travel for the enjoyment of the fruits of their own <s>karma</s>? For [the text] shows that, having ascended to the moon by the path of the ancestors through smoke and so forth, they become food — 'This is King <s>Soma</s>; that is the food of the <s>devas</s>; the <s>devas</s> consume that' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.4), and the parallel <s>śruti</s> on the same topic: 'Having reached the moon, they become food; there the <s>devas</s> consume them as [they consume] King <s>Soma</s> — "increase, decrease" — thus they consume them' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.16). And for those being consumed by the <s>devas</s> like [prey] by tigers and the like, enjoyment is not possible. To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the next [<s>sūtra</s>]:

children.text: bhāktaṃ vānātmavittvāt tathā hi darśayati | BBs_3,1.7 |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāktaṃ vānātmavittvāt tathā hi darśayati</s> — Or [the food-hood] is figurative, because of the non-knowers-of-the-Self status [of the sacrificers]; for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.7 |

children.text:
vāśabdaścoditadoṣavyāvartanārthaḥ /
bhāktameṣāmannatvaṃ na mukhyam /
mukhye hyannatve svargakāmo yajeta ityevañjātīyakādhikāraśrutirupapadhyeta /
candramaṇḍale cediṣṭādikāriṇāmupabhogo na syātkimarthamadhikāriṇa iṣṭādyāyāsabahulaṃ karma kuryuḥ /
annaśabdaścopabhogahetutvasāmānyādanne 'pyupacaryamāṇo dṛśyate /
yathā viśo 'nnaṃ rājñāṃ paśavo 'nnaṃ viśāmiti /
tasmādiṣṭastrīputramitrabhṛtyādibhiriva guṇabhāvopagatairiṣṭādikāribhiryatsukhaviharaṇaṃ devānāṃ tadaiveṣāṃ bhakṣaṇamabhipretaṃ na modakādivaccarvaṇaṃ nigaraṇaṃ vā /
'na ha vai devā aśnanti na pibantyetadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyanti' (chā. 3.6.1) iti ca devānāṃ carvaṇādivyāpāraṃ vārayati /
teṣāṃ ceṣṭādikāriṇāṃ devānprati guṇabhāvopagatānāmapyupabhoga upapadyate rājopajīvināmiva parijanānām /
children.translated_text: And even for those performers of sacrifices and the like who have attained a subordinate status with respect to the <s>devas</s>, enjoyment is possible — like the retinue of a king who subsists on the king's [bounty].

children.text: anātmavittvācceṣṭādikāriṇāṃ devopabhogyabhāva upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And because the performers of sacrifices and the like are non-knowers-of-the-Self, their status of being enjoyable by the <s>devas</s> is proper.

children.text: tathāhi śrutiranātmavidāṃ devopabhogyatāṃ darśayati- 'atha yo 'nyāṃ devatāmupāste 'nyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmīti na sa veda yathā paśurevaṃ sa devānām' (bṛ. 1.4.10) iti /
children.translated_text: For thus the <s>śruti</s> shows the status of non-knowers-of-the-Self as being enjoyable by the <s>devas</s>: 'Now, he who worships another deity, thinking "He is one, I am another" — he does not know. He is like a domestic animal to the <s>devas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10).

children.text: sa cāsminnapi loka iṣṭādibhiḥ karmabhiḥ prīmanpaśuvaddevānāmupakarotīti loke tadupajīvī tadādiṣṭaṃ phalamupabhuñjānaḥ paśuvaddevānāmupakarotīti gamyate //
children.translated_text: And he, even in this world, by pleasing the <s>devas</s> through rituals like <s>iṣṭi</s> and the like, serves the <s>devas</s> like a domestic animal — and in the other world too, subsisting on [the <s>devas</s>'] [bounty], enjoying the fruit ordained by them, he serves the <s>devas</s> like a domestic animal — this is understood.

The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) is for setting aside the stated fault. The food-hood of these [performers of sacrifices] is figurative, not literal. For if it were literal food-hood, the injunctive scripture of the kind 'Let one who desires heaven sacrifice' — such eligibility-determining <s>śruti</s> — would be contradicted. And if the performers of sacrifices and the like had no enjoyment in the moon-sphere, for what purpose would the eligible persons undertake the laborious rituals of <s>iṣṭi</s> and the like? And the word 'food' is seen to be used figuratively for what is the cause of enjoyment, because of the common feature of being the means of enjoyment — even for [things that are] not actually food. Just as [one says]: 'The subjects are the food of kings; cattle are the food of the subjects.' Therefore, just as with beloved wives, sons, friends, servants, and the like who have attained a subordinate status [to their master], the happy companionship of the performers of sacrifices and the like — who have attained a subordinate status to the <s>devas</s> — that alone is meant by their 'being consumed,' not the chewing and swallowing of sweets and the like. And [the <s>śruti</s>]: 'The <s>devas</s> neither eat nor drink; they are satisfied merely by seeing this nectar' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.6.1) — this bars the <s>devas</s> from activities like chewing and the like.

children.text:
anātmavittvāttathāhi darśayatītyasyāparā vyākhyā- anātmavido hyete kevalakarmiṇaiṣṭādikāriṇo na jñānakarmasamuccayānuṣṭhāyinaḥ /
pañcāgnividyāmihātmavidyetyupacaranti prakaraṇāt /
pañcāgnivijñānavihīnatvāccedamiṣṭādikāriṇāṃ guṇavādenānnatvamudbhāvyate pañcāgnivijñānapraśaṃsāyai /
pañcāgnividyā hīha vidhitsitā /
vākyatātparyāvagamāt /
tathāhi śrutyantaraṃ candramaṇḍale bhogasadbhāvaṃ darśayati- 'sa somaloke vibhūtimanubhūya punarāvartate' (pra. 5.4) iti /
children.translated_text: For thus another <s>śruti</s> shows the existence of enjoyment in the moon-sphere: 'Having enjoyed [his] glory in the <s>Soma</s>-world, he returns again' (<s>Praśna</s> 5.4).

children.text: tathānyadapi śrutyantaram 'atha ye śataṃ pitṛṇāṃ jitalolokānāmānandāḥ sa ekaḥ karmadevanāmānando ye karmaṇā devatvamabhisaṃpadyate' (bṛ. 4.3.33) itīṣṭādikāriṇāṃ devaiḥ saṃvasatāṃ bhogaprāptiṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, yet another <s>śruti</s>: 'A hundred [measures] of bliss of the ancestors who have won their world — that is one [measure] of bliss of the <s>karma-devas</s>, those who attain divinity through action' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.33) — this shows the attainment of enjoyment for the performers of sacrifices and the like who dwell together with the <s>devas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bhāktatvādannabhāvavacanasyeṣṭādikāriṇo 'tra jīvāraṃhantīti pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, because the statement of food-hood is figurative, it is understood that the <s>jīvas</s> who are performers of sacrifices and the like travel here [along this path].

children.text: tasmādraṃhati saṃpariṣvakta iti yuktamevoktam // 7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it was rightly said: 'The enveloped one travels.' // 7 //

There is another interpretation of 'because of being non-knowers-of-the-Self, for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows': These performers of sacrifices and the like who are non-knowers-of-the-Self are mere ritualists — not practitioners of the combination of knowledge and action. In this context, the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s> is figuratively called 'knowledge of the Self' because of its being in a [relevant] context. Because the performers of sacrifices and the like lack the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, their food-hood is brought up through a laudatory passage — for the purpose of praising the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>. For the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s> is what is intended to be enjoined here — as understood from the purport of the passage.

children.text: FN: adhikriyate puruṣo vidhinā saṃbadhyate 'nenetyadhikāraḥ phalakāmanā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Adhikāra</s>' (eligibility) — the person is connected by the injunction, and this [eligibility] is the desire for the fruit.

children.text: yathā paśurbhogya evamajñaḥ na bhedadhīmāndevānāṃ bhogya ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as an animal is [an object of] enjoyment [for humans], so too the ignorant one — not one who has the cognition of non-duality — is [an object of] enjoyment for the <s>devas</s>.

children.text: 2 kṛtātyayādhikaraṇam / sū. 8-11
children.translated_text: Section 2: <s>Kṛtātyayādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 8-11

children.text: kṛtātyaye 'nuśayavān dṛṣṭasmṛtibhyāṃ yathetamanevaṃ ca | BBs_3,1.8 |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛtātyaye 'nuśayavān dṛṣṭasmṛtibhyāṃ yathetamanevaṃ ca</s> — When the [merit of] performed [actions] is exhausted, the one possessing residual impressions (<s>anuśaya</s>) [descends] — from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, [going] in the same manner [as described] and not [in any other way]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.8 |

children.text:
iṣṭādikāriṇāṃ dhūmādinā vartmanā candramaṇḍalamadhirūḍhānāṃ bhuktabhogānāṃ tataḥ pratyavaroha āmnāyate- 'tasminyāvatsaṃpātamuṣitvāthaitamevādhvāṃ punarnivartante tathetam' (chā. 5.10.5) ityārabhya yāvadramaṇīyacaraṇā brāhmaṇādiyonimāpadyante kapūyacaraṇāḥ śvādiyonimiti /
tatredaṃ vicāryate- kiṃ niranuśayā bhuktakṛtsnakarmāṇo 'varohantyāhosvitsānuśayā iti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
niranuśayā iti /
kutaḥ - yāvatsaṃpātamiti viśeṣaṇāt /
saṃpātaśabdenātra karmāśaya ucyate- saṃpatantyanenāsmāllokādamuṃ lokaṃ phalopabhogāyeti /
yāvatsaṃpātamuṣitveti ca kṛtsnasya tasya kṛtasya tatraiva bhuktatāṃ darśayati /
teṣāṃ yadā tatparyaveti' (bṛ. 6.2.16) iti ca śrutyantareṇaiva evārthaḥ pradarśyate /
syādetat /
yāvadamuṣmiṃlloka upabhoktavyaṃ karma tāvadupabhuṅ kta iti kalpayiṣyāmīti /
naivaṃ kalpayituṃ śakyate yatkiñcetyanyatra parāmarśāt /
prāpyantaṃ karmaṇastasya yatkiñceha karotyayam /
tasmāllokātpunaraityasmai lokāya karmaṇe (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti hyaparā śrutiryatkiñcetyaviśeṣaparāmarśena kṛtsnasyeha kṛtasya karmaṇastatra kṣayitāṃ darśayati /

prākprāyaṇādārabdhaphalena karmaṇā pratibaddhasyābhivyaktyanupapatteḥ /
taccāviśeṣādyāvatkiñcidanārabdhaphalaṃ tasya sarvasyābhivyañjakam /

tataḥ kṛtātyaye kṛtasyeṣṭādeḥ karmaṇaḥ phalopabhogenopakṣaye sati sānuśayā evemamavarohanti /
kena hetunā /
dṛṣṭasmṛtibhyāmityāha /
tathāhi pratyakṣā śrutiḥ sānuśayānāmavarohaṃ darśayati- 'tadya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yatte ramaṇīyāṃ yonimāpadyeranbrāhmaṇayoniṃ vā kṣatriyayoniṃ vā vaiśyayoniṃ vātha yaiha ka pūyacaraṇāṃ abhyāśo ha yatte kapūyāṃ yonimāpadyerañśvayoniṃ vā sūkarayoniṃ vā caṇḍālayoniṃ vā' (chā. 5.10.7) iti /
caraṇaśabdenānuśayaḥ sūcyata iti varṇayiṣyati /
dṛṣṭaścāyaṃ janmanaiva pratipaṇyuccāvacarūpa upabhogaḥ pravibhajyamāna /
ākasmikatvāsaṃbhavādanuśayasadbhāvaṃ sūcayati, abhyudayapratyavāyayoḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtahetutvasya sāmānyataḥ śāstreṇāvagamitvāt /
smṛtirapi 'varṇā āśramāśca svakarmaniṣṭhāḥ pretya karmaphalamanubhūya tataḥ śeṣeṇa viśiṣṭadeśajātikularūpāyuḥśrutavṛttasukhamedhaso janma pratipadyante' iti sānuśayānāmevāvarohaṃ darśayati - kaḥ punaranuśayo nāmeti /
kecittāvadāhuḥ - svargārthasya karmaṇo bhuktaphalasyāvaśeṣaḥ kaścidanuśayo nāma bhāṇḍānusārisnehavat /
yathāhi snehabhāṇḍaṃ ricyamānaṃ na sarvātmanā ricyate bhāṇḍānusāryeva kaścitsnehaśeṣo 'vatiṣṭhate tathānuśayo 'pīti /
