children.translated_text: The descent of those who have performed sacrifices and such, who have ascended to the lunar sphere by the path of smoke and such, and whose enjoyments have been exhausted — is taught: beginning with 'Having dwelt there as long as the residue [of <s>karma</s>] lasts, they return again by this very path' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.5), [and ending with]: those of pleasant conduct obtain a birth as <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and such; those of foul conduct obtain a birth as dogs and such. Therein, this is investigated: do they descend without any residual <s>karma</s>, having exhausted all their <s>karma</s>? Or do they descend with residual [<s>karma</s>]? What is the initial position? They descend without residual [<s>karma</s>]. Why? Because of the qualifier 'as long as the residue lasts.' The word '<s>saṃpāta</s>' here means the stock of <s>karma</s> — 'by which they travel from this world to that world for the enjoyment of fruits.' And 'having dwelt there as long as the residue lasts' shows that all of that performed [<s>karma</s>] is exhausted there. And by another <s>śruti</s> — 'When that of theirs is exhausted' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.16) — this very meaning is demonstrated. One might say: 'I will interpret it as meaning that [only] the <s>karma</s> whose enjoyment belongs to that [other] world is enjoyed.' This interpretation is not possible, because of the unqualified reference 'whatever' elsewhere: 'Having reached the end of that <s>karma</s> — whatever one does here — from that world one returns again to this world for [further] action' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6) — for this other <s>śruti</s>, by its unqualified reference 'whatever,' shows the exhaustion there of all <s>karma</s> done here. Moreover, the departure [from the body at death] is the manifestor of <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not yet begun. Because the manifestation of [<s>karma</s>] that is blocked by <s>karma</s> whose fruit has already begun, prior to departure, is impossible. And because this [manifestation] is unqualified, [the departure] manifests all <s>karma</s> whatever whose fruit has not yet begun. For a common cause cannot produce an uncommon effect. For it is not justified that in the undifferentiated presence of a lamp, a pot is manifested but not a cloth. Therefore, they descend without residual [<s>karma</s>] — this being the position reached, we say: upon the exhaustion of [<s>karma</s>], one [descends] with residual [<s>karma</s>]. The group of <s>karma</s> by which they ascended to the lunar sphere for the enjoyment of fruits — that is exhausted through enjoyment; their body composed of [the merit of] that [<s>karma</s>], which was begun for enjoyment in the lunar sphere, [melts away] — like the hardening of ghee [melting] through contact with the fire of exhaustion-of-enjoyment and grief. Then, upon the exhaustion of the performed <s>karma</s> — sacrifices and such — through the enjoyment of its fruits, they descend with residual [<s>karma</s>]. For what reason? 'Because of scripture and <s>Smṛti</s>' — he says. For thus the directly heard <s>śruti</s> shows the descent of those who have residual [<s>karma</s>]: 'Those here whose conduct is pleasant — it is near-certain that they would obtain a pleasant birth: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> birth, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> birth, or a <s>Vaiśya</s> birth. But those here whose conduct is foul — it is near-certain that they would obtain a foul birth: a dog birth, a pig birth, or a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> birth' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.7). That the word '<s>caraṇa</s>' (conduct) indicates residual [<s>karma</s>] (<s>anuśaya</s>) will be explained. And this enjoyment — being differentiated into higher and lower forms from birth itself — since it cannot be accidental, indicates the existence of residual [<s>karma</s>], because the causation of prosperity and adversity by good and bad deeds is generally understood from scripture. <s>Smṛti</s> too — 'The <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>, devoted to their respective duties, having died and experienced the fruit of [their predominant] <s>karma</s>, then by the remainder [of <s>karma</s>] attain a birth distinguished by [specific] land, species, family, form, lifespan, learning, conduct, happiness, and intellect' — shows the descent of those with residual [<s>karma</s>] alone. But what is this residual [<s>karma</s>]? Some say: the residual [<s>karma</s>] is a remainder of the <s>karma</s> intended for heaven, whose fruit has [mostly] been enjoyed — like oil adhering to a vessel. For just as an oil vessel being emptied is not emptied entirely — some residue of oil adhering to the vessel remains — so too is the residual [<s>karma</s>].

children.text: nanu kāryavirodhitvādadṛṣṭasya na bhuktaphalasyāvaśeṣāvasthānaṃ nyāyyam /
children.translated_text: But because unseen <s>karma</s> (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) is opposed by its [complete] fruition, it is not justified that a remainder should persist after the fruit has been enjoyed.

children.text:
nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
nahi sarvātmanā bhuktaphalatvaṃ karmaṇaḥ pratijānīmahe /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. For we do not assert that the <s>karma</s> has its fruit entirely exhausted.

children.text:
nanu niravaśeṣakarmaphalopabhogāya candramaṇḍalamārūḍhaḥ /
bāḍham /
tathāpi svalpakarmāvaśeṣamātreṇa tatrāvasthātuṃ na labhyate /
yathā kila kaścitsevakaḥ sakalaiḥ sevopakaraṇai rājakulamupasṛpaścirapravāsātparikṣīṇavahūpakaraṇaśchatrapādukādimātrāvaśeṣo na rājakule 'vasthātuṃ śaknoti /
evamanuśayamātraparigraho na candramaṇḍalo 'vasthātuṃ śaknotīti /
nacaitadyuktamiva /
nahi svargasthasya karmaṇo bhuktaphalasyāvaśeṣānuvṛttirupapadyate kāryavirodhitvādityuktam /
children.translated_text: But did [the soul] not ascend to the lunar sphere for the complete exhaustion of the fruit of <s>karma</s>? Yes indeed. Nevertheless, with merely a small residue of <s>karma</s> remaining, it cannot continue to abide there. Just as a certain servant who approaches the royal court with all the provisions for service, but after a long sojourn, with most of his provisions exhausted and only an umbrella, shoes, and such remaining, cannot continue to stay in the royal court — so too, one possessing only residual [<s>karma</s>] cannot continue to stay in the lunar sphere. But this is not quite right either. For the persistence of a remainder of <s>karma</s> whose fruit has been enjoyed, for one who was in heaven, is not justified — because [complete fruition] is opposed [by the remainder] — as has been said.

children.text:
nanvetadayuktam /
na svargaphalasya karmaṇo nikhilasya bhuktaphalatvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti /
tadetadapeśalam /
svargārthaṃ kila karma svargasthasyaiva svargaphalaṃ nikhilaṃ na janayati svagracyutasyāpi kañcitphalaleśaṃ janayatīti /
na śabdapramāṇakāmānīdṛśī kalpanāvakalpate /
snehabhāṇḍe tu snehaleśānuvṛttirdṛṣṭatvādupapadyate /
tathā sevakasyopakaraṇaleśānuvṛttiśca dṛśyate /
natviha tathā svargaphalasya karmaṇo leśānuvṛttirdṛśyate nāpi kalpayituṃ śakyate svargaphalatvaśāstravirodhāt /
avaśyaṃ caitadevaṃ vijñeyam /
na svargaphalasyeṣṭādeḥ karmaṇo bhāṇḍānusārisnehavadekadeśo 'nuvartamāno 'nuśaya iti /
yadihi yena sukṛtena karmaṇeṣṭādinā svargamanvabhūvaṃstasyaiva kaścidekadeśo 'nuśayaḥ kalpyeta tato ramaṇīya evaiko 'nuśayaḥ syānna viparītaḥ /
tatreyamanuśayavibhāgaśrutiruparudhyeta- 'tadya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇā, atha kapūyacaraṇāḥ' (chā. 5.10.7) iti /
tasmādāmuṣmikaphale karmajāta upabhukte 'vaśiṣṭamaihikaphalaṃ karmāntarajātamanuśayastadvanta'varohantīti /
yaduktaṃ yatkiñcetyaviśeṣaparāmarśātsarvasyeha kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalopabhogenāntaṃ prāpya niranuśayā avarohantīti /
children.translated_text: But this is unjustified — for the <s>karma</s> intended for heaven will not have its fruit completely exhausted — [so one might object]. This is inelegant. For the idea that the <s>karma</s> intended for heaven produces its full fruit only while one is in heaven, and also produces some residual fraction of fruit even after falling from heaven — such a fabrication is not warranted [for a topic] whose authority is scripture alone. In the case of the oil-vessel, the persistence of a trace of oil is justified because it is observed. Similarly, the persistence of a trace of the servant's provisions is observed. But here, no such persistence of a trace of the heavenly-fruiting <s>karma</s> is observed, nor can it be fabricated — because it conflicts with the scriptural [teaching] of its heavenly fruition. And this must be understood thus: the residual [<s>karma</s>] is not a fraction of the sacrifice-and-such <s>karma</s> intended for heaven, persisting like oil in a vessel. For if a fraction of that very good <s>karma</s> — the sacrifice and such by which they went to heaven — were posited as the residual [<s>karma</s>], then there would be only a pleasant residue, never an unpleasant one. And then this <s>śruti</s> on the division of residual [<s>karma</s>] would be contradicted: 'Those here of pleasant conduct — and those of foul conduct' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.7). Therefore, when the group of <s>karma</s> bearing otherworldly fruit is exhausted through enjoyment, the residual [<s>karma</s>] is a different group of <s>karma</s> bearing fruit in this world — and those possessing it descend. As for the statement that because of the unqualified reference 'whatever,' all <s>karma</s> done here is exhausted through the enjoyment of its fruit and they descend without residue —

children.text:
naitadevam /
anuśayasadbhāvasyāvagamitatvāt /
yatkiñcidiha kṛtamāmuṣmikaphalaṃ karmārabdhabhogaṃ tatsarvaṃ phalopabhogena kṣapayitveti gamyate /
yadapyuktaṃ prāyaṇamaviśeṣādanārabdhaphalaṃ kṛtsnameva karmābhivyanakti tatra kenacitkarmaṇāmuṣmiṃlloke phalamārabhyate kenacidasminnityatvaṃ pratyuktam /
apicakena hetunā prāyaṇamanārabdhaphalasya karmaṇo 'bhivyañjakaṃ pratijñāyata iti vaktavyam /
yathaiva tarhi prākprayāṇādārabdhaphalena karmaṇā pratibaddhasyetarasya vṛttyudbhavānupapattirityevaṃ prāyaṇakāle 'pi viruddhaphalasyānekasya karmaṇo yugapatphalārambhāsaṃbhavādbalavatā pratibaddhasya durbalasya vṛttyuddhavānupapatitiriti /
nahyanārabdhaphalatvasāmānyena jātyantaropabhogyaphalamapyanekaṃ karmaikasminprāyaṇe yugapadabhivyaktaṃ sadekāṃ jātimārabhata iti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ, pratiniyataphalatvavirodhāt /
nāpi kasyacitkarmaṇaḥ prāyaṇe 'bhivyaktiḥ kasyaciduccheda iti śakyate vaktum /
children.translated_text: [because] it cannot be said that some <s>karma</s> is manifested at death while some is destroyed,

children.text: aikāntikaphalatvavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: because of the conflict with the invariability of their fruits.

children.text: nahi prāyaścittādibhirhetubhirvinā karmaṇāmucchedaḥ saṃbhāvyate /
children.translated_text: For the destruction of <s>karma</s> is not conceivable without causes such as <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory rites) and such.

children.text: smṛtirapi viruddhaphalena karmaṇā pratibaddhasya karmāntarasya ciramavasthānaṃ darśayati- 'kadācitsukṛtaṃ karma kūcasthamiha tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> too shows that <s>karma</s> blocked by <s>karma</s> of opposing fruit persists for a long time: 'Sometimes meritorious <s>karma</s>, standing firm like a mountain, remains here;

this is not so. Because the existence of residual [<s>karma</s>] has been established. [The passage] 'whatever one does here' is understood as: all <s>karma</s> done here that bears otherworldly fruit and whose enjoyment has begun is exhausted through the enjoyment of its fruit. As for the statement that death, being unqualified, manifests all <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not begun — to that it has been replied: some <s>karma</s> begins its fruit in the other world, and some in this world. Moreover, it must be stated for what reason death is asserted to be the manifestor of <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not begun. For just as prior to death, the manifestation of [<s>karma</s>] that is blocked by <s>karma</s> whose fruit has already begun is impossible — so too, at the time of death, since the simultaneous beginning of the fruit of many mutually opposing <s>karmas</s> is impossible, the manifestation of the weaker [<s>karma</s>] that is blocked by the stronger is impossible. For it cannot be said that many <s>karmas</s> — merely by being alike in having their fruit unbegun, even though their fruits are to be enjoyed in different births — being simultaneously manifested in a single death, initiate a single birth; because this contradicts the specificity of their fruits. Nor can it be said that some <s>karma</s> is manifested at death while other [<s>karma</s>] is destroyed —

children.text:
majjamānasya saṃsāre yāvadduḥkhādimucyate ityevañjātīyakā /
yadi ca kṛtsnamanārabdhaphalaṃ karmaikasminprāyaṇe 'bhivyaktaṃ sadekāṃ jātimārabheta tataḥ svarganarakatiryagyoniṣvadhikārānavagamāddharmādharmānutpattau nimittābhāvānnottarā jātirupapadyeta /
brahmahatyādīnāṃ caikaikasya karmaṇo 'nekajanmanimittatvaṃ smaryamāṇamuparudhyeta /
naca dharmādharmayoḥ svarūpaphalasādhanādisamadhigame śāstrādatiriktaṃ kāraṇaṃ śakyaṃ saṃbhāvayatum /
naca dṛṣṭaphalasya karmaṇaḥ kārīryādeḥ prāyaṇamabhivyañjakaṃ saṃbhavatītyavyāpikāpīyaṃ prāyaṇasyābhivyañjakatvakalpanā /
pradīpopanyāso 'pi karmabalābalapradarśanenaiva pratinītaḥ /
sthūlasūkṣmarūpābhivktyanabhivyaktivaccedaṃ draṣṭavyam /
yathāhi pradīpaḥ samāne 'pi saṃnidhāne sthūlaṃ rūpamabhivyanakti na sūkṣmam /
evaṃ prāyaṇaṃ samāne 'pyanārabdhaphalasya karmajātasya prāptāvasaratve balavataḥ karmaṇo vṛttimudbhāvayati na durbalasyeti /
tasmācchrutismṛtinyāyavirodhādaśliṣṭo 'yamaśeṣakarmābhivyaktyabhyupagamaḥ /
śeṣakarmasadbhāve 'nirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ ityayamapyasthāne saṃbhramaḥ /
samyagdarśanādaśeṣakarmakṣayaśruteḥ /
tasmātsthitametadevānuśayavanto 'varohantīti /
te cāvarohanto yathetamanevaṃ cāvarohanti /
yathetamiti yathāgatamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As they came' (<s>yathetam</s>) means 'in the same way as they went' — this is the meaning.

children.text: anevamiti tadviparyayeṇetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not in this way' (<s>anevam</s>) means 'in the reverse [order]' — this is the meaning.

children.text: dhūmākāśayoḥ pitṛyāṇe 'dhvanyupāttayoravarohe saṃkīrtanādyathetaṃśabdācca yathāgatamiti pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Because smoke and space — which were mentioned in the path of the <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s> [during ascent] — are mentioned [again] in the descent, and from the word 'as they came,' [the descent] in the same way as the ascent is understood.

children.text: rātryādyasaṃkīrtanādabhrādyupasaṃkhyānācca viparyayo 'pi pratīyate // 8 //
children.translated_text: And because night and such are not mentioned [in the descent], and because cloud and such are additionally enumerated, a reversed [order] too is understood. // 8 //

for one drowning in <s>saṃsāra</s>, until one is freed from suffering' — and such passages. And if all <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not begun were manifested in a single death and initiated a single birth, then since there would be no scope for [further activity in] heaven, hell, and animal wombs, and since in the absence of a cause for the non-production of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, a subsequent birth would not be possible. And the teaching in <s>Smṛti</s> that each single <s>karma</s> like the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is the cause of many births would be contradicted. And no cause other than scripture can be conceived for knowing the nature, fruit, and means of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. And since death cannot be the manifestor of <s>karma</s> that bears visible fruit — like agriculture — this positing of death as the manifestor is also not all-encompassing. And the lamp illustration has been answered by demonstrating the difference in the strength and weakness of <s>karma</s>. This should be viewed like the manifestation and non-manifestation of gross and subtle forms. For just as a lamp, even though equally present, manifests a gross form but not a subtle one — so death, even though the opportunity has equally arrived for the entire group of <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not begun, gives rise to the activity of the strong <s>karma</s> but not the weak. Therefore, because of the conflict with <s>śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and reasoning, this assumption that all <s>karma</s> is manifested [at death] is inconsistent. And the apprehension that 'if residual <s>karma</s> exists, there would be no liberation' — this too is misplaced alarm. Because of the <s>śruti</s> that through right knowledge, all <s>karma</s> is completely destroyed. Therefore, it stands that they descend with residual [<s>karma</s>]. And they, while descending, descend 'as they came' and also 'not in this way.'

children.text: FN: anuśayaḥ karma /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Anuśaya</s>' means <s>karma</s>.

children.text:
tat karma /
pratyavaiti parikṣīṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: 'That' [means] that <s>karma</s>. '<s>Pratyavaiti</s>' means 'becomes exhausted.'

children.text: abhivyaktiḥ phalonmukhatā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Abhivyakti</s>' means the orientation toward fruition.

children.text:
tat tatrāvarohatāṃ jīvānāṃ madhye iha karmabhūmau ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ iti yat tat ābhyāśoha avaśyaṃ hītyarthaḥ /
kapūyaṃ pāpam /
children.translated_text: 'That' — among those <s>jīvas</s> who descend here to the plane of action — 'those of pleasant conduct' means those of meritorious <s>karma</s> — that which [is said]. '<s>Ābhyāśoha</s>' means 'near-certainly' — the meaning is 'inevitably.' '<s>Kapūya</s>' means evil.

children.text: ricyamānaṃ viyujyamānam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ricyamāna</s>' means 'being separated.'

children.text: caraṇād iti cen nopalakṣaṇārtheti kārṣṇājiniḥ | BBs_3,1.9 |
children.translated_text: If [one says it is] because of conduct (<s>caraṇa</s>) — no, because it is used in the sense of indicating — [says] <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.9 |

children.text:
atāpi syāt /
yā śrutiranuśayasadbhāvapratipādanāyodāhṛtā- 'tadya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ' (chā. 5.10.7) iti /
sā khalu caraṇādyonyāpattiṃ darśayati nānuśayāt /
anyaccaraṇamanyo 'nuśayaḥ /
caraṇaṃ cāritramācāraḥ śīlamityanarthāntaram /
anuśayastu bhuktaphalātkarmaṇo 'tiriktaṃ karmābhipretam /

śrutiśca karmācaraṇe bhedena vyapadiśati- 'yathākārī yathācārī tathā bhavati' (bṛ. 4.4.5) iti, 'yānyanavadyāni karmāṇi tāni sevitavyāni no itarāṇi, yānyasmākaṃ sucaritāni tāni tvayopasyāni' (tai. 1.11.2) iti ca /
children.translated_text: And scripture designates <s>karma</s> and conduct as distinct: 'As one acts, as one conducts oneself, so one becomes' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.5); and 'Those actions that are blameless — those should be practiced by you, not others; and those that are our good practices — those should be adopted by you' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.11.2).

children.text: tasmāccaraṇādyonyāpattiśruternānuśayasiddhiriticet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the <s>śruti</s> that birth follows from conduct, the existence of residual [<s>karma</s>] is not established — [is this the objection?]

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: yato 'nuśayopalakṣaṇārthaivaiṣā caraṇaśrutiriti kārṣṇājinirācāryo manyate // 9 //
children.translated_text: Because the teacher <s>Kārṣṇājini</s> holds that this <s>śruti</s> on '<s>caraṇa</s>' is intended to indicate residual [<s>karma</s>] (<s>anuśaya</s>). // 9 //

One might further [object]: the <s>śruti</s> cited for establishing the existence of residual [<s>karma</s>] — 'Those here of pleasant conduct' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.7) — surely shows that birth follows from conduct (<s>caraṇa</s>), not from residual [<s>karma</s>] (<s>anuśaya</s>). Conduct and residual [<s>karma</s>] are different things. '<s>Caraṇa</s>' is the same as <s>caritra</s> (conduct), <s>ācāra</s> (behavior), <s>śīla</s> (character). But <s>anuśaya</s> is intended as <s>karma</s> additional to [the heavenly] <s>karma</s> whose fruit has been enjoyed.

children.text: ānarthakyam iti cen na tadapekṣatvāt | BBs_3,1.10 |
children.translated_text: If [one says] there would be purposelessness — no, because [one term] depends on [the other]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.10 |

children.text:
syādetat /
kasmātpunaścaraṇaśabdena śrautaṃ śīlaṃ vihāya lākṣaṇiko 'nuśayaḥ pratyāyyate /
children.translated_text: One might ask: why is the meaning of 'residual impression' (<s>anuśaya</s>) conveyed by the word '<s>caraṇa</s>' (conduct) through secondary signification, setting aside the primary scriptural meaning of 'conduct' (<s>śīla</s>)?

children.text:
nanu śīlasyaiva śrautasya vihitapratiṣddhasya sādhvasādhurūpasya śubhāśubhayonyāpattiḥ phalaṃ bhaviṣyati /
avaśyaṃ ca śīlasyāpi kiñcitphalamabhyupagantavyam /
anyathā hyānarthakyameva prasajyateti cet /
children.translated_text: Would not conduct itself — the primary scriptural meaning, either prescribed or prohibited, of the nature of good or bad — have the attainment of good or bad births as its fruit? And some fruit of conduct must necessarily be accepted — for otherwise, it would be utterly purposeless.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
kutaḥ - tadapekṣitatvāt /
iṣṭādi hi karmajātaṃ caraṇāpekṣam /
nahi sadācārahīnaḥ kaścidadhikṛtaḥ syāt- 'ācārahīnaṃ na punanti vedāḥ' ityādismṛtibhyaḥ puruṣārthatve 'pyācārasya nānarthakyam /
iṣṭādau hi karmajāte phalamārabhamāṇe tadapekṣa evācārastatraiva kañcidatiśayamārapsyate /
karma ca sarvārthakārīti śrutismṛtiprasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And that <s>karma</s> accomplishes all purposes — this is well known from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: tasmātkarmaiva śīlopalakṣitamanuśayabhūtaṃ yonyāpattau kāraṇamiti kārṣṇājinermatam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is <s>karma</s> itself — indicated by conduct, [and existing] in the form of residual impression — that is the cause of the attainment of [various] births. This is the view of <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>.

children.text: nahi karmaṇi saṃbhavati śīlādyonyāpattiryuktā /
children.translated_text: For when <s>karma</s> [as the cause] is available, it is not proper to [attribute] the attainment of births to conduct [separately].

children.text: nahi padbhyāṃ palāyituṃ pārayamāṇo jānubhyāṃ raṃhitumarhatīti // 10 //
children.translated_text: For one who is able to flee with one's feet should not resort to crawling on one's knees. // 10 //

This is not a fault. Why? Because [conduct] is required by that [karma]. For the class of actions beginning with <s>Iṣṭa</s> (sacrificial rites) requires conduct. No one devoid of good conduct is qualified [for ritual action] — as is known from <s>smṛtis</s> such as 'The <s>Vedas</s> do not purify one devoid of conduct.' Even though conduct has [its own] purpose as a human goal, it is not purposeless. For when the class of actions beginning with <s>Iṣṭa</s> is producing its fruit, conduct — being required by that [karma] — will produce some enhancement therein.

children.text: sukṛtaduṣkṛte eveti tu bādariḥ | BBs_3,1.11 |
children.translated_text: [The word '<s>caraṇa</s>' means] good and evil deeds alone — so says <s>Bādari</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.11 |

children.text:
bādaristvācāryaḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛte eva caraṇaśabdena pratyāyyete iti manyate /
caraṇamanuṣṭhānaṃ karmetyanarthāntaram /
tathāhi- aviśeṣeṇa karmamātre caratiḥ prayujyamāno dṛśyate /
yo hīṣṭādilakṣaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ karma karoti taṃ laukikā ācakṣate dharmaṃ caratyeṣa mahātmeti /
children.translated_text: For when someone performs meritorious action characterized by <s>Iṣṭa</s> and the like, people say: 'This noble one practices (<s>carati</s>) <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: ācāro 'pi ca dharmaviśeṣa eva /
children.translated_text: And conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) too is a specific form of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: bhedavyapadeśastu karmacaraṇayorbāhmaṇaparivrājakanyāyenāpyupapadyate /
children.translated_text: And the distinction of designation between '<s>karma</s>' and '<s>caraṇa</s>' is also tenable by the principle of '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>parivrājakas</s>' [i.e., the general includes the specific].

children.text: tasmādramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ praśastakarmaṇāḥ kapūyacaraṇā ninditakarmāṇa iti nirṇayaḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the settled conclusion is: 'those of pleasant conduct' means those of praiseworthy <s>karma</s>; 'those of foul conduct' means those of condemned <s>karma</s>. // 11 //

But the teacher <s>Bādari</s> holds that the word '<s>caraṇa</s>' conveys good and evil deeds alone. '<s>Caraṇa</s>' means performance, which is synonymous with <s>karma</s>. For the root '<s>car</s>' is seen to be used with reference to action in general, without restriction.

children.text: FN: gobalīvardanyāyo 'pyayameva /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The 'bull and ox' principle is also of this very kind [i.e., the general includes the specific].

children.text: 3 aniṣṭādikāryadhikaraṇam / sū. 12-21
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Aniṣṭādikārya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Those Who Perform Undesirable Deeds). <s>Sūtras</s> 12-21.

children.text: aniṣṭādikāriṇām api ca śrutam | BBs_3,1.12 |
children.translated_text: And it is heard even for those who perform undesirable deeds and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.12 |

children.text:
iṣṭādikāriṇaścandramasaṃ gacchatītyuktam /
ye tvitare 'niṣṭādikāriṇaste 'pi kiṃ candramasaṃ gacchantyuta na gacchantīti cintyate /
tatra tāvadāhuḥ - iṣṭādikāriṇa eva candramasaṃ gacchantītyetanna /
kasmāt /
yato 'niṣṭādikāriṇāmapi candramaṇḍalaṃ gantavyatvena śrutam /
ethāhyaviśeṣeṇa kauṣītakinaḥ samāmananti- 'ye vai ke cāsmāllokātprayanti candramasameva te sarve gacchanti' (kauṣī. 1.2) iti /
pañcabhyāmāhutāvityāhutisaṃkhyāniyamāt /
yasmātsarva eva candramasamāsīdeyuḥ /
iṣṭādikāriṇāmitareṣāṃ ca samānagatitvaṃ na yuktamiti cet /
children.translated_text: It was stated that those who perform <s>Iṣṭa</s> and other [rituals] go to the moon. But do the others — those who perform undesirable deeds — also go to the moon, or do they not? Therein, some say: only those who perform <s>Iṣṭa</s> and other [rituals] go to the moon. This is not so. Why? Because it is heard that even those who perform undesirable deeds must go to the lunar sphere. For the <s>Kauṣītakins</s> recite without restriction: 'All those who depart from this world go to the moon' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 1.2). And because of the rule regarding the number of oblations — 'at the fifth oblation' — all [beings] would arrive at the moon. If it is objected that it is not proper that those who perform <s>Iṣṭa</s> and the others should have the same destination —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: itareṣāṃ candramaṇḍale bhogābhāvāt // 12 //
children.translated_text: Because the others have no enjoyment in the lunar sphere. // 12 //

children.text: saṃyamane tv anubhūyetareṣāmārohāv arohau tadgatidarśanāt | BBs_3,1.13 |
children.translated_text: But [those others go] to <s>Saṃyamana</s> (the abode of <s>Yama</s>), and having experienced [punishment] there, the ascent and descent of those others. Because of the observation of that path. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.13 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati /
naitadasti sarve candramasaṃ gacchantīti /
etatkasmāt /
yato bhogāyaiva candrārohaṇaṃ na niṣprayojanam /
nāpi pratyavarohāyaiva /
yathā kaścidvṛkṣamārohati puṣpaphalopādānāyaiva na niṣprayojanaṃ nāpi patanāyaiva /
bhogaścāniṣṭādikāriṇāṃ candramasi nāstītyuktam /
tasmādiṣcādikāriṇa eva candramasamārohanti netare /
te tu saṃyamanaṃ yamālayamavagāhya svaduṣkṛtānurūpā yāmīryātanā anubhūya punarevemaṃ lokaṃ pratyavaronti /
evaṃbhūtau teṣāmārohāvarohau bhavataḥ /
kutaḥ - tadgatidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: How is this known? Because of the observation of that path.

children.text: tathāhi yamavacanasarūpā śrutiḥ prayatāmaniṣṭādikāriṇāṃ yamavaśyatāṃ darśayati- 'na sāṃparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham /
children.translated_text: For a <s>śruti</s> resembling the words of <s>Yama</s> shows the subjection to <s>Yama</s> of those of undesirable deeds: 'The hereafter does not reveal itself to the childish one who is heedless, deluded by the glamour of wealth.

children.text: ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punarvaśamāpadyate me' (kaṭha. 2.6) iti /
children.translated_text: "This world [alone exists], there is no other" — thinking thus, he falls again and again under my control' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.6).

children.text: 'vaivasvataṃ saṃgamanaṃ janānām' ityevañjātīyakaṃ ca bahveva yamavaśyatāprāptiliṅgaṃ bhavati // 13 //
children.translated_text: And 'the gathering place of <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>) for people' — such [passages] provide abundant indicatory marks of the attainment of subjection to <s>Yama</s>. // 13 //

The word 'but' reverses the [previous] position. It is not so that all go to the moon. Why? Because the ascent to the moon is for the purpose of enjoyment alone — not purposeless. Nor is it for the purpose of descending alone. Just as someone climbs a tree for the purpose of gathering flowers and fruits alone — not purposelessly, and not for the purpose of falling alone. And it was stated that the others — those who perform undesirable deeds — have no enjoyment on the moon. Therefore, only those who perform <s>Iṣṭa</s> and other [rituals] ascend to the moon, not the others. Those others, having descended into <s>Saṃyamana</s> — the abode of <s>Yama</s> — and having experienced torments inflicted by <s>Yama</s> corresponding to their evil deeds, return again to this very world. Such are their ascent and descent.

children.text: smaranti ca | BBs_3,1.14 |
children.translated_text: And [<s>Smṛti</s>] texts remember [this]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.14 |

children.text: apica manuvyāsaprabhṛtayaḥ śiṣṭāḥ saṃyamane pure yamāyattaṃ kapūyakarmavipākaṃ smaranti nāciketopākhyānādiṣu // 14 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, learned authorities such as <s>Manu</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and others remember that the ripening of foul <s>karma</s> is subject to <s>Yama</s> in the city of <s>Saṃyamana</s>, in narratives such as the story of <s>Naciketas</s> and the like. // 14 //

children.text: api ca sapta | BBs_3,1.15 |
children.translated_text: And moreover, the seven [hells]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.15 |

children.text: apica sapta narakā rauravapramukhā duṣkṛtaphalopabhogabhūmitvena smaryante paurāṇikaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, seven hells beginning with <s>Raurava</s> are remembered by the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (authors of <s>Purāṇas</s>) as places for experiencing the fruits of evil deeds.

children.text: tānaniṣṭādikāriṇaḥ prāpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: Those who perform undesirable deeds reach them.

children.text: kutaste candraṃ prāpnuyurityabhiprāyaḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: How then could they reach the moon? — this is the intent. // 15 //

children.text:
nanu viruddhamidaṃ yamāyattā yātanāḥ pāpakarmaṇo 'nubhavantīti /
yāvatā teṣu rauravādiṣvanye citraguptādayo nānādhiṣṭhātāraḥ smaryanta iti /
children.translated_text: But is this not contradictory — that the sufferings of the evil-doer are subject to <s>Yama</s>? For in those [hells] beginning with <s>Raurava</s>, other administrators — <s>Citragupta</s> and the like — are remembered.

children.text: netyāha-
children.translated_text: To this he says: No.

children.text: tatrāpi ca tadvyāpārādavirodhaḥ | BBs_3,1.16 |
children.translated_text: Even there, because of his (<s>Yama</s>'s) jurisdiction — there is no contradiction. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.16 |

children.text: teṣvapi saptasu narakeṣu tasyaiva yamasyādhiṣṭhātṛtvavyāpārābhyupagamādavirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in those seven hells, because <s>Yama</s> himself is accepted as the jurisdictional authority — there is no contradiction.

children.text: yamaprayuktā eva hi te citraguptādayo 'dhiṣṭhātāraḥ smaryante // 16 //
children.translated_text: For <s>Citragupta</s> and the other administrators are remembered as being appointed by <s>Yama</s>. // 16 //

children.text: vidyākarmaṇor iti tu prakṛtatvāt | BBs_3,1.17 |
children.translated_text: 'Of knowledge and <s>karma</s>' — because of being the topic [under discussion]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.17 |

children.text:
pañcāgnividyāyām 'vettha yathāsau loko na saṃpūryate' (chā. 5.3.3) ityasya praśnasya prativacanāvasare śrūyate- 'athaitayoḥ pathorna katareṇacana tānīmāni kṣudrāṇyasakṛdāvartīni bhūtāni bhavanti /
jāyasva mriyasvetyetattṛtīyaṃ sthānaṃ tenāsau loko na saṃpūryate' (chā. 5.10.8) iti /
tatraitayoḥ pathoriti vidyākarmaṇorityetat /
kasmāt /
prakṛtatvāt /
vidyākarmaṇī hi devayānapitṛyāṇayoḥ pathoḥ pratipattau prakṛte /
'tadya itthaṃ viduḥ' iti vidyā tayā pratipattavyo devayānaḥ panthāḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
'iṣṭāpūrte dattam' (chā. 5.10.1,3) iti karma tena pratipattavyaḥ pitṛyāṇaḥ panthāḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
tatppakriyāyām- 'athaitayoḥ pathorna katareṇacana' iti śrutam /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- ye na vidyāsādhanena devayāne patyadhikṛtā nāpi karmaṇā pitṛyāṇe teṣāmeṣa kṣudrajantulakṣaṇo 'sakṛdāvartī tṛtīyaḥ panthā bhavatīti /
tasmādapi nāniṣṭādikāribhiścandramāḥ prāpyate /
syādetat /
te 'pi candrabimbamāruhya tato 'varuhya kṣudrajantutvaṃ pratipatsyanta iti /
tadapi nāsti /
ārohānarthakyāt /
apica sarveṣu prayatsu candralokaṃ prāpnuvatsvasau lokaḥ prayadbhiḥ saṃpūryetetyataḥ praśnaviruddhaṃ prativacanaṃ prasajyeta /
tathāhi prativacanaṃ dātavyaṃ yathāsau loko na saṃpūryate /
avarohābhyupagamādasaṃpūrṇopapattiriti cet /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, at the occasion of answering the question 'Do you know why that world is not filled up?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.3.3), it is heard: 'Now, those who [travel] by neither of these two paths — they are those small creatures that are repeatedly born [and die]. "Be born, die" — this is the third state; by this, that world is not filled up' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.8). Therein, 'by these two paths' means of knowledge and <s>karma</s>. Why? Because of being the topic. For knowledge and <s>karma</s> are the topics in the context of attaining the two paths — the <s>Devayāna</s> and the <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s>. 'Those who know thus' — knowledge is the means by which the <s>Devayāna</s> path is proclaimed to be attained. '<s>Iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrifice and charitable works), giving' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1,3) — <s>karma</s> is the means by which the <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s> path is proclaimed to be attained. And in that very context, 'by neither of these two paths' is heard. This is what is stated: those who are qualified neither for the <s>Devayāna</s> through knowledge, nor for the <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s> through <s>karma</s> — for them, this third path, characterized by being small creatures repeatedly born, exists. Therefore, from this too, those who perform undesirable deeds do not reach the moon. One might suggest: they too, having ascended to the lunar sphere and having descended from there, will attain the state of small creatures. That too is not so — because of the purposelessness of the ascent. Moreover, if all those departing were to reach the lunar world, that world would be filled up by those departing — and the answer would then contradict the question. For the answer must be given [in terms of] why that world is not filled up. If it is said that because of the acceptance of descent, the non-filling-up is tenable —

children.text:
na /
aśrutatvāt /
satyamavarohādapyasaṃpūraṇamupapadyate /
śrutistu tṛtīyasthānasaṃkīrtanenāsaṃpūraṇaṃ darśayati- 'etattṛtīyaṃ sthānaṃ tenāsau loko na saṃpūryate' (chā. 5.10.8) iti /
tenānārohādevāsaṃpūraṇamiti yuktam /
avarohasyeṣṭādikāriṣvapyaviśiṣṭatve sati tṛtīyasthānoktyānarthakyaprasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because if descent were equally shared by those who perform <s>Iṣṭa</s> and the others, the mention of the third state would be purposeless.

children.text: tuśabdastu śākāntarīyavākyaprabhavāmaśeṣagamanāśaṅkāmucchinatti /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) [in the <s>sūtra</s>] removes the doubt — arising from the passage of another branch [of the <s>Veda</s>] — that all [beings] go [to the moon].

children.text: evaṃ satyadhikṛtāpekṣaḥ śākhāntarīye vākye sarvaśabdo 'vatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: This being so, the word 'all' in the passage of the other branch [of the <s>Veda</s>] is understood with reference to those who are qualified [for the <s>Devayāna</s> and <s>Pitṛyāṇa</s> paths].

children.text: ye vai kecidadhikṛtā asmāllokātprayanti candramasameva te sarve gacchantīti // 17 //
children.translated_text: 'All those who are qualified and depart from this world go to the moon.' // 17 //

No. Because it is not heard [in that way]. True, the non-filling-up is tenable even through descent. But the <s>śruti</s> shows the non-filling-up through the mention of the third state: 'This is the third state; by this, that world is not filled up' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.8). Therefore, it is proper that the non-filling-up is due to non-ascent alone.

children.text: yatpunaruktaṃ dehalābhopapattaye sarve candramasaṃ gantumarhanti, pañcamyāmāhutāvityāhutisaṃkhyāniyamāditi /
children.translated_text: As for the further statement that all should go to the moon to make the obtaining of a body tenable, because of the rule regarding the number of oblations — 'at the fifth oblation' —

children.text: tatpratyucyate-
children.translated_text: to that the reply is:

children.text: na tṛtīye tathopalabdheḥ | BBs_3,1.18 |
children.translated_text: Not in the third [state], because it is so observed. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.18 |

children.text:
na tṛtīye sthāne dehalābhāya pañcasaṃkhyāniyama āhutīnāmādartavyaḥ /
kutaḥ - tathopalabdheḥ /
tathāhyantareṇaivāhutisaṃkhyāniyamaṃ varṇitena prakāreṇa tṛtīyasthānaprāptirupalabhyate 'jāyasva mriyasvetyetattṛtīyaṃ sthānam' (chā. 5.10.8) iti /
apica 'pañcamyāmāhutāvāpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti' (chā. 5.3.3) iti manuṣyaśarīrahetutvenāhutisaṃkhyā saṃkīrtyate na kīṭapataṅgādiśarīrahetutvena, puruṣaśabdasya manuṣyajātivacanatvāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'At the fifth oblation, water becomes endowed with a human voice' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.3.3) — the number of oblations is mentioned as the cause of a human body, not as the cause of the bodies of insects, moths, and such — because the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' denotes the human species.

children.text: apica pañcamyāmāhutāvapāṃ puruṣavacastvamupadiśyate nāpañcamyāmāhutau puruṣavacastvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, vākyasya dvyarthatādoṣāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, what is taught is that 'at the fifth oblation, water becomes endowed with a human voice' — it is not denied that 'without the fifth oblation, water does not become endowed with a human voice' — because of the fault of the sentence having two meanings.

children.text: tatra yeṣāmārohāvarohau saṃbhavatasteṣāṃ pañcamyāmāhutau deha udbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Therein, for those whose ascent and descent are possible — for them, the body will arise at the fifth oblation.

children.text: anyeṣāṃ tu vinaivāhutisaṃkhyayā bhūtāntaropasṛṣṭābhiradbhirdeha ārabhyate // 18 //
children.translated_text: But for the others, the body is begun by water that is sent forth by [other] beings, without any [specific] number of oblations. // 18 //

In the third state, the rule of five as the number of oblations for the obtaining of a body should not be insisted upon. Why? Because it is so observed. For the attainment of the third state is observed through the process described — even without the rule regarding the number of oblations: 'Be born, die — this is the third state' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.8).

children.text: smaryate 'pi ca loke | BBs_3,1.19 |
children.translated_text: And it is remembered in the world. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.19 |

children.text:
apica smaryate loke /
droṇadhṛṣṭadyumnaprabhṛtīnāṃ sītādraupadīprabhṛtīnāṃ cāyonijatvam /
tatra droṇādīnāṃ yoṣidviṣayaikāhutirnāsti /
children.translated_text: In the case of <s>Droṇa</s> and others, the one oblation pertaining to a woman is absent.

children.text: dhṛṣṭadyumnādīnāṃ tu yoṣitpuruṣaviṣaye dve apyāhutī na staḥ /
children.translated_text: In the case of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and others, the two oblations pertaining to a woman and a man are both absent.

children.text: yathā ca tatrāhutisaṃkhyānādaro bhavatyevamanyatrāpi bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Just as there is disregard for the number of oblations in those cases, so too it will be in other cases.

children.text: balākāpyantareṇaiva retaḥsekaṃ garbhaṃ dhatta iti lokarūḍhiḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: And a she-crane conceives without insemination — this is common knowledge. // 19 //
Moreover, it is remembered in the world that <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, and others — and <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Draupadī</s>, and others — were not born from a womb.

children.text: darśanāc ca | BBs_3,1.20 |
children.translated_text: And because of observation. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.20 |

children.text: apica caturvidhe bhūtagrāme jarāyujāṇḍajasvedajodbhijjalakṣaṇe svedajodbhijjayorantareṇaiva grāmyadharmamutpattidarśanādāhutisaṃkhyānādaro bhavati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, among the four classes of beings — those born from a womb, from an egg, from moisture, and from the ground — since the birth of those born from moisture and from the ground is observed even without sexual intercourse, the disregard for the number of oblations follows.

children.text: evamanyatrāpi bhaviṣyati // 20 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, it will be in other cases too. // 20 //

children.text: FN: jīvajaṃ jarāyujam , udbhijjaṃ vṛkṣādi /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Jīvaja</s>' means born from a womb (<s>jarāyuja</s>). '<s>Udbhijja</s>' means trees and the like.

children.text:
nanu 'teṣāṃ khalveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ trīṇyeva bījāni bhavanti aṇḍajaṃ jīvajamudbhijjam' (chā. 6.3.1) iti /
atra trividha eva bhūtagrāmaḥ śrūyate kathaṃ caturvidhatvaṃ bhūtagrāmasya pratijñātamiti /
atrocyate-
children.translated_text: But [the <s>śruti</s>] says 'There are only three kinds of seeds for these beings: born from an egg, born from a living being, and born from a sprout' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.1). Here only three classes of beings are heard [in <s>śruti</s>] — how was the fourfold nature of beings claimed? To this it is said:

children.text: tṛtīyaśabdāvarodhaḥ saṃśokajasya | BBs_3,1.21 |
children.translated_text: The inclusion of the moisture-born under the third term. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.21 |

children.text: 'āṇḍajaṃ jīvajamujadbhijam' (chā. 6.3.1) ityatra tṛtīyenodbhijjaśabdenaiva svedajopasaṃgrahaḥ kṛtaḥ pratyetavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In 'born from an egg, born from a living being, born from a sprout' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.1) — by the third term '<s>udbhijja</s>' (born from a sprout), the inclusion of the moisture-born (<s>svedaja</s>) should be understood.

children.text: ubhayorapi svedajodbhijjayorbhūmyudakodbhedaprabhavatvasya tulyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because for both the moisture-born and the sprout-born, the emergence from earth and water is equally characteristic.

children.text: sthāvarodbhedāttu vilakṣaṇo jaṅgamodbheda ityanyatra svedajodbhijjayorbhedavāda ityavirodhaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: But the emergence of mobile [beings] is distinguished from the emergence of stationary [beings] — therefore, in other contexts, the distinction between the moisture-born and the sprout-born is spoken of. There is no contradiction. // 21 //

children.text: FN: saṃśokajaṃ svedajam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Saṃśokaja</s>' means moisture-born.

children.text: 4 sābhāvyāpatyadhikaraṇam / sū. 22
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Sābhāvyāpatti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Attainment of Specific Nature). <s>Sūtra</s> 22.

children.text: sābhāvyāpattirupapatteḥ | BBs_3,1.22 |
children.translated_text: The attainment of a specific nature [is established], because of its tenability. | <s>BBs</s> 3.1.22 |

children.text:
iṣṭādikāriṇaścandramasamāruhya tasminyāvatsaṃpātamuṣitvā tataḥsānuśayā avarohantītyuktam /
atāvarohaprakāraḥ parīkṣyate /
tatreyamavarohaśrutirbhavati- 'athaicamevādhvānaṃ punarnivartante yathetamākāśamākāśādvāyuṃ vāyirbhūtvā dhūmo bhavati dhūmo bhūtvābhraṃ bhavatyabhraṃ bhūtvā megho bhūtvā pravarṣati' (chā. 5.10.5) iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimākāśādisvarūpamevāvārohantaḥ pratipadyante kiṃvākāśādisāmyamiti /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvadākāśādisvarūpameva pratipadyanta iti /
kutaḥ evaṃ hi śrutirbhavati /
itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt /
śrutilakṣamāviṣaye ca śrutirnyāyyā na lakṣaṇā /
tathāca vāyurbhūtvā dhūmo bhavatītyevamādīnyakṣarāṇi tattatsvarūpopattāvāñjasyenāvakalpante /
tasmādākāśādisvarūpapratipattiriti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ākāśādisāmyaṃ pratipadyanta iti /
candramaṇḍale yadaṃmayaṃ śarīramupabhogārthamārabdhaṃ tadupabhogakṣaye sati pravilīyamānaṃ sūkṣmamākāśasamaṃ bhavati tato vāyorvaśameti tato dhūmādibhiḥ saṃpṛcyata iti /
tadetaducyate- 'yathetamākāśamākāśādvāyum' (chā. 5.10.5) ityevamādinā /
kuta etat /
upapatteḥ /
evaṃ hyetadupapadyate /
nahyanyasyānyabhāvo mukhya upapadyate /
ākāśasvarūpapratipattau ca vāyvādikrameṇāvaroho nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: And if one were to assume the nature of space, the descent through the sequence of wind and the rest would not be proper.

children.text: vibhutvāccākāśena nityasaṃbandhavattvānna tatsādṛśyāpatteranyastatsaṃbandho ghaṭate /
children.translated_text: And because space is all-pervading, since one is always in connection with it, attaining similarity with it — which is [always already the case] — does not warrant a separate connection with it.

children.text: śrutyasaṃbhave ca lakṣaṇāśrayaṇaṃ nyāyyameva /
children.translated_text: And when the literal meaning is impossible, resorting to the figurative meaning is indeed proper.

children.text: ata ākāśāditulyatāpattirevātrākāśādibhāva ityupacaryate // 22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the attainment of equality with space and the rest is what is figuratively called 'becoming space and the rest.' // 22 //

It has been stated that those who have performed sacrifices (<s>iṣṭa</s>) and the like, having ascended to the moon, dwell there as long as their [merit] lasts, and then descend with residual impressions (<s>anuśaya</s>).
Now the manner of descent is examined.
The <s>śruti</s> on descent is as follows: 'They return by the same path — from space to space, from space to wind; having become wind, one becomes smoke; having become smoke, one becomes mist; having become mist, one becomes a cloud; having become a cloud, one rains down' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.5).
There arises a doubt: Do those descending actually assume the very nature of space and the rest, or do they merely attain similarity with space and the rest?
The prima facie view is that they assume the very nature of space and the rest.
Why? Because the <s>śruti</s> says so.
Otherwise, it would be figurative.
And where both literal and figurative meanings are possible, the literal meaning is proper, not the figurative.
And thus the words 'having become wind, one becomes smoke' and so forth straightforwardly apply to the assumption of those very natures.
Therefore, the conclusion is that they assume the very nature of space and the rest.
Given this position, we say: They attain similarity with space and the rest.
The body that was assumed for the purpose of enjoyment in the lunar sphere, upon the exhaustion of that enjoyment, dissolves and becomes subtle, equal to space; then it comes under the power of the wind; then it comes into contact with smoke and the rest.
This is stated by 'From space to space, from space to wind' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.5) and so forth.
Why is this so?
Because of propriety.
For this alone is proper.
For the literal transformation of one thing into another is not proper.

children.text: 5 nāticirādhikaraṇam / sū. 23
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Nāticirādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of 'Not Too Long'). <s>Sūtra</s> 23.

children.text: nāticireṇa viśeṣāt | BBs_3,1.23 |
children.translated_text: Not too long [a time] — because of the specification. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.23 |

children.text:
tatrākāśādipratipattau prāgvirīhyādipratipatterbhavati viśayaḥ /
kiṃ dīrghaṃ kālaṃ pūrvapūrvasādṛśyenāvasthāyottarasādṛśyaṃ gacchantyutālpamiti /
tatrāniyamo niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasyābhāvāditi /
evaṃ prāpta idamāha- nāticireṇeti /
alpamalpaṃ kālamākāśādibhāvenāvasthāya varṣadhārābhiḥ sahemāṃ bhuvamāpatanti /
kuta etat /
viśeṣadarśanāt /
tathāhi vrīhyādibhāvāpatteranantaraṃ viśinaṣṭi- 'ato vai khalu durniṣprapataram'
children.translated_text:
In the attainment of [the states of] space and the rest, prior to the attainment of the state of rice and the like, there is a question:
Do they remain for a long time in the similarity with each preceding [state] before passing to the next similarity, or for a short time?
The prima facie view is that there is no restriction, because of the absence of a restrictive scripture.
Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: 'Not too long.'
They remain for a short, short time in the states of space and the rest, and then descend to this earth along with the streams of rain.
Why is this so?
Because of the specification.
For thus, immediately after [stating] the attainment of the state of rice and the rest, [the <s>śruti</s>] specifies: 'From this, it is extremely difficult to emerge'

children.text:
(chā. 5.10.6) iti /
takāra etaścandasyāṃ prakriyāyāṃ lupto mantavyaḥ /
durniprapatataraṃ durniṣkramataraṃ duḥkhataramasmādvrīhyādibhāvānniḥsaraṇaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
tadatra duḥkhaṃ niṣprapatanaṃ pradarśayanpūrveṣu sukhaṃ niṣprapatanaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: In showing the painful emergence at that [later stage], [the <s>śruti</s>] thereby shows the easy emergence at the earlier stages.

children.text: sukhaduḥkhatāviśeṣaścāyaṃ niṣprapatanasya kālālpatvadīrghatvanimittaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this distinction of ease and pain in emergence is caused by the shortness and length of the time [spent in each state].

children.text: tasminnavadhau śarīrāniṣpatterupabhogāsaṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Because at that stage, since the body has not yet been produced, enjoyment is impossible.

children.text: tasmādvrīhyādibhāvāpatteḥ prāgalpenaiva kālenāvarohaḥ syāditi // 23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the descent prior to the attainment of the state of rice and the like should take only a short time. // 23 //

(<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.6).
The letter '<s>t</s>' in this word should be understood as elided according to <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic) usage.
'<s>Durniṣpratataram</s>' means 'more difficult to come out of,' i.e., the emergence from the state of rice and the like is more painful — this is the meaning.

children.text: 6 anyādhiṣṭhitādhikaraṇam / sū. 24-27
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Anyādhiṣṭhitādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of [Bodies] Presided Over by Others). <s>Sūtras</s> 24-27.

children.text: anyādhiṣṭhiteṣu pūrvavadabhilāpāt | BBs_3,1.24 |
children.translated_text: In [bodies] presided over by others — as before, because of the mention [being without reference to karma]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.24 |

children.text: tasminnevārohe pravarṣaṇānantaraṃ paṭhyate- 'ta iha vrīhiyavā oṣadhivanaspatayastilamāṣā iti jāyante' (chā. 5.10.6)
children.translated_text: In that very descent, after raining down, [the <s>śruti</s>] reads: 'They are born here as rice, barley, herbs, trees, sesame, and beans' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.6).

children.text:
iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimasminnavadhau sthāvarajātyāpannāḥ sthāvarasukhaduḥkhabhājo 'nuśāyino bhavatyāhosvitkṣetrajñāntarādhiṣṭhiteṣu sthāvaraśarīreṣu saṃśleṣamātraṃ gacchantīti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
sthāvarajātyāpannāstatsukhaduḥkhabhājo 'nuśayino bhavantīti /
kuta etat /
janermukhyārthatvopapatteḥ sthāvarabhāvasya ca śrutismṛtyorupabhogasthānatvaprasiddheḥ /
paśuhiṃsādiyogācceṣṭādeḥ karmajātasyāniṣṭaphalatvopapatteḥ /
tasmānmukhyamevedamanuśayināṃ vrīhyādijanma /
śvādijanmavat /
yathā śvayoniṃ vā sūkarayoniṃ vā camḍālayoniṃ veti mukhyamevānuśayināṃ śvādijanma tatsukhaduḥkhānvitaṃ bhavati /
evaṃ vrīhyādiṣu saṃsargamātramanuśayinaḥ pratipadyante na tatsukhaduḥkhānvitaṃ bhavati /
evaṃ vrīhyādijanmāpīti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ anyairjīvairadhiṣṭhiteṣu vrīhyādiṣu saṃsargamātramanuśayinaḥ pratipadyante na tatsukhaduḥkhabhājo bhavanti /
pūrvavat /
yathā vāyudhūmādibhāvo 'nuśayināṃ tatsaṃśleṣamātram /
evaṃ vrīhyādibhāvo 'pi jātisthāvaraiḥ saṃśleṣamātram /
kuta etat /
tadvadevehāpyabhilāpāt /
ko 'bhilāpasya tadvadbhāvaḥ /
karmavyāpāramantareṇa saṃkīrtanam /
yathākāśādiṣu pravarṣaṇānteṣu na kañcitkarmavyāpāraṃ parāmṛśatyevaṃ vrīhyādijanmanyapi /
tasmānnāstyatra sukhaduḥkhabhāktvamanuśayinām /
yatra tu sukhaduḥkhabhāktvamabhipraiti parāmṛśati tatra karmavyāpāraṃ ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ kapūyacaraṇā iti ca /
apica mukhye 'nuśayināṃ vrīhyādijanmani vrīhyādiṣu lūyamāneṣu kaṇḍyamāneṣu pacyamāneṣu bhakṣyamāṇeṣu ca tadabhimānino 'nuśayinaḥ pravaseyuḥ /
yo hi jīvo yaccharīramabhimanyate sa tasminpīḍyamāne pravasatīti prasiddham /
tatra vrīhyādibhāvādretaḥsigbhāvo 'nuśayināṃ nābhilapyeta /
ataḥ saṃsargamātramanuśayināmanyādhiṣṭhiteṣu vrīhyādiṣu bhavati /
etena janermukhyārthatvaṃ pratibrūyādupabhogasthānatvaṃ ca sthāvarabhāvasya /
children.translated_text: By this, the literal meaning of 'birth' and the status of plant-existence as a place of experience are answered.

children.text: naca vayamupabhogasthānatvaṃ sthāvarabhāvasyāvajānīmahe /
children.translated_text: And we do not deny that plant-existence is a place of experience.

children.text: bhavatvanyeṣāṃ jantūnāmapuṇyasāmarthyena sthāvarabhāvamupagatānāmetadupabhogasthānam /
children.translated_text: Let it be a place of experience for other beings who have attained plant-existence by the force of demerit.

children.text: candramasastvavarohanto 'nuśayino na sthāvarabhāvamupabhuñjata ityācakṣmahe // 24 //
children.translated_text: But we say that those possessing residual impressions who are descending from the lunar sphere do not experience plant-existence. // 24 //

There arises a doubt: At this stage, do those possessing residual impressions (<s>anuśayin</s>) attain the status of plant-species and experience the pleasures and pains of plants, or do they merely come into contact with plant-bodies that are presided over by other <s>jīvas</s>?
What is the prima facie view?
That they attain the status of plant-species and experience the pleasures and pains of those [plants].
Why?
Because the literal meaning of 'birth' [as actual birth] is proper, and because the status of plant-existence is well known from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> as a place of experience.
And because it is proper that rituals involving animal sacrifice and the like, being of the nature of undesirable action, yield undesirable fruits.
Therefore, the birth of those possessing residual impressions as rice and the like is indeed literal —
like the birth as dogs and the like.
Just as the birth of those possessing residual impressions as dogs, pigs, or <s>caṇḍālas</s> is literal and accompanied by the pleasures and pains of those [species] — 'They attain the womb of a dog, the womb of a pig, or the womb of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>' —
so too, those possessing residual impressions attain mere contact with rice and the like, not [birth] accompanied by the pleasures and pains of those [plants].
[Correction:] So too the birth as rice and the like [should be literal] — this is [the prima facie view].
Given this position, we say: Those possessing residual impressions attain mere contact with rice and the like that are presided over by other <s>jīvas</s> — they do not experience the pleasures and pains of those [plants].
As before.
Just as the states of wind, smoke, and the rest for those possessing residual impressions were mere contact with those [elements] —
so too the state of rice and the like is mere contact with the stationary beings [i.e., plants].
Why is this so?
Because of the mention being the same as before.
What is the sameness of mention?
The mention without reference to any activity of <s>karma</s>.
Just as in [the stages of] space and the rest, ending with rain, [the <s>śruti</s>] does not refer to any activity of <s>karma</s> — so too in the birth as rice and the like.
Therefore, there is no experience of pleasure and pain for those possessing residual impressions here.
But where [the <s>śruti</s>] intends experience of pleasure and pain, there it does refer to the activity of <s>karma</s> — 'those of pleasant conduct' and 'those of foul conduct.'
Moreover, if the birth of those possessing residual impressions as rice and the like were literal, then when rice and the like are cut, husked, cooked, and eaten, those possessing residual impressions who identify with those [plant-bodies] would depart [from them at each stage].
For it is well known that a <s>jīva</s> who identifies with a particular body departs when that [body] is afflicted.
In that case, the state of being semen after the state of rice and the like would not be stated for those possessing residual impressions.
Therefore, those possessing residual impressions have mere contact with rice and the like that are presided over by other [<s>jīvas</s>].

children.text: aśuddham iti cen na śabdāt | BBs_3,1.25 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said the ritual is] impure — [we say] no, because of the scriptural word. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.25 |

children.text:
yatpunaruktaṃ paśuhiṃsādiyogādaśuddhamādhvarikaṃ karma tasyāniṣṭamapi phalamavakalpata ityato mukhyamevānuśayināṃ vrīhyādijanmāstu tatra gauṇī kalpanānarthiketi tatparihriyate /
na, śāstrahetutvāddharmādharmavijñānasya /
ayaṃ dharmo 'yamadharma iti śāstrameva vijñāne kāraṇam /
atīndriyatvāttayoḥ aniyatadeśakālanimittatvācca /
yasmindeśe kāle nimitte ca yo dharmo 'nuṣṭhīyate sa eva deśakālanimittāntareṣvadharmo bhavati /
tena śāstrādṛte dharmādharmaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ na kasyacidasti /
śāstrācca hiṃsānugrahādyātmako jyotiṣṭomo dharma ityavadhāritaḥ sa kathamaśuddha iti śakyate vaktum /
children.translated_text:
As for the statement that Vedic ritual involving animal sacrifice and the like is impure, and that its fruit too can be undesirable — and therefore the birth of those possessing residual impressions as rice and the like should be literal, the figurative interpretation being unnecessary — that is answered:
No, because <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are known only through scripture.
'This is <s>dharma</s>, this is <s>adharma</s>' — scripture alone is the means of knowledge for this.
Because they are beyond the senses.
And because the place, time, and occasion [that determine them] are not fixed.
The very <s>dharma</s> that is practiced at a particular place, time, and occasion becomes <s>adharma</s> at other places, times, and occasions.
Therefore, without scripture, no one has knowledge regarding <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
And since from scripture the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, whose nature involves both slaughter and benefit, has been ascertained as <s>dharma</s> — how can it be called impure?

children.text:
nanu 'na hiṃsyātsarvā bhūtāni' iti śāstrameva bhūtaviṣayāṃ hiṃsāmadharma ityavagamayati /
bāḍham /
utsargastu saḥ /
apavādaḥ 'agnīṣomīyaṃ paśumālabheta' iti /
utsargāpavādayośca vyavasthitaviṣayatvam /
tasmādviśuddhaṃ karma vaidikaṃ, śiṣṭairanuṣṭhīyamānatvādanindyamānatvācca /
tena na tasya pratirūpaṃ phalaṃ jātisthāvaratvam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, plant-existence is not a fitting fruit for such [pure ritual].

children.text: naca śvādijanmādivadapi vrīhyādijanma bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: And the birth as rice and the like cannot be like the birth as dogs and the like.

children.text: taddhi kapūyataraṇānadhikṛtyocyate naivamiha vaiśeṣikaḥ kaścidadhikāro 'sti /
children.translated_text: For that [birth as dogs etc.] is stated with reference to those of 'more foul conduct' — but here there is no such specific qualification.

children.text: ataścandramaṇḍalaskhalitānāmanuśāyināṃ vrīhyādisaṃśleṣamātraṃ tadbhāva ityupacaryate // 25 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for those possessing residual impressions who have fallen from the lunar sphere, mere contact with rice and the like is figuratively called 'becoming those.' // 25 //

But does not scripture itself, through 'One should not harm any being,' make known that harming beings is <s>adharma</s>?
Indeed.
But that is the general rule (<s>utsarga</s>).
The exception (<s>apavāda</s>) is: 'One should sacrifice the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal.'
And the general rule and exception have their respective fixed domains.
Therefore, Vedic ritual is pure — because it is practiced by the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) and because it is not censured.

children.text: retaḥsigyogo 'tha | BBs_3,1.26 |
children.translated_text: Then [comes] the conjunction with semen. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.26 |

children.text:
itaśca vrīhyādisaṃśleṣamātraṃ tadbhāvo yatkāraṇaṃ vrīhyādibhāvasyānantaramanuśayināṃ retaḥsigbhāva āmnāyate - 'yo yo hyannamatti yo retaḥ siñcati tadbhūya eva bhavati' (chā. 5.10.6) iti /
nacātra mukhyo retaḥsigbhāvaḥ saṃbhavati /
cirajāto hi prāptayauvano retaḥsigbhavati /
children.translated_text: For one becomes capable of discharging semen only after being born long ago and having attained youth.

children.text: kathamivānupacaritaṃ tadbhāvamadyamānānnānugato 'nuśayī pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: How can those possessing residual impressions, who follow the food being eaten, assume the state of being semen in a non-figurative sense?

children.text: tatra tāvadavaśyaṃ retaḥsigyoga eva retaḥsigbhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the state of being semen must necessarily be understood as merely conjunction with semen.

children.text: tadvadvrīhyādibhāvo 'pi vrīhyādiyoga evetyavirodhaḥ // 26 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the state of rice and the like too is merely conjunction with rice and the like — there is no contradiction. // 26 //

And for this further reason, the state of rice and the like is mere contact: because after the state of rice and the like, the state of semen is taught for those possessing residual impressions — 'Whoever eats the food and discharges semen, one becomes that again' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.6).
And a literal state of being semen is not possible here.

children.text: yoneḥ śarīram | BBs_3,1.27 |
children.translated_text: From the womb, [comes] the body. | <s>BBs</s> 3,1.27 |

children.text: atha retaḥsigbhāvasyānantaraṃ yonau niṣikte retasi yoneradhikaśarīramanuśayināmanuśayaphalopabhogāya jāyata ityāha śāstram - ''tadya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ' (chāya 5.10.7) ityādi /
children.translated_text: Then, after the state of being semen, when the semen is deposited in the womb, scripture states that from the womb a further body is born for those possessing residual impressions, for the purpose of experiencing the fruits of their residual impressions: 'Now, those who are of pleasant conduct here' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.7) and so forth.

children.text: tasmādapyavagamyate nāvarohe vrīhyādibhāvāvasare taccharīrameva sukhaduḥkānvitaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: From this too it is understood that during the descent, at the stage of the state of rice and the like, the body [of rice etc.] itself is not accompanied by pleasure and pain.

children.text: tasmādvrīhyādisaṃśleṣamātramanuśayināṃ tajjanmeti siddham // 27 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the birth of those possessing residual impressions as rice and the like is mere contact with those [plants]. // 27 //

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye tṛtīyādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 1 //

children.text: tṛtīyādhyāye dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: atrapāde tattvaṃpadārthapariśodhanavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: In this <s>pāda</s>, the examination for the purification of the meaning of 'That thou art' is presented.

children.text: 1 saṃdhyādhikaraṇam / sū. 1-6
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Saṃdhyādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Twilight State). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-6.

children.text: sandhye sṛṣṭirāha hi | BBs_3,2.1 |
children.translated_text: In the twilight state [i.e., dream], there is creation — for [the <s>śruti</s>] says so. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.1 |

children.text:
atikrīnte pāde pañcāgnividyāmudāhṛtya jīvasya saṃsāragatiprabhedaḥ prapañcitaḥ /
idānīṃ tu tasyaivāvasthābhedaḥ prapañcyate /
idamāmananti- 'sa yatra prasvapiti' (bṛ. 4.3.9) ityupakramya 'na tatra rathā na rathayogā na panthāno bhavantyatha rathānrathayogānpathaḥ sṛjate' (bṛ. 4.3.10) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ prabodha iva svapne 'pi pāramārthikī sṛṣṭirāhosvinmāyāmayīti /
tatra tāvatpratipadyate saṃdhye tathyarūpā sṛṣṭiriti /
saṃdhyamiti svapnānamācaṣṭe, vede prayogadarśanāt 'saṃdhyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ svapnasthānam' (bṛ. 4.3.9) iti /
dvayorlokasthānayoḥ prabodhasaṃprasādasthānayorvā saṃdhau bhavatīti saṃdhyam /
children.translated_text: It is [called] '<s>saṃdhya</s>' (twilight) because it occurs at the junction (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of the two states of waking and deep sleep.

children.text: tasminsaṃdhye sthāne tathyarūpaiva sṛṣṭirbhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: In that twilight state, the creation should indeed be of a real nature.

children.text: kutaḥ - yataḥ pramāṇabhūtā śrutirevamāha 'atha rathānnathayogānpathaḥ sṛjate' (bṛ. 4,3.10) ityādi /
children.translated_text: Why? Because the authoritative <s>śruti</s> itself says so: 'It creates chariots, chariot-yokes, and roads' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.10) and so forth.

children.text: sa hi karteti copasaṃhārādevamevāvagamyate // 1 //
children.translated_text: And because of the conclusion 'For it is the creator' — this very understanding [of real creation] follows. // 1 //

In the preceding <s>pāda</s>, having cited the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, the different courses of the <s>jīva</s>'s transmigration were elaborated.
Now, the different states of that very [<s>jīva</s>] are elaborated.
The following is taught: Beginning with 'Where it sleeps' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.9), [the <s>śruti</s> states]: 'There are no chariots there, no chariot-yokes, no roads — but it creates chariots, chariot-yokes, and roads' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.10) and so forth.
There arises a doubt: Is the creation in dream real, as in the waking state, or is it merely illusory (<s>māyāmaya</s>)?
The prima facie view is: In the twilight state, the creation is of a real nature.
The word '<s>saṃdhya</s>' (twilight) denotes dream, because of the observed Vedic usage: 'The twilight is the third state, the dream state' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.9).

children.text: nirmātāraṃ caike putrādayaś ca | BBs_3,2.2 |
children.translated_text: And some [teach that the Self is] the fashioner, and also sons and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.2 |

children.text:
apicaike śākhino 'sminneva saṃdhye sthāne kāmānāṃ nirmātāramātmānamāmananti- 'ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ' (ka. 5.8) iti /
putrādayaśca tatra kāmā abhipreyante kāmyanta iti /
children.translated_text:
Moreover, some <s>śākhins</s> (followers of a particular Vedic recension) teach that in this very twilight state, the Self is the fashioner of desires: 'He who is awake among those who sleep, the <s>Puruṣa</s> fashioning desire after desire' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.8).
And 'sons and the like' — there, [objects of] desire such as sons and the like are intended, [called] desires because they are desired.

children.text: nanu kāmaśabdenecchāviśeṣā evocyeran /
children.translated_text: Objection: By the word '<s>kāma</s>' (desire), only specific desires would be denoted.

children.text:
na /
'śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrānvṛṇīṣva' (ka. 1.23) iti prakṛtyānte 'kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi' (ka. 1.24) iti prakṛteṣu tatra tatra putrādiṣu kāmaśabdasya prayuktatvāt /
prājñaṃ cainaṃ nirmitāraṃ prakaraṇavākyaśeṣābhyāṃ pratīmaḥ /
prājñasya hīdaṃ karaṇam 'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmāt' (ka. 2.24) ityādi, tadviṣaya eva ca vākyaśeṣo 'pi- 'tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate /
tasmiṃllokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana'' (ka. 5.8) iti /
children.translated_text: 'That alone is the pure, that is <s>Brahman</s>, that alone is called the immortal; in it all worlds are established, and no one ever transcends it' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.8).

children.text: prājñakartṛkā ca sṛṣṭistathyarūpā samadhigatā jāgaritāśrayā tathā svapnāśrayāpi sṛṣṭirbhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: And since the creation attributed to <s>Prājña</s> has been established as real in the waking state, so too the dream-state creation should be [considered] real.

children.text: tathāca śrutiḥ - atho khalvāhurjāgaritadeśa evāsyaiṣa iti yāni hyeva jāgratpaśyati tāni suptaḥ (bṛ. 4.3.14) iti svapnajāgaritayoḥ samānanyāyatāṃ śrāvayati /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Now, they say that his [creation in dream] is the same as in the waking region — for whatever he sees while awake, he [also sees while] asleep' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.14) — [this] teaches the equal validity of dream and waking.

children.text: tasmāttathyarūpaiva saṃdhye sṛṣṭariti // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the creation in the intermediate state [of dreams] is of a real nature alone. // 2 //

No. Because the word '<s>kāma</s>' is used for the specific things — sons and the like — that are set forth in the context, with 'Choose sons and grandsons of a hundred years' life' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.23) and, at the end of the context, 'I make you the recipient of desires' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 1.24). And we understand this creator to be <s>Prājña</s> (<s>Brahman</s>), from both the context and the remainder of the passage. For the description of <s>Prājña</s> is: 'Beyond <s>dharma</s>, beyond <s>adharma</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.14) and the like, and the remainder of the passage too pertains to that very [<s>Prājña</s>]:

children.text: evaṃ prāpte pratyāha-
children.translated_text: Having set forth this [prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] replies:

children.text: māyāmātraṃ tu kārtsnyenānabhivyaktasvarūpatvāt | BBs_3,2.3 |
children.translated_text: <s>Māyāmātraṃ tu kārtsnyenānabhivyaktasvarūpatvāt</s> — But [the dream-creation] is mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion), because its nature is not fully manifest in all respects. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.3 |

children.text:
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyavartayati /
naitadasti yaduktaṃ saṃdhye sṛṣṭiḥ pāramārthikīti /
māyaiva saṃdhye sṛṣṭirna pāramārthagandho 'pyasti /
kutaḥ - kārtsnyenānabhivyaktasvarūpatvāt /
nahi kārtsnyenapāramārthavastudharmeṇābhivyaktasvarūpaḥ svapnaḥ /
kiṃ punaratra kārtsnyamabhipretaṃ deśakālanimittānyabādhaśca /
nahi paramārthavastuviṣayāṇi deśakālanimittānyabādhāśca svapne saṃbhāvyante /
na tāvatsvapne rathādīnāmucito deśaḥ saṃbhavati /
nahi saṃvṛte dehadeśerathādayo 'vakāśaṃ labheran /
syādetat /
bahirdehātsvapnam drakṣyati deśāntaritadravyagrahaṇāt /
darśayati ca śrutirbahirdehātsvapnam- 'bahiṣkulāyādamṛtaścaritvā /
sa īyate 'mṛto yatra kāmam' (bṛ. 4.3.12) iti sthitigatipratyayabhedaśca nāniṣkrānte jantau sāmañjasyāmaśnuvīteti /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) sets aside the [prima facie] position. What was said — that the creation in the intermediate state is ultimately real — that is not so. The creation in the intermediate state is mere <s>māyā</s>; there is not even a trace of ultimate reality [in it]. Why? Because its nature is not fully manifest in all respects. For a dream is not one whose nature is manifest with all the properties of ultimately real things. What then is meant by 'in all respects'? Place, time, efficient cause, and non-sublation. For in dreams, the place, time, efficient causes, and non-sublation that pertain to ultimately real things are not conceivable. First, in a dream, no proper place for chariots and the like is possible. For within the confined space of the body, chariots and the like would find no room. It might be said: one sees dreams while outside the body, because of the apprehension of objects located in other places. And the <s>śruti</s> shows that dreams occur outside the body: 'Having wandered about immortally outside the nest [i.e., the body], he goes, the immortal one, wherever he wishes' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.12) — and the difference between cognitions of staying and going would not be coherent if the being had not gone out.

children.text:
netyucyate /
nahi suptasya jantoḥ kṣaṇamātreṇa yojanaśatāntaritaṃ deśaṃ paryetuṃ viparyetuṃ ca tataḥ sāmarthyaṃ saṃbhāvyate /
kvacicca pratyāgamanavarjitaṃ svapnaṃ śrāvayati kuruṣvahamadya śayāno nidrayābhiplutaḥ svapne pañcālānabhigataścāsminpratibuddhaśceti /
dehāccedapeyātpañcāleṣu pratihudhyeta na tānasāvabhigata iti kuruṣveva tu pratibudhyate /
yena cāyaṃ dehena deśāntaramaśnuvāno manyate tamanye pārśvasthāḥ śayanadeśa eva paśyanti /
yathābhūtāni cāyaṃ deśāntarāṇi svapne paśyati na tāni tathābhūtānyeva bhavanti /
paridhāvaṃścetpaśyejjāgradvadvastubhūtamāra athamākalayet /
darśayati ca śrutirantareva dehe svapnam- 'sa yatraitatsvapnyayā carati' ityupakramya 'sve śarīre yathākāmaṃ parivartate' (bṛ. 2.1.18) iti /
ataśca śrutyupapattivirodhādbahiṣkulāyaśrutirgauṇī vyākhyātavyayā bahiriva kulāyādamṛtaścaritveti /
yo hi vasannapi śarīre na tena prayojanaṃ karoti sa bahiriva śarīrādbhavatīti /
sthitigatipratyayabhedo 'pyevaṃ sati vipralambha evābhyupagantavyaḥ /
kālavisaṃvādo 'pi ca svapne bhavati rajanyāṃ supto vāsaraṃ bhārate varṣe manyate /
tathā muhūrtamātravartini svapne kadācidbahuvarṣapūgānativāhayati /
nimittānyapi ca svapne na buddhaye karmaṇe vocitāni vidyante /
karaṇosaṃhārāddhi nāsya rathādigrahaṇāya cakṣurādīni santi /
rathādinirvartane 'pi kuto 'sya nimeṣamātreṇa sāmarthyaṃ dāruṇī vā /
bādhyante caite rathādayaḥ svapnadṛṣṭāḥ prabodhe /
svapna eva caite sulabhabādhā bhavanti /
ādyantayorvyabhicāradarśanāt /
children.translated_text: because of the observation of deviation at the beginning and end [of dream-cognitions].

children.text: ratho 'yamiti hi kadācitsvapne nirdhāritaḥ kṣaṇena manuṣyaḥ saṃpadyate manuṣyo 'yamiti nirdhāritaḥ kṣaṇena vṛkṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: For what was determined in a dream as 'this is a chariot' becomes in an instant a man; and what was determined as 'this is a man' becomes in an instant a tree.

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ cābhāvaṃ rathādīnāṃ svapne śrāvayati śāstram - ''na tatra rathā na rathayogā na panthāno bhavanti' (bṛ. 4.3.10) ityādi /
children.translated_text: And the scripture clearly teaches the absence of chariots and the like in dreams: 'There are no chariots there, no chariot-harnesses, no roads' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.10) and the like.

children.text: tasmānmāyāmātraṃ svapnadarśanam // 3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the dream-vision is mere <s>māyā</s>. // 3 //

No, it is said. For it is not conceivable that a sleeping being has the capacity to travel to a place hundreds of <s>yojanas</s> away and return in a mere instant. And in some cases, [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches a dream without return: 'Being in the <s>Kuru</s> country, I, overcome by sleep while lying down, saw in a dream that I had gone to <s>Pañcāla</s> — and I awoke in that [very <s>Kuru</s> country].' For if he had departed from his body, he would have awakened in <s>Pañcāla</s> — [but] he [says] 'I did not go there,' and indeed awakens in the <s>Kuru</s> country. And the body by which he thinks he is reaching another place — that [body], others standing nearby see lying right there in the sleeping-place. And the places in other lands that he sees in dreams as they are — those are not necessarily so in reality. And if one were to see while moving about [in dreams], one would truly encounter real things as in waking — and then [upon waking] one would lay claim to them. And the <s>śruti</s> shows that dreams occur within the body itself: having introduced [the topic] with 'Where he wanders about with this dream-[faculty],' [it concludes:] 'He moves about at will within his own body' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.18). And therefore, because of the contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and reasoning, the 'outside the nest' <s>śruti</s> must be explained figuratively — as meaning 'as if outside the nest, the immortal one having wandered about.' For one who, though dwelling in the body, does not use it for any purpose — he is as if outside the body. The difference between cognitions of staying and going, in this case, must be accepted as a mere illusion. And there is also a discrepancy of time in dreams — one sleeping at night imagines a daytime in the land of <s>Bhārata</s>. Likewise, in a dream lasting only a <s>muhūrta</s>, one sometimes passes through accumulations of many years. And in dreams, the efficient causes — appropriate for cognition or for action — are not present. Because of the withdrawal of the sense-organs, one does not have the eyes and such for apprehending chariots and the like. And for the production of chariots and the like, whence would one have the capacity in the blink of an eye, or the wood [needed]? And these chariots and the like seen in dreams are sublated upon waking. And even within the dream itself, they are easily sublated —

children.text: FN: saṃvṛte saṃkīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Saṃvṛte</s>' means confined, narrow.

children.text:
paryetuṃ gantum /
viparyetuṃ āgantum /
children.translated_text: '<s>Paryetum</s>' means to go. '<s>Viparyetum</s>' means to return.

children.text: sūcakaśca hi śruter ācakṣate ca tadvidaḥ | BBs_3,2.4 |
children.translated_text: <s>Sūcakaśca hi śruter ācakṣate ca tadvidaḥ</s> — And [dreams are] indicative, because of <s>śruti</s>; and those who know declare so. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.4 |

children.text: māyāmātratvāttarhi na kaścitsvapne paramārthagandho 'stīti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Since [dream-creation] is mere <s>māyā</s>, there is not even a trace of ultimate reality in dreams.

children.text:
netyucyate /
sūcakaśca hi svapno bhavati bhaviṣyatoḥsādhvasādhunoḥ /
tathāhi śrūyate - 'yadā karmasu kāmyeṣu striyaṃ svapneṣu paśyati /
samṛddhiṃ tatra jānīyāttasminsvapnadarśane' (chā. 5.2.9) tathā puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇadantaṃ paśyati sa enaṃ hanti ityevamādibhiḥ svapnairacirajīvitvamāvedyata iti śrāvayati /
ācakṣate ca svapnādhyāyavidaḥ - 'kuñjarārohaṇādīni svapne dhanyāni kharayānādīnyadhanyāni' iti /
mantradevatādravyaviśeṣanimittāśca kecitsvapnāḥ satyārthagandhino bhavantīti manyante /
tatrāpi bhavatu nāma sūcyamānasya vastunaḥ satyatvaṃ, sūcakasya tu strīdarśanāderbhavatyeva vaitathyaṃ bādhyamānatvādityabhiprāyaḥ /
tasmādupapannaṃ svapnasya māyāmātratvam /
yaduktam 'āha hi' iti tadevaṃ sati bhāktaṃ vyākhyātavyam /
yathā lāṅgalaṃ gavādīnudvahatīti nimittamātratvādevamucyate, natu pratyakṣameva lāṅgalaṃ gavādīnudvahati /
evaṃ nimittamātratvādevātsupto rathādīnsṛjate sa hi karteti cocyate, natu pratyakṣameva supto rathādīnsṛjati /
nimitttvaṃ tvasya rathādipratibhānanimittamodatrāsādidarśanāttannimittabhūtayoḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ kartṛtveneti vaktavyam /
apica jāgarite viṣayendriyasaṃyogādādityādijyotirvyatikarāccātmanaḥ svayañjyotiṣṭvaṃ durvivecanamiti tadvivecanāya svapna upanyastaḥ /
tatra yadi rathādisṛṣcivacanaṃ śrutyā nīyeta tadā svayañjyotiṣṭvaṃ na nirṇītaṃ syāt /
tasmādrathādyabhāvavacanaṃ śrutyā rathādisṛṣṭivacanaṃ tu bhaktyeti vyākhyeyam /
etena nirmāṇaśravaṇaṃ vyākhyātam /
yadapyuktam - 'prājñamenaṃ nirmātāramāmananti' iti /
tadapyasat /
śrutyantare 'svayaṃ vihatya svayaṃ nirmāya svena bhāsā jyotiṣā prasvapiti' (bṛ. 4.3.9) iti jīvavyāpāraśravaṇāt /
ihāpi 'ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti' (ka. 5.8) iti prasiddhānuvajjīva evāyaṃ kāmānāṃ nirmātā saṃkīrtyate /
tasya tu vākyaśeṣeṇa tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahmeti jīvabhāvaṃ vyāvartya brahmabhāva upadiśyate - 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.9.4) ityādivaditi na brahmaprakaraṇaṃ virudhyate /
nacāsmābhiḥ svapne 'pi prājñavyavahāraḥ pratiṣidhyate /
tasya sarveśvaratvātsarvāsvavasthādhiṣṭhātṛtvopapatteḥ /
pāramārthikastu nāyaṃ saṃdhyāśrayaḥ sargo viyadādisargavadityetāvatpratipādyate /
naca viyadādisargasyāpyātyantikaṃ satyatvamasti /
