pratipāditaṃ hi 'tadananyatvamārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ' (bra. sū. 2.1.14) ityatra samastasya prapañcasya māyāmātratvam /
children.translated_text: For it has been established in 'Its non-difference, because of the words "origin" and the like' (<s>BBs</s> 2.1.14) that the entire phenomenal world is mere <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: prāktu brahmātmatvadarśanādviyadādiprapañco vyavasthitarūpo bhavati /
children.translated_text: But prior to the realization of <s>Brahman</s> as the Self, the phenomenal world of space and the like has a stable form.

children.text: saṃdhyāśrayastu prapañcaḥ pratidinaṃ bādhyata iti /
children.translated_text: Whereas the dream-world is sublated every day.

children.text: ato vaiśeṣikamidaṃ saṃdhyasya māyāmatratvamuditam // 4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this specific <s>māyā</s>-nature of the dream-[state] has been stated. // 4 //

No, it is said. Dreams are indeed indicative — [they indicate] good and bad [events] that are about to happen. For thus it is heard: 'When in desired actions one sees a woman in dreams, one should know prosperity from that dream-vision' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.9); likewise, [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches that seeing a black man with black teeth [in a dream portends that] 'he kills him' — i.e., through such dreams, short life-span is indicated. And those who are experts in the science of dreams declare: 'Riding an elephant and the like are auspicious in dreams; riding a donkey-cart and the like are inauspicious.' And some hold that certain dreams, caused by specific <s>mantras</s>, deities, or substances, have a trace of real content. Even so, let the thing indicated be real — but the indicator itself, such as the vision of a woman and the like, is indeed unreal, because it is sublated — this is the intent. Therefore, the mere <s>māyā</s>-nature of dreams is well established. As for what was said — 'For [the <s>śruti</s>] says so' [i.e., the <s>śruti</s> says that <s>Prājña</s> creates] — that, in the present context, must be explained as figurative. Just as [the expression] 'the plough brings up cows and the like' is said merely because it is the cause [of their acquisition] — not that the plough literally brings up cows — so too, merely because the sleeper is the [indirect] cause, it is said that 'he creates chariots and the like in sleep, for he is the creator' — not that the sleeper literally creates chariots and the like. But his being the cause must be explained thus: from the observation of joy, fear, and the like occasioned by the appearance of chariots and the like [in dreams], he is the agent of the merit and demerit that are the causes of those [experiences]. Moreover, in the waking state, because of the conjunction of objects and sense-organs and because of the intermingling of the light of the sun and the like, the Self's self-luminosity is difficult to discern — therefore, the dream [state] is introduced for the purpose of discerning it. If, therein, the statement about the creation of chariots and the like were taken literally by <s>śruti</s>, then the self-luminosity [of the Self] would not be established. Therefore, the statement about the absence of chariots and the like is to be taken literally by <s>śruti</s>, while the statement about the creation of chariots and the like is to be explained as figurative. By this, the hearing about [the Self's] 'creating' [in dreams] is explained. As for the further claim — 'They teach this [dreamer] as <s>Prājña</s>, the creator' — that too is incorrect. Because in another <s>śruti</s>: 'Having himself destroyed [the waking impressions], having himself created [dream-impressions], he sleeps by his own light' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.9) — the activity of the <s>jīva</s> is heard. Here too, 'He who is awake among those who sleep' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.8) — in accordance with well-known [usage], it is the <s>jīva</s> alone that is mentioned as the creator of desires. But through the remainder of the passage — 'That alone is the pure, that is <s>Brahman</s>' — having set aside the <s>jīva</s>-nature, the <s>Brahman</s>-nature is taught — as in 'That you are' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.9.4) and the like — so there is no contradiction with the <s>Brahman</s>-context. Nor do we deny the operation of <s>Prājña</s> even in dreams. Because of its being the Lord of all, its presiding over all states is proper. But the point being established is just this: that this dream-creation is not ultimately real like the creation of space and the like. And even the creation of space and the like does not have absolute reality —

children.text: parābhidhyānāt tu tirohitaṃ tato hyasya bandhaviparyayau | BBs_3,2.5 |
children.translated_text: <s>Parābhidhyānāt tu tirohitaṃ tato hyasya bandhaviparyayau</s> — But because of meditation on the Supreme, [the concealed knowledge and power] is revealed; for from That [Supreme] indeed arise the bondage and its opposite [liberation] of this [<s>jīva</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.5 |

children.text:
athāpi syātparasyaiva tāvadātmanoṃ'śo jīvo 'gniriva visphuliṅgaḥ /
tatraivaṃ sati yathāgnivisphuliṅgayoḥ samāne dahanaprakāśanaśaktī bhavata evaṃ jīveśvarayorapi jñānaiśvaryaśaktī, tataśca jīvasya jñānaiśvaryavaśātsāṃkalpikī svapne rathādisṛṣṭirbhaviṣyatīti /
atrocyate- satyapi jīveśvarayoraṃśāṃśibhāve pratyakṣameva jīvasyeśvaraviparītadharmatvam /
kiṃ punarjīvasyeśvarasamānadharmatvaṃ nāstyeva /
na nāstyeva /
vidyamānamapi tattirohitamavidyādivyavadhānāt /
tatpunastirohitaṃ satparameśvaramabhidhyāyato yatamānasya jantorvidhūtadhvāntasya timiratiraskṛteva dṛkśaktirauṣadhavīryādīśvaraprasādātsaṃsiddhasya kasyacidevāvirbhavati na svabhāvata eva sarveṣāṃ jantūnām /
kutaḥ - tato hīśvarāddhetorasya jīvasya bandhamokṣau bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text: Why? Because from That — from the Lord — indeed arise the bondage and liberation of this <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: īśvarasvarūpāparijñānādbandhastatsvarūpaparijñānāttu mokṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bondage is due to the non-recognition of the true nature of the Lord; liberation is due to the recognition of that true nature.

children.text: tathāca śrutiḥ - 'jñātvā devaṃ sarvapāśāpahāniḥ kṣīṇaiḥ kleśairjanmamṛtyuprahāṇiḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'By knowing God, [there is] the falling away of all bonds; with the diminishing of afflictions, [there is] the cessation of birth and death;

children.text: tasyābhidhyānāttṛtīyaṃ dehabhede viśvaiśvaryaṃ kevala āptakāmaḥ' (śve. 1.11) ityevamādyā // 5 //
children.translated_text: by meditating on Him, [there is,] at the third [stage — i.e.,] at the dissolution of the body, universal lordship; alone, [he becomes one whose] desires are fulfilled' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 1.11) — and such passages. // 5 //

It might still be maintained: The <s>jīva</s> is indeed a portion (<s>aṃśa</s>) of the supreme Self — like a spark of fire. This being so, just as fire and spark have the same powers of burning and illuminating, so too the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord would have the powers of knowledge and lordship — and therefore, the <s>jīva</s>'s deliberate creation of chariots and the like in dreams would be possible through the force of its knowledge and lordship. To this it is said: Even if the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord have the part-whole relationship, it is directly evident that the <s>jīva</s> has properties opposite to those of the Lord. But then, does the <s>jīva</s> have no properties in common with the Lord at all? Not that it has none at all. Even though present, those [common properties] are concealed — because of the obstruction of <s>avidyā</s> and the like. That concealment, however, for a being who meditates on the supreme Lord and strives [for realization] — whose darkness has been dispelled — becomes revealed, like the power of vision obscured by cataract [which is restored] through the efficacy of medicine — [it becomes manifest] through the grace of the Lord for some accomplished person alone, not naturally for all beings.

children.text: dehayogādvā so 'pi | BBs_3,2.6 |
children.translated_text: <s>Dehayogādvā so 'pi</s> — Or that [concealment] too is because of the connection with the body. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.6 |

children.text:
kasmātpunarjīvaḥ paramātmāṃśa eva saṃstiraskṛtajñānaiśvaryo bhavati /
yuktaṃ tu jñānaiśvaryayoratiraskṛtatvaṃ visphuliṅgasyeva dahanaprakāśanayoriti /
children.translated_text: But why does the <s>jīva</s>, being a portion of the supreme Self, have its knowledge and lordship concealed? It would be reasonable for the knowledge and lordship to remain unconcealed — just as the powers of burning and illuminating [remain unconcealed] for a spark [of fire].

children.text:
ucyate /
satyamevaitat /
so 'pi tu jīvasya jñānaiśvaryatirobhāvo dehayogāddehendriyamanobuddhiviṣayavedanādiyogādbhavati /
asti cātropamā yathāgnerdahanaprakāśanasaṃpannasyāpyaraṇitasya dahanaprakāśane tirohite bhavato yathā vā bhasmacchannasya /
evamavidyāpratyupasthāpitanāmarūpakṛtadehādyupādhiyogāttadavivekabhramakṛto jīvasya jñānaiśvaryatirobhāvaḥ /
vāśabdo jīveśvarayoranyatvāśaṅkāvyāvṛttyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is said: True, this is so. But that concealment of the <s>jīva</s>'s knowledge and lordship is because of the connection with the body — the connection with body, sense-organs, mind, intellect, objects, and sensations. And there is an analogy here: just as fire, even though endowed with the powers of burning and illuminating, has those powers concealed when it is enclosed within wood (<s>araṇi</s>), or when it is covered by ashes — so too, the concealment of the <s>jīva</s>'s knowledge and lordship arises from the connection with the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) of body and the like, which are brought about by name-and-form produced by <s>avidyā</s>, and is caused by the error of non-discrimination from those [<s>upādhis</s>]. The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) is for the purpose of removing the suspicion of a [real] difference between the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord.

children.text: nanvasya eva jīva īśvarādastu tiraskṛtajñānaiśvaryatvātkiṃ dehayogakalpanayā /
children.translated_text: Objection: Let this <s>jīva</s> be different from the Lord precisely because it has concealed knowledge and lordship — what need is there to postulate the connection with the body [as the cause]?

children.text:
netyucyate /
nahyanyatvaṃ jīvasyeśvarādupapadyate 'seyaṃ devataikṣata' (chā. 6.3.2) ityupakramya 'anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya' (chā. 6.3.2) ityātmaśabdena jīvasya parāmarśāt /
'tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi śvetaketo' (chā. 6.9.4) iti ca jīvāyopadiśatīśvarātmatvam /
ato 'nanya eveśvarājjīvaḥ sedehayogāttirohitajñānaiśvaryo bhavati /
ataśca na sāṃkalpikī jīvasya svapne rathādisṛṣṭirghaṭate /
yadi ca sāṃkalpikī svapne rathādisṛṣṭiḥ syānnaivāniṣṭaṃ kaścitsvapnaṃ paśyet /
nahi kaścidaniṣṭaṃ saṃkalpyate /
yatpunaruktaṃ jāgaritadeśaśrutiḥ svapnasya satyatvaṃ sthāpayatīti na tatsāmyavacanaṃ satyatvābhiprāyaṃ svayañjyotiṣṭvavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: As for the statement that the <s>śruti</s> comparing the dream state with the waking state establishes the reality of dream — that comparison does not intend [to establish] reality, because there is no conflict with the self-luminous nature [of the Self].

children.text: śrutyaiva ca svapne rathādyabhāvasya darśitatvāt /
children.translated_text: And because the <s>śruti</s> itself has shown the absence of chariots and the like in dream.

children.text: jāgaritaprabhavavāsanānirmitatvāttu svapnasya tattulyanirbhāsatvābhiprāyaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: Rather, because dream is constructed by impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) arising from waking experience, that [comparison] is intended [to show] that dream appears similar to [waking experience].

children.text: tasmādupapannaṃ svapnasya māyāmātratvam // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the illusory nature (<s>māyāmātra</s>) of dream is well established. // 6 //

No, it is said.
For the otherness of the <s>jīva</s> from <s>Īśvara</s> is not tenable — since, beginning with 'This deity thought' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2), [the text says] 'Having entered with this living Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2), referring to the <s>jīva</s> by the word 'Self' (<s>ātman</s>).
And 'That is the truth, that is the Self — thou art that, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.9.4) — thus [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches <s>Śvetaketu</s>, who is a <s>jīva</s>, that he is identical with <s>Īśvara</s>.
Therefore, the <s>jīva</s> is none other than <s>Īśvara</s> — it is through connection with the body that its knowledge and lordly power become concealed.
And therefore, a volitional creation of chariots and the like in dream is not possible for the <s>jīva</s>.
Moreover, if the creation of chariots and the like in dream were volitional, no one would ever see an unpleasant dream.
For no one wills what is unpleasant.

children.text: 2 tadabhāvādhikaraṇam / sū. 7-8
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Tadabhāvādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Absence of That [Dream-State]). <s>Sūtras</s> 7-8.

children.text: tadabhāvo nāḍīṣu tacchruter ātmani ca | BBs_3,2.7 |
children.translated_text: The absence of that [dream-experience occurs] in the <s>nāḍīs</s> — because of the <s>śruti</s> [to that effect] — and in the Self. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.7 |

children.text:
svapnāvasthā parīkṣitā suṣuptāvasthedānīṃ parīkṣyate /
tatraitāḥ suṣuptiviṣayāḥ śrutayo bhavanti /
kvacicchrūyate- 'tadyatraitatsuptaḥ samastaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānātyāsu tadā nāḍīṣu sṛpo bhavati' (chā. 8.6.3) iti /
anyatra tu nāḍīrevānukramya śrūyate - 'tābhiḥ pratyavasṛpya purītati śete' (bṛ. 2.1.19) iti /
tathānyatra nāḍīrevānukramya 'tāsu tadā bhavati yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kañcana paśyatyathāsminprāṇa evaikadhā bhavati' (kauṣī. 4.19) iti /
tathānyatra 'ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasmiñchete' (bṛ. 2.1.17) iti /
tathānyatra 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati svamapīto bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti /
'prājñenātmanā saṃpariśvakto na bāhyaṃ kiñcana veda nāntaram' (bṛ. 4.3.21) iti ca /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimetāni nāḍyādīni parasparanirapekṣāṇi bhinnāni suṣuptisthānānyāhosvitparasparāpekṣayaikaṃ suṣuptisthānamasti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ bhinnānīti /
kutaḥ - ekārthatvāt /
nahyekārthānīṃ kvacitparasparāpekṣatvaṃ dṛśyate vrīhiyavādīnām /
nāḍyādīnāṃ tvekārthatā suṣuptau dṛśyate - 'nāḍīśu sṛpto bhavati' (chā. 8.6.3) 'purītati śete'
children.translated_text:
The dream-state has been examined. Now the deep-sleep state is examined.
The following <s>śrutis</s> pertain to deep sleep:
In one place it is heard: 'When this [person] is thus asleep, composed, serene, and knows no dream — then he has crept into those <s>nāḍīs</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.3).
Elsewhere, after enumerating the <s>nāḍīs</s>, it is heard: 'Having crept back through those [<s>nāḍīs</s>], he sleeps in the <s>purītat</s> (pericardium)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.19).
Likewise elsewhere, after enumerating the <s>nāḍīs</s>: 'He is in those [<s>nāḍīs</s>] when, being asleep, he sees no dream whatsoever — then he becomes unified in this <s>prāṇa</s> alone' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 4.19).
Likewise elsewhere: 'In this space within the heart, he sleeps' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.17).
Likewise elsewhere: 'Then, dear one, he has merged with Being (<s>sat</s>); he has gone to his own' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1).
And: 'Embraced by the all-knowing Self (<s>prājña ātman</s>), he knows nothing external nor internal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.21).
There arises a doubt: Are these — <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest — mutually independent, distinct loci of deep sleep, or is there, in mutual dependence, a single locus of deep sleep?
What is the prima facie view? That they are distinct.
Why? Because they serve the same purpose.
For things serving the same purpose — like rice, barley, and the like — are never seen to be mutually dependent.
And the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest are seen to serve the same purpose in deep sleep — 'He has crept into the <s>nāḍīs</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.3) and 'He sleeps in the <s>purītat</s>'

children.text: (bṛ. 2.1.19) iti ca tatra tatra saptamīnirdeśasya tulyatvāt /
children.translated_text: (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.19) — because the locative case is used equally in both places.

children.text: nanu naivaṃ sati saptamīnirdeśo dṛśyate - 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti /
children.translated_text: But is not the locative case not [directly] seen in [the passage]: 'Then, dear one, he has merged with Being (<s>sat</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1)?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
tatrāpi saptamyarthasya gamyamānatvāt /
vākyaśeṣo hi tatrāyatanaiṣī jīvaḥ sadupasarpatītyāha - 'anyatrāyatanamalabdhvā prāṇamevopaśrayate' (chā. 6.8.2) iti prāṇaśabdena tatra prakṛtasya sata upādanāt /
āyatanaṃ ca saptamyarthaḥ /
saptamīnirdeśo 'pi tatra vākyaśeṣe dṛśyate - 'sati saṃpadya na viduḥ sati saṃpadyāmahe' (chā. 6.9.2) iti /
sarvatra ca viśeṣavijñānoparamalakṣaṇaṃ suṣuptaṃ na viśiṣyate /
tasmādekārtatvānnāḍyādīnāṃ vikalpena kadācitkiñcitsthānaṃ svāpāyopasarpatīti /
evaṃ prāpte pratipādyate - tadabhāvo nāḍīṣvātni ceti /
tadabhāva iti tasya prakṛtasya svapnadarśanasyābhāvaḥ suṣuptamityarthaḥ /
nāḍīṣvātmani ceti samuccayenaitāni nāḍyādīni svāpāyopaiti na vikalpenetyarthaḥ /
kutaḥ - tacchruteḥ /
tathāhi - sarveṣāmeva nāḍyādīnāṃ tatra tatra suṣuptisthānatvaṃ śrūyate tacca masuccaye saṃgṛhītaṃ bhavati /
vikalpe hyeṣāṃ pakṣe bādhaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
Because even there, the meaning of the locative is understood [implicitly].
For the remainder of the passage states that the <s>jīva</s>, seeking a resting-place, approaches Being (<s>sat</s>): 'Not finding another resting-place, it takes refuge in <s>prāṇa</s> alone' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.2) — where the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' refers to the previously mentioned Being (<s>sat</s>) in that context.
And 'resting-place' (<s>āyatana</s>) is the meaning of the locative.
And the locative is also seen in the remainder of the passage there: 'Having merged with Being (<s>sat</s>), they do not know — "We have merged with Being"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.9.2).
And everywhere, deep sleep — characterized by the cessation of particular cognitions — does not differ [in its nature].
Therefore, because [the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest] serve the same purpose, by way of option, [the <s>jīva</s>] sometimes approaches one locus and sometimes another for sleep.
Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] establishes: 'The absence of that [dream-experience occurs] in the <s>nāḍīs</s> and in the Self.'
'The absence of that' means the absence of the previously discussed dream-perception — that is, deep sleep.
'In the <s>nāḍīs</s> and in the Self' — by way of combination, [the <s>jīva</s>] approaches all of these — <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest — for sleep, not by way of option.
Why? Because of the <s>śruti</s>.
For thus — the <s>śruti</s> in each place states that all of these — <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest — are the locus of deep sleep, and all of these are included in the combination.
If there were an option, there would be mutual contradiction among these [<s>śrutis</s>].

children.text: nanvekārthatvādvikalpo nāḍyādīnāṃ vrīhiyavādivatyuktam /
children.translated_text: But it was said that because they serve the same purpose, there is an option among the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest, like rice and barley and the like.

children.text:
netyucyate /
nahyekavibhaktinirdeśamātreṇaikārthatvaṃ vikalpaścāpatati /
nānārthatvasamuccayayorapyekavibhaktinirdeśadarśanāprāsāde śete paryaṅ ke śeta ityevamādiṣu /
tathehāpi nāḍīṣu purītati brahmaṇi ca svapitītyetadupapadyate samuccayaḥ /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'tāsu tadā bhavati yadā suptaḥ svapnaṃ na kañcana paśyatyathāsminprāṇa evaikadhā bhavati' (kauṣī. 4.19) iti samuccayaṃ nāḍīnāṃ prāṇasya ca suṣuptau śrāvayatyekavākyopādānāt /
prāṇasya ca brahmatvaṃ samadhigatam - 'prāṇastathānugamāt' (bra.sū. 1.1.28) ityatra /
yatrāpi nirapekṣā iva nāḍīḥ suptisthānatvena śrāvayati - 'āsu tadā nāḍīṣu sṛpto bhavati' (chā. 8.6.3) iti /
children.translated_text:
No, it is said.
For merely because the same case-ending is used, sameness of purpose and optionality do not follow.
Because the same case-ending is seen used even for different purposes and for combination — as in 'He sleeps in the palace, he sleeps on the couch' and similar [expressions].
Likewise here too — 'He sleeps in the <s>nāḍīs</s>, in the <s>purītat</s>, and in <s>Brahman</s>' — this combination is proper.
And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'He is in those [<s>nāḍīs</s>] when, being asleep, he sees no dream whatsoever — then he becomes unified in this <s>prāṇa</s> alone' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 4.19) — teaches the combination of the <s>nāḍīs</s> and <s>prāṇa</s> in deep sleep, through their being mentioned together in a single sentence.
And the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of <s>prāṇa</s> has been ascertained — in the [<s>sūtra</s>] '<s>Prāṇa</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the concordance [of attributes]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.28).
Even where [the <s>śruti</s>] seems to teach the <s>nāḍīs</s> alone — independently — as the locus of sleep: 'He has crept into those <s>nāḍīs</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.3) —

children.text:
tatrāpi pradeśāntaraprasiddhasya brahmaṇo 'pratiṣedhānnāḍīdvāreṇaiva brahmaṇyevāvatiṣṭhata iti pratīyate /
nacaivamapi nāḍīṣu saptamī virudhyate /
nāḍīdvārāpi brahmopasarpansṛpta eva nāḍīṣu bhavati /
yo hi gaṅgayā sāgaraṃ gacchati gata eva sa gaṅgāyāṃ bhavati /
apicātra raśmīnāḍīdvārātmakasya brahmalokamārgasya vivakṣitatvānnāḍīstutyarthaṃ sṛptisaṃkīrtanam /
'nāḍīṣu sṛpto bhavati' (chā. 8.6.3) ityuktvā 'taṃ na kaścana pāpmā spṛśati' (chā. 8.6.3) iti bruvannāḍīḥ praśaṃsati /
bravīti ca pāpmasparśābhāve hetum - tejasā nāḍīgatena pittākhyenābhivyāptakaraṇo na bāhyānviṣayānīkṣata ityarthaḥ /
athavā tejaseti brahmaṇa evāyaṃ nirdeśaḥ /
śrutyantare -' brahmaiva teja eva' (bṛ. 4.4.7) iti tejaḥ śabdasya brahmaṇi pratyuktatvāt /
brahmaṇā hi tadā saṃpanno bhavati nāḍīdvāreṇātastaṃ na kaścana pāpmāna spṛśatītyarthaḥ /
brahmasamapattiśca pāpmasparśābhāve hetuḥ samadhigataḥ - 'sarve pāpmāno 'ta nivartante 'pahatapāpmā hyeṣa brahmalokaḥ' (chā.
children.translated_text:
Even there, because the well-known <s>Brahman</s> established from other passages is not negated, it is understood that through the <s>nāḍīs</s> as the doorway, [the <s>jīva</s>] rests in <s>Brahman</s> alone.
And even so, the locative with respect to the <s>nāḍīs</s> is not contradicted.
For even one who approaches the ocean through the Ganges has indeed traveled along the Ganges.
Just as one who goes to the ocean via the <s>Gaṅgā</s> has indeed traversed the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Moreover, because the path to the world of <s>Brahman</s> — consisting of rays and <s>nāḍīs</s> — is intended here, the mention of creeping [into the <s>nāḍīs</s>] is for the purpose of praising the <s>nāḍīs</s>.
Having said 'He has crept into the <s>nāḍīs</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.3), [the <s>śruti</s>] then saying 'No evil touches him' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.3) — praises the <s>nāḍīs</s>.
And [the <s>śruti</s>] states the reason for the absence of contact with evil: 'Because he is pervaded by the radiance (<s>tejas</s>) present in the <s>nāḍīs</s>, called bile' — meaning his sense-organs are pervaded [by it], so he does not perceive external objects.
Alternatively, the word '<s>tejas</s>' (radiance) here refers to <s>Brahman</s> itself.
Because in another <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Brahman</s> is indeed radiance' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.7) — the word '<s>tejas</s>' has been established as [a designation of] <s>Brahman</s>.
For at that time, he has merged with <s>Brahman</s> through the doorway of the <s>nāḍīs</s> — therefore, no evil touches him — this is the meaning.
And the merger with <s>Brahman</s> has been ascertained as the reason for the absence of contact with evil — from <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'All evils turn back from there, for this world of <s>Brahman</s> is free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s>

children.text:
8.4.2) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
evañca sati pradeśāntaraprasiddhena brahmaṇā suṣuptisthānenānugato nāḍīnāṃ samuccayaḥ samadhigato bhavati /
tathā purītato 'pi brahmaprakriyāyāṃ saṃkīrtanāttadanuguṇameva suptisthānatvaṃ vijñāyate - 'ya eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasmiñchete' (bṛ. 2.1.17) iti hṛdayākāśe suptisthāne prakṛta idamucyate 'purītati śete' (bṛ. 2.1.19) iti /
purītaditi hṛdayapariveṣṭanamucyate /
tadantarvartinyāpi hṛdayākāśe śayānaḥ śakyate purītati śeta iti vaktum /
prākāraparikṣipte 'pi pure vartamānaḥ prākāre vartata ityucyate /
hṛdayākāśasya ca brahmatvaṃ samadhigatam - 'dahara uttarebhyaḥ' (bra.sū. 1.3.14) ityatra /
tathā nāḍīpurītatsamuccayo 'pi - 'tābhiḥ pratyavasṛtya purītati śete' (bṛ. 2.1.19) ityekavākyopādānādavagamyate /
satprājñayośca prasiddhameva brahmatvam /
evametāsu śrutiṣu trīṇyeva suṣuptisthānāni saṃkīrtitāni nāḍyaḥ purītadbrahma ceti /
tatrāpi dvāramātraṃ nāḍyaḥ purītacca, brahmaiva tvekaṃ suṣupti sthānam /
apica nāḍyaḥ purītadvā jīvasyopādhyādhāra eva bhavati tatrāsya karaṇāni vartanta iti /
nahyupādhisaṃbandhamantareṇa svata eva jīvasyādhāraḥ kaścitsaṃbhavati, brahmāvyatirekeṇa svamahimapratiṣṭhitatvāt /
brahmādhāratvamapyasya suṣupte naivādhārādheyabhedābhiprāyeṇocyate kathaṃ tarhi tādātmyābhiprāyeṇa /
yata āha - 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati svamapīto bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti /
svaśabdenātmābhilapyate, svarūpamāpannaḥ supto bhavatītyarthaḥ /
apica na kadācijjīvasya brahmaṇā saṃpattirnāsti svarūpasyānapāyitvāt /
svapnajāgaritayostūpādhisaṃparkavaśātpararūpāpattimivāpekṣya tadupaśamātsuṣupteḥ svarūpāpattirvakṣyate /
ataśca suptāvasthāyāṃ kadācitsatāṃ saṃpadyate kadācinna saṃpadyata ityayuktam /
apica sthānavikalpābhyupagame 'pi viśeṣavijñānopalakṣaṇaṃ tāvatsuṣuptaṃ na kvacidviśiṣyate /
tatra sati saṃpannastāvattadekatvānna vijānatīti yuktam /
'ttakena kaṃ vijānīyāt /
' (bṛ. 2.4.14) iti śruteḥ /
nāḍīṣu puratīti ca śayānasya na kiñcidavijñāne kāraṇaṃ śakyaṃ vijñātuṃ, bhedaviṣayatvāt 'yatra vā anyadiva syāttatrānyo 'nyatpaśyet' (bṛ. 4.3.31) iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text:
8.4.2) and the like.
And thus, the combination of the <s>nāḍīs</s> with <s>Brahman</s> — well known from other passages as the locus of deep sleep — is ascertained.
Likewise, the mention of the <s>purītat</s> too, being within the context of a discussion of <s>Brahman</s>, its being a locus of sleep is understood accordingly — 'In this space within the heart, he sleeps' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.17) — with the space within the heart as the locus of sleep being the context, this is stated: 'He sleeps in the <s>purītat</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.19).
The <s>purītat</s> is said to be the covering of the heart.
Even one sleeping in the space within the heart, which is inside the <s>purītat</s>, can be said to sleep in the <s>purītat</s>.
Just as one dwelling in a city enclosed by walls is said to dwell in the walls.
And the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of the space within the heart has been ascertained — in the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'The small [space is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the subsequent [statements]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.3.14).
Likewise, the combination of <s>nāḍīs</s> and <s>purītat</s> too is understood from the single-sentence mention: 'Having crept back through those [<s>nāḍīs</s>], he sleeps in the <s>purītat</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.19).
And the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of Being (<s>sat</s>) and the All-knowing (<s>prājña</s>) is well established.
Thus, in all these <s>śrutis</s>, only three loci of deep sleep are mentioned: the <s>nāḍīs</s>, the <s>purītat</s>, and <s>Brahman</s>.
And of these, the <s>nāḍīs</s> and <s>purītat</s> are merely doorways; <s>Brahman</s> alone is the single locus of deep sleep.
Moreover, the <s>nāḍīs</s> and <s>purītat</s> serve only as the substrate of the <s>jīva</s>'s limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) — the sense-organs of the [<s>jīva</s>] reside there.
For the <s>jīva</s>, apart from the connection with limiting adjuncts, no substrate is possible by its own nature — because, being non-different from <s>Brahman</s>, it is established in its own glory.
And even the statement that <s>Brahman</s> is the substrate [of the <s>jīva</s>] in deep sleep is not meant with reference to a distinction between substrate and that which is supported. Rather, how [is it meant]? With reference to identity.
Because [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'Then, dear one, he has merged with Being (<s>sat</s>); he has gone to his own' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1).
The word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) denotes the Self — meaning: he has attained his own true nature and sleeps.
Moreover, the <s>jīva</s> is never without merger with <s>Brahman</s>, because its true nature never departs.
But because in dream and waking, due to the contact with limiting adjuncts, there appears to be an assumption of a different form — relative to the cessation of that [appearance], the attainment of one's own true nature in deep sleep is stated.
And therefore, [the idea] that sometimes in the state of sleep [the <s>jīva</s>] merges with Being (<s>sat</s>) and sometimes does not — is untenable.
Moreover, even if one were to accept the option of different loci, deep sleep — characterized by the cessation of particular cognitions — does not differ anywhere [in its essential nature].
With respect to that, it is proper [to say] that one who has merged with Being (<s>sat</s>) does not know, because of their identity.
'By what would one know what?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14) — because of this <s>śruti</s>.
But for one sleeping in the <s>nāḍīs</s> or in the <s>purītat</s>, no cause for non-cognition can be identified — because cognition pertains to [the realm of] difference: 'Where there seems to be another, there one sees another' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.31) — because of this <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: nanu bhedaviṣayasyāpyatidūrādikāraṇamavijñāne syāt /
children.translated_text: But might not the cause of non-cognition, even for [one in] the realm of difference, be [something like] great distance and the like?

children.text:
bāḍham /
evaṃ syādyadi jīvaḥ svataḥparicchinno 'bhyupagamyate, yathā viṣṇumitraḥ pravāsī svagṛhaṃ na paśyati /
natu jīvasyopādhivyatirekeṇa paricchedo vidyate /
upādhigatamevātidūrādikāraṇamavijñāna iti yadyucyeta tathāpyupādherupaśāntatvātsatyeva saṃpanno na vijānatīti yuktam /
naca vayamiha tulyavannāḍyādisamuccayaṃ pratipādayāmaḥ /
nahi nāḍyaḥ suptisthānaṃ purītadvetyanena vijñānena kiñcitprayojanamasti /
nahyetadvijñānapratibaddhaṃ kiñcitphalaṃ śrūyate /
nāpyetadvijñānaṃ phalavataḥ kasyacidaṅgamupadiśyate /
brahma tvanapāyi suptisthānamityetatpratipādayāmaḥ /
tena tu vijñānena prayojanamasti jīvasya brahmātmatvāvadhāraṇaṃ svapnajāgaritavyavahāravimuktatvāvadhāraṇaṃ ca /
tasmādātmaiva suptisthānam /
children.translated_text:
Indeed.
This would be so if the <s>jīva</s> were accepted as intrinsically limited — just as <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>, being away from home, does not see his own house.
But the <s>jīva</s> has no limitation apart from [that imposed by] limiting adjuncts.
If it be said that the cause of non-cognition — great distance and the like — pertains to the limiting adjuncts [rather than the <s>jīva</s> itself], even so, because the limiting adjuncts have subsided [in deep sleep], it is proper that one who has merged with Being (<s>sat</s>) does not know.
And we do not here establish the combination of the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rest as if they were of equal [importance].
For there is no purpose served by the knowledge that 'The <s>nāḍīs</s> are a locus of sleep' or 'The <s>purītat</s> [is a locus of sleep].'
For no fruit dependent on this knowledge is heard.
Nor is this knowledge taught as an auxiliary of any fruit-bearing [practice].
Rather, we establish that <s>Brahman</s> — from which [the <s>jīva</s>] never separates — is the locus of sleep.
For the purpose of that knowledge is: the ascertainment of the <s>jīva</s>'s identity with <s>Brahman</s>, and the ascertainment that [the <s>jīva</s>] is free from the transactions of dream and waking.
Therefore, the Self alone is the locus of sleep.

children.text: ataḥ prabodho 'smāt | BBs_3,2.8 |
children.translated_text: Therefore, awakening is from this [Self]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.8 |

children.text: yasmāccātmaiva suptisthānamata eva ca kāraṇānnityavadevāsmādātmanaḥ prabodhaḥ svāpādhikāre śiṣyate - 'kuta etadāgāt' (bṛ. 2.1.16) ityasya praśnasya prativacanāvasare 'yathāgneḥ kṣudrā visphuliṅgā vyuccārantyevamevaitasmādātmanaḥ sarve prāṇāḥ' (bṛ. 2.1.20) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: And because the Self alone is the locus of sleep, for this very reason, awakening is always taught in the context of the sleep-discussion as being from this Self alone: In response to the question 'Where did this [person] come from?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.16), [the answer is given] by means of 'Just as tiny sparks fly forth from a fire, so too from this Self all <s>prāṇas</s> [fly forth]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.20) and the like.

children.text: 'sata āgamya na viduḥ sata āgacchāmahe' (chā. 6.10.2) iti ca /
children.translated_text: And: 'Having come from Being (<s>sat</s>), they do not know — "We have come from Being"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.10.2).

children.text: vikalpyamāneṣu tu suṣuptisthāneṣu kadācinnāḍībhyaḥ pratibudhyate kadācitpurītataḥ kadācidātmana ityaśāsiṣyat /
children.translated_text: But if the loci of deep sleep were optional, [the <s>śruti</s>] would have taught: 'Sometimes one awakens from the <s>nāḍīs</s>, sometimes from the <s>purītat</s>, sometimes from the Self.'

children.text: tasmādapyātmaiva suptisthānamiti // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the Self alone is the locus of sleep. // 8 //

children.text: 3 karmānusmṛtiśabdavidhyadhikaraṇam / sū. 9
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Karmānusmṛtiśabdavidhyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of <s>Karma</s>-Memory, Scriptural Word, and Injunction). <s>Sūtra</s> 9.

children.text: sa eva tu karmānusmṛtiśabdavidhibhyaḥ | BBs_3,2.9 |
children.translated_text: It is the same [self] indeed — because of <s>karma</s>-memory, scriptural word, and injunction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.9 |

children.text:
tasyāḥ punaḥ satsaṃpatteḥ pratibudhyamānaḥ kiṃ ya eva satasaṃpannaḥ sa eva pratibudhyata uta sa vānyo veti cintyate /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvadaniyama iti /
kutaḥ - yadā hi jalarāśau kaścijjalabinduḥ prakṣipyate jalarāśireva sa tadā bhavati punaruddharaṇe ca sa eva jalabindurbhavatīti duḥsaṃpādam /
tadvatsuptaḥ pareṇaikatmāpannaḥ saṃprasīdatatīti na sa eva punarutthātumarhati /
tasmātsa eveśvaro vānyo vā jīvaḥ pratibudhyata ityevaṃ prāpta idamāha - sa eva tu jīvaḥ luptaḥ svāsthyaṃ gataḥ punaruttiṣṭhati nānyaḥ /
kasmāt /
karmānusmṛtiśabdavidhibhyaḥ /
vibhajya hetuṃ darśayiṣyāmi /
karmaśeṣānuṣṭhānadarśanāttāvatsa evotthātumarhati nānyaḥ /
tathāhi - pūrvedyuranuṣṭhitasya karmaṇo 'paredyuḥ śeṣamanutiṣṭhandṛśyate /
nacānyena sāmikṛtasya karmaṇo 'nyaḥ śeṣakriyāyāṃ pravarititumarhati /
atiprasaṅgāt /
tasmādeka eva pūrvedyuraparedyuścaikasya karmaṇaḥ karteti gamyate /
itaśca sa evottiṣṭhati yatkāraṇamatīte 'hanyahamado 'drākṣamiti pūrvānubhūtasya paścātsmaraṇamanyasyotthāne nopapadyate /
nahyanyadṛṣṭamanyo 'nusmartumarhati /
so 'hamasmīti cātmānusmaraṇamātmāntarotthāne nāvakalpate /
śabdebhyaśca tasyaivotthānamavagamyate /
tathāhi - 'punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyonyādravati buddhāntāyaiva' (bṛ. 4.3.16) 'sarvāḥ prajā aharahargacchantya etaṃ brahmalokaṃ na vindanti' (chā. 8.3.2) 'ta iha vyāghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yadyadbhavanti tadābhavanti'
children.translated_text:
Now, regarding that very merging into <s>Sat</s> (Being), the question is examined: Does the very same one who has merged into <s>Sat</s> awaken, or is it someone else?
Therein, the initial position is that there is no fixed rule.
Why? For when a drop of water is cast into a body of water, it becomes just the body of water; and upon extraction, it is difficult to ascertain that the very same drop is [retrieved].
Likewise, the sleeper, having become one with the Supreme, 'becomes merged' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1) — and so that very same one cannot be expected to arise again.
Therefore, it is either the Lord Himself or some other <s>jīva</s> that awakens — having set forth this [prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: It is that very same <s>jīva</s> that has lost [its individuality] and returned to its own natural state that rises again — not another.
Why?
Because of <s>karma</s>, recollection, scriptural texts, and injunctions.
I shall demonstrate [these] reasons separately.
From the observation of the completion of a remaining action, it must be that the very same one rises — not another.
For thus: the remainder of an action commenced on the previous day is observed to be continued on the following day.
And another [person] is not entitled to engage in the completion of an action initiated by someone else.
Because of excessive implication (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).
Therefore, it is understood that the one on the previous day and the one on the following day are the same — a single agent of a single action.
And for this further reason that very same one rises: because the subsequent recollection of what was previously experienced — 'On such-and-such a past day, I saw such-and-such' — would not be possible if another were to rise.
For another cannot recollect what was seen by someone else.
And the self-recollection 'I am the same one' would not be tenable if a different self were to rise.
And from scriptural texts too, the rising of that very same one is understood.
For thus: 'He runs back again in the same way, to the very place from which he set out, just for the sake of waking' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.16); 'All these creatures, day after day, go to this <s>Brahma</s>-world and yet do not find it' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.2); 'Whatever they were here — whether tiger, lion, wolf, boar, worm, moth, gadfly, or mosquito — that they become again' —

children.text:
(chā. 6.9.3) ityevamādayaḥ śabdāḥ svāpaprabodhādhikāre paṭhitā nātmāntarotthāne sāmañjasyamīyuḥ /
karmavidyāvidhibhyaścaivamevāvagamyate /
anyathā hi karmavidyāvidhayo 'narthakāḥ syuḥ /
anyotthānapakṣe hi suptamātro mucyata ityāpadyeta /
evaṃ cetsyādvada kiṃ kālāntaraphalena karmaṇā vidyayā vā kṛtaṃ syāt /
apicānyotthānapakṣe yadi tāvaccharīrāntare vyavaharaṇamāṇo jīva uttiṣṭhettatratyavyavahāralopaprasaṅgaḥ syāt /
atha tatra supta uttiṣṭhetkalpanānarthakyaṃ syāt /
yohi yasmiñśarīre suptaḥ sa tasminnotiṣṭhatyanyasmiñśarīre supto 'nyasminnuttiṣṭhatīti ko 'syāṃ kalpanāyāṃ lābhaḥ syāt /
atha mukta uttiṣṭhedantavānmokṣa āpadyeta /
nivṛttāvidyasya ca punarutthānamupapannam /
eteneśvarasyotthānaṃ pratyuktam /
nityanivṛttāvidyatvāt /
akṛtābhyāgamakṛtavipraṇāśau ca durnivāravanyotthānapakṣe syātām /
tasmātsa evottiṣṭhati nānya iti /
yatpunaruktaṃ yathā jalarāśau prakṣipto jalabindurnoddhartuṃ śakyata evaṃ sati saṃpanno jīvo notpatpatitumarhatīti, tatparihriyate /
yuktaṃ tatra vivekakāraṇābhāvājjalabindoranuddharaṇam /
iha tu vidyate vivekakāraṇaṃ karma cāvidyā ceti vaiṣamyam /
dṛśyate ca durvivecayorapyasmajjātīyaiḥ kṣīrodakayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭayorhaṃsena vivecanam /
apica na jīvo nāma kaścitparasmādanyo vidyate yo jalabinduriva jalarāśeḥ sato vivicyeta /
sadeva tūpādhisaṃparkājjīva ityasakṛtprapañcitam /
children.translated_text: Rather, it is <s>Sat</s> (Being) itself that, through association with <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts), is called '<s>jīva</s>' — this has been elaborated many times.

children.text: evaṃ sati yāvadekopādhigatā bandhānuvṛttistāvadekajīvavyavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: This being so, as long as the continuity of bondage pertains to a single set of <s>upādhis</s>, so long is there the conventional usage of a single <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: upādhyantaragatāyāṃ tu bandhānuvṛttau jīvāncataravyavahāraḥ /
children.translated_text: But when the continuity of bondage passes to another set of <s>upādhis</s>, there is the conventional usage of another <s>jīva</s>.

children.text: sa evāyamupādhiḥ svāpaprabodhayorbījāṅ kuranyāyenetyataḥ sa eva jīvaḥ pratibudhyata iti yuktam // 9 //
children.translated_text: This very same <s>upādhi</s> operates in sleep and waking according to the principle of seed and sprout — therefore, it is proper that the very same <s>jīva</s> awakens. // 9 //

(<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.9.3) — these and similar scriptural texts, read in the context of sleep and waking, would not yield coherence if a different self were to rise.
And from the injunctions of <s>karma</s> and <s>vidyā</s> too, this very same [conclusion] is understood.
For otherwise, the injunctions of <s>karma</s> and <s>vidyā</s> would be purposeless.
For on the view that another rises, it would follow that one is liberated merely by sleeping.
And if that were so, tell me — what would be accomplished by <s>karma</s> or <s>vidyā</s> whose fruits come at a later time?
Moreover, on the view that another rises: if a <s>jīva</s> engaged in activities in another body were to rise [here], there would be the unwanted consequence of the loss of the activities [performed] there.
Alternatively, if one [already] asleep there were to rise [here], the supposition would be pointless.
For what gain would there be in supposing that one who sleeps in one body rises in that [same] body, while one who sleeps in another body rises in yet another?
Alternatively, if a liberated one were to rise, liberation would turn out to be finite.
But the re-arising of one whose <s>avidyā</s> has ceased is indeed reasonable.
By this [argument], the rising of the Lord [as the awakener] is also refuted.
Because [the Lord's] <s>avidyā</s> has been eternally eliminated.
And on the view that another rises, the two [faults of] the accrual of what was not done (<s>akṛtābhyāgama</s>) and the loss of what was done (<s>kṛtavipraṇāśa</s>) would be impossible to avert.
Therefore, that very same one rises — not another.
Now, as for the objection that just as a drop of water cast into a body of water cannot be retrieved, so too the <s>jīva</s> merged into <s>Sat</s> cannot be expected to rise — that is answered:
In that case, the non-retrieval of the drop of water is justified because of the absence of a cause for differentiation.
But here, there does exist a cause for differentiation — namely, <s>karma</s> and <s>avidyā</s> — hence the disparity.
And it is observed that even things difficult to differentiate — such as milk and water mixed together — are differentiated by a swan, among beings of our kind.
Moreover, there is no entity called '<s>jīva</s>' that is truly other than the Supreme, which could be separated from <s>Sat</s> as a drop of water [is separated] from a body of water.

children.text: 4 mugdher'dhasaṃpattyadhikaraṇam / sū. 10
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Mugdher'dhasaṃpatti Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Half-Attainment in Swooning). <s>Sūtra</s> 10.

children.text: mugdher'dhasaṃpattiḥ pariśeṣāt | BBs_3,2.10 |
children.translated_text: In swooning, there is half-attainment — by the process of elimination. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.10 |

children.text:
asti mugdho nāma yaṃ mūrchita iti laukikāḥ kathayanti /
satu kimavastha iti parīkṣāyāmucyate /
tisrastāvadavasthāḥ śarīrasthasya jīvasya prasiddhā jāgaritaṃ svapnaḥ suṣuptiriti /
caturthī śarīrādapasṛptiḥ /
natu pañcamīkācidavasthā jīvasya śrutau smṛtau vā prasiddhāsti /
tasmāccatasṛṇāmevāvasthānāmanyatamāvasthā mūrchetyevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- na tāvanmugdho jāgaritāvastho bhavitumarhati /
nahyayamindriyairviṣayānīkṣate /
syādetat /
iṣukāranyāyena mugdho bhaviṣyati /
yatheṣukāro jāgradapīṣvāsaktamanastayā nānyānviṣayānīkṣata evaṃ mugdho musalasaṃpātādijanitaduḥkhānubhavavyagramanastayā jāgradapi nānyānviṣayānīkṣata iti /
children.translated_text:
There is [a state called] swooning (<s>mugdha</s>), which ordinary people call 'being unconscious' (<s>mūrcchita</s>).
What state is this? — when examined, [we find the following]:
Three states of the <s>jīva</s> embodied in a body are well known — waking, dream, and deep sleep.
The fourth is departure from the body [i.e., death].
But no fifth state of the <s>jīva</s> is known either in <s>śruti</s> or <s>smṛti</s>.
Therefore, swooning must be one of these four states — having set forth this [prima facie view], we say: First, the swooned one cannot be in the waking state.
For this [person] does not perceive objects through the sense-organs.
It might be said: The swooned one may be [in a state] like the arrow-maker.
Just as the arrow-maker, though awake, being absorbed in his arrow with single-pointed mind, does not perceive other objects — so too the swooned one, being absorbed in the experience of pain produced by the blow of a pestle and the like, though awake, does not perceive other objects.

children.text:
na /
acetayamānatvāt /
iṣukāro hi vyāpṛtamanā bravītīṣumevāhametāvantaṃ kālamupalabhamāno 'bhūvamiti /
mugdhastu labdhasaṃjño bravītyandhe tamasyahametāvantaṃ kālaṃ prakṣipto 'bhūvaṃ na kiñcinmayā cetitamiti /
jāgrataścaikaviṣayaviṣaktacetaso 'pi deho vidhriyate /
mugdhasya tu deho dharaṇyāṃ patati /
tasmānna jāgarti nāpi svapnānpaśyati niḥsaṃjñakatvāt /
nāpi mṛtaḥ prāṇoṣmaṇorbhāvāt /
mugdhe hi jantau mṛto 'yaṃ syānna vā mṛta iti saṃśayānā ūṣmāsti nāstīti hṛdayadeśamālabhante niścayārthaṃ prāṇo 'sti nāstīti ca nāsikādeśam /
yadi prāṇoṣmaṇorastitvaṃ nāvagacchanti tato mṛto 'yamityadhyavasāya dahanāyāraṇyaṃ nayanti /
atha tu prāṇamūṣmāṇaṃ vā pratipadyante tato nāyaṃ mṛta ityadhyavasāya saṃjñālābhāya bhiṣajyanti /
punarutthānācca na diṣṭaṃ gataḥ /
nahi yamarāṣṭrātpratyāgacchati /
astu tarhi suṣupto niḥsaṃjñatvādamṛtatvācca /
na /
vailakṣaṇyāt /
mugdhaḥ kadācicciramapi nocchvasiti savepathurasya deho bhavati bhayānakaṃ ca vadanaṃ visphārite netre /
suṣuptastu prasannavadanastulyakālaṃ punaḥ punarucchvasiti nimīlite asya netre bhavataḥ /
nacāsya deho vepate /
pāṇipeṣaṇamātreṇa ca suṣuptamutthāpayanti natu mugdhaṃ mudgaraghātenāpi /
nimittabhedaśca bhavati mohasvāpayoḥ /
musalasaṃpātādinimittatvānmohasya, śramādinimittatvācca svāpasya /
naca loke 'sti prasiddhirmugdhaḥ supta iti /
pariśeṣādardhasaṃpattirmugdhatetyavagacchāmaḥ /
nīḥsaṃjñatvātsaṃpanna itarasmādvailakṣaṇyādasaṃpanna iti /
kathaṃ punarardhasaṃpattirmugdhateti śakyate vaktum /
yāvatā suptaṃ prati tāvaduktaṃ śrutyā - 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti 'atra steno 'steno bhavati' (bṛ. 4.3.22) 'naitaṃ setumahorātre tarato na jarā na mṛtyurna śoko na sukṛtaṃ na dṛṣkṛtam' (chā. 8.4.1) ityādi /
jīve hi sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ prāptiḥ sukhitvaduḥkhitvapratyayotpādanena bhavati /
naca sukhitvapratyayo duḥkhitvapratyayo vā suṣupte vidyate, mugdhe 'pi tau pratyayau naiva vidyete /
tasmādupādhyupaśamātsuṣuptavanmugdhe 'pi katsnasaṃpattireva bhavitumarhati nārdhasaṃpattiriti /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because [the swooned one] is unconscious.
For the arrow-maker, whose mind is occupied [with his task], says: 'I was perceiving just this arrow for that length of time.'
But the swooned one, upon regaining consciousness, says: 'I was cast into blind darkness for that length of time; nothing was cognized by me.'
And even for one who is awake with the mind fixed on a single object, the body remains supported.
But the body of the swooned one falls to the ground.
Therefore, [the swooned one] neither wakes nor sees dreams — because of being devoid of consciousness.
Nor is [the swooned one] dead — because of the presence of <s>prāṇa</s> and warmth.
For when an animal has swooned, people who are uncertain whether it has died or not feel the region of the heart [to check] whether warmth exists or not, for the sake of certainty; and [they feel] the region of the nose [to check] whether <s>prāṇa</s> exists or not.
If they do not ascertain the existence of <s>prāṇa</s> and warmth, then, concluding 'this one has died,' they carry [the body] to the cremation ground.
But if they ascertain <s>prāṇa</s> or warmth, then, concluding 'this one has not died,' they administer medical treatment for the recovery of consciousness.
And because of re-arising [from swooning], [the swooned one] has not gone to [the realm of] destiny [i.e., death].
For no one returns from the realm of <s>Yama</s>.
Let it then be deep sleep, because of the absence of consciousness and because of not being dead.
No.
Because of dissimilarity.
The swooned one sometimes does not breathe for a long time; the body trembles; the face is frightful; the eyes are wide open.
But the one in deep sleep has a serene face, breathes in and out at regular intervals, and the eyes are closed.
Nor does the body tremble.
And [people] wake up one in deep sleep by a mere touch of the hand, but cannot [wake] the swooned one even by a blow with a club.
And the causes differ for swooning and sleep.
Swooning is caused by the blow of a pestle and the like; sleep is caused by fatigue and the like.
And there is no common understanding in the world that 'the swooned one is asleep.'
By the process of elimination, we understand that swooning is a half-attainment [of <s>Brahman</s>].
[It is] attained because of the absence of consciousness; [yet] not [fully] attained because of dissimilarity from the other [i.e., deep sleep].
But how can it be said that swooning is a half-attainment?
Since regarding the sleeper, <s>śruti</s> has stated: 'He becomes merged in <s>Sat</s>, O dear one' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1); 'Here, a thief is no thief' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.22); 'This bridge, neither day nor night crosses, nor old age, nor death, nor sorrow, nor merit, nor sin' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.1) — and so forth.
For the <s>jīva</s>'s attainment of merit and sin occurs through the generation of the cognitions of pleasure and pain.
And the cognition of pleasure or of pain does not exist in deep sleep; in swooning too, those two cognitions do not exist at all.
Therefore, because of the subsidence of the <s>upādhis</s>, in swooning too — just as in deep sleep — there ought to be complete attainment [of <s>Brahman</s>], not half-attainment.

children.text:
atrocyate - na brūmo mugdher'dhasaṃpattirjīvasya brahmaṇā bhavatīti /
kiṃ tarhyardhena suṣuptapakṣasya bhavati mugdhatvamardhenāvasthāntarapakṣasyeti brūmaḥ /
darśite ca mohasya svāpena sāmyavaiṣamye /
dvāraṃ caitanmaraṇasya /
yadāsya sāvaśeṣaṃ karma bhavati tadā vāṅmanase pratyāgacchataḥ /
yadā tu niravaśeṣaṃ karma bhavati tadā prāṇoṣmāṇāvapagacchataḥ /
tasmādardhasaṃpattiṃ brahmavida icchanti /
yattūktaṃ na pañcamī kācidavasthā prasiddhāstīti /
children.translated_text:
To this we reply: We do not say that the half-attainment in swooning is of the <s>jīva</s> with <s>Brahman</s>.
Rather, we say: swooning partakes half of the deep-sleep position and half of the position of another state [i.e., death].
And the similarity and dissimilarity of swooning with sleep have been shown.
And this [swooning] is a doorway to death.
When [the swooned one's] <s>karma</s> has a remainder, then speech and mind return.
But when [the swooned one's] <s>karma</s> has no remainder, then <s>prāṇa</s> and warmth depart.
Therefore, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> consider [swooning] to be a half-attainment.
As for the objection that no fifth state is known —

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: kadācitkīyamavastheti na prasiddhā syāt /
children.translated_text: Being an occasional state, it may not be well known.

children.text: prasiddhā caiṣā lokāyurvedayoḥ /
children.translated_text: And this [state] is indeed well known in common experience and in <s>Āyurveda</s> (medical science).

children.text: ardhasaṃpattyabhyupagamācca na pañcamī gaṇyata ityanavadyam // 10 //
children.translated_text: And because a half-attainment is accepted, it is not counted as a fifth [state] — this is unobjectionable. // 10 //

children.text: 5 ubhayaliṅgādhikaraṇam / sū. 11-21
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Ubhayaliṅga Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Twofold Characterization). <s>Sūtras</s> 11-21.

children.text: na sthānato 'pi parasyobhayaliṅgaṃ sarvatra hi | BBs_3,2.11 |
children.translated_text: Not even from the standpoint [of <s>upādhis</s>] does the twofold characterization belong to the Supreme — because everywhere [<s>Brahman</s> is taught as without distinctions]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.11 |

children.text:
yena brahmaṇā suṣuptyādiṣu jīva upādhyupaśamātsaṃpadyate tasyedānīṃ svarūpaṃ śrutivaśena nirdhāryate /
santyubhayaliṅgāḥ śrutayo brahmaviṣayāḥ 'sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityelamādāyāḥ saviśeṣaliṅgāḥ /
'asthūlamanaṇvarhrasvamadīrdham' (bṛ. 3.8.8) ityevamādyāśca nirviśeṣaliṅgāḥ /
kimāsu śrutiṣūbhayaliṅgaṃ brahmapratipattavyamutānyataraliṅgam /
yadāpyanyataraliṅgaṃ tadāpi kiṃ saviśeṣamuta nirviśeṣamiti mīmāṃsyate /
tatrobhayaliṅgaśrutyanugrahādubhayaliṅgameva brahmetyevaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - na tāvatsvata eva parasya brahmaṇa ubhayaliṅgatvamupapadyate /
children.translated_text:
Now, the true nature of that <s>Brahman</s> — into which the <s>jīva</s> merges in deep sleep and similar [states] through the subsidence of <s>upādhis</s> — is to be ascertained on the basis of <s>śruti</s>.
There are <s>śrutis</s> of twofold characterization (<s>ubhayaliṅga</s>) concerning <s>Brahman</s>: those such as 'It is the agent of all actions, the possessor of all desires, all fragrances, all tastes' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and similar ones bear the mark of [positive] attributes (<s>saviśeṣa</s>).
And those such as 'Not gross, not subtle, not short, not long' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8) and similar ones bear the mark of the absence of attributes (<s>nirviśeṣa</s>).
Among these <s>śrutis</s>, is <s>Brahman</s> to be understood as having a twofold characterization, or as having only one characterization?
And if only one characterization, then is it with attributes (<s>saviśeṣa</s>) or without attributes (<s>nirviśeṣa</s>)? — this is what is investigated.
Therein, having set forth [the prima facie view] that <s>Brahman</s> has a twofold characterization because of the support of <s>śrutis</s> of both kinds, we say: First, the twofold characterization does not belong to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> from its own nature.

children.text:
nahyekaṃ vastu svata eva rūpādiviśeṣopetaṃ tadviparītaṃ cetyādhārayituṃ śakyaṃ virodhāt /
astu tarhi sthānataḥ pṛthivyādyupādhiyogāditi /
tadapi nopapadyate /
nahyupādhiyogādapyanyādṛśasya vastuno 'nyādṛśaḥ svabhāvaḥ saṃbhavati /
nahi svacchaḥ sansphaṭiko 'laktakādyupādhiyogādasvaccho bhavati bhramamātratvādasvacchatābhiniveśasya /
upādhīnāṃ cāvidyāpratyupasthāpitatvāt /
children.translated_text: And because the <s>upādhis</s> are presented by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: ataścānyataraliṅgaparigrahe 'pi samastaviśeṣarahitaṃ nirvikalpameva brahma pratipattavyaṃ na tadviparītam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when one of the two characterizations is accepted, <s>Brahman</s> is to be understood as devoid of all distinctions, undifferentiated alone — not the contrary.

children.text: sarvatra hi brahmasvarūpapratipādanapareṣu vākyeṣu 'aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayam' (ka. 3.15 /
children.translated_text: For everywhere, in passages whose purport is to set forth the true nature of <s>Brahman</s> — such as 'Soundless, touchless, formless, imperishable' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.15;

children.text: muktiko. 2.72) ityevamādiṣvapāstasamastaviśeṣameva brahmopadiśyate // 11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Muktikā</s> 2.72) — <s>Brahman</s> is taught as devoid of all distinctions whatsoever. // 11 //

For it is impossible for a single entity to be, by its own nature, both endowed with specific features such as form and the like and devoid of them — because of contradiction.
Let it then be from the standpoint [of <s>upādhis</s>] — from the association with <s>upādhis</s> such as earth and the like.
That too is not tenable.
For even through the association of <s>upādhis</s>, an entity of one nature cannot acquire a nature of a different kind.
For a crystal that is inherently clear does not become actually non-clear through the association of <s>upādhis</s> such as red dye and the like — because the conviction of non-clarity is merely an illusion.

children.text: FN: sthānaṃ upādhistadyogāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Sthāna</s>' means <s>upādhi</s>; 'from its association' [means from the association with <s>upādhis</s>].

children.text: na bhedād iti cen na pratyekamatadvacanāt | BBs_3,2.12 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that <s>Brahman</s> has attributes] because of difference [in the meditations] — [we say] no, because [the texts] state individually that it is not that. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.12 |

children.text:
athāpi syādyaduktaṃ nirvikalpamekaliṅgameva brahma nāsya svataḥ sthānato vobhayaliṅgatvamastīti /
tannopapadyate /
kasmāt /
bhedāt /
bhinnā hi pratividyaṃ brahmaṇa ākārā upadiśyante /
catuṣpādbrahma ṣoḍaśakalaṃ brahma vāmanītvādilakṣaṇaṃ brahma trailokyaśarīravaiśvānaraśabdoditaṃ brahmetyevañjātīyakāḥ /
tasmātsaviśeṣatvamapi brahmaṇo 'bhyupagantavyam /
children.translated_text:
Still, it might be said: What has been stated — that <s>Brahman</s> is undifferentiated, of a single characterization alone, and that it has no twofold characterization either from its own nature or from the standpoint [of <s>upādhis</s>] — that is not tenable.
Why?
Because of difference.
For different forms of <s>Brahman</s> are taught in different meditations (<s>vidyās</s>).
<s>Brahman</s> with four feet; <s>Brahman</s> with sixteen parts; <s>Brahman</s> characterized by the <s>Vāmana</s> (dwarf) form and the like; <s>Brahman</s> denoted by the term <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, whose body is the three worlds — such are [the various forms].
Therefore, the attribute-bearing nature (<s>saviśeṣatva</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> too must be accepted.

children.text:
nanūktaṃ nobhayaliṅgatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ saṃbhavatīti /
ayamapyavirodhaḥ /
upādhikṛtatvādākārabhedasya /
anyathā hi nirviṣayameva bhedaśāstraṃ prasajyeteti cet /
children.translated_text: But it was said that <s>Brahman</s> cannot have both characteristics — [is this not contradicted]? This too is not a contradiction — because the differentiation of form is caused by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>). Otherwise, the scripture teaching difference would be without an object — [is this the objection?]

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ /
kasmāt /
pratyekamatadvacanāt /
pratyupādhibhedaṃ hyabhedameva brahmaṇaḥ śrāvayati śāstram - 'yaścāyamasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaścāyamadhyātmaṃ śārīrastejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yameva sa yo 'yamātmā' (bṛ. 2.5.1) ityādi /
ataśca na bhinnākārayogo brahmaṇaḥ śāstrīya iti śakyate vaktum /
bhedasyopāsanārthatvādabhede tātparyāt /
children.translated_text: No, we say. Why? Because, for each [limiting adjunct], non-difference alone is taught. For scripture teaches the very non-difference of <s>Brahman</s>, corresponding to each limiting adjunct: ‘And he who is this person in the earth, luminous, immortal — and he who is this bodily person in the individual, luminous, immortal — this indeed is that Self’ (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.1), and so on. Therefore, it cannot be said that the conjunction of differentiated forms with <s>Brahman</s> is the teaching of scripture — because the [teaching of] difference serves the purpose of meditation, and the purport is non-difference.

children.text: api caivam eke | BBs_3,2.13 |
children.translated_text: Moreover, thus [teach] some [branches of the <s>Veda</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.13 |

children.text: apicaivaṃ bhedadarsananindāpūrvakamabhedadarśanamevaike śākhinaḥ samāmananti - 'manasaivedamāptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiñcana /
children.translated_text: Moreover, thus — having prefaced with the censure of the vision of difference — some followers of [particular] branches teach the vision of non-difference itself: ‘This is to be attained by the mind alone; there is no multiplicity here whatsoever.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyupamāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati' (ka. 4.11) iti /
children.translated_text: He goes from death to death who sees, as it were, multiplicity here’ (<s>Kaṭha</s> 4.11).

children.text: tathānyepi 'bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā sarvaṃ trividhaṃ brahma me tat' (śve. 1.12) iti samastasya bhogyabhoktṛniyantṛlakṣaṇasya prapañcasya brahmaikasvabhāvatāmadhīyate // 13 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, others too — ‘Knowing the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and the impeller — all [this] threefold [world] is that <s>Brahman</s>’ (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 1.12) — teach the single <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the entire phenomenal world characterized by the enjoyed, the enjoyer, and the controller. // 13 //

children.text:
kathaṃ punarākāravadupadeśinīṣvanākāropadeśinīṣu ca brahmaviṣayāsu śrutiṣu satīṣvanākārameva brahmāvadhāryate na punarviparītamti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: But how, when there are <s>śrutis</s> about <s>Brahman</s> that teach it with form and [others] that teach it without form, is <s>Brahman</s> determined to be without form alone, and not the opposite? To this he replies:

children.text: arūpavadeva hi tatpradhānatvāt | BBs_3,2.14 |
children.translated_text: It is formless indeed, because of the predominance of that [teaching]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.14 |

children.text:
rūpādyākārarahitameva brahmāvadhārayitavyaṃ na rūpādimat /
kasmāt /
tatpradhānatvāt /
''asthūlamanaṇvarhrasvamadīrdham' (bṛ. 3.8.8) 'aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayam' (kaṭha. 3.15 /
mukti. 2.72) 'ākāśo vai nāma nāmarūpayornirvahitā te yadantarā tadbrahma' (chā. 8.14.1) 'divyo hyamūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ'' (muṇḍa. 2.1.2), 'tadetadbrahmāpūrvamanaparamanantaramabrahmamayamātmā brahagma sarvānabhūḥ' (bṛ. 2.5.19) ityevamādīni vākyāni niṣprapañcabrahmātmatattvapradhānāni narthāntarapradhānānītyetatpratiṣṭhāpitaṃ 'tattu samanvayāt' (bra.sū. 1.1.4) ityatra /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> must be determined as devoid of form and such features, not as possessing form and such. Why? Because of the predominance of that [teaching]. ‘Neither gross nor minute, neither short nor long’ (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8); ‘Without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable’ (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.15); ‘<s>Ākāśa</s> is the name, the differentiator of name and form; that which is between them is <s>Brahman</s>’ (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1); ‘The divine <s>Puruṣa</s> is without a body, both without and within, unborn’ (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2); ‘This is <s>Brahman</s>, without a prior, without a posterior, without an interior, without an exterior; this Self is <s>Brahman</s>, the all-perceiving’ (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19) — such passages predominantly convey the reality of the undifferentiated <s>Brahman</s>-Self and are not predominantly about another subject — this was established in ‘<s>Tattu samanvayāt</s>’ (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.4).

children.text:
tasmādevañjātīyakeṣu vākyeṣu yathāśrutaṃ nirākārameva brahmāvadhārayitavyam /
itarāṇi tvākārapavadbrahmaviṣayāṇi vākyāni na tatpradhānāni /
upāsanāvidhipradhānāni hi tāni teṣvasati virodhe yathāśrutamāśrayitavyam /
children.translated_text: For those [passages] are predominantly injunctions of meditation (<s>upāsanāvidhi</s>); in the absence of contradiction, they should be relied upon as heard.

children.text: sati tu virodhe tatpradhānānyatatpradhānebhyo balīyāṃsi bhavantīti /
children.translated_text: But when there is contradiction, the passages that predominantly [teach <s>Brahman</s>’s nature] are stronger than those that do not.

children.text: eṣa vinigamanāyāṃ hetuḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the reason for the determination —

children.text: yenobhayīṣvapi śrutiṣu satīṣvanākārameva brahmāvadhāryate na punarviparītamiti // 14 //
children.translated_text: by which, even though both types of <s>śrutis</s> exist, <s>Brahman</s> is determined to be formless alone and not the opposite. // 14 //

Therefore, in such passages, <s>Brahman</s> must be determined as formless, just as heard. But the other passages about <s>Brahman</s> with form are not predominantly [teaching <s>Brahman</s>’s nature].

children.text: kā tarhyākāravadviṣayāṇāṃ śrutīnāṃ gatirityata āha -
children.translated_text: What, then, is the interpretation of the <s>śrutis</s> whose subject is [<s>Brahman</s>] with form? To this he says:

children.text: prakāśavaccāvaiyarthyāt | BBs_3,2.15 |
children.translated_text: And like light, because of [avoiding] purposelessness. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.15 |

children.text:
yathā prakāśaḥ sauraścāndramaso vā viyadvyāpyāvatiṣṭhamāno 'ṅgulyādyupādhisaṃbandhātteṣvṛjuvakrādibhāvaṃ pratipadyamāneṣu tadbhāvamiva pratipadyate /
evaṃ brahmāpi pṛthivyādyupādhisaṃbandhāttadākāratāmiva pratipadyate tadālambano brahmaṇa ākāraviśeṣopadeśa upāsanārtho na virudhyate /
evamavaiyarthyamākāravadbrahmaviṣayāṇāmapi vākyānāṃ bhaviṣyati /
nahi vedavākyānāṃ kasyacidarthavattvaṃ kasyacidanarthavattvamiti yuktaṃ pratipattuṃ pramāṇatvāviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: Just as the light of the sun or moon, pervading space, when it comes into contact with limiting adjuncts like a finger and such — as those [adjuncts] assume straight, curved, and other configurations — appears to assume those configurations; so too <s>Brahman</s>, through its contact with limiting adjuncts such as earth and such, appears to assume their forms. A particular form-teaching of <s>Brahman</s> based on such [limiting adjuncts], for the purpose of meditation, is not contradictory. Thus, the passages about <s>Brahman</s> with form too will have their purpose. For it is not proper to understand that some Vedic passages are meaningful and others are not — because there is no distinction in their authoritative status.

children.text: nanvevamapi yatpurastātpratijñātaṃ nopādhiyogādapyubhayaliṅgatvaṃ brahmaṇo 'stīti tadvirudhyate /
children.translated_text: But even so, is not the thesis asserted earlier contradicted — that <s>Brahman</s> does not have both characteristics even through the conjunction with limiting adjuncts?

children.text: neti brūmaḥ /
children.translated_text: No, we say.

children.text: upādhinimittasya vastudharmatvānupapacatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because what is occasioned by limiting adjuncts cannot be a real property of the entity.

children.text: upādhīnāṃ cāvidyāpratyupasthāpitatvāt /
children.translated_text: And because the limiting adjuncts are presented by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: satyāmeva ca naisargikyāmavidyāyāṃ lokavedavyavahārāvatāra iti tatra tatrāvocāma // 15 //
children.translated_text: And we have stated in various places that the engagement in worldly and Vedic transactions occurs only when innate <s>avidyā</s> exists. // 15 //

children.text: āha ca tanmātram | BBs_3,2.16 |
children.translated_text: And [scripture] states: that alone [is <s>Brahman</s>’s nature]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.16 |

children.text: āha ca śrutiścaitanyamātraṃ vilakṣaṇarūpāntararahitaṃ nirviśeṣaṃ brahma - 'sa yathā saindhavaghano 'ntaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsno rasaghana evaivaṃ vā are 'yamātmānantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva' (bṛ. 4.5.13) iti /
children.translated_text: And scripture states that <s>Brahman</s> is pure consciousness alone, devoid of any other distinct form, undifferentiated: ‘As a lump of salt is without interior, without exterior, entirely a mass of taste — so indeed this Self is without interior, without exterior, entirely a mass of consciousness’ (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.13).

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati - nāsyātmano 'ntarbahirvā caitanyādanyadrūpamasti lavaṇarasa eva nirantaro bhavati na rasāntaraṃ tathaiveti // 16 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: this Self has no form other than consciousness, either within or without — just as [a lump of] salt-taste is uniform and contains no other taste. // 16 //

children.text: FN: saindhavaghano lohapiṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: ‘<s>Saindhavaghana</s>’ is a lump of [rock] salt.

children.text: darśayati cātho api smaryate | BBs_3,2.17 |
children.translated_text: And [scripture] shows [this]; and moreover, [this] is remembered [in <s>Smṛti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.17 |

children.text:
darśayati ca śrutiḥ pararūpapratiṣedhenaiva brahma nirviśeṣatvāt- 'athāta ādeśo neti neti' (bṛ. 2.3.6) iti, 'anyadeva tadviditādatho aviditādadhi (ke. 1.3) 'yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha' (tai. 2.4.1) ityevamādyā /
bāṣkalinā ca bādhvaḥpṛṣṭaḥ sannavacanenaiva brahma provāceti śrūyate - 'sa hovācādhīhi bho iti sa tūṣṇīṃ babhūva taṃ ha dvitīye vā tṛtīye vā vacana uvāca brūmaḥ khalu tvaṃ tu na vijānāsi /
upaśānto 'yamātmā' iti /
tathā smṛtiṣvapi parapratiṣedhenaivopadiśyate - 'jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvāmṛtamaśnute /
anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate' (13.12) ityevamādyāsu /
tathā viśvarūpadharo nārāyaṇo nāradamuvāceti smaryate - 'māyā hyeṣā mayā sṛṣṭā yanmāṃ paśyasi nārada /
sarvabhūtaguṇairyuktaṃ naivaṃ māṃ jñātumarhasi' iti /
children.translated_text: And scripture shows <s>Brahman</s> precisely through the negation of other forms, because of its undifferentiated nature: ‘Now, the teaching: Not this, not this’ (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6); ‘It is other than the known and also above the unknown’ (<s>Kena</s> 1.3); ‘From which words return, together with the mind, without reaching [It]’ (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.4.1) — and such passages. And <s>Bāṣkali</s>, when questioned by <s>Bādhva</s>, taught <s>Brahman</s> by silence itself, it is heard: ‘He said: Teach, revered sir. He remained silent. When he was addressed a second and a third time, he said: I am teaching, but you do not understand.’

children.text:
FN: adhi anyat /
upaśānto nirastadvaitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This Self is quiescent. Similarly, in <s>Smṛtis</s> too, [<s>Brahman</s>] is taught only through the negation of other [attributes]: ‘I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality — the beginningless Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; it is called neither existent nor non-existent’ (<s>Gītā</s> 13.12) — and such passages. Similarly, it is remembered that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who had assumed the universal form, said to <s>Nārada</s>: ‘This <s>Māyā</s> has been created by Me — that you see Me thus, O <s>Nārada</s>; endowed with the qualities of all beings — you should not know Me thus.’

children.text: ata eva copamā sūryakādivat | BBs_3,2.18 |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the analogy is like a reflection of the sun and such. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.18 |

children.text: yata eva cāyamātmā caitanyarūpo nirviśeṣo vāṅmanasātītaḥ parapratiṣedhopadeśyo 'ta eva cāsyopādhinimittapāramārthikīṃ viśeṣavattābhipretya jalasūryakādivadityupamopādīyate mokṣaśāstreṣu - 'yathā hyajaṃ jyotirātmā vivasvānapo bhinnā bahudhaiko 'nugacchan /
children.translated_text: Because this Self is of the nature of consciousness, undifferentiated, beyond speech and mind, teachable only through the negation of other [attributes] — for this very reason, intending the non-ultimate nature of its possession of specific attributes caused by limiting adjuncts, the analogy ‘like a reflection of the sun in water’ and such is employed in the scriptures of liberation: ‘Just as the unborn light — the self-luminous sun — following the waters divided into many [reflections], being one,

children.text: upādhinā kriyate bhedarūpo devaḥ kṣetreṣvevamajoyamātmā' iti /
children.translated_text: is made to assume the form of difference by the limiting adjunct — so too this unborn Self [enters] into fields [of bodies].’

children.text: 'eka eva hi bhūtātmā bhūte bhūte vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: ‘For the one Self of all beings, established in each being,

children.text: ekadhā bahudhā caiva dṛśyate jalacandravat' (bra.biṃ 12) ityevamādiṣu // 18 //
children.translated_text: is seen as one and as many — like the moon in water’ (<s>Brahmabindu</s> 12) — and such passages. // 18 //

children.text: atra pratyavasthīyate -
children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised:

children.text: ambuvadagrahaṇāt tu na tathātvam | BBs_3,2.19 |
children.translated_text: But because [<s>Brahman</s> is] not apprehended like water, there is no such similarity. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.19 |

children.text: na jalasūryakāditulyatvamihopapadyate tadvadagrahaṇāt /
children.translated_text: The equality with a reflection of the sun in water is not justified here — because [<s>Brahman</s>] is not apprehended like that [i.e., like water].

children.text: sūryādibhyo hi mūrtebhyaḥ pṛthagbhūtaṃ viprakṛṣṭadeśaṃ mūrtaṃ gṛhyate tatra yuktaḥ sūryādipratibimbodayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For from the sun and such, which have form, a formed [reflection], existing separately and at a distant location, is apprehended — there the arising of a reflection of the sun and such is justified.

children.text: natvātmā mūrto nacāsmātpṛthagbhūtā viprakṛṣṭadeśāścopādhayaḥ sarvagatatvātsarvānanyatvācca /
children.translated_text: But the Self has no form, nor are the limiting adjuncts separate from It or at a distant location — because of Its all-pervasiveness and because It is non-different from everything.

children.text: tasmādayukto 'yaṃ dṛṣṭānta iti // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this illustration is unjustified. // 19 //

children.text: atra pratividhīyate -
children.translated_text: To this, the answer is given:

children.text: vṛddhihrāsabhāktvamantarbhāvādubhayasāmañjasyādevam | BBs_3,2.20 |
children.translated_text: Because of partaking in increase and decrease, because of being included [in the limiting adjuncts], and because of the consistency of both — it is thus. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.20 |

children.text:
yukta eva tvayaṃ dṛṣṭānto vivakṣitāṃśasaṃbhavāt /
nahi dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭrāntikayoḥ kvacitkañcidvivakṣitāṃśaṃ mukattvā sarvasārūpyaṃ kenaciddarśayituṃ śakyate /
sarvasārūpye hi dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭrāntikabhāvoccheda eva syāt /
nacedaṃ svamanīṣayā jalasūryakājadidṛṣṭāntapraṇayanam /
śāstrapraṇītasya tvasya prayojanamātramupanyasyate /
kiṃ punaratra vivakṣitaṃ sārūpyamiti /
taducyate - vṛddhihrāsabhāktvamiti /
children.translated_text: To that he says: partaking in increase and decrease.

children.text: jalagataṃ hi sūryapratibimbaṃ jalavṛddhau vardhate jalahrāse hrasati jalacalane calati jalabhede bhidyata ityevaṃ jaladharmānuyāyi bhavati natu paramārthataḥ sūryasya tathātvamasti /
children.translated_text: For the reflection of the sun in water increases when the water increases, decreases when the water decreases, moves when the water moves, and splits when the water splits — thus it follows the properties of the water. But in reality, the sun does not have such properties.

children.text: evaṃ paramārthato 'vikṛtamekarūpamapi sadbrahma dehādyupādhyantarbhāvādbhajata ivopādidharmānvṛddhirhrāsādīn /
children.translated_text: Similarly, <s>Brahman</s> — though in reality unchanged and of a single nature — because of its inclusion within the limiting adjuncts of body and such, seems to partake in the properties of the limiting adjuncts — increase, decrease, and such.

children.text: evamubhayordṛṣṭāntadārṣṭrāntikayoḥ sāmañjasyādavirodhaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: Thus, because of the consistency of both — the illustration and the illustrated — there is no contradiction. // 20 //

This illustration is indeed justified — because of the possibility of the intended aspect of similarity. For no one can show complete similarity in all respects between an illustration and the thing illustrated, apart from some intended aspect. For if there were complete similarity, the very distinction between illustration and illustrated would be destroyed. And this employment of the illustration of the sun’s reflection in water and such is not of our own contrivance — rather, only the purpose of [the illustration] as presented by scripture is being explained. What, then, is the intended similarity?

children.text: darśanāc ca | BBs_3,2.21 |
children.translated_text: And because of [scriptural] showing. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.21 |

children.text:
darśayati ca śrutiḥ parasyaiva brahmaṇo dehādiṣūpādhiṣvantaranupraveśam - 'puruścakre dvipadaḥ puruścakre catuśpadaḥ /
puraḥ sa pakṣī bhūtvā puraḥ puruṣa āviśat' (bṛ. 2.5.18) iti /
'anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya' (chā. 6.3.2) iti ca /
tasmādyuktametat - 'ata eva caipamā sūryakādivat' (bra.sū. 3.2.18) iti /
tasmānnirvikalpakaikaliṅgameva brahma nobhayaliṅgaṃ viparītaliṅgaṃ ceti siddham /
atra keciddve adhikaraṇe kalpayanti /
prathamaṃ tāvat- kiṃ pratyastamitāśeṣaprapañcamekākāraṃ brahmota prapañcavadanekākāropetamiti /
dvitīyaṃ tu - sthite pratyastamitaprapañcatve kiṃ sallakṣaṇaṃ brahmota bodhalakṣaṇamutobhayalakṣaṇamiti /
atra vayaṃ vadāmaḥ - sarvathāpyānarthakyamadhikaraṇāntarārambhasyeti /
yadi tāvadanekaliṅgatvaṃ parasyabrahmaṇo nirākartavyamityayaṃ prayāsastatpūrveṇaiva na sthānato 'pi ityanenādhikaraṇena nirākartavyamityayamuttaramadhikaraṇaṃ prakāśavacca etadvyarthameva bhavet /
naca sallakṣaṇameva bhma na bodhalakṣaṇamiti śakyaṃ vaktum /
vijñānaghana evetyādiśrutivaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt /
kathaṃ vā nirastacaitanyaṃ brahma cetanasya jīvasyātmatvenopadiśyeta /
nāpi bodhalakṣaṇameva brahma na sallakṣaṇamiti śakyaṃ vaktum astītyevopalabdhavyaḥ (pha. 6.13)
children.translated_text: And scripture shows the entry of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself into the limiting adjuncts of body and such: ‘He made two-footed bodies; He made four-footed bodies; having become a bird, He — the <s>Puruṣa</s> — entered the bodies’ (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.18). And: ‘Having entered through this <s>jīva</s>-self’ (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.3.2). Therefore, this is fitting: ‘For this very reason, the analogy is like a reflection of the sun and such’ (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.2.18). Therefore, it is established that <s>Brahman</s> has only the single characteristic of being undifferentiated — not both characteristics, nor the opposite characteristic. Here, some posit two separate topics (<s>adhikaraṇas</s>). The first: is <s>Brahman</s> of a single nature with all phenomenal diversity dissolved, or does it possess many forms including the phenomenal? The second: granted that the phenomenal is dissolved, is <s>Brahman</s> characterized by Being (<s>sat</s>), or by consciousness (<s>bodha</s>), or by both? We say: in any case, the commencement of a separate topic is purposeless. For if the effort is to negate the multiplicity of characteristics of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — this was already negated by the earlier topic ‘not even by [its assuming a] position [in limiting adjuncts].’ And if the later topic is to negate [multiplicity], then ‘like light’ and so on would be purposeless. Nor can it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is characterized by Being alone and not by consciousness — because of the contingency of passages like ‘a mass of consciousness alone’ becoming purposeless. And how could <s>Brahman</s> devoid of consciousness be taught as the Self of the conscious <s>jīva</s>? Nor can it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is characterized by consciousness alone and not by Being — because of the contingency of passages like ‘It is to be realized as existing’ (<s>Kaṭha</s> 6.13)

children.text:
ityādiśrutivaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt /
kathaṃ vā nirastasattāko bodho 'bhyupagamyeta /
nāpyubhayalakṣaṇameva brahmeti śakyaṃ vaktum /
pūrvābhyupagamavirodhaprasaṅgāt /
sattāvyāvṛttena ca bodhena bodhavyāvṛttayā ca sattayopetaṃ brahma pratijānānasya tadeva pūrvādhikaraṇapratiṣiddhaṃ saprapañcatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prasajyeta /
children.translated_text: and such becoming purposeless. And how could consciousness devoid of Being be accepted? Nor can it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is characterized by both — because of the contingency of contradicting the previous acceptance. For one who asserts that <s>Brahman</s> possesses Being distinct from consciousness and consciousness distinct from Being would incur the very phenomenal plurality of <s>Brahman</s> that was rejected in the previous topic.

children.text: śrutatvādadoṣa iti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one says] there is no fault because of its being taught [in <s>śruti</s>] —

children.text:
na /
ekasyānekasvabhāvatvānupapatteḥ /
atha sattaiva bodho bodha eva ca sattā nānayoḥ parasparavyāvṛttirastīti yadyucyeta tathāpi kiṃ sallakṣaṇaṃ brahmota bodhalakṣaṇamutobhayalakṣaṇamityevaṃ vikalpo nirālambana eva syāt /
sūtrāṇi tvekādhikaraṇatvenaivāsmābhirnītāni /
