apica brahmaviṣayāsu śrutiṣvākāravadanākārapratipādanena vipratipannasvānākāre brahmaṇi parigṛhīte 'vaśyaṃ vaktavyetarāsāṃ śrutīnāṃ gatiḥ /
tādarthyena prakāśavaccetyādīni sūtrāṇyarthavattarāṇi saṃpadyante /
children.translated_text: No. Because it is not possible for one [entity] to have multiple natures. And if it is said that Being is indeed consciousness and consciousness is indeed Being, and there is no mutual exclusion between them — even then, the question ‘Is <s>Brahman</s> characterized by Being, or by consciousness, or by both?’ would be entirely groundless. But the <s>sūtras</s> have been construed by us as belonging to a single topic. Moreover, when <s>Brahman</s> is determined as formless — since the <s>śrutis</s> about <s>Brahman</s> teach both with form and without form, and since those teaching the formless are accepted as dominant — the interpretation of the other <s>śrutis</s> must necessarily be stated. For this purpose, the <s>sūtras</s> ‘like light’ and such become more meaningful.

children.text:
yadyapyāhurākāravādinyo 'pi śrutayaḥ prapañcapravilayamukhenānākārapratipattyarthā eva na pṛthagarthā iti tadapi na samīcīnamiva lakṣyate /
katham /
ye hi paravidyādhikāre kecitprapañcā ucyante yathā - 'yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā deśetyaya vai harayo 'yaṃ vai sahasrāṇi bahūni cānantāni ca' (bṛ. 2.5.19) ityevamādayaste bhavanti pravilayārthāḥ 'tadetadbrahmāpūrvamanaparamanantaramabāhyam' (bṛ. 2.5.19) ityupasaṃhārāt /
ye punarupāsanādhikāre prapañcā ucyante yathā 'manomayaḥ prāṇasīro bhārūpaḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityevamādayo na teṣāṃ pravilayārthatvaṃ nyāyyam /
'sa kratuṃ kurvīta' (chā. 3.14.1) ityevañjātīyakena prakṛtenaivopāsanavidhinā teṣāṃ saṃbandhāt /
śrutyā caivañjātīyakānāṃ guṇānāmupāsanārthatve 'vakalpyamāne na lakṣaṇayā pravilayārtatvamavakalpate /
sarveṣāṃ ca sādhāraṇe pravilayārthatve sati 'arūpavadeva hi tatpradhānatvāt' (bra. sū. 3.2.14) iti vinigamanakāraṇavacanamanavakāśaṃ syāt /
phalamapyeṣāṃ yathopadeśaṃ kvacidduritakṣayaḥ kvacidaiśvaryaprāptiḥ kvacitkramamuktirityavagamyata evetyataḥ pārthagartyamevopāsanāvākyānāṃ brahmavākyānāṃ ca nyāyyaṃ naikavākyatvam /
kathaṃ caiṣāmekavākyatotprekṣyata iti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: Even though some say that the <s>śruti</s> passages teaching form (<s>ākāravādin</s>) too are intended solely for the understanding of the formless, through the dissolution of phenomenal expansion — and are not independently purposeful — even that does not appear correct. How so? Those phenomenal elaborations that are stated in the context of the higher knowledge (<s>paravidyā</s>) — such as 'His horses are yoked, a hundred and ten in each region; these horses are in thousands, many and infinite' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19) and the like — those are indeed for the purpose of dissolution, because of the conclusion: 'This is <s>Brahman</s>, without a before, without an after, without an inside, without an outside' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19). But those phenomenal elaborations that are stated in the context of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) — such as 'consisting of mind, having <s>Prāṇa</s> as its body, having the form of light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and the like — it is not proper for them to have the purpose of dissolution, because of their connection with the meditation-injunction that is the subject: 'He should form a resolve' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1) and such. And when the purpose of such qualities for meditation is established directly by <s>śruti</s>, the purpose of dissolution cannot be established through secondary signification. And if the purpose of dissolution were common to all [passages], then the statement of a ground for determination — 'As if formless, because that is predominant' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.2.14) — would have no scope. Moreover, the fruit of these [meditations] is understood as taught: in some cases, the destruction of demerits; in some, the attainment of sovereignty; in some, gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>). Therefore, it is proper that the meditation-passages and the <s>Brahman</s>-passages have independent purposes — not a single-sentence reading. And it must be explained how their single-sentence reading can even be imagined.

children.text: ekaniyogapratīteḥ prayājadarśapūrṇamāsavākyavaditi cet /
children.translated_text: If [it is said] that because of the apprehension of a single injunction, [they have single-sentence reading] — like the passages of the <s>Prayāja</s> rites and the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> —

children.text:
na /
brahmavākyeṣu niyogābhāvāt /
vastumātraparyavasāyīni hi brakahmavākyāni na niyogopadeśīnītyetadvistare pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ 'tattu samanvayāt (bra. sū. 1.1.4) ityatra /
kiṃviṣayaścātra niyogo 'bhipreyata iti vaktavyam /
puruṣo hi niyujyamānaḥ kurviti svavyāpāre kasmiṃścinniyujyate /
children.translated_text: No. Because there is no injunction in the <s>Brahman</s>-passages. For the <s>Brahman</s>-passages culminate in mere reality — they do not teach an injunction. This was established at length in [the discussion of] 'But that, because of consistency' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.4). And it must be stated: what is the object of the injunction intended here? For a person being enjoined 'do!' is enjoined with respect to some action within his own power.

children.text:
nanu dvaitaprapañcavilayo na yogaviṣayo bhaviṣyati /
apravilāpite hi dvaitaprapañce brahmatattvāvabodho na bhavatyato brahmatattvāvabodhapratyanīkabhūto dvaitaprapañcaḥ pravilāpyaḥ /
yathā svargāmasya yāgo 'nuṣṭhātavya upadiśyata evamapavargakāmasya prapañcapravilayaḥ /
yathāca tamasi vyavasthitaṃ ghaṭāditattvamavabubhutsamānena tatpratyanīkabhūtaṃ tamaḥ pravilāpyata evaṃ brahmatattavamavabubhutsamānena tatpratyanīkabhūtaḥ prapañcaḥ pravilāpayitavyaḥ /
brahmasvabhāvo hi prapañco na prapañcasvabhāvaṃ brahma, tena nāmarūpaprapañcapravilāpanena brahmatattvāvabodho bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: But [one might argue:] will not the dissolution of the phenomenal duality be a suitable object of effort? For without dissolving the phenomenal duality, the realization of the truth of <s>Brahman</s> does not occur. Therefore, the phenomenal duality — which is opposed to the realization of the truth of <s>Brahman</s> — must be dissolved. Just as one who desires heaven is taught to perform sacrifice, so one who desires liberation should [be taught to perform] the dissolution of phenomenal expansion. And just as one wishing to know the true nature of a pot and such standing in darkness must dissolve the darkness that is opposed to [seeing] it — so one wishing to know the truth of <s>Brahman</s> must dissolve the phenomenal expansion that is opposed to it. For the phenomenal world has <s>Brahman</s> as its nature, but <s>Brahman</s> does not have the phenomenal world as its nature. Therefore, through the dissolution of the phenomenal expansion of name and form, the realization of the truth of <s>Brahman</s> occurs.

children.text:
atra vayaṃ pṛcchāmaḥ - ko 'yaṃ prapañcapravilayo nāma /
kimagnipratāpasaṃparkādghṛtakāṭhinyapravilaya iva ppapañcapravilayaḥ kartavya āhosvidekasmiṃścandre timirakṛtānekacandraprapañcavadavidyākṛto brahmaṇi nāmarūpaprapañco vidyayā pravilāpitavya iti /
tatra tāvadvidyāmano 'yaṃ prapañco dehādilakṣaṇa ādhyatmiko bāhyaśca pṛthivyādilakṣaṇaḥ pravilāpayitavya ityucyeta sa puruṣamātreṇāśakyaḥ pravilāpayitumiti tatpravilayopadeśo 'śakyaviṣaya eva syāt /
ekena cādimuktena pṛthivyādipravilayaḥ kṛta itīdānīṃ pṛthivyādiśūnyaṃ jagadabhaviṣyat /
athāvidyādhyasto brahmaṇyekasminnayaṃ prapañco vidyayā pravilāpyata iti brūyāt /
tato brahmaivāvidyādhyastaprapañcapratyākhyānenāvedayitavyam ekamevādvitīyaṃ brahma, tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tatvamasi (chā. 6.8.7) iti tasminnāvedite vidyā svayamevotpadyate tayā cāvidyā bādhyate.
children.translated_text: Here we ask: what exactly is this 'dissolution of phenomenal expansion'? Is the dissolution of phenomenal expansion to be accomplished [in reality] — like the dissolution of the hardness of ghee through contact with the heat of fire? Or is the phenomenal expansion of name and form in <s>Brahman</s>, created by <s>avidyā</s>, to be dissolved by knowledge — like the phenomenal expansion of multiple moons in the one moon, created by an eye-disease? In the first case — if this phenomenal expansion, both internal (characterized by body and such) and external (characterized by earth and such), is said to be real and to be dissolved — that would be impossible for a mere person to dissolve, so the teaching of its dissolution would have an impossible object. And if one liberated person had dissolved earth and the like, then the world would now be devoid of earth and the like. But if one were to say that this phenomenal expansion, superimposed on the one <s>Brahman</s> through <s>avidyā</s>, is to be dissolved by knowledge — then <s>Brahman</s> itself must be made known through the negation of the phenomenal expansion superimposed by <s>avidyā</s>: '<s>Brahman</s> alone, one without a second; that is the Real; that is the Self; you are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7). When that is made known, knowledge arises spontaneously, and by it, <s>avidyā</s> is sublated.

children.text:
tataścāvidyadhyastaḥ sakalo 'yaṃ nāmarūpaprapañcaḥ svapnaprapañcavatpravilīyate /
anāvedite tu brahmaṇi brahmavijñānaṃ kuru prapañcapravilayaṃ ceti śatakṛtvo 'pyukte, na brahmavijñānaṃ prapañpapravilayo vā jāyate /
children.translated_text: And thereupon, this entire phenomenal expansion of name and form, superimposed by <s>avidyā</s>, dissolves like the phenomenal expansion of a dream. But if <s>Brahman</s> is not made known, even if one says a hundred times 'produce the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>!' or 'dissolve the phenomenal expansion!' — neither the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> nor the dissolution of phenomenal expansion arises.

children.text: nanvāvedite brahmaṇi tadvijñānaviṣayaḥ prapañcavilayaviṣayo vā niyogaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: But [one might say:] when <s>Brahman</s> has been made known, there could be an injunction regarding the knowledge of it, or regarding the dissolution of phenomenal expansion.

children.text:
na /
niṣprapañcabrahmātmatvāvedanenaivobhayasiddheḥ /
rajjusvarūpaprakāśanenaiva hi tatsvarūpavijñānamavidyādhyastasarpādiprapañcapravilayaśca bhavati /
naca kṛtameva punaḥ kriyate /
niyojyoñapi ca prapañcāvasthāyāṃ yo 'vagamyate jīvo nāma sa prapañcasyaiva vā syādbrahmapakṣasyaiva vā /
prathame vikalpe niṣprapañcabrahmatattvapratipādanena pṛthivyādivajjīvasyāpi pravilāpitatvātkasya prapañcavilaye niyoga ucyeta kasya vā niyoganiṣṭhatayā mokṣo 'vāptavya ucyeta /
dvitīye 'pi brahmaivāniyojyasvabhāvaṃ jīvasya svarūpaṃ jīvatvaṃ tvavidyākṛtameveti pratipādite brahmaṇi niyojyābhāvānniyogābhāva eva /
draṣṭavyādiśabdā api paravidyādhikārapaṭhitāstattvābhimukhīkaraṇapradhānā na tatvāvabodhavidhipradhānā bhavanti /
loke 'pīdaṃ paśyedamākārṇayeti caivañjātīyakeṣu nirdeśeṣu praṇidhānamātraṃ kurvityucyate na sākṣājjñānameva kurviti /
jñeyābhimukhasyāpi jñānaṃ kadācijjāyate kadācinna jāyate tasmāttaṃ prati jñānaviṣaya eva darśayitavyo jñāpayitukāmena /
tasmindarśite svayameva yathāviṣayaṃ yathāpramāṇaṃ ca jñānamutpadyate /
naca pramāṇāntareṇānyathāprasiddher'the 'nyathājñānaṃ niyuktasyāpyupapadyate /
yadi punarniyukto 'hamityanyathā jñānaṃ kuryānna tu tajjñānaṃ kiṃ tarhi mānasī sā kriyā /
svayameva cedanyathotpadyeta bhrāntireva syāt /
jñānaṃ tu pramāṇajanyaṃ yathābhūtaviṣayaṃ ca na tanniyogaśatenāpi kārayituṃ śakyate /
naca pratiṣedhenāpi vārayituṃ śakyate /
nahi tatpuruśatantraṃ, vastutantrameva hi tat /
ato 'pi niyogābhāvaḥ /
kiñcānyanniyoganiṣṭhatayaiva paryavasyāmnāye yadabhyupagatamaniyojyabrahmātmatvaṃ jīvasya tadapramāṇakameva syāt /
atha śāstramevāniyojyabrahmātmatvamapyācakṣīta tadavabodhe ca puruṣaṃ niyuñjīta tato brahmaśāstrasyaikasya dvyarthaparatā viruddhārthaparatā ca prasajyetām /
niyogaparatāyāṃ ca śrutahāniraśrutakalpanā karmaphalavanmokṣasyādṛṣṭaphalatvamanityatvaṃ cetyevamādayo doṣā na kenacitparihartuṃ śakyāḥ /
tasmādavagataniṣṭhānyeva brahmavākyāni na niyoganiṣṭhāni /
ataścaikaniyogapratīterekavākyatetyayuktam /
abhyupagamyamāne 'pi ca brahmavākyechu niyogasadbhāve tadekatvaṃ niṣprapañcopadeśeṣu saprapañcopajadeśeṣu cāsiddham /
nahi śabdāntarādibhiḥ pramāṇairniyogabhede 'vagamyamāne sarvatraikā niyoga iti śakyamāśrayitum /
prayājadarśapūrṇamāsavākyechu tvadhikārāṃśenābhedādyuktamekatvam /
natviha saguṇanirguṇacodanāsu kaścidekatvādhikīrāṃso 'sti /
nahi bhārūpatāvādayo guṇāḥ prapañcapravilayopakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the qualities such as 'having the form of light' and the like do not assist the dissolution of phenomenal expansion.

children.text: nāpi prapañcapravilayo bhārūpatvādiguṇopakārī, parasparavirodhitvāt /
children.translated_text: Nor does the dissolution of phenomenal expansion assist the qualities such as 'having the form of light' — because they are mutually opposed.

children.text: nahi kṛtsnaprapañcapravilāpanaṃ prapañcaikadeśāpekṣaṇaṃ caikasmindharmiṇi yuktaṃ samāveśayitum /
children.translated_text: For it is not proper to combine in one subject both the dissolution of the entire phenomenal expansion and the dependence on one part of the phenomenal expansion.

children.text: tasmādasmādukta eva vibhāga ākāravadanākāropadeśānāṃ yuktatara iti // 21 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the very distinction stated by us between the passages teaching [<s>Brahman</s>] with form and those teaching without form is more reasonable. // 21 //

No. Because both are accomplished by the very making known of <s>Brahman</s> as the Self that is free from phenomenal expansion. For by the mere illumination of the true nature of the rope, both the knowledge of its true nature and the dissolution of the phenomenal expansion of the snake and such superimposed by <s>avidyā</s> occur. And what is already accomplished is not accomplished again. Moreover, the one who is to be enjoined — the <s>jīva</s> that is apprehended in the state of phenomenal expansion — either belongs to the phenomenal side or to the <s>Brahman</s> side. In the first alternative, since the <s>jīva</s> too is dissolved — like earth and the like — by the teaching of the truth of <s>Brahman</s> that is free from phenomenal expansion, to whom would the injunction of phenomenal dissolution be addressed, and for whom would liberation — as the fruit of fulfilling the injunction — be said to be attained? In the second alternative too — when it is taught that the true nature of the <s>jīva</s> is <s>Brahman</s> itself, which is by nature not subject to injunction, and that its <s>jīva</s>-status is created by <s>avidyā</s> alone — then, because of the absence of one who can be enjoined regarding <s>Brahman</s>, there is simply no injunction. The words 'should be seen' and such, found in the context of the higher knowledge, are primarily directed toward turning [the seeker] toward the truth — they are not primarily injunctions of the realization of truth. In ordinary life too, in expressions like 'see this!' 'listen to this!' — only attention is being directed; it is not being said 'produce knowledge itself.' For even when one is directed toward the object of knowledge, knowledge sometimes arises and sometimes does not. Therefore, one who wishes to make [another] know must show the object of knowledge. When that is shown, knowledge arises spontaneously, in accordance with the object and the means of knowledge. And it is not tenable that even an enjoined person would have different knowledge about a matter that is already established otherwise through another means of knowledge. If an enjoined person were to produce different knowledge [contrary to reality] — that would not be knowledge but a mental action. And if [such different knowledge] were to arise spontaneously, it would be mere error. But knowledge — being produced by a means of valid knowledge and having reality as its object — cannot be caused even by a hundred injunctions. Nor can it be prevented by a prohibition. For it is not dependent on a person; it is dependent on the reality itself. Therefore, from this too, there is no injunction. Moreover, if the teaching culminated solely in injunction, then the [teaching that] the <s>jīva</s> has the non-enjoinable <s>Brahman</s> as its Self — which is accepted [in the <s>Vedānta</s>] — would be without any valid authority. But if scripture both declares that the Self has the nature of non-enjoinable <s>Brahman</s> and also enjoins a person regarding its realization — then the one <s>Brahma</s>-scripture would have two objects and contradictory purports. And if the injunction-interpretation [is insisted upon], faults such as abandonment of what is heard, imagination of what is not heard, the invisible-fruit nature of liberation (like the fruit of <s>karma</s>), and the non-eternality [of liberation] — such faults cannot be resolved by anyone. Therefore, the <s>Brahman</s>-passages culminate in [pure] knowledge alone, not in injunction. And therefore, the [claim of] single-sentence reading based on 'apprehension of a single injunction' is unjustified. Even if injunction were accepted in the <s>Brahman</s>-passages, its unity with the [meditation] passages that teach with phenomenal elaboration and those that teach without cannot be established. For when different injunctions are apprehended through different statements and other means of knowledge, one cannot hold that there is a single injunction everywhere. In the <s>Prayāja</s> and <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> passages, unity is justified because of non-difference in the qualification-aspect. But here, in the <s>saguṇa</s> (with attributes) and <s>nirguṇa</s> (without attributes) injunctions, there is no aspect of qualification that would provide unity.

children.translated_text: Beginning with 'There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s> — the formed and the formless' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.1), having divided the five great elements into two groups, and having shown the forms — such as <s>Mahārajana</s> (great golden) and the like — of the <s>Puruṣa</s> described in the formed and the formless [groups], it then reads: 'Now the teaching: "not this, not this" (<s>neti neti</s>) — for there is nothing higher than this "not this"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6). Therein, we inquire: what is the object of this negation? For here, nothing specific is perceived as 'this particular thing is to be negated.' But by the word '<s>iti</s>' here, something to be negated is implied — since the use of the negative '<s>na</s>' follows after '<s>iti</s>.' And the word '<s>iti</s>' — which takes as its basis [what precedes it] and has the same function as the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus), taking a proximate referent — is seen to be used [in expressions such as:] 'thus indeed the teacher spoke' and the like. And what is proximate here — by the force of the context — is the twofold form of <s>Brahman</s> with its elaboration, and the <s>Brahman</s> to which these two forms belong. Therein, our doubt arises: does this negation negate both — the forms and that which possesses the forms? Or only one of them? And if only one, does it negate <s>Brahman</s> — leaving the forms as the remainder? Or does it negate the forms — leaving <s>Brahman</s> as the remainder? Therein, because both are equally the subject, we suspect that it negates both. And these two negations [correspond to] the double use of the word '<s>neti</s>.' By one, the form of <s>Brahman</s> with its elaboration is negated; by the other, the notion that <s>Brahman</s> has form arises. Or alternatively, <s>Brahman</s> itself — which has form — is negated. For that [<s>Brahman</s>], being beyond speech and mind, has its existence inconceivable, and is therefore fit for negation. But the phenomenal expansion of forms — being within the range of perception and other [means of knowledge] — is not fit for negation. And the repetition [of '<s>neti</s>'] is for emphasis. Having stated this [prima facie view], we say: first, the negation of both is not tenable — because of the consequence of the doctrine of the void (<s>śūnyavāda</s>). For something is negated [only] by taking recourse to some other ultimate reality — as snakes and the like in ropes and the like. And this is possible only when some positive entity remains [after the negation]. But in the negation of both, what other positive entity would remain? And if no other entity remains — that [very entity] whose negation is being attempted, being impossible to negate precisely because it is the ultimate reality, cannot [itself] be negated. Nor is the negation of <s>Brahman</s> tenable — because it would contradict the opening statement: 'Let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.1). Because it would contradict the censure: 'He becomes non-being; if one knows <s>Brahman</s> as non-being' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.6.1). Because it would contradict the determination: 'It is to be apprehended as "It is"' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 6.13). And because of the consequence of overturning all the <s>Vedānta</s> [texts].

children.translated_text: The transcendence of speech and mind taught regarding <s>Brahman</s> is not stated with the intention of [teaching <s>Brahman</s>'s] non-existence. For it would not be proper, having established <s>Brahman</s> in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts with great elaboration — 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the Supreme' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1), 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1) and such — to then declare the very same [<s>Brahman</s>'s] non-existence. For the maxim is: 'Rather than washing off mud, it is better not to touch it from afar.' But this [statement 'from which words turn back, not reaching it, together with the mind' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.4.1)] is a method of teaching [<s>Brahman</s>]. What is stated amounts to this: <s>Brahman</s> transcends speech and mind, does not fall within the domain of objects, is the inner Self, and is of the nature of eternal purity, consciousness, and freedom. Therefore, it must be accepted that [the negation 'not this, not this'] negates the elaboration of forms superimposed on <s>Brahman</s>, and thus [the residue] is <s>Brahman</s>. This is what is stated by [the <s>sūtra</s>] 'For it negates this much — which has been set forth in the context.' The form of <s>Brahman</s> that has been set forth in the context — this limited, delimited [form] characterized as formed and formless — that is what this word [<s>neti neti</s>] negates. For that which has been set forth and elaborated in the preceding section — both macrocosmically (<s>adhidaivata</s>) and microcosmically (<s>adhyātma</s>), and also the second form produced from that, characterized by impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), having the nature of the formless essence, denoted by the word '<s>Puruṣa</s>,' residing in the subtle body (<s>liṅgātman</s>), described through comparisons such as 'like saffron cloth' and the like. Because it is untenable that the formless-essence <s>Puruṣa</s> should be endowed with form perceivable by the eye. That very elaborate form of <s>Brahman</s> — it is understood — is brought face to face with the negating particle '<s>na</s>' (not) by means of the proximate referent [expressed by] '<s>iti</s>' (this). But <s>Brahman</s> was indicated in the preceding section through the genitive case as what the forms qualify — not as the primary subject itself. And when both forms belonging to it have been elaborated, this [passage] commences with the desire to know the true nature of the possessor of forms: 'Now, therefore, the teaching: not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6). Therein, it is determined that this is the revelation of <s>Brahman</s>'s true nature through the rejection of the superimposed forms. For this entire effect-world — which is the basis of those [forms] — is negated by 'not this, not this.' And it is proper that the effect — which is unreal, from [<s>sūtras</s> such as] 'being a mere name dependent on speech' and the like — should be negated by 'not this, not this,' but not <s>Brahman</s> [itself]. Because [the effect-world] is rooted in the imagination of effects. And the following doubt should not be entertained: 'How can scripture first present the twofold form and then negate it itself — [for] rather than washing off mud, it is better not to touch it from afar.' Because this scripture does not present <s>Brahman</s>'s twofold form as something to be established; rather, it takes up the twofold form well known in the world as superimposed on <s>Brahman</s>, for the purpose of negating it and establishing the true nature of pure <s>Brahman</s> — and this is unobjectionable. And these two negations negate both the formed and the formless, respectively, in accordance with the principle of sequential correspondence. Alternatively, the first negation negates the aggregate of [gross] elements; the second negates the aggregate of impressions. Or again, 'not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6) is a repetition (<s>vīpsā</s>), meaning: whatever is conceived — all that is 'not so.' For if the negation were specific [i.e., limited to enumerated items], one might wonder: 'If this is not <s>Brahman</s>, then what else could <s>Brahman</s> be?' But when [the negation] is by way of repetition, since the entire class of objects is negated, the inquiry 'what then is <s>Brahman</s>?' — regarding the non-objectifiable inner Self — is resolved. Therefore, the conclusion is that [<s>neti neti</s>] negates precisely the phenomenal world superimposed on <s>Brahman</s>, and [the residue] is <s>Brahman</s>. And this conclusion is [confirmed] for the following further reason: because after the negation, [the text] further says 'there is something higher' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6). For if the negation resulted in non-existence, who would say 'there is something higher'? Therein, the following arrangement of words [is possible]: Having indicated <s>Brahman</s> by 'not this, not this,' [the text] further explains that very teaching. What is the meaning of 'not this, not this'? The meaning is: There is nothing apart from this <s>Brahman</s> — and therefore it is said 'not this, not this'; not that [<s>Brahman</s>] itself does not exist. And [the text] shows this by [saying] 'there is something higher' — namely, the unnegated <s>Brahman</s>. When, however, the words are arranged as: 'There is nothing apart from this' — thus 'not this, not this' —

children.text:
nahi prapañcapratiṣedharūpādādeśanādanyatparādeśanaṃ brahmaṇo 'stīti /
tadā tato bravīti ca bhūya ityetannāmadheyaviṣayaṃ yojayitavyam /
atha nāmadheyam - 'satyasya satyamiti prāṇa vai satyaṃ teṣāmeṣa satyam' (bṛ. 2.1.20) iti hi bravītiti /
children.translated_text: Now the name [of <s>Brahman</s>]: 'The Real of the real — the <s>prāṇas</s> are indeed the real; of them, this [<s>Brahman</s>] is the Real' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.1.20) — for thus it says.

children.text: tacca brahmāvasāne pratiṣedhe samañjasaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: And this [name 'the Real of the real'] is coherent when the negation has <s>Brahman</s> as its terminus [i.e., when the negation leaves <s>Brahman</s> as the remainder].

children.text: abhāvāvasāne tu pratiṣedhe kiṃ satyasya satyamityucyeta /
children.translated_text: But if the negation had non-existence as its terminus, what sense would there be in saying 'the Real of the real'?

children.text: tasmādbrahmāvasāno 'yaṃ pratiṣedho nābhāvāvasāna ityadhyavasyāmaḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, we ascertain that this negation has <s>Brahman</s> as its terminus — not non-existence as its terminus. // 22 //

meaning: there is no teaching of <s>Brahman</s> other than the teaching in the form of the negation of the phenomenal world — then the statement 'further, it says' should be connected with the passage about the name [that follows].

children.text: FN: pṛthivyaptejorūpaṃ bhūtatrayaṃ mūrtaṃ, vāyvākāśarūpaṃ cāmūrtamiti dvirāśitvena /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The triad of elements — earth, water, and fire — is the 'formed' (<s>mūrta</s>); air and space are the 'formless' (<s>amūrta</s>) — thus in twofold classification.

children.text: mahārājanaṃ haridrā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mahārājana</s>' is turmeric.

children.text: tadavyaktamāha hi | BBs_3,2.23 |
children.translated_text: <s>Tadavyaktamāha hi</s> — That [<s>Brahman</s>] is unmanifest; for [the <s>śruti</s>] says so. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.23 |

children.text: yatpratiṣiddhātprapañcajātādanyatparaṃ brahma tadasti cetkasmānna gṛhyata iti /
children.translated_text: If there exists that higher <s>Brahman</s> which is other than the negated phenomenal world, why is it not perceived?

children.text: ucyate - tadavyaktamanindriyagrāhyaṃ sarvadṛśyasākṣitvāt /
children.translated_text: It is said: That [<s>Brahman</s>] is unmanifest — not graspable by the sense-organs — because it is the witness of all that is visible.

children.text: āha hyevaṃ śrutiḥ 'na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā nānyairdevaistapasā karmaṇā vā' (muṇḍa. 3.1.8) 'sa eṣa neti netyātmāgṛhyo nahi gṛhyate' (bṛ. 3.9.23) yattadadreśyamagrāhyam (muṇḍa. 1.1.6) 'yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnadṛśye 'nātmye 'nirukte 'nilayane' (tai. 2.7.1) ityādyā /
children.translated_text: For thus says the <s>śruti</s>: 'It is not grasped by the eye, nor by speech, nor by the other gods, nor by austerity, nor by action' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.8); 'This Self is [described as] "not this, not this" — ungraspable, for it is not grasped' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.26); 'That which is unseeable, ungraspable' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.6); 'When indeed one [finds rest] in that which is invisible, bodiless, inexpressible, without foundation' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7.1) — and such passages.

children.text: smṛtirapi - 'avyakto 'yamacintyo 'yamavikāryo 'yamucyate' (bha. gī. 2.25) ityādyā // 23 //
children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s> too: 'It is called unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchangeable' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 2.25) and such passages. // 23 //

children.text: api ca saṃrādhane pratyakṣānumānābhyām | BBs_3,2.24 |
children.translated_text: <s>Api ca saṃrādhane pratyakṣānumānābhyām</s> — Moreover, in [the state of] complete devotion, [this is established] from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.24 |

children.text:
apicainamātmānaṃ nirastasamastaprapañcamavyaktaṃ saṃrādhanakāle paśyanti yoginaḥ /
saṃrādhanaṃ ca bhaktidhyānapraṇidhānādyanuṣṭhānam /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate saṃrādhanakāle paśyantīti /
pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ śrutismṛtibhyāmityarthaḥ /
tathāhi śrutiḥ - 'parāñci khāni vyatṛṇatsvayaṃ bhūtasmātparāṅpaśyati nāntarātman /
kaściddhīraḥ pratyagātmānamaikṣadāvṛttacakṣuramṛtatvamicchan' (ka. 4.1) iti /
children.translated_text: some wise one, desiring immortality, turned his gaze inward and saw the inner Self' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 4.1).

children.text: 'jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattvastatastu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ' (mu. 3.1.8) iti caivamādyā /
children.translated_text: 'Through the serenity of knowledge, with purified being (<s>sattva</s>), he then sees that partless [<s>Brahman</s>] while meditating' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.8) — and such passages.

children.text: smṛtirapi - 'yaṃ vinidrā jitaśvāsāḥ saṃtuṣṭāḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s> too: 'Those who are free from drowsiness, who have conquered their breath, who are content, who have restrained their senses —

children.text: jyotiḥ paśyanti yuñjānāstasmai yogātmane namaḥ //
children.translated_text: the yogins who are concentrated see the light; salutation to that <s>yoga</s>-Self!

Moreover, this Self — from which all phenomenal elaboration has been removed, [which is] unmanifest — <s>yogins</s> see at the time of complete devotion (<s>saṃrādhana</s>). And <s>saṃrādhana</s> is the practice of devotion, meditation, concentration, and the like. But how is it known that they see [it] at the time of <s>saṃrādhana</s>? From <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct testimony, i.e., <s>śruti</s>) and <s>anumāna</s> (inferential testimony, i.e., <s>smṛti</s>) — the meaning is: from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. For thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'The Self-born One pierced the openings [of the senses] outward — therefore one sees outward, not the inner Self;

children.text: yoginastaṃ prapaśyanti bhagavantaṃ sanātanam' iti caivamādyā // 24 //
children.translated_text: The yogins perceive that eternal Lord' — and such passages. // 24 //

children.text:
FN: svayaṃbhūrīśvaraḥ khānīndriyāṇi parāñci anātmagrāhakāṇi kṛtvā vyatṛmat nāsitavān /
āvṛttacakṣurniruddhendriyaḥ /
vinidrā vitamaskāḥ /
yuñjānaḥ dhyāyinaḥ /
yogalabhya ātmāyogātmā /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The Self-born Lord pierced (<s>vyatṛṇat</s>) — that is, created — the openings, i.e., the sense-organs, as outward-facing, not grasping the non-Self [sic: not grasping the inner Self]. '<s>Āvṛttacakṣuḥ</s>' means one whose sense-organs are restrained. '<s>Vinidrāḥ</s>' means free from <s>tamas</s> (inertia). '<s>Yuñjānāḥ</s>' means meditators. '<s>Yogātman</s>' — the Self attainable through <s>yoga</s>.

children.text:
nanu saṃrādhyasaṃrādhakabhāvābhyupagamātparetarātmanoranyatvaṃ syāditi /
netyucyate -
children.translated_text: Objection: By accepting the relationship of the one to be propitiated and the propitiant, a difference between the individual Self and the Supreme Self would follow. To this it is said: No —

children.text: prakāśādivaccāvaiśeṣyaṃ prakāśaś ca karmaṇyabhyāsāt | BBs_3,2.25 |
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśādivaccāvaiśeṣyaṃ prakāśaśca karmaṇyabhyāsāt</s> — The non-difference [of the <s>jīva</s> from <s>Brahman</s>] is like [that of] light and the like [from their source]; and the [teaching of their] distinctness [is] in the context of action, because of repetition. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.25 |

children.text: yathā prakāśākāśasavitṛprabhṛtayo 'ṅgulikarakodakaprabhṛtiṣu karmasūpādhibhūteṣu saviśeṣā ivāvabhāsante, naca svābhāvikīmaviśeṣātmatāṃ jahati, evamupādhinimitta evāyamātmabhedaḥ svatatvaikātmyameva /
children.translated_text: Just as light, space, the sun, and the like — though appearing differentiated in [their association with] actions that serve as <s>upādhis</s>, such as fingers, rooms, water-vessels, and the like — do not abandon their natural undifferentiated nature; so too, this difference of the Self is merely caused by <s>upādhis</s> — in its own true nature, there is oneness alone.

children.text: tathāhi - vedānteṣvabhyāsenāsakṛjjīvaprājñayorabhedaḥ pratipādyate // 25 //
children.translated_text: For thus — in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, the non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Prājña</s> (<s>Brahman</s>) is taught repeatedly. // 25 //

children.text: ato 'nantena tathā hi liṅgam | BBs_3,2.26 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ato 'nantena tathā hi liṅgam</s> — Therefore, [the <s>jīva</s> attains identity] with the infinite [<s>Brahman</s>]; for thus is the indication. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.26 |

children.text: ataśca svābhāvikatvādabhedasyāvidyākṛtatvācca bhedasya vidyayāvidyāṃ vidhūya jīvaḥ pareṇānantena prājñenātmanekatāṃ gacchati /
children.translated_text: And therefore, since non-difference is natural and difference is produced by <s>avidyā</s>, the <s>jīva</s> — having dispelled <s>avidyā</s> through knowledge — attains oneness of Self with the infinite <s>Prājña</s> (<s>Brahman</s>).

children.text: tathāhi liṅgam - 'sa yo ha vai tatparamaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' (mu. 3.2.9) 'brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti' (bṛ. 4.4.6) ityādi // 26 //
children.translated_text: For thus is the indication [in <s>śruti</s>]: 'He who knows that supreme <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.9), 'Being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges in <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6) — and the like. // 26 //

children.text: ubhayavyapadeśāttvahikuṇḍalavat | BBs_3,2.27 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ubhayavyapadeśāttvahikuṇḍalavat</s> — But because of the designation of both [difference and non-difference], [the relationship is] like a snake and its coils. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.27 |

children.text:
tasminneva saṃrādhyasaṃrādhakabhāve matāntaramupanyasyati svamataviśuddhaye /
kvacijjīvaprājñayorbhedo vyapadiśyate 'tatastu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ' (muṇḍa. 3.1.8) iti dhyātṛdhyātavyatvena draṣṭṛdraṣṭavyatvena ca /
parātparaṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam (mu. 3.2.8) iti gantṛgantavyatvena /
kvacittu tayorevābhedo vyapadiśyate 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' (bṛ. 1.4.10) 'eṣa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ' (bṛ. 3.4.1) 'eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ' (bṛ. 3.7.3) iti /
children.translated_text: But in some places, the non-difference of those very two is designated: 'That you are' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10), 'This is your Self, the inner [controller] of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1), 'This is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.3).

children.text: tatraivamubhayavyapadeśe sati yadyabheda evaikāntato gṛhyate bhedavyapadeśo nirālambana eva syāt /
children.translated_text: Now, given this twofold designation, if non-difference alone were exclusively accepted, the designation of difference would be left without any basis.

children.text: ata ubhayavyapadeśadarśanādahikuṇḍalavadatra tattvaṃ bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from observing the twofold designation, the truth here should be like [the relationship of] a snake and its coils.

children.text: yathāhirityabhedaḥ kuṇḍalābhogaprāṃśutvādīnīti tu bheda evamihāpīti // 27 //
children.translated_text: Just as [the word] 'snake' [expresses] non-difference, while the coiled shape, length, and such [express] difference — so too here. // 27 //

Regarding that very relationship of the one to be propitiated and the propitiant, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] presents an alternative view for the purpose of refining his own position. In some places, a difference between the <s>jīva</s> and <s>Prājña</s> is designated — 'Then he sees that partless [<s>Brahman</s>] while meditating' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.8) — as meditator and object of meditation, as seer and object to be seen; 'He attains the divine <s>Puruṣa</s> beyond the beyond' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.8) — as goer and destination.

children.text: prakāśāśrayavadvā tejastvāt | BBs_3,2.28 |
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśāśrayavadvā tejastvāt</s> — Or, [it is] like light and its substratum, because of their common luminosity. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.28 |

children.text: athavā prakāśāśrayavadetatpratipattavyam /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, this should be understood as [the relationship of] light and its substratum.

children.text: yathā prakāśaḥ savitrastadāśrayaśca savitā nātyantabhinnāvubhayorapi tejastvāviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text: Just as the light of the sun and the sun — its substratum — are not absolutely different, because of the non-difference in luminosity of both,

children.text: atha ca bhedavyapadeśabhājau bhavata evamihāpīti // 28 //
children.translated_text: and yet they do admit of the designation of difference — so too here. // 28 //

children.text: pūrvavadvā | BBs_3,2.29 |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrvavadvā</s> — Or, as [stated] before. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.29 |

children.text: yathā vā pūrvamupanyastaṃ prakāśādivaccāvaiśeṣyamiti tathaivaitadbhavitumarhati /
tathāhyavidyākṛtatvādbandhasya vidyayā mokṣa upapadyate /
children.translated_text: For thus, since bondage is produced by <s>avidyā</s>, liberation through knowledge is proper.

children.text: yadi punaḥ paramārthata eva baddhaḥ kaścidātmāhikuṇḍalanyāyena parasyātmanaḥ saṃsthānabhūtaḥ prakāśāśrayanyāyena caikadeśabhūto 'bhyupagamyeta tataḥ pāramārthikasya bandhasya tiraskartumaśakyatvānmokṣaśāstravoyarthyaṃ prasajyeta, nacātrobhāvapi bhedābhedau śrutistulyavadvyapadiśati /
children.translated_text: But if some Self were accepted as truly bound — as a configuration of the Supreme Self, according to the snake-coil analogy, or as a part [of the Supreme Self], according to the light-substratum analogy — then, since real bondage cannot be removed, the futility of the scripture of liberation would follow. And scripture does not designate both difference and non-difference here with equal weight.

children.text: abhedameva hi pratipādyatvena nirdiśati bhedaṃ tu pūrvaprasiddhamevānuvadatyarthāntaravivakṣayā /
children.translated_text: Rather, it presents non-difference as what is to be established, while merely restating the previously well-known difference for the purpose of conveying another meaning [i.e., for practical instruction].

children.text: tasmātprakāśādivaccāvaiśeṣyamityeṣa eva siddhāntaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'The non-difference is like light and the like' — this alone is the established conclusion. // 29 //
Or, just as was previously stated — 'The non-difference [is] like light and the like' [<s>BBs</s> 3.2.25] — so too should this be understood.

children.text: pratiṣedhāc ca | BBs_3,2.30 |
children.translated_text: <s>Pratiṣedhāc ca</s> — And because of the negation [of anything other than <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.30 |

children.text: ataścaiṣa eva siddhāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for this further reason, this alone is the established conclusion.

children.text: yatkāraṇaṃ parasmādātmano 'nyaṃ cetanaṃ pratiṣedhati śāstram - 'nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā' (bṛ. 3.7.23) ityevamādi /
children.translated_text: Because scripture negates any conscious entity other than the Supreme Self: 'There is no other seer than this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.23) — and such passages.

children.text: atāta ādeśo neti neti (bṛ. 2.3.6) tadetadbrahmāpūrvamanaparamanantaramabāhyam (bṛ. 2.5.19) iti ca brahmavyatiriktaprapañcanirākaraṇādbrahmamātrapariśeṣāccaiva eva siddhānta iti gamyate // 30 //
children.translated_text: And from 'Now, therefore, the teaching: not this, not this' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.3.6) and 'This <s>Brahman</s> is without a prior, without a posterior, without an interior, without an exterior' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19) — because of the negation of the phenomenal world other than <s>Brahman</s>, and because of the residue being <s>Brahman</s> alone — this alone is the established conclusion, it is understood. // 30 //

children.text: 7 parādhikaraṇam / sū. 31-37
children.translated_text: Section 7: <s>Parādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 31-37

children.text: paramataḥ setūnmānasaṃbandhabhedavyapadeśebhyaḥ | BBs_3,2.31 |
children.translated_text: <s>Paramataḥ setūnmānasaṃbandhabhedavyapadeśebhyaḥ</s> — The Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] is higher [than the <s>jīva</s>], because of the designations of bridge, measure, connection, and difference. | <s>BBs</s> 3.2.31 |

children.text:
yadetannirastasamastaprapañcaṃ brahma nirdharitamasmātparamanyattattvamasti nāstīti śrutivipratipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ /
kāniciddhi vākyānyāpātenaiva pratibhāsamānāni brahmaṇo 'pi paramanyattattvaṃ pratipādayantīva /
teṣāṃ hi parihāramabhidhātumayamupakramaḥ kriyate /
paramato brahmaṇo 'nyattattvaṃ bhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ - setuvyapadeśādunmānavyapadeśātsaṃbandhavyapadeśādbhedavyapadeśācceti /
setuvyapadeśastāvat - 'atha ya ātmā sa seturvidhṛtiḥ' (chā. 8.4.1) ityātmaśabdābhihitasya brahmaṇaḥ setuttavaṃ saṃkīrtayati /
setuśabdaśca hi loke jalasaṃtānavicchedakare mṛddārvādipracaye prasiddhaḥ /
iha tu setuśabda ātmani prayukta iti laukikasetorivātmasetoranyasya vastuno 'stitvaṃ gamayati /
'setuṃ tīrtvā' (chā. 8.4.2) iti ca taratiśabdaprayogāt /
yathā laukikaṃ setuṃ tīrtvā jāṅgalamasetuṃ prāpnotyevamātmānaṃ setuṃ tīrtvānātmānamasetuṃ prāpnotīti gamyate /
unmānavyapadeśaśca bhavati 'tadetadbrahma catuṣpādaṣṭāśaphaṃ ṣoḍaśakalami'ti /
yacca loke unmitametāvadidamiti pariccinnaṃ kārṣāpaṇādi tato 'nyadvastvastīti prasiddham /
tathā brahmaṇo 'pyunmānāttato 'nyena vastunā bhavitavyamiti gamyate /
tathā saṃbandhavyapadeśo 'pi bhavati - 'satā somya tadā saṃpanno bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti 'śārīra ātmā' (tai. 2.3.1) 'prājñenātmanā saṃpariṣvaktaḥ' (bṛ. 4.3.21) iti ca /
mitānāṃ ca mitena saṃndho dṛṣṭo yathā narāṇāṃ nagareṇa /
jīvānāṃ ca brahmaṇā saṃbandhaṃ vyapadiśati suṣuptau /
atastataḥ paramanyadamitamastīti gamyate /
bhedavyapadeśaścaitamevārthaṃ gamayati /
tathāhi - 'atha ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā.
children.translated_text:
This <s>Brahman</s> — from which all phenomenal multiplicity has been negated — has been ascertained. Whether any other reality exists beyond It or not — this doubt arises from the conflict among <s>śruti</s> passages.
For some statements, as they appear at first glance, seem to teach that there is another reality beyond <s>Brahman</s>.
To provide a resolution of those [statements], this section is undertaken.
There could be another reality beyond <s>Brahman</s>.
Why? Because of the designation as a bridge (<s>setu</s>), because of the designation of measure (<s>unmāna</s>), because of the designation of relation (<s>saṃbandha</s>), and because of the designation of difference (<s>bheda</s>).
First, the designation as a bridge: 'Now, this Self is the bridge (<s>setu</s>), the support' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.1) — [this passage] declares the bridge-hood of <s>Brahman</s>, which is denoted by the word 'Self.'
And the word '<s>setu</s>' (bridge) is well known in the world as referring to an accumulation of earth, wood, and the like that cuts across the continuity of water.
But here the word '<s>setu</s>' is applied to the Self — hence, just as a worldly bridge [implies the existence of land] on the other side, so too the Self-as-bridge implies the existence of another entity [beyond it].
And because of the use of the verb '<s>tarati</s>' (crosses) in 'Having crossed the bridge' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.2).
Just as one who crosses a worldly bridge reaches the dry land beyond the bridge — so too, one who crosses the Self-as-bridge reaches the non-Self beyond the bridge — this is what is implied.
And the designation of measure: '<s>Brahman</s> has four feet, eight hooves, sixteen parts' — and so on.
And whatever in the world is measured as 'this much is this' — being delimited, like a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin) — it is well known that another entity exists beyond it.
Likewise, from the measurement of <s>Brahman</s> too, there must be another entity beyond It — this is what is implied.
Also, the designation of relation: 'He becomes merged with <s>Sat</s>, O dear one' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1); 'The embodied Self' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.3.1); 'Embraced by the all-knowing Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.21) — and the like.
And a relation between things that are [both] delimited is observed — as of persons with a city.
And [the <s>śruti</s>] designates a relation of the <s>jīvas</s> with <s>Brahman</s> in deep sleep.
From this, it is implied that there is another, unlimited [entity] beyond That.
And the designation of difference too implies this very meaning.
For thus: 'Now, the golden person who is seen within the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s>

children.text:
1.6.6) ityādityādhāramīśvaraṃ vyapadiśyatato bhedenākṣyādhāramīśvaraṃ vyapadiśati - 'atha ya eṣo 'ntikṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā. 1.7.5) iti /
atideśaṃ cāsyāmunā rūpādiṣu karoti - 'tasyaitasya tadeva rūpaṃ yadamuṣya rūpaṃ yāvamuṣya geṣṇau yannāma tannāma' (chā. 1.7.5)
children.translated_text:
1.6.6) — having designated the Lord as abiding in the sun, [the <s>śruti</s>] then, as different [from that], designates the Lord as abiding in the eye: 'Now, the person who is seen within the eye' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.5).
And it applies to the latter the form and other [attributes] of the former by extension (<s>atideśa</s>): 'Of this one, that alone is the form which is the form of the other; the chant (<s>geṣṇau</s>) of the other is the name of this one; the name [of the other is the name of this one]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.5).

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: sāvadhikaṃ ceśvaratvamubhayorvyapadiśati - 'ye cāmuṣmātparāñco lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe devakāmānāṃ ca' (chā. 1.6.8) ityekasya /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] designates bounded lordship for each of the two: 'The worlds beyond this one and the desires of the <s>devas</s> — he controls them' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.8) — for the one;

children.text: 'ye caitasmādarvāñco lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyakāmānāṃ ca' (chā. 1.7.6) ityekasya /
children.translated_text: 'The worlds on this side and the desires of men — he controls them' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.6) — for the other.

children.text: yathedaṃ māgadhasya rājyamidaṃ vaidehasyeti // 31 //
children.translated_text: Just as [one says]: 'This is the kingdom of the king of <s>Magadha</s>; this is [the kingdom] of the [king] of <s>Videha</s>.' // 31 //

children.text: FN: vātapracuro deśo jāṅgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: A region abounding in wind is called '<s>jāṅgala</s>' (arid land).

children.text: evametebhyaḥ setvādivyapadeśebhyo brahmaṇaḥ paramastītyevaṃ prāpte pratipādyate -
children.translated_text: Thus, having set forth [the prima facie view] that there is [something] beyond <s>Brahman</s> — based on these designations of bridge and the like — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] responds:

children.text: sāmānyāt tu | BBs_3,2.32 |
children.translated_text: But because of the common feature [of supporting]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.32 |

children.text:
tuśabdena pradarśitāṃ prāptiṃ niruṇaddhi /
na brahmaṇo 'nyatkiñcidbhavitumarhati pramāṇābhāvāt /
nahyanyasyāstitve kiñcitpramāṇamupalabhāmahe /
sarvasya hi janimato vastujātasya janmādi brahmaṇo bhavatīti nirdhāritam /
ananyatvaṃ ca kāraṇātkāryasya /
'naca brahmavyatiriktaṃ kiñcidajaṃ saṃbhavati sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1) ityavadhāraṇāt /
ekavijñānena ca sarvavijñānapratijñānānna brahmavyatiriktavastvastitvamavakalpate /
children.translated_text:
By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] blocks the stated prima facie view.
Nothing else can exist beyond <s>Brahman</s>, because of the absence of a means of knowledge [for it].
For we do not find any means of knowledge for the existence of another [entity].
For it has been ascertained that the origination and such of all things that have come into being proceeds from <s>Brahman</s>.
And the non-difference of the effect from the cause [has been established].
And nothing unborn that is different from <s>Brahman</s> is possible — because of the definitive statement: 'Being alone, O dear one, was this in the beginning — one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1).
And because of the promise that through the knowledge of one, everything is known — the existence of an entity distinct from <s>Brahman</s> is not tenable.

children.text: nu setvādivyapadeśā brahmavyatiriktaṃ tattvaṃ sūcayantītyuktam /
children.translated_text: Now, it has been said that the designations of bridge and the like indicate a reality distinct from <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
netyucyate /
setuvyapadeśastāvanna brahmaṇo bāhyasya sadbhāvaṃ pratipādayituṃ kṣamate /
seturātmeti hyāha na tataḥ paramastīti /
tatra parasminnasati setutvaṃ nāvakalpata iti paraṃ kimapi kalpyeta /
nacaitannyāyyaṃ /
ajatvādiśrutivirodhāt /
setusāmānyāttu setuśabda ātmani prayukta iti ś liṣyate /
jagatastanmaryādānāṃ ca vidhārakatvaṃ setusāmānyamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The common feature between the Self and a bridge is the function of upholding the world and its boundaries.

children.text: ataḥ seturiva seturiti prakṛta ātmā stūyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [it means:] the Self under discussion is praised as 'a bridge, as it were' — [that is,] like a bridge.

children.text: setuṃ tīrtvetyapi tarateratikramāsaṃbhavātprāpnotyartha eva vartate /
children.translated_text: And 'having crossed the bridge' (<s>setuṃ tīrtvā</s>) — since it is impossible for the verb '<s>tarati</s>' to mean 'crossing over,' it has the meaning of 'attaining.'

children.text: yathā vyākaraṇaṃ tīrṇa iti prāpta idamucyate nātikrāntastadvat // 32 //
children.translated_text: Just as [when one says] 'he has crossed (<s>tīrṇa</s>) grammar,' the meaning is 'he has mastered [it]' — not 'he has gone beyond it.' Similarly here. // 32 //

We reply: No.
First, the designation as a bridge is not capable of establishing the existence of [something] external to <s>Brahman</s>.
For [the <s>śruti</s>] says 'the bridge is the Self' — not 'beyond it there is [something else].'
If [one were to argue:] without [something] beyond, bridge-hood would not be tenable — and therefore some further [entity] should be postulated;
[we say:] This is not proper.
Because it would contradict <s>śrutis</s> [stating <s>Brahman</s>'s] unborn nature and the like.
Rather, the word '<s>setu</s>' is applied to the Self because of the common feature of supporting (<s>sāmānya</s>) — this is the connection.

children.text: buddhyarthaḥ pādavat | BBs_3,2.33 |
children.translated_text: [The designation of measure] is for the purpose of meditation, as with the 'feet' [of <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.33 |

children.text:
yadapyuktamunmānavyapadeśādasti paramiti, tatrābhidhīyate - unmānavyapadeśo 'pi na brahmavyatiriktavastvastitvapratipattyarthaḥ /
kimarthastarhi buddhyarthaḥ, upāsanārtha iti yāvat /
children.translated_text:
As for the objection that there is [something] beyond [<s>Brahman</s>] because of the designation of measure — to that we say: The designation of measure too is not for the purpose of establishing the existence of an entity distinct from <s>Brahman</s>.
For what purpose then? For the purpose of meditation (<s>buddhi</s>) — that is to say, for the purpose of <s>upāsanā</s> (contemplation).

children.text:
catuṣpādaṣṭāśaphaṃ ṣoḍaśakalamityevaṃrūpā buddhiḥ kataṃ nu nāma brahmaṇi sthirā syāditi vikāradvāreṇa brahmaṇa unmānakalpanaiva kriyate /
nahyavikāre 'nante brahmaṇi sarvaiḥ puṃbhiḥ śakyā bujaddhiḥ sthāpayituṃ mandamadhyamottamabuddhitvātpuṃsāmiti /
pādavat /
children.translated_text: As with the 'feet' [of <s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: yathā mana ākāśayoradhyātmamadhidaivataṃ ca brahmapratīkayorāmnātayoścatvāro vāgādayo manaḥsaṃbandhinaḥ pādāḥ kalpyante catvāraścāgnyādaya ākāśasaṃbandhinaḥ ādhyānāya tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as, for the inner and outer aspects of mind and space — which are taught as symbols (<s>pratīka</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> — four feet such as speech and the like are devised as related to mind, and four [feet] such as fire and the like as related to space, for the purpose of meditation — similarly [here].

children.text: athavā pādavaditi yathā kārṣāpaṇe pādavibhāgo vyavahāraprācuryāya kalpyate /
children.translated_text: Or, 'as with the feet' means: just as in a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin), a division into quarter-parts is devised for the sake of facilitating commercial transactions.

children.text: nahi sakalenaiva kārṣāpaṇena sarvadā sarve janā vyavahartumīśate krayavikraye parimāṇāniyamāttadvadityarthaḥ // 33 //
children.translated_text: For not all people at all times are able to transact with just the whole <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>, because of the lack of a fixed limit in the measures of buying and selling — this is the meaning. // 33 //

The measurement-attribution to <s>Brahman</s> in the form of 'four-footed, eight-hooved, sixteen-parted' is devised through [the medium of] modifications, [asking:] 'How indeed might the intellect become steadily fixed on <s>Brahman</s>?'
For it is not possible for all persons to fix their intellect on <s>Brahman</s>, which is without modification and infinite — because persons are of dull, middling, and sharp intellects.

children.text: FN: brahmaṇa unmānakalpanaṃ mandadhiyāṃ dhyānavyavahārāya kārṣāpamasya pādavyavahārāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The measurement-attribution to <s>Brahman</s> is for facilitating the meditation-practice of those of dull intellect — as the quarter-transaction of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> [facilitates trade].

children.text: sthānaviśeṣātprakāśādivat | BBs_3,2.34 |
children.translated_text: Because of particular location, like light and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.34 |

children.text:
iha sūtre dvayorapi saṃbandhabhedavyadeśayoḥ parihāro vidīyate /
yadapyuktaṃ saṃbandhavyapadeśādbhedavyapadeśācca paramataḥ syāditi tadapyasat /
yata ekasyāpi sthānaviśeṣāpekṣayaitau vyapadeśāvupapadyate /
saṃbandhavyapadeśe tāvadayamarthaḥ /
buddyādyupādhisthānaviśeṣayogādudbhūtasya viśeṣavijñānasyopādyupaśame ya upaśamaḥ sa paramātmanā samabandha ityupādhyapekṣayaivopacaryate na parimititvāpekṣayā /
children.translated_text: The subsidence of specific cognition — which had arisen through the particular location of <s>upādhis</s> such as the intellect and the like, and which [now] subsides with the subsidence of the <s>upādhis</s> — that is figuratively spoken of as a 'relation' with the supreme Self, with reference to the <s>upādhis</s> alone — not with reference to [<s>Brahman</s>'s] delimitedness.

children.text: tathā bhedavyapadeśo 'pi brahmaṇa upādhibhedāpekṣayopacaryate na svarūpabhedāpekṣayā prakāśādivadityupamopādānāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the designation of difference too is figuratively applied to <s>Brahman</s> with reference to the difference of <s>upādhis</s> — not with reference to a difference in its own nature — as [indicated by] the adoption of the simile 'like light and the like.'

children.text: yathaikasya prakāśasya sauryasya cāndramasasya vopādhiyogādupajātaviśeṣasyopādhyupaśamātsaṃbandhavyapadeśo bhavatyupādhibhedācca bhedavyapadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as for a single light — whether solar or lunar — which has acquired specific features through the association with <s>upādhis</s>, there is a designation of 'relation' through the subsidence of the <s>upādhis</s>, and a designation of 'difference' through the difference of <s>upādhis</s>;

children.text: yathāvā sūcīpāśākāśādiṣūpādhyapekṣayaivaitau saṃbandhabhedavyapadeśau bhavatastadvat // 34 //
children.translated_text: or just as, in the case of the space within a needle, a cup, and the like, these two designations — of relation and of difference — are made only with reference to the <s>upādhis</s> — similarly here. // 34 //

In this <s>sūtra</s>, the resolution of both designations — of relation and of difference — is provided.
As for the objection that there must be [something] beyond because of the designation of relation and the designation of difference — that too is incorrect.
Because these two designations are tenable with reference to the particular location [of <s>upādhis</s>], even for a single [entity].
First, regarding the designation of relation, the meaning is this:

children.text: upapatteś ca | BBs_3,2.35 |
children.translated_text: And because of reasonableness. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.35 |

children.text:
upapadyate cātredṛśa eva saṃbandho nānyādṛśaḥ 'svamapīto bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) iti hi svarūpasaṃbandhamenamāmananti svarūpasya cānapāyitvāt /
na naranagaranyāyena saṃbandho ghaṭate /
upādhikṛtasvarūpatirobhāvāttu - 'svamapīto bhavati' (chā. 6.8.1) ityupapadyate /
children.translated_text: But because of the concealment of one's true nature caused by <s>upādhis</s>, the statement 'He reaches his own' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1) is tenable.

children.text: tathā bhedo 'pi nānyādṛśaḥ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, difference of any other kind too is not possible.

children.text: bahutaraśrutiprasiddhaikeśvaratvavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: Because it would contradict the well-established unity of the Lord [taught] in numerous <s>śrutis</s>.

children.text: tathāca śrutirekasyāpyākāśasya stānakṛtaṃ bhedavyapadeśamupapādayati - 'yo 'yaṃ bahirdhā puruṣādākāśaḥ' (chā. 3.12.8), 'yo 'yamantarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ' (chā. 3.12.9) iti // 35 //
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s> demonstrates a location-based designation of difference even for the single space: 'The space that is outside the person' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.8); 'The space that is within the heart' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.9). // 35 //

And in this context, only such a relation is reasonable — not one of any other kind. 'He reaches his own' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1) — for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches this as a relation with one's own nature, and one's own nature is never lost.
A relation after the manner of persons and cities is not fitting [here].

children.text: tathānyapratiṣedhāt | BBs_3,2.36 |
children.translated_text: And because of the negation of the other. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.36 |

children.text: evaṃ setvādivyapadeśānparapakṣahetūnunmathya saṃprati svapakṣaṃ hetvāntareṇopasaṃharati /
children.translated_text: Having thus refuted the prima facie arguments based on the designations of bridge and the like, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] now concludes his own position with a further argument.

children.text: tathānyapratiṣedhāpi na brahmaṇaḥ paraṃ vastvantaramastīti gamyate /
children.translated_text: And because of the negation of the other, it is understood that no other entity exists beyond <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tathāhi - sa evādhastāt (chā. 7.25.1), ahamevādhastāt (chā. 7.25.1), ātmaivādhastāt (chā. 7.25.2), sarvaṃ taṃ parādādyo 'nyatrātmanaḥ sarvaṃ veda (bṛ. 2.4.6), brahmaivedaṃ sarvam ātmaivedaṃ sarvam (chā. 7.25.2), neha nānāsti kiñcana (bṛ. 4.4.1), yasmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiñcit (śve. 3.9), tadetadbrahmāpūrvamanaparamanantaramabāhyam (bṛ. 2.5.19) ityevamādivākyāni svaprakaraṇastānyanyārthatvena pariṇetumaśakyāni brahmavyatiriktaṃ vastvantaraṃ vārayanti /
children.translated_text: For thus: 'He alone is below' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.1); 'I alone am below' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.1); 'The Self alone is below' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2); 'Everything abandons him who knows everything as other than the Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6); '<s>Brahman</s> indeed is all this'; 'The Self indeed is all this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2); 'There is no diversity here whatsoever' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.19); 'Than which there is nothing higher, nothing smaller' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.9); 'This is <s>Brahman</s> — without prior, without posterior, without interior, without exterior' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.5.19) — such passages, being situated in their own contexts and incapable of being construed to a different meaning, negate any entity other than <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: sarvāntaraśruteśca na paramātmano 'nyo 'ntarātmāstītyavadhāryate // 36 //
children.translated_text: And from the <s>śruti</s> on [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the innermost of all, it is ascertained that there is no inner Self other than the supreme Self. // 36 //

children.text: anena sarvagatatvamāyāmaśabdādibhyaḥ | BBs_3,2.37 |
children.translated_text: By this [refutation], the all-pervasiveness [of <s>Brahman</s> is established] — from the words [denoting] measure (<s>āyāma</s>) and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.37 |

children.text:
anena setvādivyapadeśanirākaraṇenānyapratiṣedhasamāśrayaṇena ca sarvagatatvamapyātmanaḥ siddhaṃ bhavati /
anyathā hi tanna siddyet /
setvādivyapadeśeṣu hi mukhyeṣvaṅgīkriyamāṇeṣu pariccheda ātmanaḥ prasajyeta setvādīnāmevātmakatvāt /
children.translated_text:
By this refutation of the designations of bridge and the like, and by recourse to the negation of the other, the all-pervasiveness of the Self too is established.
For otherwise, it would not be established.
For if the designations of bridge and the like were accepted in their primary sense, delimitation of the Self would follow — since the bridges and the like would [themselves] constitute the Self.

children.text: tathānyapratiṣedhe 'pyasati vastu vastvantarādvyāvartata iti pariccheda evātmanaḥ prasajyeta /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the absence of the negation of the other, an entity [being] differentiated from another entity would result in the delimitation of the Self.

children.text: sarvagatatvaṃ cāsyāyāmaśabdādibhyo vijñāyate /
children.translated_text: And the all-pervasiveness of the [Self] is known from words denoting measure (<s>āyāma</s>) and the like.

children.text: āyāmaśabdo vyāptivacanaḥ śabdaḥ 'yāvānvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ' (chā. 8.1.3) 'ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ' 'jyāyāndivaḥ' (chā. 3.14.3) 'jyāyānākāśāt' 'nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ' (bha.gī. 2.24)ityevamādayo hi śrutismṛtinyāyāḥ sarvagatatvamātmano 'vabodhayanti // 37 //
children.translated_text: The word '<s>āyāma</s>' means a word denoting extension (pervasion): 'As far as this space extends, so far extends this space within the heart' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.3); 'All-pervading like space and eternal'; 'Greater than the sky' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.3); 'Greater than space'; 'Eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable, everlasting' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 2.24) — for these and similar <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and reasoning passages make known the all-pervasiveness of the Self. // 37 //

children.text: 7 phalādhikaraṇam / sū. 38-41
children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Phalādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Fruit). <s>Sūtras</s> 38-41.

children.text: phalamata upapatteḥ | BBs_3,2.38 |
children.translated_text: The fruit [of actions proceeds] from That [<s>Brahman</s>] — because of reasonableness. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.38 |

children.text: tasyaiva brahmaṇo vyāvahārikyāmīśitrīśitavyavibhāgāvasthāyāmayamanyaḥ svabhāvo varṇyate /
children.translated_text: Another characteristic of that very <s>Brahman</s> — in the transactional state [consisting] of the division into ruler and ruled — is now described.

children.text:
yadtadiṣṭāniṣṭavyāmiśralakṣaṇaṃ karmaphalaṃ saṃsāragocaraṃ trividhaṃ prasiddhaṃ jantūnāṃ kimetatkarmaṇo bhavatyāhosvidīśvarāditi bhavati vicāraṇā /
tatra tāvatpratipādyate phalamata īśvarādbavitumarhati /
kutaḥ - upapatteḥ /
sa hi sarvādhyakṣaḥ sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārānvicitrānvidadhaddeśakālaviśeṣābhijñatvātkarmiṇāṃ karmānurūpaṃ phalaṃ saṃpādayatītyupapadyate /
karmaṇāstvanukṣaṇavināśinaḥ kālāntarabhāvi phalaṃ bhavatītyanupapannam /
abhāvāddhāvānutpatteḥ /
syādetat /
karma vinaśyatsvakālameva svānurūpaṃ phalaṃ janayitvā vinaśyati tatphalaṃ kālāntaritaṃ kartrā bhokṣyata iti /
tadapi na pariśudhyati prāgbhoktṛsaṃbandhātphalatvānupapatteḥ /
yatkālaṃ hi yatsukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vātmanā bhujyate tasyaiva loke phalatvaṃ prasiddham /
nahyasaṃbaddhasyātmanā sukhasya duḥkhasya vā phalatvaṃ pratiyanti laukikāḥ /
athocyate mā bhūtkarmānantaraṃ phalotpādaḥ /
karmakāryādapūrvātphalamutpatsyata iti /
tadapi nopapadyate /
apūrvasyācetanasya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamasya cetanenāprartitasya pravṛttyanupapatteḥ /
tadastitve ca pramāṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text:
The well-known threefold fruit of action pertaining to <s>saṃsāra</s> — characterized as desirable, undesirable, and mixed — [belongs] to beings. There arises an inquiry: Does this [fruit] arise from <s>karma</s> or from <s>Īśvara</s>?
The prima facie view is: The fruit should come from <s>Īśvara</s>.
Why? Because of reasonableness.
For He, the overseer of all, effecting the manifold [processes of] creation, sustenance, and dissolution — being omniscient regarding the particularities of place and time — bestows upon the performers of action the fruit corresponding to their <s>karma</s>: this is reasonable.
But that <s>karma</s>, which perishes moment by moment, should produce a fruit arising at a later time — this is unreasonable.
Because from the non-existence [of <s>karma</s> at the time of fruition], there can be no production [of fruit].
It might be said: <s>Karma</s>, at its own time of perishing, produces a fruit corresponding to itself and then perishes, and that fruit is enjoyed by the doer at a later time.
But even this is not satisfactory — because prior to the connection with the experiencer, the status of being a 'fruit' is untenable.
For only that pleasure or pain which is experienced by the self at a particular time is well known in the world as a 'fruit.'
For worldly people do not regard any pleasure or pain unconnected with the self as a 'fruit.'
If it be said: Let there be no production of the fruit immediately after the <s>karma</s>; the fruit will arise from the <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency), which is the effect of <s>karma</s> —
even that is untenable.
Because the <s>apūrva</s>, being non-conscious, being equal to a piece of wood or a clod of earth, and not being directed by a conscious agent, cannot possibly act [to produce fruit].
And because there is no means of knowledge for the existence of such [an <s>apūrva</s>].

children.text: arthāpattiḥ pramāṇamiti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: Presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) is the means of knowledge [for the <s>apūrva</s>] —

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: īśvarasiddherarthāpattikṣayāt // 38 //
children.translated_text: Because the presumption is exhausted by the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s> [as the fruit-bestower]. // 38 //

children.text: FN: iṣṭaṃ svargaḥ, aniṣṭamavīcyādisthānayogyam , vyāmiśraṃ manuṣyabhogyam /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'Desirable' is heaven; 'undesirable' is that which leads to places like <s>Avīci</s> and the like; 'mixed' is that which is enjoyed by humans.

children.text: saṃsāro janmamṛtipravāho āśrayo yasya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Saṃsāra</s>' — the flow of birth and death — is the domain [of these fruits].

children.text: śrutatvāc ca | BBs_3,2.39 |
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>śruti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.39 |

children.text: na kevalamupapattereveśvaraṃ phalahetuṃ kalpayāmaḥ kiṃ tarhi śrutatvādapīśvarameva phalahetuṃ manyāmahe /
children.translated_text: It is not merely from reasonableness alone that we posit <s>Īśvara</s> as the cause of the fruit; rather, from the <s>śruti</s> too we regard <s>Īśvara</s> alone as the cause of the fruit.

children.text: tathāca śrutirbhavati - 'sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmānnādo vasudānaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.24) ityevañjātīyakā // 39 //
children.translated_text: For thus is the <s>śruti</s>: 'That great unborn Self, the eater of food, the giver of wealth' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.24) — and passages of this kind. // 39 //

children.text: FN: annamāsamantātprāṇibhyo dadātītyannādaḥ , vasudāno dhanadātā /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'The eater of food' (<s>annāda</s>) — one who gives food (<s>anna</s>) on all sides to beings; 'the giver of wealth' (<s>vasudāna</s>) — the bestower of riches.

children.text: dharmaṃ jaiminirata eva | BBs_3,2.40 |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> [is the cause of fruit] — so [says] <s>Jaimini</s>, for that very reason. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.40 |

children.text:
jaiministvācāryo dharmaṃ phalasya dātāraṃ manyate /
ata eva hetoḥ śrutarupapatteśca /
śrūyate tāvadayamarthaḥ svargakāmo yajeta ityevamādiṣu vākyeṣu /
tatra ca vidhiśruterviṣayabhāvopagamādyāgaḥ svargasyotpādaka iti gamyate /
anyathā hyananuṣṭhātṛko yāga āpadyeta tatrāsyopadeśavaiyarthyaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text:
But the teacher <s>Jaimini</s> regards <s>dharma</s> as the bestower of the fruit.
For the very same reasons — <s>śruti</s> and reasonableness.
This meaning is heard in passages such as 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice' and the like.
And there, because of the acceptance that [the sacrifice] becomes the object of the injunctive <s>śruti</s>, the sacrifice is understood to be the producer of heaven.
For otherwise, the sacrifice would have no performer, and in that case, the teaching [of sacrifice] would be purposeless.

children.text: nanvanukṣaṇavināśinaḥ sarmaṇaḥ phalaṃ nopapadyata iti parityakto 'yaṃ pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: But was not this position — that <s>karma</s>, which perishes moment by moment, cannot [produce] a fruit — already rejected?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
śrutiprāmāṇyāt /
śrutiścetpramāṇaṃ yathāyaṃ karmaphalasamabandhaḥ śruta upapadyate tathā kalpayitavyaḥ /
nacānutpādya kimapyapūrvaṃ karma vinaśyatkālāntaritaṃ phalaṃ dātuṃ śaknoti /
ataḥ karmaṇo vā sūkṣmā kāciduttarāvasthā phalasya vā pūrvāvasthāpūrvaṃ nāmāstīti tarkyate /
upapadyate cāyamarthaṃ uktena prakāreṇa /
children.translated_text: And this meaning is reasonable in the manner stated.

children.text: īśvarastu phalaṃ dadātītyanupapannam /
children.translated_text: But that <s>Īśvara</s> bestows the fruit — this is untenable.

children.text: avicitrasya kāraṇasya vicitrakāryānupapattervaiṣamyanairghṛmyaprasaṅgādanuṣṭhānavaiyartyāpatteśca /
children.translated_text: Because a uniform cause cannot produce varied effects; because the consequences of partiality and cruelty [would follow]; and because the purposelessness of [ritual] performance would result.

children.text: tasmāddharmādeva phalamiti // 40 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the fruit arises from <s>dharma</s> alone. // 40 //

This is not a fault.
Because of the authority of <s>śruti</s>.
If <s>śruti</s> is authoritative, then one must devise [a theory] by which the heard connection between <s>karma</s> and fruit is made tenable.
And <s>karma</s>, without producing some <s>apūrva</s> (unseen potency), cannot, while perishing, bestow a fruit arising at a later time.
Therefore, it is inferred that either there is a subtle subsequent state of <s>karma</s>, or a prior state of the fruit — [and this is what is] called <s>apūrva</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ tu bādarāyaṇo hetuvyapadeśāt | BBs_3,2.41 |
children.translated_text: But the earlier [view is held by] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — because of the designation of [<s>Īśvara</s> as] the cause. | <s>BBs</s> 3,2.41 |

children.text:
bādarāyaṇastvācāryaḥ pūrvoktameveśvaraṃ phalahetuṃ manyate /
kevalākarmaṇo 'pūrvādvā kevalātphalamityayaṃ pakṣastuśabdena vyāvartyate /
karmāpekṣādapūrvāpe 'kṣādvā yathā tathāstvīśvarātphalamiti siddhāntaḥ /
kutaḥ - hetuvyapadeśāt /
darmādharmayorapi hi kārayitṛtveneśvaro heturvyapadiśyate phalasya ca dātṛtvena 'eṣa hyeṣa sādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamebhyo lokebhya unninīṣate /
children.translated_text: For <s>Īśvara</s> is designated as the cause even of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — as their instigator — and as the bestower of the fruit: 'He indeed causes the one whom He wishes to lead upward from these worlds to perform good action;

children.text: eṣa u evāsādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamadho ninīṣate' iti /
children.translated_text: He indeed causes the one whom He wishes to lead downward to perform bad action' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 3.8).

children.text: smaryate cāyamartho bhagavadgītāsu - 'yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati /
children.translated_text: And this meaning is recorded in the <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>: 'Whatever form each devotee wishes to worship with faith,

children.text: tasya tasyācalāṃ śradjhadhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham //
children.translated_text: I make that very faith of his steady;

But the teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> regards the previously stated <s>Īśvara</s> as the cause of the fruit.
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) sets aside the position that the fruit arises from <s>karma</s> alone or from the <s>apūrva</s> alone.
The established conclusion is: Whether depending on <s>karma</s> or depending on <s>apūrva</s>, in either case the fruit [proceeds] from <s>Īśvara</s>.
Why? Because of the designation of [<s>Īśvara</s> as] the cause.

children.text: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate /
labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaiva vihitānhitān' (7.21) iti /
children.translated_text: and from that he obtains the desired [objects], which are indeed ordained by Me alone' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 7.21-22).

children.text: sarvavedānteṣu ceśvarahetukā eva sṛṣṭayo vyapadiśyante /
children.translated_text: And in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, creations are designated as having <s>Īśvara</s> as their cause.

children.text: tadeva ceśvarasya phalahetutvaṃ yatsvakarmānurūpāḥ prajāḥ sṛjatīti /
children.translated_text: And this indeed is <s>Īśvara</s>'s being the cause of the fruit — that He creates beings in accordance with their own <s>karma</s>.

children.text: vicitrakāryānupapattyādayo 'pi doṣāḥ kṛtaprayatnāpekṣatvādīśvarasya na prasajyante // 41 //
children.translated_text: And the faults of impossibility of varied effects and the like do not apply — because <s>Īśvara</s> [acts] in dependence on the effort (<s>karma</s>) already made [by beings]. // 41 //
Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that [deity],

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau śrīmacchārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye tṛtīyādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 2 //

children.text: tṛtīyādhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The third <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: atra parāparabrahmavidyāguṇopasaṃhāravivaraṇam
children.translated_text: Here, the examination of the inclusion and exclusion of attributes in the higher and lower <s>Brahman</s>-meditations is presented.

children.text: 1 sarvavedāntapratyayādhikaraṇam / sū. 1-4
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Sarvavedāntapratyayādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Cognition from All <s>Vedāntas</s>). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-4.

children.text: sarvavedāntapratyayaṃ codanādyaviśeṣāt | BBs_3,3.1 |
children.translated_text: The cognition [is the same] across all <s>Vedāntas</s> — because of the non-difference in injunction and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.1 |

children.text:
vyākhyātaṃ vijñeyasya brahmaṇastattvam /
idānīṃ tu prativedāntaṃ vijñānāni bhidyante na veti vicāryate /
children.translated_text:
The true nature of <s>Brahman</s> that is to be known has been explained.
Now, the question is examined: Do the cognitions (<s>vijñānas</s>) differ from one <s>Vedānta</s> [passage] to another, or not?

children.text:
nanu vijñeyaṃ brahma pūrvāparādibhedarahitamekarasaṃ saindhavaghanavadavadhāritaṃ tatra kuto vijñānabhedābhedacintāvatāraḥ /
nahi karmabahutvavadbrahmabahutvamapi vedānteṣu pratipipādayiṣitamiti śakyaṃ vaktum /
brahmaṇa ekavākyatvādekarūpatvācca /
nacaikūpe brahmaṇyanetarūpāṇi vijñānāni saṃbhavanti /
nahyanyathārtho 'nyathā jñānamityabhrāntaṃ bhavati /
yadi punarekasminbrahmaṇi bahūni vijñānāni vedāntāntareṣu pratipipādayiṣitāni teṣāmekamabhrāntaṃ bhrāntānītarāṇītyanāśvāsaprasaṅgo vedānteṣu /
tasmānna tāvatprativedāntaṃ brahmavijñānabheda āśaṅkituṃ śakyate /
nāpyasya codanādyaviśeṣādabheda ucyate /
brahmavijñānasyācodanālakṣaṇatvāt /
avidhipradhānairhi vastuparyavasāyibhirbrahmavākyairbrahmavijñānaṃ janyata ityavocadācāryaḥ 'tattu samanvayāt' (bra.sū. 1.1.4) ityatra /
children.translated_text:
But [one might ask]: <s>Brahman</s>, which is to be known, has been ascertained as homogeneous — without distinctions of before, after, and so forth — like a solid mass of salt. Then where is the occasion for inquiring into the difference or non-difference of cognitions?
For it cannot be said that the <s>Vedāntas</s> intend to teach a multiplicity of <s>Brahman</s>s, as the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> teaches a multiplicity of rituals.
[This is so] because of <s>Brahman</s>'s being the subject of a single statement, and because of its being of a single form.
And regarding <s>Brahman</s>, which is of a single form, cognitions of a different form are not possible.
For a cognition whose content differs from how the thing actually is cannot be non-erroneous.
Moreover, if many cognitions are intended to be taught in the various <s>Vedāntas</s> regarding a single <s>Brahman</s>, one of them would be non-erroneous and the others erroneous — leading to a loss of confidence in the <s>Vedāntas</s>.
Therefore, a difference in <s>Brahman</s>-cognitions from one <s>Vedānta</s> to another cannot be suspected.
Nor is their non-difference stated here because of the non-difference in injunction and the like.
Because <s>Brahman</s>-cognition is not of the nature of an injunction.
For the teacher has stated that <s>Brahman</s>-cognition is generated by <s>Brahman</s>-statements that are not primarily injunctive but are fact-revealing — in the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'But that [<s>Brahman</s> is known from the <s>Vedānta</s>], because of the consistency [of all <s>Vedānta</s> passages]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.1.4).

children.text: tatkathamimāṃ bhedābhedacintāmārabhata iti /
