children.translated_text: Then how does [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] undertake this inquiry into difference and non-difference?

children.text:
taducyate - saguṇabrahmaviṣayā prāṇādiviṣayā ceyaṃ vijñānabhedābhedacntetyadoṣaḥ /
atra hi karmavadupāsanānāṃ bhedābhedau saṃbhavataḥ karmavadeva copāsanāni dṛṣṭaphalāni cocyante /
kramamuktiphalāni ca kānicitsamyagjñānotpattidvāreṇa /
teṣveṣā cintā saṃbhavati /
kiṃ prativedāntaṃ vijñānabheda āhosvinneti /
tatra pūrvapakṣahetavastāvadupanyasyante /
nāmnāstāvadbhedapratipattihetutvaṃ prasiddhaṃ jyotirādiṣu /
asti cātra vedāntāntaravihiteṣu vijñāneṣvanyadanyannāma taittirīyakaṃ vājasaneyakaṃ kauthumakaṃ śāṭyāyanakamityevamādi /
tathā rūpabhedo 'pi karmabhedasya pratipādakaḥ prasiddho 'vaiśvadevyāmikṣā vājibhyo vājina' mityevamādiṣu /
asti cātra rūpabhedaḥ /
tadyathā - kecicchākhinaḥ pañcāgnividyāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhamaparamagnimāmananyatpare punaḥ pañcaiva paṭhanti /
tathā prāṇasaṃvādādiṣu kecidūnānvāgādīnāmananti kecidadhikān /
tathā dharmaviśeṣo 'pi karmabhedasya pratipādaka āśaṅkitaḥ kārīryādiṣu /
asti cātra dharmaviśeṣaḥ /
yathātharvaṇikānāṃ śirovratamiti /
evaṃ punaruktyādayo 'pi bhedahetavo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vedāntāntareṣu yojayitavyāḥ /
tasmātprativedāntaṃ vijñānabheda iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sarvavedāntapratyayāni vijñānāni tasmiṃstasminvedānte tāni tānyeva bhavitumarhanti /
kutaḥ - cedanādyaviśeṣāt /
ādigrahaṇena śākhāntarādhikaraṇasiddhāntasūtroditā abhedahetava ihākṛṣyante /
saṃyogarūpacodanākhyāviśeṣādityarthaḥ /
yathaikasminnagnihotre śākhābhede 'pi puruṣaprayatnastādṛśa eva codyate juhuyāditi /
evam 'yo ha vai jyoṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda' (bṛ.6.1.1, chā. 5.1.1) iti vājasaneyināṃ chandogānāṃ ca tādṛśyeva codanā /
prayojanasaṃyogo 'pyaviśiṣṭa eva 'jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca svānāṃ bhavati'' (bṛ. 6.1.1) iti /
rūpamapyubhayatra tadeva vijñānasya yaduta jyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhādiguṇaviśeṣaṇānvitaṃ prāṇatattvam /
yathā ca dravyadevate yāgasya rūpamevaṃ vijñeyaṃ rūpaṃ vijñānasya tena hi tadrūpyate /
samākhyāpi saiva prāṇavidyeti /
children.translated_text: The name too is the same — '<s>Prāṇavidyā</s>' (knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s>).

children.text: tasmātsarvavedāntapratyayatvaṃ vijñānānām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the cognitions are the same across all <s>Vedāntas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ pañcāgnividyā vaiśvānaravidyā śāṇḍilyavidyetyevamādiṣu yojayitavyam /
children.translated_text: The same should be applied to the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, the <s>Vaiśvānaravidyā</s>, the <s>Śāṇḍilyavidyā</s>, and the like.

children.text: ye tu nāmarūpādayo bhedahetvābhāsāste prathama eva kāṇḍe na nāmnā syādacodanābhidhānatvāt ityārabhya parihṛtāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: As for the apparent grounds for difference — name, form, and the like — those have already been refuted in the first <s>kāṇḍa</s> (section), beginning with 'Not by name, because of [its being merely] an expression of the non-enjoined.' // 1 //

To this it is said: This inquiry into the difference and non-difference of cognitions pertains to meditations on the qualified <s>Brahman</s> (<s>saguṇa Brahman</s>) and to those concerning <s>prāṇa</s> and the like — there is no fault in this.
For here, just as with rituals, both difference and non-difference are possible for meditations; and meditations, just like rituals, are said to have visible fruits [as well].
Some also have the fruit of gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>), through the door of the arising of right knowledge.
Regarding these, this inquiry is possible:
Is there a difference in cognition from one <s>Vedānta</s> to another, or not?
The prima facie arguments are first presented.
First, it is well known that difference in name is a ground for perceiving difference — as in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like.
And here, among the cognitions taught in different <s>Vedāntas</s>, there is one name or another — <s>Taittirīyaka</s>, <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>, <s>Kauthuma</s>, <s>Śāṭyāyanaka</s>, and so forth.
Likewise, difference in form (<s>rūpa</s>) is also well known as indicating a difference in ritual — as in '<s>Avaiśvadevī</s> curds for the <s>Vājins</s>' and the like.
And there is a difference in form here as well.
For example: Some <s>śākhins</s>, in the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, teach a sixth additional fire, while others read only five.
Likewise, in the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s> (dispute of the <s>prāṇas</s>), some teach fewer [<s>prāṇas</s>] such as speech and the like, and some teach more.
Likewise, a particular attribute (<s>dharmaviśeṣa</s>) too has been suspected as indicating a difference in ritual — as in the <s>Kārīrī</s> and the like.
And there is a particular attribute here too.
For example, the head-vow (<s>śirovrata</s>) [taught] by the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s>.
Likewise, repetition (<s>punarukti</s>) and other grounds for difference should be applied, as appropriate, to the various <s>Vedāntas</s>.
Therefore, there is a difference in cognition from one <s>Vedānta</s> to another.
Given this position, we say: The cognitions across all <s>Vedāntas</s> — those very cognitions should be [understood as] the same in each <s>Vedānta</s>.
Why? Because of the non-difference in injunction and the like.
By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), the grounds for non-difference stated in the <s>sūtras</s> establishing the <s>siddhānta</s> regarding topics in other <s>śākhās</s> are drawn in here.
The meaning is: because of the non-difference in injunction, connection, and form.
Just as in a single <s>Agnihotra</s>, despite the difference of <s>śākhā</s>, the same kind of human effort is enjoined: 'One should offer' —
so too, in [the meditations such as] 'He who knows the eldest and the best' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.1, <s>Chāndogya</s> 5.1.1), the injunction is of the same kind for both the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> and the <s>Chandogas</s>.
The connection with the purpose too is undifferentiated: 'One becomes the eldest and the best among one's own [people]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.1).
And the form of the cognition is the same in both — namely, the reality of <s>prāṇa</s> qualified by attributes such as 'eldest' and 'best.'
And just as the form of a sacrifice consists in the substance and deity [offered to], so too the form of a cognition consists in the object to be known — for by that [object] it is given its character.

children.text: FN: codyata iti codanā puruṣaprayatnaḥ sa hi puruṣavyāpāraḥ /
children.translated_text: NOTE: 'That which is enjoined' (<s>codanā</s>) — [means] the human effort; for that is the human activity.

children.text: ihāpi kañcidviśeṣamāśaṅkya pariharati -
children.translated_text: Now, having anticipated a certain specific [objection], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] responds:

children.text: bhedān neti cen naikasyām api | BBs_3,3.2 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that the cognitions are] not [the same] because of differences [in attributes] — [we say] no, because [they occur] even within a single [<s>vidyā</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.2 |

children.text:
syādetat /
sarvavedāntapratyayatvaṃ vijñānānāṃ guṇabhedānnopapadyate /
tathāhi vājasaneyinaḥ pañcāgnividyāṃ prastutyaḥ ṣṭhamaparamagnimāmananti - 'tasyāgnirevāgnirbhavati' (bṛ. 6.2.14) ityādinā /
chandogāstu taṃ nāmananti pañcasaṃkhyayaiva ca ta upasaṃharanti 'atha ha ya etānevaṃ pañcāgnīnveda' (chā. 5.10.10) iti /
yoṣāṃ ca sa guṇo 'sti yeṣāṃ ca nāsti kathamubhayeṣāmekā vidyopapadyeta /
nacātra guṇopasaṃhāraḥ śakyate pratyetuṃ, pañcasaṃkhyāvirodhāt /
tathā prāṇasaṃvāde śreṣṭhādanyāṃścaturaḥ prāṇānvākcakṣuḥ śrotamanāṃsi chandogā āmananti /
vājasaneyinastu pañcamamapyāmananti 'reto vai prajāpatiḥ prajāyate ha prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda' (bṛ. 6.1.6) iti /
children.translated_text:
It might be said:
The sameness of cognitions across all <s>Vedāntas</s> is untenable because of the differences in attributes.
For thus: The <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, in expounding the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>, teach a sixth additional fire: 'Of that [man], the fire is indeed the fire' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.14) and so forth.
But the <s>Chandogas</s> do not teach that, and conclude with the number five alone: 'Now, he who thus knows these five fires' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.10).
Some have that attribute and some do not — how can there be one single <s>vidyā</s> for both?
And here, the inclusion of attributes [from other <s>śākhās</s>] cannot be accepted, because it would conflict with the number five.
Likewise, in the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s>, the <s>Chandogas</s> teach four <s>prāṇas</s> other than the chief — speech, eye, ear, and mind.
But the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> teach a fifth as well: 'Semen is <s>Prajāpati</s>; he who knows thus is born with offspring and cattle' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.6).

children.text: āvāpodvāpabhedācca vedyabhedo bhavati vedyabhedācca vidyābhedo dravyadevatābhedādiva yāgasyeti cet /
children.translated_text: And because of the difference of inclusion and exclusion [of attributes], there is a difference in the object to be known; and because of the difference in the object to be known, there is a difference in the <s>vidyā</s> (meditation) — just as [there is] a difference of sacrifice because of the difference of substance and deity — if this is the objection:

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
yata ekasyāmapi vidyāyāmevañjātīyako guṇabheda upapadyate /
yadyapi ṣaṣṭhasyāgnerupasaṃhāro na saṃbhavati tathāpi dyuprabhṛtīnāṃ pañcānāmagnīnāmubhayatra pratyabhijñāyāmānatvānna vidyābhedo bhavitumarhati /
nahi ṣoḍaśigrahaṇāgrahaṇayoratirātro bhidyate /
paṭhyate 'pi ca ṣaṣṭho 'gniśchandogaiḥ - 'taṃ pretaṃ diṣṭamito 'gnaya evaṃ haranti'
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
For such a difference in subsidiary details is tenable even within a single <s>vidyā</s>.
Even though the incorporation of the sixth fire is not possible, nevertheless, since the five fires — beginning with the heavenly world — are recognized [as the same] in both [recensions], there should be no difference in the <s>vidyā</s>.
For indeed, the <s>Atirātra</s> [sacrifice] does not become different [merely] because of the inclusion or non-inclusion of the <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> cup.
And the sixth fire is indeed recited by the <s>Chāndogas</s>: 'They carry the one who has departed to the destined [world] — these fires indeed thus carry him'

children.text:
(chā. 5.9.2) iti /
vājasaneyinastu sāṃpādikeṣu pañcasvagniṣvanuvṛttāyāḥ samiddhūmādikalpanāyā nivṛttaye 'tasyāgnirevāgnirbhavati samitsamit' (bṛ. 6.2.14) ityādi samāmananti sa nityānuvādaḥ /
athāpyupāsanārtha eṣa vādastathāpi sa guṇaḥ śakyatechandogairapyupasaṃhartum /
nacātra pañcasaṃkhyāvirodhe āśaṅkyaḥ /
sāṃpādikāgnyabhiprāyā hyeṣā pañcasaṃkhyā nityānuvādabhūtā na vidhisamavāyinītyadoṣaḥ /
evaṃ prāṇasaṃvādeṣvapyadhikasya guṇasyetaratropasaṃhāro na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even in the <s>Prāṇa-Saṃvāda</s> [passages], the incorporation of an additional subsidiary detail from one [recension] into another is not contradicted.

children.text: nacāvāpodvāpabhedādvedyabhedo vidyābhedaścāśaṅkyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And no difference in the object of meditation and hence no difference in the <s>vidyā</s> should be apprehended because of the inclusion or exclusion [of certain details].

children.text: kasyacidvedyāṃśasyāvāpodvāpayorapi bhūyaso vedyarāśerabhedāvagamāt /
children.translated_text: For even when there is inclusion or exclusion of some portion of the object of meditation, the non-difference is understood from the greater mass of the object of meditation [remaining the same].

children.text: tasmādaikavidyameva // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is a single <s>vidyā</s> only. // 2 //

(<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.9.2).
But the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, in order to prevent the continuation of the attribution of fuel, smoke, and the like [to the sixth fire] — which had been ongoing in the five fires that are objects of meditation — recite: 'Of that, fire itself is the fire, fuel the fuel' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.14) and the like — that is merely a restatement of what is eternally known.
Even if this statement is for the purpose of meditation, still, that subsidiary detail can be incorporated by the <s>Chāndogas</s> as well.
And no contradiction with the number five need be apprehended here.
For this number five, having reference to the fires that are objects of meditation, is merely a restatement of what is eternally known — not one that is connected with an injunction — hence there is no fault.

children.text: FN: ito 'smāllokān diṣṭaṃ lokāntaraṃ pretaṃ gataṃ jñātayo 'gnaye harantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Itas</s>' means from this world; '<s>diṣṭam</s>' means the other world; '<s>pretam</s>' means one who has departed — the meaning is: the relatives carry [him] to the fire.

children.text: svādhyāyasya tathātvena hi samācāre 'dhikārāc ca savavac ca tanniyamaḥ | BBs_3,3.3 |
children.translated_text: Because [this observance] has the character of [being a duty of] one's own Vedic study — since it is [treated] thus in the [traditional] practice, and because of the eligibility, and like the <s>sava</s> [rite], that is its restriction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.3 |

children.text:
yadapyuktamātharvaṇikānāṃ vidyāṃ prati śirovratādyapekṣaṇādanyeṣāṃ ca tadanapekṣaṇādvadyābheda iti tatpratyucyate /
svādhyāyasyaiṣa dharmo na vidyāyāḥ /
kathamidamavagamyate /
yatastathātvena svādyāyadharmatvena samācāre vedavratopadeśapare granta ātharvaṇikā idamapi vedavratatvena vyākyātamiti samāmananti /
'naitadacīrṇavrato 'dhīte' (mu. 3.2.11) iti cādikṛtaviṣayādecchabdādadhyayanaśabdācca svopaniṣadadhyayanadharma evaiṣa iti nirdāryate /
children.translated_text:
As for the objection that because the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s> require the head-vow (<s>śirovrata</s>) and the like for their <s>vidyā</s>, while others do not require it, there must be a difference in the <s>vidyās</s> — to that we reply:
This is a duty belonging to one's own Vedic study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), not to the <s>vidyā</s> [itself].
How is this understood?
Because in the [traditional] practice — that is, in the texts devoted to the teaching of Vedic observances (<s>vedavrata</s>) — the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s> explain this too as a Vedic observance, in its character as belonging to [Vedic] study.
And from the passage 'One who has not observed this vow should not study it' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.11) — because of the word '<s>iccha</s>' (desiderative, implying 'wishes [to study]') in [the passage] pertaining to the subject at hand, and because of the word '<s>adhyayana</s>' (study) — it is determined that this is indeed a duty pertaining to the study of one's own <s>Upaniṣad</s>.

children.text: nanu ca 'teṣāmevaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta śirovrataṃ vidhivadyaistu cīrṇam' (muṇḍa. 3.2.10) iti brahmavidyāsaṃyogaśravaṇādekaiva sarvatra brahmavidyeti saṃkīryetaiṣa dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: But [the passage] 'One should impart this <s>Brahmavidyā</s> to those who have duly observed the head-vow' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.10) — because of hearing the connection with <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, this duty would be mixed up with all <s>Brahmavidyā</s> everywhere, [implying] that there is but one <s>Brahmavidyā</s> everywhere.

children.text:
na /
tatrāpyetāmiti prakṛtyapratyavamarśāt /
praka-tatvaṃ ca brahmavidyāyā granthaviśeṣāpekṣamiti granthaviśeṣasaṃyogyevaiṣa dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the proximate reference of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> depends on the particular [Vedic] text — hence this duty is connected only with the particular [Vedic] text [of the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s>].

children.text: savavacca tanniyama iti nidarśananirdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And like the <s>sava</s> [rite], that is its restriction' — this is a citation of an illustration.

children.text: yathāca savāḥ sapta sauryādayaḥ sathaudanaparyantā vedāntaroditatretāgnyanabhisaṃbandhādatharvaṇoditaikāgnyabhisaṃbandhāccātharvaṇikānāmeva niyamyante tathaivāyamapi dharmaḥ svādhyāyaviśeṣasaṃbandhāttatraiva niyamyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the seven <s>savas</s> — beginning with the <s>Saurya</s> and ending with the <s>Sathaudana</s> — are restricted to the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s> alone, because of their non-connection with the three fires taught in other <s>Vedas</s> and their connection with the single fire taught in the <s>Atharva</s> — so too, this duty is restricted to that [particular Vedic study] alone, because of its connection with a particular branch of Vedic study.

children.text: tasmādapyanavadyaṃ vidyaikatvam // 3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this [consideration] too, the unity of the <s>vidyā</s> is faultless. // 3 //

No.
Because even there, the word '<s>etām</s>' (this) refers back to the proximate [text] — [indicating that it pertains only to that particular <s>Brahmavidyā</s>].

children.text: darśayati ca | BBs_3,3.4 |
children.translated_text: [The <s>Veda</s>] also shows [this]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.4 |

children.text:
darśayati ca vedo 'pi vidyaikatvaṃ sarvavedānteṣu vedyaikatvopadeśāt sarve vedā yatparamāmananti (ka. 2.15) iti /
tathā etaṃ hyeva bahvṛcā mahatyukthe mīmāṃsanta etamagnāvadhvarya etaṃ mahāvrate chandogāḥ iti ca /
tathā 'mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyatam' (ka.6.2) iti kāṭhaka uktasyeśvaraguṇasya bhayahetukasya taittirīyake bhedarśananindāyai parāmarśo dṛśyate 'yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnudaramantaraṃ kurute /
atha tasya bhayaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: then he has fear.

children.text: tattveva bhayaṃ viduṣo 'manvānasya' (tai. 2.7.1) iti /
children.translated_text: And that very [<s>Brahman</s>] is the source of fear for the knower who does not reflect [on its unity]' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.7.1).

children.text: tathā vājasaneyake prādeśamātrasaṃpāditasya vaiśvānarasya chāndogye siddhavadupādānam 'yastvetamevaṃ prādeśamātramabhivimānamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaramupāste' (chā. 5.18.1) iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, who is established in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> as a <s>prādeśamātra</s> (a span in measure), is taken up in the <s>Chāndogya</s> as already established: 'He who meditates on <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as the Self, a span in measure, with clear perception' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.1).

children.text: tathā sarvavedāntapratyayatvenānyatra vihitanāmukthādīnāmanyatropāsanavidhānāyopādānātprāyadarśananyāyenopāsanānāmapi sarvavedāntapratyayatvasiddhiḥ // 4//
children.translated_text: Likewise, because names such as <s>uktha</s> and the like — which are enjoined in one place — are taken up in another place for the purpose of enjoining meditation, by the principle of representative illustration, the [conclusion] that meditations too belong to all the <s>Vedāntas</s> is established. // 4 //

The <s>Veda</s> too shows the unity of the <s>vidyā</s>, because of the teaching of the unity of the object of knowledge (<s>vedya</s>) in all the <s>Vedāntas</s> (Upaniṣads): 'All the <s>Vedas</s> proclaim That which is supreme' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.15).
Likewise: 'The <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (followers of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>) investigate It in the <s>Mahad Uktha</s>; the <s>Adhvaryus</s> in the fire-ritual; the <s>Chāndogas</s> in the <s>Mahāvrata</s>' — and the like.
Likewise, a quality of the Lord stated in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [Upaniṣad] — that He is the cause of fear — 'The great terror, the upraised thunderbolt' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 6.2) — is seen to be referred to in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s> for the purpose of censuring the perception of difference: 'When indeed this [person] makes even the slightest distinction in That —

children.text: 2 upasaṃhārādhikaraṇam / sū. 5
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Upasaṃhāra Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Incorporation). <s>Sūtra</s> 5.

children.text: upasaṃhāror'thābhedādvidhiśeṣavatsamāne ca | BBs_3,3.5 |
children.translated_text: Incorporation [of subsidiary details from one recension into another takes place] because of non-difference of meaning — as with the subsidiary details of injunctions, [and] when [the meditation] is the same. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.5 |

children.text:
idaṃ prayojanasūtram /
sthite caivaṃ sarvavedāntapratyayatve sarvavijñānānāmanyatroditānāṃ vijñānaguṇānāmanyatrāpi samāne vijñāna upasaṃhāro bhavati /
arthābhedāt /
ya eva hi teṣāṃ guṇānāmekatrārtho viśiṣṭavijñānopakārakaḥ sa evānyatrāpi /
ubhayatrāpi hi tadevaikaṃ vijñānaṃ tasmādupasaṃhāraḥ /
vidhiśeṣavat /
yathāhi vidhiśeṣāṇāmagnihotrādidharmāṇāṃ tadevaikamagnihotrādi karma sarvatretyarthābhedādupasaṃharaṇamevamihāpi /
children.translated_text: Just as the subsidiary details of injunctions — the rules pertaining to the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like — are incorporated [from one recension into another] because of non-difference of meaning, since it is one and the same <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like ritual everywhere — so too here.

children.text: yadi hi vijñānabhedo bhavettato vijñānāntaranibaddhatvādguṇānāṃ prakṛtivikṛtibhāvābhāvācca na syādupasaṃhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: For if there were a difference in the meditations, then — because the subsidiary details would be bound to a different meditation, and because there would be no relation of archetype and modification (<s>prakṛti-vikṛti</s>) — there would be no incorporation.

children.text: vijñānaikatve tu naivamasti /
children.translated_text: But when the meditation is one, this [problem] does not arise.

children.text: asyaiva tu prayojanasūtrasya prapañcaḥ sarvābhedādityārabhya bhaviṣyati // 5 //
children.translated_text: The elaboration of this very <s>sūtra</s> [stating] the practical consequence will come later, beginning with '<s>sarvābhedāt</s>' (because of non-difference in all respects). // 5 //

This is the <s>sūtra</s> [stating] the practical consequence.
When the principle that [meditations] belong to all the <s>Vedāntas</s> has been established in this way, the subsidiary qualities of meditations (<s>vijñāna</s>) that are stated in one place are incorporated into the same meditation [as found] in another place as well.
Because of non-difference of meaning.
For the purpose that those subsidiary qualities serve in one place — namely, assisting the qualified meditation — is the same in another place as well.
For in both places, the meditation is one and the same — therefore the incorporation.
As with the subsidiary details of injunctions.

children.text: 3 anyathātvādhikaraṇam / sū. 6-8
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Anyathātva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Difference in Mode). <s>Sūtras</s> 6-8.

children.text: anyathātvaṃ śabdād iti cen nāviśeṣāt | BBs_3,3.6 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that there is] difference in mode because of the [Vedic] text — [we say] no, because of non-distinction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.6 |

children.text: vājasaneyake 'te ha devā ūcurhantāsurānyajña udgīthenātyayāmeti' (bṛ. 1.3.1) 'te ha vācamucustvaṃ na udgāya' (bṛ.
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>: 'The <s>devas</s> said: "Come, let us overcome the <s>asuras</s> in sacrifice through the <s>udgītha</s>"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.1); 'They said to speech: "You sing the <s>udgītha</s> for us"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>

children.text:
1.3.2) iti prakramya vāgādīnprāṇānasurapāpmaviddhatvena ninditvā mukhyaprāṇaparigrahaḥ paṭhyate - 'atha hemamāsanyaṃ prāṇamūcustvaṃ na udgāyeti tatheti tebhya eṣa prāṇa udagāyat' (bṛ. 1.3.7) iti /
tathā chāndogye 'pi - 'taddhadevā udgīthamājagmuranenainānabhibhaviṣyāmaḥ' (chā. 1.21) iti prakramyetarānprāṇānasurapāpmaviddhatvena ninditvā tathaiva mukhyaprāṇaparigrahaḥ paṭhyate - 'atha ha ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇastamudgīthamupāsāṃcakrire' (chā. 1.2.7) iti /
ubhayatrāpi ca prāṇapraśaṃsayā prāṇavidyāvidhiradhyavasīyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimatra vidyābhedaḥ syādāhosvidvidyaikatvamiti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ pūrveṇa nyāyena vidyaikatvamiti /
children.translated_text:
1.3.2) — having thus begun, and having censured the <s>prāṇas</s> such as speech and the like as being afflicted by the <s>asura</s>-evil, the acceptance of the chief <s>prāṇa</s> is recited: 'Then they said to this <s>prāṇa</s> in the mouth: "You sing the <s>udgītha</s> for us"; "So be it" — that <s>prāṇa</s> sang the <s>udgītha</s> for them' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.7).
Likewise, in the <s>Chāndogya</s> too: 'The <s>devas</s> resorted to the <s>udgītha</s> [thinking]: "By this we shall overcome them"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.2.1) — having thus begun, and having censured the other <s>prāṇas</s> as afflicted by the <s>asura</s>-evil, the acceptance of the chief <s>prāṇa</s> is recited in the same way: 'Then they meditated upon this chief <s>prāṇa</s> as the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.2.7).
And in both [recensions], through the praise of <s>prāṇa</s>, the injunction of the <s>Prāṇavidyā</s> (meditation on <s>prāṇa</s>) is understood.
Therein, the doubt arises: Is there a difference in the <s>vidyā</s> here, or is it a single <s>vidyā</s>?
What is the initial position? By the preceding reasoning, [it should be] a single <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text:
nanu na yuktaṃ vidyaikatvaṃ prakramabhedāt /
anyathā hi prakramante vājasaneyino 'nyathā chandogāḥ 'tvaṃ na udgāya' (bṛ. 1.3.2) iti vājasaneyina udgīthasya kartṛtvena prāṇamāmananti /
chandogāstūdgīthatvena 'tamudgīthamupāsaṃcakrire' (chā. 1.2.7) iti /
children.translated_text:
Objection: The unity of the <s>vidyā</s> is not proper — because of the difference in the introductory context (<s>prakrama</s>).
For the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> begin differently from the <s>Chāndogas</s>. 'You sing the <s>udgītha</s> for us' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.2) — the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> teach <s>prāṇa</s> as the performer (<s>kartṛ</s>) of the <s>udgītha</s>.
But the <s>Chāndogas</s> [teach it] as [being identified with] the <s>udgītha</s> itself: 'They meditated upon it as the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.2.7).

children.text: tatkathaṃ vidyaikatvaṃ syāditi cet /
children.translated_text: How then can there be unity of the <s>vidyā</s>?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
na hyetāvatā viśeṣeṇa vidyaikatvamapagacchati /
aviśeṣasyāpi bahutarasya pratīyamānatvāt /

tathāhi - devāsurasaṃgrāmopakramatvamasurātyayābhiprāya udgīthopanyāso vāgādisaṃkīrtanaṃ tannindayā mukhyaprāṇavyapāśrayastadvīryāccāsuravidhvaṃsanamaśmaloṣṭanidarśanenetyevaṃ bahavor'thā ubhayatrāpyaviśiṣṭāḥ pratīyante /
children.translated_text: For thus — the introductory context of the war between the <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>, the mention of the <s>udgītha</s> with the purpose of overcoming the <s>asuras</s>, the enumeration of speech and the like, the censure of those followed by recourse to the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, the destruction of the <s>asuras</s> through its power, the illustration of the stone and clod — these many [points of] meaning are perceived as non-distinct in both [recensions].

children.text: vājasaneyake 'picodgīthasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ prāṇasya śrutam - 'eṣa u vā udgīthaḥ' (bṛ. 1.3.23) iti /
children.translated_text: And even in the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>, the co-referentiality of <s>prāṇa</s> with <s>udgītha</s> is heard: 'This indeed is the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.23).

children.text: tasmācchāndogye 'pi kartṛtvaṃ lakṣayitavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Chāndogya</s> too, the performer-ship [of <s>prāṇa</s>] should be inferred.

children.text: tasmācca vidyaikatvamiti // 6 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, [this is] a single <s>vidyā</s>. // 6 //

This is not a fault.
For the unity of the <s>vidyā</s> is not negated by this much distinction alone.
Because the greater mass [of details] is perceived as non-distinct.

children.text: FN: āsanyaṃ āsye bhavam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Āsanya</s>' means situated in the mouth.

children.text: asurātyayābhiprāyo 'surajayārthaṃ saṃvādaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Asurātyayābhiprāya</s>' — the dialogue has the purpose of defeating the <s>asuras</s>.

children.text: na vā prakaraṇabhedāt parovarīyastvādivat | BBs_3,3.7 |
children.translated_text: Or rather, [there is] no [unity] — because of the difference in context, as with the <s>parovarīyastva</s> (quality of supreme greatness) and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.7 |

children.text:
na vā vidyaikatvamātra nyāyyaṃ vidyābheda evātra nyāyyaḥ /
kasmāt /
prakaraṇabhedāditi /
prakramabhedādityarthaḥ /
tathāhi - iha prakramabhedo dṛśyate /
chāndogye tāvat - omityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta (chā. 1.1.1) ityevamudgīthāvayavasyoṅkārasyopāsyatvaṃ prastutya rasatamādiguṇopavyākhyānaṃ tatra kṛtvā atha khalvetasyaivākṣarasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhavati (chā. 1.1.10) iti punarapi tamevodgīthāvayavamoṅkāramanuvartya devāsurākhyāyikādvāreṇa tam prāṇamudgīthamupāsāṃcakrire (chā. 1.2.2) ityāha /

upakramānurodhena caikasminvākya upasaṃhāreṇa bhavitavyam /

sakalabhaktiviṣaya eva ca tatrāpyudgīthaśabda iti vaiṣamyam /

children.translated_text: So too here, because of the difference in introductory context, there is a difference in the <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: parovarīyastvādivat /
children.translated_text: As with the <s>parovarīyastva</s> (quality of supreme greatness) and the like.

children.text: yathā paramātmadṛṣṭyadhyāsasāmye 'pi 'ākośo hyevaibhyo jyāyānākśaḥ parāyaṇam' (chā. 1.9.1) 'sa eṣa parovarīyānudgīthaḥ sa eṣo 'nantaḥ' (chā. 1.9.2) iti parovarīyastvaguṇaviśiṣṭamudgīthopāsanamakṣyādityādigatahiraṇyaśmaśrutvādiguṇaviśiṣṭodgīthopāsanādbhinnam /
children.translated_text: Just as — even though the superimposition of the supreme Self is common [to both] — the meditation on the <s>udgītha</s> qualified by the quality of supreme greatness: 'Space indeed is greater than these — space is the final resort' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.9.1); 'This is the <s>udgītha</s> that is supremely great, this is infinite' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.9.2) — is different from the meditation on the <s>udgītha</s> qualified by qualities such as golden-beardedness and the like, attributed to [the person in] the eye, the sun, and the like.

children.text: nacetaretaraguṇopasaṃhāra ekasyāmapi śākhāyāṃ tadvacchākhāntarastheṣvapyevañjātīyakeṣūpāsaneṣviti // 7 //
children.translated_text: And just as there is no incorporation of qualities from one into the other even within a single Vedic branch — so too in meditations of this kind that are found in other branches. // 7 //

Or rather, the unity of the <s>vidyā</s> is not proper here — a difference in the <s>vidyā</s> is indeed proper here.
Why?
Because of the difference in context — that is, because of the difference in the introductory framework.
For thus, a difference in the introductory framework is observed here.
In the <s>Chāndogya</s>: 'One should meditate on the syllable <s>Om</s> as the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1) — having thus introduced the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, a component of the <s>udgītha</s>, as the object of meditation, and having provided an elaboration through qualities like being the quintessence (<s>rasatama</s>) and the like, [the text says:] 'Now, there is yet another elaboration of this very syllable' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) — again taking up that very <s>Oṃkāra</s>, a component of the <s>udgītha</s>, [the text] then says, through the narrative of the <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>: 'They meditated upon this <s>prāṇa</s> as the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.2.2).
There, if the word '<s>udgītha</s>' were intended to refer to the entire chant (<s>bhakti</s>), then the <s>udgātṛ</s> priest would be the performer, the introductory context would be different, and a figurative interpretation would follow.
But in accordance with the introductory context, the conclusion must be [drawn] within a single passage.
Therefore, here at least, a meditation on <s>prāṇa</s> superimposed on the <s>Oṃkāra</s> — a component of the <s>udgītha</s> — is being taught.
In the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>, however — since there is no reason to take the word '<s>udgītha</s>' as referring to a component — the entire chant is what is conveyed.
And 'You sing the <s>udgītha</s> for us' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.2) — the performer of that [entire chant], namely the <s>udgātṛ</s> priest, is identified as <s>prāṇa</s> — hence a different approach.
As for the co-referentiality of <s>prāṇa</s> with <s>udgītha</s> mentioned there — that too is intended to demonstrate the all-Self-hood (<s>sarvātmatva</s>) of <s>prāṇa</s>, which was meant to be shown as the <s>udgātṛ</s> — and hence does not establish the unity of the <s>vidyā</s>.
And even there, the word '<s>udgītha</s>' refers to the entire chant — hence the disparity.
And the <s>udgātṛ</s>-ship of <s>prāṇa</s> is not to be abandoned because of the [supposed] reason of impossibility — for the <s>udgātṛ</s>-status, like the <s>udgītha</s>-status, is taught for the purpose of meditation.
And the <s>udgātṛ</s> performs the <s>udgāna</s> (chanting) by the power of <s>prāṇa</s> itself — hence there is no impossibility.
And thus it is stated there itself: 'For with speech and with <s>prāṇa</s> indeed he chanted the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.24).
And when a difference in the intended meaning is being ascertained, it is not proper to determine identity of meaning merely from the surface resemblance of sentences.
For thus, in the <s>abhyudaya</s> (prosperity) passage and the <s>paśukāma</s> (desire for cattle) passage — even though the prescription 'One should divide the grains into three parts; those that are medium should be used to make a <s>puroḍāśa</s> on eight potsherds for <s>Agni Dātṛ</s>' and the like is similar in both — because of the difference in introductory context, the <s>abhyudaya</s> passage is understood as a rite of deity-appeasement, while the <s>paśukāma</s> passage is understood as an injunction of sacrifice.

children.text: FN: vaiṣamyamubhayatra vidyānānātvam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Vaiṣamya</s>' means the plurality of <s>vidyās</s> in both [recensions].

children.text: apanayo viyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Apanaya</s>' means separation.

children.text: parasmātparo varācca varataraḥ parovarīyān /
children.translated_text: '<s>Parovarīyān</s>' — greater than the great and better than the better — supremely great.

children.text: saṃjñātaś cet tad uktam asti tu tad api | BBs_3,3.8 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that there is unity] because of identity of name — that has been stated; but there is [a counter-argument] to that as well. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.8 |

children.text:
athocyate saṃjñaikatvādvidyaikatvamatra nyāyyamudgīthavidyeti hyubhayaṇāpyekā saṃjñeti /
tadapi nopapadyate /
uktaṃ hyetat - 'na vā prakaraṇabhedātparovarīyastvādivat' (bra. sū. 3.3.7) iti /
tadeva cātra nyāyyataraṃ śrutyakṣarānugataṃ hi tatsaṃjñaikatvaṃ tu śrutyakṣarabāhyamudgīthaśabdamātraprayogāllaukikairvyahartṛbhirupacaryate /
children.translated_text: And precisely that [the specification-view] is more reasonable here. For the identity of the <s>vidyā</s> based on name alone is external to the letter of <s>śruti</s>, [whereas] the identity based on name alone is figuratively spoken of by worldly speakers merely from the use of the word '<s>udgītha</s>.'

children.text: asti caitatsaṃjñaikatvaṃ prasiddhabhedeṣvapi parovarīyastvādyupāsaneṣūdgīthavidyeti /
children.translated_text: And this identity of name exists even in <s>upāsanas</s> such as the '<s>parovevarīyastva</s>' and others, which are known to be different — [yet they bear] the label '<s>udgītha-vidyā</s>.'

children.text: tathā prasiddhabhedānāmapyagnihotradarśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ kāṭhakaikagranthaparipaṭhitānāṃ kāṭhakasaṃjñakatvaṃ dṛśyate tathehāpi bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even for <s>agnihotra</s>, <s>darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the like — which are known to be different — when compiled in a single text of the <s>Kāṭhakas</s>, they are seen to bear the label '<s>Kāṭhaka</s>.' The same will apply here too.

children.text: yatra tu nāsti kaścidevañjātīyako bhedahetustatra bhavatu saṃjñaikatvādvidyaikatvaṃ yathā saṃvargavidyādiṣu // 8 //
children.translated_text: But where there is no such cause of difference, there may be identity of the <s>vidyā</s> [itself] based on identity of name — as in the <s>Saṃvarga-vidyā</s> and the like. // 8 //

Now, if it be said: The unity of the <s>vidyā</s> is proper here because of the identity of the name — for in both [recensions] there is one name, '<s>Udgīthavidyā</s>' — [we reply:] even that is not tenable.
For this has been stated: 'Or rather, [there is] no [unity] — because of the difference in context, as with the <s>parovarīyastva</s> and the like' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.3.7).

children.text: 4 vyāptyadhikaraṇam / sū. 9
children.translated_text: Section 4: <s>Vyāptyadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 9

children.text: vyāpteś ca samañjasam | BBs_3,3.9 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāpteśca samañjasam</s> — And because of [Oṃkāra's] pervasiveness, [the specification-view] is fitting. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.9 |

children.text:
'omtyetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.1.1) ityatrākṣarodgīthaśabdayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇye śrūyamāṇe 'dhyāsāpavādaikatvaviśeṣaṇapakṣāṇāṃ pratibhāsanātkatamo 'tra pakṣo nyāyyaḥ syāditi vicāraḥ /
tatrādhyāso nāma dvayorvastunoranivartitāyāmevānyatarabuddhāvanyatarabuddhiradhyasyate /

yathā vā digbhrāntibuddhirdigyāthātmyabuddhyā nivartyate /
yathā vā digbhrāntibuddhirdigyāthātmyabuddhyā nivartyate /
evamihāpyakṣarabuddhyodgīthabuddhirnivartyata udgīthabuddhyā vākṣarabuddhiriti /
ekatvaṃ tvakṣarodgīthaśabdayoranatiriktārthavṛttitvam /

yathā nīlaṃ yadutpalaṃ tadānayeti /
evamihāpyudgītho ya oṅkārastamupāsīteti /

caśabdo 'yaṃ tuśabdasthānaniveśī pakṣatrayavyāvartanaprayojana- /
tadiha kṣayaḥ pakṣāḥ sāvadyā iti paryudasyante /
viśeṣaṇapakṣa evaiko niravadya ityupādīyate /

tasyānyaphalatvāt /
āptyādidṛṣṭiphalaṃ hi tannodgīthādhyāsaphalam /

children.translated_text: In the passage 'One should meditate on this syllable Oṃ as the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1), when the co-referentiality of the words '<s>akṣara</s>' (syllable) and '<s>udgītha</s>' is heard, the [four] alternatives of superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>), sublation (<s>apavāda</s>), identity (<s>ekatva</s>), and specification (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) present themselves — [and] the investigation is: which of these alternatives is proper? Therein, superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) means: when, of two things, the cognition of one has not been removed, the cognition of the other is superimposed [upon it]. The cognition that is superimposed on the other [object] continues to persist in that [object] on which it is superimposed — it is not removed by the other cognition. Just as, when the cognition of <s>Brahman</s> is superimposed on a name [of <s>Brahman</s>], the cognition of the name continues to persist — it is not removed by the <s>Brahman</s>-cognition. Or, as in the superimposition of the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-cognition and the like on images and such. Similarly here too: the <s>udgītha</s>-cognition is superimposed on the syllable [Oṃ], or the syllable-cognition on the <s>udgītha</s>. Sublation (<s>apavāda</s>) means: regarding some object in which a prior false cognition has been established, a subsequent true cognition arises that removes the prior false cognition. Just as the <s>ātman</s>-cognition regarding the aggregate of body and senses is subsequently removed by the true cognition 'That you are' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) — which is the <s>ātman</s>-cognition regarding the true Self. Or, as the false cognition of direction is removed by the true cognition of direction. Or, as the false cognition of direction is removed by the true cognition of direction. Similarly here too: the <s>udgītha</s>-cognition is removed by the <s>akṣara</s>-cognition, or the <s>akṣara</s>-cognition by the <s>udgītha</s>-cognition. Identity (<s>ekatva</s>) means that the two words '<s>akṣara</s>' and '<s>udgītha</s>' have a non-distinct referent — as in 'the best among the twice-born,' 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,' 'an earthly deity.' Specification (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), on the other hand, is the assignment to the <s>audgātra</s>-specific [portion] of the syllable Oṃ, which pervades all <s>Vedas</s> and might [otherwise] be taken [in its universal sense]. Just as [one says:] 'Bring me the blue lotus' — [where 'blue' specifies which lotus]. Similarly here too: 'The <s>udgītha</s> which is Oṃkāra — meditate on that.' Thus, when this co-referential statement is examined, these alternatives present themselves. Since there is no ground for determining one [over the other], and thus [the matter is] undetermined — this is said: 'And because of pervasiveness, [the specification-view] is fitting.' The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) here stands in the place of '<s>tu</s>' (but), serving to exclude the [other] three alternatives. Thus here the [first] three alternatives are set aside as faulty. The specification-alternative alone, being faultless, is adopted. Therein, first regarding superimposition: the word for the cognition that is superimposed on the other would be functioning by secondary designation (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), and the fruit [of the meditation] would have to be postulated. [Objection:] But the fruit is indeed heard [in the text]: 'He becomes one who fulfills desires' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.7) and the like. No. Because that fruit belongs to something else. For the fruit [described] as the attainment [of desires] and the like is not the fruit of the superimposition of <s>udgītha</s>[-cognition on Oṃkāra]. In the sublation-[view] too, the same fault of absence of fruit [applies]. [Objection:] The fruit is the removal of false cognition. No.

children.text:
puruṣārthopayogānavagamāt /
naca kadācidapyoṅkārādoṅkārabuddhirnivartata udgīthādvedgīthabuddhiḥ /
nacedaṃ vākyaṃ vastutattvapratipādanaparam /
upāsanāvidhiparatvāt /
nāpyekatvapakṣaḥ saṃgacchate niṣprayojanaṃ hi tadā śabdadvayoccāraṇaṃ syāt /
ekenaiva vivakṣitārthasamarpaṇāt /
naca hautraviṣaya ādhvaryavaviṣaye vākṣara oṅkāraśabdavācya udgīthaśabdaprasiddhirasti /
nāpi sakalāyāṃ sāmno dvitīyāyāṃ bhaktāvudgīthaśabdaprasiddhirasti /
nāpi sakalāyāṃ sāmno dvitīyāyāṃ bhaktāvudgīthaśabdavācyāyāmoṅkāraśabdaprasiddhiryenānatiriktārthatā syāt /
pariśeṣādviśeṣaṇapakṣaḥ parigṛhyate /
vyāpteḥ sarvavedasādhāraṇyāt /
sarvavyāpyakṣaramiha mā prasañjītyata udgīthaśabdenākṣaraṃ viśeṣyate kathaṃ nāmodgīthāvayavabhūta oṅkāro gṛhyeteti /
children.translated_text: Because the contribution to the highest human goal is not apprehended [in this case]. And never does the Oṃkāra-cognition get removed from Oṃkāra, or the <s>udgītha</s>-cognition from the <s>udgītha</s>. And this passage is not aimed at establishing the truth about an entity — because it is aimed at enjoining a meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>). Nor does the identity-view fit, for then the use of two words would be purposeless — since the intended meaning would be conveyed by one alone. And the syllable Oṃ, which pertains to the <s>hautra</s> (domain of the <s>hotṛ</s>), is not known by the word '<s>udgītha</s>' when it pertains to the <s>ādhvaryava</s> (domain of the <s>adhvaryu</s>). Nor is the word '<s>oṃkāra</s>' well-known in the entire second division of the <s>sāman</s> — which is denoted by the word '<s>udgītha</s>' — such that the two words could be non-distinct in referent. By the process of elimination, the specification-view is adopted. Because of pervasiveness — because [Oṃkāra] is common to all <s>Vedas</s>. Lest the all-pervading syllable [Oṃ] be taken [in its universal sense] here, it is specified by the word '<s>udgītha</s>': [the meaning is] 'how should we understand this as the Oṃkāra that is a component of the <s>udgītha</s>?'

children.text:
nanvasminnapi pakṣe samānā lakṣaṇā /
udgīthaśabdasyāvayavalakṣaṇārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: Even in this [specification-]view, there is the same [problem of] secondary designation — because the word '<s>udgītha</s>' has its primary meaning in [referring to the whole] component [of the <s>sāman</s>].

children.text: satyametat /
children.translated_text: True, this is so.

children.text: lakṣaṇāyāmapi tu saṃnikarṣaviprakarṣo bhavata eva /
children.translated_text: But even among secondary designations, there is a difference of proximity and distance.

children.text: adhyāsapakṣe hyarthāntarabuddhirarthāntare nikṣipyata iti viprakṛṣṭā lakṣaṇā viśeṣaṇapakṣe pravṛttāḥ śabdā avayaveṣvapi pravartamānā dṛṣṭāḥ paṭagrāmādiṣu /
children.translated_text: In the superimposition-view, the cognition of one thing is placed upon another thing — that is a distant [secondary] designation. In the specification-view, [however,] words referring to wholes are seen to apply to parts also — as in [the usage of] '<s>paṭa</s>' (cloth) and '<s>grāma</s>' (village) [for their parts].

children.text: ataśca vyāpterhetoromityetadakṣaramityetasyodgīthamityetadviśeṣaṇamiti samañjasametanniravadyamityarthaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, because of [Oṃkāra's] pervasiveness, [the statement] 'this syllable Oṃ' is specified by 'the <s>udgītha</s>' — [and] this is fitting, that is, faultless — this is the meaning. // 9 //

children.text: 5 sarvābhedādhikaraṇam / sū. 10
children.translated_text: Section 5: <s>Sarvābhedādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 10

children.text:
vājināṃ chandogānāṃ ca prāṇasaṃvāde śraiṣṭhyaguṇānvitasya prāṇasyopāsyatvamuktam /
vāgādayo 'pi hi tatra vasiṣṭhatvādiguṇānvitā uktāḥ te ca prāṇe punaḥ pratyarpitāḥ - 'yadvā ahaṃ vasiṣṭho 'smi tvaṃ tadvasiśṣo 'si' (bṛ. 6.1.14) ityādinā /
anyeṣāmapi tu śākhināṃ kauṣītaki prabhṛtīnāṃ prāṇasaṃvādeṣu athāto niḥśreyasādānam 'etā ha vai devatā ahaṃśreyase vivadamānāḥ' (kau. 2.14) ityevañjātīyakeṣu prāṇasya śraiḥṣṭamuktaṃ na tvime vasiṣṭhatvādayo 'pi guṇā uktāḥ /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimime vasiṣṭhatvādayo guṇāḥ kvaciduktā anyatrāpyasyerannuta nāsyeranniti /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvannāsyeranniti /
kutaḥ - evaṃśabdasaṃyogāt /
'atho ya evaṃ vidvānprāṇe niḥśreyasaṃ viditvā' iti tatratatraivaṃśabdena vedyaṃ vastu nivedyate /
evaṃśabdaśca saṃnihitāvalambano na śākhāntaraparipaṭhimevañjātīyakaṃ guṇajātaṃ śaknoti nivedayitum /
tasmātsvaprakaraṇasthaireva guṇairnirākāṅkṣatvamiti /
evaṃ prāpte pratyāha - asyetanniyame guṇāḥ kvaciduktā vasiṣṭhatvādayo 'nyatrāpi /
kutaḥ - sarvābhedāt /
sarvatraiva hi tadevaikaṃ prāṇavijñānamabhinnaṃ pratyabhijñāyate /
prāṇasaṃvādādisārūpyāt /
abhede ca vijñānasya kathamime guṇāḥ kvaciduktā anyatra nāsyeran /
children.translated_text: In the <s>prāṇa-saṃvāda</s> (dispute of the vital functions) of the <s>Vājins</s> (<s>Vājasaneyins</s>) and the <s>Chandogas</s> (<s>Chāndogyas</s>), the worshipfulness of <s>prāṇa</s> — endowed with the quality of supremacy — is stated. And speech and the other [faculties] too are stated there as endowed with qualities such as '<s>vasiṣṭhatva</s>' (being the most excellent) and the like, and those are re-attributed to <s>prāṇa</s>: 'Whatever excellence I have, you have that [same] excellence' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.14) and so forth. But in the <s>prāṇa-saṃvādas</s> of other <s>śākhins</s> (followers of [Vedic] branches) such as the <s>Kauṣītakins</s> and others — in passages of the kind 'Now, the determination of [what is] best: these deities, disputing among themselves about [their] pre-eminence...' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 2.14) — the supremacy of <s>prāṇa</s> is stated, but these qualities such as '<s>vasiṣṭhatva</s>' and the like are not stated. The question is: Should these qualities such as '<s>vasiṣṭhatva</s>' and the like — stated in one place — be transferred to other places as well, or not? The prima facie view is that they should not be transferred. Why? Because of the connection with the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus). 'Now, he who, knowing thus, knows the supreme [quality of <s>prāṇa</s>]' — in each place, the word '<s>evam</s>' indicates the object to be known. And the word '<s>evam</s>' — which refers to what is proximately available — cannot indicate qualities enumerated in another <s>śākhā</s> [that are not present in its own context]. Therefore, the [meditation is] complete with just the qualities present in its own context. Having set forth this [prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] responds: One should transfer the qualities — such as '<s>vasiṣṭhatva</s>' and the like — stated in one place, to other places as well. Why? Because of the non-difference [of <s>prāṇa</s>] in all [recensions]. For everywhere, the very same, single <s>prāṇa-vijñāna</s> (knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s>) is recognized as non-different — because of the similarity [consisting] of the <s>prāṇa-saṃvāda</s> and the like. And when the <s>vijñāna</s> is non-different, how could these qualities — stated in one place — not apply elsewhere?

children.text: nanvevaṃśabdastatra tatra bhedenaivañjātīyakaṃ guṇajātaṃ vedyatvāya samarpayatītyuktam /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it was said that the word '<s>evam</s>' in each place indicates only a specific set of qualities for the thing to be known [in that place].

children.text:
atrocyate - yadyapi kauṣītakibrāhmaṇagatenaivaṃśabdena vājasaneyibrāhmaṇagataṃ guṇajātamasaṃśabditamasaṃnihitatvāttathāpi tasminneva vijñāne vājasaneyibrāhmaṇagatenaivaṃśabdena tatsaṃśabditamiti na paraśākhāgatamapyabhinnavijñānāvaruddhaṃ guṇajātaṃ svaśākhāgatādviśiṣyate /
nacaivaṃ sati śrutahāniraśrutakalpanā vā bhavati /
ekasyāmapi hi śākhāyāṃ śrutā guṇāḥ śrutā eva sarvatra bhavanti guṇavato bhedābhāvāt /
nahi devadattaḥ śauryādiguṇatvena svadeśe prasiddho deśāntaraṃ gatastaddeśyairavibhāvitaśauryādiguṇo 'pyatadguṇo bhavati /
children.translated_text: For <s>Devadatta</s>, who is well known in his own country for qualities such as valor and the like, does not lose those qualities when he goes to another country — even if the people of that country have not recognized [those qualities of] his.

children.text: yathāca tatra paricayaviśeṣāddeśāntare 'pi devadattaguṇā vibhāvyante /
children.translated_text: And just as, through closer acquaintance, <s>Devadatta</s>'s qualities are recognized in another country as well —

children.text: evamabhiyogaviśeṣācchākhāntare 'pyupāsyā guṇāḥ śākhāntare 'pyasyeran /
children.translated_text: so too, through specific application [of reasoning], the qualities to be meditated upon — [which are mentioned] in another <s>śākhā</s> — should be transferred to yet another <s>śākhā</s>.

children.text: tasmādekapradhānasaṃbaddhā dharmā ekatrāpyucyamānāḥ sarvatraivopasaṃhartavyā iti // 10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the attributes connected with a single principal [entity] — even when stated in one place — should be gathered [and applied] everywhere. // 10 //

To this we say: Even though the word '<s>evam</s>' occurring in the <s>Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa</s> does not directly refer to the set of qualities occurring in the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s> — because they are not mentioned [there] and not proximate — nevertheless, in that very same <s>vijñāna</s> [i.e., the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s>], the word '<s>evam</s>' occurring in the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s> does refer to them. Therefore, the set of qualities occurring in another <s>śākhā</s> — being confined to the same non-different <s>vijñāna</s> — is not distinguished from the [qualities] occurring in one's own <s>śākhā</s>. And in this case, there is neither the abandonment of what is heard nor the postulation of what is unheard. For the qualities heard in even one <s>śākhā</s> are [considered] heard everywhere — because of the non-difference of the qualified [entity, i.e., <s>prāṇa</s>].

children.text: FN: niḥśreyasasya śraiṣṭhyasyādānaṃ nirdhāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Niḥśreyasādāna</s>' means the determination of supremacy.

children.text: ahaṃśreyase svaśraiṣṭhyāya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ahaṃśreyase</s>' means for [establishing] one's own supremacy.

children.text: 6 ānandādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 11-13
children.translated_text: Section 6: <s>Ānandādyadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 11-13

children.text: ānandādayaḥ pradhānasya | BBs_3,3.11 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ānandādayaḥ pradhānasya</s> — [The attributes of] bliss and the rest [belong] to the principal [<s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.11 |

children.text:
brahmasvarūpapratipādanaparāsu śrutiṣvānandarūpatvaṃ vijñānaghanatvaṃ sarvagatatvaṃ sarvātmatvamityevañjātīyakā brahmaṇo dharmāḥ kvacitkecicchrūyante /
teṣu saṃśayaḥ - kimānandādayo brahmadharmā yatra yāvantaḥ śrūyante tāvanta eva tatra pratipattavyāḥ kiṃvā sarve sarvatreti /
tatra yathāśrutivibhāgaṃ dharmapratipattau prāptāyāmidamucyate - ānandādayaḥ pradhānasya brahmaṇo dharmāḥ sarve sarvatra pratipattavyāḥ /
kasmāt /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: sarvābhedādeva /
children.translated_text: Because of the non-difference [of <s>Brahman</s>] in all [passages].

children.text: sarvatra hi tadevaikaṃ pradhānaṃ viśeṣyaṃ brahma na bhidyate /
children.translated_text: For everywhere, the very same, single <s>Brahman</s> — the principal object to be qualified — is not different.

children.text: tasmātsārvatrikatvaṃ brahmadharmāṇāṃ tenaiva pūrvādhikaraṇoditena devadattaśauryadinidarśanena // 11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the universality of <s>Brahman</s>'s attributes [is established] — by the very same illustration of <s>Devadatta</s>'s valor and the like stated in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>. // 11 //

In the <s>śrutis</s> whose purpose is to set forth the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>, such attributes of <s>Brahman</s> as being of the nature of bliss, being a mass of consciousness, being all-pervading, being the Self of all — such qualities are heard, some in some places. The question is: Should the attributes of <s>Brahman</s> such as bliss and the rest be understood only as many as are heard in each particular place, or should all [be understood] everywhere? When the view that attributes should be understood according to each specific <s>śruti</s>-division is prima facie established, this is said: The attributes of bliss and the rest — belonging to the principal <s>Brahman</s> — should all be understood everywhere.

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati priyaśirastvādayo 'pi dharmāḥ sarvatra saṃkīryeran /
tathāhi - taittirīyaka ānandamayamātmānaṃ prakramyāmnāyate - 'tasya priyameva śiraḥ /
modo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ /
pramoda uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ /
ānanda ātmā /
brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' (tai. 2.5) iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But in that case, the attributes of '<s>priyaśirastva</s>' (having joy as the head) and the like would also be mixed in everywhere. For thus, in the <s>Taittirīya</s>, having introduced the <s>ānandamaya</s> Self, [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches: 'Of it, joy (<s>priya</s>) is indeed the head; delight (<s>moda</s>) is the right wing; great delight (<s>pramoda</s>) is the left wing; bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) is the body (<s>ātman</s>); <s>Brahman</s> is the tail, the support' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.5).

children.text: ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the next [<s>sūtra</s>]:

children.text: priyaśirastvādyaprāptirupacayāpacayau hi bhede | BBs_3,3.12 |
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaśirastvādyaprāptirupacayāpacayau hi bhede</s> — The non-applicability of [the attributes of] having joy as the head and the like [elsewhere is established]; for increase and decrease [presuppose] difference. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.12 |

children.text:
priyaśirastvādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ taittirīyaka āmnātānāṃ nāstyanyatra prāptiḥ /
yatkāraṇaṃ priyaṃ modaḥ pramoda ānanda ityete parasparāpekṣayā bhoktrantarāpekṣayā copacitāpacitarūpā upalabhyante /
upacayāpacayau ca sati bhede saṃbhavataḥ /
nirbhedaṃ tu brahma 'ekamevādvitīyam' (chā. 6.2.1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
nacaite priyaśirastvādayo brahmadharmāḥ, kośadharmāstveta ityupadiṣṭamasmābhiḥ 'ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt' (bra.sū. 1.1.12) ityatra /
apica parasminbrahmaṇi cittāvatāropāyamātratvenaite parikalpyante na draṣṭavyatvena /
evamapi sutarāmanyatrāprāptiḥ priyaśirastvādīnām /
brahmadharmāstvetānkṛtvā nyāyamātramidamācāryeṇa pradarśitaṃ priyaśirastvādyaprāptiriti /
sa ca nyāyo 'nyeṣu niściteṣu brahmadharmeṣūpāsanāyopadiśyamāneṣu netavyaḥ saṃyadvāmādiṣu satyakāmādiṣu ca /
teṣu hi satyapyupāsyasya brahmaṇa ekatme prakramabhedādupāsanābhede sati nānyonyadharmāṇāmanyonyatra prāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: For in those cases, even though the object of <s>upāsanā</s> — <s>Brahman</s> — is one, because of the difference of approach [in different meditations], when the <s>upāsanās</s> are different, the attributes of one [meditation] do not apply to another.

children.text: yathā ca dve nāryāvekaṃ nṛpatimupāsate chatreṇaikā cāmareṇānyā tatropāsyaikatve 'pyupāsanābhedo dharmavyavasthā ca bhavetyevamihāpīti /
children.translated_text: And just as two queens serve one king — one with an umbrella and the other with a fly-whisk — even though the object of service is one, the services are different and the attributes [of each service] are distinct; so too here.

children.text: upacitāpacitaguṇatvaṃ hi sati bhedavyavahāre saguṇe brahmaṇyupapadyate na nirguṇe parasminbrahmaṇi /
children.translated_text: For the property of having increasing and decreasing qualities is possible with respect to <s>Brahman</s> with attributes (<s>saguṇa</s>) — in the context of transactional [difference-based] usage — not with respect to the attributeless (<s>nirguṇa</s>) supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ato na satyakāmatvādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kvacicchrutānāṃ sarvatra prāptirityarthaḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the qualities such as being one whose desires are true (<s>satyakāmatva</s>) and the like, which are heard in certain [passages], do not apply everywhere — this is the meaning. // 12 //

The attributes of having joy as the head and the like — taught in the <s>Taittirīya</s> — do not apply elsewhere. The reason is that joy, delight, great delight, and bliss are found to be of increasing and decreasing degree — relative to each other and relative to different classes of experiencers. And increase and decrease are possible only when there is difference. But <s>Brahman</s> is without difference — from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'One only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) and the like. And these attributes of having joy as the head and the like are not attributes of <s>Brahman</s> — rather, they are attributes of the sheaths (<s>kośas</s>), as we have explained in [the discussion of] '<s>Ānandamayo 'bhyāsāt</s>' (<s>BBs</s> 1.1.12). Moreover, regarding the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, these [attributes] are devised merely as a means for the descent of the mind [toward <s>Brahman</s>] — not as [attributes] to be contemplated [as belonging to <s>Brahman</s> itself]. Even so, all the more is there the non-applicability of the attributes of having joy as the head and the like elsewhere. But taking these as attributes of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>ācārya</s> has demonstrated only the principle [that certain attributes do not transfer] through [the example of] 'the non-applicability of having joy as the head and the like.' And this principle should be applied to other well-established attributes of <s>Brahman</s> that are taught for <s>upāsanā</s> — in [meditations] such as <s>Saṃyadvāma</s> and the like, <s>Satyakāma</s> and the like.

children.text: itare tvarthasāmānyāt | BBs_3,3.13 |
children.translated_text: The others, however, [do apply everywhere] because of the commonality of subject matter. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.13 |

children.text: itare tvānandādayo dharmā brahmasvarūpapratipādanāyaivocyamānā arthasāmānyātpratipādyasya brahmaṇo dharmiṇa ekatvātsarve sarvatra pratīyeranniti vaiṣamyaṃ pratipattimātraprayojanā hi ta iti // 13 //
children.translated_text: The others, however — qualities such as bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) and the like — which are stated for the purpose of establishing the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s>, would be recognized everywhere because of the commonality of subject matter — that is, because of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s>, the qualified entity (<s>dharmin</s>) to be taught. The distinction [from the previous case] is that these serve the purpose of apprehension alone. // 13 //

children.text: 7 ādhyānādhikaraṇam / sū. 14-15
children.translated_text: 7 The <s>Ādhyāna</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 14-15.

children.text: ādhyānāya prayojanābhāvāt | BBs_3,3.14 |
children.translated_text: Because there would be no purpose for progressive meditation (<s>ādhyāna</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.14 |

children.text:
kāṭhake hi paṭhyate - 'indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā arthebhyaśca paraṃ manaḥ /
manasastu parā buddhiḥ' (ka. 3.10) ityārabhya 'puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ' (ka. 3.11 ) iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimime sarva evārthādayastatastataḥ paratvena pratipādyanta uta puruṣa evaibhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ paraḥ pratipādyata iti /
tatra tāvatsarveṣāmevaiṣāṃ paratvena pratipādanamiti bhavati matiḥ /
tathāhi śrūyate -
children.translated_text:
For in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] it is stated: 'Higher than the senses are the objects; higher than the objects is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.10) — beginning thus up to 'There is nothing higher than the <s>Puruṣa</s>; that is the culmination, that is the supreme goal' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.11).
A doubt arises there: Are all these — the objects and the like — being taught as progressively higher than the preceding, or is only the <s>Puruṣa</s> alone being taught as higher than all of these?
The initial view is that all of these are being taught as progressively higher.
For thus it is heard —

children.text: idamasmātparamidamasmātparam iti /
children.translated_text: 'This is higher than that, this is higher than that.'

children.text: nanu bahuṣvartheṣu paratvena pratipipādayiṣiteṣu vākyabhedaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: But if many objects are intended to be taught as progressively higher, there would be a division of the sentence [into multiple sentences].

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
vākyabahutvopapatteḥ /
bahūnyevahyetāni vākyāni prabhavanti bahuviṣayānparatvopetānpratipādayitum /
tasmātpratyekameṣāṃ paratvapratipādanamiti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - puruṣa eva hyebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ paraḥ pratipādya iti yuktaṃ na pratyekameṣāṃ paratvapratipādanam /
kasmāt /
prayojanābhāvāt /
nahītareṣu paratvena pratipanneṣu kiñcitprayojanaṃ dṛśyate prayojanaṃ mokṣasiddhiḥ /
tathāca śrutiḥ - 'nicāyya taṃ mṛtyumukhātpramucyate' (ka. 3.15) iti /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'Having determined that, one is freed from the mouth of death' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.15).

children.text: apica parapratiṣedhena kāṣṭhāśabdena ca puruṣaviṣayamādaraṃ darśayanpuruṣapratipattyarthaiva pūrvāparapravāhoktiriti darśayati - ādhyānāyeti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, showing that the emphasis (<s>ādara</s>) is directed toward the <s>Puruṣa</s> through the negation of anything higher and through the word '<s>kāṣṭhā</s>' (culmination), [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] indicates that the sequential mention of prior and later [entities] is solely for the purpose of apprehending the <s>Puruṣa</s> — thus [it is said:] 'for progressive meditation (<s>ādhyāna</s>).'

children.text: ādhyānapūrvakāya samyagdarśanāyetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: for the sake of right vision (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) preceded by progressive meditation (<s>ādhyāna</s>).

children.text: samyagdarśanārthameva hīhādhyānamupadiśyate na tvādhyānameva svapradhānam // 14 //
children.translated_text: For here, progressive meditation is taught for the purpose of right vision alone — not that progressive meditation itself is the primary end. // 14 //

This is not a defect.
Because a plurality of sentences is possible.
For indeed, many sentences are possible, capable of teaching many objects endowed with progressive superiority.
Therefore, the progressive superiority of each of these [is taught individually].
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we reply: It is proper that only the <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is being taught as higher than all these — not the progressive superiority of each individually.
Why?
Because there would be no purpose [for teaching the others individually].
For when the others are understood as progressively superior, no purpose is seen — the purpose [of the teaching] being the attainment of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).

children.text: ātmaśabdāc ca | BBs_3,3.15 |
children.translated_text: And because of the word '<s>Ātman</s>.' | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.15 |

children.text:
itaśca puruṣapratipattyarthaiveyamindriyādipravāhoktiḥ /
yatkāraṇam 'eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhotmā na prakāśate /
dṛśyate tvagryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ' (kaṭha. 3.12) iti prakṛtaṃ puruṣamātmetyāha /
ataścānātmatvamitareṣāṃ vivakṣitamiti gamyate /
tasyaiva ca durvijñānatāṃ saṃskṛtamitigamyatāṃ ca darśayati /
tadvijñānāyaiva 'yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñaḥ' (kaṭha. 3.13) ityādhyānaṃ vidadhāti /
children.translated_text: For the sake of knowing That alone, [the <s>śruti</s>] prescribes progressive meditation: 'The wise one should merge speech into the mind' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.13).

children.text: tadvyākhyatam 'ānumānikamapyekamapyekeṣām' (bra.sū. 1.4.1) ityatra /
children.translated_text: This has been explained in [the discussion of the <s>sūtra</s>]: 'That which is inferred by some' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.4.1).

children.text: evamanekaprakāra āśayātiśayaḥ śruteḥ puruṣe lakṣyate netareṣu /
children.translated_text: Thus, the intentional emphasis (<s>āśayātiśaya</s>) of the <s>śruti</s> is directed toward the <s>Puruṣa</s> in manifold ways — not toward the others.

children.text: apica 'so 'dhvanaḥ pāramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam' (ka. 3.9) ityukte kiṃ tadadhvanaḥ pāraṃ viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padamityasyāmākāṅkṣāyāmindriyādyanukramaṇātparamapadapratipattyartha evāyamāyāma ityavasīyate // 15 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, when it is said 'He reaches the end of the road — that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.9), the question arises: What is that end of the road, that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? In response to this expectation, through the sequential enumeration of the senses and the like, it is ascertained that this entire effort is solely for the purpose of apprehending the supreme abode. // 15 //

And for this further reason, this sequential statement about the senses and the like is for the purpose of apprehending the <s>Puruṣa</s> alone: because [the <s>śruti</s>] calls the <s>Puruṣa</s> under discussion '<s>Ātman</s>' — 'This Self (<s>Ātman</s>), hidden in all beings, does not shine forth; but it is seen by the sharp and subtle intellect of those who see subtly' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.12).
And from this it is understood that the non-Self-hood of the others is intended.
And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows its being difficult to know and its being accessible through purification —

children.text: 8 ātmagṛhītyadhikaraṇam / sū. 16-17
children.translated_text: 8 The <s>Ātmagṛhīti</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 16-17.

children.text: ātmagṛhītir itaravad uttarāt | BBs_3,3.16 |
children.translated_text: The apprehension of the Self [in the <s>Aitareya</s>] is like in the other [<s>Upaniṣads</s>], because of the subsequent [passages]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.16 |

children.text:
aitareyake śrūyate - 'ātmā vā idameka evāgra āsīnnānyatkiñcana miṣatsa īkṣata lokānnu sṛjā' (ai. 1.1) iti 'sa imāṃllokānasṛjatāmbho marīcīrmaramāpaḥ' (ai. 1.2) ityādi /

children.translated_text:
In the <s>Aitareyaka</s> it is heard: 'The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) alone indeed was this in the beginning — one only, nothing else was awake. It thought: Let me create worlds' (<s>Aitareya</s> 1.1); 'It created these worlds — the waters (<s>ambhas</s>), the light-rays (<s>marīci</s>), the mortal [realm] (<s>mara</s>), the waters below (<s>āpas</s>)' (<s>Aitareya</s> 1.2) — and so on.
A doubt arises there: Is it the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) that is denoted by the word '<s>Ātman</s>,' or some other [entity]?
What is the initial view? The supreme Self is not the one denoted here by the word '<s>Ātman</s>.'
Why? Because of the observable sequence of the sentence (<s>vākyānvaya</s>).

children.text: nanu vākyānvayaḥ sutarāṃ paramātmaviṣayo dṛśyate prāgutpatterātmaikatvāvadhāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: But surely the sentence-connection is all the more evidently directed toward the supreme Self, because of the definitive assertion of the oneness of the Self prior to creation.

children.text: īkṣaṇapūrvakasraṣṭṛvacanācca /
children.translated_text: And because of the statement of a creator preceded by deliberation (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>).

children.translated_text: Just as in the other creation-passages — 'From that Self indeed, space arose' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1) — and the like, the supreme Self is apprehended,

children.text: yathā cetarasmiṃllaukikātmaśabdaprayoge pratyagātmaiva mukhya ātmaśabdena gṛhyate tathehāpi bhavitumarhati yatra tu 'ātmaivedamagra āsīt' (bṛ. 1.4.1) ityevamādau 'puruṣavidhaḥ' (bṛ. 1.4.1) ityevamādi viśeṣaṇāntaraṃ śrūyate bhavettatra viśeṣata ātmano grahaṇam /
children.translated_text: and just as in common usage of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (self), it is the inner Self that is primarily denoted by the word '<s>Ātman</s>' — so here too it should be the same. But where [a passage says] 'The Self alone was this in the beginning' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.1) and a further qualifier such as 'in the form of a person' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.1) is heard, there the apprehension of the Self may be particularized on account of that qualifier.

children.text: atra punaḥ paramātmagrahaṇānuguṇameva viśeṣaṇamapyuttaramupalabhyate 'sa īkṣata lokānnu sṛjā iti' (ai. 1.1) 'sa imāṃllokānasṛjata' (ai. 1.2) ityevamādi /
children.translated_text: But here, the qualifier found subsequently is favorable to the apprehension of the supreme Self: 'It thought: Let me create worlds' (<s>Aitareya</s> 1.1); 'It created these worlds' (<s>Aitareya</s> 1.2) — and so on.

children.text: tasmāttasyaiva grahaṇamiti nyāyyam // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper that the supreme Self alone is apprehended [here]. // 16 //

[The pūrvapakṣin] says: No.
Because of the mention of world-creation.
For if the supreme Self were accepted as the creator, the creation of the great elements should be stated first — but here the creation of worlds is stated first.
And worlds are [merely] particular arrangements of the great elements.
And thus [the text] describes the waters (<s>ambhas</s>) and the like as worlds alone: 'That which is above the sky is the waters (<s>ambhas</s>)' (<s>Aitareya</s> 1.2) — and so on.
And world-creation could be [accomplished] by some other lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — one presided over by the supreme Lord — as [in the passage]: 'He was in the form of a person' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.1) and the like.
The <s>smṛti</s> also [says]: 'He is the first embodied being; he is called the <s>Puruṣa</s>; the primordial creator of beings, <s>Brahmā</s>, arose in the beginning.'
The <s>Aitareyins</s> themselves, in the preceding section — 'Now, from the seed of <s>Prajāpati</s>: the seed, the <s>devas</s>' — narrate a variegated creation authored by <s>Prajāpati</s>.
The word '<s>Ātman</s>' too is seen to be applied to that [<s>Prajāpati</s>] — as in: 'The Self alone was this in the beginning, in the form of a person' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.1).
And the definitive assertion of oneness prior to creation can be explained with reference to [the creator's own] modifications.
And deliberation (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>) is possible for him as well, since his sentience is accepted.
Moreover, the specific activities such as 'From those [cows] bring a cow, from those bring a horse, from those bring a person' — and such detailed operations — are observed here as analogous to [activities] of worldly, differentiated individual selves.
Therefore, some differentiated self must be [meant as] '<s>Ātman</s>' here.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we reply: The supreme Self alone is apprehended here by the word '<s>Ātman</s>,' like in the other [<s>Upaniṣads</s>].

children.text: FN: ambhaḥ svargaḥ , marīcayo 'ntarikṣalokaḥ , maro martyalokaḥ , āpaḥ pātālalokaḥ //
children.translated_text: Footnote: <s>Ambhas</s> = the heavenly world; <s>marīci</s> = the intermediate world; <s>mara</s> = the mortal world; <s>āpas</s> = the netherworld. //

children.text:
puruṣavidho narākāraḥ /
ātmā hiraṇyagarbhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the form of a person' (<s>puruṣavidha</s>) means having a human shape. '<s>Ātman</s>' [here refers to] <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.

children.text: retaḥ retaḥkāryam /
children.translated_text: 'Seed' (<s>retas</s>) means the product of the seed.

children.translated_text: If [one objects:] because of the sentence-connection — [we reply:] it would be established because of the definitive assertion. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.17 |

children.translated_text:
The objection that the supreme Self is not apprehended because of the observable sentence-connection — that must be refuted. And to this we say:
It would be established because of the definitive assertion (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>).
The apprehension of the supreme Self would be well-established.
Why? Because of the definitive assertion.
For when the supreme Self is accepted, the definitive assertion of the oneness of the Self prior to creation is straightforward (<s>āñjasa</s>).
Otherwise it would have to be construed non-straightforwardly.
As for the mention of world-creation, I shall connect it as [occurring] after the creation of the great elements that is well-established in other <s>śrutis</s>.
Just as [in the passage] 'That created fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3), I have connected it as [occurring] after the creation of space and air that is well-established in other <s>śrutis</s> — so too here.
For a particular detail well-established in one <s>śruti</s> regarding the same subject must be incorporated into other <s>śrutis</s> [on the same subject].
As for the analogous specific activities such as 'From those, bring a cow' and the like — these too must be understood in conformity with the established purport (<s>vivakṣitārtha</s>).
For it cannot be said that this entire narrative is itself the intended purport, since there would be no human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) in understanding it [as such].
Rather, the identity of the Self with <s>Brahman</s> is what is intended here.
For thus, after teaching the creation of the worlds beginning with the waters (<s>ambhas</s>), of the world-guardians such as <s>Agni</s> and the like, and of the senses and the body as the seat of the senses, that very creator — [thinking] 'How indeed could this [exist] without me?' (<s>Aitareya</s> 3.11) — having reflected thus, shows that he entered this body: 'He split open this very seam and entered through that door' (<s>Aitareya</s> 3.12).
And again, through a prior discrimination of the functions of the senses — 'If it were uttered by speech, if it were breathed by the <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Aitareya</s> 3.12) — and the like, having reflected 'Who then am I?' (<s>Aitareya</s> 3.11), [the text] establishes the realization of the identity of the Self with <s>Brahman</s>: 'He saw this very person as <s>Brahman</s>, the most pervasive' (<s>Aitareya</s> 3.13).
Likewise, subsequently — 'This is <s>Brahman</s>, this is <s>Indra</s>' (<s>Aitareya</s> 5.3) — and so on, having enumerated the entire range of differentiation together with the great elements, [the text] establishes the very realization of the identity of the Self with <s>Brahman</s>: 'All this is guided by consciousness (<s>prajñā</s>), is established in consciousness; the world is guided by consciousness; consciousness is the foundation; consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya</s> 5.3).
Therefore, the apprehension of the Self here [as the supreme Self] is irrefutable.
Alternative interpretation: 'The apprehension of the Self is like in the other [<s>Upaniṣads</s>], because of the subsequent [passages].'
In the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>], beginning with the word '<s>Ātman</s>' — 'Which is the Self? This person made of cognition (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), the light within the <s>prāṇas</s>, the person within the heart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7) — [the text] then establishes its identity with <s>Brahman</s> by teaching that it is free from all attachments.
For thus it concludes: 'This is indeed the great, unborn Self — ageless, undying, immortal, fearless — <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.25).
But in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, beginning without the word '<s>Ātman</s>' — 'Being (<s>Sat</s>) alone, O dear one, was this in the beginning, one only, without a second' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) — [the text] teaches identity at the end: 'That is the Self; that art thou' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7).
A doubt arises: Do these two passages have the same purport, or different purports?
The initial view is that they have different purports, because of the dissimilarity of the passages.
For when there is dissimilarity in the passages, it is not proper to assume identity of meaning — since the determination of meaning depends on the passage [itself].
In the <s>Vājasaneyi</s>, because the word '<s>Ātman</s>' appears at the beginning, it is understood as a teaching about the nature of the Self.
But in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, because the opening is the opposite [i.e., begins with <s>Sat</s>, not <s>Ātman</s>], the teaching too is opposite [in approach].

children.translated_text: And the meaning of the word '<s>sat</s>' (Being), when carefully considered, cannot be anything other than the principal Self — because all other categories of things are established as unreal (<s>anṛta</s>) from the [teaching through] words like '<s>ārambhaṇa</s>' (modification) and the like.

children.text: āmnānavaiṣamyamapi nāvaśyamarthavaiṣamyamāvahati /
children.translated_text: And the difference in wording does not necessarily entail a difference in meaning.

children.text: āhara pātraṃ pātramāharetyevamādiṣvarthasāmye 'pi taddarśanāt /
children.translated_text: For this is observed even where the meaning is the same — as in [expressions like] 'Bring the vessel' and 'The vessel — bring it!' and the like.

children.text: tasmādevañjātīyakeṣu vākyeṣu pratipādanaprakārabhede 'pi pratipādyārthābheda iti siddham // 17 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that in passages of this kind, even when the mode of presentation differs, the meaning presented is the same. // 17 //

True, this has been said.
But [the opponent] thinks that because the conclusion (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) is governed by the opening (<s>upakrama</s>), the conclusion is one of identity-attainment (<s>tādātmyasaṃpatti</s>).
Given this position, it is stated: 'The apprehension as the Self' — 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone, O dear one, was this in the beginning' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1) — here too, for the <s>Chandogas</s>, the apprehension as the Self is proper, just as for the others.
Just as in 'Which is the Self?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.7), the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>' apprehension is as the Self — so too [here].
Why?
Because of the subsequent teaching of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>).
If [it be said that identity follows] from the continuity [of the opening] — [we say:] It would [still follow] because of the definitive statement (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>).
As for the objection that because of the continuity with the opening, and because the word 'Self' is not heard in the opening, the apprehension is not as the Self — what is the response to that?
To that it is said: It would [be proper], because of the definitive statement.
The apprehension as the Self is indeed proper here.
Because of the definitive statement.
For thus — having ascertained that 'By knowing one thing, everything becomes known' — 'That by which the unheard becomes heard, the unthought becomes thought, the unknown becomes known' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.1.1) — with the intention of establishing that, [the <s>śruti</s>] says 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone [was this in the beginning]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.1).
And that [all-knowledge] is accomplished only if the apprehension is as the Self.
Otherwise — if the principal Self were not known — the knowledge of everything would not be accomplished.
