Likewise, the definitive statement of oneness before creation, the reference to the <s>jīva</s> by the word 'Self,' the description of its attainment of its own nature in the state of deep sleep, and the repeated definitive statement 'Thou art That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) preceded by objections — all of this is appropriate only for establishing identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), not for effecting an identity [that does not already exist].
Nor is the objection based on the opening being a general statement valid.
For in the opening, there is neither a statement of Self-hood nor a statement of non-Self-hood.
And a general opening does not conflict with a specific [conclusion] found in the remainder of the passage — because a general statement expects specification.

children.text:
FN: tatamaṃ vyāptatamam /
takāralopaśchāndasaḥ /
children.translated_text:
NOTE: '<s>Tatama</s>' means 'most pervading.'
The elision of the letter '<s>t</s>' is a Vedic (<s>Chāndasa</s>) [form].

children.text: udarka upasaṃhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Udarka</s>' means conclusion (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>).

children.text: 9 kāryākhyānādhikaraṇam / sū. 18
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Kāryākhyānādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Description of What is Already Established). <s>Sūtra</s> 18.

children.text: kāryākhyānādapūrvam | BBs_3,3.18 |
children.translated_text: Because of the description of [an already] established [practice], [the meditation on nakedness of <s>prāṇa</s>] is new (<s>apūrva</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.18 |

children.text:
chandogā vājasaneyinaśca prāṇasaṃvāde śvādisaṃvāde śvādimaryādaṃ prāṇasyānnamāmnānya tasyaivāpo vāsa āmananti /
anantaraṃ ca chandogā āmananti -'tasmādvā etadaśiṣyantaḥ purastāccoṣṭāccādbhiḥ paridadhāti' (chā. 5.2.2) iti /
vājasaneyinastvāmananti - 'tadvidvāṃsaḥ śrotriyā aśiṣyanta ācāmantyaśitvācāmantyetameva tadanamanagnaṃ kurvanto manyante' (bṛ. 6.1.14) 'tasmādevaṃvidaśiṣyannācāmedaśitvā cācāmedetameva tadanamanagnaṃ kurute' iti /
tatra tvācamanamanagnatācintanaṃ ta prāṇasya pratīyate tkimubhayamapi vidhīyata utācamanamevotānagnatācintanameveti vicāryate /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Chandogas</s> and the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, in the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s>, having taught that food is the nourishment of <s>prāṇa</s> — up to the boundary of dogs and the like — teach that water is its garment.
Immediately after, the <s>Chandogas</s> teach: 'Therefore, those who are about to eat and those who have eaten — they surround [the food] with water from both sides' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.2).
But the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> teach: 'Knowing this, the learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, when about to eat, sip water, and after eating, sip water — thinking thereby they make the <s>prāṇa</s> non-naked' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.14); 'Therefore, one who knows thus, when about to eat, should sip water, and after eating, should sip water — thereby one makes it non-naked.'
There, the sipping of water (<s>ācamana</s>) and the contemplation of [<s>prāṇa</s>'s] non-nakedness — both are understood as relating to <s>prāṇa</s>. The question is: Are both enjoined, or only the sipping, or only the contemplation of non-nakedness?

children.text:
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
ubhayamapi caitadapūrvatvādvidhyarham /
athavācamanameva vidīyate /
vispaṣṭā hi tasminvidhivibhaktistasmādevaṃvidaśṣyannācāmedaśitvā cācāmediti /
tasyaiva stutyarthamanagnatāsaṃkīrtanamiti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - nācamanasya vidheyatvamupapadyate kāryākhyānāt /
prāptameva hīdaṃ kāryatvenācamanaṃ prāyatyārthaṃ smṛtiprasiddhamanvākhyāyate /
children.translated_text:
What is the prima facie view?
Both are new (<s>apūrva</s>) and worthy of being enjoined.
Alternatively, only the sipping is enjoined.
For the injunctive verbal ending is clear in that [passage]: 'Therefore, one who knows thus, when about to eat, should sip water, and after eating, should sip water.'
The mention of non-nakedness is merely for praising that [sipping].
Given this position, we say: The sipping cannot be what is enjoined — because of the description of [an already] established [practice].
For this sipping — already established as a duty (<s>kārya</s>) for purification (<s>prāyatya</s>) — is well known from <s>smṛti</s>, and is merely being described [here, not newly enjoined].

children.text: nanviyaṃ śrutistasyāḥ smṛtermūlaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: But might not this <s>śruti</s> be the root [source] of that <s>smṛti</s>?

children.text:
netyucyate /
viṣayanānātvāt /
sāmānyaviṣayā hi smṛtiḥ puruṣamātrasaṃbaddhaṃ prāyatyārthamācamanaṃ prāpayati /
śrutistu prāṇavidyāprakaraṇapaṭhitā tadvaṣayamevācamanaṃ vidadhatī vidadhyāt /
naca bhinnaviṣayayoḥ śrutismṛtyormūlamūlibhāvo 'vakalpate /
naceyaṃ śrutiḥ prāṇavidyāsaṃyogyapūrvamācamanaṃ vidhāsyatīti śakyamāśrayitum /
pūrvasyaiva puruṣamātrasaṃyogina ācamanasyeha pratyabhijñāyamānatvāt /
ata eva ca nobhayavidhānam /
ubhayavidhāne ca vākyaṃ bhidyeta /
tasmātprāptamevāśisiṣatāmaśitavatāṃ cobhayata ācamanamanūdya 'etameva tadanamanagnaṃ kurvanto manyante' (bṛ. 6.1.14) iti prāṇasyānagnatākaraṇasaṃkalpo 'nena vākyenācamanīyāsvapsu prāṇavidyāsaṃbandhitvenāpūrva upadiśyate /
nacāyamanagnatāvāda ācamanastutyartha iti nyāyyam /
ācamanasyāvidheyatvāt /
svayaṃ cānagnatāsaṃkalpasya vidheyatvapratīteḥ /
nacaivaṃ satyekasyācamanasyobhayārthatābhyupagatā bhavati prāyatyārthatā paridhānārthā cheti /
kriyāntaratvābhyupagamāt kriyāntarameva hyācamanaṃ nāma prāyatyārthaṃ puruṣasyābhyupagamyate, tadīyāsu tvapsu vāsaḥsaṃkalpanaṃ nāma kriyāntarameva paridhānārthaṃ prāṇasyābhyupagamyata ityanavadyam /
apica 'yadidaṃ kiñcāśvasya ā kṛmibhya ā kīṭapataṅgebhyastatte 'nnam (bṛ. 6.1.14) ityatra sarvānnābhyavahāraścodyata iti śakyaṃ vaktum /
aśabdatvādaśakyatvācca /
sarvaṃ tu prāṇasyānnamitīyamannadṛṣṭiścodyate tatsāhacaryāccāpo vāsa ityatrāpi nāpāmācamanaṃ codyate prasiddhāsvevatvācamanīyāsvapsu paridhānadṛṣciścodyata iti yuktam /
nahyardhavaiśasaṃ saṃbhavati /
apicācāmantīti vartamānāpadeśitvam śabdo vidhikṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text:
No, it is said.
Because of the difference in subject matter.
For the <s>smṛti</s> is general in scope — it establishes sipping for purification as connected with any person whatsoever.
But the <s>śruti</s>, being read within the context of the <s>Prāṇavidyā</s>, if it were enjoining sipping, would enjoin it only as connected with that [<s>vidyā</s>].
And it is not possible for a <s>śruti</s> and a <s>smṛti</s> with different subject matters to stand as root and derivative.
Nor can this <s>śruti</s> be taken as enjoining sipping as something new that was previously unconnected with the <s>Prāṇavidyā</s>.
Because the very same sipping — previously connected with any person — is recognized here [as already known].
And for this very reason, both are not enjoined [together].
For if both were enjoined, the sentence would be split.
Therefore, having restated the already established sipping — for those about to eat and those who have eaten — on both sides, [the passage] 'thinking thereby they make the <s>prāṇa</s> non-naked' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.14) — by this sentence, the contemplation of making <s>prāṇa</s> non-naked, in connection with the water used for sipping, is taught as something new (<s>apūrva</s>) connected with the <s>Prāṇavidyā</s>.
Nor is it proper [to say] that the statement of non-nakedness is for praising the sipping.
Because the sipping is not being newly enjoined.
And because the contemplation of non-nakedness is itself perceived as what is to be enjoined.
Nor, in this case, is it to be admitted that a single act of sipping serves a dual purpose — purification and clothing [of <s>prāṇa</s>].
Because what is accepted is that they are different actions: the sipping is accepted as one action — for the person's purification — and the contemplation of clothing in the waters [used for sipping] is accepted as a different action — for [the purpose of] clothing <s>prāṇa</s>. This is faultless.
Moreover, in [the passage] 'Whatever food there is — from worms to moths — that is your food' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.14), it cannot be said that the eating of all food is being enjoined.
Because it has no injunctive form, and because it is impossible [to eat all food].
Rather, 'everything is the food of <s>prāṇa</s>' — this is a contemplative view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) of food that is being enjoined. And by association with that, in 'Water is its garment' — here too, it is not the sipping of water that is being enjoined; rather, it is the contemplative view of clothing in the already well-known sipping-waters that is being enjoined. This is proper.
For a half-split [interpretation of the sentence] is not possible.
Moreover, [in the passage] 'they sip' (<s>ācāmanti</s>) — the word, being in the present-tense descriptive form, is not fit for an injunction.

children.text:
nanu manyanta ityapi samānaṃ vartamānāpadeśitvam /
satyamevametat /
avaśyavidheye tvanyatarasminvāsaḥkāryākhyānādapāṃ vāsaḥsaṃkalpanamevāpūrvaṃ vidhīyate nācamanaṃ pūrvavaddhi tadityupapāditam /
yadapyuktaṃ vispaṣṭā cācamane vidhivibhaktiriti tadapi pūrvavattvenaivācamanasya pratyuktam /
ata evācamanasyāvidhitsitatvādetameva tadanamanagnaṃ kurvanto manyanta ityatraiva kāṇvāḥ paryavasyanti nāmananti tasmādevaṃvidityādi /
children.translated_text: For this very reason — because the sipping is not intended to be enjoined — the <s>Kāṇvas</s> conclude with just 'thinking thereby they make it non-naked' and do not read 'Therefore, one who knows thus...' and so forth [which contains the injunctive form for sipping].

children.text: tasmānmādhyandinānāmapi pāṭha ācamanānuvādenaivaṃvittvameva prakṛtaprāṇavāsovittvaṃ vidhīyata iti pratipattavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the reading of the <s>Mādhyandinas</s>, it should be understood that through the restatement of the [already established] sipping, what is being enjoined is the knowledge connected with the <s>Prāṇa</s>-clothing — namely, the status of knowing thus.

children.text: yo 'pyayamabhyupagamaḥ kvacidācamanaṃ vidhīyate kvacidvāsovijñānamiti so 'pi na sādhuḥ /
children.translated_text: And the alternative position — that in one place sipping is enjoined and in another the clothing-contemplation — is also not proper.

children.text: āpo vāsa ityādikāyā vākyapravṛtteḥ sarvatraikarūpyāt tasmādvāsovijñānameveha vidhīyate nācamanamiti nyāyyam // 18 //
children.translated_text: Because the sentence-structure beginning with 'Water is its garment' has the same form everywhere. Therefore, it is proper that only the clothing-contemplation is enjoined here, not the sipping. // 18 //

But [one might say]: 'They think' (<s>manyante</s>) is also equally in the present-tense descriptive form.
True, this is so.
But since one of the two must necessarily be what is enjoined, the contemplation of <s>prāṇa</s>'s clothing in water alone is enjoined as new (<s>apūrva</s>) — not the sipping — because the latter is already established, as has been demonstrated.

children.text: 10 samānādhikaraṇam / sū. 19
children.translated_text: 10. The <s>Samānādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Same [<s>Vidyā</s>]). <s>Sūtra</s> 19.

children.text: samāna evaṃ cābhedāt | BBs_3,3.19 |
children.translated_text: It is the same [<s>vidyā</s>] — and thus, because of non-difference [of the object]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.19 |

children.text:
vājasaneyiśākhāyamaginirahasye śāṇḍulyanāmāṅ kitā vidyā vijñātā /
tatra ca guṇāḥ śrūyante - sa ātmānamupāsīta manamayaṃ prāṇaśarīraṃ bhārūpam ityevamādayaḥ. tasyāmeva śāstrāyāṃ bṛhadāraṇyake punaḥ paṭhyate - 'manomayo 'yaṃ puruṣo bhāḥ satyasminnantarhadaye yadā vrīhirvā yavo vā sa eṣa sarvasyeśānaḥ sarvasyādhipatiḥ sarvamidaṃ praśāsti yadidaṃ kiñca' (bṛ. 5.6.1) iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimiyamekā vidyāgnirahasyabṛhadāraṇyakayorguṇopasaṃhāraścota dve ime vidye guṇānupasaṃhāraśceti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
vidyābhedo guṇavyavasthā ceti /
kutaḥ - paunaruktyaprasaṅgāt /
bhinnāsu hi śākhāsvadhyetṛbhedātpaunaruktasyaparihāramālocya vidyaikatvamadhyavasāyaikatrātiriktā guṇā itaratropasaṃhriyante prāṇasaṃvādādiṣvatyuktam /
ekasyāṃ punaḥ śākhāyāmadhyetṛveditṛbhedābhāvādaśakyaparihāre paunaruktye na viprakṛṣṭadeśasthaikā vidyā bhavitumarhati /
nacātraikamāmnānaṃ vidyāvidhānārthamaparaṃ guṇavidhānārthamiti vibhāgaḥ saṃbhavati /
tadā hyatiriktā eva guṇā itaratretaratra cāmnāyeranna samānā api tūbhayatrāmnāyante manomayatvadayaḥ /
tasmānnānyonyaṃ guṇopasaṃhāra iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmahe - yathā bhinnāsu śākhāsu vidyaikatvaṃ guṇopasaṃhāraśca bhavatyevamekasyāmapi śākhāyāṃ bhavitumarhati /
upāsyābhedāt tadeva hi brahma manomayatvādiguṇakamubhayatrāpyupāsyamabhinnaṃ pratyabhijānīmaḥ /
upāsyaṃ ca rūpaṃ vidyāyāḥ /
naca vidyamāne rūpābhede vidyābhedamadhyavasātuṃ śaknumaḥ /
nāpi vidyābhede guṇavyavasthānam /
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> recension, in the <s>Agnirahasya</s>, a <s>vidyā</s> named after <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> is known.
And the following attributes are heard there: 'One should meditate on the Self as mind-made (<s>manomaya</s>), having <s>prāṇa</s> as its body, having light as its form' and so forth.
In that very same recension, in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, it is again read: 'This person is mind-made, of the nature of light, of the nature of truth, within the inner space of the heart, like a grain of rice or barley — this one is the ruler of all, the lord of all, he governs all that there is' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.6.1).
There arises a doubt: Is this one single <s>vidyā</s> in both the <s>Agnirahasya</s> and the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, with a mutual inclusion of attributes, or are these two [different] <s>vidyās</s> without mutual inclusion of attributes?
What is the prima facie view?
That they are different <s>vidyās</s>, with a fixed distribution of attributes.
Why? Because of the consequence of repetition (<s>punarukti</s>).
For it has been said that in different <s>śākhās</s>, considering that repetition can be resolved because of the difference of students, the unity of the <s>vidyā</s> is determined, and attributes that are additional in one [<s>śākhā</s>] are included in the other — as in the <s>Prāṇasaṃvāda</s> and the like.
But within a single <s>śākhā</s>, since there is no difference of students and learners, repetition — which cannot be resolved — makes it improper to regard a <s>vidyā</s> taught in distant passages as one.
And here, the division that 'one teaching is for enjoining the <s>vidyā</s> and the other for enjoining attributes' is not possible.
For then, only additional attributes would be taught in the other [passage], not attributes common [to both] — but [in fact] common attributes like 'mind-made' and the like are taught in both.
Therefore, there is no mutual inclusion of attributes.
Given this position, we say: Just as in different <s>śākhās</s> there is unity of the <s>vidyā</s> and inclusion of attributes, so too even within a single <s>śākhā</s> this should be the case.
Because of the non-difference of the object of meditation (<s>upāsya</s>). For we recognize that the same <s>Brahman</s>, qualified by attributes such as 'mind-made' and the like, is the undifferentiated object of meditation in both [passages].
And the object of meditation is the form of the <s>vidyā</s>.
And when there is no difference in form, we cannot determine a difference in the <s>vidyā</s>.
Nor, if the <s>vidyā</s> is one, is there a fixed distribution of attributes [between the two passages].

children.text: nanu paunaruktyaprasaṅgadvidyābhedo 'dhyavasitaḥ /
children.translated_text: But was not the difference of <s>vidyā</s> determined because of the consequence of repetition?

children.text:
netyucyate /
arthavibhāgopapatteḥ /
ekaṃ hyāmnānaṃ vidyāvidyāvidhānārthamaparaṃ guṇavidhānārthamiti na kiñcinnopapadyate /
children.translated_text:
No, it is said.
Because a division of purpose is possible.
For [saying] that one teaching is for enjoining the <s>vidyā</s> and the other is for enjoining attributes — nothing in this is untenable.

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati yadupaṭhimagnirahasye tadeva bṛhadāraṇyake paṭhitavyam sa eṣa sarvasyeśānaḥ ityādi /
yattu paṭhitameva manomaya ityādi cenna paṭhitavyam /
children.translated_text: But if this is so, then what is taught in the <s>Agnirahasya</s> [should be the vidyā-portion], and [only] 'This one is the ruler of all' and the like — which is read in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> — [should be the attribute-portion]. But what is already read — 'mind-made' and the like — should not be read [again].

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
tadbalenaiva pradeśāntarapaṭhitavidyāpratyabhijñānāt /
masānaguṇāmnānena hi viprakṛṣṭadeśāṃ śāṇḍilyavidyāṃ pratyabhijñāpya tasyāmīśānatvādyupadiśyate /
children.translated_text: For by teaching the common attributes, the <s>Śāṇḍilyavidyā</s> taught in a distant passage is made recognizable, and [then] attributes such as 'lordship' and the like are taught for that [<s>vidyā</s>].

children.text: anyathā hi kathaṃ tasyāmayaṃ guṇavidhirabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: For otherwise, how would this teaching of attributes be stated as pertaining to that [<s>vidyā</s>]?

children.text: apicāprāptāṃśopadeśenārthavati vākye saṃjāte prāptāṃśaparāmarśasya nityānuvādatayāpyupapadyamānatvānna tadbalena pratyabhijñopodituṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, once the sentence becomes purposeful through the teaching of the un-obtained portion [i.e., new attributes], the mention of the already-obtained portion — being naturally explicable as mere restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) — cannot be used as a basis to block recognition [of the <s>vidyā</s>].

children.text: tasmādatra samānāyāmapi śākhāyāṃ vidyaikatvaṃ guṇopasaṃhāraścetyupapannam // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even within the same <s>śākhā</s>, the unity of the <s>vidyā</s> and the inclusion of attributes are well established. // 19 //

This is not a fault.
Because the recognition of the <s>vidyā</s> taught in the other passage is accomplished precisely by the force of those [common attributes].

children.text: 11 saṃbandhādhikaraṇam / sū. 20-21
children.translated_text: 11. The <s>Saṃbandhādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Connection). <s>Sūtras</s> 20-21.

children.text: saṃbandhādevamanyatrāpi | BBs_3,3.20 |
children.translated_text: Because of the connection, likewise elsewhere too. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.20 |

children.text:
bṛhadāraṇyake 'satyaṃ brahma' (bṛ. 5.5.1) ityukramya 'tadyattatsatyamasau sa ādityo ya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣo yaścāyaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣaḥ' (bṛ. 55.2) iti tasyaiva satyasya brahmaṇo 'dhidaivatamadhyātmaṃ cāyatanaviśeṣamupadiśya vyāhṛtiśarīratvaṃ ca saṃpādya dve upaniṣadāvupadiśyete /
tasyopaniṣaharityadhidaivatam /
tasyopaniṣadahamityadhyātmam /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimavibhāgenaivobhe apyupaniṣadāvubhayatrānusaṃgātavye uta vibhāgenaikādhidaivamekādhyātmamiti /
tatra sūtreṇaivopakramate /
yathā śāṇḍilyavidyāyāṃ vibhāgenāpyadhītāyāṃ guṇopasaṃhāra ukta evamanyatrāpyevañjātīyake viṣaye bhavitumarhati /
ekavidyābhisaṃbandhāt /
ekā hīyaṃ satyavidyādhidaivamadhyātmaṃ cādhītā /
upakramābhedādvyatiṣaktapāṭhācca /
kathaṃ tasyāmudito dharmastasyāmeva na syāt /
children.translated_text: How could an attribute taught in a particular [meditation] not apply in that very [meditation]?

children.text: yohyācāryo kaścidanugamanādirācāraścoditaḥ sa grāmagate /
children.translated_text: For a prescribed conduct such as following the teacher and the like — that applies equally whether [the teacher] is in a village

children.text: raṇyagate ca tulyavadeva bhavati /
children.translated_text: or in a forest.

children.text: tasmādubhayorapyupaniṣadorubhayatra prāptiriti // 20 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, both <s>upaniṣads</s> (secret teachings) apply in both [locations] — this [is the prima facie view]. // 20 //

In the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>, having introduced '<s>Brahman</s> is Truth (<s>satya</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.1), and having then taught particular loci — cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) and individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) — of that very Truth which is <s>Brahman</s>: 'That which is Truth — that is the sun, and the person within that orb, and the person in the right eye' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.2) — and having established for it a body consisting of the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), two secret names (<s>upaniṣads</s>) are taught.
'Its secret name is <s>ahar</s>' — this is the cosmic [name].
'Its secret name is <s>aham</s>' — this is the individual [name].
There arises a doubt: Are both secret names to be connected with both [loci] without distinction, or distinctly — one cosmic and one individual?
There, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] begins with the <s>sūtra</s> itself.
Just as in the <s>Śāṇḍilyavidyā</s>, even though taught separately, the inclusion of attributes was stated — so too elsewhere, in topics of this kind, it should be the case.
Because of the connection with one single <s>vidyā</s>.
For this is one single <s>Satyavidyā</s> (meditation on Truth), taught both in its cosmic and individual aspects.
Because of the non-difference of the opening and because of the interwoven reading.

children.text: evaṃ prāpte pratividhatte -
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the prima facie view, [the sūtrakāra] responds:

children.text: na vā viśeṣāt | BBs_3,3.21 |
children.translated_text: Or not, because of the specific distinction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.21 |

children.text:
na vobhayorubhayatra prāptiḥ /
kasmāt /
viśeṣāt /
upāsanasa atānaviśeṣopanibandhādityarthaḥ /
kathaṃ sthānaviśeṣopanibandha ityucyate - 'ya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣaḥ' (bṛ. 5.5.3) iti hyādhidaivakaṃ puruṣaṃ prakṛtya tasyopaniṣadahariti śrāvayati /
'yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣaḥ' (5.5.4) iti hyadhyātmikaṃ puruṣaṃ prakṛtya tasyopaniṣadamiti /
tasyeti caitatsaṃnihitāvalambanaṃ sarvanāma, tasmādāyatanaviśeṣavyapāśrayeṇaivaite upaniṣadāvupadiśyete /
kuta ubhayorubhayatra prāptiḥ /
children.translated_text:
Or, there is no application of both [upaniṣads] in both [locations].
Why?
Because of the specific distinction.
The meaning is: because the meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) is tied to a specific location (<s>sthāna</s>).
How is it tied to a specific location? It is said: 'The person who is in this [solar] disc' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.3) — having introduced the cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) person, [the śruti] teaches the secret teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>) of that one as 'ahar' (day).
'The person who is in the right eye' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.4) — having introduced the individual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) person, [the śruti teaches] the secret teaching of that one.
And 'tasya' (of that one) is a pronoun depending on what is proximate — therefore, these two secret teachings are taught specifically with reference to their respective locations.
How could both apply in both [locations]?

children.text: nanveka evāyamadhidaivatamadhyātmaṃ ca puruṣa ekasyaiva satyasya brahmaṇa āyatanadvayapratipādanāt /
children.translated_text: But is this not one and the same person, both cosmically and individually, since a single true <s>Brahman</s> is being taught as having two locations?

children.text:
satyamevetat /
ekasyāpi tvavasthāviśeṣopādānenaivopaniṣadviśeṣopadeśāttadavasthāsyaiva sā bhavitumarhati /
asti cāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ satyapyācāryasvarūpāpānapāye yadācāryasyāsīnasyanuvartanamuktaṃ na tattiṣṭhato bhavati /
children.translated_text: And there is this illustration: Even though the teacher's essential nature does not change, the conduct prescribed for when the teacher is seated does not apply when he is standing.

children.text: yacca tiṣṭhata uktaṃ na tadāsīnasyeti /
children.translated_text: And what is prescribed for when he is standing does not apply when he is seated.

children.text: grāmāraṇyayostvācāryasvarūpānāpāyāttatsvarūpānubuddhasya ca dharmasya grāmāraṇyakṛtaviśeṣābhāvādubhayatra tulyavadbhāva ityadṛṣṭāntaḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: But in the case of village and forest, since the teacher's essential nature does not change, and since the prescribed conduct — being understood with reference to the teacher's nature [itself] — has no specific difference caused by village or forest, there is equal applicability in both — that [is the illustration]. That was a non-analogous case.

children.text: tasmādvyavasthānayorupaniṣadoḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, these two secret teachings are [to be kept] distinct. // 21 //

That is indeed true.
But even for one [entity], since the specific secret teaching is instructed by specifying a particular state, that [teaching] should belong to that particular state alone.

children.text: darśayati ca | BBs_3,3.22 |
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows [this]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.22 |

children.text:
api caivañjātīyakānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vyavastheti liṅgadarśanaṃ bhavati - 'tasyaitasya tadeva rūpaṃ yāvamuṣya geṣṇau tau geṣṇau yannāma tannāma' (chā. 1.7.5) iti /
kathamasyaliṅgatvamiti taducyate /
children.translated_text:
Moreover, there is an indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>) that attributes of this kind are [to be kept] distinct: 'Of this one, that alone is the form which is the form of the other; the chants of the other are its chants; the name [of the other] is its name' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.5).
How is this an indicatory sign? It is explained:

children.text: akṣyādinityasthānabhedabhinnāndharṇānanyonyasminnanupasaṃhāryānpaśyannihātideśenādityapuruṣagatānrūpādīnakṣipuruṣa upasaṃharati - 'tasyaitasya tadeva rūpam' (chā. 1.7.5) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: Observing the attributes — which are differentiated by the permanent difference of location such as the eye and the like, and which are not to be transferred to one another — [the śruti] here, by extension (<s>atideśa</s>), transfers the form and the like belonging to the solar person to the eye-person: 'Of this one, that alone is the form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.5) — and so on.

children.text: tasmādvyavasthite evaite upaniṣadāviti nirṇayaḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the conclusion is that these two secret teachings are indeed distinct. // 22 //

children.text: 12 saṃbhṛtyadhikaraṇam / sū. 23
children.translated_text: 12 The <s>Saṃbhṛti</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 23.

children.text: saṃbhṛtidyuvyāptyapi cātaḥ | BBs_3,3.23 |
children.translated_text: The [attributes of] gathering of powers, pervading the sky, and the like too — [are not to be transferred] for the same reason. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.23 |

children.text:
brahmajyeṣṭhā viryā saṃbhṛtāni brahmāgre jyeṣṭhaṃ divamātatāna ityevaṃ rāṇāyanīyānāṃ khileṣu vīryasaṃbhṛtidyuniveśaprabhṛtayo brahmaṇo vibhūtayaḥ paṭhyante /
teṣāmeva copaniṣadi śāṇḍilyavidyāprabhṛtayo brahmavidyāḥ paṭhyante /
tāsu brahmavidyāsu tā brahmavibhūtaya upasaṃhriyeranna veti vicāraṇāyāṃ brahmasaṃbandhādupasaṃhāraprāptāvevaṃ paṭhati /
saṃbhṛtidyuvyāptiprabhṛtayo vibhūtayaḥ śāṇḍilyavidyāprabhṛtiṣu nopasaṃhartavyāḥ /
ata eva cāyatanaviśeṣayogāt /
tathāhi śāṇḍilyavidyāyāṃ hṛdayāyatanatvaṃ brahmaṇa uktam - 'eṣa ma ātmāntarhṛdaye' (chā. 3.14.3) iti /
tadvadeva daharavidyāyāmapi 'daharaṃ puṇḍarīke veśma daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ' (chā. 8.1.1) iti /
upakosalavidyāyāṃ tvakṣyāyatanatvam 'ya eṣo 'kṣaṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā. 4.15.1) iti /
evaṃ tatra tatrat tadādhyātmikamāyatanametāsu vidyāsu pratīyate /
ādhidaivikyastvetā vibhūtayaḥ saṃbhṛtidyuvyāptiprabhṛtayastāsāṃ kuta etāsu prāptiḥ /
children.translated_text:
In the supplementary (<s>khila</s>) [portions] of the <s>Rāṇāyanīyas</s>, the glories (<s>vibhūti</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> such as the gathering of powers, establishment in the sky, and the like are stated: '<s>Brahman</s> is the eldest; powers are gathered; <s>Brahman</s>, the eldest, pervaded the sky.'
And in their <s>Upaniṣad</s>, <s>brahmavidyās</s> (forms of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) such as the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> meditation and the like are taught.
The question arises whether those glories of <s>Brahman</s> should be incorporated into those <s>brahmavidyās</s> or not. When the view that they should be incorporated — because of their connection with <s>Brahman</s> — is prima facie established, [the sūtrakāra] states:
The glories of gathering of powers, pervading the sky, and the like should not be incorporated into the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> meditation and the like.
And for this very reason — because of the association with a specific location.
For thus, in the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> meditation, the heart is stated as the location of <s>Brahman</s>: 'This is my Self within the heart' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.3).
Likewise in the <s>Dahara</s> meditation: 'In the small lotus is an abode; in it is a small inner space' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1).
But in the <s>Upakosala</s> meditation, the eye is the location: 'The person who is seen in the eye' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.1).
Thus, in each of these meditations, an individual (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) location is recognized.
But these glories — gathering of powers, pervading the sky, and the like — are cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>). How could they apply to these [individual-location meditations]?

children.text:
nanvetāsvapyādhidaivikyo vibhūtayaḥ śrūyante - 'jyāyāndivo jyāyānebhyo lokebhyaḥ' (chā. 3.14.3) 'eṣa u eva bhāmanīreṣa hi sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti' (chā. 4.15.4) 'yāvānvā ayamākāśastāvāneṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśa ubhe asmindyāvāpṛthivī antareva samāhite' (chā. 8.1.3) ityevamādyāḥ /
santi cānyā āyatanaviśeṣahīnā apīha brahmavidyāḥ ṣoḍaśakalādyāḥ /
satyametat /
tathāpyatra vidyate viśeṣaḥ saṃbhṛtyādyanupasaṃhārahetuḥ /
samānaguṇāmnānena hi pratyupasthāpitāsu viprakṛṣṭadeśāsvapi vidyāsu viprakṛṣṭadeśā guṇā upasaṃhriyeranniti yuktam /
saṃbhṛtyādayastu śāṇḍilyādivākyagocarāśca manomayatvādayo guṇāḥ parasparavyāvṛttasvarūpatvānna pradeśāntaravartividyāpratyupasthāpanamityucyate vidyābhede 'pi tadupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: It is stated that even though the meditations [may be about] the same <s>Brahman</s>, this [non-incorporation] is tenable because the two [sets of attributes] do not recall each other — due to their being mutually distinct in nature — and even when the <s>vidyā</s> is the same [in subject], this is appropriate.

children.text: ekamapi hi brahma vibūtibhedairanekadhopāsyata iti sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: For the established position is that even a single <s>Brahman</s> is contemplated in manifold ways through different glories.

children.text: parovarīyastavādivadbhedadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the observation of difference, as in [the discussion of] the greater and lesser [meditations].

children.text: tasmādvīryasaṃbhṛtyādīnāṃ śāṇḍilyavidyādiṣvanupasaṃhāra iti // 23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the gathering of powers and the like are not to be incorporated into the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> meditation and the like. // 23 //

But are not cosmic glories heard in these [meditations] as well? — 'Greater than the sky, greater than these worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.3); 'This indeed is <s>Bhāmanī</s>; for it shines in all worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.4); 'As vast as this space is, so vast is this space within the heart; in it both heaven and earth are contained' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.3) — and the like.
And there are other <s>brahmavidyās</s> here that are devoid of a specific location — such as the <s>Ṣoḍaśakala</s> (sixteen-part) [meditation] and the like.
This is true.
Nevertheless, there is a distinction here that provides the reason for not incorporating the gathering of powers and the like.
For when meditations [taught] even in distant locations are brought to mind through the recitation of common attributes, it is proper that distant attributes too are incorporated.
But the gathering of powers and the like, and the attributes such as being made of mind (<s>manomayatva</s>) and the like that fall within the scope of the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and similar passages — since they are mutually distinct in nature — [we say:] they do not bring to mind meditations found in other places.

children.text:
FN: brahmajyeṣṭhā brahmajyeṣṭhāni nilopaśchāndasaḥ /
vīryā vīryāṇi parākramabhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Brahmajyeṣṭhā</s>' means '<s>brahmajyeṣṭhāni</s>' — the dropping of the nasal is Vedic usage. '<s>Vīryā</s>' means '<s>vīryāṇi</s>' — various forms of power.

children.text: 13 puruṣādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 24
children.translated_text: 13 The <s>Puruṣādi</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 24.

children.text: puruṣavidyāyāmiva cetareṣām anāmnānāt | BBs_3,3.24 |
children.translated_text: As in the <s>Puruṣavidyā</s>, [the attributes] of the others [are not to be transferred], because they are not mentioned [there]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.24 |

children.text:
asti tāṇḍināṃ paiṅgināṃ ca rahasyabrāhmaṇe puruṣavidyā /
tatra puruṣo yajñaḥ kalpitaḥ /
tadīyamāyustredhā vibhajya savanatrayaṃ kalpitam /
aśiśiṣādīni ca dīkṣādibhāvena kalpitāni /
anye ca dharmastatra samadhigatā āśīrmantraprayogādayaḥ /
taittirīyakā api kañcitpuruṣayajñaṃ kalpayanavti - 'tasyaivaṃ viduṣo yajñasyātmā yajamānaḥ śraddhā patnī' (nārā. 80) ityetenānuvākena /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ ya itaratroktāḥ puruṣayajñasya dharmāste taittirīyakeṣūpasaṃhartavyāḥ kiṃvā nopasaṃhartavyā iti /
puruṣayajñatvviśeṣādupasaṃhāraprāptāvācakṣmahe - nopasaṃhartavyā iti /
kasmāt /
tadrūpapratyabhijñānābhāvāt /
tadāhācāryaḥ - puruṣavidyāyāmiveti /
yathaikeṣāṃ śākhināṃ tāṇḍināṃ paiṅgināṃ ca puruṣavidyāyāmāmnānaṃ naivamitareṣāṃ taittirīyāṇāmāmnānamasti /
teṣāṃ hūtaravilakṣaṇameva yajñasaṃpādanaṃ dṛśyate patnīyajamānavedavedibarhiryūpājyaśvṛtvigādyanukramaṇāt /
yadapi savanasaṃpādanaṃ tadapītaravilakṣaṇameva 'yatprātarmadhyandinaṃsāyaṃ ca tāni' (nārā. 80) iti /
yadapi kiñcinmaraṇāvabhṛthatvādisāmyaṃ tadapyalpīyastavādbhūyasā vailakṣaṇyenābhibhūyamānaṃ na pratyabhijñāpanakṣamam /
naca taittirīyake puruṣasya yajñatvaṃ śrūyate /
viduṣo yajñasyeti hi nacaite samānādhikaraṇe ṣaṣṭhyau vidvāneva yoyajñastasyeti /
nahi puruṣasya mukhyaṃ yajñatvamasti /
vyadhikaraṇe tvete ṣaṣṭhyau viduṣo yo yajñastasyeti /
bhavati hi puruṣasya mukhyo yajñasaṃbandhaḥ /
satyāṃ ca gatau mukhya evārtha āśrayitavyo na bhāktaḥ /
ātmā yajamāna iti ca yajamānatvaṃ puruṣasya nirbruvanvaiyadhikaraṇyenaivāsya yajñasaṃbandhaṃ darśayati /
apica tasyaivaṃviduṣaiti siddhavadanuvādaśrutau satyāṃ puruṣasya yajñabhāvamātmādīnāṃ ca yajamānādibhāvaṃ pratipitsamānasya vākyabhedaḥ syāt /
apica saṃsanyāsāmātmavidyāṃ purastādupadiśyānantaraṃ tasyaivaṃviduṣa ityādyanukramaṇaṃ phasyantaḥ pūrvaśeṣa evaiṣa āmnāyo na svatantra iti pratīmaḥ /
tathācaikameva phalamubhayorapyanuvākayorupalabāmahe 'brahmaṇo mahimānamāpnoti' (nārā. 80) iti /
children.translated_text: And accordingly, we find one and the same result for both <s>anuvākas</s>: 'He attains the greatness of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> 80).

children.text: itareṣāṃ tvananyaśeṣaḥ puruṣavidyāmnāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣavidyā</s> passage of the others [the <s>Tāṇḍins</s> and <s>Paiṅgins</s>], however, is not a supplement to anything else.

children.text: āyurabhivṛddhiphalo hyasau 'sa ha --ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśataṃ jīvati ya evaṃ veda' (chā. 3.16.7) iti samabhivyāhārāt /
children.translated_text: For that [<s>Puruṣavidyā</s>] has the fruit of the extension of life-span, as is evident from the co-occurring statement: 'He who knows thus lives a hundred and sixteen years' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.16.7).

children.text: tasmācchākhāntarādhītānāṃ puruṣavidyādharmāṇāmāśīrmantrādīnāmaprāptistaittirīyake // 24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the attributes of the <s>Puruṣavidyā</s> — such as the benedictory hymns and the like — which are learned in another school, do not apply in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>. // 24 //

There is a <s>Puruṣavidyā</s> (meditation on the person as sacrifice) in the esoteric <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Tāṇḍins</s> and the <s>Paiṅgins</s>.
There, the person is imagined as a sacrifice.
His life-span, divided into three parts, is imagined as the three <s>savanas</s> (pressings).
Hunger and the like are imagined as [corresponding to] consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and the like.
And other attributes are also found there — such as the use of benedictory hymns (<s>āśīrmantra</s>) and the like.
The <s>Taittirīyakas</s> too devise a certain person-sacrifice: 'Of the sacrifice of one who knows thus — the Self is the sacrificer, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is the wife' (<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> 80) — by means of this <s>anuvāka</s>.
A doubt arises: Should the attributes of the person-sacrifice stated elsewhere be incorporated into the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>, or not?
When the view that they should be incorporated — because of the common feature of being a person-sacrifice — is prima facie established, we say: They should not be incorporated.
Why?
Because of the absence of recognition of the same form.
The <s>ācārya</s> states this: 'As in the <s>Puruṣavidyā</s>.' —
Just as the <s>Puruṣavidyā</s> as taught by certain schools — the <s>Tāṇḍins</s> and <s>Paiṅgins</s> — is so taught [in their recension], it is not so taught for the others, the <s>Taittirīyakas</s>.
For their sacrifice-construction is seen to be entirely different from the other, given the enumeration of wife, sacrificer, Vedas, altar, sacrificial grass, post, clarified butter, officiating priests, and the like.
And the construction of the <s>savanas</s> too is entirely different from the other: 'The morning, midday, and evening [are those]' (<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> 80).
And whatever slight similarity there may be — such as death being [imagined as] the final bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) — that too, being minor, is overwhelmed by the preponderant dissimilarity and is not capable of establishing recognition [of identity].
Moreover, in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>, the person is not heard [as being] the sacrifice [directly]. For [the text says] 'the sacrifice of the knower' — and these two genitives are not in co-reference (i.e., it does not say 'the knower who is the sacrifice'); rather, [it means] 'the sacrifice belonging to the knower.'
For the person does not have the primary nature of a sacrifice.
But these genitives are in different reference — 'the sacrifice belonging to the knower.'
For the person does have a primary relation with sacrifice [as its performer].
And when a primary meaning is possible, one should resort to the primary sense, not the secondary.
And by saying 'the Self is the sacrificer,' [the text] shows the person's relation to sacrifice precisely through different reference — [i.e., as performer, not as being the sacrifice itself].
Furthermore, since the statement 'of one who knows thus' is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) presupposing something already established, anyone wishing to establish [both] the person's being the sacrifice and the Self and the like's being the sacrificer and the like would face a splitting of the sentence [i.e., the sentence could not bear both meanings simultaneously].
Moreover, since the <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) form of self-knowledge is taught first, and the subsequent enumeration beginning with 'of one who knows thus' follows, we understand that this latter passage is merely a supplement to the former — not an independent [teaching].

children.text: 14 vedhādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 25
children.translated_text: 14 The <s>Vedhādi</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 25.

children.text: vedhādyarthabhedāt | BBs_3,3.25 |
children.translated_text: Because of the difference in purpose of the piercing (<s>vedha</s>) and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.25 |

children.text:
astyātharvaṇikānāmupaniṣadārambhe mantrasamāmnāyaḥ - 'sarvaṃ pravidhya hṛdayaṃ pravidhya dhamanīḥ pravṛjya śiro 'bhipravṛjyatridhā vipṛktaḥ' ityādiḥ /
tāṇḍinām - 'deva savitaḥ prasuva yajñam' ityādiḥ /
śāṭhyāyaninām - 'śvetāśvo haritanīlo 'si' ityādiḥ /
kaṭhānāṃ taittirīyāṇāṃ - 'śaṃ no mitraḥ śaṃ varuṇaḥ' (tai. 1.1.1) ityādiḥ /
vājasaneyināṃ tūpaniṣadārambhe pravargyabrāhmaṇaṃ paṭhyate - 'devā ha vai niṣeduḥ' ityādi /
kauṣītakināmapyagniṣṭomabrāhmaṇam - 'brahma vā agniṣṭomo brahmaiva tadaharbrahmaṇaiva te brahmopayanti te 'mṛtatvamāpnuvanti ya etadaharupayanti' iti /
kimime sarve pravidhyamādayo mantrāḥ pravargyādīni ca karmāṇi vidyāsūpasaṃhriyerankiṃvā nopasaṃhriyeranniti mīmāṃsāmahe /
kiṃ tāvannaḥ pratibhāti upasaṃhāra evaiṣāṃ vidyāsviti /
kutaḥ /
vidyāpradhānānāmupaniṣadgranthānāṃ samīpe pāṭhāt /
children.translated_text:
At the beginning of the <s>Upaniṣad</s> of the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s>, there is a recitation of mantras: 'Having pierced through everything, having pierced through the heart, having pierced through the channels (<s>dhamanī</s>), having pierced through the head, divided threefold' — and so on.
Of the <s>Tāṇḍins</s>: 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel the sacrifice' — and so on.
Of the <s>Śāṭhyāyanins</s>: 'You are the white horse, the tawny one, the dark one' — and so on.
Of the <s>Kaṭhas</s> and <s>Taittirīyakas</s>: 'May <s>Mitra</s> be propitious to us, may <s>Varuṇa</s> [be propitious]' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.1.1) — and so on.
But at the beginning of the <s>Upaniṣad</s> of the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, the <s>Pravargya</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is recited: 'The gods indeed sat down' — and so on.
And of the <s>Kauṣītakins</s>, the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: '<s>Brahman</s> indeed is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; <s>Brahman</s> indeed is that day; by <s>Brahman</s> alone they approach <s>Brahman</s>; they attain immortality — those who approach that day.'
Should all these mantras beginning with the piercing, and the rituals such as <s>Pravargya</s> and the like, be incorporated into the meditations (<s>vidyās</s>) or not? — this is the inquiry.
What is our initial view? That they should indeed be incorporated into the meditations.
Why?
Because they are recited in proximity to the <s>Upaniṣad</s> texts, which have meditations as their primary subject.

children.text: nanveṣāṃ vidyārthatayā vidhānaṃ nopalabāmahe /
children.translated_text: But we do not find them prescribed as being for the purpose of the meditations.

children.text:
bāḍham /
anupalabhamānā api tvanumāsyāmahe saṃnidhisāmārthyāt /
nahi saṃnidherarthavattve saṃbhavatyakasmādasāvanāśrayituṃ yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text:
True.
But even without finding [explicit prescription], we may infer [their purpose] from the force of proximity.
For when proximity has the capacity to yield meaning, it is not proper to leave it purposeless without reason.

children.text:
nanu naiṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ vidyāviṣayaṃ kiñcitsāmarthyaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
kathaṃ ca pravargyādīni karmāṇyanyārthatvenaiva viniyuktāni santi vidyārthatvenāpi pratipadyemahīti /
children.translated_text:
But we see no capacity of these mantras that is relevant to the meditations.
And how could rituals such as <s>Pravargya</s> and the like — which are already employed for their own separate purposes — be accepted as also serving the purpose of the meditations?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
sāmarthyaṃ tāvanmantrāṇāṃ vidyāviṣayamapi kiñcicchakyaṃ kalpayituṃ hṛdayādisaṃkīrtanāt /
hṛdayādīni hi prayeṇopāsaneṣvāyatanādibhāvenopadiṣṭāni taddvāreṇa ca hṛdayaṃ pravidhyetyevañjātīyakānāṃ mantrāṇāmupapannamupāsanāṅgatvam /
dṛṣṭaścopāsaneṣvapi mantraviniyogaḥ 'bhūḥ prapadye 'munāmunāmunā' (chā. 3.15.3) ityevamādiḥ /
tathā pravargyādīnāṃ karmaṇāmanyatrāpi viniyuktānāṃ satāmaviruddho vidyāsu viniyogo vājapeya iva bṛhaspatisavasyeti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text:
This is not a defect.
First, some capacity of the mantras relevant to the meditations can be devised — because of their mention of the heart and the like.
For the heart and the like are generally taught in <s>upāsanās</s> as locations and the like, and through that connection, it is fitting that mantras of the type 'having pierced through the heart' are ancillary to <s>upāsanā</s>.
And the employment of mantras in <s>upāsanās</s> is observed: '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, I take refuge; by this, by this, by this' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.15.3) — and the like.
Likewise, the employment of rituals such as <s>Pravargya</s> and the like in the meditations — even though they are already employed elsewhere — is not contradictory, just as the <s>Vājapeya</s> [is employed] for the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we reply:

children.text:
naiṣāmupasaṃhāro vidyāsviti /
kasmāt /
vedhārthabhedāt /
hṛdayaṃ pravidhyetyevañjātīyakānāṃ hi mantrāṇāṃ yer'thā hṛdayavedhādayo bhinnā anabhisaṃbaddhāsta upaniṣaduditābhirvidyābhiḥ /
na teṣāṃ tābhiḥ saṃgantuṃ sāmarthyamasti /
children.translated_text:
These [mantras and rituals] should not be incorporated into the meditations.
Why?
Because of the difference in purpose of the piercing (<s>vedha</s>) and the like.
For the purposes of mantras of the type 'having pierced through the heart' — namely, the piercing of the heart and the like — are different [from the meditations] and unconnected with the meditations taught in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>.
They do not have the capacity to be joined with those [meditations].

children.text: nanu hṛdayasyopāsaneṣvapyupayogāttaddvāraka upāsanasaṃbandha upanyastaḥ /
children.translated_text: But has it not been suggested that because the heart is useful in <s>upāsanās</s> as well, a connection with <s>upāsanā</s> through that medium has been proposed?

children.text:
netyucyate /
hṛdayamātrasaṃkīrtanasya hyevamupayogaḥ kathañcidutprekṣyeta naca hṛdayamātramatra mantrārthaḥ /
hṛdayaṃ pravidhya dhamanīḥ pravṛjyetyevañjātīyako hi na sakalo mantrārthe vidyābhirabhisaṃbadhyate /
ābhicārikaviṣayo hyeṣor'thastasmādābhicārikeṇa karmaṇā sarvaṃ pravidhyetyetasya mantrasyābhisaṃbandhaḥ /
tadviśeṣasaṃbandhastu pramāṇāntarādanusartavyaḥ /
evamanyeṣāmapi mantrāṇāṃ keṣācilliṅgena keṣāñcidvacanena keṣāñcitpramāṇāntareṇātyevamarthāntareṣu viniyuktānāṃ rahasyapaṭhitānāmapi satāṃ na saṃnidhimātreṇa vidyāśeṣatvopapattiḥ /
durbalo hi saṃnidhiḥ śrutyādibhya ityuktaṃ prathame tantre 'śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ samavāye pāradaurbalyamarthaviprakarṣāt' (jai. sū. 3.3.13) ityatra /
children.translated_text:
We reply: No.
For the usefulness of mere proximity to the heart [in establishing a connection with the <s>vidyā</s>] might somehow be conjectured, but the heart alone is not the meaning of the <s>mantra</s> here.
For this type of [<s>mantra</s>]: 'Having pierced the heart, having severed the veins' — such a <s>mantra</s>, whose complete meaning is [of this nature], is not connected with the <s>vidyā</s> in its entirety.
For its meaning pertains to sorcery (<s>ābhicārika</s>); therefore, this <s>mantra</s> is connected with a rite of sorcery — 'piercing everything' [being its import].
But its connection with a specific [sorcery rite] must be ascertained from another means of knowledge.
Similarly, other <s>mantras</s> too — some by indicative mark (<s>liṅga</s>), some by explicit statement (<s>vacana</s>), some by another means of knowledge — even though recited in the <s>Āraṇyaka</s> (forest-section), being applied to other purposes, their subsidiary status with respect to the <s>vidyā</s> is not established merely by proximity.
For proximity is a weak [means of determining connection] compared to <s>śruti</s> and the like — as stated in the First <s>Tantra</s> (i.e., <s>Pūrvamīmāṃsā</s>): 'When <s>śruti</s>, indicative mark, passage, context, position, and name are combined, each subsequent one is weaker [than the preceding], because of distance from the intended meaning' (<s>Jaimini Sūtra</s> 3.3.13).

children.text:
tathākarmaṇāmapi pravargyādīnāmanyatra viniyuktānāṃ na vidyāśeṣatvopapattiḥ /
nahyeṣāṃ vidyābhiḥ sahaikārthyaṃ kiñcidasti /
vājapeye tu bṛhaspatisavasya spaṣṭaṃ viniyogāntaram - 'vājapeyeneṣṭvā bṛhaspatisavena yajeta' iti /
api caiko 'yaṃ pravargyaḥ sakṛdutpanno balīyasā pramāṇenānyatra viniyukto na durbalena pramāṇenānyatrāpi viniyogamarhati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, this <s>Pravargya</s> — being a single [ritual] — once established as applied elsewhere by a stronger means of knowledge, does not merit application elsewhere [additionally] by a weaker means of knowledge.

children.text: agṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatve hi pramāṇayoretadevaṃ syānnatu balavadabalavatoḥ pramāṇayoragṛhyamāṇaviśeṣatā saṃbhavati balavadabalavattvaviśeṣādeva /
children.translated_text: For if no distinction [in strength] between the two means of knowledge could be ascertained, this [mutual application] might obtain — but it is not possible that no distinction in strength be ascertained between a stronger and a weaker means of knowledge, precisely because of the distinction of being stronger or weaker.

children.text: tasmādevañjātīyakānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ vā na saṃnidhipāṭhamātreṇa vidyāśeṣatvamāśaṅkitavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the subsidiary status with respect to the <s>vidyā</s> of <s>mantras</s> and rituals of this kind should not be suspected merely from their being recited in proximity.

children.text: araṇyānuvacanādidharmasāmānyāttu saṃnidhipāṭha iti saṃtoṣṭavyam // 25 //
children.translated_text: Rather, one should be satisfied that the proximity in recitation is due to the common feature of being duties pertaining to forest-recitation (<s>āraṇyānuvacana</s>) and the like. // 25 //

Likewise, rituals such as the <s>Pravargya</s> and the like, which are applied elsewhere, do not have the status of being subsidiary to the <s>vidyā</s>.
For these have no single-purposeness (<s>ekārthya</s>) whatsoever with the <s>vidyās</s>.
But in the <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifice], the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s> has a clearly [stated] separate application: 'Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, one should sacrifice with the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>.'

children.text: 15 hānyadhikaraṇam / sū. 26
children.translated_text: 15. The <s>Hāna Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Casting Off [of Merit and Demerit]). <s>Sūtra</s> 26.

children.text: hānau tūpāyanaśabdaśeṣatvāt kuśāc chandaḥstutyupagānavat tad uktam | BBs_3,3.26 |
children.translated_text: But in the casting off [of merit and demerit], [the taking up by others also applies] because of being a complement to the word [expressing] offering (<s>upāyana</s>) — as with the <s>kuśa</s> grass, the <s>chandas</s> (meter), the laudatory passage, and the accompaniment (<s>upagāna</s>). That has been stated. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.26 |

children.text:
asti tāṇḍānāṃ śrutiḥ - 'aśva iva romāṇi vidhūya pāpaṃ candra iva rāhormukhātpramucya dhūtvā śarīramakṛtaṃ kṛtātmā brahmalokamabhisaṃbhavāmi' (chā. 8.13.1) iti /
tathātharṇikānāma 'tathā vidvānnāmarūpādvimuktaḥ parātparaṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam' (muṇḍa. 3.2.8) iti /
tathā śāṭyāyaninaḥ paṭhanti 'tasya putrā dāyamupayanti sihṛdaḥ sādhukṛtyāṃ dviṣantaḥ pāpakṛtyām' iti /
tathaiva kauṣītakinaḥ 'tatsukṛtaduṣkṛte vidhūnute tasya priyā jñātayaḥ sukṛtamupantyapriyā duṣkṛtam' (kau. 1.4) iti /
tadiha kvacitsukṛtaduṣkṛtayorhānaṃ śrūyate kvacittayoreva vibhāgena priyairapriyaiścopāyanaṃ kvacittūbhayamapi hānamupāyanaṃ ca tadyatrobhayaṃ śrūyate tatra tāvanna kiñcidvaktavyamasti /
yatrāpyupāyanameva śrūyate na hānaṃ tatrāpyarthādeva hānaṃ saṃnipatati /
anyairātmīyayoḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtayorupeyamānayorāvaśyakatvāttaddhānasya /
yatra tu hānameva śrūyate nopāyanaṃ tatropāyanaṃ sanipatedvā na veti vicikitsāyāmaśravaṇādasaṃnipātaḥ /
vidyāntaragocaratvācca śākhāntarīyasya śravaṇasya /
apicātmakartṛkaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛtayorhānaṃ parakartṛkaṃ tūpāyanaṃ tayorasatyāvaśyakabhāve kathaṃ hānenopāyamākṣipyeta /
tasmādasaṃnipāto hānāvupāyanasyeti /
asyāṃ prāptau paṭhati - hānau tviti /
hānau tvetasyāṃ kevalāyāmapi śrūyamāṇāyāmupāyanaṃ saṃnipatitumarapahati /
taccheṣatvāt /
hānaśabdaśeṣo hyupāyanaśabdaḥ samadhigataḥ kauṣītakirahasye /
tasmādanyatra kevalahānaśabdaśravaṇe 'pyupāyanānuvṛttiḥ /
yaduktamaśravaṇādvidyantaragocaratvādanāvaśyakatvāccāsaṃnipāta iti,
children.translated_text:
There is a <s>śruti</s> of the <s>Tāṇḍins</s> (followers of the <s>Chāndogya</s>): 'Like a horse shaking off its hairs, shaking off evil, like the moon freeing itself from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>, having shaken off the body, having become perfected in self — I attain the <s>Brahma</s>-world' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.13.1).
Likewise, of the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s>: 'Thus the knower, freed from name and form, attains the divine <s>Puruṣa</s> who is higher than the highest' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.8).
Likewise, the <s>Śāṭyāyanins</s> recite: 'His sons inherit [his] inheritance; his friends [receive] his good deeds; his enemies [receive] his evil deeds.'
Likewise, the <s>Kauṣītakins</s>: 'He shakes off his good and evil deeds; his dear relatives take up the good deeds, [his] disliked [relatives take up] the evil deeds' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 1.4).
Now here, in some [passages] the casting off (<s>hāna</s>) of merit and demerit is heard; in some, the offering (<s>upāyana</s>) [i.e., the taking up by others] of those very [merit and demerit] through [their distribution to] dear and non-dear ones is heard; and in some, both the casting off and the offering are heard. Where both are heard, nothing needs to be said.
Where only the offering is heard and not the casting off, even there the casting off follows of necessity.
Since the [knower's] own merit and demerit, being taken up by others, [are necessarily] cast off by him.
But where only the casting off is heard and not the offering — there, the question is whether the offering [also] follows or not. Because of non-hearing, it does not follow.
And because the hearing [of offering] in another branch pertains to a different <s>vidyā</s>.
Moreover, the casting off of merit and demerit is performed by the Self [of the knower], while the offering [i.e., taking up by others] is performed by others — and since there is no necessary connection between the two, how could the casting off imply the offering?
Therefore, in the case of casting off alone, the offering does not follow.
Having set forth this [prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads: 'But in the casting off [too]' — even when the casting off alone is heard, the offering is fit to follow.
Because of being a complement to [the word expressing] offering.
For the word [expressing] offering is understood as a complement to the word [expressing] casting off — in the <s>Kauṣītaki Rahasya</s>.
Therefore, even where the word [expressing] casting off alone is heard elsewhere, the offering also continues [to apply].
As for the objection — that because of non-hearing, because of pertaining to a different <s>vidyā</s>, and because of lack of necessary connection, the offering does not follow —

children.text:
taducyate /
bhavedeṣā vyavasthoktiryadyanuṣṭheyatvena saṃkīrtyate /
vidyāstutyarthaṃ tvanayoḥ saṃkīrtanam /
itthaṃ mahābhāgā vidyā yatsāmarthyādasya viduṣaḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛte saṃsārakāraṇabhūte vidhūyate te cāsya suhṛdviṣatsu niviśete itai /
stutyarthe cāsminsaṃkīrtane hānānantarabhāvitvenopāyasya kvacicchrutatvādanyatrāpi hānaśrutāvupāyanānuvṛttiṃ manyate stutiprakarṣalābhāya /
prasiddhā cārthavādāntarāpekṣārthavādāntarappavṛttiḥ - 'ekaviṃśo vā itho 'sāvādityaḥ' (chā. 2.10.5) ityevamādiṣu /
kathaṃ hīhaikaviṃśatādityasyābhidhīyatānapekṣyamāṇer'thavādāntare dvādaśa māsāḥpañcartavastraya ime lokā asāvāditya ekaviṃśaḥ ityetasmin /
tathā triṣṭubhau bhavataḥ sendriyatvāya ityevamādiṣu indriyaṃ vai triṣṭup ityevamādyarthavādāntarāpekṣā dṛśyate /
vidyāstutyarthatvāccāsyopāyanavādasya kathamanyadīye sukṛtaduṣkṛte anyairupeyete iti nātīvābhiniveṣṭavyam /
upāyanaśabdaśeṣatvāditi tu śabdaśabdaṃ samuccārayanstutyarthameva hānāvupāyanānuvṛttiṃ sūcayati /
guṇopasaṃhāravivakṣāyāṃ hyupāyanārthasyaiva hānāvṛttiṃ brūyāt /
tasmādguṇopasaṃhāravicāraprasaṅgena stutyupasaṃhārapradarśanārthamidaṃ sūtram /
kuśācchandastutyupagānavadityupamopādānam /
tadyathā bhāllavinām - 'kuśā vānaspatyāḥ stha tā mā pāta' ityetasminnigame kuśānāmaviśeṣeṇa vanaspatiyonitvena śravaṇe śāṭyāyanināmaudumbarāḥ kuśā iti viśeṣavacanādaudumbaryaḥ kuśā āśrīyante /
yathāca kvaciddevāsuracchandasāmaviśeṣeṇa paurvāparyaprasaṅge 'devacchandāṃsi pūrvāṇi' iti paiṅgyāmnānātpratīyante /
yathāca ṣoḍaśustotre keṣāñcitkālāviśeṣaprāptau 'samayādhyuṣite sūrye' ityārcaśruteḥ kālaviśeṣapratipattiḥ /
yathaiva cāviśeṣeṇopagānaṃ kecitsamāmananti viśeṣeṇa bhāllavinaḥ /
yathaiteṣu kuśādiṣu śrutyantaragataviśeṣairanvaya evaṃ hānāvapyupāyanānvaya ityarthaḥ /
śrutyantarakṛtaṃ hi viśeṣaṃ śrutyantare 'nabhyupagacchataḥ sarvatraiva vikalpaḥ syāt /
sa cānyāyyaḥ satyāṃ gatau /
taduktaṃ dvādaśalakṣaṇāyām - 'api tu vākyaśeṣatvāditaraparyudāsaḥ syātpratiṣedhe vikalpaḥ syāt' iti /
athavaitāsveva vidhūnavaśrutiṣvetena sūtreṇaitaccintayitavyam /
kimanena vidhūnanavacanena sukṛtaduṣkṛtayorhānamabhidhīyate kiṃvār'thāntaramiti /
tatra caivaṃ prāpayitavyam /
na hānaṃ vidhūnanamabhidhīyate 'dhañ kampane' iti smaraṇāt /
dodhūyante dhvajāgrāṇīti ca vāyunā cālyamāneṣu dhvajāgreṣu prayogadarśanāt /
tasmāccālanaṃ vidhūnanamabhidhīyate /
cālanaṃ tu suṣkṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ kañcitkālaṃ phalapratibandhanādityevaṃ prāpayya prativaktavyam /
hānāvevaiṣa vidhūyananaśabdo vartitumarhati /
upāyanaśabdaśeṣatvāt /
nahi paraparigrahabhūtayoḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoraprahīṇayoḥ parairupāyanaṃ saṃbhavati /
yadyapīdaṃ parakīyayoḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ parairupāyanaṃ nāñjasaṃ saṃbhāvyate tathāpi tatsarntanāttāvattadānuguṇyena hānameva vidhūnanaṃ nāmeti nirṇetuṃ śakyate /
kvacidapi cedaṃ vidhūnanasaṃnidhāvupāyanaṃ śrūyamāṇaṃ kuśāchandastutyupagānavadvidhanūnaśrutyā sarvatrāpekṣāmāṇaṃ sārvatrikaṃ nirṇayakāraṇaṃ saṃpadyate /
naca cālanaṃ dhvajāgravatsukṛtaduṣkṛtayormukhyaṃ saṃbhavati /
adravyatvāt /
aśvaśca romāṇi vidhūnvānastyajanrajaḥ sahaiva tena romāṇyapi jīrṇāni śātayati 'aśva iva romāṇi vidhūya pāpam' (chā. 8.13.1) iti ca brāhmaṇam /
anekārthatvābhyupagamācca dhātūnāṃ na smaraṇavirodhaḥ /
taduktamiti vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text:
to that we reply:
This argument for [separate] arrangement (<s>vyavasthā</s>) would hold if [the offering] were recited as something to be performed.
But the recitation of both [casting off and offering] is for the purpose of praising the <s>vidyā</s>.
[The sense is:] 'How great is this <s>vidyā</s>, by whose power the merit and demerit of this knower — which are the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> — are shaken off, and they settle upon his dear and non-dear relatives' — thus [it is] for praise.
And since this recitation is for the purpose of praise, and since the offering is heard somewhere as immediately following the casting off, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] considers the continuity of the offering even where [only] the casting off is heard — for the sake of enhancing the praise.
And the dependence of one laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) on another is well known — as in 'Twenty-one indeed is this [sun] there' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.10.5) and similar [passages].
For how could the twenty-one-ness of the sun be stated here without depending on the other laudatory passage — 'twelve months, five seasons, three worlds, this sun — twenty-one'?
Likewise, in [passages like] 'The [meters] are in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> — for the sake of being endowed with the sense-organs' and the like, the dependence on another laudatory passage such as '<s>Triṣṭubh</s> indeed is the sense-organ' is observed.
And since this statement about offering is for the purpose of praising the <s>vidyā</s>, one should not insist too strongly on [the question] 'How can one person's merit and demerit be taken up by others?'
'Because of being a complement to the word [expressing] offering' — by using the word '<s>śabda</s>' (word) in this expression, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] indicates that the continuity of the offering in the case of casting off is only for the purpose of praise.
For if the intention were the incorporation of a subsidiary detail, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] would state only the continuity of the meaning of offering in the case of casting off.
Therefore, this <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of demonstrating the incorporation of praise — in the course of the discussion on the incorporation of subsidiary details.
'As with the <s>kuśa</s> grass, the <s>chandas</s> (meter), the laudatory passage, and the accompaniment (<s>upagāna</s>)' — this is a citation of analogies.
Just as — among the <s>Bhāllavins</s>, in the <s>nigama</s> (Vedic passage) 'You <s>kuśa</s> grasses are of tree-origin; protect me' — when the <s>kuśa</s> grasses are heard without specification as being of tree-origin, from the specific statement of the <s>Śāṭyāyanins</s> that '<s>kuśa</s> grasses are of <s>udumbara</s> [origin],' <s>udumbara kuśa</s> grasses are adopted.
And just as — when in some context there is a question of the order of <s>deva</s> and <s>asura</s> meters without specification, they are understood from the <s>Paiṅgi</s> tradition: 'The <s>deva</s> meters come first.'
And just as — in the <s>Ṣoḍaśi Stotra</s>, when for some [priests] the time is unspecified, the specific time is understood from the <s>ṛc</s>-<s>śruti</s>: 'When the sun has well risen.'
And just as — some recite the accompaniment (<s>upagāna</s>) without specification, while the <s>Bhāllavins</s> [recite it] with specification.
Just as in these cases of <s>kuśa</s> grass and the like, there is connection with specific details found in another <s>śruti</s> — so too in the case of casting off, there is connection with the offering — this is the meaning.
For if one does not accept a specific detail established in another <s>śruti</s> in [yet] another <s>śruti</s> [on the same topic], there would be optionality (<s>vikalpa</s>) everywhere.
And that would be improper when a [definite] course of action is available.
That has been stated in the <s>Dvādaśalakṣaṇī</s> (the twelve-section [of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>]): 'But because of being a complement to the passage, the exclusion of the other would obtain; in the case of [actual] prohibition, there would be optionality.'
Alternatively, by this <s>sūtra</s>, the following should be considered in these very passages about shaking off (<s>vidhūnana</s>):
Does this word '<s>vidhūnana</s>' (shaking off) denote the casting off of merit and demerit, or something else?
Therein, the prima facie view should be stated thus: Shaking off does not denote casting off — because of the grammatical reminder '<s>dhañ kampane</s>' (the root <s>dhu</s> means shaking/trembling).
And because of the observed usage in 'The tops of the banners are shaken' — where banner-tops being moved by the wind are described with this word.
Therefore, shaking off denotes shaking — that is, moving.
And shaking of merit and demerit would mean the temporary obstruction of their fruition for some time — having stated this prima facie view, the reply should be:
The word '<s>vidhūnana</s>' (shaking off) is properly used in the sense of casting off alone.
Because of being a complement to the word [expressing] offering.
For it is not possible that merit and demerit that have not been cast off — that are [still] the property of someone else — could be taken up (<s>upāyana</s>) by others.
Even though this taking up of another's merit and demerit by others is not straightforwardly (<s>āñjasa</s>) possible, still, [the word '<s>vidhūnana</s>'] can be determined to mean casting off alone, in conformity with [the statement about offering] — because of the praise-intention.
And whenever the offering is heard in proximity to the shaking off, [the offering] — being dependent on the shaking-off <s>śruti</s> everywhere, like the <s>kuśa</s> grass, the meter, the laudatory passage, and the accompaniment — becomes a universal ground for determination.
And the shaking of merit and demerit in the primary sense — like banner-tops — is not possible.
Because they are not material substances.
And a horse, while shaking off its hairs, discarding dust, throws off even old hairs together with it — [and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> passage says:] 'Like a horse shaking off its hairs, shaking off evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.13.1).
And because roots are accepted as having multiple meanings, there is no contradiction with the grammatical reminder.
The [words] 'That has been stated' — [mean:] this has been explained [in <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>].

children.text: 16 sāṃparāyādhikaraṇam / sū. 27-28
children.translated_text: 16. The <s>Sāṃparāya Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of [Events at] Departure). <s>Sūtras</s> 27-28.

children.text: sāṃparāye tartavyābhāvāt tathā hy anye | BBs_3,3.27 |
children.translated_text: At departure [from the body], [the casting off occurs at that time] — because there is nothing to be attained [thereafter]; for thus other [<s>śrutis</s> too teach]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.27 |

children.text:
devayānena pathā paryaṅ kasthaṃ brahmābhiprastitasya vyadhvani sukṛtaduṣkṛtayorvibhāgaṃ kauṣītakinaḥ paryaṅ kavidyāyāmamananti 'sa etaṃ devayānaṃ pantānamāsādyāgnilokamāgacchati' (kau. 1.3) ityupakramya 'sa āgacchati virajāṃ nadīṃ tāṃ manasaivātyeti tatsukṛtaduṣkṛte vidhūnute' (kau. 1.4) iti /
tatkiṃ yathāśrutaṃ vyadhvanyeva viyogavacanaṃ pratipattavyamāhosvidādāveva dehādapasarpaṇa iti vicāraṇāyāṃ śrutiprāmāṇyādyathāśruti pratipattiprasaktau paṭhati - sāṃparāya itai /
sāṃparāye gamana eva dehādapasarpaṇa idaṃ vidyāsāmarthyātsukṛtaduṣkṛtahānaṃ bhavatīti pratijānīte /
hetuṃ cācaṣṭo tartavyābhāvāditi /
nahi viduṣaḥ saṃparetasya vidyayā brahma saṃprepsato 'ntarāle sukṛtaduṣkṛtābhyāṃ kiñcitprāptavyamasti yadarthaṃ katicitkṣaṇānakṣīṇe te kalpeyātām /
children.translated_text: For the knower who has departed [from the body], who seeks to reach <s>Brahman</s> through <s>vidyā</s>, there is nothing to be attained midway through merit and demerit — for whose sake those two might be supposed to endure for some moments.

children.text: vidyāviruddhaphalatvāttu vidyāsāmarthyena tayoḥ kṣayaḥ sa ca yadaiva vidyā phalābhimukhī tadaiva bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: But because [merit and demerit] produce fruits contrary to [the fruit of] <s>vidyā</s>, their destruction occurs through the power of <s>vidyā</s> — and that [destruction] must occur at the very moment when the <s>vidyā</s> becomes fruit-directed.

children.text: tasmātprāgeva sannayaṃ sukṛtaduṣkṛtakṣayaḥ paścātpaṭhyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this destruction of merit and demerit, though occurring earlier [at departure], is recited later [in the passage about the midway journey].

children.text: tathā hyanye 'pi śikhinastāṇḍinaḥ śāṭyāyaninaśca prāgavasthāyāmeva sukṛtaduṣkṛtahānamāmananti 'aśva iva romāṇi vidhūya pāpam' (chā. 8.13.1) iti, 'tasya putrā dāyamupayanti suhṛdaḥ sādhukṛtyāṃ dviṣantaḥ pāpakṛtyām' iti ca // 27 //
children.translated_text: For thus, other [teachers] too — the <s>Śikhin</s> [followers] (<s>Tāṇḍins</s>) and the <s>Śāṭyāyanins</s> — teach the casting off of merit and demerit at the prior stage [of departure itself]: 'Like a horse shaking off its hairs, shaking off evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.13.1); and 'His sons inherit [his] inheritance; his friends [receive] his good deeds; his enemies [receive] his evil deeds.' // 27 //

The <s>Kauṣītakins</s>, in the <s>Paryaṅkavidyā</s>, teach the distribution of merit and demerit midway on the path by which one proceeds to <s>Brahman</s> via the <s>devayāna</s> (path of the gods): 'He reaches this path of the gods; he comes to the world of <s>Agni</s>' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 1.3) — having begun thus, [they say:] 'He comes to the river <s>Virajā</s>; he crosses it by the mind alone; he shakes off his merit and demerit there' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 1.4).
The question is: Should the statement about the separation [of merit and demerit] midway on the journey be taken literally, or [does the separation occur] at the very beginning — at the departure from the body?
When the literal acceptance [of the midway-separation] is prima facie established on the authority of <s>śruti</s>, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads: 'At departure' — this.
At departure alone — at the very departure from the body — this casting off of merit and demerit occurs by the power of the <s>vidyā</s> — thus [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] asserts.
And [he] states the reason: 'Because there is nothing to be attained.'

children.text: chandata ubhayāvirodhāt | BBs_3,3.28 |
children.translated_text: By will — because of non-contradiction with both [statements]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.28 |

children.text: yadi ca dehādapasṛptasya devayānena pathā prasthitasyārdhapathe sukṛtaduṣkṛtakṣayo 'bhyupagamyeta tataḥ patite dehe yamaniyamavidyābhyāsātmakasya sukṛtaduṣkṛtakṣayahetoḥ puruṣaprayatnasyecchāto 'nuṣṭhānānupapatteranupapattireva taddhetukasya sukṛtaduṣkṛtakṣayasya syāt /
children.translated_text: And if one accepts that the destruction of merit and demerit occurs midway on the <s>devayāna</s> path for one who has departed from the body — then, since the body has fallen and the person's effort in the form of discipline (<s>yama</s>), observances (<s>niyama</s>), and the practice of <s>vidyā</s> — which is the cause of the destruction of merit and demerit — cannot be performed voluntarily [at that midway point], the destruction of merit and demerit caused by that [effort] would itself be impossible.

children.text: tasmātpūrvameva sādhakāvasthāyāṃ chandato 'nuṣṭhānaṃ tasyasyāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the performance of that [effort] must be voluntary (<s>chandatas</s>) — [occurring] beforehand, in the state of being a practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>).

children.text: tatpūrvakaṃ ca sukṛtaduṣkṛtahānamiti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: And the casting off of merit and demerit should be seen as preceded by that [voluntary effort].

children.text: evaṃ nimittanaimittikayorupapattistāṇḍiśāṭyāyaniśrutyośca saṃgatiriti // 28 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the reasonableness of cause and effect [is maintained], and the coherence with the <s>śrutis</s> of the <s>Tāṇḍins</s> and <s>Śāṭyāyanins</s> [is also maintained]. // 28 //

children.text: 17 gaterarthavattvādhikaraṇam / sū. 29-30
children.translated_text: 17. The <s>Gater Arthavattva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Meaningfulness of the Journey). <s>Sūtras</s> 29-30.

children.text: gater arthavattvam ubhayathānyathā hi virodhaḥ | BBs_3,3.29 |
children.translated_text: The journey [to <s>Brahman</s>] has meaning in both ways; for otherwise, there would be contradiction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.29 |

children.text:
kvacitpuṇyapāpahānasaṃnidhau devayānaḥ panthāḥ śrūyate kvacinna /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ hānāvaviśeṣeṇaiva devayānaḥ panthāḥ saṃnipateduta vibhāgena kvacitsaṃnipatet kvacinneti /
yathā tāvaddhānāvaviśeṣeṇaivopāyanānuvṛttiruktaivaṃ devayānānuvṛttirapi bhavitumarhatītyasyāṃ prāptāvācakṣmahe /
gaterdevayānasya pathor'thavattvamubhayathā vibhāgena bhavitumarhati kvacidarthavatī gatiḥ kvacinneti nāviśeṣeṇa /
anyathā hyaviśeṣeṇaivaitasyāṃ gatāvaṅgīkriyamāṇāyāṃ virodhaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: For otherwise, if [the <s>devayāna</s> path] were accepted universally without distinction, there would be a contradiction.

children.text: 'puṇyapārape vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaiti' (mu. 3.1.3) ityasyāṃ śrutau deśāntaraprāpaṇī gatirvirudhyeta /
children.translated_text: In the <s>śruti</s> 'Having shaken off merit and sin, [becoming] stainless, he attains supreme equality' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.3) — a journey that transports [the soul] to another place would be contradicted.

children.text: kathaṃ hi nirañjano 'gantā deśāntaraṃ gacchet /
children.translated_text: For how could one who is stainless and devoid of going reach another place?

children.text: gantavyaṃ ca paramaṃ sāmyaṃ na deśāntaraprāptyāyattamityānarthakyamevātra gatermanyāmahe // 29 //
children.translated_text: And the supreme equality to be attained does not depend on reaching another place — therefore we consider that the journey is purposeless here. // 29 //

In some places, the <s>devayāna</s> path is heard in proximity to the abandonment of merit and sin, and in some places it is not. The question is: Does the <s>devayāna</s> path universally accompany the abandonment [of merit and sin], or does it accompany [it] selectively — in some cases [it does] and in some cases [it does not]? Just as the universal accompaniment of offerings (<s>upāyana</s>) in the case of abandonment [of merit and sin] has already been stated, so too the universal accompaniment of the <s>devayāna</s> [path] should obtain — when this [view] is prima facie established, we say: The purposefulness of the journey through the <s>devayāna</s> path should be determined selectively, in both ways — the journey is purposeful in some cases, and not in others — not universally.

children.text: upapannas tallakṣaṇārthopalabdher lokavat | BBs_3,3.30 |
children.translated_text: <s>Upapannas tallakṣaṇārthopalabder lokavat</s> — This is fitting, because the purpose characteristic of that [journey] is found [in some cases], as in the world. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.30 |

children.text:
upapannaścāyamubhayathābhāvaḥ kvacidarthavatī gatiḥ kvacinneti /
tallakṣaṇārthopalabdheḥ /
gatikāraṇabhūto hyarthaḥ paryaṅ kavidyāsu saguṇeṣūpāsaneṣūpalabhyate /
yatra hi paryaṅ kārohaṇaṃ paryaṅ kastena brahmaṇā saṃvadanaṃ viśiṣṭagandhādi prāptiścetyevamādi bahu deśāntaraprāptyāyattaṃ phalaṃ śrūyate tatrārthavatī gatiḥ /
nahi samyagdarśane tallakṣaṇārtopalabdhirasti /
children.translated_text: But in right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), there is no finding of such a purpose.

children.text: nahyātmaikatvadarśināmāptakāmānāmihaiva dagdhāśeṣakleśabījānāmārabdhabhogakarmāśayakṣapaṇavyatirekeṇāpekṣitavyaṃ kiñcidasti tatrānarthikā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: For those who see the oneness of the Self, whose desires are fulfilled, whose residual seeds of affliction have been burned up right here [in this life] — for them there is nothing to be accomplished beyond the exhaustion of the <s>karma</s> whose fruition has already commenced. For them, the journey is purposeless.

children.text: lokavaccaiṣa vibhāgo draṣṭavyo yathā loke grāmaprāptau deśāntaraprāpaṇaḥ panthā apekṣyate nārogyaprāptāvevamihāpīti /
children.translated_text: And this distinction should be understood as in the world: just as in the world a road leading to another place is needed for reaching a village, but not for attaining health — so too here.

children.text: bhūyaścainaṃ vibhāgaṃ caturthādhyāye nipuṇataramupapādayiṣyāmaḥ // 30 //
children.translated_text: And we shall demonstrate this distinction more precisely in the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>. // 30 //

And this dual mode — the journey being purposeful in some cases and not in others — is fitting. Because of the finding of the purpose characteristic of that [journey]. For the purpose that is the cause of the journey is found in the <s>paryaṅka-vidyā</s> and similar meditations on <s>Brahman</s> with attributes (<s>saguṇa</s>). For where much fruit that depends on reaching another place is heard — such as the ascent of the couch (<s>paryaṅka</s>), the conversation with that <s>Brahman</s>, the attainment of special fragrance and the like — there the journey is purposeful.

children.text: 18 aniyamādhikaraṇam / sū. 31
children.translated_text: Section 18: <s>Aniyamādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 31

children.text: aniyamaḥ sarvāsām avirodhaḥ śabdānumānābhyām | BBs_3,3.31 |
children.translated_text: <s>Aniyamaḥ sarvāsāmavirodhaḥ śabdānumānābhyām</s> — There is no restriction [of the <s>devayāna</s> path to specific <s>vidyās</s>]; [it applies to] all [<s>saguṇa vidyās</s>] without contradiction — from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.31 |

children.text:
saguṇāsu vidyāsu gatirarthavatī na nirguṇāyāṃ paramātmavidyāyāmityukhtam /
saguṇāsvapi vidyāsu kāsucidgatiḥ śrūyate yathā paryaṅ kavidyāyāmupakosalavidyāyāṃ pañcāgnividyāyāṃ daharavidyāyāmiti /
nānyāsu yathā madhuvidyāyāṃ śāṇḍilyavidyāyāṃ ṣoḍaṣakalavidyāyāṃ vaiśvānaravidyāyāmiti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ yāsvevaiṣā gatiḥ śrūyate tāsveva niyamyetotāniyamena sarvābhirevañjātīyakābhirvidyābhirabhisaṃbadhyateti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ niyama iti /
yatraiva śrūyate tatraiva bhavitumarhati /
prakaraṇasya niyāmakatvāt /
yadyanyatra śrūyamāṇāpi gatirvidyāntaraṃ gacchecchrutyādīnāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ hīyeta sarvasya sarvārthatvaprasaṅgāt /
apicārcirādikaikaiva gatirupakosalavidyāyāṃ pañcāgnividyāyāṃ ca tulyavatpaṭhyate tatsarvārthatve 'narthakaṃ punarvacanaṃ syāt /
tasmānniyama ityevaṃ prāpte paṭhati - aniyama iti /
sarvāsāmevābhyudayaprāptiphalānāṃ saguṇānāṃ vidyānāmaviśeṣeṇaiṣā davayānākhyā gatirbhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: It has been said that the journey is purposeful in meditations on <s>Brahman</s> with attributes (<s>saguṇa</s>), but not in the knowledge of the supreme Self without attributes (<s>nirguṇa</s>). But even among the <s>saguṇa vidyās</s>, the journey [through the <s>devayāna</s> path] is heard in some — such as the <s>Paryaṅka-vidyā</s>, the <s>Upakosala-vidyā</s>, the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s>, and the <s>Dahara-vidyā</s> — but not in others — such as the <s>Madhu-vidyā</s>, the <s>Śāṇḍilya-vidyā</s>, the <s>Ṣoḍaśakala-vidyā</s>, and the <s>Vaiśvānara-vidyā</s>. The question is: Is this journey restricted to only those [<s>vidyās</s>] in which it is heard, or does it apply without restriction to all <s>vidyās</s> of this kind? What is the prima facie view? There is restriction. [The journey] should belong only where it is heard. Because the context is determinative. If the journey, though heard in one place, were to cross over to another <s>vidyā</s>, the authoritativeness of <s>śruti</s> and the like would be undermined — because everything would be applicable to everything [without limit]. Moreover, the one and the same journey through [the stations of] light (<s>arcis</s>) and the rest is read equally in the <s>Upakosala-vidyā</s> and the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s> — if it were applicable to all, the repetition would be purposeless. Therefore, there is restriction. Having thus set forth [the prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads: 'There is no restriction.' This journey called the <s>devayāna</s> should apply without distinction to all <s>saguṇa vidyās</s> whose fruit is the attainment of prosperity.

children.text: nanvaniyamābhyupagame prakaraṇavirodha uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it has been said that accepting the non-restriction would contradict the context.

children.text:
naiṣo 'sti virodhaḥ śabdānumānābhyāṃ śrutismṛtibhyāmityarthaḥ /
tathāhi śrutiḥ - 'tadya itthaṃ viduḥ' (chā. 5.10.1) iti pañcāgnividyāvatāṃ devayānaṃ panthānamavatārayantī 'ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhātapa ityupāsate' (chā. 5.10.1) iti vidyāntaraśīlināmapi pcāgnividyāvidbhiḥ samānamārgatāṃ gamayati /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate vidyāntaraśīlināmiyaṃ gatiriti /
children.translated_text: This is not a contradiction — from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, that is, from direct scripture and tradition — this is the meaning. For thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Those who know this thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1) — while introducing the <s>devayāna</s> path for those who possess the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s>, [the text continues:] 'And those who in the forest worship faith and austerity' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1) — [thus] it leads those who practice other <s>vidyās</s> too to the same path as those who possess the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s>. But how is it known that this journey [applies to] those who practice other <s>vidyās</s>?

children.text: nanu śraddhātapaḥparāyaṇānāmeva syāttanmātraśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: Perhaps it is meant only for those devoted to faith and austerity alone — since only those are mentioned.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
nahi kevalābhyāṃ śraddātapobhyāmantareṇa vidyābalameṣā gatirlabhyate 'vidyayā tadārohanti yatra kāmāḥ parāgatāḥ /
na tatra dakṣiṇā yanti nāvidvāṃsastapasvinaḥ' iti śrutyantarāt /
tasmādiha śraddhātapobhyāṃ vidyāntaropalakṣaṇam /
vājasaneyinastu pañcāgnividyādhikāre 'dhīyate - 'ya evametadvidurye cāmī araṇye śraddhāṃ satyamupāsate' (bṛ. 6.2.15) iti /
tatra śraddhalavo ye satyaṃ brahmopāsata iti vyākhyeyam /
satyaśabdasya brahmaṇyasakṛtprayuktatvāt /

'atha ya etau panthānau na viduste pataṅgā yadidaṃ dandaśūkam' (bṛ. 6.2.16) iti ca mārgadvayabhraṣṭānāṃ kaṣṭāmadhogatiṃ gamayantī śrutirdevayānapitṛyāṇayorevainānantarbhāvayati /
tatrāpi vidyāviseṣādeṣāṃ devayānapratipattiḥ /
