children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s> too: 'These two paths — the bright and the dark — are considered eternal for the world;

children.text: ekayā yātyānāvṛttimanyayāvartate punaḥ' (bha.gī. 8.23) iti /
children.translated_text: by one, one goes to non-return; by the other, one returns again' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 8.26).

children.text: yatpunardevayānasya patho dvirāmnānamupakosalavidyāyāṃ pañcāgnividyāyāṃ ca tadubhayatrāpyanucintanārtham /
children.translated_text: As for the double reading of the <s>devayāna</s> path in both the <s>Upakosala-vidyā</s> and the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s> — that is for the purpose of repeated contemplation in both places.

children.text: tasmādaniyamaḥ // 31 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no restriction. // 31 //

This is not a fault. For this journey is not attainable through mere faith and austerity without the power of <s>vidyā</s> — from the other <s>śruti</s>: 'Through <s>vidyā</s> they ascend to the place where desires have fully departed; not there do [mere] gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) go, nor the ignorant even if they are ascetics' (<s>Kaṭha</s>). Therefore, here faith and austerity serve as an indication of other <s>vidyās</s> [as well]. And the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, in the context of the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s>, read: 'Those who know this thus, and those who in the forest worship faith and truth (<s>satya</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15). There, it should be explained: those who have faith and worship truth, i.e., <s>Brahman</s>. Because the word '<s>satya</s>' is used for <s>Brahman</s> more than once. And since those who possess the <s>Pañcāgni-vidyā</s> are already included by the expression '<s>itthaṃ vidvān</s>' (those who know thus), the inclusion of those devoted to other <s>vidyās</s> [by the phrase about faith and truth] is proper. And the <s>śruti</s> that leads those who have fallen from both paths [<s>devayāna</s> and <s>pitṛyāṇa</s>] to a miserable downward journey — 'But those who do not know these two paths — they become insects, moths, and biting creatures' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.16) — includes them within the two paths of <s>devayāna</s> and <s>pitṛyāṇa</s> alone. And therein, because of the specificity of <s>vidyā</s>, their attainment is of the <s>devayāna</s> [path].

children.translated_text: But the fruit of knowledge is directly experienced — as stated in the <s>śruti</s>: 'That <s>Brahman</s> which is directly perceived and not indirectly known' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1); and because of the teaching in the form of an established fact: '<s>Tattvamasi</s>' (Thou art That) (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7).

children.text: nahi 'tattvamasi' ityasya vākyasyārthastattvaṃ mṛto bhaviṣyasītyevaṃ pariṇetuṃ śakyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the meaning of the sentence '<s>Tattvamasi</s>' cannot be construed as 'You will become That after death.'

children.text: 'taddhaitatpaśyannṛṣirvāmadevaḥ pratipede 'haṃ manurabhavaṃ sūryaśca' (bṛ. 1.4.10) iti ca samyagdarśanakālameva tatphalaṃ sarvātmatvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And: 'Seeing this, the seer <s>Vāmadeva</s> realized: I was <s>Manu</s> and the sun' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10) — [this passage] shows that the fruit of right knowledge — the state of being the Self of all — [occurs] at the very time of right knowledge.

children.text: tasmādaikāntikī viduṣaḥ kaivalyasiddhiḥ // 32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the attainment of <s>kaivalya</s> by the knower is absolute. // 32 //

It is investigated whether, after the fall of the present body of the knower [of <s>Brahman</s>], another body arises or not. One might ask: when the means — namely <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) — is perfected, does <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) result or not? This investigation is not warranted. For no one doubts whether rice is cooked or not when the cooking and the means are complete. Nor does one doubt whether the eater is satisfied or not while eating. However, this investigation is warranted — because even for some knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, the arising of another body is seen in the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>. For thus they remember: the Vedic teacher named <s>Apāntaratamas</s>, the ancient sage, by the command of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, was reborn as <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> at the junction of the <s>Kali</s> and <s>Dvāpara</s> [ages]. And <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the mind-born son of <s>Brahmā</s>, having lost his former body through the curse of <s>Nimi</s>, was reborn again from <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> by the command of <s>Brahmā</s>. The rebirth of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others too — who were mind-born sons of <s>Brahmā</s> — is heard [as occurring] at the <s>Vāruṇa</s> sacrifice. <s>Sanatkumāra</s> too, a mind-born son of <s>Brahmā</s> himself, by his own boon-granting to <s>Rudra</s>, manifested as <s>Skanda</s>. Similarly, abundant rebirth in other bodies is narrated for <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and others, on various occasions, in <s>Smṛti</s>. In <s>śruti</s> too, [such rebirth] is generally found in <s>mantras</s> and <s>arthavādas</s>. And among them, some assume another body after the former body has fallen, while others — even while remaining in that [body] — by the power of yogic mastery, assume multiple bodies simultaneously. And all of these are remembered as having comprehended the entire meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>. Therefore, from seeing the arising of other bodies for these [sages], it follows that <s>brahmavidyā</s> is only optionally the cause of liberation — [or perhaps] not the cause at all. To this, the answer is given: No. Because the situation of those [sages] — <s>Apāntaratamas</s> and the rest — who are appointed to offices that are causes of the world's sustenance, such as the propagation of the <s>Vedas</s> and the like, depends on their office. Just as the blessed Sun, having performed the office for the world for a thousand <s>yugas</s>, at the end of that [period] experiences <s>kaivalya</s> free from rising and setting — as stated in the <s>śruti</s>: 'Then, rising beyond, he neither rises nor sets; he stands alone in the middle' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.11.1). And just as present-day knowers of <s>Brahman</s> experience <s>kaivalya</s> upon the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> whose fruition has already begun — as stated in the <s>śruti</s>: 'For him, the delay is only so long until he is freed [from the body]; then he will attain [<s>Brahman</s>]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.14.2). So too, <s>Apāntaratamas</s> and the others — being lords (<s>īśvaras</s>) appointed by the Supreme Lord to their respective offices — even though right knowledge, the cause of <s>kaivalya</s>, is present, they remain with unexhausted <s>karma</s> for as long as their office lasts, and at the end of that [office], they are released — this is not contradictory. For they, carrying forward a <s>karma</s>-residue that was set in motion once for the purpose of bearing fruit, move independently from one body to another — like from one house to another — for the fulfillment of their office, with memory unimpaired, and because of their mastery over body, senses, and nature, they create bodies and preside over them simultaneously or successively. And they are not called 'those who remember past births' (<s>jātismaras</s>) — because they are well-known in tradition as 'they are the very same ones.' For just as it is remembered that the female ascetic named <s>Sulabhā</s>, a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, wishing to debate with <s>Janaka</s>, abandoned her own body, entered <s>Janaka</s>'s body, debated with him, and afterwards re-entered her own body. If, when <s>karma</s> set in motion once has not yet been discharged, another <s>karma</s> — the cause of beginning another body — were to manifest, then yet another unburnt seed of <s>karma</s> would likewise follow — and thus one might apprehend that <s>brahmavidyā</s> is only optionally the cause of liberation, or not the cause at all. But this apprehension is not reasonable — because the burning of the seed of <s>karma</s> by knowledge is well-known from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. For the <s>śruti</s> says: 'The knot of the heart is pierced, all doubts are cut asunder, and one's <s>karmas</s> are destroyed — when that [<s>Brahman</s>], both higher and lower, is seen' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.8). And: 'Upon the attainment of memory [of the Self], all knots are released' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.26.2) — and such passages. The <s>smṛti</s> too says: 'Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O <s>Arjuna</s>, so too the fire of knowledge reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes' (<s>Gītā</s> 4.37). 'Just as seeds scorched by fire do not sprout again, so too, with afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) burnt by knowledge, the Self is not born again' — and such passages. And when the afflictions beginning with <s>avidyā</s> are burnt, it is not possible that only part of the <s>karma</s>-residue — which is the seed of affliction — is burnt and part sprouts. For a rice-seed burnt by fire is not seen to partially sprout. But for the <s>karma</s>-residue whose fruition has already commenced, cessation comes through the exhaustion of its momentum — like an arrow already released. Because the <s>śruti</s> 'For him, the delay is only so long' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.14.2) postpones [liberation] until the fall of the body. Therefore, the persistence [of embodiment] for as long as the office lasts, for those who hold such offices, is well-established. And there is no non-universality of the fruit of knowledge. And thus the <s>śruti</s> shows liberation from knowledge without distinction for all: 'Whoever among the <s>devas</s> awakened to this — he became that; likewise among the sages; likewise among humans' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10). And the great sages may have been attached to other kinds of knowledge whose fruits are lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>) and such. They, afterwards, seeing the destruction of that lordship and becoming disenchanted, firmly established in the knowledge of the Supreme Self, attained <s>kaivalya</s> — this is reasonable. Because of the tradition: 'Together with <s>Brahmā</s>, all of them, at the occurrence of the universal dissolution, having perfected themselves, enter the Supreme Abode.' And because knowledge has its fruit directly perceptible, the apprehension of absence of fruit is unreasonable. For regarding the fruit of <s>karma</s> — heaven and the like — which has not yet been experienced, there might be doubt: will it occur or not?

children.text:
vājasaneyake śrūyate - 'etadvai tadakṣaraṃ gārgi brāhmaṇā abhivadantyasthūlamanaṇvahrasvamadīrghamalohitamasneham' (bṛ. 3.8.8) ityādi /
tathātharvaṇe śrūyate - 'atha parā yayā tadakṣaramadigamyate /
yattadadreśyamagrāhyamagotramavarṇam' (mu. 1.1.5) ityādi /
tathaivānyatrāpi viśeṣanirākaraṇadvāreṇākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahmaśrāvyate /
tatra ca kvacitkecidatiriktā viśeṣāḥ pratipadyante /
tāsāṃ viśeṣapratiṣedhabuddhīnāṃ kiṃ sarvāsāṃ sarvatra prāptiruta vyavastheti saṃśaye śrutivibhāgādvyavasthāprāptāvucyate - akṣaraviṣayāstu viśeṣapratiṣedhabuddhayaḥ sarvāḥ sarvatrāvaroddhavyāḥ sāmānyatadbhāvābhyām - samāno hi sarvatra viśeṣanirākaraṇarūpo brahmapratipādanaprakāraḥ /
tadeva ca sarvatra pratipādyaṃ brahmābhinnaṃ pratyabhijñāyate /
tatra kimityanyatra kṛtā buddhayo 'nyatra na syuḥ /
tathāca 'ānandādayaḥ pradhānasya' (bra.sū. 3.3.11) ityatra vyākhyātam /
tatra vidhirūpāṇi viśeṣaṇāni cintitānīha pratiṣedharūpāṇīti viśeṣaḥ /
prapañcārthaścāyaṃ cintābhedaḥ /
aupasadavaditi nidarśanam /
yathā jāmadagnye 'hīne puroḍāśinīṣūpasatsu coditāsu puroḍāśapradānamantrāṇām agnerverhetraṃ veradhvaram ityevamādīnāmudgātṛvedotpannānāmapyadhvaryubhirabhisaṃbandho bhavati /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension], it is heard: 'This is that Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, which the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> describe — not gross, not minute, not short, not long, not red, not adhesive' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8) — and so on. Similarly, in the <s>Atharva</s> [<s>Veda</s>], it is heard: 'But the higher [knowledge] is that by which the Imperishable is apprehended — that which is invisible, ungraspable, without lineage, without color' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.5) — and so on. Likewise, elsewhere too, the Imperishable — the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — is taught through the negation of specific attributes. And therein, in some [passages], certain additional specific attributes are learned. The question is: do all those meditations on the negation of specific attributes apply everywhere, or is there a fixed distribution? When the doubt arises, and when a fixed distribution is reached based on the division of <s>śruti</s> [passages], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: The meditations on the negation of specific attributes relating to the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) should all be included everywhere — because of the commonality and identity of the object. For the mode of teaching <s>Brahman</s> through the negation of specific attributes is the same everywhere. And the very same <s>Brahman</s> that is to be taught is recognized as undifferentiated everywhere. Given this, why should meditations performed in one [passage] not apply in another? And thus it has been explained in '<s>Ānandādayaḥ pradhānasya</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.3.11). There, affirmative attributes were considered; here, attributes in the form of negation [are considered] — this is the distinction. And this difference in investigation is merely for the purpose of elaboration. 'As in the case of the <s>Aupasada</s>' — this is an illustration. Just as in the <s>Jāmadagnya Ahīna</s> [sacrifice], when the <s>Upasad</s> offerings are enjoined along with the offering of rice-cakes (<s>puroḍāśa</s>), the <s>mantras</s> for the rice-cake offering — 'Of <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Veṣṭa</s>, of <s>Agni</s> is the sacrifice' and such — though originating in the <s>Udgātṛ</s>-<s>Veda</s>, are connected with the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priests as well —

children.text: adhvaryukartṛtvātatpuroḍāśapradānasya pradhānatantratvāccaṅgānām /
children.translated_text: because of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s agency in [performing] that rice-cake offering, and because of the subsidiary elements being dependent on the principal act.

children.text: evamihāpyakṣaratantratvāttadviśeṣaṇānāṃ yatra kvacidapyutpannānāmakṣareṇa sarvatrābhisaṃbandha ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly here too, because the attributes of the negation [of specific qualities] are dependent on the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), wherever they originate, they are connected with the Imperishable everywhere — this is the meaning.

children.text: taduktaṃ prathame kāṇḍe - 'guṇamukhyavyatikrame tadarthatvānmukhyena vedasaṃyogaḥ' (jai. sū. 3.3.8) ityatra // 33 //
children.translated_text: This has been stated in the first book [of <s>Pūrvamīmāṃsā</s>]: '<s>Guṇamukhyavyatikrame tadarthatvānmukhyena vedasaṃyogaḥ</s>' (<s>Jaiminisūtra</s> 3.3.8) — in that context. // 33 //

children.text: 21 iyadadhikaraṇam / sū. 34
children.translated_text: 21. <s>Iyadadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 34

children.text: iyadāmananāt | BBs_3,3.34 |
children.translated_text: Because of the limited extent (<s>iyattā</s>) being taught [as the same]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.34 |

children.text:
'dvā suparṇāsayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte /
tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti' (mu. 3.1.1) ityadhyātmādhikāre mantramātharvamikāḥ śvetāśvatarāśca paṭhanti /
tathā kaṭhāḥ 'ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe /
chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ' (ka. 3.1) iti /
kimatra vidyaikatvamuta vidyānānātvamiti saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ, vidyānānātvamiti /
kutaḥ /
viśeṣadarśanāt /
dvā suparṇetyatra hyekasya bhoktṛtvaṃ dṛśyate /
ekasya cābhoktṛtvaṃ dṛśyate /
ṛtaṃ pibantāvityatrobhayorapi bhoktṛtvameva dṛśyate tadvedyarūpaṃ bhidyamānaṃ vidyāṃ bhindyādityevaṃ prāpte bravīti vidyaikatvamiti /
kutaḥ - yata ubhayorapyanayormantrayoriyattāparicchinnaṃ dvitvopetaṃ vedyarūpamabhinnamāmananti /
children.translated_text: The followers of <s>Atharva</s> (<s>Māṇḍūkya</s>) and <s>Śvetāśvatara</s> recite, in the context of the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), the <s>mantra</s>: 'Two birds, companions, clasping the same tree — one of them eats the sweet fruit; the other, not eating, looks on' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.1.1). Similarly, the <s>Kaṭha</s> [recension reads]: 'The two who drink <s>ṛta</s> (truth) in the world of good deeds, having entered the cave, in the highest space — the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> call them shadow and light, as do the householders who maintain five fires and those who perform the <s>Nāciketāgni</s> [sacrifice] thrice' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.1). The question here is: is there unity of <s>vidyā</s> or diversity of <s>vidyā</s>? What is the prima facie view? There is diversity of <s>vidyā</s>. Why? Because of the seeing of differences. For in 'Two birds,' the enjoyership of one is seen, and the non-enjoyership of the other is seen. But in 'The two who drink <s>ṛta</s>,' the enjoyership of both is seen. Since the object of knowledge differs in this way, it would break the <s>vidyā</s> [into two] — this being the prima facie position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: there is unity of <s>vidyā</s>. Why? Because both of these <s>mantras</s> teach a limited extent (<s>iyattā</s>) characterized by duality — the same undifferentiated [content].

children.text: nanu darśito rūpabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the difference in form [of the two objects of knowledge] has been shown.

children.text:
netyucyate /
ubhāvapyetau mantrau jīvadvitīyamīśvaraṃ pratipādayato nārthāntaram /
dvā suparṇā ityatra tāvat anaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti ityaśanāyādyatītaḥ paramātmā pratipādyate /
vākyaśeṣe 'pi ca sa eva pratipādyamno dṛśyate /
'juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśamasya mahimānam' (śve. 4.7) iti /
ṛtaṃ pibantau ityatra tu jīve pibatyaśanāyādyatītaḥ paramātmāpi sāhacaryācchatrinyāyena pibatītyupacaryate /
paramātmaprakaraṇaṃ hyetat 'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmāt' (ka. 2.14) ityupakramāt /
tadviṣaya eva cātrāpi vākyaśeṣo bhavati 'yaḥ seturījānānāmakṣaraṃ brahma yatparam' (ka. 3.2) iti /
'guhāṃ praviṣṭāvātmānau hi' (bra.sū. 1.2.11) ityatra caitatprapañcitam /
tasmānnāsti vedyabhedastasmācca vidyaikatvam /
apica triṣvapyeteṣu vedānteṣu paurvāparyalocane paramātmavidyaivāvagamyate tādātmyavivakṣayaiva jīvopādānaṃ nārthāntaravivakṣayā /
children.translated_text: Moreover, upon examining the sequential context in all three of these <s>Vedānta</s> passages, only the knowledge of the Supreme Self is understood — the mention of the <s>jīva</s> is for the purpose of teaching identity [with the Supreme Self], not for teaching a separate entity.

children.text: naca paramātmavidyāyāṃ bhedābhedavicārāvatāro 'stītyuktam /
children.translated_text: And it has been stated that in the knowledge of the Supreme Self, there is no scope for investigating difference and non-difference.

children.text: tasmātprapañcārtha evaiṣa yogaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this conjunction [of the two mantras] is merely for the purpose of elaboration.

children.text: tasmāccādhikadharmopasaṃhāra iti // 34 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, the inclusion of additional attributes [follows]. // 34 //

No, it is said. Both of these <s>mantras</s> teach <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) as accompanied by the <s>jīva</s> — nothing else. In 'Two birds,' the Supreme Self — who is beyond hunger and the like — is taught by 'the other, not eating, looks on.' And in the continuation of the passage too, He alone is seen as being taught: 'When [the individual self] sees the other — the Lord, His greatness' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.7). But in 'The two who drink <s>ṛta</s>,' while the <s>jīva</s> drinks, the Supreme Self too — who is beyond hunger and the like — is figuratively said to drink, by association, through the maxim of 'the one with the umbrella' (<s>chatrinyāya</s>). For this is a context about the Supreme Self — from the opening: 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.14). And the continuation of the passage here too pertains to that [Supreme Self]: 'He who is the bridge for the sacrificers, the imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 3.2). And this has been elaborated in '<s>Guhāṃ praviṣṭāv ātmānau hi</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 1.2.11). Therefore, there is no difference in the object of knowledge, and therefore there is unity of <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: 22 anantarādhikaraṇam / sū. 35-36
children.translated_text: 22. <s>Antarādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 35-36

children.text: antarā bhūtagrāmavatsātmanaḥ | BBs_3,3.35 |
children.translated_text: In between [birth as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and as an animal], [one is born] among the classes of beings, just as [<s>Brahman</s> is] the Self [of all]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.35 |

children.text:
'yatsākṣādaparokṣādbrahma ya ātmā sarvāntaraḥ' (bṛ. 3.4.1 - 3.5.1)ityevaṃ dviruṣstakaholapraśnayornairaltaryeṇa vājasaneyinaḥ samāmananti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - vidyaikatvaṃ vā syādvidyānānātvaṃ veti /
vidyānānātvamiti tāvatprāptam /
abhyāsasāmarthyāt /
anyathā hyanyūnānātiriktārthe dvirāmnānamarthakameva syāt /
tasmādyathābhyāsātkarmabheda evamabhyāsādvidyābheda ityevaṃ prāpte pratyāha - antarāmnānāviśeṣātsvātmano vidyaikatvamiti /
sarvāntaro hi svātmobhayatrāpyaviśiṣṭaḥ pṛcchyate ca pratyucyate ca /
nahi dvāvātmānāvekasmindehe sarvāntarau saṃbhavataḥ /
tadā hyekasyāñijasaṃsarvāntaratvamavakalpyeta /
ekasya tu bhūtagrāmavannaiva sarvāntaratvaṃ syāt /
yathāca pañcabhūtasamūhe dehe pṛthivyā āpontarā adbhyastejo 'ntaramiti satyapyāpekṣike 'ntaratve naiva mukhya sarvāntaratvaṃ bhavati tathehāpītyarthaḥ /
athavā bhūtagrāmavaditi śrutyantaraṃ nidarśayati /
yathā 'eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā' (śve.
children.translated_text: 'That which is directly and immediately <s>Brahman</s>, which is the Self innermost of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1; 3.5.1) — thus the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> teach [this passage] twice, as [two] questions of <s>Uṣasta</s> and <s>Kahola</s> [that are answered] invariably [the same way]. The question is: Is there one <s>vidyā</s> [here] or a plurality of <s>vidyās</s>? The prima facie view is that there is a plurality of <s>vidyās</s> — because of the force of the repetition. For otherwise, the double teaching of a meaning that is neither deficient nor excessive would be purposeless. Therefore, just as repetition [of a ritual] establishes a difference of <s>karmas</s>, so too repetition establishes a difference of <s>vidyās</s>. Having set forth this [prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] responds: Because of the non-difference of the Self — which is taught within both [passages] — the <s>vidyā</s> is one. For the Self innermost of all — one's own Self — is asked about and answered identically in both. For it is not possible that there be two Selves, both 'innermost of all,' in a single body. For in that case, the 'innermost-of-all' status of one would be straightforward, but for the other, just as in the case of a group of elements, there would be no [genuine] 'innermost-of-all' status. And just as in the body consisting of the five-element aggregate, earth is more interior than water, water than fire — even though there is a relative interiority, there is no genuine 'innermost-of-all' status — so too here, this is the meaning. Alternatively, 'as in the case of the group of elements' points to another <s>śruti</s>. Just as in the <s>mantra</s> 'One God, hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s>

children.text: 6.11) ityasminmantre samasteṣu bhūtagrāmyeṣveka eva sarvāntara ātmāmnāyate /
children.translated_text: 6.11) — in this <s>mantra</s>, in all classes of beings, one Self alone is taught as innermost of all.

children.text: evamanayorapi brāhmaṇayorityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: So too in these two <s>brāhmaṇas</s> [passages] — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasmādvedyaikyādvidyaikatvamiti // 35 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the oneness of what is to be known, the <s>vidyā</s> is one. // 35 //

children.text: anyathā bhedānupapattir iti cen nopadeśāntaravat | BBs_3,3.36 |
children.translated_text: <s>Anyathā bhedānupapattiriti cen nopadeśāntaravat</s> — If [it be said that] otherwise the non-occurrence of difference [i.e., the repetition] would be inexplicable — [we say] no, because it is like other [repeated] teachings. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.36 |

children.text:
atha yaduktamanabhyupagamyamāne vidyābheda āmnānabhedānupapattiriti tatparihartavyam /
atrocyate - nāyaṃ doṣaḥ /
upadeśāntaravadupapatteḥ /
yathā tāṇḍināmupaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhe prapāṭhake - 'sa ātmā tattvamasi śvekateto' (chā. 6.8.7) iti navakṛtvo 'pyupadeśe na vidyābhedo bhavatyevamihāpi bhaviṣyati /
kathaṃ na navakṛtvo 'pyupadeśe vidyābhedo na bhavati /
upakramopasaṃhārābhyāmekārthatāvagamāt /
'bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatu' (chā. 6.5.4) iti caikasyaivārthasya punaḥ punaḥ pratipipādayiṣitavyatvenopakṣepāt /
āśaṅkāntaranirākaraṇena cāsakṛdupadeśopapatteḥ /
evamihāpi praśnarūpābhedāt ato 'nyadārtam' (bṛ. 3.4.2 - 3.5.1) iti ca parisamāptyaviśeṣādupakramopasaṃhārau tāvadekārthaviṣayau dṛśyate /
'yadeva sākṣādaparokṣādbrahma' (bṛ. 3.5.1) iti dvitīye praśna evakāraṃ prayuñjānaḥ pūrvapraśnagatamevārthamuttaratrānukṛṣyamāṇaṃ darśayati /
pūrvasminśca brāhmaṇo kāryakaraṇavyatiriktasyātmanaḥ sadbhāvaḥ kathyate /
children.translated_text: And in the first <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the existence of the Self as distinct from the body and the instruments is taught.

children.text: uttarasmiṃstu tasyaivāśanāyādisaṃsāradharmātītatvaṃ kathyate /
children.translated_text: And in the second, the transcendence of that very [Self] over the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> such as hunger and the like is taught.

children.text: ityekārthatopapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the propriety of a single meaning [is established].

children.text: tasmādekā vidyeti // 36 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is one <s>vidyā</s>. // 36 //

Now, what was said — that if the difference of <s>vidyās</s> is not accepted, the difference in teaching [i.e., the repetition] would be inexplicable — that must be resolved. To this we say: This is not a fault. Because of the propriety [of repetition], as in other [repeated] teachings. Just as in the <s>Upaniṣad</s> of the <s>Tāṇḍins</s>, in the sixth chapter, even though the teaching 'That is the Self; that you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) is repeated nine times, there is no difference of <s>vidyā</s> — so too here. How is it that even with nine repetitions of the teaching, there is no difference of <s>vidyā</s>? Because the singleness of meaning is understood from the introduction and the conclusion. And because the same topic is introduced again and again as something to be further explained — 'Let my lord teach me further' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.5.4). And because the repeated teaching is justified by the removal of different doubts each time. Similarly here too, because of the non-difference in the form of the questions — and because of the non-difference in the conclusion: 'anything other than this is afflicted' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.2; 3.5.1) — the introduction and conclusion are seen to pertain to a single meaning. And in the second question, by using the emphatic particle '<s>eva</s>' in 'that which is directly and immediately <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.1), [the text] shows that the very same meaning from the first question is being drawn over to the second.

children.text: 23 vyatihārādhikaraṇam / sū. 37
children.translated_text: Section 23: <s>Vyatihārādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 37

children.text: vyatihāro viśiṃṣanti hītaravat | BBs_3,3.37 |
children.translated_text: <s>Vyatihāro viśiṃṣanti hītaravat</s> — The interchange [of identities between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> is for meditation], for [the teachers] specify — as with the other [attributes]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.37 |

children.text:
tathā - 'tadyo 'haṃ so 'sau yo 'sau so 'ham' ityādityapuruṣaṃ prakṛtyaitareyiṇaḥ samāmananti, tathā jābālāḥ tvaṃ vā ahamasmi bhagavo devate 'haṃ vai tvamasi' iti /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimiha vyatihāreṇobhayarūpā matiḥ kartavyotaikarūpaiveti /
ekarūpaiveti tāvadāha /
nahyatrātmana īśvareṇaikatvaṃ muktvānyatkiñciccintayitavyamasti /
yadi caivaṃ cintayitavyo viśeṣaḥ parikalpyeta saṃsāriṇastāvadīśvarātmamīśvarasya saṃsīryātmatvamiti /
tatra saṃsāriṇastāvadīśvarātmatva utkarṣo bhavedīśvarasya tu saṃsāryātmatve nikarṣaḥ kutaḥ syāt /
tasmādaikārūpyameva mateḥ /
vyatihārāmnāyastvekatvadṛḍhīkārārtha iti /
evaṃ prāpte pratyāha - vyatihāro 'yamādhyānāyāmanāyate itaravat /
yathetaraṃ guṇāḥ sarvātmatvaprabhṛtaya ādhyānāyāmnāyante tadvat /
tathāhi viśiṃṣanti samāmnātāra ubhayoccāraṇena 'tvamahamasmyahaṃ ca tattvamasi' iti /
taccobhayarūpāyāṃ matau kartavyāyāmarthavadbhavati /
anyathā hīdaṃ viśeṣeṇobhayāmnānamanarthakaṃ syāt /
ekenaiva kṛtatvāt /
children.translated_text: Thus — 'He who I am, he is that [sun]; he who is that, he is I' — having set forth [the meditation on identity with] the person in the sun, the <s>Aitareyins</s> teach this; likewise the <s>Jābālas</s>: 'You are I, O Lord-deity, and I am you.' The question is: Should the meditation here involve a twofold cognition through the interchange, or only a single cognition [of identity]? The prima facie view says: Only a single cognition. For here, apart from the oneness of the Self with the Lord, there is nothing else to be contemplated. And if a difference were imagined for such contemplation, [it would mean:] the <s>saṃsārin</s> would have Lord-Self-hood, and the Lord would have <s>saṃsārin</s>-Self-hood. Of these, the <s>saṃsārin</s>'s having the nature of the Lord would be an elevation; but the Lord's having the nature of a <s>saṃsārin</s> — how would that be a degradation? Therefore, the meditation should be of a single form [only]. And the interchange-teaching is merely for the purpose of strengthening the [conviction of] oneness. Having set forth this [prima facie view], [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] responds: This interchange is taught for the purpose of meditation (<s>ādhyāna</s>), as with the other [attributes]. Just as the other attributes — beginning with all-Self-hood — are taught for the purpose of meditation, so too [this interchange]. For thus the teachers specify through the utterance of both [forms]: 'You are I and I am you' (<s>Jābāla</s>). And that [specification] is meaningful when a twofold meditation is to be performed. For otherwise, this specific double utterance would be purposeless — since the intended meaning would be conveyed by one [utterance] alone.

children.text: nanūbhayāmnānasyārthaviśeṣe parikalpyamāne devatāyāḥ saṃsāryātmatvāpatternikarṣaḥ prasajyetetyuktam /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it has been said that if a specific meaning were imagined for the double utterance, the degradation of the deity — by acquiring the nature of a <s>saṃsārin</s> — would follow.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
aikātmyasyaivānena prakāreṇānucintyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because it is the very identity that is being contemplated in this manner [through interchange].

children.text:
nanvevaṃ sati sa evaikatvadṛḍhīkāra āpadyeta /
na vayamekatvadṛḍhīkāraṃ vārayāmaḥ /
kiṃ tarhi vyatihāreṇeha dvirūpā matiḥ kartavyā vacanaprāmāṇyānnaikarūpetyetāvadupapādayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: What then? We are establishing only this much: that here the meditation should be twofold through the interchange — because of the authority of the [scriptural] statement — not single-formed.

children.text: phalatastvekatvamapi dṛḍhībhavati /
children.translated_text: And as a result, the oneness too is strengthened.

children.text: yathādhyānārtho 'pi satyakāmādiguṇopadeśe tadguṇa īśvaraḥ prasiddhyati tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as the teaching of attributes such as '<s>Satyakāma</s>' and the like, even though for the purpose of meditation, results in the Lord becoming well known as possessing those attributes — so too [here].

children.text: tasmādayamādhyātavyo vyatihāraḥ samāne ca viṣaya upasaṃhartavyo bhavatīti // 37 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this interchange is to be meditated upon, and where the subject matter is the same, it should be included. // 37 //
Objection: But in that case, the result would be just the strengthening of the [conviction of] oneness. We do not reject the strengthening of oneness.

children.text: FN: jīveśayormitho viśeṣaṇaviśeśyābhāvo vyatihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: The mutual predication (<s>vyatihāra</s>) of the <s>jīva</s> and the Lord as qualifier and qualified of each other.

children.text: 24 satyādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 38
children.translated_text: Section 24: <s>Satyādyadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 38

children.text: saiva hi satyādayaḥ | BBs_3,3.38 |
children.translated_text: <s>Saiva hi satyādayaḥ</s> — It is the same [<s>vidyā</s>]; for [the attributes of] truth and the rest [should be combined]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.38 |

children.text:
'sa yo haitaṃ mahadyakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda brahma' (bṛ. 5.4.1) ityādinā vājasaneyake satyavidyāṃ sanāmākṣaropāsanāṃ vidhāyānantimāmnāyate - 'tadyattatsatyamaso sa ādityo ya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣo yaścāyaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣaḥ' (bṛ. 5.5.2) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ -' kiṃ dve ete satyavidye kiṃvaikaiveti /
dve iti tāvatprāptam /
bhedena hi phalasaṃyogo bhavati jayatīmāṃllokān' (bṛ. 5.4.12) iti purastāt /
hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca (bṛ. 5.5.3,4) ityupariṣcāt /
prakṛtākarṣaṇaṃ tūpāsyaikatvāditi /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ekaiveyaṃ satyavidyeti /
kutaḥ - 'tadyattatsatyam' (bṛ. 5.5.2) iti prakṛtākarṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension], having enjoined the <s>Satya-vidyā</s> — the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> as the syllables of the name [<s>Satya</s>] — with 'He who knows this great first-born wonder as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.4.1) and the like, [the text] subsequently teaches: 'That which is <s>Satya</s> (truth) — that is the <s>Āditya</s>-person who is within that orb, and the person who is in the right eye' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.2) and the like. The question is: Are these two <s>Satya-vidyās</s>, or is it one? The prima facie view is that there are two. For the connection with fruit is separate: 'He conquers these worlds' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.4.1.2) in the earlier [passage], and 'He destroys sin and abandons [it]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.3-4) in the later [passage]. But the drawing in of the earlier subject matter [in the later passage] is because of the oneness of the object of meditation. Having set forth this [prima facie view], we say: This is one single <s>Satya-vidyā</s>. Why? Because of the drawing in of the earlier subject matter — [as shown by the phrase] 'That which is <s>Satya</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.5.2).

children.text: nanu vidyābhede 'pi prakṛtākarṣaṇamupāsyaikatvādupapadyata ityuktam /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it was said that even with a difference of <s>vidyās</s>, the drawing in of the earlier subject matter is proper because of the oneness of the object of meditation.

children.text:
naitadevam /
yatra tu vispaṣṭātkāraṇāntarādvidyābhedaḥ pratīyate tatraitadevaṃ syāt /
atra tūkṣayā saṃbhave tadyattatsatyamiti prakṛtākarṣaṇātpūrvavidyāsaṃbaddameva satyamuttaratrākṛṣyata ityekavidyātvaniścayaḥ /
yatpunaruktaṃ phalāntaraśravaṇādvidyāntaramiti /
atrocyate - tasyopaniṣadaharahamiti cāṅgāntaropadeśasya stāvakamidaṃ phalāntaraśravaṇamityadoṣaḥ /
apicārthavādādeva phale kalpayitavye sati vidyaikatve cāvayaveṣu śrūyamāṇāni bahūnyapi phalānyavayavinyāmeva vidyāyāmupasaṃhartavyāni bhavanti /
tasmātsaiveyamekā satyavidyā tena tena viśeṣaṇopetāmnātetyataḥ sarva eva satyādayo guṇā ekasminneva prayoga upasaṃhartavyāḥ /
kecitpunarasminsūtra idaṃ ca vājasaneyakamakṣyādityapuruṣaviṣayaṃ vākyaṃ, chāndogye ca - 'atha ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā. 1.6.6) 'atha ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā. 4.15.1) ityudāha-tya saiveyamakṣyādityapuruṣaviṣayā vidyobhayatraikaiveti kṛtvā satyādīnguṇānvājasaneyibhyaśchandogānāmupasaṃhāryānmanyante /
tanna sādhu lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: That does not appear proper.

children.text: chāndogye hi jyotiṣṭomakarmasamabandhinīyamudgīthavyapāśrayā vidyā vijñāyate tatra hyadimadhyāvasāneṣu hi karmasaṃbandhacihnāni bhavanti 'iyamevargagniḥ sāma' (chā. 1.6.1) ityupakrame, 'tasyarkka sāma ca geṣṇau tasmādudgīthaḥ' (chā. 1.6.8) iti madhye, 'ya evaṃ vidvānsāma gāyati' (chā. 1.7.9) ityupasaṃhāre /
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, this <s>vidyā</s> is understood as connected with the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> ritual, being dependent on the <s>udgītha</s>-[chanting]. For there, at the beginning, middle, and end, there are marks of connection with ritual: at the introduction — 'This indeed is the <s>Ṛk</s>, fire is the <s>Sāman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.1); in the middle — 'Of it, the <s>Ṛk</s> and the <s>Sāman</s> are the chanting components; therefore it is the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.8); and at the conclusion — 'He who, knowing thus, chants the <s>Sāman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.9).

children.text: naivaṃ vājasaneyake kiñcitkarmasaṃbandhi cihnamasti /
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension], there is no such mark of connection with ritual.

children.text: tatra prakramabhedādvidyābhede sati guṇyavasthaiva yukteti // 38 //
children.translated_text: Since the <s>vidyās</s> are different because of the difference of approach, the attributes should remain in their respective places alone — this is proper. // 38 //

This is not so. Where a difference of <s>vidyā</s> is understood from some other clear ground, there this [argument] might hold. But here, when oneness is possible, 'That which is <s>Satya</s>' — through the drawing in of the earlier subject matter — the very <s>Satya</s> connected with the earlier <s>vidyā</s> is drawn over to the later [passage]. Hence the determination that it is one <s>vidyā</s>. As for the statement that there must be a difference of <s>vidyā</s> because of the hearing of different fruits — to that we say: Since 'That is its <s>upaniṣad</s> [i.e., secret name], day after day' — this hearing of different fruits is laudatory of the teaching of an additional component (<s>aṅga</s>) — and so there is no fault. Moreover, when fruit must be postulated from laudatory passages alone, and when the <s>vidyā</s> is one, even many fruits heard for the components should be gathered into the one whole <s>vidyā</s>. Therefore, this is one and the same <s>Satya-vidyā</s>, taught with various qualifications. Hence, all the attributes beginning with <s>Satya</s> and the rest should be gathered into a single practice. But some, regarding this <s>sūtra</s>, cite both the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> passage about the eye-and-sun-person and the <s>Chāndogya</s> [passage]: 'Now, the golden person who is seen within the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.6), 'Now, the person who is seen in the eye' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.1) — and taking these as the same <s>vidyā</s> concerning the eye-and-sun-person in both [recensions], they hold that the attributes beginning with <s>Satya</s> should be gathered from the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> and included in the <s>Chāndogya</s>.

children.text:
FN: geṣṇau gāyakau /
tasmādṛksāmageṣṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Geṣṇau</s>' means singers [i.e., chanting components]. Therefore, because of [their] being chanting components of <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: 25 kāmādyadhikārādhikaramam / sū. 39
kāmādītaratra tatra cāyatanādibhyaḥ | BBs_3,3.39 |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmādītaratra tatra cāyatanādibhyaḥ</s> — [The attributes of] desire and the rest [are to be included] from one [recension] to the other, because of the [common] abode and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.39 |
Section 25: <s>Kāmādyadhikārādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 39

children.text:
atha yadidamasminbrahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminnantarākāśaḥ (chā. 8.1.1) iti prastutya chandogā adhīyate 'eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyurviśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' (chā. 8.1.5) ityādi /
tathā vājasaneyinaḥ - sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmā yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu ya eṣo 'ntarhadaya ākāśastasmiñchete sarvasya vaśī (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityādi /
tatra vidyaikatvaṃ parasparaguṇayogaśca kiṃ vā neti saṃśaye vidyaikatvamiti /
tatredamucyate - kāmādīti /
satyakāmādityarthaḥ /
yathā devadatto dattaḥ satyabhāmā bhāmeti /
yadetaccāndogye hṛdayākāśasya satyakāmatvādiguṇajātamulabhyate taditaratra vājasaneyake vaśitvādyupalabhyate tadapītaratra chāndogye eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā (chā. 8.1.5) ityatra saṃbadhyate /
kutaḥ - āyatanādisāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Having introduced [the topic] with 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s> there is a small lotus-dwelling; within it there is a small inner space' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1), the <s>Chandogas</s> teach: 'This is the Self — free from evil, ageless, deathless, sorrowless, hungerless, thirstless, whose desires are true (<s>satyakāma</s>), whose intentions are true (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5) and the like. Likewise, the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>: 'This great unborn Self, which is constituted of consciousness, is among the <s>prāṇas</s> — that which is the space within the heart, in it he lies, the controller of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) and the like. The question is: Is the <s>vidyā</s> one [in both], with a mutual inclusion of attributes, or not? When there is doubt, [the answer is:] the <s>vidyā</s> is one. Therein, this is stated: '<s>Kāmādi</s>' — meaning <s>Satyakāma</s> and the like. Just as [one abbreviates] <s>Devadatta</s> as '<s>Datta</s>' and <s>Satyabhāmā</s> as '<s>Bhāmā</s>.' The set of qualities such as <s>Satyakāma</s> and the like, which is found in the <s>Chāndogya</s> for the heart-space — and the [qualities] found in the other, the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension], such as lordship (<s>vaśitva</s>) and the like — these latter are included in the other [i.e., the <s>Chāndogya</s>] too, in the passage 'This is the Self, free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5). Why? Because of the commonality of abode and the like.

children.text: samānaṃ hyubhayamatrāpi hṛdayamātanaṃ samānaśca vedya īśvaraḥ samānaṃ ca tasya setutvaṃ lokāsaṃbhedaprayojanamityevamādi bahu sāmānyaṃ dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For the abode — the heart — is common to both. And the object to be known — the Lord — is the same. And its bridge-hood and the purpose of non-confusion of the worlds are the same — and many such similarities are observed.

children.text:
nanu viśeṣo /
ñapi dṛśyate chāndogye hṛdayākāśasya guṇayogo vājasaneyake tvākāśāśrayasya brahmaṇa iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But a difference is also observed — in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, the attributes are connected with the heart-space, while in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s>, [they are connected with] <s>Brahman</s> abiding in space.

children.text:
na /
'dahara uttarebhyaḥ' (bra.sū. 1.3.14) ityatra chāndogye 'pyākāśaśabdaṃ brahmaiveti pratiṣṭhāpitatvāt /
ayaṃ tvatra vidyate viśeṣaḥ /
saguṇā hi brahmavidyā chāndogya upadiśyate 'atha ya ihātmānamanuvidya vrajantyetāṃśca satyānkāmān' (chā. 8.1.6) ityātmavatkāmānamapi vedyatvaśravaṇāt /
vājasaneyake tu nirguṇameva paraṃ brahmopadiśyamānaṃ dṛśyate 'ata ūrdhvaṃ vimokṣāya brūhi' (bṛ. 4.3.14) asaṅgo hyayaṃ puruṣaḥ (bṛ. 4.3.15) ityādipraśnaprativacanasamanvayāt /
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension], the supreme <s>Brahman</s> without attributes (<s>nirguṇa</s>) alone is seen to be taught — from the coherence of the question and answer: 'Henceforth, teach for the sake of liberation' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.14), 'This <s>Puruṣa</s> is unattached' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.15) and the like.

children.text: vaśitvādi tu tatstutyarthameva guṇajātaṃ vājasaneyake saṃkīrtyate /
children.translated_text: And the set of qualities such as lordship (<s>vaśitva</s>) and the like is recited in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> merely for the purpose of praising that [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: tathācopariṣṭāt 'sa eṣa neti netyātmā' (bṛ. 3.9.26) ityādinā nirguṇameva brahmopasaṃharati /
children.translated_text: And subsequently, [the text] concludes with the attributeless <s>Brahman</s> alone: 'This Self is [described as] "not this, not this"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.26) and the like.

children.text: guṇavatastu brahmaṇa ekatvādvibhūtipradarśanāyāyaṃ guṇopasaṃhāraḥ sūtrito nopāsanāyeti draṣṭavyam // 39 //
children.translated_text: But since <s>Brahman</s> with attributes is one, this gathering of attributes stated in the <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of displaying [<s>Brahman</s>'s] glories — not for [the purpose of] meditation [in the <s>nirguṇa</s> context]. This should be understood. // 39 //

No. Because in [the discussion of] '<s>Dahara</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of what follows' (<s>BBs</s> 1.3.14), it has been established that in the <s>Chāndogya</s> too, the word '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) [denotes] <s>Brahman</s> itself. But the following difference does exist here: In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, a <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> is taught — because the hearing of desires (<s>kāmas</s>) too as objects to be known, along with the Self, is found in: 'Now, those who, having found the Self here, depart — and these true desires' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.6).

children.text: 26 ādarādhikaraṇam / sū. 40-41
children.translated_text: Section 26: <s>Ādarādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 40-41

children.text: ādarādalopaḥ | BBs_3,3.40 |
children.translated_text: <s>Ādarādalopaḥ</s> — Because of the emphatic injunction, there is no omission. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.40 |

children.text:
chāndogye vaiśvānaravidyāṃ prakṛtya śrūyate - 'tadyadbhaktaṃ prathamamāgacchettaddhomīyaṃ sa yāṃ prathamāmāhutiṃ juhuyāttāṃ juhuyātprāṇasya svāhā' (chā. 5.19.1) ityādi /
tatra pañca prāṇāhutayo vihitāḥ /
tāsu ca parastādagnihotraśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ 'ya etadevaṃ vidvānagnihotraṃ juhoti' (chā. 5.24.2) iti 'yatheha kṣudhitā bālā mātaraṃ paryupāsate /
evaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyagnihotramupāsate' (chā. 5.24.5) iti ca /
tatredaṃ vicāryate - kiṃ bhojanalope lopaḥ prāṇāgnihotrasyotālopa itai /
tadyadbhavati bhaktāgamanasaṃyogaśravaṇādbhaktāgamanasya ca bojanārthatvādbhojanalope lopaḥ prāṇāgnihotrasyeti /
evaṃ prāpte na lupyeteti tāvadāha /
kasmāt /
ādarāt /
tathāhi vaiśvāravidyāyāmeva jābālānāṃ śrutiḥ - 'pūrvo 'tithibhyo 'śnīyāt /
yathā ha vai svayamahutvāgnihotraṃ parasya juhuyādevaṃ tat' ityatithibhojanasya prāthamyaṃ ninditvā svāmibhojanaṃ prathamaṃ prāpayantī prāṇāgnihotra ādaraṃ karoti /
yā hi na prāthamyalopaṃ sahate netarāṃ sā prāthamyavato 'gnihotrasya lopaṃ sahateti manyate /
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Chāndogya</s>, in connection with the <s>Vaiśvānaravidyā</s>, it is heard: 'Whatever food arrives first — that is fit for offering. The first oblation that one offers — that one should offer [with the mantra] "To <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.19.1) and so forth.
There, five oblations to the <s>prāṇas</s> are enjoined.
And in connection with those [oblations], the word '<s>agnihotra</s>' is used subsequently: 'He who, knowing this thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.24.2); and 'Just as hungry children gather around their mother, so all beings gather around the <s>agnihotra</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.24.5).
Here, the following is examined: When eating is omitted, is the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> also omitted, or not?
The prima facie view is: Because of the hearing that [the oblation is] connected with the arrival of food, and because the arrival of food is for the purpose of eating — when eating is omitted, the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> too is omitted.
Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] first states: It is not omitted.
Why?
Because of the emphasis (<s>ādara</s>).
For thus, in the <s>Vaiśvānaravidyā</s> itself, the <s>śruti</s> of the <s>Jābālas</s> [states]: 'One should eat before the guests.
For one who offers the <s>agnihotra</s> to another without first offering it himself — that is like [offering to another without having offered oneself]' — thus, by censuring the priority of feeding guests, and by establishing that the householder should eat first, [the text] shows emphasis on the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>.
For [a text] that does not tolerate even the loss of priority would not, it is thought, tolerate the omission of the <s>agnihotra</s> whose priority [it guards].

children.text: nanu bhojanārthabhaktāgamanasaṃyogādbhojanalope lopaḥ prathitaḥ /
children.translated_text: But was not the omission [of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>] upon the omission of eating established by the hearing of [the offering's] connection with the arrival of food meant for eating?

children.text: na /
tasya dravyaviśeṣavidhānārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because that [passage] is intended for enjoining a specific substance.

children.text: prākṛte hyagnihotre payaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ dravyāṇāṃ niyatatvādihāpyagnihotraśabdātkauṇḍapāyināmayanavattaddharmaprāptau satyāṃ bhaktadravyaikatāguṇaviśeṣavidhānārthamidaṃ vākyaṃ tadyadbhaktamiti /
children.translated_text: For in the regular (<s>prākṛta</s>) <s>agnihotra</s>, since substances like milk and the like are fixed, here too — because of the word '<s>agnihotra</s>' — just as in the case of the <s>Kauṇḍapāyins</s>' lunar fortnight [ritual], when the properties of the [regular <s>agnihotra</s>] would be inherited, this passage 'Whatever food [arrives first]' is meant for enjoining the specific quality that the substance should be [the first] food.

children.text: ato guṇalope na mukhyasyetyeṃ prāptam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the accessory [substance] is absent, the principal [rite] is not [omitted] — this is the position established.

children.text: bhojanalope 'pyadbhirvānyena vā dravyeṇāviruddhena pratinidhānanyāyena prāṇāgnihotrasyānuṣṭhānamiti // 40 //
children.translated_text: Even when eating is omitted, the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> should be performed through substitution — with water or with another non-contradictory substance — by the principle of substitution. // 40 //
No.

children.text: ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: Now [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the reply:

children.text: upasthite 'tastadvacanāt | BBs_3,3.41 |
children.translated_text: When [food] has arrived — from that [food] itself, because of the statement [to that effect]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.41 |

children.text:
upasthite bhojane 'tastasmādeva bhojanadravyātprathamopanipatitātprāṇāgnihotraṃ nirvartayitavyam /
kasmāt /
tadvacanāt /
tathāhi - 'tadyadbhaktaṃ prathamamāgacchettaddhomīyam' (chā. 5.19.1) iti /
siddhavadbhaktopanipātaparāmarśena parārthadravyasādhyatāṃ prāṇāhutīnāṃ vidadhāti /
tā aprayojakalakṣaṇāpannāḥ satyaḥ kathaṃ bhojanalope dravyāntaraṃ pratinidhāpayeyuḥ /
nacātra prākṛtāgnihotradharmaprāptirasti /
kuṇḍapāyināmayane hi māsāgnihotraṃ juhotīti vidhyuddeśagato 'gnihotraśabdastadvadbhāvaṃ vidāpayediti yuktā taddharmaprāptiḥ /
iha punarartavādagato 'gnihotraśabdo na tadvadbhāvaṃ vidhāpayitumarhati /
taddharmaprāptau cābhyupagamyamānāyāmagnyuddharaṇādayoṣa-pi prāpyeran /
nacāsti saṃbhavaḥ /
agnyuddharaṇaṃ tāvaddhomādhikaramabhāvāya /
nacāyamagnau homo bhojanārthatāvyāghātaprasaṅgāt /
bhojanopanītadravyasaṃbandhāccāsya evaiṣa homaḥ /
tathāca jābālaśrutiḥ pūrvo 'tithibhyo 'śnīyādityāsyādhārāmevemāṃ homanirvattiṃ darśayati /
ata eva cehāpi sāṃpādikānyevāgnihotrāṅgāni darśayati - 'ura eva vedirlomāni bahurhṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo mano 'nvāhāryapacana āsyamāhavanīyaḥ' (chā. 5.18.2) iti /
vediśrutiścātra sthaṇḍilamātropalakṣaṇārthā draṣṭavyā /
mukhyāgnihotre vedyābhāvāt /
tadaṅgānāṃ ceha saṃpipādayiṣitatvāt /
bhojanenaiva ca kṛtakālena saṃyogānnāgnihotrakālāvarodhasaṃbhavaḥ /
evamanye 'pyupasthānādayo dharmāḥ kecitkathañcidvirudhyante /
tasmādbhojanapakṣa evaite mantradravyadevatāsaṃyogātpañca homā nirvartayitavyāḥ /
yattvādaradarśanavacanaṃ tadbhojanapakṣe prāthamyavidhānārtham /
children.translated_text: As for the statement about showing emphasis (<s>ādara</s>) — that is meant, in the context of the eating interpretation, for enjoining the priority [of one's own eating].

children.text: nahyasti vacanasyātibhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: For there is no over-burdening of the statement [by this interpretation].

children.text: na tvanenāsya nityatā śakyate darśayitum /
children.translated_text: But by that [statement], the permanence (non-omissibility) [of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s>] cannot be demonstrated.

children.text: tasmādbhojanalopa eva prāṇāgnihotrasyeti // 41 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, when eating is omitted, the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> too is omitted. // 41 //

When eating is available — from that very food-substance that has first arrived — the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> should be performed.
Why?
Because of the statement [to that effect].
For thus — 'Whatever food arrives first — that is fit for offering' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.19.1) — by referring to the arrival of food as if it were already established, [the text] enjoins that the oblations to the <s>prāṇas</s> are to be accomplished with that other [i.e., non-self] substance.
If those [oblations] had the character of being purposeless [without food], how could they, when eating is omitted, cause the substitution of another substance?
And here, there is no inheritance of the properties of the regular (<s>prākṛta</s>) <s>agnihotra</s>.
For in the case of the <s>Kauṇḍapāyins</s>' lunar fortnight, the word '<s>agnihotra</s>' occurs in the injunctive statement itself — 'He offers the <s>agnihotra</s> on the new moon day' — so it is proper that the properties of [the regular <s>agnihotra</s>] are inherited.
But here, the word '<s>agnihotra</s>' occurring in an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) is not capable of establishing such an inheritance.
And if the inheritance of [regular <s>agnihotra</s>] properties were accepted, the extraction of fire and the like would also have to be inherited.
And that is not possible.
First, the extraction of fire [is impossible] because [this offering] has no [separate] fire-receptacle.
And this is not an offering into [a separate] fire — because it would contradict the purpose of eating.
And because of the connection with the substance brought for eating, this offering belongs to that [eating process] itself.
And thus the <s>Jābāla śruti</s> — 'One should eat before the guests' — shows that this offering is accomplished through eating itself.
For this very reason, [the text] here shows figurative (<s>sāṃpādika</s>) limbs of the <s>agnihotra</s>: 'The chest is the altar (<s>vedi</s>), the body-hair is the sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>), the heart is the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire, the mind is the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> fire, the mouth is the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.2).
And the mention of '<s>vedi</s>' here should be understood as indicating merely a leveled ground (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>).
Because in the regular <s>agnihotra</s>, there is no [separate] <s>vedi</s>.
And because the limbs [mentioned] here are intended to be figuratively established [as equivalents].
And because of the connection with eating, which has a fixed time, it is not possible to restrict [this offering] to the time of [the regular] <s>agnihotra</s>.
Thus, other properties too — such as the <s>upasthāna</s> (approach) and the like — in some way or other conflict [with the eating context].
Therefore, only when eating is available should these five oblations be performed — [since they require] the conjunction of <s>mantras</s>, substance, and deities.

children.text: 27 tannirdhāraṇādhikaraṇam / sū. 42
children.translated_text: 27. The <s>Tannirdhāraṇādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Determination of Those [Meditations]). <s>Sūtra</s> 42.

children.text: tannirdhāraṇāniyamastaddṛṣṭeḥ pṛthagghyapratibandhaḥ phalam | BBs_3,3.42 |
children.translated_text: The determination of those [as accessories of ritual] is not binding — because of the observation [that they have independent fruit]; for separately, [they are] without obstruction [and have their own] fruit. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.42 |

children.text:
santi karmāṅgavyapāśrayāṇi vijñānāni - 'omityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.1.1) ityevamādīni /
kiṃ tāni nityānyeva syuḥ karmasu parṇamayītvādivadutānityāni godohanādivaditi vicārayāmaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ - nityānīti /
kutaḥ - prayogavacanaparigrahāt /
anārabhyādhītānyapi hyetānyudgīthādidvāreṇa kratusaṃbandhātkratuprayogavacanenaivāṅgāntaravatsaṃspṛśyante /
yattveṣāṃ svavākyeṣu phalaśravaṇam 'āpayitā ha vaikāmānāṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.7) ityādi tadvartamānāpadeśarūpatvādarthavādamātramevāpāpaślokaśravaṇādivanna phalapradānam /
tasmādyathā yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti ityevamādīnāmaprakaraṇapaṭhitānāmapi juhvādidvāreṇa kratupraveśātprakaraṇapaṭhitavannityataivamudgīthādyupāsanānāmapīti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tannirdhāraṇaniyama iti /
yānyetānyudgīthādikarmaguṇayāthātmyanirdhāraṇāni rasatama āptiḥ samṛddhirmukhyaprāṇa āditya ityevamādīni naitāni nityavatkarmasu niyamyeran /
kutaḥ - taddṛṣṭeḥ /
tathāhyaniyatatvamevañjātīyakānāṃ darśayati śrutiḥ - 'tenobhau kuruto yaścaitadevaṃ veda yaśca na veda' (chā. 1.110) ityaviduṣo 'pi kriyābhyanujñānāt /
prastāvādidevatāvijñānavihīnānāmapi prastotrādīnāṃ yājanādhyavasānadarsanāt 'prastotaryā devatā prastāvamanvāyattā tāṃ cedavidvānprastoṣyasi' (chā. 1.10.9) 'tāṃ cedavidvānudgāsyasi' (chā. 1.10.10) 'tāṃ cedavidvānpratihariṣyasi' (chā. 1.10.11) iti ca /
api caivañjātīyakasya karmavyapāśrayasya vijñānasya pṛthageva karmaṇaḥ phalamupalabhyate karmaphalasiddhiddyapratibandhastatsamṛddhiratiśayaviśeṣaḥ kaścit 'tenobhau kuruto yaścaitadevaṃ veda yaśca na veda /
nānā tu vidyā cāvidyā ca yadeva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tadeva vīryavattaraṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.10) iti /
tatra nānā tviti vidvadavidvatprayogayoḥ pṛthakkaraṇādvīyarvattaramiti ca tarappratyayaprayogādvidyāvihīnamapi karmaviryavaditi gamyate /
taccānityatve vidyāyā upapadyate /
nityatve tu kathaṃ tadvihīnaṃ karmaviryavadityanujñāyeta /
sarvāṅgopasaṃhāre hi vīryavatkarmeti sthitiḥ /
tathā lokasāmādiṣu pratiniyatāni pratyupāsanaṃ phalāni śiṣyante 'kalpante hāsmai lokā ūrdhvāścāvṛttāśca' (chā. 2.2.3) ityevamādīni, nacedaṃ phalaśravaṇamarthavādamātraṃ yuktaṃ pratipattum /
tathāhi guṇavāda āpadyeta /
phalopadeśe tu mukhyavādopapattiḥ /
prayājādiṣu tvitikartavyatākāṅkṣasya kratoḥ prakṛtatvāttādarthye sati yuktaṃ phalaśruterarthavādatvam /
tathānārabhyādhīteṣvapi parṇamayītvādiṣu /
nahi parṇamayītvādīnāmakriyātmakānāmāśrayamantareṇa phalasaṃbandho 'vakalpate /
godohanādīnāṃ hi prakṛtāppraṇayanādyāśrayalābhādupapannaḥ phalavidhiḥ /
tathā bailvādīnāmapi prakṛtayūpādyāśrayalābhādupapannaḥ phalavidhiḥ /
natu parṇamayītvādiṣvevaṃvidhaḥ kaścidāśrayaḥ prakṛto 'sti /
vākyenaiva tu juhvādyāśrayatāṃ vivakṣitvā phale 'pi vidhiṃ vivakṣato vākyabhedaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: And if one intended to establish, by the sentence itself, the substrate-relation [of the leaf-cup] with the ladle and the like, and [also] to intend a fruit-injunction — then the sentence would be split [into two purposes].

children.text: upāsanānāṃ tu kriyātmatvādviśiṣṭavidhānopapatterudgīthādyāśrayāṇāṃ phale vidānaṃ na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: But for the meditations — because they are of the nature of action, and because an injunction qualifying [them with a specific fruit] is tenable — the fruit-injunction for those [meditations] dependent on the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like is not contradictory.

children.text: tasmādyathā kratvāśrayāṇyapi godohanādīni phalasaṃyogādanityānyevamudgīthādyupāsanānyapīti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the cow-milking and the like — though connected with rituals — are optional because of their connection with [independent] fruit, so too the meditations on the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like should be regarded [as optional].

children.text: ata eva ca kalpasūtrakārā naivañjātīyakānyupāsanāni kratuṣu kalpayāñcakruḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, the authors of the <s>Kalpasūtras</s> did not include meditations of this kind in the ritual procedures. // 42 //

There are cognitions (<s>vijñānas</s>) that are dependent on ritual accessories — such as 'One should meditate on the syllable <s>Om</s> as the <s>Udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1) and the like.
The question is: Are these always obligatory [parts] of rituals — like [the use of] leaf-cups (<s>parṇamayī</s>) and the like — or are they optional — like milking the cow [for a specific ritual] (<s>godohana</s>) and the like?
What is the prima facie view? That they are always obligatory.
Why? Because they are subsumed under the statement of performance.
For even these [meditations], though not belonging to the [same] beginning-section, are touched by the very performance-statement of the ritual — through the medium of the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — like other accessories, because of their connection with the ritual.
As for the hearing of a fruit in their own passages — 'He becomes indeed the fulfiller of desires' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.7) and the like — that, being in the form of a present-tense description, is mere <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) and does not confer the fruit — like the hearing of absence of ill-repute [for leaf-cups].
Therefore, just as leaf-cups and the like — though read outside the ritual-context — have permanence [as ritual accessories] because of their entry into the ritual through [their connection with] the ladle (<s>juhū</s>) and the like, so too the meditations on the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like [are permanent accessories].
Given this position, we say: 'The determination of those [as obligatory accessories of ritual] is not binding.'
These determinations of the true nature of the ritual accessories of <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — [such as] 'the quintessence,' 'attainment,' 'prosperity,' 'the chief <s>prāṇa</s>,' 'the sun,' and so forth — should not be bound as obligatory parts of rituals.
Why? Because of the observation [of non-restriction].
For thus, the <s>śruti</s> shows that [these meditations] of this kind are not binding: 'By this [syllable <s>Om</s>], both perform — he who knows this thus and he who does not know' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) — [this passage] permits even the one who does not know [the meditation] to perform the ritual.
And the determination that priests (<s>prastotṛ</s> etc.) who lack the knowledge of the deity of the <s>prastāva</s> and the like may still officiate is observed: 'O <s>Prastotṛ</s>, if you, not knowing that deity which is connected with the <s>prastāva</s>, will sing the <s>prastāva</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.10.9); 'If you, not knowing, will sing the <s>Udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.10.10); 'If you, not knowing, will sing the <s>Pratihāra</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.10.11).
Moreover, for a cognition of this kind — one dependent on a ritual accessory — a fruit separate from the ritual is obtained: not an obstruction of the ritual's fruit-accomplishment, but rather a certain special enrichment and excellence beyond it — 'By this both perform — he who knows this and he who does not. But knowledge and ignorance are different; what one does with knowledge, with faith, with meditation (<s>upaniṣad</s>) — that alone is more powerful' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10).
There, the phrase 'but different' shows the separateness of the performance by the knower and the non-knower; and the comparative suffix in 'more powerful' indicates that even the <s>karma</s> without knowledge is [already] powerful.
And this [independence] is proper if the knowledge is optional.
But if [knowledge were] obligatory, how could <s>karma</s> without knowledge be permitted as 'powerful'?
For the position is: only when all accessories are combined is the <s>karma</s> powerful.
Likewise, in the <s>Lokasāma</s> and the like, specific fruits are taught for each meditation: 'Worlds above and below become his' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.3) and so forth — and it is not proper to understand this statement of fruit as mere <s>arthavāda</s>.
For thus, it would turn out to be a <s>guṇavāda</s> (accessory-statement).
But if the fruit-teaching is understood as primary, the primary statement is tenable.
In the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) and the like, however, because the ritual — which expects those as 'things to be done' — is the main topic, it is proper for the statement of fruit to be [mere] <s>arthavāda</s> when they are understood as serving [the ritual].
Likewise, even for [things] read outside the beginning-section (<s>anārabhyādhīta</s>), such as the leaf-cup characteristic and the like.
For there is no fruit-connection for things like the leaf-cup characteristic — which are not of the nature of action — without a substrate [i.e., a ritual to be part of].
For the cow-milking (<s>godohana</s>) and the like, because they gain a substrate through [their connection with] the established water-carrying (<s>praṇayana</s>) and the like, a fruit-injunction is tenable.
Likewise for the <s>bailvī</s> (wood of <s>bilva</s>) and the like, because they gain a substrate through the established sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) and the like, a fruit-injunction is tenable.
But for the leaf-cup characteristic and the like, no such established substrate exists in the main topic.

children.text: 28 pradānādhikaraṇam / sū. 43
children.translated_text: 28. The <s>Pradānādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Principal [<s>Prāṇa</s>]). <s>Sūtra</s> 43.

children.text: pradānavadeva taduktam | BBs_3,3.43 |
children.translated_text: Just as with the principal (<s>pradāna</s>) — this has been stated. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.43 |

children.text: vājasaneyake - 'vadiṣyāmyevāhamīti vāgdadhre' (bṛ. 1.5.21) ityatrādhyātmaṃ vāgādīnāṃ śreṣṭho 'vadhārito 'dhidaivatamagnyādīnāṃ vāyuḥ tathā chāndogye - 'vāyurvāva saṃvargaḥ' (chā. 4.3.1) ityatrādhidaivatamagnyādīnāṃ vāyuḥ sarṅgo 'vadhāritaḥ 'prāṇo vāva saṃvargaḥ' (chā. 4.3.2) ityatrādhyātmaṃ vāgādīnāṃ prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>: 'I shall speak — speech resolved' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21) — here, in the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) aspect, [<s>prāṇa</s>] is ascertained as the best among speech and the other [<s>prāṇas</s>]; and in the cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) aspect, wind (<s>vāyu</s>) [is ascertained as the best] among fire and the other [deities]. Likewise, in the <s>Chāndogya</s>: 'Wind indeed is the absorber' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.1) — here, in the cosmic aspect, wind is ascertained as the absorber (<s>saṃvarga</s>) of fire and the other [elements]; 'The vital breath indeed is the absorber' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.2) — here, in the individual aspect, <s>prāṇa</s> [is ascertained as the absorber] of speech and the other [senses].

children.text:
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ pṛthagevemau vāyuprāṇāvupagantavyau syātāmapṛthagveti /
apṛthageveti tāvatprāptaṃ tattvabhedāt /
nahyabhinne tattve pṛthaganucintanaṃ nyāyyam /
darśayati ca śrutiradhyātmamadhidaivataṃ ca tattvābhedam - 'agnirvāgbhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśat' (ai. 2.4) ityārabhya /
tathā 'ta ete sarva eva samāḥ sarvo 'nantāḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.13) ityādhyātmikānāṃ prāmānāmādhidaivikīṃ vibūtimātmabhūtāṃ darśayati /
tathānyatrāpi tatra tatrādhyātmamadhidaivataṃ ca bahudhā tattvabhedadarśanaṃ bhavati /
kvacicca 'yaḥ prāṇaḥ sa vāyuḥ iti spaṣṭameva vāyuṃ prāṇaṃ caikaṃ karoti /
tathodāhṛte 'pi vājasaneyibrāhmaṇe yataścedeti sūryaḥ (bṛ. 1.5.23) ityasminnupasaṃhāraśloke 'prāṇādvā eṣa udeti prāṇe 'stameti' (bṛ. 1.5.23) iti prāṇenaivopasaṃharannetvaṃ darśayati /
tasmādekameva vrataṃ caretprāṇyāccaivāpāyānyācca' (bṛ. 1.5.23) iti ca prāṇavratenaikenopasaṃharennetadeva draḍhayati /
tathā chāndogye 'pi parastāt 'mahātmanaścaturo deva ekaḥ kaḥ sa jāgara bhuvanasya gopāḥ' (chā. 4.3.6) ityekameva saṃvargaṃ gamayati na bravītyeka ekeṣāṃ caturṇāṃ saṃvargo 'paro 'pareṣāmiti /
tasmādapṛthaktvamupagamanasyeti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - pṛthageva vāyuprāṇāvupagantavyāviti /
kasmāt /
pṛthagupadeśāt /
ādhyānārtho hyayamadhyātmādhidaivavibhāgopadeśaḥ so 'satyādhyānapṛthaktve 'narthaka eva syāt /
children.translated_text:
There arises a doubt: Should wind (<s>vāyu</s>) and <s>prāṇa</s> be understood as separate, or as non-separate?
The prima facie view is: They are non-separate — because of the non-difference of their essential nature (<s>tattva</s>).
For it is not proper to contemplate separately when the essential nature is not different.
And the <s>śruti</s> shows the non-difference of essential nature between the individual and the cosmic — beginning with 'Fire, having become speech, entered the mouth' (<s>Aitareya</s> 2.4).
Likewise, 'All of these are equal, all are infinite' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.13) — [the <s>śruti</s>] shows for the individual <s>prāṇas</s> their cosmic glory as identical with their own nature.
Likewise, elsewhere too, in various places, the non-difference of essential nature between the individual and the cosmic is observed.
And in some places, 'That which is <s>prāṇa</s>, that is <s>vāyu</s>' — [the text] explicitly makes wind and <s>prāṇa</s> one.
Likewise, in the <s>Vājasaneyi Brāhmaṇa</s> cited above, in the concluding verse 'From where the sun rises' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23) — 'From <s>prāṇa</s> indeed it rises, in <s>prāṇa</s> it sets' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23) — by concluding with <s>prāṇa</s> alone, [the text] indicates this [non-duality].
'Therefore, one should practice one single vow — one should breathe in and breathe out' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23) — by concluding with the single vow of <s>prāṇa</s>, [the text] confirms this very [point].
Likewise, in the <s>Chāndogya</s> too, subsequently: 'These great beings (<s>mahātmans</s>), four deities [absorbed into] one — who is that one (<s>ka</s>), the guardian of the world?' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.6) — [the text] points to a single absorber, and does not say that one [absorber] belongs to one set of four and another to another [set].
Therefore, the non-separateness of the contemplation [is established].
Given this position, we say: Wind and <s>prāṇa</s> should indeed be contemplated separately.
Why?
Because of the separate teaching.
For the purpose of this teaching — the division into individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) and cosmic (<s>adhidaivata</s>) — is meditation. And if the meditations were not separate, [the division] would be purposeless.

children.text: nanūktaṃ na pṛthaganucintanaṃ tattvābhedāditi /
children.translated_text: But was it not said that separate contemplation is not proper because of the non-difference of essential nature?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
tattvābhede 'pyavasthābhedādupadeśabhedavaśenānucintanabhedopapatteḥ /
ślokopanyāsasya ca tattvābhedābhiprāyeṇāpyupapadyamānasya pūrvoditadhyeyabhedanirākaraṇasāmarthyābhāvāt /
'sa yathaiṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇa evametāsāṃ devatānāṃ vāyuḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.22) iti copamānopameyakaraṇāt /
etena vratopadeśo vyākhyātaḥ /

'ekameva vrataṃ caret' (bṛ. 1.5.23) iti cektvā 'teno etasyai devatāyai sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati (bṛ. 1.5.23) iti vāyuprāptiṃ phalaṃ bruvanvāyuvratamanivartitaṃ darśayati /
dvatetyatra vāyuḥ syādapariccinnātmakatvasya prepsitatvāt /

tasmātpṛthagevopagamanam /
pradānavat /
yathendrāya rājñe puroḍāśamekādaśakapālamindrāyādhirājāyendrāya svarājña ityasyāṃ tripuroḍāśinyāmiṣṭau sarveṣāmabhigamayannavadyatyachaṃbaṭkāramiti /
ato vacanādindrābhedācca sahapradānāśaṅkāyāṃ rājādiguṇabhedādyājyānuvākyavyatyāsavidhānācca yathānyasameva devatāpṛthaktvātpradānapṛthaktvaṃ bhavati /
evaṃ tattvābhede 'pyādhyeyāṃśapṛthaktvādādhyānapṛthaktvamityarthaḥ /
taduktaṃ saṃkarṣe 'nānā vā devatā pṛthagjñānāt' iti /
tatra tu dravyadevatābhedādyāgabhedo vidyate naivamiha vidyābhedo 'sti /
children.translated_text: But there, because of the difference of material substance and deity, there is a difference of sacrifices — here, however, there is no such difference of <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: upakramopasaṃhārābhyāmadhyātmādhidaivopadeśeṣvekavidyāvidhānapratīteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because from the introduction (<s>upakrama</s>) and conclusion (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>), the prescription of a single <s>vidyā</s> is understood for the inner (<s>adhyātma</s>) and outer (<s>adhidaiva</s>) teachings.

children.text: vidyaikasthe 'pi tvadhyātmādhidaivabhedātpravṛttibhedo bhavati agnihotra iva sāyaṃprātaḥkālabhedāt /
children.translated_text: But even though the <s>vidyā</s> is one, the difference in practice is due to the difference of inner (<s>adhyātma</s>) and outer (<s>adhidaiva</s>) [aspects] — like the <s>Agnihotra</s> [which is one sacrifice but differs] because of the difference of evening and morning times.

children.text: ityetāvadabhipretya pradānavadityuktam // 43 //
children.translated_text: With just this much in view, it was said: 'As with the offering.' // 43 //

This is not a fault.
Even though there is no difference in the [underlying] reality, because of the difference in states [i.e., inner and outer], the difference in contemplation is tenable on account of the difference in teaching.
And the citation of the verse — even though it is tenable with the intention of non-difference in reality — is not capable of negating the previously stated difference in the objects of contemplation.
And because [the <s>śruti</s>] makes [<s>prāṇa</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>] the subject of comparison and that to which the comparison is made: 'Just as among these <s>prāṇas</s>, [the chief] <s>Prāṇa</s> is the middle one, so among these deities, <s>Vāyu</s> [is the middle one]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.22).
By this, the teaching of the observance (<s>vrata</s>) is explained.
And the word '<s>eva</s>' (alone) in 'One observance alone [should one practice]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23) is for the purpose of apprehending the <s>prāṇa</s>-observance, by setting aside the observances of speech and the like.
For speech and the like have been declared as having broken observances — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Death, in the form of fatigue, seized them' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21).
It is not for the purpose of negating the <s>Vāyu</s>-observance — because, having introduced [the topic] with 'Now, the investigation of the observance' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.21), the unbroken observance of both <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s> equally has been ascertained.
And having said 'One observance alone should one practice' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23), [the <s>śruti</s>] states the fruit as the attainment of <s>Vāyu</s>: 'Thereby he wins union (<s>sāyujya</s>) and co-residence (<s>salokatā</s>) with that deity' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23) — thus showing that the <s>Vāyu</s>-observance has not been negated.
'That deity' here would be <s>Vāyu</s> — since it is the unlimited Self-nature that is desired.
And because of prior usage [in the passage]: 'This is the deity that never sets — namely <s>Vāyu</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.22).
Likewise, 'These two are indeed the two absorbers (<s>saṃvargas</s>) — <s>Vāyu</s> among the deities and <s>Prāṇa</s> among the <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.4) — [the <s>śruti</s>] designates them with difference; and 'These are indeed the five and five, the ten — and that is the <s>kṛta</s> [the highest throw]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.8) — [the <s>śruti</s>] concludes with difference too.
Therefore, the approach [to <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s>] is separate.
As with the offering (<s>pradāna</s>).
Just as in the sacrifice with three <s>puroḍāśas</s> — 'A <s>puroḍāśa</s> on eleven potsherds for <s>Indra</s> the King; for <s>Indra</s> the Supreme Ruler; for <s>Indra</s> the Self-Sovereign' — even though the deity is one [<s>Indra</s>], someone [might suspect] a joint offering based on the statement and the non-difference of <s>Indra</s>; yet because of the difference of qualities such as 'King' and the like, because of the prescription of the interchange of <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> [verses], the offering is separate for each, [since] the separation of deities [entails] separation of offerings — just as [separate] entities.
Similarly, even though there is no difference in reality, because of the difference in the aspects to be contemplated, there is a difference in practice — this is the meaning.
This has been stated in the <s>Saṃkarṣa</s> [section of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>]: 'The deities are indeed different — because of the separateness of the designations.'

children.text: 29 liṅgabhūyastvādhikaraṇam / sū. 44-52
children.translated_text: 29. The <s>Liṅgabhūyastva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Preponderance of Indicative Marks). <s>Sūtras</s> 44-52.

children.text: liṅgabhūyastvāttaddhi balīyastadapi | BBs_3,3.44 |
children.translated_text: Because of the preponderance of indicative marks — for that [i.e., the indicative mark] is stronger; [and] that too [is considered]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.44 |

children.text:
vājasaneyino 'gnirahasye - 'naiva idamagre sadāsīt' ityetasminbrāhmaṇe mano 'dhikṛtyādhīyate 'tatṣaṭtriṃśatsahasrāṇyapaśyadātmano 'gnīnarkānmanomayāmanaścitaḥ' ityādi /
tathaiva 'vākcitaḥ prāṇacitaścakṣuścitaḥ śrotracitaḥ karmacito 'gnicitaḥ' iti pṛthagagamanīnāmananti sāṃpādikān /
teṣu saṃśayaḥ - kimete manaścidādayaḥ kriyānupraveśinastaccheṣabhūtā uta svatantrāḥ kevalavidyātmakā iti /
tatra prakaraṇākriyānupraveśe prāpte svātantryaṃ tāvatpratijānīte liṅgabhayastvāditi /
children.translated_text: Therein, when the prima facie view is that they are subsidiary to ritual action because of the context — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] first asserts independence: 'Because of the preponderance of indicative marks.'

children.text: bhūyāṃsi hiliṅgānyasminbrāhmaṇe kevalavidyātmakatvameṣāmupodbalayanti dṛśyante tadyatkiñcemāni bhūtāni manasā saṃkalpayanti teṣāmeva sā kṛtiḥ iti, 'tānhaitānevaṃvide sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtāni cinvantyapi svapate' iti caivañjātīyakāni /
children.translated_text: For numerous indicative marks (<s>liṅga</s>) in this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> are seen to reinforce the conclusion that these are of the nature of pure meditation (<s>vidyā</s>) alone: 'Whatever these beings conceive with the mind — that indeed is their creation'; 'For one who knows thus, all beings always build [these fires], even while he sleeps' — and such passages.

children.text: taddhi liṅgaṃ prakaraṇādbalīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For that indicative mark is stronger than the context.

children.text: tadapyuktaṃ pūrvasminkāṇḍe - 'śrutiliṅgavākyaprakaraṇasthānasamākhyānāṃ samavāyepāradaurbalyamarthaviprakarṣāt' (jai.sū. 3.3.13) iti // 44 //
children.translated_text: That too has been stated in the prior <s>kāṇḍa</s> (i.e., <s>Pūrvamīmāṃsā</s>): 'When <s>śruti</s>, indicative mark, passage, context, position, and name are combined, each subsequent one is weaker, because of distance from the intended meaning' (<s>Jaimini Sūtra</s> 3.3.13). // 44 //

The <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, in the <s>Agnirahasya</s> (Secret of the Fire), read the following in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> passage beginning with 'In the beginning, this was neither being nor non-being': 'Those thirty-six thousand [fires] — fires of the Self, consisting of <s>arka</s> [hymns], made of mind, built with mind' — and so on.
Likewise, 'Built with speech, built with <s>prāṇa</s>, built with the eye, built with the ear, built with action, built with fire' — they teach these as separate [fires] that are objects of meditative construction (<s>sāṃpādika</s>).
Regarding these, the doubt arises: Are these fires — built with mind and the like — subsidiary to ritual action, being accessories to it, or are they independent, consisting solely of <s>vidyā</s> (meditation)?

children.text: pūrvavikalpaḥ prakaraṇātsyāt kriyāmānasavat | BBs_3,3.45 |
children.translated_text: The first [i.e., previously stated] option — [that these fires are] subsidiary to ritual action, because of the context — [would apply] as with the mental [cup]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.45 |

children.text:
naitaduktaṃ svatantrā ete 'gnayo 'nanyaśeṣabhūtā iti /
pūrvasya kriyāmayasyāgneḥ prakaraṇāttadviṣaya evāyaṃ vikalpaviśeṣopadeśaḥ syānna svatantraḥ /
