children.translated_text:
[Objection:] It was not rightly said that these fires are independent and not subsidiary to anything else.
Because of the context of the previous fire — the one consisting of ritual action — this specific teaching of an alternative option pertains to that [ritual fire] alone and is not independent.

children.text: nanu prakaraṇālliṅgaṃ balīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the indicative mark is stronger than the context.

children.text:
satyametat /
liṅgamapi tvevañjātīyakaṃ na prakaraṇādbalīyo bhavati /
anyārthadarśanaṃ hyetat /
sāṃpādikāgnipraśaṃsārūpatvāt /
anyārthadarśanaṃ cāsatyāmanyasyāṃ prāptau guṇavādenāpyupapadyamānaṃ na prakaraṇaṃ bādhitumutsahate /
tasmātasāṃpādikā apyete 'gnayaḥ prakaraṇātkriyānupraveśina eva syuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though these fires are objects of meditative construction, they would be subsidiary to ritual action, because of the context.

children.text: mānasavat /
children.translated_text: As with the mental [cup].

children.text: yathā daśarātrasya dasaṇe 'hanyavivākye pṛthivyā pātreṇa samudrasya somasya prajāpataye devatāyai guhyamāṇasya grahaṇāsādanahavanāharaṇopahvānabhakṣaṇāni mānasānyevāmnāyante /
children.translated_text: Just as, in the <s>Daśarātra</s> [ten-night rite], on the <s>Avivākya</s> day, the grasping, placing, offering, bringing, invoking, and drinking of [the cup of <s>Soma</s>] — which is to be extracted from the earthen vessel into the ocean of <s>Soma</s> for the deity <s>Prajāpati</s> — are taught as mental [i.e., performed mentally, not actually].

children.text: sa ca mānaso 'pi grahakalpaḥ kriyāprakaraṇātkriyāśeṣa eva bhavatyevamayamapyagnikalpa ityarthaḥ // 45 //
children.translated_text: And even that mental cup-ritual, though mental, is subsidiary to ritual action because of the context of ritual action — so too this fire-meditation — this is the meaning. // 45 //

True.
But an indicative mark of this kind is not stronger than the context.
For this is a 'seeing of another purpose' (<s>anyārthadarśana</s>) — being of the nature of praise for the fires that are objects of meditative construction.
And a 'seeing of another purpose' — which is tenable even as a subsidiary statement (<s>guṇavāda</s>) when there is no other established claim — is not capable of overriding the context.

children.text: FN: avivākyamiti daśamasyāhno nāmadheyam /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Avivākya</s>' is the name of the tenth day [of the <s>Daśarātra</s>].

children.text: atideśāc ca | BBs_3,3.46 |
children.translated_text: And because of extension (<s>atideśa</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.46 |

children.text: atideśaścaiṣāmagnīnāṅkriyānupraveśamupodbalayati - 'ṣaṭtriṃśatsahasasrāṇyagnayor'kāsteṣāmekaika eva tāvanyāvānasau pūrvaḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: And extension too reinforces the subsidiary status of these fires with respect to ritual action: 'Thirty-six thousand fires of <s>arka</s> — each one of them is as great as the former one' — [this is the extension].

children.text: sati hi sāmānye 'tideśaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: For extension operates [only] when there is a common feature.

children.text: tataśca pūrveṇeṣṭakācitena kriyānupraveśināgninā saṃpādikānagnīnatidiśankriyānupraveśamevaiṣāṃ dyotayati // 46 //
children.translated_text: And thus, by extending [the qualities of] the former fire — the one built with bricks and subsidiary to ritual action — to the fires of meditative construction, [the text] indicates precisely the subsidiary status of these [meditative fires] with respect to ritual action. // 46 //

children.text: vidyaiva tu nirdhāraṇāt | BBs_3,3.47 |
children.translated_text: But [they consist of] <s>vidyā</s> alone — because of the definitive statement. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.47 |

children.text: tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyāvartayati /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) sets aside the [opposing] position.

children.text: vidyātmakā evaite svatantrā manaścidādayo 'gnayaḥ syurna kriyāśeṣabhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: These fires — the mind-built and the like — are of the nature of <s>vidyā</s> alone, being independent — not subsidiary to ritual action.

children.text: tathāhi nirdhārayati - 'te haite vidyācita eva' iti /
children.translated_text: For thus [the <s>śruti</s>] definitively states: 'These are indeed built with <s>vidyā</s> alone.'

children.text: vidyayā haivaita evaṃvidaścitā bhavanti iti ca // 47 //
children.translated_text: 'For one who knows thus, these are indeed built with <s>vidyā</s>' — and so on. // 47 //

children.text: darśanāc ca | BBs_3,3.48 |
children.translated_text: And because of observation. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.48 |

children.text: dṛśyate caiṣāṃ svātantrye liṅgam /
children.translated_text: And an indicative mark for their independence is observed.

children.text: tatpurastāddarśitam liṅgabhūyastvāt (bra. sū. 3.3.44) ityatra // 48 //
children.translated_text: That has been shown previously in [the discussion of the <s>sūtra</s>] 'Because of the preponderance of indicative marks' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.3.44). // 48 //

children.text: nanu liṅgamapyasatyāṃmanyasyāṃ prāptāvasādhakaṃ kasyacidarthasyetyapāsya tatprakaraṇasāmarthyātkriyāśeṣatvamadhyavasitamityata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: Objection: But the indicative mark too — when there is no other established claim — has been set aside as incapable of establishing any [particular] meaning; and from the strength of the context, subsidiary status with respect to ritual action has been determined. Therefore, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the following reply:

children.text: śrutyādibalīyastvāc ca na bādhaḥ | BBs_3,3.49 |
children.translated_text: And because of the greater strength of <s>śruti</s> and the like — there is no overriding. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.49 |

children.text:
naivaṃ prakaraṇasāmarthyātkriyāśeṣatvamadhyavasāya svātantrayapakṣo bādhitavyaḥ /
śrutyāderbalīyastvāt /
balīyāṃsi hi prakaraṇācchrutiliṅgavākyānīti sthitaṃ śrutiliṅgasūtre /
tāni ceha svātantryapakṣaṃ sādhayanti dṛśyante /
katham /
śrutistāvat 'te haite vidyācita eva' iti /
tathā liṅm 'sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtāni cinvantyapi svapate' iti /
tathā vākyamapi 'vidyayā haivaita evaṃvidāśritābhavanti' iti /
'vidyācita eva' iti hi sāvadhāraṇeyaṃ śrutiḥ kriyānupraveśe 'mīṣāmabhyupagamyamāne pīḍitā syāt /
children.translated_text:
One should not thus, on the strength of the context, determine the subsidiary status with respect to ritual action and thereby override the independence-position.
Because of the greater strength of <s>śruti</s> and the like.
For it has been established in the '<s>śruti-liṅga</s>' <s>sūtra</s> [of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>] that <s>śruti</s>, indicative mark, and passage are stronger than context.
And these are seen here to establish the independence-position.
How?
First, <s>śruti</s>: 'These are indeed built with <s>vidyā</s> alone.'
Likewise, indicative mark: 'All beings always build [these fires], even while he sleeps.'
Likewise, passage: 'For one who knows thus, these are indeed built with <s>vidyā</s>.'
For this <s>śruti</s> — with its restrictive particle (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>) '[built with] <s>vidyā</s> alone' — would be strained if the subsidiary status of these [fires] with respect to ritual action were accepted.

children.text: nanvabāhyasādhanatvābhiprāyamidavadhāraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Objection: But this restrictive statement may be intended [merely] to convey that [these fires] do not require external materials.

children.text:
netyucyate /
tadabhiprāyatāyāṃ hividyocita itīyatā svarūpasamakīrtanenaiva kṛtatvādanarthakamavadhāraṇaṃ bhavet /
svarūpameva hyeṣāmabāhyasādhanamiti /
abāhyasādhanatve 'pi tu mānasagrahavatkriyānupraveśaśaṅkāyāṃ tannivṛttiphalamavadhāraṇarthavadbhaviṣyati /
tathā 'svapate jāgrate caivaṃvide sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtānyetānyetānagniṃścinvanti' iti sātatyadarśanameṣāṃ svātantrye 'vakalpate /
yathā sāṃpādike vākyaprāṇamaye 'gnihotre 'prāṇaṃ tadā vāci juhoti - vācaṃ tadā prāṇe juhoti' (kau. 2.5) iti coktvocyate - 'ete anante āhutī jāgracca svapaṃśca satataṃ - juhoti' (kauṣī. 2.5) iti /
tadvat /
kriyānupraveśe tu kriyāprayogasyālpakālatvena na sātatyeṣāṃ prayogaḥ kalpeta /
nacedamarthavādamātramiti nyāyyam /
yatra hi vispaṣṭo vidhāyako liṅgādirupalabhyate yuktaṃ tatra saṃkīrtanamātrasyārthavādatvam /
iha hi vispaṣṭovidhyantarānupalabdheḥ saṃkīrtanādevaiṣāṃ vijñānavidhānaṃ kalpanīyam /
tacca yathāsaṃkīrtanameva kalpayituṃ śakyata iti sātatyadarśanāttathābhūtameva kalpyate /
tataśca sāmarthyādeṣāṃ svātantryasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And from this reasoning, the independence of these [mind-built fires] is established.

children.text: etena tadyatkiñcemāni bhūtāni manasā saṃkalpayanti teṣāmeva sā kṛtiḥ ityādi vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: By this, [passages like] 'Whatever these beings conceive with the mind — that indeed is their creation' and the like are explained.

children.text: tathā vākyamapi evaṃvide iti puruṣaviśeṣasaṃbandhamevaiṣāmācakṣaṇaṃ na kratusaṃbandhaṃ mṛṣyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the passage 'For one who knows thus' — indicating the connection of these [fires] with a specific person [i.e., the knower] — admits [only] a connection with the [knowing] person, not with a ritual.

children.text: tasmātsvātantryapakṣa eva jyāyāniti // 49 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the independence-position alone is the stronger one. // 49 //

We reply: No.
For if that were the intention, the statement of their essential nature — merely '[built with] <s>vidyā</s>' — would already suffice, and the restrictive particle would be purposeless.
For their very nature is that they do not require external materials.
But even with [the understanding that they require] no external materials, there could still be a suspicion of subsidiary status with respect to ritual action — as with the mental cup; and the restrictive particle would then have the purpose of removing that suspicion.
Likewise, 'For one who knows thus, all beings always build these fires, whether he sleeps or is awake' — the observation of constancy (<s>sātatya</s>) is fitting [only] for their independence.
Just as, in the <s>Prāṇamaya Agnihotra</s> — a meditative construction — it is said: 'He offers <s>prāṇa</s> in speech; he offers speech in <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 2.5) and then: 'These two infinite oblations — [he offers them] constantly, whether waking or sleeping' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 2.5).
Similarly [here].
But if they were subsidiary to ritual action, since the performance of ritual action is of limited duration, constancy of practice for these [fires] could not be conceived.
Nor is it proper [to say] that this is mere <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory statement).
For where a clear injunctive [element] such as an indicative mark and the like is found, there alone it is proper for the recitation to be [treated as mere] <s>arthavāda</s>.
But here, since no other clear injunction is found, the injunction of meditation for these [fires] must be derived from the recitation itself.
And since [the injunction] can be derived exactly as recited, from the observation of constancy, it is derived as being of just that [constant] nature.

children.text: anubandhādibhyaḥ prajñāntarapṛthaktvavaddṛṣṭaś ca taduktam | BBs_3,3.50 |
children.translated_text: Because of the colophon (<s>anubandha</s>) and the like — as is observed in the case of other meditations being treated as separate. That has been stated. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.50 |

children.text:
itaśca prakaraṇamupamṛdya svātantryaṃ manaścidādīnāṃ pratipattavyam /
yatkriyāvayavānmana-ādivyāpāreṣvanubadhnāti 'te manasaivādhīyanta manasācīyanta manasaiva grahā agṛhyanta manasāstuvanmanasāśaṃsanyatkiñca yajñe karma kriyate yatkiñca yajñiyaṃ karma manasaiva teṣu tanmanomayeṣu manaścitsu manomayameva kriyate' ityādinā /
saṃpatphalo hyayamanubandhaḥ /
naca pratyakṣāḥ kriyāvayavāḥ santaḥ saṃpadā lipsitavyāḥ /
nacātrodgīthādyupāsanavatkriyāṅgasaṃbandhāttadanupraveśitvamāśaṅkitavyaṃ śrutivairūpyāt /
nahyatra kriyāṅgaṃ kiñcidādāya tasminnado nāmādhyavasitavyamiti vadati /
ṣaṭtriṃśatsahasrāṇi tu manovṛttibhedānādāya teṣvagnitvaṃ grahādīṃśca kalpayati puruṣayādivat /
saṃkhyā ceyaṃ puruṣāyuṣasyāhaḥsu dṛṣṭā satī tatsaṃbandhinīṣu manovṛttiṣvāropyata iti draṣṭavyam /
evamanubandhātsvātantryaṃ manaścidādīnām /
ādiśabdādatideśādyapi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojayitavyam /
tathāhi - 'teṣāmekaika eva tāvānyānānasau pūrvaḥ' iti kriyāmayasyāgnermāhātmyaṃ jñānamayānāmekaikasyātidiśankiriyāyāmanādaraṃ darśayati /
naca satyeva kriyāsaṃbandhe vikalpaḥ pūrveṇottareṣāmiti śakyaṃ vaktum /
nahi yena vyāpāreṇāhanīyadhāraṇādinā pūrvaḥ kriyāyāmupakaroti tenottara upakartuṃ śaknuvanti /
yattu pūrvapakṣe 'pyatideśa upodbalaka ityuktaṃ sati hi sāmānye 'tideśaḥ pravartata iti tadasmātpakṣe 'gnitvasāmānyenātideśasaṃbhavātpratyuktam /
asti hi sāṃpādikānāmapyagnīnāmagnitvamiti /
śrutyādīni ca kāraṇāni darśitāni /
evamanubandhādibhyaḥ kāraṇebhyaḥ svatāntryaṃ manaścidādīnāma /
prajñāntarapṛthaktvavat /
children.translated_text: As is observed in the case of other meditations being treated as separate.

children.text: yathā prajñāntarāṇi śāṇḍilyavidyāprabhṛtīni svena svenānubadhyamānāni pṛthageva karmabhyaḥ prajñāntarebhyaśca svatantrāṇi bhavantyevamiti /
children.translated_text: Just as other meditations such as the <s>Śāṇḍilya-vidyā</s> and the like — each being connected to its own [context] — are independent from rituals (<s>karmas</s>) and from other meditations, so too [are these].

children.text: dṛṣṭaścāveṣṭe rājasūyaprakaraṇapaṭhitāyāḥ prakaraṇādutkarṣo varṇatrayānubandhādrājayajñatvācca rājasūyasya /
children.translated_text: And it is observed that the <s>Aveṣṭi</s>, though recited in the context of the <s>Rājasūya</s>, has a higher standing than [that] context, because of its connection with the three <s>varṇas</s> and because the <s>Rājasūya</s> is a royal sacrifice.

children.text: taduktaṃ prathame kāṇḍe - 'kratvarthāyāmiti cenna varṇatrayasaṃyogāt' (jai.sū. 11.4.7) iti // 50 //
children.translated_text: This has been stated in the First <s>Kāṇḍa</s>: 'If [one says] because of the purpose of the sacrifice — no, because of the connection with three <s>varṇas</s>' (<s>Jaimini Sūtra</s> 11.4.7). // 50 //

And for this further reason, overriding the context, the independence of the mind-built fires and the like is to be accepted.
Because [the <s>śruti</s>] connects the parts of ritual action with mental operations and the like through [a passage like]: 'Those were studied by the mind, were built with the mind; the cups were grasped by the mind; they praised with the mind; they recited with the mind; whatever ritual action is performed in the sacrifice, whatever sacrificial action — all of that, in those [fires] which are made of mind, built with mind, is performed as made of mind alone' — and so on.
For this colophon is for the purpose of meditative superimposition (<s>saṃpat</s>).
And the directly perceived parts of ritual action, being [actually] present, are not to be sought through [mere] superimposition.
Nor should the subsidiary status with respect to ritual action be suspected here — as in the case of the <s>udgītha</s> and similar meditations — because of [the supposed] connection with a component of ritual action. Because of the dissimilarity of <s>śruti</s>.
For here, [the text] does not take up some component of ritual action and say 'such-and-such a name should be superimposed upon it.'
Rather, [the text] takes up thirty-six thousand mental modifications and superimposes upon them fire-nature, cup-rituals, and the like — as in the <s>Puruṣa-Medhā</s> (human sacrifice [performed through meditation]).
And this number [thirty-six thousand] — having been observed in the days of a human lifespan — should be understood as superimposed upon the mental modifications pertaining to those [days].
Thus, from the colophon, the independence of the mind-built fires and the like [is established].
By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like), extension (<s>atideśa</s>) and the like should also be applied as appropriate.
For thus: 'Each one of them is as great as the former one' — by extending the greatness of the ritual fire to each one of the knowledge-based fires, [the text] shows disregard for [mere] ritual action.
And it cannot be said that, since there is indeed a connection with ritual action, the [ritual fire] is an option [alternative] for the latter [knowledge-based fires].
For the latter ones — [the knowledge-based fires] — cannot serve the ritual action by the same operations — such as day-long sustaining and the like — by which the former [ritual fire] serves the ritual action.
As for the objection stated in the prima facie view — that extension reinforces [the subsidiary status with respect to ritual action], because extension operates [only] when there is a common feature — that is refuted by this [our] position, since extension is possible based on the common feature of fire-nature even for the meditative-construction fires.
For even the meditative-construction fires have fire-nature.
And the reasons based on <s>śruti</s> and the like have been shown.
Thus, from the colophon and the like, the independence of the mind-built fires and the like [is established].

children.text: FN: aveṣṭiretannāmnī iṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: <s>Aveṣṭi</s> is the name of a particular <s>iṣṭi</s> (offering).

children.text: na sāmānyādapyupalabdhermṛtyuvanna hi lokāpattiḥ | BBs_3,3.51 |
children.translated_text: Not even from [mere] similarity, because of the finding [of its independent purpose] — like death; for there is no [complete] assimilation [of one thing to another on the basis of] the world-[analogy]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.51 |

children.text:
yaduktaṃ mānasāvaditi tatpratyucyate /
na mānasagrahasāmānyādapi manaścidādīnāṃ kriyāśeṣatvaṃ kalpyam /
pūrvoktebhyaḥ śrutyādihetubhyaḥ kevalapuruṣārthatvopalabdheḥ /
nahi kiñcitkasyacitkenacitsāmānyaṃ na saṃbhavati /
naca tāvatā yathātvaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ nivartate /
children.translated_text: And that much [similarity] alone does not remove the actual difference.

children.text: mṛtyuvat /
children.translated_text: Like death.

children.text: yathā 'sa vā eṣa eva mṛtyurya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣaḥ' iti 'agnirvai mṛtyuḥ' (bṛ. 3.2.10) iti cāgnyādityapuruṣayoḥ samāne 'pi mṛtyuśabdaprayoge nātyantasāmyāpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as, even when the word 'death' (<s>mṛtyu</s>) is used equally for the person in the solar disc — 'He indeed is death, the person who is in this disc' — and for fire — '<s>Agni</s> indeed is death' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.10) — there is no complete assimilation of the fire-person and the sun-person,

children.text: yathā ca 'asau vāva loko gautamāgnistasyāditya eva samit' (chā. 5.4.1) ityatra na samidādisāmānyāllokasyāgnibhāvāpattistadvat // 51 //
children.translated_text: and just as, in 'That world, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed the fire; its fuel is the sun itself' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.4.1), there is no assimilation of the world to fire merely because of the similarity in [possessing] fuel and the like — so too [here]. // 51 //

To the objection that was stated — 'Like the mental [fire-construction]' — this is the reply.
Even from the mere similarity of being mental constructions, the subsidiary status of the <s>manaścit</s> and the like [meditations] with respect to rituals should not be postulated.
Because, from the previously stated reasons based on <s>śruti</s> and the like, [their] purpose as solely for human benefit (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) is found.
For there is nothing whatsoever that does not share some similarity with something else.

children.text: pareṇa ca śabdasya tādvidhyaṃ bhūyastvāt tv anubandhaḥ | BBs_3,3.52 |
children.translated_text: And the subsequent [passage confirms] the nature of the word as such; but because of preponderance, the connection [with the <s>vidyā</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.52 |

children.text:
parastādapi 'ayaṃ vāva loka eṣo 'gniścittaḥ' ityasminnanantare brāhmaṇe tāvadvadhyaṃ kevalavidyāvidhitvaṃ śabdasya prayojanaṃ lakṣyate na śuddhakarmāṅgavidhitvam /
tatra hi -' vidyayā tadārohanti yatra kāmāḥ parāgatāḥ /
na tatra dakṣīṇā yanti nāvidvāṃsastapasvinaḥ' ityanena ślokena kevalaṃ karmanindanvidhyāṃ ca praśaṃsannidaṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text:
'By <s>vidyā</s> they ascend to the place where desires have fully departed;
not there do gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) go, nor the ignorant even if they are ascetics' — by this verse, censuring <s>karma</s> alone and praising <s>vidyā</s>, [the text] conveys this [independence of the <s>vidyā</s>].

children.text: tathā purastādapi yadetanmaṇḍalaṃ tapati ityasminbrāhmaṇe vidyāpradhānatvameva lakṣyate so 'mṛto bhavati mṛtyurhyasyātmā bhavati iti vidyāphalenaivopasaṃhārānna karmapradhānatā tatsāmānyādihāpi tathātvam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the preceding <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too — 'That disc which shines' — the primacy of <s>vidyā</s> alone is perceived, because [the text] concludes with the fruit of <s>vidyā</s> alone: 'He becomes immortal; for death becomes his Self' — not with the primacy of <s>karma</s>. And because of the similarity [between the two passages], the same holds here as well.

children.text: bhūyāṃsastvagnyavayavāḥ saṃpādayitavyā vidyāyāmityetasmātkāraṇādagninānubadhyate vidyā na karmāṅgatvāt /
children.translated_text: But because the preponderant [elements] are the parts of the fire (<s>agni</s>) that are to be imagined in the <s>vidyā</s>, for this reason the <s>vidyā</s> is connected with fire — not because of being subsidiary to <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tasmānmanaścidādīnāṃ kevalavidyātmakatvasiddhiḥ // 52 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the establishment of the <s>manaścit</s> and the like as being solely of the nature of <s>vidyā</s> [is proven]. // 52 //

In the subsequent <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too — 'This world indeed is this mentally constructed fire' — such a nature of the word is perceived, namely, the purpose of establishing a pure meditation (<s>vidyā</s>) alone, not of prescribing a subsidiary of a ritual.
For there —

children.text: 30 aikātmyādhikaraṇam / sū. 53-54
children.translated_text: 30 The <s>Aikātmya</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 53-54.

children.text: eka ātmanaḥ śarīre bhāvāt | BBs_3,3.53 |
children.translated_text: One [Self exists] — because of [its] existence in the body. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.53 |

children.text:
iha dehavyatiriktasyātmanaḥ sadbhāvaḥ samarthyate bandhamokṣādhikārasidamadhayo /
nahyasati dehavyatiriktātmani paralokāścodanā upapajadyerankasya vā brahmātmatvamupadiśyeta /
children.translated_text:
Here, the existence of a Self distinct from the body is argued for — this being a prerequisite for the doctrines of bondage and liberation.
For if there were no Self distinct from the body, the injunctions regarding the other world would not be tenable, nor would the teaching of the identity of the Self with <s>Brahman</s> [have a subject].

children.text: nanu śāstrapramukha eva prathame pāde śāstraphalopabhogyasya dehāvyatiriktasyātmano 'stitvamuktam /
children.translated_text: But has not the existence of a Self distinct from the body — which is the experiencer of the fruits of scripture — already been stated at the very outset, in the first <s>pāda</s>, as a preliminary to the scripture?

children.text:
satyamuktaṃ bhāṣyakṛcā natu tatrātmāstitve sūtramasti /
iha tu svayameva sūtrakṛtā tadastitvamākṣepapuraḥsaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam /
ita eva cākṛṣyācāryeṇa śabarasvāminā pramāṇalakṣaṇe varṇitam /
ata eva ca bhagavatopavarṣeṇa prathame tantra ātmāstitvābhidhānaprasaktau śārīrake vakṣyamāḥ ityuddhāraḥ kṛtaḥ /
iha cedaṃ codanālakṣaṇeṣūpāsaneṣu vicāryamāṇeṣvātmāstitvaṃ vicāryate kṛtsnaśāstraśeṣatvapradarśanāya /
apica pūrvasminnadhikaraṇe prakaraṇotkarṣābhyupagamena manaścidādīnāṃ puruṣārthatvaṃ varṇitaṃ ko 'sau puruṣo yadarthā ete manaścidādaya ityasyāṃ prasaktāvidaṃ dehavyatiriktasyātmano 'stitvamucyate /
tadastitvākṣepārthaṃ cedamādimaṃ sūtram /
ākṣepapūrvikā hi parihāroktirvivakṣiter'the sthūṇānikhanananyāyena dṛḍhāṃ buddhimutpādayati /
atraike dehamātrātmadarśino lokāyatikā dehavyatiriktasyātmano 'bhāvaṃ manyamānāḥ samastavyasteṣu bāhyeṣu pṛthivyādiṣvadṛṣṭamapi caitanyaṃ śarīrākārapariṇateṣu bhūteṣu syāditi saṃbhāvayantastebhyaścaitanyaṃ madaśaktivadvijñānaṃ caitanyaviśiṣṭaḥ kāyaḥ puruṣa iti cāhuḥ /
na svargagamanāyāpavargagamanāya vā samartho dehavyatirikta ātmāsti /
hetuṃ cācakṣataśarīre bhāvāditi /
children.translated_text: And they state the reason: 'Because of [its] existence in the body.'

children.text: yaddhi yasminsati bhavatyasati ca na bhavati tattaddharmatvenādhyavasīte yathāgnidharmāvauṣṇyaprakāśau /
children.translated_text: For whatever exists when something is present and does not exist when it is absent — that is understood as a property of that [thing] — just as heat and light are properties of fire.

children.text: prāṇaceṣṭācaitanyasmṛtyāścātmadharmatvenābhimatā ātmavādināṃ te 'pyantareva deha upalabhyamānā bahiścānupalabhyamānā asiddhe dehavyatirikte dharmiṇi dehadharmā eva bhavitumarhanti /
children.translated_text: And the vital breath, movement, consciousness, and memory — which are accepted as properties of the Self by the proponents of the Self (<s>ātmavādins</s>) — being observed only within the body and not observed outside — in the absence of a proven Self-entity (<s>dharmin</s>) distinct from the body, they must be properties of the body alone.

children.text: tasmādavyatirikto dehādātmana iti // 53 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the Self is not distinct from the body. // 53 //

True, it was stated by the commentator (<s>bhāṣyakṛt</s>), but there is no <s>sūtra</s> on the existence of the Self at that point.
Here, however, the <s>sūtrakāra</s> himself, preceded by a prima facie objection, establishes that existence.
And it is precisely from here that the teacher <s>Śabarasvāmin</s> has cited [the argument] in [his discussion of] the definition of valid means of knowledge.
And it is for this very reason that the revered <s>Upavarṣa</s>, when the occasion arose to discuss the existence of the Self in the first <s>tantra</s>, made the deferral: 'It will be stated in the <s>Śārīraka</s> [i.e., the Brahmasūtra].'
And here, this existence of a Self distinct from the body is examined in the course of the inquiry into meditations that have the nature of injunctions — in order to demonstrate that [this discussion] is a complement to the entire [Vedic] scripture.
Moreover, in the previous <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, the human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) of the <s>manaścit</s> and the like was established by accepting the superiority over the context. The question then arises: Who is that person for whose sake the <s>manaścit</s> and the like [exist]? In this connection, the existence of a Self distinct from the body is stated.
The first <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of [presenting] the objection to that existence.
For a reply that is preceded by an objection produces firm conviction regarding the intended meaning — by the analogy of driving in a post.
Here, certain <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists) — who consider the body alone to be the Self — holding that there is no Self distinct from the body, and surmising that consciousness, which is not observed in any external [elements] such as earth and the like taken separately, might arise in [those very] elements when configured in the form of a body, [claim:] 'From those [elements arises] consciousness; knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) is [like] the power of intoxication; the body endowed with consciousness is the person' — thus they say.
There is no Self distinct from the body that is capable of going to heaven or [attaining] liberation.

children.text: FN: uddhāraḥ uparamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Uddhāra</s>' means deferral.

children.text: evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the prima facie view, we reply:

children.text: vyatirekastadbhāvabhāvitvānna tūpalabdhivat | BBs_3,3.54 |
children.translated_text: There is distinctness [of the Self from the body], because [the properties of the Self] are not present when the body is [merely] present; not [is the case] as with perception. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.54 |

children.text:
natvedamasti yaduktamavyatireko dehādātmana iti /
vyatireka evāsya dehādbhavitumarhati tadbhāvābhvitvāt /
yadi dehabhāve bhāvāddehadharmatvamātmadharmāṇāṃ manyeta tato dehabhāve 'pyabhāvādataddharmatvamevaiṣāṃ kiṃ na manyeta /
dehadharmavailakṣaṇyāt /
yehi dehadharmā rūpādayaste yāvaddehaṃ bhavati /
prāṇaceṣṭādayastu satyapi dehe mṛtāvasthāyāṃ na bavanti /
dehadharmāśca rūpādayaḥ parairapyupalabhyante natvātmadharmāścaitanyasmṛtyādayaḥ /
apica sati hi tāvaddehe jīvadavasthāyāmeṣāṃ bhāvaḥ śakyate niścetuṃ natvasatyabhāvaḥ /
patite 'pi kadācidasmindehe dehāntarasaṃcāreṇātmadharmā anuvarteran /
saṃśayamātreṇāpi parapakṣaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
kimātmakaṃ ca punaridaṃ caitanyaṃ manyate yasya bhūtebhya utpattimicchatīti paraḥ paryanuyoktavyaḥ /
nahi bhūtacatuṣṭayavyatirekeṇa lokāyatikaḥ kiñcittattvaṃ pratyeti /
yadanubhavanaṃ bhūtabhautikānāṃ taccaitanyamiti cet /
tarhi viṣayatvātteṣāṃ na taddharmatvamaśnuvīta svātmani kriyāvirodhāt /
nahyagniruṣṇaḥ sansvātmānaṃ dahati /
nahi naṭaḥ śikṣitaḥ sansvaskandhamadhirokṣyati /
nahi bhūtabhautikadharmeṇa satā caitanyena bhūtabhautikāni viṣayīkriyeran /
nahi rūpādibhiḥ svarūpaṃ pararūpaṃ vāviṣayīkriyate /
viṣayīkriyante tu bāhyādhyātmikāni bhūtabhautikāni caitanyena /
ataśca yathaivāsyā bhūtabhautikaviṣayāyā upalabdherbhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ /
upalabdhisvarūpa eva ca na ātmetyātmano dehavyatiriktatvam /
nityatvaṃ copalabdheraikarūpyāt /
ahamidamadrākṣamiti cāvasthāntarayoge 'pyupalabdhṛtvena pratyabhijñānāt /
smṛtyādyupapatteśca /
yattūktaṃ śarīre bhāvāccharīradharma upalabdairiti tadvarṇitena prakāreṇa pratyuktam /
apica satsupradīpādiṣūpakaraṇeṣūpalabdhirbhavatyasatsu na bhavati /
nacaitāvatā pradīpādidharma evopalabdhirbhavati /
evaṃ sati deha upalabdhirbhavatyasati ca na bhavatīti na dehadharmau bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, perception exists when the body is present and does not exist when it is absent — but it does not thereby become a property of the body.

children.text: upakaraṇatvamātreṇāpi pradīpādivaddehopayogopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the body's role can be explained as merely that of an instrument, like a lamp and the like.

children.text: nacātyantaṃ dehasyopalabdhāvupayogo 'pi dṛśyate niśceṣṭe 'pyasmindehe svapne nānāvidhopalabdhidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: And indeed, the body's role in perception is not at all observed to be absolute — for even in this body, when it is motionless [in deep sleep], various perceptions are seen in dreams.

children.text: tasmādanavadyaṃ dehavyatiriktasyātmano 'stitvam // 54 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the existence of a Self distinct from the body is beyond reproach. // 54 //

This is not correct — the claim that the Self is not distinct from the body.
The Self must indeed be distinct from the body — because [the properties of the Self] are not [always] present when the body is present.
If one holds that the properties of the Self are properties of the body because they are present when the body is present, then why does one not also hold that they are not properties of the body, since they are absent even when the body is present?
Because of the dissimilarity from [actual] body-properties.
For those properties that are body-properties — such as form and the like — persist as long as the body persists.
But vital breath, movement, and the like do not persist even when the body is present — in the state of death.
And body-properties such as form and the like are perceived by others, but the properties of the Self — consciousness, memory, and the like — are not.
Furthermore, while this much can be ascertained — that in the living state when the body is present, these [properties] exist — it cannot be ascertained that they do not exist when [the body] is absent.
For even when this body has fallen, by transmigration to another body, the properties of the Self might continue.
Even by mere doubt [regarding this], the opponent's position is refuted.
Moreover, the opponent should be cross-questioned: What is the nature of this consciousness that [you claim] arises from the elements?
For the <s>Lokāyatika</s> does not accept any reality beyond the four elements.
If [the opponent says:] consciousness is the experiencing of the elemental and material [things] —
then, since those [elements] are [in that case] the objects [of consciousness], consciousness cannot be their property — because of the contradiction of an action [operating] upon its own self.
For fire, while being hot, does not burn itself.
A trained acrobat does not climb on his own shoulders.
Consciousness, being a property of elements and their products, could not objectify those very elements and products.
For form and the like do not objectify their own nature or another's nature.
But both external and internal elemental and material [things] are objectified by consciousness.
And therefore, just as the existence of this perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>) — which has elemental and material things as its objects — must be accepted,
so too the perceiver whose very nature is perception — that indeed is the Self — and hence the distinctness of the Self from the body [is established].
And the eternality of perception [is established] from its uniform nature.
And because, even in the conjunction with different states, recognition [operates]: 'I saw this' — [one recognizes the continuity of the perceiver].
And because of the tenability of memory and the like.
As for the objection that was stated — that perception is a property of the body because it exists when the body is present — that has been refuted in the manner described.
Moreover, perception exists when instruments such as a lamp and the like are present, and does not exist when they are absent.
But that does not make perception a property of the lamp and the like.

children.text: 31 aṅgāvabaddhādhikaraṇam / sū. 55-56
children.translated_text: 31 The <s>Aṅgāvabaddha</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 55-56.

children.text: aṅgāvabaddhāstu na śākhāsu hi prativedam | BBs_3,3.55 |
children.translated_text: But those [meditations] connected with [ritual] limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>) are not [restricted to particular] branches [of the Veda], for [they apply] to every Veda. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.55 |

children.text: samāptā prāsaṅgikī kathā, saṃprati tu prakṛtāmevānuvartāmahe - 'omtyetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta' (chā.
children.translated_text: The incidental discussion is concluded; now we resume the main topic.

children.text:
1.1.1) 'lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.1.1), 'ukthamukthamiti vai prajā vadanti tadidamevoktham', 'iyameva pṛthivī', 'ayaṃ vāva loka eṣo 'gniścitaḥ' ityevamādyā ya udgīthādikarmāṅgāvabaddhāḥ pratyayāḥ prativedaṃ śākhābhedeṣu vihitāste tattacchākhāgateṣvevodgīthādiṣu bhaveyurathavā sarvaśākhāgateṣviti viśayaḥ /
pratiśākhaṃ na svarādibedādudgīthādiṣu vidhīyeranniti /
kutaḥ - saṃnidhānāt /
'udgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.1.1) iti hi sāmānyavihitānāṃ viśṣākāṅkṣāyāṃ saṃnikṛṣṭenaiva svaśākhāgatena viśeṣaṇākāṅkṣādinivṛtteḥ /
tadatilaṅghanena śākhāntaravihitaviśeṣopādāne kāraṇaṃ nāsti /
tasmātpratiśākhaṃ vyavastheti /
evaṃ prāpte bravītyaṅgāvabaddhāstviti /
tuśabdaḥ pakṣaṃ vyavartayati /
naite prativedaṃ svaśākhāsveva vyavatiṣṭheran /
apitu sarvaśākhāsvanuvarteran /
kutaḥ - udgīthādiśrutyaviśeṣāt /
svaśākhāvyavasthāyāṃ hyudgīthamupāsīteti sāmnyaśrutiraviśeṣapravṛttā satī saṃnidhānavaśena viśeṣe vyavasthāpyamānā pīḍitā syāt /
nacaitannyāyyam /
children.translated_text: And this is not proper.

children.text: saṃnidhānāttu śrutirbalīyasī /
children.translated_text: For <s>śruti</s> is stronger than proximity.

children.text: naca sāmānyāśrayaḥ pratyayo nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that a meditation based on a general [category] is untenable.

children.text: tasmātsvarādibhede satyapyudgīthatvādyaviśeṣātsarvaśākhāgateṣvevodgīthādiṣvevañjātīyakāḥ pratyayāḥ syuḥ // 55 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, despite the difference in accents and the like, because of the non-distinction of being an <s>udgītha</s> and the like, such meditations should apply to the <s>udgītha</s> and the like as found in all branches. // 55 //

'One should meditate on the <s>udgītha</s> as the syllable <s>Om</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1); 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.1.1); 'The people say <s>uktha, uktha</s> — that indeed is the <s>uktha</s>'; 'This earth itself'; 'This world indeed is this mentally constructed fire' — such meditations (<s>pratyayas</s>) that are connected with ritual limbs such as the <s>udgītha</s> and the like — should they belong only to the <s>udgītha</s> and the like as found in their own particular Vedic branch, or should they apply to those [elements] found in all branches? The topic [of inquiry] is this.
[The prima facie view is:] They should be prescribed only for the <s>udgītha</s> and the like within each particular branch — not in [the elements of] other branches, because of the difference of accents and the like.
Why? Because of proximity.
For when 'One should meditate on the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1) is prescribed in general terms, and the specificity is sought, the expectation is satisfied by the specific [<s>udgītha</s>] of one's own branch, which is proximate; there is no reason to bypass that and adopt a specific [<s>udgītha</s>] prescribed in another branch.
Therefore, [the meditations] are restricted to each particular branch.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: 'But those connected with limbs' — the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) overturns the [prima facie] position.
These [meditations] should not be restricted to their own branches within each Veda.
Rather, they should apply in all branches.
Why? Because of the non-distinction in the <s>śruti</s> regarding the <s>udgītha</s> and the like.
For if restricted to one's own branch, the general <s>śruti</s> 'One should meditate on the <s>udgītha</s>' — which extends without distinction — would be constrained by proximity, and thus would be strained.

children.text: mantrādivadvāvirodhaḥ | BBs_3,3.56 |
children.translated_text: As with mantras and the like — there is no contradiction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.56 |

children.text:
athavā naivātra virodhaḥ śaṅkitavyaḥ /
kathamanyaśākhāgateṣūdgīthādiṣvanyaśākhāvihitā pratyayā bhaveyuriti /
mantrādivavirodhopapatteḥ /
tathāhi mantrāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ guṇānāṃ ca śākhāntarotpannānāmapi śākhāntara upasaṃgraho dṛśyate /
yeṣāmapi hi śākhināṃ kuṭarurasītyaśmādānamantro nāmnātasteṣāmapyasau viniyogo dṛśyate kukkuṭarasītyaśmādānamantro nāmnātasteṣāmapyasau viniyogo dṛśyate kukkuṭo 'sītyaśmādānamādatte kudarurasīti veti /
yeṣāmapi samidādayaḥ prayājaḍā nāmnātasteṣāmapi teṣu guṇavidhirāmnāyate - ṛtavo vai prayājāḥ samānatra hotavyāḥ iti /
tathā yeṣāmapi ajo 'gnīṣomīyaḥ iti jātiviśeṣopadeśo nāsti teṣāmapi tadviṣayo mantravarṇa upalabhyate - chāgasya vapāyā medaso 'nurbrūhi iti /
children.translated_text: Likewise, even for those who do not have the specific instruction that the <s>Agniṣṭomīya</s> animal should be a goat (<s>aja</s>) — for them too the <s>mantra</s>-text pertaining to that is found: 'Recite after [the cutting of] the <s>vapā</s> (omentum), the fat of the goat.'

children.text: tathā vedāntarotpannānāmapi 'agnerverhetraṃ veradhvaram' ityevamādimantrāṇāṃ vedāntare parigraho dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the incorporation of mantras such as '<s>Agneḥ vṛhetraṃ vṛhadhvaram</s>' and the like, which have arisen in one Veda, into another Veda, is observed.

children.text: tathābahvṛcapaṭhitasya sūktasya yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān (ṛ.saṃ 2.6.7) ityasya adhvaryave sajanīyaṃ śasyam ityatra parigraho dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the incorporation of the hymn recited by the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (followers of the Ṛgveda) — '<s>Yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān</s>' (<s>Ṛg Veda</s> 2.6.7) — into [the context of] 'For the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, the <s>Sajanīya</s> [hymn] is to be recited as a <s>śastra</s>' — is observed.

children.text: tasmādyathāśrayāṇāṃ karmāṅgānāṃ sarvatrānuvṛttirevamāśritānāmapi pratyayānāmityavirodhaḥ // 56 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the subsidiary elements of ritual that are the basis [of meditations] recur everywhere, so too the meditations that depend on them [recur everywhere] — thus there is no contradiction. // 56 //

Or rather, no contradiction should be suspected here at all — [namely,] how could meditations prescribed in one branch apply to the <s>udgītha</s> and the like of another branch?
Because non-contradiction is established, as with mantras and the like.
For thus, the incorporation of mantras, rituals, and subsidiary details (<s>guṇas</s>) that have arisen in one branch into another branch is observed.
For even those who do not have the mantra '<s>kuṭaruḥ asi</s>' ('You are a chopper') as their stone-picking mantra by name — for them too its application is observed: '[One picks up the stone saying either] <s>kukkuṭaḥ asi</s> or <s>kuṭaruḥ asi</s>.'
And even for those who do not have the preliminary offerings (<s>prayāja</s>) designated as fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>) and the like by name — for them too the subsidiary rule regarding those is taught: 'The <s>prayājas</s> are indeed the seasons; they should be offered in the same [fire].'

children.text: 32 bhūmajyāyastvādhikaraṇam / sū. 57
children.translated_text: 32. <s>Bhūmajyāyastvādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 57

children.text: bhūmnaḥ kratuvajjyāyastvaṃ tathā hi darśayati | BBs_3,3.57 |
children.translated_text: The aggregate (<s>bhūman</s>) is superior, as in the case of a sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>); for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.57 |

children.text:
'prācīnaśāla aupamanyavaḥ' (chā. 5.11.1) ityasyāmākhyāyikāyāṃ vyastasya samastasya ca vaiśvānarasyopāsanaṃ śrūyate /
vyastopāsanaṃ tāvat 'aupamanyava kaṃ tvamātmānamupāḥsa iti devameva bhagavo rājanniti hovācaiṣa vai sutejā ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvamātmānamupāḥse' (chā. 5.12.1) ityādi /
tathā samastopāsanamapi 'tasya ha vā etasyātmano vaiśvānarasyamūrdhaiva sutejāścakṣurviśvarūpa prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā saṃdeho bahulo bastireva rayiḥ pṛthivyeva pādau' (chā. 5.18.2) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kimihobhayathāpyupāsanaṃ syādvyastasya samastasya cota smastasyaiveti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
pratyavayavaṃ sutejaḥprabhṛtiṣūpāḥsa iti kriyāpadaśravaṇāt 'tasmāttava sutaṃ prasutamāsutaṃ kule dṛśyate' (chā. 5.12.1) ityādiphalabhedaśravaṇācca vyastānyapyupāsanāni syuriti prāptam /
tato 'bidhīyate - bhūnnaḥ padārthopacayātmakasya samastasya vaiśvānaropāsanasya jyāyastvaṃ prādhānyamasminvākye vivakṣitaṃ bhavitumarhati na pratyekamavayavopāsanānāmapi /
kratuvat /
yathā kratuṣu darśapūrṇamāsāprabhṛtiṣu sāmastyena sāṅgapradhānaprayoga evaikovivakṣyate na vyastānāmapi prayogaḥ prayājādīnām /
nāpyekadeśāṅgayuktasya pradhānasya tadvat /
kuta etadbhūmaiva jyāyāniti /
tathāhi śrutirbhūmno jyāyastvaṃ darśayati ekavākyatāvagamāt /
ekaṃ hīdaṃ vākyaṃ vaiśvānaravidyāviṣayaṃ paurvāparyālocanātpratīyate /
tathāhi - prācīnaśālaprabhṛtaya uddālakāvasānāḥ ṣaḍṛṣayo vaiśvānaravidyāyāṃ pariniṣṭhamapratipadyamānā aśvapatiṃ kaikeyaṃ rājānamabhyājagmurityupakramyaikaikasyarṣerupāsyaṃ dyuprabhṛtīnāmekaikaṃ śrāvayitvā 'mūrdhā tveṣa ātmana iti hovāca' (chā. 5.12.2) ityādinā mūrdhādibhāvaṃ teṣāṃ vidadhāti /
'mūrdhā tevyapatiṣyadyanmāṃ nāgamiṣyaḥ' (chā. 5.12.2) ityādinā ca vyastopāsanamapavadati /
punaśca vyastopāsanaṃ vyāvartya samastopāsanamevānuvartya 'sa sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣvātmasvannamatti' (chā. 5.18.1) iti bhūmāśrayameva phalaṃ darśayati /
yattu pratyekaṃ sutejaḥprabhṛtiṣu phalabhedaśravaṇaṃ tadevaṃ satyaṅgaphalāni pradhāna evābhyupagatānīti draṣṭavyam /
tathopāḥsa ityapi pratyavayavamākhyātaśravaṇaṃ parābhiprāyānuvādārthaṃ na vyastopāsanavidhānārtham /
tasmātsamastopāsanapakṣa eva śreyānīti /
kecittvatra samastopāsanapakṣaṃ jyāyāṃsaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya jyāyastvavacanādeva kila vyastopāsanapakṣamapi sūtrakāro 'numanyata iti kathayanti tadayuktam /
ekavākyatāvagatau satyāṃ vākyabhedakalpanasyānyāyyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because, when the single-sentence character has been understood, it is improper to fabricate a division of sentences.

children.text: 'mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat' (chā. 5.12.2) iti caivamādinindāvacanavirodhāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the contradiction with the censure-statements such as 'Your head would have fallen off' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.12.2) and the like.

children.text: spaṣṭo copāsaṃhārasthe samastopāsanāvagame tadabhāvasya pūrvapakṣe vaktumaśakyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because, when the understanding of the aggregate meditation is clearly established through the inclusion [of all components], the absence of that [aggregate meditation] cannot be stated even as a prima facie view.

children.text: sautrasya ca jyāyastvavacanasya pramāṇavattvābhiprāyeṇāpyupapadyamānatvāt // 57 //
children.translated_text: And because the word 'superior' in the <s>sūtra</s> can be explained as intended to convey authoritative validity [of the aggregate meditation]. // 57 //

In the narrative beginning with '<s>Prācīnaśāla Aupamanyava</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.11.1), the meditation on <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is heard both in its distributed and aggregate forms. The distributed meditation is [illustrated by]: '<s>Aupamanyava</s>, on what do you meditate as the Self? On heaven alone, O venerable king — he replied. This indeed is <s>Sutejā</s> (the effulgent), the Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, on whom you meditate as the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.12.1) and so on. And the aggregate meditation: 'Of this Self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the head is <s>Sutejā</s>, the eye is <s>Viśvarūpa</s> (the all-formed), the breath is <s>Pṛthagvartmā</s> (the one of separate paths), the trunk is <s>Bahula</s> (the abundant), the bladder is <s>Rayi</s> (wealth), the feet are the earth' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.2) and so on. There arises the doubt: Is the meditation to be performed in both ways — on the distributed and on the aggregate — or only on the aggregate? What is the prima facie view? Because of the hearing of the verb 'you meditate' for each component individually — such as <s>Sutejā</s> and the rest — and because of the hearing of distinct fruits: 'Therefore, in your family, the pressed, the well-pressed, and the fully-pressed are seen' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.12.1) and so on, the distributed meditations too should be valid — this is the prima facie position. To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] states: The aggregate (<s>bhūman</s>) — the meditation on the whole <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, consisting of the accumulation of components — its superiority, its primacy, is what is intended in this passage, not the component-meditations individually. As in the case of a sacrifice (<s>kratu</s>). Just as in sacrifices like the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the rest, only the whole performance together with the principal and subsidiary elements is intended — not the separate performance of the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) and the like alone, nor the principal with only a partial set of subsidiaries — so too here. How is it known that the aggregate alone is superior? Because the <s>śruti</s> shows the superiority of the aggregate, from the understanding that [the passage constitutes] a single sentence. For this is understood, upon examining the sequential context, to be a single passage concerning the <s>Vaiśvānaravidyā</s>. For thus — having begun with 'The six sages, <s>Prācīnaśāla</s> and the rest, ending with <s>Uddālaka</s>, not attaining certainty in the <s>Vaiśvānaravidyā</s>, approached King <s>Aśvapati Kaikeya</s>' — and having presented to each sage individually his object of meditation, one of [the components] beginning with heaven, [the king] assigns them the status of being the head and so on [of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>]: 'This is only the head of the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.12.2) and so on. And by 'Your head would have fallen off if you had not come to me' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.12.2) and the like, [the <s>śruti</s>] censures the distributed meditation. And again, having set aside the distributed meditation and continuing with the aggregate meditation alone, [the <s>śruti</s>] shows a fruit based on the aggregate: 'He eats food in all worlds, in all beings, in all selves' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.18.1). As for the hearing of distinct fruits for each [component] — such as <s>Sutejā</s> and the rest — this being so, should be regarded as fruits of the subsidiaries being subsumed into the principal [sacrifice] itself. And the hearing of the verb 'you meditate' for each component is for the purpose of restating the views of others — not for enjoining distributed meditations. Therefore, the position favoring the aggregate meditation alone is superior. Some, however, having established the superiority of the aggregate meditation, say that the <s>sūtrakāra</s>, by the very word 'superior,' also approves the distributed meditation — that is not correct.

children.text: 33 śabdādibhedādhikaraṇam / sū. 58
children.translated_text: 33. <s>Śabdādibhedādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 58

children.text: nānā śabdādibhedāt | BBs_3,3.58 |
children.translated_text: [The <s>vidyās</s> are] different, because of the difference of words and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.58 |

children.text:
pūrvasminnadhikaraṇe satyamapi sutejaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ phalabhedaśrutau samastopāsanaṃ jyāya ityuktam /
ataḥ prāptā buddhiranyānyapi bhinnaśrutīnyupāsanāni samasyopāśiṣyanta iti /
apica naiva vedyābhede vidyābhedo vijñātuṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: In the previous topic, it was stated that even though distinct fruits are heard for each [component] such as <s>Sutejā</s> and the rest, the aggregate meditation is superior. From this, the following thought might arise: other meditations too, read in separate <s>śrutis</s>, should be combined and meditated upon together. Moreover, when there is no difference in the object of knowledge, the difference of <s>vidyā</s> cannot be understood.

children.text:
vedyaṃ hi rūpaṃ vidyāyā dravyadaivatamiva yāgasya /
vedyaścaika evesvaraḥ śrutinānatve 'pyavagamyate 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) 'kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' (chā. 4.10.5) 'satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' (chā. 8.1.5) ityevamādiṣu /
tathā eka eva prāṇaḥ prāṇo vāva saṃvargaḥ' (chā. 4.3.3) 'prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca' (chā. 5.1.1) 'prāṇo ha pitā prāṇo mātā' (chā. 7.15.1) ityevamādiṣu /
children.translated_text: For the object of knowledge is the form of the <s>vidyā</s> — just as the substance and deity are [the form] of a sacrifice. And though the <s>śrutis</s> are many, the same one Lord is understood [as the object of knowledge] in passages such as 'Mind-made, having <s>prāṇa</s> as body' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2), '<s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10.5), 'Whose desires are true, whose intentions are true' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5), and such. Likewise, the same one <s>Prāṇa</s> [is understood] in passages such as '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the absorber' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.3), '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the eldest and the best' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.1.1), '<s>Prāṇa</s> is the father, <s>Prāṇa</s> is the mother' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.15.1), and such.

children.text:
vaidyaikatvāccavidyaikatvam /
śrutinānātvamapyasminpakṣe guṇāntaraparatvānnānārthakam /
tasmātsvaparaśākhāvihitamekadyavyapāśrayaṃ guṇajātaṃmupasaṃhartavyaṃ vidyākārtsnyāyeti /
evaṃ prāpte pratipadyate nāneti /
vedyābhede 'pyevañjātīyakāvidyā bhinnā bhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ śabdādibhedāt /
bhavati hi śabdabhedaḥ 'veda' 'upāsīta' 'sa kratuṃ kurvati' (chā. 3.14.1) ityevamādiḥ /
śabdabhedāśca karmabhedahetuḥ samadhigataḥ purastācchabdāntare karmabhedaḥ kṛtānubandhatvāditi /
ādigrahaṇādguṇādayo 'pi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ bhedahetavo yojayitavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the oneness of the object of knowledge, there should be oneness of <s>vidyā</s>. The multiplicity of <s>śrutis</s>, on this view, is not purposeless — because it serves to teach additional attributes. Therefore, the set of attributes taught in one's own and in other <s>śākhās</s>, which are based on one common object such as heaven and the like, should be gathered together for the completeness of the <s>vidyā</s> — [this is the prima facie view]. Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] determines: [The <s>vidyās</s> are] different. Even though the object of knowledge is the same, <s>vidyās</s> of this kind should be regarded as different. Why? Because of the difference of words and the like. For there is a difference of words: '<s>veda</s>' (knows), '<s>upāsīta</s>' (should meditate), '<s>sa kratuṃ kurvīta</s>' (one should form an intention) (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.1) — and such. And difference of words is understood as a cause of difference of action — as established earlier: 'When the word is different, the action is different, because of the [different] connections.' And by the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), attributes and such differences too should be applied as causes of difference, as applicable.

children.text:
nanu vedetyādiṣu śabdabheda evāvagamyate na yajatītyādivadarthabhedaḥ sarveṣāmevaiṣāṃ manovṛttyarthatvābhedāt arthāntarāsaṃbhavācca /
tatkathaṃ śabdabhedādvidyābheda iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: In words like '<s>veda</s>' (knows) and such, only a verbal difference is perceived, not a difference of meaning as in '<s>yajati</s>' (sacrifices) and the like — because all of these are alike in having the meaning of a mental activity, and because no other meaning is possible. How then can the difference of <s>vidyā</s> follow from the difference of words?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
manovṛttyarthatvābhede 'pyanubandhabhedādvedyabede sati vidyābhedopapatteḥ /
ekasyāpīśvarasyopāsyasya pratiprakaraṇaṃ vyāvṛttā guṇāḥ śiṣyante /
tathaikasyāpi prāṇasya tatra tatropāsyasyabhede 'pyanyādṛgguṇo 'nyatropāsitavyo 'nyādṛgguṇaścāntretyevamanubandhabhedādvedyabhede sati vidyābhedo vijñāyate /
nacātraiko vidyāvidhiritare guṇavidhaya iti śakyaṃ vaktum /
viniyogamanāyāṃ hetvabhāvāt /
anekatvācca pratiprakaraṇaṃ guṇānāṃ prāptavidyānuvādena vidhānānupapatteḥ /
nacāsminpakṣe samānāḥ santaḥ satyakāmādayo guṇā asakṛcchrāvayitavyāḥ /
pratiprakaraṇaṃ cedaṅkāmenedamupāsitavyamidaṅkāmena cedamiti nairākāṅkṣyāvagamānnaikavākyatāpattiḥ /
nacātra vaiśvānaravidyāyāmiva samastacodanāparāsti yadbalena pratiprakaraṇavartinyavayavopāsanāni bhūtvaikavākyatāmiyuḥ /
children.translated_text: And here, unlike in the <s>Vaiśvānaravidyā</s>, there is no additional injunction pointing to an aggregate — by whose force the component-meditations in each context would, having become parts, merge into a single sentence.

children.text: vidyaikatvanimitte ca vidyaikatve sarvatra niraṅ kuśe pratijñāyamāne samastaguṇopasaṃhāro 'śakyaḥ pratijñāyeta /
children.translated_text: And if unity of <s>vidyā</s> — on the ground that 'identity of object entails identity of <s>vidyā</s>' — were to be accepted universally without restriction, then the inclusion of all attributes everywhere could not be maintained.

children.text: tasmātsuṣṭhūcyate nānā śabdādibhedāditi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is well said: '[The <s>vidyās</s> are] different, because of the difference of words and the like.'

children.text: sthite cetasminnadhikaraṇe sarvavedāntapratyayamityādi draṣṭavyam // 58 //
children.translated_text: And once this topic is established, the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'The meditation on [<s>Brahman</s>] common to all <s>Vedānta</s> [passages]' and so on should be understood [accordingly]. // 58 //

This is not a fault. Even though the meaning of mental activity is the same, because of the difference of associated elements (<s>anubandha</s>), when the object of knowledge differs, the difference of <s>vidyā</s> is justified. For even though <s>Īśvara</s> is one and the same object of meditation, distinct attributes are taught in each context. Likewise, even though <s>Prāṇa</s> is one and the same object of meditation in different places — since in one place one kind of attribute is to be meditated upon and in another place another kind — thus, because of the difference of associated elements, when the object of knowledge [as qualified] differs, the difference of <s>vidyā</s> is understood. And here it cannot be said that one [passage] is an injunction of the <s>vidyā</s> and the others are injunctions of attributes — because there is no ground for fixing [which is which]. And because the attributes are many in each context — and since what is already obtained [by a prior <s>vidyā</s>] cannot be newly enjoined by restating a previously obtained <s>vidyā</s> — [this interpretation fails]. And on this view, the common attributes such as <s>Satyakāma</s> and the like need not be repeated in each context. And because in each context, the understanding arises complete — 'with this desire, this is to be meditated upon; with that desire, that is to be meditated upon' — [each passage] is self-sufficient, and there is no occasion for treating them as a single sentence.

children.text: 34 vikalpādhikaramam / sū. 59
children.translated_text: 34. <s>Vikalpādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 59

children.text: vikalpo 'viśiṣṭaphalatvāt | BBs_3,3.59 |
children.translated_text: There is option (<s>vikalpa</s>) [among the <s>vidyās</s>], because of the non-difference of fruit. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.59 |

children.text:
sthite vidyābhede vicāryate kimāsāmicchayā samuccayo vikalpo vā syāt, athavā vikalpa eva niyameneti /
tatra sthitatvāttāvadvidyābhedasya na samuccayaniyame kiñcitkāraṇamasti /
children.translated_text: Once the difference of <s>vidyās</s> is established, it is investigated: Should these [different <s>vidyās</s>] be combined together by one's choice, or should there be option [among them], or should there necessarily be option alone? Since the difference of <s>vidyās</s> is established, there is no reason for a mandatory combination.

children.text: nanu bhinnānāmapyagnihotradarśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ samuccayaniyamo dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the mandatory combination of different [rites] like the <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the like is observed.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
nityatāśrutirhi tatra kāraṇaṃ naivaṃ vidyānāṃ kācinnityatāśrutirasti /
tasmānna samuccayaniyamaḥ /
nāpi vikalpaniyamaḥ /
vidyāntarādhikṛtasya vidyāntarāpratiṣedhāt /
pāriśeṣyādyāthākāmyamāpadyate /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. For the reason there [for mandatory combination] is the <s>śruti</s> of permanence (<s>nityatā</s>) — but no such <s>śruti</s> of permanence exists for <s>vidyās</s>. Therefore, there is no mandatory combination. Nor is there mandatory option — because one who is eligible for one <s>vidyā</s> is not prohibited from [undertaking] another <s>vidyā</s>. By elimination, the result is freedom of choice (<s>yathākāmya</s>).

children.text:
nanvaviśiṣṭaphalatvādāsāṃ vikalpo nyāyyaḥ /
tathāhi - manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ (chā. 3.14.2) 'kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' (chā.4.105) 'satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' (chā. 8 1.5) ityevamādyāstulyavadīśvaraprāptiphalā lakṣyante /
children.translated_text: Objection: Because of the non-difference of fruit, option among them is reasonable. For thus — 'Mind-made, having <s>prāṇa</s> as body' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2), '<s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10.5), 'Whose desires are true, whose intentions are true' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.5) — and such <s>vidyās</s> appear to have the same fruit: the attainment of <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
samānaphaleṣvapi svargādisādhaneṣu karmasu yatākāmyadarśanāt /
tasmādyathākāmyaprāptāvucyate vikalpa evāsāṃ bhavitumarhati na samuccayaḥ /
kasmāt /
aviśiṣṭaphalatvāt /
aviśiṣṭaṃ hyāsāṃ phalamupāsyaviṣayasākṣātkaraṇam /
ekena copāsanena sākṣātkṛ upāsye viṣaya īśvarādau dvitīyamanarthakam /
api cāsaṃbhavaḥ /
sākṣātkaraṇasya samuccayapakṣe cittavikṣepahetutvāt /
sākṣātkaraṇasādyaṃ ca vidyāphalaṃ darśayanti śrutayaḥ -
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because even among <s>karmas</s> that are means to the same fruit, such as heaven and the like, freedom of choice is observed. Therefore, once freedom of choice is arrived at, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: option alone should obtain among these [<s>vidyās</s>], not combination. Why? Because of the non-difference of fruit. For the fruit of these [<s>vidyās</s>] is the same — namely, the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of the object of meditation. And when, by a single meditation, the object of meditation — such as <s>Īśvara</s> and the like — has been directly realized, a second [meditation] is purposeless. Moreover, [combination] is impossible — because in the case of combination, [multiple meditations would cause] distraction of the mind, [defeating the very purpose] of direct realization. And the <s>śrutis</s> show that the fruit of <s>vidyā</s> — direct realization — is [immediately] attainable —

children.text: 'yasya syādaddhā na vicikitsāsti' (chā. 3.14.4) iti 'devo bhūtvā devānapyeti' (bṛ. 4.1.2) iti caivamādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He in whom there is truly no doubt whatsoever' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.4) — and 'Having become a <s>deva</s>, he enters among the <s>devas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.1.2) — and such passages.

children.text: tasmādaviśiṣṭaphalānāṃ vidyānāmanyatamāmādāya tatparaḥ syādyāvadupāsyaviṣayasākṣātkaramena tatphalaṃ prāptamiti // 59 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, among <s>vidyās</s> with non-different fruit, one should adopt whichever one [chooses] and be devoted to it — until the fruit is attained through the direct realization of the object of meditation. // 59 //

children.text: 35 kāmyādhikaraṇam / sū. 60
children.translated_text: 35. <s>Kāmyādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 60

children.text: kāmyāstu yathākāmaṃ samuccīyeranna vā pūrvahetvabhāvāt | BBs_3,3.60 |
children.translated_text: But the desire-fulfilling [<s>vidyās</s>] may be combined at will or not — because of the absence of the previous reason. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.60 |

children.text: aviśiṣṭaphalatvādityasya pratyudāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: This is the counter-example to 'because of the non-difference of fruit.'

children.text: yāsu punaḥ kāmyāsu vidyāsu 'sa ya etamevaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda na putrarodaṃ roditi' (chā. 3.15.2) 'sa yo nāma brahmetyupāste yāvannāmno gataṃ tatrāsya yatākāmacāro bhavati' (chā. 7.1.5) iti caivamādyāsu kriyāvadadṛṣṭenātmanātmīyaṃ phalaṃ sādhayantīṣu sākṣātkaraṇāpekṣā nāsti /
children.translated_text: But in the case of those desire-fulfilling (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>vidyās</s> — such as 'He who knows this wind as the calf of the quarters does not weep the weeping of a son' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.15.2), 'He who meditates on Name as <s>Brahman</s> — as far as Name extends, so far does he have freedom of action' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.5), and such — which, like [ritual] actions, accomplish their own fruit through an unseen power (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) — there is no need for direct realization.

children.text: tā yatākāmaṃ samuccīyeranna vā samuccīyeranpūrvahetvābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: These may be combined at will or not combined — because of the absence of the previous reason.

children.text: pūrvasyāviśiṣṭaphalatvādityasya vikalpahetorabhāvāt // 60 //
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of the previous reason — namely 'because of the non-difference of fruit' — which was the cause of option. // 60 //

children.text: 36 yathāśrayabhāvādikaraṇam / sū. 61-66
children.translated_text: 36. <s>Yathāśrayabhāvādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 61-66

children.text: aṅgeṣu yathāśrayabhāvaḥ | BBs_3,3.61 |
children.translated_text: In the subsidiary elements [of ritual], [meditations] follow the pattern of their substrates. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.61 |

children.text: karmāṅgeṣūdgīthādiṣu ya āśritāḥ pratyayā vedatrayavihitāḥ kiṃ te samuccīyerankiṃvā yathākāmaṃ syuriti saṃśaye yathāśrayabhāva ityāha /
children.translated_text: The meditations that depend on ritual accessories such as the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like, which are taught in all three <s>Vedas</s> — should these be combined, or should they follow one's choice? When this doubt arises, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: they follow the pattern of their substrates.

children.text: yataivaiṣāmāśrayāḥ stotrādayaḥ saṃbhūya bhavantyevaṃ pratyayā api āśrayatantratvātpratyayānām // 61 //
children.translated_text: Just as their substrates — the <s>stotra</s> (chanting) and the like — come together [in a single ritual], so too the meditations [come together] — because the meditations are dependent on their substrates. // 61 //

children.text: śiṣṭeś ca | BBs_3,3.62 |
children.translated_text: And because of the teaching [to that effect]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.62 |

children.text: yathā vāśrayāḥ stotrādayastriṣu śiṣyanta evamāśritā api pratyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the substrates — the <s>stotra</s> and the like — are taught [as belonging] to all three [<s>Vedas</s>], so too the meditations that depend on them.

children.text: nopadeśakṛto 'pi kaścidviśeṣo 'ṅgānāṃ tadāśrayāṇāṃ ca pratyayānāmityarthaḥ // 62 //
children.translated_text: There is no distinction whatsoever in the teaching between the subsidiary elements [of ritual] and the meditations that depend on them — this is the meaning. // 62 //

children.text: samāhārāt | BBs_3,3.63 |
children.translated_text: Because of inclusion (<s>samāhāra</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.63 |

children.text: hotṛṣadanāddhaivāpi durudgīthamanusamāharati (chā. 1.5.5) iti ca praṇavodgīthaikatvāvijñānamāhātmyādudgātāsvakarmaṇayutpannaṃ kṣataṃ hotrātkarmaṇaḥ pratisamādadhātīti bruvanvedāntaroditasya pratyayasya vedāntaroditapadārthasaṃbandhasāmānyātsravavedoditapratyayopasaṃhārasūcayatīti liṅgadarśanam // 63//
children.translated_text: 'From the seat of the <s>Hotṛ</s>, one remedies even a badly-chanted <s>Udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.5.5) — and thus, [the text] says that through the greatness of the knowledge of the oneness of <s>Praṇava</s> and <s>Udgītha</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> remedies in his own rite a defect that arose from the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s rite. By saying this, [the text] provides an indication (<s>liṅga</s>) that suggests the inclusion of meditations taught in one <s>Veda</s> with elements taught in another <s>Veda</s> — because of the commonality of the connection of the meditation with the element [across <s>Vedas</s>]. // 63 //

children.text: guṇasādhāraṇyaśruteś ca | BBs_3,3.64 |
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>śruti</s> of the commonality of the attributes. | <s>BBs</s> 3.3.64 |

children.text:
vidyāyāṃ ca vidyāśrayaṃ santamoṅkāraṃ vetrayasādhāraṇāṃśrāvayati- 'teneyaṃ trayī vidyā vartata omityāśrāyatyomiti śaṃsatyomityudgāyati' (chā. 1.1.9) iti ca /
tataścāśrayasādāraṇyādāśritasādhāramyamiti liṅgadarśanameva /
athavā guṇasādhāraṇyaśruteśceti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, [the co-occurrence may be inferred] because of the <s>śruti</s> on the commonality of the accessories (<s>guṇa</s>).

children.text: yadīme karmaguṇā udgīthādayaḥ sarve sarvaprayogasādhāraṇā na syurna syāttatastadāśrayāṇāṃ pratyayānāṃ sahabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: If these ritual accessories — the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — were not all common to all ritual performances, then the co-occurrence of the meditations depending on them would not follow.

children.text: te tūdgīthādayaḥ sarvāṅgagrāhiṇā prayogavacanena sarve sarvaprayogasādhāraṇāḥ śrāvyante /
children.translated_text: But these — the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — are heard as common to all performances, through the performance-statement that encompasses all accessories.

children.text: tathaścāśrayasahabhāvātpratyayasahabhāva iti // 64 //
children.translated_text: And thus, from the co-occurrence of the substrates, the co-occurrence of the meditations [follows]. // 64 //

And in the <s>vidyā</s> [section], [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches that <s>Oṃkāra</s>, being the substrate of the <s>vidyā</s>, is common to the three [<s>Vedas</s>]: 'By this, this threefold knowledge proceeds — with <s>Om</s> one recites, with <s>Om</s> one chants the <s>Śastra</s>, with <s>Om</s> one sings the <s>Udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.9).
And from the commonality of the substrate, the commonality of what is supported [follows] — this is merely an indication (<s>liṅga</s>).

children.text: na vā tatsahabhāvāśruteḥ | BBs_3,3.65 |
children.translated_text: Or rather not — because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s> for their co-occurrence. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.65 |

children.text:
na veti pakṣavyāvartanam /
na yatāśrayabhāva āśritānāmupāsanānāṃ bhavitumarhati /
kutaḥ - tatsahabhāvāśruteḥ /
yathā hi trivedīvihitānāmaṅgānāṃ stotrādīnāṃ sahabhāvaḥ śrūyate - 'grahaṃ vā gṛhītvā camasaṃ vonnīya stotramupākaroti stotramanuśaṃsati prastotaḥ sāma gāya hotaretadyaja' ityādinā /
naivamupāsanānāṃ sahabhāvaśrutirasti /
children.translated_text:
'Or rather not' — reverses the position.
The co-occurrence of the meditations that depend on [the substrates] should not follow from the co-occurrence of the substrates.
Why? Because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s> for their co-occurrence.
For just as the co-occurrence of the <s>stotra</s> and other accessories prescribed by the three <s>Vedas</s> is heard — 'Having taken the cup (<s>graha</s>), having lifted the ladle (<s>camasa</s>), he begins the <s>stotra</s>, he recites after the <s>stotra</s>; "O <s>Prastotṛ</s>, sing the <s>Sāman</s>"; "O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice this"' — and so forth;
there is no such <s>śruti</s> for the co-occurrence of the meditations.

children.text: nanu prayogavacana eṣāṃ sahabhāvaṃ prāpayet /
children.translated_text: But might not the performance-statement lead to their co-occurrence?

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ - puruṣārthatvādupāsanānām /
prayogavacano hi ṛtvartānāmudgīthādīnāṃ sahabhāvaṃ prāpayet /
udgīthādyupāsanāni ṛtvarthāśrayāṇyapi godohanādivatpuruṣārthanītvocāma 'pṛthagghyapratibandhaḥ phalam' (bra.saba. 3.3.42) ityatra /
ayameva copadeśāśrayo viseṣo 'ṅgānāṃ tadālambanānāṃ copāsanānāṃ yadekeṣāṃ kratvarthatvamekeṣāṃ puruṣārthatvamiti /
paraṃ ca liṅgadvayamakāraṇamupāsanasahabhāvasya śrutinyāyābāvāt /
naca pratiprayogamāśrayakārtsnyopasaṃhārādāśritānāmapi tathātvaṃ vijñātuṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: And from the complete inclusion of all substrates in each performance, the same [complete inclusion] cannot be inferred for the meditations that depend on them.

children.text: atatpratyuktatvādupāsanānām /
children.translated_text: Because the meditations are not governed by the same [principle as the substrates].

children.text: āśrayatantrāṇyapi hyupāsanāni kāmamāśrayābhāve mā bhūvanna tvāśrayasahabhāvena sahabhāvaniyamamarhanti tatsahabhāvāśrutereva /
children.translated_text: For even meditations that depend on substrates may certainly be absent when the substrate is absent — but they should not be compelled to co-occur merely because the substrates co-occur, precisely because of the absence of a <s>śruti</s> for their co-occurrence.

children.text: tasmādyathākāmamevopāsanānyanuṣṭhīyeran // 65 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meditations should be practiced as one wishes — [either in combination or separately]. // 65 //

No, we say — because the meditations serve the person's purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).
The performance-statement would lead to the co-occurrence of the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like that serve the ritual's purpose.
But the meditations on the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like — though depending on ritual-serving substrates — are for the person's purpose, like cow-milking (<s>godohana</s>) and the like — as we stated in 'For separately, without obstruction, [there is] fruit' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.3.42).
And this is precisely the distinguishing feature taught between the accessories [of ritual] and the meditations based on them: that some serve the ritual's purpose and others serve the person's purpose.
Moreover, the two indications [for co-occurrence] are not valid grounds for the co-occurrence of meditations — because of the absence of <s>śruti</s> and reasoning [for it].

children.text: darśanāc ca | BBs_3,3.66 |
children.translated_text: And because of the observation. | <s>BBs</s> 3,3.66 |

children.text: darśayati ca śrutisahabhāvaṃ pratyayānam - 'evaṃviddha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃścartvijo 'bhirakṣati'
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> shows [that the meditations do] not [all] co-occur: 'The <s>Brahman</s> priest who knows thus protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the <s>ṛtvijs</s>'
(<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.17.10).

children.text: sarvapratyayopasaṃhāre hi sarve sarvavidaḥ iti na vijñānavatā brahmaṇā paripālyatvamitareṣāṃ saṃkīrtyeta /
children.translated_text: For if all meditations were required to co-occur, all [priests] would be knowers of all [meditations] — and then the protection of the others by the all-knowing <s>Brahman</s> priest would not be mentioned.

children.text: tasmādyathākāmamupāsanānāṃ samuccayo vikalpo veti // 66 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meditations should be combined or optionally [practiced], as one wishes. // 66 //

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau śrīmacchārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye tṛtīyādyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 3 //

children.text: tṛtīyādhyāye caturthaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: atra nirguṇavidyāyā antaraṅgabahiraṅgasādhanavicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Here, the examination of the inner and outer means of the meditation on the attributeless (<s>nirguṇa</s>) <s>Brahman</s> [is presented].

children.text: 1 puruṣārthādhikaraṇam / sū. 1-17
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Puruṣārthādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Human Purpose). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-17.

children.text: puruṣārtho 'taḥ śabdād iti bādarāyaṇaḥ | BBs_3,4.1 |
children.translated_text: The human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) [is accomplished] from this [knowledge] — because of the scriptural word: thus [holds] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.1 |

children.text:
athedānīmaupaniṣadamātmajñānaṃ kimadhikāridvāreṇa karmaṇyevānupraviśatyāhosvitsvatantrameva puruṣārthasādhanaṃ bhavatīti mīmāṃsamānaḥ siddhāntenaiva tādupakramate puruṣārtho 'ta iti /
asmadvedāntavihitādātmajñānātsvatanatrātpuruṣārthaḥ siddyatīti bādarāyaṇa ācāryo manyate /
kuta etadavagamyate śabdādityāha /

tathāhi - 'tarati śokamātmavit' (chā. 7.1.3) 'sa yo ha vai tatparamaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati' (mu. 3.2.9) 'brahmavidāpnoti param' (tai. 2.1.1) 'ācāryavānpuruṣo veda tasya tāvadeva ciraṃ yāvannavimokṣye 'tha saṃpatsye' (chā /
children.translated_text: For thus: 'The knower of the Self crosses over sorrow' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.3); 'He who knows that supreme <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.9); 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1); 'A person with a teacher knows; for him the delay is only as long as he is not liberated — then he reaches [<s>Brahman</s>]' (<s>Chāndogya</s>

children.text: 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā' (chā. 8.7.1) ityupakramya 'sarvāṃśca lokānāpnoti sarvāṃśca kāmānyastamātmānamanuvidya vijānāti (chā. 8.7.1) iti /
children.translated_text: Beginning with 'This Self, free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) — 'He who has found the Self and knows it — he attains all worlds and all desires' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1).

children.text: 'ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ' (bṛ. 4.5.6) ityupakramya 'etāvadare khalvamṛtatvam' (bṛ. 4.5.15) ityevañjātīyakā śrutiḥ kevalāyā vidyāyāḥ puruṣārthahetutvaṃ śrāvayati // 1 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with 'The Self indeed is to be seen' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6) — 'This much indeed is immortality' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15) — <s>śruti</s> passages of this kind proclaim that knowledge alone is the cause of the human purpose. // 1 //

Now, the inquiry is: Does the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> knowledge of the Self enter into ritual action through the medium of eligibility, or does it independently serve as the means to the human purpose?
Examining this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] begins with the established conclusion itself: 'The human purpose from this.'
The teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds that the human purpose is accomplished from the knowledge of the Self taught in our <s>Vedānta</s> [texts], independently.
How is this known? He says: 'Because of the scriptural word.'

children.text: athātra pratyavatiṣṭhate -
children.translated_text: Now an objection is raised:

children.text: śeṣatvātpuruṣārthavādo yathānyeṣv iti jaiminiḥ | BBs_3,4.2 |
children.translated_text: Because of [knowledge's] being subsidiary [to action], the statement of the human purpose is [merely] laudatory — as in other cases: so [holds] <s>Jaimini</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.2 |

children.text:
kartṛtvamātmanaḥ karmaśeṣatvāttadvijñānamapi vrīhiprokṣaṇādivadviṣayadvāreṇa karmasaṃbandhyevetyatastasminnavagataprayojana ātmajñāne yā phalaśrutiḥ sārthavāda iti jaiminirācāryo manyate yathānyeṣu dravyasaṃskārakarmasu 'yasya parṇamayī juhūrbhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇoti /
yadaṅ ke cakṣureva bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅ kte /
yatprayājānuyājā ijyante varma vā etadyajñasya kriyate karma yajamānasya bhrātṛvyābhibhūtyai' ityevañjātīyakā phalaśrutirarthavādaḥ /
tadvat /
children.translated_text:
The self is an agent; because of its being subsidiary to action, the knowledge of it too — like the sprinkling of rice and the like — is connected with ritual through the medium of its subject matter. Therefore, in the case of the knowledge of the Self — whose purpose is already understood [as serving ritual] — the statement of fruit is merely laudatory (<s>arthavāda</s>): so holds the teacher <s>Jaimini</s>. As in other cases of rituals involving the preparation of substances — 'He who uses a leaf-ladle does not hear ill-repute'; 'Thereby he plucks out the eye of the rival'; 'The preliminary (<s>prayāja</s>) and concluding (<s>anuyāja</s>) offerings are performed [because] this is the armor of the sacrifice, the action is for the sacrificer's overpowering of the rival' — in such cases the statement of fruit is [merely] laudatory.
Likewise [with knowledge].

children.text:
kathaṃ punarasyānarabhyādhītasyātmajñānasya prakaraṇādīnāmanyatamenāpi hetunā vinā kratupraveśa āśaṅkyate /
kartṛdvāreṇa vākyāttadvijñānasya kratusaṃbandha iti cet /
children.translated_text:
But how can entry into ritual be suspected for this knowledge of the Self — which is read outside the beginning-section (<s>anārabhyādhīta</s>) — without any ground such as context and the like?
If it be said: Through the medium of the agent, from the sentence, there is a connection of the knowledge of the Self with ritual —

children.text:
na /
vākyāttadviniyogānupapatteḥ /
avyabhicāriṇā hi kenaciddvāreṇānārabhyādhītānāmapi vākyanimittaḥ kratusaṃbandho 'vakalpate /
kartā tu vyabhicāri dvāraṃ lokikavaidikakarmasādhāraṇyāt /
tasmānna taddvāreṇātmajñānasya kratusaṃbandhasiddhiriti /
na /
vyatirekavijñānasya vaidikebhyaḥ karmabhyo 'nyatrānupayogāt /
nahi dehavyatiriktātmajñānaṃ lokikeṣu karmasūpayujyate /
sarvathā dṛṣṭārthapravṛttyupapatteḥ /
vaidikeṣu tu dehapātottarakālaphaleṣu dehavyatiriktātmajñānamantareṇa pravṛttirnopapadyata ityupayujyate vyatirekavijñānam /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because a deployment [of knowledge into ritual] from the sentence through that [medium of the agent] is untenable.
For the connection of things read outside the beginning-section with ritual is possible through some non-deviant medium.
