But the agent is a deviant medium — because it is common to both worldly and Vedic actions.
Therefore, the connection of Self-knowledge with ritual through that [medium] is not established.
[But actually,] no [this objection is not valid].
Because the knowledge of [the Self's] distinctness [from the body] has no use apart from Vedic rituals.
For the knowledge that the Self is distinct from the body is not useful in worldly actions.
Because [in worldly actions] activity is entirely explicable from visible purposes alone.
But in Vedic rituals — whose fruits come after the fall of the body — activity is not explicable without knowledge of a Self distinct from the body; hence the knowledge of distinctness is useful [there].

children.text: nanvapahatapāpmatvādiviśeṣaṇādasaṃsāryātmaviṣayamaupaniṣadaṃ darśanaṃ na pravṛttyaṅgaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: But since the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> vision is about the Self qualified by being free from evil (<s>apahatapāpman</s>) and the like — [i.e.,] a non-transmigratory Self — it should not be an accessory to [ritual] activity.

children.text: na /
priyādisaṃsūcitasya saṃsāriṇa evātmano draṣṭavyatvenopadeśāt /
children.translated_text: Because the teaching is that the Self — indicated by [attributes of] dearness and the like as belonging to the transmigratory [self] — is to be seen.

children.text: apahatapāpmatvādi viśeṣaṇaṃ tu stutyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And the qualification by freedom from evil and the like will be for the purpose of praise.

children.text: nanu tatra tatra prasīdhitametadadhikamasaṃsāri brahma jagatkāraṇaṃ tadeva ca saṃsāriṇa ātmanaḥ pāramārthikaṃ svarūpamupaniṣatsūpadiśyata iti /
children.translated_text: But has it not been established in various places that the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — which is beyond <s>saṃsāra</s> and is the cause of the universe — is identical with the ultimate true nature of the transmigratory self, and that this is what the <s>Upaniṣads</s> teach?

children.text: satyaṃ prasāditaṃ tasyaiva tu sthūṇānikhananavatphaladvāreṇākṣepasamādhāne kriyete dārḍhyāya // 2 //
children.translated_text: True, this has been established. But like the driving of a post [deeper] into the ground, the objection and its resolution are being carried out through [the discussion of] the fruit — for the sake of firmness [of conviction]. // 2 //
No.

children.text: ācāradarśanāt | BBs_3,4.3 |
children.translated_text: Because of the observation of conduct. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.3 |

children.text: 'janako ha vaideho bahudakṣiṇena yajñeneje' (bṛ. 3.1.1) 'yakṣyamāṇo vai bhagavanto 'hamasmi' (chā. 5.11.5) ityevamādīni brahmavidāmapyanyapareṣu vākyeṣu karmasaṃbandhadarśanāni bhavanti /
children.translated_text: '<s>Janaka</s>, [king] of <s>Videha</s>, performed a sacrifice with abundant gifts (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.1.1); 'I am about to perform a sacrifice, revered sirs' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.11.5) — such passages in other <s>Vedānta</s> texts show the connection of knowers of <s>Brahman</s> too with ritual action.

children.text: tathoddālakādīnāmapi putrānuśāsanādidarśanādgārhasthyasaṃbandho 'vagamyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, from the observation of <s>Uddālaka</s> and others instructing their sons and the like, their connection with the householder's life is understood.

children.text: kevalāccejjñānātpuruṣārthasiddhiḥ syātkimarthamanekāyāsasamanvitāni karmāṇi te kuryuḥ 'arke cenmadhu vindeta kimarthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet' iti nyāyāt // 3 //
children.translated_text: If the human purpose were accomplished from knowledge alone, why would they perform rituals accompanied by much effort? — by the principle 'If one can find honey on a tree, why would one climb a mountain?' // 3 //

children.text: tacchruteḥ | BBs_3,4.4 |
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s> [for the subsidiarity of knowledge]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.4 |

children.text: 'yadeva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tadeva vīryavattaraṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.10) iti ca karmaśeṣatvaśravaṇādvidyāyā na kevalāyāḥ puruṣārthahetutm // 4 //
children.translated_text: 'What one does with knowledge, with faith, with meditation (<s>upaniṣad</s>) — that alone is more powerful' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) — because of the hearing of knowledge's subsidiarity to action, knowledge alone is not the cause of the human purpose. // 4 //

children.text: samanvārambhaṇāt | BBs_3,4.5 |
children.translated_text: Because of the co-commencement. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.5 |

children.text: 'taṃ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhete' (bṛ. 4.4.2) iti ca vidyākarmaṇoḥ phalārambhe sahakāritvadarśanānna svātantryaṃ vidyāyāḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: 'Knowledge and action together take hold of him [at the time of death]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2) — because of the observation that knowledge and action cooperate in the commencement of fruit, knowledge has no independence. // 5 //

children.text: tadvato vidhānāt | BBs_3,4.6 |
children.translated_text: Because of the injunction for one who possesses that [knowledge]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.6 |

children.text: 'ācāryakulādvedamadhītya yathāvidānaṃ guroḥ karmātiśeṣeṇābhisamāvṛttya kuṭumbe śucau deśe svādhyāyamadhīyānaḥ' (chā. 8.15.1) iti caivañjātīyakā śrutiḥ samastavedārthavijñānavataḥ karmādhikāraṃ darśayati tasmādapi na vijñānasya svātantryeṇa phalahetutvam /
children.translated_text: 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s> from the teacher's family, as prescribed by the teacher, upon completion of the remaining duties, returning to the household — studying the sacred texts in a pure place' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.15.1) — <s>śruti</s> passages of this kind show that one who possesses the knowledge of the entire meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> is [still] eligible for ritual action. Therefore, knowledge is not independently the cause of the fruit.

children.text: nanvatrādhītyetyadhyayanamātraṃ vedasya śrūyate nārthavijñānam /
children.translated_text: But here, only the study (<s>adhyayana</s>) of the <s>Veda</s> is heard — 'Having studied' — not the knowledge of its meaning.

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: dṛṣṭārthatvādvedādhyayanamarthāvabodhaparyantamitisthitam // 6 //
children.translated_text: Because the study of the <s>Veda</s>, having a visible purpose, culminates in the understanding of its meaning — this is the established position. // 6 //

children.text: niyamāc ca | BBs_3,4.7 |
children.translated_text: And because of the restriction. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.7 |

children.text: 'kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Performing actions here [in this world] alone, one should wish to live a hundred years;

children.text: evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto 'sti na karma lipyate nare' (īśa. 2) iti /
children.translated_text: thus for you — there is no other way than this — action does not cling to a person' (<s>Īśa Upaniṣad</s> 2).

children.text: tathā 'etadvai jarāmaryaṃ satraṃ yadagnihotraṃ jarayā vā hyevāsmānmucyate mṛtyunā vā' ityevañjātīyakānniyamādapi karmaśeṣatvameva vidhyayā iti // 7 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'This is the session (<s>sattra</s>) that lasts until old age and death — namely, the <s>Agnihotra</s>; for by old age alone one is released from it, or by death' — because of the restriction from passages of this kind too, knowledge is subsidiary to action. // 7 //

children.text: evaṃ prāpte pratividhatte -
children.translated_text: Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] responds:

children.text: adhikopadeśāt tu bādarāyaṇasyaivaṃ taddarśanāt | BBs_3,4.8 |
children.translated_text: But because of the teaching of what is beyond [the transmigratory self] — this is the view of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because of the observation of that. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.8 |

children.text:
tuśabdātpakṣo viparivartate /
yaduktam - 'śeṣatvātpuruṣārthavādaḥ' (bra. sū. 3.4.2) iti tannopapadyate /
kasmāt /
adhikopadeśāt /
yadi saṃsāryevātmā śārīraḥ kartā bhoktā ca śarīramātravyatirekeṇa vedānteṣūpadiṣṭaḥ syāttato varṇitena prakāreṇa phalaśruterarthavādatvaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text:
The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) reverses the position.
The statement 'Because of subsidiarity, the statement of the human purpose is laudatory' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.2) — that is untenable.
Why?
Because of the teaching of what is beyond [the transmigratory self].
If in the <s>Vedāntas</s> the Self were taught as merely embodied, transmigratory, an agent and experiencer — distinct from the body alone — then the statement of fruit would be laudatory in the manner described.

children.text:
adhikastāvaccharīrādātmano 'saṃsārīśvaraḥ kartṛtvādisaṃsāridharmarahito 'pahatapāpmatvādiviśeṣaṇaḥ paramātmā vedyatvenopadiśyate vedānteṣu /
naca tadvijñānaṃ karmaṇāṃ pravartakaṃ bhavati pratyuta karmāṇyucchinattīti vakṣyati 'upamardaṃ ca' (bra.sū. 3.4.16) ityatra /
tasmāt 'puruṣārtho 'taḥ śabdāt' (bra.sū. 3.4.1) iti yanmataṃ bhagavato bādarāyaṇasya tattathaiva tiṣṭhati na śeṣatvaprabhṛtibhirhetvābhāsaiścālayituṃ śakyate /
tathāhi tamadhikaṃ śārīrādīśvaramātmānaṃ darśayanti śrutayaḥ - 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit' (muṇḍa. 1.19) 'bhīṣāsmādvātaḥ pavate' (tai. 2.8.1) 'mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyatam' (kaṭha. 6.2) 'etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi' (bṛ. 3.8.9) 'tadaikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti tattejo 'sṛjata' (chā. 6.2.3) ityevamādyāḥ /
yattu priyādisaṃsūcitasya saṃsāriṇa evātmano vedyatayānukarṣaṇam 'ātmanastu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati /

ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ' (bṛ. 2.4.5) 'yaḥ prāṇena prāṇiti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ' (bṛ. 3.4.1) 'ya eṣo 'kṣīṇi puruṣo dṛśyate' (chā. 8.7.4) ityupakramya 'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyasyāmi' (chā. 8.9.3) iti caivamādi tadapi 'asya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitametadyadṛgvedaḥ' (bṛ. 2.4.10) 'yo 'śanāyāpipāse śokaṃ mohaṃ jarāṃ mṛtyumatyeti' (bṛ. 3.5.1) 'paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svenarūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ' (chā. 8.12.3) ityevamādibhirvākyaśeṣaiḥ satyāmevādhikopadidikṣāyāmatyantābhedābhiprāyamityavirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The Self indeed is to be seen' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.5), 'He who breathes through <s>prāṇa</s> — that is the Self, the innermost of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1), 'The person who is seen within the eye' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.4) — having introduced [the topic] thus, [the text continues:] 'This itself I shall explain to you further' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.9.3) — and so on. These passages too, through their subsequent statements such as 'Of this great being, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the exhalation' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.10), 'He who transcends hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age, and death' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.1), 'Reaching the supreme light, he manifests in his own form — that is the highest <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3) — through such concluding passages, when the true import of the teaching is absolute non-difference, there is no contradiction.

children.text: pārameśvarameva hi śārīrasya pāramārthikaṃ svarūpam /
children.translated_text: For the true nature of the embodied self (<s>śārīra</s>) is indeed that of the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>).

children.text: upādhikṛtaṃ tu śārīratvam 'tatvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) 'nānyodato 'sti draṣṭṛ' (bṛ. 3.8.11) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The state of being an embodied self is only due to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) — as known from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) and 'There is no other seer besides [Him]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11) and the like.

children.text: sarvaṃ cātadvistareṇāsmābhiḥ purastāttatra tatra varṇitam // 8 //
children.translated_text: And all this has been explained by us at length in the relevant places previously. // 8 //

But what is taught as the object of knowledge in the <s>Vedāntas</s> is the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) — which is beyond the embodied [self], which is the Lord beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>, devoid of transmigratory properties such as agency and the like, and qualified by freedom from evil (<s>apahatapāpmatva</s>) and the like.
And the knowledge of That does not promote ritual actions; on the contrary, it cuts off actions — as will be stated in the [<s>sūtra</s>] 'And because of the destruction [of ignorance]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.16).
Therefore, the view of the revered <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — that 'The human purpose [is accomplished] from this, because of the scriptural word' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.1) — stands as it is, and cannot be shaken by the semblances of reasoning (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) beginning with subsidiarity and the like.
For thus the <s>śrutis</s> show the Self that is beyond the embodied [self] and is the Lord: 'He who is omniscient, all-knowing' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.1.9); 'Out of fear of Him the wind blows' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.8.1); 'A great fear, a thunderbolt upraised' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 6.2); 'Under the rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.9); 'It thought: "Let me become many, let me be born. It created fire"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.2.3) — and passages of this kind.
As for the drawing in [of this knowledge] to apply to the transmigratory self indicated by dearness and the like — 'For the sake of the Self alone is everything dear;'

children.text: tulyaṃ tu darśanam | BBs_3,4.9 |
children.translated_text: But the observation [of conduct] is the same. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.9 |

children.text:
yattūktamācāradarśanātkarmaśeṣo vidyeti /
atra brūmaḥ - tulyāmācāradarśanamakmaśeṣitve 'pi vidyāyāḥ /
tathāhi śrutirbhavati - 'etadvā sma vai tadvidvāṃsa āhurṛṣayaḥ kāvaṣeyāḥ kimarthā vayamadhyeṣyāmahe kimarthāvayaṃ yakṣyāmahe /
etaddha sma vai tatpūrve vidvāṃso 'gnihotraṃ na juhavāñcakrire' 'etaṃ vai tamātmānaṃ viditvā brāhmaṇāḥ putraiṣaṇāyāśca vittaiṣaṇayāśca lokaiṣaṇāyāśca vyutthāyātha bhikṣācaryaṃ caranti' (bṛ. 3.5.1) ityevajātīyakā /
yājñavalkyādīnāmapi brahmavidāmarmaniṣṭhatvaṃ dṛśyate - 'etāvadare khalvamṛtatvamiti hoktvā yājñavalkyo vijahāra' (bṛ. 4.5.15) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
apica yakṣyamāṇo vai bhagavanto 'hamasami (chā. 5.11.5) ityetalliṅgadarśanaṃ vaiśvānaravidyāviṣayam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the indication 'I am about to perform a sacrifice, venerable ones' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.11.5) pertains specifically to the <s>Vaiśvānara-vidyā</s>.

children.text: saṃbhavati ca sopādhikāyāṃ brahmavidyāyāṃ karmasāhityadarśanam /
children.translated_text: And it is possible to observe the association of <s>karma</s> with a <s>Brahma-vidyā</s> that involves limiting adjuncts (<s>sopādhikā</s>).

children.text: natvatrāpi karmāṅgatvamasti /
children.translated_text: But even there, <s>vidyā</s> does not have the status of being a subsidiary of <s>karma</s>.

children.text: prakaraṇādyabhāvāt // 9 //
children.translated_text: Because there is no [supporting] context or the like. // 9 //

As for the objection that <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is subsidiary to <s>karma</s> (action) because of the observation of conduct — to that we say: The observation of conduct is the same even when <s>vidyā</s> is not subsidiary to <s>karma</s>. For thus the <s>śruti</s> states: 'Those ancient sages, the descendants of <s>Kavaṣa</s>, who knew this, said: "Why should we study? Why should we sacrifice? Having known this very [Self], the ancient knowers did not offer the <s>agnihotra</s>"' [and] 'Having known this Self, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, rising above the desire for sons, the desire for wealth, and the desire for worlds, live as mendicants' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.1) — such are the passages of this kind. The fact that <s>Yājñavalkya</s> and other knowers of <s>Brahman</s> were established in renunciation is also seen — from <s>śrutis</s> such as 'Having said "This much indeed is [the means to] immortality," <s>Yājñavalkya</s> renounced' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15) and the like.

children.text: yatpunaruktam - 'tacchruteḥ' (bra.sū. 3.4.4) iti atra brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: As for the further objection stated in 'Because of the <s>śruti</s> [to that effect]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.4), to that we say:

children.text: asārvatrikī | BBs_3,4.10 |
children.translated_text: [That <s>śruti</s>] is not universal. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.10 |

children.text:
'yadeva vidyayā karoti' (chā. 1.1.10) ityeṣā śrutirna sarvavidyāviṣayā /
prakṛtavidyābhisaṃbandhāt /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever one does with knowledge' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) — this <s>śruti</s> does not pertain to all <s>vidyās</s>. Because it is connected with the <s>vidyā</s> under discussion.

children.text: prakṛtā codgīthavidyā 'omityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.1.1) ityatra // 10 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>vidyā</s> under discussion is the <s>Udgītha-vidyā</s> — in the passage 'One should meditate on the syllable <s>Om</s> as the <s>Udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1). // 10 //

children.text: vibhāgaḥ śatavat | BBs_3,4.11 |
children.translated_text: The division [should be understood] as in the case of a hundred. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.11 |

children.text:
yadapyuktam - 'taṃ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhete' (bṛ. 4.4.2) ityetatsamānvārambhavacanamasvatantrye vidyāyā liṅgamiti tatpratyucyate /
vibhāgo 'tra draṣṭavyo vidyānyaṃ puruṣamanvārabhate karmānyamiti /
śatavat /
yathā śatamābhyāṃ dīyatāmityukte vibhajya dīyate pañcāśadekasmai pañcāśadaparasmai tadvat /
nacedaṃ samanvāramabhavacanaṃ mumukṣuviṣayam 'iti nu kāmayamānaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti saṃsāriviṣayatvopasaṃhārāt /
'athākāmayamānaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti ca mumukṣoḥ pṛthagupakramāt /
children.translated_text: And because of the separate introduction of the <s>mumukṣu</s> in 'But he who is without desire' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6).

children.text: tatra saṃsāriviṣaye vidyā vihitā pratiṣiddhā ca parigṛhyate viśeṣābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: There, in the case of the <s>saṃsārin</s>, <s>vidyā</s> — both enjoined and prohibited — is accepted, because there is no distinction [made].

children.text: karamāpi vihitaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ ca yathāprāptānuvāditvāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> too — both enjoined and prohibited — [is accepted], because it merely restates what is already obtained.

children.text: evaṃ satyavibhāgenāpīdaṃ samanvārambhavacanamavakalpate // 11 //
children.translated_text: Thus, even with the division, this statement of joint pursuit is well accounted for. // 11 //

As for the further objection that the statement of joint pursuit — '<s>Vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> accompany him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2) — is an indication of the non-independence of <s>vidyā</s>, to that we reply: A division should be seen here — <s>vidyā</s> accompanies one person and <s>karma</s> accompanies another. As in the case of a hundred: just as when it is said 'Give a hundred to these two,' it is divided — fifty to one and fifty to the other — so too here. And this statement of joint pursuit does not pertain to the <s>mumukṣu</s> (seeker of liberation), because of the concluding reference to the <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being) in 'Thus does he who desires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6).

children.text: yaccaitat 'tadvato vidhānāt' (bra. sū. 3.4.6) ityata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: And as for the reply to the [objection] stated in 'Because of the injunction for one who possesses that' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.6) — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] now reads:

children.text: adhyayanamātravataḥ | BBs_3,4.12 |
children.translated_text: [The injunction is] only for one who has merely studied. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.12 |

children.text: 'ācāryakulādvedamadhītya' (chā. 8.15.1) ityadhyayanamātrasya śravaṇādadhyayanamātravata eva karmavidhirityadhyavasyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having studied the <s>Veda</s> from the teacher's family' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.15.1) — since only mere study is heard [as the qualification], we determine that the injunction of <s>karma</s> is for one who has merely studied.

children.text: nanvevaṃ satyāvidyatvānadhikāraḥ karmasu prajyeta /
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, would not the disqualification for rituals follow for one who lacks <s>vidyā</s>?

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: na vayamadhyayanaprabhavaṃ karmāvabodhanamadhikārakāraṇaṃ vārayāmaḥ kiṃ tarhyeniṣadamātmajñānaṃ svātantryeṇaiva prayojanavatpratīyamānaṃ na karmādhikārakāraṇatāṃ pratipadyata ityetāvatpratipādayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: We do not deny that the comprehension of <s>karma</s> arising from study is the cause of qualification [for rituals]. What we establish is only this much: that the knowledge of the Self (<s>Ātmajñāna</s>), which is independently understood as having its own purpose, does not serve as the cause of qualification for <s>karma</s>.

children.text: yathāca na kratvantarajñānaṃ kratvantarādhikāreṇāpekṣyata evametadapi draṣṭavyamiti // 12 //
children.translated_text: And just as the knowledge of one ritual does not require qualification for another ritual, so too should this [Self-knowledge] be viewed. // 12 //

children.text: yadapyuktaṃ niyamacca (bra. sū. 3.4.7) ityatrābhidhīyate -
children.translated_text: As for the further objection stated in 'And because of the restrictive rule' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.7), to that we state:

children.text: nāviśeṣāt | BBs_3,4.13 |
children.translated_text: Not so, because there is no specification. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.13 |

children.text: 'kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣet' (īśā. 2) ityelamādiṣu niyamaśravaṇeṣu na viduṣa iti viśeṣo 'sti /
children.translated_text: In passages containing restrictive rules such as 'Performing actions here, one should wish to live [a hundred years]' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 2) and the like, there is no specification that [the subject is] 'a knower.'

children.text: aviśeṣeṇa niyamavidhānāt // 13 //
children.translated_text: Because the restrictive injunction is given without any specification. // 13 //

children.text: stutaye 'numatirvā | BBs_3,4.14 |
children.translated_text: [It is] for the purpose of praise, or [it is] a permission. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.14 |

children.text:
'kurvanneveha karmāṇi' (īśā. 2) ityatrāparo viśeṣa ākhyāyate yadyapyatra prakaraṇasāmarthyādvidvāneva kurvanniti saṃbadhyate tathāpi vidyāstutaye karmānujñānametaddraṣṭavyam /
'na karma lipyate nare' (īśā. 2) iti hi vakṣyati /
etaduktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: This is what is meant:

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ karma kurvatyapi viduṣi puruṣe hi vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Even for a knowing person who performs <s>karma</s> throughout life, [the text] will indeed say:

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: This is what is meant:

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ karma kurvatyapi viduṣupuruṣe na karma lepāya bhavati vidyāsāmarthyāditi tadevaṃ vidyā stūyate // 14 //
children.translated_text: Even for a knowing person who performs <s>karma</s> throughout life, <s>karma</s> does not result in bondage, by the power of <s>vidyā</s>. Thus, <s>vidyā</s> is praised. // 14 //

In the passage 'Performing actions here' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 2), another distinction is declared: Even though, by the force of context, it is connected as 'the knower, while performing [actions],' nevertheless, this should be seen as a permission of <s>karma</s> for the purpose of praising <s>vidyā</s>. For [the text] will say: '<s>Karma</s> does not cling to a person' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 2).

children.text: kāmakāreṇa caike | BBs_3,4.15 |
children.translated_text: And some [do so] by their own choice. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.15 |

children.text: apicaike vidvāṃsaḥ pratyakṣīkṛtavidyāphalāḥ santastadavaṣṭabhyātphalāntarasādhaneṣu prajādiṣu prayojanābhāvaṃ parāmṛśanti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, some knowers who have directly realized the fruit of <s>vidyā</s>, relying on that [realization], reflect on the purposelessness of means to other fruits such as progeny and the like.

children.text: kāmakāreṇeti śrutirbhavati vājasaneyinām 'etaddha sma vai tatpūrve vidvāṃsaḥ prajāṃ na kāmayante kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmo yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ lokaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti anubhavārūḍhameva ca vidyāphalaṃ na kriyāphalavatkālāntarabhāvītyasakṛdavocāma /
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> of the <s>Vājasaneyins</s> with the word 'by [their own] choice' states: 'Those ancient knowers said: "We do not desire progeny — what shall we do with progeny, we for whom this Self is [our] world?"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22). And we have stated repeatedly that the fruit of <s>vidyā</s>, being a matter of direct experience, is not something that comes about at a future time like the fruit of action.

children.text: ato 'pi na vidyāyāḥ karmaśeṣatvaṃ nāpi tadviṣayāyāḥ phalaśruterayathārthatvaṃ śakyamāśrayitum // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the subsidiarity of <s>vidyā</s> to <s>karma</s> cannot be maintained, nor can the non-reality of the fruit declared for <s>vidyā</s> be accepted. // 15 //

children.text: upamardaṃ ca | BBs_3,4.16 |
children.translated_text: And [there is] the annulment. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.16 |

children.text: apica karmākārahetoḥ kriyākārakaphalalakṣaṇasya samastasya prapañcasyāvidyākṛtasya vidyāsāmarthyātsvarūpopamardamāmananti - 'yatra vā asya sarvamātmatmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyettatkena kaṃ jighret' (bṛ. 2.4.14) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: Moreover, they declare the complete annulment of the entire phenomenal world — characterized by action, agent, and fruit, and created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — through the power of <s>vidyā</s>, by the cause of action: 'Where, for him, everything has become the Self alone — then by what should one see whom? By what should one smell whom?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14) and so on.

children.text: vedāntoditātmajñānapūrvikāṃ tu karmādhikārasiddhiṃ pratyāśāsanasya karmādhikārocchittireva prasajyeta /
children.translated_text: And if the establishment of qualification for <s>karma</s> were to require Self-knowledge as taught in the <s>Vedānta</s> as its prerequisite, then the very destruction of qualification for <s>karma</s> would result.

children.text: tasmādapi svātantryaṃ vidyāyāḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the independence of <s>vidyā</s> [is established]. // 16 //

children.text: ūrdhvaretassu ca śabde hi | BBs_3,4.17 |
children.translated_text: And in the celibate [<s>āśramas</s>], for there is the scriptural word. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.17 |

children.text:
ūrdhvaretaḥsu cāśrameṣu vidyā śrūyate /
naca tatra karmāṅgatvaṃ vidyāyā upapadyate /
karmābhāvāt /
nahyagnihotrādīni vaidikāni karmāṇi teṣāṃ santi /
syādetat /
ūrdhvaretasa āśramā na śrūyante veda iti tadapi nāsti /
children.translated_text: The celibate <s>āśramas</s> are not taught in the <s>Veda</s>. That too is not so.

children.text: te 'pi hi vaidikeṣu śabdeṣvavagamyante 'trayo dharmaskandhāḥ' (chā. 2.23.1) 'ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ityupāsate' (chā. 5.10.1) 'tapaḥśraddhe yo hyupavasantyaraṇye' (mu. 1.2.11) 'etameva pravājino lokamicchantaḥ pravajanti' (bṛ. 4.4.22) 'brahmacaryādeva pravrajet' (jā. 4) ityevamādiṣu /
children.translated_text: For they too are known from Vedic statements: 'There are three branches of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1), 'Those who in the forest practice faith and austerity' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1), 'Those who practice austerity and faith while dwelling in the forest' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.11), 'Desiring this very world, renunciants renounce' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22), 'One should renounce from the state of <s>brahmacarya</s> itself' (<s>Jābāla</s> 4) — and such passages.

children.text: pratipannāpratipannagārhasthyānāmapākṛtānāpākṛtarṇatrayāṇāṃ cordhvaretastvaṃ śrutismṛtiprasiddham /
children.translated_text: The celibacy of those who have entered household life and those who have not, of those who have discharged the three debts and those who have not — is well-known from both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: tasmādapi svātantryaṃ vidyāyāḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, the independence of <s>vidyā</s> [is established]. // 17 //

<s>Vidyā</s> is heard [as taught] in the celibate <s>āśramas</s> (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>). And there, the subsidiarity of <s>vidyā</s> to <s>karma</s> is not tenable — because of the absence of <s>karma</s>. For the Vedic rituals such as <s>agnihotra</s> and the like do not exist for them. It might be objected:

children.text: 2 parāmarśādhikaraṇam / sū. 18-20
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Parāmarśādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Allusion). <s>Sūtras</s> 18-20.

children.text: parāmarśaṃ jaiminiracodanāccāpavadati hi | BBs_3,4.18 |
children.translated_text: <s>Jaimini</s> holds that [the other <s>āśramas</s>] are [merely] alluded to, and he negates [their independent injunction] — because there is no injunctive [statement], and because [the <s>śruti</s>] contradicts [them]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.18 |

children.text:
'trayo dharmaskandhāḥ' (chā. 2.2.3.1) ityādayo ye śabdā ūrdhvaretasāmāśramāṇāṃ sadbhāvāyodāhṛtā na te tatpratipādanāya prabhavanti /
yataḥ parāmarśameṣu śabdeṣvāśramāntarāṇāṃ jaiminirācāryo manyate na vidim /
kutaḥ - nahyatra liṅgādīnāmanyatamaścodanāśabdo 'sti /
arthāntaraparatvaṃ caiṣu pratyekamupalabhyate /
trayo dharmaskandhā ityatra tāvadyajño 'dhyayanaṃ dānamiti prathamastapa eva dvitīyo brahmacāryācāryakulavāsī tṛtīyo 'tyantamātmānamācāryakule 'vasādayansarva ete puṇyalokā bhavantīti parāmarśapūrvakamāśramāṇāmanātyantikaphalatvaṃ saṃkīrtyātyantikaphalatayā brahmasaṃsthatā stūyate - 'brahmasaṃstho 'mṛtatvameti' (chā. 2.23.1) iti /
children.translated_text: The passages such as 'There are three branches of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1) and the like that were cited to establish the existence of the celibate <s>āśramas</s> — they are not capable of establishing them. For the teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds that in these passages, the other <s>āśramas</s> are [merely] alluded to, not enjoined. Why? Because in these passages there is no injunctive word belonging to any of the indicators (<s>liṅga</s>) and the like. And each of these passages is seen to have a different purport. In 'Three branches of <s>dharma</s>' — the first [branch] is 'sacrifice, study, and charity'; the second is 'austerity alone'; the third is 'a <s>brahmacārin</s> dwelling in the teacher's house, completely establishing himself in the teacher's family.' By mentioning the <s>āśramas</s> in the form of allusion, [the text] declares their non-ultimate fruit, and then, for the purpose of praising, [declares] establishment in <s>Brahman</s> as having the ultimate fruit: '<s>Brahmasaṃstha</s> (one established in <s>Brahman</s>) attains immortality' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1).

children.text: nanu parāmarśe 'pyāśramā gamyanta eva /
children.translated_text: Objection: But even in the allusion, the <s>āśramas</s> are understood.

children.text:
satyaṃ gamyante /
smṛtyācārābhyāṃ tu teṣāṃ prasiddhirna pratyakṣaśruteḥ /
ataśca pratyakṣaśrutivirodhe satyanādaraṇīyāste bhaviṣyanti /
anadhikṛtaviṣayā vā /
children.translated_text: True, they are understood. But their well-known status comes from <s>smṛti</s> and established practice, not from direct <s>śruti</s>. Therefore, in the presence of a contradicting direct <s>śruti</s>, they would become disregardable — or [applicable] only to those who are not qualified [for knowledge].

children.text: nanu gārhasthyamapi sahaivordhvaretobhiḥ parāmṛṣṭaṃ yajño 'dhyayanaṃ dānamiti prathama iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the householder's life too is merely alluded to along with the celibate [<s>āśramas</s>] — in 'sacrifice, study, and charity is the first [branch].'

children.text:
satyamevaṃ tathāpi tu gṛhasthaṃ pratyevāgnihotrādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ vidhānācchrutiprasiddhameva hi tadastitvam /
tasmātstutyartha evāyaṃ paramarśo na codanārthaḥ /
apicāpavadati hi pratyakṣā śrutirāśramāntar 'vīrahā vā eṣa devānāṃ yo 'gnimudvāsayate', 'ācāryāya priyaṃ dhanamāhṛtya prajātantuṃ mā vyavacchetsīḥ' (tai. 1.11.1) 'nāputrasya loko 'stīti tatsarve paśavo viduḥ' ityevamādyā /
tathā 'ye cemeraṇye śraddhā tapa ityupāsate' (chā. 5.10.1) 'tapaḥśraddhe ye hyupāsantyaraṇye' (muṇḍa. 1.2.11) iti ca devayānopadeśo nāśramāntaropadeśaḥ /
saṃdigdhaṃ cāśramāntarābhidhānam 'tapa eva dvitīyaḥ' (chā. 2.2.3.1) ityevamādiṣu /
tathā etameva pravrājino lokamicchantaḥ pravrajanti' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti lokasaṃstavo 'yaṃ na pārivrājyavidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: True, that is so. Nevertheless, since rituals such as <s>agnihotra</s> and the like are enjoined specifically for the householder, the existence of the householder's [<s>āśrama</s>] is established from <s>śruti</s> itself. Therefore, this allusion is merely for the purpose of praise, not for injunction. Moreover, direct <s>śruti</s> contradicts the other <s>āśramas</s>: 'He is indeed a slayer of heroes among the gods who extinguishes the [sacred] fire'; 'Having brought the beloved wealth to the teacher, do not cut off the thread of progeny' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.11.1); 'There is no world for one without a son — all animals know this' — and such passages. Likewise, 'Those who in the forest practice faith and austerity' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1), 'Those who practice austerity and faith while dwelling in the forest' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.11) — these teach the <s>devayāna</s> path, not the other <s>āśramas</s>. And the reference to other <s>āśramas</s> is doubtful in passages like 'Austerity alone is the second [branch]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1) and the like. Likewise, 'Desiring this very world, renunciants renounce' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) — this is a praise of the world [of <s>Brahman</s>], not an injunction of renunciation.

children.text: nanu brahmacaryādeva pravrajeditivispaṣṭamidaṃ pratyakṣaṃ privrājyavidhānaṃ jābālānām /
children.translated_text: Objection: But 'One should renounce from the state of <s>brahmacarya</s> itself' — this is clearly a direct injunction of renunciation from the <s>Jābālas</s>.

children.text: satyametat /
children.translated_text: True, that is so.

children.text: anapekṣya tvetāṃ śrutimayaṃ vicāra iti draṣṭavyam // 18 //
children.translated_text: But it should be understood that this discussion proceeds without taking that <s>śruti</s> into consideration. // 18 //

children.text: anuṣṭheyaṃ bādarāyaṇaḥ sāmyaśruteḥ | BBs_3,4.19 |
children.translated_text: [The other <s>āśramas</s>] are to be practiced — [so holds] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, because of the <s>śruti</s> declaring [them] equal. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.19 |

children.text:
anuṣṭheyamāśramāntaraṃ bādarāyaṇa ācāryo manyate /
vede śravaṇāt /
agnihotrādīnāṃ cāvaśyānuṣṭhoyatvāttadvirodhādanadhikṛtānuṣṭheyamāśramāntaramitihīmāṃ matiṃ nirākaroti gārhasthyavadevāśramāntaramapyanicchatā pratipattavyamiti manyamānaḥ /
kutaḥ sāmyaśruteḥ /
samā hi gārhastyenāśramāntarasya parāmarśaśrutirdṛśyate 'trayo dharmaskandhāḥ' (chā. 2.2.3.1)ityādyā /
yatheha śrutyantaravihitameva gārhastyaṃ parāmṛṣṭamevāśramāntaramapīti pratipattavyam /
yathāca śāstrāntaraprāptayoreva nivītaprācīnavītayoḥ parāmarśa upavītavidhipare vākye /
tasmāttulyamanuṣṭheyatvaṃ gārhasthyenāśramāntarasya /
tathā 'etameva pravrājino lokamicchantaḥ pravrajanti' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityasya vedānuvacanādibhiḥ samabhivyāhāraḥ /
'ye ceme 'ramye śraddā tapa ityupāsate' (chā. 5.101) ityasya ca pañcāgnividyayā /
yattūktam 'tapa eva dvitīyaḥ (chā. 2.2.3.1) ityādiṣvāśramāntarābhidhānaṃ saṃdigdhamiti /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
niścayakāraṇasadbhāvāt /
'trayo dharmaskandhāḥ' (chā. 2.23.1) iti hi dharmaskandhatritvaṃ pratijñātam /
naca yajñādayo bhūyāṃso dharmā utpattibhinnāḥ santo 'nyatrāśramasaṃbandhātritve 'ntarbhāvayituṃ śakyante /
children.translated_text: And the numerous <s>dharmas</s> such as sacrifice and the like — being distinct in origin — cannot be included within the [number] three except through an <s>āśrama</s>-connection.

children.text: tatra yajñādiliṅgo gṛhāśrama eko dharmaskandho nirdiṣṭo brahmacārīti ca spaṣṭa āśramanirdeśastapaityapi ko 'nyastapaḥpradhānādāśramāddharmaskandho 'bhyupagamyeta /
children.translated_text: Among those, the householder <s>āśrama</s> — characterized by the indicative marks of sacrifice and the like — is designated as one branch of <s>dharma</s>; and 'the student of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahmacārī</s>) is a clear designation of an <s>āśrama</s>; and 'austerity' — what other branch of <s>dharma</s> could be accepted, apart from the <s>āśrama</s> in which austerity predominates?

children.text: 'ye ceme 'raṇye' (chā. 5.10.1) iti cāraṇyaliṅgācchraddhātapobhyāmāśramagṛhītiḥ /
children.translated_text: And in 'Those who in the forest' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1), because of the indicative mark of 'forest,' the <s>āśrama</s> is grasped through faith and austerity.

children.text: tasmātparāmarśe 'pyanuṣṭheyamāśramāntaram // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if [these passages are] mere references, the other <s>āśramas</s> are to be practiced. // 19 //

The teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> considers that the other stages of life (<s>āśramas</s>) are to be practiced.
Because they are heard in the <s>Veda</s>.
And [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] refutes the view that, because of the obligatory nature of <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, and because of contradiction with those [duties], the other <s>āśramas</s> are to be practiced only by those who are not eligible [for <s>Agnihotra</s> etc.] — [he refutes this] by considering that the other <s>āśramas</s> too must be adopted, even unwillingly, just like the householder stage.
Why? Because of the <s>śruti</s> that treats them equally.
For a <s>śruti</s> that mentions the other <s>āśramas</s> on an equal footing with the householder stage is observed: 'Three are the branches of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1) and the like.
Just as the householder stage — which is enjoined in another <s>śruti</s> — is here [merely] referred to, so too the other <s>āśramas</s> should be understood as [already] enjoined [elsewhere and merely] referred to [here].
Just as, in a passage concerned with the injunction of the sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>), the <s>nivīta</s> and <s>prācīnavīta</s> [modes of wearing the thread] — which are already established by another <s>śāstra</s> — are [merely] referred to.
Therefore, the obligation to practice is equal for the other <s>āśramas</s> and the householder stage.
Likewise, 'Wandering ascetics (<s>pravrājins</s>) go forth desiring this very world' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) — this is mentioned together with Vedic recitation and the like.
And 'Those who in the forest worship faith and austerity' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1) — this is [mentioned] together with the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>.
As for the objection that in passages like 'Austerity alone is the second [branch]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1) and the like, the reference to other <s>āśramas</s> is doubtful —
this is not a fault.
Because there exists a ground for certainty.
For the triad of branches of <s>dharma</s> has been declared: 'Three are the branches of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1).

children.text: vidhir vā dhāraṇavat | BBs_3,4.20 |
children.translated_text: Or [they are] an injunction — as with the holding [of the fuel-stick]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.20 |

children.text: vidhirivāyamāśramāntarasya na parāmarśamātram /
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is an injunction for the other <s>āśramas</s> — not a mere reference.

children.text: nanu vidhitvābhyupagama ekavākyatāpratītiruparudhyeta pratīyate cātraikavākyatā puṇyalokaphalāstrayo dharmaskandhā brahmasaṃsthātā tvamṛtatvaphaleti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But if the injunctive nature [of these passages] is accepted, the perception of single-sentence unity (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) would be obstructed. And single-sentence unity is perceived here: 'The three branches of <s>dharma</s> [have] the fruit of a meritorious world; but one who is established in <s>Brahman</s> [has] the fruit of immortality.'

children.text:
satyametat /
satīmapi tvekavākyatāpratītiṃ parityajya vidhirevābhyupagantavyo 'pūrvatvāt /
vidhyantarasyādarśanāt /
children.translated_text:
True.
But even setting aside this perception of single-sentence unity, the injunctive nature alone must be accepted — because of its being unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>).
Because no other injunction [for these <s>āśramas</s>] is found.

children.text:
vispaṣṭāccāśramāntarapratyayādguṇavādakalpanayaikavākyatvāyojanānupapatteḥ /
dhāraṇavat /
yathā 'adhastatsamidhaṃ dhārayannanudravedupari hi devebhyo dhārayati' ityatra satyāmapyavirodhodhāraṇainaikavākyatāpratītau vidhīyata evoparidhāraṇamapūrvatvāt /
tathācoktaṃ śeṣalakṣaṇe - 'vidhistu dhāraṇe 'pūrvatvāt' iti /
tadvadihāpyāśramaparāmarśaśrutirvidhiriveti kalpyate /
yadāpi parāmarśa evāyamāśramāntarāṇāṃ tadapi brahmasaṃsthatā tāvatsaṃstavasāmarthyādavaśyaṃ vidheyābhyupagantavyā /
sā ca kiṃ caturṣvāśrameṣu yasya kasyacidāhosvitparivrājakasyaiveti vivektavyam /
yadi ca brahmācāryanteṣvāśrameṣu parāmṛśyamāneṣu parivrājako 'pi parāmṛṣṭastaścaturṇāmapyāśramāṇāṃ parāmṛṣṭatvāviśeṣādanāśramitvānupapatteśca yaḥ kaściccaturṣvāśrameṣu brahmasaṃstho bhaviṣyati /
atha na parāmṛṣṭastataḥ pariśiṣyamāṇaḥ parivrāḍeva brahmasaṃstha iti saṃtsyati /
tatra tapaḥśabdena vaikhānasagrāhiṇāparāmṛṣṭaḥparivrāḍapīti kecit /
tadapyuktam /
nahi satyāṃ gatau vānaprasthaviśeṣaṇena parivrājako grahaṇamiti /
yathātra brahmacārigṛhamedhināvasādāraṇenaiva svena svena viśeṣaṇena viśeṣitāvevaṃ bhikṣuvaikhānasāvapīti yuktam /
tapaścāsādhāraṇodharmo vānaprasthānāṃ kāyakleśapradhānatvāt /
tapaḥśabdasya tatra rūḍheḥ /
bhikṣostu dharma indriyasaṃyamādilakṣaṇo naiva tapaḥśabdenābhilapyate /
catuṣṭhvena ca prasiddhā āśramāstritvena parāmṛśyanta ityanyāyyam /
apica bhedavyapadeśo 'tra bhavati 'traya ete puṇyalokabhāja eko 'mṛtatvabhāk' iti /
pṛthaktveva caiṣa bhedavyapadeśo 'vakalpate /
nahyevaṃ bhavati devadattayajñadattau mandaprajñāvanyastvanayormahāprajña iti /
bhavati tvevaṃ devadattayajñadattau mandaprajñau viṣṇumitrastu mahāprajña iti /
tasmātpūrvo traya āśramiṇaḥ puṇyalokabhājaḥ pariśiṣyamāṇaḥ parivrāḍevāmṛtatvabhāk /
kathaṃ punarbrahmasaṃsthaśabdo yogātpravartamānaḥ sarvatra saṃbhavanparivrājaka evāvatiṣṭheta /
rūḍhyabhyupagame cāśramamātrādamṛtatvaprāpterjñānānarthakyaprasaṅga iti /
children.translated_text:
And because, the recognition of the other <s>āśramas</s> being clear, it is not tenable to construe single-sentence unity by treating [the reference] as a subsidiary statement (<s>guṇavāda</s>).
As with the holding [of the fuel-stick].
Just as in 'Holding the fuel-stick below, he presses upward; for he holds it above for the <s>devas</s>' — even though there is a perception of single-sentence unity [with the preceding sentence] that is non-contradictory, the upward-holding is indeed enjoined — because of its being unprecedented.
And thus it is stated in the <s>Śeṣalakṣaṇa</s> [section of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>]: 'It is an injunction, regarding the holding — because of its being unprecedented.'
Similarly here too, this <s>śruti</s> that references the other <s>āśramas</s> is construed as an injunction.
Even if this is [merely] a reference to the other <s>āśramas</s>, at least the [phrase] '<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>' (one established in <s>Brahman</s>) must be accepted as enjoined — because of the commending power of the laudatory passage.
And [the question arises:] Does that [<s>brahmasaṃstha</s> status] belong to any one of the four <s>āśramas</s>, or to the wandering ascetic (<s>parivrājaka</s>) alone? — this is to be investigated.
If, among the <s>āśramas</s> being referred to — ending with the student (<s>brahmacārī</s>) — the wandering ascetic is also referred to, then — because there is no distinction in being referred to among all four <s>āśramas</s>, and because the absence of any <s>āśrama</s> [for such a person] is not tenable — whoever among the four <s>āśramas</s> is established in <s>Brahman</s> [will be meant].
But if [the wandering ascetic] is not referred to, then the remaining one — the wandering ascetic alone — will be the one 'established in <s>Brahman</s>,' by the process of elimination.
Regarding this: some [say] that the wandering ascetic too is referred to by the word '<s>tapas</s>' (austerity), as [that word] includes the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> [forest-dweller].
But that too has been stated [to be incorrect].
For when a definite interpretation is available, it is improper to include the wandering ascetic through a designation that specifies the forest-dweller.
Just as here the student (<s>brahmacārī</s>) and the householder (<s>gṛhamedhin</s>) are each qualified by their own distinctive qualifications, so too the mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) and the forest-dweller (<s>vaikhānasa</s>) should be [separately qualified] — this is proper.
And austerity is the distinctive <s>dharma</s> of forest-dwellers, because bodily mortification predominates [for them].
Because the word '<s>tapas</s>' has its established usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) there.
But the <s>dharma</s> of the mendicant — characterized by sense-control and the like — is not at all expressed by the word '<s>tapas</s>.'
And it is improper that [stages] well known as four should be referred to as three.
Moreover, there is a designation of difference here: 'These three [have] the fruit of meritorious worlds; the one [other has] the fruit of immortality.'
And this designation of difference is tenable only when [the parties] are separate.
For one does not [say]: '<s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s> are of dull intellect, but the other of these two is of sharp intellect.'
But one does [say]: '<s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s> are of dull intellect, but <s>Viṣṇumitra</s> is of sharp intellect.'
Therefore, the first three <s>āśramins</s> have the fruit of meritorious worlds; the remaining one — the wandering ascetic alone — has the fruit of immortality.
But how could the word '<s>brahmasaṃstha</s>' — which [can] operate by [mere] derivation (<s>yoga</s>) and is possible in all [<s>āśramas</s>] — be restricted to the wandering ascetic alone?
And if an established conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) is accepted, the consequence of the purposelessness of knowledge would arise — since immortality would be attained from the <s>āśrama</s> alone.

children.text:
atrocyate - brahmasaṃstha iti hi brahmaṇi parisamptirananyavyāpāratārūpaṃ tanniṣṭhatvamabhidhīyate /
tacca trayāṇāmā8māṇāṃ na saṃbavati /
svāśramavihitakarmānanuṣṭhāne pryavāyaśravaṇāt /
parivrājakasya tu sarvakarmasaṃnyāsātapratyavāyo na saṃbhavatyananuṣṭhānanimittaḥ /
śamadamādistu tadīyo dharmo brahmasaṃsthatāyā upodbalako na virodhī /
brahmaniṣṭhatvameva hi tasya śamadamādyupabṛṃhitaṃ svāśramavihitaṃ karma yajñādīni cetareṣāṃ tadvyatikrame ca tasya pratyavāyaḥ tathāca 'nyāsa iti brahmā brahmā hi paraḥ paro hi brahma tāni vā etānyavarāṇi tapāṃsi nyāsa evātyarecayat' (nārā. 78) 'vedāntavijñānasuniṣcitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogādyatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ' (muṇḍa. 3.2.6. nārā. 1.2.3. kaivalya. 3) ityādyāḥ śrutayaḥ /
smṛtayaśca -'tadbuddhayastadātmānastanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ' (gī. 5.17) ityādyā brahmasaṃsthasya karmābhāvaṃ darśayanti /
tasmātaparivrājakasyāśramamātrādamṛtatvaprāpterjñānānarthakyaprasaṅga ityeteṣo 'pi doṣo nvatarati /
tadevaṃ parāmarśo 'pītareṣāmāśramāṇāṃ pārivrājyaṃ tāvadbrahmasaṃsthatālakṣaṇaṃ labhyetaiva /
anapekṣyaiva jābālaśrutimāśramāntaravidhāyinīmayamācryoṇa vicāraḥ pravartitaḥ /
vidyata eva tvāśramāntaravidhiśrutiḥ pratyakṣā /
'brahmacaryaṃ parisampya gṛhī bhavedgṛhī bhūtvā vanībhavedvanī bhūtvā pravrajet /
yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva brahmacaryādeva pravrajedgṛhādvā vanādvā' (jābā. 4) iti /
na ceyaṃ śrutiranadikṛtāviṣayā śakyā vaktum /
aviśeṣaśravaṇāt /
pṛthagnidhānāccānadhikṛtānāma 'atha punareva vratī vāvratī vā snātako vāsnātako votsannāgniranagniko vā' (jābā. 4) ityādinā /
brahmadānaparipākāṅgatvācca pārivrājyasya nānadhikṛtaviṣayatvam /
children.translated_text: And because <s>parivrājya</s> (renunciation) is an integral part of the maturation of the gift of <s>Brahman</s> [-knowledge], it cannot pertain to the ineligible alone.

children.text: tacca darśayati - 'atha parivrāḍvivarṇavāsā muṇḍo 'parigrahaḥ śuciradrohī bhaikṣāṇo brahmabhūyāya bhavati' (jābā. 5) iti /
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows this: 'Then the wandering ascetic — wearing discolored garments, shaven-headed, without possessions, pure, non-hostile, living on alms — becomes [one who is heading for] <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Jābāla</s> 5).

children.text: tasmātsiddhā ūrdhvaretasāmāśramāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>āśramas</s> of the <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (celibates / those of upward-flowing vitality) are established.

children.text: siddhaṃ cordhvaretaḥsu vidānādvidyāyāḥ svātantryamiti // 20 //
children.translated_text: And the independence of <s>vidyā</s> — when imparted among the <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> [renunciants] — is also established. // 20 //

To this we reply: '<s>Brahmasaṃstha</s>' denotes being exclusively devoted to <s>Brahman</s> — a state of absorption in <s>Brahman</s> characterized by having no other occupation.
And that is not possible for the [first] three <s>āśramins</s>.
Because a decline (<s>pratyavāya</s>) is heard [in scripture] for the non-performance of the <s>karmas</s> enjoined upon their respective <s>āśramas</s>.
But for the wandering ascetic, since he has renounced all <s>karma</s>, no decline due to non-performance is possible.
And his <s>dharmas</s> — tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-control (<s>dama</s>), and the like — reinforce his being established in <s>Brahman</s> and do not conflict [with it].
For being established in <s>Brahman</s> — strengthened by tranquility, self-control, and the like — is indeed his <s>āśrama</s>-enjoined duty. And sacrifice and the like are the [duties] of the others — and in transgressing those, there is a decline for them.
And thus [the <s>śrutis</s>]: '<s>Nyāsa</s> (renunciation) is <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Brahman</s> indeed is the Supreme; the Supreme indeed is <s>Brahman</s> — these are indeed inferior austerities; renunciation alone surpassed [them all]' (<s>Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s> 78); 'Those whose aims are firmly ascertained through the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, purified in their being through the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.6; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> 1.2.3; <s>Kaivalya</s> 3) — and such <s>śrutis</s>.
And <s>smṛtis</s> such as 'Their intellects [absorbed] in That, their selves in That, established in That, devoted to That as their supreme goal' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 5.17) and the like show that one who is established in <s>Brahman</s> has no <s>karma</s>.
Therefore, the fault of the purposelessness of knowledge — [arising] from the attainment of immortality from the <s>āśrama</s> alone, for one who is not a wandering ascetic — does not arise here either.
Thus, even if [the passage is taken as] a mere reference to the other <s>āśramas</s>, the <s>parivrājya</s> (state of wandering asceticism) — characterized by being established in <s>Brahman</s> — is obtained [as enjoined].
This investigation has been carried out by the teacher [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] without relying on the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> — which enjoins the other <s>āśramas</s> [i.e., renunciation].
But there indeed exists a directly explicit <s>śruti</s> that enjoins the other <s>āśramas</s>:
'Having completed the period of studentship (<s>brahmacarya</s>), one should become a householder; having been a householder, one should become a forest-dweller; having been a forest-dweller, one should go forth [as a renunciant]. Or alternatively — from studentship itself one may go forth; from the householder stage or from the forest' (<s>Jābāla</s> 4).
And this <s>śruti</s> cannot be said to pertain to those who are ineligible [for the householder stage].
Because [the text] is heard without specification.
And because of the separate mention of the ineligible: 'Whether one has observed the vow or not, whether one has completed the bath [at the end of studentship] or not, whether one's fires have ceased or one has no fires' (<s>Jābāla</s> 4) — and the like.

children.text: stutimātrādhikaraṇam / sū. 21-22
children.translated_text: The <s>Stutimātra Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Mere Praise). <s>Sūtras</s> 21-22.

children.text: stutimātram upādānād iti cen nāpūrvatvāt | BBs_3,4.21 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that the <s>udgītha</s> and similar <s>śrutis</s>] are mere praise, because [they] take up [ritual components] — [we say] no, because of their being unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.21 |

children.text:
'sa eṣa rasānāṃ rasatamaḥ paramaḥ parārdhyo 'ṣṭamo yadudgīthaḥ' (chā. 1.1.3) 'ityevamāgniḥ sāma' ( chā. 1.6.1) ayaṃ vāva loka eṣo 'gniścitaḥ /
tadidamevokthamiyameva pṛthivī' ityevañjātīkāḥ śrutayaḥ kimudgīthādeḥ stutyarthā āhosvidupāsanāvidyarthā ityasminsaṃśaye stutyarthā iti yuktam /
udgīthādīni karmāṅgānyupādāya śravaṇāt /
yathā 'iyameva juhūrādityaḥ kūrmaḥ svargo loka āhavanīyaḥ' ityādyā juhvādistutyarthāstadvaditi cet /
children.translated_text:
'This is the quintessence of essences, the supreme, the highest, the eighth — namely the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.3); 'Thus the fire is the <s>Sāman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.1); 'This world is indeed this fire-built [fire]'; 'That is indeed the <s>uktha</s>; this is indeed the earth' — regarding such <s>śrutis</s>, the doubt arises: Are they for the purpose of praising the <s>udgītha</s> and the like, or for the purpose of enjoining meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>)?
In this doubt, [the prima facie view is:] They are for the purpose of praise.
Because [they] are heard as taking up the <s>udgītha</s> and the like, which are components of ritual action.
Just as 'This <s>juhū</s> ladle indeed is the sun; the tortoise is the heavenly world; [the vessel] is the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire' — and the like are for the purpose of praising the <s>juhū</s> and the like, so too [these passages] — if this is the objection,

children.text:
netyāha /
nahi stutimātramāsāṃ śrutīnāṃ prayojanaṃ yuktamapūrvatvāt /
vidhyarthatāyāṃ hyapūrvor'tho vihito bhavati stutyarthatāyāṃ tvānarthakyameva syāt /
vidhāyakasya hi śabdasya vākyaśeṣabhāvaṃ pratipadyamānā stutirupayujyata ityuktam 'vidhinā tvekavākyatvātstutyarthena vidhīnāṃ syuḥ ityatra /
children.translated_text: For it has been stated that praise is useful when it attains the status of being a complement to an injunctive statement: 'By being single-sentenced with an injunction, [they] would be for the purpose of praise of the injunctions' — in that context.

children.text: pradeśāntaravihitānāṃ tūdgīthādīnāmiyaṃ pradeśāntarapaṭhitā stitirvākyaśeṣabhāvamapratipadyamānānarthikaiva syāt /
children.translated_text: But this praise of the <s>udgītha</s> and the like — which are enjoined in another context — being recited in yet another context, would be purposeless, since it does not attain the status of being a complement to [any injunctive passage here].

children.text: iyameva juhūrityādi tu vidhisaṃnidhāvevāmnatamiti vaiṣamyam /
children.translated_text: But 'This <s>juhū</s> ladle indeed' and the like are recited in the immediate proximity of an injunction — hence the disparity.

children.text: tasmādvidhyarthā evaivañjātīyakāḥ śrutayaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>śrutis</s> of this kind are for the purpose of injunction [of meditation] alone. // 21 //

We say: No.
For mere praise alone is not a fitting purpose for these <s>śrutis</s> — because of their being unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>).
For if they are injunctive in purpose, an unprecedented meaning is enjoined; but if their purpose is mere praise, there would be purposelessness alone.

children.text: bhāvaśabdāc ca | BBs_3,4.22 |
children.translated_text: And because of the word [expressing] 'being' (<s>bhāva</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.22 |

children.text: 'udgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.1.1) 'sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.2.1) 'ahamukthamasmīti vidyāt' ityādayaśca vispaṣṭā vidhiśabdāḥ śrūyante te ca stutimātraprayojanatāyāṃ vyāhanyeran /
tathāca nyāyavidāṃ smaraṇam -'kuryātkriyeta kartavyaṃ bhavetasyāditi pañcamam /
children.translated_text:
And thus the tradition of the logicians [says]:
'One should do, it should be done, it is to be done, it would be, it may be — the fifth [form] —

children.text: etatsyātsarvavedeṣu niyataṃ vidhilakṣaṇam' iti liṅgādyartho vidhiriti manyamānāsta evaṃ smaranti /
children.translated_text: this would be the fixed injunctive mark in all the <s>Vedas</s>' — holding that the optative (<s>liṅg</s>) and the like have injunctive meaning, they thus declare.

children.text: pratiprakaraṇaṃ ca phalāni śrāvyate - 'āpayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.7) 'eṣa hyeva kāmāgānasyeṣṭe' (chā. 1.7.9) 'kalpante hāsmai lokā ūrdhvaścāvṛttāśca' (chā. 2.2.3) ityādīni /
children.translated_text: And fruits are heard in each context: 'He becomes the attainer of desires' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.7); 'For this indeed fulfills the desire of what is wished' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.9); 'For him the worlds are arranged, both the upward and the downward ones' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.3) — and the like.

children.text: tasmādapyupāsanāvidhānārthā udgīthādiśrutayaḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore too, the <s>udgītha</s> and similar <s>śrutis</s> are for the purpose of enjoining meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>). // 22 //

'One should meditate on the <s>udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1); 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.1); 'One should know: I am the <s>uktha</s>' — and the like. Clear injunctive words are heard. And those would be contradicted if the purpose were mere praise.

children.text: 4 pāriplavādhikaraṇam / sū. 23-24
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Pāriplava Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Revolving [Narratives]). <s>Sūtras</s> 23-24.

children.text: pāriplavārthā iti cen na viśeṣitatvāt | BBs_3,4.23 |
children.translated_text: If [it be said that the Vedāntic narratives] are for the purpose of the <s>pāriplava</s> [recitation in the <s>Aśvamedha</s>] — [we say] no, because of specification. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.23 |

children.text:
'atha ha yājñavalkyasya dve bhārye babhūvaturmaitreyī ca kātyayanī ca' (bṛ. 4.5.1) 'pratardano ha vai daivodāsirindrasya priyaṃ dhāmopajagāma' (kauṣī. 3.1) 'jānaśrutirha pautrāyaṇaḥ śraddhādeyo bahudāyī bahupākya āsa' (chā. 4.1.1) ityevamādiṣu vedāntapaṭhiteṣvākhyāneṣu saṃśayaḥ - kimimāni pāriplavaprayogārthānyohosvitsaṃnihitavidyāpratipattyarthānīti /
pāriplavārthā imā ākhyānaśrutayaḥ /
ākhyānasāmānyāt /
ākhyānaprayogasya ca pariplave coditatvāt /
tataśca vidyāpradhānatvaṃ vedāntānāṃ na syāt, mantravatprayogaśeṣatvāditi cet /
children.translated_text:
'Now, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> had two wives — <s>Maitreyī</s> and <s>Kātyāyanī</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.1); '<s>Pratardana</s>, the son of <s>Divodāsa</s>, reached the beloved abode of <s>Indra</s>' (<s>Kauṣītakī</s> 3.1); '<s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> was a man of faith, a great giver, a great provider of cooked food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.1.1) — regarding such narratives recited in the <s>Vedānta</s>, the doubt arises: Are these for the purpose of application in the <s>pāriplava</s> [rite], or for the purpose of apprehending the <s>vidyā</s> that is proximate [to them]?
[The prima facie view:] These narrative <s>śrutis</s> are for the purpose of the <s>pāriplava</s>.
Because of the general [feature of being] narratives.
And because the application of narratives is enjoined in the <s>pāriplava</s>.
And consequently, the <s>Vedāntas</s> would not have <s>vidyā</s> as their primary [purpose] — being accessories to ritual application, like <s>mantras</s> — if this is the objection,

children.text:
tanna /
kasmāt /
viśeṣitatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because of specification.

children.text: 'pāriplavamācakṣīta' iti hi prakṛtya 'manurvaivasvato rājā' ityevamādīni kānicidevākhyānāni tatra viśeṣyante /
children.translated_text: For having introduced [the topic] with 'One should recite the <s>pāriplava</s>,' certain specific narratives alone are specified there: '<s>Manu Vaivasvata</s> was a king' — and the like.

children.text: ākhyānasāmānyāccetsāmānyāccetsarvagṛhītiḥ syādanarthakamevedaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: And if, because of the general [feature of being] narratives, all [narratives] were included, then this specification would be purposeless.

children.text: tasmānna pāriplavārthā etā ākhyānaśrutayaḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, these narrative <s>śrutis</s> are not for the purpose of the <s>pāriplava</s>. // 23 //

No.
Why?

children.text: tathā caikavākyatopabandhāt | BBs_3,4.24 |
children.translated_text: And also because of the syntactic unity. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.24 |

children.text:
asati ca pariplavārthatva ākhyānānāṃ saṃnihitavidyāpratipādanopayogitaiva nyāyyā /
ekavākyatobandhāt /
tathāhi ta6 tatra saṃnihitābhirekavākyatā dṛśyate prarocanopayogātpratipattisaukaryopayogācca /
maitreyībrāhmaṇe tāvat - 'ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ' (bṛ. 4.5.6) ityādyā vidyayaikavākyatā dṛśyate /
prātardane 'pi prāṇo 'smi prajñātmā ityādyayā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Prātardana</s> [narrative] too, with [the <s>vidyā</s> beginning with:] 'I am <s>Prāṇa</s>, the conscious Self' and so on.

children.text: jānaśrutiriyyatrāpi 'vāyurvāva saṃvargaḥ' (chā. 4.3.1) ityādyā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Jānaśruti</s> narrative too, with [the <s>vidyā</s> beginning with:] '<s>Vāyu</s> indeed is the absorber (<s>saṃvarga</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.3.1) and so on.

children.text: yathā 'sa ātmāno vapāmudakhidat' ityevamādīnāṃ karmaśrutigatānāmākhyānāṃ saṃnihitavidhistutyarthatā tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as narratives such as 'He cut out the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) of the Self' and the like — which are found in the <s>karma</s> portion of the <s>śruti</s> — serve the purpose of praising the proximate injunction, so too [here].

children.text: tasmānna pāriplavārthatvam // 24 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the narratives] do not have the purpose of [providing] circulating recitations. // 24 //

And in the absence of the purpose of [providing] circulating recitations (<s>pariplava</s>), the proper [view] is that the narratives serve the purpose of elucidating the meditation (<s>vidyā</s>) proximate to them.
Because of syntactic unity.
For thus, syntactic unity with the [meditations] proximate to those [narratives] is observed — both for the purpose of arousing interest (<s>prarocana</s>) and for the purpose of facilitating apprehension.
In the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s>, for instance, the syntactic unity with the <s>vidyā</s> beginning with 'The Self indeed is to be seen' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6) is observed.

children.text: 5 agnīndhanādyadhikaraṇam / sū. 25
children.translated_text: 5 The <s>Agnīndhanādi</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 25.

children.text: ata eva cāgnīndhanādyanapekṣā | BBs_3,4.25 |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, there is no dependence on fire-kindling and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.25 |

children.text: 'puruṣārtho 'taḥ śabdāt' (bra.sū. 3.4.1) ityetadvyavahitamapi saṃbhavādata iti parāmṛśyate /
children.translated_text: The [<s>sūtra</s>] 'The human goal — because of the word [of <s>śruti</s>]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.1) — though separated [by intervening <s>sūtras</s>], is recalled here as still relevant.

children.text: ateva ca vidyāyāḥ puruṣārthahetutvādagnīndhanādīnyāśramakmāṇi vidyayā svārthasiddhau nāpekṣitavyānītyādyasyaivādhikaraṇasya phalamupasaṃharatyadhikavivakṣayā // 25 //
children.translated_text: And for this very reason — because <s>vidyā</s> is the cause of the human goal — <s>āśrama</s> duties such as fire-kindling and the like are not depended upon by <s>vidyā</s> for the accomplishment of its own purpose. Thus [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] concludes the result of this very [first] <s>adhikaraṇa</s>, with the intention of stating something additional. // 25 //

children.text: 6 sarvāpekṣādhikaraṇam / sū. 26-27
children.translated_text: 6 The <s>Sarvāpekṣā</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 26-27.

children.text: sarvāpekṣā ca yajñādiśruter aśvavat | BBs_3,4.26 |
children.translated_text: And there is dependence on all [<s>āśrama</s> duties] — because of the <s>śruti</s> on sacrifice and the like; like a horse. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.26 |

children.text:
idamidānīṃ cintyate kiṃ vidyāyā atyantamevānapekṣāśramakarmamāmutāsti kācidapekṣeti /
tatrāta evāgnīndhanādīnyāśramakarmāṇi vidyā svārthasiddhau nāpekṣyanta evamatyantamevānapekṣāyāṃ prāptāyāmidamucyate sarvāpekṣā ceti /
apekṣata ca vidyā sarvāṇyāśramakarmāṇi nātyantamanapekṣaiva /
children.translated_text:
This is now examined: Does <s>vidyā</s> have absolutely no dependence on <s>āśrama</s> duties, or is there some dependence?
When it is prima facie established that there is absolutely no dependence — since fire-kindling and other <s>āśrama</s> duties are not depended upon by <s>vidyā</s> for the accomplishment of its own purpose — this is stated: 'And there is dependence on all.'
<s>Vidyā</s> does depend on all <s>āśrama</s> duties; it is not absolutely independent.

children.text: nanu viruddhamidaṃ vacanamapekṣate cāśramakarmāṇi vidyā nāpekṣate ceti /
children.translated_text: But is this not a contradictory statement — that <s>vidyā</s> depends on <s>āśrama</s> duties and [yet] does not depend on them?

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ /
utpannā hi vidyā phalasiddhiṃ prati na kiñcidanyadapekṣata utpattiṃ prati tvapekṣate /
kutaḥ - yajñādiśruteḥ /
tathāhi śrutiḥ - 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasānāśakena' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti yajñādīnāṃ vidyāsādhanabhāvaṃ darśayati /
vividiṣāsaṃyogāccaiṣāmutpattisādhanabhāvoṣavasīyate /
'atha yadyajña ityācakṣate brahmacaryasya yajñādibhiḥ yaṃstavādyajñādīnāmapi hi sādhanabhāvaḥ sūcyate /
'sarve vedā yatpadamāmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yadvadanti /
yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tatte padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmi' (kaṭha. 2.15) ityevamādyā ca śrutirāśramakarmaṇāṃ vidyāsādhanabhāvaṃ sūcayati /
smṛtirapi - 'kaṣāyapakatiḥ karmāṇi jñānaṃ tu paramā gatiḥ /
kaṣāye karmabhiḥ pakke tato jñānaṃ pravartate' ityevamādyā /
children.translated_text: when the stain has been ripened by <s>karmas</s>, then knowledge arises' — and the like.

children.text: aśvavaditi yogyatānidarśanam /
children.translated_text: 'Like a horse' — this is an illustration of fitness.

children.text: yathāca yogyatāvaśenāśvo na lāṅgalākarṣaṇe yujyate rathacaryāyāṃ tu yujyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a horse, by its fitness, is not yoked to plowing but is yoked to chariot-driving,

children.text: evamāśramakarmāṇi vidyayā phalasiddhau nāpekṣyanta utpattau cāpekṣyanta iti // 26 //
children.translated_text: so too <s>āśrama</s> duties are not depended upon by <s>vidyā</s> for the accomplishment of its fruit, but are depended upon for its origination. // 26 //

No, we say.
For <s>vidyā</s>, once arisen, does not depend on anything else for the accomplishment of its fruit; but for its origination, it does depend [on them].
Why? Because of the <s>śruti</s> on sacrifice and the like.
For thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know That through the recitation of the Vedas, through sacrifice, through charity, through austerity, through fasting' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) — shows that sacrifice and the like are means to <s>vidyā</s>.
And because of their conjunction with the desiderative '<s>vividiṣanti</s>' (they desire to know), their status as means to the origination [of <s>vidyā</s>] is ascertained.
'Now, what is called sacrifice — that indeed is the student-life of <s>Brahman</s>; through sacrifice and the like' — thus the status of sacrifice and the like as means is indicated.
'All the Vedas declare that goal; all austerities speak of it; desiring which they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> — that goal I tell you briefly' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.15) — such <s>śrutis</s> and the like indicate that <s>āśrama</s> duties are means to <s>vidyā</s>.
The <s>smṛti</s> also [says]: 'The stain is ripened by <s>karmas</s>; knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the supreme goal;

children.text: śamadamādyupetas syāt tathāpi tu tadvidhes tadaṅgatayā teṣām apy avaśyānuṣṭheyatvāt | BBs_3,4.27 |
children.translated_text: One should be endowed with tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-restraint (<s>dama</s>), and the like — and moreover, because of the injunction regarding those, and because they [are prescribed] as ancillary to that [<s>vidyā</s>], they too must necessarily be practiced. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.27 |

children.text:
yadikaścinmanyeta yajñādīnāṃ vidyāsādhanabhāvo na nyāyyo vidhyabāvāt /
'yajñena vividiṣanti' ityevañjātīyakā hi śrutiranuvādasvarūpāvidyābhiṣṭavaparā na yajñādividhiparā /
itthaṃ mahābhāgā vidyā syādvidyārthī 'tasmādevaṃvicchanto dānta uparatastitikṣuḥ samāhito bhūtvātmaneyevātmānaṃ paśyati' (bṛ. 4.4.23) iti vidyāsādhanatvena śamadamādīnāṃ vidhānādvihitānāṃ cāvaśyānuṣṭheyatvāt /
children.translated_text:
If someone were to think: The status of sacrifice and the like as means to <s>vidyā</s> is not proper, because there is no injunction.
For <s>śrutis</s> of the type 'They seek to know through sacrifice' are restatements (<s>anuvāda</s>) in nature, intended for praising <s>vidyā</s> — not intended as injunctions of sacrifice and the like.
So great indeed is <s>vidyā</s>!
[We reply:] Because the seeker of <s>vidyā</s> should be endowed with tranquility, self-restraint, and the like — 'Therefore, one who is thus inclined, being tranquil, self-controlled, patient, and concentrated, sees the Self in the Self itself' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.23) — since tranquility, self-restraint, and the like are enjoined as means to <s>vidyā</s>, and since what is enjoined must necessarily be practiced,

children.text: nanvatrāpi śamādyupeto bhūtvā paśyatīti vartamānāpadeśa upalabhyate na vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: But here too, [the objector says,] what is found is a present-tense description — 'being endowed with tranquility and the like, one sees' — not an injunction.

children.text:
neti brūmaḥ /
tasmāditi prakṛtapraśaṃsāparigrahādvidhitvapratīteḥ /
paśyediti na mādhyandinā vispaṣṭameva vidhimadhīyate /
tasmādyajñādyanapekṣāyāmapi śamadīnyapekṣitavyāni /
yajñādīnyapi tvapekṣitavyānīti yajñādiśrutereva /
children.translated_text:
No, we say.
Because of the word '<s>tasmāt</s>' (therefore), which takes up the preceding praise, the perception of an injunction [is established].
The <s>Mādhyandinas</s> read even more clearly an injunction: '<s>paśyet</s>' (one should see) [in the optative].
Therefore, even when there is no dependence on sacrifice and the like, tranquility and the like must be depended upon.
But sacrifice and the like too must be depended upon — because of the very <s>śruti</s> on sacrifice and the like.

children.text:
nanūktaṃ yajñādibhirvividiṣantītyatra na vidhirupalabhyata iti /
satyamuktaṃ tathāpi tvatpūrvatvātsaṃyogasya vidhiḥ parikalpyate /
nahyayaṃ yajñādīnāṃ vividiṣāsaṃyogaḥ pūrvaṃ prāpto yenānūdyeta /
'tasmātpūṣā prapiṣṭabhāgo 'dantako hi ityevamādiṣu cāśrutavidhikeṣvapi vākyeṣvapūrvatvādvidhiṃ parikalpya pauṣṇaṃ peṣaṇaṃ vikṛtau pratīyetyādivicāraḥ prathame tantre pravartitaḥ /
tathācoktam 'vidhirvā dhāraṇavat' (bra, sū. 3.4.20) iti /
children.translated_text: And thus it has been stated: 'Or it is an injunction, like the holding' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.20).

children.text: smṛtirapi bhagavadgītādyāsvanabhisaṃdhāya phalamanutiṣṭhitāni yajñādīni mumukṣorjñānasādhanāni bhavantīti prapañcitam /
children.translated_text: In the <s>smṛti</s> also — in the <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> and the like — it has been elaborated that sacrifice and the like, performed without attachment to their fruits, become means to knowledge for the seeker of liberation.

children.text: tasmādyajñādīni śamadamādīni ca yathāśramaṃ sarvāṇyevāśramakarmāṇi vidyotpattāvapekṣitavyāni /
children.translated_text: Therefore, all <s>āśrama</s> duties — sacrifice and the like, tranquility and self-restraint and the like — must be depended upon as appropriate to one's <s>āśrama</s>, for the origination of <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: tatrāpyevaṃviditi vidyāsaṃyogātpratyāsannāni vidyāsādhanāni śamādīni, vividiṣāsaṃyogāttu brahyatarāṇi yajñādīnīti vivektavyam // 27 //
children.translated_text: And among those, the ones such as tranquility and the like — being proximate to <s>vidyā</s> because of their conjunction with [the expression] 'one who is thus [inclined]' — are proximate means to <s>vidyā</s>; while sacrifice and the like — being connected with the desire to know (<s>vividiṣā</s>) — are more remote means. This distinction should be understood. // 27 //

But was it not said that in 'they seek to know through sacrifice and the like,' no injunction is found?
True, that was said. But still, because the conjunction [of sacrifice with the desire to know] is unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>), an injunction is inferred.
For this conjunction of sacrifice and the like with the desire to know was not previously established, such that it could be merely restated.
And in passages like 'Therefore <s>Pūṣan</s> eats ground [food] because he is toothless' — where no explicit injunction is heard either — because of the unprecedented [connection], an injunction is inferred, and the inquiry 'The grinding for <s>Pūṣan</s> would be [applicable] in the modified [rite]' and the like has been undertaken in the First <s>Tantra</s>.

children.text: 7 sarvānnānumatyadhikaraṇam / sū. 28-31
children.translated_text: 7 The <s>Sarvānnānumati</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 28-31.

children.text: sarvān nānumatiś ca prāṇātyaye taddarśanāt | BBs_3,4.28 |
children.translated_text: And the permission regarding all food [applies only] in danger to life — because of what is seen [in the <s>śruti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.28 |

children.text:
prāṇasaṃvāde śrūyate chandogānām - 'na ha vā evaṃvidi kiñcanānannaṃ bhavati' (chā. 5.2.1) iti /
tathā vājasaneyinām - 'na ha vā asyānnaṃ jagdhaṃ bhavati nānannaṃ pratigṛhītam' (bṛ. 6.1.14) iti /
sarvamevāsyādanīyameva bhavatītyarthaḥ /
kimidaṃ sarvānnānujñānaṃ śamādivadvidyāṅgaṃ vidhīyata uta stutyarthaṃ saṃkārtyata iti saṃśaye vidhiriti tāvatprātm /
tathāhi - pravṛttiviśeṣakara upadeśo bhavatyataḥ prāṇavidyāsaṃnidhānāttadaṅgatveneyaṃ niyamanivṛttirupadiśyate /
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Prāṇa-saṃvāda</s> (dialogue of the vital breaths), it is heard among the <s>Chāndogas</s>: 'For one who knows thus, nothing is non-food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.1).
Likewise among the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>: 'His food is not [merely] eaten; [nothing] is received as non-food' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.1.14).
The meaning is: everything becomes fit to be eaten by him.
The question is: Is this permission regarding all food being enjoined as an ancillary to <s>vidyā</s> — like tranquility and the like — or is it stated for the purpose of praise?
When the injunctive view is prima facie established —
for thus [it is argued]: The teaching produces a specific activity; therefore, because of its proximity to the <s>Prāṇa-vidyā</s>, this removal of restriction is taught as its ancillary.

children.text: nanvevaṃsati bhakṣyābhakṣyavibhāgaśāstravyāghātaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: But in that case, there would be a conflict with the scripture that distinguishes between fit and unfit food.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
smānyaviśeṣabhāvādbādhopapatteḥ /
yathā prāṇihiṃsāpratiṣedhasya paśusaṃjñāpanavidhinā bādhaḥ /
yathāca 'na kāñcana pariharettadvratam' (chā. 2.13.2) ityanena vāmadevyāvidyāviṣayeṇa sarvastrayaparihāravacanena tatsāmānyaviṣayaṃ gamyāgamyavibhāgaśāstraṃ bādhyate /
evamanenāpi prāṇavidyāviṣayeṇa sarvānnabhakṣaṇavacanena bhakṣyābhakṣyavibhāgaśāstraṃ bādhyateti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - nedaṃ sarvānnānujñānaṃ vidhīyata iti /
nahyatra vidhāyakaḥ śabda upalabhyate 'na ha vā evaṃvidi kiñcanānannaṃ bhavati' (chā. 5.2.1) iti vartamānāpadeśāt /
nacāsatyāmapi vidhipratītau pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvalobhenaiva vidhirabhyupagantuṃ śakyate /
apica śvādimaryādaṃ prāṇasyānnamityuktvedamucyate 'naivaṃvidaḥ kiñcidanannaṃ bhavati' iti /
naca śvādimaryāmannaṃ mānuṣeṇa dehenopabhoktuṃ śakyate /
śakyate tu prāṇasyānnamidaṃ sarvamiti vicintayitum /
tasmātprāṇānnavijñānapraśaṃsārtho 'yamarthavādo na sarvānnānujñānavidhiḥ /
taddarśayati 'sarvānnānumatiśca prāṇātyaye' iti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati- prāṇātyaya eva hi parasyāmāpadi sarvamannamadīyatvenābhyanujñāyate taddarśanāt /
tathāhi śrutiścākrāyaṇasyerṣeḥ kaṣṭāyāmavasthāyāmabhakṣyabhakṣaṇe pravṛttiṃ darśayati - 'maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣu' (chā. 1.10.1) ityasminbrāhmaṇe /
cākrāyaṇaḥ kilarṣirāpadgata ibhyena sāmikhādintānkulmāṣāṃścakhāda /
anupānaṃ tu tadīyamucchiṣṭadoṣātpratyācacakṣe /
kāraṇaṃ cātrovāca 'na vā ajīviṣyamimānakhādan' (chā. 1.10.4) iti, 'kāmo ma udapānam' (chā. 1.10.4) iti ca /
pinaścottaredyustāneva svaparocchiṣṭānparyuṣitānkulmāṣānbhakṣayāṃbabhūveti /
children.translated_text: And again, on the next day, he ate those very stale, left-over beans.

children.text: tadetaducchiṣṭaparyuṣitabhakṣaṇaṃ darśayantyāḥ śruterāśayātiśayo lakṣyate prāṇātyayaprasaṅge prāṇasaṃdhāraṇāyābhakṣyamapi bhakṣayitavyamiti /
children.translated_text: The intention of the <s>śruti</s> — in narrating this eating of left-over and stale food — is clearly directed [at teaching that]: in the situation of danger to life, one should eat even unfit food for the sake of sustaining life.

children.text: svasthāvasthāyāṃ tu tanna kartavyaṃ vidyāvatāpītyanupānapratyākhyānādgamyate /
children.translated_text: But in a normal state, even a knower should not do so — this is understood from [<s>Cākrāyaṇa</s>'s] refusal of the water.

children.text: tasmādarthavādo 'na ha vā evaṃvidi' (cā. 5.2.1) ityevamādiḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the passage] 'For one who knows thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.1) and the like is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>). // 28 //

This is not a defect.
Because the overriding [of the general rule by the specific] is tenable, due to the relation of general and particular.
Just as the prohibition against harming living beings is overridden by the injunction to immolate the sacrificial animal.
And just as, by the statement 'One should not reject anyone — that is the observance' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.13.2) — which pertains to the <s>Vāmadevya-vidyā</s> and prescribes the non-rejection of all food — the scripture distinguishing between what may and may not be approached, which pertains to the general [domain], is overridden.
So too, by this statement about eating all food — which pertains to the <s>Prāṇa-vidyā</s> — the scripture distinguishing fit from unfit food is overridden.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: This permission regarding all food is not an injunction.
For no injunctive word is found here — because [the text] 'For one who knows thus, nothing is non-food' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.1) is a present-tense description.
And even in the absence of the perception of an injunction, one cannot adopt it as an injunction merely out of eagerness [to find] that it produces specific activity.
Moreover, having stated that the food of <s>prāṇa</s> extends even to dogs and the like, [the text] then says: 'For one who knows thus, nothing is non-food.'
And food extending to dogs and the like cannot be consumed by a human body.
But it is possible to contemplate: 'All this is the food of <s>prāṇa</s>.'
Therefore, this is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) for the purpose of praising the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s>'s food — not an injunction permitting all food.
This is what [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] demonstrates: 'And the permission regarding all food [applies only] in danger to life.'
The meaning is: It is only in extreme distress — in danger to life (<s>prāṇātyaya</s>) — that all food is permitted as edible — because of what is seen [in the <s>śruti</s>].
For thus the <s>śruti</s> shows the sage <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s>'s resort to eating unfit food in a desperate situation — in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [beginning with] 'In the Kuru country afflicted by hail' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.10.1).
The sage <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s>, it is said, being in distress, ate the remnant beans of an elephant-keeper.
But he refused the accompanying water — because of the fault of being left-over [food of another].
