And he stated the reason: 'Had I not eaten these, I would not have survived' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.10.4); and 'Water was [available] to me as I desired' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.10.4).

children.text: abādhāc ca | BBs_3,4.29 |
children.translated_text: And because of non-overriding. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.29 |

children.text: evañca satyāhāraśuddhau sattvaśuddhirityevamādi bhakṣyābhakṣyavibhāgaśāstramabādhitaṃ bhaviṣyati // 29 //
children.translated_text: And being so, the scripture [on food-distinction] such as 'When food is pure, the mind becomes pure' — the scripture distinguishing fit from unfit food — will remain unoverridden. // 29 //

children.text: api ca smaryate | BBs_3,4.30 |
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>smṛti</s> states [this]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.30 |

children.text: apicāpadi sarvānnabhakṣaṇamapi smaryateviduṣo.viduṣaścāviśeṣeṇa - 'jīvitātyayamāpanno yo 'nnamatti yatastataḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>smṛti</s> also states that eating all food [applies only] in distress — for both the knower and the non-knower without distinction: 'One who, having reached mortal danger, eats food from whatever source —

children.text: lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā' iti /
children.translated_text: he is not tainted by sin, like a lotus-leaf by water.'

children.text: tathā 'madyaṃ nityaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ', 'surāpasya brāhmaṇasyoṣṇāmasiṃceyuḥ', 'surāpāḥ kṛmayo bhavantyabhakṣyabhakṣaṇāt' iti ca smaryatevarjanamannasya // 30 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>smṛti</s> also states the prohibition of [unfit] food: 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [should not drink] liquor ever'; 'They should pour hot [liquor] on a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who drinks liquor'; 'Liquor-drinkers become worms; from eating unfit food [they fall].' // 30 //

children.text: FN: uṣṇamatitaptām /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Uṣṇam</s>' means extremely hot.

children.text: śabdaś cāto 'kāmakāre | BBs_3,4.31 |
children.translated_text: And the word [of <s>śruti</s> too confirms this] — regarding the prohibition of acting according to one's desire. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.31 |

children.text: śabdaścānannasya pratiṣedhakaḥ kāmakāranivṛttiprayojanaḥ kāṭhakānāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ śrūyate - 'tasmādbrahmaṇaḥ surāṃ na pibet' iti /
children.translated_text: And a word [of <s>śruti</s>] that prohibits [unfit] food — whose purpose is to prevent acting according to whim — is heard in the <s>Saṃhitā</s> of the <s>Kāṭhakas</s>: 'Therefore, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not drink liquor.'

children.text: so 'pi 'na ha vā evaṃvidi' (chā. 5.2.1) ityasyārthavādatvādupapannataro bhavati /
children.translated_text: And this [prohibition] becomes all the more tenable precisely because 'For one who knows thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.1) is a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>).

children.text: tasmādevañjātīyakā arthavādā na vidhaya iti // 31 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, statements of this kind are laudatory passages, not injunctions. // 31 //

children.text: 8 āśramakarmādhikaraṇam / sū. 32-36
children.translated_text: 8 The <s>Āśramakarma</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 32-36.

children.text: vihitatvāc cāśramakarmāpi | BBs_3,4.32 |
children.translated_text: And because of being enjoined — [one should perform] <s>āśrama</s> duties also. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.32 |

children.text:
'sarvāpekṣā ca -' (bra. sū. 3.4.23) ityatrāśramakarmaṇāṃ vidyāsādhanatvamavadhāritam /
idānīṃ tu kimamumukṣorapyaśramamātraniṣṭhasya vidyāmakāmamayamānasya tānyanuṣṭheyānyutāho neti cintyate /
tatra 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityādināśramakarmaṇāṃ vidyāsādhanatvena vihitatvādvidyāmanicchataḥ phalāntaraṃ kāmayamānasya nityanyananuṣṭheyāni /
children.translated_text: Since <s>āśrama</s> duties have been enjoined as means to <s>vidyā</s> by passages such as 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know That through the recitation of the Vedas' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) and the like, they must certainly be performed by one who does not desire <s>vidyā</s> and desires other fruits — [this is the prima facie view].

children.text: atha tasyāpyanuṣṭheyāni na tarhyeṣāṃ vidyāsādhanatvaṃ nityānityasaṃyogavirodhāditi /
children.translated_text: But if they must be performed by him too, then their status as means to <s>vidyā</s> would be negated — because of the contradiction of combining the eternal (<s>nitya</s>) and the non-eternal (<s>anitya</s>) [purposes].

children.text: asyāṃ prāptau paṭhati - 'āśramamātraniṣṭhasyāpyamumukṣoḥ kartavyanyeva nityāni karmāṇi yāvajjīvamagnihotraṃ juhoti' ityādinā vihitatvāt /
children.translated_text: In response to this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads: Even for one who merely abides in an <s>āśrama</s> and does not seek liberation, the permanent (<s>nitya</s>) duties must certainly be performed — because they have been enjoined [by śrutis such as:] 'One should perform the <s>Agnihotra</s> throughout life' and the like.

children.text: nahi vacanasyātibhāro nāma kaścidasti // 32 //
children.translated_text: For there is no limit to the force of a [Vedic] statement. // 32 //

In [the discussion of] 'And there is dependence on all' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.26), the status of <s>āśrama</s> duties as means to <s>vidyā</s> has been established.
Now the question is: Should those [<s>āśrama</s> duties] be performed also by one who does not seek liberation — one who merely abides in an <s>āśrama</s> and who does not desire <s>vidyā</s> — or not?

children.text: atha yaduktaṃ naivaṃ sati vidyāsādhanatveṣāṃ syādityata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: Now, to the objection that was stated — that in that case, these [duties] would not have the status of means to <s>vidyā</s> — to that, the next <s>sūtra</s> is read:

children.text: sahakāritvena ca | BBs_3,4.33 |
children.translated_text: And [they serve <s>vidyā</s>] in a cooperative capacity (<s>sahakāritva</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.33 |

children.text:
vidyāsahakārīṇi caitāni syurvihitatvādeva 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityādinā /
taduktam - 'sarvāpekṣā ca yajñādiśruteraśvavat' (bra. sū. 3.4.26) iti /
nacedaṃ vidyāsahakāritvāvacanamāśramakarmaṇāṃ prayājādivadvidyāphalaviṣayaṃ mantavyam /
avidhilakṣaṇatvādvidyāyāḥ /
asādhyatvācca vidyāphalasya /
vidhilakṣaṇaṃ hi sādhanaṃ darśapūrṇamāsādi svargaphalasiṣādhayiṣayā sahakārisādhanāntaramapekṣate naivaṃ vidyā /
tathācoktam 'ata eva cāgnīndhanādyanapekṣā' (bra. sū. 3.4.25) iti /
tasmāduttpattisādhanatva evaiṣāṃ sahakāritvavācoyuktiḥ /
nacātra nityānityasaṃyogavirodha āśaṅkayaḥ, karmābhede 'pi saṃyogabhedāt /
nitye hyekaḥ saṃyogo yāvajjīvādivākyakalpito na tasya vidyāphalatvam /
anityastvaparaḥ saṃyogaḥ 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena' (bṛ. 4.4.22)
children.translated_text: And these [ritual duties] would be auxiliaries to knowledge, because they are enjoined — as stated in 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know It through Vedic recitation' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) and the like. This has been stated: 'And the expectation of all [means], because of the <s>śruti</s> of sacrifice and the like — as with a horse' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.26). And this statement of the auxiliary role of the <s>āśrama</s>-duties to knowledge should not be understood as applying to the fruit of knowledge — like the <s>prayājas</s> (preliminary offerings) [which are accessories to ritual fruit]. Because knowledge is not of the nature of an injunction [producing an unseen result]. And because the fruit of knowledge cannot be produced [through action]. For a means of the nature of an injunction — such as the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like — requires other auxiliary means in order to accomplish the fruit of heaven; but knowledge is not like that. And thus it has been stated: 'For this very reason, there is no dependence on fire-kindling and the like' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.25). Therefore, the propriety of calling these [duties] auxiliaries lies only in their being means for the origination [of knowledge]. And here, the objection of a contradiction between the combination of permanent and non-permanent [duties] should not be apprehended — because even though the action is the same, the combinations are different. For there is one combination [of ritual duties] — permanent — that is established by statements like 'as long as one lives' and the like; the fruit of knowledge does not belong to that [combination]. But there is another combination — non-permanent — that is established by statements like 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know It through Vedic recitation' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22)

children.text: ityādivākyakalpitastasya vidyāphalatvam /
children.translated_text: and the like; the fruit of knowledge belongs to that [combination].

children.text: yathaikasyāpi khādiratvasya nityena saṃyogena kratvarthatvamanityena saṃyogena puruṣārthatvaṃ tadvat // 33 //
children.translated_text: Just as the same <s>khadira</s>-wood [used for the sacrificial post] has ritual purpose (<s>kratvarthatva</s>) through its permanent combination and human purpose (<s>puruṣārthatva</s>) through its non-permanent combination — so too here. // 33 //

children.text: sarvathāpi ta evobhayaliṅgāt | BBs_3,4.34 |
children.translated_text: In any case, those very [duties should be performed], because of both kinds of indicators. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.34 |

children.text:
sarvathāpyāśramakarmapakṣe vidyāsahakāritvapakṣe ca ta evāgnihotrādayo dharmā anuṣṭoyāḥ /
ta evetyavadhārayannācryaḥ kiṃ nivartayati /
karmabhedaśah kāmiti brūmaḥ /
yathā kuṇḍapāyināmayane 'māsamagnihotraṃ jihoti' ityatra nityādagnihotrātkarmāntaramupadiśyate naivamiha karmabhedo 'stītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: In any case — whether in the view that <s>āśrama</s>-duties [are to be performed independently], or in the view that they are auxiliaries to knowledge — those very same duties such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like are to be performed. By the emphatic 'those very same' (<s>ta eva</s>), what does the teacher negate? We say: The difference of action. Just as in the case of the <s>Kuṇḍapāyins</s>' seasonal rite — '[He] offers the monthly <s>Agnihotra</s>' — a different action from the regular <s>Agnihotra</s> is taught; but here no such difference of action exists — this is the meaning.

children.text:
kutaḥ -ubhayaliṅgāt /
śrutiliṅgātsmṛtiliṅgācca /
śrutiliṅgaṃ tāvat 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti siddhavadutpannarūpāṇyeva yajñādīni vividiṣāyāṃ viniyuṅ kte natu juhvatītyādivadapūrvameṣāṃ rūpamutpādayatīti /
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s>-indicator is as follows: 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know It through Vedic recitation' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) — [this passage] employs sacrifices and the like in their already established, arisen form for the purpose of the desire to know; it does not produce a new form for them, as 'he offers' and the like [would do].

children.text: smṛtiliṅgamapi 'anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ' (6.1) iti vijñātakartavyatākameva karma vidyotpattyarthaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s>-indicator too: 'He who performs the duty that must be done without attachment to the fruit of action' (<s>Gītā</s> 6.1) — shows that the very same action whose obligatory nature is already known [serves] the purpose of the origination of knowledge.

children.text: yasyaite 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskārā ityādyā ca saṃskāratvaprasiddhirvaidikeṣu karmasu tatsaṃskṛtasya vidyotpattimabhipretya smṛtau bhavati /
children.translated_text: And the well-known statement of purificatory status for Vedic actions — 'These forty-eight <s>saṃskāras</s>' and the like — the <s>smṛti</s> teaching about one thus purified having the origination of knowledge [as the goal] has this [already established action] in view.

children.text: tasmātsādvidamabhedāvadhāraṇam // 34 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this determination that [the actions are] non-different [from the already known ones] is well-established. // 34 //
Why? Because of both kinds of indicators — that is, because of the indicator from <s>śruti</s> and the indicator from <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: anabhibhavaṃ ca darśayati | BBs_3,4.35 |
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows non-overwhelment. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.35 |

children.text: sahakāritvasyaivaitadupodbalakaṃ liṅgadarsanamanabhibhavaṃ ta darśayati śrutirbrahmacaryādisādhanasaṃpannasya rāgadibhiḥ kleśaiḥ 'eṣa hyātmā na naśyati yaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindate' (chā. 8.5.3) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: This observation of an indicator is a corroboration of the auxiliary role [of ritual duties to knowledge]. And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows the non-overwhelment by afflictions such as passion and the like, of one endowed with means such as <s>brahmacarya</s> and the like: 'This Self is not destroyed — the one attained through <s>brahmacarya</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.5.3) and such passages.

children.text: tasmādyajñādīnyāśramakarmāṇi ca bhavanti vidyāsahakārīṇi ceti niścitam // 35 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that sacrifices and the like, as well as <s>āśrama</s>-duties, both exist [as valid] and are auxiliaries to knowledge. // 35 //

children.text: 9 vidhurādikaraṇam / sū. 36 -39
children.translated_text: 9. <s>Vidhurādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 36-39

children.text: antarā cāpi tu taddṛṣṭeḥ | BBs_3,4.36 |
children.translated_text: But those who are in between [<s>āśramas</s>] also [have eligibility for knowledge] — because of the observation of that. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.36 |

children.text: vidhurādīnāṃ dravyādisaṃpadrahitānāṃ cānyatamāśramapratipattihīnānāmantarālavartināṃ kiṃ vidyāyāmadhikāro 'sti kiṃvā nāstīti saṃśaye nāstīti tāvatprāptam /
āśramakarmaṇāṃ vidyāhetutvāvadhāraṇādāśramakarmāsaṃbhavāccaiteṣāmiti /
children.translated_text: Because it has been determined that <s>āśrama</s>-duties are the cause of knowledge, and because of the impossibility of <s>āśrama</s>-duties for these [persons].

children.text: evaṃ prāpta idamāha - antarā cāpi tvanāśramitvena vartamāno 'pi vidyāyāmadhikriyate /
children.translated_text: Given this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: But even one who exists without belonging to an <s>āśrama</s> is eligible for knowledge.

children.text: kutaḥ taddṛṣṭeḥ /
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the observation of that.

children.text: raikvavācaknavīprabhṛtīnāmevaṃbhūtānāmapi brahmatvaśrutyupalabdheḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: Because the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge is observed [in scripture] even for those of this kind — such as <s>Raikva</s>, <s>Vācaknavi</s>, and others. // 36 //

For those such as the <s>vidhura</s> (widower) and the like — who lack the requisites of material and the like, and who have not attained any of the <s>āśramas</s>, being situated in the interval [between them] — there arises the doubt: do they have eligibility for knowledge, or not? The prima facie view is: they do not.

children.text: api ca smaryate | BBs_3,4.37 |
children.translated_text: Moreover, [this] is remembered [in <s>Smṛti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.37 |

children.text: saṃvartaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca nagnacaryādiyogādanapekṣitāśramakarmāṇāmapi mahāyogitvaṃ smaryata itihāse // 37 //
children.translated_text: And the great yogic attainment of <s>Saṃvarta</s> and others — who, because of practices like going naked and the like, did not observe <s>āśrama</s>-duties — is remembered in the <s>Itihāsa</s>. // 37 //

children.text: nanu liṅgamidaṃ śrutismṛtidarśanamipanyastaṃ kā nu khalu prāptiriti sābhidhīyate -
children.translated_text: Now, this indicator from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> has been adduced — what then is the established conclusion? That is stated:

children.text: viśeṣānugrahaś ca | BBs_3,4.38 |
children.translated_text: And there is the grace of special [duties]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.38 |

children.text:
teṣāmapi ca vidhurādīnāmaviruddhaiḥ puruṣamātrasaṃbandhibhirjapopavāsadevatārādhanādibhirdharmaviśeṣairanugraho vidyāyāḥ saṃbhavati /
tathāca smṛtiḥ - 'japyenaiva tu saṃsiddhyedbrāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ /
kuryādantra vā kuryānmantro brāhmaṇa ucyate' ityasaṃbhavadāśramakarmāṇo 'pi japye 'dhikāraṃ darśayati /
janmāntarānuṣṭhitairapi cāśramakarmabhiḥ saṃbhavatyeva vidyāyā anugrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the grace [of support] for knowledge is indeed possible through <s>āśrama</s>-duties performed in previous births.

children.text: tathāca smṛtiḥ - 'anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim' (6.45) iti janmāntarasaṃcitānāmapi saṃskāraviśeṣānanugrahītṛnvidyāyāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Having attained perfection through many births, one then reaches the supreme goal' (<s>Gītā</s> 6.45) — shows that the special <s>saṃskāras</s> accumulated over previous births too serve as auxiliaries for knowledge.

children.text: dṛṣṭārthā ca vidyā pratiṣedhābhāvamātreṇāpyartinamadhikaroti śravaṇādiṣu /
children.translated_text: And since knowledge has a directly perceptible result, merely by the absence of prohibition, it entitles the afflicted person to hearing [of <s>Vedānta</s>] and the like.

children.text: tasmādvidhurādīnāmapyadhikāro na virudhyate // 38 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the eligibility of <s>vidhuras</s> and the like is not contradicted. // 38 //

For those <s>vidhuras</s> and the like too, the grace [i.e., auxiliary support] for knowledge is possible through specific <s>dharmas</s> that are non-contradictory and relate to any person — such as <s>japa</s> (recitation), fasting, worship of deities, and the like. And thus the <s>smṛti</s> says: 'Through <s>japa</s> alone the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> may attain perfection — there is no doubt about this; whether he performs [other duties] or not, the <s>mantra</s>-knower is called a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — [this passage] shows eligibility for <s>japa</s> even for one who cannot perform <s>āśrama</s>-duties.

children.text: atas tv itarajjyāyo liṅgāc ca | BBs_3,4.39 |
children.translated_text: But for this [very] reason, the other [i.e., belonging to an <s>āśrama</s>] is superior — because of the indicators. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.39 |

children.text: atastvantarālavartitvāditaradāśramavartitvaṃ jyāyo vidyāsādhanam /
śrutismṛtisaṃdṛṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because it is seen in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: śrutiliṅgācca 'tenaiti brahmavitpūṇyakṛttejasaśca' (bṛ. 4.4.1) iti /
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>śruti</s>-indicator: 'By that [path] goes the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the doer of good, and the radiant one' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.1).

children.text: 'anāśramī na tiṣṭheta dinamekamapi dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A twice-born should not remain without an <s>āśrama</s> even for a single day;

children.text: saṃvatsaramanāśramī sthitvā kṛcchramekaṃ caret' iti ca smṛtiliṅgāt // 39 //
children.translated_text: having remained without an <s>āśrama</s> for a year, he should perform one <s>kṛcchra</s> [penance]' — and because of such <s>smṛti</s>-indicators. // 39 //
But for this reason — compared to being situated in the interval [between <s>āśramas</s>] — the other, namely being situated in an <s>āśrama</s>, is a superior means for knowledge.

children.text: 10 tadbhūtādhikaraṇam / sū. 40
children.translated_text: 10. <s>Tadbhūtādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 40

children.text: tadbhūtasya tu nātadbhāvo jaiminer api niyamāt tadrūpābhāvebhyaḥ | BBs_3,4.40 |
children.translated_text: For one who has become that [i.e., entered an <s>ūrdhvareta</s> order], there is no reverting to the state of not being that — [this is the view] of <s>Jaimini</s> too, because of the restriction [and] because of [the absence of] the characteristics of that [reversal]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.40 |

children.text:
santyūrdhvaretasā āśramā iti sthāpitam /
tāṃstu prāptasya kathañcittataḥ pracyutirasti nāsti veti saṃśayaḥ /
pūrvakarmasvanuṣṭhānacikīrṣayā vā rāgādivaśena vā pracyuto 'pi syādviśeṣābhāvāditi /
evaṃ prāpta ucyate - tadbhūtasya tu pratipannordhvaretobhāvasya na kathañcidapyatadbhāvo na tataḥ pracyutiḥ syāt /
kutaḥ - niyamātadrūpābhāvebhyaḥ /
tathāhi - 'atyantamātmānamācāryakule 'vasādayan' (chā. 2.23.1) iti 'araṇyamiyāditi padaṃ tato na punareyādityupaniṣat' iti 'ācāryeṇābhyanujñātaścaturṇāmekamāśramam /
ā vimokṣāccharīrasya so 'nutiṣṭhedyathāvidi' iti caivañjātīyake niyamaḥ pracyutyaprabhāvaṃ darśayati /
yathāca 'brahmacaryaṃ samāpya gṛhī bhavet' (jā. 4) 'brahmacaryādeva pravrajet' (jā. 4) iti caivamādīnyāroharūpāṇi vacāṃsyupalabhyante naivaṃ pratyavaroharūpāṇi /
nacaivamācārāḥ śiṣṭhā vidyante /
yattu pūrvakarmasvanuṣṭhānacikīrṣayā pratyavarohaṇamiti tadasat 'śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt' (3.35) iti smaraṇāt /
nyāyācca /
yo hi yaṃ prati vidhīyate sa tasya dharmo natu yo yena svanuṣṭhātuṃ śakyate /
codanālakṣaṇatvāddharmasya /
children.translated_text: Because <s>dharma</s> is defined by [Vedic] injunction.

children.text: naca rāgādivaśātpracyutiḥ /
children.translated_text: And there is no falling away through the influence of passion and the like.

children.text: niyamaśāstrasya balīyastvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the restrictive scripture is stronger [than passion].

children.text: jaiminerapītyapiśabdena jaiminibādarāyaṇayoratra saṃpratipattiṃ śāsti pratipattidārḍhyāya // 40 //
children.translated_text: By the word 'too' (<s>api</s>) in 'of <s>Jaimini</s> too,' [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] indicates the agreement of both <s>Jaimini</s> and <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> on this point — for the firmness of the determination. // 40 //

It has been established that there are <s>āśramas</s> for the celibate (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>). But for one who has entered them, there arises a doubt: is there in any way a falling away from that [state], or not? The prima facie view is: even one who has fallen — whether through the desire to perform previously [obligatory] rites, or through the influence of passion and the like — may [revert], because there is no distinguishing ground [against it]. Given this prima facie view, we say: For one who has become that — who has entered the state of celibacy (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>) — there is in no way whatsoever a reverting to the state of not being that, no falling from it. Why? Because of the restriction [and] the absence of the characteristics of that [reversal]. For thus: 'Devoting himself entirely to [the study of the <s>Vedas</s>] throughout his life in the teacher's family' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1); and 'One should go to the forest — that is the step from which one should not return, according to the secret teaching (<s>upaniṣad</s>)'; and 'Having been permitted by the teacher, one should enter one of the four <s>āśramas</s>; until the release of the body, one should observe [it] properly' — such restrictive passages show the impossibility of falling away. And while statements of ascending form are found — such as 'Having completed <s>brahmacarya</s>, one should become a householder' (<s>Jābāla</s> 4); 'From <s>brahmacarya</s> itself one may renounce' (<s>Jābāla</s> 4) — statements of descending form are not found. Nor do the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) follow such a practice [of reversal]. As for [the suggestion of] reverting in order to perform previously [obligatory] rites — that is wrong, because of the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Better is one's own <s>dharma</s>, though deficient, than another's <s>dharma</s> well-performed' (<s>Gītā</s> 3.35). And because of reasoning. For the <s>dharma</s> that is enjoined for a person is that person's <s>dharma</s> — not that which one is merely able to perform well.

children.text: 11 adhikārādhikaraṇam / sū. 41 - 42
children.translated_text: 11. <s>Adhikārādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 41-42

children.text: na cādhikārikam api patanānumānāt tadayogāt | BBs_3,4.41 |
children.translated_text: And even the [<s>prāyaścitta</s>] taught in the context of eligibility [is not applicable] — because of the inference of falling, [and] because of the unfitness of that [penance]. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.41 |

children.text: yadi naiṣṭhiko brahmacārī pramādādavakīryeta kiṃ tasya 'brahmacaryāvakīrṇī nairṛtaṃ gardabhamālabhet' ityetatprāyaścittaṃ syāduta neti /
children.translated_text: If the lifelong (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>) <s>brahmacārin</s> should involuntarily lose his celibacy, the question arises: Does the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) 'He who has broken his vow of <s>brahmacarya</s> should sacrifice a donkey to <s>Nirṛti</s>' apply to him, or not?

children.text:
netyucyate /
yadapyadhikāralakṣaṇe nirṇītaṃ prāyaścittam 'avakīrṇipaśuśca tadvadādhānasyāprāptakālatvāt' (jai. sū /
6.8.21) iti tadapina naiṣṭhikasya bhavitumarhati /
children.translated_text: (<s>Jaiminisūtra</s> 6.8.21) — even that is not applicable to the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> [<s>brahmacārin</s>].

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇam - 'ārūḍho naiṣṭhikaṃ dharmaṃ yastu pracyavate pinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For what reason? 'He who, having ascended to the <s>naiṣṭhika dharma</s>, falls back again —

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ na paśyāmi yena śuddhyetsa ātmahā' ityapratisamādheyapatanasmaraṇācchinnaśirasa iva pratikriyānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: I see no expiation by which he may be purified; he is a self-slayer' — because of the <s>smṛti</s> that his falling is irremediable, just as for one whose head has been severed, no remedy is possible.

children.text: upakurvāṇasya tu tādṛkpatanasmaraṇābhāvādupapadyate tatprāyaścittam // 41 //
children.translated_text: But for the <s>upakurvāṇa</s> [<s>brahmacārin</s>, i.e., one who studies temporarily], that <s>prāyaścitta</s> is applicable — because there is no <s>smṛti</s> declaring such a [catastrophic] fall for him. // 41 //

It does not, we say. For even the <s>prāyaścitta</s> that has been determined in the context of eligibility — 'The animal [sacrifice] for the one who has broken his vow is likewise [to be performed], because the time for establishing the [sacred] fires has not yet arrived'

children.text: upapūrvam api tv eke bhāvamaśanavat tad uktam | BBs_3,4.42 |
children.translated_text: But some [teachers hold] it is a minor sin (<s>upapātaka</s>), and that it [i.e., expiation] exists — as in the case of [prohibited] eating. This has been stated. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.42 |

children.text:
apitveka ācāryā upapātakamevaitaditi manyate /
yannaiṣṭhikasya gurudārādibhyo 'nyatra brahmacaryaṃ viśīryeta na tanmahāpātakaṃ bhavati gurutalpādiṣu mahāpātakeṣvaparigaṇanāt /
tasmādupakurvāṇavannaiṣṭhikasyāpi prāyaścittasya bhāvamicchanti brahmacāritvāviśeṣādavakīrṇitatvāviśeṣācca /
aśanavat /
yathā brahmacāriṇo madhumāṃsāśane vratalopaḥ punaḥsaṃskāraścaivamiti /
ye hi prāyaścittasyābhāvamicchanti teṣāṃ na mūlamupalabhyate /
ye tu bhāvamicchanti teṣāṃ brahmacāryavakīrṇetyadaviśeṣaśravaṇaṃ mūlam /
tasmādbhāvo yuktataraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the existence [of expiation] is more reasonable.

children.text: taduktaṃ pramāṇalakṣaṇe - 'samā vipratipattiḥ syāt' (jai. sū. 1.3.8) 'śāstrasthā vā tannimittatvāt' (jai. sū. 1.3.9) iti /
children.translated_text: This has been stated in the [section on] the definition of valid means of knowledge: 'When there is equal disagreement' (<s>Jaiminisūtra</s> 1.3.8); 'Or [it is resolved by] what is based on scripture, because it is the cause of that' (<s>Jaiminisūtra</s> 1.3.9).

children.text: prāścittābhāvasmaraṇaṃ tvevaṃ sati yatnagauravotpādanārthamiti vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: But the <s>smṛti</s> that denies expiation — given this [interpretation], it is explained as being for the purpose of generating the gravity of effort [to maintain the vow].

children.text: evaṃ bhikṣuvaikhānasayorapi vānaprastho dīkṣābhede kṛcchraṃ dvādaśarātraṃ caritvā mahākakṣaṃ vardhayet bhikṣurvānaprasthavatsomavalliṅgavarjaṃ svaśāstrasaṃskāraśca ityavamādi prāyaścittasmaraṇamanuvartavyam // 42 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, for the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) and the <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest-hermit), the following <s>smṛti</s> about expiation should be followed: 'The forest-hermit, upon [improper] change of consecration, should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> of twelve nights and then increase the great fire; the mendicant [should do] as the forest-hermit, except for the <s>soma</s>-vow marks, and should perform his own consecration according to his order's rules' — and such passages. // 42 //

But some teachers hold that this is only a minor sin (<s>upapātaka</s>). For when the <s>naiṣṭhika</s>'s <s>brahmacarya</s> is violated with someone other than the teacher's wife and the like — it is not a major sin (<s>mahāpātaka</s>), because it is not enumerated among the major sins such as violating the teacher's bed. Therefore, they hold that expiation exists for the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> too, just as for the <s>upakurvāṇa</s> — because there is no distinction in their being <s>brahmacārins</s>, and no distinction in their being transgressors. As in the case of [prohibited] eating. Just as for a <s>brahmacārin</s> who eats honey or meat, there is a breach of vow and a re-consecration — so too here. For those who hold that expiation does not exist — no scriptural basis is found for their view. But for those who hold that it does exist — the undifferentiated <s>śruti</s> 'the <s>brahmacārin</s> who has broken his vow' is the basis.

children.text: 12 bahiradhikaramam / sū. 43
children.translated_text: 12. <s>Bahiradhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 43

children.text: bahis tūbhayathāpi smṛter ācārāc ca | BBs_3,4.43 |
children.translated_text: But, in either case, [they should be treated as] outside [the community] — because of <s>smṛti</s> and because of practice. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.43 |

children.text:
yadūrdhvaretasāṃ svaśramebhyaḥ pracyavanaṃ mahāpātakaṃ yadi vopapātakamubhayathāpi śiṣṭhaiste bahirkartavyāḥ /
'ārūḍho naiṣṭhikaṃ dharmaṃ yastu pracyavate punaḥ /
prāyaścittaṃ na paśyāmi yena śudhyetsa ātmahā' iti 'ārūḍhapatitaṃ vipraṃ maṇḍalācca viniḥsṛtam /
children.translated_text: I see no expiation by which he may be purified; he is a self-slayer'; and 'Having touched a twice-born who has fallen from his established [vow], who has departed from the circle [of propriety],

children.text: udbaddhaṃ kṛmidaṣṭaṃ ca spṛṣṭvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret' iti caivamādinindātiśayasmṛtibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: or who has hanged himself or been bitten by worms — one should perform a <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> [penance]' — because of such <s>smṛti</s> passages expressing the extreme of censure.

children.text: śiṣṭācārācca /
children.translated_text: And because of the practice of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>).

children.text: nahi yajñādhyayanavivāhādīni taiḥ sahācaranti śiṣṭāḥ // 43 //
children.translated_text: For the learned do not associate with them in sacrifices, Vedic study, marriages, and the like. // 43 //

Whether the falling of the celibates (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>) from their <s>āśramas</s> is a major sin or a minor sin — in either case, they should be excluded by the learned. 'He who, having ascended to the <s>naiṣṭhika dharma</s>, falls back again —

children.text: 13 svāmyadhikaraṇam / sū. 44 -46
children.translated_text: 13. <s>Svāmyadhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 44-46

children.text: svāminaḥ phalaśruter ity ātreyaḥ | BBs_3,4.44 |
children.translated_text: The owner (<s>svāmin</s>, i.e., the sacrificer) [is the agent of the meditations on ritual accessories] — because of the <s>śruti</s> of fruit: thus [holds] <s>Ātreya</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3.4.44 |

children.text:
aṅgeṣūpāsaneṣu saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāni yajamānakarmāṇyāhosvidṛtvikkarmāṇīti /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam yajamānakarmāṇīti /
kutaḥ - phalaśruteḥ /
phalaṃ hi śrūyate - 'varṣati hāsmai varṣayati ha ya etadevaṃ vidvānvṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste' (chā. 2.3.2) ityādi /
tacca svāmigāmi nyāyyam /
tasya sāṅge prayoge 'dhikṛtatvāt /
adhikṛtādhikāratvāccaivañjātīyakasya /
phalaṃ ca kartaryupāsanānāṃ śrūyate - 'varṣatyasmai ya upāste' ityādi /
nanvṛtvijo 'pi phalaṃ dṛṣṭam 'ātmane vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tamāgāyati' (bṛ. 1.3.28) iti /
children.translated_text: Regarding the meditations on [ritual] accessories, a doubt arises: Are they the duties of the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>), or of the officiating priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>)? What is the prima facie view? They are the duties of the sacrificer. Why? Because of the <s>śruti</s> of fruit. For the fruit is heard: 'It rains for him, and he causes it to rain — for one who, knowing this thus, meditates on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in the rain' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.3.2) and the like. And that [fruit] properly belongs to the owner [i.e., sacrificer] — because he is the one eligible for the complete performance with all accessories. And because eligibility for such [meditations] belongs to the one who is [already] eligible [for the sacrifice itself]. And the fruit is heard as belonging to the agent of the meditations: 'It rains for the one who meditates' and the like. Objection: But a fruit for the priests too is observed: 'He sings for himself whatever desire he desires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.3.28).

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: tasya vācanikatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because that [fruit for the priest] is by [special] stipulation [and not the general rule].

children.text: tasmātsvāmina eva phalavatsūpāsaneṣu kartṛtvamityātreya ācāryo manyate // 44 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the teacher <s>Ātreya</s> holds that the agency in the meditations that bear fruit belongs to the owner [i.e., the sacrificer] alone. // 44 //

children.text: ārtvijyam ity auḍulomiḥ tasmai hi parikrīyate | BBs_3,4.45 |
children.translated_text: [It is] the duty of the <s>ṛtvij</s> (officiating priest) — so [holds] <s>Auḍulomi</s>, because one is hired for that. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.45 |

children.text:
naitadasti svāmikarmāṇyupāsanānīti /
ṛtvikkarmāṇyetāni syurityauḍulomirācāryo manyate /
kiṃ kāraṇaṃ, tasmai hi sāṅgāya karmaṇe yajamānenartvikparikrīyate /
tatprayogāntaḥpātīni codgīthādyupāsanānyadhikṛtādhikārakatvāt /
tasmādgodohanādiniyamavadevartvigbhirnirvartyetan /
tathāca 'taṃ ha bako dālbhyo vidāñcakāra sa ha naimiśīyānāmudgātā babhūva (chā. 1.2.13) ityudgātṛkatṛrkatāṃ vijñānasya darśayati /
yattūktaṃ kartrāśrayaṃ phalaṃ śrūyata iti /
children.translated_text:
This [view] — that the meditations are the duties of the sacrificer — is not correct.
The teacher <s>Auḍulomi</s> holds that these are the duties of the <s>ṛtvijs</s>.
What is the reason? Because the <s>ṛtvij</s> is hired by the sacrificer for that complete ritual with its accessories.
The meditations on the <s>Udgītha</s> and the like, being within the scope of that [ritual] performance, belong to those [<s>ṛtvijs</s>] who are qualified for those [ritual] duties.
Therefore, like the restriction regarding cow-milking (<s>godohana</s>) and the like, these are to be performed by the <s>ṛtvijs</s> alone.
And thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that the <s>Udgātṛ</s> is the agent of the cognition: 'Him, <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> knew; he became the <s>Udgātṛ</s> of the <s>Naimiśīyas</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.2.13).
As for the objection that the fruit is heard as belonging to the agent [i.e., the sacrificer] —

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: parārthatvādṛtvijo 'nyatra vacanātphalasaṃbandhānupapatteḥ // 45 //
children.translated_text: Because the <s>ṛtvij</s> serves another's purpose, the fruit-connection [with someone other than the <s>ṛtvij</s>] is untenable except where stated [by scripture]. // 45 //

children.text: śruteśca | BBs_3,4.46 |
children.translated_text: And because of the <s>śruti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.46 |

children.text:
yāṃ vai kāñcana yajña ṛtvija āśiṣamāśāsata iti yajamānāyaiva tāmāśāsata iti hovāceti tasmādu haivaṃvidudgātā brūyātkaṃ te kāmamāgāyāni (chā. 1.7.8 - 9) iti /
taccarvitvakkartṛkasya vijñānasya yajamānagāmi phalaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text:
'Whatever blessing the <s>ṛtvijs</s> invoke in a sacrifice — they invoke it for the sacrificer alone' — so he said; 'Therefore, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows thus should say: "What desire shall I sing for you?"' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.8-9).
This shows that the fruit of the cognition, which is performed by the <s>ṛtvij</s>, goes to the sacrificer.

children.text: tasmādaṅgopāsanānāmṛtvikkarmatvasiddhiḥ // 46 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the conclusion is that the meditations on the accessories [of ritual] are the duties of the <s>ṛtvijs</s>. // 46 //

children.text: 14 sahakāryantaravidhyadhikaraṇam / sū. 47 - 49
children.translated_text: 14. The <s>Sahakāryantaravidhyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Injunction of Another Auxiliary). <s>Sūtras</s> 47-49.

children.text: sahakāryantaravidhiḥ pakṣeṇa tṛtīyaṃ tadvato vidhyādivat | BBs_3,4.47 |
children.translated_text: The injunction of another auxiliary [is established] optionally as the third — for one who possesses that [knowledge], like the injunction and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.47 |

children.text:
'tasmādbrahmaṇaḥ pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidya bālyena tiṣṭhāsedbālyaṃ ca pāṇḍityaṃ ca nirvidyātha muniramaunaṃ ca monaṃ ca nirvidyātha brāhmaṇaḥ' (bṛ. 3.5.1) iti bṛhadāraṇyake śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ maunaṃ vidīyate na veti /
na vidīyata iti tāvatprāptam /
bālyena tiṣṭhāsedityatraiva vidheravasitatvāt /
nahyatha munirityatra vidāyakā vibhaktirupalabhyate tasmādayamanuvādo yuktaḥ /
kutaḥ prāptiriti cet /
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> it is heard: 'Therefore, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having become weary of learning (<s>pāṇḍitya</s>), should abide in childlikeness (<s>bālya</s>); having become weary of both childlikeness and learning — then he becomes a sage (<s>muni</s>); having become weary of both non-silence and silence — then he is a true <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.1).
There arises a doubt: Is silence (<s>mauna</s>) being enjoined or not?
The prima facie view is: It is not being enjoined.
Because the injunction is completed with 'He should abide in childlikeness.'
For in 'then he becomes a sage (<s>muni</s>),' no injunctive verbal ending is found — therefore this is merely a restatement.
If it be asked: From where does [<s>mauna</s>] arrive [as an already established practice]?

children.text:
munipaṇḍitaśabdayorjñānārthatvātpāṇḍityaṃ nirvidyetyevaṃ prāptaṃ maunam /
apicāmaunaṃ ca maunaṃ ca nirvidyātha brāhmaṇa ityatra tāvanna brāhmaṇatvaṃ vidhīyate prāgeva prāptatvāt /
tasmādatha brāhmaṇa iti praśaṃsāvadastathaivātha munirityapi bhavitumarhati samānanirdeṣatvāditi /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - sahakāryantaravidhiriti /
vidyāsahakāriṇo maunasya bālyapāṇḍityavadvidhirevāśrayitavyo 'pūrvavat /
children.translated_text:
Because the words '<s>muni</s>' and '<s>paṇḍita</s>' both mean 'knowledge,' having become weary of learning — silence is thereby already obtained.
Moreover, in 'having become weary of both non-silence and silence — then he is a true <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — here, the status of being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is not being enjoined, as it is already obtained beforehand.
Therefore, just as 'then he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' is a laudatory statement, so too 'then he becomes a sage' should be — because of the similarity of construction.
Given this position, we say: 'The injunction of another auxiliary' — [silence (<s>mauna</s>) as] an auxiliary to knowledge, like childlikeness (<s>bālya</s>) and learning (<s>pāṇḍitya</s>), should indeed be accepted as enjoined, being new (<s>apūrva</s>).

children.text: nanu pāṇḍityaśabdenaiva maunasyāvagatatvamuktam /
children.translated_text: But was it not said that silence is already known from the word '<s>pāṇḍitya</s>' (learning) itself?

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
muniśabdasya jñānātiśayārthatvāt /
mananānmuniriti ca vyutpattiriti ca vyutpattisaṃbhavāt /
'munīnāmapyahaṃ vyāsaḥ' (gī. 10.37) iti ca prayogadarśanāt /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
Because the word '<s>muni</s>' denotes a superior degree of knowledge.
Because the derivation '<s>muni</s>' from '<s>manana</s>' (reflection) is possible.
And because the usage is observed: 'Among sages, I am <s>Vyāsa</s>' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 10.37).

children.text: nanu muniśabda uttamāśramavacano 'pi śrūyate 'gārhasthyamācāryakulaṃ maunaṃ vānaprastham' ityatra /
children.translated_text: But the word '<s>muni</s>' is also heard as denoting the highest <s>āśrama</s> — 'Householder's life, student life, silence (<s>mauna</s>), forest-dweller's life' — in that passage.

children.text:
na /
'vālmīkirmunipuṅgavaḥ' ityādiṣu vyabicāradarśanāt /
itarāśramasaṃnidhānāttu pāriśeṣyāttatrottamāśramopādānaṃ jñānapradhānatvādutmāśramasyaṣa tasmādbālyapāṇḍityāpekṣayā tṛtīyamidaṃ maunaṃ jñānātiśayarūpaṃ vidīyate /
yattu bālya eva vidheḥ paryavasānamiti tathāpyapūrvatvānmunitvasya vidheyatvāmāśrīyate muniḥ syāditi /
nirvedanīyatvanirdeśādapi maunasya bālyapāṇḍityavadvidheyatvāśrayaṇam /
tadvato vidyāvataḥ sanyāsinaḥ /
kathañca vidyāvaḥ saṃnyāsina ityavagamyate /
tadadhikārāt 'ātmānaṃ viditvā putrādyeṣaṇābhyo vyutthāyātha bhikṣācaryaṃ caranti' iti /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because deviation [from that meaning] is observed in [expressions like] '<s>Vālmīki</s>, the best of sages' and the like.
But because of the proximity of the other <s>āśramas</s> [in that passage], the highest <s>āśrama</s> is taken by elimination — because the highest <s>āśrama</s> has knowledge as its primary [feature].
Therefore, in relation to childlikeness and learning, this silence — in the form of a superior degree of knowledge — is being enjoined as the third [stage].
Even if the injunction terminates in childlikeness alone, nevertheless, because <s>muni</s>-hood is new (<s>apūrva</s>), its being enjoined is accepted — 'One should become a <s>muni</s>.'
And because silence is mentioned as something to be 'become weary of' (<s>nirvedanīya</s>), its being enjoined — like childlikeness and learning — is accepted.
This is for one who possesses knowledge, [i.e.,] a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> who has knowledge.
And how is it known that the <s>saṃnyāsin</s> possesses knowledge?
Because of his eligibility [being established from the <s>śruti</s>]: 'Having known the Self, having arisen from the desires for sons and the like, they then live the life of mendicancy (<s>bhikṣācaryam</s>).'

children.text:
nanu sati vidyāvattve prāpnotyeva tatrātiśayaḥ kiṃ monavidhinetyata āha - pakṣeṇeti /
etaduktaṃ bhavati -
children.translated_text:
But if one already possesses knowledge, the superior degree [of knowledge] is already obtained — what is the point of the injunction of silence?
To this [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: 'Optionally' — this means:

children.text: yasminpakṣe bhedadarśanaprābalyānna prāpnoti tasminneṣa vidhiriti /
children.translated_text: In the case where, due to the strength of the perception of difference, [the superior knowledge] is not obtained — in that case this injunction [applies].

children.text: vidhyādivat /
children.translated_text: Like the injunction and the like.

children.text: yathā - 'darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ svargakāmo yajeta' ityevañjātīyake vidhyādau sahakāritvenāgnyanbādhānādikamaṅgajātaṃ vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Just as in [the injunction] 'One who desires heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — in such an injunction and the like, the set of accessories such as the kindling of fire and the like are enjoined as auxiliaries —

children.text: evamavipradhāne 'pyasminvidyāvākye maunavidhirityarthaḥ // 47 //
children.translated_text: so too, even in this sentence about knowledge — which is not primarily [about ritual] — the injunction of silence [is to be understood]. // 47 //

children.text:
evaṃ bālyādiviśiṣṭe kaivalyāśrame śrutimati vidyamāne kasmācchāndogye gṛhiṇopasaṃhāraḥ 'abhisamāvṛtya kuṭumbe' (chā. 8.15.1) ityatra /
tena hyupasaṃharaṃstadviṣayamādaraṃ darśatīti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text:
When the <s>āśrama</s> of renunciation (<s>kaivalya</s>), characterized by childlikeness and the rest, is thus heard in <s>śruti</s>, why does the <s>Chāndogya</s> conclude with the householder — 'Having returned [to the household]' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.15.1)?
For by that conclusion, [the text] shows emphasis on that [householder] topic.
To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the reply:

children.text: kṛtsnabhāvāt tu gṛhiṇopasaṃhāraḥ | BBs_3,4.48 |
children.translated_text: But the conclusion with the householder is because of [the householder's] comprehensiveness. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.48 |

children.text: tuśabdo viśeṣaṇārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for specifying.

children.text: kṛtsnabhāvo 'sya viśeṣyate /
children.translated_text: The comprehensiveness [of the householder's life] is being specified.

children.text: bahulāyāsāni hi bahūnyāśramakarmāṇi yajñādīni taṃ prati kartavyatayopadiṣṭānyāśramāntarakarmāṇi ca yathāsaṃbhavamahiṃsendriyasaṃyamādīni tasya vidyante /
children.translated_text: For the many ritual duties of the <s>āśramas</s> — sacrifices and the like — which involve much effort, are taught as duties to be performed by him; and the duties of the other <s>āśramas</s> too — non-violence, sense-restraint, and the like — as far as possible, are also present in his [life].

children.text: tasmādgṛhamedhinopasaṃhāro na virudhyate // 48 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the conclusion with the householder is not contradictory. // 48 //

children.text: maunavad itareṣām apy upadeśāt | BBs_3,4.49 |
children.translated_text: Like silence, for the others too — because of the teaching. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.49 |

children.text: yathā maunaṃ gārhasthyaṃ caitāvāśramau śrutimantāvevamitarāvapi vānaprasthagurukulavāsau /
children.translated_text: Just as silence (<s>mauna</s>, i.e., <s>saṃnyāsa</s>) and household life (<s>gārhasthya</s>) — these two <s>āśramas</s> are based on <s>śruti</s> — so too the other two — the forest-dweller's life (<s>vānaprastha</s>) and the student's life in the teacher's house (<s>gurukulavāsa</s>).

children.text: darśitā hi purastācchrutiḥ- 'tapaḥ eva dvitīyo brahmacaryācāryakulavāsī tṛtīyaḥ' (chā. 2.23.1) ityādyā /
children.translated_text: For the <s>śruti</s> has been cited earlier: 'Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the second; the third is the student dwelling in the teacher's house' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.23.1) and the like.

children.text: tasmāccaturṇāmapyāśramāṇāmupadeśāviśeṣāttulyavadvikalpasamuccayābhyāṃ pratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the non-difference in the teaching of all four <s>āśramas</s>, [the mode of] practice is understood as either option (<s>vikalpa</s>) or combination (<s>samuccaya</s>) — equally.

children.text: itareṣāmiti dvayorāśramayorbahuvacanaṃ vṛttibhedāpekṣayānuṣṭhātṛbhedāpekṣayā veti draṣṭavyam // 49 //
children.translated_text: The plural in 'for the others' — referring to two <s>āśramas</s> — should be understood as based on the difference of sub-types [within each <s>āśrama</s>] or on the difference of practitioners. // 49 //

children.text: 15 anāviṣkārādhikaraṇam / sū. 50
children.translated_text: 15. The <s>Anāviṣkārādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Non-display). <s>Sūtra</s> 50.

children.text: anāviṣkurvann anvayāt | BBs_3,4.50 |
children.translated_text: Not displaying [oneself] — because of the continuity [of this meaning with the context]. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.50 |

children.text:
'tasmādbrahmaṇaḥ pāṇḍityaṃ nirvedya bālyena tiṣṭhāset' (bṛ. 3.5.1) iti bālyamanuṣṭheyatayā śrūyate /
tatra bālasya bhāvaḥ karma vā bālyamitiraddhite sati bālabhāvasya vayoviśeṣasyecchāyā saṃpādayitumaśakyatvādyathopapādaṃ mūtrapurīṣatvādibālacaritantargatā vā bhāvaviśuddhiraprarūḍhendriyatvaṃ dambhadarpādirahitatvaṃ vā bālyaṃ syāditi saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvatprāptaṃ kāmacāravādabhakṣaṇatā yathopapādamūtrapurīṣatvaṃ ca prasiddhataraṃ loke bālyamiti tadgrahaṇaṃ yuktam /
children.translated_text:
'Therefore, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having become weary of learning, should abide in childlikeness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.5.1) — childlikeness is heard as something to be practiced.
There, '<s>bālya</s>' — [meaning either] the state or the conduct of a child — when the suffix is applied, a doubt [arises]: Since the state of being a child, i.e., a particular age, cannot be intentionally produced, <s>bālya</s> would be either: the child's behavior of urinating and defecating anywhere and the like, or inner purity of disposition — the state of having undeveloped sense-organs, being free from hypocrisy, pride, and the like.
What is the prima facie view? Unrestrained conduct, eating indiscriminately, urinating and defecating wherever — this is the more commonly known meaning of childlikeness in the world, so its adoption is proper.

children.text: nanu patitatvādidoṣaprāpterna yuktaṃ kāmacāratādyāśrayaṇam /
children.translated_text: But because of the consequence of [incurring] faults such as loss of caste and the like, the adoption of unrestrained conduct and the like is not proper.

children.text:
na /
vidyāvataḥ saṃnyāsino vacanasmarthyāddoṣanivṛtteḥ paśuhiṃsādiṣviveti /
evaṃ prāpte 'bhidhīyate /
na /
vacanasya gatyantarābhāvāt /
aviruddhe hyanyasminbālyaśabdābhilapye labhyamāne na vidhyantaravyāghātakalpanā yuktā /
pradhānopakārāya cāṅgaṃ vidhīyate /
jñānābhyāsaśca pradhānamiha yatīnāmanuṣṭheyam /
naca sakalāyāṃ bālacaryāyāmaṅgīkriyamāṇāyāṃ jñānābhyāsaḥ saṃbhāvyate /
tasmādāntaro bhāvaviśeṣo bālyasyāprarūḍhendriyatvādiriha bālyamāśrīyate /
tadāha - anāviṣkurvanniti /
jñānādhyayanadhārmikatvādibhirātmānamavikhyāpayandambhadarpādirahito bhavet /
yathā bālo 'prarūḍhendriyatayā na pareṣāmātmānamāviṣkartumīhate tadvat /
children.translated_text: Just as a child, because of having undeveloped sense-organs, does not seek to display itself to others — so too [the knower should be].

children.text: evaṃ hyasya vākyasya pradhānopakāryārthānugama upapadyate /
children.translated_text: For in this way, the continuity of meaning serving the principal [practice] is established for this sentence.

children.text: tathācoktaṃ smṛtikāraiḥ - 'yaṃ na santaṃ na cāsantaṃ nāśrutaṃ na bahuśrutam /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>smṛti</s>-authors have said: 'He whom no one knows as good or bad, as unlearned or greatly learned,

children.text: na suvṛttaṃ na durvṛttaṃ veda kaścitsa brāhmaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: as well-conducted or ill-conducted — he is a [true] <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

No.
Because for the <s>saṃnyāsin</s> who possesses knowledge, faults are averted by the power of the [scriptural] statement — just as in the case of animal sacrifice and the like.
Given this position, it is stated:
No.
Because the statement has no alternative interpretation.
For when another meaning of the word '<s>bālya</s>' is available that does not conflict [with propriety], it is not proper to imagine a conflict with another injunction.
And an accessory is enjoined to serve the principal [practice].
And the principal [practice] to be performed here by the <s>yatis</s> (renunciants) is the cultivation of knowledge (<s>jñānābhyāsa</s>).
And if the entirety of childish behavior were accepted, the cultivation of knowledge would not be possible.
Therefore, the inner disposition (<s>bhāvaviśeṣa</s>) of childlikeness — having undeveloped sense-organs and the like — is what is meant by '<s>bālya</s>' here.
This is stated: 'Not displaying' — not publicizing oneself through knowledge, learning, religiousness, and the like — one should be free from hypocrisy, pride, and the like.

children.text: gūḍhadharmāśrito vidvānajñātacaritaṃ caret /
children.translated_text: The wise one, devoted to hidden <s>dharma</s>, should behave with unknown conduct;

children.text: andhavajjaḍavaccāpi mūkavacca mahīṃ caret' //
children.translated_text: he should move about the earth like a blind man, like an inert one, like a mute one.'

children.text: 'avyaktaliṅgo 'vyaktācāraḥ' iti caivamādi // 50 //
children.translated_text: 'Of undisclosed insignia, of undisclosed conduct' — and passages of this kind. // 50 //

children.text: 16 aihikādhikaraṇam / sū. 51
children.translated_text: 16. The <s>Aihikādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of [Knowledge Arising] in This Life). <s>Sūtra</s> 51.

children.text: aihikam apy aprastutapratibandhe taddarśanāt | BBs_3,4.51 |
children.translated_text: [Knowledge arises] in this [very life] too — when there is no obstruction to what has commenced; because of the observation of that. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.51 |

children.text:
'sarvāpekṣā ca yajñādiśruteraśvavat (bra.sū. 3.4.23) ityata ārabhyoccāvacaṃ vidyāsādhanamavadhāritaṃ, tatphalaṃ vidyā siddhyantī kimihaiva janmani siddhyatyuta kadācidamutrāpīti cnavtyate /
kiṃ tāvatprāptam /
ihaiveti /
children.translated_text:
Beginning from '<s>Sarvāpekṣā ca</s>' ('And all prerequisites, because of the <s>śruti</s> on sacrifice and the like, like a horse' — <s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.4.23), various high and low means of knowledge have been ascertained. The question arises: Does the knowledge that is the fruit [of those means] arise in this very life, or does it sometimes arise in the next [life] as well?
What is the prima facie view? In this very life.

children.text:
kiṃ kāraṇam /
śravaṇādipūrvikā hi vidyā /
naca kaścidamutra me vidyā jāyatāmityabhisaṃdhāya śravaṇādiṣu pravartate /
samāna eva tu janmani vidyājanmābhisaṃdhāyaiteṣu pravartamāno dṛśyate /
yajñādīnyapi śravaṇādidvāreṇaiva vidyāṃ janayanti prāmāṇajanyatvādvidyāyāḥ /
tasmādaihikameva vidyājanmeti /
evaṃ prāpte vadāmaḥ - aihikaṃ vidyājanma bhavatyasati prastutapratibandha iti /
etadapaktaṃ bhavati - yadā prakrāntasya vidyāsādhanasya kaścitpratibandho na kriyata upasthitavipākena karmāntareṇa tadehaiva vidyotpadyate, yadā tu khalu tatpratibandhaḥ kriyate tadāmutreti /
upasthitavipākatvaṃ ca karmaṇo deśakālanimittopaninipātādbhavati /
yāni cākasya karmaṇo vipācakāni deśakālanimittāni tānyevānyasyāpīti na niyantuṃ śakyate /
yato viruddhaphalānyapi karmāṇi bhavanti /
śāstramapyasya karmaṇa idaṃ phalaṃ bhavatītyetāvati paryavasitaṃ na deśakālanimittaviśeṣamapi saṃkārtayati /
sādhanavīryaviśeṣāttvatīndriyā kasyacicchaktirāvirbhavati tatpratibaddhā parasya tiṣṭhati /
nacāviśeṣeṇa vidyāyāmabhisaṃdhirnotpadyata ihāmutra vā me vidyā jāyatāmityabhisaṃdherniraṅ kuśatvāt /
śravaṇādi dvāreṇāpi vidyotpadyamānā pratibandhakṣayāpekṣayaivotpadyate /
tathācaśrutirdurbodhatvamātmano darśayati - 'śravaṇāyāpi bahubhiryo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ /
āścaryo 'sya vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhāścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ' (ka. 2.7) iti /
garbhasya eva ca vāmadevaḥ pratipede brahmabhāvamiti vadantī janmāntarasaṃcitātsādhanājjanmāntare vidyotpattiṃ darśayati /
nahi garbhasyaivaihikaṃ kiñcitsādhanaṃ saṃbhāvyate /
samṛtāvapi - 'aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati' (gī. 6.36) ityarjunena pṛṣṭo bhagavānvāsudevaḥ 'nahi kalyāṇakṛtkaściddurgatiṃ tāta gacchati' (gī. 6.40) ityuktvā punastasya puṇyalokaprāptiṃ sādhukule saṃbūtiṃ cābhidhāyānantaram 'tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam' (gī.
children.translated_text:
What is the reason?
For knowledge is preceded by hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and the like.
And no one engages in hearing and the like with the intention 'May knowledge arise for me in the next life.'
Rather, one who engages in these [practices] is observed to intend the arising of knowledge in this very same life.
And sacrifices and the like too generate knowledge only through the medium of hearing and the like — because knowledge is produced by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).
Therefore, the arising of knowledge is in this life alone.
Given this position, we say: The arising of knowledge is in this [very] life when there is no obstruction to what has commenced.
The meaning is this: When no obstruction is created by some other <s>karma</s> whose fruition is imminent, then knowledge arises in this very life. But when such obstruction occurs, then [knowledge arises] in the next [life].
And the imminence of fruition of a <s>karma</s> occurs from the coincidence of place, time, and occasion.
And it cannot be determined that the same place, time, and occasion that ripen one <s>karma</s> will [also] ripen another.
Because <s>karmas</s> have mutually contradictory fruits.
And scripture too concludes only with 'This <s>karma</s> has this fruit' — it does not specify the particularities of place, time, and occasion.
Due to a special power of the means, a supersensory capacity manifests for one person; for another it remains obstructed.
And one cannot claim that the intention [for knowledge] does not arise indiscriminately — whether [directed at] this life or the next — because intention is unconstrained.
And knowledge, even when arising through the medium of hearing and the like, arises only in dependence on the exhaustion of obstructions.
And thus the <s>śruti</s> shows the difficulty of comprehending the Self: 'Even to hear of It is not available to many; many who hear of It do not know It; wondrous is the teacher of It, skilled is the one who attains It; wondrous is the knower, instructed by the skilled' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.7).
And [the <s>śruti</s>] stating that <s>Vāmadeva</s> realized <s>Brahman</s>-hood while still in the womb — shows the arising of knowledge in another life from means accumulated in previous lives.
For no means [of knowledge] accomplished in this very life can be attributed to one still in the womb.
In <s>smṛti</s> too: When <s>Arjuna</s> asked, 'Having failed to attain perfection in <s>yoga</s>, what path does one go to, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 6.37), the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, having said 'No one who does good ever comes to a bad end, dear one' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 6.40), and then having described his attainment of meritorious worlds and birth in a virtuous family — subsequently: 'There he obtains the mental disposition from the previous body' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s>

children.text: 6.43) ityādinā 'anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim' (gī. 6.45) ityetenaitadeva darśayati /
children.translated_text: 6.43) — and continuing with 'Perfected through many births, he then attains the supreme goal' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 6.45) — shows this very [point].

children.text: tasmādaihikamāmuṣmikaṃ vā vidyājanma pratibandhakṣayāpekṣayeti sthitam // 51 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the arising of knowledge may be either in this life or in the next — depending on the exhaustion of obstructions: this is the established conclusion. // 51 //

children.text: 17 muktiphalādhikaraṇam / sū. 52
children.translated_text: 17. The <s>Muktiphalādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Liberation as the Fruit). <s>Sūtra</s> 52.

children.text: evaṃ muktiphalāniyamas tadavasthāvadhṛtes tadavasthāvadhṛteḥ | BBs_3,4.52 |
children.translated_text: Likewise, there is no restriction regarding the fruit of liberation — because of the ascertainment of that state [of knowledge being firmly established], because of the ascertainment of that state. | <s>BBs</s> 3,4.52 |

children.text:
yathā mumukṣorvidyāsādhanāvalambinaḥ sādhanavīryaviśeṣādvidyalakṣaṇe phala aihikāmuṣmikaphalatvakṛto viśeṣapratiniyamo dṛṣṭaḥ /
evaṃ muktilakṣaṇe 'pyutkarṣīpakarṣakṛtaḥ kaścidviśeṣapratiniyamaḥ /
syādityāśaṅkyāha - evaṃ muktiphalāniyama iti /
na khalu muktiphale kaścidevaṃbhūto viśeṣapratiniyama āśaṅkitavyaḥ /
kutaḥ - tadavasthāvadhṛteḥ /
muktyavasthā hi sarvavedānteṣvekarūpaivāvadhāryate /
brahmaiva hi muktyavasthā naca brahmaṇo 'nekākārayogo 'sti /
ekaliṅgatvāvadhāraṇāt 'astūlamanaṇu' (bṛ. 3.8.8) 'sa eṣa neti netyātmā' (bṛ. 3.9.23) 'yatra nānyatpaśyati' (chā. 7.24.1) 'brahmaivedamamṛtaṃ purastāt' (muṇḍa. 2.2.11) 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' (bṛ. 2.4.6) 'sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma' (bṛ. 4.4.25) 'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛ. 4.5.15) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
apica vidyāsādhanaṃ svavīryaviśeṣāsvaphala eva vidyāyāṃ kañcidatiśayamāsañjayenna vidyāphale muktau /
taddhyasādhyaṃ nityasiddhasvabhāvameva vidyāyādhigamyata ityasakṛdavādiṣma /
naca tasyāmapyutkarṣanikarṣātmako 'tiśaya upapadyate nikṛṣṭāyā vidyātvābhāvādutkṛṣṭaiva hi vidyā bhavati /
tasmāttasyāṃ cirācirotpattirūpo 'tiśayo bhavanbhavet /
natu muktau kaścidatiśayasaṃbhavo 'sti /
vidyābhedābhāvādapi tatphalabhedaniyamābhāvaḥ karmaphalavat /
nahi muktisādhanabhūtāyā vidyāyāḥ karmaṇāmiva bhedo 'stīti /
saguṇāsu tu vidyāsu - 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīraḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityādyāsu guṇāvāpodvāpavaśādbhedopapattau satyāmupapadyate yathāsvaṃ phalabhedaniyamaḥ karmaphalavat /
tathāca liṅgadarśanam - 'taṃ yathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati' iti /
children.translated_text: And thus an indicatory mark is observed: 'As one meditates upon [<s>Brahman</s>], so one becomes.'

children.text: naivaṃ nirguṇāyāṃ vidyāyāṃ guṇābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: But this is not so in the case of <s>nirguṇa vidyā</s>, because of the absence of attributes.

children.text: tathāca smṛtiḥ - 'nahi gatiradhikāsti kasyacitsati hi guṇe pravadantyatulyatām' iti /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>smṛti</s> states: 'There is no higher path for anyone — for when the attribute is the same, they declare equality.'

children.text: tadavasthāvadhṛtestadavasthādhṛteriti padābhyaso 'dhyāyaparisamāptiṃ dyotayati // 52 //
children.translated_text: The repetition of the phrase '<s>tadavasthāvadhṛteḥ</s>' (because of the ascertainment of that state) indicates the conclusion of the chapter. // 52 //

Just as, for the seeker of liberation who relies on the means of <s>vidyā</s>, a definite restriction of results is observed — pertaining to the fruit of <s>vidyā</s>, whether worldly or other-worldly — due to the distinctive power of the means, so too in the case of the fruit called liberation, there might be some restriction of results due to degrees of superiority and inferiority — anticipating this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: 'Thus, there is no restriction regarding the fruit of liberation.' Indeed, no such restriction of results should be apprehended in the case of the fruit of liberation. Why? Because the state [of liberation] is firmly ascertained. For the state of liberation is ascertained as having one single form in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts. For the state of liberation is <s>Brahman</s> itself, and a multiplicity of forms is not possible for <s>Brahman</s> — because of the ascertainment that it has a single characteristic, from <s>śrutis</s> such as: 'It is neither gross nor subtle' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8), 'That Self is [described as] "not this, not this"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.23), 'Where one sees nothing else' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1), 'This <s>Brahman</s> indeed is immortal in front' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.11), 'All this is this Self' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.6), 'This great unborn Self is ageless, undying, immortal, fearless — <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.25), 'Where, for him, everything has become the Self alone — then by what should one see whom?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15) and the like. Moreover, the means of <s>vidyā</s>, by its own distinctive power, may produce some special excellence in <s>vidyā</s> itself — but not in liberation, which is the fruit of <s>vidyā</s>. For that [liberation] is unproduced — it is realized by <s>vidyā</s> as being of an eternally established nature — we have stated this repeatedly. And in <s>vidyā</s> itself, no excellence consisting of superiority and inferiority is possible — for inferior <s>vidyā</s> is not <s>vidyā</s> [at all]; only superior [knowledge] is truly <s>vidyā</s>. Therefore, the only possible excellence in <s>vidyā</s> would be in terms of its arising sooner or later. But no possible excellence exists in liberation [itself]. Because there is no difference in <s>vidyā</s> [of <s>nirguṇa Brahman</s>], there is no restriction of difference in its fruit — unlike the fruit of <s>karma</s>. For there is no difference in <s>vidyā</s> — which is the means to liberation — as there is in <s>karmas</s>. But in the case of <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>vidyās</s> — such as 'Constituted of mind, having <s>prāṇa</s> as body' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and the like — since a difference [among them] is tenable due to the inclusion and exclusion of attributes, a restriction of difference in their respective fruits is tenable — like the fruit of <s>karma</s>.

children.text: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye tṛtīyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the third <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Śārīraka-mīmāṃsā-bhāṣya</s> composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the most venerable <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya</s>. // 4 //

children.text: atha caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: atra asmin phalādhyāye prathamapāde jīvanmuktinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: Here, in this <s>adhyāya</s> on fruit, the first <s>pāda</s> contains the determination of liberation while living (<s>jīvanmukti</s>).

children.text: 1 āvṛtti adhikaraṇam / sū. 1-2
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Āvṛttyadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Repetition). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-2.

children.text: āvṛttir asakṛdupadeśāt | BBs_4,1.1 |
children.translated_text: Repetition [is required] — because of the repeated instruction. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.1 |

children.text:
tṛtīye adhyāye parā aparāsu vidyāsu sādhana āśrayo vicāraḥ prāyeṇātyagāt /
atha iha caturthe phalāśraya āgamiṣyati /
prasaṅgāgataṃ ca anyadapi kiñcit cintayiṣyate /
prathamaṃ tāvat katibhiḥ cidadhikaraṇaiḥ sādhana āśrayavicāraśeṣameva anusarāmaḥ /
'ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.21) 'tameva dhīro vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta'(bṛ. 4.5.6) 'so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ' (chā. 8.7.1) iti ca evamādiśravaṇeṣu saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ sakṛt pratyayaḥ kartavya āhosvit āvṛttya iti /
kiṃ tāvat prāptaṃ sakṛt pratyayaḥ syāt prayājādivat /
tāvatā śāstrasya kṛtārthatvāt /
aśrūyamāṇāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyām aśāstrārthaḥ kṛto bhavet /
children.translated_text: In the third <s>adhyāya</s>, the inquiry concerning the higher and lower <s>vidyās</s> has for the most part dealt with the means (<s>sādhana</s>) aspect. Now here, in the fourth [<s>adhyāya</s>], [the inquiry] concerning the fruit (<s>phala</s>) aspect will follow. And whatever else arises incidentally will also be considered. First, through a few <s>adhikaraṇas</s>, we shall pursue the remainder of the inquiry concerning the means aspect. In passages such as 'The Self indeed is to be seen, to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.21), 'The wise one, having known That, should cultivate wisdom' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6), 'He is to be sought, He is to be desired to be known' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) — in such teachings, a doubt arises: Should the cognitive act be performed once, or repeatedly?

children.text:
nanu asakṛt upadeśā udāhṛtāḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavya iti evamādayaḥ /
evam api yāvat śabdam āvartayet sakṛt śravaṇaṃ sakṛt mananaṃ sakṛt nididhyāsanaṃ ca iti na atiriktam /
sakṛt upadeśeṣu tu veda upāsīta iti evamādiṣu anāvṛttiḥ iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: To begin with, the prima facie view would be that a single cognition suffices — like the preliminary offerings (<s>prayājas</s>). Because the scripture's purpose is fulfilled by that much. If repetition — which is not heard [as enjoined] — were performed, it would be an unscriptural act. Objection continued: But the instructions that were cited — 'to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon' — are instructions of repeated [practice]! Even so, following the words literally, one hearing, one reflection, and one meditation — nothing more [is required]. But in the case of instructions using single [verbs] such as 'one should know,' 'one should meditate' and the like — no repetition [at all is required].

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - pratyayāvṛttiḥ kartavyā /
kutaḥ - asakṛt upadeśāt /
'śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ' iti evañjātīyako hi asakṛt upadeśaḥ pratyayāvṛttiṃ sūcayati /
children.translated_text: Given this prima facie view, we say: Repetition of the cognitive act must be performed. Why? Because of the repeated instruction. For the repeated instruction of the type 'to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon' indicates the repetition of the cognitive act.

children.text: nanu uktaṃ yāvat śabdameva āvartayet na adhikam iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it was said that one should repeat only as many times as the words [indicate] — no more.

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: darśanaparyavasitatvāt adoṣam /
children.translated_text: There is no fault, because [these practices] culminate in direct realization (<s>darśana</s>).

children.text: darśanaparyavasānāni hi śravaṇādīni āvartyamānāni dṛṣṭārthāni bhavanti /
children.translated_text: For hearing and the like, when repeated, become purposeful [only when they] culminate in direct realization.

children.text: yathā avaghātādīni taṇḍulādi niṣpattiparyasānāni tadvat //
children.translated_text: Just as pounding and the like culminate in the production of rice and the like — so too.

children.text:
api ca upāsanaṃ nididhyāsanaṃ ca iti atyantarṇītāvṛttiguṇa eva kriyābhidhīyate /
tathā hi - loke gurum upāste rājānam upāsta iti ca yaḥ tātparyeṇa gurvādīn anuvartate sa evam ucyate /
tathā dhyāyati proṣitanāthā patim iti yā nirantara smaraṇā patiṃ prati sā utkaṇṭhā sā evam abhidhīyate /
vidyupāstyoḥ ca vedānteṣu avyatirekeṇa prayogo dṛśyate /
kvacit vidinā upakramya upāsina upasaṃharati yathā - 'yastadveda yatsa veda sa mayaitaduktaḥ' (chā. 4.1.4) iti atra 'anu ma etāṃ bhagavo devatāṃ śādhi yāṃ devatāmupāḥse' (chā. 5.2.2) iti /
children.translated_text: In some places, beginning with the root '<s>vid</s>' (to know), [the text] concludes with '<s>upās</s>' (to meditate) — as in: 'He who knows this, as he knows, is told by me' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.1.4); and there: 'Teach me, venerable one, the deity that you meditate upon' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.2.2).

children.text: kvacit ca upāsina upakramya vidinā upasaṃharati yathā - 'mano brahmetyupāsīta' (chā. 3.18.1) iti atra 'bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda' (chā. 3.18.3) iti /
children.translated_text: And in some places, beginning with '<s>upās</s>' (to meditate), [the text] concludes with '<s>vid</s>' (to know) — as in: 'One should meditate on mind as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.1); and there: 'He shines and warms with fame, glory, and the radiance of <s>Brahman</s> — he who knows thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.3).

children.text: tasmat sakṛt upadeśeṣu api āvṛttisiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the case of single instructions, the establishment of repetition [follows].

children.text: asakṛt upadeśaḥ tu āvṛtteḥ sūcakaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: The repeated instruction, however, is an indicator of repetition. // 1 //

Moreover, meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) and deep contemplation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>) denote an activity whose essential quality is inherently repetitive. For thus in ordinary usage — 'He serves (<s>upāste</s>) the teacher,' 'He served the king' — one who devotedly and continually attends upon the teacher and the like is spoken of thus. Likewise, 'She meditates upon (<s>dhyāyati</s>) her husband who is away' — the uninterrupted remembrance and longing toward the absent husband is spoken of thus. And in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts, the usage of '<s>vid</s>' (to know) and '<s>upās</s>' (to meditate) is seen without distinction.

children.text: liṅgāc ca | BBs_4,1.2 |
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory mark. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.2 |

children.text:
liṅgam api pratyayāvṛttiṃ pratyāyayati /
tathā hi udgīthavijñānaṃ prastutya 'āditya udgīthaḥ' (chā. 1.5.1) iti etat ekaputratādoṣeṇa āpodya 'raśamīṃstavaṃ paryāvartayāt' (chā. 1.5.2) iti raśmibahutva vijñānaṃ bahuputratāyai vidadhat siddhavat pratyayāvṛttiṃ darśayati /
tasmāt tat sāmānyāt sarvapratyayeṣu āvṛttisiddhiḥ /
atra āha - bhavatu nāma sādhyaphaleṣu pratyayeṣu āvṛttiḥ /
teṣu āvṛttisādyasya atiśayasya saṃbhavāt /
yaḥ tu parabrahmaviṣayaḥ pratyayo nitya śuddha buddha mukta svabhāvameva ātmabhūtaṃ paraṃ brahma samarpayati tatra kim arthāvṛttiḥ iti /
children.translated_text: An indicatory mark too conveys the repetition of the cognitive act. For thus, having introduced the knowledge of the <s>Udgītha</s> — 'The sun is the <s>Udgītha</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.5.1) — and having set aside this [meditation] through the fault of having [only] one result (as if having only one son), [the text] — 'He turned [his mind] back to the rays' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.5.2) — prescribing the knowledge of the multitude of rays for the sake of many results (many sons), shows the repetition of the cognitive act as if already established. Therefore, by analogy, the establishment of repetition [applies] to all cognitions. Here [the opponent] says: Let there be repetition in the case of cognitions that have a result to be accomplished. For in those, the existence of an excellence to be accomplished through repetition is possible. But the cognition pertaining to the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — which presents the supreme <s>Brahman</s> as the Self, whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and free — what purpose would repetition serve there?

children.text: sakṛt śrutau ca brahma ātmatvapratīti anupapatteḥ āvṛtti abhyupagama iti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: Because the realization of <s>Brahman</s> as the Self is not possible from a single hearing, repetition is accepted —

children.text:
na /
āvṛttau api tat anupapatteḥ /
yadi hi 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) iti evañjātīyakaṃ vākyaṃ sakṛt śrūyamāṇaṃ brahmātmatva pratītiṃ na utpādayet tataḥ tadeva āvartyamānam utpādayiṣyati iti kā pratyāśā syāt /
atha ucyeta na kevalaṃ vākyaṃ kañcidarthaṃ sākṣātkartuṃ śaknoti ato yuktyapekṣaṃ vākyam anubhāvayiṣyati brahmātmatvam iti /
tathā api āvṛtti ānarthakyameva /
sā api hi yuktiḥ sakṛt pravṛttaiva svam artham anubhāvayiṣyati /
athāpi syāt uktyā vākyena ca sāmānyaviṣayameva vijñānaṃ kriyate na viśeṣaviṣayam /
yathā asti me hṛdaye śūlam ityato vākyāt gātra kampādi liṅgāt ca śūlasadbhāva sāmānyameva paraḥ pratipadyate na viśeṣam anubhavati yathā sa eva śūlī /
children.translated_text: No. Because even with repetition, that [realization] is not possible [by the same logic]. For if a sentence of the type 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), when heard once, cannot produce the realization of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and Self, then what hope is there that the very same [sentence], when repeated, will produce it? If one were to say: A sentence alone cannot directly realize any meaning — therefore the sentence, with the aid of reasoning, will bring about the experience of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and Self — even so, the repetition would be purposeless. For that reasoning too, once employed, will bring about its result. Or if one were to say: Through reasoning and the sentence, only a general cognition is produced, not a particular [direct] one — just as from the sentence 'I have a pain in my heart,' and from indicatory marks such as trembling of the limbs, another person understands only the general existence of the pain but does not experience the particular [pain] as the sufferer himself does —

children.text: viśeṣa anubhavaḥ ca avidyāyā nivartakaḥ tataḥ tadartha āvṛttiḥ iti cet /
children.translated_text: And [if it be said that] the particular experience is what removes <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and therefore repetition is for that purpose —

children.text:
na /
asakṛt api tāvat mātre kriyamāṇe viśeṣavijñāna utpatti asaṃbhavāt /
na hi sakṛt prayuktābhyāṃ śāstrayuktibhyām anavagato viśeṣaḥ śatakṛtvaḥ api prayujyamānābhyām avagantuṃ śakyate /
tasmāt yadi śāstrayuktibhyāṃ viśeṣaḥ pratipādyate yadi vā sāmānyameva ubhayathā api sakṛt pravṛtte eva te svakāryaṃ kuruta iti āvṛtti anupayogaḥ /
na ca sakṛt prayukte śāstrayuktī kasyacit api anubhavaṃ na utpādayata iti śakyate niyantuṃ vicitraprajñatvāt pratipattṛṇām /
api ca aneka aṃśopete laukike padārthe sāmānya viśeṣavat ekena avadhānena ekam aṃśam avadhārayati apareṇa aparam iti syāt api abhyāsa upayogo yathā dīrghaprapāṭhakagrahaṇādiṣu /
na tu nirviśeṣe brahmaṇi sāmānya viśeṣarahite caitanyamātrātmake pramā utpattau abhyāsāpekṣā yukta iti /
children.translated_text: No. Because even when [hearing and reasoning are] performed many times, the arising of particular knowledge is not possible [from mere repetition]. For a particular [realization] not grasped by scripture and reasoning employed once cannot be grasped even when they are employed a hundred times. Therefore, whether scripture and reasoning teach the particular or only the general — in either case, once employed, they accomplish their purpose, and repetition is useless. And it cannot be definitively stated that scripture and reasoning, when employed once, do not produce the experience for anyone at all — because of the diversity of intelligence among recipients. Moreover, in a worldly object that has many aspects — having both general and particular features — one may apprehend one aspect through one act of attention and another through another, so there might indeed be a use for practice, as in the case of grasping a long passage for recitation. But in the case of attributeless <s>Brahman</s> — devoid of general and particular features, being of the nature of pure consciousness alone — it is not reasonable that practice should be required for the arising of true knowledge.

children.text:
atra ucyate - bhavet āvṛtti ānarthakyaṃ taṃ prati yaḥ tattvamasi iti sakṛt uktameva brahmātmatvam anubhavituṃ śaknuyāt /
yastu na śaknoti taṃ pratyupayujyata eva āvṛttiḥ /
tathā hi chāndogye 'tattvamasi śvetaketo' (chā. 6.8.7) iti udiśya 'bhūya eva mā bhagavānvijñāpayatu' (chā. 6.8.7) iti punaḥ paricodyamānaḥ tat tat
children.translated_text: To this we reply: The purposelessness of repetition may hold for one who is able to experience the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and Self from a single utterance of 'You are That.' But for one who is unable — repetition is indeed useful. For thus, in the <s>Chāndogya</s>, having declared 'You are That, <s>Śvetaketu</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), when [<s>Śvetaketu</s>] again requests 'Please instruct me further, venerable one' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7), [<s>Uddālaka</s>] — removing the respective

children.text:
ādāśaṅkā kāraṇaṃ nirākṛtya tattvamasi iti eva asakṛt upadiśate /
tathā ca 'śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ' (bṛ. 4.5.6) ityādi darśitam /
children.translated_text: causes of doubt — instructs 'You are That' repeatedly. And likewise, 'It is to be heard, to be reflected upon, to be meditated upon' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.6) and the like has been shown [as evidence].

children.text: nanu uktaṃ sakṛt śrutaṃ cet tattvamasi vākyaṃ svam artham anubhāvayituṃ na śaknoti tata āvartyamānam api na eva śakṣyati iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it was stated that if the sentence 'You are That,' when heard once, cannot bring about the experience of its meaning, then even when repeated, it will not be able to do so —

children.text:
na eṣa doṣaḥ /
nahi dṛṣṭe anupapannaṃ nāma /
dṛśyante hi sakṛt śrutāt vākyāt mandapratītaṃ vākyārtham āvartayantaḥ tat tat ābhāsavyudāsena samyak pratipadyamānāḥ /
api ca tattvamasi iti etat vākyaṃ tvaṃ padārthasya tat padārthabhāvam ācaṣṭe /
tat padena ca prakṛtaṃ sat brahma īkṣitṛ jagato janmādikāraṇam abhidhīyate 'satyaṃ jñānamananta brahma' (tai. 2.1.1) 'vijñānamānandaṃ brahma' (bṛ. 3.8.11) 'adṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭṛ' (bṛ. 3.8.11) 'avijñātaṃ vijñātṛ' (bṛ. 3.8.11) 'ajamajaramamaram asthūlamanaṇvahrasvamadīrgham' (bṛ. 3.8.8) ityādi śāstra prasiddham /
tatra ajādiśabdaiḥ janmādayo bhāvavikārā nivartitāḥ /
asthūlādiśabdaiḥ ca sthaulyādayo dravyadharmāḥ /
vijñānādiśabdaiḥ ca caitanyaprakāśātmakatvam uktam /
eṣa vyāvṛttasarvasaṃsāradharmakaḥ /
anubhāvātmako brahmasaṃjñakaḥ tat padārtho vedānta abhiyuktānāṃ prasiddhaḥ /
tathā tvaṃpadārthaḥ api pratyagātmā śrotā dehāt ārabhya pratyagātmatayā saṃbhāvyamānaḥ caitanyaparyantatvena avadhāritaḥ /
