tatra yeṣām etau padārthau ajñāna saṃśaya viparyaya pratibaddhau teṣāṃ tatvamasi ityetat vākyaṃ svārthe pramāṃ na utpādayituṃ śaknoti padārthajñānapūrvakatvāt vākyārthasya iti atastāt pratyeṣṭavyaḥ padārthavivekaprayojanaḥ śāstrayuktyabhyāsaḥ /
yadyapi ca pratipattavya ātmā niraṃśaḥ tathā api adhyāropitaṃ tasmin bahu aśatvaṃ deha indriya mano buddhi viṣaya vedanādi lakṣaṇaṃ tatra ekena avadhānena ekam aṃśam apohati apareṇa aparam iti yujyate tatra kramavatī pratipattiḥ /
tat tu pūrvarūpameva ātmapratipatteḥ /
yeṣāṃ punaḥ nipuṇamatīnāṃ na ajñānasaṃśayaviparyayalakṣaṇaḥ padārthaviṣayaḥ pratibandhaḥ asti te śaknuvanti sakṛt uktameva tattvamasi vākyārtham anubhavitum iti tān pratyāvṛtti ānarthakyam iṣṭameva /
sakṛt utpanna eva hi ātmapratipattiḥ avidyāṃ nivartayati iti na atra kaścit api kramaḥ abhyupagamyate /
satyamevaṃ yujyeta yadi kasyacit evaṃ pratipattiḥ bhavet /
balavatī hi ātmano duḥkhatvādi pratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
For what is observed cannot be called untenable.
For it is observed that [students], after hearing a statement once, [when] the meaning of the sentence is only dimly understood, repeat the meaning of the sentence, and — by removing each successive [false] appearance — come to correctly understand [it].
Moreover, the statement '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) declares the identity of the meaning of the word 'thou' (<s>tvam</s>) with the meaning of the word 'That' (<s>tat</s>).
And by the word 'That,' the proximate <s>Sat</s> — <s>Brahman</s>, the seer, the cause of the origination and such of the universe — is denoted. [This <s>Brahman</s> is] well known in scripture through [passages like]: 'Truth, knowledge, infinite is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1); 'Consciousness, bliss, <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11); 'The unseen seer' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11); 'The unknown knower' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.11); 'Unborn, unaging, undying, immortal, not gross, not subtle, not short, not long' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8) — and the like.
There, by the words 'unborn' and the like, the modifications of existence — birth and the rest — are negated.
And by the words 'not gross' and the like, the properties of material substances — grossness and the rest — [are negated].
And by the words 'consciousness' (<s>vijñāna</s>) and the like, [<s>Brahman</s>'s] nature as the effulgence of consciousness is stated.
This [entity] — from which all properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> have been excluded, which is of the nature of pure experience, designated as <s>Brahman</s> — is the meaning of the word 'That,' well known to those versed in <s>Vedānta</s>.
Likewise, the meaning of the word 'thou' — the inner Self, the hearer — being identified as the inner Self starting from the body and ascertained [ultimately] as terminating in consciousness, [is also established].
Now, for those in whom the meanings of these two words are obstructed by ignorance, doubt, or error — for them, the sentence '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' cannot produce valid knowledge (<s>pramā</s>) of its meaning, since the knowledge of the sentence-meaning presupposes knowledge of the word-meanings. Therefore, the study and reflection — aided by scripture and reasoning — whose purpose is the discrimination of the word-meanings, must be sought out.
And even though the Self to be apprehended is partless, still, since much non-Self-hood — in the form of body, sense-organs, mind, intellect, objects, sensations, and the like — is superimposed upon it, it is proper that with one act of attention one removes one superimposed [element], and with another, another. Hence, the apprehension [of the Self] can be gradual.
But that [gradual process] is merely the preliminary stage of the apprehension of the Self.
However, for those of sharp intellect who have no obstruction — in the form of ignorance, doubt, or error — regarding the word-meanings, they are able to experience the meaning of the sentence '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' from a single utterance alone. For them, the purposelessness of repetition is indeed accepted.
For indeed, the apprehension of the Self, once arisen, removes <s>avidyā</s> — hence no gradual process is accepted here.
True, this would hold if such apprehension were to arise for anyone.
But the apprehension that the Self is characterized by suffering and the like is powerful.

children.text: ato na duḥkhitvādi abhāvaṃ kaścit pratipadyata iti cet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, no one [easily] apprehends the absence of suffering and the like — if this is the objection,

children.text:
na /
dehādi abhimānavat duḥkhitvādi abhimānasya mithyā abhimānatva upapatteḥ /
pratyakṣaṃ hi dehe chidyamāne dahyamāne vā ahaṃ chidye dahya iti ca mithyā abhimāno dṛṣṭaḥ /
tathā bāhyatareṣu api putramitrādiṣu saṃtapyamāneṣu ahameva saṃtapya ityadi āropo dṛṣṭaḥ /
tathā duḥkhitvādi abhimānaḥ api syāt /
dehādivat eva caitanyāt bahiḥ upalabhamānatvāt duḥkhitvādīnāṃ suṣuptādiṣu ca ananuvṛtteḥ /
caitanyasya tu suṣupte api anuvṛttim āmananti 'yadvai tanna paśyati paśyanvai tanna paśyati' (bṛ. 4.3.23) ityādinā /
tasmāt sarvaduḥkhavinirmukta ekacaitanyātmakaḥ aham ityeṣa ātmānubhavaḥ /
na ca evam ātmānam anubhavataḥ kiñcit anyat kṛtyam avaśiṣyate /
tathā ca śrutiḥ - 'kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmo yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ lokaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti ātmavidaḥ kartavya abhāvaṃ darśayati /
smṛtiḥ api - 'yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ /
ātmanyeva ca saṃtuṣṭasya kāryaṃ na vidyate' (gī. 3.17) iti /
yasya tu na eṣaḥ anubhavo drāgiva jāyate taṃ pratyanubhavārtha eva āvṛtti abhyupagamaḥ /
tatra api na tattvamasi vākyārthāt pracyāvyāvṛttau pravartayet /
na hi varaghātāya kanyām udvāhayanti /
children.translated_text: For one does not marry off a girl for the purpose of widowhood.

children.text: niyuktasya ca asmin adhikṛtaḥ ahaṃ kartā mayā idaṃ mandam apratibhānāt taṃ brahmapratyayāt viparītapratyaya utpadyate /
children.translated_text: And for one who has been engaged [in the practice], [the thought] 'I am the eligible person, I am the agent; this [understanding of mine] is dull because of lack of comprehension' — from that <s>Brahman</s>-cognition, the opposite cognition arises.

children.text: yaḥ tu svayameva mandamatiḥ apratibhānāt taṃ vākyārthaṃ jihāset tasya etasmin eva vākyārthe sthirīkāra āvṛttyādi vāco yuktyā abhyupeyate /
children.translated_text: But one who is dull-witted on his own — who, because of lack of comprehension, would abandon that sentence-meaning — for him, the stabilization in this very sentence-meaning through repetition and the like is accepted through reasoning.

children.text: tasmāt parabrahmaviṣaye api pratyaye tat upāya upadeśeṣu āvṛttisiddhiḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even regarding the cognition of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the efficacy of repetition in the teachings of the means [to that cognition] is established. // 2 //

We say: No.
Because the conviction of suffering and the like — like the conviction of being the body and the like — is tenable as a false conviction.
For it is directly perceived that when the body is being cut or burned, the false conviction 'I am being cut' or 'I am being burned' is observed.
Likewise, even regarding more external things like sons, friends, and the like — when they are tormented — the superimposition 'I myself am being tormented' and the like is observed.
Similarly, the conviction of suffering and the like would [also] be [a false superimposition].
Because suffering and the like — like the body and the like — are perceived as external to consciousness; and because they do not persist in deep sleep and the like.
But [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches the persistence of consciousness even in deep sleep: 'What it does not see — though seeing, it does not see' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.23) — and the like.
Therefore, the experience of the Self is: 'I am of the nature of pure, singular consciousness, free from all suffering.'
And for one who thus experiences the Self, nothing else remains to be done.
And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'What shall we do with offspring — we for whom this Self is this world?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) — shows the absence of anything to be done for the knower of the Self.
The <s>smṛti</s> also: 'For the person who delights in the Self alone, who is satisfied in the Self, who is content in the Self alone — for him there is nothing to be done' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 3.17).
But for one in whom this experience does not arise quickly — for him, the acceptance of repetition is precisely for the sake of [producing] the experience.
Even there, [the teacher] should not divert [the student] from the sentence-meaning of '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' and engage [him] in repetition.

children.text: 2 ātmatva upāsana adhikaraṇam / sū. 3
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Ātmatva-Upāsana Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Meditation on [<s>Brahman</s> as] the Self). <s>Sūtra</s> 3.

children.text: ātmeti tūpagacchanti grāhayanti ca | BBs_4,1.3 |
children.translated_text: They approach [<s>Brahman</s>] as the Self, and [the scriptures] teach [It] thus. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.3 |

children.text:
yaḥ śāstroktaviśeṣaṇa paramātmā sa kim aham iti grahītavyaḥ kiṃvā mat anya iti etat vicārayati /
kathaṃ punaḥ ātmaśabde pratyagātmaviṣaye śrūyamāṇe saṃśaya iti /
ucyate - ayam ātmaśabdo mukhyaḥ śakyate abhyupagantuṃ sati jīva īśvarayoḥ abhedasaṃbhava itarathā tu gauṇaḥ ayam abhyupagantavya iti manyate /
kiṃ tāvat prāptaṃ na aham iti grāhyaḥ /
na hi apahatapāpmatvādi guṇo viparīta guṇatvena śakyate grahītuṃ viparīta guṇo ca apahatapāpmatvādi guṇatvena /
apahatapāpmatvādi guṇaḥ ca parameśvaraḥ tadviparītaguṇaḥ tu śārīraḥ /
īśvarasya ca saṃsāri ātmatva īśvara abhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
tataḥ śāstra ānarthakyam /
saṃsāriṇaḥ api īśvara ātmatve adhikāri abhāvāt śāstra ānarthakyameva, pratyakṣādi virodhaḥ ca /
anyatve api tādātmya darśanaṃ śāstrāt kartavyaṃ pratimādiṣu iva viṣṇu ādidarśanam iti cet kāmamevaṃ bhavatu /
na tu saṃsāriṇo mukhya ātma īśvara ityetat naḥ prāpayitavyam /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ātma ityeva parameśvaraḥ pratipattavyaḥ /
tathā hi parameśvara prakriyāyāṃ jābālā ātmatvena eva etam upagacchanti - 'tvaṃ vā ahamasmi bhagavo devato 'haṃ vai tvamasi bhagavo deveti' iti /
tathā anye api 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' ityevam ādaya ātmatva upagamā draṣṭavyāḥ /
grāhayanti ca ātmatvena eva īśvaraṃ vedāntavākyāni 'eṣa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ' (bṛ. 3.4.1) 'eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ' (bṛ. 3.7.3) 'tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) iti evamādīni /
yat uktaṃ pratīka darśanam idaṃ viṣṇupratimā nyāyena bhaviṣyati iti tat ayuktaṃ gauṇatva prasaṅgāt /
vākya vairūpyāt ca /
yatra hi pratīkadṛṣṭiḥ abhipreyate sakṛdeva tatra vacanaṃ bhavati yathā - 'mano brahma' (chā. 3.18.1) 'ādityo brahma' (chā. 3.19.1) ityādi /
iha punaḥ tvam aham asmi ahaṃ ca tvam asi iti āha, ataḥ pratīka śruti vairūpyāt abhedapratipattiḥ /
bhedadṛṣṭi apavādāt ca /
tathā hi - 'atha yo 'nyāṃ devatāmupāste 'nyo 'sāvanyo 'hamīti na sa veda' (bṛ. 1.4.10) 'mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati' (bṛ. 4.5.7) iti evamādyā bhūyasī śrutiḥ bhedadarśanam apavadati /
children.translated_text:
Is the supreme Self — qualified by the attributes stated in scripture — to be apprehended as 'I' [i.e., as the Self], or as other than myself? — this is what [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] examines.
But how can there be a doubt when the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (Self) is heard with reference to the inner Self?
We reply: This word '<s>Ātman</s>' can be accepted as primary [only] if the non-difference of the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) and the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is possible; otherwise, it must be accepted as figurative — so one thinks.
What is the initial position? [<s>Brahman</s>] should not be apprehended as 'I.'
For the qualities of being free from evil and the like cannot be apprehended by one who has the opposite qualities; nor can one with the opposite qualities [be apprehended] as having the qualities of being free from evil and the like.
And the supreme Lord has the quality of being free from evil and the like; while the embodied self has the opposite qualities.
And if the Lord were identical with the transmigrating self, the consequence would be the non-existence of the Lord.
From that, the purposelessness of scripture [would follow].
And even if the transmigrating self were identical with the Lord, because of the absence of a [qualified] person, scripture would be purposeless; and there would be a contradiction with perception and the like.
If [it be said that] even though they are different, the vision of identity should be performed on the authority of scripture — like the vision of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like in images and the like — very well, let it be so.
But it should not be established for us that the Lord is the primary Self of the transmigrating being.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: The supreme Lord should be apprehended as the Self alone.
For thus, in the <s>Paramātman</s> teaching, the <s>Jābālas</s> approach Him as the Self itself: 'You indeed are I, O blessed deity; I indeed am you, O blessed deity.'
Likewise, other [passages of] Self-identification should be considered: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' — and the like.
And the <s>Vedānta</s> sentences teach the Lord as the Self itself: 'This is your Self, the inner [controller] of all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1); 'This is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.7.3); 'That is the truth, that is the Self; that thou art' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) — and the like.
As for the objection that this would be a symbol-vision (<s>pratīka-darśana</s>) like the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-in-an-image principle — that is improper, because of the [unwanted] consequence of figurativeness.
And because of the dissimilarity of the [textual] expression.
For where a symbol-vision is intended, the statement is made only once — as in: 'Mind is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.1); 'The sun is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.19.1) — and the like.
But here [the text] says: 'You are I, and I am you.' Therefore, because of the dissimilarity from symbol-<s>śrutis</s>, [this is] the apprehension of non-difference.
And because the vision of difference is sublated.
For thus — 'Now, he who worships another deity, thinking "He is one, I am another" — he does not know' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10); 'From death to death he goes, who sees diversity here' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.19) — such and numerous <s>śrutis</s> sublate the vision of difference.

children.text: yat tu uktaṃ na viruddhaguṇayoḥ anyonya ātmasaṃbhava iti /
children.translated_text: As for the objection that for two [entities] with contradictory qualities, mutual Self-hood is not possible —

children.text:
na ayaṃ doṣaḥ /
viruddhaguṇatāyā mithyātva upapatteḥ /
yatpunaḥ uktam īśvara abhāvaprasaṅga iti /
tat asat /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
Because it is tenable that the contradictoriness of qualities is false.
As for the objection that the consequence would be the non-existence of the Lord —
that is incorrect.

children.text:
śāstraprāmāṇyāt anabhyupagamāt ca /
na hi īśvarasya saṃsāri ātmatvaṃ pratipādyata iti abhyupagacchāmaḥ kiṃ tarhi saṃsāriṇaḥ saṃsāritva apohena īśvarātmatvaṃ pratipipāyiṣitam iti /
evaṃ ca sati advaita īśvarasya apahatapāpmatvādiguṇatā viparītaguṇatā tu itarasya mithyā iti vyavatiṣṭhate /
yat api uktam adhikāri abhāvaḥ pratyakṣādivirodhaḥ ca iti /
tat api asat /
prākprabodhāt saṃsāritva abhyupagamāt /
tadviṣayatvāt ca pratyakṣādi vyavahārasya /
'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛ. 2.4.14) ityādinā hi prabodhe pratyakṣādi abhāvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text:
Because of the authority of scripture, and because we do not accept [the objection's premise].
For we do not accept that the Lord's nature as the transmigrating self is being taught. Rather, what is desired to be taught is the Lord-nature of the transmigrating being — by removing its transmigrating nature.
This being so, the non-dual Lord's quality of being free from evil and the like stands firm; while the opposite qualities of the other [the individual self] are false — this is established.
As for the objection that there would be an absence of eligible persons and a contradiction with perception and the like —
that too is incorrect.
Because prior to awakening, transmigrating nature is accepted.
And because perception and other modes of transaction pertain to that [transmigrating state].
For 'Where, for him, all has become the Self alone — then by what and whom should he see?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14) — and the like, [the <s>śruti</s>] shows the absence of perception and the like at the time of awakening.

children.text: pratyakṣādi abhāve śruteḥ api abhāvaprasaṅga iti cet /
children.translated_text: If, in the absence of perception and the like, there would be the consequence of the absence of <s>śruti</s> too —

children.text:
na /
iṣṭatvāt /
'atra pitāpitā bhavati' (bṛ. 4.3.22) iti upakramya 'vedā avedāḥ' (bṛ. 4.3.22) iti vacanāt iṣyata eva asmābhiḥ śruteḥ api abhāvaḥ prabodhe /
children.translated_text:
We say: No.
Because that is desired [by us].
For having introduced [the topic] with 'Here, a father is no father' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.22), [the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'The <s>Vedas</s> are no <s>Vedas</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.22) — by this statement, the absence of <s>śruti</s> too at the time of awakening is indeed accepted by us.

children.text: kasya punaḥ ayam aprabodha iti cet /
children.translated_text: If [it be asked:] Whose is this non-awakening?

children.text: ya- tvaṃ pṛcchasi tasya ta iti vadāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: We reply: It belongs to you who are asking — so we say.

children.text: nanu aham īśvara eva uktaḥ śrutyā, yadi evaṃ pratibuddhaḥ asi na asti kasyacit aprabodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: But I have been declared by <s>śruti</s> to be the Lord Himself. If that is so, and you are awakened, then there is no one's non-awakening.

children.text: yaḥ api doṣaḥ codyate kaiścit avidyā kila ātmanaḥ sadvitīyatvāt advaita anupapattiḥ iti saḥ api etena pratyuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the fault raised by some — that <s>avidyā</s> belongs to the Self, and because of its having a second (<s>sadvitīya</s>), non-duality would be untenable — that too is refuted by this.

children.text: tasmāt ātma iti eva īśvare mano dadhīta // 3 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should fix the mind on the Lord as the Self alone. // 3 //

children.text: 3 pratīka adhikaraṇam / sū. 4
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Pratīka Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Symbols). <s>Sūtra</s> 4.

children.text: na pratīke na hi saḥ | BBs_4,1.4 |
children.translated_text: Not in symbols — for that [the symbol] is not [the Self]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.4 |

children.text:
'mano brahmetyupāsītetyadhyātmamathādhidaivatamākāśo brahmeti' (chā. 3.18.1) 'tathā ādityo brahmetyādeśaḥ' (chā. 3.19.1) 'sa yo nāma brahmetyupāste' (chā. 7.1.5) iti evamādiṣu pratīka upāsaneṣu saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ teṣu api ātmagrahaḥ kartavyo na vā iti /
kiṃ tāvat prāptam /
teṣu api ātmagraha eva yuktaḥ /
kasmāt /
brahmaṇaḥ śrutiṣu ātmatvena prasiddhatvāt pratīkānām api brahmavikāratvāt brahmatve satyām ātmatva upapatteḥ iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - na pratīkeṣu ātma matiṃ badhnīyāt /
na hi sa upāsakaḥ pratīkāni vyastāni ātmatvenākalayet /
yat punaḥ brahmavikāratvāt pratīkānāṃ brahmatvaṃ tataḥ ca ātmatvam iti /
tat asat /
pratīka abhāvaprasaṅgāt /
vikārasvarūpa upamardena hi nāmādi jātasya brahmatvameva āśrite bhavati /
svarūpa upamarde ca nāmādīnāṃ kutaḥ pratīkatvam ātmagraho vā /
na ca brahmaṇa ātmatvāt brahmadṛṣṭi upadeśeṣu ātmadṛṣṭiḥ kalpyā /
kartṛtvādi anirākaraṇāt /
kartṛtvādi saṃvarga saṃsāra dharmanirākaraṇe hi brahmaṇa ātmatva upadeśaḥ /
tat anirākaraṇena ca upāsanavidhānam /
ataḥ ca upāsakasya pratīkaiḥ samatvāt ātmagraho na upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And therefore, because the meditator is on the same level as the symbols, the Self-apprehension is not tenable.

children.text: na hi rūcaka svastikayoḥ itaretara ātmatvam asti /
children.translated_text: For there is no mutual Self-hood between a pendant (<s>rūcaka</s>) and a <s>svastika</s> ornament.

children.text: suvarṇa ātmatvena iva tu brahma ātmatvena ekatve pratīka abhāvaprasaṅgam avocāma /
children.translated_text: But just as [we said that] if [gold] has Self-hood through <s>Brahman</s>'s Self-hood, the consequence would be the non-existence of the symbol — we have stated [this already].

children.text: ato na pratīkeṣu ātmadṛṣṭiḥ kriyate // 4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the Self-vision is not applied in symbol-meditations. // 4 //

'One should meditate on mind as <s>Brahman</s> — this is with reference to the Self; with reference to the deity: one should meditate on space as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.18.1); 'Likewise, the sun is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the instruction' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.19.1); 'He who meditates on name as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.5) — in such symbol-meditations (<s>pratīka-upāsanā</s>), the doubt arises: Should the Self-apprehension be done in these too, or not?
What is the initial position?
Even in these, the Self-apprehension alone is proper.
Why?
Because <s>Brahman</s> is well known in the <s>śrutis</s> as the Self; and because the symbols too — being modifications of <s>Brahman</s> — when <s>Brahman</s>-hood [is established for them], the Self-hood is also tenable.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: One should not fix the Self-notion on symbols.
For the meditator would not identify the individual symbols as the Self.
As for the claim that because symbols are modifications of <s>Brahman</s>, they have <s>Brahman</s>-hood, and therefore Self-hood —
that is incorrect.
Because of the consequence of the non-existence of the symbols [as such].
For when the modification-nature of name and the like is sublated, what results is <s>Brahman</s>-hood alone.
And when the [individual] nature of name and the like is sublated, whence would there be symbol-status or Self-apprehension?
Nor should the Self-vision be construed in teachings of <s>Brahman</s>-vision, [merely] because <s>Brahman</s> is the Self.
Because agency and the like are not negated [in symbol-meditations].
For the teaching of <s>Brahman</s>'s Self-hood is [precisely] for the negation of <s>saṃsāra</s>-properties such as agency and the all-absorbing [character of <s>saṃsāra</s>].
But without such negation, [what is] enjoined is [merely] meditation.

children.text: 4 brahma dṛṣṭi adhikaraṇam / sū. 5
brahmadṛṣṭir utkarṣāt | BBs_4,1.5 |
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahman</s>-vision [should be applied to symbols] — because of the elevation [it produces]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.5 |
4. The <s>Brahmadṛṣṭi Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Vision of <s>Brahman</s>). <s>Sūtra</s> 5.

children.text:
teṣu eva udāharaṇeṣu anyaḥ saṃśayaḥ - kim ādityādi dṛṣṭayo brahmaṇi adhyasitavyāḥ kiṃvā brahmadṛṣṭiḥ ādityādiṣu iti /
kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ -sāmānādhikaramye kāraṇa anavadhāraṇāt /
atra hi brahmaśabdasya ādityādiśabdaiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyam upalabhyate /
ādityo brahma prāṇo brahma vidyut brahma ityādi samāna vibhakti nirdeśāt /
na ca atra āñjasaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyam avakalpate /
arthāntaravacanatvāt brahma ādityādiśabdānām /
na hi bhavati gauḥ aśva iti sāmānādhikaraṇyam /
children.translated_text:
In those very examples, another doubt [arises]: Should the visions of the sun (<s>āditya</s>) and the like be superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s>, or should the vision of <s>Brahman</s> [be superimposed] upon the sun and the like?
Whence the doubt? Because the cause cannot be determined from the co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>).
For here, the co-reference of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' with the words '<s>āditya</s>' and the like is observed — '<s>Āditya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>,' '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>,' 'Lightning is <s>Brahman</s>' — and the like, because of the designation in the same grammatical case.
But here, genuine co-reference is not possible.
Because the words '<s>Brahman</s>' and '<s>āditya</s>' and the like denote different things.
For there is no [genuine] co-reference in 'a cow is a horse.'

children.text: nanu prakṛtivikārabhāvāt brahma ādityānāṃ mṛt śarāvādivat sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: But perhaps, because of the cause-effect relationship between <s>Brahman</s> and the sun and the like — as between clay and pots — there could be co-reference?

children.text:
na iti ucyate /
vikārapravilayo hi evaṃ prakṛtisāmānādhikaraṇyāt syāt /
tataḥ ca pratīka abhāvaprasaṅgam avocāma /
paramātma vākyaṃ ca idaṃ tadānīṃ syāt tataḥ ca upāsana adhikāro bādhyeta /
parimitavikāra upādānaṃ ca vyartham /
tasmāt brāhmaṇaḥ agniḥ vaiśvānara ityādivat anyatra anyadṛṣṭi adhyāse sati kva kindṛṣṭiḥ adhyasyatām iti saṃśayaḥ /
tatra aniyamo niyamakāriṇaḥ śāstrasya abhāvāt ityevaṃ prāptam /
athavā ādityādi dṛṣṭaya eva brahmaṇi kartavyā iti evaṃ prāptam /
evaṃ hi ādityādi dṛṣṭibhiḥ brahma upāsitaṃ bhavati brahma upāsanaṃ ca phalavat iti śāstramaryādā /
tasmāt na brahmadṛṣṭiḥ ādityādiṣu iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - brahmadṛṣṭiḥ eva ādityādiṣu syāt iti /
kasmāt /
utkarṣāt /
evam utkarṣeṇa ādityādayo dṛṣṭā bhavanti /
utkṛṣṭadṛṣṭeḥ teṣu adhyāsāt /
tathā ca laukiko nyāyo anugato bhavati /
utkṛṣṭadṛṣṭiḥ hi nikṛṣṭe adhyasitavya iti laukiko nyāyaḥ /
yathā rājadṛṣṭiḥ kṣattari /
sa ca anusartavyaḥ /
viparyaye pratyavāya prasaṅgāt /
na hi kṣattṛdṛṣṭiparigṛhīto rājā nikarṣaṃ nīyamānaḥ śreyase syāt /
children.translated_text:
No, we say.
For such [genuine] co-reference with the cause would entail the dissolution of the effect.
And from that, we have already stated the consequence of the non-existence of the <s>pratīka</s> (symbol).
And this would then become a statement about the supreme Self, and consequently the context of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) would be undermined.
And the specification of limited effects [as objects of meditation] would be purposeless.
Therefore — as in cases like 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is [meditated upon as] fire,' '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>' [superimposed on something else], and the like — given the superimposition of one vision upon another, the doubt is: Where should which vision be superimposed?
The prima facie view is: There is no restriction, because there is no scripture that creates a restriction.
Alternatively, the prima facie view may be: The visions of the sun and the like should be superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s>.
For thus, when the sun and the like are contemplated through the visions of the sun and the like, <s>Brahman</s> would be the object of meditation, and the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> is what bears fruit — this being the boundary of scripture.
Therefore, the vision of <s>Brahman</s> should not be [superimposed] on the sun and the like.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: The vision of <s>Brahman</s> alone should be [superimposed] on the sun and the like.
Why?
Because of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] superiority.
Thus, the sun and the like are seen as exalted.
Because of the superimposition of an exalted vision upon them.
And thus the worldly principle is followed.
For the worldly principle is: An exalted vision should be superimposed upon an inferior [object].
Just as the vision of a king [is superimposed] upon a door-keeper.
And this [principle] should be followed.
Because if reversed, there would be the consequence of disadvantage.
For a king upon whom the vision of a door-keeper has been imposed, being lowered in status, would not conduce to well-being.

children.text: nanu śāstraprāmāṇyāt anāśaṅkanīyaḥ atra pratyavāya prasaṅgo na ca lokikena nyāyena śāstrīyā dṛṣṭiḥ niyantuṃ yukta iti /
children.translated_text: But since by the authority of scripture, the consequence of disadvantage need not be apprehended here, and since a scriptural vision should not be governed by a worldly principle —

children.text:
atra ucyate - nirdhārite śāstrārtha etat evaṃ syāt /
saṃdigdhe tu tasmin nirṇayaṃ prati lokikaḥ api nyāya āśrīyanāṇo na virudhyate /
tena ca utkṛṣṭadṛṣṭi adhyāse śāstrārthe avadhāryamāṇe nikṛṣṭadṛṣṭim adhyasyan pratyaveyāt iti śliṣyate /
prāthamyāt ca ādityādi śabdānāṃ mukhyārthatvam avirodhāt gṛhītavyam /
taiḥ svārthavṛttibhiḥ avaruddhāyāṃ buddhau paścāt avatarato brahmaśabdasya mukhyayā vṛttyā sāmānādhikaraṇya asaṃbhavāt brahmadṛṣṭividhānārthata eva avatiṣṭhate /
itiparatvāt api brahmaśabdasya eṣa eva artho nyāyyaḥ /
tathā hi 'brahmetyādeśaḥ' 'brahmetyupāsīta' 'brahametyupāste' iti ca sarvatra itiparaṃ brahmaśabdam uccārayati śuddhān tu ādityādi śabdān /
tata- ca yathā śuktikāṃ rajatam iti pratyeti ityatra śuktivacana eva śuktikā śabdo rajataśabdaḥ tu rajatapratīti lakṣaṇārthaḥ /
pratyetyeva hi kevalaṃ rajatam iti na tu tatra rajatam asti /
evam atra api ādityādīn brahma iti pratīyāt iti gamyate /
vākyaśeṣaḥ api ca dvitīyānirdeśena ādityādīneva upāstikriyayā vyāpyamānān darśayati - 'sa ya etamevaṃ vidvānādityaṃ brahmetyupāste' (chā. 3.19.4), 'yo vācaṃ brahmetyupāste' (chā. 7.2.2), 'yaḥ saṃkalpaḥ brahmetyupāste' (chā. 7.4.3) iti ca /
yat tu uktaṃ brahma upāsanām eva atra ādaraṇīyaṃ phalatvāya iti /
tat ayuktam /
uktena nyāyena ādityādīnām eva upāsyatva avagamāt /
children.translated_text: Because, by the reasoning stated, it is understood that the sun and the like are the objects of meditation.

children.text: phalaṃ tu atithyādi upāsana iva ādityādi upāsane 'pi brahma eva dāsyati sarva adhyakṣatvāt /
children.translated_text: But the fruit will be given by <s>Brahman</s> alone — just as in the meditation on a guest (<s>atithi</s>) and the like, so too in the meditation on the sun and the like — because of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being the overseer of all.

children.text: varṇitaṃ ca etat 'phalamata upapatteḥ' (bra.sū. 3.2.38) iti atra /
children.translated_text: And this has been explained in [the discussion of] 'The fruit [proceeds] from That — because of tenability' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.2.38).

children.text: īdṛśaṃ ca atra brahmaṇa upāsyatvaṃ yat pratīkeṣu tat dṛṣṭi adhyāropaṇaṃ pratimādiṣu iva viṣṇu ādīnām // 5 //
children.translated_text: And the mode of <s>Brahman</s> being the object of meditation here is such that it consists in superimposing the vision of It upon <s>pratīkas</s> (symbols) — just as [one superimposes the vision of] <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like upon images and the like. // 5 //

To this we say: This would be so if the meaning of scripture were determined. But when it is in doubt, there is no contradiction in resorting to a worldly principle for the purpose of resolution.
And when, by that [worldly principle], the meaning of scripture is determined as the superimposition of an exalted vision, one who superimposes an inferior vision would suffer disadvantage — this fits [the principle].
Moreover, since the words '<s>āditya</s>' and the like come first [in the sentence], their primary meaning should be accepted — there being no contradiction.
When the intellect has been engaged by those [words] in their own literal meaning, the word '<s>Brahman</s>' — entering subsequently — since co-reference in its primary sense is not possible, remains with the sole purpose of prescribing the vision of <s>Brahman</s> [to be superimposed on the sun and the like].
Also because the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is preceded by '<s>iti</s>' — this very meaning is proper.
For thus, everywhere [the <s>śruti</s>] utters the word '<s>Brahman</s>' preceded by '<s>iti</s>': '<s>Brahman</s> — such is the instruction (<s>ādeśa</s>),' 'One should meditate [on it] as <s>Brahman</s>,' 'He meditates [on it] as <s>Brahman</s>' — while the words '<s>āditya</s>' and the like are used without '<s>iti</s>.' And therefore, just as in 'One perceives a shell as silver' — there the word 'shell' (<s>śuktikā</s>) denotes the shell [itself], while the word 'silver' (<s>rajata</s>) has the meaning of indicating the perception of silver [superimposed upon it] — for one merely perceives silver, but silver is not actually there — so too here, it is understood that one should perceive the sun and the like as <s>Brahman</s>.
And the remainder of the sentence, by the accusative case, shows that the sun and the like are the objects pervaded by the action of meditation: 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on the sun as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.19.4); 'He who meditates on speech as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.2.2); 'He who meditates on resolve (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) as <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.4.3) — and the like.
As for the objection that the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> alone should be valued here for the sake of bearing fruit — that is improper.

children.text: ādityādimati adhikaraṇam / sū. 6
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityādimati</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 6.

children.text: ādityādimatayaś cāṅga upapatteḥ | BBs_4,1.6 |
children.translated_text: The visions of the sun and the like [are to be superimposed] upon the limbs [of ritual] — because of tenability. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.6 |

children.text:
'ya evāsau tapati tamudgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.3.1), 'lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.2.1), 'vāci saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.8.1), 'iyamevargagniḥ sāma' (chā. 1.6.1) iti evamādiṣu aṅgāvabaddheṣu upāsaneṣu saṃśayaḥ kim ādityādiṣu udgīthādi dṛṣṭayo vidhīyante kiṃ vā udgīthādiṣu eva ādityādi dṛṣṭaya iti /
tatra aniyamo niyamakāraṇa abhāvāt iti prāptam /
na hi atra brahmaṇa iva kasyacit utkarṣaviśeṣaḥ avadhāryate 'brahma hi samasta jagat kāraṇatvāt apahatapāpmatvādi guṇayogāt ca ādityādibhya utkṛṣṭam iti śakyam avadhārayituṃ na tu āditya udgīthādīnāṃ vikāratva aviśeṣāt kañcit utkarṣaviśeṣa avadhāraṇe kāraṇam asti /
athavā niyamena udgīthādimataya ādityādiṣu adhyasyeran /
kasmāt /
karmātmakatvāt udgīthādīnāṃ karmaṇaḥ ca phalaprāptiprasiddheḥ /
udgīthādimatibhiḥ upāsyamānā ādityādayaḥ karmātmakāḥ santaḥ phalahetavo bhaviṣyanti /
tathā ca 'iyamevargagniḥ sāma'(chā. 1.6.1) iti atra 'tadetadetasyāmṛcyadhyūḍhaṃ sāma' (chā. 1.6.1) iti ṛkśabdena pṛthivīṃ nirdiśati sāmaśabdena agniṃ tat ca pṛthivi agnyoḥ rṛk sāmadṛṣṭicīkīrṣāyām avakalpate na ṛk sāmayoḥ pṛthivi agnidṛṣṭi cikīrṣāyām /
kṣattari hi rājadṛṣṭikaraṇāt rājaśabda upacaryate na rājani kṣattṛśabdaḥ /
api ca 'lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.2.1) iti adhikaraṇanirdeśāt lokeṣu sāma adhyasitavyam iti pratīyate /
'etadgāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protam' (chā. 2.11.1) iti ca etadevaṃ darśayati /
prathamanirdiṣṭeṣu ca ādityādiṣu caramanirdiṣṭaṃ brahma adhyastam 'ādityo brahmetyādeśaḥ' (chā. 3.19.1) ityādiṣu /
prathamanirdiṣṭāḥ ca pṛthivyādayaḥ caramanardiṣṭā hiṅkārādayaḥ 'pṛthivī hiṅkāraḥ' (chā. 2.2.1) ityādi śrutiṣu /
ataḥ
children.translated_text:
In [passages such as:] 'One should meditate on the <s>udgītha</s> as the sun that shines' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.3.1); 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.1); 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as sevenfold in speech' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.8.1); 'This earth indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>; fire is the <s>Sāman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.1) — in such meditations that are connected with ritual limbs, the doubt is: Are the visions of the sun and the like prescribed in the <s>udgītha</s> and the like, or are the visions of the <s>udgītha</s> and the like [prescribed] in the sun and the like?
The prima facie view is: There is no restriction, because there is no reason for restriction.
For here, unlike in the case of <s>Brahman</s>, no particular superiority is ascertainable — for <s>Brahman</s> can be ascertained as superior to the sun and the like because of being the cause of the entire universe and because of possessing qualities such as being free from evil and the like; but since the sun, the <s>udgītha</s>, and the like are equally modifications [of <s>Brahman</s>], there is no reason for ascertaining any particular superiority.
Alternatively, the prima facie view may be: The visions of the <s>udgītha</s> and the like should be restricted to [being superimposed upon] the sun and the like.
Why? Because the <s>udgītha</s> and the like are of the nature of <s>karma</s> (ritual action), and <s>karma</s> is well known to produce fruits.
When the sun and the like are meditated upon with the visions of the <s>udgītha</s> and the like, the sun and the like — becoming of the nature of <s>karma</s> — will become causes of fruit.
And thus, in 'This earth indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>; fire is the <s>Sāman</s>; the <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed upon this <s>Ṛc</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.1) — [the text] designates the earth by the word '<s>Ṛc</s>' and fire by the word '<s>Sāman</s>,' and this fits the intention of superimposing the vision of <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> on the earth and fire — not the intention of superimposing the vision of earth and fire on <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.
For when the vision of a king is superimposed on a door-keeper, the word 'king' is figuratively applied [to the door-keeper] — not the word 'door-keeper' to the king.
Moreover, 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.1) — because of the locative case designation, it is understood that the <s>Sāman</s> is to be superimposed in the worlds.
And 'This <s>Gāyatra</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] is woven in the <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.11.1) shows this very [point].
And in [passages where] the sun and the like are stated first and <s>Brahman</s> is stated last — '<s>Āditya</s> is <s>Brahman</s> — such is the instruction' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.19.1) and the like — <s>Brahman</s>, stated last, is superimposed on the sun and the like stated first.
And the earth and the like are stated first and the <s>hiṅkāra</s> and the like are stated last — in <s>śrutis</s> like 'The earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.1) and the like. Therefore,

children.text:
anaṅgeṣu ādityādiṣu aṅgam atinikṣepa iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ādityādimataya eva aṅgeṣu udgīthādiṣu kṣipyeran /
kutaḥ - upapatteḥ /
upapadyate hi evam apūrvasaṃnikarṣāt ādityādimatibhiḥ saṃskriyamāṇeṣu udgīthādiṣu karmasamṛddhiḥ /
'yadeva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tadeva vīryavattaraṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.10) iti ca vidyāyāḥ karmasamṛddhihetutvaṃ darśayati /
bhavatu karmasamṛddhiphaleṣu evaṃ, svatantraphaleṣu tu katham 'ya etadevaṃ vidvāṃllokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste' (chā. 2.2.3) ityādiṣu /
teṣu api adhikṛta adhikārāt prakṛta apūrvasaṃnikarṣeṇa eva phalakalpanā yuktā godohanādīniyamavat /
phalātmakatvāt ca ādityādīnām udgīthādibhyaḥ karmātmakebhya utkarṣa upapattiḥ ādityādiprāptilakṣaṇaṃ hi karmaphalaṃ śiṣyate śrutiṣu /
api ca 'omityetadakṣaramudgīthamupāsīta' (chā. 1.1.1) 'khalvetasyaivākṣarasyopavyākhyātaṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.10)
children.translated_text:
the [visions of] the non-limbs (<s>anaṅga</s>), namely the sun and the like, are superimposed upon the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>).
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: The visions of the sun and the like should be superimposed upon the limbs, the <s>udgītha</s> and the like.
Why? Because of tenability.
For it is tenable that when the <s>udgītha</s> and the like are enhanced by the visions of the sun and the like through the contact with something unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>), there is the enrichment of ritual action (<s>karmasamṛddhi</s>).
And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows that <s>vidyā</s> is the cause of the enrichment of <s>karma</s>: 'Whatever one performs with <s>vidyā</s>, with faith, with the <s>Upaniṣad</s>, that alone becomes more powerful' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10).
But granted this for meditations whose fruit is the enrichment of <s>karma</s> — how about those with independent fruit, such as 'He who, knowing thus, meditates on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.3) and the like?
In those cases too, since the eligible person has eligibility [for both], the proper [approach] is to devise the fruit precisely through the contact with the unprecedented [superimposition under discussion] — like the regulations regarding cow-milking and the like.
And because the sun and the like are of the nature of fruit, the superiority [of the sun and the like] over the <s>udgītha</s> and the like — which are of the nature of <s>karma</s> — is tenable; for the fruit of <s>karma</s>, taught in the <s>śrutis</s>, takes the form of attaining the sun and the like.
Moreover, 'One should meditate on the <s>udgītha</s> as the syllable <s>Om</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.1); 'It is indeed an exposition of this very syllable' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) —

children.text:
iti ca udgīthameva upāsyatvena upakramya ādityādimatīḥ vidadhāti /
yat tu uktam udgīthādimatibhiḥ upāsyamānā ādityādayaḥ karmabhūyaṃ bhūtvā phalaṃ kariṣyanti iti /
tat ayuktam /
svayameva upāsanasya karmatvāt phalavattva upapatteḥ /
ādityādibhāvena api ca dṛśyamānānām udgīthādīnāṃ karmātmakatvān apāyāt /
'tadetadetasyāmṛcyadhyūḍhaṃ sāma' (chā. 1.6.1) iti tu lākṣaṇika eva pṛthivī agnyoḥ ṛk sāmaśabdaprayogaḥ /
lakṣaṇā ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ saṃnikṛṣṭena viprakṛṣṭena vā svārthasaṃbandhena pravartate /
tatra yadi api ṛk sāmayoḥ pṛthivī agnyoḥ ca saṃnidhānayoreva eṣa ṛk sāmaśabdaprayoga ṛk sāmasaṃbandhāt iti niścīyate /
kṣattṛśabdaḥapi hi kutaścit kāraṇāt rājānam upasarpan na nivārayituṃ pāryate /
'iyamevarka'(chā. 1.6.1) iti ca yathā akṣaranyāsam ṛca eva pṛthivītvam avadhārayati /
pṛthivyā hi aktve avadhāryamāṇa iyam ṛk eva ityakṣaranyāsaḥ syāt /
'ya evaṃ vidvānsāma gāyati' (chā. 1.7.7) iti ca aṅgāśrayameva vijñānam upasaṃharati na pṛthivyādi āśrayam /
tathā 'lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.2.1) iti yadi api saptamīnirdiṣṭā lokāḥ tathāpi sāmnyeva te adhyasyeran dvitīyānirdeśena sāmna upāsyatva avagamāt /
sāmani hi lokeṣu adhyasyamāneṣu sāma lokātmana upāsitaṃ bhavati /
anyathā punaḥ lokāḥ sāmā ātmana upāsitāḥ syuḥ /
etena 'etadgāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protam' (chā. 2.11.1) ityādi vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: By this, [the passage] 'This <s>Gāyatra</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] is woven in the <s>prāṇas</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.11.1) and the like is also explained.

children.text: yatra api tulyo dvitīyanirdeśaḥ - 'atha khalvamumādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta' (chā. 2.9.1) iti, tatra api 'samastasya khalu sāmna upāsanaṃ sādhu' (chā. 2.8.1) 'iti ca pañcavidhasya' (chā. 2.7.2 ) 'atha saptavidhasya' (chā. 2.8.1) iti ca sāmna eva upāsyatva upakramāt tasmin eva ādityādi adhyāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: And even where there is an equal accusative-case designation — 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as sevenfold in the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.9.1) — even there, because of the introductory statement 'The meditation on the <s>Sāman</s> in its entirety is indeed good' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.8.1), and 'of the fivefold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.7.2), and 'now of the sevenfold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.8.1) — since the <s>Sāman</s> alone is introduced as the object of meditation, the superimposition of the sun and the like is upon it alone.

children.text: etasmāt eva ca sāmna upāsyatva avagamāt 'pṛthivī hiṅkāraḥ' (chā. 2.2.1) ityādinirdeśaviparyaye api hiṅkārādiṣu eva pṛthivyādi dṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: And precisely because of this understanding — that the <s>Sāman</s> is the object of meditation — even when the statement is reversed, as in 'The earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.1) and the like, the vision of the earth and the like is [to be superimposed] upon the <s>hiṅkāra</s> and the like alone.

children.text: tasmāt anaṅgāśrayā ādityādimatayaḥ aṅgeṣu udgīthādiṣu kṣipyeran iti siddham // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the visions of the sun and the like — which are based on non-limbs (<s>anaṅga</s>) — are to be superimposed upon the limbs [of ritual], the <s>udgītha</s> and the like. // 6 //

having thus introduced the <s>udgītha</s> itself as the object of meditation, [the <s>śruti</s>] prescribes the visions of the sun and the like [upon it].
As for the objection that was stated — that when the sun and the like are meditated upon with the visions of the <s>udgītha</s> and the like, they would become [of the nature of] <s>karma</s> and would produce fruit — that is improper.
Because <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation) itself being a <s>karma</s> (act), the tenability of its being fruit-bearing [is already established without this device].
And because, when the <s>udgītha</s> and the like are seen as [having the nature of] the sun and the like, their nature as <s>karma</s> would be lost.
As for 'The <s>Sāman</s> is superimposed upon this <s>Ṛc</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.1) — the use of the words '<s>Ṛc</s>' and '<s>Sāman</s>' for the earth and fire is figurative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>).
And figurative usage operates through a connection with the primary meaning — whether proximate or remote — as the case may be.
Therein, even though both [pairs] — <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> on the one hand, and earth and fire on the other — are equally proximate [in the passage], this use of the words '<s>Ṛc</s>' and '<s>Sāman</s>' is determined to be because of [the earth's and fire's] connection with [the actual] <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>.
For the word 'door-keeper' (<s>kṣattṛ</s>) too, approaching the king for some reason, cannot be prevented [from being applied figuratively to the king].
And 'This earth indeed is the <s>Ṛc</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.6.1) — according to the order of the words, [the <s>śruti</s>] determines the earth-hood of the <s>Ṛc</s> [i.e., the earth-vision is superimposed on the <s>Ṛc</s>].
For if earth-hood were being determined [for something], the word order would be: 'This <s>Ṛc</s> indeed is the earth.'
'He who, knowing thus, sings the <s>Sāman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.7.7) — this concludes the knowledge as based on the limb [of ritual] (<s>aṅga</s>) — not as based on the earth and the like.
As for 'One should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold in the worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 2.2.1) — even though the worlds are designated in the locative case, they should [nonetheless] be superimposed upon the <s>Sāman</s> alone — because of the understanding, from the accusative case, that the <s>Sāman</s> is the object of meditation.
For when the worlds are superimposed upon the <s>Sāman</s>, the <s>Sāman</s> is meditated upon as having the nature of the worlds.
Otherwise, the worlds would be meditated upon as having the nature of the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: 6 āsīna adhikaraṇam / sū. 7-10
children.translated_text: 6 The <s>Āsīna</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 7-10.

children.text: āsīnaḥ saṃbhavāt | BBs_4,1.7 |
children.translated_text: One should [meditate while] seated — because of feasibility. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.7 |

children.text:
karmāṅgasaṃbaddheṣu tāvat upāsaneṣu karmatantratvāt na āsanādicintā na api samyak darśane vastutantratvāt vijñānasya /
itareṣu tu upāsaneṣu kim aniyamena tiṣṭhan āsīnaḥ śayāno vā pravarteta uta niyamena āsīna eva iti cintayati /
tatra mānasatvāt upāsanasya aniyamaḥ śarīrasthiteḥ iti /
evaṃ prāpte bravīti - āsīna eva upāsīta iti /
kutaḥ - saṃbhavāt /
upāsanaṃ nāma samānapratyayapravāhakaraṇaṃ na ca tat gacchato dhāvato vā saṃbhavati gatyādīnāṃ cittavikṣepakatvāt /
children.translated_text: Meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>) is the maintenance of a continuous flow of the same cognition. And this is not possible for one who is walking or running — because walking and the like cause distraction of the mind.

children.text: tiṣṭhataḥ api dehadhāraṇe vyāpṛtaṃ mano na sūkṣmavastunirīkṣaṇakṣamaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Even for one standing, the mind — occupied with sustaining the body — is not capable of observing subtle objects.

children.text: śayānasya api akasmāt eva nidrayā abhibhūyeta /
children.translated_text: Even for one lying down, one might suddenly be overcome by sleep.

children.text: āsīnasya tu evañjātīyako bhūyān doṣaḥ suparihara iti saṃbhavati tasya upāsanam // 7 //
children.translated_text: But for one seated, faults of this kind are largely avoidable — therefore, meditation is possible for the seated one. // 7 //

In meditations connected with the limbs of ritual action, because they are dependent on the ritual, there is no inquiry into sitting posture and the like; nor in right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), because knowledge is dependent on the reality [of its object, not on bodily posture].
But in other meditations, the question arises: Should one proceed without restriction — standing, sitting, or lying down — or should one proceed with the restriction of sitting alone?
The prima facie view is: Because meditation is mental, there is no restriction regarding bodily posture.
Having stated this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: One should meditate while seated alone.
Why? Because of feasibility.

children.text: dhyānāc ca | BBs_4,1.8 |
children.translated_text: And because of [the meaning of the word] '<s>dhyāna</s>' (meditation). | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.8 |

children.text: api ca dhyāyati arthaṃ eṣa yat samānapratyayapravāhakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, this maintaining of a continuous flow of the same cognition is what [the root] '<s>dhyai</s>' (to meditate) means.

children.text: dhyāyatiḥ ca praśithila aṅgaceṣṭeṣu pratiṣṭhitadṛṣṭiṣu ekaviṣaya ākṣiptacitteṣu upacaryamāṇo dṛśyate dhyāyati bako dhyāyati proṣitabandhuḥ iti /
children.translated_text: And the [usage of] 'meditates' is observed figuratively for those who have relaxed limbs, fixed gaze, and mind absorbed in a single object — 'The crane meditates,' 'The woman whose loved one is away meditates.'

children.text: āsīnaḥ ca anāyāso bhavati /
children.translated_text: And one who is seated is without strain.

children.text: tasmāt api āsīnakarma upāsanam // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, from this too, meditation is an activity of the seated. // 8 //

children.text: acalatvaṃ cāpekṣya | BBs_4,1.9 |
children.translated_text: And with reference to motionlessness. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.9 |

children.text: api ca 'dhyāyatīva pṛthivī' (chā. 7.6.1) iti atra pṛthivyādiṣu acalatvameva apekṣya dhyāyativādo bhavati tat ca liṅgam upāsanasya āsīnakarmatve // 9 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, in 'The earth, as it were, meditates' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.6.1), the usage of 'meditates' for the earth and the like is made with reference to motionlessness alone. And this is an indication (<s>liṅga</s>) that meditation is an activity of the seated. // 9 //

children.text: smaranti ca | BBs_4,1.10 |
children.translated_text: And the <s>smṛtis</s> [say so]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.10 |

children.text: smaranti api ca śiṣṭā upāsana aṅgatvena āsanam - 'śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ' (gī. 6.11) ityādinā /
children.translated_text: And the learned authorities (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) too record a seat (<s>āsana</s>) as an auxiliary of meditation: 'Having established a firm seat for oneself in a clean place' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 6.11) and the like.

children.text: ata eva padmakādīnām āsanaviśeṣāṇām upadeśo yogaśāstre // 10 //
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, in the <s>Yoga-śāstra</s>, the teaching of specific seats such as the lotus posture (<s>padmaka</s>) and the like [is given]. // 10 //

children.text: 7 ekāgratā adhikaraṇam / sū. 11
children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Ekāgratādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of One-pointedness). <s>Sūtra</s> 11.

children.text: yatraikāgratā tatrāviśeṣāt | BBs_4,1.11 |
children.translated_text: Wherever there is one-pointedness — because of the non-difference [in that regard everywhere]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.11 |

children.text:
dik deśakāleṣu saṃśayaḥ - kim asti kaścit niyamo na asti vā iti /
prāyeṇa vaidikeṣu ārambheṣu digādiniyamadarśanāt syāt iha api kaścit niyama iti yasya matiḥ taṃ prati āha dik deśakāleṣu arthalakṣaṇa eva niyamaḥ /
yatra eva asya diśi deśe kāle vā manasaḥ sokaryeṇa ekāgratā bhavati tatra eva upāsīta prācīdik pūrvāhna prācīna pravaṇādivat viśeṣa aśrāvaṇāt /
ekāgratayā iṣṭāyāḥ sarvatra aviśeṣāt /
children.translated_text:
Regarding direction, place, and time, a doubt [arises]: Is there some restriction, or not?
For one who thinks 'There should be some restriction here too, since restriction of direction and the like is generally observed in Vedic undertakings,' to such a person [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: The restriction regarding direction, place, and time is determined by the purpose alone.
Wherever — in whatever direction, place, or time — one-pointedness of mind arises easily for him, there alone one should meditate — because no specific [direction, place, or time] is heard, unlike the east-facing direction, the forenoon, the east-sloping [ground], and the like.
Because one-pointedness, which is what is desired, does not differ anywhere.

children.text: nanu viśeṣam api kecit āmananti - 'same śucau kharkarāvahnivālukāvivarjite śabdajalāśrayādibhiḥ /
manonukūle natu cakṣupīḍane guhānivātāśrayaṇe prayojayet' (śve. 2.10) iti yathā iti /
children.translated_text: in a place agreeable to the mind but not painful to the eyes — in a cave, in a windless shelter, one should practice' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 2.10).

children.text: ucyate - satyam asti evañjātīyako niyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is said: True, such a restriction does exist.

children.text: sati tu etasmin tadgateṣu viśeṣaniyama iti suhṛt bhūtvā ācārya ācaṣṭe /
children.translated_text: But this being so, the specific restriction regarding [the details] within that [general condition] — the teacher states it as a friend [offering helpful guidance].

children.text: 'manonukūle' iti ca eṣā śrutiḥ yatra ekāgratā tatra eva iti etat eva darśayati // 11 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> 'agreeable to the mind' shows precisely this — that wherever there is one-pointedness, there alone [one should meditate]. // 11 //
But some do teach specific [conditions]: 'On level, clean [ground], free from pebbles, fire, and sand, free from sounds, water, and shelters;

children.text: 8 āprāyaṇa adhikaraṇam / sū. 12
children.translated_text: 8. The <s>Āprāyaṇādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of [Repetition] Until Death). <s>Sūtra</s> 12.

children.text: ā prayāṇāt tatrāpi hi dṛṣṭam | BBs_4,1.12 |
children.translated_text: Until departure [from the body] — for even there [at the time of death] this is observed. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.12 |

children.text:
āvṛttiḥ sarva upāsaneṣu ādartavya iti sthitam ādye adhikaraṇe /
tatra yāni tāvat samyak darśanārthāni upāsanāni tāni avaghātādivat kāryaparyavasānāni iti jñātameva eṣām āvṛttiparimāṇam /
na hi samyak darśane kārye niṣpanne yatnāntaraṃ kiñcit śāsituṃ śakyam /
aniyojyabrahmātmatvapratipatteḥ śāstrasya aviṣayatvāt /
yāni punaḥ abhyudayaphalāni teṣu eṣā cintā kiṃ kiyantañcit kālaṃ pratyayam āvartya uparamet uta yāvajjīvam āvartayet iti /
kiṃ tāvat prāptam /
kiyantañcit kālaṃ pratyayam abhyasya utsṛjet āvṛttiviśiṣṭasya upāsanaśabdārthasya kṛtatvāt iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - āprāyaṇāt eva āvartayet pratyayam /
antyapratyayavaśāt adṛṣṭaphalaprāpteḥ /
karmāṇi api hi janmāntara upabhogyaṃ phalam ārabhamāṇāni tat anurūpaṃ bhāvanāvijñānaṃ prāyaṇakāla ākṣipanti, 'savijñāno bhavati savijñānamevānvavakrāmati' 'yaccittastenaiṣa prāṇamāyāti, prāṇastejasā yuktaḥ sahātmanā yathāsaṃkalpitaṃ lokaṃ nayati' iti ca evamādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tṛṇajalūkānidarśanāt ca /
pratyayāḥ tu ete svarūpa anuvṛttiṃ muktvā kim anyat prāyaṇakālabhāvi bhāvanāvijñānam apekṣeran /
tasmāt ye pratipattavyaphalabhāvanātmakāḥ pratyayaḥ teṣu aprāyaṇāt āvṛttiḥ /
tathā ca śrutiḥ -'sa yāvatkraturayamasmāllokātpraiti' iti prāyaṇakāle api pratyaya anuvṛttiṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'As is his intention when he departs from this world' — shows the continuity of cognition even at the time of death.

children.text: smṛtiḥ api - 'yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram /
children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s> too: 'Whatever being one remembers at the time of leaving the body,

children.text: taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ' (gī. 8.6) iti 'prayāṇakāle manasācalena' (gī. 8.10) iti ca /
children.translated_text: that alone one attains, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, being always absorbed in that [thought]' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.6); and 'At the time of death, with an unwavering mind' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.10).

children.text: 'so 'ntavelāyāmetattrayaṃ pratipadyeta' iti ca maraṇavelāyām api kartavyaśeṣaṃ śrāvayati // 12 //
children.translated_text: 'At the final hour, one should realize these three' — this teaches a remaining duty even at the time of death. // 12 //

Repetition (<s>āvṛtti</s>) is to be observed in all meditations — this was established in the first topic.
Of these, the meditations aimed at right knowledge (<s>samyag darśana</s>) — like [repeated] striking — culminate in their effect. Their measure of repetition is already known.
For once right knowledge — the effect — has been accomplished, no further effort can be enjoined.
Because the realization of one's <s>Brahman</s>-nature, which is not subject to injunction, falls outside the scope of scripture.
But regarding those [meditations] whose fruit is prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>), the inquiry is: Should one repeat the cognition for a limited time and then stop, or should one repeat it lifelong?
What is the prima facie view? One should practice the cognition for a limited time and then give it up — because the meaning of the word '<s>upāsanā</s>' (meditation), characterized by repetition, will have been fulfilled.
Given this position, we say: One should repeat the cognition until the time of departure from the body.
Because the attainment of the unseen fruit depends on the last cognition [at death].
For even <s>karmas</s> — when commencing a fruit to be enjoyed in another life — attract, at the time of death, a mental disposition and knowledge corresponding to that [fruit]: 'He becomes endowed with knowledge, he departs endowed with knowledge'; 'With whatever [thought] his mind [is occupied], with that he goes to <s>prāṇa</s>; <s>prāṇa</s>, united with fire, along with the self, leads [him] to the world that has been contemplated' — from <s>śruti</s> passages of this kind.
And from the illustration of the caterpillar (<s>tṛṇajalūkā</s>) [reaching toward the next blade before leaving the current one].
But these cognitions — what other mental disposition at the time of death would they require, other than their own continued repetition?
Therefore, for those cognitions whose nature is the mental disposition leading to the fruit to be attained, repetition [should be practiced] until death.

children.text: 9 tat adhigama adhikaraṇam / sū. 13
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Tadadhigamādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Attainment of That [<s>Brahman</s>]). <s>Sūtra</s> 13.

children.text: tadadhigama uttarapūrvāghayor aśleṣavināśau tadvyapadeśāt | BBs_4,1.13 |
children.translated_text: Upon the attainment of That [<s>Brahman</s>], there is non-attachment to subsequent [<s>karma</s>] and destruction of prior [<s>karma</s>] — because of the statement to that effect. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.13 |

children.text:
gataḥ tṛtīyaśeṣaḥ /
atha idānīṃ brahmavidyāphalaṃ prati cintā pratāyate /
brahma adhigame sati tat viparītaphalaṃ duritaṃ kṣīyate na kṣīyate vā iti saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvat prāptam /
phalārthatvāt karmaṇaḥ phalam adatvā na saṃbhāvyate kṣayaḥ /
phaladāyinī hi asya śaktiḥ śrutyā samadhigatā /
yadi tadantareṇa eva phala upabhogam apavṛjyeta śrutiḥ kadarthitā syāt /
smaranti ca 'nahi karma kṣīyate' iti /
children.translated_text:
The remainder of the third [<s>adhyāya</s>] has been completed.
Now, reflection on the fruit of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge is set forth.
When <s>Brahman</s> is attained [through knowledge], the question arises: Is the sin (<s>durita</s>) — which produces the opposite fruit — destroyed, or not?
What is the prima facie view?
Because <s>karma</s> is for the purpose of [producing] fruit, it is not conceivable that it would be destroyed without giving its fruit.
For its fruit-producing capacity is ascertained from <s>śruti</s>.
If it were to lose its force without the experience of the fruit, the <s>śruti</s> would be rendered meaningless.
And the <s>smṛti</s> says: 'Karma is never destroyed.'

children.text: nanu evaṃ sati prāyaścitta upadeśaḥanarthakaḥ prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: But in that case, the teaching of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) would become purposeless.

children.text:
na eṣa doṣaḥ /
prāyaścittānāṃ naimittikatva upapatteḥ gṛhadāha iṣṭyādivat /
api ca prāyaścittānāṃ doṣasaṃyogena vidānāt bhavet api doṣakṣapaṇārthatā na tu evaṃ brahmavidyāyāṃ vidhānam asti /
children.translated_text:
This is not a fault.
Because <s>prāyaścittas</s> can be understood as occasional duties (<s>naimittika</s>) — like the fire-oblation (<s>iṣṭi</s>) performed upon the burning of a house.
Moreover, because <s>prāyaścittas</s> are enjoined in conjunction with faults, they may indeed have the purpose of removing faults — but no such injunction exists for <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge.

children.text: nanu anabhyupagamyamāne brahmavidaḥ karmakṣaye tatphalasya avaśyaṃ bhoktavyatāvāt anirmokṣaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: But if the destruction of <s>karma</s> by the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is not accepted, then — because the fruit [of <s>karma</s>] must necessarily be experienced — there would be no liberation.

children.text:
na iti ucyate /
deśakālanimittāpekṣo mokṣaḥ karmaphalavat bhaviṣyati /
tasmāt na brahma adhigame duritanivṛttiḥ iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ- tat adhigame brahma adhigame sati uttarapūrvayoḥ aghayoḥ aśleṣavināśau bhavataḥ uttarasya aśleṣaḥ pūrvasya vināśaḥ /
kasmāt /
tat vyapadeśāt /
tathā hi brahmavidyā prakriyāyāṃ saṃbhāvyamānasaṃbandhasya āgāmino duritasya anabhisaṃbandhaṃ viduṣo vyapadiśati - 'yathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evamevaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate' (chā.4.14.3) iti /
tathā vināśam api pūrva ucitasya duritasya vyapadiśati - 'tadyatheṣīkātūlamagnau protaṃ pradūyetaivaṃ hāsya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante' (chā. 5.24.3) iti /
ayam aparaḥ karmakṣayavyapadeśo bhavati - 'bhidyate hṛdayagranthiśchidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ /
kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare' (mu. 2.2.8) iti /
yat uktam anupabhuktaphalasya karmaṇaḥ kṣayakalpanāyāṃ śāstraṃ kadarthitaṃ syāt iti /
children.translated_text:
No, it is said.
Liberation, like the fruit of <s>karma</s>, will come about in dependence on place, time, and occasion.
Therefore, there is no destruction of sin upon the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>.
Given this position, we say: Upon the attainment of That — upon the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> — there is non-attachment (<s>aśleṣa</s>) to subsequent sin and destruction (<s>vināśa</s>) of prior sin. Non-attachment for the subsequent; destruction for the prior.
Why?
Because of the statement to that effect.
For thus, in the context of the procedure of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, [the <s>śruti</s>] declares the non-attachment of forthcoming sin — whose connection [with the knower] is anticipated — to the knower: 'As water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so evil action does not cling to one who knows thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.14.3).
Likewise, [the <s>śruti</s>] declares the destruction of previously accumulated sin: 'Just as a ball of cotton thread, when thrown into fire, is burnt up — so all his sins are burnt up' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.24.3).
Here is another statement declaring the destruction of <s>karma</s>: 'The knot of the heart is pierced, all doubts are resolved, and all his <s>karmas</s> are destroyed — when That which is both the higher and the lower is seen' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.8).
As for the objection that imagining the destruction of <s>karma</s> whose fruit has not been experienced would render scripture meaningless —

children.text:
na eṣa doṣaḥ /
na hi vayaṃ karmaṇaḥ phaladāyinīṃ śaktim avajānīmahe, vidyata eva sā, sā tu vidyādinā kāraṇāntareṇa pratibadhyata iti vadāmaḥ /
śaktisadbhāvamātre ca śāstraṃ vyāpriyate na pratibandha apratibandhayoḥ api /
na hi karma kṣīyata iti etat api smaraṇam autsargikaṃ na bhogāt ṛte karma kṣīyata tadarthatvāt iti /
iṣyata eva tu prāyaścittādinā tasya kṣayaḥ 'sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ tarati' 'tarati brahmahatyāṃ yo 'śvamedhena yajate ya u cainameva vada' ityādi śrutismṛtibhyaḥ /
yat tu uktaṃ naimittikāni prāyaścittāni bhaviṣyanti iti /
tat asat /
doṣasaṃyogena codyamānānām eṣāṃ doṣanirghātaphalasaṃbhave phalāntarakalpanā anupapatteḥ /
yatpunaḥ etat uktaṃ na prāyaścittavat doṣakṣaya uddeśena vidyāvidānam asti iti /
atra brūmaḥ - saguṇāsu tāvat vidyāsu vidyata eva vidhānam /
tāsu ca vākyaśeṣa aiśvaryaprāptiḥ pāpanivṛttiḥ ca vidyāvata ucyate /
tayoḥ ca avivakṣākāraṇaṃ na asti iti ataḥ pāpmaprahāṇapūrvaka aiśvaryaprāptiḥ tāsāṃ phalam iti niścīyate /
nirguṇāyāṃ tu vidyāyāṃ yadi api vidhānaṃ na asti tathā api akartṛ ātmatvabodhāt karmapradāhasiddhiḥ /
aśleṣa iti ca āgāmiṣu karmasu kartṛtvameva na pratipadyate brahmavit iti darśayati /
atikrānteṣu tu yadi api mithyājñānāt kartṛtvaṃ pratipeda iva tathā api vidyāsāmarthyāt mithyājñānanivṛtteḥ tāni api pravilīyanta iti āha vināśa iti /
pūrvasiddhakartṛtva bhoktṛtva viparītaṃ hi triṣu api kāleṣu akartṛtva abhoktṛtvasvarūpaṃ brahma aham asmi na itaḥ pūrvam api kartā bhoktā vā aham āsaṃ na idānīṃ na api bhaviṣyatkāla iti brahmavit avagacchati /
evam eva ca mokṣa upapadyate /
anyathā hi anādikālapravṛttānāṃ karmāṇāṃ kṣayābhāve mokṣa abhāvaḥ syāt /
na ca deśakālanimittāpekṣo mokṣaḥ karmaphalavat bhavitum arhati /
children.translated_text: And liberation cannot be like the fruit of <s>karma</s> — dependent on place, time, and occasion.

children.text: anityatva prasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because [that] would entail impermanence.

children.text: parokṣatva anupapatteḥ ca jñānaphalam /
children.translated_text: And because the fruit of knowledge cannot be indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>).

children.text: tasmāt brahma adhigame duritakṣaya iti sthiram // 13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the destruction of sin upon the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> is firmly established. // 13 //

This is not a fault.
For we do not deny the fruit-producing capacity of <s>karma</s>; that capacity indeed exists. But we say that it is obstructed by another cause — namely, knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and the like.
And scripture concerns itself only with the existence of the capacity — not with [the question of whether there is] obstruction or non-obstruction.
And the <s>smṛti</s> statement 'Karma is never destroyed' too is a general rule (<s>autsargika</s>) — [meaning that] <s>karma</s> is not destroyed without experience [of its fruit], because it exists for that purpose. But its destruction through <s>prāyaścitta</s> and the like is indeed accepted — from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> passages such as 'He crosses over all sin,' 'He who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> — and he who knows this — crosses over even the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s>' and the like.
As for the statement that <s>prāyaścittas</s> will be occasional duties (<s>naimittika</s>) —
that is incorrect.
Because these [<s>prāyaścittas</s>], being enjoined in conjunction with faults, when the possibility of the fruit being the removal of those faults exists, it is untenable to imagine a different fruit.
As for the further statement that there is no injunction of knowledge for the purpose of removing faults, as there is for <s>prāyaścitta</s> —
to this we say: In the case of meditations on the qualified <s>Brahman</s> (<s>saguṇa vidyā</s>), there is indeed an injunction.
And in those, the remainder of the passage teaches both the attainment of sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) and the removal of sin for the knower.
And there is no reason to leave either of these unintended. Therefore, the fruit of those [meditations] is determined as the attainment of sovereignty preceded by the removal of sin.
But in the case of the meditation on the attributeless <s>Brahman</s> (<s>nirguṇa vidyā</s>) — even if there is no injunction as such — nevertheless, through the realization that the Self is a non-agent, the burning up of <s>karma</s> is accomplished.
And [the word] 'non-attachment' (<s>aśleṣa</s>) shows that regarding future <s>karmas</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> does not assume agency at all.
And regarding past [<s>karmas</s>] — even though, through false knowledge, he had, as it were, assumed agency — nevertheless, through the power of knowledge, since false knowledge is removed, those too are dissolved — this is indicated by [the word] 'destruction.'
For the knower of <s>Brahman</s> realizes: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature — in all three times — is non-agency and non-experiencership, the opposite of the previously established agency and experiencership. Not in the past was I ever an agent or experiencer, nor now, nor in the future.'
And only thus is liberation tenable.
For otherwise — if the <s>karmas</s> accumulated since beginningless time were not destroyed — there would be no liberation.

children.text: 10 itara asaṃśleṣa adhikaraṇam / sū. 14
children.translated_text: 10. The <s>Itarāsaṃśleṣādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Non-attachment to the Other [Merit]). <s>Sūtra</s> 14.

children.text: itarasyāpy evam asaṃśleṣaḥ pāte tu | BBs_4,1.14 |
children.translated_text: For the other [i.e., merit] too, likewise there is non-attachment — but [its effects persist] until the fall [of the present body]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,1.14 |

children.text:
pūrvasmin adhikaraṇe bandhahetoḥ aghasya svābhāvikasya aśleṣavināśau jñānanimittau śāstravyapadeśāt nirūpitau /
dharmasya punaḥ śāstrīyatvāt śāstrīyeṇa jñānena avirodha iti āśaṅkya tat nirākaraṇāya pūrva adhikaraṇanyāya atideśaḥ kriyate /
itarasya api puṇyasya karmaṇa evam aghavat asaṃśleṣo vināśaḥ ca jñānavato bhavataḥ /
kutaḥ - tasya api svaphalahetutvena jñānaphalapratibandhitvaprasaṅgāt /
'ubhe u haivaiṣa ete tarati' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityādiśrutiṣu ca duṣkṛtavat sukṛtasya api praṇāśavyapadeśāt /
akartṛ ātmatvabodhanimittasya ca karmakṣayasya sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ tulyatvāt 'kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi' (mu. 2.2.8) iti ca aviśeṣaśruteḥ /
yatra api kevala eva pāpmaśabdo dṛśyate tatra api tena eva puṇyam api akalitam iti draṣṭavyam /
jñānaphala apekṣayā nikṛṣṭaphalatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because [merit has] an inferior fruit compared to the fruit of knowledge.

children.text: asti ca śrutau puṇye api pāpmaśabdaḥ 'nainaṃ setumahorātre tarataḥ' (chā. 8.4.1) iti atra saha duṣkṛtena sakṛtamapi anukramya sarve pāpmānaḥ ato nivartanta iti aviśeṣeṇa eva prakṛte puṇye pāpmaśabdaprayogāt /
children.translated_text: And in <s>śruti</s>, the word '<s>pāpman</s>' (sin) is used even for merit: In 'Neither day nor night crosses this bridge' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.1) — there, having enumerated both evil deeds and good deeds together, [the text says] 'all sins turn back from here' — because the word '<s>pāpman</s>' is used without distinction even for merit that is under discussion.

children.text: pāte tu iti tu śabdaḥ avadhāraṇārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) in 'upon the fall [of the body]' is for the purpose of emphasis.

children.text: evaṃ dharma adharmayoḥ bandhahetvoḥ vidyāsāmarthyāt aśleṣavināśasiddheḥ avaśyaṃbhāvinī viduṣaḥ śarīrapāte muktiḥ iti avadhārayati // 14//
children.translated_text: Thus — since the non-clinging and destruction of both <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, which are the causes of bondage, are established through the power of knowledge — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] determines that liberation upon the fall of the body is inevitable for the knower. // 14 //

In the preceding topic, the non-attachment and destruction of sin — the cause of bondage, which is natural [to the <s>jīva</s>] — were established as caused by knowledge, from the scriptural statement.
But because <s>dharma</s> (merit) is scriptural [i.e., enjoined by scripture], one might suspect that there is no conflict between it and scriptural knowledge. To remove that [suspicion], the principle of the preceding topic is extended.
For the other too — for meritorious <s>karma</s> as well — just as for sin, non-attachment and destruction occur for the knower.
Why? Because that [merit] too, by being the cause of its own fruit, would obstruct the fruit of knowledge.
And in <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'He indeed crosses over both' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22), the destruction of merit too, like that of sin, is declared.
And because the destruction of <s>karma</s> — caused by the realization that the Self is a non-agent — is the same for both merit and sin: 'And all his <s>karmas</s> are destroyed' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.8) — because of this <s>śruti</s> that makes no distinction.
Even where only the word '<s>pāpman</s>' (sin) is seen, there too it should be understood that merit is included by it.

children.text: 11 anārabdha adhikaraṇam / sū. 15
children.translated_text: 11. <s>Anārabdhādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 15

children.text: anārabdhakārye eva tu pūrve tadavadheḥ | BBs_4,1.15 |
children.translated_text: But [the destruction applies] only to those [<s>karmas</s>] whose effects have not yet begun — because of the limit set by that [i.e., the fall of the body]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.15 |

children.text:
pūrvayoḥ adhikaraṇayoḥ jñānanimittaḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ vināśaḥ avadhāritaḥ sa kim aviśeṣeṇa ārabdhakāryayoḥ anārabdhakāryayoḥ ca bhavati uta viśeṣeṇa anārabdhakāryayoḥ eva iti vicāryate /
'tatra ubhe u haivaiṣa ete tarati' (bṛ. 4.4.22) iti evamādiśrutiṣu aviśeṣaśravaṇāt aviśeṣeṇa eva kṣaya iti /
evaṃ prāpte pratyāha - anārabdhakārye eva tu iti /
apravṛttaphale eva pūrve janmāntarasaṃcite asmin api ca janmani prāk jñāna utpatteḥ saṃcite sukṛtaduṣkṛte jñāna adhigamāt kṣīyete na tu ārabdhakārye sāmibhuktaphale yābhyām etat brahmajñāna āyatanaṃ janma nirmitam /
kuta etat - 'tasya tāvadeva ciraṃ yāvanna vimokṣye 'tha saṃpatsye' (chā. 6.14.2) iti śarīrapātau adhikaraṇāt kṣemaprāpteḥ /
itarathā hi jñānāt aśeṣakarmakṣaye sati sthitihetu abhāvāt jñānaprāpti anantarameva kṣemamśnu avīta, tatra śarīrapātapratīkṣāṃ na ācakṣīta /
children.translated_text: In the two previous topics, the destruction of merit and demerit caused by knowledge has been determined. The question is: Does this [destruction] apply without distinction to both — <s>karma</s> whose effects have already begun (<s>ārabdhakārya</s>) and <s>karma</s> whose effects have not yet begun (<s>anārabdhakārya</s>) — or does it apply specifically only to that whose effects have not yet begun? From the undifferentiated hearing in <s>śrutis</s> such as 'There indeed he crosses over both' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22), the destruction would apply without distinction — [this is the prima facie view]. Given this position, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] replies: 'But only to those whose effects have not yet begun.' Only those merit and demerit whose fruit has not yet commenced — those accumulated in previous births and also those accumulated in this birth prior to the arising of knowledge — are destroyed through the attainment of knowledge; but not those whose effects have already begun and whose fruit is being enjoyed — those by which this very birth, the abode of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge, has been produced. How is this known? Because of the <s>śruti</s> 'For him, the delay is only so long until he is freed [from the body]; then he will attain' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.14.2) — which postpones the attainment of the goal to the fall of the body. For otherwise, if all <s>karma</s> whatsoever were destroyed through knowledge, then — since the cause of continued existence would be absent — one would attain the goal immediately after the attainment of knowledge, and [the <s>śruti</s>] would not speak of waiting for the fall of the body.

children.text:
nanu vastubalena eva ayam akartṛ ātmāvabodhaḥ karmāṇi kṣapayan kathaṃ kānicit kṣapayet kānicit ca upekṣeta /
na hi samāne agnibījasaṃparke keṣāñcit bījaśaktiḥ kṣīyate keṣāñcit na kṣīyata iti śakyam aṅgīkartum iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: This knowledge of the Self as non-agent, being of the nature of reality itself, while destroying <s>karmas</s>, how could it destroy some and disregard others? For it is not possible to accept that, in the same contact of fire with seeds, the potency of some seeds is destroyed while that of others is not.

children.text:
ucyate - na tāvat anāśritya ārabdhakāryaṃ karmāśayaṃ jñāna utpattiḥ upapadyate /
āśrite ca tasmin kulālacakravat pravṛttavegasya antarāle pratibandha asaṃbhavāt bhavati vegakṣayapratipālanam /
akartṛ ātmabodhaḥ api hi mithyājñānabādhanena karmāṇi ucchinatti /
bādhitam api tu mithyājñānaṃ dvicandrajñānavat saṃskāravaśāt kañcitkālam anuvartata eva /
api ca na eva atra vivaditavyaṃ brahmavidā kañcitkālaṃ śarīraṃ dhriyate na vā dhriyata iti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is no need to dispute here whether the body is sustained for some time by the knower of <s>Brahman</s> or not.

children.text: kathaṃ hi ekasya svahṛdayapratyayaṃ brahmavedanaṃ dehadhāraṇaṃ ca apareṇa pratikṣeptuṃ śakyeta /
children.translated_text: For how could another person deny the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> and the sustaining of the body — which are matters of one's own inner experience?

children.text: śrutismṛtiṣu ca sthitaprajñalakṣaṇanirdeśena etadeva nirucyate /
children.translated_text: And in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, this very [point] is elucidated through the description of the characteristics of one who is firmly established in wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>).

children.text: tasmāt anārabdhakāryayoḥ eva sukṛtaduṣkṛtayoḥ vidyāsāmarthyāt kṣaya iti nirṇayaḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is determined that only the merit and demerit whose effects have not yet begun are destroyed through the power of knowledge. // 15 //

We reply: The arising of knowledge is not possible without depending on the <s>karma</s>-residue whose effects have already begun. And once that [<s>karma</s>] has been resorted to — like a potter's wheel whose momentum has been set in motion — since obstruction in the interim is impossible, one must wait for the exhaustion of its momentum. The knowledge of the Self as non-agent too destroys <s>karmas</s> by sublating false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>). But false knowledge, even when sublated, continues for some time due to the force of impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — like the perception of a double moon.

children.text: 12 agnihotrādi adhikaraṇam / sū. 16-17
children.translated_text: 12. <s>Agnihotrādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtras</s> 16-17

children.text: agnihotrādi tu tatkāryāyaiva taddarśanāt | BBs_4,1.16 |
children.translated_text: But the <s>Agnihotra</s> and such [are performed] for the sake of that very effect [of knowledge] — because of the observation of that. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.16 |

children.text:
puṇyasya api aśleṣavināśayoḥ aghanyāyaḥ atidiṣṭaḥ saḥ atideśaḥ sarvapuṇyaviṣaya iti āśaṅkya prativakti - agnihotrādi tu iti /
tu śabda āśaṅkām upanudati /
yat nityaṃ karma vaidikam agnihotrādi tat tat kāryāya eva bhavati, jñānasya yatkāryaṃ tadeva asya api kāryam ityarthaḥ /
kutaḥ - 'tametaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena' (bṛ. 4.4.22) ityādidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: The principle applied to sin — of non-clinging and destruction — has been extended to merit as well. Apprehending that this extension applies to all merit, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] replies: 'But the <s>Agnihotra</s> and such.' The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) dispels the apprehension. The permanent Vedic actions such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like — they serve that very effect [of knowledge]: the effect of knowledge is their effect too — this is the meaning. Why? Because of the observation [in <s>śruti</s>]: 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know It through Vedic recitation, sacrifice, charity' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.22) and the like.

children.text: nanu jñānakarmaṇoḥ vilakṣaṇakāryatvāt kārya ekatva anupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since knowledge and action have entirely different effects, the unity of their effect is not tenable.

children.text:
na eṣa doṣaḥ /
jvaramaraṇakāryayoḥ api dadhiviṣayoḥ guḍamantrasaṃyuktayoḥ tṛptipuṣṭikāryadarśanāt /
tadvat karmaṇaḥ api jñānasaṃyuktasya mokṣakārya upapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.
