For even curd and poison — which [ordinarily] cause fever and death — when combined with jaggery and <s>mantras</s>, are observed to cause satisfaction and nourishment. Similarly, action too, when combined with knowledge, can produce the effect of liberation.

children.text: nanu anārabhyo mokṣaḥ katham asya karmakāryatvam ucyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: But liberation is not something to be produced — so how can it be called the effect of action?

children.text:
na eṣa doṣaḥ /
ārāt upakārakatvāt karmaṇaḥ /
jñānasya eva hi prāpakaṃ satkarma prāṇāḍyā mokṣakāraṇam iti upacaryate /
ata eva ca atikrāntaviṣayam etat kārya ekatva abhidhānam /
na hi brahmavida āgāmi agnihotrādi saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: For there is no possibility of future <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: aniyojyabrahmātmatva pratipatteḥ śāstrasya aviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because, having realized the Self as <s>Brahman</s> — which is not subject to injunction — the scriptures [of injunction] have no domain [over him].

children.text: saguṇāsu tu vidyāsu kartṛtva anativṛtteḥ saṃbhavati āgāmi api agnihotrādi /
children.translated_text: But in the case of <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>vidyās</s>, since the sense of agency has not been transcended, future <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like are possible.

children.text: tasya api nirabhisaṃdhinaḥ kāryāntara abhāvāt vidyāsaṃgati upapattiḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: And for those [actions] too — being performed without self-interested motive, and having no other effect — their connection with knowledge is justified. // 16 //

This is not a fault. Because action is an auxiliary from afar. For only good action, combined with <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, is figuratively called the cause of liberation — because it leads [only] to knowledge. And for this very reason, this statement of unity of effect pertains to [actions in] the past.

children.text:
kiṃviṣayaṃ punaḥ idam aśleṣavināśa vacanaṃ kiṃviṣayaṃ vā ado viniyogavacanam ekeṣāṃ śākhinām 'tasya putrā dāyamupayanti suhṛdaḥ sādhukṛtyāṃ dviṣantaḥ pāpakṛtyām' iti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: What is the subject of this statement about non-clinging and destruction? And what is the subject of that statement about apportionment [of <s>karma</s>], read by certain <s>śākhā</s>-followers: 'His sons inherit the wealth, his friends the good deeds, his enemies the evil deeds'? To this, the next [<s>sūtra</s>] is read:

children.text: ato 'nyāpi hy ekeṣām ubhayoḥ | BBs_4,1.17 |
children.translated_text: And from that [permanent <s>karma</s>], the other [<s>karma</s> too is different] — for some [<s>śākhā</s>-followers], in both [cases]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.17 |

children.text: ataḥ agnihotrādeḥ nityātkarmaṇaḥ anyāpi hi asti sādhukṛtyā yā phalam abhisaṃdhāya kriyate tasyā eṣa viniyoga ukta ekeṣāṃ śākhinām 'suhṛdaḥ sādhukṛtyāmupayanti' iti /
children.translated_text: Other than the permanent <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, there is also the meritorious action (<s>sādhukṛtyā</s>) that is performed with a desired result in mind — it is for that [<s>karma</s>] that the apportionment is stated by certain <s>śākhā</s>-followers: 'Friends inherit the good deeds.'

children.text: tasyā eva ca idam aghavat aśleṣavināśanirūpaṇam itarasya api evam aśleṣa iti /
children.translated_text: And it is for that [desire-motivated <s>karma</s>] alone that this description of non-clinging and destruction applies — just as for sin; and for the other [sin] too, the non-clinging [applies] likewise.

children.text: tathā jātīyakasya kāmyasya karmaṇo vidyāṃ prati anupakārakatve saṃpratipattiḥ ubhayoḥ api jaiminibādarāyaṇayoḥ ācāryayoḥ // 17 //
children.translated_text: And the agreement of both teachers — <s>Jaimini</s> and <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — is that such desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>karma</s> has no beneficial role for knowledge. // 17 //

children.text: 13 vidyājñānasādhana adhikaraṇam / sū. 18
children.translated_text: 13. <s>Vidyājñānasādhanādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 18

children.text: yad eva vidyayeti hi | BBs_4,1.18 |
children.translated_text: That which [is performed] with knowledge indeed — for [the <s>śruti</s> says] so. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.18 |

children.text:
samadhigatam etat anantara adhikaraṇe nityam agnihotrādikaṃ karma mumukṣuṇā mokṣaprayojana uddeśena kṛtam upāttaduritakṣayahetutvadvāreṇa sattvaśuddhikāraṇatāṃ pratipadyamānaṃ mokṣaprayojanabrahma adhigamanimittatvena brahmavidyayā saha ekakāryaṃ bhavati iti /
tatra agnihotrādi karmāṅgavyapāśrayavidyāsaṃyuktaṃ kevalaṃ ca asti /
'ya evaṃ vidvānayajati' 'ya evaṃ vidvāñjuhoti' 'ya evaṃ vidvāñchaṃsati' 'ya evaṃ vidvāngāyati' 'tasmādevaṃvidameva brahmāṇaṃ kurviti nānevaṃ vidaṃ' (chā. 4.17.10) 'tenobhau kuruto yaścaitadevaṃ veda yaśca na veda' (chā. 1.1.10) ityādivacanebhyo vidyāsaṃyuktam asti kevalam api asti /
tatra idaṃ vicāryate - kiṃ vidyāsaṃyuktameva agnihotrādikaṃ karma mumukṣoḥ vidyāhetutvena tayā saha ekakāryatvaṃ pratipadyate na kevalam uta vidyāsaṃyuktaṃ kevalaṃ ca aviśeṣeṇa iti /
kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ - 'tametamātmānaṃ yajñena vividiṣanti' iti yajñādīnāmvi aśeṣeṇa ātmavedanāṅgatvena śravaṇāt /
vidyāsaṃyuktasya ca agnihotrādīnām aviśeṣatva avagamāt /
kiṃ tāvat prāptaṃ vidyāsaṃyuktam eva karmāgnihotrādi ātmavidyāśeṣatvaṃ pratipadyate na vidyāhīnam /
vidyā upetasya viśiṣṭatva avagamāt vidyāvihīnāt /
'yadahareva juhoti tadahaḥ punarmṛtyumapajayatyevaṃvidvān' ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
'buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi' (gī. 2.39) 'dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya' (gī. 2.49)
children.translated_text: It has been ascertained in the immediately preceding topic that permanent <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, performed by the seeker of liberation with the purpose of liberation, by serving as the cause of purification of the mind (<s>sattvaśuddhi</s>) through the destruction of accumulated demerits that obstruct [knowledge] — becomes unified in purpose with <s>brahmavidyā</s>, serving as the cause for the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>. Now, there is <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> that is performed with the meditations dependent on ritual accessories, and [<s>karma</s>] that is performed without them. From passages such as: 'He who, knowing thus, sacrifices,' 'He who, knowing thus, offers,' 'He who, knowing thus, chants,' 'He who, knowing thus, sings,' 'Therefore, they appoint as the <s>Brahman</s> priest only one who knows thus, not one who does not know thus' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.17.10), 'By that, both perform — he who knows this thus and he who does not know' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) — and such passages, [we know that] <s>karma</s> combined with knowledge exists, and <s>karma</s> without knowledge also exists. The question investigated here is: Does only <s>karma</s> combined with knowledge — the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like — become unified in purpose with knowledge as a cause of knowledge for the seeker of liberation, and not <s>karma</s> without knowledge? Or do both — combined with knowledge and without it — [serve equally], without distinction? What is the source of the doubt? Because of the undifferentiated hearing in 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know It through sacrifice' — where all sacrifice and the like, without distinction, are heard as ancillary to Self-knowledge. And because the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like combined with knowledge are understood as not different [from those without knowledge]. What is the prima facie view? Only <s>karma</s> combined with knowledge — the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like — attains the status of being ancillary to Self-knowledge, not that devoid of knowledge. Because the superior status of one endowed with knowledge, compared to one devoid of knowledge, is understood. From <s>śrutis</s> such as: 'On whatever day he offers, on that day he conquers death again — thus knowing' and the like. And from <s>smṛtis</s> such as: 'Endowed with <s>buddhi-yoga</s>, you shall cast off the bondage of <s>karma</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>' (<s>Gītā</s> 2.39); 'Action is far inferior to <s>buddhi-yoga</s>, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>' (<s>Gītā</s> 2.49)

children.text:
ityādismṛtibhya- ca iti /
evaṃ prāpte pratipadyate - yadeva vidyayā iti hi /
satyam etat /
vidyāsaṃyuktaṃ karmāgnihotrādikaṃ vidyāvihīnāt karmaṇaḥ agnihotrāt viśiṣṭaṃ vidvāniva brāhmaṇo vidyāvihīnāt brāhmaṇāt /
tathā api na atyantam anapekṣaṃ vidyāvihīnaṃ karmāgnihotrādikam /
kasmāt - 'tametamātmānaṃ yajñena vividiṣanti' iti aviśeṣeṇa agnihotrādeḥ vidyāhetutvena śrutatvāt /
children.translated_text: and such passages. Given this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] determines: 'That which is performed with knowledge indeed — for so [says the <s>śruti</s>].' This is true: <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> combined with knowledge is indeed superior to <s>karma</s> devoid of knowledge — just as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is a knower [is superior] to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is ignorant. Nevertheless, <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> devoid of knowledge is not absolutely without regard [for knowledge]. Why? Because of the undifferentiated hearing in 'The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know It through sacrifice' — where the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like are heard as causes of knowledge without distinction.

children.text: nanu vidyāsaṃyuktasya agnihotrādeḥ vidyāvihīnāt viśiṣṭatva avagamāt vidyāvihīnam agnihotrādi ātmavidyāhetutvena anapekṣameva iti yuktam /
children.translated_text: Objection: Since <s>karma</s> combined with knowledge is understood as superior to that devoid of knowledge, it is reasonable that <s>karma</s> devoid of knowledge has absolutely no regard as a cause of Self-knowledge.

children.text:
na etat evam /
vidyāsahāyasya agnihotrādeḥ vidyānimittena sāmarthya atiśayena yogāt ātmajñānaṃ prati kaścit kāraṇa atiśayo bhaviṣyati na tathā vidyāvihīnasya iti yuktaṃ kalpayitum /
natu 'yajñena vividiṣanti' iti atra aviśeṣeṇa ātmajñānāṅgatvena śrutasya agnihotrādeḥ anaṅgatvaṃ śakyam abhyupagantum /
children.translated_text: But it is not possible to accept the non-ancillary status of the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like that have been heard in 'Through sacrifice they seek to know' as ancillary to Self-knowledge without distinction.

children.text: tathā hi śrutiḥ - 'yadeva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tadeva vīryavattaraṃ bhavati' (chā. 1.1.10) iti vidyāsaṃyuktasya karmaṇaḥ agnihotrādeḥ vīryavattaratva abhidhānena svakāryaṃ prati kañcit atiśayaṃ bruvāṇā vidyāvihīnasya tasya eva tat prayojanaṃ prati vīryavattvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: For thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'That which one does with knowledge, with faith, with meditation (<s>upaniṣad</s>) — that alone is more powerful' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 1.1.10) — by declaring the greater power of <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> combined with knowledge, [and thus] speaking of some special excellence with respect to its own purpose — [the <s>śruti</s>] shows the power of that very [<s>karma</s>] devoid of knowledge for that same purpose.

children.text: karmaṇa- ca vīryavattvaṃ tat yat svaprayojanasādhanaprasahatvam /
children.translated_text: And the power of <s>karma</s> is its capacity to accomplish its own purpose.

children.text: tasmāt vidyāsaṃyuktaṃ nityam agnihotrādi vidyāvihīnaṃ ca ubhayam api mumukṣuṇā mokṣaprayojana uddeśena iha janmani janmāntare ca prāk jñāna utpatteḥ kṛtaṃ yat tat yathāsāmarthyaṃ brahma adhigamapratibandhakāraṇa upāttaduritakṣayahetutvadvāreṇa brahma adhigamakāraṇatvaṃ pratipadyamānaṃ śravaṇa manana śraddhā tātparyādi antaraṅgakāraṇāpekṣaṃ brahmavidyayā saha ekakāryaṃ bhavati iti sthitam // 18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, both — the permanent <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like combined with knowledge, and that devoid of knowledge — both performed by the seeker of liberation with the purpose of liberation, whether in this birth or in previous births prior to the arising of knowledge — becoming, according to their respective capacity, the cause of the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> through the destruction of accumulated demerits that obstruct the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>, depending on the proximate causes of hearing, reflection, faith, absorption, and the like, [such <s>karma</s>] becomes unified in purpose with <s>brahmavidyā</s> — this is established. // 18 //

No, this is not so. <s>Karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> assisted by knowledge, having a surplus of capacity due to knowledge, may have some special excellence as a cause of Self-knowledge — but not that devoid of knowledge — this is reasonable to suppose.

children.text: 14 itarakṣapaṇa adhikaraṇam / sū. 19
children.translated_text: 14. <s>Itarakṣapaṇādhikaraṇa</s> / <s>Sūtra</s> 19

children.text: bhogena tv itare kṣapayitvātha saṃpadyate | BBs_4,1.19 |
children.translated_text: But the other [<s>karmas</s> — i.e., <s>prārabdha</s>] — having exhausted them through experience, then one attains [<s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.1.19 |

children.text: anārabdhakāryayoḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ vidyāsāmarthyāt kṣaya uktaḥ itare tu ārabdhakārye puṇyapāpe upabhogena kṣapayitvā brahma saṃpadyate 'tasya tāvadeva ciraṃ yāvanna vimokṣye 'tha saṃpatsye' (chāndo. 6.14.2) iti 'brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti' iti ca evamādiśrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The destruction of merit and demerit whose effects have not yet begun has been stated [as occurring] through the power of knowledge. But the other — the merit and demerit whose effects have already begun — having exhausted them through experience, [the knower] attains <s>Brahman</s>: 'For him, the delay is only so long until he is freed [from the body]; then he will attain' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.14.2); and 'Being <s>Brahman</s>, he attains <s>Brahman</s>' — from such <s>śrutis</s>.

children.text: nanu sati api samyak darśane yathā prāk dehapātāt bhedadarśanaṃ dvicandradarśananyāyena anuvṛttamevaṃ paścāt api anuvarteta /
children.translated_text: Objection: Even when right knowledge exists — just as, prior to the fall of the body, the vision of difference continues by the principle of the double-moon [perception] — so too, even after [death], it might continue.

children.text:
na /
nimitta abhāvāt /
upabhogaśeṣakṣapaṇaṃ hi tatra anuvṛttinimittaṃ na ca tādṛśamātra kiñcit asti /
children.translated_text: No. Because of the absence of the cause. For the cause of [the vision of difference] continuing is the remainder of enjoyment [of <s>prārabdha karma</s>] yet to be exhausted — and no such [cause] exists [after death].

children.text: nanu aparaḥ karmāśayoḥ abhinavam upabhogm ārapsyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: But another <s>karma</s>-residue might initiate a new [round of] experience.

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: tasya dagdhabījatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because its seeds have been burnt.

children.text: mithyājñāna avaṣṭambhaṃ hi karmāntaraṃ dehapāta upabhogāntaram ārabhate tat ca mithyājñāna avaṣṭambhaṃ hi karmāntaraṃ dehapāta upabhogāntaram ārabhate tatca mithyājñānaṃ samyak jñānena dagdham ityataḥ sādhu etat ārabdhakāryakṣaye viduṣaḥ kaivalyam avaśyaṃ bhavati iti // 19 //
children.translated_text: For it is [other] <s>karma</s> supported by false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) that, at the fall of the body, initiates another [round of] experience; and that false knowledge has been burnt by right knowledge — therefore it is well-established that upon the exhaustion of the <s>karma</s> whose effects have already begun, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) necessarily ensues for the knower. // 19 //

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye caturthādhyāyasya prathamaḥ pādaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsā</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>. // 1 //

children.text: caturthādhyāye dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the fourth <s>adhyāya</s>, the second <s>pāda</s>.

children.text: atra pāde utkrāntigatinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: In this <s>pāda</s>, the determination of the departure [of the soul] and the path [after death] is [discussed].

children.text: 1 vāgādhikaraṇam / sū. 1-2
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Vāgādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Speech). <s>Sūtras</s> 1-2.

children.text: vāṅmanasi darśanāc chabdāc ca | BBs_4,2.1 |
children.translated_text: Speech [merges] in the mind — because of observation and because of the scriptural word. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.1 |

children.text:
atha aparāsu vidyāsu phalaprāptaye devayānaṃ panthānam avatārayiṣyan prathamaṃ tāvat yathāśāstram utkrāntikramam anvācaṣṭe /
samānā hi vidvat aviduṣoḥ utkrāntiḥ iti vakṣyati /
asti prāyaṇaviṣayā śrutiḥ 'asya somya puruṣasya prayato vāk manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇa- tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām' (chā. 6.8.6) iti /
kim iha vāca eva vṛttimattyā manasi saṃpattiḥ ucyata uta vāgvṛtteḥiti viśayaḥ /
tatra vāk eva tāvat manasi saṃpadyata iti prāptam /
tathā hi śrutiḥ anugṛhītā bhavati /
itarathā lakṣaṇā syāt /
śrutilakṣaṇa aviśaye ca śrutiḥ nyāyyā na lakṣaṇā /
tasmāt vāca eva ayaṃ manasi pralaya iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - vāk vṛttiḥ iti vyākhyāte yāvatā vāk menasi iti eva ācāryaḥ paṭhati /
satyam etat /
paṭhiṣyati tu purastāt 'avibhāgo vacanāt' (bra. sū. 4.2.16) iti /
tasmāt atra vṛtti upaśamamātraṃ vivakṣitam iti gamyate /
tattvapralayavivakṣāyāṃ tu sarvatra eva avibhāgasāmyāt kiṃ paratra eva viśiṣyāt avibhāga iti /
tasmāt atra vṛtti upasaṃhāravivakṣā /
vāk vṛttiḥ pūrvam upasaṃhriyate manovṛttau avasthitāyām iti arthaḥ /
kasmāt /
darśanāt /
dṛśyate hi vāk vṛtteḥ pūrva upasaṃhāro manovṛttau vidyamānāyām /
children.translated_text: Now, intending to introduce the <s>devayāna</s> path for the attainment of the fruit of the lower <s>vidyās</s>, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] first describes the order of departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) as stated in scripture. For it will be said that the departure is the same for the knower and the non-knower. There is a <s>śruti</s> pertaining to death: 'Of this person, O dear one, when dying, speech merges in the mind, the mind in <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> in fire (<s>tejas</s>), and fire in the supreme deity' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.6). The question here is: Does this describe the merging of speech itself — possessing its function — into the mind, or [the merging of] the function of speech? To begin with, the prima facie view is that speech itself merges in the mind. For thus the <s>śruti</s> is taken in its primary sense. Otherwise, there would be a secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>). And when there is no reason to choose between primary and secondary meaning, the primary meaning is proper, not the secondary. Therefore, this is the dissolution of speech itself into the mind. Given this prima facie view, we say: [The <s>sūtrakāra</s>] explains it as 'the function of speech' — since the teacher reads merely 'Speech [merges] in the mind.' True, this is so. But subsequently [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] will read: 'Non-distinction, because of the statement' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.2.16). Therefore, it is understood that only the cessation of function is intended here. For if the dissolution of the real substance were intended, then — since non-distinction would be the same everywhere — what would be special about the non-distinction mentioned later? Therefore, what is intended here is the withdrawal of function. The meaning is: The function of speech is withdrawn first, while the function of the mind still persists. Why? Because of observation. For the withdrawal of the function of speech is observed [to occur] first, while the function of the mind is still present.

children.text: nanu śrutisāmarthyāt vāca eva ayaṃ manasi apyayo yukta iti uktam /
children.translated_text: Objection: But it was said that by the force of the <s>śruti</s>, the dissolution of speech itself into the mind is proper.

children.text:
na iti āha /
atatprakṛtitvāt /
yasya hi yata utpattiḥ tasya tatra pralayo nyāyyo mṛdīva śarāvasya /
na ca manaso vāk utpadyata iti kiñcana pramāṇam asti /
vṛttyutti udbhava abhibhavau tu aprakṛtisamāśrayau api dṛśyete /
pārthivebhyo hi indhanebhyaḥ taijasasya agneḥ vṛttiḥ udbhavati apsu ca upaśāmyati /
children.translated_text: For the function of fire, which is luminous, arises from earthly fuel and subsides in water.

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi asmin pakṣe śabdo vāk manasi saṃpadyata iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: How then, on this view, is the scriptural statement 'Speech [merges] in the mind' [to be explained]?

children.text: ata āha śabdāt ca iti /
children.translated_text: To this [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: 'And because of the [scriptural] word.'

children.text: śabdaḥ api asmin pakṣe avakalpate vṛttivṛttimatoḥ abheda upacārāt iti arthaḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: The scriptural word too is tenable on this view — because of the figurative identification (<s>upacāra</s>) of the function with the possessor of the function. // 1 //

[The <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: No. Because [mind] is not its material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>). For the dissolution of something into that from which it originated is proper — like a pot into clay. And there is no evidence whatsoever that speech originates from the mind. But the arising and subsiding of functions are seen even without reference to a material cause.

children.text: FN: prayato mriyamāṇasya /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Prayato</s>' means 'of one who is dying.'

children.text: ata eva ca sarvāṇyanu | BBs_4,2.2 |
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, all [sense-organs follow the same pattern]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.2 |

children.text: 'tasmādupaśāntatejāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, when [<s>tejas</s>] has subsided,

children.text: punarbhavamindriyairmanasi saṃpadyamānaiḥ' (praśna. 3.9) iti atra aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣām eva indriyāṇāṃ manasi saṃpattiḥ śrūyate /
children.translated_text: the sense-organs, merging in the mind, [lead to] rebirth' (<s>Praśna</s> 3.9) — here, without distinction, the merging of all sense-organs in the mind is heard.

children.text: tatra api ata eva vāca iva cakṣurādīnām api savṛttike manasi avasthite vṛttilopadarśanāt tattvapralaya asaṃbhavāt śabda upapatteḥ ca vṛttidvāreṇa eva sarvāṇi indriyāṇi manaḥ anuvartante /
children.translated_text: There too, for this very reason — just as with speech, so too with the eye and the other [organs] — because of the observation that their functions cease while the mind, together with its function, still persists; because of the impossibility of a real dissolution of their substance; and because of the tenability of the scriptural word [through figurative identification] — all the sense-organs follow the mind through the medium of [the cessation of] their functions.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ manasi upasaṃhāra aviśeṣe sati vācaḥ pṛthak grahaṇaṃ vāk manasi saṃpadyata iti udāharaṇa anurodhena // 2 //
children.translated_text: Given that the merging of all sense-organs in the mind is without distinction, the separate mention of speech in 'Speech [merges] in the mind' is in accordance with the illustration [provided by that specific passage]. // 2 //

children.text: manodhikaraṇam / sū. 3
children.translated_text: The <s>Manoadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Mind). <s>Sūtra</s> 3.

children.text: tanmanaḥ prāṇa uttarāt | BBs_4,2.3 |
children.translated_text: That mind [merges] in <s>prāṇa</s> — because of the subsequent [statement]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.3 |

children.text:
samadhigatametat 'vāṅmanasi saṃpadyate' (chā. 6.8.6) iti atra vṛttisaṃpattivivakṣa iti /
atha yat uttaravākyam 'manaḥ prāṇe' (chā. 6.8.6) iti kim atra api vṛttisaṃpattiḥ eva vivakṣyata uta vṛttimat saṃpattiḥ iti vicikitsāyāṃ vṛttimat saṃpattiḥ eva atra iti prāptam /
śruti anugrahāt tat prakṛtikatva upapatteḥ ca /
tathā hi - 'annamayaṃ hi somya mana āpomayaḥprāṇaḥ' (chā. 6.5.4) iti annayoni mana ātmananti ap yoniṃ ca prāṇam /
'āpaścānnamasṛjanta' iti śrutiḥ /
ata- ca yat manaḥ prāṇe prakṛtivikāra abhedāt iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tat api agṛhīta bāhya indriyavṛtti mano vṛttidvāreṇa eva prāṇe pralīyate iti uttarāt vākyāt avagantavyam /
tathā hi suṣupso- mumūrṣoḥ ca prāṇavṛttau parispanda ātmikāyām avasthitāyāṃ manovṛttīnām upaśamo dṛśyate /
na ca manasaḥ svarūpa apyayaḥ prāṇe saṃbhavati /
atat prakṛtitvāt /
children.translated_text: It has been ascertained that in 'Speech merges in the mind' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.6), the merging of the function is intended. Now, regarding the subsequent statement 'The mind [merges] in <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.6) — is the merging of the function intended here too, or [the merging of] the substance possessing the function? When there is doubt, the prima facie view is: The merging here is of the substance possessing the function. Because of conformity with the primary meaning of the <s>śruti</s>, and because the causal relation (<s>prakṛti</s>) is tenable. For thus: 'The mind, O dear one, is made of food; <s>prāṇa</s> is made of water' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.5.4) — the mind has food as its source, and <s>prāṇa</s> has water as its source. [And] the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'Waters created food.' Therefore, the mind [dissolves] in <s>prāṇa</s> because of the non-difference of cause and effect. Given this prima facie view, we say: That [mind] too — having withdrawn the functions of the external sense-organs — merges in <s>prāṇa</s> through the medium of its function alone — this is to be understood from the subsequent statement. For thus, when a person falls asleep or is dying, the cessation of the functions of the mind is observed while the function of <s>prāṇa</s> — consisting of pulsation — still persists. And the dissolution of the substance of the mind into <s>prāṇa</s> is not possible — because [<s>prāṇa</s>] is not its material cause.

children.text: nanu darśitaṃ manasaḥ prāṇaprakṛtitvam /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the causal relation of <s>prāṇa</s> to the mind was demonstrated.

children.text: na etat sāram /
na hi īdṛśena prāṇāḍikena tat prakṛtitvena manaḥ prāṇe saṃpattum arhati /
children.translated_text: For by such a causal relation — through <s>prāṇa</s> and the like — the mind cannot properly merge in <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: evam api hi anne manaḥ saṃpadyeta apsu ca annam apsu eva ca prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For even on that [view], the mind would [have to] merge in food, and food in water, and <s>prāṇa</s> too in water.

children.text: na hi etasmin api pakṣe prāṇabhāvapariṇatābhyaḥ adbhyo mano jāyata iti kiñcana pramāṇam asti tasmāt na manasaḥ prāṇe svarūpa apyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: For even on this view, there is no evidence whatsoever that the mind is born from water that has been transformed into the state of <s>prāṇa</s>. Therefore, there is no dissolution of the substance of the mind in <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: vṛtti apyaye api tu śabdaḥ avakalpate vṛttivattimatoḥ abheda upacārāt iti darśitam // 3 //
children.translated_text: But the scriptural word is tenable even in the case of the dissolution of the function — because of the figurative identification of the function with the possessor of the function — as was shown. // 3 //
That is not sound.

children.text: 3 adhyakṣa adhikaraṇam / sū. 4-6
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Adhyakṣādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Presiding [Self]). <s>Sūtras</s> 4-6.

children.text: so 'dhyakṣe tadupagamādibhyaḥ | BBs_4,2.4 |
children.translated_text: That [<s>prāṇa</s> merges] in the presiding [Self] — because of approaching It and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.4 |

children.text:
sthitam etat yasya yato na utpattiḥ tasya tasmin vṛttipralayo na svarūpapralaya iti /
idam idānīṃ prāṇaḥ tejasi iti atra cintyate -
children.translated_text: It is established that when something does not originate from another, its dissolution in that [other] is of function, not of substance. Now, regarding 'The <s>prāṇa</s> [merges] in fire (<s>tejas</s>)' — this is examined:

children.text:
kiṃ yathāśruti prāṇasya tejasi eva vṛtti upasaṃhāraḥ kiṃvā deha indriyapañjara adhyakṣe jīva iti /
tatra śruteḥ anatiśaṅkyatvāt prāṇasya tejasi eva saṃpattiḥ syāt aśrutakalpanāyā anyāyyatvāt iti /
evaṃ prāpte pratipadyate saḥ adhyakṣa iti /
sa prakṛtaḥ prāṇaḥ adhyakṣe avidyākarmapūrvaprajña upādhike vijñāna ātmani avatiṣṭhate /
tat pradhānā prāṇavṛttiḥ bhavati iti arthaḥ /
kutaḥ - tat upagamādibhyaḥ /
evam eva imam ātmānam antakāle sarve prāṇā abhisāmayanti yatra etat ūrdhva ucchvāsī bhavati iti hi śrutyantaram adhyakṣa upagāminaḥ sarvān prāṇān aviśeṣeṇa darśayati /
viśeṣeṇa ca 'tamutkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmati' (bṛ. 4.4.2) iti pañcavṛtteḥ prāṇasya adhyakṣa anugāmitāṃ darśayati tat anuvṛttitāṃ ca itareṣām /
'prāṇamanūtkrāmantaṃ sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmati' (bṛ. 4.4.2) iti /
'savijñāno bhavati' iti ca adhyakṣasya antarvijñānavattva pradarśanena tasmin apītakaraṇagrāmasya prāṇasya avasthānaṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text: Does the withdrawal of the function of <s>prāṇa</s> [occur] in fire as the <s>śruti</s> literally states, or in the presiding [Self] (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) — the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) who is the master of the body-and-organ complex? Since the <s>śruti</s> should not be doubted, the prima facie view is that the merging of <s>prāṇa</s> should be in fire itself — because the postulation of what is not stated in <s>śruti</s> is improper. Given this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] determines: 'That in the presiding [Self].' That <s>prāṇa</s> under discussion comes to rest in the presiding [Self] — the <s>vijñānātman</s> (the consciousness-self) conditioned by the <s>upādhis</s> of <s>avidyā</s>, <s>karma</s>, and prior impressions (<s>pūrvaprajñā</s>). The meaning is: the function of <s>prāṇa</s> becomes subordinate to that [Self]. Why? Because of approaching It and the like. For another <s>śruti</s> shows, without distinction, all <s>prāṇas</s> approaching the presiding [Self]: 'All <s>prāṇas</s> gather around this Self at the time of death — when he draws up these [final] breaths.' And specifically: 'When he departs, <s>prāṇa</s> follows after him' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2) — [this] shows the fivefold <s>prāṇa</s> following after the presiding [Self], and the others following after that: '<s>Prāṇa</s> follows after the departing [Self]; all <s>prāṇas</s> follow after <s>prāṇa</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2). And [the statement] 'He becomes endowed with consciousness (<s>savijñāna</s>)' — by showing that the presiding [Self] possesses inner consciousness — indicates that <s>prāṇa</s>, together with the aggregate of organs, rests in It.

children.text: nanu prāṇaḥ tejasi iti śrūyate kathaṃ prāṇaḥ adhyakṣa iti adhikāvāpaḥ kriyate /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the <s>śruti</s> states '<s>Prāṇa</s> [merges] in fire (<s>tejas</s>)' — how can the additional reading '<s>prāṇa</s> [merges] in the presiding Self' be introduced?

children.text: na eṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: adhyakṣapradhānatvāt utkramaṇādivyavahārasya śrutyantaragatasya api ca viśeṣasya apekṣaṇīyatvāt // 4 //
children.translated_text: Because the presiding [Self] is primary in the process of departure and the like, and because the specific details found in other <s>śruti</s> passages must also be taken into account. // 4 //

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi prāṇaḥ tejasi iti śrutiḥ iti ata āha -
children.translated_text: How then is the <s>śruti</s> '<s>Prāṇa</s> [merges] in fire (<s>tejas</s>)' [to be understood]? To this [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says:

children.text: bhūteṣu tacchruteḥ | BBs_4,2.5 |
children.translated_text: [The presiding Self abides] in the elements — because of the <s>śruti</s> [to that effect]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.5 |

children.text:
sa prāṇasaṃpṛktaḥ adhyakṣaḥ tejaḥsahacariteṣu bhūteṣu dehabījabhūteṣu sūkṣmeṣu avatiṣṭhata iti avagantavyam /
prāṇaḥ tejasi iti śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: That presiding [Self], conjoined with <s>prāṇa</s>, abides in the subtle elements — accompanied by fire — which are the seeds of the [future] body. This is to be understood from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>Prāṇa</s> [merges] in fire (<s>tejas</s>).'

children.text: nanu ca iyaṃ śrutiḥ prāṇasya tejasi sthitiṃ darśayati na prāṇasaṃpṛktasya adhyakṣasya /
children.translated_text: Objection: But this <s>śruti</s> shows the abiding of <s>prāṇa</s> in fire, not of the presiding [Self] conjoined with <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: na eṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: saḥ adhyakṣa iti adhyakṣasya api antarāle api upasaṃkhyātatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because in 'That [merges] in the presiding [Self],' the presiding [Self] too has been included in the intermediate [stage].

children.text: yaḥ api hi srughnānmathurāṃ gatvā mathurāyāḥ pāṭaliputraṃ vrajati saḥ api srughnātpāṭaliputraṃ yāti iti śakyate vaditum /
children.translated_text: For indeed, one who travels from <s>Srughna</s> to <s>Mathurā</s> and from <s>Mathurā</s> to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> can be said to have traveled from <s>Srughna</s> to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.

children.text: tasmāt prāṇaḥ tejasi iti prāṇasaṃpṛktasya adhyakṣasya eva etat tejaḥ sahacariteṣu bhūteṣu avasthānam // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, '<s>Prāṇa</s> [merges] in fire (<s>tejas</s>)' means that the presiding [Self], conjoined with <s>prāṇa</s>, abides in the elements accompanied by fire. // 5 //

children.text:
kathaṃ tejaḥsahacariteṣu bhūteṣu iti ucyate yāvat ekameva śrūyate prāṇaḥ tejasi iti /
ata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: How can one say 'in the elements accompanied by fire' when only one [element] is heard — '<s>prāṇa</s> in fire'? To this [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says:

children.text: naikasmin darśayato hi | BBs_4,2.6 |
children.translated_text: Not in one alone — because [the scripture] shows [otherwise]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.6 |

children.text:
na ekasmin eva tejasi śarīrāntaraprepsāvelāyāṃ jīvaḥ avatiṣṭhate kāryasya śarīrasya anekātmakatvadarśanāt /
darśayataḥ ca etam arthaṃ praśnaprativacane 'āpaḥ puruṣavacasaḥ' (chā. 5.3.3) iti /
tat vyākhyātam 'tryātmakatvāttu bhūyastvāt' (bra.sū. 3.1.2) iti atra /
śrutismṛtī ca etamarthaṃ darśayataḥ /
śrutiḥ 'pṛthvīmaya āpomayo vāyumaya ākāśamayastojomayaḥ' ityādyā /
smṛtiḥ api 'aṇvyo mātrāvināśinyo daśārdhānāṃ tu yāḥsmṛtāḥ /
tābhiḥ sārdhamidaṃ sarvaṃ saṃbhavatyanupūrvaśaḥ' ityādyā /
children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> does not abide in fire alone at the time of seeking a new body — because of the observation that the effect, the body, is constituted of multiple [elements]. And the question-and-answer shows this meaning: 'Waters, O dear one, bear the form of the person' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.3.3). This has been explained in [the discussion of] 'But because of the tripartite nature, [fire predominates] on account of preponderance' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.1.2). Both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> show this meaning. The <s>śruti</s>: 'Made of earth, made of water, made of air, made of space, made of fire' and the like. The <s>smṛti</s> also: 'The subtle particles, imperishable, of the five [elements] —

children.text: nanu ca upasaṃhṛteṣu vāk ādiṣu karaṇeṣu śarīrāntaraprepsāvelāyāṃ 'kvāyaṃ tadā puruṣo bhavati' (bṛ. 3.2.13) iti upakramya śrutyantaraṃ karmāśrayatāṃ nirūpayati - 'tau ha yadūcatuḥ karma haiva tadūcaturatha ha yatpraśaśaṃsatuḥ karma haiva tatpraśaśaṃsatuḥ' (bṛ. 3.2.13) iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But another <s>śruti</s>, having introduced [the topic] with 'Where then does this person go [at death]?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.13) — when the sense-organs are withdrawn at the time of seeking a new body — determines the dependence on <s>karma</s>: 'What those two spoke about — they spoke about <s>karma</s> indeed; what they praised — they praised <s>karma</s> indeed' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.13).

children.text: atra ucyate - tatra karmaprayuktasya graha atigrahasaṃjñakastha indriyaviṣayātmakasya bandhanasya pravṛttiḥ iti karmāśrayatā uktā /
children.translated_text: To this we say: There, the dependence on <s>karma</s> is stated as the operation of the bondage — consisting of the sense-organs and their objects, designated as '<s>graha</s>' and '<s>atigraha</s>' — which is impelled by <s>karma</s>.

children.text: iha punaḥ bhūta upādānāt dehāntara utpattiḥ iti bhūtāśrayatvam uktam /
children.translated_text: But here, the dependence on the elements is stated — [meaning] that the production of a new body occurs from the material elements.

children.text: praśaṃsāśabdāt api tatra prādhānyamātraṃ karmaṇaḥ pradarśitaṃ na tu āśrayāntaraṃ nivāritam /
children.translated_text: And from the word 'praised' (<s>praśaṃsā</s>), only the primacy of <s>karma</s> [in the process] is shown — not the exclusion of another basis [i.e., the elements].

children.text: tasmāt avirodhaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no contradiction. // 6 //

children.text: FN: daśārdhānāṃ pañcabhūtānāṃ , aṇvyaḥ sūkṣmāḥ , mīyanta iti mātrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Footnote: '<s>Daśārdhānām</s>' means of the five elements. '<s>Aṇvyaḥ</s>' means subtle. '<s>Mātrāḥ</s>' means that which is measured (<s>mīyante</s>).

children.text: 4 āsṛtyupakrama adhikaraṇam / sū. 7
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Āsṛtyupakramādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Beginning of the Journey). <s>Sūtra</s> 7.

children.text: samānā cāsṛtyupakramād amṛtatvaṃ cānupoṣya | BBs_4,2.7 |
children.translated_text: And [the departure] is the same — because of the beginning of the journey [being common]; and immortality too [is attained] without nourishing [the body]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.2.7 |

children.text:
sā iyam utkrāntiḥ kiṃ vidvat aviduṣoḥ samānā kiṃvā viśeṣavati iti viśayānānāṃ viśeṣavati iti tāvat prāptam /
bhūtāśrayaviśiṣṭā hi eṣā /
punaḥ bhavāya ca bhūtāni āśrīyante /
na ca viduṣaḥ punarbhavaḥ saṃbhavati /
'amṛtatvaṃ hi vidvānaśnute' iti sthitiḥ /
tasmat aviduṣa eva eṣa utkrāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: Is this departure the same for the knower and the non-knower, or is it different? The prima facie view is that it is different. For this [departure] involves dependence on the elements. And the elements are resorted to for rebirth. And rebirth is not possible for the knower. For the established position is: 'The knower attains immortality.' Therefore, this departure belongs to the non-knower alone.

children.text: nanu vidyāprakaraṇe samāmnānāt viduṣa eva eṣā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Objection: But since [this departure] is taught in the context of <s>vidyā</s>, it should belong to the knower alone.

children.text:
na /
svāpādivat yathāprāpta anukīrtanāt /
tathā hi 'yatraitatpuruṣaḥ svapiti nāma' 'aśiśiṣati nāma' 'pipāsati nāma' (chā. 6.8.3,5) iti ca sarvaprāṇisādhāraṇā eva svāpādayaḥ anukīrtyante vidyāprakaraṇe api pratipādayiṣitavastupratipādana anuguṇyena na tu viduṣo viśeṣavanto vidhitsyante /
evam iyam api utkrāntiḥ mahājanagata eva anukīrtyate yasyāṃ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ puruṣasya prayataḥ tejaḥ saṃpadyate sa ātmā tattvamasi iti etat pratipādayitum /
pratiṣiddhā ca eṣā viduṣaḥ 'na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti /
tasmāt aviduṣa eva eṣa iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - samānā ca eṣa utkrāntiḥ vāk manasi ityādyā vidvat aviduṣoḥ āsṛti upakramāt bhavitum arhati /
aviśeṣaśravaṇāt /
aviruddhān dehabījabhūtāni bhūtasūkṣmāṇi āśritya karmaprayukto dehagrahaṇam anubhavituṃ saṃsarati /
vidvān tu jñānaprakāśitaṃ mokṣanāḍīdvāram āśrayate /
tat etat āsṛti upakramāt iti uktam /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because it is a recounting of what occurs naturally (<s>yathāprāpta</s>), like sleep and the like.
For thus, 'When this person sleeps' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.3), 'when he hungers,' 'when he thirsts' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.5) — sleep and the like, which are common to all living beings, are merely recounted even in the context of <s>vidyā</s>, in conformity with the presentation of the intended subject matter — but they are not being specially enjoined for the knower.
Likewise, this departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) too is merely recounted as pertaining to all people — in order to teach: 'In which supreme deity the person's fire (<s>tejas</s>) merges — that is the Self; thou art That.'
And this [departure] has been negated for the knower: 'His <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6).
Therefore, this [departure pertains] to the non-knower alone.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: This departure — 'speech merges into the mind' and so on — is common to both the knower and the non-knower, because of the commencement of the journey (<s>āsṛti</s>).
Because of the non-specific hearing [which does not distinguish between knower and non-knower].
The non-knower, taking support of the subtle elements — which are the seeds of the body and are uncontradicted — transmigrates, impelled by <s>karma</s>, to experience the acquisition of [another] body.
But the knower takes the door of the <s>nāḍī</s> of liberation illumined by knowledge.
This is what is meant by 'because of the commencement of the journey.'

children.text: nanu amṛtatvaṃ hi viduṣā prāptavyaṃ na ca tat deśāntara āyattaṃ tatra kṛto bhūta āśrayatvaṃ sṛti upakramo vā iti /
children.translated_text: But immortality is what the knower is to attain, and that does not depend on reaching another place — so how could there be a commencement of a journey or a taking support of elements?

children.text: atra ucyate - anupoṣya ca idam, adagdhvā atyantam avidyādīn kleśān aparavidyāsāmarthyāt āpekṣikam amṛtatvaṃ prepsate saṃbhavati tatra sṛti upakramo bhūta āśrayatvaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: To this we say: One who, without fully nourishing [the knowledge and] without completely burning the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) such as <s>avidyā</s> and the like, seeks relative (<s>āpekṣika</s>) immortality through the power of the lower <s>vidyā</s> (<s>aparavidyā</s>) — for such a one, the commencement of a journey and the taking support of elements is possible.

children.text: ne hi nirāśrayāṇāṃ prāṇānāṃ gatiḥ upapadyate /
children.translated_text: For the journey of <s>prāṇas</s> without a support is not tenable.

children.text: tasmāt adoṣaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no fault. // 7 //

children.text: 5 saṃsāravyapadeśa adhikaraṇam // sū. 8-11
children.translated_text: 5 The <s>Saṃsāravyapadeśa</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 8-11.

children.text: tadāpīteḥ saṃsāravyapadeśāt | BBs_4,2.8 |
children.translated_text: Until the merger into That, [the subtle body persists] — because of the designation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.8 |

children.text:
'tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām' (chā. 6.8.6) iti atra prakaraṇasāmarthyāt tat yathāprakṛtaṃ tejaḥ sādhyakṣaṃ saprāṇaṃ sakaraṇagrāmaṃ bhūtāntarasahitaṃ prayataḥ puṃsaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ saṃpadyata iti etat uktaṃ bhavati /
kīdṛśī punaḥ iyaṃ saṃpattiḥ syāt iti cintyate /
tatra ātyantika eva tāvat svarūpapravilaya iti prāptam /
tat prakṛtitva upapatteḥ /
sarvasya hi janimato vastujātasya prakṛtiḥ parā devatā iti pratiṣṭhāpitam /
tasmāt ātyantikīyam avibhāgāpattiḥ iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - tat teja ādi bhūtasūkṣmaṃ śrotrādikaraṇāśrayabhūtamāpīterā saṃsāramokṣāt samyak jñānanimittāt avatiṣṭhate /
'yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ /
sthāṇumanye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarmayathāśrutam' (ka. 5.7) ityādi saṃsāravyapadeśāt /
children.translated_text:
'The fire [merges] in the supreme deity' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.6) — here, by the force of the context, the meaning is that the fire (<s>tejas</s>) as described — together with the senses, the <s>prāṇas</s>, the aggregate of organs, and accompanied by the other elements — of the departing person merges in the supreme deity.
Now, what would be the nature of this merger? This is examined.
The prima facie view is: It is an absolute dissolution of the individual nature [into <s>Brahman</s>].
Because of the tenability of That being the material cause.
For it has been established that the supreme deity is the material cause of all things that have come into being.
Therefore, this is an absolute reaching of non-differentiation.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: That subtle body consisting of fire (<s>tejas</s>) and the like — which serves as the support of the senses such as hearing and the like — persists until liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is [attained] through right knowledge.
Because of the designation of <s>saṃsāra</s>: 'Some enter a womb for embodiment; others go to a stationary [form] — according to their <s>karma</s> and according to their knowledge' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.7) — and the like.

children.text: anyathā hi sarvaḥ prāyaṇasamaya eva upādhipratyastamayāt atyantaṃ brahma saṃpadyeta /
children.translated_text: For otherwise, everyone would absolutely merge into <s>Brahman</s> at the very time of death, because of the dissolution of the <s>upādhis</s>.

children.text: tatra vidhiśāstram anarthakaṃ syāt vidyāśāstraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: In that case, the scriptural injunctions would be purposeless, and so too the scripture on <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: mithyājñānanimittaḥ ca bandho na samyak jñānāt ṛte visraṃsitum arhati /
children.translated_text: And bondage, which is caused by false knowledge, cannot be released without right knowledge.

children.text: tasmāt tat prakṛtitve api suṣuptapralayavat bījabhāva avaśeṣa eva eṣā saṃtsapattiḥ iti // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though That [<s>Brahman</s>] is the material cause, this merger — like the dissolution in deep sleep or cosmic dissolution — is one in which the residual seed-form remains. // 8 //

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ pramāṇataś ca tathopalabdheḥ | BBs_4,2.9 |
children.translated_text: The subtle [body] is so in [its own] nature and in measure — because of such being observed. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.9 |

children.text: tat ca itarabhūtasahitaṃ tejo jīvasya asmāt śarīrāt pravasata āśrayabhūtaṃ svarūpataḥ pramāṇataḥ ca sūkṣmaṃ bhavitum arhati /
tathā hi - nāḍīniṣkramaṇaśravaṇādibhyaḥ asya saukṣmyam upalabhyate /
children.translated_text: For thus, its subtlety is observed from [the <s>śruti</s>'s description of] the departure through the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the like.

children.text: tatra tanutvāt saṃcāra upapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of its thinness, the tenability of [its] movement [through the <s>nāḍīs</s> is established].

children.text: svacchatvāt ca apratīghāta upapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of its transparency, the tenability of [its] non-obstruction [is established].

children.text: ata eva ca dehāt nirgacchan pārśvasthaiḥ na upalabhyate // 9 //
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, [the <s>jīva</s>] departing from the body is not perceived by those standing nearby. // 9 //

And that [body] — consisting of fire (<s>tejas</s>) combined with the other elements — which serves as the support for the <s>jīva</s> departing from this body, must be subtle in its own nature and in measure.

children.text: nopamardenātaḥ | BBs_4,2.10 |
children.translated_text: Not by the destruction [of the gross body is the subtle body destroyed] — for this reason. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.10 |

children.text: ata eva sūkṣmatvāt na asya sthūlasya śarīrasya upamardena dāhādinimittena itarat sūkṣmaṃ śarīram upapadyate // 10 //
children.translated_text: For this very reason — because of its subtlety — the other, subtle body is not destroyed by the destruction (burning, etc.) of this gross body. // 10 //

children.text: asyaiva copapatter ūṣmā | BBs_4,2.11 |
children.translated_text: And the warmth is of this [subtle body] alone — because of tenability. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.11 |

children.text: asya eva ca sūkṣmasyā śarīrasya eṣa ūṣmā yam etasmin śarīre saṃsparśena ūṣmāṇaṃ vijānanti /
children.translated_text: And this warmth — which is known by touch in this [gross] body — belongs to this subtle body alone.

children.text: tathā hi mṛtāvasthāyām avasthite api dehe vidyamāneṣu api ca rūpādiṣu dehaguṇeṣu na ūṣma upalabhyate jīvat avasthāyām eva tu upalabhyata iti ata dehaguṇeṣu na ūṣma upalabhyate jīvat avasthāyām eva tu upalabhyata iti ata upapadyate prasiddhaśarīravyatiriktavyapāśraya eva eṣa ūṣma iti /
children.translated_text: For thus, even when the body remains in the state of death, and even when bodily qualities such as form and the like still exist, warmth is not perceived — but it is perceived only in the living state. Therefore, it is tenable that this warmth has its support in [something] distinct from the well-known [gross] body.

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ - 'uṣṇa eva jīviṣyañśito mariṣyan iti' // 11 //
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'Warm, he will live; cold, he will die.' // 11 //

children.text: 6 pratiṣedha adhikaraṇam / sū. 12-14
children.translated_text: 6 The <s>Pratiṣedha</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 12-14.

children.text: pratiṣedhād iti cen na śārīrāt | BBs_4,2.12 |
children.translated_text: If [one objects:] because of the negation — [we reply:] no, [the negation is] from the embodied [Self, not from the body]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.12 |

children.text:
'amṛtatvaṃ cānupoṣya' iti ato viśeṣaṇāt ātyantike amṛtatve gati utkrāntyoḥ abhāvo abhyupagataḥ /
tatra api kenacit kāraṇena utkrāntim āśaṅkya pratiṣedhati - 'athākāmayamāno yo 'kāmo niṣkāma āptakāma ātmakāmo bhavati na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti ataḥ paravidyāviṣayāt pratiṣedhāt na parabrahmavido dehāt prāṇānām utkrāntiḥ asti iti cet /
children.translated_text:
By the qualification 'without fully nourishing immortality' — it has been accepted that for absolute immortality, there is no journey or departure.
Even so, if someone suspects departure [even for the supreme knower], [the <s>śruti</s>] negates it: 'One who is desireless, who is free from desire, whose desires are fulfilled, whose desire is the Self — his <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart; being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges into <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6). From this negation — which pertains to the subject of the higher <s>vidyā</s> (<s>paravidyā</s>) — [one might argue that] there is no departure of the <s>prāṇas</s> from the body for the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
na iti ucyate /
yataḥ śārīrāt ātmana eṣa utkrāntipratiṣedhaḥ prāṇānāṃ na śarīrāt /
katham avagamyate 'na tasmātprāṇā utkrāmanti' iti śākhāntare pañcamī prayogāt /
saṃbandhasāmānyaviṣayā hi ṣaṣṭhī śākhāntaragatayā pañcamyā saṃbandhaviśeṣe vyavasthāpyate /
children.translated_text: For the sixth case (genitive), which denotes relation in general, is determined to express a specific relation by the fifth case (ablative) found in another recension.

children.text: tasmāt iti ca prādhānyāt abhyudayaniḥśreyasa adhikṛto dehī saṃbadhyate na dehaḥ /
children.translated_text: And by '<s>tasmāt</s>' — because of [the Self's] primacy — it is the embodied [Self], which is the subject of the teaching on prosperity and liberation, that is connected — not the body.

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: tasmāt uccikramiṣoḥ jīvāt prāṇā apakrāmanti saha eva tena bhavanti iti arthaḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: From the <s>jīva</s> who is about to depart, the <s>prāṇas</s> do not go away [separately]; rather, they remain together with him. // 12 //

No, it is said.
Because this negation of departure pertains to [departure] from the embodied Self (<s>śārīra ātman</s>) — not from the body.
How is this understood? Because in another recension, the ablative (<s>pañcamī</s>) is used: 'From him (<s>tasmāt</s>) the <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart.'

children.text: saprāṇasya ca pravasato bhavati utkrāntiḥ dehāt iti evaṃ prāpte prati ucyate -
children.translated_text: When the prima facie view that there is departure from the body for one who departs with the <s>prāṇas</s> is [thus] stated, it is replied:

children.text: spaṣṭo hyekeṣām | BBs_4,2.13 |
children.translated_text: [This is] clear in [the recension of] some. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.13 |

children.text:
na tat asti yat uktaṃ parabrahmavidaḥ api dehāt asti utkrāntiḥ utkrāntipratiṣedhasya deha upādānatvāt iti /
yato deha upādāna eva utkrāntipratiṣedha ekeṣāṃ samāmnātṛṇāṃ spaṣṭa upalabhyate /
tathā hi - ārtabhāgapraśne 'yatrāyaṃ puruṣo mriyata udasmātprāṇāḥ krāmantyāho neti' (bṛ. 3.2.11) iti atra 'neti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ' (bṛ. 3.211) iti anutkrāntipakṣaṃ parigṛhya na tarhi ayam anutkrānteṣu prāṇeṣu mriyata iti asyām āśaṅkāyām 'atraiva samavanīyanta' iti pravilayaṃ prāṇānāṃ pratijñāya tat siddhaye 'sa ucchvayatyādhyātmāyatyādhmāto mṛtaḥ śete' (bṛ. 3.2.11) iti saśabdaparāmṛṣṭasya prakṛtasya utkrānti avadheḥ ucchvayanādīni samāmananti /
dehasya ca etāni syuḥ
children.translated_text:
What was stated — that even for the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> there is departure from the body, because the negation of departure has the body as its reference — that is not correct.
Because the negation of departure with the body as the referent is clearly found in [the recension of] certain teachers.
For thus, in the question of <s>Ārtabhāga</s> — 'When this person dies, do the <s>prāṇas</s> depart from him or not?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.11) — there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> accepts the position of non-departure: 'No, said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.11). Then, when the doubt arises that without the <s>prāṇas</s> departing, this person does not die, [the <s>śruti</s>] asserts the dissolution of the <s>prāṇas</s> [within the body]: 'They dissolve right here.' And to establish that, [the <s>śruti</s>] recounts the swelling and the like of the body — referred to by the word 'sa' (that) — as the terminus of the non-departure: 'He swells, he inflates; inflated, he lies dead' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.2.11).
And these [swelling, etc.] would be [properties] of the body,

children.text:
na dehinaḥ /
tat sāmānyāt 'na tasmātprāṇā utkrāmantyatraiva samavanīyante' iti atra api abheda upacāreṇa dehāpādānasya eva utkramaṇasya pratiṣedhaḥ /
yadi api prādhānyaṃ dehina iti vyākhyeyaṃ yeṣāṃ pañcamī pāṭhaḥ /
yeṣāṃ tu ṣaṣṭhīpāṭhaḥ teṣāṃ vidvat saṃbandhini utkrāntiḥ pratiṣidhyata iti prāpta utkrāntipratiṣedhārthatvāt asya vākyasya dehapādāna eva sā pratiṣiddhā bhavati, dehāt utkrāntiḥ prāptā na dehinaḥ /

api ca 'cakṣuṣo vā mūrdhno vānyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhyastamutkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmati prāṇo 'nūtkrāmantaṃ sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmanti' (bṛ. 4.4.2) iti evam avidvat viṣayaṃ saprapañcam utkramaṇaṃ saṃsāragamanaṃ ca darśayitvā 'iti nu kāmayamānaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti upasaṃhṛtya avidvat kathām 'athākāmayamānaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti vyapadiśya vidvāṃsaṃ yadi tat viṣaye api utkrāntameva prāpadeyasamañjasa eva vyapadeśaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Moreover, having shown in detail the departure and transmigration of the non-knower — 'From the eye, or from the crown of the head, or from other parts of the body, as it [the Self] departs, the <s>prāṇa</s> departs after it; and as the <s>prāṇa</s> departs, all the [other] <s>prāṇas</s> depart after it' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2) — having concluded the account of the non-knower with 'Thus is the one with desires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6), and having designated the knower with 'But the one without desires' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6) — if departure were to be arrived at even in the case of the knower, the designation [of the contrast] would be pointless.

children.text: tasmāt avidviṣaye prāptayoḥ gati utkrāntyoḥ vidvat viṣaye pratiṣedha iti evameva vyākhyeyaṃ vyapadeśārthavattvāya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the departure and the journey — which are prima facie expected in the case of the non-knower — are negated in the case of the knower. This alone should be the interpretation, for the designation [of contrast] to have meaning.

children.text: na ca brahmavidaḥ sarvagatabrahmātmabhūtasya prakṣīṇakāmakarmaṇa utkrāntiḥ gatiḥ vā upapadyate nimitta abhāvāt /
children.translated_text: And for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> — who has become one with the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, whose desires and <s>karmas</s> are exhausted — neither departure nor journey is tenable, because of the absence of a cause.

children.text: 'atra brahma samaśnute' iti ca evañjātīyakāḥ śrutayo gati utkrāntyoḥ abhāvaṃ sūcayanti // 13 //
children.translated_text: And <s>śrutis</s> of the type 'Here he attains <s>Brahman</s>' indicate the absence of journey and departure. // 13 //

not of the embodied [Self].
Because of the similarity [with the present passage], in 'From him the <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart; they dissolve right here' — here too, by figurative identification (<s>abheda-upacāra</s>), the negation is of departure from the body as the point of origin.
Even if, for those whose reading has the ablative (<s>pañcamī</s>), it should be explained that the primary referent is the embodied [Self] — for those whose reading has the genitive (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>), the departure is negated in relation to the knower (<s>vidvat</s>). And since this passage has the purpose of negating the departure that is already prima facie expected, it is the departure from the body — which is prima facie expected — that is negated [here]; departure from the embodied [Self] is not prima facie expected.

children.text: smaryate ca | BBs_4,2.14 |
children.translated_text: And it is remembered [in the <s>smṛti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.14 |

children.text:
smaryate api ca mahābhārate gati utkrāntyoḥ abhāvaḥ - 'sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya samyagbhūtāni paśyataḥ /
devā api mārge muhyantyapadasya padaiṣiṇaḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> too, the absence of journey and departure is remembered: 'Of one who has become the Self of all beings, who sees all beings rightly — even the gods are confounded about his path, seeking the tracks of the trackless one.'

children.text: nanu gatiḥ iti brahmavidaḥ sarvagatabrahmātmabhūtasya smaryate 'śukaḥ kila vaiyāsakirmumukṣurādityamaṇḍalamabhipratasthe pitrā cānugamyāhūto bho iti pratiśuśrāva' iti /
children.translated_text: But is not a journey remembered for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> who has become one with the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>? For '<s>Śuka</s>, the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, seeking liberation, proceeded toward the solar disc; and being called by his father who followed him — "<s>Bho</s>!" — he echoed back [from all directions].'

children.text:
na /
saśarīrasya eva ayaṃ yogabalena viśiṣṭadeśaprāptipūrvakaḥ śarīra utsarga iti draṣṭavyam /
sarvabhūtadṛśyatvādi upanyāsāt /
na hi aśarīraṃ gacchantaṃ sarvabhūtāni draṣṭuṃ śaknuyuḥ /
tathā ca tatra evaupasaṃhṛtam- 'śukastu mārutācchīghrāṃ gatiṃ kṛtvāntarikṣagaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus it is concluded there: '<s>Śuka</s>, moving through the sky with a speed swifter than the wind,

children.text: darśayitvā prabhāvaṃ svaṃ sarvabhūtagato 'bhavat' iti /
children.translated_text: having displayed his own power, became one with all beings.'

children.text: tasmāt abhāvaḥ parabrahmavido gati utkrāntyoḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no journey or departure for the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: gatiśrutīnāṃ tu viṣayam upariṣṭāt vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // 14 //
children.translated_text: And we shall explain the scope of the <s>śrutis</s> on the journey further on [in later <s>sūtras</s>]. // 14 //

No.
This should be seen as the discarding of the body by one who is still embodied, preceded by reaching a special place through the power of <s>yoga</s>.
Because of the mention of being visible to all beings and the like.
For all beings could not see one traveling without a body.

children.text: 7 vāgādilaya adhikaraṇam / sū. 15
children.translated_text: 7 The <s>Vāgādilaya</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 15.

children.text: tāni pare tathā hy āha | BBs_4,2.15 |
children.translated_text: Those [dissolve] in the supreme [Self] — for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] says. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.15 |

children.text:
tāni punaḥ prāṇaśabdoditāni indriyāṇi bhūtāni ca parabrahmavidaḥ tasmin eva parasmin ātmani pralīyante /
kasmāt /
tathā hi āha śrutiḥ - 'evamevāsya paridraṣṭurimāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ puruṣāyaṇāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpyāstaṃ gacchanti (praśna. 6.5) iti.
children.translated_text:
And those senses and elements — denoted by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' — of the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> dissolve in that very supreme Self.
Why?
For thus the <s>śruti</s> says: 'Thus indeed, for this seer, these sixteen parts whose goal is the <s>Puruṣa</s>, reaching the <s>Puruṣa</s>, set [like the sun]' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.5).

children.text: nanu 'gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhāḥ' (mu. 3.2.7) iti vidvat viṣaya eva aparā śrutiḥ parasmāt ātmanaḥ anyatra api kalānāṃ pralayam āha sma /
children.translated_text: But does not another <s>śruti</s> — 'The fifteen parts have gone to their [respective] supports' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 3.2.7) — which pertains to the knower, teach the dissolution of the parts elsewhere than in the supreme Self?

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: sā khalu vyavahārāpekṣā, pārthivādyāḥ kalāḥ pṛthivyādiḥ eva svaprakṛtīḥ apīyanti iti /
children.translated_text: That [passage] is from the transactional perspective: the earthy and other parts return to their own respective material causes — earth and the like.

children.text: itarā tu vidvat pratipatti apekṣā, kṛtsnaṃ kalājātaṃ parabrahmavido brahma eva saṃpadyata iti /
children.translated_text: But the other [passage] is from the perspective of the knower's realization: the entire aggregate of parts of the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s> merges into <s>Brahman</s> alone.

children.text: tasmāt adoṣaḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no fault. // 15 //

children.text: 8 avibhāga adhikaraṇam / sū. 16
children.translated_text: 8 The <s>Avibhāga</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 16.

children.text: avibhāgo vacanāt | BBs_4,2.16 |
children.translated_text: Non-differentiation [is the result] — because of the statement [of scripture]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.16 |

children.text:
sa puna- viduṣaḥ kalāpralayaḥ kim itareṣām iva sāvaśeṣo bhavati āhosvit niravaśeṣa iti /
tatra pralayasāmānyāt śakti avaśeṣatāprasaktau bravīti - avibhāgāpattiḥ eva iti /
kutaḥ - vacanāt /
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the statement [of scripture].

children.text: tathā hi kalāpralayam uktvā vakti - 'bhidyate tāsāṃ nāmarūpe puruṣa ityevaṃ procyate sa eṣo 'kalo 'mṛto bhavati' (pra. 6.5) iti /
children.translated_text: For thus, having stated the dissolution of the parts, [the <s>śruti</s>] says: 'Their names and forms are destroyed; he is called simply "<s>Puruṣa</s>" — he becomes partless, immortal' (<s>Praśna</s> 6.5).

children.text: avidyā nimittānāṃ ca kalānāṃ na vidyānimitte pralaye sāvaśeṣatva upapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: And of the faculties (<s>kalās</s>) whose cause is <s>avidyā</s>, there is no tenability of a remainder in the dissolution whose cause is <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: tasmāt avibhāga eva iti // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [there is] non-distinction alone. // 16 //

Now, is this dissolution of the parts of the knower one that leaves a remainder (as in the case of others) — or is it complete, without remainder?
When the view that it leaves a remainder of potentiality (<s>śakti</s>) is prima facie established — because of the general [notion of] dissolution — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: [The result is] the attainment of non-differentiation alone.

children.text: 9 tadokaḥ adhikaraṇam / sū. 17
children.translated_text: 9. The <s>Tadokas Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Abode of That). <s>Sūtra</s> 17.

children.text: tadokograjvalanaṃ tatprakāśitadvāro vidyāsāmarthyāt taccheṣagatyanusmṛtiyogāc ca hārdānugṛhītāḥ śatādhikayā | BBs_4,2.17 |
children.translated_text: The tip of that — its abode — blazes forth; the door illuminated by that; by the power of <s>vidyā</s>, and because of the connection with the practice of the path that is the sequel of that; favored by the One in the heart, [the soul departs] through the one hundred and first [<s>nāḍī</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.17 |

children.text:
samāptā prāsaṅgikī paravidyāgatā cintā /
saṃpratitu aparavidyāviṣayām eva cintām anuvartayati /
samānā ca asṛti upakramāt vidvat aviduṣoḥ utkrāntiḥiti uktaṃ tam idānīṃ sati upakramaṃ darśayati /
tasya upasaṃhṛtavāgādi kalāpasya uccikramiṣato vijñānātmana oka āyatanaṃ hṛdayam 'sa etāstejomātrāḥ samabhyādadāno hṛdayamevānvavakrāmati' iti śruteḥ /
tat agraprajvalanapūrvikā cakṣurādisthāna apādānā ca utkrāntiḥ śrūyate - 'tasya haitasya hṛdayasyāgraṃ pradyotate tena pradyotenaiṣa ātmā niṣkrāmati cakṣuṣo vā mūrdhno vānyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhyaḥ' (bṛ. 4.4.2) iti /
sā kim aniyamena eva vidvat aviduṣoḥ bhavati atha asti kaścit viduṣo viśeṣaniyama iti vicikitsāyāṃ śruti aviśeṣāt aniyamaprāptau ācaṣṭe - samā api hi vidvat aviduṣoḥ hṛdayāgrapradyotane tat prakāśitadvāratve ca mūrdhasthānāt eva vidvān niṣkrāmati sthānāntarebhyaḥ tu itare /
kutaḥ - vidyāsāmarthyāt /
yadi vidvān apītaravat yataḥ kutaścit dehadeśāt utkrāmeta na eva utkṛṣṭaṃ lokaṃ labheta /
tatra ānarthikā eva vidyā syāt /
tat śeṣagati anusmṛtiyogāt ca vidyāśeṣabhūtā ca mūrdhani anāḍīsaṃbaddhā gatiḥ anuśīlayitavyā vidyāviśeṣeṣu vihitā tām abhyasyan tasya eva pratiṣṭhita iti yuktam /
children.translated_text: And because of the connection with the practice of the path that is the sequel of that [<s>vidyā</s>] — the path connected with the crown of the head and associated with the <s>nāḍī</s> is to be practiced, being prescribed in specific <s>vidyās</s>. One who practices that is established in that [path] alone — this is fitting.

children.text: tasmāt hṛdayālayena brahmaṇā su upāsitena anugṛhītaḥ tadbhāvaṃ samāpanno vidvān mūrdhanyayā eva śatādhikayā śatāt atiriktayā ekaśatatamyā nāḍyā niṣkrāmati itarābhiḥ itare /
children.translated_text: Therefore, favored by <s>Brahman</s> who dwells in the heart and has been well meditated upon, having attained the state of That, the knower departs through the one hundred and first <s>nāḍī</s> alone — the one that goes to the crown of the head, exceeding one hundred — while the others [depart] through the other [<s>nāḍīs</s>].

children.text: tathā hi hārdavidyāṃ prakṛtya samāmananti - 'śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyastāsāṃ mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtaikā /
children.translated_text: For thus, having introduced the <s>hārda-vidyā</s> (meditation on the One in the heart), they (<s>śrutis</s>) declare: 'One hundred and one are the <s>nāḍīs</s> of the heart; of these, one has proceeded to the crown of the head.

children.text: tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti viṣvaṅṅnyā utkrameṇa bhavanti' (chā. 8.6.6) iti // 17 //
children.translated_text: Going upward through that, one attains immortality; the others, at the time of departure, go in various directions' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.6). // 17 //

The incidental inquiry concerning <s>paravidyā</s> (higher knowledge) is concluded.
Now [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] continues the inquiry pertaining to <s>aparavidyā</s> (lower knowledge) alone.
It was stated that the departure (<s>utkrānti</s>) of the knower and the non-knower is the same from the standpoint of the commencement of the path. Now, when there is a commencement [of departure], he shows [the process].
For that <s>vijñānātman</s> (conscious self) who has withdrawn the aggregate of faculties beginning with speech, and who wishes to depart — the abode (<s>okas</s>) is the heart, as [stated in] the <s>śruti</s>: 'Having gathered these luminous particles, he descends into the heart itself' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5).
The departure — preceded by the blazing of its (the heart's) tip, and originating from the stations of the eye and the like — is heard [in the <s>śruti</s>]: 'The tip of this heart blazes forth; by that blazing, this Self departs — either through the eye, or through the crown of the head, or through other parts of the body' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.2).
Is this [departure] the same for the knower and the non-knower without distinction? Or is there some specific restriction for the knower? — When this doubt arises, and when [the prima facie view] that there is no restriction — because the <s>śruti</s> makes no distinction — is arrived at, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] declares: Even though the blazing of the heart's tip and the illumination of the door [of departure] are the same for both the knower and the non-knower, the knower departs through the station at the crown of the head alone, while the others [depart] through the other stations.
Why? Because of the power of <s>vidyā</s>.
If the knower were to depart — like others — from any random part of the body, he would not attain an exalted world.
In that case, <s>vidyā</s> would be pointless.

children.text: raśmi adhikaraṇam / sū. 18
children.translated_text: The <s>Raśmi Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Rays). <s>Sūtra</s> 18.

children.text: raśmyanusārī | BBs_4,2.18 |
children.translated_text: Following the rays [of the sun]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.18 |

children.text: asti hārdavidyā - 'atha yadidamasminbrahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma' (chā. 8.1.1) iti upakramya vihitā /

tat prakriyāyām 'atha yā etā hṛdayasya nāḍyaḥ' (chā. 8.6.1) iti upakramya saprapañcaṃ nāḍīraśmisaṃbandham uktvā uktam 'atha yatraitadasmāccharīrādutkrāmatyathaitaireva raśmibhirūrdhvamākramate' (chā. 8.6.5) iti /
children.translated_text: In that context, having introduced [the topic] with 'Now, these <s>nāḍīs</s> of the heart' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.1), and having described in detail the connection between the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rays [of the sun], it was stated: 'Now, when he departs from this body, he ascends upward by these very rays' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5).

children.text: punaḥ ca uktam 'tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti' (chā. 8.6.6) iti /
children.translated_text: And again it was stated: 'Going upward through that, one attains immortality' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.6).

children.text: tasmāt śatādhikayā nāḍyā niṣkrāman raśmi anusārī niṣkrāmati iti gamyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is understood that one who departs through the one hundred and first <s>nāḍī</s> departs following the rays [of the sun].

children.text: tat kiṃm aviśeṣeṇa eva ahani rātrau vā mriyamāṇasya raśmi anusāritvam āhosvit ahani eva iti saṃśaye sati aviśeṣaśravaṇāt aviśeṣeṇa eva tāvat raśmi anusāri iti pratijñāyate // 18 //
children.translated_text: Now, does this following of the rays apply without distinction to one who dies during the day or at night? Or does it apply only during the day? — When this doubt arises, since the <s>śruti</s> makes no distinction, it is first maintained that [the soul] follows the rays without distinction, [whether death occurs by day or night]. // 18 //
There is the <s>hārda-vidyā</s> — which is taught beginning with: 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s>, there is a small lotus-shaped dwelling' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1).

children.text: niśi neti cen na sambandhasya yāvaddehabhāvitvād darśayati ca | BBs_4,2.19 |
children.translated_text: [If one objects:] Not at night — [we say:] No, because the connection [between <s>nāḍīs</s> and rays] lasts as long as the body lasts; and [the <s>śruti</s>] shows this. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.19 |

children.text:
asti ahani nāḍīraśmisaṃbandha iti ahani mṛtasya syāt raśmi anusāritvaṃ rātrau tu pretasya na syāt /
nāḍīraśmisaṃbandhavicchedāt iti cet /
children.translated_text: The connection between the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rays exists during the day; therefore, for one who dies during the day, there would be the following of the rays, but for one who dies at night, there would not be — because of the severance of the connection between the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rays — if this is the objection,

children.text:
na /
nāḍīraśmisaṃbandhasya yāvat dehabhāvitvāt /
yāvat dehabhāvī hi śirākiraṇasaṃparkaḥ /
darśayati ca etamarthaṃ śrutiḥ - 'amuṣmādādityātpratāyante tā āsu nāḍīṣu sṛptā ābhyo nāḍībhyaḥ pratāyante te 'muṣminnāditye sṛptāḥ' (chā. 8.6.2) iti nidāghasamaye ca niśāsu api kiraṇa anuvṛttiḥ upalabhyate pratāpādikāryadarśanāt /
stoka anuvṛtteḥ tu durlakṣyatvam ṛtvantararajanīṣu śaiśireṣu iva durdineṣu /
'aharevaitadrātrau dadhāti' iti ca etadeva darśayati /
yadi ca rātrau preto vinā eva raśmi anusāreṇa ūrdhvam ākrameta raśmi anusāra ānarthakyaṃ bhavet /
na hi etat viśiṣya adhīyate yo divā praiti sa raśmīn apekṣya ūrdvam ākramate yaḥ tu rātrau saḥ anapekṣya eva iti /
atha tu vidvān api rātriprāyaṇa aparādhamātreṇa na ūrdhvam ākrameta pākṣikaphalā vidyā iti apravṛttiḥ eva tasyāṃ syāt /
mṛtyukālāniyamāt /
atha api rātrau uparataḥ aharāgamam udīkṣeta /
children.translated_text: And even if one who dies at night were to wait for the arrival of day,

children.text: aharāgame api asya kadācit araśmisaṃbandhārhaṃ śarīraṃ syāt pāvakādisaṃparkāt /
children.translated_text: even when day arrives, his body might sometimes be unfit for connection with the rays, because of contact with fire and the like [i.e., cremation].

children.text: 'sa yāvatkṣipyenmanastāvadādityaṃ gacchati' (chā. 8.6.5) iti ca śrutiḥ anudīkṣāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> — 'As quickly as the mind [can reach], so quickly he goes to the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5) — shows that there is no waiting.

children.text: tasmāt tat aviśeṣeṇa eva idaṃ rātridivaṃ raśmi anusāritvam // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this following of the rays [applies] without distinction, whether by night or by day. // 19 //

No.
Because the connection between the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rays lasts as long as the body lasts.
For the contact between the veins (<s>śirā</s>) and the rays persists as long as the body persists.
And the <s>śruti</s> shows this meaning: 'From that sun the [rays] extend and are inserted into these <s>nāḍīs</s>; from these <s>nāḍīs</s> they extend and are inserted into that sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.2). And even during nights in the hot season, the continuation of the rays is perceived, because of the observation of effects such as heat and the like.
The imperceptibility in nights of other seasons — such as the cold season — is due to their slight continuation, as on cloudy days.
And [the <s>śruti</s>] 'By day alone it establishes this at night' shows this very [point].
Moreover, if one who dies at night were to ascend upward without following the rays, the following of the rays would be purposeless.
For [the <s>śruti</s>] does not specifically teach that one who dies during the day ascends upward depending on the rays, while one who [dies] at night [ascends] independently [of them].
Furthermore, if even a knower, merely because of the fault of dying at night, were not to ascend upward, then — <s>vidyā</s> having only a partial fruit — there would be no engagement in it at all,
because the time of death is not fixed.

children.text: 11 dakṣiṇāyana adhikaraṇam / sū. 20-21
children.translated_text: 11. The <s>Dakṣiṇāyana Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Southern Path). <s>Sūtras</s> 20-21.

children.text: ataś cāyane 'pi dakṣiṇe | BBs_4,2.20 |
children.translated_text: And therefore, even [if death occurs] during the southern course [of the sun]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.20 |

children.text: ata eva ca udīkṣā anupapatteḥ apākṣikaphalatvāt ca vidyāyā aniyatakālatvāt ca mṛtyoḥ dakṣiṇa ayane api mriyamāṇo vidvān prāpnoti eva vidyāphalam /

uttarāyaṇa maraṇa prāśasti aprasiddherbhīṣmasya ca pratīkṣādarśanāt 'āpūryamāṇapakṣādyānṣaḍudaṅṅeti māsāṃstān' (chā. 4.15.5) iti ca śruteḥ apekṣitavyam uttarāyaṇam iti imām āśaṅkām anena sūtreṇa apanudati /
children.translated_text: The apprehension — that, because of the well-known praise of dying during <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> (the northern course), because of the observation of <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s waiting [for <s>uttarāyaṇa</s>], and because of the <s>śruti</s> 'From the bright half onward, through the six months during which [the sun] moves northward' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.5), one should wait for <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> — this apprehension he removes by this <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: prāśastyaprasiddhiḥ avidvat viṣayā /
children.translated_text: The well-known praise [of <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> death] pertains to the non-knower.

children.text: bhīṣmasya pratipālanam ācārapratipālanārthaṃ pitṛprasādalabdhasvacchandamṛtyutākhyāpanārthaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣma</s>'s waiting was for the purpose of upholding traditional practice, and for the purpose of making known his power of dying at will, obtained by the grace of his father.

children.text: śruteḥ tu arthaṃ vakṣyati 'ātivāhikāstalliṅgāt' (bra. sū. 4.3.4) iti // 20 //
children.translated_text: But the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>, he will explain [later] in '<s>Ātivāhikās</s> — because of the indicative mark' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.3.4). // 20 //

For this very reason — because waiting is untenable, because <s>vidyā</s> does not have a partial fruit, and because the time of death is not fixed — even one who dies during the <s>dakṣiṇāyana</s> (southern course of the sun), if he is a knower, attains the fruit of <s>vidyā</s> indeed.

children.text:
nanu ca - 'yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ /
prayātā yānti taṃ phalaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha' (gī. 8.23) iti kālaprādhānyena upakramya aharādikālaviśeṣaḥ smṛtau apunarāvṛttaye niyamitaḥ kathaṃ rātrau dakṣiṇāyane vā prayāto anāvṛttiṃ yāyāditi /
children.translated_text: But [an objection arises:] Having introduced [the topic] with [the <s>Gītā</s> verse]: 'The time at which <s>yogins</s>, departing, attain non-return or return — that I shall declare to you, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.23) — giving primacy to time — a specific time-period of day and the like is fixed in the <s>smṛti</s> for the sake of non-return. How then could one who departs at night or during <s>dakṣiṇāyana</s> attain non-return?

children.text: atra ucyate -
children.translated_text: To this we say:

children.text: yoginaḥ prati ca smaryete smārte caite | BBs_4,2.21 |
children.translated_text: And [this time-restriction applies] with reference to <s>yogins</s> in the <s>smṛti</s>; and these [paths] too are of <s>smṛti</s> [origin]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,2.21 |

children.text:
yoginaḥ prati ca ayam aharādikālaviniyogaḥ anāvṛttaye smaryate /
smārte ca ete yogasāṃkhye na śraute /
ato viṣayabhedāt pramāṇāviśeṣāt ca na asya smārtasya kālaviniyogasya śrauteṣu vijñāneṣu avatāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
And this assignment of specific times — day and the like — for the sake of non-return is stated in the <s>smṛti</s> with reference to <s>yogins</s>.
And these two [paths — <s>devayāna</s> and <s>pitṛyāna</s> — mentioned there] belong to <s>smṛti</s>, being of the <s>Yoga</s> and <s>Sāṃkhya</s> systems, not of the <s>śruti</s>.
Therefore, because of the difference in subject matter and because of the non-superiority of this [<s>smṛti</s>] authority, this <s>smṛti</s>-based time-assignment does not enter into the <s>śruti</s>-based <s>vidyās</s>.

children.text:
nanu - 'agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam' /
'dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam' (gī. 8. 24,25) iti ca śrautau etau devayānapitṛyāṇau pratyabhijñāyete smṛtau api iti /
children.translated_text: But [one might object:] '<s>Agni</s>, light, day, the bright [fortnight], the six months of the northern course' and '<s>Dhūma</s> (smoke), night, the dark [fortnight], the six months of the southern course' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.24-25) — these two, the <s>devayāna</s> and <s>pitṛyāna</s> known from <s>śruti</s>, are recognized in the <s>smṛti</s> as well!

children.text: ucyate - 'taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi' (gī. 8.23) iti smṛtau kālapratijñānāt virodham āśaṅkya parihāra uktaḥ /
children.translated_text: We reply: In the <s>smṛti</s>, because of the declaration 'I shall declare that time' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 8.23) — apprehending a contradiction [with <s>śruti</s>] because of the <s>smṛti</s>'s emphasis on time — the resolution was stated [in the <s>sūtra</s>].

children.text: yadā punaḥ smṛtau api agnyādyā devatā eva ativāhikyo gṛhyante tadā na kaścit virodha iti // 21 //
