children.translated_text: But when, even in the <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Agni</s> and the like are understood as <s>ātivāhika</s> deities (escorting deities) [rather than time-periods], then there is no contradiction whatsoever. // 21 //

children.text: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye caturthādhyāyasya dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣya</s> composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, the supreme <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya</s>. // 2 //

children.text: caturthe 'dhyāye tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fourth <s>adhyāya</s>, third <s>pāda</s>.

children.text: atra pāde saguṇavidyāvato mṛtasya uttaramārga abhidhānam
children.translated_text: In this <s>pāda</s>, the northern path of one who has died possessing <s>saguṇa-vidyā</s> (qualified knowledge) is described.

children.text: 1 arcirādi adhikaraṇam / sū. 1
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Arcirādi Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Path Beginning with Light). <s>Sūtra</s> 1.

children.text: arcirādinā tatprathiteḥ | BBs_4,3.1 |
children.translated_text: Through the path beginning with light (<s>arcis</s>) — because that [path] is well known. | <s>BBs</s> 4,3.1 |

children.text:
āsṛti upakramāt samāna utkrāntiḥ iti uktam /
sṛtistu śrutyantareṣu anekadhā śrūyate /
nāḍīraśmisaṃbandhena ekadhā 'athaitaireva raśmibhirūrdhva ākramate' (chā. 8.6.5) iti /
arcirādika ekā 'te 'rciṣamabhisaṃbhavantyarciṣo 'haḥ' (bṛ. 6.2.15) iti /
'sa etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānamāsādyāgnilokamāgacchati' (kau. 1.3) iti anyā /
'yadā vai puruṣo 'smāllokātpraiti sa vāyumāgacchati' (bṛ. 5.10.1) iti aparā /
'sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti' (muṇḍa, 1.2.11) iti ca aparā /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ parasparaṃ bhinnā etāḥ sṛtaya kiṃ va eka eva anekaviśeṣaṇa iti /
tatra prāptaṃ tāvat bhinnāḥ etāḥ sṛtaya iti /
bhinnaprakaraṇatvāt /
bhinna upāsanāśeṣatvāt ca /
api ca 'athaitaireva raśmibhiḥ'(chā. 8.6.5) iti avadhāraṇam arcirādi apekṣāyām uparudhyeta /
tvarāvacanaṃ ca pīḍyeta 'sa yāvatkṣipyenmanastāvadādityaṃ gacchati' (chā. 8.6.5) iti /
tasmāt anyonyabhinnā eva ete panthāna iti /
evaṃ prāpte abhidadhmahe - arcirādina iti - sarvo brahmaprepsuḥ arcirādina eva adhvanā raṃhati iti pratijānīmahe /
kutaḥ - tat prathiteḥ /
prathito hi eṣa mārgaḥ sarveṣāṃ viduṣām /
tathā hi pañcāgnividyāprakaraṇe 'ye 'cāmī araṇye śraddhāṃ satyamupāsate' (bṛ. 6.2.15) iti vidyāntaraśīlinām api arcirādikā sṛtiḥ śrāvyate /
syāt etat /
yāsu vidyāsu na kācit gatiḥ ucyate tāsu iyam arcirādika upatiṣṭhatāṃ yāsu tu anyā śrāvyate tāsu kim iti arcirādi āśrayaṇam iti /
children.translated_text:
It was stated that the departure [of the knower and the non-knower] is the same from the standpoint of the commencement of the path.
But the path (<s>sṛti</s>) is heard in various ways in different <s>śrutis</s>.
In one way, through the connection of the <s>nāḍīs</s> and the rays: 'He ascends upward by these very rays' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5).
One [path begins] with light (<s>arcis</s>) and the like: 'They reach the light (<s>arcis</s>); from light, the day' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15).
'He, reaching this <s>devayāna</s> path, arrives at the world of <s>Agni</s>' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.3) — this is another.
'When a person departs from this world, he reaches <s>Vāyu</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.10.1) — this is yet another.
'Through the door of the sun, they go forth, free from stain' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 1.2.11) — and this is yet another.
There, the doubt arises: Are these paths mutually different, or is there a single [path] with multiple qualifications?
The prima facie view is: These paths are different,
because they occur in different contexts,
and because they are subsidiary to different <s>upāsanās</s>.
Moreover, the emphatic particle in 'by these very rays' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5) would be obstructed if the path beginning with light were also required.
And the statement of swiftness — 'As quickly as the mind [can reach], so quickly he goes to the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.5) — would be compromised.
Therefore, these paths are indeed mutually different.
Having thus arrived [at the prima facie view], we say: 'Through the path beginning with light' — every seeker of <s>Brahman</s> travels by the path beginning with light (<s>arcis</s>) alone — this we maintain.
Why? Because that [path] is well known.
For this path is well known for all knowers.
For thus, in the context of the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s>, even for practitioners of other <s>vidyās</s>, the path beginning with light is taught: 'Those who in the forest meditate with faith on truth' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15).
One might think:
Let this path beginning with light serve those <s>vidyās</s> in which no particular path is mentioned; but in those where another [path] is taught, why should the path beginning with light be resorted to?

children.text:
atra ucyate - bhavet etadevaṃ yadi atyantabhinnā eva etāḥ sṛtayaḥ syuḥ /
eka eva tu eṣā sṛtiḥanekaviśeṣaṇā brahmalokaprapadanī kvacit kenacit viśeṣaṇena upalakṣita iti vadāmaḥ /
sarvatra ekadeśapratyabhijñānāt itaretara viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva upapatteḥ /
prakaraṇabhede api hi vidyā ekatve bhavati itaretara viśeṣaṇa upasaṃhāravat gativiśeṣaṇānām api upasaṃhāraḥ /
vidyābhede api tu gati ekadeśapratyabhijñānāt gantavya abhedāt ca gati abheda eva /
tathā hi 'te teṣu brahmalokeṣu parāḥ parāvato vasanti' (bṛ. 6.2.15) 'tasminvasanti śāśvatīḥ samāḥ' (bṛ. 5.101) 'sā yā brahmaṇo jitiryā vyuṣṭistāṃ jitiṃ jayati tāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ vyaśnute' (kauṣī. 1.4) 'tadya evaitaṃ brahmalokaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindati' (chā. 8.4.3) iti ca tatra tatra tat eva ekaṃ phalaṃ brahmalokaprāptilakṣaṇaṃ pradarśyate /
yat tu etaiḥ eva iti avadhāraṇam arcirādi āśrayaṇe na syāt iti /
children.translated_text:
To this we say: This would be so if these paths were entirely different.
But we say that this is a single path with multiple qualifications — sometimes identified by one qualification in one place.
Because of the recognition of common elements everywhere, the mutual qualifier-qualified relationship is tenable.
For even when the contexts differ, just as there is the gathering of qualifications from different <s>vidyās</s> when the <s>vidyā</s> is one, so too there is the gathering of path-qualifications.
And even when the <s>vidyās</s> differ, because of the recognition of common elements in the path and because of the non-difference of the destination, the path is indeed one.
For thus, in various places, the same single fruit — characterized by the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> — is shown: 'In those <s>Brahmalokas</s>, they dwell as the highest of the highest' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15); 'They dwell therein for eternal years' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.10.1); 'That which is the victory of <s>Brahman</s>, that which is the dawn — he wins that victory, he attains that dawn' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.4); 'Those who find this <s>Brahmaloka</s> through <s>brahmacarya</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.4.3).
As for the objection that the emphatic particle 'eva' (alone/very) in 'by these very rays' would be inapplicable if the path beginning with light were also required —

children.text:
na eṣa doṣaḥ /
raśmiprāptiparatvāt asya /
na hi eka eva śabdo raśmīn ca prāpayitum arhati arcirādīn ca vyāvartayitum /
tasmāt raśmisaṃbandha eva ayamavadhāryata iti draṣṭavyam /
tvarāvacanaṃ tu arcirādi apekṣāyām api gantavyāntarāpekṣā śaighryārthatvāt na uparudhyate /
yathā nimiṣamātreṇa atra āgamyata iti /
children.translated_text: Just as [one says] 'He arrived here in the blink of an eye.'

children.text: api ca 'athaitayoḥ pathornakatareṇācana' (chā. 5.108) iti mārgadvayabhraṣṭānāṃ kaṣṭaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sthānam ācakṣāṇā pitṛyāṇavyatiriktam ekameva devayānam arcirādiparvāṇaṃ panthānaṃ prathayati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, [the <s>Chāndogya</s> passage] 'Now, those who follow neither of these two paths' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.8) — describing a wretched third state for those who have fallen from both paths — proclaims only one single <s>devayāna</s> path, distinct from the <s>pitṛyāṇa</s>, having stages beginning with <s>arcis</s> (flame).

children.text: bhūyāṃsi arcirādisṛtau mārgaparvāṇi alpīyāṃsi tu anyatra /
children.translated_text: On the path through <s>arcis</s> and the like, the stages of the route are more numerous, while on the other [<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>], they are fewer.

children.text: bhūyasāṃ ca anuguṇyena alpīyasāṃ nayanaṃ nyāyyam iti ataḥ api arcirādinā tat prathiteḥ iti uktam // 1 //
children.translated_text: And it is proper to incorporate the fewer [stages] in accordance with the more numerous [stages] — therefore, it is said: 'Because of that being made known through the [path of] <s>arcis</s> and the like.' // 1 //

This is not a defect. Because this [statement about the rays] is directed at the attainment of the rays [of the sun]. For a single word cannot serve both to bring [the soul] to the rays and to exclude the [path through] <s>arcis</s> (flame) and the like. Therefore, it should be understood that what is ascertained here is the connection with the rays alone. And the statement about quickness, even while the dependence on the [stages of] <s>arcis</s> and the like [is maintained], is not obstructed — because it is meant to indicate the swiftness [of the journey] in relation to the remaining distances to be traversed.

children.text: 2 vāyu adhikaraṇam / sū. 2
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Vāyvādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of <s>Vāyu</s>). <s>Sūtra</s> 2.

children.text: vāyum abdād aviśeṣaviśeṣābhyām | BBs_4,3.2 |
children.translated_text: [The soul reaches] <s>Vāyu</s> after the year — because of both the non-specific and the specific [statements]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.2 |

children.text:
kena punaḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣeṇa gativiśeṣāṇānām itaretara viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva iti tat etat suhṛt bhūtvā ācāryo grathayati /
'sa etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānamāpadyāgnilokamāgacchati sa vāyulokaṃ sa indralokaṃ sa prajāpatilokaṃ sa brahmalokam'(kau. 1.3) iti kauṣītakīnāṃ devayānaḥ panthāḥ paṭhyate /
tatra arciḥ agnilokaśabdau tāvat ekārthau jvalanavacanatvāt iti na atra saṃniveśakramaḥ kvacit anveṣyaḥ /
vāyuḥ tu arcirādau vartmani na śrutaḥ katam asmin sthāne niveśayitavya iti /
children.translated_text: Now, in what particular arrangement are the various stages of the journey to be understood as qualifying one another? The teacher, acting as a friend, weaves [the arrangement] together. 'He reaches this <s>devayāna</s> path — he comes to the world of fire, to the world of <s>Vāyu</s>, to the world of <s>Indra</s>, to the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>, to the world of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.3) — thus the <s>devayāna</s> path is read among the <s>Kauṣītakins</s>. There, '<s>arcis</s>' (flame) and '<s>agniloka</s>' (world of fire) — since both denote fire — are synonymous, so no question of arrangement arises here. But <s>Vāyu</s> is not mentioned in the [<s>Chāndogya</s>] path beginning with <s>arcis</s> — in what position should it be placed?

children.text:
ucyate - 'te 'rciṣamevābhisaṃbhavantyarciṣo 'harahna āpūryamāṇapakṣamāpūryamāṇapakṣādyānṣaḍudaṅṅeti māṃsāstān māsebhyaḥsaṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsarādityam' (chā. 5.10.1,2) iti atra saṃvatsarāt parāñcam ādityāt arvāñcaṃ vāyum abhisaṃbhavanti /
kasmāt /
aviśeṣaviśeṣābhyām /
tathā hi - 'sa vāyulokam '(kau. 1.3) iti atrāviśeṣa upadiṣṭasya vāyoḥ śrutyantare viśeṣa upadośo dṛśyate 'yadā vai puruṣo 'smāllokātpraiti sa vāyumāgacchati tasmai sa tatra vijihīte yathā rathacakrasya khaṃ tena sa ūrdhvamākramate sa ādityamāgacchati' (bṛ. 5.101) iti /
etasmāt ādityāt vāyoḥ pūrvatvadarśanāt viśeṣāt abda ādityayoḥ antarāle vāyuḥ niveśayitavyaḥ /
kasmāt punaḥ agneḥ paratvadarśanāt viśeṣāt arciṣaḥ anantaraṃ vāyuḥ na niveśyate /
na eṣaḥ asti viśeṣa iti vadāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: We say: In 'They reach the flame, from the flame the day, from the day the bright fortnight, from the bright fortnight the six months during which the sun moves northward, from those months the year, from the year the sun' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.1-2) — after the year and before the sun, they reach <s>Vāyu</s>. Why? Because of both the non-specific and the specific [statements]. For thus: '<s>Vāyu</s>' — mentioned without specific [positional] indication in 'He [reaches] the world of <s>Vāyu</s>' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.3) — is seen to receive a specific indication in another <s>śruti</s>: 'When a person departs from this world, he comes to <s>Vāyu</s>; there [<s>Vāyu</s>] opens for him like the hole of a chariot-wheel; through that he ascends upward; he reaches the sun' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 5.10.1). From this specific indication showing that <s>Vāyu</s> comes before the sun, <s>Vāyu</s> should be placed between the year and the sun. But why is <s>Vāyu</s> not placed immediately after the flame — from the specific indication showing it comes after fire?

children.text: nanu udāhṛtā śrutiḥ - 'sa etaṃ devayānaṃ panthānamāpadyāgnilokamāgacchati sa vāyulokaṃ sa varuṇalokam' (kauṣī. 1.3) iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the <s>śruti</s> was cited: 'He reaches this <s>devayāna</s> path — he comes to the world of fire, [then] the world of <s>Vāyu</s>, the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.3).

children.text:
ucyate - kevala- atra pāṭhaḥ paurvāparyeṇāvasthito na atra kramavacanaḥ /
kaścit śabdaḥ asti /
padārtha upadarśanamātraṃ hi atra kriyate etam etaṃ ca āgacchati iti itaratra punaḥ vāyuprattena rathacakramātreṇa cchidreṇa ūrdhvam ākramya ādityam āgacchati iti avagamyate kramaḥ /
tasmāt sūktam aviśeṣaviśeṣābhyām iti /
vājasaneyinaḥ tu 'māsebhyo devalokaṃ devalokādādityam' (bṛ. 6.2.15) iti samāmananti /
tatra ādityān antaryāya devalokāt vāyum abhisaṃbhaveyuḥ /
vāyum abdāt iti tu chandogaśruti apekṣayā uktam /
children.translated_text: But '[<s>Vāyu</s> is placed] after the year' is stated with reference to the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: chāndogya vājasaneyakayoḥ tu ekatra devaloko na vidyate paratra saṃvatsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Between the <s>Chāndogya</s> and the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s> [recensions], in one the 'world of the gods' (<s>devaloka</s>) is absent, and in the other the 'year' (<s>saṃvatsara</s>) [is absent].

children.text: tatra śrutidvayapratyayāt ubhau api ubhayatra grathayitavyau /
children.translated_text: Since both [stages] are known from the two <s>śrutis</s>, both should be woven into both [recensions].

children.text: tatra api māsasaṃbandhāt saṃvatsaraḥ pūrvaḥ paścimo devaloka iti vivektavyam // 2 //
children.translated_text: There too, because of the connection with the months, the year comes first and the world of the gods later — this should be distinguished. // 2 //

We say: There, the mere listing does not indicate a fixed order — there is no word [in that passage] expressing sequence. What is done there is merely a display of the items — 'he reaches this one and that one.' But in the other [passage], the sequence is understood — that by <s>Vāyu</s> opening an aperture the size of a chariot-wheel, [the soul] ascends upward and reaches the sun. Therefore, it is well said: 'Because of both the non-specific and the specific.' The <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, however, recite: 'From the months to the world of the gods, from the world of the gods to the sun' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15). There, [<s>Vāyu</s>] would be reached — going between the sun — from the world of the gods to <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: 3 taḍidadhikaraṇam / sū. 3
children.translated_text: 3. The <s>Taḍidadhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Lightning). <s>Sūtra</s> 3.

children.text: taṭito 'dhi varuṇaḥ saṃbandhāt | BBs_4,3.3 |
children.translated_text: After lightning [comes] <s>Varuṇa</s> — because of the connection. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.3 |

children.text:
'ādityāccandramasaṃ candramaso vidyutam' (chā. 4.15.5) iti asyā vidyuta upariṣṭāt sa varuṇalokam iti ayaṃ varuṇaḥ saṃbadhyate /
asti hi saṃbandho vidyut varuṇayoḥ /
yadā hi viśāla avidyutaḥ tīvraḥ tanitaniḥ ghoṣā jīmūta udareṣu pranṛtyanti āthāpaḥ prapatanti /
vidyotate stanayati 'varṣiṣyati vā' (chā. 7.11.1) iti ca brāhmaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'It flashes, it thunders — it is about to rain' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.11.1) — thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [states].

children.text: apāṃ ca adhipatiḥ varuṇa iti śrutismṛtiprasiddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And the well-known understanding from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> is that <s>Varuṇa</s> is the lord of waters.

children.text: varuṇāt adhīndraprajāpatī sthānāntara abhāvāt pāṭhasāmarthyāt ca /
children.translated_text: After <s>Varuṇa</s> [come] <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> — because of the absence of another place [for them] and because of the force of the textual reading.

children.text: ānantukatvāt api varuṇādīnām anta eva niveśo vaiśeṣikasthānābhāvāt vidyut ca antya arcirādau vartmani // 3 //
children.translated_text: Because <s>Varuṇa</s> and the others are supplementary [to the path], they are placed at the end [of the route] — since there is no specific place for them; and lightning is the last [stage] in the path beginning with <s>arcis</s>. // 3 //

'From the sun to the moon, from the moon to lightning' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.5) — above this lightning, <s>Varuṇa</s> is to be connected — '[He reaches] the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>.' For there is a connection between lightning and <s>Varuṇa</s>. For when vast, thunderless, intense rumbles dance in the bellies of the clouds — then the waters fall.

children.text: 4 ātivāhika adhikaraṇam / sū. 4-6
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Ātivāhikādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Guides). <s>Sūtras</s> 4-6.

children.text: ātivāhikās talliṅgāt | BBs_4,3.4 |
children.translated_text: They are guides (<s>ātivāhikas</s>) — because of the indicatory mark. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.4 |

children.text:
teṣu eva arcirādiṣu saṃśayaḥ - kim etāni mārgacihnāni uta bhogabhūmayaḥ athavā netāro gantṛṇām iti /
tatra mārgalakṣaṇabhūtā arcirādaya iti tāvat prāptam /
tatsvarūpatvāt upadeśasya /
yathā hi loke kaścit grāmaṃ nagaraṃ vā pratiṣṭhāsamānaḥ anuśiṣyate gacchetaḥ tvam amuṃ giriṃ tato nyagrodhaṃ tato nadīṃ tato grāmaṃ tato nagaraṃ vā prāpsyasi iti evam iha api arciṣo aharahna āpūryamāṇapakṣim ityādi āha /
athavā bhogabhūmaya iti prāptam /
tathā hi - 'lokaśabdenāgnyādīnanubadhnāti agnilokamāgacchati' (kauṣī. 1.3) ityādi /
lokaśabdaḥ ca prāṇināṃ bhogāyataneṣu bhāṣyate - 'manuṣyalokaḥ pitṛloko devalokaḥ' (bṛ. 1.5.16) iti ca /
tathā ca brāhmaṇam - 'ahorātreṣu te lokeṣu sajjante' ityādi /
tasmāt na ativāhikā arcirādayaḥ /
acetanatvāt api eteṣām ativāhikatva anupapattiḥ /
cetanā hi loke rājaniyuktāḥ puruṣā durgeṣu mārgeṣu ativāhyān ativāhayanti iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - ātivāhikā eva ete bhavitum arhanti /
kutaḥ - talliṅgāt /
tathā hi 'candramaso vidyutaṃ tatpuruṣo 'mānavaḥ sa etānbrahma gamayati' (chā. 4.15.5) iti siddhat gamayitṛtvaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: Regarding these very [stages] beginning with <s>arcis</s>, a doubt [arises]: Are these landmarks of the route, or realms of enjoyment, or guides (<s>ātivāhikas</s>) for the travelers? The prima facie view is that <s>arcis</s> and the rest are landmarks of the route. Because the instruction has that very nature. For just as in the world, someone setting out for a village or a city is instructed: 'Go — [you will reach] that mountain, then the banyan tree, then the river, then the village or city' — so too here, [the text] says: 'from the flame, the day, the bright fortnight' and so on. Alternatively, the prima facie view is that they are realms of enjoyment. For thus, [the <s>Kauṣītaki</s>] connects fire and the others with the word 'world' (<s>loka</s>): 'He reaches the world of fire' (<s>Kauṣītaki</s> 1.3) and so on. And the word '<s>loka</s>' is used for the dwelling-places of enjoyment of living beings — 'the human world, the world of the fathers, the world of the gods' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.16). And thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [says]: 'They are stuck in the worlds of days and nights' and the like. Therefore, <s>arcis</s> and the others are not guides (<s>ātivāhikas</s>). And because these [stages] are non-conscious, their being guides is not tenable. For in the world, conscious persons appointed by the king convey travelers through difficult routes. Given this prima facie view, we say: These should indeed be guides. Why? Because of the indicatory mark. For thus: 'From the moon to the lightning — a non-human (<s>amānava</s>) person — he leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.5) — [this] shows an established status as guides.

children.text: tat vacanaṃ tat viṣayam eva upakṣīṇam iti cet /
children.translated_text: Objection: That statement is exhausted [in its application] to that [final stage] alone.

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: prāptamānavatva nivṛttiparatvāt viśeṣaṇasya /
children.translated_text: Because the qualifier [<s>amānava</s>] is intended to negate the expectation of humanness.

children.text: yadi arcirādiṣu puruṣā gamayitāraḥ prāptāḥ te ca mānavāḥ tato yuktaṃ tat nivṛttyarthaṃ puruṣaviśeṣaṇam amānava iti // 4 //
children.translated_text: If it were accepted that at the [stages of] <s>arcis</s> and the like, persons are the guides, and they are human — then the qualifying term '<s>amānava</s>' (non-human) would be appropriate for negating [that expectation]. // 4 //

children.text: nanu talliṅgamātram agamakaṃ nyāya abhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Objection: But a mere indicatory mark, without a [supporting] reasoning, is inconclusive.

children.text: na eṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect.

children.text: ubhayavyāmohāt tat siddheḥ | BBs_4,3.5 |
children.translated_text: Because it is established through the perplexity of both [the travelers and the stages]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.5 |

children.text:
ye tāvat arcirādimārgāḥ te dehaviyogāt saṃpiṇḍitakaraṇagrāmā iti asvatantrā arcirādīnām api acetanatvāt asvātantryam iti ataḥ arcirādi abhimāninaḥ cetanā devatāviśeṣā atiyātrāyāṃ niyuktā iti gamyate /
loke api hi matta mūrcchitādayaḥ saṃpiṇḍitakaraṇāḥ paraprayuktavartmāno bhavanti /
children.translated_text: As for the travelers — since at the separation from the body their sense-organs are gathered together — they are not independent. As for <s>arcis</s> and the rest too — being non-conscious — they are not independent. Therefore, it is understood that specific conscious deities who preside over <s>arcis</s> and the rest are appointed as escorts for the journey. For in the world too, intoxicated, unconscious, and similar persons whose sense-organs are gathered together have their course directed by others.

children.text:
anavasthitatvāt api arcirādīnāṃ na mārgalakṣaṇatva upapattiḥ /
na hi rātrau pretasya ahaḥsvarūpa abhisaṃbhava upapadyate /
na ca pratipālanamasti iti uktaṃ purastāt /
dhruvatvāt tu devatā ātmānāṃ na ayaṃ doṣo bhavati /
arcirādi śabdatā ca eṣām arcirādi abhimānāt upapadyate 'arciṣo 'haḥ'(chā. 4.15.5, 5,10.1) ityādinirdeśaḥ tu ativāhikatve api na virudhyate arciṣā hetunā ahaḥ abhisaṃbhavati /
ahnā hetunā āpūryamāṇapakṣam iti /
tathā ca loke prasiddheṣu api ativāhikeṣu evañjātīyaka upadeśo dṛśyate /
gaccha tvam ito balavarmāṇaṃ tato jayasiṃhaṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇaguptam iti /
api ca upakrame 'te 'rcirabhisaṃbhavanti' (bṛ. 6.2.15) iti saṃbandhamātramuktaṃ na saṃbandhaviśeṣaḥ kaścit /
upasaṃhāre tu 'sa etānbrahma gamayati (chā. 4.15.6) iti saṃbandhaviśeṣaḥ ativāhi ativāhakatva lakṣaṇa uktaḥ tena sa eva upakrame api iti nirdhāryate /
saṃpiṇḍitakaraṇatvāt eva ca gantṛṣu na tatra upabhogasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: And precisely because the travelers have their sense-organs gathered together, enjoyment in those [stages] is not possible.

children.text: lokaśabdaḥ tu anupabhuñjāneṣu api gantṛṣu gamayituṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: And the word '<s>loka</s>' (world) can be understood even when the travelers do not enjoy [those realms].

children.text: anyeṣāṃ tat lokavāsināṃ bhogabhūmitvāt /
children.translated_text: Because [those realms] are places of enjoyment for other beings who dwell in those worlds.

children.text: ataḥ agnisvāmikaṃ lokaṃ prāptaḥ agninā ativāhyate vāyusvāmikaṃ prāpto vāyunā iti yojayitavyam // 5 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it should be construed thus: Having reached the world whose lord is <s>Agni</s>, [the soul] is escorted by <s>Agni</s>; having reached the world whose lord is <s>Vāyu</s>, [it is escorted] by <s>Vāyu</s>. // 5 //

Moreover, because <s>arcis</s> and the rest are not fixed [celestial bodies], their being route-landmarks is not tenable. For a person who dies at night cannot actually encounter the daytime form [of the 'day']. And it has been said earlier that there is no waiting. But because the deities who are the selves [presiding over these stages] are permanent, this fault does not apply. And their being designated by the words '<s>arcis</s>' and the like is tenable because of their presiding over <s>arcis</s> and the like. The designation 'From the flame, the day' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.5, 5.10.1) and the like is not contradicted even on the view that they are guides — [meaning:] by means of the flame, one reaches the day; by means of the day, the bright fortnight — and so on. And thus, in the world too, regarding well-known guides, such instruction is seen: 'Go from here to <s>Balavarman</s>, from him to <s>Jayasiṃha</s>, from him to <s>Kṛṣṇagupta</s>.' Moreover, at the beginning, 'They reach the flame' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15) — only a connection [with the flame] is stated, not any specific type of connection. But in the conclusion — 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.6) — a specific connection of the nature of guide-and-guided is stated; and from that, the same [type of connection] is determined for the beginning as well.

children.text:
kathaṃ punaḥ ativāhikatvapakṣe varuṇādiṣu tatsaṃbhavaḥ /
vidyuto hi adhi varuṇādaya upakṣiptā vidyutaḥ tu anantaramā brahmaprāpteḥ amānavasya eva puruṣasya gamayitṛtvaṃ śrutam iti /
ata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: But how is the status of being guides possible in the case of <s>Varuṇa</s> and the others? For <s>Varuṇa</s> and the others were added above lightning; but from lightning onward until reaching <s>Brahman</s>, the guiding role is heard only of the non-human (<s>amānava</s>) person. Therefore, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the reply:

children.text: vaidyutenaiva tatas tacchruteḥ | BBs_4,3.6 |
children.translated_text: By the one born of lightning itself, from that [point onward] — because of the <s>śruti</s> to that effect. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.6 |

children.text: tato vidyut abhisaṃbhavanāt ūrdhvaṃ vidyut anantaravartina eva amānavena puruṣeṇa varuṇalokādiṣu ativāhyamānā brahmalokaṃ gacchanti iti avagantavyam /
children.translated_text: From the encounter with lightning onward, it should be understood that [the souls] are escorted through the worlds of <s>Varuṇa</s> and the rest by the very non-human person who is stationed next to lightning, and [thus] they go to the world of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: 'tānvaidyutātpuruṣo 'mānavaḥ sa etya brahmalokaṃ gamayati' iti tasya eva gamayitṛtvaśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That person born of lightning, the non-human one — he, having reached [them], leads [them] to the world of <s>Brahman</s>' — because the guiding role is heard of him alone.

children.text: varuṇādayaḥ tu tasya eva apratibandhakaraṇena sāhāyya anuṣṭhānena vā kenacit anugrāhakā iti avagantavyam /
children.translated_text: But <s>Varuṇa</s> and the others should be understood as supporters — either by not obstructing him or by rendering some assistance.

children.text: tasmāt sādhu uktam ativāhikā devatātmānaḥ arcirādaya iti // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is well said that <s>arcis</s> and the others, being deities in their essence, are guides (<s>ātivāhikas</s>). // 6 //

children.text: 5 kārya adhikaraṇam / sū. 7-14
children.translated_text: 5. The <s>Kāryādhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the [Lower] Effect-<s>Brahman</s>). <s>Sūtras</s> 7-14.

children.text: kāryaṃ bādarirasya gatyupapatteḥ | BBs_4,3.7 |
children.translated_text: [They are led] to the effect-<s>Brahman</s> — [so holds] <s>Bādari</s>, because of the tenability of a journey to it. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.7 |

children.text:
'sa enānbrahma gamayati (chā. 4.15.5) iti atra vicikitsyate - kiṃ kāryam aparaṃ brahma gamayati āhosvit param eva avikṛtaṃ mukhyaṃ brahma iti /
kutaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
brahmaśabdaprayogāt gatiśruteḥ ca /
tatra kāryameva saguṇam aparaṃ brahma enān gamayati amānavaḥ puruṣa iti bādariḥ ācāryo manyate /
kutaḥ - asya gati upapatteḥ /
asya hi kāryabrahmaṇo gantavyatvam upapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: For to this effect-<s>Brahman</s>, the status of being a destination is tenable.

children.text: asya hi kāryabrahmaṇo gantavyatvam upapadyate pradeśavattvāt /
children.translated_text: For the status of this effect-<s>Brahman</s> as a destination is tenable — because it has a location.

children.text: na tu parasmin brahmaṇi gantṛtvaṃ gantavyatvaṃ gatiḥ vā avakalpate /
children.translated_text: But in the case of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, neither the status of being a traveler, nor the status of being a destination, nor the journey itself is tenable.

children.text: sarvagatatvāt pratyagātmatvāt ca gantṛṇām // 7 //
children.translated_text: Because [the supreme <s>Brahman</s>] is all-pervading and is the inner Self of the travelers. // 7 //

In 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.5), a doubt arises: Does [the guide] lead them to the effect-<s>Brahman</s> — the lower [<s>Brahman</s>] — or to the supreme, unmodified, primary <s>Brahman</s>? Whence the doubt? Because of the use of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' and because of the hearing of a journey. The teacher <s>Bādari</s> holds that the non-human person leads them to the effect-<s>Brahman</s> alone — the lower, qualified (<s>saguṇa</s>) <s>Brahman</s>. Why? Because a journey to it is tenable.

children.text: viśeṣitatvāc ca | BBs_4,3.8 |
children.translated_text: And because [the <s>Brahman</s> described in this context] is specified [with attributes]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.8 |

children.text:
brahmalokāngamayati te teṣu brahmalokeṣu parāḥ parāvato vasanti' (bṛ. 6.2.15) iti ca śrutyantare viśeṣitatvāt kāryabrahmaviṣaya eva gatiḥ iti gamyate /
nahi bahuvacanena viśeṣaṇaṃ parasmin brahmaṇi avakalpate /
kārye tu avasthābheda upapatteḥ saṃbhavati bahuvacanam /
lokaśrutiḥ api vikāragocarāyāma eva saṃniveśaviśiṣṭāyāṃ bhogabhūmāvau āñjasī /
gauṇī tu anyatra 'brahmaiva loka eṣa samrāṭ' ityādiṣu /
adhikaraṇa adhikartavyanirdeśaḥ api parasmin brahmaṇi anāñjasaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: 'He leads them to the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>; they, in those worlds of <s>Brahman</s>, dwell as the highest of the high' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15) — because in another <s>śruti</s>, [<s>Brahman</s>] is qualified by the plural number, it is understood that the journey refers only to the <s>kārya-Brahman</s> (the effected <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>). For the qualification by the plural number is not possible in the case of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. But in the case of the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>], the plural is possible because of the difference of states. The word '<s>loka</s>' (world) too is proper in its primary sense only with reference to an abode of enjoyment (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>) characterized by spatial arrangement, which falls within the domain of modification (<s>vikāra</s>). But it is figurative elsewhere — as in '<s>Brahman</s> alone is this world, O Emperor' and the like. The indication of a place and something to be reached would also be non-literal in the case of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmāt kāryaviṣayameva idaṃ nayanam // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this leading [of the soul] pertains only to the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>]. // 8 //

children.text: nanu kāryaviṣaye api brahmaśabdo na upapadyate samanvaye hi samastasya jagato janmādikāraṇaṃ sthāpitam iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is not appropriate even for the <s>kārya</s>, since in the harmonization [of <s>Vedānta</s> texts], it was established that [<s>Brahman</s> is] the cause of the origination and the like of the entire universe.

children.text: atra ucyate -
children.translated_text: To this we say:

children.text: sāmīpyāt tu tadvyapadeśaḥ | BBs_4,3.9 |
children.translated_text: But because of proximity, [the <s>kārya</s>] is designated by that [name '<s>Brahman</s>']. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.9 |

children.text: tu śabda āśaṅkā vyāvṛttyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for dispelling the apprehension.

children.text: parabrahmasāmīpyāt aparasya brahmaṇaḥ tasmin api brahmaśabdaprayogo na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: Because of the proximity of the lower <s>Brahman</s> to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the use of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' even for it [the lower] is not contradicted.

children.text: param eva hi brahma viśuddha upādhisaṃbandhaṃ kvacit kaiścit vikāradharmaiḥ manomayatvādibhiḥ upāsanāya upadiśyamānam aparam iti sthitiḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: For the established position is: It is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself that, in connection with a pure limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>), is taught in certain places with certain properties of modification — such as being mind-made (<s>manomaya</s>) and the like — for the purpose of meditation, and is [thereby designated as] the lower [<s>Brahman</s>]. // 9 //

children.text:
nanu kāryaprāptau anāvṛttiśravaṇaṃ na ghaṭate /
na hi parasmāt brahmaṇaḥ anyatra kvacit nityatāṃ saṃbhāvayanti /
darśayati ca devayānena pathā prasthitānām anāvṛttim /
'etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavamāvartaṃ nāvartante' (chā. 4.15.6) iti teṣām iha na punarāvṛttiḥ asti 'tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti' (chā. 8.6.6), ka. 6.16) iti cet /
atra brūmaḥ -
children.translated_text: Objection: But the hearing of non-return is not compatible with [a journey to] the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>]. For permanence is not possible anywhere other than the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows non-return for those who have set forth on the <s>devayāna</s> path: 'Those who attain [<s>Brahman</s>] by this path do not return to this cycle of human existence' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.6); and for them there is no return here: 'Going upward by that [path], one attains immortality' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.6, <s>Kaṭha</s> 6.16). To this we say:

children.text: kāryātyaye tadadhyakṣeṇa sahātaḥ param abhidhānāt | BBs_4,3.10 |
children.translated_text: Upon the dissolution of the <s>kārya</s> [world], together with the ruler of that [world], from there [they attain] the Supreme — because of the statement. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.10 |

children.text: kāryabrahmalokapralayapratyupasthāne sati tatra eva utpannasamyagdarśanāḥ santaḥ tat adhyakṣeṇa hiraṇyagarbheṇa sahātaḥ paraṃ pariśuddhaṃ viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ pratipadyanta iti /
children.translated_text: When the dissolution of the world of <s>kārya-Brahman</s> approaches, those who have attained right knowledge there — together with the ruler of that [world], <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — attain from there the Supreme, the perfectly pure, the highest abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kramamuktiḥ anāvṛttyādi śruti abhidhānebhyo abhyupagantavyā /
children.translated_text: Gradual liberation (<s>kramamukti</s>) must be accepted — because of the statements about non-return and the like.

children.text: na hi āñjasa eva gatipūrvikā paraprāptiḥ saṃbhavati iti upapaditam // 10 //
children.translated_text: For it has been shown that a direct attainment of the Supreme preceded by a journey is not possible. // 10 //

children.text: smṛteś ca | BBs_4,3.11 |
children.translated_text: And because of <s>smṛti</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.11 |

children.text: smṛtiḥ api etam artham anujānāti - 'brahmaṇā saha te sarve saṃprāpte pratisaṃcare /
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> too approves this meaning: 'Together with <s>Brahmā</s>, all of them, at the occurrence of the universal dissolution,

children.text: parasyānte kṛtātmānaḥ praviśanti paraṃ padam'iti /
children.translated_text: having perfected themselves, enter the Supreme Abode.'

children.text: tasmāt kāryabrahmaviṣayā gatiḥ śrūyata iti siddhāntaḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is the established conclusion that the <s>gati</s>-<s>śrutis</s> (passages about the journey) pertain to the <s>kārya-Brahman</s>. // 11 //

children.text:
kaṃ puna- pūrvapakṣam āśaṅkya ayaṃ siddhāntaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ 'kāryaṃ bādariḥ' (bra.sū. 4.3.7) ityādina iti /
sa idānīṃ sūtraiḥ eva upadarśyate -
children.translated_text: What, then, is the prima facie view that was apprehended, against which this established conclusion — '<s>Kāryaṃ Bādariḥ</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.3.7) and so on — was established? That is now shown through the <s>sūtras</s> themselves:

children.text: paraṃ jaiminir mukhyatvāt | BBs_4,3.12 |
children.translated_text: [The journey is] to the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] — [this is the view of] <s>Jaimini</s>, because of the primary meaning [of the word '<s>Brahman</s>']. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.12 |

children.text: jaiminiḥ tu ācāryaḥ 'sa enānbrahma gamayati'(chā. 4.15.6) iti atra parameva brahma prāpayati iti manyate /
children.translated_text: But the teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds that in 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.6), it is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself that is attained.

children.text: kutaḥ - mukhyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the primary meaning.

children.text: paraṃ hi brahma brahmaśabdasya mukhyam ālambanaṃ, gauṇam aparaṃ, mukhyagauṇayogaḥ ca mukhye saṃpratyayo bhavati // 12 //
children.translated_text: For the primary referent of the word '<s>Brahman</s>' is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; the lower [<s>Brahman</s>] is its figurative [referent]. And when both primary and figurative meanings are available, the understanding should be in favor of the primary. // 12 //

children.text: darśanāc ca | BBs_4,3.13 |
children.translated_text: And because of the observation [in <s>śruti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.13 |

children.text: 'tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti' (chā. 8.6.6, ka. 6.16) iti ca gatipūrvakam amṛtatvaṃ darśayati /
amṛtatvaṃ ca parasmin brahmaṇi upapadyate na kārye, vināśitvāt kāryasya /
children.translated_text: And immortality is possible [only] in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, not in the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>] — because the <s>kārya</s> is perishable.

children.text: 'atha yatrānyatpaśyati tadalpaṃ tanmartyam' (chā. 7.24.1) iti pravacanāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the teaching: 'But wherever another thing is seen — that is finite, that is mortal' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1).

children.text: paraviṣaya eva ca eṣā gatiḥ kaṭhavallīṣu paṭhyate /
children.translated_text: And this journey is recited in the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s> as pertaining to the Supreme alone.

children.text: na hi tatra vidyāntaraprakramaḥ asti 'anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmāt' (ka. 2.14) iti parasya eva brahmaṇaḥ prakrāntatvāt // 13 //
children.translated_text: For there, there is no context of another <s>vidyā</s> — since the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone has been introduced: 'Other than <s>dharma</s>, other than <s>adharma</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 2.14). // 13 //
And: 'Going upward by that [path], one attains immortality' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.6, <s>Kaṭha</s> 6.16) — [this] shows the attainment of immortality preceded by a journey.

children.text: na ca kārye pratipattyabhisaṃdhiḥ | BBs_4,3.14 |
children.translated_text: And the resolve of attainment is not directed toward the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4.3.14 |

children.text:
api ca 'prajāpateḥ sabhāṃ veśma prapadye' (chā. 8.14.1) iti na ayaṃ kāryaviṣayaḥ pratipatti abhisaṃdhiḥ 'nāmarūpayornirvahitā te yadantarā tadbrahma' (chā. 8.14.1) iti kāryavilakṣaṇasya parasya eva brahmaṇaḥ prakṛtatvāt /
'yaśo 'haṃ bhavāmi brāhmaṇānām' (chā. 8.14.1) iti ca sarvātmatvena upakramaṇāt /
'na tasya pratimā asti, yasya nāmamahadyaśaḥ' (śvetā. 4.19) iti ca parasya eva brahmaṇo yaśonāmatva prasiddheḥ /
'sā ceyaṃ veśmapratipattirgatipūrvikā hārdavidyāyāmuditā tadaparājitā pūrbrahmaṇaḥ prabhuvimitaṃ hiraṇmayam' (chā. 8.5.3) iti atra /
paderapi ca gatyarthatvāt mārga apekṣā avasīyate /
tasmāt parabrahmaviṣayā gatiśrutaya iti pakṣāntaram /
tau etau dvau pakṣau ācāryeṇa sūtritau gati upapattyādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'I enter the hall and abode of <s>Prajāpati</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1) — this resolve of attainment does not pertain to the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>]; because the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone — distinct from the <s>kārya</s> — is the subject under discussion: 'The differentiator of name and form — that which is between them is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1). And because of the introduction with universal selfhood: 'I become the glory of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1). And because the word 'glory' (<s>yaśas</s>) is well-known as a name of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone: 'He has no image; His name is Great Glory' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 4.19). And this attainment of the abode, preceded by a journey, has been stated in the <s>Hārdavidyā</s>: 'That [city of <s>Brahman</s>] called <s>Aparājitā</s> [the unconquered], an abode measured by the Lord of <s>Brahman</s>, golden' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.5.3). And because even the word '<s>pada</s>' (step, abode) has the meaning of going, the expectation of a path is established. Therefore, the <s>gati</s>-<s>śrutis</s> pertain to the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — this is the alternative view. These two views have been formulated by the teacher in <s>sūtras</s> — one with grounds such as the tenability of the journey and the like,

children.text:
eko mukhyatvādibhiḥ aparaḥ /
tatra gati upapattyādayaḥ prabhavanti mukhyatvādīna ābhāsayituṃ na tu mukhyatvādayo gati upapattyādīn ityādya eva siddhānto vyākhyāto dvitīyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ /
na hi asati api saṃbhave mukhyasya eva arthasya grahaṇam iti kaścit ājñāpayitā vidyate /
paravidyāprakaraṇe api ca tat stutyarthaṃ vidyāntara āśrayagati anukīrtanam upapadyate 'viṣvaṅṅanyā utkramaṇe bhavanti' (chā. 8.6.6) itivat /
'prajāpateḥ sabhāṃ veśma prapadye' (chā. 8.14.1) iti tu pūrvavākyavicchedena kārye api pratipatti abhisaṃdhiḥ na virudhyate /
saguṇe api ca brahmaṇi sarvātmatva saṃkīrtanaṃ sarvakarmā sarvakāma ityādivat avakalpate /
tasmāt aparaviṣayā eva gatiśrutayaḥ /
kecit punaḥ pūrvāṇi pūrvapakṣasūtrāṇi bhavanti uttarāṇi siddhāntasūtrāṇi iti etāṃ vyavasthānam anurudhyamānāḥ paraviṣayā eva gatiśrutīḥ pratiṣṭhāpayanti tat anupapannaṃ gantavyatva anupapatteḥ brahmaṇaḥ /
yat sarvagataṃ sarvāntaraṃ sarvātmakaṃ ca paraṃ brahma 'ākāśavatsarvagataśca nityaḥ' 'yatsākṣādaparokṣādbrahma' (bṛ. 3.4.1) 'ya ātmā sarvāntaraḥ' (bṛ. 3.4.1) 'ātmaivedaṃ sarvam' (chā. 7.25.2) 'brahmaivedaṃ viśvamidaṃ variṣṭham' (mu. 2.2.11) ityādi śrutinirdhārita viśeṣaṃ tasya gantavyatā na kadācit api upapadyate /
na hi gatameva gamyate /
anyo hi anyat gacchati iti prasiddhaṃ loke /
children.translated_text: the other with grounds such as the primary meaning and the like. Of these, the grounds such as the tenability of the journey and the like have the power to show the grounds such as the primary meaning and the like to be merely apparent — but the grounds such as the primary meaning and the like do not have [the power to refute] the grounds such as the tenability of the journey and the like. Therefore, the first [view] alone has been explained as the established conclusion, and the second as the prima facie view. For there is no authority whatsoever that dictates that the primary meaning alone must be grasped even when there is no possibility [of it being correct]. And even in the context of the supreme <s>vidyā</s>, the mention of a journey associated with another <s>vidyā</s> for the purpose of praising [the supreme <s>vidyā</s>] is possible — just as [it is possible] in 'Some [<s>prāṇas</s>] go in all directions at the time of departure' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.6). And 'I enter the hall and abode of <s>Prajāpati</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.14.1) — by separating [this] from the preceding sentence, the resolve of attainment can pertain to the <s>kārya</s> [<s>Brahman</s>] without contradiction. And even in the case of <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) <s>Brahman</s>, the mention of universal selfhood is possible — as in 'He who is all-acting, all-desiring' and the like. Therefore, the <s>gati</s>-<s>śrutis</s> pertain to the lower [<s>Brahman</s>] alone. Some, however, conforming to the arrangement that the earlier [<s>sūtras</s>] are the prima facie view and the later ones the established conclusion, establish that the <s>gati</s>-<s>śrutis</s> pertain to the Supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] alone — that is untenable, because the character of being a destination is not possible for <s>Brahman</s>. For the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — which is all-pervading, interior to all, the Self of all — whose specific character has been determined by <s>śrutis</s> such as 'Pervading all like space, eternal' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s>), 'That <s>Brahman</s> which is directly perceived and not indirectly known' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1), 'The Self that is interior to all' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.4.1), 'All this is this Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2), 'This <s>Brahman</s> indeed is this entire universe, the greatest' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.11) — the character of being a destination is never possible for It. For what has already been reached is not [something to be] reached [again]. For it is well known in the world that one thing goes to another.

children.text:
nanu loke gatasya api gantavyatā deśāntaraviśiṣṭā dṛṣṭā /
yathā pṛthivīstha eva pṛthivīṃ deśāntaradvāreṇa gacchati iti /
tathā ananyatve api sarvaśakti upetatvāt kathañcit gantavyatā syāt iti /
children.translated_text: Objection: But even in the world, the character of being a destination is observed for what has already been reached — when qualified by a different location. Just as one who is already on the earth goes to [another part of] the earth by way of a different region. Similarly, even though [the Self] is non-different [from <s>Brahman</s>], because [<s>Brahman</s>] is endowed with all powers, the character of being a destination might somehow apply.

children.text:
na /
pratiṣiddhasarvaviśeṣatvāt brahmaṇaḥ /
'niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntaṃ niravadyaṃ nirañjanam'(śvetā. 6.19) 'asthūlamanaṇvahrasvamadīrgham'(bṛ. 3.8.8) 'sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ'(mu. 2.1.2) 'sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma'(bṛ. 4.4.25) 'sa eṣa neti netyātmā'(bṛ. 3.9.23) ityādi śruti smṛti nyāyebhyo na deśakālādi viśeṣayogaḥ paramātmani kalpayituṃ śakyate /
yena bhūpradeśa vayovasthā nyāyena asya gantavyatā syāt /
bhūvayasoḥ tu pradeśa avasthādi viśeṣayogāt upapadyate deśa kāla viśiṣṭā gantavyatā /
jagat utpatti sthiti pralayahetutva śruteḥ anekaśaktitvaṃ brahmaṇa iti cet /
children.translated_text: No. Because all specific attributes have been negated of <s>Brahman</s>. 'Without parts, without action, tranquil, faultless, untainted' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.19); 'Neither gross, nor minute, neither short, nor long' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.8.8); 'Both without and within, unborn' (<s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.1.2); 'This great unborn Self is ageless, undying, immortal, fearless — <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.25); 'This Self is [described as] "not this, not this"' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 3.9.23) — from such <s>śrutis</s>, <s>smṛtis</s>, and reasoning, no specific qualification of place, time, and the like can be attributed to the Supreme Self by which, through the principle of [different] regions of earth or stages of age, the character of being a destination might apply. For earth and age, having specific qualifications of region, stage, and the like, can have the character of a destination qualified by place and time. If [one objects]: Because of the <s>śruti</s> that [<s>Brahman</s>] is the cause of the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe, <s>Brahman</s> has many powers [and therefore could be a destination] —

children.text:
na /
viśeṣanirākaraṇaśrutīnām ananyārthatvāt /
children.translated_text: No. Because the <s>śrutis</s> that negate specific attributes have no other purpose [and must be taken at face value].

children.text: utpattyādiśrutīnām api samānam ananyārthatvam iti cet /
children.translated_text: Objection: But the <s>śrutis</s> about origination and the like equally have no other purpose.

children.text:
na /
tāsām ekatvapratipādanaparatvāt /
mṛdādi dṛṣṭāntaiḥ hi sato brahmaṇa ekasya satyatvaṃ vikārasya ca āvṛtatvaṃ pratipādayat śāstraṃ na utpattyādiparaṃ bhavitum arhati /
kasmāt punaḥ utpattyādi śrutīnāṃ viśeṣatvaṃ na punaḥ itara śeṣatvam itarāsām iti /
children.translated_text: No. Because those [origination-<s>śrutis</s>] are intended for the purpose of teaching oneness. For scripture, teaching through illustrations of clay and the like the reality of the one existing <s>Brahman</s> and the falsity of modification, cannot be primarily about origination and the like. But why then is the specificity [of the negation-<s>śrutis</s>] not reversed — why are not the origination-<s>śrutis</s> taken as primary and the negation-<s>śrutis</s> made subordinate to them?

children.text:
ucyate - viśeṣanirākaraṇaśrutīnāṃ nirākāṅkṣārthatvāt /
na hi ātmana ekatva nityatva śuddhatvādi avagatau satyāṃ bhūyaḥ kācit ākāṅkṣā upajāyate puruṣārthasamāptibuddhi upapatteḥ /
'tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śoka ekatvamanupaśyataḥ' (īśā. 7) 'abhayaṃ vai janaka prāpto 'si' (bṛ. 4.2.4) 'vidvānna bibheti kutaścana /
etaṃ ha vāva na tapati kimahaṃ sādhu nākaravaṃ kimahaṃ pāpamakaravam' (taitti. 2.9.1) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
tathā eva ca viduṣāṃ tuṣṭi anubhavādi darśanāt /
vikāra anṛta abhisaṃdhi apavādāt ca 'mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati' iti /
ato na viśeṣanirākaraṇa śrutīnām anyaśeṣatvam avagantuṃ śakyate /
na evam utpattyādi śrutīnāṃ nirākāṅkṣārtha pratipādanasāmarthyam asti /
pratyakṣaṃ tu tāsām anyārthatvaṃ samanugamyate /
tathā hi 'tatraitacchruṅgamutpatitaṃ somya vijānīhi nedamamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati' (chā. 6.8.3) iti upanyasya udarke sata eva ekasya jagat mūlasya vijñeyatvaṃ darśayati /
'yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante /
yena jātāni jīvanti yatprayantyabhisaṃviśanti /
tadvijijñāsasva /
tadbrahmeti' (tai. 3.1.1) iti ca /
evam utpattyādiśrutīnām aikātmya avagamaparatvāt na anekaśaktiyogo brahmaṇaḥ /
ataḥ ca gantavyatva anupapattiḥ /
'na tasya prāṇā utkramanti brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti ca parasmin brahmaṇi gatiṃ nivārayati /
tat vyākhyātaṃ 'spaṣṭo hyekeṣām' (bra. sū. 4.2.13) ityatra /
gatikalpanāyāṃ ca gantā jīvo gantavyasya brahmaṇaḥ avayavo vikāro vā tataḥ syāt /
atyanta tādātmye gamana anupapatteḥ /
yadi evaṃ tataḥ kiṃ syāt /
ucyate /
yadi ekadeśaḥ tena ekadeśino nityaprāptatvāt na punaḥ brahmagamanam upapadyate /
ekadeśitva kalpanā ca brahmaṇi anupapannā niravayavatva prasiddheḥ /
vikārapakṣe api etat atulyaṃ vikāreṇa api vikāriṇo nityaprāptatvāt /
na hi ghaṭo mṛdātmatāṃ parityajya avatiṣṭhate parityāge vā abhāvaprāpteḥ /
vikāra avayavapakṣayoḥ ca tadvataḥ sthiratvāt brahmaṇaḥ saṃsāragamanam api anavakḷptam /
atha anya eva jīvo brahmaṇaḥ /
saḥ aṇuḥ vyāpī madyama parimāṇo vā bhavitum arhati /
vyāpitve gamana anupapattiḥ /
madhyama parimāṇatve ca anityatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
aṇutve kṛtsnaśarīravedanā anupapattiḥ /
pratiṣiddhe ca aṇutva madhyama parimāṇatve vistareṇa purastāt /
parasmāt ca anyatve jīvasya 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) ityādi śāstra bādha prasaṅgaḥ /
vikāra avayavapakṣayoḥ api samānaḥ ayaṃ doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text:
It is said: Because the <s>śruti</s> passages that negate specific attributes convey a meaning that is complete in itself.
For when the oneness, eternality, purity, and the like of the Self are known, no further expectation whatsoever arises — because the understanding that the human purpose is accomplished is well-founded.
[This is known] from <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'Where then is delusion, where is sorrow, for one who sees oneness?' (<s>Īśā Upaniṣad</s> 7); 'You have attained fearlessness, O <s>Janaka</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.2.4); 'The wise one does not fear from anywhere; this indeed does not torment him — "Why did I not do good? Why did I do evil?"' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.9.1).
And likewise, because the contentment, experience, and the like of knowers are observed.
And because of the denial of modification, unreality, and false intention: 'He who sees diversity here, as it were, goes from death to death' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.19).
Therefore, it is not possible to understand the <s>śruti</s> passages that negate specific attributes as being subsidiary to something else.
But the <s>śruti</s> passages about origination and the like do not have the capacity to convey a meaning complete in itself.
Rather, their serving another purpose is directly ascertained.
For thus, having introduced [the topic] with 'This sprout has shot up from it, O dear one — know that it would not be without a root' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.3), [the <s>śruti</s>] shows in the sequel that <s>Sat</s> (Being) alone — the one root of the universe — is to be known.
And: 'From which indeed these beings are born; by which, once born, they live; into which, departing, they enter — seek to know That; That is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 3.1.1).
Thus, since the <s>śruti</s> passages about origination and the like are aimed at the realization of the oneness of the Self, <s>Brahman</s> does not possess multiple powers.
And from this, the impossibility of being a destination [to which one can travel].
And [the <s>śruti</s>] 'His <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart; being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges into <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6) negates a journey to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
That has been explained under 'For some [<s>prāṇas</s> do not depart] — this is clear' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.2.13).
And if a journey were imagined, the traveler — the <s>jīva</s> — would have to be either a part or a modification of <s>Brahman</s>, the destination —
because a journey is impossible in the case of absolute identity.
If so, then what [would follow]?
It is said:
If [the <s>jīva</s>] is a part, then — since a part eternally abides in the whole — a further journey to <s>Brahman</s> is not tenable.
Moreover, the supposition of parts in <s>Brahman</s> is untenable — because it is well-known to be without parts.
Even on the modification view, this [objection] applies equally — because a modification too eternally abides in the thing modified.
For a pot does not abandon its clay-nature and stand on its own — and if it did abandon it, non-existence would result.
And on the views that [the <s>jīva</s>] is a modification or a part, since the possessor of these [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>] is stable, it remains unexplained how <s>Brahman</s> could enter <s>saṃsāra</s>.
But if the <s>jīva</s> is altogether different from <s>Brahman</s> —
then it must be either atomic, all-pervading, or of medium size.
If all-pervading, a journey is impossible.
If of medium size, impermanence would follow.
If atomic, the experience of sensation throughout the entire body would be impossible.
And the atomic and medium-size [views] have been refuted in detail earlier.
Moreover, if the <s>jīva</s> is different from the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>], there would be the problem of contradicting scripture such as 'You are That' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7) and the like.
On the modification and part views too, this same fault applies.

children.text: vikāra avayavayoḥ tadvatoḥ ananyatvāt adoṣa iti cet /
children.translated_text: Objection: Because a modification or a part is non-different from its possessor, there is no fault.

children.text:
na /
mukhya ekatva anupapatteḥ /
sarveṣu eteṣu pakṣeṣu anirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ /
saṃsāri ātmatva anivṛtteḥ /
nivṛttau vā svarūpanāśaprasaṅgaḥ /
brahmātmatva anabhyupagamāt ca /
yat tu kaiścit jalpyate nityāni naimittikāni karmāṇi anuṣṭhīyante pratyavāya anutpattaye kāmyāni pratiṣiddhāni ca parihriyante svarganarakān avāptaye sāṃpratadeha upabhogyāni ca karmāṇi upabhogena eva kṣapyanta ityato vartamānadehapātāt ūrdhvaṃ dehāntara pratisaṃdhāna kāraṇa abhāvāt svarūpa avasthānalakṣaṇaṃ kaivalyaṃ vinā api brahmātmataya evaṃvṛttasya setsyati iti /
tat asat /
pramāṇa abhāvāt /
na hi etat śāstreṇa kenacit pratipāditaṃ mokṣārthi itthaṃ samācaret iti /
svamanīṣayā tu etat tarkitaṃ yasmāt karmanimittaḥ saṃsāraḥ tasmāt nimitta abhāvāt na bhaviṣyati iti /
na ca etat tarkayitum api śakyate nimitta abhāvasya durjñānatvāt /
bahūni hi karmāṇi jātyantarasaṃcitāni iṣṭa aniṣṭavipākāni ekaikasya jantoḥ saṃbhāvyante /
teṣāṃ viruddha phalānāṃ yugapat upabhoga asaṃbhavāt kānicit labdha avasarāṇi idaṃ janma nirmimate kānicit tu deśakālanimittapratīkṣāṇi asata iti ataḥ teṣām avaśiṣṭānāṃ sāṃpratena upabhogena kṣapaṇāsaṃbhavāt na yathāvarṇitacaritasya api vartamānadehapāte dehāntaranimitta abhāvaḥ śakyate niścetum /
karmaśeṣasadbāvasiddhaḥ ca 'tadya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇāstataḥ śeṣeṇa' ityādi śruti smṛtibhyaḥ /
syāt etat /
nitya naimittikāni teṣāṃ kṣepakāṇi bhaviṣyanti iti /
tat na /
virodha abhāvāt /
sati hi virodhe kṣepyakṣepakabhāvo bhavati /
na ca janmāntara saṃcitānāṃ sukṛtānāṃ nitya naimittikaiḥ asti virodhaḥ /
śuddharūpatva aviśeṣāt /
duritānāṃ tu aśuddhirūpatvāt sati virodhe bhavatu kṣapaṇaṃ na tu tāvatā dehāntara nimitta abhāvasiddhiḥ /
sukṛtanimittatva upapatteḥ /
duścaritasya api aśeṣakṣapaṇa anavagamāt /
na ca nitya naimittikānuṣṭhānāt pratyavāya anutpattimātraṃ na punaḥ phalāntara utpattiḥ iti pramāṇam asti phalāntarasya api anuniṣpādinaḥ saṃbhavāt /
smarati hi āpastambaḥ - 'tadyathāmre phalārte nimitte chāyāgandhāvanūtpadyete evaṃ dharmaṃ caryamāṇārthā anūtpadyante' iti /
na ca asati samyak darśane sarvātmanā kāmyapratiṣiddhavarjanaṃ janmaprāyaṇāntarālaṃ kenacit pratijñātuṃ śakyam /
sunipuṇānam api sūkṣma aparādhadarśanāt /
saṃśayitavyaṃ tu bhavati tathā api nimitta abhāvasya durjñānatvameva /
na ca anabhyupagamyamāne jñānagamye brahmātmatve kartṛtva bhoktṛtva svabhāvasya ātmanaḥ kaivalyam ākāṅkṣituṃ śakyam /
agni auṣṇyavat svabhāvasya aparihāryatvāt /
children.translated_text:
No.
Because primary oneness is impossible [on those views].
In all these positions, the problem of the impossibility of liberation [arises] —
because the nature of being a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigratory being) would not be removed.
Or, if it were removed, the destruction of one's own essential nature would follow —
because the Self's identity with <s>Brahman</s> is not accepted [on these views].
As for what some assert — that by performing obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) <s>karmas</s> to prevent adversity (<s>pratyavāya</s>), by abstaining from desire-prompted (<s>kāmya</s>) and prohibited (<s>pratiṣiddha</s>) <s>karmas</s> to avoid heaven and hell, and by exhausting through experience the <s>karmas</s> to be experienced in the present body — after the fall of the present body, since there would be no cause for the connection with another body, <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), characterized by abiding in one's own essential nature, will be accomplished even without [accepting] identity with <s>Brahman</s> for one who conducts himself thus —
that is incorrect.
Because of the absence of a valid means of knowledge [for such a view].
For no scripture whatsoever teaches that 'one who seeks liberation should conduct oneself in this manner.'
This is merely conjectured by one's own intellect — that since <s>saṃsāra</s> is caused by <s>karma</s>, in the absence of the cause, it will not occur.
But this cannot even be conjectured — because of the difficulty of knowing the absence of the cause.
For many <s>karmas</s> accumulated in other births — having both desirable and undesirable fruits — are conceivable for each being.
Since those [<s>karmas</s>] with mutually opposed fruits cannot be experienced simultaneously, some that have found their occasion produce this birth, while others await [favorable] place, time, and occasion.
Therefore, since the exhaustion of those remaining [<s>karmas</s>] through present experience is impossible, even for one who conducts himself as described, it is not possible to ascertain the absence of a cause for [connection with] another body at the fall of the present body.
And the existence of a residue of <s>karma</s> is established from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> passages such as 'Those who have performed praiseworthy conduct here — by that remainder' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 5.10.7) and the like.
One might say: The obligatory and occasional [<s>karmas</s>] will be the destroyers of those [residual <s>karmas</s>].
That is not so.
Because there is no conflict [between them].
For the relation of destroyer and destroyed exists [only] when there is conflict.
And there is no conflict between the merits accumulated in other births and the obligatory and occasional [<s>karmas</s>] —
because of the non-difference in their pure nature.
As for demerits — because they are of an impure nature, let there be destruction when there is conflict; but that alone does not establish the absence of a cause for another body —
because it is tenable that merit too can be the cause [of rebirth].
And because the complete exhaustion of demerit too is not ascertained.
Moreover, there is no valid means of knowledge for [the claim] that from the performance of obligatory and occasional [<s>karmas</s>] there is only the non-arising of adversity and no production of another fruit — because another fruit too may well result.
For <s>Āpastamba</s> records: 'Just as when a mango tree is cultivated for the sake of fruit, shade and fragrance too arise, so when <s>dharma</s> is practiced for a [specific] purpose, [other results] too arise.'
And without right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), no one can guarantee the complete abstention from desire-prompted and prohibited [<s>karmas</s>] throughout the interval between birth and death —
because even the most scrupulous are seen to commit subtle transgressions.
Even so, there remains a doubt — because of the very difficulty of knowing the absence of a cause.
And without accepting the Self's identity with <s>Brahman</s>, which is attained through knowledge, the <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) of the Self — whose nature is agency and experiencership — cannot be desired —
because what is inherent in one's nature cannot be avoided, like the heat of fire.

children.text:
syāt etat /
kartṛtva bhoktṛtva kāryam anartho na tat śaktiḥ tena śakti avasthāne 'pi kāryaparihārat upapanno mokṣa iti /
tatca na /
śaktisadbhāve kāryaprasavasya durnivāratvāt /
atha api syāt na kevalā śaktiḥ kāryam ārabhate anapekṣya anyāni nimittāni /
ata ekākinī sā sthitāpi na aparādhyati iti /
tat ca na /
nimittānām api śaktilakṣaṇena saṃbandhena nityasaṃbaddhatvāt /
tasmāt kartṛtva bhoktṛtva svabhāve satyām anyasatyāṃ vidyāgamyāyāṃ brahmātmatāyāṃ na kathañcana mokṣaṃ pratyāśā asti /
śrutiḥ ca - 'nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya' (śvetā. 3.8) iti jñānāt anyaṃ mokṣamārgaṃ vārayati /
parasmāt ananyatve api jīvasya sarvavyavahāra lopaprasaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text:
One might say: Agency and experiencership are effects (<s>kārya</s>), not [the Self's essential] power (<s>śakti</s>); and therefore, even when the power remains, liberation is tenable because the effect is averted.
But this too is not so.
Because when the power exists, the arising of the effect is irresistible.
Even if one were to say that the power alone does not produce the effect without depending on other contributing causes, and therefore, standing alone, it does no harm —
that too is not so.
Because the contributing causes too are eternally connected [with the power] through the connection characterized by power.
Therefore, if the nature of agency and experiencership is real, and if the Self's identity with <s>Brahman</s> — attainable through knowledge — is not [accepted], then there is no hope of liberation in any way whatsoever.
And the <s>śruti</s>: 'There is no other path known for going [to liberation]' (<s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 3.8) — bars any path to liberation other than knowledge.
Even if the <s>jīva</s> is non-different from the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>], there would be the problem of the cessation of all empirical activity.

children.text: pratyakṣādi pramāṇa apravṛtteḥ iti cet /
children.translated_text: Objection: Because perception and the other means of valid knowledge would cease to operate.

children.text:
na /
prāk prabodhāt svapnavyavahāravat tat upapatteḥ /
śāstraṃ ca 'yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati taditara itaraṃ paśyati (bṛ. 2.4.14, 4.5.15) ityādinā aprabuddhaviṣaye pratyakṣādi vyavahāram uktvā punaḥ prabuddhaviṣaye 'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet' (bṛ. 2.4.14, 4.5.15) ityādinā tat abhāvaṃ darśayati /
tat evaṃ parabrahmavido gantavyādi vijñānasya bādhitatvāt na kathañcana gatiḥ upapādayituṃ śakyā /
kiṃviṣayāḥ punaḥ gatiśrutaya iti /
ucyate - saguṇavidyāviṣayā bhaviṣyanti /
tathā hi kvacit pañcāgnividyāṃ prakṛtya gatiḥ ucyate yathā 'prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma' (chā. 4.10.5) iti 'atha yadidamasminbrahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma' (chā. 8.1.1) iti ca tatra api vāmanītvādibhiḥ satyakāmādibhiḥ ca guṇaiḥ saguṇasya eva upāsyatvāt saṃbhavati gatiḥ /
na kvacit parabrahmaviṣayā gatiḥ śrāvyate yathā gatipratiṣedhaḥ śrāvitaḥ 'na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti /
'brahmavidāpnoti param'(tai. 2.1.1) ityādiṣu tu satyapi āpnoteḥ gatyarthatve varṇitena nyāyena deśāntaraprāpti asaṃbhavāt svarūpapratipattiḥ eva iyam avidyā adhyāropita nāma rūpa pravilaya apekṣayā abhidhīyate 'brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti' (bṛ. 4.4.7) ityādivat iti draṣṭavyam /
api ca paraviṣayā gatiḥ vyākhyāyamānā prarocanāya vā syāt anucintanāya vā /
tatra prarocanaṃ tāvat
children.translated_text:
No.
Because before awakening [to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>], that [empirical activity] is tenable — like the activity in a dream.
And scripture, having stated the operation of perception and the like in the domain of the unawakened — 'Where there is, as it were, duality, there one sees the other' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14, 4.5.15) — then shows its absence in the domain of the awakened: 'But where for him everything has become the Self alone, then by what and whom would he see?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14, 4.5.15).
Thus, since the cognition of a destination and the like is sublated for the knower of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, a journey cannot be established in any way.
What then are the <s>śruti</s> passages about the journey about?
It is said: They will pertain to the meditations on the qualified [<s>Brahman</s>] (<s>saguṇa vidyā</s>).
For thus, in some [passages], the journey is stated with reference to the five-fire meditation (<s>pañcāgnividyā</s>); as in '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Ka</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kha</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.10.5), and 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s>, there is a small lotus — a dwelling' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.1) — there too, since the object of meditation is the qualified [<s>Brahman</s>] with attributes such as smallness (<s>vāmanītva</s>) and true desires (<s>satyakāma</s>), a journey is possible.
But nowhere is a journey taught with respect to the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — just as the negation of a journey has been heard: 'His <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6).
In passages such as 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 2.1.1) — even though the word '<s>āpnoti</s>' (attains) may have the sense of reaching a destination — because, by the reasoning already explained, reaching a different place is impossible, this [attainment] is simply the realization of one's own true nature, expressed with reference to the dissolution of the name and form superimposed by <s>avidyā</s> — just as [in the statement] 'Being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges into <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.7). This is how it should be understood.
Moreover, even if a journey to the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] were explained, it would be either for the purpose of inducing interest (<s>prarocanā</s>) or for the purpose of repeated contemplation (<s>anucintana</s>).
Of these, as for inducing interest —

children.text:
brahmavido na gati uktyā kriyate /
svasaṃvedyena eva avyavahitena vidyāsamarpitena svāsthyena tat siddheḥ /
na ca nityasiddhaniḥśreyasanivedanasya asādhyaphalasya vijñānasya gati anucintane kācit apekṣā upapadyate /
tasmāt aparabrahmaṇi vartamānā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text:
the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is not induced by a statement of a journey.
Because that [inducement] is accomplished by the well-being bestowed by knowledge itself, which is immediate and direct.
And no dependence on the repeated contemplation of a journey is tenable for a cognition whose fruit — the eternally established highest good — is not something to be accomplished.
Therefore, the journey pertains to the lower <s>Brahman</s>, not to the supreme.

children.text:
tatra para aparabrahmaviveka anavadhāraṇena aparasmin brahmaṇi vartamānā gatiśrutayaḥ parasmin adhyāropyante /
kiṃ dve brahmaṇī param aparaṃ ca iti /
bāḍhaṃ dve 'etadvai satyakāma paraṃ cāparaṃ brahmayadoṅkāraḥ' (pra. 5.2) ityādi darśanāt /
kiṃ punaḥ paraṃ brahma kim aparam iti /
children.translated_text:
In that connection, because of the failure to discriminate between the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>śruti</s> passages about a journey — which pertain to the lower <s>Brahman</s> — are superimposed on the supreme.
Are there then two <s>Brahmans</s> — a higher and a lower?
Certainly, there are two — as seen from [the <s>śruti</s>]: 'This indeed, O <s>Satyakāma</s>, is both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s> — namely, <s>Oṃkāra</s>' (<s>Praśna</s> 5.2) and the like.
But what is the higher <s>Brahman</s>, and what is the lower?

children.text:
ucyate /
yatra avidyākṛta nāma rūpādi viśeṣapratiṣedhāt asthūlādiśabdaiḥ brahma upadiśyate tat param /
tat eva yatra nāmarūpādiviśeṣeṇa kenacit viśiṣṭam upāsanāya upadiśyate 'manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ' (chā. 3.14.2) ityādiśabdaistadaparam /
children.translated_text:
It is said:
Where <s>Brahman</s> is taught by words such as 'not gross' (<s>asthūla</s>) and the like — through the negation of specific attributes created by <s>avidyā</s>, such as name and form — that is the higher [<s>Brahman</s>].
That very same [<s>Brahman</s>], where it is taught as qualified by some specific attribute of name, form, and the like for the purpose of meditation — as in '<s>manomaya</s> (made of mind), having <s>prāṇa</s> as body, having the form of light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.14.2) and similar words — that is the lower [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: nanu evam advitīyaśrutiḥ uparudhyeta /
children.translated_text: Objection: But in that case, the <s>śruti</s> declaring non-duality would be compromised.

children.text:
na /
avidyākṛta nāma rūpa upādhikatayā parihṛtatvāt /
tasya ca aparabrahma upāsanasya tat saṃnidhau śrūyamāṇam 'sa yadi pitṛlokakāmo bhavati' (chā. 8.2.1) ityādi jagat aiśvaryalakṣaṇaṃ saṃsāragocaram eva phalaṃ bhavati /
anivartitatvāt avidyāyāḥ /
tasya ca deśaviśeṣa avabaddhatvāt tatprāptyarthaṃ gamanam aviruddham /
children.translated_text: And because that [lower <s>Brahman</s>] is confined to a specific place, a journey for the purpose of reaching it is not contradictory.

children.text: sarvagatatve api ca ātmana ākāśasya iva ghaṭādigamane budhyādi upādhigamane gamanaprasiddhiḥ iti avādiṣma 'tadguṇasāratvāt' (bra.sū. 2.3.29) ityatra /
children.translated_text: And even though the Self is all-pervading, a journey is well-known in terms of the movement of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) such as the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — just as movement is attributed to space (<s>ākāśa</s>) through the movement of a pot and the like — as we stated under 'Because of the predominance of that quality' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 2.3.29).

children.text: tasmāt 'kāryaṃ bādariḥ (bra. sū. 4.3.7) ityeṣa eva sthitaḥ pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the very position established is: '<s>Bādari</s> [holds that] it is the effected [<s>Brahman</s>]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.3.7).

children.text: 'paraṃ jaiminiḥ' (bra.sū. 4.3.12) iti tu pakṣāntarapratibhānamātrapradarśanaṃ prajñāvikāsanāya iti draṣṭavyam // 14 //
children.translated_text: But the [statement of the] alternative view — 'The supreme [<s>Brahman</s> is the destination], according to <s>Jaimini</s>' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.3.12) — should be seen as merely displaying an alternative position for the purpose of expanding wisdom. // 14 //

No.
Because [the lower <s>Brahman</s>] is accounted for as being [merely] an <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct) created by <s>avidyā</s> in the form of name and form.
And the fruit of the meditation on the lower <s>Brahman</s> — heard in proximity to it — such as 'If he desires the world of the ancestors' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.2.1) and the like — is characterized by lordship over the world, and belongs to the sphere of <s>saṃsāra</s> alone.
Because <s>avidyā</s> has not been removed.

children.text: 6 apratīka ālambana adhikaraṇam / sū. 15-16
children.translated_text: 6 The <s>Apratīkālambana</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 15-16.

children.text: apratīkālambanān nayatīti bādarāyaṇa ubhayathā ca doṣāt tatkratuś ca | BBs_4,3.15 |
children.translated_text: The non-human [<s>Puruṣa</s>] leads [to <s>Brahmaloka</s>] those who do not meditate on symbols (<s>pratīkas</s>) — thus [holds] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>; and because there would be a defect in both ways [otherwise]; and because of the <s>tatkratu</s> principle. | <s>BBs</s> 4,3.15 |

children.text:
sthitam etat kāryaviṣayā gatiḥ na paraviṣayā iti /
idam idānīṃ saṃdihyate kiṃ sarvān vikāra ālambanān aviśeṣeṇa eva amānavaḥ puruṣaḥ prāpayati brahmalokam uta kāṃścit eva iti /
kiṃ tāvat prāptaṃ sarveṣām eva eṣāṃ viduṣām anyatra parasmāt brahṇaṇo gatiḥ syāt /
tathā hi - 'aniyamaḥ sarvāsām' - (bra. sū. 3.3.31) iti atrāviśeṣeṇa eva eṣāṃ vidyāntareṣu avatārita iti /
evaṃ prāpte pratyāha - apratīka ālambanān iti /
pratīka ālambanān varjayitvā sarvān anyān vikāra ālambanān nayati brahmalokam iti bādarāyaṇa ācāryo manyate /
na hi evam ubhayathā
children.translated_text:
It is established that the journey pertains to <s>kārya-Brahman</s> (the effected <s>Brahman</s>) — not to the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>].
Now the doubt arises: Does the non-human person (<s>amānava puruṣa</s>) lead all those who meditate on modifications [of <s>Brahman</s>] to <s>Brahmaloka</s> without distinction, or only some of them?
What is the prima facie view? All these knowers — other than [knowers of] the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — should have the journey.
For thus, in 'There is no restriction [of the <s>devayāna</s> path] to all [<s>vidyās</s>]' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.3.31), [the journey] has been introduced for all these <s>vidyās</s> without distinction.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] replies: 'Those who do not meditate on <s>pratīkas</s>.' —
Excluding those who meditate on <s>pratīkas</s>, the <s>ācārya</s> <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds that [the non-human <s>Puruṣa</s>] leads all others who meditate on modifications to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
For there is no defect in accepting

children.text:
abhāva abhyupagame kaścit doṣaḥ asti /
aniyama nyāyasya pratīkavyatirikteṣu api upāsaneṣu upapatteḥ /
tatkratuḥ ca asya ubhayathābhāvasya samarthako hetuḥ draṣṭavyaḥ /
yo hi brahmakratuḥ sa brāhmam aiśvaryam āsīdediti śliṣyate 'taṃ yathā yatopāsate tadeva bhavati' iti śruteḥ /
na tu pratīkeṣu brahma akratutvam asti pratīkapradhānatvāt upāsanasya /
children.translated_text:
the absence [of the journey for <s>pratīka</s>-meditators] and its presence [for others].
Because the principle of non-restriction is tenable even for <s>upāsanās</s> other than those on <s>pratīkas</s>.
And the <s>tatkratu</s> principle should be seen as the supporting reason for this [distinction in] both ways.
For one whose meditation is focused on <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmakratu</s>) — he attains the lordship of <s>Brahman</s> — this fits [the principle]. For the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'As one meditates, so one becomes' [<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s>].
But in <s>pratīka</s>-meditations, there is no <s>Brahman</s>-focused meditation (<s>brahmakratutva</s>), because the meditation has the <s>pratīka</s> as its principal [object].

children.text: nanu abrahmakratuḥ api brahmagacchati iti śrūyate yathā pañcāgni vidyāyām 'sa enānbrahma gamayati' (chā. 4.15.5) iti bhavatu yatra evam āhatyavāda upalabhyate tat abhāve tu autsargikeṇa tat kratunyāyena brahmakratūnām eva tatprāptiḥ na itareṣām iti gamyate // 15 //
children.translated_text:
But is it not heard that even one who does not have <s>Brahman</s>-focused meditation reaches <s>Brahman</s> — as in the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s>: 'He leads them to <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 4.15.5)?
Let that be so where such a general statement is found. But in the absence of that, it is understood — by the default <s>tatkratu</s> principle — that the attainment of [<s>Brahmaloka</s>] belongs only to those whose meditation is <s>Brahman</s>-focused, not to others. // 15 //

children.text: viśeṣaṃ ca darśayati | BBs_4,3.16 |
children.translated_text: And [the <s>śruti</s>] shows a distinction. | <s>BBs</s> 4,3.16 |

children.text: nāmādiṣu pratīka upāsaneṣu pūrvasmāt pūrvasmāt phalaviśeṣam uttarasmin uttarasmin upāsane darśayati - 'yāvannāmno gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati' (chā. 7.1.5) 'vāgvāva nāmno bhūyasī' (chā. 7.2.1) 'yāvadvāco gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati'(chā. 7.2.2) 'mano vāva vāco bhūyaḥ' (chā. 7.3.1)
children.translated_text: In the <s>pratīka</s>-meditations on Name and the like, [the <s>śruti</s>] shows a specific difference in fruit in each successive meditation compared to the preceding: 'As far as the domain of Name extends, so far he has freedom of movement' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.1.5); 'Speech is indeed greater than Name' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.2.1); 'As far as the domain of Speech extends, so far he has freedom of movement' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.2.2); 'Mind is indeed greater than Speech' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.3.1) —

children.text: ityādinā /
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: sa ca ayaṃ phalaviśeṣaḥ pratīka tantratvāt upāsanānām upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And this specific difference in fruit is tenable precisely because the meditations are governed by the <s>pratīkas</s>.

children.text: brahma tantratve tu brahmaṇaḥ aviśiṣṭatvāt kathaṃ phalaviśeṣaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: But if they were governed by <s>Brahman</s>, then since <s>Brahman</s> is undifferentiated, how could there be a difference in fruit?

children.text: tasmāt na pratīka ālambanānām itaraiḥ tulyaphalatvam iti // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who meditate on <s>pratīkas</s> do not have the same fruit as the others. // 16 //

children.text: iti śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīśaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau śrīmacchārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye caturthādhyāyasya tṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣya</s> composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the pupil of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda</s>, the supreme <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya</s>. // 3 //

children.text: caturtho 'dhyāye caturthaḥ pādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fourth <s>adhyāya</s>, fourth <s>pāda</s>.

children.text: atra pāde brahmaprāpti-brahmalokasthitinirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: In this <s>pāda</s>, the determination of the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> and the state in <s>Brahmaloka</s> is provided.

children.text: 1 saṃpadyāvirbhāva adhikaraṇam / sū. 1-3
children.translated_text: 1 The <s>Saṃpadyāvirbhāva</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 1-3.

children.text: saṃpadyāvirbhāvaḥ svena śabdāt | BBs_4,4.1 |
children.translated_text: The manifestation upon merging [is] in [the Self's] own [nature] — because of the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>). | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.1 |

children.text:
