evam eva eṣa saṃprasādaḥ asmāt śarīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotiḥ upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyata iti śrūyate /
tatra saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ devalokādi upabhogasthāneṣu iva āgantukena kenacit viśeṣeṇa abhiniṣpadyata āhot ātmamātreṇa iti /
kiṃ tāvat prāptam /
sthānāntareṣu iva āgantukena kenacit rūpeṇa abhiniṣpattiḥ syāt /
mokṣasya api phalatvaprasiddheḥ /
abhiniṣpadyata iti ca utpattiparyāyatvāt /
svarūpamātreṇa cet abhiniṣpattiḥ pūrvāsu api avasthāsu svarūpa anāpāyāt vibhāvyeta /
tasmāt viśeṣeṇa kenacit abhiniṣpadyata iti /
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ - kevalena eva ātmana āvirbhavati na dharmāntareṇa iti /
kutaḥ - svena rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyata iti svaśabdāt /
anyathā hi svaśabdena iti viśeṣaṇam anavakḷptaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text:
It is heard: 'This serene one (<s>saṃprasāda</s>), having risen from this body and having reached the supreme light, manifests in its own form' [<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3].
A doubt arises: Does he manifest with some adventitious special quality — as in the stations of enjoyment such as the world of the gods and the like — or with the Self alone?
What is the prima facie view? He would manifest with some adventitious form, as in other stations.
Because liberation too is well known as a result [of practice].
And because '<s>abhiniṣpadyate</s>' (manifests) is synonymous with origination.
And if the manifestation were with one's own essential nature alone, it would be [already] perceivable even in the prior states — since the essential nature is never lost.
Therefore, he manifests with some special quality.
Having thus stated the prima facie view, we say: He manifests with the Self alone — not with any other quality.
Why? Because of the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) in 'manifests in its own form.'
For otherwise, the qualification by the word 'own' would be unexplained.

children.text: nanu ātmīya abhiprāyaḥ svaśabdo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: But perhaps the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) means 'belonging to oneself.'

children.text: na /
children.translated_text: No.

children.text: tasya avacanīyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because that [interpretation] would be vacuous.

children.text: yena eva hi kenacit rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyate tasya eva ātmīyatva upapatteḥ svena iti viśeṣaṇamna arthakaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: For whatever form one manifests in — that is automatically 'one's own'; hence the qualification 'own' would be meaningless.

children.text: ātmavacanatāyāṃ tu arthavat kevalena eva ātmarūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyate na āgantukena apararūpeṇāpi iti // 1 //
children.translated_text: But when [the word 'own'] is taken as denoting the Self, it is meaningful: [the meaning is that] he manifests with the essential nature of the Self alone — not with any adventitious, additional form. // 1 //

children.text: kaḥ punaḥ viśeṣaḥ pūrvāsu avasthāsu iha ca svarūpa anapāyasāmye sati ityata āha -
children.translated_text: But what is the specific difference between the prior states and this state, given that in both [cases] the essential nature is not lost? To this, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says:

children.text: muktaḥ pratijñānāt | BBs_4,4.2 |
children.translated_text: [He is] liberated — because of the promise [of the <s>śruti</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.2 |

children.text:
yaḥ atra abhiniṣpadyata iti uktaḥ sa sarvabandha vinirmuktaḥ śuddhena eva ātmanā avatiṣṭhate /
pūrvatra tu andho bhavati api roditi iva vināśameva apīto bhavati iti ca avasthātraya kaluṣitena ātmana iti ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
kathaṃ punaḥ avagamyate muktaḥ ayam idānīṃ bhavati iti - pratijñānāt ityāha /
tathā hi 'etaṃ tveva te bhūyo 'nuvyākhyāsyāmi' (chā. 8.9.3, 8.10.4, 8.11.3) iti avasthātraya doṣavihīnam ātmānaṃ vyākhyeyatvena pratijñāya 'aśarīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ (chā. 8.12.1) iti ca upanyasya 'svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ' (chā. 8.12.3) iti ca upasaṃharati /
tathā ākhyāyika upakrame api 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā' (chā. 8.7.1) ityādi mukta ātmaviṣayam eva pratijñānam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, at the beginning of the narrative too: 'The Self that is free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) — and the like — the promise itself pertains to the liberated Self.

children.text: phalatvaprasiddhiḥ api mokṣasya bandhanivṛttimātra apekṣā na apūrva upajanana apekṣā /
children.translated_text: And the well-known status of liberation as a fruit requires only the removal of bondage — not the generation of something unprecedented.

children.text: yat api abhiniṣpadyata iti utpattiparyāyatvaṃ tat api pūrva avasthāpekṣaṃ yathā roganivṛttau arogaḥabhiniṣpadyata iti tadvat /
children.translated_text: And the synonymity of '<s>abhiniṣpadyate</s>' with origination is also relative to the prior state — as when, upon the removal of disease, one says 'a healthy person has come into being.' Similarly here.

children.text: tasmāt adoṣaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no fault. // 2 //

He who is said to 'manifest' here — he abides with the pure Self alone, completely freed from all bondage.
But in the prior states, [his Self was] stained by the three states [of waking, dream, and deep sleep]: 'he becomes blind, as it were'; 'he weeps, as it were'; 'he goes to destruction, as it were' — this is the specific difference.
But how is it known that he is now liberated? [The <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says: because of the promise.
For thus, having promised to explain the Self that is free from the defects of the three states — 'I shall explain this to you further' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.9.3, 8.10.4, 8.11.3) — and having presented: 'While [the Self] is indeed bodiless, the pleasant and the unpleasant do not touch it' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.1), [the <s>śruti</s>] concludes: 'It manifests in its own form — that is the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3).

children.text: ātmā prakaraṇāt | BBs_4,4.3 |
children.translated_text: [The word 'light' refers to] the Self — because of the context. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.3 |

children.text:
kathaṃ punaḥ mukta iti ucyate - yāvatā 'paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya' (chā. 8.12.3) iti kāryagocaram eva enaṃ śrāvayati /
jyotiḥśabdasya bhautike jyotiṣi rūḍhatvāt /
na ca anativṛtto vikāraviṣayāt kaścit mukto bhavitum arhati /
vikārasya ārtatvaprasiddheḥ iti /
children.translated_text:
But how can he be said to be liberated — when [the <s>śruti</s>] makes him hear about a produced [entity]: 'Having reached the supreme light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3)?
For the word 'light' (<s>jyotis</s>) is established [as referring to] material light.
And no one who has not transcended the domain of modifications can be liberated.
Because modifications are well known to involve affliction.

children.text: na eṣa doṣaḥ /
yata jyotiḥ śabdena āvedyate prakaraṇāt 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyuḥ' (chā. 8.7.1) iti hi prakṛte parasmin ātmani na akasmāt bhautikaṃ jyotiḥ śakyaṃ grahītum /
children.translated_text: Because that which is conveyed by the word 'light' is — because of the context — 'The Self that is free from evil, ageless, deathless' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) — since the supreme Self is the subject under discussion, material light cannot be arbitrarily taken.

children.text: prakṛtahāna aprakṛtaprakriyā prasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because there would be the consequence of abandoning the subject and introducing a non-subject.

children.text: jyotiḥśabdaḥ tu ātmani api dṛśyate 'taddevā jyotiṣaṃ jyotiḥ (bṛ. 4.4.16) iti /
children.translated_text: And the word 'light' is seen [applied] to the Self as well: 'That light of lights the gods [worship]' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.16).

children.text: prapañcitaṃ caitat'(bra. sū. 1.3.40) ityatra // 3 //
children.translated_text: And this has been elaborated in [the discussion of <s>Brahmasūtra</s>] 1.3.40. // 3 //
This is not a fault.

children.text: 2 avibhāgena dṛṣṭatva adhikaraṇam / sū. 4
children.translated_text: 2 The <s>Avibhāgena Dṛṣṭatva</s> section. <s>Sūtra</s> 4.

children.text: avibhāgena dṛṣṭatvāt | BBs_4,4.4 |
children.translated_text: Because of being seen as non-different [from <s>Brahman</s>]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.4 |

children.text:
paraṃ jyotiḥ upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyate yaḥ sa kiṃ parasmāt ātmanaḥ pṛthageva bhavati uta avibhāgena eva avatiṣṭhata vīkṣāyām sa 'tatra paryeti' ( 8.12.3) iti adhikaraṇa adhikartavya nirdeśāt jyotiḥ upasaṃpadya (chā. 8.12.3) iti ca kartṛkarmanirdeśāt bhedena eva avasthānam iti yasya matiḥ taṃ vyutpādayati avibhakta eva pareṇa ātmanā muktaḥ avatiṣṭhate /
kutaḥ - dṛṣṭatvāt /
tathā hi 'tattvamasi' (chā. 6.8.7) 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi' (bṛ. 1.4.10) 'yatra nānyatpaśyati' (chā. 7.24.1) 'na tu taddvitīyamasti tato 'nyadvibhaktaṃ yatpaśyet' (bṛ. 4.3.23) iti evamādīni vākyāni avibhāgena eva paramātmānaṃ darśayanti /
yathādarśanam eva ca phalaṃ yuktaṃ tatkratu nyāyāt /
'yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddhamāsiktaṃ tādṛgeva bhavati /
evaṃ muneḥ vijānata ātmā bhavati gautama' (ka. 4.15) iti ca evamādīni muktasvarūpanirūpaṇaparāṇi vākyāni avibhāgameva darśayanti /
children.translated_text: so becomes the Self of the sage who knows, O <s>Gautama</s>' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 4.15) — such passages, which are devoted to determining the nature of the liberated [Self], show non-differentiation alone.

children.text: nadī samudrādi nidarśanāni ca /
children.translated_text: And [so do] the illustrations of rivers and ocean and the like.

children.text: bhedanirdeśaḥ tu abhede api upacaryate /
children.translated_text: And the designation of difference is figuratively applied even in [the state of] non-difference.

children.text: 'sa bhagavaḥ kasminpratiṣṭhita iti sve mahimni' (chā. 7.24.1) iti 'ātmaratirātmakrīḍaḥ' (chā. 7.25.2) iti ca evamādidarśanāt // 4 //
children.translated_text: Because of the observation [in the <s>śruti</s>]: 'In what, O Lord, is he established? In his own greatness' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1); 'He delights in the Self, he plays in the Self' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2) — and the like. // 4 //

He who, 'having reached the supreme light, manifests in his own form' — does he exist as separate from the supreme Self, or does he abide in non-differentiation alone?
To one who thinks: 'He exists separately' — based on the locative-agent designation 'He moves about there' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3), and the agent-object designation in 'Having reached the light' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3) — [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] instructs: The liberated one abides as non-different from the supreme Self.
Why? Because of being seen [thus in the <s>śruti</s>].
For thus, 'That art thou' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.7); 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.4.10); 'Where one sees nothing else' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.24.1); 'There is not that second thing, something else separate from it, that one could see' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.23) — such passages show the supreme Self as non-different.
And the fruit should properly correspond to the vision, by the <s>tatkratu</s> principle.
'As pure water poured into pure water becomes just like it —

children.text: 3 brāhma adhikaraṇam / sū. 5-7
children.translated_text: 3 The <s>Brāhma</s> section. <s>Sūtras</s> 5-7.

children.text: brāhmeṇa jaiminir upanyāsādibhyaḥ | BBs_4,4.5 |
children.translated_text: [He manifests] with the nature of <s>Brahman</s> — [thus holds] <s>Jaimini</s>, because of the introduction and the like. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.5 |

children.text:
sthitam etat 'svena rūpeṇa'(chā. 8.3.4) iti atra ātmamātrarūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyata na āgantukena apararūpeṇa iti /
adhunā tu tat viśeṣabubhutsāyām abhidhīyate svam asya rūpaṃ brāhmam apahatapāpmatvādi satyasaṃkalpatva avasānaṃ tathā sarvajñatvaṃ sarveśvaratvaṃ ca tena svarūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyata iti jaiminiḥ ācāryo manyate /
kutaḥ - upanyāsādibhyaḥ tathātva avagamāt /
tathā hi - 'ya ātmāpahatapāpmā' (chā. 8.7.1) ityādinā 'satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ' (chā. 8.7.1) iti evam antena upanyāsena evam ātmakatām ātmano bodhayati /
children.translated_text: For thus, through the introduction 'The Self that is free from evil' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1) and the like, up to 'whose desires are true, whose will is true' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.7.1), [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches the Self as having this nature.

children.text: tathā 'sa tatra paryeti jakṣankrīḍanramamāṇaḥ' (chā. 8.12.3) iti aiśvaryarūpam āvedayati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'There he moves about, eating, playing, delighting' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.3) reveals a form of lordship.

children.text: 'tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati' (chā. 7.25.2) iti ca /
children.translated_text: 'He has freedom of movement in all worlds' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2) — likewise.

children.text: 'sarvajñaḥ sarveśvaraḥ' ityādi vyapadeśāḥ ca evam upapannā bhaviṣyanti iti // 5 //
children.translated_text: And designations such as 'omniscient,' 'omnipotent,' and the like will thus be fitting. // 5 //

It is established that in 'in its own form' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.3.4), he manifests with the form of the Self alone — not with any adventitious other form.
Now, in the desire to know the specific nature [of that form], it is stated: His own form is that of <s>Brahman</s> — consisting of freedom from evil and the like, extending up to truth of will (<s>satyasaṃkalpatva</s>), and likewise omniscience and omnipotence — he manifests with that form. This is what the <s>ācārya</s> <s>Jaimini</s> holds.
Why? Because such a nature is understood from the introduction and the like.

children.text: cititanmātreṇa tadātmakatvād ity auḍulomiḥ | BBs_4,4.6 |
children.translated_text: [He manifests] with consciousness alone as his essence — because of being of that nature; [thus holds] <s>Auḍulomi</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.6 |

children.text:
yadyapi apahapāpmatvādayobhedena eva dharmā nirdiśyante tathā api śabdavikalpajā eva ete /
pāpmādinivṛttimātraṃ hi tatra gamyate /
caitanyameva tu asya ātmanaḥ svarūpam iti tanmātreṇa svarūpeṇa abhiniṣpattiḥ yuktā /
tathā ca śrutiḥ - 'evaṃ vā are 'yamātmānantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva' (bṛ. 4.5.13) iti evañjātīyakā anugṛhītā bhaviṣyati /
satyakāmatvādayaḥ tu yadi api vastusvarūpeṇa eva dharmā ucyante satyāḥ kāmā asya iti /
tathā api upādhisaṃbandha adhīnatvāt teṣāṃ na caitanyavat svarūpasaṃbhavaḥ /
aneka ākāratvapratiṣedāt /
pratiṣiddhaṃ hi brahmaṇaḥ aneka ākāratvam 'na sthānato 'pi parasyobhayaliṅgam' (bra.sū, 3.2.11) ityatra /
children.translated_text: For the multiplicity of form of <s>Brahman</s> has been negated in [the discussion of] 'Nor even from the standpoint [of location] does the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>] have both characteristics' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 3.2.11).

children.text: ata eva ca jakṣaṇādi saṃkīrtanam api duḥkha abhāvamātra abhiprāyaṃ stutyartham ātmaratiḥ ityādivat /
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, the mention of eating, playing, and the like too is intended merely to convey the absence of suffering — for the purpose of praise, like [the expressions] 'He delights in the Self' and the like.

children.text: na hi mukhyāni eva ratikrīḍāmithunāni ātmani śakyante varṇayituṃ dvitīya viṣayatvāt teṣām /
children.translated_text: For it is not possible to describe actual delight, play, or sexual union in the Self — because those [require] a second [object].

children.text: tasmāt nirasta aśeṣaprapañcena prasannena avyapadeśyena bodhātmanā abhiniṣpadyata iti auḍulomiḥ ācāryo manyate // 6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the liberated soul] is accomplished as the nature of pure consciousness (<s>bodhātman</s>) — serene, indescribable, with all multiplicity removed — so holds the teacher <s>Auḍulomi</s>. // 6 //

Although attributes such as freedom from evil and the like are designated as [apparently] distinct qualities, they are merely products of verbal differentiation.
For only the removal of evil and the like is to be understood there.
But the essential nature of this Self is consciousness alone — and manifestation in that essential nature alone is proper.
And thus, the <s>śruti</s>: 'This Self, O revered one, is without interior, without exterior, a complete mass of consciousness alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.13) — such a [passage] will be supported [by this view].
As for [the attributes of] truth of desire and the like — even if they are said to be qualities of the real nature, as in 'whose desires are true' — still, because they depend on the association with <s>upādhis</s>, they are not [intrinsic to] the essential nature like consciousness.
Because multiplicity of form is negated.

children.text: evam apy upanyāsāt pūrvabhāvād avirodhaṃ bādarāyaṇaḥ | BBs_4,4.7 |
children.translated_text: Even so, because of the mention [of lordly powers], and because of the prior state, there is no contradiction — [so holds] <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.7 |

children.text: evam api pāramārthika caitanyamātrasvarūpa abhyupagame api vyavahāra apekṣayā pūrvasya api upanyāsādibhyaḥ avagatasya brāhmasya aiśvaryarūpasya apratyayākhyānāt avirodhaṃ bādarāyaṇa ācāryo manyate //7 //
children.translated_text: Even when the ultimate nature is accepted as being of the form of pure consciousness alone — from the standpoint of transactional reality (<s>vyavahāra</s>), because the lordly power of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, previously known through mention and the like, is not contradicted — so the teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> holds that there is no contradiction. // 7 //

children.text: 4 saṃkalpa adhikaraṇam / sū. 8-9
children.translated_text: 4. The <s>Saṃkalpa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Will). <s>Sūtras</s> 8-9.

children.text: saṃkalpād eva tu tacchruteḥ | BBs_4,4.8 |
children.translated_text: But by will alone — because of the <s>śruti</s> to that effect. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.8 |

children.text:
hārdavidyāyāṃ śrūyate - 'sa yadi pitṛlokakāmo bhavati saṃkalpādevāsya pitaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti' (chā. 8.2.1) ityādi /
tatra saṃśayaḥ kiṃ saṃkalpa eva kevalaḥ pitrādisamutthāne hetuḥ uta nimittāntara sahita iti /
tatra sati api saṃkalpādeva iti śravaṇe lokavat nimittāntara apekṣatā yuktā /
yathā loke asmadādīnāṃ saṃkalpāt gamanādibhyaḥ ca hetubhyaḥ pitrādi saṃpattiḥ bhavati evaṃ muktasya api syāt /
evaṃ dṛṣṭaviparītaṃ na kalpitaṃ bhaviṣyati /
saṃkalpādeva iti tu rājña iva saṃkalpitārthasiddhikarīṃ sādhanāntarasāmagrīṃ sulabhām apekṣya ucyate /
na ca saṃkalpamātrasam utthānāḥ pitrādayo manorathāvijṛmbhitavat calatvāt puṣkalaṃ bhogaṃ samarpayituṃ paryāptāḥ syuḥ iti /
children.translated_text:
In the <s>hārda-vidyā</s>, it is taught: 'If he desires the world of the fathers, by his will alone (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) the fathers arise for him' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.2.1) and so on.
There, a doubt arises: Is will (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) alone the cause of the arising of fathers and the like, or is it [effective only] together with other instrumental causes?
The prima facie view is: Even though 'by will alone' is heard, dependence on other causes is reasonable, as in the world.
Just as in the world, for us and the like, the attainment of fathers and the like results from will together with other causes such as going and the like — so too it would be for the liberated one.
Thus, nothing contrary to what is observed would need to be imagined.
The expression 'by will alone' is said with reference to the easy availability of other instrumental means that accomplish the desired end — as in the case of a king.
Nor would fathers and the like arising from mere will — being fleeting like the products of daydreaming — be capable of delivering substantial enjoyment.

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ saṃkalpādeva tu kevalāt pitrādisamutthānam iti /
kutaḥ - tat śruteḥ /
'saṃkalpādevāsya pitaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti' (chā. 8.2.1) ityādikā hi śrutiḥ nimittāntara apekṣāyāṃ pīḍyeta /
nimittāntaram api tu yadi saṃkalpa anuvidhāyi eva syāt bhavatu na tu prayatnāntarasaṃpādyaṃ nimittāntaram iti iṣyate /
children.translated_text: But if another cause too were to follow will alone [i.e., arise spontaneously from will], let it be so — however, it is maintained that no other cause requiring separate effort is [needed].

children.text: prāk tat saṃpatteḥ vandhyasaṃkalpatva prasaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: Because before the attainment of that [other cause], there would be the unwanted consequence of will being barren.

children.text: na ca śruti avagamye arthe lokavat iti sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ kramate /
children.translated_text: And when the meaning is ascertained from <s>śruti</s>, inference from worldly analogy does not apply.

children.text: saṃkalpabalāt eva ca eṣāṃ yāvat prayojanaṃ sthairya upapattiḥ. prākṛtasaṃkalpavilakṣaṇatvāt muktasaṃkalpasya // 8 //
children.translated_text: And for these [objects arising from will], their stability for as long as needed is tenable by the power of will alone — because the will of the liberated one is of a different kind from ordinary will. // 8 //

Having arrived at this prima facie view, we say: But by will (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) alone — the arising of fathers and the like is from will alone.
Why? Because of the <s>śruti</s> to that effect.
For the <s>śruti</s> 'By his will alone the fathers arise for him' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.2.1) and the like would be compromised if dependence on other causes were required.

children.text: ata eva cānanyādhipatiḥ | BBs_4,4.9 |
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, [the liberated soul] has no other master. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.9 |

children.text: ata eva ca avandhyasaṃkalpatvāt ananya adhipatiḥ vidvān bhavati na asya anyaḥ adhipatiḥ bhavati ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for this very reason — because his will is never barren — the knower has no other master; that is, no one else is his overlord — this is the meaning.

children.text: na hi prākṛto api saṃkalpayan anyasvāmikatvam ātmanaḥ satyāṃ gatau saṃkalpayati /
children.translated_text: For even an ordinary person, when exercising his will, does not, when there is actually a possibility [of fulfillment], will that he be subject to another's mastery.

children.text: śrutiḥ ca etat darśayati - 'atha ya ihātmānamanuvidya vrajantyeśca satyānkāmāṃsteṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati' (chā. 8.1.6) iti // 9 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> shows this: 'Now, those who, having found the Self here, depart, and [have found] the true desires — for them, in all worlds, there is freedom of movement' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.1.6). // 9 //

children.text: abhāva adhikaraṇam / sū. 10-14
children.translated_text: The <s>Abhāva Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Absence [of Body]). <s>Sūtras</s> 10-14.

children.text: abhāvaṃ bādarir āha hy evam | BBs_4,4.10 |
children.translated_text: <s>Bādari</s> says there is absence [of body and sense-organs] — for thus [the <s>śruti</s> declares]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.10 |

children.text:
'saṃkalpādevāsya pitaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti' (chā. 8.2.1) ityādi śruteḥ manaḥ tāvat saṃkalpasādhanaṃ siddham /
śarīra indriyāṇi punaḥ prāpta aiśvaryasya viduṣaḥ santi na vā santi iti samīkṣyate /
tatra bādariḥ tāvat ācāryaḥ śarīrasya indriyāṇāṃ ca abhāvaṃ mahīyamānasya viduṣo manyate /
children.translated_text: The teacher <s>Bādari</s> holds that for the exalted knower, there is the absence of body and sense-organs.

children.text: kasmāt /
children.translated_text: Why?

children.text: evaṃ hi āha āmnāyaḥ 'manasaitānkāmānpaśyanramate' (chā. 8.12.5) 'ya ete brahmaloke' (chā. 8.13.1) iti /
children.translated_text: Because thus declares the scripture: 'By the mind, seeing these desires, he rejoices' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.12.5); 'Those who are in <s>Brahmaloka</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.13.1) and the like.

children.text: yadi manasā śarīra indriyāṇāṃ mokṣe // 10 //
children.translated_text: If by the mind [alone one fulfills desires], then there is liberation from body and sense-organs. // 10 //

From the <s>śruti</s> 'By his will alone the fathers arise for him' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.2.1) and the like, it is established that the mind is the instrument of will.
But does the knower who has attained lordly powers possess a body and sense-organs, or not? — This is examined.

children.text: bhāvaṃ jaiminir vikalpāmananāt | BBs_4,4.11 |
children.translated_text: <s>Jaimini</s> [holds that] there is existence [of body] — because of the mention of the alternative of multiple [forms]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.11 |

children.text: jaiminiḥ tu ācāryo manovat śarīrasya api sendriyasya bhāvaṃ muktaṃ prati manyate /
children.translated_text: But the teacher <s>Jaimini</s> holds that, like the mind, the body too — together with sense-organs — exists for the liberated one.

children.text: yataḥ 'sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati'(chā. 7.23.2) ityādinā anekadhā abhāvavikalpam āmananti /
children.translated_text: Because [the <s>śruti</s>] mentions the alternative of multiple forms: 'He becomes one, he becomes threefold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.23.2) and so on.

children.text: na hi anekavidhatā vinā śarīrabhedena āñjasī syāt /
children.translated_text: For manifoldness would not be straightforward without the distinction of bodies.

children.text: yadi api nirguṇāyāṃ bhūmavidyāyām ayam anekadhā abhāvavikalpaḥ paṭhyate tathā api vidyamānameva idaṃ saguṇāvasthāyām aiśvaryaṃ bhūmavidyā stutaye saṃkīrtyata iti ataḥ saguṇavidyāphalabhāvena upatiṣṭhata iti // 11 //
children.translated_text: Even though this alternative of multiple forms is recited in the attributeless <s>Bhūma-vidyā</s>, still, this lordly power — which exists [in the state of qualified <s>Brahman</s>] — is mentioned in praise of the <s>Bhūma-vidyā</s>. Therefore, it stands as the fruit of qualified (<s>saguṇa</s>) <s>vidyā</s>. // 11 //

children.text: ucyate -
children.translated_text: We reply:

children.text: dvādaśāhavad ubhayavidhaṃ bādarāyaṇo 'taḥ | BBs_4,4.12 |
children.translated_text: <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds that it is] of both kinds — like the twelve-day [sacrifice] — because of this. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.12 |

children.text:
bādarāyaṇaḥ punaḥ ācāryaḥ ata eva ubhayaliṅgaśrutidarśanāt ubhayavidhatvaṃ sādhu manyate yadā saśarīratāṃ saṃkalpayati tadā saśarīro bhavati yadā tu aśarīratāṃ tadā aśarīra iti /
satyasaṃkalpatvāt /
saṃkalpa vaicitryāt ca /
children.translated_text: And because of the variety of his will.

children.text: dvādaśa ahavat /
children.translated_text: Like the twelve-day [sacrifice].

children.text: yathā dvādaśa ahaḥsatram ahīnaḥ ca bhavati /
children.translated_text: Just as the twelve-day rite is both an <s>ahīna</s> sacrifice and a <s>sattra</s>,

children.text: ubhayaliṅga śrutidarśanāt evam idam api iti // 12 //
children.translated_text: because of the observation of <s>śruti</s> texts bearing both kinds of indicative marks — so too is this [matter of embodiment]. // 12 //

But the teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — precisely because of the observation of <s>śruti</s> texts bearing both kinds of indicative marks — holds that both forms are proper: when [the liberated one] wills embodiment, he becomes embodied; when he wills disembodiment, he becomes disembodied.
Because his will is unfailingly true (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>).

children.text: tanvabhāve sandhyavad upapatteḥ | BBs_4,4.13 |
children.translated_text: When the body is absent — as in the dream state — because of tenability. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.13 |

children.text: yadā tanoḥ sendriyasya śarīrasya abhāvaḥ tadā yathā saṃdhye sthāne śarīra indriyaviṣayeṣu avidyamāneṣu api upalabdhimātrā eva pitrādikāmā bhavati evaṃ mokṣe api syuḥ evaṃ hi etat upapadyate // 13 //
children.translated_text: When there is the absence of the body together with sense-organs, then — just as in the dream state, even though body, sense-organs, and objects are absent, the desires for fathers and the like consist in perception alone — so too in liberation, it would be so. For this is how it is tenable. // 13 //

children.text: bhāve jāgradvat | BBs_4,4.14 |
children.translated_text: When the body is present — as in the waking state. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.14 |

children.text: bhāve punaḥ tanoḥ yathā jāgarite vidyamānā eva pitrādikāmā bhavanti evaṃ muktasya api upapadyate // 14 //
children.translated_text: But when the body is present, just as in the waking state the desires for fathers and the like are of actually existing [entities] — so too it is tenable for the liberated one. // 14 //

children.text: 6 pradīpa adhikaraṇam / sū. 15-16
children.translated_text: 6. The <s>Pradīpa Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of the Lamp). <s>Sūtras</s> 15-16.

children.text: pradīpavadāveśas tathā hi darśayati | BBs_4,4.15 |
children.translated_text: Entry [into multiple bodies] is like a lamp — for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.15 |

children.text:
bhāvaṃ 'jaiminirvikalpāmananāt' ( bra.sū. 4.4.11) iti atra saśarīratvaṃ muktasya uktam /
tatra tridhābhāvādiṣu anekaśarīrasarge kiṃ nirātmakāni śarīrāṇi dāruyantrāṇi iva sṛjyante kiṃ vā sātmakāni asmadādi śarīravat iti bhavati vīkṣā /
tatra ca ātma manasoḥ bheda anupapatteḥ ekena śarīreṇa yogāt itarāṇi śarīrāṇi nirātmakāni iti /
evaṃ prāpte pratipadyate - pradīpavat āveśa iti /
yathā pradīpa ekaḥ anekapradīpabhāvam āpadyate vikāraśaktiyogāt /
evam ekaḥ api san vidvāna aiśvaryayogāt anekabhāvam āpadya sarvāṇi śarīrāṇi āviśati /
kutaḥ, tathā hi darśayati śāstram ekasya anekabhāvam - 'sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati pañcadhā saptadhā navadhā' (chā. 7.26.2) ityādi /
children.translated_text:
Embodiment for the liberated one was stated in '<s>Jaimini</s> [holds] existence [of body] because of the mention of the alternative' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.4.11).
There, in the creation of multiple bodies — as in the threefold state and the like — the inquiry arises: Are the bodies created without a Self, like wooden automata, or are they ensouled, like our bodies and the like?
And because of the impossibility of the Self and mind being different, and because of the connection with one body, the other bodies would be without a Self.
Having arrived at this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] concludes: The entry [into multiple bodies] is like a lamp.
Just as a single lamp assumes the state of many lamps through the power of transformation,
so too, even though the knower is one, through the power of lordly sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), assuming a manifold state, he enters all the bodies.
Why? Because thus the scripture shows the manifoldness of one: 'He becomes one, he becomes threefold, fivefold, sevenfold, ninefold' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.26.2) and so on.

children.text:
na etat dāruyantra upamā abhyupagame avakalpate na api jīvāntarāveśe /
na ca nirātmakānāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ saṃbhavati /
yat tu ātma manasoḥ bheda anupapatteḥ anekaśarīrayoga asaṃbhava iti /
children.translated_text:
This does not fit the hypothesis of the analogy with wooden automata, nor the hypothesis of the entry of other <s>jīvas</s>.
Nor is the functioning of bodies without a Self possible.
As for the [objection that] because of the impossibility of the Self and mind being different, the connection with multiple bodies is impossible —

children.text: na eṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: ekamanonuvartini samanaskāni eva aparāṇi śarīrāṇi satyasaṃkalpatvāt srakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Because he — whose will is unfailingly true — will create the other bodies as endowed with minds that follow a single mind.

children.text: sṛṣṭeṣu ca teṣu upādhibhedāt ātmanaḥ api bhedena adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ yokṣyate /
children.translated_text: And when those [bodies] are created, because of the difference of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), the Self too will preside over [them] as if differentiated.

children.text: eṣa eva ca yogaśāstreṣu yoginām anekaśarīraprayogakriyā // 15 //
children.translated_text: And this very [principle] is the procedure in the <s>Yoga</s> scriptures — the practice of <s>yogins</s> assuming multiple bodies. // 15 //

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ muktasya anekaśarīra āveśādilakṣaṇam aiśvaryam abhyupagamyate yāvatā 'tatkena kaṃ vijānīyāt' (bṛ. 4.5.15) 'na tu taddvitīyamasti tato 'nyadvibhaktaṃ yadvijānīyāt' (bṛ. 4.3.30) 'salila eko draṣṭādvaito bhavati' (bṛ. 4.3.32) iti ca evañjātīyakā śrutiḥ viśeṣavijñānaṃ vārayati ityata uttaraṃ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: But how can lordly sovereignty characterized by entry into multiple bodies and the like be accepted for the liberated one, given that <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'By what and whom should he know?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.5.15); 'There is nothing other than It, nothing separate that It could know' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.30); 'He becomes a seer without a second, like water alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.32) — such <s>śrutis</s> negate specific cognition? Therefore, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads the reply:

children.text: svāpyayasaṃpatyor anyatarāpekṣam āviṣkṛtaṃ hi | BBs_4,4.16 |
children.translated_text: With reference to either deep sleep or complete dissolution — for [the negation] is made manifest [only with reference to those]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.16 |

children.text:
svāpyayaḥ suṣuptam 'svamapīto bhavati tasmādenaṃ svapitītyācakṣate' (chā. 6.8.1) iti śruteḥ /
saṃpattiḥ kaivalyam, 'brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti' (bṛ. 4.4.6) iti śruteḥ /
tayoḥ anyatarām avasthām apekṣya etat viśeṣasaṃjñābhāva vacanam /
kvacit suṣupta avasthām apekṣya ucyate kvacit kaivalya avasthām /
children.translated_text: In some cases, it is said with reference to the state of deep sleep; in some cases, with reference to the state of absolute liberation.

children.text: katham avagamyate yataḥ tatra eva etat adhikāravaśāt āviṣkṛtam 'etebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tānyevānu vinaśyati na pretya saṃjñāstīti' (bṛ. 2.4.14) 'yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūt' (bṛ. 2.4.14) 'yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati' (bṛ. 4.3.19, māṇḍū. 5) ityādi śrutibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: How is this known? Because in those very [passages], this is made manifest by the force of the context: 'Having risen from these elements, [the Self] is destroyed along with them; after departing, there is no consciousness' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14); 'Where, for him, all has become the Self alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 2.4.14); 'Where, asleep, one desires no desire and sees no dream' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.3.19, <s>Māṇḍūkya</s> 5) — and the like <s>śrutis</s>.

children.text: saguṇavidyāvipāka avasthānaṃ tu etat svargādivat avasthāntaraṃ yatra etat aiśvaryam upavarṇyate /
children.translated_text: But this [state of lordly sovereignty] is the state resulting from the fruition of <s>saguṇa-vidyā</s> — a different state, like heaven and the like — where this lordly sovereignty is described.

children.text: tasmāt adoṣaḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no fault. // 16 //

<s>Svāpyaya</s> is deep sleep — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'He has gone to his own (<s>svam apīto bhavati</s>) — therefore they call him one who sleeps (<s>svapiti</s>)' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 6.8.1).
<s>Saṃpatti</s> is absolute liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges into <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 4.4.6).
With reference to one or the other of these two states, this statement of the absence of specific cognition is made.

children.text: 7 jagat vyāpāra adhikaraṇam / sū. 17-22
children.translated_text: 7. The <s>Jagadvyāpāra Adhikaraṇa</s> (Topic of Cosmic Functions). <s>Sūtras</s> 17-22.

children.text: jagadvyāpāravarjaṃ prakaraṇād asaṃnihitatvāc ca | BBs_4,4.17 |
children.translated_text: Except for cosmic functions — because of the context and because [the liberated souls] are not [directly] present [in that role]. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.17 |

children.text:
ye saguṇabrahma upāsanāt saha eva manasā īśvarasāyujyaṃ vrajanti kiṃ teṣāṃ niravagraham aiśvaryaṃ bhavati āhosvit sāvagraham iti saṃśayaḥ /
kiṃ tāvat prāptam /
niraṅ kuśameva eṣām aiśvaryaṃ bhavitum arhati 'āpnoti svārājyam' (tai. 1.6.2) 'sarve 'smai devā balimāvahanti' (tai. 1.5.3) 'teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati' (chā. 7.25.2, 8.1.6) ityādi śrutibhya iti /
evaṃ prāpte paṭhati - jagat vyāpāravarjam iti /
jagat utpattyādi vyāpāraṃ varjayitvā anyat aṇimādi ātmakam aiśvaryaṃ muktānāṃ bhavitum arhati jagat vyāpāraḥ tu nityasiddhasya eva īśvarasya /
kutaḥ - tasya tatra prakṛtatvāt asaṃnihitatvāt ca itareṣām /
para eva hi īśvaro jagat vyāpāre adhikṛtaḥ /
tam eva prakṛtya utpattyādi upadeśāt /
nityaśabdanibandhanatvāt ca /
tat anveṣaṇavijijñāsanapūrvakaṃ tu itareṣām aṇimādi aiśvaryaṃ śrūyate /
children.translated_text: But for the others, lordly sovereignty of <s>aṇimā</s> and the like — preceded by seeking and investigating That — is heard.

children.text: tena asaṃnihitāḥ te jagat vyāpāre /
children.translated_text: Therefore, they are not present [in the role of] cosmic functions.

children.text: samanaskatvāt eva ca eteṣām anaikamatye kasyacit sthiti abhiprāyaḥ kasyacit saṃhāra abhiprāya iti evaṃ virodhaḥ api kadācit syāt /
children.translated_text: And because these [liberated souls] have minds, when there is disagreement [among them] — one intending preservation, another intending destruction — there could even be contradiction.

children.text: atha kasyacit saṃkalpam anvayasya saṃkalpa iti avirodhaḥ samarthyeta tataḥ parameśvara ākūtatantratvam eva itareṣām iti vyavatiṣṭhate // 17 //
children.translated_text: Now, if it were argued that there is no contradiction because the will of one follows the will of another — then it is established that the others are dependent on the intention of the supreme Lord alone. // 17 //

Those who, through the meditation on qualified <s>Brahman</s> (<s>saguṇa-brahma-upāsanā</s>), together with the mind, attain union with the Lord (<s>īśvara-sāyujya</s>) — does their lordly sovereignty have no restriction, or does it have a restriction? This is the doubt.
What is the prima facie view?
Their lordly sovereignty should be unrestricted, [as follows from] <s>śrutis</s> such as: 'He attains self-sovereignty' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2); 'All the gods bring tribute to him' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.5.3); 'For them, in all worlds, there is freedom of movement' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 7.25.2, 8.1.6) and the like.
Having arrived at this prima facie view, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] reads: 'Except for cosmic functions.'
Except for the cosmic functions of creation and the like of the universe, other lordly sovereignty — of the nature of <s>aṇimā</s> and the like — is proper for the liberated ones. But cosmic functions belong to the eternally established Lord alone.
Why? Because He is the one who is contextually relevant there, while the others are not present [in that role].
For the supreme Lord alone is the one authorized in cosmic functions.
Because the teaching of creation and the like is given with reference to Him alone.
And because [that role] is established through eternal scriptural terms.

children.text: pratyakṣopadeśād iti cen nādhikārikamaṇḍalasthokteḥ | BBs_4,4.18 |
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] because of the direct teaching [of unrestricted sovereignty, the liberated souls should have cosmic powers] — [we say:] No, because the statement is about the one who is established in the sphere of authority. | <s>BBs</s> 4,4.18 |

children.text: atha yat uktam 'āpnoti svārājyam' (tai. 1.6.2) ityādi pratyakṣa upadeśāt niravagraham aiśvaryaṃ viduṣāṃ nyāyyam iti tatparihartavyam /
children.translated_text: Now, the objection that was raised — that unrestricted lordly sovereignty for the knowers is proper because of the direct teaching 'He attains self-sovereignty' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2) and the like — this must be answered.

children.text:
atra ucyate /
na ayaṃ doṣaḥ /
ādhikārikamaṇḍalastha ukteḥ /
ādhikāriko yaḥ savitṛmaṇḍalādiṣu viśeṣa āyataneṣu avasthitaḥ para īśvaraḥ tadāyatta eva iyaṃ svārājyaprāptiḥ ucyate /
yatkāraṇam anantaram 'āpnoti manasaspatim' (tai. 1.6.2) ityāha /
children.translated_text: For the reason that immediately after, [the text] says: 'He attains the lord of the mind' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2).

children.text: yo hi sarvamanasāṃ patiḥ pūrvasiddha īśvaraḥ taṃ prāpnoti iti etat uktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: For He who is the lord of all minds — the eternally established Lord — it is said that [the liberated soul] attains Him.

children.text: tat anusāreṇa eva ca anantaram 'vākpatiścakṣuṣpatiḥ śrotrapatirvijñānapatiśca bhavati' (tai. 1.6.2) ityāha /
children.translated_text: And in accordance with that [attainment], immediately after, [the text] says: 'He becomes the lord of speech, the lord of the eye, the lord of the ear, the lord of cognition' (<s>Taittirīya</s> 1.6.2).

children.text: evam anyatra api yathāsaṃbhavaṃ nityasiddha īśvara āyattam eva itareṣām aiśvaryaṃ yojayitavyam // 18 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in other cases too, the lordly powers of the others should be construed as dependent on the eternally established Lord, as appropriate. // 18 //

To this we say:
This is not a fault.
Because the statement pertains to the one established in the sphere of authority — the supreme Lord who is established in specific abodes such as the orb of the sun and the like. This attainment of self-sovereignty is said to be dependent on Him alone.

children.text: vikārāvarti ca tathā hi sthitim āha | BBs_4,4.19 |
children.translated_text: And [the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>] transcends modification — for thus [the <s>śruti</s>] states [Its] abiding. | <s>BBs</s> 4.4.19 |

children.text: vikārāvartyapi ca nityamuktaṃ pārameśvaraṃ rūpaṃ na kevalaṃ vikāramātragocaraṃ savitṛmaṇḍalādi adhiṣṭhānam /
tathā hi asya dvirūpāṃ sthitim āha āmnāyaḥ 'tāvānasya mahimā tato jyāyāṃśca puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: For thus the Vedic scripture states a twofold abiding of this [<s>Brahman</s>]: 'So great is His majesty; and the <s>Puruṣa</s> is greater still.

children.text: pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni, tripādasyāmṛtaṃ divi' (chā. 3.12.6) iti evamādiḥ /
children.translated_text: One quarter of Him is all beings; three quarters [constitute] the immortal in heaven' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 3.12.6) — and passages of this kind.

children.text: na ca tat nirvikāraṃ rūpam itara ālambanāḥ prāpnuvanti iti śakyaṃ vaktum atatkratutvāt teṣām /
children.translated_text: And it cannot be said that those who are dependent on the other [modified <s>Brahman</s>] attain that unmodified form — because their resolve (<s>kratu</s>) is not directed toward that [unmodified form].

children.text: ataḥ ca yathā eva dvirūpe parameśvare nirguṇaṃ rūpam anavāpya saguṇa eva avatiṣṭhanta evaṃ saguṇaḥ api niravagraham aiśvaryam anavāpya sāvagraha eva avatiṣṭhanta iti draṣṭavyam // 19 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as, regarding the twofold [nature of] the Supreme Lord, they do not attain the <s>nirguṇa</s> (attributeless) form and remain in the <s>saguṇa</s> (qualified) alone, so too even within the <s>saguṇa</s>, they do not attain unrestricted lordship and remain with restricted [lordship] alone — this should be understood. // 19 //

The form of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) is eternally free and transcends modification — not merely a presiding [principle] over the domain of modifications such as the orb of the sun and the like.

children.text: darśayataś caivaṃ pratyakṣānumāne | BBs_4,4.20 |
children.translated_text: And [both] direct perception and inference (<s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>) show [it to be] thus. | <s>BBs</s> 4.4.20 |

children.text: darśayataḥ ca vikāra āvartitvaṃ parasya jyotiṣaḥ śruti smṛtī /
children.translated_text: And both <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> show that the Supreme Light transcends modification.

children.text: 'na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yamagniḥ' (kaṭha. 5.15, śvetā. 6.14, muṇḍa. 2.2.10) iti /
children.translated_text: 'There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine — what to speak of this fire?' (<s>Kaṭha</s> 5.15, <s>Śvetāśvatara</s> 6.14, <s>Muṇḍaka</s> 2.2.10).

children.text: 'na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅ ko na pāvakaḥ' (gī. 15.6) iti ca /
children.translated_text: 'Neither the sun illuminates That, nor the moon, nor fire' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 15.6).

children.text: tat evaṃ vikāra āvartitvaṃ parasya jyotiṣaḥ prasiddham iti abhiprāyaḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: Thus, the transcendence of the Supreme Light over modification is well-established. // 20 //

children.text: bhogamātrasāmyaliṅgāc ca | BBs_4,4.21 |
children.translated_text: And because of the indicatory mark that [their] equality [with the Lord is] in enjoyment alone. | <s>BBs</s> 4.4.21 |

children.text: itaḥ ca na niraṅ kuśaṃ vikāra ālambanānām aiśvaryaṃ yasmāt bhogamātram eva eṣām anādisiddhena īśvareṇa samānam iti śrūyate - 'tamāhāpo vai khalu mīyante loko 'sau' iti 'sa yathaitāṃ devatāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyavantyevaṃ haivaṃvidaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyavanti teno etasyai devatāyai sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati'(bṛ. 1.5.23) ityādibhedavyapadeśaliṅgebhyaḥ // 21 //
children.translated_text: For this further reason, the lordship of those who depend on modification is not unrestricted — because the <s>śruti</s> states that their [equality] with the beginninglessly established Lord is in enjoyment alone: 'Him the waters approach: "[We] measure [constitute] worlds"' — and 'Just as all beings serve this deity, so do all beings serve one who knows thus — by that he conquers communion and co-residence with that deity' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 1.5.23) — from such indicatory marks expressing difference [between the liberated soul and the Lord]. // 21 //

children.text: nanu evaṃ sati sātiśayatvāt antavattvam aiśvaryasya syāt tataḥ ca eṣām āvṛttiḥ prasajyeta ityata uttaraṃ bhagavān bādarāyaṇa ācāryaḥ paṭhati -
children.translated_text: Objection: But if so — since [their lordship] is limited, it would be finite; and consequently, their return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>] would follow. Therefore, the revered teacher <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> reads the reply:

children.text: anāvṛttiḥ śabdād anāvṛttiḥ śabdāt | BBs_4,4.22 |
children.translated_text: Non-return — because of the [scriptural] word. Non-return — because of the [scriptural] word. | <s>BBs</s> 4.4.22 |

children.text:
nāḍīraśmisamanvitena arcirādiparvaṇā devayānena pathā ye brahmalokaṃ śāstroktaviśeṣaṇaṃ gacchanti yasminnaraśca ha vai ṇyaścārṇavau brahmaloke tṛtīyasyāmito divi yasminnaśvatthaḥ somasavano yasminnaparājitā pūrbrahmaṇo yasmiṃśca prabhuvimitaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ veśma yaścānekadhā mantrārthavādādipradeśeṣu prapañcyate te taṃ prāpya na candralokādivabhuktabhogā āvartante /
kutaḥ /
'tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti' (chā. 8.6.6, kaṭha. 6.16) 'teṣāṃ na punarāvṛttiḥ' (bṛ. 6.2.15) 'brahmalokamabhisaṃpadyate' (chā. 8.15.1) 'na ca punarāvartate' (chā. 8.15.1) ityādi śabdebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of scriptural words such as: 'Going upward by that [path], one attains immortality' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.6.6, <s>Kaṭha</s> 6.16); 'For them there is no return' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> 6.2.15); '[He] attains the world of <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.15.1); and 'He does not return again' (<s>Chāndogya</s> 8.15.1).

children.text: antavattve api tu aiśvaryasya yathā anāvṛttiḥ tathā varṇitam 'kāryātyaye tadadhyakṣeṇa sahātaḥparam' (bra.sū. 4.3.10) ityatra /
children.translated_text: And how there is non-return even though the lordship is finite has been explained in [the discussion of] 'Upon the dissolution of the <s>kārya</s> [world], together with the ruler of that [world], from there [they attain] the Supreme' (<s>Brahmasūtra</s> 4.3.10).

children.text: samyak darśanavidhvasta tamasāṃ tu nityasiddhanirvāṇaparāyaṇānāṃ siddha eva anāvṛttiḥ tadāśrayaṇena eva hi nityasiddhanirvāṇaparāyaṇānāṃ siddhā eva anāvṛttiḥ tadāśrayaṇena eva hi saguṇaśaraṇānām api anāvṛttisiddhiḥ iti /
children.translated_text: But for those whose darkness has been destroyed by right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), who are devoted to the eternally established <s>nirvāṇa</s> — for them, non-return is already accomplished. Indeed, it is only by taking refuge in that [<s>nirguṇa Brahman</s>] that non-return is accomplished even for those who take refuge in <s>saguṇa</s> [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: anāvṛttiḥ śabdāt anāvṛttiḥ śabdāt iti sūtra abhyāsaḥ śāstraparisamāptiṃ dyotayati // 22 //
children.translated_text: The repetition of the <s>sūtra</s> 'Non-return — because of the [scriptural] word; non-return — because of the [scriptural] word' indicates the completion of the <s>śāstra</s>. // 22 //

Those who, through the <s>nāḍīs</s> and rays [of the sun], by the <s>devayāna</s> path with stages beginning with <s>arcis</s> (flame), go to the world of <s>Brahman</s> — [the world] that is described in scripture with specific attributes: 'In the world of <s>Brahman</s> [there are] the lake <s>Ara</s> and [the lake] <s>Ṇya</s>, in the third heaven from here; there is the <s>Aśvattha</s> tree dripping with <s>Soma</s>; there is the city <s>Aparājitā</s> (the unconquered); there is the golden hall measured by the Lord of <s>Brahman</s>' — and which is elaborated in many passages of <s>mantras</s>, <s>arthavādas</s>, and the like — they, having reached that [world], do not return like those who have enjoyed their merits in the world of the moon and the like. Why?

children.text: iti śrīmacchārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣye śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmadgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyaśrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpūjyapādakṛtau caturthādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>pāda</s> of the fourth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Śārīraka-mīmāṃsā-bhāṣya</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, the most venerable <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya</s>. // 4 //

children.text: samāptamidaṃ brahmasūtraśāṅ karabhāṣyam //
children.translated_text: This <s>Brahmasūtra-Śāṅkara-bhāṣya</s> is complete.
